This recipe works best with fat free cream cheese.  The consistancy works out the best for me.  I use this recipe all the time.  Great!!!

Great recipe!  This is exactly what I was looking for.  It is a creamy cheesy sauce, so different from the bland Alfredo sauces I've tried before.  Best of all, it is easy to prepare.

I ended up not using all of the milk (maybe about 1 cup) and adding some salt.  Also, I didn't have any garlic powder, so I added in some fresh minced chives at the very end of cooking.  I also added some frozen peas near the end of cooking for color and texture though that may not be to everyone's taste.  Next time, I might saute some onions and mushrooms and add them, too.
So easy to make and no fuss!!!  Excellent!
If the cream cheese has trouble melting at first, add a little milk to the mix, and the cream cheese liquifies more efficiently.

Made it in a hurry tonight. Very easy to make. Did it while talking on the phone! It was really quite heavy and both my son and I didn't finish our plate. May have been the whole wheat spaghetti we were eating it or could have been the margarine...I don't know. I found it didn't really have a lot of flavour and needed some salt, but when I'm eating my leftovers tomorrow for lunch, I'll toss it with some pesto. Who knows, it might work! lol

Excellent and resturant quality. Here is what I did differently: I had some extra heavy whipping cream left over from the crab soup I made so I used half milk (skim) and half cream. I also didn't have enough cream cheese, I did have some neufchatel cheese so I used it too. (Again, half cream cheese and the other half nuefchatel.) I also used 2 cloves garlic, not garlic powder. Then I added a splash of basil. I threw in some scallops with butter and garlic in a pan and seared each side for a couple of minutes. I topped each plate of fettucine with a couple scallops and a splash of parsley and served it. Everyone loved it. Great!!!
I did not have milk on hand so I used whipping cream and water. Added more garlic because my family likes a lot!
It was quick, easy and delicious.  I added chicken, broccoli and a little extra milk.

I made this sauce to go with another recipe and though I never tasted it alone, my finished product was wonderful!  I believe this sauce was a great contribution to the dish and I will use it from now on when I make meals that require alfredo sauce.
very good!

I really love this sauce. My older son doesn't like tomato sauce on pasta, so I've looked for recipes for alfredo. It is fantastic as written, but I have added fresh herbs, mushrooms, italian sausage at different times; all to great results. Thanks for the recipe. A definite keeper for me.
Made this alfredo sauce twice so far because it's that good! Had the family over for the second time and everyone thought it was great! Loved it! Thank You!

I made this for my family, and the keds really loved it, even my picky daughter who generally doesn't like alfredo.  I made it according to directions, except I used minced garlic instead of granulated, and I added about 1/3 of a 28-oz can of tomato puree to make a tomato alfredo (haven't been able to find a decent recipe for that!).  It turned out wonderful!  However, it didn't thicken up much while it was cooking, but it did while it cooled.  We will definitely make this one again... and again.

I gave it 3 stars because while it was ok, it wasn't exactly a traditional Alfredo sauce. It's more of a cheese sauce. And i used shredded parmesan like someone suggested to get a smoother texture and it was still gritty and left a gritty feeling on my teeth. Gross. If you want traditional alfredo sauce don't use this one.

This was the 2nd time I have attempted to make alfredo from scratch, and this one was a hit! Both my girls even said they liked it better than the jar sauce I usually buy. I only gave it 4 stars because it isn't quite the same consistency as a real alfredo, but it was good. Best of all, I usually have all of these ingredients on hand. Awesome! Thanks!

This Alfredo sauce is the best I've ever had.  It is tasty and light, not too heavy.  I used it over a penne and mushroom dish.  The did decrease the milk to 1-1/2 cups and used a little less then 1/4 cup of grated cheese and it was perfect!!!

Yum! This truly is "easy" -- and delicious! I substituted the butter with lower fat margarine (smart balance), low-fat cream cheese, and used 1% milk - and it was still creamy and tasty. Served it over whole wheat penne, and some blackened chicken breast - and it was great. Will definitely make this one again!

The consistency for this recipe was PERFECT, but I, too, was overpowered by the creamcheese taste. However, the recipe is good enough that I'm going to continue to play with the recipe. If I can tweak it enough, I'll change my rating and share my changes!!!

I made this recipe for the time EVER and my boyfriend loved it. I now have to make it once a week! LOL I did add oregano, minced garlic and added more butter and parmesean cheese, also instead of whole milk I used 2% reduced fat milk and tasted GREAT! I'm not much of an alfredo eater BUT this recipe is by far the BEST I've had.

Wonderful and very rich sauce, I made this for my boyfriend and his parents and they loved it. Most alfredo sauces are solely based on the butter but this one is actually based on the cheese, which makes it even more delicious.
Omg this recipe is amazing!!! Tasted amazing and came out amazing!! Love it!

I don't cook.  At all.  Never really have.  But I had leftover chicken and was desperate to find something my picky teenage daughter would eat.  She recently had surgery and all the meds have really been bothering her stomach and decreasing her appetite.  I  used some light cream cheese in the tub I had in the frig, 1/4 cup butter, 1/4 cup margarine, frozen fresh minced garlic cube and skim milk.  Took others' advice and added more pepper and some oregano (didn't have nutmeg, will definitely get some now).  Also took the advice of adding the parmesan (used shredded paremesan in the tub) before the milk.  Also threw some frozen petite broccoli in with my whole wheat fettucini halfway through.  Not only did my daughter eat two plates, so did my 11 year old son and husband.  My son asked me to make it again and my daughter didn't argue with him.  Thanks so much for posting this and inspiring me to cook!
Quick.  Easy.  Needs salt.

Turned out great. I used whipped cream cheese (since that's what I had on hand) and it was fine. It's not a real thick sauce which is what I prefer. I added butter sautéed frozen shrimp and crumbled up some cooked bacon and voila!! Yum yum dinner per my kids. Served pizza on the side and salad.
Very Easy, Very good.  I reduced the butter by a few TBS and it worked fine.

First of all, don't be surprised if your cream cheese doesn't get smooth before adding the milk. Mine stayed quite granular, but smoothed out as soon as I added the milk. I did add a little nutmeg and that perked it up nicely. My husband is a James Beard award-wining restaurant critic and he enjoyed it, but thought the cream cheese was "a little weird." I called him a Poopy Head and informed him I'd be making it a lot, so he'd better just shut up. I think I have a pretty good palate and thought it was yummy-ummy-umptious. I enjoyed it more than the alfredo sauces at most restaurants and it couldn't be easier. This is a keeper, folks. And can be easily modified to fit your personal preferences.
VERY good. I loved it. I added mushrooms to the chicken before adding the sauce. Yum Yum.

I made this for my son's birthday because he loves fettucini alfredo.  Everyone absolutely loved it!  I have some comments though.  I took other reviewers advice and used 1 cup milk and 1 cup half and half.  The sauce didn't thicken up as well as it could have so I made a roux and threw that in and it turned out fine. Also, I will probably only make this on special occasions as it's so rich and high in fat and calories.  It's an awesome sauce nontheless!
This was great...pretty easy too...took me a bit longer than the 10 minutes though...overall it was a HIT with the wife and kids.
Delicious and creamy!
This was a little cream cheesy but just added some italian spice mix and it was great.

This is fantastic- and really easy- I pair it with very spicy Cajun-style chicken- the cool of the dairy offsets anything spicy very well. One warning! do not use low fat cream cheese! -you can do without the butter but even 2/3 fat cream cheese made this sauce loose its creaminess significantly- thanks for sharing this recipe.

I used light cream cheese and half and half.  It was easily 6-7 servings and pretty thick.  It was really good, my fiance says he'd have it again! I think next time I'd use less butter and maybe add some veggies.  All said and done great dinner!
SO good! The only problem is I want to eat it with a spoon before the pasta is finished. I add a dash of nutmeg.
I made this recipe and it came out disgusting.  I added all of the correct ingredients and it just tasted to much like cream cheese.

Sorry, guess I'll have to stick to my "regular" alfredo sauce.  I followed the directions to the T and it never came together, just stayed a separated mess.  With the addition of the milk, it came together a little, enough so that I could at least use it and not toss it, but it was never smooooooth and creamy like alfredo should be.  Thanks anyway, it was worth a shot.

I loved this recipe!  The sauce was creamy and flavorful, even with the lower calorie changes I made.  I used a stick of 50/50 butter and Omega3 spread, reduced calorie cream cheese, 1 1/2c. skim milk, and 4oz of freshly grated aged parm.  I agree with other posters that whisking the butter and cream cheese was key, as was adding the milk slowly.  I didn't have any issues with lumps, and my hubs was impressed!  This will be my alfredo recipe from now on.

Great! I changed a few things- used minced garlic instead of garlic powder & only like 2oz cream cheese & like 8-10oz Parmesan because I didn't have a full package of cream cheese. Also added a little lemon juice because my bf likes it that way.

Just made it and I like it. It seems to be a very forgiving recipe. I didn't measure anything, and made it all in my vitamix blender. Tossed it all in and Just let it run on high about 7 mins to heat it up and it came out great! I added chopped dried garlic instead of garlic powder, since I was low on milk, did half milk, half heavy cream because that's what I had on hand.

I will make it again!

This is absolutely fabulous!  I put it on angel hair pasta and then threw some shrimp scampi on top.  It passed my teen son's taste test as well and that's a big accomplishment.  I pass this recipe on to anyone who says "I wish I knew how to make alfredo sauce."  It doesn't get any easier than this!  Thank you for sharing!
This is a keeper.  So easy to make with ingredients I generally have in my home.
It's my go-to Alfredo sauce! Love it!

Wow this sauce was fabulous and SO easy! My family absolutely loved it. I doubled the recipe, and sliced up mesquite chicken breasts and tossed into the recipe after it was well blended. I stored the leftover sauce and we had it again 2 days later. Like other reviewers I highly recommend making sure it is well blended first. Because the parmesan cheese is a bit grainy you will want to make sure it is fully melted and blended. Otherwise I made this recipe exactly as written and it was perfect. This one is definitely a keeper and the family has already asked when I am going to make it again.

I love it and will use it again. The only thing I didn't like was how it looked a bit curdled after settling. That may have been because I mixed the sauce and noodles all together so after sitting when I went to put it in Tupperware it looked a little funky. After reheating and stirring it looked fine.

dynamite!!! easily the best alfredo sauce i've ever eaten.. my mother-inlaw who is full italian even said it is better than hers..we added shrimp and veggies to the pasta and it was simply delicious..cant say enough.

I thought this was wonderful! I used lower fat versions of the ingredients and turned out delicious. I used this sauce over cut up grilled chicken, cheese tortelini, and sauteed mushrooms. Toast up some garlic bread and you have such a decadent meal. Yumm!
This was very very tasty.  I had some trouble getting it to thicken up, but that didn't change how yummy it was.
Really good!  I was amazed at how easy it was to make and how good it tasted.  I even froze half of the sauce for another meal and it was just as good the second time around!
LOVED this. All the fam eats this up.

Sooo simple and soooo delicious!!!
A++++++
i had my doubts while making it because of the cream cheese, but this is a genius idea. easy and yummy!
My son and husband can not stop talking about this sauce. it was really good, and easy.
Fantastic! Had the ingrediants on hand. Added some gruiarre cheese for an awesome flavor.

I am so glad I came upon this Alfredo sauce. So quick and easy! I cut this recipe in half since it was just me and still had enough sauce left for another dinner. My only change was I minced one clove of  fresh garlic instead of powder and sautéed in the butter. Served this over crab and shrimp filled ravioli topped with sautéed bay scallops.  Delicious!! This is a keeper for sure!
So easy and so tasty-- my husband now says I make better Alfredo than he does!
So easy and tasty! The cream cheese doesn't come through except to make it creamy.
Wow! I am a novice cook and I was afraid to try making alfredo sauce. It turned out very well and my husband was pleased. Thank you for the EASY recipe.
This was great. All of my family loved it and they can't wait until I fix this again.

LOVE how easy  this is! I followed the recipe exactly the first time. This time I sauteed 1 small onion and 2 garlic cloves in butter. Then added a few finely chopped mushrooms and sauteed until they were cooked through. Then I added 2 cups of frozen peas and about 3/4 cup cubed up roasted chicken breast.  I let that heat through about 4 minutes then transferred it to a bowl. I used the same skillet to follow the original recipe but cut the amount of garlic powder in half. After the cheese was added, I added a Tablespoon of chopped parsley and a few grinds of black pepper. Then I stirred the chicken breast mixture back in.  Just as it started to bubble, I took it off the heat and added it to hot pasta.
I made this exactly as instructed. Big hit with the family. Hubby loved it and he can be picky. Thanks!
Nice and creamy, works best with whole milk or cream, but the best "easy" alfredo sauce I've tried yet.
This was really good and very easy.  Thank you
Really good..if done right it taste pretty close to Olive Gardens sauce (which i love).
Killer recipe.... easy and one of the Alfreado's we;ve had at any price.....

I have a different recipe for alfredo, but couldn't find it.  This was the closest that I could come to mine....this was MUCH better!  Mine always seemed too greasy (butter) and never mixed into a smooth mixture.  I will use this again and again from now on!!!
I didn't have any garlic powder on hand, so I used 1 1/4 teaspoons of garlic salt.  I thought that it was just the right amount of salt.  I only used 2 Tablespoons of butter, also.  This was a very smooth and creamy mixture.
excellent!!!

three stars because although it was ok, it just didnt wow me or my family. I believe this recipe calls for too much cream cheese. I do like the cream cheese but it was just to much. I also added 2 cups heavy cream but it was just too thick, so I added about a 1/2 cup of milk and that helped. Dont skimp on the parmesan because then the sauce would def. taste just like cream cheese. I also added oregano and more pepper and Im glad I did because with out it, it was just to bland. We have left over sauce so Im gonna tweak it again tonight for left overs.
Oh my goodness!!This was so good.  I think I might try it on pizza that calls for white sauce.

SO SO SO DELICIOUS!!! I made a few changes, but the original recipe is excellent, too. I added about half the butter, because mine turned out a little too oily with a whole stick. Also, I did minced garlic instead of garlic powder, and added slightly less milk because I like thicker sauces. Other than that, I went by the recipe. This is soooo delicious, a must for any cream sauce lover!
Easy, rich and creamy!  I followed the directions with no changes and this sauce was fantastic.  I will certainly make it again!
This is an excellent recipe, so simple and easy.  My husband won't eat the store bought alfredo any more.  Thank you.
Tasted more like cream cheese than alfredo.

Mamma Mia!!  This pasta sauce really is quick, easy and delicious!  My family loved it!  I was short 1/4 cup milk so substituted white wine.  Extra parmesan also added to the flavor.  Grilled chicken breast and steamed broccoli made a wonderful meal.  Thanks Dawn!
Just wonderful... that is all I can say about this.
Wonderful recipe! Everyone loved it. Although, I didn't put 6 oz of Parmesan cheese. I used 3 oz of Parmesan and 3 oz of Romano.
Super fast and tasty. The whole family loved it.
delicious! amazing! and so simple and inexpensive.
Quick and easy. I used 8 oz. cream cheese and extra gaarlic.

So easy! Great taste! Never buying jarred sauce again. I thought it was going to be a buttery mess for a bit with the cream cheese, it just wouldn't incorporate, but once you put the milk in, it all comes together perfectly. I added a little dried basil and parsley for some color and taste. Fresh grated parmesan is a must for flavor! Thanks for the recipe!
Didn't taste like any Alfredo I've ever had. It had no real taste to it - sure, it was creamy and garlicky, but even with some other added spices to try and jazz it up, it was disappointing.
This was amazingly easy and is the best Alfredo sauce I have ever made ...
This is great!  I use this all of the timenow.  Thank you.
AWESOME - SAUCE!! I cut the milk to 1-1/2c. added parsley, also some bacon bits and tossed the whole thing with elbow macaroni. Can;t wait to use this as a base for Tomato Cream sauce!

I had high hopes for this recipe, but it didn't reach them. This sauce was not exactly my cup of tea. When I was done making the sauce to the tee, it didn't taste all that amazing, so I added 1/4 tsp basil, and 1/4 cup mozzarella cheese to it, which seemed to make it more flavorful, and I liked how the mozzarella made it more cheesy. The sauce wasn't horrible, it's just not something I would probably make on a weekly, or even monthly basis. Maybe if I had the ingredients at hand, I would give it another shot.

Excellent! The flavor did not taste at all like cream cheese to me. I added extra garlic powder to the butter, and some basil paste. Also, I only used a 1 1/2 cups of milk as the sauce was pretty thin. I added 2 cups each of diced ham and green peas and served over fettuccine. Delish!!

This sauce turned out very well.  However, you have to serve it immediately, because it tends to thicken up rather quickly.  I didn't have plain cream cheese, so in a pinch, substituted chive and onion cream cheese, which complimented it nicely.  Leftovers of this dish were tasty also!

Best, easiest Alfredo I've ever made!  I tried this out a year or more ago now and It gets made frequently.  I have made this for company or just a regular family supper.  My four year old loves it as chicken broccoli alfredo....and So do I.  I always get compliments on this meal.  Delish!

I just made this! Like another reviewer I couldn't stop TASTING it!! I didn't bother to use garlic powder, I used fresh minced garlic. I sent my brother to the market a few hours ago to get jarred sauce...but I will be returning the jarred sauce to the market today. Never again will I use jarred sauce. Thanks for this great recipe!!
really easy recipe but awesome taste. Compares to the ones served in restaurants. THANKS
The best Alfredo Sauce I've ever tasted.  Everyone loved it!
Excellent!  So good and rich and creamy and ymummy!!!
The best!! I used minced garlic & added chicken & shrimp. My husband & very picky daughter said it was better then any restaurant.
I changed the amount of cream cheese I added but other than that everything was great...I love it!

For a homemade sauce, this is quick, easy and tasty! And the only things I did different was to use fresh garlic instead of powdered and added a dash of nutmeg. The only reason why I didn't give this five stars was the whole stick of butter! It makes it taste good but, holy moly! The coronary! :o)
easy, quick, tasty, but very high in calories!

I thought this was really good! I used light cream cheese, and skim milk, and instead of butter used smart balance with omega 3 along with adding a touch of low fat mozzarella cheese, garlic and herb seasoning, two tablespoons of reduced sodium cream of mushroom soup and a dollop of light sour cream to make it a little extra creamy. came out fantastic and my whole family loved it!
WOW!  This was easy, actually reheated unlike other Alfredo sauces and was super easy.  The cream cheese makes it.  Don't use fat-free.  It just didn't taste right.  The texture was off.

Ok, so I can't eat dairy right now because I'm breastfeeding and my baby can't tolerate it. Alfredo is my favorite food group and i was dying without it. I was able to find a vegan cream cheese spread, and vegan grated parmesean topping. i subbed almond milk for regular milk. I did use the butter, but probably would have been ok subbing olive oil if needed to be completely dairy free. It was pretty good. Only slightly worse than the dairy version. I'm giving this 4 stars because I have an amazing alfredo recipe that no other recipe can beat, and I can't wait to get back to making that one!
Quick, easy and versitile.  I added chicken and spinach for a great meal, second time I added chicken and diced tomatoes.

This is OK, though I really wasn't all that impressed. I think that the cream cheese is way to overpowering. Usually I'm a cream cheese finatic, but this is just too much. I prefer a cream and wine alfredo suace I think. Sorry :(

This recipe is very good and very easy to make.  I usually tweak recipes a lot but followed this fairly closely. I didn't have any fresh garlic  which I would have preferred, so I used the powder instead.
It takes a little patience to make...I would tell other people who had trouble to let the cream cheese soften slightly before starting to cook, cut it into smaller blocks so its easier to combine. Once the cream cheese breaks down in the pan (part way) add a small amount of milk and whisk. Add the milk bit by bit and continue to whisk.
And lastly....use REAL Parmesan or Pecorino Romano (I prefer Romano)...it may be more expensive but its so much better than that junk in the green can - buy a block and grate it yourself, your taste buds and your dinner guests will thank you!! You will also see that the sauce doesn't come out gritty at all....the Parmesan should melt very easily wi no grit. 
So, overall...I'm not a fan of cheese or cream sauces but this was tasty, was not overly rich and most importantly, everyone in my family of 5 will eat it, so this will become an addition to our monthly meal plan! Thanks for posting!!
I can't get mine to thicken quiet enough, until it is cold! but it's still very tasty!!
I was about to use a jar of alfredo for my shrimp but decided to make this one and I honestly did not expect it to be this good! It was delicious and better than some restaurant alfredo!

this was definately a great and easy alfredo sauce.  Next time I will cut back on the garlic and also I will use fresh parmesean to get rid of some of the grainy texture.  Would be great with shrimp alfredo.
This is a good alfredo recipe. It's so fast and easy! I love alfredo and I'm always looking for new ways to make it. This is a definite keeper. Perfect for a quick and easy meal.
This recipe is everthing it claims...quick, easy and tastes fantastic.
I made this for my father who despises white sauce of any kind and he thought it was great!
I used this as a "sauce" to drizzle over the fillings of our Lettuce Leaf Tacos. After the sauce thickened, I wisked in about a cup of cotija cheese. Excellent sauce.
I was looking for a sauce that I had at a restaurant here in Puerto Vallarta. This is great! I use it on shrimp and wings.
Multi use sauce! Creamy and Spicy... love the smokey flavor! Tis Hot!!!

Easy and refreshing. The recipe as written will make about 1 gallon. I had to cut the recipe in half since my ice cream freezer is a 2 quart. I will definately keep this recipe handy. It really is very good. Thanks!
The recipe is great. I blended the pineapple in the blender before adding it to the other ingredients. This achieved a smoother end result since I don't care for the larger chunks.

I didn't like it, but my husband did. It turned out very dry and almost flaky. I also thought the sweetened condensed milk gave it a strange taste mixed with the orange flavor. I may try it again but I'm not sure what to adjust.

This was super easy and tasty. Only change I made was I only used 3 cans of soda. I'm not sure what type of ice cream maker the original recipe writer has, but I'm pretty sure more than three cans and you'd have overflow... But, other than that, it's a terrific refreshing dessert.

I halved the recipe and tweaked the fresh orange juice to sweetened condensed milk ratio. I also reduced the orange soda amount to 2/3rds of the halved amount. Ended up using: 3/4 cup fresh squeezed blood orange juice, 1/3rd of a 2 liter bottle of orange soda, half a can of crushed pineapple and 2/3rds a can of sweetened condensed milk. Turned out splendidly! Sweet, fruity and not overly sugary. Seriously good. The blood orange juice made it a pleasing raspberry color.
Found this really refreshing!

I made this for Thanksgiving, and to my surprise it was actually pretty easy!  I used a wicker serving basket with cloth napkins, to set it in, and filled it with fruit.  Everyone loved it- thought I had made something super special!  All the fruit got eaten and most of the cornucopia remained- so I made bread pudding out of it!  I made it again for Christmas upon request, only that time the fruit and ALL the bread got eaten!  Just make sure the bread dough is pressed/pinched well to the adjoining pieces : )

I just made this with my husband. I only had 12 inch wide aluminum foil, which worked fine. I skipped the egg part for joining them together. As long as you work the breadsticks together they should look fine. Mine might have come out a bit smaller than others, due to the aluminum foil thing, but it looks yummy. I baked at center rack for 350 for about 30 minutes instead of the 45 because it was starting to brown, even though I covered it in tinfoil in some spots on the top. Aluminum foil came out very easily. Will eat tomorrow with Thanksgiving. Going to stuff it with carrots/broccoli and cauliflower.
Easy to make and looks amazing for a centerpiece, was told this must be a new yearly tradition!

The dough was a little tricky to work with and hard to hide the seams but the presentation was worth it. Such a pretty centerpiece! This freezes well so you can definitely make it several days beforehand.
This is a great recipe, I've made it three times and have never had any problems.

I made this for a Thanksgiving dinner I was invited to. I am not a great cook but love to try new things, especially when it is for a party. This was a total hit!!! I had so many compliments.
I did take the advice of others and used the egg/water mix at the end to massage together pieces that were not sticking together well.  I also recommend keeping the breadstick rolls in the fridge and pulling out one at a rime. The colder the dough, the easier it was to form.
Good recipe but make sure you spray the foil a lot!  Had to make a second one after the first stuck pretty badly to the foil.  Also make sure you can get the foil out (if you want it out)

I made this as a trial run for Thanksgiving. I used a disposable cookie sheet, wrapped it with foil and extended it up at the end for the "tail", covered it with strips of French bread dough I made in the bread machine. It turned out great and wasn't nearly as much work as it looks!

I made this for Thanksgiving this year. Didn't get a chance to photo it, but it was so much fun to make. I made the foil shape a week or so ahead of time as not to run out of foil the day of and my youngest thought it was a dead fish with it's head cut off before I started the actual process of wrapping it with bread stick dough. Which was soo funny.  Will make this again for future centerpieces. It was a great way to draw attention to the table. TY

This was such a cute idea.  The compliments overflowed just like my Cornucopia did!  I baked mine in a convection oven and it only took 30 minutes for the braid to be beautifully brown(covered the braid with foil at that point to protect it from overbrowning), and an additional 10 minutes for the rest of it to cook to a golden brown.  I too, recommend 2 people to handle the dough for ease of wrapping it around the foil form.  Thanks for the idea!
So easy to make! Followed the directions and it came out perfect. Everyone loved it and I got rave reviews! Thanks for the amazing idea.

Had a little trouble with the bread sticks sliding off the form.  probably because I used too much Pam but I was worried it would stick otherwise.  I used a heavy tin disposable baking sheet as the base.  After initially opening the oven door a few times to replace the dough that had slipped,  it finally baked and browned fine and was a unique addition to the table.
I made this last year on thanksgiving, and loved it, well worth the time. I filled it with frosted peacans and assorted nuts.
This was so fun and easy to make. We loved having it on our table for Thanksgiving, and enjoying it for the following weekend.

This came out very well for me.  I overstretched the breadsticks and when they baked they cracked on the bottom of the cornucopia.  No big deal, the veggies inside covered that.  Also, don't curve the end part too much, because I had a hard time getting the foil out and the end piece partially broke.  Once again, not a big deal, since it wasn't even noticable.  Best part was the WHOLE thing was edible, yummy yummy

my friends and i did a trial run of this recipe for thanksgiving, it was a fun recipe to do with a crowd!!! our centerpieces turned out SUPER and we will be putting bread and rolls in it for dinner.  We also think that this recipe makes a wonderful hostess gift!! Maybe even a house warming gift filled with mouthwatering rolls, breads, muffins !!!
Easy as pie to make...now my family thinks I'm a genius !!!
Very awesome item! My family was very impressed with the one I made for the centerpiece of our Christmas dinner. I used it to hold the rolls, etc for dinner! Thanks so much for sharing!
First magazine had a real similar recipe but braided. I used frozen bread dough ( 2 loaves) & this turned out great. I baked it 30 min. Much less expensive than the bread stick dough.
B-E-A-UTIFUL!! It was fun to make and great to munch on. I believe this will become a staple of our household for Thanksgiving dinners!

I made this for a centerpiece and it turned out perfect!  I recommend using a throw away cookie sheet with the raised edge cut off as the cone since it is more stable.  I was able to make this by myself since it was more sturdy, also if you overlap the bread stick as you wrap it around the mold it won't slip off as some people commented on.  Definitely will make this for many years to come!!
Made this for Thanksgiving! Very easy to make, just follow the instructions. Will do this every year now.
I loved making this.  I used it as my bread basket for Thanksgiving dinner - I put fresh made corn muffins, bread sticks and dinner rolls in the cornucopia and it was beautiful.
Definately have two people, looks fantastic when done

I used the instructions here with my bread machine breadstick dough.   I used 2 large (2 lb) batches and had a little dough left for breadsticks.  I filled it with red grapes and various cubed cheeses and it was well worth the time.  I put a little foil under the grapes to keep it from getting soggy. After Thanksgiving, I cut the open part off straight, several inches back from the opening.  Then set it on the cut end.  I froze it and plan to put a roll in it to use as "floral foam".  Rosemary sprigs will be stuck in that and perhaps a few little chocolate ornaments will finish it  off as a Christmas centerpiece.  The rest of the cornucopia I cubed and will use in bread pudding.  Thanks for the wonderful instructions!
This was a striking centerpiece, filled with vegie crudites.  We will definitely do this again. It's fun to do this with teenagers, as  they enjoy the creative aspect of preparing food.

I LOVE this! I made it for Thanksgiving and it was so easy and everyone praised it! I didn't brush it with butter or egg and it come out perfect! One bit of advice I would give, is don't stretch the dough to much as you wrap it around the aluminum foil because it will cause issues and as it bakes it may split and you will end up with holes here and there. I did also make a bowl to but dip in. I used the ame technique as the cornucopia and it turned out wonderful! I had made a lattes pattern for the bottom and it was so neat looking! I may try and use that same pattern on my next cornucopia!

This was an amazing centerpiece/appetizer at Thanksgiving dinner. Looked so cool, we didnt want to destroy it or throw it away, so I filled it with bird seed and let our feathered friends enjoy it on the back porch. We will be making this every year!

My husband helped me make this (and I'm glad he did, I can see how making this by myself would have been frustrating!) and it "wowed" everyone this Thanksgiving!  My mom was so impressed she made it the centerpiece of the appetizer table.  This will be a yearly tradition for sure.

This was great.  But wasn't very child-friendly as written.  Here is an easier way:  purchase a disposable pizza-pan (as shown in the All Recipes video) or a smallish rectangle (with low edges).  I couldn't find a pizza pan anywhere, but the rectangular disposable pan turned out even better IMO.  Manipulate into a cone/cornucopia shape.  Do NOT spray cone with cooking spray (although it is good to spray the baking sheet you plan to place the cornucopia on).  Wrap with bread stick dough as written.  Pinch edges well or some pieces may come apart while baking.  If braiding is too difficult, then simple 'twists' are fine around the opening.  The disposable pan holds it shape much better than foil and it's easy to fill.  My 5 year old did all the wrapping while I 'helped' by holding the cone in place.  This will be an annual tradition.  :)
So easy, use less or add more for different sizes.

Fairly simple to assemble. For some reason, I only required 2 (11 ounce) containers of bread sticks! But it came out just fine. I needed to put foil over the tip and braid about halfway through cooking to prevent burning. I made this a week before Christmas, froze it with the foil inside, and defrosted on Christmas Eve. It made a wonderful display on my dinner table - I filled it with grapes and vegetables. Thanks!
Great idea. Mine just came out of the oven after 35 minutes perfect golden brown.  Will make changes to how I constructed, no fault of recipe.

I made this to use as a Thanksgiving centerpiece.  Everyone thought it was adorable and I got a lot of compliments, but they didn't know that I had covered up a hole because the breadsticks had slid after I put it in the oven.  My advice would be to check on it after a short time, while you could still fix it if holes appear where the bread sticks should overlap.  Otherwise, it wasn't that hard.  Would also recommend 2 people for the job.

A few years ago, I saw bread cornucopia at a Thanksgiving party. So I always make it since then. Looks great with veggies! I served it with Avocado dressing (from this site).
Update: I make it every year now, but I use paulas breadsticks recipe for the dough.
This was so pretty, my family was afraid to eat it so I was the first to tear off a piece! We love fresh veggies and fruit, so nothing went to waste.

Very easy to make! I use one can of crescent rolls and one can of bread sticks. I shape my cornucopia with foil and lightly spray the foil with cooking spray. I then wrap the crescent rolls around the foil pinching the pieces together to connect them. I use the bread sticks to make the braid. I also picked up a tip from another review and used toothpicks to hold it together while baking. I have made this using only bread sticks and it was not as successful, the crescent rolls work so much better and look better as a finished product I highly recommend doing it this way. Allow it to cool completely before trying to remove the foil, if you have trouble getting the foil out try pulling it in a twisting motion. Also I only use the egg wash for the top of the cornucopia I never use it to hold the dough together as it makes everything very messy, slippery, and wet resulting in a very difficult time putting it all together.

I wanted to make this as my husband does all the cooking and gets all the glory on Thanksgiving.  It turned out PERFECT!  Figuring out the foil was a little tricky but I got it!  Also, they didn't have refrigerated bread sticks, so I used the roll out dough that you can cut.  It worked great.  I just cut them into stripes.  I stuffed mine with crackers and served with pepperoni, mozzarella, and a variety of italian meat.  Toward the end of the platter someone asked if they could eat the bread, and they said it was yummy!

This was so much fun! My first attempt had bumps and the dough slid off the mold when it got warm.  I stuck toothpicks in my second one to keep the warm dough from sliding off the mold and instead of attaching new pieces as I went around (this is how I got bumps) I attached each piece to its self on the underside of the mold where the bumps can not be seen.  I will submit a picture of precooked with toothpicks and the final product so you can see what I'm talking about.

This came out great!! I wasn't able to find breadstick dough but I used Philsbury sheet of dough and then sliced sticks from it! After reading comments I thought I would need more hands so I got my most creative friend but this was soo easy one pair of hands works fine!
Awesome and easy!
I filled mine with a variety of dinner rolls for a wonderful Thanksgiving centerpiece. Thanks for the great idea.

This is awesome. I had to use pizza dough, because I couldnt find breadstick dough, and it came out great. I  only had to use 2 containers of the pizza dough. Tricky to get the foil out though, I ended up having to leave the tiny bit of foil at the very tip because it tore and got stuck. Maybe I didnt spray it enough.
This was amazing! Followed directions to a T! Turned put perfect! Only problem, no one wanted to eat the veggies because it was so pretty! Lol

I just finished with the conucopia for thanksgiving, it turned out fantastic. I can hardly wait for the oohs and ahs from everyone. Thanks so much for posting. It was a very fun recipe to make

This turned out better than I thought and was  much easier than I'd envisioned.  I didn't have any trouble with slippage but the braid did fall off during baking.  I think it was too heavy.  I pinned it back in place with wood picks.  Can't wait to fill it with fresh cut veggies - it will be a conversation piece as well as a nice change from the old "relish tray"!
I had trouble getting the pieces to stick together but was surprised at the result.  looked great. thanks
I thought this was a wonderful centerpeice. I got rave reviews. Fun to make. I also sprinkeled Italian seasoning on top before I baked it. I will be making it again.

What a great recipe! I did it on a lark and was very pleased with the results. (And my husband was too, surprisingly.) It does help if you have experience doing craftsy projects, especially for wrapping the dough around the foil cone, but it's not a requirement.

this was extremely easy for someone who is not a fancy baker.  i didn't even use the glaze except to adhere the braided piece to the rest of the horn.  then the glaze over the whole piece gives it such a nice golden brown color.  will definitely make again!

I just made this for the second time and it looks so impressive when finished.  I found this very easy and did not need more than one person.  Last year, I made it for the first time and was too picky with my foil shape and over worked it trying to make it look like a perfect cornucopia.  This time I was less fussy and it comes out great once dough is on it and wrapped.  I will fill it with veggies and serve for Thanksgiving tomorrow.  My suggestion is work quickly with the dough.  As it warms, it expands and can get a little tacky.  You need not be fussy with it, it will turn out great.  Breadstick dough is pricey, I remember using an alternative last year as someone suggested, but couldn't remember which of the pillsbury doughs it was.  I definitely give this 5 stars!
This was amazing!!! Really easy, absolutely gorgeous and tasty, too. I will make this every year.

This looked very impressive as a centerpiece. I cut out a section of plastic wrap and put the cornucopia on the plastic on the table. I used a half of a red cabbage for my dip container. 
The dough is VERY SLIPPERY, I recommend two people do this and you have to work very quickly. One more helpful hint. I did not spray the foil with the cooking spray, instead I used that Reynolds Release foil with the non-stick side on the outside that the dough would touch, worked very well.

This was SUCH an amazing idea!!!  I only had 2 packages of breadstick dough, so I made my horn'a'plenty with no bottom (but you totally couldn't tell) and then I just brushed it with melted butter before sticking it in the oven. Fun project but beware when shaping the curved end. When mine baked it formed a perfect replica of the male genitalia. We had a good laugh over it since we were all adults but would not be appropriate for children. Guests were impressed.
This is a wonderful center. Not hard to make and I filled it with Frosted Pecans bites. I also made leaf's with cookie cutter and extra dough then  attached before baking. looked even more festive.

This was perfectly easy for a great centerpiece. We put the fresh veggies inside lining the bottom with plastic wrap so it wouldn't get soaked and yucky. fun to make and received so many compliments! Such a decorative piece, I served fruit but there are so many different ways to present this!

I am so excited how well this turned out. My guests will be so impressed (my husband was!) It was much easier than I thought and I only ended up using 2 cans of breadsticks. Looks like something from a professional bakery! Thanks!!!

Very clever idea! However, my grocery store didn’t have refrigerated bread sticks dough, but did have refrigerated French bread dough. After reading the label where it says to “place dough seam-side down”, I took a chance and bought 3 11-oz tubes. The dough does unroll, leaving one large rectangle. I placed one on a silicone baking mat, placed the form on top with the opening of the cornucopia at one corner of the bread dough, cut around the form on both sides, but leave some to wrap up and around the tail. The 2nd roll went on top of the form with the short edge of the dough rectangle at the open end of the cornucopia. Leaving 5/8” or so to tuck under the bottom layer, trim away dough along both sides, leaving some near the tail to continue covering that part. Use cut-off pieces to patch any holes, then roll out the remaining scraps and cut 5/8” strips for the braid. So only 2 11-oz packages of French bread dough is needed.
This seems an easier, and less time-consuming project than winding strips around the form. As other reviewers’ suggested, I also covered the form with non-stick foil (non-stick side out) to avoid the oil spray which seems to allow the dough to slip off; and, my husband was nearby to provide extra hands; but I was able to do it alone since no wrapping was involved.I braided the strips on the edge of the form.
