Tastes like a tart lemonade. Very good. But absolutely EXCELLENT when made with Sake.
Careful - these go down so smoothly!  Would add more lime juice to cut some of the sweetness of the limeade.  Love the graham crackers!

For the graham cracker crust, try dipping the martini glass edge in lime juice and then into a container of finely powdered graham crackers.  It is like adding the salt to a margarita - the finishing touch!!

I made this drink this weekend for a family bbq..they were great! I added 1/2 cup of half and half and 1/2 cup of water to cut the sour of the limeade mix a little..I topped them off with whipped cream!! I will definately make these again.

This was great.  I had minimal ingredients and a friend coming over for a cocktail and it was a hit. Now I have a reason to buy vanilla extract in bulk.  Thanks for a simple easy recipe.  I didn't have any limes so I did without but I would only imagine that it would make it better.  They definitely go down a little too easy but considering the vodka to limeaid ratio I knew what I was getting myself into.
Maybe I did something wrong with these--I didn't think that they tasted at all like the pie nor did they taste good at all.
I knew this was going to be sour so I dipped the rim of my martini glass in sugar. This did not taste like key lime pie to me.
This was another BOMB, I love lime and I love margaritas, this was a total disappointment in taste
this tastes nothing like the pie!!!         Trust me on this!
YUM!  This was delicious.  I used frozen peaches and it turned out fantastic.

I was excited to make this because it was rated so well. I took it to a get together of friends. Thankfully they were all FRIENDS because this really wasn't that great. The texture was odd and a little runny and it was TOO sweet. I was not impressed.
Mine turned out like peach soup- recipe did not say to pour off the peach juice.

Very nice.  I cut down the white sugar a bit and added abt /4 cup more graham crackers.  This is not really a torte to me, although it's not really a cake in my opinion either.  With more peaches it would end up more like a cobbler, which might be a cool idea for next time.  This is plenty sweet even without the full amount of sugar, and it's easy and fun to make.  The topping sort of absorbed into the peaches, so I might not do that again--I might do a cinnamon sugar layer instead.  Thanks for the recipe!

I definitely enjoyed the taste of this cake, but I cut down the sugar to 1/2 cup, which was enough for me. If I made it again I would add less milk because I think the batter was too runny. That might also help the peaches brown a little.
I made this exactly as directed. It looked gorgeous and tasted delicious.  I would definitely make this again.

I used 1/2 package of vanilla instant pudding mix and 1 small package of Kellogg's Frosted Flakes (crumbled) instead of the 3/4 cup sugar to make the cake more firm and not-as-sweet. The result is pretty good. Worth a try. ^-^.

very good. don't overbake this cake, the special flavor of the crackers combines wonderfully with it being so moist. i added 1/4 tsp. peach extract to the batter and it was definatelly a special cake.
i'm a beginner. i'm trying hard to learn how to cook and bake for my family. this is the first (of a series of cakes) that i baked for the family and all of them really enjoyed it! ^_^

Hmmm...this crust would have made a good cookie.  I loved the fact that it only took me about 5 minutes to make and it used melted butter rather than room temp.  I paired this with a French Silk Chocolate Pie which was a bad idea..(I should have used a more delicate crust).  I think this would be good with maybe a pumpkin or lemon pie.  I'm giving this 4 stars for the ease and taste..(it was like a pecan shortbread).  Thanks for sharing.

I almost rated this at four stars due to the crust sticking to the bottom of the pie pan but thought better of it as I might have left it cook too long, plus I used coconut instead of pecans.  Sweet, but not too sweet, crunchy, and best yet, EASY.  My kind of pie crust...a no-brainer for non-bakers! Thanks so much Sara!

If you're looking for a tastier alternative to a graham cracker crust, this is it.  It's pretty yummy.  I don't know how you could get enough out of this recipe to use half for the crust and half for topping.  It has to be miswritten.  My modifications:  I toasted the pecans for a more intense flavor.  I also toasted some coconut and ground it up in my food processor and added that in.  The nuts and coconut came out to about 3/4 cup, so I decreased the flour by 1/4 cup.  That was a good change, and was awesome with coconut cream pie.
Absolutely delicious. I would make this crust again and again; I think it will go quite well with a pumpkin or sweet potato pie.

It's very tasty. Very simple and is a snap to make. I had this crust paired up with chocolate pudding mixed with 1/2 a tub of coolwhip and used the other 1/2 for the topping. My friends raved about it at a party.

I loved this recipe. This was my first time ever making a pie crust, and it was quick, easy and the best crust I have ever eaten. The first one I made with the pecans was a little difficult to press into the pan but was good, the second without the pecans was easy to press and tasted heavenly. 

I made this with the cinnamon pie recipe on this site and with the first one sort of overpowered the taste of the filling, but the second one complimented it perfectly because I added a little cinnamon. If you are not so big on pecans like me, I would recomend making this without them and adding a tbls of cinnamon and/or nutmeg.
Excellent!

Absolutely fantastic recipe!  I made it exactly like the recipe but used a lightly greased 10 inch glass  pie pan instead of the 9 inch. I used the whole recipe for the crust instead of saving half of it for the topping and it covered the pan nicely.  I did not bake it before putting the filling in.  I made the Cinnamon Pie from this site that was submitted by Sharon Miller and the crust complimented the pie superbly!  This is a real keeper.  Would have given it 10 stars if I could.  Will be making this often.

This crust was wonderful as a flan base. I pressed all the ingredients into a flan pan and after it was cooked and cooled, I filled it with a cool whip/cream cheese/sugar mixture and topped it with fresh peaches and raspberries. I let it chill in the fridge. So easy, delicious and different. I'll be using this recipe a lot!

I loved this have made it more than a few times - always sooo tasty, I did change one thing and I have continued to do so - I use 1/2 cup of flour and 1/2 cup of rolled quick cooking oats instead of 1 whole cup of flour.  thanks for such a wonderful recipe!

I have been baking and cooking since I was 10 years old. I have never gotten the knack for anything that has to be rolled out. This is a great recipe for those of us that are challenged in this way. Everything about this recipe was 5 star. Easy, quick and delicious! I made it for dessert for Easter Sunday. I made the Old Fashioned Coconut Cream Pie from this site. Everyone raved about the pie. My family considers me a good cook, but even I have to admit this pie was exceptional. It will be on the most requested list for our family holidays from now on. I wouldn't even think of any other pie crust for any cream pie from now on. The only thing I did differently from the recipe was to use it all for the crust on a 9" pie. I did not save any for the top as I had home made whipped cream with toasted coconut for the top of my pie. Please, please, please try this, you will not be disappointed! Thank you for a great recipe!

This is a fabulous crust. I used it with a custard pie and it added tremendously to the pie. I substituted the margarine with oil - something I'm normally leery to do with pie crusts - but it was fine.

I was not impressed with this crust.  It was certainly easy to make and it was sufficent with the custard pie that I made, but it just lacked the flavor needed for me to give it a 5.  A tip:  if using this crust with a cooked pie (as opposed to a bannana cream or something) DO NOT COOK THE CRUST SEPERATELY!  It will be overcooked.

This was my first attempt at making crust from scratch and it was EXCELLENT!! I didn't have any pecans so I used almonds instead. My husband loved it and it couldn't have been easier or quicker. If you're like me and terrible at rolling things out then this recipe is definitely for you.

Yummy, this crust was good. Ironically though, I am not a fan of most nuts so I substituted with Grape Nuts cereal and that worked very well. Very easy to prepare. This is also excellent with cheesecake. Great variation from boring old graham crackers!!

This Recipe was fantastic, Highly recommend, except before baking I would suggest
sticking the crust with a fork before baking to prevent any bubbles from forming.
totally delicious, even my non-crust eating teenager gobbled it up..

Awesome, fast and easy.  I made one crust as stated for a coconut custard pie, then one with roasted peanuts for a peanut butter pie.  Awesome!  Loved the crust as much as the pie.  Do not however pre-bake if you are going to bake the filling.  Leave it uncooked, fill then bake.  Excellent.

This was delicious.  I surfed the net since I had extra pie filling but lacked pie crust.  Perfect pumpkin pie (using walnuts).  I'm not an avid cook and was very pleased how easy this was to make!  Hopefully I will find more receipes like this one!!!
Delicious and easy. I cannot roll a piecrust so this recipe is perfect for me. I used a little coconut along with the nuts.
This was the first pie crust I have ever made. I baked a perfect pie crust to compliment a coconut cream pie.
Super Easy & great for many differnt types of pies. Used this with the Cinnamon Pie from this site and it was really good. Thanks for sharing.
A wonderful complement to a no bake cheesecake (try No Bake Cheesecake I on this site) that everyone raved about.  I made no changes.

did not love this crust.  enjoyed the idea of not having to roll out the dough, but in practice it was a pain in its own way.  the dough was very dry and crumbly. I added another 2 tsp. of butter and that barely  helped.  then I prebaked it for about 8 min.  Used it with the cinnamon pie recipe from this site, but that pie cooks for like and hour and the crust was seriously over done by that point.  I guess the flavor was good, on the parts at the bottom that didn't burn, but overall, not loving this recipe.

This rating is probably mostly my fault.  I only had walnuts on hand, so used them instead.  Would be much better with the pecans, I'm sure.  Also, This didn't make much crust for me.....I only ended up with a bottom crust.  Not sure how I could've messed that up.  I might try this again, as it's easy enough, and maybe I can figure out where I went wrong.
Perfection!  Toasted the pecans, then used  this crust with Sweet Potato Pie.  This amount made one pie crust; don't pre-bake crust, gets pretty dark with baking.
This crust just makes the pie filling seem like something you add to have the excuse to eat the crust.  YUMMY! and easy too.
best buttery crunch crust with cinnamon pie
I loved this crust! I used a ceramic pie plate and had difficulty getting the crust out intact. Next time I'll grease the pan.

This is so good, I could eat it plain.  I used this with a cream cheese cake recipe, using cream cheese and condensed milk...  It was excellent.  Today, I'm making my mom's rhubarb bars with this crust for a variation!
An easy way to jazz up canned, condensed soup.
Loved this soup. I didn't change anything. Everyone I have served it to has told me they enjoyed it very much. Goes great a long with salad.

Still tasted like condensed soup to me... but the onions and peas did give it a lift.  I used "Roasted Garlic" flavor condensed mushroom soup, as it was what I had on hand. Found it too plain via the recipe, so added a pinch of cayenne pepper and a few twists of fresh black pepper as well.  A friend liked it, but she's dieting and cheated by trying... If you like/are used to canned condensed soup, you will like this.
my family loved this soup. i added chopped carrots and frech white mushrooms, the soup was great thank you for your recipe.
Tastes like canned mushroom soup with stuff in it.
amazing! a simple, quick recipe that is absolutely fabulous! the sour cream gives a great flavor! i also added celery and mushrooms to add to the flavour.
I sauteed up some fresh mushrooms and added those, also some pepper.

A Fresher/Healthier Option (I made up on the fly): I used the 98% Fat Free Mushroom Soup. I subbed fresh asapargus (coursely chopped) for the frozen peas. I sauteed fresh sliced baby Bella mushrooms, yellow onion, and the asparagus. I try to keep my butter intake light, so cut back on some of the butter & added some olive oil to make up the difference for the sautee. I added herbs to the sautee mix (garlic salt, garlic powder, a pinch of dill, a dash of black pepper, and some freshly chopped parsley). Instead of Sour Cream, I used Laughing Cow Light Swiss wedges (Qty 3). It turned out great, and my skeptical boyfriend was singing praises once he actually tried it. Definitely making this again! I loved how thick the soup turned out too.
This is a surprisingly good shortcut to enhancing a can of cream of mushroom soup. The results were very good and I thank you so much for the recipe.
good, milk can be substituted with water

OMG! This is a favorite new recipe! Had last minute guests & had to raid the fridge and pantry.  Used sweet onion, chopped celery, a container of sliced brown mushrooms. Before I chopped the above ingredients and then sauteed, I chopped 6 small red and purple potatoes,added evoo, tarragon, a sea salt herb blend and then oven roasted for about a half hour. Then I blended all the veggies and potato together, added the soup (3 cans & 3 cups milk)sour cream and peas. EVERYONE went WILD over this !! Didn't share my secret since the unexpected guests are food snobs. Served w/ a spinach salad.  Have also made it since, omitted the potato and served over brown rice or herb and wild rice---in this instance, used a little less milk, instead of soup it's a savory sauce. Thanks Lois for a fabulous recipe, I would NEVER had tried this w/ canned soup before!
Universally it appears that the reviewers with the poor reviews did not follow any of the tips offered by the reviewers with the good reviews. ;)
Great recipe...easy to make and tasted wonderful.

I didn't think you could deepen the flavor of a recipe that pretty much had one main ingredient, but it's amazing what a little lemon oil will do! Loved the intensity it brought. My rinds were fairly thin so I just put them cut-side down into a 9x9 Pyrex, layered the sugar on top, then poured the hot water over it when it was time. Because the lemons floated, I flipped them over to not get any of the bitter pith to seep into the mixture and as it sat, the aroma was amazing! Be aware of the size of your lemons too, as well as their tartness. My lemons were small/medium-sized and a not as tart, so I could have added a bit more lemon juice to balance the sugar, or else cut back the sugar a little, but when poured over ice it helped balance the flavors too, and was a wonderfully refreshing drink!

I have made this exactly as it is instruced many times, and loved it. Eventually I played around with the number of lemons (4), and amount of sugar (scant 1 cup) to get it to my personal taste. I have found that when lemons are not on sale, I will switch out a few lemons for a few limes and it is just as wonderful.

This is how I make lemonade when I have the time. The zest makes it really special. For an extra kick, try adding a few white pepper corns when you heat the water. it adds a demension to the zest that is really, Really special.
Refreshing drink, especially on a hot day. I used stevia rather than sugar. Will certainly make again. Thanks for sharing!
This is THE lemonade recipe, the way to go.  It's not really much trouble, but it's DELICIOUS and the perfect blend of sweet and sour.

Using the lemon peel really made a difference with the colour of the lemonade. It was a beautiful pale yellow. The taste however was too lemony. I'm looking for something with more of a balance. Will keep trying!
I made the recipe exactly as described and it was delicious! The whole family loved it. You will never use frozen mix again.

I came across this recipe and thought it was totally unique, I had lemons I needed to use and glad I made this recipe. I instantly doubled the batch for my thirsty broad. Peeling the 1st patch I quickly wondered if using a zester what easier and would eliminate a step by slicing the peel in the 2nd step. I tried it and it was just as much work as doing it the way it was written. But either way, the zester works just as good. Little hard on the wrist. But all in all I followed the recipe to the T and it was quite refreshing and light, the how smelled nicely of lemons for a bit. And my kids drank it all up. It was worth just trying because of the different way this was made. I did strain out the lemon peel and the pulp because of the kiddos. Thank you for sharing such a nice recipe. I will be trying this again with a sugar free way with Splenda for my benefit.
I just made this and WOW!! It's EXACTLY what I was looking for! Thanks for sharing!
Delightful, fun to make with the little ones.  Did as another reviewer suggested and juiced the lemons and put the cut halves in a bowl with the sugar to cut down the labor.
This recipe is good. I prefer to do the rinds like it says and use a different sugar lemon water ratio.

This lemonade is amazing!! It is the BEST lemonade I have EVER had!! It has the perfect amount of sweet and sour! I miss read the directions and added 1 1/4 CUPS of water instead of QUARTS. It was an easy fix, I just added a lot more water!! VERY VERY reccomended! :)

For all the people who said this is bitter you do not want the white part of the rind. A microplane works great to get just the yellow zest and that is where all the flavor is. It allows all the oils to release into the suger and the into the simple syurp you are making.
This was great.  I peeled the zest from the lemons with a good vegetable peeler so as not to get any of the bitter white part.
Absolutely the best I've ever had!  I will never try another lemonade recipe again, I have found my favorite.

Great way to use up a huge bag of lemons from Costco.  The kids loved this lemonade over ice. For the festive adults at our party, we added a bit of lemon flavored vodka and it was a huge hit as well.

Absolutely delicious! I ended up using the same proportions and it was perfect combination of tart and sweet, and it was strong but I didn't feel the need to water it down any more.     I only take off a star because it is a bit of a hassle. To avoid the bitter white part, I just zested the lemons because cutting only the yellow part of the peel was too difficult. I'd say zest the lemons, then squeeze them. Then strain in a fine sieve to get all the peel out.
make sure to pour boiled water over the peels deffinately affects the taste
Tasted too much of the lemon rinds.
I was pleasantly surprised! Just the right combination of sweet and tart. I'll make this again.

your lemonade was great but try mine too:
1 lime
2 lemons
20 tsp of sugar
1 cup of water

Squeeze the lime and lemons, mix in the sugar and 
water. Add ice and your drink is ready. it is delicious! 
Sebastian with a little help from her sister Hanna

Like other reviewers have said, DO NOT stir the rinds, sugar and water.  Just let it sit.  I would also recommend straining everything.  I strained the juice through a fine mesh strainer and after removing the rinds, I strained the sugar water mixture through a fine mesh strainer.  My kids LOVE this and ask for it all summer long!  Great with vodka too for the adults!

This was wonderful!  We loved it!  I followed the recipe exactly.  I wouldn't change a thing.  Thanks for sharing.

Update:  I have made this several times, and it has been delicous every single time.  My husband says it is enough to get a marriage proposal out of a man!
EXCELLENT!
This lemonade reminds me of what my Grandmother used to make when I was little.  Love this recipe and thanks for bringing back some wonderful memories!

I have made this twice and the first time I put the original amount of sugar, which I found too sweet. I reduced the sugar to one cup the second time around and it had the right sweetness for me. I also squeezed the lemons the first time around and didn't care for that at all. The second time around I juiced the lemons first and then I added the sugar to the halved peels. The "modern" method doesn't compromise the flavour at all. Will definitely keep making this again and again. Thanks for sharing, Aunt Suzie!
The taste is worth the effort! I zested the lemons & used half the sugar, then stirred that occasionally.
This is THE BEST I have ever made in all my years upon this Earth!!!

Lovely lemonade.  The lemon oil adds extra depth and gives this lemonade a handsome yellow shade without any food coloring.  My family went crazy for this when I made it.  I absolutely love this recipe.    Thanks to reviewers for the tip on not messing with the zest and sugar, they are so RIGHT!  Totally recommend this recipe to friends whenever I get the chance!  Thanks so much for sharing!!

My daughters and I love this recipe! How can you go wrong with a classic?....You can't! Here are the changes I made: I used 9 lemons, 1 1/2 cups of sugar, and 1 1/2 quarts of water. I juiced the lemons first and then just added the juiced rinds to a bowl. Other than that...followed exactly. This is my only Lemonade recipe that I will use from now on!

I made this earlier today-it is wonderful,I did read some of the reviews beforehand (thank you all).I peeled just the yellow part,cut small-layered /w/ just 1 cup sugar.Cut the pith off the lemons.Quartered them and ran through my juicer.What took the most time was cutting the peel into 1/2 inch pieces.Next time will use my box grater and shred.We don't drink soda-so this will be a welcome change from Cranberry juice or try mixing them...
Nice taste, but one tip...  resist the urge to press the peel or stir it around in the sugar.  Just put it in, mix it lightly and let it alone!  Otherwise the end result will be bitter.  Trust me.
Good, double the batch, for the amount of work involved it is just smart to double the batch.

It was very good; however there was a slight bitterness along with the sweet lemony taste.  I'm not sure if that's from the lemons I used, or what...or maybe that's just how it's suppose to taste?  

It was fun to watch the sugar turn to goop in the lemon rinds. :)

I just cut the lemons in half, juiced them and threw the whole juiced half (pith, pulp and all) into my roasting pan.
Poured HALF the amount of sugar (because I was adding strawberry puree) over them, let them sit for 40 minutes, I even stirred them up a bit at the start before I read not to.
Then I read the other reviews about the pith and bitter flavour, so after 40 minutes of the sugar on the lemon halves I poured over the boiling water and tasted it every 5 minutes or so to see if there was a hint of bitterness and after 20 minutes there was none.

We used 30 lemons and made this (x 6) for a weekend at the cottage with strawberry puree and added vodka for the adults - delicious!
I have been using this recipe for a few years now. It is absolutely wonderful!! I love it so much I usually make a triple batch. This is the best lemonade I have ever had!
Wow - this is the best lemonade I have ever tasted.  It didn't hurt that the lemons were picked fresh from our tree!!  Will absolutely make this again!

I tried this recipe yesterday, me and my boyfriend loved it. I used more water than the recipe called for though. I think it is the best I have ever had though, nice lemon flavor but not too sweet. I will be using this recipe from now on.

This is by far, the best lemonade I have ever tasted! Followed recipe exactly. Avoided stirring the rinds/water/sugar mixture. Just let it steep for the 20 minutes, strained into the pitcher and ... DEEELICIOUS! :) 5 stars

This lemaonade is amazing as is. and to make it greater i used 4 lemons and 1 grapefruit, (peel and juice), it makes a great pink lemonade. I have done it with 3 lemons and 2 limes, quite sour but good.  and today i used 4 lemones and 2 clementine oranges. yum!   AND the rinds that are left over after taken out are good if sprinkled with sugar and let dry a bit, great candied peel!

This was absolutely the best lemonade ever.  For those who complained of bitterness, you probably used the entire peel. It might be better to say to use the zest, the white is very bitter.  I even substituted half the sugar for Splenda (added after it was all mixed together, I only used sugar with the zest).  Thanks for sharing such a wonderful recipe. Tested and true through the years.
The taste of this lemonade makes the time spent making it worthwhile. Tangy and refreshing. My children loved it!!!
So delicious sometimes, other times it's bitter.  We keep trying though because when it's good, it can't be beat.   Thanks!

This was delicious.  I more than doubled the recipe for a picnic and it turned out great.  The only tedious thing was peeling the lemons to get the rinds off.  While they were marinating in the sugar, I ran the lemons through my juicer.  Quick and easy.
yummy! I have always liked fresh squeezed lemonade, but doing it this way, WOW! I will never make it any other way now. I love that you can taste the oil from the peels and not just lemon juice.

I sliced the rind off like you would a pineapple, that made the lemons so easy to squeeze over a strainer. I was able to just mash the whole thing down over the strainer. This was awesome lemonade! Very yummy, not too sweet, not too sour!

Best lemonade that can be made in a regular kitchen.  It has that "bite" to it that really makes it thirst-quenching for some reason.  The chemistry explains it; the oils get carried by the sugar into solution with the juice & water.  Every time I serve this to guests, I get compliments and they always want the recipe!  Sometimes if lemons are out of season or expensive, I mix this with some frozen to make it go farther.  Be careful not to let the sugar/rind mixture sit for more than an hour or you'll end up with bitter lemonade.

Tasty! After reading through the reviews, I didn't cut out very much of the pith - only where it was especially thick on one lemon. I reduced the sugar to 1C and added a teaspoon of dried lavender. I accidentally added too much water, filling the bowl to almost 2Qts with the lemon, lavender and sugar... and yet, this was fabulous! Can't wait to make it again.
Love this recipe, read the tips and your results are fabulous~
So sweet and so refreshing! A natural lemonade has such a different flavor compared to the artificially flavored drink mixes.

Great homemade lemonade recipe!  Leaves a very refreshing, cool taste in your mouth.  My family loved the now discontinued Kool-Aid flavor "Lemon Ice" which left your mouth feeling cold - this recipe comes very close to that but in a much better way!  Thanks for the recipe!
Oh my this was wonderful.  This is the only way I will make lemonade from now on.  Thanks for sharing this historical recipe.
Once you've made this recipe, all other lemonade recipes will pale in comparison!  Simply outstanding!
I used 6 lemons instead of 5 and cut the sugar to 1 cup and it was still sweet enough. I decided to use the microwave to boil the water. Awesome recipe, easy and delicious, thank you for sharing!!

I like me lemonade good and strong, so I used some extra lemons when I made my first batch.  It ended up actually being too strong.  I suspect this recipe will satisfy the lemon lovers like me out there exactly as stated in the recipe.  The flavor truly is incredible, like peeling a fresh lemon!

So Good! Followed directions exactly.  I filled the jug I was going to use, and just boiled that much water. A lemon flavor, that's strong enough to swallow without going all "squinty eyed" and enough sugar to make it taste very smooth.  Will definitely add it to the list.  Have to admit, I played with the sugared rind, and don't notice any bitterness.
Lemonade at it's best!  Classic as the classic in Coke.

This was fantastic! One other reviewer said to use a veggie peeler on the rinds and this work beautifully. I will make this again with out a doubt. Now I want to experiment and add strawberries or other fruit to it too. BTW I also used the Splenda granulated sugar substitute (not the packets) and it turned out great and lower calorie.

Fabulous lemonade. I definitely juiced the lemons first and set the juice aside. Then I just cut up the rinds to add the sugar to. It was a lot less work for the same result. Great for summer parties with kids. Serve with a shot of vodka for the adults and a sprig of mint. Yum!
Tastes really good! I used the zest instead of whole peels. 1 cup sugar and 5 cups water. Great great great. From now on this is gonna be my summer chiller! Thanks for the recipe.
The best lemonade ever! I used only half the sugar and that was sweet enough for us! Also, good tip from previous reviewer about the membrane.
This is a great recipe. I used more water and more sugar. In all, my family loves the lemonade and I will DEF use it again. Next time I will try pink lemonade.

Best Lemonade recipe!!!!! I only used 1 cup of sugar and added about 1 cup more water. Perfect balance of tart and sweet. No more store brands ever. I did not find it bitter at all. If it comes out  bitter just adjust with water and/or simple syrup.
Amazing!  Had it at my July 4th party earlier this year and I didn't quite make enough for the demand!

Scrumptious!  Just like down south.  For the reviewers who said it was bitter, try not getting any of the white part of the peel.  Only the outside yellow.  The sugar pulls the oils and flavor right out of the rind.  Thanks for a great recipe!

I reduced the sugar a bit in mine... I like my lemonade *very* tart.  Delicious!  This is a very simple recipe and very easy to customize as well.  Try using lemons and limes, makes a great summer combination!
Wow, really delicious and refreshing.  We were just given a bag of lemons from a friend and we wondered what we could do with them. Now we know.
The best lemonade I've ever tasted- you can make this recipe simpler by juicing the lemons first, then adding sugar to the rinds.

This is a great recipe and I will be making it again. I'm going to cut back a bit on the sugar, I like lemonade with a bit more whang!  Using the lemon peel really adds a richer lemon flavor.  Can't wait to hand a glass to my husband when he gets home! Thanks so much for sharing this recipe and thanks to those who forwarned me NOT to mess the sugar and peels. I was tempted........  :)
Yummy, will be making this alot...

i love this recipe! i've made this a couple of times already, and i totally agree with the mods - scrape off the piths, less sugar (~1 cup total) and more water (~1cup more).  i also like to throw in some thinly sliced ginger peels (fresh) into the sugar to add a different taste!  this recipe takes more time, but it is worth it! :)
Every bit as good as you get at the fair.  I made exactly as directed with my 4 yo and we had so much fun doing it.  My lemons were a little small though, so I used six.
If you just use the lemon zest as opposed to the whole peel, the lemonade will not be bitter.
This was fantastic! Great lemon flavor, perfect amount of sweetness. Kids loved it. Will definitely make this again!
This was exactly the kind of recipe I was looking for, and I wasn't disappointed.  I took it to a picnic and it went over quite well.  I've already made it for a second time this week.

Can I leave SIX stars? This is delicious as written! It was really good! I love this recipe and it's pretty easy compared to some more complicated ones! Unfortunately I didn't have enough lemons for a whole pitcher, i only had one, but I added some lemon juice and it tasted pretty good!

OMGosh! This lemonade is AWESOME!   A teeny bit time consuming...but so worth it.  I used a veggie peeler to remove the skin.  My only change would be less sugar.  Next time I will use only 1 cup. Well, my daughter finally likes lemonade now, thanks to this vintage recipe.  To me, the recipe as written seems almost more like a concentrate. I  make this all summer long, nothing like a summer hummer out by the pool on a hot Arizona day.
Greatest lemonade ever, follow what other reviews said, sweeten to taste, then it's time for a real treat.
Best lemonade I ever had. I am not a lemonade person but I will drink this all the time. Takes a while to make but it is worth it.

I tried it before it was cooled all the way and I'm really pleased with the flavor. It's intense and far superior to anything I've had at a restaurant!  I refuse to make anything from "concentrate" so I thought I'd try and make my favorite drink the old fashioned way. Perfect and just the right kind of flavor!  Thanks for the recipe!

Thank you for this recipe!!  It is the best lemonade I have ever had.  It takes very little time to prepare,  you just have to wait for the lemon rinds and sugar to do their work. It is a mellow lemonade.  Maybe a little sweet but you can adjust that. Thanks again :)
I have made this recipe many times always receiving rave reviews. It is the best lemonade I have ever tasted.  I use our juice extractor to juice the lemons.

So good.  I couldn't resist the urge to stir the lemon rinds in the hot water and it turned out fine.  I used lemons that a woman from work brought me from her tree.  I think I will use about a quarter to a half a cup less sugar next time.

Awesome lemonade! I juice the lemons first too. I also do six lemons with 1 extra cup of water - keeping the sugar the same or a little less. Making more than one batch at a time is smart or you will have to repeat the whole process again as soon as you finish off that one pitcher! SO GOOD!

When I made this, I was looking forward to the lemon oil/lemon rind giving it a nice kick, but the taste was just overpowering. I used the corrrect amount of sugar but it also seemed a bit overly sweet as well.

I just made this lemonade today and I couldn't wait to rave about it. Let me just say- DELICIOUS! My whole family loved it. Really good Lemonade!  I made it according to directions (other than juicing, since I have a juicer).  Next time  however I will use less lemon rind.  It was a little more bitter than I like.

I am not usually a huge fan of Lemonade, which is why I went searching for a recipe.  This was delicious: Not to bitter not too sour, but sweet with a bite!   Perfect.  And I went on to use the peels in the Candied Lemon Peel recipe , found on this site.  I now have Lemonade, candied peels, and lemon simple syrup, all fantastic, and all from 5 lemons!
Tastes just like Hot Dog And A Stick Lemonade...yum!!!!

We have a lemon tree in our backyard and since I discovered this recipe last summer, I've made so many batches of lemonade I don't even follow a recipe anymore! This is the best lemonade recipe!

Typically, I take 4-5 lemons, peel the rind off a couple of them (I use a potato peeler), place them in a bowl and pour a cup or so of sugar over them. Then I squeeze the lemons and boil however much water looks like is needed to fill my pitcher. When the water has boiled, I put the sugar/rind mixture in a fine strainer, pour the water over it, and then pour the lemon juice into the strainer as well. What I like about this way is that from there, I can season to taste. I can either add more sugar (and because the mixture is still warm, it will dissolve) or more lemon juice, or more warm water from the tap. Once it tastes perfect, I leave it on the counter to cool some and then put it in the fridge to chill.
This is the best lemonaid I've ever drank. The recipe is strong but it's perfect because when you add ice it doesn't become too diluted.

This was the best lemonade ever!!  I make it all the time now!  I made it and mixed it with vodka for New Years and it was fabulous!!  The lemon oil from the skins really overpowers even the cheap party vodka I used and made for a really nice tasty drink for my guests.  Everyone wanted the recipe.

Wonderful lemonade!  Incorporating the flavor from the peels is such a great idea.  Instead of peeling the rinds and cutting them into slices, I used a microplane to take just the zest off and mixed that into the sugar.  After the sugar is dissolved in the hot water I strain the zest out with a fine mesh strainer.  I would recommend not tweeking out and trying to get every last bit of the zest off the peel and to take care to get as little of the white part as possible.  The first time I made this I tried to get ALL the zest off and I think it caused me to go over the same area more than once and even that little bit of white part added some bitterness to the end result.  I also added a little extra water because the flavor was kind of strong for my taste but that could just be me.  Great lemon flavor does lie in the zest and now I can't imagine why I never thought of using it before.
Perfect and refreshing.
this is excellent bee making it for a tear and a half very good next time i will try to peel the zest see how that is
This is bitter. I even got as much of the white off the rind as I could. I followed the directions 100%. Sure is a lot of work.

DELICIOUS!!  This is the second time I've made this in the last week.  My family LOVED it so much I couldn't get a photo before it was all gone! I suppose the peels would also be good in a cup of hot or iced tea... whatever you do, don't just throw them away!

WARNING - DO NOT USE PLASTIC BOWLS TO MAKE THIS RECIPE.  Use glass or ceramic. The high acidity of the lemons can leach chemicals out of the plastic and at a minimum affect the flavor, but possibly be much more hazardous than that. I used melamine the first time and noticed a weird chemical taste and Googled it and found dozens of articles about the dangers of high acid foods in plastic bowls.

Splendid! I'm a lemon lover so this was like a god-sent gift to me! I made this but incorporated the pulp by simply adding all of the ingredients, chopped, to a pot and boiling for 20 minutes.

Using the ingredients listed, only varying with a whole red and a whole green bell pepper and medium carrot, yielded a bit more than 48 ounces.

Second variation: 
Juice all the vegetables and set juice aside. 

Return all the pulp to a pot, add water and all other ingredients to soften for the blender and allow flavors to come together.

Add juice and boiled ingredients to a blender and puree.

This has the double advantage of keeping much of the nutrients intact through the juice of the vegetables that is not boiled and enhancing anti-oxidants that are created by boiling the pulp (tomatoes and carrots for instance are more nutritional cooked).

In order to get authentic tasting chile rellenos, you should use a couple of eggs, seperated.  Whip the whites w/an electric mixer until stiff peaks form.  Beat the yolks seperatley and fold them into the whites (preseverving the volume of the whites).  Then you can dip the stuffed chiles into the egg...and don't worry about slopping it on.  You want the entire chile covered.  When your chile comes out of the oil, you'll have a nice fluffy coating...rather than a heavy egg-y tasting batter that most homemade recipes call for.

An easy way to char your chiles is to heat up the broiler in your oven and toss the peppers directly on to the racks.  (Poblano's can be substituted w/great results). You want the entire surface to be browned and blistered, so you will have to flip them occasionally.  Then, stick the peppers in a zip-lock and let them steam for about 1/2 an hour or so.  When you return to them, they'll be cool enough to handle, and the skin will be really easy to peel off!!  Make sure not to remove the stems when you slit open the chiles to remove the seeds and membranes.
Follow these tips, and you will have one tasty little treat!!
Also, I use white cheese rather than cheddar (I use Oaxacan cheese...but for areas where Mexican cheese isn't available, Monterey Jack is a good substitute)

Although I've not tried this one yet, I do intend to do so.  These are the kind of Rellenos I grew up on when I lived on the border.  Mexican food varies by region based on what is most readily available.  Throughout the border area along the New Mexico/Far West Texas area, Green chile is a common ingredient in Mexican food.  It is also commonly used for Chile Rellenos.  Hatch, New Mexico is also know as the Chile Capital of the world which is in this region.  Other parts of Mexico use Poblano.  Both create authentic dishes even though they are different peppers.   

When using Long Green chile (Anaheim, Big Jim etc.) try to get chiles that are straight and not curled up or twisted.  Roast them in your oven under the broiler or put them on your grill.  Turn them as the chile skin is charred.  Once the skin is charred, put them in a plastic bag or a bowl covered with plastic for about 30 minutes.  The skins should then come off very easily.

My changes:  I agree with another cook, clean out the seeds and membranes of the chiles before roasting. They are so delicate once they're cooked!  
I also doubled the batter recipe.  I added a good amount of salt to the flour , based on the comments of other cooks, so the end result was flavorful.  The batter was a lot of work to beat those egg whites, but SOOOO worth it!  I ran out of the egg batter with the last 3 chiles, so I basically just used the dusting flour  with the remaining liquid egg and those turned out ok.  Next time, for a dozen chiles, I will use 5 eggs so there will be enough batter.  Also, the technique for coating the chiles with just the right amount of fluffy batter takes a minute to get the hang of.   You have to move quickly and gently, or they will be smothered.  That's probably why I ran out at the end.  The first few were over-battered, due to my lack of skill.   Overall

Some suggestion. Since you are using only the outer skin of the lemon, look for organic lemons that have not been treated with nasty stuff.   Look for lemon varieties that have a thick skin and are high in essential oils.  Try peeling thin strips with a potato peeler.  A zester will prematurely release the oils in the skin.  Try to avoid the pith (white part) as this is what causes bitterness.  Also try an alternative sweetener such as agave instead of refined sugar for a warmer palate feel.  This recipe will create a Limoncello that is a little low in alcohol over traditional Limoncello. If you are using Vodka (40% 80 proof) the final alcohol will be less that 20% instead of 30-35%. It will freeze at this proof.  A higher proof alcohol will extract out the oils and color faster. We love Limoncello so much we started a company in Sonoma to produce it commercially.  Check out www.hellosonoma.com  Salute!  Limoncello di Sonoma

Very good recipe, quick, easy, and very tasty. However, to those who are avoiding sugar, to be clear, any kind of juice concentrate has A LOT of sugar. Concentrate refers to the way it is made. The fruit is put into a huge maceration chamber where several bags of granulated sugar are added to the fruit and left there for sometimes months at a time. The reason why this is done is so that these companies can offer the product year round. Bacteria and other pathogens will not grow in sugar, so they're able to pile on crop after crop of fruit without a loss. So don't think there is no sugar in this recipe. There is some.

I really didn't expect to enjoy this as much as I did (I was really making it for the kiddos) but it turns out the big kiddo (DH) and baby (14mo) loved this best, while me and the in between kiddo (8yo) and her friends weren't blown away. I used Boars Head hot dogs (figured if the main protein "star" of the dish was hot dog then I'd better use a good quality one!) and the only sub that I had to make was a bell and a cubanelle for the poblano. I liked that mashing some of the beans along the edge of the pot made it thicken up even more so that it was nice and goopy and just right for scooping onto pieces of toast.
Made exactly as stated.  Didn't like, won't make again.  It wasn't inedible, which is why it gets 2 stars.

I substituted cayenne for ground fresh chili paste (what I had available) and chives in place of green onions. My husband and I both liked it but it was to spicy for my son (17 months). To be honest I could have used less sweet and more spice. I think I will only use half a tbl. Spoon of brown sugar next time and replace the celery stalk with a sprinkle of celery salt. Altogether it had many bold flavors and was cheap and quick to make.

This is now a family favorite. Quite simple to make and a very tasty and hearty meal. The only change I make is that I haven't been able to find fresh cayenne peppers at the stores I usually shop at, so I substitute ground cayenne instead. Thank you for another winner, Chef John.
Really good, cheap and easy.
quite good, kids liked it too

In lieu of poblano and cayenne, I used equal amounts of green and red bell peppers...and just a dash of chili powder, because I was not sure what the heat factor, spice-wise of a poblano & cayenne pepper pile would be. This was easy, and, for me, at least, it was helpful to view Chef John's how-to video. Besides being entertaining, the video via C.J. gives you permission to play things by ear, a bit. DH liked this, actually voicing (in WORDS) his approval vs. the more subtle grunt approvals, or the ever uninspiring "I ate it, didn't I?" compliments.

I made no changes whatever. Used poblano pepper.  Used beef franks from one of the mail order steak purveyors. Not quite Wagu, but reasonably close. Beats heck out of any other franks & beans!  Without the franks , this would be great bean soup. With vegetable broth rather than chicken, would probably be a  great vegetarian bean soup. Many layers of flavor. Will make again!
Grown up beans and franks! My husband I loved this! easy, quick and inexpensive.

Hi. I make this cocktail  with lemon-lime seltzer water. It is very refreshing but not sweet. The ingredients were changed during publication, however I bet the lemon-lime soda would be a sweet treat.
WE make a recipe like this at my work but instead of onions and tomatoes we put diced chicken on it. It's so delicious!!
Quick yummy lunch. Instead of using regular flour tortillas I used a spinach herb sandwich wrap... perfect!

I made this tonight because I wanted something simple to use up my abundance of cherry tomatoes.  I'm not one to follow recipes exactly, but I tried on this one.  My husband grilled salmon and we put this over it.  It was a winner! Will definitely make this again. Next time will try with steak.

I had the last of the season smallish (roma and cherry) tomatoes sitting on the counter top for about a week.  After deciding to grill swordfish steaks but not having carb side dish, I looked around to see what I could find to put on top of the fish to add interest and flavor.  This recipe popped up and the tomatoes called to me.  I didn't have red wine vinegar and just added red cooking wine - more than a splash if you get my drift!  Then I added an additional clove of garlic, some snipped fresh parsley and a teaspoon or so of capers.  After it sat in the fridge for about an hour, I put the sauce with the chopped tomatoes in the pan and cooked it down to the thickened stage.  We found it a perfect accompaniment to the swordfish and will definitely even buy tomatoes to make this again.
This drink is very good. Quick to prepare too. Now next time I might add more sweet and sour because I found it a bit too sweet.
Very good. I don't know if I've had anything like this before. I really enjoyed this. Second one I made, I added an additional finger of tequila.
Excellent chick drink.

I served this cocktail to a a group of friends, who had various tastes. It was a hit with everyone. Perfect balance of sweet/sour taste. Pretty pink color, and it was the only one out of several recipes we tasted that earned a second pitcher request.  Use a good quality grenadine, it is the key flavor componet in this drink. Will keep this recipe as a permanent favorite/
This was delicious.  I did use just one more ounce of tequila.  Wouldn't this make a great drink for July Fourth?!

Don't know if it's becuase of the brand of sweet and sour I used (Daily's); but there was way too much sweet and sour for my taste.  I ended up adding water to dilute the overwhelming pungency of the sweet and sour.

Excellent!  This makes way too much for 4 people. You could cut the recipe in half and still have lots of leftovers.  Next time I will add more carrot, and some toasted sliced almonds.  It was just a little bland, but that was fine, because the other dishes we served at this meal were so flavorful.  It was a really nice side dish with everything else.
I made it as is, except didn't add the carrots as my husband doesn't like cooked carrots.  It was a little bland.  I think it needed more herbs.

Originally from Minnesota, now living in New Mexico.  My family came down for a visit and brought the wild rice!  I didn't have any chicken broth so I sautéed the onions and carrots in about a half stick of butter, added water and a smack ramen chicken flavor pack.  Added the herbs, the wild and brown rice and simmered for about 10 minutes.  The  crowning touch was the dried cranberries and raisins.  I could not get over how flavorful this was, the raisins and cranberries delivered a sweet and tangy zip.  Along with the thyme and sweet marjoram it was a savory blend.    Thank you I needed a start, never have made wild rice before.
Very good. But I made it with half as much rice to have a higher  ratio of the other flavorings and vegetables.

Added the vegetables 30 minutes into the cook time, since someone else said the veggies got mushy. Perfect consistency. Added a layer of black beans and turkey jerky 10 minutes before the end of the cook time. Delicious. Will make again. Looking forward to left overs for lunch this week.
I have made this as stated, and it is a really good side dish. After a person tries this as written, you can find ways to personalize it too. Thanks for the submission!
Absolutely love this recipe! I bought wild rice on impulse and then realized I had no idea what to do with it. Luckily I found this recipe, which I made and served with grilled salmon. Perfect!

This was really tasty and easy. After soaking the wild rice - I dumped all of the ingredients in my rice cooker. (I added some sliced baby bello mushrooms) and pressed brown. 

I think I’ll try halving the recipe next time - it makes a TON!

I was not a fan of the combined wild and brown rice, especially in addition to the celery.  That was just too many textures at once for my taste.  The marjoram really was not a welcome addition either.  I think I'll pass on this one in the future.

I didn’t say a word at the dinner table to Hubs to announce that we were having wild and brown rice with the Salisbury Steak.  He dislikes both.  I hoped that since the rice was all dolled up that it would make a difference.  It obviously did, because he cleaned up his plate rather enthusiastically.  And indeed, this was surprisingly good, far exceeding even my own expectations.  I did deviate from the recipe, adding some zucchini I wanted to use, using fresh thyme (and no marjoram) rather than ground, and beef broth rather than chicken as I already had a carton opened that I had used for another dish.  I chose to cook the vegetables in butter separately from the rice, adding some fresh minced garlic.  I set that aside until the rice was cooked, stirring it in at the end.  How much my changes influenced the final outcome I can’t be sure.  What I do know is that this was colorful, flavorful, and had great texture.  I started off with slim expectations for this but we ended  up polishing it off. I served this with Salisbury Steak with Mushrooms, and Peas and Pancetta, both recipes also from this site.

I had just received some wild rice straight from Wisconsin and then found this recipe.  I cut it down to one-third the amount, and that easily was enough for six servings.  My problem with this was that the vegetables were total mush by the time it was done, so I'd caution people to add them just near the very end.  I felt it was bland, so maybe one could up the seasonings and add some crunch from toasted almonds.  I really do like the idea of the combination of the two rices.  I'll give this another try with a different method of cooking.  Thank you for this!

I made this for my family and it was delicious! I skipped the lemon zest and added the lemon extract. If I left the lemon extract out it would have been better. I am excited to experiment with other fruits. I have already tried grapefruit and it came out beautifully. I plan to make a watermelon one and I hope it will be as good as the others. This technique is very easy and I would reccommend it to anyone. A great recipe to try with kids!
This was so good!  i made it more like a slushy with a straw in a glass.  i think i ate an iceburgs worth!

My Mom used to make lemon "sherbet" like this when I was little.  I remember she poured it into a metal ice cube tray to freeze after she took out the cube dividers.  It was always one of my favorite desserts. (I DON'T remember her taking it out and stirring it frequently, tho')
I made this with grapefruit juice instead and it was really good! I can't wait to make it again!
AMAZING!! Love it.

This was so simple and delicious.  I added a little more sugar as we prefer a sweeter pizza sauce. This has a much fresher taste than jarred sauces and packs a lot more flavor!
Good dipping sauce.  Used it with the spinach appetizers from allrecipes.  Omitted the sugar.  Flavor is better after it sits.

This was truly "WAY EASY"!  I added a little bit more fresh garlic and some minced fresh cilantro for more impact and it turned out very flavorful.  I would definately make this again.  Thanks for the great recipe.
Didn't change it at all, used it for French bread pizza and it was a hit!
Good and easy.  I used Garlic, Basil and Oregano tomato sauce and paste.  So I didn't use garlic or oregano.  However, I did use garlic salt along with the other spices.
pretty good i made it on a smaller scale, ommited the garlic + parsley, added garlic powder instead of salt, and    added more oregeno, and used chopped tomatos instead of tomato paste.

I scaled this down to 4 servings and added chopped pepperoni.  This is quick to make if you do not have jarred sauce available.  I thought it was a bit too thick and was missing something in taste for a bread dip but would work with with pizza because of all the additional toppings.  I served this with Jimmbo's garlic knots recipe from this site.
This recipe is ridiculously simple to make and very tasty.
Great.. And much cheaper than canned pizza sauce.. Fresher tasting too!

This sauce was SOOOOO good!  However, I did make some minor changes to my taste.
I used 1 can of crushed tomatoes, 1/2 can of tomato paste, 1/2 tsp oregano, 1 tsp sugar, dash of garlic powder and 1/2 tsp of dried parsley.  I mixed all the ingredients together and heated in the microwave and used for dipping "Paula's bread sticks"  (another fabulous recipe from this site)!

This sauce good but I'm sure there are probably even better recipes out there.  However, I always use this recipe when I make pizza because it's way better than the jarred stuff, it's super easy/fast to make and most importantly I have all the spices on hand! I use dried parsley because it's more convenient and it tastes just fine.
Really good.  Be careful not to add too much sauce but it will still turn out!

This was good.  A little bland. I added some italian seasoning.

Good in a pinch and better than the jarred variety.

This was very simple to do.  Like some other reviewers, I added more flavorings.  I doubled the oregano, used a full teaspoon of sugar, minced two garlic cloves, substituted 1/2 tsp. garlic powder for the garlic salt, used 1/4 tsp. dried parsley rather than fresh (didn't have fresh on hand), and added about 1/4 cup (drained) diced tomatoes.  The flavor wasn't quite right once mixed so I put it in the microwave on medium heat for three minutes, stirred, and then let cool slightly.  I served this as the dipping sauce for "Real Italian Calzones" also featured at allrecipes.com.  Both were delicious!

This is good! I do agree w/ others that said it was too thick for pizza sauce...I just added a bit of water and that fixed that problem right up. We thought the flavors were nice...not too overpowering, which was what I was after. I subbed Italian seasoning for the oregano and added a bit of pepper and parmesan cheese...worked nicely and can't wait to try this for breadsticks! Thanks for sharing. :)

This was defintely way easy!  We used this sauce on Jay's signature Pizza crust and really enjoyed it. There was alot of flavor!  I made it exactly to the recipe except that the tomato paste I used had italian seasonings.  I will definitely use this sauce again.  Thanks Dan!

I was very pressed for time when I decided to make this, and was surprised by the quality of it, considering the minimal amount of work involved.  Very easy and simple, and I'll use this again when I need a quick pizza sauce.
Delicious, but just a little thick for pizza sauce.
Very tomatoey flavor. This made enough for 3 pizzas. It was okay, but not one of my favorites.

So so easy and good! I doubt if I will ever buy pizza sauce again since this took only a couple of minutes to put together and tastes so much better than store bought sauce. It had a good garlic taste to it, but I thought the other spices could be stronger. Next time I might try doubling the oregano and parsley and see how that turns out. Still great though, no complaints, I just like to experiment. I doubled the recipe so I could use part of it for a pizza and the rest as a dipping sauce for breadsticks, and I thought it worked out great for both. Thank you for a nice, really simple sauce, Laguna!

This was a very very good recipe.  I liked how simple it was.  I accidentally put 1/4 tsp of dried basil in it because I could have sworn this recipe mentioned it, but I am positive it would still be at least a 4.5 star without the basil.  Excellent and easy.
I have made this a lot and we like it. I have tasted others with a little better flavor but this is the best fast and easy sauce.
Good Stuff!
we used this on crazy crust pizza dough from this site and it was good. and very easy to make. we made 2 pizzas for 5 people and there was none left.

I liked it because it's easy. Since we do not like sweet pizzas, I eliminated the sugar, used all fresh ingredients, and added some more fresh garlic and basil. Good recipe for a light sauce if wise amount is used. Thanks Dan, it's great.
WOW, I couldn't believe how easy and tasty this sauce was.  I did use about 3/4 tsp sugar instead of the 1/2 it called for.  Thank you for sharing your recipe.
Very good!  I didn't want it to have a strong garlic flavor so I omitted the chopped garlic but did add garlic powder and onion powder.  I also added extra basil and it had a great pizzeria flavor.

This is almost identical to the recipe that I made up myself about ten years ago on the fly, except I made mine with just the paste and water. I used a 14oz can of sauce instead, with the 6oz can of paste, and used 1/2 tsp ea: salt, sugar, garlic powder, dried parsley, and oregano. It turned out fantastic. Thanks so much for the inspiration! :)
Yummy... always use on my pizza... and for dipping breadsticks...

This was pretty good on my Bisquick pizza crust.  I added several dashes of onion salt, and used garlic pepper since I didn't have any garlic salt.  I think I'll try adding some other seasonings, but overall, this recipe is a keeper.

Perfect for breadsticks. Pretty good on pizza, too!
Very good - too easy to not give it a try.
I would say 3.5 stars. It's easy, but nothing special. Provides a good base to experiment with though.
She like.. Me like...
WOW! Is this stuff good! My dear hubby said it was the best pizza I'd ever made (and I make pretty darn good pizza!). I'll never used canned pizza sauce again ... this was so simple to make!
Tasty. The garlic salt made me want this more as a marinara sauce with breadsticks rather than pizza. I'll have to try breadsticks next time.
Very good,my kids loved it.Added a little basil and more garlic and a pinch of cayenne.Wonderful!!

I doubled the recipe so that I could use it for our pizzas tonight. I also made Italian Herb Bread (also from this site) into breadsticks and thought this would also make for a great dipping sauce. Although I did NOT care for this as a dipping sauce, it worked well on our pizzas. Even my guests commented that the "sauce" was very tasty.
I made the sauce just as the recipes instructed.  It turned out perfect.  Great base sauce!

I made this with breadsticks for a Halloween party.  It was so good!  I added a little extra garlic, and it turned out great.  This was the 'blood' to dip your 'fingers' in.  For the breadsticks I put almonds on the end before baking.  Very YUMMY!

Perfect sauce! Made it ahead of time and the flavors absorbed in the tomato mixture. It is nice and thick so you can spread it around. Not watery at all. I used 1 clove of garlic instead of the minced, and I used dried parsley instead of fresh. Thank you for a good down to earth recipe! It was enough to make four 12 inch pizzas.
Not a bad dipping sauce. Kids liked it and that is what matters.
Nice flavor. So simple.  We had 7 kids over to make the sauce and they had a blast making pizza's.  A winner! Was a little thick.  Added a bit more water. Very yummy. Enjoyed. Thanks!

This is probably one of the easiest best pizza dough recipes I've ever tried.  I use "way easy pizza sauce/bread stick dip" from here and just add my own cheeses and toppings. Everyone in my family loves it when I make pizza now.
Easy, tasty, perfect for last minute snacks and French bread pizza!

Delicious! And could it be any easier? Well, yes! Forget the bowl and grab a clean recycled jar 10oz or larger. Simple it is, but it is very bland.  I ended up using pizza sauce vs. tomato sauce, but it still needed a LOT more additional seasonings.  Don't get me wrong, it wasn't disgusting or anything, we have just had better.  Thanks anyway Dan ;)
My kids liked it better than the regular sauce I make so I guess it is my new pizza sauce.
Left out the tamota paste ( for some reason I never buy it canned and haven't found the tubes of it) and used no salt added tomato sauce. Used this for buscuit pizzas.
Very simple to prepare; added fresh garlic and seasoning salt instead of using garlic salt. Also added basil and used dried parsley.
This is really easy and just as tasty as more time consuming recipes.
This was very good and extremely easy. I added a little bit more sugar and a little more of the dried herbs. Thanks for the recipe!
This was alright, needs more sugar and spice.  I'd leave out the garlic salt next time or swap for powder.

Delish! I followed the recipe with exception that I added 1 teaspoon of sugar instead of 1/4 teaspoon and I didn't have a garlic clove so I used garlic powder instead of minced garlic.  I also didn't have any minced fresh parsley so I omitted that.  This was delish!  I was making homemade pizza and realized I that the jar sauce I usually use had gone bad so I used this recipe.  Two thumbs up from my kids and I.  We used it to dip garlic toast in while waiting for the pizza's to cook and it was so yummy!!!  Thank you for a wonderful and easy recipe.  I will no longer buy jarred pizza sauce!

Way easy is the right word and tastes good, too!  I followed the advice of other ratings and added a little more sugar -- was wonderful considering how quickly it was ready.  We ate this on Triscuit Pizzas and with breadsticks and loved it.  I always have this stuff on hand and will never be at a loss for a jar of pizza sauce again!
This is so easy it's ridiculous.  I made 2x the serving just so I could eat more.
This is a very versatile recipe, and any pizza topping works with it. This is my go-to recipe. It is nice to have a recipe where I know I will always have all the ingredients in the cupboard!

Easy and inexpensive.  Thanks!
I've used this recipe for quite some time now.  The fresh garlic made the sauce too "intense" for the kids, but I liked it.

Absolutely fabulous!  Quick, easy, and delicious.  This is going to be the only pizza sauce I make from now on.
This recipe was "way easy" and tasted delicious, definitely not like store bought but just as easy to prepare.  I will use this always.

Even my very selective 6 year old ate this! I left out the parsley and I blended up canned tomatoes since that was what we had in the pantry. We used it as our pizza sauce on English Muffin pizzas. Yum!
The BEST pizza sauce ever! Perfect combination of spices.  Simmered on the stove for 20 minutes so the spices melded together.  Didn't add sugar as we don't like a sweet sauce.  Absolutely the BEST!!

This is the base recipe that I've been using for pizza sauce for a while now.

2.  To freeze extras - put in ice cube trays to freeze and place in ziploc bags.  Take out what you want the night before using to thaw in refridgerator.

This is SO good, and SO simple.  I made Pepperoni Rolls and we dipped them into this sauce - perfect.  One of my children said that she liked how the Roll was hot, but the sauce was cold (room temp).   I thought about warming the sauce but tried it "cold" and it was excellent.
It's good for pizza, don't know if I'll use it for dipping.
Super yummy and super easy, so a for sure winner!!  Comes together in a snap, my only mistake/downfall was using store bought crust instead of homemade :(
This recipe is GREAT!  I added a little sugar to the sauce and it was perfect.  As long as I have tomato paste on hand, I will NEVER use any other!!
i dont always have pizza sauce on hand,  this is great when in a pinch!!!  it is not hte best sauce that i have had, but it was much better than just using a jar of spagetti sauce for a substitute!!!

YUM! I used this as a base recipe and modified it for what I had on hand (stewed tomatoes vs paste & sauce) and doubled the spices and also added basil. I didn't have parsley wither but so far this is THE best sauce recipe I've made! Thanks!!
excellent sauce.

My family loves this recipe. We've been using it with the pizza crust recipe we found for months and months now. The spices were good, but I think I will try it with crushed tomatoes instead of tomatoe paste.
The best!!
This was a good easy sauce.  I liked how it included fresh garlic and was made with common items I always have on hand.  I used this for two pizzas.
VERY easy and VERY good!!

This recipe is wonderfully easy to  make, just make sure all of your seasonings are finely ground (my garlic salt was gritty). The only thing I would change is the thickness, it's a little too thick for dipping, but a little water made it perfect. Absolutely de-lish!

Quick, easy, and tasty.  I doubled the oregano, added about 1/4 tsp of dried basil, skipped the garlic salt & parsley since I don't have any, and added a dash of salt.  I used it as a dipping sauce for calzones and it was great.  I simmered it on the stovetop a little while so that the flavors could meld.
It was so good! i am a 13 year old and it was simple. i didnt have any tomato sauce so i used pasta sauce, it gave it a spagetti'ish quality, that evryone loved. thanks!

Very good flavor, quick and easy to assemble too. I wasn't happy with the consistency for a dipping sauce (I imagine it would be perfect for an actual pizza though) so I blended in 1/4 C of water with no noticeable effect on the flavor. Also I simmered it on the stovetop for a bit and served it warm to rave reviews. My breadsticks will be naked no longer... Thanks for posting!

We've been using this recipe for over a year, and it's the only pizza sauce recipe for us.  Easy and quick to make and it always tastes fresh.  We use it with "Jay's Signature Pizza Crust" recipe on this site.

I will never buy pizza sauce in a jar again!  OMGoodness, this is sooo good.  My family and daycare all loved the pizza I made tonight.  I used "Jay's Signature pizza crust"(from this site) and this sauce.  It made a wonderful Gourmet Pizza.  thanks for sharing this recipe.
Simple, easy recipe.  I added a little too much sugar, but will use less next time.

I scaled this down to 1 quart and found the sweet-tart level just about perfect. Thanks, hypermice, this was appreciated after four hours doing yard work in 90 degree weather.

Seriously refreshing. I gave it a kick with a jigger of vodka. VERY tasty.
Refreshing...
This was very refreshing and I thouroughly enjoyed it. Thanks for sharing.

This is a great drink for those tired of cola drinks. I vary this all the time. Lime seems to be my favorite, but lemon is also good. For a little added sweetness I do two jiggers of the raspberry syrup and 1/2t sugar. Thanks, Kent!

This was to DIE for!! It is a "10*" recipe! I loved that it was thick and it took care of my chocolate fix! I think I overdid the cinnamon but it made it better! I did not have instant coffee in the jar but I had these maxwellhouse coffee singles (they look like tea bags but with coffee) and I cut the bag and put the coffee from that into the mixing glass I used and it came out super yummy! Thank you Drew!

I was really lazy with this drink, but it turned out really good.  I didn't have any semi-sweet chocolate chips, so I used the regular.  (keep in mind...much more sweet!!)  I didn't add the chili powder because I wasn't sure how it would taste, and I didn't want to ruin a perfectly good cup of hot chocolate, so I wimped out on that part.  I had to add 3/4 of a cup of cold milk because my chocolate was really sweet and I didn't strain mine.  I had to reheat it a bit, but it tasted really good and I like the idea of using chips rather than cocoa powder.  Thanks Drew.

Excellent for a windy and chilly "spring" day.  I would suggest adding more milk unless you really want a thick, delicious syrupy chocolate drink.  Another flavor addition:  I added a fresh mint sprig to the milk mixture as it was heating.    This is so rich that I probably shouldn't make it on a regular basis...but I WILL make it again for a special chocolately treat.

The hot chocolate was ok, but as the recipe suggested, it definitely needed to be thinned with more milk, otherwise it is like drinking chocolate syrup. It was good enough, but I think I'll keep looking.

Well, it was very rich and thick.  Very tasty though too!!  I didn't strain mine, and I think next time I will make sure to do that.  I also added a little more chili powder, and that made it darn tasty!  I'm going to be making this one over and over.

WOW!!!!! I was leery of the combo of flavors, but it was incredible. I used one and half cups of milk—otherwise it would be way too strong—and also heated up all the milk so I wouldn't have a lukewarm drink.

to get a spicy bitterness, i used bittersweet chocolate chips, and also tripled the amount of cinnamon and chili powder, adding an extra 1/4-1/2 cup of milk (i've made it twice already).  after all the ingredients were in, I churned it for 1 minute with one of those handheld devices.  it made it much lighter, fluffier, so that it was still rich, but no longer heavy. churning it also eliminated the graininess others reported---i would still strain it before though, for the ultimate smooth texture.  my family could only take a shot of it because it was so filling---but they LOVED the unique flavor.  next time i am going to add more milk so that people can actually handle a whole mug of this---a dark chocolate lover's wish come true.

I just made this for a cold winter evening, and it was DELICIOUS! It is very thick and chocolatey. My husband loved it. Next time I will add a little more chili powder and more milk. Excellent recipe!

Whoa - this was chocolately!!  I love chocolate, but this was a bit too much - I thinned it with additional milk and it was still a bit much.  Next time I will try 1/4 c chips instead of 1/2 c.  I loved the mix of the spices - this is definitely a "gourmet" hot chocolate!
This was delicious!  I used Cayenne pepper instead of chili simply because I mis read the recipe.  It was still amazing and had a great kick!  I can't wait to make this for my fiance!

I made this exactly as directed, but after everything was mixed together, I strained it through a sieve and cheese cloth. I recommend making this in a glass measuring cup with a spout so it is easy to strain.

This was the best hot chocolate ever.  Omitted the coffee-- and only had milk chocolate chips (which I don't even like, they were bought by mistake), but did everything else- including pouring thru a metal strainer.  So good.

I made this using vegan carob chips since it was the only form of chocolate I had on hand during an especially rainy day. It still came out great, the perfect blend of flavors! I will be making this again, it's super easy and very comforting!

This was a great recipe. I was a little wary about the coffee, even though I love coffee, but it was great. Every ingredient was evident in the taste and it was wonderful. Some people suggested adding more milk because it was to sweet but I don't think so. I did add about a tsp. of vanilla though. I also found it didn't really make enough for two people. I'd add maybe a half a cup of milk or more, a 1/4 a cup more of choc. chips, and maybe a bit more of the chili powder, coffee, and cinammon. You get the point.

Made a bunch of this and served it at a party and received many compliments.  I wound up adding quite a bit of milk to taste, however, since the recipe makes very rich hot chocolate.  People detected the cinnamon but were surprised to hear about the chili pepper!  Good recipe, just expect to use about 1.5x the milk/water the recipe calls for unless you like drinking chocolate syrup.

Hot chocolate for the true chocoholic, Drew! This was soooo rich, just the way we like it here in Rainy Northwest. I made it with espresso powder and little more than a dash of chili powder. WOW!
This is a keeper. And I think for summer time, I'll put this mixture in my blender with some ice cream. What a great shake this would make! Thanks for sharing.

I rated this 5 stars because my husband and I loved it. Anything with a little kick gets a thumbs up from me. But my kids would probably rate it a 2, I had to add a lot of extra milk to get them to drink it. I think they would have liked it better without the extra spices. 
 
 But still an A+.   :)

I was craving hot cocoa and had no cocoa powder in the house... and I am so glad that I didn't!  This is wonderful.  Thick and rich, and the coffee, cinnamon, and yes, even the chili powder, add such a depth of flavor that I can only say you have to make it with the chili powder.  The only change I made was to melt the chocolate and milk on the stove and then heat everything together, rather than use the microwave.  This is definitely "sipping" chocolate, as it is very thick and rich.  Thanks for sharing the recipe.  I can't wait for the next cold night to warm up with this.  Might try it with a touch of cayenne next time, to have a little more heat at the back, but wonderful as is.
The taste isn't too bad (though I'm not a fan of cinnamon) but even after straining the drink has a powdery texture. I couldn't drink it and ended up dumping it down the drain.
delicious - I sometimes add an extra tsp of skim milk powder for even more richness!
Fantastic. I didn't have chocolate chips so I sweetened up some cocoa powder. Added a touch of vanilla just to see how it tasted. Love the chili powder and coffee flavor. Try it!
i didn't like it.

This was good, but for special occasions only. I didn't have a problem with non dissolved granules, because I stirred everything really well in very warm milk. It is rich and filling, but too much to have on a daily basis.
Best ever.  I had extra hot (habanero) powder so used very little, and my cinnamon was a drop of essential oil.  Otherwise followed pretty close and WOW!

This recipe immediately caught my eye because my hubby's name is Drew, so I just had to make it. It's one of those days anyway where I'm craving chocolate in any way, shape or form. I didn't have any chocolate chips in the house, so I subbed with Hershey's syrup. I was literally eating spoonfuls of the syrup as I was making this. Well, Mr. Drew, I must say that this is absolutely fantastic!!!! I'm sipping as I'm writing and LOVING every taste. I'll definitely make this for the kids when they get home. Thanks so much!
excellent! A definite chocolate lovers hot drink.
The tastiest hot chocolate I've ever had, just watch out for the grainy bottoms.
This stuff really has to be strained.  It tastes great, but I was choking on powdery contents the entire time.
Awesome. I didn't strain, but used a mexican hot chocolate "frother" that made it even creamier. I used Hersheys Special Dark chips, and added extra milk. Thanks, Drew!
Pretty good for something different.  I still like "Rich 'N Thick Hot Chocolate" from this site the best!

This was an amazing recipe!!! I cooked the chocolate chips and cold milk on the stove and used a whisk so i didn't have to strain it, it came out delicious. i added way more then a pinch of chili powder and it gave it a nice kick. i will be making this again.

I'm drinking a version of this as m typing this review, and let me say, IT'S AMAZING! I say version, because I really only used this recipe as a guide, because I only has chocolate chips, and no cocoa powder. I used about 3/4 cup of milk and a little over 1/2c. Of chocolate chips. I used 1/4 teaspoon of cinnamon. I left out the chili powder, because I feel like hat would be really weird, and instant coffee and instead I added a little over a teaspoon of really maple syrup. So good! Creamy, and chocolatey and delicious!
Delicious.  This is going into my regular rotation.

I was inspired to try this out after reading some of the reviews.  I couldn't find my Ghirardelli hazelnut hot chocolate so I melted a 1/4 cup of milk chocolate chips in just over a 1/2 cup of milk then added just under a tsp of hazelnut instant coffee.
