Delicious!
Delicious!  The cinnamon adds a really nice flavour and the chili gives just a subtle "kick".  Very rich and great on a cold, snowy house-bound day!  Thanks for sharing this, Drew.

really yummy n rich... very very sweet cuz i dint have semi sweet chocolate chips and added half the amount of normal ones.also i increased the amount of milk.. truly my fantasy of having the hot chocolate in the movie chocolat has come true!
*WARNING* recipe made "as is" is like drinking a candy bar - Good but rich.  I diluted it down with milk and half/half
Incredible. I added just a little more instant coffee, just for my taste. Very, very good.
This was really delicious! I loved the flavour but found it a little too rich, so I just added more milk.
very good!  i don't have instant coffee (can't stand the stuff!)so i substituted a 1/2 cup of real coffee for the instant coffee and 1/2 cup cold milk
this is delicious and it's also really good with shot of good spice rum--my sister and I drank these while she was helping me make the 14 dozen cookies I make over the winter holidays--thanks so much
Rich and very chocolatey.  Used soymilk and it came out great.
This was incredible! best hot chocolate ever! i am a rich chocolate lover and this is RICH! just the perfect satisfaction to my craving
Oh yum.  Very good.
Thick, rich, and delicious. I added more chili powder for a kick though. It's very quick to make too. I dont think I will use instant hot cocoa mix again. Good job Drew. You've outdone yourself.

Just the thick and rich - with a kick - hot chocolate recipe I was looking for! I did add a spot of half and half to thicken it up more, and picked a hazelnut-flavored coffee, but the recipe as is would have still been terrific.

This is too sweet for my taste (yes, I used semi-sweet, still too sweet), perhaps next time I'll use half semi-half cocoa...

In terms of time-quality correlation, this is great for being a 5 minute nuke chocolate
Really chocolatey! And my boyfriend didn't like having to stir the chocolate every 20 seconds...but overall, it was delicious with some freshly ground cinnamon
This hot chocolate was sooo good!  Warm and rich with a little kick to it.  It was just how I would imagine the hot chocolate to be in the movie Chocolat!

Marvelous!!!  I just made this and it is wonderful.  My only criticism is that it is a touch on the sweet side.  I would definitely add even more milk at the end. Really good! Instead of chocolate chips I used some Irish Cream Hershey Kisses I had and it was awesome!

Delicious! Like the recipe says, I thinned it with more milk because it was extra rich!  But it's better to start rich and thin it than try to make a thin recipe rich! If folks had a grainy brew it's because they didn't let the milk get hot enough to dissolve the coffee.  Try Folgers Singles - it's like a tea bag of coffee - or add crystals when the milk is hotter and whisk, whisk, whisk!  Excellent recipe!  Thanks for it!
Made this the old fashioned way: on the stove. Good Stuff!

Great stuff.  It is a bit grainy, but it's really chocolatey and reminds me of the spicy truffles my aunt made once (except it's a drink).  Give it a try!  (Upgraded my review to 5 stars because I've made this drink a million times.  I think it's going to make me fat!)

Oh this is fantastic! I LOVE chocolate, so this was nice and sweet for me. Some whipped cream on top would be divine! Instead of microwaving it, I melted the chocolate, and then heated up the milk on my stovetop in a small sauce pan. This is what I did: 1 Cup semisweet chocolate chips, let those melt completely to a smooth consistency. Add 1 cup of milk, wisk until well combined. Add another cup of milk and again wisk your heart you. The more you wisk it, the better it mixes together and the creamier it gets. I used 1.5 cups of milk in total. After it was all combined I added 1tsp of cinnamon and 1/2 tsp of chili powder. Heat it up to your desired temperature and pour into a mug!  I've tried it the microwave version first, and it was grainy as other people have complained. Doing it on the stovetop I had no graininess! Enjoy this fabulous recipe!

Absolutely DELICIOUS!!!  My children loved it and asked me to make it again before they were finished.  I don't think I will ever be able to give them the package stuff again.  We will definitely make this again and again.
very rich and chocolatey.  one of the best cups of hot choc. I've ever had and I'm a hard critic since I always make mine homemade.
I'm sipping my hot chocolate, and it is really good!  This made enough for a big cup of hot chocolate.

Different, but good.I used 2 sq. Ghiredelli semi-sweet choc. and the  rest choc. chips, used a mixture of skim and 2% milk. Because I found the coffee flavor a bit to strong for me I used a bit more milk and nuked it to heat it up some more.
next time I would do half the coffee amount.Will definitely make again, thanks for sharing!
I'm not sure what everybody who has rated this recipe as good actually drank, but it wasn't this one! I followed the recipe exactly, so i know it was no error on my part.

This was excellent, nice and thick and rich.  Nothing like the watery powder mix from the grocery store.  I have been looking for a hot chocolate recipe like this.  I had all the ingredients on hand (except for heavy cream…I really wanted whipped cream on the top)!!  I added about ½ tablespoon of chili powder and only a smidge of cold milk.

It is almost 95 degrees outside today, I cannot wait till it is cold and snowy to really enjoy this!
Drew this was great!!! I absolutely loved it. My family thought I was crazy when I said it had chili powder. But everybody loved it! Next time I'll use marshmallows! Thanks!!!

This was delicious, but personally a bit too rich for my taste. I thinned it quite a bit with skim milk. Still, the chili/cinnamon/chocolate combo is a winner, and the coffee gives it a considerable jolt.

Yikes!  I can't believe I had all of these liquors in my cabinet!  What does that say about me?!?  I guess that I like a good drink, including this one!  I had just enough cream of coconut leftover from coconut poke cake (from this site) to make this drink.  It's creamy and refreshing, perfect to serve with a spicy meal.  I made 1/2 recipe, which was just right for the two of us.  We loved the nutmeg on top too!

This is an amazing indulgence!  I first tried these in St. Thomas - a restaurant/bar offered samples on the street, and they SO hit the spot in the humid climate - was I ever hooked!  Every time we return to the island, we stop in to our favorite bar for a few of these, then I take my hubby jewelry shopping..:-)  I like to add some ice to mine to make them more like a milkshake, which is the way they serve them at the Happy Buzzard in St. Thomas.  Thanks so much for the recipe!

Very tasty! I will make it again. I did change the cooking method. I pre cooked minute rice then added it to all the ingredients on the stove top. This allowed me to avoid heating up the kitchen with the oven.

I love this recipe, and my family does too! Full disclosure: I have used the recipe twice now, but not exactly as written either time. This is what I changed (my daughter is pescetarian): 14 oz. Tofurkey Italian Sausage instead of hot dogs; 1 lbs. raw peeled shrimp instead of vegetarian fried chicken; 1.5 cups wild rice blend instead of 1 cup brown rice; ground thyme instead of dried. Also, the recipe calls for 2 tsp. cajun seasoning; I used 1 tsp of Tony Chacere's Cajun Seasoning, which has a lot of salt, and 1 tsp of creole spices with no salt added, which gives it a little more kick. Also, the first time I used dry rice, which did not cook thoroughly on the top layer, so the second time, I partially cooked the rice first.
awesome. used tofu instead of the imitation meat products and no celery due to lack of said ingredients but was still great.
I mixed it up a bit by adding some black beans and halved grape tomatoes. I also cooked the rice hall the time prior to baking. Will make again and again.

I loved it! I bought the spicy buffalo wings from Morning Star to give an extra kick and the diced tomatoes with the green chillies in them.
My partner loved this recipe!

We loved this!  I didn't use a whole can of hotdogs and only 1 can of FriChik, but it was really good!  Next time I will probably use a little less cayenne. And leftovers are good combined with refried beans in a bean/rice burrito.

I put this sauce on some home-made quesadillas, my boyfriend said it was like taco bell at home... when we ran out of those he used it as a dip for anything else he could find, it was a big hit!

awesome on shrimp tacos with avocado slices I will use it on many more mexican dishes planning on using it with chicken wraps

Yum! I made this super easy on myself by defrosting part of a bag of frozen onion/bell pepper mix, throwing in several slices of jalepeno from a jar, and mashing it with my potato masher. He said, "Now all you have to do is figure out that Bloomin' Onion sauce."  Thanks for the recipe - we were thrilled.
This receipe was close to taco Bells

This sauce was great, we made grilled stuffed burritos just like Taco Bells and with sauce it really made it perfect.  I did everything just to the recipe with a few exceptions, I read the other reviews and I used a little sour cream in it as well, and I used all the pepper mix instead of a few tbs.  It was great!

This was wonderful....I ended up using a whole bell pepper and half of an onion with the jalapeno, I didn't seed the jalapeno, so adding the extra bell and onion mellowed out the heat for my kids. But when adding it to the mayo, 1 used a total of 8 tsp of mixture and I did 1/2 cup mayo and 1/2 cup of sour cream and added 1 tbsp chili powder, 1 tsp cayenne and 1 tsp paprika and Man Alive was get awesome. I'd rate this a good recipe, because it is a good recipe, we just modified it a little more for us.

This is an amazing tasting sauce, I cant get enough of it. Feel free to throw in an extra jalepeno if you like a little spice. Also they don't mention it in the recipe, but when you chop up the bell pepper, jalepeno and onion, it actually produces enough to make more than 2 recipes worth. So if you want, double up on the mayo/vinegar/spices since you will have enough of the other mixture for more than twice as much.

Absolutely perfect as is!  This was exactly what I needed on my Mock Quizno's Baja Chicken sub. Just combine with Chipotle Mayo and BAM! FLAVOR! My family even said that it came out better!  THANK YOU!!! putting this in my hardback recipe book that will be an heirloom!

Pretty close tot he taco bell version.  I found it hard to puree such a small amount of stuff.  And as others have said, the amount of peppers and onions listed makes enough for a double batch.  I did double the mayo and other wet ingredients to make up for that.  Next time I will try roasting the pepper and onion first.  I think it will intensify the flavors. This is awesome! It taste like the sauce at Taco Bell.
So good!!!!
This has become a family/friend favorite. We add more jalepeno and sometimes some cayenne pepper to spice it up a bit. I also use LITE mayo to cut back on calories.
it tastes and smells just like Taco Bells baja sauce! I left out the bell pepper and added a little extra jalapenos. I can't live with out it now.

I love this recipe!  I changed it just a bit for my taste.  I used fresh garlic and instead of a rich mayo flavor I split the portion of mayo with mayo, soften cream cheese and sour cream.  I love it on fish tacos!
yummy! eat this with fish tacos and raw veggies.
Fresh tasting but needs to be intensified more next time. I had let it rest for several hours until dinner time. It paired very nicely with our pan-seared striped bass.
I really enjoyed this ... I prefer with a 50/50 mix of mayo & sour cream tho.  Great as a topping for spanish rice, tacos, etc.  Similar to Taco Bell baja sauce.
This is a HUGE hit with my family and large groups for mexican meals in general!
VERY YUMMY! Addictive!
For sure!!!!!!! Lovin this one! So easy too! We used this on tortilla chips and our chimi's. You could just about eat this with a spoon!

I also minced the jalapeno, and used green pepper because that was what I had. I also minced up some fresh garlic instead of powder, which I always think has a bit more flavor. Very simple and quick, and when I put it together with my fried fish and shredded cabbage it really did remind me of vacations at Rosarito Beach in Baja. Thanks!

Love this recipe! I don't totally puree the pepper mixture, I just mix enough so that it is super finely chopped. Very Good, but only for about 1-3 days. After that it liquified.

Pretty close to Taco Bell's Baja Sauce. VERY simple. I would make this again but I think I might try this with half sour cream next time and increase the garlic powder and cumin. Heat-wise, it's perfect.
simply amazing, man it added so much to our home cooked mexican food, thank you for putting it on here

Great sauce for blackened fish tacos with a little shredded cabbage and avocado! Great sauce! We added it to steak burritos along with rice and beans, then grilled them in a G.F. grill. The sauce really added more flavor. We loved it.

good addition to mexican food.

used this for nachos, tacos, and taco salad, wow what a great addition.

IT SEEMS THICK BUT ONCE IT SETS IN THE FRIDGE FOR 4 HOURS IT HAS GREAT FLAVOR....FOR NOW ON JUST MAYO!****
This sauce is WONDERFUL on grilled fish tacos! Thanks for the great recipe.
A very nice sauce to compliment many of my Spanish inspired dishes definitely a keeper. I like a little bite to my sauce, and a few more jalapenos did just that. great recipe.
I loved this sauce. I used this with chicken tacos. I also diced up onion and tomatoes with some lime juice for some acidity and topped the tacos with shredded lettuce. Very good and so fresh!

I suggest doubling up on the first part of this; use 1/2 red bell pepper, 2 jalapenos & about half of an onion. Then mix the 2nd part of the recipe as stated. I mixed half of the pepper mixture with the mayo mixture. Then reserved the other half of the pepper mix in the fridge. Later in the week I used it blended with some melted butter to have as topping for crab cakes. This was incredibly yummy both ways, with the mayo mix AND with the melted butter! It's also simple enough to make it to your liking... add more or less jalapeno, depending on how spicy you want it. Also, some of the reviewers thought the mayo was too heavy. If you feel that way, just add a few more splashes of vinegar. Overall, a great recipe that is versatile and extremely tasty. Well worthy of 5 stars!

Awesome recipe!! Tastes just like the real thing, only thing I changed was I added a tiny bit more cumin and garlic powder and 1 more jalapeno because we like things hot and spicy in the house!!!  After it sit it was AWESOME!!!
I liked it. It didn't remind me of Sprite® but it was very refreshing on a hot, humid day. The only thing that I changed was  decreasing the sugar to 2 tablespoons. Thanks for the recipe.

This was delish! I spread it on some grilled baguette slices. Next time I make it, and there will be a next time, I'll use less salt. Hubby said he'd like it over some pasta so I'll give it a try! Thanks so much for this recipe!

I wouldn't change a thing unless I could make the calories disappear. I'd just said this week that I was going on a quest for the best hot cocoa around. Well that was a short journey. I've found it! It's like "sipping chocolate" that I've had in NYC.

I made this for New Years day.  I'm not much of a cook and this sounded simple and easy.  Just one pot, low heat, readily available ingredients with some measuring.  What could go wrong?  I made it exactly as written and after stirring for 30 minutes the chocolate chips were melted I guess.  I wasn't sure because although everything seemed smooth there were lots and lots of little tiny  dark chocolate colored specks throughout the mixture.  I decided to continue stirring  on low heat for another 10 minutes to see if these needed to "melt" and become incorporated with the mix.  That didn't work so I decided to try the hot chocolate as is.  Everyone thought it was OK but they would also have been happy with Swiss Miss and extra marshallows.  I put the mix into the crock pot as suggested to try some later.   Later arrived and all of the chocolate specks were floating on the top and had to be stirred into the hot chocolate.  Taste was still OK but I wanted GREAT after stirring for 40 minutes.  Much later arrived and everything had thickened.  Stirring didn't help and I ended up with chocolatety lumpy porridge.   Bah Hum Bug.  I gave it 3 stars because I'm sure I messed up somehow.  I did learn to test new recipies before the gathering!

Loved this hot chocolat; a perfect Christmas Day treat.  It definitely needed to be cut with milk before serving.  I will use less condensed milk next time.  I added Baileys to mine and will be adding coffee for guests tomorrow!
Great!  And YES, we will make it again

I used Ghirardelli 60 % cacao chips and all other ingredients exactly as stated. I made sure to use the good Tahitian vanilla.
Excellent! I would only recommend 2 changes to the steps. I will heat the milk before adding the chocolate and I will chop up the chips so that it decreases melting time. We will make it again.
Delicious...even for Valentine's Day. Rich, creamy, and chocolate-y.

Very sweet very chocolaty... And we love chocolate but we kept adding milk and adding milk still very sweet and very rich in chocolate. We will use half of condensed milk and half of chocolate next time. I will give it another chance.. Everyone poured their mug back into pot so mom can try to fix it! :(

These are delicious! When I make these again, I'll probably try adding a bit more cinnamon and banana. I did as a previous reviewer suggested and placed the mixture into a ziploc bag and piped it in spirals into the hot oil. The result was a nice circular spiral that looked awfully close to a donut, minus the hole in the middle!

It was fine and the texture was just right, but I used nowhere near 1 quart of oil and the banana flavor was barely detectable as Chevonne said. Based on that and other people's comments of blandness, I upped the cinnamon to 1 tsp. and added an extra banana. Wonderful. Beyond that, just some tips: a) A piping bag isn't really necessary. The trick is to drop the right amount of batter in the oil all at once, otherwise you get these strings and odd shapes. I used on overfilled gravy ladle and let a dollop drop in. b) Eggs and milk should be room temp or you risk having a browned outside but uncooked middle. c) Use a lower temp. All stoves are different, so do a test batch at 325 first, then adjust. I ended up using 275 to avoid browning too fast and cooking everything in the middle. d) Don't overcrowd the pan. Each fritter lowers the oil temp, and it's much easier to manage five or six than 10. e) Don't add sugar to the batter, otherwise they'll brown faster. I also used tongs to flip and remove them from the pan before sprinkling with powdered sugar. Great recipe!
