I liked the consistency of this soup very much but it was way to much onion for us. If I ever make this again I'll only use about half as much onion.
This was a great soup, I like mine a little thicker so we had no problem with this.  Excellent.  Thanks for the post.

I used a little less onion -- i pretty much halved the recipe, as there's only 3 of us! But it turned out great.  I wanted a thicker soup and this was exactly what i was looking for.  Came out great, only change really was that i took half the cooked bacon and chopped up some chives and let it simmer all together for the last 15 to 10 minutes.  really made all the flavors come together.

A hit with me and the hubby! I will add extra real potatoes next time. I used skim milk instead of half-and-half. I used 3 cups chicken stock and 3 cups water. Used less onions, because I only had a cup. This will definitely go in the personal favorites cookbook!

I have to agree with a previous reviewer.  I made this soup exactly as the recipe indicated, and it does, indeed, taste very strongly of instant mashed potatoes.  Expecting restaurant-quality soup from potato flakes is just setting yourself up for disappointment.  

However, it definitely had potential, so I made it again using leftover homemade mashed potatoes instead of the flakes (adjusting the liquid accordingly) and it was divine.  Try it this way and you'll be in potato-soup *heaven.*  (I bet you could use a tub of pre-made real mashed potatoes from the refrigerated section in the grocery store, too.)

Good grief! I have been making this for nearly 4 years (based on the date at the bottom of the printed recipe) and somehow haven't rated it until now. We've been absolutely loving it, but I do double the amount of potatoes used (for a chunkier soup) and microwave them when I haven't planned sufficiently ahead. Sometimes I'll use potato flakes as stated, but if there are leftover mashed potatoes on hand, then those will be subbed. I also saute a clove of garlic with the chopped onion. Thankfully it's a very forgiving recipe. I've had to increase the number of servings that I make in hopes of having a bowlful leftover for lunch the next day. Yum!

This soup was exactly what I was looking for! The only real change I made was using cornstarch and extra potato flakes instead of flour to make it Gluten-Free and it still came out thick and delicious.
Oh yum!  This is the potato soup recipe I have been looking for.  No changes need to be made.

I would give this soup 3.5 stars. It was far too thick made as written (think mashed potato thick). I ended up having to add considerably more cream to thin it out. I also didn't care for the overwhelming flavor of the instant potato flakes. If I made this again I would try adding the cornstarch by itself first, letting it thicken, then add just enough potato flakes as needed to further thicken and flavor. The three toppings finish this recipe really well.
My family loved this easy to make recipe! My daughter wants me to make this for her 8th birthday.  I would serve it in small sourdough bread bowls next time.
The flavor of the instant potatoes overpowered the true flavor of the soup.
Very good..my family couldn't get enough!
this is really good. i was slightl worried because we don't eat instant potaoes, but it tasted really good. i followed the recipe to the tee. next time i will add a little less pepper
It was good

Really, really good!  I needed to make it lower in fat so here is what I did-I used 8 ounces lower sodium bacon  and coarsely diced it before crisply frying it.  I only used one cup potato flakes, used skim milk instead of half and half, and used low sodium, fat-free chicken broth.  I put the bacon right into the soup before the second simmer rather than just using as a garnish, and  I skipped the cheese entirely.  Oh, and I mixed the cornstarch in with the water before putting it into the soup.  I will make this again and again.
I made the recipe as is, and people raved over it.  Said it was the best potato soup they'd ever had!  Thanks for the recipe.

This was great.  I added another potato for more substance. I omitted the flour because one of my dinner guests has celiac's disease (can't eat gluten) and the soup still thickened up beautifully.  Garnishing the soup with the bacon just immediately before serving is a must so that it is still crisp.  I served it with a side of broccoli and fresh sourdough rolls. Everyone commented on how good it was.

This soup was very good. I would add more potatoes and serve it with cheese topping to give more flavor. Very good heated up the next day. I agree on the bacon bits . I used turkey bacon and it seemed a bit floppy in the soup.

My Fiance' dislikes soup for some reason unbeknown st  to me.  Where as I enjoy homemade soup of any kind especially in the winter.  I came across this recipe and decided I would try it out on him.  We, yes we loved it!  The texture was perfect and the flavor awesome.  This is the best potato soup recipe I have ever made!

This soup Marbalet is outstanding.  My husband said while he was eating it, this was probably the best meal I have ever made.  I wouldn't change a thing and I have been passing out the recipe to everyone.  Thank you

oh my god is this good!! I did do SOME things different though. I sauteed the bacon with the onions. And i added garlic .I also poured some milk in it along with some half and half. i added more potatoes then it said too.Not that you needed to do anything different, this is just me. I never measured anything either, only the chicken stock, and water. I also steamed some broccoli and let the kids add it to their soup if they wanted.They didn't but my husband and i did. Awesome recipe. thankyou sooo much for this recipe!!!
This is absolutely delicious...and so easy to make. I love potato soup, and thought I'd give this one a whirl and I'm glad that I did. Thanks for a great recipe!
Excellent!!!

Ohhh myyyy GOD!! This was an UNBELIEVABLE soup!!! I just finished making it for my first time and I know for a fact I will be making it again and again!!! Thank you Marbalet for this fantastic recipe!!

This is an awesome recipe.  I had searched for years for a great potato soup recipe and this is it.  I did take others' advice and cut the corn starch in half and I also used fat free half & half, broth (instead of stock) and cut the potato flakes a bit.  It is a very thick, rich and hearty soup.  Brought some into work and they loved it.  Reheats nicely (even thicker the next day).  Great for fall/winter!

This soup is absolutely delecious. I can't believe that I made something that tasted so good! On my day off, I wanted to make something for my wife when she got off work. She loves potato soup so I picked this recipe to attempt. This was my third attempt at cooking, so I consider myself a bonified rookie. The directions were easy to follow.  I did make a few changes... We had some left over corn beef from St. Patty's day so I sliced it up and added it to the soup. I also added more potatoes, some fresh mushrooms and a garlic clove. The soup was extra thick so next time I would put a little less corn starch.  I ate three bowls last night and two for breakfast this morning!! My wife said it was the best she had ever eaten. WOW!

I made this last week and loved it - I did not change much at all - used half cream and 1/2 milk because that was all I had on hand and I added a pound of bacon to the recipe (not just on top). I did not have any green onions on hand so I skipped that.  IT WAS SO GOOD - I raved about it for so long my husband asked if it was better than s** - I told him it was a toss up. ;-)

I'm giving this recipe as written 4 stars because I just can't imagine using potato flakes - yuck!  However, with my mods it was really good.  I used about 7 smallish potatoes, used the immersion blender to smooth about 5 of them, and then added the remaining potatoes in chunks to give it a little more texture.  Also, used heavy cream instead of half & half, no water - skim milk instead, and fresh basil instead of dried.  My kids loved it.
Excellent soup!  It is truly yummy.  I cut out some fat by sauteing the onions in some of the broth, then using skim milk instead of the half & half, with no sacrifice to the taste.
I love this soup.  We have made it twice and it turns out great!
I tried this tonight and it is a really awesome soup!  The only thing I had to change was adding bacon to the soup as well as some cheddar cheese.  Kudos!  Thanks!
I thought that it truly was "restaurant-quality."  AWESOME, AWESOME, AWESOME!  Husband loved to too!
This was so good we served it as the main course at a church dinner!
This was a good recipe.  My husband loved it.  I personally did not like the texture/tast from the instant mashed and did not need the additional cornstarch.  It reheated wonderfully the next day.
I loved it. I made it for a potluck and everyone loved it. it was gone before i put out the toppings! I made one change. I didn't have chicken broth so i used chicken bullion cubes instead.

I've been using this recipe for a couple of years now and I get more compiments on it - it is a staple for my winter holiday parties!  I do have to adjust it to fit my crowd so here's my 2 cents...Use a 5lb bag of russets and douple the remaining ingredints.  It feeds 10 adults nicely!  Also, I use the garlic mashed potato flakes!  Good luck and enjoy!
Excellent soup!  This is definitely a keeper.  Despite being a quick and easy recipe, it's very tasty.

Creamy and wonderful!  I took the advise of previous reviews with great results - use 3 potatoes, use only 1/8 cup of cornstarch, and use only a 4 oz. package of potato flakes.  Filling and delicious!
This was great!  It has alot of ingredients, but still really easy.  I used imitation bacon bits instead of real bacon.

This soup was delicious.  I added a little parmesan to the soup, but otherwise I did stick to the recipe.  My family loved it too.  I will definitely be making this again.  Thanks for sharing.  I'll be adding this recipe to my "favorite" recipes.
This recipe is terrific.  I've made it a couple of times and it is a hit each time!!!

ahhh i dont know how i feel about this. i  halved it, and used 3 red potatoes that were on the small side. and used skim milk instead of half and half. but i wouldnt have thought that would make it taste different! i just think it's not as good as the other potato soup recipe i tried from this website!!

This was very good. I did use flour mixed with water to thicken the soup instead of cornstarch as I find cornstarch tends to make liquid a little slimy. I used leftover ham from Easter rather than bacon but I'm sure the bacon would be good too--just wanted to use the ham up.

Use the "fresh" diced hash brown potatoes w/onion available now to make this even quicker!  Just add the pkg of potatoes along with the broth/water and simmer a few minutes before you add the potato flakes and 1/2 and 1/2.  (I still used the whole onion, sauteed as called for).  1 package (4 oz.) of "Loaded Baked" potato flakes was plenty to thicken it -- didn't need the cornstarch at all.  Added cheese to the soup AND added some on top for garnish.  Used FF half and half to cut some calories.  A great super-fast shortcut to homemade potato soup!

This is a wonderful soup for a cold wintery day.  The addition of the instant potatoes is an excellent thickener.  My local (Kroger) grocery store sells a great soup that reminds me of this, but this is cheaper to make and I like it better.
Great soup! This is about the 4th baked potato soup recipe I've tried and my family said it was the best!
Made this recipe exactly the same besides adding about 1/2 cup more bacon, turned out excellent, my mom who loves potato soup & is really picky says it was the best she`s had, better then her own.

This soup was really good...one of the best I've tried.  However, the cornstarch made lumps in the soup, so next time I'll use less.  I also substituted whole milk for the half & half to save calories. Nex time I'll try skim milk.

Delicious recipe.  Very good recipe as a base to change it to what you have around the kitchen (used flour instead of corn starch, used 2-1 cup pouches of potato flakes, used whole milk, added Queso Velveeta cheese to mine to melt, stirred the bacon into it, added a can of corn, and cooked it with bay leaves for flavor).  I'm sure it would have been great as is also.

Made the recipe as is and loved every bite of it.  Husband and son gobbled it up as well.  Will definitely make again and this time I won't forget to use the bacon bits that I bought to serve with the soup!

This was SOOO good, and so easy to make!  I made it for my daughters birthday party, and it was all gone by the end.  I had about five members of my family ask for the recipe!  The only thing about it is, the cornstarch made clumps in the soup...  I will probably make a paste with the cornstarch next time.

I made this as my first attempt at soup, I had never made a roux in my life! It turned out AMAZING, my husband and 2 toddler sons devoured it with cheese and bacon biscuits and have been begging me to make it again! I changed a few things a bit: I sauted some minced garlic with the onion; instead of fully baking the potatoes I microwaved them for about 5 minutes; I used leftover prepared mashed potatoes instead of just flakes; and I used Italian seasoning and steak seasoning instead of salt, pepper and the spices called for. Another recipe on this site: pull-apart bacon bread, it compliments this soup so well, I crumble the bread into my soup bowl. Delicious!

Since you asked if I made any changes, I will tell you that I did.  I followed the basic recipe except for the thickeners, no flour, no cornstarch, no instant potatoes.  I simply added a couple of extra potatoes and used my potato masher in the soup until I had it of the consistency that I wanted.  I also added an extra cup of FF half and half.  Other than that I followed the recipe.
Oh yeah, and a lot more bacon, but not in the soup...on the top as a garnish.
Absolutely delicious!  Yes, I will make this again.

this is beyond the best soup i have ever tasted its better than black anguses....and that is saying something..i added some celery and sauted it with the onion gives a nice flavor...also this would be a good base for clam chowder...or you could add corn, green beans anything just about...i added the bacon and cheese to the whole pot that is how my family likes it...it is some time to make but well worth it...you wont regret making it but if you are planning on serving a crowd ya better make more than one batch it dont go very far cause of how thick it is...enjoy i will make this recipe for the rest of my life

Great recipe!!! Almost didn't try because of the potato flakes, but glad I listened to the majority of the reviews and gave it a try as written.  Only change I'd make is next time I'll tmake a double batch.

This was delicious and full of flavor.  I shortened my cooking time by peeling and cutting up the potatoes before boiling.  I would probably use less half and half or cornstarch next time because mine was a bit too thick, but otherwise this recipe lived up to it's name. Thanks.

This soup is  fabulous. I made a huge pot and took it to a Lenten Soup supper potluck and it was gone in no time. Don't cut out the green onions & bacon. Without them it's a good soup. With them it's a great soup.
This was wonderful! I used 3 potatoes, sour cream and onion mashed potato flakes and only half the cornstarch. I also added corn just because we love it in potato soup. Will keep in my favorites!

This was really great but I changed it a bit. I didn't bake the potatoes until they were completely done, added a can of corn, added the bacon bits before serving and chunks of ham. Threw it all in the crock pot for a couple hours to finish cooking the potatoes and it really helped to blend the flavors together even better.

This was pretty good.  The toppings are a must to really taste like a true baked potato!  I added an extra potato and I still think it needed more chunks of potato.  I served this with mini reubens.  Yummy!
My family adored this recipe! As do I. Amazing flavor.

I was looking for an easy and great tasting potato soup recipe for me and my partner; I have never really cooked anything, unless it's boxed or frozen, but this was really good!!!  I did add 2 cans of cheddar cheese soup, because we both love cheese, but otherwise I followed the recipe exactly and it was awesome!  I wll def be making this again!

I didn't have a whole lot of time this morning to wait for potatoes to bake, so I roasted them. I used the Roast Potatoes recipe, which is also from this site. I had a couple extra potatoes so I just cubed them and threw them in, too, just to use them up. Plus, it made the soup a little "chunkier". I omitted the cornstarch only because I thought the flour and potato flakes would be enough thickener on it's own. I used Cracker Barrel 2% extra white cheddar. I did stir the original bacon and cheddar in, I just set bowls of extra on the table for garnish. We all liked this. I actually was able to make this in my crockpot without issues. Plenty of leftovers, which is always nice. I served this with Cottage Dill Bread.
Outstanding!

I am a professional chef who works as a Child Nutritionist with the
Homewood City Shcool System in Birmingham, Alabama, and am always looking
for different things to go on a school lunch program. Usually when I have soup
on the menu, we make 35 gallons of soup and have some left over. When I

hearing, "Where's that great soup we've heard about?"
When I can make that many teenagers happy with a soup, it must be 
SOME SOUP. Thanks for all the help!
Melissa Dupree CNP
Ive made this recipe twice and both times have been great.  Delicious.  I cant wait to compare it to a restaurant recipe :)
If you like the KFC mashed potato bowls, then you will love this recipe.

My boyfriend and I LOVE this soup!! I used cheddar flavored potato flakes and as other reviewers suggested, I cut down on the flakes and cornstarch.  At first I was worried that it would have a "fake" potato taste due to the flakes, but this was not an issue at all.   Yum!

VERY good!  Easy.  I dissolved the corn starch in water and had no lumps-only had about 1/8 cup of corn starch, but that was perfect.  I used 3 potatoes and didn't brown the onions-just cooked until tender.  The downside?  NO LEFTOVERS!!!  Have already emailed the recipe to 7 friends.  Thanks.
Made this tonight and it was awesome! I added some celery and used cheese and bacon in the recipe instead of just garnish.
My family loved this soup. Easy and tasty. I did add a little water as I felt it was too thick for soup. Will definately be making this again.
Delicious! My husband asked if I made it! A keeper!
Excellent. I made the recipe as written and would not change a thing.
This soup was wonderful.  It was extremely easy to make and very tasty.  I will definately make it again.

I made several changes... which turned it into a pot full of epic win. I mashed two ginormous cooked baked potatoes with sour cream and some salt, pepper, and paprika. Then I cooked everything like was stated, except instead of 2 cups water I replaced it with 2 cups milk. I skipped the potato flakes since I found it unnecessary. I added some garlic powder and paprika powder and then I added the creamed mashed potatoes into the soup. I didn't add the half and half and I added a little cheddar cheese and some bacon to the tops of the bowls. I didn't use the green onions. This was the best tasting potato soup ever. Epic soup is epic.
This was fabulous! I've also added left over hamburger & it was good too.

I did not like this at all. All I could taste was the fake potatoes. The texture was kind of gross as well. It was like runny mashed potatoes. I followed the recipe exactly. I will not be making this one again.
a little spicy, use less pepper

This was an interesing recipe. It was a bit thicker than I prefer and I thought that the taste was off abit from the instant potatoes. My husband on the other hands loved it. The next time I may just puree some of the potatoes to thicken the soup instead of adding instant potato. I would also use much less onion as the onion flavor was very pronounced.
Excellent, rich soup.  Used up some left over mashed potatoes instead of instant flakes, but otherwise didn't change a thing.  This will go in my "regulars" file to make often.
this is not restaurant quality with "potato flakes" in it, nor with margarine. good for food service or a homemaker looking for easy recipe

This is an excellent soup. Made it for the first time last night. Followed the recipe exactly, except I only had sour cream and chive instant potatoes. It was wonderful. My husband, who is an extrememly picking eater, even loved it. I will be making this again many times thru out the winter.
This recipe was a big flop with my family. All anyone could taste was Thyme.

Very good! i used chicken bouillon and 4 potatoes - it was thick but i thought it was perfect and my hubby and 4 yr. old loved it!
i did use italian seasoning instead of the other seasonings.

Even though my primary love is baking, I really enjoy cooking also.  Today we decided to go for some hot, potato soup. This wonderful, flavorful soup is great for the rainy, cold weather we're having.  My boyfriend and I paired it with hot, turkey sandwiches, while my son enjoyed a slice of toasted garlic-cheese bread with his soup.  We definitely plan on having this soup again in the very near future.  I made few changes to our version, I fried the bacon in the stock pot and drained off the fat before adding the butter and onion to give a little bacon flavor to the soup and also a tsp. of minced, roasted garlic.  At the end, I added more potato and added a little more half and half, but other than that, I definitely give this soup...5 stars!!!

This has 5 star potential with some modifications... less onion (maybe 1 cup instead of 2), and less potatoe flakes/cornstarch as the soup was a bit too thick. Also, I used evaporated skim milk instead of the cream to reduce the fat content, but this made the soup a touch too sweet. Next time I will just add 2% milk as the added thickness was not necessary.

Thanks Holly!  This has become our fave! Even my 7 yr old will eat this, and he hates soup! Some TIPS- I peel the potatoes and bake them in the microwave, it makes it go much faster. Also, used 4-5 potatoes, added cheese to the soup at the end, and mixed the cornstarch with the 2 cups of water.  I use skim milk and it's great. Thanks again!

Everyone in my family devoured every last bit of this soup. My father actually used bread to wipe the bowl clean!  I made it vegetarian by using vegetable broth and vegetarian bacon strips. I will definitely be making this again! Thanks for the knockout recipe.
This is a wonderful recipe. We had left over baked potatoes and it worked out great. I didn't change a thing, it was perfect. I will be having this soup again soon.
Very, very good. I am gluten intolerant so I left out the flour to make it a gluten free recipe - and still was perfect.
It was a little thick. I added more chicken broth and it was perfect.
Was ok. Very thick -  I didn't particularly like it, but my husband did. Won't make it again.

I can't believe I haven't rated this yet. I have made it for years. It is GREAT. I microwave the potatoes, use 1 c. onion, & use a little less potato flakes. I also use real bacon bits in a jar (easier) & omit the green onions as a garnish. This recipe is easier than it may seem.
Made with a couple changes. Used olive oil to saute the onions. Swapped the half and half for skim milk. Only used cheese for a garnish. Came out creamy and delicious. Very good!
This was a very easy and great tasting soup! I do think for us it was best right after cooking vs left overs.  I will certainly make this again! Thank you!

This is seriously the BEST baked potato soup I have ever made! I have been searching high and low for a perfect match to many potato soups I get while out and this one tops it off! I didn't change a thing from the original recipe and it was perfect!

I've been looking for a baked potato soup recipe for a long time and this is it!  This is a terrific soup and easy to make.  My husband couldn't get enough of it.  I used fat-free half and half and it was still thick and creamy.  I also used 3 potatoes instead of 2.  This is a definite keeper!!

omitted cornstarch.  plenty thick enough. used two cans of diced potatoes--busy week-night supper. NO baking required. Turned out very nice.  husband told me after we ate, that he does not like potato soup in general, not the recipe itself.  so i probably will not make again.  Oh well, more leftovers for me.

This was AWESOME!  I left out the onion because I've tried other potato soup recipes that call for it and it doesn't appeal to me.  I also left out the cornstarch and used milk instead of half and half or cream - it was SO GOOD.  My kids loved it.  I have been looking for a potato soup recipe that gets close to a favorite chain restuarant and this one is IT!!!  Thank you so much!
This soup was SOOO YUMMY!  Followed the recipe and it turned out perfect.  I have 2 picky eaters and they loved it!  Will make again!  Thanks for a great recipe!
Increased to 18 servings to make 2 pots. It was very thick and tasted good.
This is just like the potato soup at our favorite steak house!!  Now we can make it at home! Fantastic!
My family loves this recipe.

I thought that there was way too much cornstarch in this recipe.  The soup almost tasted pasty.  And the baked potatoes got really mushy and were hard to cut up.
I wouldn't make this again.

Very rich and hearty soup! Excellent flavor. I, too used chicken broth instead of stock and more cheese than it called for. This one's a keeper!
Thanks, Holly for sharing this recipe.

Great soup! I did follow some of the advice from other reviews. I didn't make the flour roux, but I did add 1/8 cup (or 4 TBsp) corn starch. Also, using the garlic flavored potato flakes is a must. It adds sooo much flavor. I would highly recommend this recipe for anyone throwing a dinner party. Very impressive even though it is not that difficult. Thanks!

This is a really good and easy soup, but as written, the consistency is way too thick.  I even cut the corn starch in half and it was still too thick.  I would suggest starting with 1/8 c. cornstarch and 1/2 c. of potato flakes.  You can add more flakes slowly as the mixture thickens until you get to a consistency you like.  I would have much preferred a more "cream soup-y" consistency and what I got was very "mashed potato-y".  I was concerned about the 1/2 tsp. basil, but it ended up being a very mellow flavor and not overpowering.  I think nest time I might add just a tiny bit of bacon grease with the butter when sautéing the onions to give it a little more bacon flavor.  Otherwise, really great.  I really like doing the baked potatoes in advance and cutting the chunks up in the soup.

Upon hearing we were having potato soup for supper, my kids all groaned. However, they LOVED this soup! I would add another potato or two next time. I boiled the potatoes in bite sized pieces, which took less time than baking.  This is absolutely delicious! I had a craving for it while we were in NYC so I ordered some from a deli. It wasn't as good as this recipe, and it cost $5.50 a bowl! I definitely recommend this recipe.
Spicier than I anticipated, but still very tasty. Used fat free half & half, reduced fat cheese, reduced sodium chicken stock and reduced sodium bacon and it was still great.

I wish I could give this 10 stars! We use 3 potatoes, garlic flavored flakes and 1/8C of cornstarch. We also add about a cup of shredded cheddar with the half & half. This is the best potato soup I've ever had, we make it at least once a month!
This was a good recipe.  However, it didn't wow me like I thought it should.

This is a truly AWESOME homemade soup. It tastes just like the one we get at our favorite restaurant. I cut the onions to 1 cup, and added one more potatoe. But other than that, the recipe was perfect for us. Thanks Holly. This is a keeper for these rainy Pacific Northwest days.
Just made this with a few minor changes and it came out SO good. Thanks, it is great!!
This soup is great!  It was easy to make and it really does taste like it came straight from a restaurant!  I added a little bit of garlic but otherwise followed the recipe word for word.

Just made the soup with some changes which will make the "it's too thick" or "potato flakes?!" crowd happy (See other comments).

I sauted the onions and a package of Hormel real bacon bits together. Added flour. Added chicken broth. 

Now I diced up 5 potatoes and let them cook in the broth. I mashed them into soup when after they cooked. Because I used so many potatoes, I cut the flakes down to 3/4's or so cup. Did not add cornstarch or salt. Added tablespoon minced garlic.  Used a mexican blend of cheese and doubled. OH my my. Made it an hour ago and it is almost gone.
This is really delicious and fairly easy to prepare.  I agree with previous reviewers and did not add the cornstarch, it doesn't need it. I did add a little more half and half though.
Just ok, really really thick

I did not care for the boxed potatoes. It has too much thyme, which was very overpowering until I added the bacon to the simmering process along with a lot of salt and pepper.  The end result was more of a mashed potato consistency than soup.  Thankfully the bread bowl I put it in saved the soup, but I would not make this again.
this was delicious! we were very pleased & it was very filling! :)

I used leftover mashed potatoes so I have no idea how many potatoes were actually involved here. I skipped the roux, threw in a can of Cream of Chicken soup, used no water, and no salt. Used more cheese than stated and ended up with a nice thick and hearty soup that my family loved. With these few changes, this recipe definitely warrants a repeat performance. Thanks Holly!
This is the exact recipe as the copy-cat one I have for Tony Roma's Baked Potato Soup.  So no wonder it is "restaurant-quality."
Very yummy!  I added the cheddar cheese to the soup like the other reviewer and found it very tasty.  Thanks!
I thought this was a little bland.  I saved it with lots of bacon, chives, cheese and salt - and then it was pretty good.  I think it had too much potato flakes perhaps.  Might make it again.

After looking through many baked potato soup recipes on Pinterest, I decided on this one.   I read many reviews on this site as well and have always found them to be very helpful.  Made some adjustments as well, I did not have the potato flakes so I admitted them as well as cornstarch and just used another potato, used half and half and skim milk.  My family loved it!  The consistency was perfect for us, as I think the potato flakes and cornstarch would have made it too thick for our taste.  The flavor was outstanding!
Didn't find this tasted anything like a baked potato - will stick to our usual recipe

This is absolutely wonderful.  I made it for the first time last winter and it was great to warm up with.  The other day I added some corn kernals and it was an awesome chowder.  There are a lot of varations you can do with this recipe. I have made it on several occasions and people always rave and ask for the recipe!

My mom visited from out of town over the Thanksgiving holidays, and I tried out this recipe to change up our usual weekend BBQ's and to accommodate the chilly weather. I had always wanted to make this resteraunt fave, but never could quite figure out how to make a thick soup without changing the robust flavor that is expected in this soup. Well, I found it...it was a huge hit! I doubled the recipe, and there were STILL no leftovers! Even the little kids enjoyed it...the fresh bacon on top helped alot! I used 2 cans no-fat, low sodium chicken broth, skim milk instead of half and half, 1/3 cup store-bought bacon bits (added at the same time as the potato flakes so they're not crunchy), and 1 package (1 cup) 4-cheese instant mashed potato flakes.  By using cheese mashed potato flakes you don't need to use the cheddar cheese.  It still tastes very cheesey (in fact, I would not use more than one cup of the flakes) and you don't add any fat.  I estimated that by making these alterations you cut the total fat by at least 70 grams.  Even with the alterations, it was fantastic. During the last year I have made this recipe over and over, using both 100% frozen or 100% bottled juices. I always have great strong wine in the end, and no two batches exactly the same. The pure grape tends to be the strongest and needs to age far longer than the others. I only use 3-1/2 cups sugar instead of 4 cups. In a saucepan I make a simple syrup by boiling approx. 2 cups water and 3-1/2 cups sugar until dissolved. This retards the growth of bacteria and makes the yeast work extremely well (fermentation).  After the syrup is some what cooled pour it into the sterile glass jug using a sterile funnel. DO NOT ADD the yeast now, wait until the gallon and its contents are back to room temperature or the yeast itself will die and not ferment.  The longer the wine sits/rests the better the taste.  Forget about it!!!  Salute!

Helpful maybe?, I am not an expert and it has been some time since I did this:
Wash the balloon.
When the balloon deflates the wine has stopped working and added time may screw the flavor and maybe turn to vinegar, earlier may taste yeasty. [actually the higher alcohol content kills the fungus making the alcohol, no longer giving off gas and the balloon goes down]
Most  rubber balloons have very small holes and will deflate over a short time, good ones may take a long time, so pricking small holes resolves this or your wine will sit too a long time with a big balloon and not working, but spoiling.  You just need to know when it stops working, that is the purpose of the balloon idea.  Timing is quite important, and sealing it in another clean bottle or refrigerating it after it is ready keeps it longer.  If you do not clean and sterilize your jug you may get contaminates that may give it a bad flavor or affect the working process.

Great intro recipe for starters into brewing your own wine at home!  Some additional tips because there are some things that you arent told:  1.  Use more cans of concentrate and less sugar for a stronger flavored wine (3 cans and 1/2 cup sugar or 2 cans and 2 1/2 cups of sugar)  2.  Siphon off after 2 weeks of starting to get the wine on the lees (dead yeast) so the wine wont taste as funky...if you leave it on the dead yeast for 5 weeks it will be super musty-flavored  3.  Use Hawaiin punch jug and drill hole in top and hot glue a 1/4" tube from Lowes (about 2ft is 20 cents) and run tube to a jar/bottle of water.  Keep submerged in water so air cant spoil wine and you dont have to worry about rubber balloon taste, etc..  4.  a 5 gram packet of wine yeast makes 5 gallons.  Im trying a batch right now just using 1 gram of yeast per gallon.  See next step of how to prep yeast to ensure survival.  Using 1 gram should cut musty bread flavor of wine, even if using bread yeast.  (packets of bread yeast are usually 7 grams)  5.  Prep yeast by rehydrating and feeding.  Put amount of yeast in lukewarm water and let it rehydrate and foam then feed it a teaspoon or 2 of sugar so it can begin multiplying the yeast count and start on its job.  Then add it to the wine mixture of juice and sugar  Hope this helps the newcomers a bit more!  Thanks for the original recipe!

I served this with a chopped salad and salmon cornbread cakes

Simply the best vegan/ vegetarian chili I've ever tasted! I skipped the sugar (not necessary) and used one square of Lindt 90% cocoa bar instead of cocoa powder, because I had it on hand.  I also omitted the corn meal, because I didn't have any. For vegans, skip the sour cream; this chili is fabulous without it.
great taste.  easy to make.
Very good with lots of flavor. I did saute crumbled Italian sausage in it too and added some cheddar cheese on top.
4.5 stars. Delicious.
Good stuff!  Big hit on a cold night!

I kept to the basic recipe and the outcome was a delicious chili which we enjoyed with thick slice of sourdough bread.  Since there's only two of us, there was a lot left over, so I've frozen the left overs and will have it over the next few weeks.  This is a fabulous meal for a damp, chilly fall or winter day.
This came out delicious!! I will def be making it again! Thanks for the recipe.
this was excellent and will make it again.
I made this this evening and it exceeded my expatiations. It did taste like chili and the family all loved it.

I have been experimenting with a lot of vegetarian dishes since my meat loving hubby turned vegan for better health.  This is the best dish by far.  I love spicy dishes, so all of the hot spices are a plus.  I am still looking for more dishes, but this one is rotated regularly.

I love sweet potatoes every which way. Hubby dislikes sweet potatoes most ways but loves them here! The recipe is a definite keeper based on that alone! I added/omitted/substituted some items due to what I had in stock. I omitted the red bell pepper, substituted cayenne for the ancho chile on the sweet potatoes during roasting, did not peel the sweet potatoes for added nutrition, de-seeded the sliced jalapenos (Hubby doesn't handle spicy foods well) and added meat and juices of a 7-bone roast that I cooked in a slow cooker.

The recipe made closer to 6 servings than the stated 4. We will be eating this for lunch throughout the week with some cornbread, of course!

First off, the baked sweet potatoes are a treat on their own.  That being said, based on other comments about this being too hot, I modified a few things.  First, I removed the seeds from the jalapeño pepper and chopped it up a bit more.  I also omitted the red pepper.  Even though I like them, they don't like me.  :-).   I used regular chile powder and I didn't add the extra pinch of cayenne pepper.  It was fabulous.  Best part of it was that my husband loved it.  I never thought I would ever get him to eat a meatless dish.  He said he would like to make this at the Fire Station but that he would add ground turkey.

This is one of the most beautiful and delicious soups I have ever tried! We didn't have ancho chili powder but we did have poblano peppers. We  sauteed the diced poblano pepper and didn't miss the powder at all. Otherwise I followed this recipe exactly and it was amazing! The only problem we had was that the roasted sweet potatoes with chipotle chili powder were so yummy, that many of them didn't make it into the soup! They are a wonderful snack or side dish on their own! Yum!

I've made this twice and it is our new favorite Chili.  It's a lot of work to make, but it makes a lot and we have it for a few nights for dinner.  I used the Jalapeno but took out the seeds.  I use the Chipolte pepper as directed but I don't put in as much of the Ancho chili pepper.  I also added a can of corn (drained) and that gave it a little more texture.  Yes, it's a lot of cutting and chopping, but it is worth it.
I made very few changes. It was the best vegitarian chili I have ever made
This is great. I doubled recipe but only had one 28oz can of diced tomatoes so added a 14 oz can of stewed tomatoes I had on hand. I used only one cup of water. That was the only change. Fabulous.

This is an awesome recipe! Since I didn't have chipotle or ancho chili powders, I just used my regular Kroger chili powder and a dash of red pepper. I also added a can of drained corn. Simply scrumptious!
Super, very easy to make and everyone loved the texture and flavor.

Great googly moogly this is delicious! The only changes I made were done so because I didn't have something on hand. I used a yellow bell pepper and 1 can black beans plus 1 can chickpeas. The rest was all the same. I was thinking about forgoing the "special" spices (chipotle and ancho) but boy am I glad I didn't! Wonderful smoky flavor they added. I don't even like cilantro much but it adds something in the end. And it wasn't too spicy for me at all. If anything next time I'll add another jalapeño.

My wife and I have never had a meatless chilli and I was really worried about how it would turn out compared to the traditional way that everyone is used to. Well, let me tell you, worry no more. This was absolutely amazing in flavor, you didn't even miss the lack of meat. The potatoes took over the show as far as that was concerned and the heat from the peppers combined with the sour cream and cilantro topped it off and made all the I,ingredients come together. This was truly a spectacular show of a well blended recipe that was might tasty, long live Chef John!

Very good...but I could see that it might easily be way too spicy for some.  Could not find any ancho chili powder at the local market...so I left that out.  The jalapenos from my garden this year are unpredictable... it took me 4 to find one with some heat... that one I deseeded....but I used all 4 peppers for the bright green color because it looked so nice :-)..... (also chopped up a couple of small yellow/orange peppers to add for the color).  Thought the toppings of sour cream, cilantro and some raw onion really added to the dish.  Served with a mixed green salad and some saltines.  Will be making this again.  Thanks for sharing.
Biggest hit at our chili party.  Roasted potato flavor infused throughout the chili.

Call me crazy, but I made this per the recipe and didn't change a thing and it was great.  Actually, I've made this 5 or 6 times over the past 2 years,  and bring it to work as a complete 1 dish lunch.  Occasionally I've been short an ingredient and substituted things (kidney for black beans once) and its still worked well. Love Chef John.
This is a keeper, wonderful taste and deep flavor. You crank the heat up or down by using the ingredients listed. Amazing and such a healthly dish to make for a cold fall day!
I couldn't believe how delicious this was. I wish I could give it ten stars!

I only scrubbed the sweet potatoes then cubed them with the skins on..... And I tossed them with olive oil, cinnamon, garlic powder & salt before roasting. Oh my! The flavors really penetrated the whole dish (and the house!)This is one of the best chili renditions. For you meat lovers add sauteed mild Italian sausage....YUM! Jogee
Delicious and very easy to make!!

I made this recipe while following the video, and did not realize the amount of chipotle pepper was as little as the recipe called for, so my chili turned out a little hotter than it was supposed to, I'm sure... but not a problem, as instead of just using the sour cream for garnish, I actually added about 1/4 cup to the chili to help tame the heat, and it turned out really creamy and delish - I will do this addition again when I make it, even though I will now go easier on the pepper.... other than that, it was a really hearty and delicious dish. I served this with the 'Mexican Corn Bread' recipe found on this site.... and it was a fantastic combination!

This is a good meatless recipe.   I substituted a jalapeno pepper and Mexican chili powder and also use a can of mild Rotel tomatoes.  It definitely has a bite, but is really good.  My girlfriend doesn't eat meat, so I gave her some and she loved it too.  You do need to add extra water also.  Thanks for sharing.

I am very calorie conscious so I took left out the sour cream and substituted Splenda for the sugar. Also left out the cornmeal and used fresh tomatos instead of canned. Thanks to the reviewers that reduced and or omitted the peppers. I decided to follow their advice and left out the spicy peppers. Excellent still with all the changes.

Easy to adjust to make it mildly spicy. I left out  the jalepeno and only used 1T Ancho chile powder (1/2 suggested). I also followed another users suggestion to use 1T of sugar and add it before roasting the sweet potatoes. Even thought I cut the sweet potatoes into fairly small chunks (about 1/2 in.), I had to roast them for 40 min, not the 20 - 25 suggested in order for them to start to caramelize and be fully cooked. I'll definitely make this again.

Does Chef John every make anything bad?  Wonderful flavors in this recipe.  I made it per the recipe and you can't go wrong with it.  It is truly something different and worth sharing with others.
MargieB

I didn't have the ancho chili powder, so I substituted 1 Tbsp chipotle chili pepper.  Soup was okay, but not so amazing that i wanted more.  I did, however, have extra sweet potatoes, and those were amazing plain!!!  I think I'll keep this recipe, but probably only to make the roasted sweet potatoes - they had a BBQ chip taste.  YUM!

I've made this several times now, and it's become my go to vegetarian chili. My family prefers a smooth sauce, but I didn't want to lose the red peppers. My solution has been to roast a whole pepper while I'm roasting the sweet potatoes. I make the tomato base without bell pepper, puree it, and then add in the beans, roasted peppers, and sweet potatoes. Delicious!

Wow, this is a good 'un!  I was looking for recipes that were lower GI & this fit the bill - you can even trade out that tiny teaspoon of sugar for agave.  Not only is it healthy, but uber tasty, too.  Nice & spicy!

I loved this dish! I made it for a dinner party and it was a hit! Sad to say I had no leftovers; I'll have to make it again soon. Sauteed ingredients in step 4 then added to all from step 5, cooking in the crockpot on high for four hours. Right before serving I added roasted sweet potatoes. I also did what reviewer Spyce recommended and reserved 1/2 cup of rinsed black beans which I mashed and added at the end with the potatoes. Great taste and full texture!
Yum.yum.yum. Deeelicious

I served this at a dinner this fall and everyone loved it.
I didnot use chipotle, as some don't really care for it. So I just used reg chilli powder. The fresh cilantro makes it taste so fresh!!
Yum'

Very happy with the results! I thought I had everything I needed but had ran out of ancho so I used regular chili powder. I love ancho and would have been even better with it. I only added a few slices of jalapeno because I'm sharing with a group and don't want to make it too spicy in case someone is a sissy and can't handle it. Everything else I followed exactly and I will definitely make again!
Way too spicy
I loved this recipe, however my husband didn't care for it.  I'll make it again :)
lzj----eliminate the ancho chili powder to reduce that HEAT and only use the flesh of the jalapeno (not the seeds and ribs)

Like this one a lot
I read other reviews but unless my chiles were a little lacking... 
i found heat levels were fine, 
in fact I over coated the sweet potatos before roasting, ooops
I omitted some spiciness due to other comments, and it was AMAZING. A new staple in my house for sure.
Family loved it. Don't skip the cilantro garnish, it really adds to the overall flavor!
Great vegetarian main dish that I'll definitely add into our rotation. I followed the recipe, then added one zucchini because I had it and served it with cornbread muffins. Yum!

Great recipe! I’ll absolutely make it again. I only changed a couple things. I cooked up and added 6 chopped up pieces of bacon. And I used a chili and chipotle infused olive oil. I also used more dark chili seasoning and cumin bc I love a lot of flavor.
Very tasty!
Loved it!  Deff worth a try if you like sweet potatoes!  And it was pretty simple to make, a little time consuming, but simple!

I made this for a Vegetarian/Vegan Potluck, and It was a great hit. Now I made this cause I wanted to make something different for the potluck. I generally don't like sweet potatoes, but I loved this and so did everyone else. It has a nice kick to it from the spices, and the sweet potatoes give the chili a really nice body. I will definately be making this again.

Very good if you leave out all the pepper and salt.  It is still very flavorful.   I chopped about 1/2 cup of cilantro and added it in at the end.  Everyone loved this dinner, kids too!  The meat eaters added chopped grilled chicken breasts to their chili.
My husband is a chef and he thinks this is great chili.  Loved it!!
I won first place in my church's chili contest with this one!! Made a batch which was allegedly 12 servings--in fact that was about 40 servings.  Will definitely make it again!
I loved it.  I took the seeds out of the jalapeno pepper to ease it up a little bit other than that it was a delicious find, and not hard to make.  I will be using this again.  Thanks!

I made this with a few modifications - I omitted the chipotle pepper, onion, red bell pepper, jalapeno pepper, cornmeal, and sour cream. Instead of the ancho chili pepper I used diced up ancho chili pods. Despite not having these other ingredients It was not lacking in flavor at all! Yum!

This was delicious, got rave reviews!  It was a bit labor intensive, but worth the effort.  I did make a few changes: I added ground beef and had to increase the amount of all the spices as it was a little bland as written.  I definitely agree that roasting the sweet potatoes is a MUST as this makes the chili.

This is great! It is non-traditional: a bit like a cross between a chili and a really hearty stew. Roasting the sweet potatoes is key (and I have done this step on its own as a fall vegetable side by itself - fabulous!). You can make this recipe straight as written or you can add small chunks of chicken breast. I tend to like a bit of acid in my stews, so I also add a small splash of white balsamic vinegar at the very end - it is slightly spicy, sweet and bright! Everyone raves, and like all stews and chills it is better on the second day if there is any left. Thank you Chef John!

We made this today and it turned out so good. Very good in fact.  The favors of all the spices really added such a great taste.  I was worried about the jalapenos, but they really added a great favor and was not very hot at all.  I will make this again.  Will not change a thing on it.

This was very good tasting & healthy too, also economical. Even my vegetarian sister & brother in law could eat this. I made this exactly as written except I deliberately I cut down on the amount of  heat by using the 1/2 t. ground dried chipotle pepper & only 1/2 of a fresh jalapeno pepper instead of a whole jalapeno. The heat from those two was plenty for us. I omitted the Ancho chili & cayenne. This had a really nice flavor especially when topped with the fresh cilantro & a dollop of sour cream.This also looks nice in the bowls with the black,red, orange, green and white colors. I'll be making this again from time to time.  Thanks for a good recipe Chef John.
It was delicious and I will definitely make it again!

Everyone loved this!  I cut the ancho chili powder in half and used small  jalapeno and diced (without seeds, of course) instead of slicing..  Also used one square of unsweetened chocolate bar instead of cocoa powder.  Just the right enough spice for all.  The texture was fabulous too.  The cost outlay was high due to special seasonings i did not have, but i figure it will cost about $15 the next time i make it!  One of the  reviews said there was too much slicing and dicing, but for me, that's the great part about preparing a meal!  Next time i think i will double the recipe so i will have plenty leftover!

I used the recommended amount of ancho chile powder and jalapeno (seeded).  I love hot/spicy food but this was RIDICULOUSLY HOT!  I can't even judge the taste because of the heat.  I might try this again without so much spice.  Good lord this is hot!

Oh my gosh! This chili is the bomb! I made it for dinner tonight and my family was going nuts. They loved it! I adjusted only a couple of things; I added only one tablespoon of ancho chili powder instead of two and I minced my jalapeño rather than slicing it. Also, I did not add cayenne pepper. Even with these changes (or omissions) the chili still had a "kick" to it....it was the perfect spicy-ness. Even my 13- and 9-year-old boys loved it! Definitely a keeper.

This recipe is amazing!! I prefer white sweet potatoes so I used both white and regular. The natural sweetest of the white sweet potatoes really made this for me. Everyone that has tasted this says it should be in a restaurant. Amazing recipe! Thx for sharing

We love the black bean-sweet potato combination in our home. Roasting the potatoes kept them from melting away in the pot. Yummy! Skipped the ancho, cornmeal and sugar...didn't need the extra heat for us, didn't have cornmeal and didn't think it needed added sweetness of sugar. Used vegetable broth for the water and it was greatly enjoyed! Thank you!!!

I entered this chili in the vegetarian category at my company's annual chili cook-off and it won!  It even came in second place overall, only losing to a more conventional meat chili.  The only thing I added was a cup or so of frozen corn for a little more texture and color.  I love this chili!

OMG. This is the best chili recipe I've ever made. Even the kids liked it. I cut out the jalapeno and cut the chile powder if half to suit them and it was just the right amount of heat.  I added a pound of ground buffalo, browned with the onions and garlic, then threw it all into the crock pot. Added the sweet potatoes near the end.  Really wonderful.
I love sweet potatoes and black beans and I really enjoyed a chimichanga that had those ingredients so I expected to like this recipe. I really disliked the flavor. I will not make it again.
I made this just as the recipe directed and it is AMAZING!
Have made it twice awesome. Added Chickpeas and put it over rice.

Being from the southwest, of course I changed this recipe for items on hand. Used roasted Hatch green chili, no jalapeno or Ancho; 1 ear of sweet corn cut off the cob; added diced chicken breast; this is a good recipe as is, but I couldn't help myself.

If you are looking for a vegetarian chili recipe, you have to try this!
It is excellent exactly as written!

I made this using regular pepper instead of chipotle pepper, and a few dashes of cayenne instead of the ancho chili powder. I also left the jalapeño seeds outs, as I was trying to minimize spice. It was tasty!
Added some sweet Italian sausage and used white kidney beans and regular chile powder as that's what I had on hand....awesome!

I loved this recipe!  I made It today for a girls lunch and it was a hit. One of the girls doesn't care for sweet potatoes but loved them in this dish!  I omitted the jalapeños but followed everything else as written. The flavor was complex and satisfying.  Interesting choice of ingredients, but they all somehow worked so well together.  Thank you for this delicious spin on chili and as other reviewers stated, you don't even miss the meat! I served it with sweet cornbread muffins. Perfect!

This is a recipe that is even better the day after. All of it sits and ruminates! There were a few things I didn't have and decided not to use (cocoa powder, jalapeno, etc). I did use Rotel in this. But, honestly the spices you have, the sweet potato and the black beans make it quite tasty!
wow, i wasn't expecting this much flavour from a vegetarian recipe!  impressive.
This was so, so good.  I added some corn and celery when I put in the beans and sweet potato, and it all blended together wonderfully in my opinion.  Will definitely make this again!

So easy, and quick. I left out the sugar and cornmeal, and substituted tomato paste (sautéed with onions and peppers) and reconstituted sun-dried tomatoes for canned, since I didn't have them. Roasting the sweet potatoes in a cast iron skillet added even more flavor. The final result was saucy, spicy, smoky and delicious. I didn't miss the meat at all, and can't wait to make this many more times.

This is awesome!!  I used 3 canned chipotle peppers and about a Tablespoon of the adobo sauce in place of the jalapeno and the ancho chile powder, because I had that on hand and also because I prefer the smokey flavor of the chipotle pepper.  Also followed the other reviewers and left out the white sugar.  It was delicious!  I will definitely make it again!

I toned down the spiciness by using Anaheim peppers instead of jalapenos and no cayenne pepper.  Otherwise followed the rest of the recipe.

Family members who did not like sweet potatoes even liked it!  Was a hit with our vegan friends.  Definitely would make again!

I loved this. I roasted the pepper with the potatoes and then decided later that I wanted more potato so I diced up two more and added them with the tomatoes and both were good but I think searing the spices to the potatoes during the roasting really added to the flavor. Roasting the potatoes really improved the texture.  I will roast sweet potatoes in these spices again to serve alone, they were so good (maybe that is why I needed more for the chili).  I made this with the Awesome and easy creamy corn casserole and they were great.  thanks for a great recipe.  Ymmmmmmm.
Truly wonderful!!!Made without jalapenos and yogurt instead of sour cream. My 3 & 4 year old's loved it as well as my husband. Its a keeper!
Wow, I made this recipe and the kitchen just smelled wonderful.  The guys all looked at it questioningly, not so sure about the sweet potatoes, but they liked it !
As usual, chef John's recipe is right on! I did make one change...  Instead of water, I used tomato juice. Just my personal preference. Thanx Chef John

I have to say this is AMAZING!!!!  I tried it as I can't eat gluten or soy, so I'm always looking for something adventurous.  It really is absolutely one of the best chilis I've ever made.  The flavors are complex and really one of the best chilis I've had, never mind meatless.   I added a bit of habanero, not jalapeño.  We like spicy here so that adds to our stars.  We used cilantro to top it off and sour cream for those who can have dairy in our household.  I'm not one to rave about a recipe, but this one rocks!!
For a deeper flavor and heartier texture, I pureed about 1/4 of the roasted sweet potatoes then threw them into the pot along with a beef bullion cube and 2 teaspoons of molasses.  Delicious!

This turned out to be amazingly good. I used Trader Joe's low sodium Garden Patch vegetable juice in place of some of the water. I did not add any salt nor did I add any sugar and skipped the cornmeal. I used a dash of cayenne pepper instead of any ancho chili powder because I did not have any ancho chili powder. All of my dinner guests also loved this dish. Thank you Chef John for the recipe and the very helpful video.

I got compliments from everyone on this chili!  I did add some shredded seasoned chicken that I had cooked in the crock pot.  Also removed the seeds from the jalapeno pepper to make less hot but used spicy black beans from Whole Foods.  Absolutely delicious and will make again!

Fantastic!  I made this for a Chili cook-off lunch.  It was nice to have a meatless chili option.  I read the comments and decided to skip the Chipotle powder and I used only half of the Ancho chili powder.  Next time (there will be a next time, for sure) I will use a little more of the Ancho chili powder .

Me and hubby are doing a 2 week no meat menu to start. Made this and it was delicious! Had to gradually add about a cup more of water, but other than that, it was a great recipe to make. Luckily I had all the ingredients.....even the sour cream and cilantro to tip it with. Also topped it a green onions.  Can't wait to try it again tomorrow when all the spices blend together.
Very yummy healthy alternative.  My "meat loving" hubby didn't even realize there was no meat in it (crazy, I know).  A winner in my book.

Amazing!! I used regular chili powder, but other than that I stuck to the recipe. Wow! Even my toddler loved it! Will definitely keep this on a regular rotation. We had enough for two dinners! Served over rice with corn chips and corn bread on the side. And used plain Greek yogurt as a topping.
The roasted sweet potatoes were amazing, both in this recipe, and cooked alone.
I make this just the way the recipes calls for. I also often make just the roasted sweet potatoes to use as a side dish.
Made this recipe for 30 people and it was a hit as many asked for seconds and for the recipe!  Always looking for a good recipe to feed a crowd, and this is a great one!
I think I doubled the chili pepper by accident and it was awesome. Veggie broth also makes it supper yummy. Don't skip on the chocolate it makes the flavor really good.

Fantastic recipe! I did make a few changes, but it was out of necessity as I couldn't find a few of the spices. In lieu of chipotle powder on the sweet potatoes, I used a combination of smoked paprika and cayenne pepper. I also used veggie stock instead of water for extra flavor, and added a lot more liquid than the recipe calls for as I like my chili on the soupier side. Other than that, followed the recipe exactly and it was a hit with my meat loving family.

This was so good. I don't normally like sweet potatoes and was looking for a way to use some up; my boyfriend couldn't believe I served him a meal without meat but even he admitted it was "decent." I didn't have ancho chile powder so left it out, I added more cayenne because it did need a bit more spice.
My dad had shingles and eating sweet potatoes was supposed to help him so I made this wonderful dish.  Very tasty and colorful.

I did make this recipe only used butternut squash instead of sweet potatoes because that was what I had. Fixed the squash like the potatoes only used smoked paprika. Didn't have jalapenos so used 1/2 can of chilpotle peppers in adobo sauce 7.5 oz chopped up. We loved it and our daughter loved it and I will definitely make it again.

Wow.  Just awesome. I didn't have a fresh bell pepper on hand so used some frozen tri-color bell peppers, added them in at the end with the beans and potatoes. Used a whole tsp oregano too, I love the stuff. Other than that I followed the recipe exactly.  The texture was spot on, that step of roasting the sweet potatoes really makes a difference.  I've never had ancho chili powder that was very hot so I used the recipe amount.  The finished dish was not that hot to me.  At first I was taken aback by the large caloric number here, until I realized this recipe thinks it's 4 servings. I'll get at least 6 servings out of this, it makes a pretty big pot.  When I use my own software to determine nutrition for 6 servings I get 350 calories, 6g fat, 68g carb, 14g fiber, 12g protein.  Now that makes more sense.  Anyway, I love this dish and will make it often.  Thanks Chef John!
Absolutely amazing.  Everyone raved about it.  Lots of ingredients but not a ton of work.  I did, however, leave out some of the peppers per other reviewers' suggestions.

Another banger of a recipe from Chef John! I made this for my meal prep Sunday last week and oh my God - this will be my go-to veggie chili from now on. I didn't miss the meat at all, and it clocked in at just over 250 cals per serving without rice. Just go very sparingly on the oil and use fat free yogurt instead of sour cream for garnish.

My tweaks - I didn’t have any cornmeal, and I added a tablespoon of guajillo chili powder in addition to the ancho and chipotle, plus a rehydrated dried mulatto chili. I like my chili to be on the spicy side and this was perfect for me. I also added a quarter cup of Mrs Renfro’s green salsa as I needed to use it up.  I didn’t put in quite as much water for a thicker chili.  

This made about 8 servings. It’s filling enough to eat without rice, and it made a great filling for corn tortillas for awesome veggie tacos. It also works nicely as a spicy brunch dish if you add a bit more water, then poach an egg in it as you reheat, for a kind of Tex-Mex shakshuka.

I came to this after I had made sweet potatoes and black beans, looking to improve what had been intended for a burrito, and create a soup or stew instead.  I added strained tomatoes, chipotle sauce, and chocolate.  Spectacular.

As a Trader Joe's cook, next time I'll use TJs cuban black beans, TJ's fire roasted onions and peppers, and pretty much follow these directions for the potatoes and other spices.  I did use some honey in the sweet potato roasting pan, so no need for sugar later.

Five stars isn't enough for this dish. We love spicy so we doubled the spices and OMGoodness this chili is by far and away my favorite. We left the potatoes in a bit longer just so they didn't get soggy and we weren't disappointed. We made this chili multiple times last season and we are excited to see chili season come around again.

I adjusted this recipe for 6 servings. It was a hit with my husband and 3 adult kids that dropped in to visit.  I loved the roasted sweet potatoes and it was so worth that step.  I followed the recipe exactly as written except I did not have cornmeal and omitted it entirely.  I added a 3rd can of beans (pinto) which gave the chili more variety, and also added 1 Tablespoon of chili powder.  I also cut up 4 boneless chicken breasts, sautéed them in olive oil, salt and pepper, then followed the recipe with the onions, etc.   I will make this version again.  Thanks for all the comments and a good recipe!

I already reviewed this recipe, but just had to add something: I was asked to make this dish twice in the SAME week!  You KNOW it's good when it gets requested twice in the same week, especially in my house.  Chef John, you scored a winner with this one!
Good, changed it up. Added steak cut back on hot spices

I really liked the taste.  With all the peppers and other ingredients, I thought it would turn out to be too hot. but it actually was very tasty with only a small amount of a heat after taste.  I wanted to make the recipe as stated even though I thought it would be too hot, but I was pleasantly surprised.  It was surprisingly easy to put together with all the detailed instructions so that even a non-cook like me could make it. I did clean the seeds out of the jalapeno pepper, but I am definitely going to make this chili for the next potluck I go to, as there are a few vegetarians (including me)who will enjoy it as well.
Excellent recipe, I froze half and found the second half gained heat, had to add about 1 cup V-8 juice to calm it down.

So Good.  I used regular chili powder and it is amazing.  Everyone wants the recipe that tastes it.  The only thing is I found that roasting the sweet potatoes takes MUCH longer.  Put aside an extra hour just to be sure.  Simply Delicious.

WOW!  This came out really good!  The grocery store was out of jalapenos, so I used a hot green pepper instead.  I also put in only a teensy bit of cayenne pepper, so overall this came out very mild.  I like a little spice, so will use a jalapeno and a little more cayenne next time.  I have to say, this is restaurant quality soup - I would buy this out to eat, and yet it was relatively easy to make right at home.  So happy with this and am sure will make this often!

This was a great alternative to regular chili! It was pretty spicy though so I substituted the ancho chile powder for regular chili powder and left out the jalapeno pepper. Also 2 pounds of sweet potatoes were too many, 1-1.5 would have been plenty.

I made this following the recipe to the letter and it came out absolutely perfectly. The sweet potatoes add such a richness, and it has perfect amount of kick from the jalapenos without the spiciness overwhelming the other flavors. It was also quite filling. Looking forward to making this one of our staple winter dishes!
I did this recipe exactly as written.. It was good but I think next time I will add chicken to it.. My family said it was the only thing lacking ;)
Amazing!  I loved it.

Very, very good and different too. I followed the recipe but added two extra ingredients. A can of corn and some chicken. I roasted the sweet potatoes (and precooked the chicken) like in the recipe but did everything else in the crockpot. My husband loved it. I would definitely make this again.
I have made this several times. It is my all time favorite chili recipe

Have made it a few times now -  fantastic  and satisfying.  Made it verbatim the first time 'round, but have added a few modest changes since.
Tonight didn't have 2lbs worth of sweet potato, so added a cubed butternut squash along w/ my one lowly (yet giant) sw. potato and tossed it all up with half the the spices.
Used red wine in place of the h2O, added some sweet crisp corn near the end, and served with cilantro-yogurt and lime tortillas. 
Excellent!
I enjoy sweet potatoes and I was looking forward to trying this recipe. The strong and spicy taste of the chile covered  the flavor of the sweet potatoes. I will not be making this recipe again.

Okay, so I've had this recipe several times. A couple things to note--roasting the sweet potatoes is genius and really helps keep the texture. The recipe calls for ancho chile powder. You HAVE to use ancho chile (or some other really mild pepper). Generic chili powder is too hot. I made this mistake the first time around when serving this at a dinner party and no one finished their bowls.

This last time I "Africanized" and it was out of this world. It was amazing. Seriously, I have made a lot of chilis in my day, but the way I modified it would have won an award. Chili is one of those things in which you can make a good recipe, but not great. This was great. I added ginger to the garlic mixture. I reduced the ancho chili to half, added some smoked paprika and a generous pinch of cardamom. I used hickory smoked salt on the sweet potatoes and at the end when seasoning. I reduced the oregano to a pinch (probably could have omitted it from the African version). I used chicken stock instead of water and added a generous dollop of peanut butter. I also used fresh heirloom tomatoes. I have nothing against canned, but I had them on hand and needed to use them. The flavor that the tomatoes added was amazing. It made a huge difference. I used black pepper instead of cayenne, and of course seasoned at the end to taste.

I followed the recipe exactly, paying no attention to those who said it was too hot because I love hot and spicy food!  I loved the layers of tastes and textures, but it IS too hot...a bit overpoweringly.  I would make this again, but I would stipulate using a *small* jalapeno pepper, and perhaps taking out the seeds.  Thanks for a vegetarian chili that really packs a punch!
Very tasty. Used half sweet potato and half butternut squash because it's what I had. The texture of the sweet potato was much better. Next time I'll try doubling the cocoa.

I have made this several times and have share the recipe with family and it is now becoming a family favorite. So easy to make, and we adjust the heat of the seasoning depending upon who is invited for supper. Definitely recommend this

This was fantastic! The only changes I made were I used vegetable spray instead of olive oil in both instances and substituted Splenda for sugar. I ended up using about 2 1/2 cups water for my chili. I also roasted, then cooled my sweet potatoes while the rest was simmering on the stove. At the 30 minute mark all was ready to combine, heat through and eat!
This chili is excellent! It has a great flavor from the chipotle and is very filling.

So delicious it was hard to stop eating it.  I used 1/2 tsp salt, not one tsp.  Discard the jalapeno seeds.  Omit the sour cream and cilantro, they take away from the chili, not add.  This is considerable work to put together, advise doing advance prep of ingredients and preparing over a couple days.

I made this recipe with some minor changes (left out the jalapeno and used red pepper flakes instead of cayenne), and it was much better than I expected. I have never made a meatless chili before, but I found this vegetarian chili very satisfying. The cocoa powder makes the broth rich in flavor and dark in color. Also, roasting the sweet potatoes ahead of time is definitely worth the extra step. I can see this recipe making its way into my regular rotation!

Its a great recipie that's fun to mix up with other chili peppers and hot sauces. I like to change up the type of chili peppers or sauce depending on how much heat I feel like. It's delicouse very time! Also, it's well worth the extra time to bake the potatoes first!

I loved it!  I didn't have dried chipotle pepper so I left that out and I couldn't find dried ancho chile but I purchased dried ancho chiles and chopped one up and added it.  I think my jalapeño pepper was rather hot enough.  It was spicy, but we like it like that. Good, healthy dish.

I have used this recipe twice, and it comes out perfect every time. It is my all time favorite chili recipe now. It is spicy, but not too hot. It is also very rich with just a hint of sweetness.

The second time I cooked it, the only thing I changed was that instead of putting a teaspoon of sugar in the chili, I put about a tablespoon of sugar on the sweet potatoes before I roasted them. This helped them brown and caramelize a little more. It came out great!

This recipe was 4 stars as written (omitting the jalapeño and decreasing chili powder). It definitely would need more liquid to be chili/soup like. What I did that made it delicious? Added a little leftover corn, then put it in a greased 13x9. I mixed up a batch of my regular CORNBREAD (buttermilk cornbread on this site), and used a little less sugar and a handful of shredded cheese. Spread the cornbread mix on top, and bake at.  375 for 20-25 min until golden. Add a dollop of sour cream and it is absolutely divine!
I added some spices to taste and a yellow pepper.

Excellent cold-weather comfort food. I make is three or four times during the winter. The jalopeno goes a long way and I adjust the amount of that ingredient depending on how spicy I want the chili to turn out.
Very Good! I have to make it at least once a week, my son-in-law can't get enough of it.

The first time I made it I thought it was the jalopena that made it too hot, so am making a big pot for a dinner party without jalopena and it's so spicy it's not even edible. And I followed to a t as well. This is extremely disappointing and I have to order a pizza in for my party. How can I be the only person to think the spiciness is unedible?  My 12 dinner guests will agree I'm sure and head right to the pizza box

This one wins every potluck I’ve ever brought it to. (Winning a potluck means no leftovers to bring home!) it’s vegetarian and gluten-free and still flavorful and kicky and delicious. Everyone asks for the recipe, so I just print out several copies in advance to bring along!

This is a great recipe, easy to make and put together, also easy to put your own spin on it.I have made it twice in a month and plan on many more times, all so makes a great vegetarian taco stuffing, simple reduce the liquid.Yum and Thank You.

Just won first place in a Chili Cookoff with this recipe!  I did cut back on the chili powder by half and used a small jalapeno.  Still had plenty of heat! And I loved the taste of the chipotle pepper.

This was outstanding!  I halved the recipe in general but was heavy on the spices.  I also added a touch of cinnamon.  The sweet potatoes didn't come through as I expected but I'm sure it was bec I gave more bite on spices.  My husband says it's a keeper!
Excellent recipe! I'm laughing at those who think 1 jalapeño and a pinch of cayenne is too spicey in like a gallon of two of chili.
Very tasty and delicious. I liked the touch of the semi-hard (as opposed to mushy) baked sweet potatoes.
Delicious and hearty vegetarian chili... So good, I'm making it again now. Yummm
It was ok but no one raved about it.  Too much cumin and that just took over the flavour.

This was great!!  The only thing I changed was to omit the sugar, and I seeded & chopped the jalapeno... it wasn't over spicy at all, and everyone (including my carnivore husband) loved it.  Thanks for another great recipe!

I love sweet potatoes and had to try this recipe. I'm glad to report that it did not disappoint! I made mine in my crockpot on low for 5-6 hours. I sauteed the onions and aromatics as directed in step 4 and added to the crockpot along with the ingredients in step 5, and the black beans in step 6. I roasted the sweet potatoes while the chili was cooking and added them to the crockpot at the end to heat through. 

I didn't reduce the water in the recipe, and the amount of liquid at the end of the cook time was just right. To add more body to the chili, I smashed some of the beans up right in the crockpot to fill it out some. Sometimes when making chili if I remember, I reserve a 1/2 cup or so of the rinsed beans to smash and add when the chili is about done. I usually forget though and just smash in the pot. 

I served this with a pan of cornbread and topped the chili with fresh cilantro and a little shredded cheddar.

We didn't use cocoa powder, cayenne pepper or corn meal. We only used one table spoon of chili powder and 3/4 teaspoon of cumin. And just a tiny bit of the jalapeno pepper. This was perfect. The chili was so flavorful! Absolutely out of this world good!! Not too spicy , just perfect. The sweet potatoes mixed in with all of these ingredients was amazing! I will definitely be making this again!!

This recipe was quite time consuming, but well worth the effort in the end.  Could not find the chipotle pepper spice, so I simple used 2 tablespoons of the sauce from a can of Chipotles in adobo sauce.  Did mostly everything by the book except I use agave in place of sugar, so substituted that.  I think this might be one of those things that is better the next day.  It was delicious for dinner, but suspect after everything has time to marry it could be even better.  I did forget the cilantro:(  Oh! Well didn't miss it anyway.  Thanks for the recipe this is a keeper!
Healthy and absolutely delicious!  I skipped the sour cream and did not have enough cumin--but followed the recipe otherwise.  Rave reviews from my husband

We have made this over & over.  Amazing.  
The only changes we made to it was that we used the southwest black beans that already have the jalapenos inside the can.  This adds a bit of heat that we love.  The other change was that instead of sour cream we used Greek Yogurt Cheese. This gives it a real ZING! Mmm! (Use 1/3 or 1/2 of the block of Yogurt Cheese)
It truly does eat like a meat dish.  Meat-eaters won't miss the meat, I promise.  So many flavors & so good for you!

The best chili hands down!!  I've added a few ingredients based on my families likes which helped make it a bit more filling & they are IN LOVE with this chili!!  1)I add a small can of tomato sauce, 2cups of water, instead of sugar, I add a natural syrup or some type of honey, lastly, I add  ground chicken. I'm telling you this dish is amazing! The baked, seasoned, sweet potatoes are the key!!  YUMMMM.....
very good - added corn and noodles plus hot sauce

I just recently went vegan and this Chilli  beats anything I ever made with meat. I'm a single person so I half the recipe and this gives me two hearty servings or 3 moderate ones.
