This soup was tasty and very easy to make. I also threw my cooked veggies into the food processor so it wasn't so chunky. I also substituted one cup of whipping cream for one of the cups of milk. You can easily add your own spices and herbs to dress it up. Cayenne pepper, ginger, basil or sage, chopped garlic, any of these would be a great addition.
Absolutely delicious!  I didn't change a thing!  Just the ticket for a bluster 18-degree night in West Michigan!

Have never made cauliflower cheese soup before so I was happy to make this recipe.  I used chicken broth instead of water, but I think I used too much.  I didn't have potatoes or celery and it still tasted great!

Good and easy to whip up.  I used frozen cauliflower that I defrosted for a couple mins. in the microwave.  I took others' recommendations and used 1 cup of chicken broth instead of the 3/4 cup of water.  The soup was still quite thick.  I also used shredded carrots instead of chopped.  I used skimmed milk and didn't notice a difference in the taste.  Also, I used Kraft "Mexican" blended cheese because that is what I had on hand.  I think next time, I will add some cooked and crumbled bacon.
Easy, delicious!  I perhaps could have cooked it a few more minutes to take the "crunch" out of the potatoes, but this recipe is a favorite and a KEEPER!

I wasn't sure about making this, but so glad I did.  This soup is sooo sooo good!  My husband, 18 month old & In-laws all loved it.  Its a keeper.  I didn't have celery or carrots on hand, but the soup still turned out great without.  I doubled the cheese, which i'd definitely recommend. I also added a dash of garlic powder. Yum!

This is an okay base recipe. I used 4 cups in total of cauliflower in place of any vegetables. I also used 2 cups of milk and 1 cup of broth as other reviewers suggested. I also used 4 cloves of garlic, 1 cup feta cheese, and smoked paprika to garnish. It came out sooo good! There were no left overs. Next time I may reduce feta, top with sour cream, and some bacon bits!
Great!  Added a good bit of pepper and garlic powder.

This is a good soup for people that like plain stuff, with not a lot of spice.  I spruced mine up a bit and it was a hit the first night, but it doesn't reheat as well... so don't make a bunch extra thinking it will get eaten over a couple days.  I would make it again if I had cauliflower to get rid of.

Thanx for the recipe ! My soup turned out very good even though, in my attempt to kick it up a notch, I added garlic and then it tasted like Alfredo sauce a bit so I wont be doing that again! I fixed this problem by adding some white wine vinegar, cayenne pepper, Tabasco and a spoonful of sugar and really it turned out delicious ! next time I also wont be adding celery because mine turned a dark green and didn't look too nice in my soup lol but will definitely be making this again
My family loved this soup. Thanks!
I added cream of onion soup for more flavor since I couldn't add chicken stock because my husband is a vegetarian. I diluted that a little bit with water.

I've been looking for a good cauliflower/cheese soup and I'm delighted that I found this one.  This is easy to make and very tasty I might add.  I would HIGHLY recommend this recipe is this is what you're looking for. Mmmmmmmm Mmmmmmmm Goooood.

Excellent recipe.  Added cornstarch in place of some flour for a faster thickening process.  Also included chicken boullion & 2 cloves of garlic for better flavor. Could use a lot of different vegetable combinations in this depending on your taste.

Ok...so I doctored it up (I find everyone has a little of their own flare to jazz it up) and I listened to some of the tips : I doubled the cheese, used chicken and veggie broth instead of just water (added a 1/4 cup white wine) and more veggies and presto!  It's a yummy comfort food for those rainy days or cold winter nights :)
Loved it, but I followed alot of reviews and added chicken stock. I added it to the water I boiled the veggies in. My mom and sister loved it! Will file this under repeat!

Excellent and easy to make.  I omitted the potatoes and added a little extra cauliflower.  Like others used chicken broth instead of water and doubled the cheese.  Loved the flavor and consistency was perfect!
Great soup for cold nights.  We followed the recipe closely and absolutely loved it.  We will definitely make it again.
Instead of using 3/4 cup of water I used1 cup of chicken broth. Sooooo delicious!!!!!
We loved this soup.  Looking for something to do with leftover cauliflower from dinner and this turned out to be a wonderful find.  Easy and usually have all of the remaining ingredients on hand.

This is such an excellent, easy, and versatile soup! I made a few changes. I used one can of chicken broth to cook the veggies in + 1/2 can water. I sauteed the onions in butter with thyme, garlic powder, salt, white pepper, and onion powder. Instead of using milk, I used half and half and a little bit of heavy cream. I did not measure out exactly three cups.  I added nutmeg, onion powder, salt, pepper, and Velveeta, 1/2 slice of swiss cheese, and shredded Mexican cheese to the Roux. Great basic recipe, I just prefer more spices. will definitely make again!
The texture was so velvety and the flavor was incredible, I'll definitely make this again!

Although this soup is very good, it needs a little help with seasonings.  I too added 2 chicken bouillon cubes, but something still is missing.  Next time I would substitute chicken broth for the water and use a little more than a the 3/4 cup, the soup was a little too thick.

I just made this, it's very good.  Will have to come back once DH tries it for his comments. I did tweak it. Used small whole head cauliflower(approx 4 cups) kept all other measures the same & added 2 bouillon cubes to veggies as cooking and another when soup was done.  Added a bit of Italian spice, garlic/onion powder & 1 t Worcester at the end.
Overall, this recipe was good.  I think that next time I will make the vegetables a little bit bigger.  I added some garlic powder (about 2 tsp.) which made the soup really tasty.

I made this for dinner last night. I pureed the whole thing and wouldn't let my husband or daughter in the kitchen while I was cooking it. My husband who hates cauliflower had 2 bowels before I told him what was in it. Loved it Thanks!

This was exactly what I was looking for to use up vegetables in my fridge that had seen better days. I used a small head of cauliflower instead of a cup,  skipped the flour and added a bit more cheese. It was already so thick with the extra cauliflower. DELISH!

Even though it always bothers me when people say "Oh I loved it!" yet they made a bunch of changes, I'm going to do something similar. I added extra potatoes (on accident; I peeled too many), added extra cheese (I LOVE CHEESE), and cooked the vegetables for some extra time because I don't like to chew my soup. It was so cheesy and excellent!

This was actually the first homemade soup I've ever made. I did use chicken stock, I also had to use gluten-free flour, and lactose-free milk. And it still turned out wonderfully! Love it! Thank you so much for the recipe!

Loved this recipe! My picky eaters were complaining when they walked through the kitchen, but everyone of them got seconds. The leftover soup was even better the next day. Thanks so much. We will make this one often.
A great recipe to start with, but needs some more flavor. I tried again with more cauliflower, a tsp of salt and nutmeg to give it more kick. Turned out ok.

This soup was excellent, I will definitely make again. It tastes similar to a California Medley that you can get at some restaurants. I made a few modifications to the recipe.  I used 1 cup of water with 2 chicken bullion cubes to boil the veggies in, I substituted brocolli for the potatoes and I used half cheddar cheese and half low fat Velveta.
It was good but very blah needed a lot of salt and pepper
It was very easy to make and good for dinner on a chilly night with grilled cheese.  I too added some chicken boullion for flavor.
Just okay. Probably wouldn't make it again.

The recipe works.  I thought it a little bland so I added a garlic clove pressed into the sauce a few minutes before it was ready and some chopped ham.  I also added quite a bit of salt and pepper.  It would be excellent with some chopped smoked sausage too.
Solid recipe.    I like a lot of flavor so I did add 3 minced garlic cloves.  I also used chicken broth.  Toward the end I thought it needed even more spice.  This is a very mild soup.

If I could give this a 'tip' of one star, I would. The only terrible receipe I've come across in the multitude of recipes on this website. The name is deceiving, as Cauliflower Cheese soup this is NOT. Bland, even with making adjustments. Tasted more like flour based chunk chowder than anything else. Do not waste your time.
Looooovveee this soup

Like many others, I didn't follow the recipe due to taste and "what do I actually have in the house now"? My differences were I used chicken bouillon broth, as I reflexively drained the boiled vegetables. Also, I used habanero jack cheese. YEESSSS!!! I highly recommend that "adjustment"!

What an unexpected delight!   I used this as a base, though I did tweak things a bit:  I sauteed the onion (and garlic I added...what's a soup w/out garlic/!) in a bit of EVOO before adding the veggies and chicken broth (instead of water). While it simmered, I made the roux and then added it to the pot. I used a whole head of cauliflower, an onion, 5-6 carrots, and 4-5 smallish white potatoes. I reduced the butter/flour/milk by about 1/2 (just looking to "save" a few calories) and used about 1.25 C of a shredded "mac & cheese" blend. So good, though not the most appetizing looking. I also blended most of it, trying my immersion blender first and finally caving and using a blender for the larger chunks.  I'm already looking forward to leftovers for lunch tomorrow.  THANKS, janiebear925!

I ate so much soup... altered the servings to 6 and it worked out perfectly. Husband ate seconds but kids wouldn't touch it. More for us... Really really good. We will have this again, just put veggies in blender instead of chopping all by hand, not much work.
Best soup I've ever made!  I added 1 cup of broccoli, 2 chicken bouillon cubes, and an extra cup of water.  My family loved it and I will definitely serve it to company! Mild fresh flavor.

Wonderful recipe!  It was so delicious, but when I made it today (the first time), it was rather time-consuming... I think it was just me though so don't let me deter you from it.  I decided to leave out the potatoes for fear that they would get too soggy, and my sister and I added more cornstarch (almost two tbsp) to it to compensate for the extra chicken broth we used.  (chicken broth was taken from previous reviews in place of water, and we found it worked very well.)  EVERYONE liked it.  My mom asked that I save the recipe.

This can be a tasty low-fat soup.  I omitted the butter and added chicken stock instead of water and used skim milk.  Also, increased the onion and added 2 cloves of garlic.  I, then blended the whole thing.  Don't forget salt, though because it needs it. The carots and cheese give it a pleasing golden hue.  The result was a 200 calorie, 6g fat soup with very good flavor.

To my surprise, my whole family loved this soup.  However, my husband made it once and didn't chop the veggies up small and the kids wouldn't eat it.  After reading some other reviews, I left out the butter to make it a little healthier.  We didn't miss it all all.  I also used chicken broth instead of water, used a little extra onion and added some fresh minced garlic.

Sooo good. I altered it for our family used 1.5 c almond milk coconut oil and water instead of butter and 2.5c water with chicken b cube and minced garlic. Used hand blender added a little more water at end to make less thick. Verrrry good would be good just as is I'm sure just don't do certain products in our house

My Husband LOVED this soup! He kept raving about it and how I should make a massive batch to put in the freezer so he can have it anytime. I added a bit more cauliflower 1-2 cups more and added sausage per someone else's review as well as used the immersion blender on it a little. It had a great consistency and felt hearty.
this was easy -- but a bit plain for my tastes -- I had to zip up the taste with lots of herbs

It was good, though a little bland. I took the suggestion of cutting down on the milk to 2 cups for that reason. It's a comfort food and I loved the texture of the veggies. However, the flour overpowered it all. I suggest using half as much or even less. It'll still come out creamy; just let it simmer with the milk a little more.
Very good vegetable flavor and smoothness. Would definitely make again.
Terrific recipe.  Very easy to prepare.  Excellent just as it is with no changes!

Mmm-Mmm Good!  I made 2 small changes with this recipe.  I added chicken bouillon to the water & veggies then pureed it using an immersion blender.  Picky eaters didn't even know it was made with vegetables.
Excellent!!!  Added a little bit more of everything,  plus added one of those Knorr Chicken Stock gel packets, used the immersion blender and yummo!

Excellent, creamy, tasty soup. My favorite comfort soup! I use celery salt instead of actual celery, since I never use celery if I buy it. Other than that I use the recipe as it's written. Super tasty on a cold day with a bit of home-baked bread!

This was amazing! My husband, who is not a soup person and likes his food piping hot, ate this cold and couldn't stop snitching! Definitely a favourite in our house now.
I followed this recipe almost exactly, except I used vegetable stock instead of water and margarine instead of butter and I puréed most of it at the end (leaving some chunks for texture). So good!

this was perfect for a cold day!  i substituted 1c chicken broth for the water, added 2 cloves of garlic, and threw in some broccoli rather than celery, per my husband's request.  i also used a little over 1 c of sharp cheddar.  towards the end i used a potato masher on the whole mixture, which helped break down the potatoes and give smaller chunks of the other veggies.  this got my 18 mo old AND my husband to eat all of their vegetables.  that's how i define success in my house!  i will be making this regularly.
The soup was very good! My brother really loved it. He ate it all (after I had a small bowl) The soup went to a blender for a smooth texture. :) Will make it again!
the dairy can be eliminated by doubling the cauliflower and food processing 1/2 of it to make this thick and creamy
I made this exactly as shown, except I used vegetable broth instead of water.  It was fantastic!    It took a while to chop the vegetables and thicken the milk, but well worth the time spent.
Very good soup.  Added some spinach,which changed the color, but otherwise very nice. My family loved it.

Wonderful soup! I had some roasted califlower and put that in. I also had a little half and half (1 cup) as part of the milk measurement. I followed the other reviews and added a chicken broth instead of water. My family loved it!

Very tasty!  I took other recommendations and used chicken broth instead of water.  I also added a little extra veggies and used whole milk to make it more creamy.  I went with sharp cheddar instead of mild which was a good move.  Delish!  Next time I may add extra onion or try garlic to add pizzazz.
This is a wonderful soup. I have made it several times. I followed the recipe exactly the first time and liked it. To get a more chowder-like consistancy I lighty mash half the veggies after cooking.

Give it 7 (yes7!!!!!) stars.   Of all the recipes for cauliflower, this is my husband's favorite.  He says it is THE BEST SOUP I HAVE EVER MADE and I make a lot of soup.   I really did not change a thing - except that I did not have celery (so I will never add it now) and I always add a pinch of thyme to this kind of recipe so I will keep doing that!   Make this soup and you will love it.  Frozen cauliflower works fine, too.  One more thing -  garnish with toasted chopped almonds for a heavenly treat.  Jack really loves that!   Thank you janiebear925!!!!!

My husband LOVES this, but I'm just not too impressed... I probably just did something wrong LOL, but it has an odd consistancy, and there was really not that much flavor to it... I added a LOT of pepper, salt, garlic, & herbs, and it's still just ok. Might've been better cooking the veggies in chicken broth instead of water. Not sure if I'll try this again...

Made this soup as directed with only 2 alterations. After reading other reviews I added about 1/2 Tablespoon chicken boulion for extra flavor. Being the only person in my household I never have milk in the 'frig, but I always have canned milk in the cupboard which I use primarily for soups. Instead of 3 cups milk I used a 12 oz can of evaporated milk and 1 1/2 cups water. I also didn't stir cheese into the soup in the pot, but chose to sprinkle it over the soup in my bowl. I added some crackers and had a very satisfying meal.

we loved it. My 2 year old son helped make it and gobbled it up. we had to add quite a bit of salt and pepper for flavour and I doubled the recipe and added almost 4 cups of shredded cheese.
I will definitely make this again.
Added tender boiled chicken and garlic.  Used chicken stock instead of water and added corn too!
So easy. Definitely add chicken bouillon cube, garlic salt and cayenne pepper. Loved it and so did my bf.
Excellent!
My family loves this soup. Very easy to prepare and so comforting.
I didn't have carrots to add but did put in some bacon bits at the end. Very good. Would definitely make again.

This was great! I just made it to get me through a cold night.  The only modifications were to mash the vegetables a little before combining with the milk.  I also doubled the cheese and served with fresh parsley.  I'll definitely make again!
Great recipe!! I used a whole cauliflower and also used a can of chicken broth instead of water.  Next time I would cut down on the butter/flour and add more liquid.  Will definately make this again.
Loved this recipe. It was quick to make and tasted great. I used powered cheddar cheese instead of the shredded. I have two kids that hate cheese and they both loved this soup!!

Delicious! I tripled this recipe and it still came out perfectly. The only thing I would comment on, is if doubling or tripling, you will need to double/triple each cooking time. And I noticed this needs a lot of salt and pepper, but when you get the seasoning right, it's delicious.
My family enjoyed eating this soup.  My kids (2 and 4) asked for seconds!

I was really surprised at how easy this was to make. All you have to do is chop up the veggies, boil them, make a quick roux, and you're all done. If you're efficient, it could take as little as 30 minutes. 

I'm not much one for measuring, so I guessed at the vegetable amounts. What I ended up using was: 1 whole russet potato, 3 whole carrots, 5 celery stalks,  1 head of cauliflower, ~1/3 of an onion (that I had left over from something else), and 5 green onions (to supplement). I also tossed in 2 cloves of garlic, which was a great addition! 

I had to use quite a bit more than 3/4 cup of water (but I didn't measure, so I'm not sure exactly how much). Most of it boiled out while cooking the veggies, so there was probably only about 1 cup left when I added the sauce. 

Like the recipe said, I added salt and pepper to taste--then added cheese to taste as well, since you can never have enough in my opinion.  

It turned out great! It's a very creamy, comforting dish, and I have enough for at least three large servings, maybe four.

This is so easy.  I make a big batch once or twice a month, but it doesn't last a week.  I made it for a formal dinner party.  I was perfect because I made it a day ahead of time and everyone loved it.
I swapped the 1 C of water for a 14.5 oz can of broth (and used 1 C less of milk) and used 2 C cauliflower and no potato.  YUM!
We loved this recipe.  It is quick and easy.  I did use chicken stock instead of water.  Serve with crusty bread......Mmmmmm good meal.

Made exactly according to recipe and it was absolutely delicious! Used lite milk instead of full-cream for a healthy version and still ended up thick and creamy and full of taste. Definitely a keeper.
Use chicken broth instead of water (a whole can) use sharp cheese, a little garlic, no potato and more cauliflower. Run it thru food processor.
Very good and very rich. Great over pasta if you leave out the potatoes
This was good. I probably won't make it again, though.
Instead of water a vegetable broth would've made this tastier. It was a little bland.
Absolutely wonderful.  Very creamy and flavourful
Followed SLJ6's advice.  More chicken broth, less milk.  More cheese, whole head cauli, more veggies.  Thyme.  Blend in blender to make real smooth.  YUM!
we loved it!! I added chx base for more flavor. Next time i will omit the potato and add diced ham (my hubby's idea). great soup,and easy to make!

I used almost a full head of cauliflower and left out the potatoes.  I added a chicken boullion cube to the 3/4 cup water.   But that wasn't enough water to cover all the vegetables so I added extra chicken broth.  We like spicier foods, so I added some red pepper flakes to the boiling pot.  

I didn't want it to be too chunky so I mashed a little bit with a potato masher after boiling.  As someone else suggested, I added a pinch of thyme.  Also I used garlic salt instead of regular salt and I doubled the amount of cheese.
Turned out great!
Delicious! I doubled the recipe and added a pinch of ground mustard and some pot herbs. everyone really enjoyed it. A keeper!
OK, but a little bland.
Made this recipe substituting brocolli for the cauliflower. It was great! Best "brocolli-cheese" soup I ever ate!
This is really good.  My husband even liked it.  It's really good if you butter some french bread and put it in the oven to get crusty and then dip the bread in the soup.  Yum.
Delicious! The soup definitely needs salt. I found that using Maggi's seasoning sauce was a good way to give the soup some kick.

This was a VERY good soup. I too saute'd up the onion and some garlic and boiled the veggies up in chicken broth. I also used up some 1/2 and 1/2 I had in the fridge instead of milk. This made it VERY good ( and rich). Instead of the 4oz Cheddar cheese, I topped it off with some grated MacLarens Imperial Sharp cheese and some bacon bits. This soup is restaurant quality!!
We agree it needs some vegetable or chicken broth, garlic and some spices, but other than that, an awesome soup.  Will enjoy often.

This is great soup! I was skeptical at first but upon tasting I found it to be very filling and quite tasty! I did add 5 cloves of garlic minced, I used a full large onion, 3 large carrots, 3 medium potatoes, 2 large shallots sauteed in the butter, and I exchanged the water for chicken broth. I also used corn starch in place of the flour and swapped on cup of the milk for light cream.

Yum! I did alter this recipe quite a bit- the only veggies I used were cauliflower and broccoli, and adjusted the amounts to my taste. I did add more cheese- I don't think I would've liked it as much with the amount of cheese called for in the recipe. Will definitely make again.

This soup is delicious! I added more cauliflower, and some broccoli, and used lowfat chicken broth instead of water. Also, 2% milk. I'm afraid that I added too much cheese though, although that's what made it taste so good. It was a little bland, so I added some hot sauce and some crushed red pepper. My husband also loved this soup and he's a tough critic.
Wonderful!  I will use this recipe again and again.  Perfect for a snowy, cold day.  Thankyou!
Delicious!  Thank you for sharing!
Yum Yum!!  I really enjoyed this and froze this is separate bowls to take for lunch at work.

Great recipe and so flexible. I live in Thailand and want to find recipes that I can find local ingredients (so it's still cheaper to make) and this is very easy to do here (even though I did bring my own cheddar from the states this year). I've made this two times now and both times didn't use celery because I couldn't find it at the local out-door market. I simply added more cauliflower, potatoes and carrots. It turned out great both times. I've been tempted to add some Thai chilli's to spice it up, but made it for guests/children both times. I've used a thicker cream for half of the milk and then water for the other half. I feel like you can't go wrong with this soup, and it's a hit every time! Thanks everyone for all the insight/ideas for this recipe!
Great soup! Only changed water to fat free chicken broth with garlic and herbs, added chopped broccoli and pepper jack cheese. It seemed to need the spice. Thank you Jane!
I'm not crazy about cauliflower, but this soup is fantastic!  You'd never even know it's cauliflower soup.  Every person who's tried it, loves it!

Very good soup!! I did add more water to the vegis while cooking, around a 1/2 cup. the soup was to thick for my taste I added half cube chicken boulion  to the vegis and water while cooking. All together VERY EASY to make!! thanx:)
A very nice cheesy, creamy soup...you can't go wrong with this recipe.

This was terrific w/a few changes.  I cooked the cauliflower and potato in chicken broth until tender but lumpy.  Separetely I cooked the celery, carrots and one pkg Lipton onion soup mix.  After tender I put through my blender to make smooth.  It didn't need any additional salt w/the Lipton soup mix.  I did add a dash of nutmeg and added Tostitos medium cheese dip.  Yummy.

This soup is very similar to one my mom makes and has passed on to me. In fact, its my daughter's favorite soup and she requests it regularly. I make a few changes: 1) I omit the potatoes 2) instead of putting the onions in the water to boil, I slice up a lb of smoked sausage (ie: Polska Kielbasa) and fry the slices with the onions. 3) Add the onions and drained sausage when the cauliflower and other veggies are tender 4)After adding the roux, use velveeta (and a little more of it) and stir until melted. Very good and creamy soup! This works as a great way to warm you winter nights!!
Cooked veggies in vegetable broth, used skim milk, used 1/2 sharp cheddar & 1/2 american cheese, added 2 chicken bouillon cubes. Loved it & even my husband who is not a soup fan ate 2 bowls!
Loved it! Since I was in the mood for green onions I added two...mmmm! I can see that this might be even better with double cauliflower and no potatoes. Every bite with cauliflower was a delight.

I think this is a very good base to start from, and like several others, added a few things.  I used vegetable stock in place of water, using a full cup and let it boil down. To the milk and roux, I used sharp cheddar, a few slices of American cheese, 1/2 cup of leftover "cream cheese sauce" from a local chain pizza joint, which is basically garlic and whipped cream cheese, and then I added a teaspoon of mustard seasoning (dry) and a pinch of cayenne. I also salted and peppered to taste. This going to be a staple here in this house! Yum!

This was a really wonderful soup. I made enough to feed a small army and took some suggestions of other reviewers as one can rarely have TOO much flavour, right? When I made the roux and the cheese sauce I added garlic and followed the same ingredients I use when making a rich cheese sauce to pour over veggies. Worcestershire sauce and mustard powder, bay leaves, and 'Season All' (souped up salt ;) ) gave it a nice kick. I also did half cauliflower and half broccoli because that's what I wanted to use. My friend brought roasted garlic bread and crusty French and we filled up a big bowl with cubes of bread for dipping in the soup. I could eat this all winter. Thanks!

This soup is phenominal!  It's thick, creamy and cheesey.  My girlfriend doesn't like cooked cauliflower but she loved this soup and was sad when it was all gone.  I added 1/4 cup dry vermouth, white pepper and black pepper, and used reserve white cheddar aged 2 years.

I will be making this soup again and again as the requests come in.

I made this soup last Saturday and my family loved it. Since I used a whole head of cauliflower I doubled the recipe and it came out wonderful. The only other change that I made was that I didn't have celery, but I will add the celery next time, which will be soon. Thanks!

This is a great recipe! I did have to alter just a bit due to low carb and what I had on hand. I had lots of cauliflower, so I used 1/2 cup butter and equal parts flour. I steamed the cauliflower and celery in chicken broth. I only added a little bit of chicken bullion and pepper. No carrots (didn't have any) and no potatoes (stupid low carb). I bet it would have been great with the carrots and potatoes. Thank you for a great recipe! Also used 2% milk. :)

Loved it!  I was looking to use up cauliflower and someone from "thebuzz" suggested this recipe.  I made as written; only doubling it.  I made it 2 days early to take to my in-laws.  The results were a nice thick and chunky soup, just what I was looking for.  It was not thick after making it, but I think sitting in the fridge for two days thickened it.  The flavors blended together nicely.  You could easily sub chicken or vegetable broth in place of the water.  I went light on the salt and pepper and let everyone season their own bowl.  Soup was enjoyed by all and will be made again.

Wonderful.  The only thing I did differently was that I pureed the cauliflower and potatoes after they were cooked.  I was trying to copy a soup from our local restraurant and I did it, thanks so much.

This was really very good.  My meat n' potatoes boyfriend liked it even better than I did!  I feel like it's missing something, but I can't put my finger on just what it is.  I added some fresh garlic and some salt & pepper but other than that I didn't make any changes and it turned out good.

Excellent...... I trippled this recipe (I never know how many I'm feeding). I had to use a shallot I had no onions. It ended up to be only four of use eating. It was gone......gone.
Excellent Soup!

Just tried this today! Delicious. I made a few variations with ingredients as well, just playing around. I made adjustments to the amounts - I didn't use carrot or celery, I used more cheese at the end, I added a little bit more potato (**used red skin potatoes; so good in everything!) and cauliflower and adjusted liquid until it was right, ended up using less milk than instructed which was okay as I feel more would give it more of a chowder-feel than I wanted it to have. I threw some sliced garlic in with the milk and added crushed red pepper at the end. Also some left over spinach I realized I had even after it was done, just stirred in. 
Over all, a good soup! The downside is it is bland, even with adjustments, which not everyone would be a fan of. I do think if I had used chicken broth as the other reviews had, I would have had some more flavor in there, but still delicious, nonetheless. 
Will try vegetable or chicken broth next time for sure, and will be making this again.
Tasty way to get cauliflower in the diet.  My three year old loved it.
Nice and quick, though nothing special -- I might make this again.

Yum!  Used broth instead of water and omitted potato as suggested by others.  Skipped the butter and flour and just used a hand blender to puree about half of the soup.  Also used up a chunk of Velveeta with this.  Will make again!
Needs more cauliflower.  Cut back on carrots as it overpowers the cauliflower.

Loved this! One of the best recipes off this site! I used chicken broth instead of water, and next time I think I will add more of the veggies, but overall it was wonderful! Served it with croutons on top. Husband and son both loved it.
This recipe was a hit with four picky kids. This is a soup that the whole family will enjoy. I love it!

I sauted the onions, garlic, celery and carrots first.  I also had a leek so I stuck that in too.  Then I added the rest of the veggies and I used chicken broth.  I am not going to make the roux next time because of the faint "pasty" taste it took on.  We all really liked the soup though.  So next time:  Puree after all the veggies are soft with the hand blender, then add some milk and half/half plus seasonings.  That should bump it up to 5 stars.  1/12/16
I made it again with no roux and wow, you really don't need the extra calories from the butter and flour.  It is 5 stars now!

I never start off my soups by boiling. Boiling to me waters down flavors.You don't extract flavors from onions by boiling them.  Sauteing is the way to go. Here are my changes. Cook cauliflower separately in water. Don't OVERCOOK. Separate a few florets for garnish. I sauteed my onion,celery (with leaves)in butter substitute. Added 2 cloves of garlic, 1/2tspn. of nutmeg(trust me on this one),and flour.  Cook for a few minutes Add chicken broth,fat free half and half and about 1 cup of water.  Simmered for a litle bit. Added cauliflower in with 3 sprigs of thyme continue to simmer and add cheddar cheese.  Allow the flavors to develop a little more and remove the thyme sprigs.  Using an immersion blender I blended it all. Garnished with the reserved florets and some lemon zest and fresh parsley.  I also sprinkled some chopped walnuts to give it a bit of crunch. Delicious ! I left out the potato and carrots.

This rating is based on the changes that I made to the recipe (which is a good starter recipe by the way): 3 cups low sodium chicken broth/1 head cauliflower, chopped/1 large carrot, diced/1 large russet potato, diced/2 cloves garlic/1 cup fat-free evaporated milk/1.5 cups shredded sharp cheddar/salt and pepper to taste.  I boiled all the veggies in the broth until softened, about 10 minutes.  Then pulsed 3/4 of the mixture in my food processor (be sure to let heat escape if using blender) until smooth.  I left the last 1/4 a little bit more coarse for some added texture.  I then returned the mixture to the stovetop, added the evaporated milk and cheese, until warmed and incorporated and seasoned with salt and pepper to taste.  The result was something that my family enjoyed very much.  Thank you for starting with a great recipe---it's allowed me to adjust to my family's personal taste.
Very very bland.  I couldn't doctor this up enough.
Quick, easy and Mmmm Mmmmm good.
This soup was excellent.  I used chicken stock because I had it but I don't believe it made any difference.  I will definitely make it again, and will use this as my base for clam chowder.
awesome

Starting off by saying the end result was ok, but I added a lot to spruce up the bland flavor. I think for me next time I make it you have to have a meat base and not water and as well I would add meat. I took one suggestion from another rater who said to bled half of it, I wouldn't do that again as it gives a grainy texture to the soup. As well I found myself spending two hours to make this soup slow chopper I guess, just way to many steps. I'm glad I tried it tho and will do it again just with my spin on it. Thanks for the base tho i'v never made cauliflower soup before and this was not too bad!

Put together with a combination of ideas from other reviewers. Used a 1 lt box of chicken broth, instead of water, and added garlic and onion sauted with the flour/butter.  Seasoned with a bit of cayenne, white pepper and a touch of salt (would leave out this bit of salt next time).  Lightly pureed about 3/4 of the mixture, and kept some chunks for body.  Used a sharp cheddar.  Very nice soup, and will certainly make again.

I always replace water with chicken broth in soup recipes - and I did that here. Also, once the soup was all together I added chicken boullion until it was at the flavor level I wanted. This. Soup. Rocks.

Yummy soup.  My husband and I really liked this one.  I would cut the veggies bigger than suggested.  Also, watch the salt.  Mine turned out a little on the salty side.  I would use less than suggested at first.

Easy, fast and super tasty. I just added more cheese since I looove the cheesy taste. I make huge pots and send it to my Mom who is a cauilflower cheese soup fanatic. Now she wont eat it at any resturant. She says this is the best. Great on those cold winter nights.

I have to admit, this was pretty good! the only reason this recipe is getting 4 stars instead of 5 is because it was a bit bland and I had to add more spices then just salt and pepper. I think nex time I make it, I'll use chicken or vegetable stock to cook the veggies like some other reviewers did. All in all a pretty good recipe!

This soup is exactly what I was looking for.  I doubled the vegetables and cut the milk to 2 cups.  I doubled the cheese.  I like a chunky soup so I made those changes. The potato gives it the body other cauliflower soup lacks.  Absolutely delicious.  Great on a cold day.

This was a good starter recipe, however I made some changes.  I cooked the chopped up vegetables in 2 tablespoons of olive oil for 5 minutes before I added the liquid.  I added a bit of garlic and used vegetable broth instead of water.  I also added some chopped fresh parsley, finished it off with a 4 year old cheddar.  Very good!

This soup came out great! Following the reviewers' advice, I did make lots of changes to enhance the flavor. For starters, I also added chopped broccoli with the cauliflower and used chicken stock instead of water. I omitted the celery and carrot while including an herb bundle of rosemary and thyme with scallions instead of onion. I cooked up lots of cripsy bacon beforehand  and added that in after the soup cooked for 20mins and let it sit a little. Before adding the roux, I used a hand blender to make the soup a little creamer like split pea soup; leaving some chunks for texture. I also added a lot more cheese.  Top with fresh chopped scallions and this soup has quickly become a fave of me and my family!!
I made this vegetarian by using vege broth and a little spicy by using pepper jack cheese. So good. Highly recommended.
its awesome

Very great, comforting soup that helped use up some Thanksgiving leftovers! I normally hate cauliflower but I didn't even notice it in the soup so that was wonderful! I doubled everything except the butter and milk, and ended up with 4-5 good sized servings. (Next time I'll probably quadruple it so I can freeze some.) I used chicken broth instead of water and also sauted the onions, carrots, and celery with butter and parsley before adding the broth, etc. Since I was worried about the cheese not reheating well, we just added cheese to taste in the individual bowls. I've added this soup to our regular rotation and also plan on making a variation of it by substituting broccoli for the potatoes so it will freeze better. Thanks for a great recipe!

My family really enjoyed this comforting soup.  I added a chicken boullion cube to the water and veggies.  I also used 7 slices of Kraft american cheese instead of cheddar chz.  Make sure to season with salt and pepper otherwise it could be pretty bland.
I made this soup the other day; it was great.  The only things I changed was that I didn't add all the vegetable water, as I like thick soups!  I also added more cheese and more veggies.

With the couple of changes I had a tasty, simple lunch that cleaned out the fridge.I needed a cup more liquid(weak broth rather than water) to boil the veggies, so I used evaporated milk instead of regular and lessened it by the same amount. I also had some leftover mashed taters(nothing added) that I used instead of cubed potatoes which thickened the base some so I only needed half the roux.  The broth surely added a little flavor but probably no more than additional salt.
I added 2 tbs. of chicken soup starter. I've had nothing bur rave reviews !!!!

I am a 15 year old vegetarian. It is very hard to find good soup recipes,  being vegetarian and all, but this soup recipe is by far my favorite yet! As a vegetarian we all know that most of our meals will not be as tasteful as meat-eaters, but given the circumstances this soup is wonderful tasting. You can not judge this soup based off of the soupy flavor. You have to eat the vegetables with the soup and it taste amazing!! I did add garlic salt to my vegetables when i was boiling it with water. The taste is wonderful! Thank you for this splended recipe! Well deserved 5/5 rating!

Comforting and delicious. Easy to make your own variation. This time I also added broccoli, turkey bacon, cheddar & gruyere, and instead of sea salt, a couple dashes of Herbamare (check it out if you don't have it in your spice cabinet!). I doubled the recipe too because leftovers are even tastier!

Delicious soup.  I did as the first reviewer suggested and left out the butter, added chicken broth instead of water and used skim milk to cut calories.  I didn't use any potato, just added extra cauliflower instead and used low fat cheese.  I used the immersion blender to blend everything together in the pot on the stove.  It was yummy.  I didn't know if it would freeze well due to the cheese and creaminess of the soup but I froze the leftover soup and it was perfect a couple of weeks later.
All the family really liked this, th only change I made was to use stock instead of water.
Like many others, I thought it had to much mustard.  Will try again with a little less mustard or a different kind of mustard.
Tasty, easy, love it!! This recipes a keeper!
Really good, easy recipe.

So tasty! I will be making this again for sure. Was easy to make and tastes wonderful & healthy.
( I didn't add the celery however because I forgot to buy it).

Perfect texture - something that can be hard to get right with cauliflower soup. However, I added quite a bit more in terms of flavour - two minced cloves of garlic, which I sautéed with the onion at the beginning; and I added fresh thyme and sage from the garden when I simmered the vegetables, as well as a little hot sauce.
Didn't add any potatoes, just doubled up on the cauliflower.  You could get away with a little less  milk. Delicious flavor! Thanks so much for sharing!

This was very good. I made a few adjustments after reading other reviews. I used one cup chicken broth, 1 1/2 cups of milk and 1/2 cup of half and half.
Also, I sauteed the onion, carrots and celery in butter first until tender, then added the flour. I think this gives extra flavor.
Also, I added 1 tsp garlic salt, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp white pepper and 1/2 tsp thyme.

I thought this was very good and tasted very rich as if it were made from cream and not skim milk which is what I used.  Like the others, I also used broth instead of water and I used the food processor to chop veggies very small before boiling.  I can't imagine the fat content listed is right since the only real thing with fat would be the better and that doesn't seem like much better for a full batch of soup.  With that said, I think you could easily leave out the cheese b/c it was plenty tasty without it.

this was wonderful----added a chicken bullion cube to the water.  This recipe is a great base for any cream soup---Im going to make corn chowder using this recipe.  Today I made it with broccoli ---used about 3 times broccoli more than called for.  Added 1 1/2 tsp of dry mustard, a few shakes of hot sauce, and thickened it a bit more with a handful of mashed potato flakes.   Needs sale and pepper to your taste.

This soup was fantastic! Almost restaurant style.  The only alteration I made was using 1 cup of chicken broth vs. the water.  I also added the salt (sea) and pepper with the boiling vegetables, and added dried parsley.  Excellent recipe!

I modified this recipe a little. We don't care for celery, so I replaced it with broccoli. I also used cheddar and mozzarella cheeses. I used the hand mixer so the chunks of vegetables weren't so large. This has got to be one of the best soups I have eaten. Thanks for sharing it.
Yum!
This soup is great. Perfect for a cool fall day or a cold winter day. I have made this twice.  Once I didn't have cheddar cheese, so I added mozzarella instead...it was delicious.
I made this with a whole head of cauliflower and omitted the potatoes and carrots.  I also doubled the sauce.  It was excellent!  I will definitely be making this again.

I just made this recipe and OMG how good.  I didn't have carrots, so I added a can of them at the end of cooking the vegetables.  I also used 1 Tblsp of chicken base in the water for added flavor as someone suggested.  I emulsified the vegetables but left it kind of chunky, then pour the sauce over the vegetables.  Only had Velveeta on hand so I used that.  I don't like to change recipes, but that is all I had on hand and my cauliflower was starting to look bad.  I don't like giving 5 stars with add-ins, but I don't think I hurt this recipe by using canned carrots. Very Very Very good - will make this again and again.  Thanks for the great recipe.  It really does make alot.  Got pretty thick as it cooled, so will use milk to thin it when I reheat tomorrow for lunch.

As written this is a 3 star. As others have mentioned it needs some flavor. I tried making adjustments and it improved it remarkably. Instead of salt I used vegetarian bouillon cubes. I added some garlic and doubled the vegetables. I used skim milk and substituted olive oil for half the butter. I was trying to make this a bit healthier. With the changes it was a 4-5 star if you like creamy soups. In the end, I decided I am just not fond of creamy soups, so will not make this again. Others will likely enjoy it very much.

YUM. I pretty much made as is but I used more cauliflower instead of potatoes, and omitted the celery (I simply forgot it!). I did add 2 tsp chicken bouillon granules, and subbed half the cheese for frito lay mild cheddar cheese dip to cut down on the calories. The recipe is delicious, and I don't believe subbing half dip on my doubled recipe made any difference in flavor. Thanks so much!
This soup was great.  I loved the chunky texture of it.

As is, I think this is a 3 star soup. It is significantly bland and is missing some necessary acidity. I was able to pull it up from a 3 star to nearly 5 stars by substituting the water for veggie broth as other raters suggested and then adding to the mix 1-2 TBS of vinegar, a half a cap full of lemon juice, 1tsp of garlic powder, and about 1/8tsp to 1/4tsp of cayenne pepper. I then served it with some egg knot rolls and garnished it with chopped scallions. YUMMY!!
The soup wasn't great, it had okay flavor but nothing outstanding. I'd make it again if I had cauliflfower I wanted to use up.

This is a delicious, hearty soup! Turns out so rich even using skim or 1% milk. Very easy to make too. I used more cauliflower and potatoes than the recipe called for so I boiled them with much more water than the recipe states. When they were tender I ladled most of the water out and kept it aside. I added the milk mixture and added the reserved water until it was the consistency I wanted.  Delicious!!
Soup was great. Entire family loved it!
This was a great soup, I gave it 5 stars even though I made a few changes.  Mostly healthwise, much less butter and less cheese.  It was still wonderfully tasty.  Thanks!

Excellent! My only comment is about the cheese...I'm from Wisconsin, so I felt the need to add about a half cup more cheese to make it cheesy enough for my tastes...if you want it cheesy, plan on adding more. Otherwise delicious!
Fantastic! I used my immersion blender to smooth it out! Even the 4 yr old loved it.
really really good

I probably would have given this 4 stars but the baby liked it so that's enough to boost it up an extra star for me!  He has been very picky lately so this must have been good :)  I blended it with the hand blender until there was still a little texture but no big chunks.  I think I liked it better that way than I would have if I hadn't blended it.  It was very easy to prepare so that is another big plus.
I also used chicken broth.
Extra cayenne and extra sharp cheddar!!

I found a fantastic price on cauliflower this week so I bought two heads. I will certainly be buying it more often after trying this recipe for the first time. I cooked 2 full heads together after removing the green and the core. I simmered them doen till thdy were very tender. I then added sea salt, black pepper, onion, fresh garlic, chicken stock gells 4) some thyme, parsley etc.this came out fantastic! And I made almost a stockpot full. It is soooo good!

Excellent, easy soup.  I also used 1 lg onion, 3 carrots, 3 potatoes, 3 stalks celery, 3 cloves garlic, minced, and 3 chicken bouillon cubes. I utilized 1 1/2 c. milk and 1 1/2 c. half-and-half.  I had good results sauteeing the onion and garlic first until translucent and then adding to the pot, which I had added an additional 1/2 c. water as well as the bouillon cubes.  I also used an immersion blender to puree the vegetables and then added the cheese as well as good amounts of salt and pepper.  It had a thick, chowder-like consistency and was a huge winner both immediately as well as leftover.  A must-have for your winter soup arsenal!

Great soup with a couple changes..Saute veggies in olive oil and 2 cloves of garlic before you add water (chix broth is better.) Run the solids through the food processor or blender after you add the cheese.  Delicious!

Fantastic soup for cold weather. Used vege boullion for more flavor, left out celery, and added way more cheese. We use frozen cauli and it comes out fine. Overall a great soup and it whips up in a flash!
Yum!! I just added some garlic and it was great!

Yum! This was good.  My whole family liked it.  My husband said it was the best soup recipe yet.  The only thing I did different was to cook the veggies in 2 cup chicken broth and add only 2 cups milk (still 4 cups total)  This could be a good base for clam chowder.  Just add clams and some bacon.  Yum!!

I wasn't disappointed, but it was ok, just ok.  Maybe I need more flavor in my recipes -it's a constant challenge.  I doubled the recipe, added about a cup more cheese, one of the comments about the carrots is correct, it colors the entire dish-but cute for Thanksgiving. Also pureed half the vegs and chopped the rest - that gives it good texture.  Garlic and more salt kicked it in a bit.  And I also added more califlower bits for more texture and crunch.

This soup is fantastic!  I made it almost exactly as written, only I substituted the water with chicken broth and I used broccoli instead of cauliflower since my kids prefer broccoli.  I pureed it before adding the milk sauce to the cooked veggies and it turned out just perfect!
This soup is delicious! I also used the chicken broth instead of water. My family loved it!
Wonderful recipe Jane, thank you! I made a couple of small changes - instead of water I used vegetable broth and I doubled the cheese.  It was great.

I wanted to give this 5 but couldn't because I tweaked it.  I used beef broth for water, doubled the cauliflower and no potato.  I also added about 2 1/2 strips of bacon, cooked and diced.  Also, 3 slices american/jalapeno cheese in addition to cheddar.  Added diced green onions at end when serving, no onion at beginning.  Big hit with both teenage sons!!
What a wonderful soup. A great winter meal served with fresh crusty bread. Will be making this again.

This is an an easy, basic soup, it took me 15-20 minutes to make. Since I'm always looking to make foods healthier, I decreased the butter to 2 tbsp and accordingly did the same with the flour. You could use any vegetables you have on hand.

My husband thought it was delicious, however,I did not think it had enough cauliflower taste. I made it exactly as written.  In the future, I will use chicken broth, use more cauliflower, less potato and carrots.

Pretty good. I made 3 times the amount because I had a whole head of cauliflower to use up. So 1 head of cauliflower, 5 carrots, 5 to 6 small russets, 1 onion, 4 stalks celery. I also added bacon and doubled the cheese. It was a bit scary when adding the milk to the flour and butter as it got very thick at first. However, it thins out after all the milk is added. I am fairly happy with the end result; however, it could use more seasoning of some kind. Next time, I'll try it with chicken stock instead of water and add garlic as some other reviews suggest.

Wow! I used a garlic and parsley buillion cube with the water and veggies. I added 3 cups of cauliflower, 3\4 cup shredded carrots and 2 cloves of garlic (and no celery). Next time I will use at least 4 cups cauliflower and 1 cup carrots, and only 1 clove of garlic. It was amazing, especially for a cauliflower soup. Thanks so much!

well, i was not too impressed with the soup made by this recipe, but added 1 t garlic salt and much better! got a little thick on me so i believe i added another 1/2 c milk so it seemed more like a soup vs a cheese sauce.
Great soup. The whole family loved it, even the kids, who are not big fans of cauliflower.

I agree, it was good, but I found it a bit bland, and the texture of the cheese totally changes when reheated, even on the stove.  I can see it being great for kids though who don't usually like overpowering flavors.
Loved this soup and will make it again.  Not only does it taste good, it's super easy to make.

I followed the recipe exactly and it was delicious.  Basically, if you like vegetables with cheese sauce, that's what this is...  I think this would be a very forgiving recipe where you could add many kinds of veggies and it would still be yummy.

Pretty good soup. I definitley went by the reviews...I used veg stock instead of water. I also boosted up the veggies with broccoli, spinach, jalapeno pepper (we like heat) and garlic. I omitted the celery. I doubled the cheese too. It turned out great. This will be keeper!
This recipe is easy, tasty, and reheats well!  Plus, it is a great way to get your veggies!

This was pretty good. I made it exactly as written, and I actually wasn't that impressed with the soup the first bowl I had. I thought it was just okay and wasn't planning on making it again. Well, the next day I decided give it another try and reheat some while taking the advice of some of the other reviewers (to puree some or all of the soup). So I added a very small amount of milk to a hand blender to the soup and pureed it, and I liked it MUCH better this way. For some reason, it made a HUGE difference whether or not to leave it "chunky" or puree it.

This definitely needs more cheese than the recipe calls for. I used extra-sharp cheddar and also a little parmesan. (Next time I would include some blue cheese such as Stilton for extra flavor.) I followed others' advice and used chicken broth. A cup of half-and-half provided extra creaminess.
Besides healthiness, this base recipe doesn't really have much in terms of flavor. I even followed suggestions on chicken stock and garlic, but it just wasn't very tastful.

I made this for dinner yesterday, and it was a huge hit! I would have given it five stars, except for the fact that the seasoning was WAY off--without a few modifications, this would have been very bland (but this is a great starter recipe, as long as you taste and season as you go).
We didn't have cauliflower, so I used a package of frozen vegetables in a steam bag (including broccoli, lima beans, carrots, and celery), steamed it in the microwave, and added it to the soup with the cheese.
I increased the amount of cheese to include a mixture of Sharp Cheddar:Monterey Jack at a ratio of 2:3. The Monterey Jack REALLY made the recipe! 
I subbed in chicken stock for the water, and boiled some frozen hashbrown cube-cut potatoes and frozen onion, which I then added to the roux, along with the steamed veggies and cheese.
The whole recipe took less than a half hour to make, and still tasted like a full, flavorful soup that had been simmering all day! I did have to add massive amounts of kosher salt, some garlic and onion powder, and a dash of oregano and terragon in order to round out the flavor profile.
The carrots gave the soup a beautiful hint of color, and the lima beans added a nice textural contrast. It was a lovely soup! Thanks so much for such a great starter to a cheese soup!!!
GREAT SOUP AND HUGE COMFORT FOOD. I used 1 1/2 c milk and 1 1/2 c half & half, upped the cheese and used 1/2 broccoli and 1/2 cauliflower.

This was exactly what I was looking for - a quick and easy soup that did not have to simmer for a long time.  Using stock instead of water, as others had recommended, I had this soup ready in fifteen minutes or so, and my family ate it up!  I would definitely consider doubling, even for my family of four, if using as a main dish.

I gave this 5 stars because I used this recipe in addition to another to get a fabulous result. I used 4 c. chicken broth and 1 c. fat free 1/2 and 1/2 as my liquids. I used 3 ribs of celery with their leaves, one whole carrot small diced, 1/2 large onion diced, a whole large head of cauliflower cut into florets and left out the potatoes completely. I used salt, pepper and thyme leaves as my seasonings and after cooked until everything was very tender, I processed in batches in my food processor(leaving some chunks for texture). I then returned to my soup pot and slowly stirred in about 1 1/2 c. of cheddar. Delicious!!!

I loved this soup! Like others, I used a whole head of cauliflower but left out the potato. I also used veggie broth and added more cheese and even leftover blue cheese that I had in my fridge. I took the suggestion of another reviewer and put all of the veggies in my food processor first, so it cut down on cooking time. Turned out delish!

I gave this recipe 5 stars. My family loves cauliflower and cheese...so I tried to please everyone. It was absolutley the best. My son had some friends over and it was dinner time and they helped themselves to 2 bowls each...My husband...who eats whatever I make no matter how horrible it was...just kept saying how delicious it was. I did tweak it a little...I didn't use any water I used 2 cans of chicken broth...no milk and no flour...I also didn't put the carrots in...I didn't want to over do the veggies. But I cooked this in my crock pot all day and the aroma was so tempting all day. Thankfully they all left me some too. I will definetly make this again.
Loved it!  I did omit the butter and flour and decreased the milk.  I also added some boullion and 1/2 and 1/2!  So good!

This recipe was excellent after a few changes.  I doubled the recipe, but halved the milk and replaced it with vegetable broth. I also added a teaspoon of Italian seasoning and a dash of garlic powder.  At the end of cooking, before adding the cheese (sharp cheddar), I pureed part of the soup with an immersion blender.  I added salt and white paper to balance the flavors as needed.

A lot of the reviews mentioned that this soup was bland. I used veggie bouillon, lots of onion and garlic, a bit more water and a bit more cheese. Fresh jalepeno pepper, Extra salt, extra pepper.This soup is THICK but not bad. I was worried about the texture not having a blender but during boiling everything broke down a bit and had a decent consistency. Got cauliflower haters to love it!
Just made this,It it great! Left out the potatoes,and used alot of garlic!

I've never low rated a recipe before but this was very bland and tasteless, I think it may work better by omitting the carrot and potato, using more cauliflower, a little more celery and definitely onion, a cup less milk, a cup of chicken stock and a teaspoon of mustard powder! I'm a big fan of Cauliflower Cheese soup but this was nothing like it - sorry.
I doubled this recipe and added extra cheese. It's a pretty good soup, very creamy and reminiscent of clam chowder. My girlfriend added New Orleans seasoning to her bowl to give it more flavor.

Excellent!  Actually this tasted a lot like a baked potato soup we love.  I doubled the ingredients so we would have some leftovers.  I subbed chicken broth for the water after reading reviews. I also sauteed the onion with some minced garlic in the butter, then added the flour to make the roux.  I mashed the veggies with a potato masher, and combined everything without using a blender-the soup was a little chunky, the way we like it.  I then added some cayenne pepper and cajun seasoning.  The seasoning was perfect-just a little bite and enough salt.

I love how quickly this comes together--a great way to use leftovers from a salad bar meal.  Using Pepper Jack cheese for part of the cheddar adds a wonderful flavor.  This is thick enough to work well over biscuits (especially when the veggies are done in the food processor.)
A truly wonderful soup. Recipe makes just enough so it doesn't take long to make.  I added 1 chicken boullion to it for extra flavor. The best soup I've ever made. Thanks Jane.
Easy to throw together, I use chicken broth to simmer the veggies.  And seasoned with salt and pepper when it was done.

I made some alterations to the recipe by using my nutri bullet.  Instead of using water, I juiced some lettuce and cooked all the vegetables in the lettuce "water".  After the vegetables were cooked, I returned them to the juicer and pureed them.  Add the milk, flour butter, and cheese mixture, stirred together added Mrs. Dash and a little seasalt to finish.
Great soup! Made a few changes - added more water, 1/4 cup cream and extra cauliflower.

This recipe was great! I did, however make some additions to it which made it even better.  I added chicken broth instead of the water.  I also had some leftover brocolli, spinach, and half of a tomato which I also added.  In addition to that, I minced my veggies in the food processor instead of chopping them, which cut down on the cooking time of my soup.  All in all it turned out just wonderful. Thank you for such an easily adjustable and yummy recipe.

This recipe turned out great for me w/the modifications from other reviews. I used chicken broth instead of water, omitted the potatoes & celery (did not even miss them), used 1 1/2 cups of cauliflower, half an onion, and doubled the cheese (definitely needed). I also only used 2 cups of milk (subbed FF half & half for 1 cup of it) and added 2 minced garlic cloves. Other modifications included sautéing the garlic, onions, & butter before adding it to the veggies and using my Vitamix to blend everything a little more. The only change I would make next time is definitely cut down on the butter! There's no need for 1/4 cup.

I mae this soup last night. It was great. AAfter it was sone I transfered it to a slow cooker because my husband works 2nd shift. I kept the crock pot on warm and it was just right for him when he came home. I omited the carrots however only because I didn't have any in the house. It was still awesome.

Not bad, but for a good flavor I use half chicken and half beef broth, little of vegeta spice and fresh parsley. As for a milk, I use 2/3 and the rest I used water. Also, I fried onion before adding to a pot. I made a huge pot, so I did everything x6. I like to freeze leftovers and have it for another day, so I don't have to cook when I'm too busy having fun with my kids.
Yum! Very simple. Just a personal preference- I would add more cauliflower next time and omit the potatoes.

This soup is very tasty! I accidentally forgot the onion...which may be why I was slightly disappointed. I will definitely be making this again though! (I found this recipe only made enough for 2 adults, so if you're cooking for a group make a little extra)

I really liked this recipe as a starting point; after making it exactly as written I give it three stars.  However, before eating it I tweaked it to push it up for five stars.  Like some other reviewers, I found it bland.  I added garlic powder, onion powder, a little cayenne pepper, and more cheese.  I think it would be even better if one subbed a cup of chicken stock for one of the cups of milk, and threw some garlic in with the veggies.
The recipe is bliss!  I usually don't review recipes, but this was a must.  The only variation I suggest is to double it, because you'll want more.
Four thumbs down at our house.   We did not like this.
This is so delicious and a nice change from a regular lemonade!
Amazing! I added about a 1/2 more water to mellow it out a bit. Can't wait to add a little rum to it...

This is an amazing recipe. I am not familiar with Brazilian anything so I made this twice, once peeling the limes and the other time leaving them whole (but cutting off the ends). A note to those confused: DON'T PEEL YOUR LIMES!
I made this for my little bros bday when my fam came up.  they all tried it and loved it!  the only thing it need is more sugar

different! delicious and refreshing

Very refreshing! I used my Blendtec, which is so powerful that there were not even any bits to sieve out! But, I think that also made it slightly bitter.

Delicious! Everyone loved it!
Awesome sweet sour creamy goodness! Made it for "girls nite" and added vodka. Yum!
Didn't change a thing, except you could maybe cut down on the sugar just a tad bit. Don't think twice and make this drink! I know y'all will absolutely love it.

Not sure why this is called "lemonade" when it has no lemons in it, but who cares, it tastes good.  Easily could be converted to an adult cocktail just by subbing some of the water with rum.  Either way, it's a nice beverage (and easy, too!).
What a great summer beverage!
July is filled with birthday, I like to try new limonade... This one comes out of the lot.    A successfull beginning of afternoon!   Before tonight's party......
Lemonade! Brazilian style yummy!
Loved these!  Drank them down by the lake, will do the same again tonight.
I made it and everyone loved it, has anyone tried it with oranges, or lemons?
Love this!

LOVE THIS!!!! INSTANTLY MAKES ME IMAGINE BEING ON AN ISLAND RELAXING.  THIS IS REALLY GOOD.  Used 4 TBS. Bottled lime juice in exchange for 2 limes. 
THANKS FOR SHARING THIS!
Simple & easy!
This drink is not only incredibly easy to make, but very refreshing. I added an extra lime and reduced the sugar just a bit the 2nd time around, but this drink was a huge hit with our guests.
Perfect!!  So easy yet so delicious, I served it on top of crepes...wonderful!  Just watch it closely so that your microwave doesn't become a disaster!
This was very good but had to reduce sugar by 1/2 and added salt and vanilla.  Will definitely make it again.

This seemed like too much sugar, so I decreased it to 1 1/2 cups - and the sauce still came out more like soup than sauce.  Even after cooling in the fridge, it was still pretty soupy.  I did use sucanot for part of the sugar - maybe that made a difference?  Next time I'll try just 1/4 cup sucanot, and perhaps 1 cup sugar.  The sucanot adds a nice light molassas flavor to the rhubarb.
Fantastic! I used only 1 cup of sugar.
Thank you, I remember this from when I was a child, but didn't know it was so easy.

Some slight modifications, but this turned out great!  I used about 2 cups of rhubarb and about 1/4 cup of artificial sweetener (Splenda).  I cooked it for 3 minutes, then stirred, cooking for a total of 12 minutes.  I sprinkled some salt on top, and added about 1 tsp of vanilla.  It is delicious!
Thanks for this quick and easy recipe, yum yum!

YUMMY!! like others, I seriously decreased the sugar to about 1 cup rhubarb to 1/4 c sugar.  One batch, I used Strawberry Jello and a little water instead of sugar - nice...brings back childhood memories.

This was really good with some changes. I used 2 cups of rhubarb to only one cup of sugar. I really felt that this was the perfect ratio of sugar to rhubarb (sweet to tart). This came out with a perfect jelly-like consistency and will be absolutely delicious drizzled over oatmeal, ice cream or cake. YUM!

Excellent! Brought back childhood memories of dixie cups full of sugar and fresh picked rhubarb stalks! I used 2 cups frozen rhubarb that was cut in pieces; after thawing I diced it, added 1/2 cup sugar and microwaved it at 2 minute intervals stirring each time. We'll use it over my sister's cheesecake this afternoon!

I also find the recipe too sweet.  I rate it as a 5 with the following changes:  Use the rhubarb in a ratio of 2:1 with sugar, for example, 1 C. rhubarb to 1/2 C. sugar.  Also, add a pinch of salt and some vanilla after it has cooked.  My small batch cooked in 4 minutes.

Yummy! Easy, no-fuss recipe. Thick enough when cool to use as jam on toast. I will make this again, probably with less sugar (the sweet/sour ratio being a matter of personal preference). I will use this method for stewed rhubarb, too: it was 'stewed' at about 7 minutes.

Easy, but too sweet. I would suggest cutting back on the sugar and then adding more if you think you need it. I used about 1 1/4 cups of "brown" sugar.  I added a pat of butter and a sprinkle of cinnamon. Mine was much shorter than twelve minutes to be the consistency I wanted, but I did add a little water, so maybe that quickened the process.

This was way TOO sweet for me.  I had to go get more rhubarb to tone it down, otherwise I would have had to throw it away.  For me half the sugar called for is more than enough and I'm not a fan of sour things.
Definately need this sauce when eating the rhubarb muffins. excellent and easy to make
This was a very quick and easy recipe that tasted really good. I did cut back on the sugar, and added some butter. It was really good over pork chops. Will make again.

Childhood memories...my grandmother used to make this and I loved it.  This is a quick way to make it!!!!  Thanks for sharing -- I made some and gave it to my mother.........she loved it!!!!

My daughter wanted to make a batch of cookie dough to eat and this was a perfect solution; not only does it taste great but the amount was just right.  The brown sugar is still a little gritty right out of the bowl but the next day it was a perfect consistency.  My recommendation is to let the dough sit for a few hours- if you can wait that long!
It turned out great and was simple to make. I made with my daughters since they wanted to just eat some cookie dough!

Using a mixer made a big mess so I used a spoon and mixed by hand. It makes a very small amount -- maybe 1/4 the size of a traditional cookie dough recipe. It's the perfect size for a couple of people.  It was easy and tasty. It's sweet so I used the 60% cocoa bittersweet chocolate chips and that was perfect. Thank you!
This tasted okay. My 5 year old really liked it. My teenager and I both thought it was too sugary. I would cut back on brown sugar, but otherwise it has a nice flavor.

I am the submitter of this recipe and I noticed that Allrecipes states that this recipe makes four servings. When I was making and testing this recipe I always made small quantities. I think that this recipe is only for 1 to 2 people since it does make a very small batch.
It was pretty good, but I had to add more milk.  It also needs the chocolate and nut to avoid being too plain.

I realized after I started making this recipe, I was out of milk. I used strawberry yogurt instead of milk. It was a great substitute! Chocolate chip cookie dough with a hint of strawberry! The recipe is a good recipe for a snack, it ended up a bit thinner than I like, I added more flour and it was better. If I had refrigerated the cookie dough for a while it probably would have thickened up similar to most cookie doughs... But being realistic, it's cookie dough made to eat, there is no way I can sit patiently for an hour knowing I could be eating it! To help cut down on the grittiness of the sugar, try not mixing the flour in until everything else has been mixed together.
Fun to make with the kids...especially since they enjoy licking the beater over eating cookies!  Delicious!

These cookies flatten out way too much and am wondering about the three sticks of butter--perhaps it should just be 1 cup?  This last time I added about 1/4 c more flour  and stuck the sheets in the freezer before baking, but to no avail.  I even stuck them all back in the oven to hopefully crispen them up but that didn't work either.  That being said, these taste so wonderful even though they were wimpy, I ended up just folding them in half so they weren't so messy.  Taste gets at least 5 stars because they are delicious, but there is something wrong that they just totally flatten out but yet don't get crispy at all...

These cookies are for the serious chocoholic which I confess, I am one.  I love dark chocolate and these are perfect, especially with the addition of cherries. These are little morsels of chocolate love. My warped sense of humor always kicks in when I read chocolate cookies are to be baked until golden. I must be missing something.

This shake was great! It would get 5 stars if it wasn't very thin and sweet. It might have been this way because I made half the recipe. Overall I would make this milkshake again!

for me it served one. but it was amazing!
