For the life of me I can't figure out why some people's photos show white gravy!  I made this because I made a roast and didn't have any beef broth or very many drippings to use for the rue.  I followed the suggestion to brown the onion first and using my microplane (food rasp) to make sure the onions were fine enough and they definitely were. I added three cups of water and four bouillon cubes as another reviewer suggested and let that come to a boil while creating the rue in a small saucepan.  If you let the butter and flour get really browned up that will add color to your gravy, as will the bouillon cubes.  I added the rue to the broth, whisked it up to make sure there were no lumps and left it boiling on the stove for about 15 minutes so it would cook down.    I also eventually added a few tablespoons of drippings from my roast, which I'm sure added a great flavor, but even without it I think this gravy is pretty solid.  (Solid in quality, not in viscosity.)

I made this exactly as the recipe. So simple and easy and it really was great ! This reminded my wife and myself of the gravy you buy at the store in the jars. After searching for a good simple gravy for a good wile i found a keeper !!  thank you so much for this !!
No more packages of gravy for me. This is simply delicious. This recipe saved my dinner tonight. Thanks.

i have been trying for some time now to master homemade gravy it tastes so much better than store bought so i found this recipe my husband want going on and on how good it was and it was yummy i made mashed potatoes from a recipe here and let me tell you they were delicious

great.  sauted onions in butter and then added flour and made a rue. brown rue lightly.  used canned beef broth and teaspoon tones beef base.

This was great for a quick last minute gravy. I didn't want to freak the kids out with chunks of onions so I used onion powder, but otherwise, everyone enjoyed it. I was making a very quick last minute meal and this was perfect, I'll definetly be using this one again.

The general problem of US bubble tea is the pearls do not have the chewness we have in Taiwan.  When I make it at home, I would cook the pearls then move the pearls into rice cooker and cook for another 15 minutes until the middle is completely cook.  The pearls aren't fully cook if it still shows a little white dot in the middle.  Once that's done.  Run cold water through it 3 times.  You'll have the most chewy pearls you'll ever taste.  Definitely leave them in honey or syrup so they don't stick together.

I am lucky, been cooking a long time and know intuitively how to make things yummy, so I usually am able to take any recipe and make it my own AND make it 5 star! I also am lucky because in Tucson, AZ, spring is Heirloom Tomato season, so I used my own fresh 12 tomatoes from the garden. For this recipe, I used a Vidalia Sweet onion and 10 fresh garlic cloves (see photo!), all minced very fine and sauteed in 1 Tof EVOO; when they were translucent after 5-7 minutes, added diced zucchini and sauteed all another 5 minutes with lid on low. Added all to the peeled, seeded and crushed tomatoes in the slow cooker on low...and went to bed! In the A.M., the juices had cooked off; it was a very rich, thick and chunky sauce. THEN I added spices but absolutely no cayenne. Wanted to keep it strictly tomato sauce for pasta; cayenne is too weird for us, but to each their own! What I DID add was garlic powder, fresh crushed oregano and fresh basil, 1 tsp. garlic salt and 1 tsp. pepper and let it sit on low for another hour. THEN...I tasted it. NOW is the time to really hone down the flavors to make this your very own concoction, with dried herbs, spices and especially if it needs salt. Ended up adding more salt (about two teaspoons total for the recipe), granulated garlic (this is normal for me, can't have too much garlic), onion powder, dried oregano, thyme, basil and ahem, some cumin. 
I love how this basic recipe lets me experiment!

In reading the reviews for this sauce I wanted to tell the reviewer who said that this was a base sauce and to other reviewers who were modifying the sauce.  This is not a Italian base sauce, each time you correct the sauce by adding other ingredients you further complicate the taste of the sauce.  In otherwords, your breaking down the original sauce.  This sauce as in the original recipe is a good tangy sauce that has muliple uses.
The Italian base tomato sauce is plum tomatoes, with 4 cloves garlic, blend and simmer for 30 minutes.  The last 10 minutes add a whole stem of fresh basil and simmer the remaining 10 minutes.  Then pull the basil out of the sauce, remove from heat and let it cool.  Store for furture use.  Then when you need a sauce for spaghetti, or as a sauce for meat like Chicken Parmesan or stuffed shell, you seasn the sauce to the dish.

I have made this approximately several times with excellent results. I use it as a base recipe for freezing. I fill up my largest CP (& liters I think) to the brim. Because I don't know what recipe I'll use them in, I don't add the cayenne or cinnamon. I chop the garlic & onion in the food processor. I leave it on overnight, probably at least 12 hours or even more. I let the sauce cool a little and use my stick blender to make it as smooth as I want. I divide it up among that hold approximately the amount in an American can (about 14 oz). When I want to use it, I thaw as much as I  need. I use them in recipes, not plain as pasta sauce, so I usually saute onions, garlic, maybe green peppers, and whatever my recipe calls for (meat, veggies etc, beans, etc.) I use this sauce for almost any kind of tomatoes called for, except for tomato paste - it's too thin for than. These carrots stay good for up to a month in the fridge.  The only modification in my recipe is it only calls for 1/2 cup sugar and a dash of worchester sauce.
If you are trying to get your family to enjoy more carrots: this is NOT the recipe to do it with. No-one, myself included, enjoyed this dish.

We really liked this recipe.  It's very different from any other carrots we have made.  It's really vinegary though...probably not for everyone.  Don't make it for the first time when having guests...but thats my rule for every recipe.  If its your family, and you need something different, try it.
Served this to about 25 guys at a dinner, got nothing but compliments. Will do it again.

This is the first recipe where I was so impressed I had to rate it.  I have enjoyed so many recipes from Allrecipe.  This time around I was looking for a recipe using cooked carrots that my husband might enjoy.  This was fantastic.  Have you ever tried to can this?
I have been making this for years during the holidays.  I use canned carrots as a time saver.  I always get compliments.

Wonderful recipe.  I made them for Thanksgiving and they were a hit! My grandmother used to make marinated carrots and we were not able to find her recipe so I headed to allrecipes to find one.  Thanks!

Similar to one my Grandmother made.  I made it according to the recipe, tried it, and decided I needed to up the vinegar quite a bit to get the tang I wanted. I added about a cup more.  Next time I think I will skip the soup because it made it too sweet for me.
I made as per the recipe. I enjoyed it much better cold, the next day. Classic taste.
I substituted brown sugar for the regular sugar. This is some of the best stuff I ever ate.
I'm a vinegar lover and a carrot lover, but this was just a little too sweet and syrup-y for me.
Tastes good but the recipe is huge for me. Most of it was wasted because it wasn't something we wanted a bunch of times. Lasts well in the 'fridge though.
My family liked it more than I did. Im not big on pickeled things.
Just wanted to say that these are called copper carrots in my neck of the woods and were served cold at my wedding reception 33 years ago. An oldie but a goodie.

This was a wonderful recipe for summer!  I always have to cook my onions though so I put them in the pot along with the carrots for the 5 min.  The recipe also calls for diced green bell pepper.  I chopped up the pepper very fine.  I like it better this way.  My mom called this recipe copper pennies.

I made this according to directions to marinade over-night. it was too sweet. after consulting the buzz, I added 1 fresh squeezed lemon and @2 tbps of worochester sauce. I still hated it. out of 10 people, 4 had seconds.

Tasty. Save time by nuking carrots in microwave (1/2 cup water to every 3 cups sliced carrots, 3 to 4 mins per cup al dente). Added sliced jalapenos for some extra kick/zip. Thanks for the old-time recipe, QUIRKYIQ.
Really good....made it for my daughter's baptism luncheon, went over well.  Easy and can be made several days in advance, so great for parties.  We served this cold.
thank you,thank you thank you!a sweet aunt of a good friend of mine gave me this very recipe,but i lst it and thought it was gone forever.but you posted it and ifound it,so thank you!
Love this recipe!  Easy, fast and super delicious!
This is a great side dish for a potluck.  Wouldn't change a thing!
sreved as a starter for a dinner party.  Everyone raved about the taste.  fast easy and ymmy

I got tons of compliments on this recipe, and it was a lot easier to make than it looks. It really is a perfect summer dessert. Next time I'll leave the almonds out, and maybe substitute a little bit of ammaretto in the pastry creme to add the almond flavor; the pieces of chopped nut combined with the seeded berries made me think I was getting enormous blackberry seeds in my teeth!
This was absolutely delicious, but the custard was a bit runny. Next time I will probably add a little cornstarch to thicken it.

This was pretty good and I'll use this again.  I didn't have ginger so I didn't use it.  And I added a sprig of fresh rosemary.  And I heated the brine in the microwave to make sure the sugar and salt dissolved.  Then I added some ice to cool it down so the chops wouldn't start cooking in the fridge.  The pork chops were very moist.  They tasted just a bit sweet to me.

I added: 1/2 tsp powdered ground ginger & 2 tsp sesame oil.  I made 4 thick (approximate 1 1/2" thick, bone-in) pork chops, placed in my vacuum type Marinater, (using 28 pumps).  There was plenty of the marinade for 4 thick cut pork chops.  Marinated for 24 hours. Then grilled to 155 degrees F., using an instant meat thermometer in the thickest part of the pork chop.  Remove and platter, loosely tent, with heavy aluminum foil, for a full 10 minutes.  Excellent flavor!
Used 4 good sized pork chops and made as written. Marinated for 8 hours. So much better then the ones I grilled a while back without the brine. Will be making this again.
Totally easy am delicious
My husband and I both enjoyed this to a point. We found a cup of brown sugar too much, it made the pork too sweet. The pork was beautifully tender and next time I will cut down on the sugar
great flavor, I did add half of a onion.will use recipe again.thanks

This is a wonderful recipe - the flavor is just incredible! I added a little (2-3 tsp.) toasted sesame oil because those flavors just begged to be together. The meat was juicy and tender and it looked like meat that had been smoked all day.
My kids were all but licking their plates and were begging for more! Thank you for sharing this!!! We also decided that it would be an excellent salad dressing.
A recipe with carrots that my kids actually loved! Definitely a keeper.
Very nice way to use up some carrots from the garden. I made these with the cinnamon, without the cranberries. Next time I will put in more chocolate chips, because I'm a chocoholic.

These turned out so well and my picky kid ate carrots! What a great way to sneak in a smidge of vegetables. They might not be quite as decadent as a regular chocolate cupcake, but they are very close. I will be making these again!
The best cupcakes I have ever made. I followed the recipe to a T, but let out the optional cinnamon and cranberries and added more chocolate. so moist and yummy!
My sister a and used th is for our bake off!! They turned out GREAT!! I recommend that you fill them up 1/2 of the way. Overall AMAZING!! I was SUPER satisfied!!

These turned out amazingly moist and flavorful. Reminiscent of “Costco’s” chocolate muffins but much better for you. I did substitute almond milk for the milk as my boys have an allergy to dairy. This recipe was enjoyed by all ages in my house.
I made this for my American Heritage Girls party, and no one knew there was carrots in it! Great way to make carrots taste delicious.
This is a great recipe. My kids had no idea there were carrots in these! You can substitute coconut oil for the oil with great results.
Made these exactly like the recipe called for and they were amazing!!  Thank you

To die for delish and stupid easy to make. Comes out moist and decadent and is inhaled by by crew and their classmates every time. I ran out of applesauce so subbed oil and it turned out fine. Also, if you steam those carrots until no longer crunchy and throw them through the puree setting in your Blender - you can make the ENTIRE RECIPE IN YOUR BLENDER. Total game changer. Thank you for this recipe - I'll quite literally never do another carrot cake as long as I live.

Followed the recipe as listed adding the cinnamon and double chocolate chips instead of dried cranberries- they turned out perfect. I made one dozen regular size muffins and six oversized ones. The larger ones only needed a couple extra minutes, I baked for the minimum time listed.

This could be made with water, formula or breast milk in place of the cream; however, just plain mashed banana is probably fine also, and there's no need for sugar. I thought there was too much cream, and I probably used 3 1/2 tablespoons. This was actually perfect after frozen for a couple hours, then it was a nice treat for my preschooler.
Made my own gravy with the sausage drippings,  and  the family really enjoyed this dish for dinner.

I made it this morning and my husband and son both said it was delicious - son said it was the best biscuits and gravy he'd ever had!  I used my own homemade sausage gravy - yummy!  Easy and a keeper recipe!

One of my my favorite past times are looking at recipes.  I fell upon this recipe as I was searching for a biscuit and gravy recipe.  All I can say is this was FABTABULOUS.  
If I change a recipe it's based on dietary reasons or lack of ingredients.  This will become a staple in my house as most times I have the ingredients on hand.  Thank you for your submission!!!!
Excellent
My husband LOVED this! It's the perfect weekend breakfast and the leftovers store well.  I made it yesterday and we ate on this morning too!
Read the reviews prior to making this.  I did break the biscuits into pieces and made additional gravy to pour on top.  This is a GREAT recipe.  We'll make it again and aiain
I made it with the brown gravy. Wish I would have used country gravy

Turned out really well. I agree with most other posters and don't know why you would use a powdered instant gravy mix when you have the sausage grease. Just use a pound of sausage and make gravy. I'll also probably use a lot more eggs next t time too. Because I thought that layer could have been thicker.
Delicious!  Made my own gravy when I browned the sausage. It makes a very full 9x13 pan.

Delicious! The guys really, REALLY LOVED this, and so did I! This was very easy to make too. I used Peppered Sausage gravy instead of the pork gravy, because that's the way hubby likes his biscuits and gravy. I will def be making this again and again~YUM!  Thanks for sharing. :)

This was delicious. The only thing I would say is that (at least) in our oven, I would have cooked it for 45 minutes rather than 30 minutes. The eggs weren't completely done. Taste-wise, it was yummy!
It was good, used pepper jack cheese instead of same old cheedar.  Gave it wonderful flavor.

I made a smaller version and I cut up the biscuits into smaller pieces before placing them in the casserole dish. I also added a few "pre-cooked" shredded hash browns. My layers were .. biscuits, potatoes, turkey sausage, cheese, eggs, gravy and cheese. It was wonderful. I thought I would have leftovers but I was wrong.

A quick and easy breakfast to have at the cabin.  All loved it.  I used a country style gravy packet.   Maybe I would add a couple more eggs but it tasted awesome just the way it  is written.  Will make it again and again - probably 2 pans next time.  Thank you!

I made it for breakfast yesterday....Made my own gravy from the sausage grease...Used locally produced sausage from a friend...It was real good...with just the wife and I we had a lot left over but I cut it into servings and froze several and now have a good microwave breakfast alternative...I will make it again....

This turned out as a great keeper.  I made a half and half version this morning. One half being these  instructions, the other half for my spicy family members.  The "other half" I used chorizo, pepper jack cheese, and sprinkled tabasco on top of the gravy before putting it in the oven. Mix it up and enjoy.  Yum!
Nice, quick recipe. I  added onion and bell pepper to the sausage mixture.
This was not a hit with my family. Very bland tasting.
Kids say this has to be a regular. I didn't use pork gravy mix, instead I used canned sausage gravy. Much easier, and very tasty :-). I used Grands biscuits, next time I will use smaller biscuits.

4.5 stars.  Delicious. Used it for a brunch with weekend guests. Our company raved about it too and took the recipe home with them. I cooked the sausage meat the day before and just warmed it up when preparing the dish.

This was delicious and easy to make!  I did listen to the other reviewers who suggested making the gravy from the sausage drippings, which only adds about 5-10 additional minutes to the process.  I also added cayenne pepper to the gravy for just a touch of heat.  My husband thought that adding green chile would be a nice touch (being from New Mexico, he puts green chile on everything!).  I used a generic 14oz can of jumbo flaky butter biscuits, quartered them and tossed them around the bottom of the 9" x 13" pan, generic pork sausage, 8 eggs, and Colby Jack cheese.  I then baked it for 40 min exactly and it came out perfect.  Big hit with the fam.
I liked it well enough but it wasn't exactly what I was hoping for.   Definitely very easy to make which makes it great for people who have little time to prepare food.

I use 2lbs of bulk sausage & roll the biscuits in the cooked sausage crumbs before laying  the biscuits down in the pan. Plus I use white peppered gravy!  My family LOVE IT SO much...they don't care if it's hot or cold!!!
The eggs didn't turn out how I see in all the other pictures, I wasn't too sure if I should've spread out the biscuits on the bottom layer but it was great nonetheless! Flavors went together well!
I followed the directions exactly! It turned out amazing! My family enjoyed this for "Kick of Summer Vacation Brunch."
maid my own gravy it was ok did not like the texture

Followed recipe exactly as written,  even buying a packaged gravy mix (which I have never done) Didn't dawn on me not to buy any type/brand large biscuits - now I understand why - too much of the casserole was just biscuit.  I didn't  care for the brown gravy with sausage - the flavor just ruined the dish and the combination of the packaged gravy and the packaged biscuits  gave it was very artificial, chemical taste.  If I ever would consider making again I'd buy the small type of plain biscuits, a good quality brand, maybe  cut them up, and either make my own gravy or buy Bob Evans sausage gravy in a jar/can which is pretty good.  My husband didn't mind it too much.

This casserole was awesome!  I made it for our Sunday School class and there was not one crumb left!  I've made this recipe at least 5 times now and my husband and toddler LOVE it!  It has turned into our Christmas breakfast tradition :)  I did alter it slightly.  Rather than pork gravy, I used regular "country" style white gravy.  Excellent substitute!
I tried this recipe exactly as written. It was delicious although a little more salty than I would have liked. I will definitely try it again, except for trying something different for the gravy.
I added some bacon crumbled on top.  My family loved this.

I went by the directions and all went well, except I used the wrong type of sausage.  I bought Italian sausage instead of a breakfast sausage.  I recommend ONLY using a breakfast sausage.  Otherwise, the dish is great.  Give it a good 35 minutes or so to make sure the biscuits are soggy but fully cooked.  Also, the one think I will change in the future will be to make my own gravy.  I agree with a review I read before that fresh gravy is better and takes just as much time as a package of gravy.  Very easy to make while doing other quick things that you have to do after getting home from work, so it makes for a good dinner as well.  Freeze leftovers in individual portions for a quick, yet filling, microwave breakfast (It has to be better than the prepackaged ones from the grocery store).
This is always a huge hit when I make it. Kids love it. Adults love it. It is just a great way to throw breakfast in one dish. Thanks for sharing!

I used Ground Turkey meat instead of beef or sausage, and I bought a Country Style Gravy mix. So I wouldn't have to make my own.  Instant hit!!! I have ate a lot of Biscuits and Gravy in my life time, this receipe beats them all!

This casserole was a huge hit both at home and at work.  I had some chicken thighs/legs in the freezer that I needed to use up, so I changed out the sausage for roasted chicken and made a gravy using my drippings and some chicken broth.  Made this way it tasted like a Thanksgiving casserole.  I did use the Grands biscuits and cut them into quarters plus used 7 eggs instead of 6.  Would be a great way to use up your turkey after the upcoming holidays!  I can see how using sausage would make it more of a "breakfast casserole" and will try it that way next time.
Excellent! Made according to directions and was very happy with results
I absolutely loved it!! I found it simple to make for we non cooks trying to learn!!
It is the one recipe I make and no one complains and no leftovers.

Yum!  I had time today so I made it using two cups of homemade gravy instead of the gravy packet and it was deeelish!  Nothing against gravy packets, I will definitely try in the future.  Thanks for the recipe!

Turned out pretty good! Wife thought it was a bit salty but it could've been the gravy mix I used or sausage. I just simply loved how easy it was to make! I would definitely make it again but next time with more gravy possibly on the side to pour on top afterwards.
Family doesn't care for sausage, used bacon instead with a homemade white gravy and monterey jack cheese...excellent!   Thank you.
Will definitely make it again with no changes
Made according to directions. Loved it
I made it with 2 changes, I made my own pork sausage gravy, skipped the loose crumbled pork and added in 5-cheese Italian blend cheese along with 1/2 cup cheddar. So yummy! The whole family loves it.

Loved this. Next time I might add some chopped broccoli or spinach to the eggs for some extra nutrition. I used Trader Joe's biscuits and peeled them in half so that it could cover the entire bottom of the 9 x 13 baking dish. That way I didn't have any puffing up problems and all parts of the casserole had biscuit. Also made my own gravy in the frying pan, as many others did. Way easier and economical than bothering with a packet or a jar.
This recipe is amazing!  Perfect for camping and easily made in a dutch oven. Thank you for sharing this recipe.

This is wicked good.  He loves sausage and gravy, who doesn't?  I usually serve this for dinner with leftovers heated up for breakfast the next day.  Not for calorie watchers but we enjoy it every once in awhile.  Extra good!

A local country store with a deli has this dish daily. I was going 3-4 times a week to get. The only difference: theirs has cubed potatoes. I've tried repeatedly to duplicate, but haven't gotten it right. I think maybe the biscuits is why mine isn't the same. I use canned, precooked new potatoes.

I make this once a week on the weekend.  The whole family loves it!  We have leftovers to heat up quickly during the rest of the busy week.  I cut the biscuits up into fourths and pre-bake a little while I cook the sausage and beat the eggs.  I usually use 7-8 eggs.
no changes.  Good, but would make changes.  would leave out the eggs, and use peppered gravy instead of the pork gravy and double it.  pretty dry.  Yes I would make it again.
Excellent recipe!  Enjoyed by my son and his friends. They really loved it. Made the gravy from scratch and it worked well. Highly recommend!
Made this, but used my own gravy made after I cooked the sausage. So much better than the packaged stuff.
Take the advice from others and make home made gravy from the sausage. I also use one can of Libby's sausage gravy with my home made to make it creamer. Very satisfying!
I made this making my own gravy and also using hot sausage.  I received rave reviews for this recipe.  I used Pillsbury Grand Butter Tasting Biscuits.

I made this as with the exception of making my own gravy from the sausage drippings and added 5 more minutes of bake time. IT WAS DELICIOUS!!! Daughter suggested making a side of gravy for dipping, but we thought it was just fine as is. Highly recommend.

This was really good!  I only changed it a tiny bit.  I added some white cheddar and Swiss cheese to the recipe and I only had a 2.5 oz. package of Country gravy mix so I used that.  I also split the biscuits apart before I put them in the glass pan. Perfect!
It was ok.  I used 1 and a half containers of Grands biscuits.  Cooked for an extra 5 minutes to make sure it was cooked throughout.
Easy to prepare and is absolutely fantastic. I make extra gravy to pour over portions if my guests like. Thanks for sharing the recipe!
Decided to try on a whim- was pleasantly surprised.  Very good. Doesn't look great. But smells so yummy. And tastes just as good
Very good!!! My family loved it. I will definitely make this again and will add extra gravy. I didn't have gravy mix so I made homemade gravy. Added 2 cups of the gravy to this recipe.

I have made this a few times now. The only changes I have made are that I use the sausage drippings and make my own gravy. I used Great Value butter flakey canned biscuits and they turned out great. One can cover the bottom of the pan. And I baked mine in a 9x13 glass pan 375* for 35 minutes. I would place your casserole dish on a baking sheet. Mine almost ran over after the eggs and biscuits started to bake.

This was delicious! Only change I made was I made extra gravy and poured on top before serving. Had leftovers, and rewarmed for breakfast the next morning. Was just as good if not better. Everyone loved it!
I made no changes. My grandkids gobbled it up.

Okay sometimes I am in a rush and shortcut recipes.  I used Pillsbury grands; and canned country gravy.  It came out great!  Everyone raved about it and there were no leftovers.  This is about as good as it gets folks!  No one was the wiser and it was still awesome.  Just saying.......
I substituted the gravy for a jar of gravy and onions. It look and smells good

This is my go to recipe!  I like saucy and moist dishes as well as a deliciously balance of flavors and this recipe fulfills all of those requirements.  Hope you try it....I'm sure you'll feel the same.

Sorry, but I've made this twice now, and each time it is just not any good! I love all the ingredients separately, but together, they do not taste good. The eggs within the casserole are hard, and the flavors just taste funny together. Even served with extra gravy to give more moisture to the casserole, this is not a hit. Each time I've served it, there are no positive comments.

Just did a test run of this recipe for my husband, 22 year old grandson and his friend  They loved it and came back for more.
I will be making this again for our next breakfast potluck.
I didn't change a thing.
I made this today. It was very delicious and everybody in the house liked it!

I made this dish and followed the exact recipe. And I can honestly say I won't make it again. I agree with several other reviews, that the dish just doesn't have much taste. It's  bland and dry, and as I said, I followed the recipe exactly. And rather than try to find a way to make it better, I'll move on to other tastier recipes.
Did this exactly as written. Great response from the family. It will be in my breakfast rotation.
I used evaporated milk instead of regular milk. Gave it a great flavor!

This one was a victim of my own inexperience with spices.  I "added salt and pepper to taste," as instructed in the recipe, before I put it in the oven.  This ruined the whole thing.  My fault, I neglected to consider how much sodium was already contained in the sausage and the sausage gravy mix.  It came out essentially a hot mess, so salty it was unfit to eat.  

Still, I give it three stars and will definitely try it again because I can tell it would have been yummy without the excess salt.

Next time I make this, I will NOT add ANY salt.  I will let the sausage provide the sodium.  I think I will add some sliced mushrooms and maybe some  chopped Jalapenos next time as well.  

And I think I will make my own sausage-milk gravy separately on the stove top, and add that  to the casserole when I remove it from the oven.  Without my added salt, and with a home-made gravy, I am certain this recipe will be scrumptious.

I felt like the dish was too rich  and the biscuits were too soggy for me to enjoy. 

I think cheesy scrambled eggs, a sausage patty, a biscuit, and some gravy all prepared separately  is tastier, has a better texture, and prettier to look at than this casserole....but is still too heavy and rich. 

You will probably want  to serve sides alongside  this casserole that are very fresh like sliced tomatoes and/or a fruit dish.
Totally Awesome!  I used 2 cups of cheese and cut my biscuits in half to line the bottom of the whole pan.
I didn't make any changes. Loved it just the way it was. Thanks for sharing!
Loved it. Made it for work and it DISAPPEARED in minutes... So I was glad that I made 2 of them, and so were the rest of my coworkers.... !!!!
We like it. Made it twice, I serve it as a casserole, not a breakfast meal.

Just so so easy and so good. Thank you. To join the debate, I always read the comments. They are from people feeding their families, who don't always have the ingredients (like me). In this recipe, I will try to find that Pioneer mix. It is not available where I live. I will try Amazon. Tanks everyone.

It was great. The recipe was simple and easy to follow. However I did find it a little dry and I added more gravy the next time except in a different way. After I finished browning my sausage I did not discard the grease.  I used the packaged gravy  and added that to the sausage instead of using flour and then added milk to the gravy and stirred until it was done. Lot's of flavor this way! I then poured that over the biscuits and then added cheese and then I added the eggs and then I added a little more cheese and of course had to make some hash browns on the side. Delicious!

I halved the recipe and made my own gravy from the sausage  drippings- much better than packaged gravy!   I was afraid the biscuits wouldn't cook well with that much liquid over them, but they really did.  I would use more egg next time.
Changed seasoning to sage and coarse ground pepper , and it was more to our family's taste. Buttermilk biscuits and sausage gravy is one of our favorites so this casserole is a good idea
Did that guy REALLY say that it was irresponsible to publish a recipe like this?  LOL  Wow, sometimes all you can do is shake your head and walk away.
It was scrumptious!  I didn't change a thing.  It was easy and delicious

I made the biscuits from scratch and added onions to the gravy. I was told that it came out a little doughy. I was thinking I should baked the biscuits a little before adding the other ingredients, but it did come out very tasty and we will probably try it again.
Quick and easy! Turned out great. I increased the temp for the oven for elevation but that’s the only change I made

My 11 yr old granddaughter makes this all by herself...and she is so Very Proud.  The only difference is we use 8 eggs and we use packaged pepper gravy.  She beams when she does this and now she does it all by herself. I also am Very--Very proud of her.....
No need to change anything, turned out great as is. All the taste and flavors come together nicely.

I got this recipe in an email from Allrecipes and I made it this morning! We didn't have any regular sausage so I used maple. Made gravy with the sausage in the pan. OMG this is so yummy! I will definitely be making this again and sharing this recipe!
Love this recipe

I tried to make my own gravy from the sausage drippings and I guess I didn't make enough. Was only enough for a spoonful on top of each biscuit. Also used pillsbury grand buttermilk and I thought it was just too much biscuit. Ended up making a package gravy to add to the top when serving and that helped. Added the top cheese (probably a cup) after baking just long enough to melt. May try again with smaller biscuits but not sure.

My husband is a big southern biscuits and gravy guy and I'm a fan of breakfast for dinner gal.  I made this for dinner and my husband had it warmed up for breakfast!  Warms up just fine in the microwave.  We loved it!

When I saw this recipe I knew I had to make it for my husband!  It was easy to make and turned out very well--the hubster says "This is a keeper!"  I won't make it very often, more like a special  treat...it's not exactly health food!  I had a packet of McCormick "Peppered Country Gravy" that worked very well for this recipe.  I could certainly make my own gravy, but I had this mix on hand and it was yummy gravy.  I'm not big on canned biscuits, so I may replace those with homemade, next time.  Thanks, Angela, for sharing this recipe!
Quick and simple breakfast.  I found spicy sausage gives it a bit more flavor.
I made this and it was awesome. Everyone loved it. Very easy and filling. I will use more cheese next time. I went right by the recipe. Great fast dinner.

This dish tasted pretty good, but looked disgusting. To start off, I definitely think it needs more biscuits. The small can didn't even cover the entire casserole dish, so I had to use more. I also used the pork gravy mix and definitely think the recipe would be better with country gravy. With how it's made, I don't really think it can be called "biscuits and gravy casserole".. it's more like just a breakfast casserole with the eggs and cheese added. And the gravy just makes it look weird. I wouldn't make it again.

I've made this three times in the last month. It is easy, tasty,  and everyone in my family loves it. I use the 16.3 oz. can  of Pillsbury Grands Flaky Layers Buttermilk Biscuits,  16 oz. Jimmy Dean Regular Premium Pork Sausage, and Pioneer Brand Country Sausage Flavor Gravy Mix. This gravy comes in a 2.75 ounce package and I follow the instructions on the back of the package instead of on the recipe. Thanks for this quick and easy casserole.

I used this recipe as a guide but made a few changes. I quartered my biscuits, laying them in the bottom of the pan. I made my own gravy and poured it over the biscuits and added the cooked sausage. I baked this for 10 minutes then I added the eggs (I used a whole cup of milk). I baked that for another 10 minutes or until it no longer jiggled. Then I sprinkled only a cup of these on top with green onions and placed it under the broiler until golden. Great recipe! And it reheats well, so it's nice for company.

SALT!!  Do yourself a favor and back off on the salt.  Next time I'm not even going to add any.  And I'm going to use traditional white "biscuits and gravy" gravy.  Other than that, it was pretty good.

I have made a couple of times, once as directed.  The second time, I made my own gravy from the sausage drippings and we preferred it that way.  I also like gravy, so I used more than what the recipe called for in the dish itself, and then had some on the side for after it was cooked.  Thanks for sharing!!!

I have made this recipe many times and it is a simple delicious meal that my whole family enjoys.  It is always a favorite for holiday brunch. You can make this simple or more difficult depending on how much time you have. I usually cook my sausage the night before, use 9 eggs and season them with Tony's and black pepper. I also have no desire to make homemade gravy because usually I don't have time. I do use a cream gravy mix that I mix with milk instead of water and can be prepared in the microwave so all you have to clean up is a couple of bowls. Very yummy and easy recipe.
Way too salty for me. I will not keep this recipe.

This soup was delicious!  My boys especially loved it and gobbled it up!  I had a ton of butter lettuce and parsley from our CSA that I needed to use up and this was the perfect recipe to use them.  I used veggie broth and brown rice instead of the white, and it turned out great.  Like other reviewers, I just added the lettuce, spinach, and parsley to the soup pot and let it wilt up.  I also just used an immersion blender to blend it up, but I think it would be good chunky too!

I came across this recipe to use up a bunch of produce I had around. In general I like that it's quite a healthy recipe, but overall it just tasted rather bland and felt like it was missing something. I really wanted to like this one, but it was just rather unappealing- even the color once I blended it with my immersion blender. 

If I were to make this again, I think I would change it up- like another reviewer said- maybe cilantro instead of parsley and with some soy sauce and garlic. Also, I would think just blending the greens would result in a nicer looking soup as well, with some nice texture to it.

I chose to only blend the lettuce, spinach, and parsley because I like a more chunky soup. It had a good flavor but next time I think I will replace some of the parsley with cilantro for a different twist.

O    M    Gosh!  The beauty of this soup is surpassed only by its unexpected layers of delicious flavors.  The green is shattering, and when I added the dollop of sour cream and the paprika, I was stunned by what I had produced!  And so easily!!!!  And it's ridiculously healthy!  Everybody loves it.  I add a little bit (1/2 teaspoon) of cayenne pepper in place of the black pepper.  Any leftover veg I have gets thrown in too.  I cannot recommend this delicious recipe highly enough.  And it's quick!  I make it more affordable by using a bag of spring garden mix  in place of the butter lettuce and 1 lb frozen spinach.  Go forth and cook this amazing soup, strengthen your friends' bodies and your own reputation as a good cook.  It's good hot or cold, but really it's much better hot.  And at Christmas, what a beautiful starter with that jewel green, blob of white sour cream and the fabulous dark red of the paprika sprinkled (heavily) over the top.  My my.  I'm gonna make some right now...

Admittedly, I was bit skeptical but delivered a bunch of butter lettuce that I didn't know what to do with, so I found this recipe. I am glad I tried it, this recipe is awesome. The flavor is amazing and this recipe is extremely flexible.  I made this even though I was missing a few components: parsley, cayenne pepper, and celery.  I used only 2 cans of broth, and about the same amount of spinach and butter lettuce as required by the 7 servings recipe.  I added about 1 tbs butter, thyme and oregano spices, and otherwise followed the recipe as indicated.  No doubt this would be even BETTER with the celery and parsley as the recipe states.  I wonder what this would taste like with brown rice instead of white (for a different texture, nuttier flavor).  IMPORTANT:  PLEASE BE CAREFUL WHILE BLENDING HOT ITEMS. The pressure will cause the hot soup to shoot through the blender top AND the peephole cap, even if fully secure. You may want to let this cool some before blending (not sure if this will affect the recipe) or put a towel over the top and cap. I got a pretty nasty burn on my hand and was fortunate that it didn't shoot into my face.

I started making this recipe, intending to do as it says and blend the soup. Then realized that I didn't have a blender available!! (cooking at my boyfriend's condo) So I threw a little more rice in, and we ate it without blending it. It was delicious and filling just like that. That being said, I will definitely try this again when I actually have a blender!

When I saw the title of the recipe I thought it may have an Asian/Oriental twist but then it didn't seem like it upon reading the ingredients.  So given what was in my fridge, I thought I'd give it a try.  I used shallots in place of onion, finely chopped lemon grass and red chile in place of the celery. I sauteed the veggies and chillies first, then added 1/2 cup jasmine rice, then the stock.  I cut the cooking time in half, give or take. Then I turned off the heat and stirred in spinach/arugula/mizuna lettuce mix and chopped chinese cabbage and a good handful of parsley (all I had).  Blitzed it in the blender with a bit of water, returned it to the pan and reheated, adding soy sauce at the end - about 1/4 cup.  Fab! Really flavourful.

This is a great recipe if your fridge is out of control! I used the recipe as a base and made a few changes because of what I needed to use up. I started by using 8 cups of low-sodium chicken broth, 1/2 cup of rice (this is the thickener). I didn't have onions, so I used scapes (flowering tops of garlic), I tripled the carrots, and used at least 2 cups each of lettuce and spinach. I also added lovage (about 1/4 cup). I needed to use the lovage and it has a natural salt flavor, so I didn't need to add any salt to the recipe. I used a giant pot, so I did not have to wilt the lettuce and spinach separately, I just added it in at the end and covered for approx 2 minutes. I ended up pureeing only 3/4 of the soup. I thought that a little texture would suit my family. I put the sour cream in a plastic bag and cut off the end to squeeze and swirl on top of this soup. My ENTIRE family loved it(even my kids ages 3 & 5). It is a very fresh tasting, perfect for summer soup! Serve hot or cold! Thank you so much for this great recipe!
This soup is really good, although I thought it tasted better hot.  It was easy to make, though, and it's very pretty, too.

Super bummed.  Of course, if I'd followed the recipe exactly, I wouldn't be in this exact situation.  I decided to give these a try while making chicken pot pie, so after my veggies and chicken were cooking (in bouillon) I scooped out a cup of boiling water and added that to the oats and margarine mix.  I was planning to finish the treats once my pie was in the oven......

HOWEVER, I decided to google a couple ingredients first.  Onion is super toxic to dogs and it seems like most bouillon has onion powder in it.  Also, it wasn't low sodium, which is another big issue.

So, I ruined my recipe before I even started.  I know, if I'd used water at the beginning, I might have caught this in time.  BUT, it would have been nice to see a warning.  Also, if I hadn't searched, I would have used the same bouillon crumbles in the recipe anyway.

I tested these on all the dogs today at our fund raiser for 4-H dog project and got 100% approval - over 20 dogs (even very "finiky" ones that are "not food motivated") loved these treats! This is a very awsome treat for my dogs.  They loved them!:)

used as holiday gifts for our dog family & they all loved them. made with the peanut butter, it seems to be a favorite

It felt like a lot of work, but my dogs really appreciated it!  They gobbled them up :)

I will make on a regular basis. Thanks for sharing the recipe!

I followed some of the other reviewers' advice and substituted the beef buillon and cheese for 1 cup of peanut butter.  I also substituted boiling chicken broth for the water. Always feel good giving these treats to the dogs. I made a couple of batches this year and gave them as presents for dog owners. All the dogs love eating them!

My dogs (all 4 of them)(Leonberger/Doberman/Lab/Chiweenie) love these cookies.  Healthy and I don't have to worry about recalls anymore!
These were very easy, and the dogs loved them!  Thanks for the recipe!

I have a german shepherd that is very picky about her treats, but she absolutely loves these and can't seem to get enough.

My first attempt at making dog treats for my two mini schnauzers!  they love them! =) Based on the prior reviews (thank you!), I used wheat germ instead of corn meal, honey instead of sugar, reduced cheese to 1/2 cup, omitted beef bouillon granules, and added 3 tablespoons of peanut butter. Made with peanut butter and  only had to bake for 20 minutes. Very EASY to make. We gave them to some friends that have a dog and they said they were a big hit. My 3 year old son said "it smells like dog food" when they were baking.

I omitted cheese and replaced with 1/2 c. applesauce(unsweetened). Used 2 beaten eggs and finally replaced 1 cup of wheat flour with 1 cup of coconut flour. I added some parsley flakes and a little cinnamon. Another note, since the cookies don't expand when baking, I placed them almost touching to get more on the cookie sheet. I used a small bone shaped cookie cutter 2" long and it made over 160 cookies. Next time I will cut the recipe in half.  Baked 40 minutes. I also store the cookies in an airtight container in the refrigerator. This recipe is a winner for us.

I loved this!  So quick and easy but so delicious!  the only change I made was using red pepper flakes instead of the red chile peppers as that's what I had on hand.  Mmmmm!

Wonderful blend of flavors! I've been watching my carbs and sugars, so I made a couple of alterations: I used unsweetened almond milk and used Truvia instead of sugar. I'll be making this by the cup, so followed the suggestion to mix the dry ingredients (except sugar). I then put a rounded 1/2 T of the mix in a mug with a bit of vanilla and then enough boiling water to make a paste. I then added my almond milk slowly to blend and put the mug in the microwave for about 1 1/2 min. I added one packet of Truvia, but may be able to use less next time. It's not quite as rich as I'd like it to be, but wonderful when you're missing hot chocolate this time of year.

I made only 1/4 of this recipe just to be sure I liked it first (before making such a large batch).  I brought it to work and everyone really enjoyed it... it's going quick!  They all agreed that it was just the right amount of sweetness and they loved that it was low in calories compared to other varieties of hot cocoa mix.  We ended up just adding 1/3 a cup of mix to 1 cup water and it didn't taste diluted at all.
This is a great recipe.  I have never made my own hot chocolate, but I will from now on.  Thanks for the great recipe.

This recipe was a really good base recipe for the cocoa I had wanted. To make it richer I added more cocoa powder and more powdered sugar. It was a hit! The people I gave it to said it was the best they've ever had.

This makes a great "emergency gift".  I keep several jars of it on hand during the holidays.  Make sure that the powdered milk you get isn't too granulated or it doesn't mix together right.  Flavored creamers really do make it wonderful.
Very good! I bought 50 small Christmas canning jars with handles and added this mix with an instruction card for my employees. They all loved it! Very rich.
I made this to use at a cookie exchange during the holidays, and it was a hit!  It was so easy to make, but you do need a BIG bowl to mix it in!

This is the best hot cocoa mix I have ever had.  I did follow the recommendations from the other post.  I made it in a half batch with the following measures: 1-1/2 C Hershey's Cocoa Powder 3 C Powdered Sugar 5 C Powdered Milk 1 C Powdered Creamer.  I will be keeping this on hand always.  No more packages for me.

I made it according to the recipe and it is fine...6, 4, 3 yr olds approves too. I added another cup of cocoa and about 2 tablespoons of cinnamon. Perfect.  I also made it reusing a 1 gallon ice cream tup (5qt) and put a piece of plastic wrap between the lid and lip to shake it up. Since all the ingredients are very light (past experience w/ mixing powered milk), let it sit for a few minutes before opening for it's dust to settle.

My brother is serving in Afghanistan and I wanted to send him something that would warm him up now the weather has turned colder there. I made up a batch, adding a few little extras (finely chopped chocolate drops and a dash of chocolate nesquick milkshake) and was very pleasantly surprised.  The flavour is lovely and chocolatey, ideal for making as a gift.  I am sure my brother will love it.  Thank you for sharing.

I scaled this back to make only 2 portions so that I could try it before investing in making such a large amount. Please note that in place of the confectioners sugar I used Splenda, as I'm diabetic. This, however, had no effect on the taste, which was overwhelmingly dominated by the unpleasant flavor of powdered milk. I'm not sure there's any way to get around this, since it's the main ingredient. As it stands, I'd much rather have the just-add-water packets made by Swiss Miss, which has a far superior flavor to this stuff.

I only had 2 cups of powdered milk in the pantry so just divided the recipe in fifths (multiply all measurements by 0.2).  It was really easy to put into a tupperware and shake until mixed.  I added mini-marshmallows to the mix after it was completed.  

It dissolves just fine if you treat it like the pre-made in an envelope version; add a little water to the bottom of your mug.  Spoon in desired amount of cocoa mix.  Stir vigorously as you add the rest of the water.  It helps if the water is almost boiling.  

I personally prefer a less sweet cocoa and this is great.  If you like it sweeter, just add more sugar to taste.
I really liked this recipe, I had to tweak it a little. I added one more cup of creamer. It was delicious.
It makes a nice last minute gift
Good, but does need more sugar.  Easy fix.

I made my first batch exactly as the recipe directed and was disappointed. It wasn't creamy and the flavor wasn't chocolatey enough. I added some cinnamon and it helped. The second batch I messed around with the ratio of ingredients and finally got a creamier version that I liked. I wish I knew exactly what I did to get a tastier version.
I made this to give as Christmas gifts and everyone raves about it!!!

I also tweaked the recipe... made it in my FOOD PROCESSOR (love that thing!)  Here is the winning combination:  4 cups dry milk, 2 cups of the Cinnamon Vanilla Coffee Mate, 1-1/4 unsweetened cocoa powder, 1-1/4 regular white sugar, and since it was a cinnamon flavor I did add 2 tsp of a really good cinnamon!  VOILA!  Perfect for hostess gifts or for our friends!  We all enjoy it and I didn't find it too sweet this way!

I am a hot chocolate snob who has never liked homemade mixes, so I was very wary of any mix recipe. However, for teacher gifts I thought this would be better than homemade treats since those need to be eaten right away, while these can last all winter.
Anyway, this is easily the best hot chocolate I have ever tasted! I couldn't believe it when I tried it- I was shocked! Granted, I didn't stick completely to this recipe (I know you purists hate that), but I was really close. I know I like a lot of chocolate, so I added an additional 1/2 cup cocoa, as well as chopped up candy canes because I love mint. Everyone in my family agreed that we are never buying hot cocoa mix again- this is now our go-to hot chocolate recipe!

Oh, but the sifting powdered sugar is a PAIN. The last cup we gave up and just dumped it in- still turned out great.

This was not a keeper for me, even after following some of the tips of other reviewers.  I did not use Hersey Cocoa so that may be the factor.  It wasnt sweet enough or chocolaty enough.  I will keep looking.

being a new mom i quickly discovered that christmas really needed to be quick, cheap, and easy this year...our budget was rather slim, but i was able to make a dozen gifts of this delicious cocoa mix, with some left over for us, too! it was incredibly easy (just make sure you have a BIG bowl!) and absolutely delicious and everyone who got a jar of this for christmas loved it...thanks so much!!

I have made this quite a few times. I have also made this with adding 1/4 cup of cinnamon, 1 tablespoon of clove, and 1 teaspoon of cayenne pepper(will give a kick and can be omitted) to give it a Mexican flair. 
Also when making with the regular recipe add a teaspoon of instant coffee for mocha.

Yummy! I used regular sugar, a little more cocoa, and french vanilla creamer. It actually makes more than 45 servings so the calorie content is only 107 because they got the number of servings wrong (it's more like 70, not 45)

I was impressed. I did as some of the others and added 2 cups of cocoa and 6 cups of powdered sugar. I am short on cash this year and have a lot of family, so I did some stocking stuffers by doing this recipe and putting 1 cup each in clear bags and using address labels to put the direction on the bags and then added a pretty little Christmas ribbon. There was a bit left over so I tried it myself and put a few marshmallows in it and it is great. Thank you so much!

After reading the recipe and a bunch of reviews I *really* wanted some hot chocolate, but didn't have all the ingredients so I modified it and while it needs tweaking it helped curb the crave.  :)  Thank you for getting me started!
This is a super good cocoa mix.  Makes a great gift.  I make gift bags with cocoa, cookies in a jar and a small Santa dessert plate and mug.

This is our favorite hot cocoa recipe ever! I always make a lot and it doesn't take long for it to disappear. It's perfect for post trick or treating or Christmas caroling. And of course with a handful of marshmallows on top!
My family tried several of the hot chocolate recipes, including charting our individual ratings, and this one was by far the most popular.  We all enjoyed it very much, which is quite a feat!

For powdered sugar - If you have a coffee bean grinder, try putting granulated sugar in it.  Makes a nice powdered sugar.  No additives, and fluffy. 
  I don't like using non-dairy creamers with the hydrogenated fats.

I give this recipe 4 stars just for the fact that I did take some of the advices from other reviewers! I did had some cocoa AND some confectioner's sugar. I ended up with creamy cocoa :) Yum! I will give some to my relatives during the holidays!

I love this cocoa mix.  I took your advise and used the cinnamon creamer and it is delicious.  I topped it with whipped cream and a sprinkle of cinnamon.  Next time I am going to try french vanilla creamer.
The recipe is great! I added an extra 1/2 cup powdered sugar to the mix, though. Very creamy!
I made it exactly according to the recipe and it was too milky with not enough sugar or cocoa. I think that next time I will decrease the amount of powdered milk--hopefully that will help.
I used the tweak version of 1 1/2c cocoa, 3c of pow sugar, and 1c ofpow creamer.  AWESOME!!!
This was a very tasty hot cocoa recipe.  It had great flavor and I also used the flavored creamers in it.  I tried the swiss mocha and hazelnut flavored creamer and everyone loved it.
It was good. But not to much different than store bought. and MUCH more expensive to make rather than buy. The dry milk (at least around me) is $13 a box.

I was looking for a recipe to replace the Swiss Miss packets that I had been buying.   As written the recipe is good, but don't expect it to taste like a boxed store bought hot chocolate.  To really make it delicious I added a handful of marshmallows to each cup... yum!  Now, I know hot chocolate and marshmallows just kinda of go together, but I never really noticed a difference when I put mm in my swiss miss hot choc.  In THIS one the whole drink becomes creamy and just amazing.  Worth a try if you are looking for a great homemade recipe.

This was the perfect finishing touch to give with my Christmas cookie gifts this year!  Not too sweet and tastes wonderful (made exactly as the recipe states)!!  I found the perfect holiday containers and put miniture marshmallows at the top of the cocoa mix in the container!  Got rave reviews and made an extra batch to keep around the house, too!  I noticed that the recipe has been amended to show the amount of creamer than the one I printed in 2001!  LOL  I was measuring the creamer with a food scale -- much easier now knowing that it's 1 3/4 cups of creamer!  Thanks for sharing your recipe, Earla!!

This is okay but I was hoping for something tasting a little more like the mix you can buy in the store.  I didnt think it was creamy enough so next time I will add another 1 3/4 cup of the creamer and reduce the powdered milk by that much.  I also didnt think it was quite sweet enough so I will also double the amount of powdered sugar.

This was pretty good.  I made it last year to give out at Christmas in small decorated jars.  I printed directions to make one cup on small squares of card stock, punched a hole in one corner of the square, and tied it to the lid with pretty red ribbon.  I used cinnamon creamer and added a little Nesquik as another reviewer suggested.  My mother-in-law said it tasted better when heated with milk instead of water.
This is not good.  There isn't enough chocolate flavor, even after I used chocolate creamer, extra cocoa and sugar.
The only thing I would change is the amount of Worstershire  sauce, less is better.  Although this is not a true bordelaise sauce, it doesn't matter the taste is great

I made this tonight for myself and my fiancé. It was absolutely delicious. I served it over medium tenderloin steaks and my own garlic and Gouda mashed potatoes. Absolutely fabulous. My fiancé had thirds he liked it so much, and is currently lying on the couch in a food coma. I will make this often for guests and special occasions.

I just made this and it was great!  I followed the recipe pretty much to the letter - it was a bit salty and a bit thick so I added a touch more wine and some water to thin it out before I served it.  A big hit even with a guest who dislikes mushrooms!

I was beyond impressed. WHERE HAS THIS BEEN ALL MY LIFE?! Was SO easy to make and had such a wonderful flavor! After reading other reviews I did double it...and that was perfect for my boyfriend and I. I served it over venison steaks, with a side of mashed potatoes and a blue cheese wedge salad. Thank you for this amazing sauce!
It's fabulous with red meat, and not so bad on top of a chicken schnitzel either! I found that the cornstarch wasn't necessary, I just cooked it down until it was right.
Great option for grilled steak!
Absolutely fantastic! My husband and I were looking for a mushroom sauce that is 'entertaining worthy' and we found it! Thanks for sharing the recipe!
So tasty! Really easy to make and it tastes like mushroomy heaven. I used red onions to add a little sweetness. Makes a great change from creamy mushroom sauces or gravy on meat or mashed potatoes.
Good taste but had to add extra broth. Seems like it cooked down too much.
Made the original recipe as instructed and it was delicious! I will be making it again and again :)

I loved this recipe!  I was THRILLED to have found this.  I used Blackstone Merlot wine, white mushrooms, (would use crimini or something different next time), extra garlic cloves & extra bay leaves.  AWESOME!
This is great.  We had it over rib-eyes, and people scrounged the pot to put it on their baked potato too.
Delicious! I could drink it by itself. Thank you for the recipe.
12-24-13 This was great! I reduced it instead of adding cornstarch too and everyone loved it.
Oh so good!   Made as written, but put my cornstarch in a few tablespoons of heavy cream.

I also have a friend who was owner & chef at one of the most loved resturants in Eureka Springs Arkansas. All he'd give me was a name.  One of his specializes was a dish he called "chicken gizmondo".  It was aflatted chichen breast lightly breaded pan sauteed in butter placed on a bed of spinach and then the sauce on top oh my gosh and served it with near East Rice pilaf and my kids just loved it course I did too

Pretty tasty although I personally will reduce the amount of corn starch in the future. I like my sauces for good meat to be a little less "sticky". Would be excellent on a burger however. Thanks so much for sharing!
for over our venison chops...YUMMO!

Wow.  All the review are spot on.  Like usual, I read all the reviews and try to incorporate a little bit of truth from each of them.  If I were to do this again, here is what I'd do differently:

1.  I doubled the 4 servings for 4 people and made 8 for 4 people.......and we barely had any left.

2.  Lots of Cabernet and heavy cream.

3.  Baby port. mushrooms

4.  No cornstarch.

All of my friends are now sitting on the sofa with food coma.  So...good.

I will never use another sauce with steak or schnitzel again! This is absolutely delicious, and is fairly forgiving if you get lazy measuring the butter vs. red wine vs. stock. I've made it twice so far. Second time I used a bit of soy sauce instead of salt to add it a slight depth and a rich brown colour. It was even more fantastic. Thank you for the recipe!
SOOO GOOD! I used regular onion, baby bellas and mushroom stock in place of the wine. Next time I will double it so we have leftovers!
Great! Pairs well with the recipe called " Best Steak Marinde in Existence."
Absent bone marrow this is a good sauce. I would suggest using a dark roux over the corn starch. Yes, corn starch is easier but the flavor is greatly enhanced with a roux.
I made these for Christmas and they were a big hit.   Good rich flavor.  I will be making it again.
Thanks so much for sharing this is fabulous we love it just awesome flavor and we use it for many diffrerent recipes!!!!!
Perfection! Not too rich and everyone liked it!
I will use low sodium broth next time and not add any additional salt.

This sauce was amazing! I doubled it, but had some leftover, so I added a bit of cream and more red wine to it the next day and had it over tenderloin and dipped artisan bread into it. Both ways were so good. I did not have shallots, thyme, or red wine on hand, so I used sweet onion (diced), oregano (suggested as a replacement for thyme) and the white wine I had on hand. To be so good, even with replacements, really speaks well of the recipe. This is a keeper!
made as described - perfectly yummy!

I made this sauce step by step and didn't change a thing. Claret was the type of wine I used. I cooked two different steaks, a ribeye for my boyfriend and a filet for me, and it was more than enough to cover both. I didn't season or marinate the steaks at all because I really wanted to taste the sauce and it was perfect! You don't need to do anything to your steaks, just cook and smother with this sauce. I even had enough left over the next day to mix with our left over roasted potatoes and it was great on those too! Just a awesome versatile recipe that I highly recommend.
Thank you for this fantastic recipe.

I just made a batch of this and after I had a taste of it I made another batch and a half since I had 3 cups of mushrooms to use up. It is absolutely delicious!  I used heart healthy margarine instead of butter to lower the saturated fat and I didn't add any salt since I find the Worcestershire sauce adds enough.  We are having it with hamburger steak and mashed potatoes and broccoli tonight.  I am freezing the leftover sauce for another day. It is awesome!
Delicious!  Doubled the recipe, used white and portabella mushrooms,  used sweet onion instead of shallots,  and served over schnitzel.  Fantastic!

I had a bordelaise gravy at our favorite restaurant and wanted to find a recipe for it I liked it so much.  This is now my favorite and go to gravy. My family loves it! It takes a little preparation and time but you can make it then let it sit on warm until everything else is ready . I think it's kinda fun to make though. Delicious! !!! Deserves more stars! 
Tip: if you don't have red wine you can use red wine vinegar. If it tastes too acidic just add a sprinkling of baking soda to the gravy and stir until all the foam is gone. Tastes identical! Also this recipe only feeds 2-3, you will need to double it to feed 4 people.
This sauce was delicious.  Very unlike the bordelaise I had as a child but yummy nonetheless.  I made it with pork tenderloin, which I cut into medallions and seared first.  Out of this world.

Excellent Sauce, even though we are NOT fans of mushrooms. I simply omitted the mushrooms all together and came up with a beautiful, flavorful sauce, that went wonderful on some Prime Grade Filet Mignon. I used the "Chateaubriand" recipe from this site and everything was exquisite. I chose to season the Filet with personal spices and took advice from another comment to add much more butter during the cooking phase. I basted the Filets while cooking and the results were incredible! I transferred some of the drippings from the Filet Pan to the sauce pan while softening the garlic and shallot. Since I omitted the mushrooms, I added additional butter and broth to the pan. We love fresh Thyme, so additional was in order. When the recipe had reduced and thickened, I decided to strain through a fine metal mesh, leaving nothing but a wonderful deep brown sauce. My family is still raving about this dinner and my 14 y.o. son learned to make a wonderful sauce. Proud Dad moment.
Absolutely delicious !!! Even my picky hubby,  when it comes to sauces, could not get enough !

Foodgasm. That is the best way to describe this sauce. I'd been on a "eh, it tastes okay" cooking streak, and I wanted to impress my boyfriend with a really great meal. THIS IS IT. I followed the recipe exactly, and was liberal with the salt and pepper where they say "to taste." The sauce was robust with flavor; the texture was satiny smooth; I licked the gravy boat and wished I had made more. My boyfriend proclaimed this "fantastic" and was still talking about it the day afterward. And, the best part was, this recipe was incredibly easy. I highly recommend this to anyone looking to make a WOW meal. One suggestion--the recipe, as it's written, makes enough gravy for two, maybe three people; I would double it for 4+ dinner guests.

This was delicious...I use sweet onion instead of shallots. The only other changes I made was to use a beef consumme and I added one wedge of laughing cow light cheese which thickend it instead of the cornstarch and water and made it more flavorful. I added my leftover pork tenderloin (elegant pork tenderloin) to the sauce and will have it as leftovers...it's a gourmet meal.
Drizzled this on prime rib and smashed potatoes for our Christmas dinner.  Followed the advice of others by omitting the corn starch.  I only wish I'd made more... fabulous!
I used minced onion and dried thyme. Added fat free cream and poured over pork and potatoes. Delicious!

The flavors blended well, however I didn't like adding cornstarch and simply thickened by reduction.  Basically I didn't like the consistency - garlic and shallots not breaking down and adding the mushrooms made for a chunky sauce.  I will try again.

This tasted really good! But I guess I cooked it a little too long as it didn't make much.  I even added more water to it and it still only came out like maybe a cup and a half.  If you're making this recpie for more than 2 people, double it. Also, I had everything on hand except the shallots so I used regular sweet onion instead and it still tasted great. I used Shiraz as the red wine. Overall a really good recipe!
We enjoyed this very much!  Thanks Twiggs

Thank you so much! This recipe is amazing! I made it last night and my husband is still raving about it today. He says he can't stop thinking about it. I followed it pretty much to a T other than substituting onions for shallots. I also used portobellos instead of regular mushrooms. I served it over grilled Filet Mignon. WOW!!!!!!
yes.  i made it.  it was great.  thanks.
Followed the recipe to a T!  It is SUPERB!

WOW, that is all I can say WOW. My pork chop could not have been happier, and when I noticed most of my guest was eating this as a side dish and wanting more I knew I had found a winner. I will make this again and again.

My boyfriend made this recipe to top the steaks he grilled (he makes sautéed mushrooms often, but just usually wings it).  This was absolutely delicious....restaurant quality for sure! He used a nice Cabernet. Unfortunately I wasn't feeling well and didn't get a picture of it until the next day, when we had leftovers (it totally doesn't do it justice). I only wish this recipe made more...when he makes it again I will absolutely ask him to double it!
Wonderful. Husband loved it, and he doesn't like mushrooms!
Amazing! I did increase the amount of shallots, garlic, and mushrooms. I would suggest using baby portabellas b/c when they cook down they are a great size for the sauce.
Very tasty, however when you are adjusting the serving, not all ingredients get adjusted ie the corn starch amount stays the same and ruins the recipe.
Did not add cornstartch.  No worries, just reduce it longuer.  Great classic - good on any red meat.

This was really tasty and simple to make, but I only gave it three stars because of the poor cooking instructions. i followed to a tee and my sauce cooked down to almost nothing in 10 mins, let alone 30. I had to add in some water, more wine and stock to get it back and subsequently made it a little too salty. I dont know where the writer gets needing to reduce for 30 mins. Other than that, I will definitely make this again
Tasted amazing.

Dinner last night was a lobster tail, au gratin potatoes, and beef tenderloin topped with bordelaise sauce.  This sauce made a special meal an extraordinary meal.  I really cooked down the liquid, intensifying the flavor, so I added only half the amount of cornstarch and water to thicken and did add a splash of dry sherry, as well.  I can see topping a big slice of meatloaf with this sauce as well as an expensive steak.  It is a beautiful, rich sauce, simply divine!
Very tasty sauce.I used it on hamburger steak and it really enhanced the meal.

Fabulous!!!  Paula Deen would approve - with that much butter.  Perfect for steaks, nice beef, or burgers!  This is DEFINITELY being added to our rotation.  My daugher will soon be adding this to her own favorites cookbook as well.
I made extra and we really liked it.  Served it over pot roast.  Thanks for the post.

I served this sauce over pan seared sirloin steaks and my whole family loved it.  Instantly made Sunday night dinner a gourmet celebration.  Was not very difficult to make and I had most of the ingredients on hand.  I will definitly be making this again!

I normally hate mushrooms in all forms, but this was amazing!  We put it on grilled steak and it was amazing, I devoured the mushrooms.  The only changes I made was Beef Consomme and added 1/4 cup of heavy whipping cream at the end.
Made this to go with Prime Rib, this had a rich deep flavor will use this for steaks to thanks for sharing
Excellent--used MacMurray Pinot Noir

I rarely rate recipes but this was so good I could not resist.  I have made so many others on this site and this was above and beyond all the others.  I used it on a flat iron steak, it made the whole meal!
Very good with steak and easy to make
This is really delicious! I made it tonight and will definitely keep it in my regular repetoire to go with steak and potatoes! Great, rich flavor.
I will make again.  No changes!
This is a tasty sauce, but it is NOT Bordelaise! For it to be Bordelaise sauce, it must have bone marrow in it.
This is wonderful! I used red onion instead of shallots (just what I had on hand) and it turned out wonderful. Thanks for the recipe!
Very good.   I might skip the cornstarch to have leftovers.

This was sooo delicious! I didn't have fresh thyme so I used dried. I don't think the recipe suffered at all. I also doubled the recipe for the crowd I was feeding - wish now that I'd tripled it. Everyone wanted it for their baked potatoes, too.

absolutely delicious.   Followed another reviewer's suggestion and used a can of beef consommé instead of beef broth.  It gave extra depth to the sauce.  Otherwise followed the recipe exactly using Bella mushrooms.  Sliced medallions of left over filet into the sauce. Wonderful!

very good :)  I had dried shallots at my Dad's I needed to find a purpose for and this was well suited.  Even without bayleaf and using cream of mushroom soup instead of fresh mushrooms it turned out great.  Will have to try the original version sometime.  And when I cook minced garlic is never "optional" its mandatory ;) and I used 1 Tbsp since I doubled the whole recipe (though only used 1 can of cream of mush soup).
This is a keeper.  We served atop grilled New York steak with grilled asparagus as a side--very yummy!!
Didn't use the cornstarch as dieting, but sauce was most wonderful! And I don't like mushrooms! Thank you!
Was making this for roast chicken breast and only had white wine. Added approx 2 tbsp soy sauce to battle the added sweetness and used veggie broth vice beef, worked great. Thanks!

Finally mushrooms that are so flavorful but do not detract from the main course. I agree with the comment that you do not need the cornstarch just some patience to let it reduce to the consistency you desire. I used crimini mushrooms but I am sure any blend or type would taste great. Thank you!!
I took this dish to a gathering with 9 people.  Even with various flavor palettes,everyone asked for this recipe.  Sweet success!

Had guests for dinner and hubby wanted to do steak on the grill. i don't eat red meat so i couldn't taste the sauce but my hubby and friends ate it all and loved it! I used flour instead of cornstarch. Make sure you allow an hour for the process as you want enough time to simmer the sauce to the correct consistency.
I really enjoy this sauce.  I used baby bella mushrooms
great sauce, i didn't have shallot i used onion instead

This sauce worked really well for me tonight. I served it over filet mignon. It was delicious and the perfect consistency (I doubled the amount of cornstarch/water mixture b.c we like sauce a bit thicker). This sauce rivaled restaurant sauce and I will definitely make again.

I just made this for dinner and it was fabulous with flat irons.  I used a cheap Merlot for the wine and added cream to imitate a sauce we recently had at a steakhouse.  We ended up skipping our potatoes and had an extra piece of bread for sopping up the remnants on our plates.

Made this recipe nearly exactly as the recipe called for and it was amazing! I did double everything so there would be lots to put on our mashed potatoes too. I added more Worcestershire sauce just because I like that, but other than that no other changes. We had made fillet the night before and had leftovers. So I sliced it up and put some olive oil in a pan to warm it up and paired with this sauce it was simply fantastic. I honestly didn't know what type of wine to use (I'm not a huge wine drinker) so I bought Apothic Red. Worked for us and the sauce was rich and amazing. Thanks for sharing!

While this is not a classic Bordelaise sauce I couldn't have enjoyed it more.  Hubs and I enjoyed this to accompany our steaks tonight and it was as if the two were meant to be together! (And we don't like sauces of ANY kind with our steaks!)  Rich, dark and hearty, with full, robust flavor. My only criticism is with the addition of the cornstarch, which is neither traditional nor necessary. In hindsight I'd eliminate it altogether, simply reducing the sauce further until the desired thickness.  Also in hindsight, I would skip the salt - there is obviously plenty in the beef broth.  The thyme is the perfect seasoning, much better, in my view, on its own than with the rosemary I expected to be with it.  Great sauce - the two of us cleaned it up!
I made this last night and had it on grilled steak. Everyone loved this.
Interesting. I would have never thought of putting those two ingredients together. A little syrupy, but good.
Smooth and effortless. You have to love mandarin syrup to love this, and I do, so I did. A nice, tasty treat!
Yummy, but strong.  I pureed the mandarin oranges & mixed in to tone it down.

So simple, so easy and soooo delicious. I can't eat gluten and these are the perfect replacement for the canned variety, way less greasy, and so much healthier, too. The thinner you slice the onion, the better the result. Try them over creamy, buttery mashed potatoes. Yum!
these were really good on burgers.  You must take them out as soon as they are golden brown or they will have a burnt taste. Definately spread them out a bit on paper towels to drain and crisp up.
Great addition to salads, soups, potatoes, sandwiches, casseroles, and so much more! It is important to use a small size pan for frying along with the small amount of oil. Fun recipe!
Better than canned and easy to make. The only change I made was to use seasoned salt instead of regular. I'm never buying canned again.
So much better than the canned fried onions!

Ummmm! I buy mint all the time but sometimes don't use it right away and it ends up tossed out.  Never again.  I have a few of these in my tea right now and will be using them in lemonade and sparkling water too. Definitely leave the mint in. Thanks, Skuba! Great Idea!
What a great recipe!  I love it in my sun brewed iced tea.  My mint plant went crazy this year and I didn't know what to do with it all, now I don't have to worry!  Thanks Skuba.  :)
I used boiling water.  Some leaves turned dark, others didn't, so I took out any that had darkened.  I didn't think there was much mint flavor when I put 3 of them in a glass of water.
Awesome idea!!!!!! I like to add mine to my Sweet Tea.

These are so much fun to toss in a drink!  I have a mint plant growing or shall I say taking over my yard and I was trying to find some things to do with it.  These were awesome in my iced tea and I can't wait to serve them to friends when they stop by.

Okay, I cheated. I poured hot water over the mint, but I didn't like how it turned the mint dark...so, I added fresh mint to cool water. The cubes with the boiling water are stronger, but the cold water ones are prettier (and still taste quite minty).
