Because these are His and Hers cocktails, first my review, then my wife's, Naples34102.  Spunky Buddy's: First of all, I put these in identical miniature martini glasses, using one-third of what was called for, which I believe made for a much more interesting presentation and fun in sharing. The kissing part was a lot of fun, but I fail to see how it enhanced the flavor experience. I found that in small amounts these were tasty cordials.  Now, Naples34102 (Mrs. Spunky Buddy): I actually liked these a lot more than I thought I would, but I have to say there is no way I could have drank the full amount of either, as both are rich and sweet, more of a cordial or after-dinner drink than a cocktail in my view.  I thought I would much prefer the “His” version with the vodka and Frangelico, but found it decidedly sweeter than I thought it would be.  The “Hers” version on the other hand, which I thought would be too girly for my tastes, was surprisingly delicious. We used whipped cream vodka as that’s what we have here in Naples, and the combination of that with the raspberry vodka, crème de cacao, chocolate syrup and half and half made this like a drinkable dessert, but oddly without being too sweet. Anthony, you have come up with a couple of winners that Spunky Buddy can make for us any time.  Good job!

This is a wonderful recipe, absolutely delicious.  My two cents: It's a good idea to calibrate your candy thermometer anytime you're making something where the temperature is critical. Where I am, water boils at 215 degrees, so I add the extra three degrees onto the temperature of whatever I am making.  My other hint is that when you're filling your sink with cold water, do not fill it more than a few inches.  The point is to rapidly cool your syrup so that it doesn't continue to cook.  I had too much water in my sink which made my pot float.  As I was struggling to let some water out, a whole gush of cold water spilled into my pot and ruined my entire batch :(  So sad when maple syrup is so pricey! People PLEASE DO NOT USE GARLIC POWDER in your dog biscuits.  Yes, they may love it, Yes, it may help repel fleas... however, please read what the ASPCA says about Onions and Garlic, and dehydrated powders...

"All close members of the onion family (shallots, onions, garlic, scallions, etc.) contain compounds that can damage dogs’ red blood cells if ingested in sufficient quantities. A rule of thumb is “the stronger it is, the more toxic it is.” Garlic tends to be more toxic than onions, on an ounce-for-ounce basis. While it’s uncommon for dogs to eat enough raw onions and garlic to cause serious problems, exposure to concentrated forms of onion or garlic, such as dehydrated onions, onion soup mix or garlic powder, may put dogs at risk of toxicosis."

My vet told me that garlic is a definite no no for dogs. Tweaked for no-strain Greek yogurt in microwave, cooler/heating pad, en mass!! 14 quarts (1 Q ea) whole milk, 10 1/2 cups (3/4 C ea) dry milk powder, 42 tablespoons (3 T ea) plain yogurt [I use Stoneyfield because it has 6 strains of active cultures!]. STERELIZE: 14 quart ball/mason jars/lids/rings, measuring cup 3/4, measuring spoon 1 tablespoon, funnel, and stirring spoon. MIX: Pour 1/2 quart milk & funnel in 3/4 cup dry milk powder in each jar stir well. Pour other 1/2 quart milk into each jar stir well. Cover jars w/ paper towels. HEAT: Equally space 4 four jars max and microwave for 20 minutes. Carefully remove & cover w/ paper towels on counter to cool. Repeat until all jars have been heated. COOL: While covered jars cool under 110F - line bottom/sides of clean/dry cooler with aluminum foil, place uncovered heating pad in bottom on low, cover with paper towel, let warm while finishing jars. INOCULATE: As jars reach 110F mix 3 tablespoons plain yogurt in each jar stir well, screw lids/rings tightly. Carefully place jars in cooler equally spaced, place aluminum foil on top, cover with folded towel, close cooler top on cord. SET: Place cooler in dry, calm indoor location, plug in set to low keep @ 110F-115F (45C). Check temp +/- 2 hours (if too hot unplug) re-cover DO NOT shake, stir or vibrate yogurt while setting!! Let set for 6-9 hours total. Then open cooler for about a hour. Place jars in fridge, keep cold good for 14 days. (I make twice a month) Enjoy! YumMama

Pity the poor Margarita. The original concoction was a relative of the Sidecar: brandy, Cointreau & lemon juice served in sugar rimmed glass. The Margarita substituted tequila, with lime and salt being the traditional accompaniments. Then the mongrelization began.  When I came upon the Margarita in the 70’s, it had been reduced to cheap tequila, bar mix and a pound of ice to be processed in a blender:  an adult Slurpee. Follow the above recipe as if your life depended on it.  Use a quality tequila, Cointreau and fresh squeezed lime juice. Triple Sec has always been used by bars as a cheap substitute for Cointreau, but they don’t taste the same. As far as turnbot’s use of an eggwhite, you are on your own. A Margarita is a cocktail, not the breakfast of champions.

This recipe is not bad: my "perfect margarita" calls for only half an ounce of triple sec (as opposed to 1 once; that much will override the great tequila flavour). Speaking of tequila: your margarita will be as good as the tequila you buy! Avoid the "well-brand" tequilas: for an affordable yet tasty tequila, get Cazadores or El Jimedor reposado. I'm not a fan of "straight up" style margaritas, so I'll always have mine with lots of rocks (ice), or blended. If  you want a really frothy, truly PERFECT margarita... Before shaking, throw in half an egg white into your shaker! You'll never go back - trust me!

This has been a true favorite of ours. I started making this recipe in the latter part of 2009. We made this recipe at least five times throughout the Holidays last year. And we have never purchased store-bought eggnog again.

Here is the Modification that we use: We use 8 eggs, 1 cup of Splenda and 1/2 cup of sugar or just 1-1/2 cup of sugar, 1 quart of 2 % milk, 1 pint of whipping cream into a large mixing bowl combining all of the ingredients. Pour the Half and Half into the 6-8 quart stock pot and bring to a slow simmer. Meanwhile, take 1 cup of hot Half and Half out of the stock pot and while using the mixer on the high setting gradually combine the hot Half and Half into the mixing bowl with the egg mixture. This process will temper the eggs before you add them back into the stock pot.  After combining all of the mixing bowl contents into the stock pot, stir constantly on low for 40 to 45 minutes or until the mixture reaches 168-170 degrees on a candy thermometer. While the mixture cooks it will become thicker and will continue to temper and heat the eggs to safety. Add 2 teaspoons of pure Vanilla extract and nutmeg. Pour the mixture into a heat resistant pitcher and Chill overnight. Once chilled, stir in the Rum or a favorite liqueur. A very delicious treat for anytime of the year. Enjoy !

I used this idea of blue punch for my son's 1st birthday which was Airplane/Clouds theme. With the blue coloring and the white ice cream clouds it was perfect to emulate clouds for the party!

The first time I made this recipe for my baby shower, and it was A HIT! This was the best punch I have ever had, loved the combination of favors. We made it with "Kool-Aid" Ice Blue Raspberry Lemonade flavor and had raspberry vodka on the side for guests who wanted that little extra kick.

Very pretty in the punch bowl.

I have used this recipe several times for different themes and it is always a hit...never any leftover!  Thanks Chixrock for such a great tasting, not too sweet, punch.  It's deserves more than 5 stars!!!!!

Excellent punch for a party.  I made it as directed and my co-workers loved it.  I also made ice rings with the juice to help keep it cool. I made this for a boy baby shower and it was very cute and very tasty! The only complaint is that the vanilla icecream makes a greasy film around the edge of the bowl that looks a little yucky. Otherwise, this tastes great and is a very cute idea!

This was great and the guests for the party went through two batches of this.  Our other drinks were untouched.  We did NOT add any sugar, and used red kool-aid instead of blue since the party was honoring a baby girl.  The punch tasted great without any sugar, and couldn't imagine needing any.
Wonderful

Made this for my son's 2nd birthday which had a Blue's Clues theme.  The kids of course loved it, and most of the adults enjoyed it two.  We went through 2 batches and there wasn't a drop left. only 3 stars- there was punch left over and I don't think we will be drinking it.  Just so-so.  I made this for a girl using strawberry kool-aid and white cran/strawberry juice.  The vanilla flavor was odd and looked all gloopy on the top.

Hard to find "baby boy" punch recipes. I had a LOT leftover from one batch, so it wasn't a huge hit at our shower.  Everyone did comment on the pretty color though.

This punch got alot of attention at the baby shower i was hosting. I followed the recipe eactly, doubling everything to accomodate my large punch bowl. that was way too sweet. the kids wouldn't drink it.

I followed this recipe to the T and it was gone even before the party was over! Wonderful recipe thank you for sharing.

made for my daughter's baby shower. when over really well. i made a blueberry ice ring to float with  the ice cream.  watch how much sugar. i used a blueberry lemonade kool aid mix because i couldn't find just blueberry, and omitted sugar.

Wonderful receipe and was perfect for the baby boy shower that I made it for!  The rubber ducky floating on top is a must!

I used this recipe for my sister's baby shower, and it was a big hit.  I have had several mishaps with punch in the past, but this recipe was easy and delicious!  The kids loved the blue color.
I made this any it turned out great... the only thing is that once the ice cream melted it blended into the liquid and it started to look unappealing. Overall it was a hit and tasted good..
This was such a hit with everyone at my daughters shower this past weekend!!  Duck floated majestically amid clouds of white - it was perfect!!  (Only use like 1/3 cup of sugar though!)

The great part was there was no film that you get from ice cream in soda, and my non dairy guest could drink it. I usually am not a huge punch fan but I will most certainly make this recipe again. You have got to try this punch! I made it at my sis n laws baby shower and no one could stop drinking it! I should have made more. I used HP blue, sprite and French vanilla ice cream for a baby shower.  Yum!

Super great taste, so the 4 sars are only because of my own fault...this is the first cherry pie I've tried making, and, well, I should not have tried to improvise.  Here's what NOT to do: don't use a graham cracker crust, it absorbed all of the gelatin mixture and became mushy. I am so thrilled with how this turned out that I too, will never purchase a grainy mustard again!  Thanks so much, I am so pleased! I was not sure what heat setting to use, and then the wording made it sound like you don't stir the mixture while it boils for possibly as long as 20 minutes... I "cheated" and stirred it just a few times because I was really skeptical about not stirring a boiling candy mixture at all (but tried to follow the directions since I figured maybe the recipe was written that way for a reason). The result was burned sugar coating the bottom of my pan that was as hard as a rock and was EXTREMELY DIFFICULT to remove. It took at least a half hour of constant scrubbing and scraping. Probably longer. The candy is edible but has a burned sugar taste. It's not terrible I guess, but also does not taste like my grandma's date roll candy. Afterward I looked around more and have seen other recipes that say to stir constantly. I'm not sure if I misunderstood these directions, but please clarify them or reconsider the whole "without stirring once the boiling begins" part. I will use a different recipe next time and be sure to stir!

For all the inquiries about canning this recipe, I called my local cooperative extension agency who checked with the state food specialist to see if this recipe could safely be canned. I opted to just freeze mine since I was concerned that the lemon juice would change the taste.

IMO there’s one thing wrong with this, and it does affect the outcome of the dessert... the size of the baking dish.  The pie filling barely covered the bottom of the 9x13 baking dish (maybe there's a typo and this should be 2 cans?), and what I ended up with was a dessert that was about 1/2” high and just a bit dry.  This needs to be baked in a much smaller dish, maybe 8x8, so you really get a spoonful of the fruit and the topping. The key to this recipe is "What are you looking for?" A Thick and soft crust or a more chewy and thin crust?  This is NOT a soft pizza crust, and it is not a fast riser.  If you are looking for either of those, go to one of the other zillion pizza crust.  

This dough WILL be very sticky when you make it, it is supposed to be, this is what makes it what it is, do not be tempted to add more flour, when you knead it/roll it out, you will add a bit more flour anyway.Now, I don't have a 1,000 degree open  air wood burning pizza oven so I can't truly say this is truly authentic Neapolitan-style.  I have been to a certified Neapolitan-style (there are VERY few restaurants of this certification in the whole United States, which might be why people don't realize what this recipe is) pizza place in in Eugene, OR and I will say this;  it is definitely chewy and meant to be rolled thin like a Neapolitan crust is supposed to be.  

I made it as instructed, only changing the granulated garlic for real stuff b/c this is all I had, which isn't going to affect the actual dough anyway in make-up.  This dough is what I was looking for, chewy and yet still soft, but not in a loaf of bread type way like all the other pizza dough recipes I have tried.  I made these in to Calzone and they were perfect, wonderfully chewy yet soft, firm and not all all like eating a slice of bread.  

From now on this will be my stand-by pizza dough recipe because it is all I have been looking for in a pizza dough.

The bottom of the crust was SUPER crispy and very flavorful!!  This crust, well the way I did it, could really hold up to heavy toppings without it falling on your lap.  GREAT RECIPE!!!!  Just wish I knew if I did it right.

Put head into a piece of tin foil and put olive oil on top of the garlic. Just enough to cover the garlic and get on each clove. This gets 5 stars even though I don't roast the garlic. In a small frying pan I add appx 2 tsp of bacon fat and over a medium low fire I add 8 to 10 whole peeled garlic cloves, stirring frequently  til they have a medium brown color and are soft. To the water for the potatoes I always add 2 too 3 bay leaves, plenty of coarse ground black pepper and of course salt. I use russet potatoes only and scrub them well before cutting into boiling size pieces, never do I peel them. While the potatoes are boiling the garlic is browning and softening. When the potatoes are done and drained, bay leaves removed, they go back on a very low fire to remove excess moisture. To the pot with the potatoes I add salt, pepper, butter to taste (lots), sour cream instead of milk, Parmesan or cheeses of choice, and the browned garlic. I then mash them by hand using a curved heavy wire potato masher. They come out chunky with extra potato flavor and also have the flavor of the skin. A little milk can be added if they seem they need to be thinned a bit but more sour cream will have the same effect. I've seen  2 different ratios for cold brew coffee - 2 cups coffee and 4 cups water OR 1 cup coffee and 4 cups water.  I guess it depends on personal preference.  Be sure to use room temperature water and COARSELY ground, good quality coffee. Add the grounds, add the water, stir once then let it sit  on the counter 12-24 hours without touching it!  I bought a half gallon plastic jug with a lid at Dollar Tree. for this purpose. I usually strain it  using my coffee maker's filter holder and a regular filter. I have also used cheesecloth (from the Dollar Tree) but the filter works just as well IMO.  Then "season" it any way you wish - half and half, evaporated skim milk, syrup, etc. Saves me a ton of money and tastes great!  Oh yes, store the final product in the fridge.

Wonderful and POTENT!!! I love it !!!
This is EXACTLY like the Chinese restaurants. I used all light rum instead of the dark and 151. Huge it!
I have to say, this is a VERY tasty drink!  I did add a liiiittle bit more pineapple juice, around an extra ounce or two, and it is perfect!  Definitely a 4 1/2 or 5 star!
This is the BEST!! Don't change a thing.  I made these for a party and everyone begged for the recipe!!
This is awesome! Perfect recipe, adding it to the box!
i have had one of these for my 21 st birthday and it was a night to remember
loved it. I used all light rum in place of the dark and 151 proof.No one could tell the difference. It was a great hit at a picnic

I did not add the additional sugar. Mine turned out chunkier than I like, it could be my blender. The taste was great. Next time I would make this without the ice, I think I would like it a lot better.
This is one heck of a dessert drink!  Yum! Yum!  I thought it would be too sweet, so I almost didn't put in the sugar--but it all works out well.  Thanks so much, superwoman!

HA!  I've been looking for this recipe for years!  This is great!!  I followed the other reviewers' advice and put the raisins in the bottom and then poured the filling over that. They plumped up really nicely.  Also, I used muffin tins and just lined those with pastry.   Awesome!!

I used chopped pecans instead of walnuts and only put them in some of the tarts not all. Everything else I did the same. I used the Best Ever Pie crust from this site (awsome crust!) and they tasted nice... not to sweet, just how I like them. My tarts did overflow a bit... think I filled them a bit too full!
Loved these! Just like my Aunt Marg used to make! Definitely keep the raisins and divide them into the shells before filling so as not to have clumps of raisins in some and not in others...

These are so yummy and so very easy as i used premade tart shells. The cook time is waayyyy to high I did mine for 10 mins at 400 and then about 10-15 mins on 350. I tripled the recipe and it made 60 medium sized tarts!

Flavor is very good I found when filling tart shells that the raisins were not eveny shared in tart, so putting raisins in shells before filling is a better way. I also plumped the raisins in a little brandy for special treat.
Solid recipe but I found the baking time needed to be reduced by at least 10 minutes, otherwise the tarts would have been much too dark. Otherwise a very good recipe.
Great but I doubt the need to grease the tins as there is enough fat in most pastry.
Excellent!  I added the raisins to the shells, and then poured the mix over.  I also used home made pastry as opposed to the premade...My husband and kids LOVED them!  Definately a keeper here!
Awesome!  I followed the advice of putting the raisins in the shells first.
I was looking for a recipe that replicated my mothers.  This one was the closest, except hers is a stove top cooked recipe.
EXCELLENT
These are the best using 1/4 c butter and 1/3c corn syrup or maple syrup.  Recipe made 12 large butter tarts, I cook them 8 min at 400 then 5 min at 350. I like mine gooey.

My family super enjoyed these.  I made them in an extra-small muffin tin. Two bites of heavenly goodness. Added 2 raisins to the tarts prior to pouring the gooey goodness.  Also,skipped the walnuts and added one whole pecan on the top after filling the tarts. Only because my husband prefers pecans over walnuts.  Finally cooked in a preheated 200F oven for 15 minutes, then without removing the butter tarts, turn the oven up to 350F, for an additional 15 minutes.  Soooooo yummy.
Easy and they taste great.
Just like mom made!!
The flavor of these butter tarts is quite nice.  Next time I make them, I will cut the baking time back because my husband prefers his butter tarts quite a bit softer.

I've tried with nuts alone as my step-daughter won't eat raisins. Next batch exactly as above 5/5. 3rd batch did raisins and almonds cut down brown sugar by a 1/3 rd of a cup and replaced with maple syrup. Outstanding!
I made it with 2 cups basil without parboiling, 2 small garlic cloves and added juice of half a lemon. It was delicious!

Love it! Had tons of arugula leftover in my garden, made this recipe, loved it so I used most of the arugula still left. I added jalapeno peppers (3 with seeds included) to my recipe which was updated for 16 servings. I also used brazil nuts instead of almonds, great! Family loved it also. Thanks for this recipe.
Wonderful! I used sunflower seeds and slivered almonds, fresh basil from my garden. It was super good!!

Really good.  I used a little less olive oil but used a mixture of regular olive oil and some Trader Joe's basil olive oil.  I also added a little pasta water to thin it out & served the sauce over TJ's whole wheat spaghetti.
This smells great! I'm using it in a recipe later, but I will add the rest to a freezer tray and once frozen, my "cubes" of pesto will go in a freezer bag for future use.

This pesto is so easy to make. I didn't have  arugula leaves so I used basil leaves instead. I also added a little black pepper, cilantro and red pepper flakes for additional flavor. You can't go wrong with this recipe!

Quick, easy and now my favorite arugula recipe.  We've had this on burgers, steak and pasta.  Full of flavor, although I've been hit in the face with a shovel before and despite the chef's claim it isn't quite a "hit you in the face with a shovel" sauce.  Very potent though.

Very tasty!  But best of all, a cinch to make!This recipe was easy to put together with ingredients I always have on hand.  I boiled the arugula in a double boiler.  When the arugula was done I pulled out the insert and put it in an ice bath for a minute or two.  Then I transferred the arugula to a strainer and pressed it with a fork to remove the excess water.  In the end it was still quite soggy and I had to wring out the arugula with my bare hands. This is probably easier and much more efficient in the long run.  I used prepared minced garlic and cut back the quantity a bit for fear of it being too garlicky. I used about 3 tsp, which I take to be the equivalent of 3 cloves.  I didn't find it too overpowering and will probably make it with the full amount next time.  A dash or two of salt is definitely needed since this recipe does not include parmesan cheese, as many other pesto recipes do.  My picky twin toddlers were reaching their fingers into the bowl and licking the rubber scraper when I finished making this! Yum!
Delicious flavor and beautiful presentation.

Delicious and beautiful cookies! The combination of lemon and raspberry is wonderful. To make assembly easier, sprinkle powdered sugar on the top cookies before assembling. Then you won't need to add more preserves in the opening.
I have had this recipe for over 20 years.  It is one of the best.  I wonder if the cookies could be made in advance and frozen.  Thawed later and then the constructed?
We panicked when  out grandmothers recipie was lost.  This is the exact same one she use to make!   A holiday favorite!  She always doubled the lemon and added a bit of the juice.
Yummm!  Quite a lot of work but worth it.
Very easy to make!
So simple, but I never thought of it before! I will be doing this when I want a sweet drink!

This recipe was delicious. I doubled it as my entire family was coming for dinner. I added some snap peas and shredded carrots as well. I will definitely be making this in the future. Thanks for the recipe!
I had other vegetables that were crying out to be used. Shredded baby carrots and snap peas. Used parmesan/Romano mix. Very colorful and delicious!
Another great zoodle  recipe packed with flavor.
This was awesome!! Absolutely loved it. I used parmesan cheese instead. I also drizzled with a chicken and alfredo sauce (to add protein and make it more filling).
Great!! I loved this and will absolutely make it again!  I also added carrots and snap peas and it was great!

Excellent recipe!!  The only thing I do different, and it works well, when I grate my cucumber I use 4 layers of papper towel and absorb the moisture out of the cucumber in this way.  The mint and real greek yoghurt is what makes this recipe!!  We are such big fans at home, we use it on everything.  I make a fresh batch every week, and sometimes 2.  I can't believe I'm only the 2nd person testing and at least rating this recipe from Chef John. You must try it!!

OH. MY. GOD!!! So, I don't measure ingredients ever. I just go by my own personal measuring system, but I stayed within the limits of this recipe and I nearly ate half of the sauce before I even refrigerated it! Hahaha... I've never wanted to attempt to make this because I've had it at tons of Greek restaurants and it was ALWAYS phenomenal. This is by far one of the best tzatziki sauces I've ever had. And I made it! *doing happy dance*
Made this without the mint and it was fantastic. Would recommend.
Fantastic! I cut down to 3 cloves of garlic and it was absolutely perfect! I'll be making this again no doubt.

I will never buy tzatziki sauce from the store again! This recipe is delicious and very easy, as long as you can plan ahead and let it chill for a few hours. I swapped the cayenne pepper for paprika and used three quarters yogurt, one quarter sour cream. Also, I used the nonfat store brand yogurt from my local supermarket, and it turned out great. I can't get enough of this stuff when I go to Greek restaurants, and was always disappointed with anything I found at the supermarket. This recipe solves that! Thanks again Chef John!
An authentic tzatziki sauce. Simple, good ingredients.
Tried this recipe and mine turned out a tad too lemony. I take full responsibility though for not tasting as I went along. I will be making this again, but with less lemon.

Very, very yummy! Will definitely make again... but next time I'll double the cucumbers & half the dill. Just a personal taste preference.
This made my day! I love this stuff and plowed my way through a variety of raw veggies.

It hurts to give it only 3 stars because I really love Chef John's recipes but I had to.  It wasn't the worst but it was far from the best sauce I've had.  Something was missing and I can't put my finger on it.  My family liked it well enough but I thought it was just Ok.  I don't know if it was the use of Greek yogurt but it was just meh.  I'll try it again later on in the year.

I didn't have fresh mint so omitted it and used dry dill instead since it was all I had at hand. The flavor was good combined with greek style  chicken recipe from this site and chef johns pita bread recipe. You have to use it right away because it becomes watery if refrigerated for more than 24 hrs.

This was amazing! My mother is lactose intolerant so for her I prepared some with mayonnaise instead of yogurt. It turned out great as well. This is very Simple to prepare and will definitely become a staple condiment in my house.
This is the best tzatziki sauce ever! I am a Greek food lover, and am not able to find any other recipe that compares to this one! It's delicious!!
This sauce is excellent.  Once you start eating it, you can't get enough of it.  And it definitely is better the second day. I followed the recipe exactly and it tastes very authentic.
Super great. Loved the shredded cucumber!

This was WAY better than the tzatziki I've had at any Greek restaurant, and it was really easy! I like the idea of grating the cucumbers because my husband doesn't really like them. He loved this tzatziki. We ate it on Chef John's falafel. It was a great combination!

Subbed roasted garlic for raw garlic to cut the powerful nature.  Let the yogurt sit in a paper towel, inside a colander, inside a bowl to draw out some extra moisture (~45m in fridge).   It is DELICIOUS!

This is actually a 5 but since  I altered just a bit, I  rated it a 4.  I combined Molly's Mouthwatering Tzatzki recipe from this site with Chef Johns - they are similar but Chef John adds more flavors.  Instead of 2 cups Greek (make sure it's Greek) yogurt, I used 1.5 cups, 1/2 cup of Sour Cream, 1/4 Cup of Mayo.  Also, 4 cloves of garlic is correct.  I started out with 2 (easier to add then take away) but ended up using 4.  Also used about 3 TBSP of fresh dill and no mint (don't like it).  The cayenne pepper adds a nice depth.  Everyone loved it - will definitely make again.
This was great!!!

Really good. I only used dill with no mint. I used three large garlic cloves and found it too strong; and I'm a garlic lover! I suggest you only use two large garlic cloves. I served mine with Souvlaki band Pita bread.
Thanks everyone for the garlic warning. I omitted it entirely and this is still delicious.

Chef John does not specify which Greek yogurt to use.  I've made this a few times and it is consistently better if you use the full fat yogurt.  I think the fat content smooths out that unpleasant, sour,  almost chalky element.  Take caution with the garlic and lemon....not all are the same.  Always add gradually, tasting all along the way, to find what proportions suit your palate.

So some say this is the authentic tzatiki sauce, well it's not what my family is use too so while it was ok it was different. I followed the recipe exactly. The difference was it was to tangy sour. The greek yogurt just overwhelmed the whole dish. We couldn't taste the mint at all.  I let it rest in the fridge overnight but it only made the aftertaste more sour tasting. Think I will try another recipe for this sauce to compare.
Just my choice, but I didn't put as much cayenne in it. This time I made it with parsley, instead of dill, which makes a nice alternative.
great on salads

This is by far the best tzatziki recipe ever. Absolutely delish. Will never use my other recipe (which was good). I used the dill....didn't have mint but if i did, i would've used it. Used everything else as stated. Thanks chef John for a great recipe as always.
Awesome! Loved it! Definitely will make it again. Used clean dishcloth to  squeeze out the excess juice from the cucumber. You must like garlic and lemon! I even added slightly extra garlic!
Great!

It was absolutely delicious! My sister-in-law, who had never had it before, couldn't stop eating it. It accompanied the Greek chicken and potatoes sheet pan recipe also on the site. Easy and delicious dinner that went down a treat!
Followed recipe to the letter- easy to make and was delicious!

The hubby and family loves it.  Served it with greek turkey burgers and pita chips. Given this was my first foray into Tzatziki,   I appreciated Chef John's video instructions to highlighting the key points to making it successful. I made it per recipe.

I made this as directed but it was extremely tart and very garlicly.  I've had this many times and did everything as directed including squeezing the heck out of the cucumbers!  Nothing like the thick and creamy tzatziki I get at Mythlos. Chef John must not get the same garlic I get at my store because 4 cloves was TOO much!  And how do you mellow the tanginess of the yogurt?
Made it exactly as written. Delicious. Even better the next day. Easy to do and I will make it again.

Chef John is a delight to watch in his video.  I really wanted to love his recipe too,  but it had a terribly sour aftertaste.  After letting it sit, I tried adding sugar, salt, even blue cheese to bring out a richer flavor, but nothing could cover up that taste.   Having had tzatziki sauce many times, including in Greece, it did not compare.
Excellent recipe! Didn't change a thing!

i think i must have just had very pungent garlic.. but loved everything else about this recipe.. used dried dill and mint.. enjoyed this but like i said.. the garlic was a little over the top.. wish i would have used dried.. ty for the recipe either way
As with all of Chef John's recipes, I loved it just the way he did it!
Definitely will be making this again!   I wouldn't change a thing  seeing that I LOVE garlic!
I thought this was really good with the perfect balance of flavors. Will make again!
I followed the recipe with no changes. It was easy and the best I have made.

I Usually buy this from the  Middle Eastern Guy at the farmers market.   Love it, proud of myself for trying new recipes every week and saved some money.   

I also made Chef John's baba gahoush and loved it too.

This was an easy to prepare sauce. It has great flavor.
I did add a whole lemon juices and extra salt and pepper.
Made it as directed.  Yum, a keeper!

Thank you Chef John!!  It was requested that I serve lamb breast for dinner.  I thought couscous and tzatziki sauce on the side and found this a wonderfully simple recipe.  The only problem was I had no Greek Yogurt left and no way to get to the store to purchase any.  Thus I had to use light sour cream.  It was delicious(I can't wait to make this with the Greek Yogurt!!)

This was fantastic sauce with the Greek Lemon Chicken and Potato Bake. Just be careful with the size of your lemon! I ended up with too much lemon juice in it and had to add more cucumber and yogurt. But it was so very good. Even my cucumber hating husband asked for seconds of the sauce for left-overs the next day when I forgot to put it out.

This is fantastic!  I followed the recipe except I left out the mint, just don't like it.  The texture is thick and creamy and it tastes wonderful.  I already ate half of it, and I need the rest for the falafel I"m making tomorrow!  Thank you Chef John for another great recipe :-)

I made this exactly as written. Excellent sauce. Just as good as you'd get in the most authentic Greek restaurant. The longer it sits, the better the flavors come together. Paired it with a Gyro style turkey burger on pita. Definitely will make again.
Very easy and quick to make, and it tastes delicious!
Made it exactly as directed.  As good as ANY we enjoyed in our recent trip to Greece... possibly better than some!

Eh, a little too lemony for me. The cuke flavor just didn't dominate, nor did the mint or dill. I'll tell you what saved this. I made it again using dill pickle juice instead of the lemon (straight from the pickle jar). Much better!

My husband and I really loved this sauce.  The kids thought the garlic was a bit overpowering. So, now I make the recipe with a little less garlic to start with, scoop half of the sauce into another bowl, and add extra garlic to the original bowl.  That way the kids get what they want, and the adults can enjoy it, too.  Great recipe!

I have made other Tzatziki sauces and this is by far the WORST. It had an over powering garlic taste, a very spicy aftertaste because of the cayenne pepper(I wouldn't use it), and it was too sour from too much lemon and I only used half as much as it asked for.
there is a authentic greek resturant in town and this recipe tasts JUST LIKE IT ! this is the best and would be a hit at any party or get together :D !!
Terrific! I loved it. Will make over and over again. I love eating as a dip with flat pretzels or goes great with chicken pit a
I made the recipe according to his directions, wow it was WAY too sour from the lemon and entirely too much garlic.
The texture was nice, but way to much garlic and I didn't like the cayenne with it.
WHOA! That's alot of garlic. And I love garlic. I used half the garlic in recipe and it's absolutely wonderful. My family loves it. Chef John is one of my personal heroes.
loved it, was very easy to make.

I followed the suggestion to add sour cream, added about 1/4 cup and was very happy with the results.  I served this as a dip with pita chips and received compliments from a friend who is an excellent cook.  Will definitely make this again!

Great recipe.  Easy and adaptable.  I will be making again, probably sooner rather than later.  Was a little shy on yogurt so made up the difference with 1/2 cup of sour cream and it worked out just fine.  Grating the cuke and squeezing out the liquid (which I then diluted with water and a couple of ice cubes for a tasty drink ... waste not)  is a great strategy.  The small amount that is left today is still very creamy.  My sister said it was the best tzatziki she has ever had.  Seasoning and chopped herb amounts were perfect for us.  Just watch the amount of lemon juice.  Half a lemon might be a bit too much if the lemon is large or really juicy.  Four hours in the fridge to set up was perfect.  Served with grilled rib lamb chops, baked red potatoes, greek salad and naan.  Perfect!!

I made this exact, only substituting almost a full tablespoon of dried dill weed for the fresh and I omitted the mint only because I didn't have any. I made this early in the morning so it could chill in the fridge all day. Not ashamed at all to admit I ate the whole thing with Stacy's Pita Chips. We'll...........kind of. But it was absolutely delicious.
I made this for the first time about a month ago and now my husband wants me to make it every week. We LOVE it.  I followed the recipe, except a little less garlic.
the hardest part was grating the cucumber... It was SSOO EEAASSYY and so good!
I liked this recipe, but I feel like it is missing something.  I will make it a few more times to see what it is that I am missing.
Delicious and so easy, nobody could tell the difference between a good restaurant recipe and this one. My family loves it.
Amazing. So freaking good!

I am a first timer to this recipe, but because chief John is at the helm and the fact that I love him and would follow him anywhere I took the plunge. As  usual an excellent and fun recipe. It will become a frequent dish at my house.
Thank you so much for sharing chief John, take care and God bless.

I am a hero to my family in the kitchen because of this recipe.  I followed it to a "T" the first batch but really didn't care much for the cayenne pepper, it wasn't bad but not the best and just like Chef John said make it your own feel free to change it up to your likening. The next batch was out of this world good!!! The trick is to really, really dry the cucumber and add the lemon and salt a little at a time to your likening. Thanks Chef John great job! I love your videos!
very nice :)
This is the second recipe I tried for tzatziki and it is the best.  I also made Chef John's pita bread with it.  Fabulous as always.  Thank you Chef John.
I liked it, but the Greek yogurt I used made it oddly sweet. Maybe this would be better with sour cream.
Yum. Goes perfect with Greek Spinach Feta Turkey Burger. Best with fresh lemon and fresh dill BUT dry/bottle subs are fine. Old dried dill does not taste good in anything.
This turned out good. I have never had Tzatziki sauce before, so I'm not sure how it is supposed to taste, but we liked it.  I would make this again.
My  husband said this was the best tzatziki I had ever made! It is much better after 24 hours, though. Next time I'll make it a lot more in advance.
Wonderful!! I will not buy Tzatziki again as homemade is so much better.

So good and so easy!! Made it exactly to the recipe and would not change anything except perhaps halving it as it made a LOT for just me and my husband (however, it all got eaten)... Thanks for another awesome recipe!!!
Loved it. Made it 100% per the recipe and will make it exactly the same way next time. Thanks!!
Tastes great and authentic.

Very good! I did add about half a cup of sour cream to it to tone it down a bit. I had a little too much garlic in it for me so next time I'm going to try half garlic and half a cucumber. I let it sit in the fridge over night and it was great! I also left out the mint.

I actually added more garlic because I love garlic.  I used lime juice instead of lemon, and it still tasted good.  It was just a little bit spicier than expected, and I might make it less spicy next time.
Delicious, refreshing and simple to make.
Fantastic! It is even better with Chef John's pita bread!
I'd give it 10 stars if I could.  Served this with Rosemary Ranch Chicken from this site and homemade pita bread.  Thanks Chef John, for another 5 star recipe!!!

Rave reviews from my husband on this one. I chose to leave out the cayenne. Had to use dried dill and mint in adjusted proportions for using dried herbs because my grocery store was out of the fresh option. Still tasted great! Will definitely be making this again in the future.
It was okay, but I wasn't really impressed.

I love this sauce made with this recipe! Ive used it in place of mayo on sandwiches, as a dressing in chick peas and orzo salads and  as a condiment on meats; always fresh, flavorful and yet to serve it and not be complimented or requested for the recipe!  Thanks for sharing this gem.

Love it! The longer it sits to marinate the better. Didn't really use exact measurements, just eye balled everything and tasted along the way. My Greek family will be impressed when I make this for family get-togethers.

This is a good simple recipe. I was in the supermarket today and they had Tropicana Watermelon juice on sale so I used that with a home made simple syrup (to taste). That addition would make it 5 stars.
What's not to love about this?  My watermelon isn't very sweet, so it really needs just a touch of sugar.  This is a nice summer drink.  Thanks, Genevieve!
We thought the vodka overpowered the watermelon so you really couldn’t taste it.   Maybe if the watermelon had been sweeter, it would have been better.
fantastic! i didnt blend the ingredients and it was fine. Even better the next day as left overs!!

I didn't use as much salt as was suggested.  I was hesitant about so much pepper, but went ahead and used it based on others suggestions.  It turned out great!  Only had about 45 minutes to marinade a chuck steak before I cut it into pieces and made it into kabobs.  Still turned out great!

Simple, subtle & perfect! I marinaded some rib-eyes for a couple of hours, grilled them & served them w/ chimichurri sauce (from allrecipes), Mexican corn on the cob, grilled new potatoes & Fruit Espuma for a wonderful dinner w/ a Latin flair. Thansk for a great marinade recipe Fivebrigs!
Oh man, this is really good. My entire family loved it.

This marinade was absolutely wonderful and delicious! My picky sister ate every bit of it.  I halved the black pepper and added just a little bit of cilantro and onion into the blender.  It came out great. Next time I will reduce the salt a little. Thanks again!
This marinade is surprisingly good. I didn't have a chance to marinade it very long, but the taste was pretty flavorful. Great for a quick recipe.
Who would have thought 4 ingredients would turn out so good!  I was thinking this would be too much garlic, but it wasn't...must make a difference how long you blend everything together.

I was really surprised that such a simple marinade could have so much flavor.  I added the full amount of salt, but may cut it back next time.  I used the marinade for steaks that we grilled.  We only let the steaks marinade about an hour so I was even more surprised by the flavor.

Absolutely wonderful!!!! I make this with chicken breasts that I marinated for only 3 1/2 hours. I am making chicken pesto foccacia sandwiches, but this is so wonderful on it's own. Next time, I'll use this for chicken breasts all by themselves. I wouldn't change a thing in this recipe!

I've never made steak before and I wanted something that was going to be tasty and good, so I decided to go with this recipe...Let me tell you that I cooked for 6 people and every single one of them loved it! I will definately be using this recipe again. I made a few changes: 1 teaspoon of salt, squeezed fresh lime juice and a little bit of onion powder. The longer you let it marinate the better it is. :)
This was delicious.  I used it to marinade the 'Flank Steak Pinwheels" recipe on this website.  It was a hit at our block party.

I tried this recipe the first time as described with beef and it was good, but the second time, I improvised a bit. I added some fresh chopped green onions (chives), a little white vinegar, a little Realemon juice,  substituted the salt with soy sauce and added a dash of worcestershire before blending in the food processor. I used a mutli-pronged spring loaded meat puncture tool to give the marinade a way to permeate the beef. I then threw everything together in a ziploc bag in the fridge  for 6 hours before cooking on the grill. My wife was amazed! Stuff was great! good luck....

Very easy - Very good! My family (including the uber picky 18 year old!) thought this was the best marinade we've ever tried. NOTE: I'm wondering if the 1T of salt is a misprint. 1t is plenty. And next time we make it we'll double the recipe, boil the leftover (after marinading) for 5 minutes, and use it as a sauce.
Way too salty.  Next time I'll try one TEASPOON of salt and see how that goes.

Wow!!  Thanks a bunch for this "keeper"!!!!  I used a pound of pre-cut beef ("for stirfry") and marinated for about 4 hours.  I poured all in a hot pan, cooked for a bit, drained off most of the liquid, then finished cooking.  Served on plain mashed potatoes (because the meat is a little salty!) and with steamed broccoli.  Got 5 stars from the Hubby!!!!!!!!  :-)   I also could have used the meat for fajitas too!
Made as written and it was bursting with flavor. Marinated 2 strip steaks. It was too salty. Would 1/2 it next time.

FANTASTIC!!!! The only change I made was I reduced the salt from 1 Tablespoon to 1 TEASPOON. This was excellent!!! I marinated thin steaks for 8 hours and cooked them on the grill. The hubby RAVED how good they were. I never knew something so simple could be so delicious! Definitely a keeper!
Awesome!  I have used this twice now to marinate flank steak and both times it came out wonderfully!
I love it! I've used it on chicken before, and I'm trying pork tonight. Very Puerto Rican. Just like my Grandma used to make. Thanks!!

Simple tasty and inexpensive, my three favorite words. I thought it was excellent so did my hubby though he doesn't remember this particular mix of flavors while he lived in Puerto Rico. Still worthy of permanent place in my rotation.

Buen Provecho! Gracias Fivebrigs, this is excelente. I added sazon to this and prepped a whole chicken as if I were cooking a turkey and baked at 275-300 for 2+ hours until cooked and the chicken was moist(it fell off the bone)and had a wonderful flavor.  I will surely use this again and again. Thanks
It is sooo delicious.  I used it to marinate chicken and ribs, both overnight, and it added so much flavor to the meat.  Great by itself and as a base for barbecue sauce.

This was pretty good, but somehow needs just a little "tweaking". I was afraid it might be too much pepper but that seemed to be fine. I've got hope for this recipe and I'm going to give it another try.

This was good.  My dh was loving it!  I did make some changes to suit what I had.  I cut the oil in half as I only had three small steaks to marinade.  I also used McCormick's hot shot pepper instead of just black pepper.  I did think it was a little salty, so next time I will reduce it a little.  Thank you so much for sharing!

Oh we wanted to be WOWed by this recipe sooo much, but it turned out bland.  I tasted the marinade before adding the meat (a 1lb round steak that I marinated for 24hrs), and I thought it tasted great.  But all the flavors got lost once the meat was grilled.  IF I used this again, I'd doctor it with some dried herbs.

I give this a five, but with my changes.  Those not familiar with tofu will need to know the following:  Remove the tofu from the box with water.  Drain water and place tofu on a tray or plate lined with two paper towels.  Place two more paper towels on top of the tofu.  Put another plate on top and finish it with something heavy to lightly weight it all down without making it crumble on the sides.  (I use a four cup measuring glass set on top of the final plate for weight)  Let the tofu set for 20-30 minutes on countertop.  This will drain all of the water out and prep the tofu for cooking.  The paper towels will be SOAKED when you take it out.  Discard them and cut the tofu into 1/4" stips longwise.  Cut those strips in half diagonally to make triangles.  Put these on a plate and freeze them for 1 hour.  They should be frozen on the edges, but not too stiff to move.  Do not thaw before cooking.  This will make the tofu chewy and "meaty" rather than the undesirable soft and gooey-centered tofu.  Heat 1-2 tbsp of olive in a non-stick pan on medium-high heat.  Cook the flash-frozen tofu 3-4 minutes on each flat side, being sure to shake the pan often so as not to allow the tofu to stick.  When the tofu is brown and crispy, turn the heat down to low-medium.  Pour bbq sauce to taste directly in the pan and shake around until tofu is completely coated.  Cook 2 minutes until sauce is crispy set to tofu.  Serve on toasted wheat buns topped with light cole slaw.  (Cole slaw pre-slic
