EXCELLENT!  I am always skeptical of recipes that have so few ingredients.  But this sauce was phenomenal in taste!  It is so easy to prepare that I will NEVER use store bought again!  I followed the recipe exactly except adding 1 tsp. of brown sugar.  I always believed that the sugar takes some of the tartness out of the tomatoes.  Thanks for sharing!

I had to find a recipe for spaghetti sauce because I wasn't sure if Ragu and Prego were kosher, besides the fact that I love cooking from scratch. I knew this recipe was worth trying because I love cooking with white wine, and it was so good and simple too. Throw everything in the blender, saute your onion and then add everything in the pot and simmer!! I used the 1 clove of garlic to blend in with the tomatoes, but I felt like that wasn't going to be enough for me, so I saute another clove with the onions, and it came out great!!! Not going back to the jar stuff!

Since I'm not a fan of jarred spaghetti sauce, I thought I'd give this a try. It was very good! I only added half of the white wine because I ran out and it was still tasty! I added some italian seasoning and ground beef and that was all I did differently. I can't wait to try this again when I have the full amount of white wine! I definitely recommend!

I just stepped away from the dinner table,and, knew I had to comment about this wonderful recipe.  I'm ashamed to admit that I was very skeptical, even after reading some of the reviews, because I have this strange belief that something this easy to make couldn't be "fabulous".  I was wrong!  This is THE recipe I will be using from now on!  Thank you!

Save yourself the trouble - just double the recipe and freeze the leftovers!  Tastes just as good thawed and reheated.   The only alteration I made to this recipe was using dry parsley instead of fresh.  

My husband loved this sauce.  I thought it was on the sweet side (I prefer a tarter red sauce), but hubby said this was just the way he liked his marinara.   Definitely a keeper recipe for us!
I made this tonight exactly to the recipe and it was awesome! I'll never buy jarred marinara again!

Amazing sauce. I added an extra 2 cloves of garlic. One to the initial purée and one to the veggie sauté. I also included a green bell pepper with the onion and garlic. I incorporated ground beef cooked with salt pepper and red pepper flake to make a delicious meat sauce. I feel like the red pepper flake was a great choice as it leaves just the slightest bit of spice on your tongue as you eat. Served it with spaghetti and garnished with fresh grated parmesan and  a leaf of fresh parsley.
Very good!! Didn't have the parsley and oregano, so I just added italian seasoning. Also added more garlic as some PP have suggested and some red pepper flakes for a kick!

This sauce is absolutely fantastic!  The white wine threw me a bit at first since I've always used cianti in marinara, but I gave it a go with Pinot Grigio and it was worth it.  Didn't have fresh parsley on hand so I estimated an equivalent with dried.  Also, didn't measure my garlic, just tossed in a few heaping tablespoons.  Midway through simmering, I added meatballs for flavor (Best Meatballs You'll Ever Have - from this site) and that enhanced this sauce even more.  Oh, and I threw in a bay leaf, too.

I love this recipe!  I was looking to impress my boyfriend buy making my own spaghetti sauce so I tried this one.  I don't like to cook, and this recipe is so simple it has become a recipe I turn to weekly.  The only problem I have is that the oil and the tomato sauce don't completely combine.

Too salty.  Other than that, though, really good!  I liked the texture.  I only had one can of tomatoes and no paste, so I put in a diced fresh tomato and a small can of tomato sauce.  I also used way less oil than recommended.  It worked pretty well.
I would say this was just ok.  I'm still on the search for a better marinara.

A very nice red sauce. Like most sauces I am sure there are an infinite number of variations that may be made, however I have found the recipe as written is excellent. It also scales very nicely; I have used it for manicotti for as few as 4 people and for chicken parmigiana for as many as 60. This has become my standard red sauce recipe ... thanks!
Tasted great, make it all the time. Wife loves it! Just a quick question can this be jarred and used later.

I did not like this marinara sauce. I was very excited to try because of so many wonderful reviews. I followed the recipe to a T until I had to try everything to fix it. The 1/2 cup of wine was too much and it would not cook off. It definitely needed some more herbs, maybe try basil and a bay leaf if I ever decide to make it again. I also added about 2 T of brown sugar and that did work at reducing the acidity.

The finished product was a five, but I had to make a few changes to get it that way.  I used red instead of white win (that's what I had and I didn't factor that into my rating).  For my taste it needed more garlic, I used three cloves.  It had too much salt, I needed to add more tomatoes to fix that.  And it did need about a tablespoon of brown sugar.

Otherwise it is amazing and I will be making this again!
I thought this was a great sauce! Very simple to make, I made it for the 'Eggplant Parmesan II' from this website...delicious! Cheers for the great recipe!
Good and easy, but not the best as the title claims.  Serve with about 2lbs of pasta.

Absolutely fabulous!!! And so easy to make. Try it and you will never buy store bought sauce again and it freezes well for a quick easy meal. A few changes I made was using dice tomatoes because I had them on hand, added more garlic and some basil. Thank you Jackie for an awesome recipe!!!
My husband and I love this sauce! I have made it 3 times now and it's my new favorite red sauce! Thanks for sharing :)

Outstanding is all I can say! I was looking for a marinara sauce to use for dipping garlic bread sticks in. This seemed easy enough and with so many reviews I thought I'd give it a try. Again... OUTSTANDING! This will definitely be in the favorites and will become our special sauce for homemade pizza as well! Thanks for sharing

We really liked the ease to make and taste of this sauce.  The only change I really made was two cloves garlic instead of one.  Next time I will make with red wine instead of white for bit of a different taste.
This was so tasty! My entire family loved it and it was so easy to make.

I was making eggplant parmesan and I ran out of the store-bought marinara sauce so I turned to this recipe to get me out of my pinch.  I didn't have stewed tomatoes, so I used fire-roasted diced tomatoes, which I had on hand.  Other than that, followed the directions to a T, and the sauce came out beautifully.  I think I will start making my own sauce more often!
Really, really good!
Amazing and easy to make! I've made this delicious sauce many, many times.

Excellent. Used brown sugar, chopped fresh basil, oregano, thyme. Otherwise followed recipe. It was very sweet but I think that was from the fresh tomatoes I used. I skinned tomatoes and boiled them down. Will use this recipe again. Very versatile.

I made this for an Italian themed dinner/potluck this weekend. Everyone loved it. I made a couple changes based on past reviews.

I used my Vitamix in place of a food processor and it turned out great. Used only 1/4 cup of white wine (some reviews stated 1/2 cup was too much). Added 1 tsp of basil and 1 TBSP of brown sugar (to counteract the tartness of the tomatoes). 

I also added the sautéed onions into the Vitamix with the rest of the ingredients to make sure they were more finely chopped and blended with the sauce. I then added it all back to the same skillet and simmered for about 25 mins.
Outstanding sauce! Only used about 2 Tbsp. of tomato paste though. Incredible flavour!!

This is wonderful!  I have been searching for a recipe like this!  I added just a bit more garlic, but otherwise made as written.  I put the sauce in a crockpot and let it cook on low all day while I was busy, made the noodles at dinner time, and felt like I was eating out, right at home!!!  Thank you for sharing this recipe!!  Wish I could give more than five stars, it rates a 10!!!!!
Easy to make and tastes great. Decreased the olive oil and added a tablespoon of brown.sugar

I added additional garlic. A second clove and then a teaspoon of powder. Also had to add additional salt. With those additions this was very, very good. I had never made marinara before, but I will probably be making more!

I will buy jarred sauce so much less now that I found this recipe.  It is just too easy to make.  But ease of reputation is not why I gave this recipe five stars.  The sauce is absolutely divine.  For my personal tastes, I agree with the notion of adding basil and white sugar to give it sweet tones.  I use two tsp basil, one tbsp sugar, and one more tsp of oregano.
This was the best Marinara sauce yet!

This is delicious! The last marinara sauce I made from scratch was so bad it almost turned me off homemade ones for good, but this one saved it for me. I think it's the white wine that really makes the difference, and the flavour is definitely better the longer it sits. The only thing I changed was to cut back on the amount of oil (to about 2-3 Tbsp), and salt (to 1/2-3/4 tsp) a little bit, just to suit my family's tastes. Yummy! This is definitely going to be my go-to recipe from now on. Thank you!
Easy and excellent!  My carnivorous husband doesn't normally like meatless pasta dishes, but he raves about spaghetti with this sauce.

I goofed this recipe because I added all ingredients to the food processor. I did not saute the onions so they were a bit "crunchy" Also, I added red wine since I had that on hand.
With these mistakes, it was still great and my two year old and 6 year old had seconds! I will make this again and again. Better than any jar that's for sure and easy too.
Really Good!

I am embarassed to admit I didn't actually READ the directions, I just threw all of the ingredients into a pot on the stove.  I did roughly chop the stewed tomatoes, but even so, my sauce turned out more chunky than it was supposed to.  It was still excellent!  I made recipe as is, but it would be easy to adjust to your personal tastes.  Thanks for the great recipe!

Yummy! Poured this over cheese ravioli in a 9x13, sprinkled some mozzarella on top, baked it, and had a delicious dinner.  Hubby and 3 young kids loved it.  I omitted the wine, and added an extra clove of garlic and it was just marvelous.
I LOVE this sauce. I have been making sauce for 20 yrs. & this is the best sauce EVER!!

Great marinara sauce!  I didn't make any changes to this and I was thrilled with it- it is the perfect consistency (thick but not gloppy)!  I made it to use on stuffed riggies on Friday (couldn't eat meat), and then I used some more of it on pizza tonight, and was very happy with the recipe both times.  In fact, I think I liked this so much, it will replace my old pizza sauce!
Finally, a good marinara recipe, I will never go back to the others. I also added 1 tsp of brown sugar and some extra garlic, and I used freeze-dried parsley and it turned out fine.  Yummy!
My husband said it was the best sauce ever.  I added shredded carrot but followed everything else exactly. Delicious.  No more jar sauce for us.
I loved it! This is a best marinara sauce I've ever made. Even my picky husband loved it, too. Thanks for sharing this recipe. I will keep it to my recipe box and will make this again.

I chose this recipe for marinara sauce because I wanted to use my new food processor.  It was amazing!  I ended up adding italian seasoning because I was out of oregano.  The wine I used was a cheap Reisling I had on hand.  I served the Marinara over Turkey Meatballs.
Great recipe! This has become a staple in my house.

This is sooooo delicious!  I use whole canned tomatoes.  I squeeze out the excess juice and seeds before putting them in the food processor.  I also add red pepper flakes in the food processor to give the sauce a kick.  I don't add quite as much olive oil to the pan when cooking the onions.  I use about 4 tablespoons.  It's so yummy!  Thanks for the recipe!  :)
Really easy and really good. My picky husband even liked it and said I should make this and sell it in jars. Had to tell him sorry hun... it's an 'allrecipe' :)
I love love LOVE the flavor, but the consistency is just a bit off for me. I'll try crushed tomatoes next time.
Excellent! Added more spices to my taste. Consistency was perfect. Used for pasta and pizza.
This was so yummy!  Thanks!  I added green peppers and mushrooms to the onion, very tasty!
I followed the directions but it had a weird after taste...
I made this for a holiday luncheon at work.  It was served over chicken parmesan bundles (stuffed chicken) with a side of pasta.  It was a big hit!! I was told it was the best lucheon ever!
Delicious and so easy. Made it either the Mozzarella Stuffed Turkey Meatballs.
What a wonderful, easy recipe!  So much better than the store bought.  I added chopped green pepper and mushrooms to the onion and it turned out great!  Even the kids loved it!

This is awesome!  I used two cans of petite diced tomatoes instead of stewed and I left them chunky. I like my marinara sauce with small chunks of tomatoes. I also added a little more garlic and some basil.  It is easy to season this the way you like.  I used this one time on parmesan chicken and another time on homemade meatballs.  I like this so much more than the jar sauces.  I think I will try making up a big batch of this and see how well it freezes.

My 5 yr old said the sauce tasted like ice cream, licked the bowl clean, and asked for more. WOW!!!!

Very easy to put together. I followed others' suggestions and made a few changes:
-Used canned crushed tomatoes
-Sub'd dried parsley
-2 cloves garlic
-1/4 cup white wine (I used chardonnay)
-Added 1 Tbsp brown sugar

Thanks for the wonderful recipe. A definite keeper!!!
This went well with the Three Animal Italian Meatballs.
My husband said this sauce was restaurant quality and my 15 month old who has wanted to eat nothing but fruit lately ate two serving.
all in all, solid recipe!. reduced the white wine down a little and added some italian seasoning- 1Tbl.  and sugar- 1tsp.

This was perfect.  I put it over some chicken for chicken parmesan and my very picky husband LOVED it.  I don't usually like plain marinara sauce (I gotta have the meat), but even we put this on spaghetti the next day it was amazing!!  I also added just a tiny bit of fresh basil (it was our anniversary and basil is an aphrodisiac)...yummy!!
Very simple and very tasty.  I did add extra garlic.  Very good. Thanks!

Love Love LOVE this recipe. Great consistency, I use it as a base for many things... add meat and it's great also. Make lasagna, dipping sauce, pizza sauce, spaghetti sauce and more with only minor additions. I did use extra garlic powder and a bay leaf (as well as only dried spices, since it's what I had on hand), but otherwise no changes. Canned stewed tomatoes really do make a difference - don't use regular canned tomatoes!

Oustanding.  I followed the recipe to the tee the first time and it was delicious.  The second time I used half the olive oil (or it's too oily), crushed tomatoes (organic) and added 2 fresh basil leaves.  I'll never buy spaghetti sauce in the store again!  And it's so easy to make!
Great and easy...added a few spices but nothing major.
Great recipe! We loved it!

Oh my goodness this recipe is awesome... the recipe doesn't say weather or not to drain the stewed tomatoes... i didn't... and I just can't belive how heavenly this taste... oh i used  this dipping sauce for calamari that i made... taste just like olive garden dipping sauce!
So simple and So Good - perfect.  I used Red Wine instead of White and for those who say they can taste the wine - either did not simmer it for the 30 min or more or it's in your head.
Pretty decent and easy to make.  I used 1 t. of basil, 1/4 t. of rosemary, 3 cloves of garlic, and and 1 T of brown sugar.

Excellent basic recipe.  I used fire-roasted tomatoes and added some basil and about 2 tsp. sugar for my taste.  Used a mild pinot grigio and it was perfect!  Husband tried to eat it all out of the pot on some bread, so I had to make another batch :-)
Made this last night with spaghetti squash.  It was fabulous.  The only things I did differently were added fresh basil and a bit of brown sugar.  This sauce is definitely a keeper.
one of the few recipes I don't alter, and so simple to make.  I use this for everything.

We were disappointed that this turned out very bland.  We followed the directions exactly, but were not thrilled with the outcome as other reviewers were.  It has a nice consistency, but there's just not much flavor.
Delicious!!!! I'll never buy sauce in a jar again!!!!
It's wasn't a great sauce, but it was certainly very decent. I served this with some Ravioli I had made.

We have been using this recipe for over a year for all our pasta and pizza sauce. We have never used store bought sauce since. I tried it once with dried parsley....no good. Definitely go with fresh. It turned out the best when I used mothers canned tomatoes.
I made this for my vegetarian daughter and I might just use this basic recipe everytime from now on! So easy and so good.

I loved this sauce.  I added more dried basil, italian seasoning, sugar and extra garlic, no onions.  I used one can of crushed tomatoes, one can of diced tomatoes.    A fabulous starter for a lot of great sauces and meals!
Great sauce. I used tomato sauce instead of stewed tomatoes (that's what I had on hand) and dried parsley instead of fresh. I had my reservations about using the wine, but I'm glad that I did.

What a wonderful homemade sauce that takes so little effort to prepare! My food processor is too small, so I just throw everything into the blender and it works great.  Thanks for this awesome recipe!

This was an amazingly simple and delicious sauce.  I left out the onions, b/c I have people who don't like "chunks".  I also did the substitution with the chicken broth.  This was awesome with bread sticks, and amazing on our stuffed crust pizza.  I will be making spaghetti with it next week.  So easy to make, and DELICIOUS!!
Not the best marinara sauce, but it was pretty good.  Would have given in 3 1/2 stars if I could.  It wasn't too flavorful, so I added some oregano, basil & garlic salt.

Hmmm. While I like this, I feel something is missing.... I've been craving a homey meal for a while, but haven't had much free time to spend in the kitchen lately. 2day was the exception. I decided to go all out - homemade pasta sauce, meatballs & garlic bread (mangia!). Since I made 14 decent sized MB's, I wanted to ensure there was enuf sauce to cover them entirely (I simmered them in this sauce). For that reason, I chose to double everything. I ended up using plain 'ol Dei Fratelli stewed tomatoes, but later when reading Jackie's instructions, I noticed that she referred to Italian seasoned ones (?). I decided to add 2 t Italian seasoning b/c of this. My choice of wine was Pinot Grigio (well, actually my fiance's choice - I sent him to the wine section while I finished the rest of our grocery shopping!). The thing I really don't like about this sauce is how runny it is. It literally slid right off my spaghetti noodles lol, but that could have been my fault (I may have pureed too long...)??? One other note: DO NOT USE 6 (or in my case, 12) T EVOO!!! You absolutely DO NOT need that much oil to saute a small onion!!! I ended up skimming a TON of oil off of my sauce (it reminded me of the horrible Gulf oil spill for lack of a more fitting analogy...). Having said that, I think this would be an easy fix, or as is, a perfect dipping sauce for fried mozza sticks or calzones. I will definitely keep this recipe handy for that! Thanks for sharing, Jackie! :-)

I left out the wine and just drank a red wine instead. This was an excellent marinara and  definitely will be my go to recipe from now on.  We served this over steamed cauliflower - suprised me how increadibly tasty this was.  I used one can of No Salt tomatos and one regular can to reduce the sodium.  My husband added salt to his serving, but it was perfect for me.
Never made this type of sauce, aalways used jar sauce.  Hubby loved  it sent it to my sister.

This was a great basic marinara sauce recipe.  My husband, who normally doesn't like marinara sauce loved it.  I did make a few changes, but still stuck to the basic recipe.  I added another clove of minced garlic and some fresh basil to the tomatoes.  Then, when I put the sauce in the pan to simmer it, I added some more, chopped resh basil.  It turned out great!!!
Very good and really easy! I followed the recipe exactly except for I used dried parsley instead of fresh. I doubled it and froze the remainder. Will make again thanks for a great recipe.

Ok seriosuly I don't understand how this recipe got such great reviews. I wanted to make a quick marinara so I tried this. I would have been much better off using jarred sauce. This was barely edible on meatball subs & I can't imagine putting it on pasta. I don't know if it was the stewed tomatoes or the wine, or the combo of the two...but I will deffinately be sticking with my regular marinara that simmers for hours. The extra time is worth it.
THIS WAS VERY GOOD. MY FAMILY ENJOYED IT. I ALSO CUT THE OLIVE OIL IN HALF AND ADDED EXTRA GARLIC. WILL BE A GREAT DIPPING SAUCE FOR MOZZORELLA STICKS.
Very good!
I've gotten compliments on this EVERY time I've made it. Great flavor, very easy to make. Someone said it's got an "old world taste" -- not that plastic, tasteless, commercial jarred sauce.
This makes a delicious sauce!  I served mine with homemade meatballs over spaghetti.  The only change I'll make is to double the recipe next time.  Thanks for a wonderful spaghetti sauce!
Just yummy, quick, thick and decadent. Feel like I just came out of a good Italian eatery. I will definitely make this again!
Made this exactly as the recipe instructed and it was incredible!  Never made marinara sauce before and my friends were impressed.  And they're old school Italians.
Used it on zucchini ravioli.... Delicious!
The name of this sauce says it all!  It is the BEST!
This was good, but when I added the wine, it totally took over. Next time, I may just leave the wine out altogether.
Wow, this stuff is good. And super easy to make!! make extra you will want it.

WOW - I wanted a nice, robust marinara sauce in my collection and found this recipe.  We added 1 tablespoon of brown sugar, 1 teaspoon of basil and cut the white wine in half - it is unbelievable how good this recipe is!!
Thought it was just alright. A basic marinara sauce for dipping.

This sauce lived up to its name!  I made this recipe like it was written except only used about 2 tbsp oil and omitted the white wine.  My girls, who are 3 and 6, absolutely loved it!  My husband and I enjoyed it quite a bit.  I will make this over and over.  Thanks so much!
This is only way I make Marinara sauce now.  It is so less acidic that I don't get heart burn.

This has to be the best marinara i have tried as of yet. A lot of marinara's are heavy and don't taste that good to me (taste more store bought sauces) and have to much seasoning in them. This was perfect. Only change i woudl probably add more garlic..not because i don't think 1 clove is sufficient but because im a garlic lover :)
This recipe was terrific in all ways. It is quick & easy. The consistancy is perfect. I used it as a dipping sauce for strombolis, but will use it in the future for misc. pasta dishes. Thanks
This is the recipe I always use now. Sometimes I add mushrooms or ground beef but usually I follow the recipe exactly. My husband LOVES this sauce.

Love this recipe! Fast and easy. Only change I made was I used 1/4 cup of wine and 1/4 cup of chicken broth so my kids wouldn't get even a hint of the wine. I too used crushed tomatoes but still put it through the food processor. Made a double batch so I will have some on hand in the freezer.

ABSOLUTELY THE BEST YET! I added some basil and cut back on the parsley. Also added some sugar cause it was alittle tart and some extra tomoatoes (not stewed, just crushed). I hand mashed the stewed tomatoes and really broke up the pieces.  Served it with Campanelle, and was heaped with praise. Thanks!

I LOVE this recipe!  Thick but not too thick with a fabulous flavor.  I used 1 1/2 tsp. dried parsley, omitted the salt since I was serving it with manicotti (all that cheese has a lot of salt!) added 1 tsp. dried basil based on TNFRENCH's recommendation and about 2 tsp. brown sugar based on TUNISIANSWIFE review.  I used red onion and reduced the olive oil to 3 tbsp (will most likely use even less next time).  Thanks Jackie for a great marinara sauce.

So good and quick and simple!  Who needs store-bought?  I added extra garlic, itslian seadonings, brown sugar and pinch of baking soda.  A touch sweet.  next time skip the sugar but do add the baking soda.  A keeper.

I'm about to make this for the 5th time. I've made it a little different every time because I use what I have on hand but it has never come out anything but perfect. Easy and freezes well so double the recipe!

To be fair, I believe you should follow a recipe in order to rate it honestly.  That being said, I must say that I was skeptical about this recipe.  I make homemade sauce all the time, but had never used stewed tomatoes.  This was really good!  The flavors all came together nicely.  I followed the recipe exactly and served it with grilled Italian sausage.  It was also very quick and easy.
Very good!  I used whole tomatoes, fresh herbs * unfiltered olive oil. Definitely use the wine!! It is a great, versatile recipe.

loved it a great base to build on.  i liked the wine in it.  brightens it up a bit.  WAY better than from a jar.  served with homemade vegetarian meatballs and spaghetti for family from out of town and it was a hit.  i had doubled the recipes and had some of the sauce left over so i froze it.  we ate it the other night and it was also really good.  good with some red pepper flakes added for a kick.

Super quick, easy and delicious! You could also use crushed tomatoes and skip the food processor. I use this recipe for simple pasta dishes like spaghetti or in lasagna. This recipe is great as is, but is also very versatile so add whatever you want to it! The sauce is really good with lot's of veggies added to it. The one change I would recommend is adding a teaspoon of brown sugar to reduce tartness.
Awesome Recipe. I pretty much followed it exactly. I added more Garlic.
Amazing!!!  I had a lot more garlic, but other than that I follow the recipe.  Really good!

I should probably rate this with 4 stars but because I made alterations I can't fault the recipe.  I used italian seasoning instead of dried oregano and crushed tomatoes instead of stewed tomatoes.  I also added a splash of pinot grigio and about 2 tablespoons of brown sugar.
This really was one of the best marinara recipes I have ever made and quick!  I omitted the olive oil because I am counting calories and it is still terrific!  Thank you Jackie!
AWESOME!  I Make a tripple batch of this all the time.  Freezes very well.
Loved it, quick easy & tasty.  I added a little sugar & some garlic powder.
This is delicious just as is!  I have used it with Italian Sausage over pasta as well as with Stuffed Peppers.  Both meals were great because of the marinara.

very good. I added one portabella mushroom, 8 oz sliced button mushrooms, more minced garlic, 1/2 c sliced kalamata olives and 4 pieces cooked, crumbled bacon. My husband and I like our marinaras a little salty (I save the sweet stuff for dessert)and this was great. Eating the stuff from the jar will be very difficult now! Thanks for the recipe.
This was a good base recipe but it needed more garlic and spices. I also added a tablespoon of sugar to cut through the bitterness of the wine.

I made this sauce on 11 May 02. The only thing I added was a tsp. of basil..it needed the extra spice. It was really good and tasted very rustic. I am not going to buy jar sauce ever again. I can't believe how easy it was to make sauce from scratch.
This is very good sauce. Nice and thick and sticks to the pasta, I like to use it with the fresh pasta you can buy, for a quick and easy supper. Probably freezes well too.

This was spot on! I used crushed tomatoes instead an the consistency was perfect. I used abt 3 cloves of garlic as I love the flavor and I didnt have any white wine on hand, so i used chicken broth. I also used abt 2 tbsp of brown sugar to help with the acidity. This was perfect for my chicken parmigiana and as a dipping sauce for my fried mac and cheese and fried mozzarella sticks. Will definitely make this again. Thank you!!

This was the easiest sauce I've ever made!  I loved that it contained most things that people already have on hand.  I did up the garlic too, to two cloves.  I added dried basil (1 tsp) as well.  I also added white sugar (1 tsp).  It does freeze well.  For wine, I used Chardonnay.

Very good!  I made this sauce at a food demo for a grocery store and it was a big hit.  I changed recipe though--used crushed tomates; no parsley; 4 cloves garlic; no oregano or salt; added 2 tsp. Italian seasoning; 1 T sugar; cut back a bit on the olive oil.  Made this with chicken floured and seasoned with Italian seasoning.  Will definitely make again!

As if this needed another review!  I liked it a lot.  Subbed out diced tomatoes for stewed and dried parsley for fresh.  I skipped the food processor step for a little bit chunkier result.  I used some leftover Pinot Grigio.  It was delish!
No changes but I thought using the  blender was an interesting idea.  I always use Pomi tomatoes.

LOVE LOVE LOVE!
This sauce is awesome! I make it in large batches and freeze for later use because it's so good. I saute the onions and garlic rather than throwing in food processor in about 1/2 the olive oil listed. Definitely use the stewed tomatoes. I use Moscato wine bc its the only wine I drink and ever have on-hand. I add at least 2 more garlic cloves, too.
This sauce tastes canned.  It is sweet and has a tang to it I didn't prefer.  Sorry

is very good.  i spare the food processor and add everything to the pot after cooking the onions then use a hand blender after simmering for 30 mins. salt and pepper before and after simmering. a teaspoon at a time of brown sugar until it suits what your serving it with.
Very tasty and easy to make sauce, I didn't add the white wine as i didn't have any and added water instead, turned great still.
Family loved it and I will definitely make it again!

This is my new go-to marinara sauce! So much tastier than the jarred stuff, and I know what is in it. Used it last week in my zucchini lasagna and will be using it tomorrow for eggplant florentini. I did substitute chicken broth for the wine and added a few extra cloves of garlic (we love garlic). I'm gonna make a triple batch tomorrow and freeze some for those busy nights. Thanks for such a simple, tasty recipe!
Very pleased with the results. Thanks

This is great. It is now my go to pasta sauce, so easy to make. I use red wine instead of white, and I add basil and a pinch of sugar to offset the sometimes bitter taste of the canned tomatoes.
