Absolutely amazing sauce. Can't go wrong, an all round winner. Very very tasty, also very easy to make.

An essential recipe in my household! It freezes well, so we make a quadruple batch. We throw in maybe 3 or 4 cloves of garlic instead of 1. Sauvignon Blanc is our favorite wine to use - just sweet enough (the wine here is replacing table sugar after all), not woody like chardonnays tend to be, and with a bright crisp citrus-like quality that works really well with the tomatoes. Right now I have a pot on the stove so I can use up a bottle of Chenin Blanc, and that seems to be working well too. This is a much fresher, more acidic taste than you get with prepared tomato sauces on the supermarket shelves, so you really only want to cook it 30 minutes or until the flavors blend. If you want something that tastes more like jarred sauce, I would look for a different recipe that has a 2-3 hour cook time and uses sugar instead of wine... though once you try this recipe, you may never want the other kind again. :)
great flavor!

Thanks for this awesome recipe! No more sauce from a jar!  There are a couple of things that you can do to take this sauce from great to spectacular.  First, double the garlic.  My family is very garlic-phobic, but they love this sauce with the extra cloves.  Add a tsp. of dried basil as well for extra flavor.  Second, add 2 tbsp. of honey AND 1 or two crumbled chicken boullion cubes as the sauce simmers.  It balances the flavors perfectly.

Fantastic! Used dried parsley, sauteed chopped green onion and minced garlic in the olive oil - pulsed everything in blender & cooked in oil-sprayed crockpot on low for 3 hours before serving w/pasta and chicken parm - SO delicious!
This was really good!  My husband's mom is Italian and even he was impressed.  He said to keep this recipe FOR SURE.  Yummy!

I love this sauce! This is the only marinara sauce I use now and I freeze extra for later. I make a few small changes. I use 2 cans of Hunts chopped tomatoes and not stewed, because that is what I buy in bulk, sub. 4tsp dried parsley for 4 Tblsp. of fresh, and I don't use any black pepper, as I don't care for it. The sauce tastes very good before even adding it to the onions and oil. The wine, garlic, and tomato combination is wonderful! I also use a hand emulsier blender instead of a food processor, which is much quicker and a lot less clean-up (a must have in the kitchen). I have been looking for some time for a fresh tasting & quick marinara sauce, and one that is not spicy, thick, and sweet like a lot of recipes out there, especially the jarred sauces. This tastes very authentic, and great in any recipe calling for marinara or spaghetti sauce. Thank you so much submitter!
Fabulous!  I had a wine tasting at my home and served this sauce over linguini.  Everyone complimented it and asked for the recipe.  Thanks for sharing!

I'm never buying jarred sauce again!!!  I prepared the recipe just as stated except I added some sugar since the cheap white cooking wine I used made it slightly on the tart side.  It balanced the flavor perfectly.  This sauce is d-licious!  I'm definitely doubling or tripling the recipe next time and will freeze it.

It was ok the first time I made this recipe, but it lacked something-I cut back to 3 tbls of Olive Oil, added 3 more cloves of garlic (we like garlic), 1 1/2 tsp of fresh Basil and 1 1/2 tsp of sugar (to cut the acidity). That improved the taste dramatically.

Good sauce. I added more garlic because I am me but to each their own. It will be fun to try different wines with it too. I used white but a merlot might be fun too.  Great place to start and easy to make.

I grew up with my Italian mother making everything from scratch, that said, I was looking for a quick pasta sauce as a base sauce (or gravy as my mom called it).    I wanted a vegetarian version.  I used organic crushed and whole tomatoes.  In place of wine I used vegetable stock, added a tbl sugar and 1 tbl of pesto sauce stirring in at the end.  Use jar or homemade, it really bumps up the flavor!

I made this marinara when I recently cooked for a wedding reception of 450. They loved it. Even my husband who usually says a new recipe is "ok", He loved it also and told me that I could make it any time.

Great sauce! a lot of flavor, although I say this having made it with a few additions: 2 cloves garlic instead of one, shake of rosemary,
1/2 tsp thyme, 
several shakes of italian seasoning, 1/2 finely diced large onion 
1 green pepper, chopped fine.

I am making lasagna from a recipe I found on here but it called for jar sauce and I did not want to use sauce from a jar. Found this recipe and not only did it sound good but also easy. I decided to add more garlic as we love garlic and 1 clove just did not sound like enough, I added 4 cloves (did I mention we love garlic). I am also cooking for a crowd and several of them do not like onions so I put the onion & olive oil in the blender with the other ingredients so no one would know they were in there (I use this trick a lot). The last thing I did different was add fresh basil in with the parsley because I couldn't imagine marinara sauce without basil plus I have tons since I grow it. This sauce turned out wonderful and I will make it again and again!
This is fantastic!  My kids loved it.  Will make again and again.
A little to sweet for me but all and all really not that bad.

I didn't like that I was supposed to simmer this for so long. I multiplied the recipe by four, but I did not have a good pot to fit it all in. So, the pot I used was overflowing. Once the simmering got going, it looked like a homicide crime scene in my kitchen.

I would recommend changing the recipe to putting a lid on the marinara while it simmers. And, you can throw some zucchini, broccoli, and spinach in there.
I've been making this recipes for several years now. It is so easy to make. I don't change a thing.
This is a great recipe. I swapped the parsley for fresh thyme and added about 5 sun dried tomatoes and it was amazing.

I needed a quick red sauce for a pasta side, but didn't have time to make my 'usual' and the thought of using a jarred sauce... well, ick.  As simple as this is, this marinara is quite good, plus I liked whirling everything in the food processor -- great way to sneak in veggies for those who 'pick out the chunks'.  To spice it up, I added a few goodly shakes of red pepper flakes.  Will make again when short on time or when it's too hot to have a sauce on the stove for hours.  Thanks!
Absolutely delicious.  I had stopped buying jarred marinara sauce due to the risk of BPA, but now I can make my own and it's even better than the jarred stuff.  Super easy, too!
This recipe was very good.  I did add fresh basil to give more flavor.  I also used crushed tomatoes in lieu of the stewed tomatoes to eliminate the blender step.
This is the best sauce ever! It's got so much flavor, I highly recommend this recipe. I will never buy sauce from the store ever again!

I love this sauce- even my meat eating friends say it is superior to theirs! I use crushed tomatoes instead of stewed as those have corn syrup in them. This eliminates the need to bust out the food processor as well. I use vermouth as I never have white wine around and add a shredded carrot to help with acidity.

I also jack up the garlic and cut the oil in half.
I made this ahead of time to let it sit for a few days and it was so good. My husband will not let me buy another premade marinara sauce again. It was a big hit for the whole family.
Excellent.  Better days later.  No white wine so added chicken stock instead. Kids and hubby ate it all!
This was great! Didnt have any wine so substituted chicken broth as others suggested. Simmered for about 2hrs. We doubled the recipe and added 2 tsp. brown sugar. EXCELLENT!

In terms of ease this certainly met the objective.  It's great how it does not require a tremendous amount of ingredients.  We also added some fresh basil and Sweet Italian sausage during the simmering phase.  The sausage seemed to complement well the sauce consistency.  All in all this is a solid sauce.

Perfect consistency and really raises any Italian dinner to a superior level. I use chicken stock rather than wine and am very heavy handed with fresh herbs when I make it (basil, cilantro and Italian parsley). It also freezes well. This has been my go to marinara for many years now. I have a big family so I double it.
I made this sauce exactly as is except I used canned diced tomatoes instead of stewed and I added an extra can. I also added a TBSP of brown sugar and used red wine instead of white. Fantastic!!!

Do NOT use cooking wine in this recipe.  The sauce is way too salty and not very good if you do.  I'm going to go ahead and give it four stars, as I think it probably would have been good if I'd used real wine.
Excellent easy sauce to make!
This sauce has never turned out poorly. It is absolutely one of our faves!

Very good!  I wouldn't say the best, but it was certainly easy to make and tasty.  I added a little sugar to sweeten it up a bit (because I like my marinara sweet) and I cut the oil in half.  Oh and I forgot the wine altogether!  I added 2 cloves of garlic, like other reviewers, and just a tad more onion as well.  Would probably make this recipe again, as it's easy and I have most of the ingredients on hand at any given time!
Family loved and my Italian hubby raves about it :)

Surely the BEST MARINARA ! I used San Marzano canned tomatoes, jaggery instead of white / brown sugar and 'cooking wine' (which I will substitute with good drinkable white wine next time). No more store bought marinara !
Fan-Fricken'-Tastic!!  Awesome in meatball subs :)
This recipe is a good base, I add my own kicks to it and it makes a perfect sauce.

It's the Best!  Made this sauce with baked ziti for a very large crowd.  It was a big hit.  I wouldn't change anything in the recipe.  Will now be making it all the time.  Thank you for an easy delicious red sauce!

This marinara sauce is absolutely delicious.  My husband, and I, as well as my two-year old daughter loved it!  My 4-year old son wasn't a fan, but he doesn't like anything!  The only thing we did different was omit the white wine, and it turned out superb.  This was so easy and just blows away the jar sauces!  Next time I'm going to double the recipe, so I can have some to freeze.
Very good. My husband and I loved it! Thanks!

This was good both times we had it, but I highly recommend using fresh tomatoes instead of canned.  First time I made this we had fresh tomatoes from our garden, and it was amazing!  When I made it the second time with canned tomatoes we didn't enjoy it as much.
I substituted Ruby Port for the white wine, substituted basil for oregano plus added mushroom, shredded carrots and chopped broccoli to the sauce.   M-m-m-m!

Recipe as given is delicious!!! I can't believe I've never thought of blending my sauces in a blender, I like the consistency. I add fresh basil, extra garlic, italian seasoning, and a tablespoon of brown sugar. For a heavier meaty sauce I cooked lean ground beef and sweet Italian sausage with the onions, drained, then poured in the marinara. Served with fresh parmesan on top.

Really good recipe, especially because it uses stuff I usually had on hand.  I used canned italian tomatoes with basil, oregano & garlic already in it but still added fresh.  It's so much better and almost as easy as the stuff in a jar  :)
A wonderful marinara sauce.  My kids love it as well.  I've also made it without the wine, when I havent had any handy, and its still very tasty!
I'm a beginner, and I have always wanted a good spaghetti sauce to brag about. Thanks so much for posting!
This is a very delicious and fresh tasting sauce.  My guests loved it.

Great flavor and my new go-to recipe for spaghetti sauce. I used tomato sauce instead of blending the stewed tomatoes and I added 1 lb ground turkey, 1 lb Italian sausage (browned first), some red bell pepper and mushrooms. Delicious!

This is an okay recipe if you like a strong tomato flavor and no spice. I added more oregano and 1 tsp. Basil, some sugar, and more salt. I excluded the wine but I would have used it if I wasn't out of it. I don't like trying to modify recipes on my own so I am going this 4 stars.

I've made this marinara sauce twice now, and each time it's been delicious. I made it first to go with meatballs, and then used it as the tomato base on homemade pizzas. I added a few touches of my own - balsamic vinegar, ketchup, Worcestershire sauce and some basil leaves, as I always add these when making a tomato pasta sauce to boost the flavour. I've now added this to my own recipe book at home so I can fall back on it again and again.
I love this sauce, I use it for my spaghetti, and there is never any leftovers
The name says it all.  This was the best marinara sauce I've ever tasted.  It was also very easy to make.

I made the sauce to go with the St. Louis Toasted Ravioli and my hubby and I weren't too impressed with it.  I have refrigerated the leftover sauce and plan to use it again with Baked Ravioli (leftover ravioli) to see how it tastes.  Several other reviewers commented that it gets better with age, so we will give it another try.  Thanks for sharing Jackie!

I really liked this sauce until I added the wine. I don't drink but I've started experimenting with cooking wine. When I first added the wine, the alcohol smell was overwhelming. After 30 minutes of simmering, the alcohol smell was less but I could still taste it. When I tasted the recipe before adding the recipe, it was really good. Maybe I'll just make the recipe and leave out the wine next time...
This sauce really is the "best marinara sauce yet".  I love garlic therefore added more.  DELISH!

This sauce is easy and so great. My mother would spend all day making sauce when I was growing up and I never thought I could be satisfied by anything this quick and convenient.  I've used both white and red wine and although I prefer white, it doesn't make much difference.  The only thing that I think can really be altered is the amount of oil, as others have said. All you need is just enough  to cook the onion, maybe 2 or 3 tbsp at most. I also add a little brown sugar and double or triple the garlic, but these are just preferences.  The recipe is great as is!  I use it with Angela's Easy  Breaded Chicken for a great, light chicken parm.
Absolutely THE BEST sauce! We were looking for a super easy recipe that would reduce the amount of sodium we eat. This was it! Never going back to store-bought sauce!
Very good.  Good consistency, easy to make, and tasty.  I didn't have white wine, I substituted a little red wine and it was good.  I will make again.

Incredible sauce!!!  Instead of stewed tomatoes I used crushed tomatoes so there was no need for the food processor.  I fried the onions in 3 cloves of minced garlic and added 1 tsp. of dried basil, used 1 Tbsp. of dried parsley instead of fresh, and added 1 Tbsp. of brown sugar to cut the acidity of the tomatoes. Other than those additions this was perfect over angel hair pasta and chicken parmesan!
need to add more garlic, add celery and onions and more spices

This sauce is delicious and just the right consistency. I sauteed fresh peppers, finely chopped, (the last from our garden!)  along with the onions. I chopped fresh basil and added it to the food processor for extra flavor.   I also used red wine rather than white because that is what I always use in tomato based sauces.  I served the sauce over pesto filled gnocchi.  What a wonderful meal!

The sauce is really good, but I find 30 minutes is too long to simmer.  I liked the taste and consistency best at 15 minutes.  Is there a reason I should keep it simmering for the additional 15 minutes?
Easy and great tasting! Everyone loved it.
I've made this one at least a dozen times since discovering it, excellent!

My family really enjoyed this. My husband ranted about how flavorful the sacue was. It was super easy and inexpensive to make. I made exactly with the exception for the suggestion for a tablespoon of brown sugar. Trying to eat healthier so served over whole wheat pasta with steamed turkey italian sausages. Very tasty. This is a great weeknight meal when you are busy! Thanks so much!
LOVE this! I like to leave ours chunky & add a bit of sugar.
I did not care for this.
This was delicious!  I did add 1 tbsp of brown sugar and added ground beef to make it a little heartier - YUM!
Easy to make and FULL of flavor.
I have made this serveral times and I have used red wine and it tastes great.(different, but still good)

Amazingly good!  I doubled it and am very glad I did.  I sautéed the onions then added all the other ingredients to the pot and just used a hand mixer to blend.  I did add some red pepper flakes and 1 T brown sugar and cut the olive oil down a lot.  Found myself eating it out of the pot!  Great on pasta too!  So glad to have a healthier alternative to jarred sauces!
Very good! Will definitely make again.

This is a great basic marinara sauce recipe but I had to tweak it just a bit.  I did add about a teaspoon or so of dried basil and about 1 1/2 tsp. Italian seasonings.  I also had to add some brown sugar to counter the tartness/acidity of the whole thing.  In the future I think I will use fresh basil instead of the fresh parsley and add dried parsley in its stead.  In the end I was left with a very flavorful sauce that went very well with meatballs that I had made from a recipe found on this site.

LOVE THIS!!!!!!!!!!!!!!  This  is so easy to make and it taste amazing.  I didn't add and omit anything.  No more jarred sauce at our house.  I made this in the evening and put it in the frig over night to get marry and happy and it was a wonder marriage with noodles and hamb.  This is wonderful!!!!   A keeper!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
Absolutely love this recipe! Great just the way it is and also for a base recipe! I add more garlic and double to freeze for later use!
Great sauce!  I served it over polenta.

Delicious and so easy! I did add some brown sugar per the recommendation of other reviewers. I like the flavor of the wine in there, but it wasn't too much for the kids. I served it over spaghetti with meatballs.  I think I might make it in a double batch next time and freeze half because it is so much etter than store bought!
No changes, entire picky family loved it.  Would definitely make it again!
My Italian husband was skeptical with this recipe since it did not contain basil and used stewed tomatoes and wine.  Needless to say it was loved by everyone in the family and will be made again!

This was a good recipe.  I didn't have any white wine, so I used red.  As with most sauces, this tastes better the next day.  A nice flavor and it is a thick sauce.  I used this with the chicken parmigiana recipe and it turned out great!!

This is very good, added a tablespoon of fresh basil(remember to cut it in half is using dried), you can leave out the pepper too,, i did with and without,  liked it both ways. One time I added peporoni, hambuger, black olives italian sausage, and used shell noodles, placed in pan covered with parmasian, and motz cheeze and baked, we called it pasta pizza.

Excellent.  I omitted wine, as I didn't have any - used water instead. Added 1 teas. basil, 3 cloves garlic and more salt, more onion, minced and some black pepper.  Prepared in the moring, refrigerated and served in evening.  Thanks for submitting.
Would not call this the best Marinara Sauce Yet. It was okay. I'm still on the hunt for the best sauce yet!
This recipe is freakin awesome! Came out perfect! Texture is excellent if you follow the recipe precisely.

I'm 15 and decided to cook for the first time for my family , 
It was really easy and fast. My parents were really impressed. Very good.

This is definately a recipe that you won't be dissapointed in.  My adult son (world's biggest critic) said this is the best sauce he has ever tasted!  I simmered the sauce a little longer than called for and added italian sausage.
wife and I loved this, best marinara sauce I have ever made. try it!

I also was very surprised by how much I liked this recipe.  I was a little suspicious of marinara sauce requiring so little time and so few ingredients, but it was very good.  I'm definitely keeping this recipe to use again!

I make this sauce every 2 weeks, although if I didn't double the recipe, I'd do it every week. A few modifications though. I use a whole vidalia onion, and add in some fresh basil.

Great recipe!

Great! Made for a fun night of cooking with my boyfriend. We made this sauce with extra portions of garlic, parsley and oregano and used red wine instead of white. Next time I will add in some mushrooms and other veggies. My first successful cooking venture! I normally end up burning the food, myself or anything else within 10 feet of the stove. =) Thanks!

This marinara sauce was pretty good and very easy to make. I added an extra clove of garlic and a little sugar.  While I did use dry basil, as called for, I think that the sauce would have been better with fresh sweet basil.
went well with hot sausages with peppers and onions.

I was so pleasantly surprised by this recipe!  It was so easy, simple, and really good.  It had a much fresher taste than a jarred sauce.  I served it with chicken parm and angel hair pasta.  Next time - I will double the recipe though.

This is the best marinara recipe I have found yet. My favorite restaruant in Cincinnati has a marinara sauce that no other sauce can be compared to. It also is hard to copy. This is getting me closer though. I left half a can of tomatoes until I combined everything and then added them to the sauce with the wine. I like it better that way.

This is my first time making sauce from scratch (I'm wary of all the store-bought marinara sauces because of the amount of preservatives in them) and I'm so happy with the results! I substituted champagne for white wine since that's all I had in the pantry, and I reduced the salt to my taste. It's perfect!

Great Recipe!!!!  On the first go around I substituted White Grape Juice in place of wine and it was a hit.  This time I am using white wine vinegar instead to add a little edge . . . will let you know how it goes.  Thank you for sharing this recipe.  Added note: I was out of white grape juice and fresh oregano.  Substituted equal part chicken stock and 1 teaspoon of dried oregano versus the 1 tablespoon of fresh.  This recipe is full proof!!!!  Excellent result again.

I will NEVER go back to bottled marinara sauce!  I used a combination of canned and fresh from my garden tomatoes (frozen from this summers batch)  I didn't have the wine so omitted it and it turned out perfect without it!  It simmered for about 30 minutes and the consistency was perfect!
I am putting it in my daughter's recipe album - a collection of favorite recipes for her to use when she moves into her own place.
This was good but I did make a few changes based on other reviews. I sauted mushrooms along with onion and also added sugar. I will make this again but not without some changes.

This was my first time making sauce and I have to say this was a good one to start with. Everyone enjoyed it just as the recipe says with no changes made.  This is a new go to for sure. No more jars of sauce for my family.

I had tried Giada's marinara and it was way too acidic, so I came across this recipe and was excited that it had so many great reviews.
During cooking, it did seem a bit acidic to me, so I used a bit of brown sugar. But other than that, I followed the recipe using a dry pinot grigio. I've read that dry white wine is very common in red sauces in Italy and adds a lovely, bright flavor. Be sure to reduce. I used San Marzano whole tomatoes & store brand paste. I hand crushed the tomatoes before whizzing everything in the blender for a bit.
My roomie and I, since we usually use jarred sauce, were honestly confused as to how it was supposed to taste, but we both loved it. It tasted light & fresh, if a bit liquid-y for my preference. Next time I might try chicken broth instead of wine to cut down on cost, add a bit more garlic and reduce longer for a thicker sauce. Great recipe, will use again! *Update* Making it now, used chicken broth, 1T brown sugar, 2t dried parsley, 1T dried Italian herbs - my herbs are always on the aged side and less potent, so I use a bit more. I sauteed the herbs with the onion & garlic for a good 15 minutes to "open" them up a bit and allow all those flavors to emerge. Simmered sauce one hour. Still unbelievably delicious! Don't be afraid to sub broth for the wine. And for the simplicity of the recipe, it smells incredible. So try it as written first, taste as you go along and tweak to your personal preference. Fantastic recipe ~ a keeper, for sure!
Great sauce!  And very easy to prepare.  I sued crushed tomatoes rather than stewed.

Love this sauce!  Tastes homemade.  Serve with Chef John's meatballs regularly.  Hubby tells everyone the sauce is his aunts' recipe -- which he says is the only sauce he'll eat.  Glad he doesn't read these reviews...
Great recipe! Everyone I've made it for loves it, and I like how simple and easy it is to put together.

We love this sauce!  The only thing I change is to add another clove or two of garlic.  I usually make a double batch to have plenty to freeze.  I make this in one big pot and then use my immersion blender on it after it has cooked for about 20 minutes.  This is much easier than putting it all in the blender.  The parsley and the wine really give it an excellent flavor.
Nothing in particular stood out but it was still delicious and easy to make.  Just make a batch and refridgerate.  Heat up whenever you have spaghetti for dinner. 100 times better then the jar stuff.

Very good sauce. I did make a couple changes to suit our taste and I think I've perfected it, after making it several times. I use 3 cloves garlic, a dash of Italion seasoning, a tsp white sugar, add about 1/4 cup of good quality grated parmesan and 1/2 tsp anchovy paste. I know the anchovy paste sounds gross, but it doesn't taste "fishy" at all and I think it really adds something to the sauce . My friend who is a chef said it is often a "secret ingredient" to a lot of marinara sauces.
Amazing! Best Marinara Recipe ive tried! My husband and i make this weekly now!
My first batch wasn't too impressive (I haven't been able to figure out why - sorry), but my second definitely ranks with the 'keepers'.

WOW! This so good and so very simple. I rarely use pasta sauce in a jar, after finding this recipe I doubt I will ever buy it in the jar again. I made 2 minor changes, I added 1 TBSP of brown sugar, like others suggested and I used chicken broth instead of wine.

This sauce is amazing on texture, easy and delicious! I tried it in the middle of the night and had no white wine or chicken stock, so I used water with a splash of balsamic. I used only about 1/4 cup of oil for 2 times the original recipe. Also, I added a couple of leaves basil to the blender, and a pinch of brown sugar and red pepper flake to the onions, which I crystallized a bit more time. Yum!!! :o)

So good!  I added more garlic and a shallot but that was the only changes I made.  A wonderful starting point for whatever else you want to add.  I will use this from now on.
UPDATE:  I added 1 whole small onion and about a cup of white wine as well as a tbsp each of oregano and basil...slowly cooking on stove for about 3 hours! Used my stick blender right in the pot to make everything smooth!
really good
I was getting sick of my own sauce, wanting to try. Very good sauce. So simple to make. Very pleased. Thx for posting.

If I could give this an extra star I would. Best sauce I've made yet. I change nothing. Honestly, the stewed tomatoes make it. Crushed does not have the richness and flavor of stewed. It's taste like some other sauce so PLEASE, honor this delicious, simple, recipe and use the stewed. I've made this three times in the past two months. I love it, I love it, I love it! Thank you so much. This is my go to now instead of the jar.
Awesome sauce! Made with 'the best meatballs' (only the best, right?) added extra meat to this sauce, sautéed with the onions.  Perfect! My new go-to! Thanks for the terrific recipe!!!

Yum! Very good marinara sauce recipe.  I halved the recipe to make only two cups, and I used one can crushed tomatoes instead of the stewed. I also added fresh basil. It came out great. This is way better than any store bought variety.
Easy & delicious.
I've made this so many times, each time I use a different wine and love how it changes the flavor.  I do have to say that switching to red wine instead of white is the way to go.

I made this last night, and I have to say it was one of the best sauces that I have made in years.  No more store bought sauces for us. This was very easy and you can double or triple and freeze.  I followed this recipe exact and it came out excellent.  My hubby loved it.

I'm Italian but I've never mastered the perfect marinara sauce. THIS IS IT. Bottom line - hands down - the best I've ever made. I used FRESH tomatoes though; dried oregano and parsley (4 tsps of each) and 2.5 tsps of fresh minced garlic from a jar; and white wine for cooking (not drinking). It simmered for less 10 minutes in a cast iron skillet before sampling it and it WAS OFF THE CHART delicious. I'm stuck and will never make any other....!

I'm not sure how to rate a spaghetti sauce recipe because spaghetti sauce is pretty hard to screw up.  I gave this four stars because it was good, but not as fantastic as I'd hoped.  This might be due to some of the changes I made:  I used diced tomatoes instead of stewed because that's all I had, I unfortunately had to replace garlic with garlic powder, I was also out of oregano and used Italian seasoning instead, and I only had dried parsley.  I used more onion (put the onion in the food processor before the sauce ingredients go in and chop them like that, then saute them!) and I added mushrooms because I love them.  I also added a bit of sugar to cut back on the tart taste and used 1/3 the olive oil (could have done with even less).  Also, how does this recipe make 32 servings?  Maybe 32 rabbit sized servings (my rabbit loves spaghetti)!  I got eight half cup servings out of it.  This was good, but I'll keep looking!  Thanks for the recipe, Jackie!

I added finely diced carrots and bell peppers, a bit more garlic, basil and some brown sugar. I used diced tomatoes AND crushed tomatoes (1 can of each) instead of stewed. The consistency came out perfect and the flavor was excellent. I'll use this one again.

I was looking for a marinara to slow cook with meatballs for subs. This was a PERFECT starting point! It is so easy, with common ingredients, of course I tweaked it a little bit for my taste... a bit more garlic, a bit more onion and oregano, and used chicken broth instead of wine (its what I had in the pantry :) Excellent recipe!

This sauce is great! I made my own turkey meatballs the first time. The second time I added browned ground turkey. I added an extra can of stewed tomatoes. It is important the type of wine you choose because it definitely makes the flavor. I used a nice white Pinot Gris and my family loved it both times! I have saved this recipe and passed it on to my daughter.

I omitted the parsley and added basil...also I only used one can of stewed tomatoes and replaced the second can with diced tomatoes.  I made it for friends who just LOVED it!  This will be the sauce I make always...it was perfect!
This was okay. A little bland and watery. Not much depth of flavor. I'm sure it will be better tomorrow, as all italian food is, so I'm giving it 4* instead of 3*.

What a GREAT recipe! EASY and delicious. I sauteed the onions in the pot and then added all the ingredients and used my immersion blender....1 pot sauce, no extra cleaning the blender! I added red wine cause that's what I had open and a few fresh mushrooms,Italian seasoning, a TBSP brown sugar and topped it off with freshly chopped basil and lots of parmesean cheese. I see all kinds of possibilities with this recipe. I will never buy Marinara sauce again!

This truly is the best marinara sauce yet!  I did make a few changes though.  I used crushed tomatoes instead of stewed, omitted the oil, pepper, onion and wine.  I added 1 t basil, 1 T sugar and a small can of mushrooms.  Delicious!

I enjoy this recipe, but I change it up a lot every time I make it, mostly using other peoples advice as well!:
I used diced tomatoes instead of stewed, much better consistency!
I used dried parsley instead of fresh
I always use pinot grigio for the wine, gives a slightly sweet, but bitter taste all at the same time.
I add 1/4 tsp crushed red pepper to give it a SLIGHT bite of heat
I add 1 tblspn brown sugar
1 tblspn italian seasoning
I also make meatballs, and let the sauce cook for a hours with meatballs and pepperoni slices. The longer the better!

My grandmother is a little Italian lady so I have a lot to live up to! This recipe fits the bill with some small changes, so thanks!

This is now the sauce that I will be making permanently.  I did not have any stewed tomatoes - only diced...so I boiled the 2 cans of diced tomatoes with a tsp of sugar.  I used a tablespoon of dried parsley (I rarely have fresh)  I used chicken broth instead of wine (I don't cook with wine)  I also added the sauteed onions, oil and chicken broth to the food processor after cooking, to puree the onions with the sauce. (Son doesn't like anything noticeable in his sauce) Then added back to the saucepan. Left on the stove for several hours and the flavors just keep getting better. Awesome recipe!!
Family favorite! We added ground turkey to it.

This recipe was all right but it didn't really impress me or my wife.  It was nice because it did taste a lot fresher than the normal jarred sauce but it just didn't have enough flavor for us to make this too often.  We used it over ravioli so maybe we'll try it on regular pasta next time.

I made this sauce and it was PERFECT!! I added more garlic and used San Marzano tomatoes and it has been added to my permanent cookbook!!! Thank you for an amazingly simple recipe with perfect flavour!!!

Absolutely amazing!  The name does not lie!  I will never buy jarred sauce again, this was just WAY too easy and much too good!

We used it last night to make a Baked Ziti recipe from this site and it was perfect!

This was excellent! My only problem was that I had a hard time getting the parsley to soften up. I made it on a lazy afternoon and let it simmer along for a couple of hours. I served it the next day as the sauce for chicken parm! Very, very yummy!
This was a really excellent marinara sauce that I'd definitely make again.  Lots of flavour.
This sauce is so quick, easy and tasty.  I'm using it for chicken parmesean and it really improved it with not much more work than using a jar of sauce.  Excellent!

my husband really liked the sweet taste of this marinara when i used it to make eggplant parmesan. i made modifications based on other reviews: added more garlic and 1 tbsp of brown sugar. i also substituted shallot for onion, and after sauteing blended the shallots with the tomatoes for a smoother consistency. this sauce was quick and easy and i will definitely use it again.

very good. i did make some changes per preference though.. omitted the onion and white wine(didn't have any on hand) and i didn't blend the ingredients together.. i like the chunks of tomatoes. very basic, but good, recipe!

The only reason I'm giving 4 stars vs 5 is because I followed other reviewers suggestions for changes. I added a heaping teaspoon of sugar, doubled the garlic, used 1 can fire roasted tomatoes (delicious ) and added a tsp of dried basil. I also let it simmer with the rind of the Parmesan I used to make parm crisps. the sauce came together quickly and we all really enjoyed this sauce.

I turned this into a meat sauce, but didn't change the rest of the recipe much.  I read reviewers' suggestions & followed a few: added about 1/4 green bell pepper, about a Tbsp. of brown sugar, and more garlic.  I browned some ground beef, tossed in the finely minced onion & minced bell pepper & sauteed that. I then poured in the puree & cooked for a 1/2 hr.  I almost forgot--I used 2 Tbsp dried parsley since I didn't have any fresh. As a marinara, this is very good.  It needs some tweeking to turn into an awesome meat sauce.  I'll work on that next time around.
Increase onion, garlic and spices, add fresh basil, and add 1 Tbl brown sugar.  Excellent!  Will make again and again.

This was super easy and cheap compared to buying a quality marinara. I added some Italian sausage by cooking it separately then adding it to the sauce half way through. Really great recipe. Will definitely make this again.

This is a really good all purpose sauce. Thick and tangy like you expect from Marinara. I doubled it expecting it would be good (used a commerical size can of tomatos which was only 2.79) used half for a large lasagana and froze the rest. This would stand up to meatballs, pizza or just about any pasta dish. I have a VERY picky daughter and have problems finding sauces she will eat (no chunks) and she loved it. I will do this one again over and over.
This is the only Marinara sauce I use!!!. Only thing I do different is add more garlic because we love garlic a lot in my house. I often make a double batch and freeze some. Thank you for sharing!!

added 1/2 teaspoon of basil
1 teaspoon of itialan herb seasoning.
add and extra 1/2 clove of garlic.

This sauce is super easy and versatile. The texture is perfect, too. I added an extra clove of garlic, brown sugar and red pepper flakes. Next time I'd probably cut the oregano in half because I'm not a big fan of oregano. Will definitely make this again.
Good sauce, very easy to make. I did think there was too much wine which is why I did not give it five stars. Will be making again but with less wine.
YUMMY and EASY!

Super recipe.  Using it and variations to bottle gravy with the many, many tomatoes from Dad's garden.  Try adding ground beef and replacing oregano with dried crushed rosemary and basil for a tangy meat sauce.
Doubled the recipe, used San Marzano tomatoes and additional garlic.  Delicious!
This sauce was really good.  I served it with meatballs and everyone ate it up.  Thanks for the recipe.
Love this recipe!!! Its so easy but it taste like you took all day making it! I use brown suagr instead of white sugar.

Followed the directions to a T and is is the worst sauce I have ever made. Was excited to make it because of the reviews, but I had to doctor this up quite a bit for it to be eaten. Sorry. Won't make this again.

Wonderful! 
I did not have any cooking wine, but didn't need any extra liquid. In the future I will cut the pepper for my sensitive toddler, but otherwise won't change a thing!
This is one of the easiest recipes, but with the best flavor.  I will be making this often.

This Marinara Sause was great. My son had seconds.
I did not change a thing. It's a keeper, I wil make it again.
I thought the wine flavor was too overpowering.  I would definatley cut the wine amount down next time I make this.
Good. substituted apple juice for wine, made it just a little bit too sweet.  next time try 1/4 apple then maybe water?
I make this atleast once a month!  Goes great with the best meatball recipe.

I made this with fresh tomatoes since I didn't have canned. I blend the tomatoes and added it to a pan with some garlic and olive oil. I added the dried oregano, paste, parsley and wine but didn't have onions. I added some sugar and pepper flakes and it was good! I like the wine flavor. I'm going to try with the canned crushed tomatoes sometime soon.
Loved it! So easy to double the batch and freeze. I did add a bit more garlic and hamburg but wouldnt change a thing!

Delicious!! Changes I made (I reduced the count to 4 servings): 1) Used canned, diced tomatoes; 2) Didn't use a food processor, I like it chunky; 3) Added 1 tbsp fresh chopped basil; 4) Added 2 tsp sugar; 5) Added 2-3 tbsp chopped fresh mushrooms (that I sautéed with the onions). Superb.
Very good base recipe. Good consistancy. I doubled the garlic and replaced the parsley with basil. I also added a little sugar to cut down on the acidity.
This was just ok for me.  It seemed to lack some herbs or something.
This sauce was excellent. I don't cook with wine so like another review I used chicken broth in place of the wine. This was great with the chicken Parmesan by Chef John. This will be a regular dish.
This was great.  I will use again and again.  Loved the wine.

This is a great recipe! I made a few changes, which is why I'm only giving it four stars. First, I only use 3-4 TBSP of olive oil, six makes the sauce a little too oily. I also add red pepper flakes to make the sauce a little spicier (I don't measure this, I just throw them in) and around 1 TSP of sugar to cut the acidity of the tomatoes. As for the wine, I throw in 1/2 cup of whatever I have open; I've found that my favorite to use is Cabernet Sauvignon (but maybe because that's my favorite to drink). This can also turn into a fabulous bolognese simply by adding 1 lb of browned ground beef and doubling the recipe. This is truly a great sauce that I make at least twice a month. Thanks for the wonderful recipe!
This was delicious! I always cook sauces a lot longer then suggested, I cooked this for about 1.5 on low.

This sauce is delicious and so easy to make! I've put it in my Recipe Box and copied by hand into a book of favorite recipes. The only changes I made was to add 1 t. of dried basil and 1 TB brown sugar. I can stop looking for marinara recipes! Thank you, Jackie!

I'm rating this a 5 because the consistency is perfect; thick enough but not too much so that if one wanted to make a meatsauce out of it, the spoon would not stand up straight in the middle of the pot. Also a 5 star for ease of preparation and ingredients one tends to have on hand.  I did have to add 2 more cloves of garlic but I am a garlic lover.  1 clove just did not seem to do it justice.  I followed exactly and used a 'Mier's Winecellar white table wine'.  I added the 1/2 cup and it was not overpowering.  I love to cook w/wines but don't drink it and although I could taste it, it wasn't overpowering.  It seemed to enhance the flavor and didn't hinder it.  It also is a sweeter sort of wine so thought it would help with that sauce tartness thing we all try to fix.  I did have to add 1 Tbsp. of BROWN sugar and that took care of it.  **I recently saw on Food Network that if you use BROWN sugar in any redsauce, it helps with that tartness fix better than white.** Thanks for the great recipe.  I'm going to let it sit in fridge overnight and make eggplant parm. tomorrow.
Yummy!!! My kitchen smelled like a Italian restuarant. The only thing I did different was use red wine instead of white:)
I made a test batch of this and found it too sweet with an off taste. I let it meld overnight and it didn't help. I think it's the sugar in the stewed tomatoes. I won't be making this again

I was not very precise with my measurements and ended up using red wine, because it is what I had in hand. But this made an excellent sauce for my lasagna. I thought it would separate too much and make the lasagna water but it really did not. Quite easy and tasty.
Great! It was easy to make and tasted good. I left out the parsley and added an extra clove of garlic.

We absolutely love this sauce!  We use it for pizza and for pasta.  Ours varies with the ingredients we have in the house.  We use dried parsley, less oil, either onion soup mix or onion powder as we don't normally have fresh onion, and haven't used wine yet (simply because we don't have any in the house) and it turns out great!  It's the first marinara that the whole family loves!

Excellent sauce!  Like others, I did alter slightly.  Used 2 cans of petite-cut tomatoes, 1/2 tsp basil, no salt, 1/4 cup wine, and 1/2 tsp sugar.  I also tripled the garlic, used 3/4 cup onion, and 8 oz. mushrooms. I will never purchase pasta sauce again.  Thank you for an outstanding recipe!

Super yummy!! I have bought many brands of marinara sauce and have not found a single one that I overly like so I decided to try making my own and I absolutely loved this recipe. I did add some basil, crushed red pepper and 1/4 cup of white grape juice (instead of white wine) to make it more to my liking. I will never buy another jar of marinara sauce again.
Worked really well with my homemade meatballs!

Very good recipe! The hardest part about it was trying to get the cork out of the wine bottle! At another reviewer's suggestion I also used canned crushed tomatoes and I added a small can of no-salt tomato sauce. I used it as a sauce for eggplant parmesan (the recipe is also somewhere on this site) for myself and I reheated it as a dipping sauce for an Italian sausage sandwich with peppers for my boyfriend. I had leftovers, so I made a Bolognese-type sauce out of it for him and added some ground sirloin and more sausage. We both decided that it would be an excellent dipping sauce for mozzarella sticks too. Can't wait to make it again! (and will be researching mozzarella sticks on this site...) Thanks for sharing, Jackie!
Tasty and easy. I just dumped stuff in based on the recipe, used red wine, added more garlic of course, and some basil. I really liked the smooth consistency and was great to sop up with bread.

Simply amazing. Everyone who has tried this recipe LOVES it! I made some slight modifications: I do not add wine, and added 1/2 tsp. crushed red pepper flakes, and 2 tsp. Italian herb seasoning. I make it at least once a week!
This sauce is amazing!  I could drink this stuff.  The only change that we made was using 4 tsp of dried parsley instead of the fresh parsley.  I will definitely make this again!

I started off making this to the recipe apart from doubling the garlic. But after tasting I added 2t of sugar and some chopped fresh basil. I probably let this simmer for longer too, maybe 45 minutes to an hour. My daughters loved it. I will definitely be doubling this recipe in future, it's going to be very handy to have in the freezer. Thankyou Jackie.

Wow, this recipe was amazingly good!Everything about it was perfect. There were a few changes I made: I added 2 more cloves of garlic,(I'm a garlic lover),lots of fresh basil about 3 tablespoons,it adds a lot of flavor, and 1 hot red chili.With the changes I made it makes it a 10 or more! It's DELISH!
Absolutely a perfect recipe.  I guarantee your family will love it as much as my wife and two kids.  Good Luck.
This sauce was delicious. I added in the brown sugar like other reviewers and it was perfect. I will definitely make it again.
Amazing!! I added ground beef to it and saved portions for the freezer for a quick family meal.

Excellent tasting, and does not get much easier than this. Used this for baked ravioli parm, came out wonderfully. Varied slightly from the recipe though. Did not have fresh parsley, used dried. Also made the sauce the day before. I think many sauces (or soups and stews) have better flavor the next day. No more jar sauce here.
The only time I ever made marinara sauce I used this recipe.  It won the marinara contest at the local Italian fest.  I'm not even Italian.  What does THAT tell you?

I was feeling lazy, and just dumped all of these ingredients in my crockpot and let cook on low for 5 or 6 hours.  I don't mind a chunky sauce so I skipped all the pureeing and saute-ing.  It was good- I don't know about the "best" but that could be due to my unorthodox cooking method.  Still, it the flavor was good and it all disappeared.

Amazingly easy and good! My husband hates onions, so I left those out. I used crushed tomatoes instead of stewed, so that I could avoid the processor, and added a Tbsp. of brown sugar to counteract the acidity. (Stewed tomatoes include more sugar.) I am at a high altitude, so I cooked it all about 10 minutes longer. Just wonderful ... I'm happy to have this recipe!
Followed the original recipe except that we did NOT run it through a food processor or strainer.  We also cooked it for a few hours while we got ready to make the pasta.  Yum Yum!
I used fresh tomatoes - 16 of them.  It turned out very good and fresh tasting.
This was quite a good sauce.  I didn't measure the spices - just threw them in.  Also added mushrooms.  If you let it cook per the directions the parsley won't be so overpowering.
Fabulous!  I saute the onions first and add a tablespoon of brown sugar.  Perfect!
I did not like this at all.
Very handy easy recipe to have.

this was super-easy and great tasting.  your backsplash and washcloth will thank you, however, if you remember to put a lid on the pot... mine are still a little grouchy with me.  I did add a little brown sugar, but otherwise stuck to the recipe.  can't wait to make this with my own tomatoes this summer!
This was a pretty good sauce.  Not the best I ever had, but was good.  Will make again, as it was simple.

Fabulous!!! 2 small changes...used 4 cloves of garlic and red wine instead of white. I make huge batches and freeze. I will never use store bought again. It's so versatile, pizza, pasta, dipping sauce..even little triscuit pizza appetizers.
Oh my goodness, this was delicious. No changes. :)
This was good but I would not call it the best I have ever had.

NOMG so good.  i halved it, then added reconstituted textured vegetable protein to the sauce, then mixed whole wheat pasta into the sauce.  i didn't have parsley or tomato paste so I used some medium salsa, added 2x the amount of oregano and garlic.  i added a couple of splashes of white wine vinegar--didn't have the white wine.  I added some chile powder and cumin to give it a slight kick.

Loved this easy recipe! Very easy to freeze and use later. I used 4 tablespoons of olive oil rather than 6 and 1/4 cup of apple cider vinegar instead of 1/2 white wine. Tasted great! I would suggest starting with 1/8 cup of apple cider vinegar and tasting first before you add the remaining 1/8th cup as this flavor is very strong.
Absolutely delicious! Tastes just like something you'd be served at a restaurant. It has a very sophisticated taste. I used red wine instead of white, and it turned out lovely.

Quick, easy, and delicious.  I 4X the recipe and freeze it for future use.  I use Italian style stewed tomatoes with basil and garlic.  I also add the garlic in with the onions and saute them together.  I use fresh cracked pepper and I throw in a bay leaf as well.  It rivals any "homemade" sauce.

Yummy! I needed marinara for stromboli I made and so I tried this rather than running to the store. Quick and easy and WAY better than the ones I have bought in the store before. This one is a keeper!
Crazy Good!  Not only was it delicious but it looked nice too!!  Definitely company worthy, I'll be making this again and again.  Loved it!
Excellent sauce. No changes made and none needed. Would like to make again with all fresh herbs. Used in conjunction w/ “Little Lamb Meatballs in a Spicy Eggplant Tomato Sauce” on this site.
This is now my go to for marinara! I use any type of tomatoes, as long as thy are from my garden. This is delicious...
Great recipe! I did as others suggested and let it simmer for 2hrs.

Didnt have the flavor I was anticipating.

Wow, this was really good, and ridiculously easy.  I'm not sure exactly how much garlic I put, but it was probably more than one clove, because I'm a garlic fan.  Same with the black pepper.  I served it with linguine and would certainly make it again.

Very Good! I will double it next time. I did  just 3 T of oil, used 1 heaping T dried parsley because I forgot to get fresh, added around a Tablespoon of white sugar and I few shakes of Italian seasoning. I didn't think there was a strong wine taste. I used Barefoot Pinot Grigio.  The stewed tomatoes give it a great flavor and sauciness.
Very simple and Easy just the way I like it. Rich in color and flavor.

This was the BEST and easiest sauce I have ever made. I added some pesto and used flat gingerale instead of white wine and was super impressed. Thank you for this awesome recipe! I will use it forever.

The sauce was very delicious. Though, i didn't read correctly at first;

i made it for meatball sub. both me and my husband enjoyed it.
2/6/11 - Easy to make - good thick flavorful sauce.  Used for dipping meatballs

This was so easy and so good! I made this in a lasagna. I used merlot and diced canned tomatoes because that's all I had. I don't have a food processor so I used my blender and it worked great. The only change I might make next time is using less olive oil; I love cooking with olive oil, but 6 tbs is a lot. This recipe is a keeper and would taste great on pizza and so many other Italian dishes. Why use yucky jar sauce when you can make this? Thanks Jackie!
Very good.
I don't know why everyone thought this was so great!
Very good!  Easy to make.  Followed recipe to a "T"!
This was a very good sauce. I am very picky about them and this really is almost 5 star worthy. It is missing something but still tastes great.
This sauce is fantastic!  I added a tablespoon of sugar...it's perfect!

Wonderful! I used chicken broth instead of white wine because i am not yet at the legal age where i can buy wine and also the stewed tomatoes i got the italian type. Also the store had no parsley but since use the italian blend it made up for that. I will make this again

Very delicious! This was my first try at from-scratch marinara sauce, and we love it. I've made it twice now and both times I've been surprised at how easy it is. The consistency is perfect. I thought this recipe was just so so.  It was better the second day but still needed something added to make it great.
Very simple and lovely recipe. everything i would always have on hand.

The title ofor this recipe does not make it justice. This is the perfect marinara sauce. I can't believe that I haven't reviewed this until now. I make this in triple batches with no tweaking. We tried this last week and were really happy w/the outcome.  Will make again for sure!
This was really good. I would recommend leaving some of the onions chunky, and maybe adding some green peppers and mushrooms. Recommended!

This was very good and easy.  I added more garlic and onion just b/c I'm a huge fan of the two.  I threw it all in the crock pot and cooked on low for about 6 hours. Great!  I like to add some basil.  I've found it turns out a little watery if I leave some tomato chunks in the sauce, but its fine if I blend it completely.
Very tasty, easy sauce.  Made with Fast and Friendly Meatballs.  I added some extra garlic to this, but otherwise stayed pretty close to the recipe.
I thought this sauce was spectacular! I didn't have any tomato paste but it still came out great. I also prefer red wine to white so I used that instead. I will be using this recipe again!
Very Good.  I didn't make any changes and we all enjoyed it.  I will make it again.

WOW, this was so flavorful!!  I have a standby sauce I use for most pasta recipes BUT this may have to replace it!  My only change was using red wine in place of the white (was out).  I did use FRESH parsley and oregano which really makes this taste so great.  I used this sauce on the "Lasagna Roll Ups" recipe from this site.
Did too much doctoring to list it all here, but very good base. Added meatballs and served over linguine.

I don't cook often. And by "often" I mean "ever." When my mom asked me to make chicken parmesan tonight, my first thought was "Wha?" I'll definitely use it again.
Very good. The white wine gives it a nice flavor. It doesn't make much so I double the recipe.
This was really good.  I added red pepper flakes to heat it up a bit.  Good stuff--Thank you!

Just by virtue of its simplicity and versatility this is by far the best marinara sauce I have ever made. Whether you choose to doctor it up a bit or not you can't beat this if you're looking for just a basic sauce.  Superb!

Thanks so much for this recipe. This is my base gravy recipe that I always use (I'm using it tonight). I don't put anything in the food processor, though. Yum!

Wow! Making it now... just took a little taste while it's simmering. Best sauce I've ever tasted, or is it gravy? Whatever you call it, this recipe is perfection!

Wonderful recipe I will never buy store bought again!! Thank you!
Made this sauce to go with gnocci and it was delicious! I added a little brown sugar to get rid of the acidic flavour.

Amazing, I added 4oz of fresh basil leaves and like other reviews 1 tbs of brown sugar. Simply amazing.

Next time I'll use 1/3 cup of white wine and all should be fine.

This was a wonderful sauce. I did add additional garlic and used fresh herbs. Per other reviewer's added a touch of brown sugar. My whole family loved, loved, loved it! Thanks Jackie for a great marinara.
I loved it but I used 2cans of (Diced Tomatoes Italian) with Basil,Garlic and Oregano.It was the BEST I my Husband and Son loved it.

I doubled the garlic, added a teaspoon of basil, cut the oil in 1/2, added a tablespoon of brown sugar and cut the white wine down to 1/3 of a cup.  Very good!
followed almost exactly.  great flavor...doubled the garlic (never too much garlic) halfed the oil.  great recipe thanks so much.  this will be a staple in my recipe box

Wonderful Marinara sauce base!  As with all recipes, each cook 'tweaks' a recipe to his/her personal taste.  I found the sauce base to be very flavorable and easy to assemble.   I alway double my sauce  recipe so I can freeze any "left-overs". As we LOVE garlic, onion and bell peppers, I finely chop one large onion, finely mince and crush six of the largest garlic cloves I have, and chop one bell pepper.  I add the veggies to a large pot with 2 to 3 TBS of EVOO; saute all of them until soft, about 5 minutes. Then, I add to the pot: two 28-ounce cans of whatever type of canned tomatoes I have on hand, one 12-ounce can tomato paste, 1 cup white or red wine, 1 cup of grated Mozzarella, 1/2 cup of grated Parmesan, 4 TBS of fresh (or 2 TBS dried) parsley, 4 TBS fresh (or 2 TBS dried) Oregano, 2 TBS fresh (or 1 TBS dried) Basil, 1/2 tsp dried Marjoram, 1/2 dried Rosemary,  1/2 tsp dried Thyme, 1 large dried Bay leaf, 1 tsp Red Pepper Flakes, 2 TBS brown sugar, salt and black pepper to taste. REMEMBER: WHEN USING DRIED HERBS (except the Bay Leaf), ALWAYS RUB THEM BETWEEN PALMS OF HANDS WHILE ADDING TO POT, AS THIS "WAKES" THE HERBS UP AGAIN. Bring sauce to boil over medium heat: turn down to low and continue simmering for at least 30 minutes, stirring occassionally. However, simmering longer lets all the flavors "meld" more. Remove Bay Leaf before serving sauce as Bay Leaf is very bitter.
