Thank you Jackie! Great sauce and so easy.  I couldn't believe that such a simple sauce could be so good.  I used 3 roasted garlic cloves, a 1/4 teaspoon of fennel seed, and a tablespoon of brown sugar.  It's the best.  No more jarred stuff for me. I forgot to say I also add 2 leaves of fresh basil.  Update:  the 1st time I made this I did not measure parsley and it was delicious.  I find measuring amount to too much parsley and the sauce is bitter.
Excellent!  I used 3 cloves sof garlic and added some basil.  Let it simmer for 2 hours.  Will never use jarred sauce again!

The name says it all!  Really!  It is the best marinara sauce and it's so easy to make.  My mom cooks hers all day and it doesn't compare (sorry mom!)  I think the white wine is what makes this recipe and i add alittle bit more than it calls for.  Delicious and healthy!

I loved this super easy and tasty sauce.  I of course made some minor adjustments, they were as follows: Used 2 cans Diced Tomatoes (1 regular, 1 w/basil, oregano & garlic), only used 2 Tbs. olive oil, added a little extra salt, added a little dried basil & some red pepper flakes, cayenne pepper instead of regular black pepper, added 2 garlic cloves and 1 Tb brown sugar. Did not put in the food processor. Simmered for 30 minutes, adjusted seasoning and simmered a few hours more.  I then put about 3/4 of the sauce in the blender, pureed and mixed in with the 1/4 of the chunky sauce.  It really tasted so fresh, was easy easy easy and soooo much better then store bought.  Thanks for a great recipe :-)

Excellent! It has a thick, complex taste-needs no meat. I did sub chicken broth for wine and added
basil(because I love basil).

I really enjoyed this sauce, it was fun to make and not difficult like I thought making my own sauce would be. I did vary the recipe a little - more garlic, red pepper flakes, extra pepper, chilli powder and some sugar. Thanks alot for the great recipe, I am making it today for my inlaws 30th anniversay dinner
Easy and awesome!

Excellent sauce!  Very little effort goes into this great recipe that tastes like it comes from a fine Italian restaurant.  I have made countless batches since I first tried this, and everyone always wants the recipe.  I usually make multiple batches at once, then divide and freeze in plastic storage containers.  Thanks so very much for this great recipe!  PS- We love it with "The Best Meatballs" from this site too!

This is an amazing recipe...I added an extra 8 oz can of crushed tomatoes to have a little extra sauce.  I also added, about a spoonful of sugar, a tablespoon of butter, crushed red peppers to give it a bit of a kick....This was FANTASTIC!

INCREDIBLE! I pretty much followed the recipe to a t, but I threw in extra garlic because that's always a good idea. I've always kind of made up my own recipe for marinara before, and it was as good or better than anything I'd had before so I figured I'd done a pretty good job. But THIS recipe... my husband and I couldn't stop eating this out of the pan. It will definitely replace my old recipe.

4 stars as written. 5 stars with these hints:  triple the garlic & use large cloves, use only 3 T olive oil, add two bay leaves, and start with the most delicious jarred tomatoes - Del Monte Garden Select Petite Diced Tomatoes with Basil, Garlic & Oregano. THIS IS THE ULTIMATE MARINARA WITH MY CHANGES! We mmm and ooh throughout each bite, every time we make it. Fresh parsley is a must. Double the recipe when you make it!
Not terrible....not good.  Won't make again.  Too sweet or something.

I've made this a few times now and some experimenting has made it much more to my liking. I found that stewed tomatoes were too sweet so I use strained crushed tomatoes that you can usually find in the Italian section of the ethnic foods aisle or near the pasta sauces. I use a little brown sugar to balance out the tartness. I use about 4 or 5 times the amount of dried oregano and 3 or 4 dried bay leaves. I also use about 5 or 6 cloves of garlic and half of a large onion that I finely dice in the food processor. Finally, instead of regular salt I use a combination of celery salt and soy sauce. The soy sauce is a trick from a food network show, and I find that celery salt always goes well with tomato sauces.

Very delicious! We wanted to make spaghetti for dinner and we had no marinara sauce, this recipe I found went the best with what ingredients I had. I changed around some things..  Instead of 2 14.5oz cans of stewed tomatos, I used 1 28oz can of diced tomatos, and I used 1 8oz can of tomato sauce instead of the 6oz. It's all I had in the pantry.  I didn't have any garlic cloves so I used 2 tbsp of Fresh Finds chopped dried garlic.  Used 1 1/2 tsp of oregano, instead of iodized salt I used sea salt. And instead of olive oil for the onions I used vegetable oil, I used 4 tbsp, definitley could've used less.. maybe 2-3?  And for my wine I used Fair Banks California White Port.. And I used a little under 1/2 Cup.  Everyone one loved it! Definitely the BEST yet.  Oh and it for sure needs 1 tbsp of brown sugar.. I tasted it without the sugar and I could feel the tart on my tongue..
This sauce was okay as is. Good starter. I like red wine with my red sauces. Personal prefrence.

I doubled this recpe but made the following changes.  I added 20 oz Turkey Italian Sausage and used 3 cloves of garlic.  I also just used 1 chopped large onion and only 6 oz of Pinot Grigio.  This is a great sauce!  I am glad I doubled it because no I have some to freeze :-)

This is a lovely (and fast) sauce, Jackie. I made a few changes though. I used diced tomatoes, upped the garlic, added about a teaspoon of basil, and used a can of tomato sauce so I could simmer a little longer.  Oh, I also threw in a bay leaf and a smidge of brown sugar.  With your basic recipe and the kind suggestions of other reviewers, I ended up with a lovely sauce.  This definitely goes in the "keeper" file.  Thanks again!
After trying many recipes for marinara sauce this is my favorite.  Not only is it simple but it is sooooo good!
My whole family lives this, I served it over homemade pasta.  Perfect!  I did use a red Cabernet wine, we enjoyed the flavor,  but we are Cabernet drinkers.

I have made this twice. The first time, exactly as written and it was great!
The second time, I only had 1 can of sauce and to make up for the 2nd can, I took a can of diced, fire roasted tomatoes & pureed them. I didn't have fresh parsley, so I used 2T of dried, only have the can of tomato paste and 1 cup of white wine and it was even better.
I paired it up with homemade meatballs and a green salad.
Both times I added about 3-4 T of brown sugar.
Quick, easy and very forgiving recipe.
Thank you!!!

I liked this sauce, but I would probably omit the wine or use a dryer wine next time.  I used a Finger Lakes Riesling, it added an odd flavor for some reason.  My boyfriend really liked it, though, so maybe it's just my taste.
I used fresh tomatoes and roasted them with onions and garlic before pureeing and putting them in instead of the canned tomatoes.  ITs very delicious!  I also added a bit of sugar.
Very good however next time I wouldn’t use as much wine.
This marinara sauce is good for all your red sauce needs. Loved it!
This is a great base for anything that needs a tomato base.  I tweek it and always add more olive oil to make it rich and delish.
added half an onion, a dozen cloves of garlic and a cup of fresh basil... with a doubled recipe. Awesome. Thank you.
Thank you Jackie. This sauce is great. I make it a lot, and always get rave reviews!

This was a good quick sauce, but it wasn't the best.  Personally I thought it tasted too tomato-ey.  I added brown sugar, fresh parsley, basil, italian seasoning and a bay leaf but nothing helped.  Maybe it was the brand tomatoes I used, but I will most likely not try this again.  Thank you for sharing, I did receive rave reviews on my stuffed shells, I was just personally disappointed in the sauce.

Great, basic sauce, very quick and simple to put together.  It takes as much effort to make a little as to make a lot, so make a lot and freeze what you don't use straight away.  The only modifications I've made to this recipe is using more garlic (partly because there's never too much garlic, and partly because authentic marinara sauce uses lots), and omitting the tomato paste.  Tomato paste is only for long-simmered, sturdy winter sauces, and without it, this sauce is light and lively, which is how I like my sauce most of the time.
I love this recipe.. it is now my standard red sauce.. i add a lot of parsley.  Thanks for the recipe!
This was really flavorful; will definitely make it again.
PERFECT!!!  Served it with linguine noodles and it was a HUGE hit!
Substituted Ginger Ale for the white wine, but don't use too much otherwise it turns out too runny.  Easy, fast, and delicious sauce to make.  Plus I've found it's cheaper than the jar stuff.
One of the best Marinara sauces I've ever tried. I used about half the recommended oil and I doubled up the garlic. I've used it with cannelloni and grilled mozzarella sandwiches. Yummy!!

This is a great base recipe that produces a perfect consistency--no watery puddle under the pasta!
My wife is Italian (I'm German), and she said she liked this recipe more than her grandma's!
I agree with most of the reviewers that suggest 1) less olive oil, as 6 tablespoons is too much. I'd go with 4; 2) Add 1 tablespoon of sugar to help cut down the acidity; and 3) More garlic. I went with 3 grated cloves.
Beyond that, I'd add more salt (maybe double?). But you can judge that by tasting the sauce as it simmers.

This tasted great, and smelled so good while cooking, and was very very smooth. I made this with the Hearty Vegetable Lasagna, and got great reviews. The only thing I would say about this sauce is that it looks a little bland, since it's so smooth, and if I was using just that over pasta, I would definately add some vegetables. But in lasagna, wow, it was perfect!! =)
This is 'our' marinara sauce from now on.  Devine!

Perfect! I used for a catering gig. I did some things out of order. I sautéed onion, carrots, and celery, then added Campari tomatoes till soft, then tomato paste, then the wine. I then followed every step, except I added more garlic and some basil. Slow simmered for an hour or so.

Wonderful, thank you!  I didn't think that the addition of the tomato paste made the final product heavy, just gave it a more complex flavor.  My 3 year old little girl is in a light eating phase, but she chowed down on this.  Thanks for the recipe, it's a keeper!
I added a pinch of sugar to recipe to remove bitter taste! Thanks for recipe.
Very simple but delicious recipe. I may buy never jar sauce again. I like my sauces a little spicey added extra clove of garlic to food processer  and 1/4 tsp of red pepper flakes to sauteing onions,
A great recipe, adult tastes that are kid-approved.
The whole family loved it. My friend owns a restaurant and this sauce rivals his. Sub; cooking sherry for white wine.Use Delmonte stewed tomatoes.
Add a little sugar & this is great!  Anyone that would pick any jarred sauce over this has no taste buds!  Thank you Jackie!

My kids love this, no more jarred sauce for us.  They were ready to eat it cold!  I used chicken stock, no wine on hand, and I also used a stick blender to mix it all up.  No need for the food processor, sauted onions, add everything else and pulse a few times and sauce is on!  Excellent.

I loved this recipe so much that I am posting another review of 5 stars. I'm from an italian background and this is an amazing sauce for how easy it was to make. I've made others that were 2x the wrok and don't even compare..BRILLIANT recipe. Thank you.
Absolutely amazing!
I did not like this sauce.  It had too much oil in it, and I did not like the flavor.  I wouldn't make this again.

A great sauce.  It is very easy to make and hardly takes up any time at all.  The only problem, in my opinion, is that it needs a little more taste.  A bite.  Maybe at some cilantro or something to give it a little kick.  Just as Emerial say......we have to KICK IT UP A NOTCH!!!!

This sauce is AWESOME! I doubled the garlic, added a tsp of dried basil and pureed muchrooms to put in too. It goes great with "Florentine Stuffed Chicken" (on allrecipes). I cooked the sauce in the crockpot from around lunch until dinnertime and it was super tasty (I am also a big crokpot fan). Thanks for the recipe!!!
great for spaghetti - but nothing else. And one tip - red wine is also really good instead of white wine and  I boiled it a bit and it was best sauce for spaghetti i have ever made!

Easy and delicious - this is now one of my staple recipes!  I substitute Italian seasoning for the oregano and I dump in more garlic to suit my personal taste.  Red wine is also good in this recipe, and I usually decrease the olive oil to about 4 Tbsp.  I also add about a tablespoon of chili powder for some heat.  I use this recipe about once every two weeks, and everyone loves it!  It also freezes well.  Thank you, Jackie!
Loved this sauce.  Added fresh basil and more garlic, as well.

This is the first time I've been able to make a red sauce that I liked! Personally I had to add more spice because the initial recipe was too sweet for my personal taste, but that is more personal preference than anything. I added more garlic, bay leaf, and a little more oregano and cooked it a little longer.
Absolutely delicious! My husband made this tonight with homemade meatballs.  Sooooo good!
This was fantastic! I have tried many many marinara recipes and this one is by far the best.

This recipe was wonderful. I had fresh tomatoes and herbs from my garden that I had to use or lose, so I substituted fresh tomatoes for the can of stewed and used all fresh herbs (oregano, basil, rosemary, parsley). At the suggestion of other reviewers, I upped the spices to my family's taste. I recommend starting with this recipe and then tasting as you go - very easy to make adjustments as you go along. 
However, I would DEFINITELY take the advice of others and cut the oil in half. I did not cut the oil and my sauce had too much.
I make this with 'ParmesanChicken' from this site and the whole family loves it. Very tasty.

delicious! I totally loved it. I used it in chicken parm and it was perfect. I added a few more cloves of garlic (4 cloves) and I reduced the wine by 1/4 cup. I also sautéed the garlic together with the onion. towards the end, I added about 1/2 tablespoon of brown sugar to counteract the slight acidity of the tomatoes. I'm thinking I'll be using this again for my meatball recipe.

This sauce is like Baby Bear, it's "just right"! I've made many, and most are too thin or too chunky. This sauce's combination of canned tomatoes and tomato paste yields the perfect consistency. I have to admit, I changed the recipe to use ingredients I had on hand. I used a 28oz can of San Marzano whole tomatoes, the tomato paste, about 1 tablespoon homemade Italian seasoning in place of the parsley/oregano, 3 cloves of garlic (because if some garlic is good, a lot is better), about 2 tablespoons dried minced onions, salt, black pepper, olive oil, and whoops!, didn't even realize it was supposed to have wine. I blended it all in my food processor and cooked it as directed. It was a bit too acidic for my taste, so I added about 1 teaspoon brown sugar. So let's say this recipe was my inspiration. The Dude said it was the best marinara he's ever had, and I have to agree. We like it better than Chef John's tomato sauce! Served over spicy beef & sausage ravioli, it was pasta perfection.
Excellent and so much easier than the marinara recipe I have made for years.  This is my new go -to recipe.

Made this recipe and it is excellant, added more garlic and simmered for 2 hours , served it over chicken parmesan and spag noodles. Lots of compliments from friend. Next time I will make a double batch and freeze some
This is my "go to " recipe ! It's so easy to make and always tastes so fresh.

very yummy! I added fresh basil since I have it growing and some brown sugar as I do to any tomato sauces and I actually used RED WINE instead of white because red is all I ever have on hand. I think I put more onion than the recipe calls for and minced garlic too. (I didnt have parsley so that was skipped as well) 

It was so good, I cant wait to make this again. The left overs were even great spooned over toast and eaten up with a knife and fork! The flavours go through even more the next day. I can't tell you how good this is... I hope someone reading this tries it!!

This was my 1st homemade sauce I have ever made.  And it was easy and so great.  I used 4 cloves of garlic cause I love garlic and it could have used more.  I also added basil.  This is so great goodbye jar sauce

I loved it.  I also like to add 2 T of simple syrup (to cut the acid) and 2 T of balsamic vinegar to add a little more depth of flavor.  For additional taste and vitamins, I add a small can of carrots (drained) when blending up the tomatos.  Excellent!

Made this tonight for dinner.  Really good fresh tasting sauce.  I found the olive oil to be a bit excessive.  I cut back and still ended up taking a paper towel to the top of the sauce to soak up some excess oil.  Like some others, I added some basil to taste.  Also used chicken broth instead of wine.

This was great.  Much thicker sauce than I thought it would be.  I used crushed tomatoes, 2T dried parsley, about 3 cloves garlic, omitted white wine, added 1T sugar, and 1/2t sweet basil.  My husband thought it needed to be a little more sweet so next time I will add 1.5 to 2T sugar.  I threw all this in a crock pot on low for 5 hours.  Easy, simple, and delicious.  This served only 4 servings in my family.  Thanks for the recipe.
This sauce was great, and i will be using it a lot in Italian dishes. Thanks!
Great recipe, nice flavor.  I used only half of the olive oil and it was fine.  Will make for many more years.  Thanks for a great recipe.
This sauce is a lifesaver! Very easy and delicious!!
I followed the recipe exactly.  I didn't care for it and was disappointed, however I did have two of my dinner guests think it was the best they had ever tasted.
This is the BEST marinara sauce EVER!!

Great flavour and texture! I read the reviews and made the following changes: 1. I added 1 tbsp of brown sugar 2. I didn't have any white wine on hand so I used chicken stock 3. I added and extra clove of garlic 4. I used half the amount of olive oil to saute the onions. Since everything was going into the food processor, I didn't bother mincing the garlic or chopping the parsley. Finally, I used a half recipe of Italian Stewed Tomatoes (from this site) instead of canned tomates. Very yummy!

This sauce takes some time to make but it is worth it.  Next time, I will add a little sugar.  I did not add any salt.  Will keep this one around for sure. Made this to go with "chicken parmesan casserole" from this site.
Yummy, and sooo easy!  I served this as a dipping sauce for toasted ravioli last night, it got rave reviews, thanks so much Jackie!
This was delicious! I added a little more garlic, but other than that, a keeper!
I followed these instructions to the letter but found that the final product needed sugar. So I did add 2 tbsp of sugar. I'll make it again.
Love this sauce. It is my go to sauce for all pasta dishes. Haven't used store bought since I started making this!
Delicious!  Added basil and meatballs.

Very good for lasagna and other baked dishes.

I omitted the salt, used 2 cloves of garlic, and added a tbsp of sugar at the end as others have suggested.  I also like to blend or process tomato sauces after they're done (and cooled) and refrigerate overnight.  They always seem to taste better the next day.

This is delicious!  I made a slightly healthier version by using 'no salt added' tomatoes and paste, then added just a little sea salt.  Really lets the flavors of the herbs come through.  So easy to make -- dinner was one the table in 30 minutes.  How cool is that??

Wonderful sauce!  My fiance gave it a 5, which he rarely gives (usually 4 or 4.5).  I had it with meatballs, added a little basil, and didn't have any wine so had to use chicken broth.  Next time I will try the wine.  Thank you for the recipe!

I cooked up some sausage with onion and garlic then added all the ingredients (added Italian Seasoning v. just oregano and used Italian-style stewed tomatoes). Did not add the olive oil (why so much?) - did not run thru the food processor either (too busy or too lazy...hmmm)- simmered and then set on the stove during baseball practice and wahlaaa - came out great - my husband loved it! Also added fresh basil and served over penne. Thanks! Easy!!
I've made homemade sauce many times and have been disappointed.  But not this time.  This sauce is wonderful!
It was ok, but I have had better out of a jar.  :(
This was delicious!  I added basil...because I'm a basilaholic and some crushed red pepper...because I like a little kick.  Thank you!

Just made this for a lasagna. forgot all about the wine, but as is, the sauce is great, full of flavor and love the fresh parsley.Next time I'll experiment a little with this recipe, just to make it my own, and give it a little heat. Thanks so much for sharing! =)

One of the best sauces I have ever had. Very easy to make. And the whole house smells wonderfully of garlic and spices!!! 
HMMM... add 1/4 cup of whipping cream for an amazing cream sauce!! with chicken on angel hair pasta - wow!!

This is sooo good! I made a couple modifications.!I doubled the garlic and added a tbsp of brown sugar. I used canned diced tomatoes (organic ones from Costco) and didn't use the blender. I just squished the tomatoes with my hand as I poured them out of the can. Sooo good! I made a quadruple batch last time and froze the extra in gallon freezer bags (portioned so I could defrost for two dinners). Oh, and I also sautéed the chopped garlic with the onions and olive oil. I waited till the onions were almost done cooking before I added the garlic. That way the garlic didn't burn.
Really good. Made it for spaghetti squash. Yummy

First time to make homemade marinara sauce and this recipe is the best. I will never buy again. I didn't have white wine so I used red one. I don't like tomato paste so I used fresh tomato, tomato sauce and I put one table spoon of ketchup. It is just lovely. By the way I made as a pizza sauce.

This was a decent marinara, but it had a bitter taste and the wine flavor was too strong.  I felt like I was drinking a glass of wine while eating marinara sauce.  Next time, I'll use less wine and a little sugar.
Definitely a good everyday marinara. My family has an old Sicilian recipe that we make for special occasions, but this one will do for quick pasta bakes and meatball subs.
This is the best and simpelist recipe ever.  I did add some basil , crushed red pepper and a bit more garlic.  My husband is a meat eater so Half the sauce i put some beef in and he loved it!
This is without a doubt the most flavorful spagettie sauce I have ever made!  It just melts in your mouth.  A big hit at home.  Thanks!
This is really good.  I add ground turkey meat to give it some umph.
I enjoy this so much...I could just drink it!

We made this to go on a meatball sandwich, and it was pretty darn good. The white wine taste was a bit strong to me, so next time I'll use chicken stock instead. It was also too acidic, so I added a teaspoon or so of sugar to mellow things out. That made a huge difference. Overall, though, it was a quick and delicious recipe! I'll be making it again.
This was great!  I omitted the white wine and used tomato sauce instead of tomato paste, just because that's what I had on hand.  Excellent!!
Really easy to make! DELICIOUS! I added some mushrooms and green peppers for texture!
This was super easy and we enjoyed it with our cheese sticks. I really like the flavor the wine added. Thanks for the great recipe.
Delicious and easy! I chopped up half a green pepper and added it to the mix. This marinara tastes very fresh, and waaaaaay better than jarred sauce. Next time I will double it and freeze some. Yum!

I give this 3 stars because the directions are different than the ingredients, i.e. Italian tomatoes instead of Stewed, and Tomato sauce instead of paste.  There's a huge different between sauce and paste, especially.  I used paste and the pasta sauce was too acidic.   When using paste there should be some addition of water, and I didn't put enough water in the recipe.

1st time attempting homemade sause and it came out great. Like everyone else I added my own touched. Added some hot sausage, used organic crushed tomatoes as opposed to stewed. Halfed the paprike and added an equal amount of basil. No oregano on hand :( so I used italian seasoning. And I added a bit of hot cracked pepper plus doubled up on the garlic. Came out great!  Will make this Sunday for sure.
Extremely good and easy to make, however I accidentally burned my onions a bit…can be made without a food processor
Luv it!

This was great sauce. I like adding wine to the recipe. I also added mushrooms sauted with the onions. It was great. I have made this a few times now. Combined it yesterday for Christmas with the "Baked Ziti I" and everyone loved it.
Great recipe for winter when garden fresh tomatoes aren't around!  Perfect as is!
So amazing!  This sauce was spectacular.  I used a Pinot Grigio and it was fantastic!  I will absolutely make this again and again!  Thank you!
Best marinara I've had to date.  a tsp of sugar and mushrooms and make it even better.
Great basic sauce and easy to tweak for your family's taste. I often double it and cook in my slow cooker!
No more buying canned sauce!  This recipe is really good and so fast and easy to make.  I froze the left over sauce, and when I reheated it, it was even better.  Thanks Jackie!

I've made this recipe a few times, tastes great.  I changed a few things up; I also added more onion, less wine, basil and more garlic.  Biggest change though is I use chunky style crushed tomatoes (pastene makes a great one) instead of the stewed tomatoes.  You get a much heartier sauce and the entire italian family loves it!
Super! I use it for everything that needs a red suace. Pizza, spagehetti, chicken parmesean etc

I have made this many times. The flavor is delicious and fresh tasting. I double the amount of garlic and add fresh basil. I saute the garlic with the onion and then pour all other ingredients in the pan. Then I use an immersion blender to blend all together. I have a double batch simmering right now and my house smells incredible! Thank you for a great recipe!
To say this is the best red sauce ever is just plain silly. BUT it is good. BUT not better, or certainly easier, than the better jarred brands.
I like how simple and easy this recipe is but, like other reviewers, find it a bit too acidic.  I even let it sit overnight to see if it mellowed any and it didn't.  Not sure that I'll make it again.

I didn't think that this was going to turn out that great, but it was really good! I was really surprised since while cooking it, I didn't think it smelled that great. I omitted the 1/2 cup white wine and instead used a 1/2 cup white grape juice. The initial recipe didn't make up that much, so next time I'll double the recipe. Tastes even better the second day!
Oh.  My.  God.  This really IS the best marinara sauce yet.  I added an extra clove or two of garlic and a little bit of brown sugar, and received RAVE reviews from many, many taste buds.

Great sauce....made a few changes.  Added 2-3 garlic cloves and extra red pepper flakes (probably about 1/2 tsp.).  Also added a bay leaf and then if bitter added a titch of salt.  Just made it again and this time made four times the amount.  Still turned out great.
Nice sauce but I did modify it a little.  I added a whole medium onion, 1 extra can of diced tomatoes, 2 tsp. sugar and splash of cinnamon.  Turned out great!
Great recipe!! I added veggies and it made a great spaghetti sauce. Loved it!

Very good sauce.  I added some brown sugar to counter the tang from the tomatoes & wine.  It did seem like it was missing something, though.  I may add a touch of chili powder or some fresh herbs next time to adjust the flavor.  But it was still very good.
Very easy to make with on-hand ingredients.  Only change is I let it simmer about an hour. Excellent. Used in on a Meatball Bake recipe I found on-line.

I love this recipe because it's so easy and so delicious. I did have to make some substitutes though. I used crushed tomatoes, not stewed. I also add 1 tsp basil, 1/2 Tbsp salt, 1 Tbsp sugar, and usually use less olive oil than it calls for because I don't like it too oily. It is a good base to add onto with good proportions, which is why I gave it 4 stars. But honestly, who doesn't tweak pasta sauce to suit their own tastes??

My wife says it tastes better than the store brands.  Costco has #10 cans of peeled tomatoes for $2.69.  That's 6 and a half pounds.  I just made another 8 containers of 16 oz each for the freezer.  They will be gone in a month or less.  This sauce I make "plain" and jazz it up to suit what I am fixing.  Really a good recipe, really good flavor and really easy to change and adapt.  Try it!  You will like it!

Great marinara!  I halved the recipe since I didnt need as much.  Instead of pureeing, I just added the stewed tomatoes whole since I wanted it chunky.  After the sauce simmers a bit the tomatoes tend to break down anyways.  I also added more garlic, a little basil, and red wine instead of white.  This was great over top of some chicken parm that I was making!  It would be great over lots of other recipes as well.  Thanks so much for the great and easy recipe!  I will make many times more!
By far the best and easiest Marinara out there.  The only thing I add is more garlic...but I always add more garlic.  A huge crowd favorite and easy to double also.
Very easy! Nice tangy sauce! I also eliminated the food processor, used a 28 oz can of crushed tomatoes and combined all ingredients in the pan.  Added a few red pepper flakes.  Yum!
YUM, I totally forgot about the wine and it still turned out great. Love the fact that there is not sugar in it.
fast & good

I've made this recipe a few times now, and it's ALWAYS a hit! The second time, I drained the stewed tomatoes and it was PERFECTION! It gave me a bit thicker consistancy, which I prefer. I do up the garlic content quite a bit, and took a tip from a previous reviewer adding brown sugar. Those are the only changes I make, and this is now my staple recipe for sauce. Yesterday, I made and froze about 16 quarts!!!! Yes, it's THAT good!
ABSOLUTELY AMAZING!!  I tweeked it a little by leaving out one can of tomatoes and keeping the rest of the recipe the same.  It makes it very flavorful!

Excellent. Puts jarred sauces to shame. I decreased the oil to 4 tablespoons, and after reading other reviews, used an additional clove of garlic and used italian seasoning liberally. I used sweet Reisling wine and a touch of brown sugar to decrease the acidity. It was excellent fresh made, but when I tried it again, I let sit overnight as other reviewers suggested, and I concur. The stewed tomatoes gave such a wonderful flavor.  I used the original recipe tomatoes but I also saw Italian recipe.  I was afraid the Italian migh have competing flavors.  The only change I made was to use more garlic- 2 large cloves.  I am eating the leftovers today and it is even better. Cant wait to use it on eggplant parm.  Thanks a bunch!!

This was good, but it was great when I cooked the garlic and the onions first.  I also blended only some of the tomatoes and smashed up the others with my hands.  This helped the sauce be a little more chunky instead of a puree all of the way through.  YUM

I was looking for a quick pasta sauce to make for my bf's birthday - something simple but tasty and this was fantastic! I had never made my own sauce and I was so pleased. Will make this again and again.

Great recipe and super easy. 

In addition, I added:
3 anchovies (canned in oil, about 1 tablespoon mashed)
1 red pepper (needed to use it, and it added some sweetness)
1/2 cup chicken broth instead of wine
Used 1 whole onion because I love onions
Used a bit more garlic, probably 2-3 cloves, because garlic is delicious
Also used dried parsley instead of fresh as it is all I had
Added about 10 small fresh basil leaves at the end just before serving. 

Note: If you can use good quality San Marzano tomatoes for this, I highly suggest it! 


AMAZING. Simmered on low for about 50 minutes because it's so thick that it splatters a lot. Make sure you have a lid and are wearing long sleeves!
Great sauce! Easy to make. You can really taste the wine though...but that's ok I love wine :)
Everyone is the house gave this a 10!  This was so easy to make. I will be making this again and again.

Quick, easy and delicious! This is a very versatile sauce. The stewed tomatoes give it a nice flavor and it has a thick, slightly chunky consistency. I have used it for chicken parmesean, eggplant parmesean and served over plain pasta. It works well with just about everything.  I've had to make it several times since finding the recipe 1 month ago because of family requests.  The only changes I made to the recipe are: substitute basil for the oregano and chicken stock for the wine.  I also added a little sugar to cut the acidity. Also, I removed Italian sausage from the casing, browned the meat in a separate pan to add to the sauce.  I used the dripping from the sausage in place of the olive oil and sauteed the onions in that.  I also eliminated the salt since there was plenty in the sausage.   

I found that I needed to double the recipe if I was using it for chicken or eggplant parmesean.  Now, I just double the recipe all the time and freeze what I don't use.  It freezes and reheats very well.

Wow, wow, wow!  This is my first attempt at making any type of pasta sauce and I will not buy jarred any more!  The only addition I made was the tablespoon of brown sugar as others suggested.  I used a pino grigio wine.  I doubled so I could freeze it for another time and I'm glad I did!  This will be my "go to" sauce recipe from now on.  Thanks!

Awesome. I used marsala wine rather than regular white (our favorite place uses marsala in their sauce so I figured I would give it a try) and it was a little over a half cup. Also added probably a teaspoon of white sugar. When sauteing the onions I let them sit for a bit, they were just about caramelized; I didn't use 6 tbsp of oil either, it was probably 2 or 3. I made the sauce, simmered for at least 30 min., cooled it down then heated it back up at dinner time. I think it really gave the flavors time to meld. Next time I will blend the tomatoes a little better, I like a thinner sauce. I made chicken parm to go with the sauce & my father in law said it was the best he ever had.

A good starting place. Probably a three star, but   I like vegies and added  what I had.   I sauted onion, garlic, green pepper, and mushrooms. Lots of mushrooms.  Then I chopped and added six  leftover slices of cooked bacon, a can of diced tomatoes as I had no fresh, and a generous amount of basil, oregano, and paprika.  Mixed in  into some hot rotini and enjoyed  the result along with a salad.  It was a light and tasty dish. Great for summer fare.  Tonight  being the third night,  I will dice and saute some cherry tomatoes and more onion to moisten the left overs up.

I have never made good spaghetti sauce in my life but this recipe was amazing! It was really easy and came out perfect. I hate chunks in sauce so using the food processor was a great way to eliminate them! I put the onions right in the food processor (since I hate lumps) and it comes out fine.  I also cooked ground beef in the pan before adding the tomato mixture and wine, and used the sauce in the 'Baked Ziti I' recipe from this site. This recipe is awesome, thanks so much!

This was the best marinara sauce ever.  I just used diced tomatoes and added a little more garlic.  It had a great taste.  My husband said it was a nice change from the meat and sausage I usually make.

This is such a great and forgiving recipe b/c it still comes out amazing even if you don't follow it 100%. I modified it based on what I had at home. I used crushed tomatoes instead of stewed and used 3 gloves of garlic. I didn't have fresh parsley so added about 1 tsp of italian seasoning and then more dried oregano, basil and thyme. I also don't use wine so just replaced it w/ water. Was a bit acidic so added at least one Tbsp brown sugar  as others suggested and toward the end, I added some shredded parmesan and mozarella. Whole thing took about 45 min and YES, it does get better the next day. My brother said it was the best pasta sauce he'd ever had. Definitely not using store bought anymore. Thank you Jackie!
great sauce and very easy.  My kids liked the sauce but i think that the wine in it was just a bit too strong for them.  but for adult taste it was great

One of the best marinara sauces I've had-- and I used to live in Italy!  I followed other's suggestions and added 1 tbsp of brown sugar and some red pepper flakes.  Next time I might add a few drops of Worchestershire sauce just because of personal taste, but this recipe is amazing as it is!  It isn't too often you find Italian food in the US that compares to the original.
The is the best marinara sauce! Even my picky eaters loved it!
Perfect blend of flavors.  I use it to make Eggplant Parmesan.
Too tomato paste-like. It smelt remarkable...I think I will have to give this a go-again and experiment.

The first time, I followed the recipe and it was very good. The second time I took the advice of another and added 1 Tblspn of brown sugar and that made it even better. This recipe is so simple, quick to make and whole family loves it. Thanks for posting.

For a quick sauce this was OK.  It was too light in seasoning for my family's taste.  I make a really great sauce, but it is an all day event.  I think with a lot of doctoring up, this would be easy to put together for a last minute meal.
Anyone ever made this with non-alcoholic wine? Tempted to try it as I don't drink. Otherwise, a great recipe!

Mmmm...delicious recipe. The best way to take the tartness/bitterness out of a tomato sauce is to add a tsp. of baking soda and stir for several minutes. It cuts the acidity of the tomatoes and creates a sweet, smooth sauce.

I loved how it was easy to make. My husband and son are VERY picky on pasta sauce and they just LOVED it. I had added ground beef cooked with salt and 1/2 tsp. Italian Seasoning. I thought it was good but not "out of this world". I did add an extra clove of garlic like other reviewers suggested.  I may add some Italian Seasoning to the sauce next time. I'd say I will definitely make this again. It's wasn't the best I've had but as easy as it is to make it's a keeper!
somewhat complicated with all of the ingredients, but it turned out fantastic!

my first ever time trying a marinara sauce! I love it! A few changes. I used pasta sauce instead of stewed tomatoes and didn't use the food processor at all though I used an electric mixer to blend everything together in the pot. Also used dried pasley.
Very fast and easy, not to mention delicious!

Delicioso! I made this for an eggplant parm recipe and it turned out PERFECT. I made the recipe as directed, except I added some fresh basil instead of the parsley. The consistency is excellent, not too thin or thick. This made enough for probably three batches of eggplant so I now have leftover for spaghetti!

Great recipe, thanks!
This is the best sauce I've made! I've already made it twice. I let the sauce boil for about an hour so it's nice and reduced. I did add 1 tsp of brown sugar to reduce the acidic bite of the sauce.
Easy, delicious, good. Made a bunch and used for different purposes throughout the week. Used my favorite Muir Glen canned tomatoes.
Great recipe! I don't have a food processor, so I substituted crushed tomatoes for the stewed tomatoes.
This is a great recipe !  Very light and tasty.  Great for a side item with pasta.  I make in large quantity and freeze in small containers.

Mmmmmm!  Not having any Italians in my family, marinara sauce wasn't an easy recipe to come up with.  But, after making this & serving it several times, I've impressed a lot of people!  It's SO flavorful & easy to make, too!  I double it & freeze it.  Still tastes delicious after being frozen.  Thanks!  (Also DELICIOUS w/ St. Louis toasted ravioli from this site)
It was very good. I did saute the onions with carrots and mushrooms as one review stated added some red pepper and brown sugar to taste and it turned out yummy. Thanks for sharing.
Just ok. I followed the recipe exactly. It was very tomato-y and acidic. I was a little disappointed.
This was really great and unusal! Thanks so much for a great recipe!
Easy, delicious and I used 5 cloves of garlic - we love garlic, added a bit of basil and crushed red pepper.  Perfect!
Making it again tonight.  I had some fresh basil so I chopped a couple of leaves into it along with the parsley.
This recipe is truly 5 stars and it was extremely complementry to my meatballs.  Thank you for sharing it.  Pat
Very flavourful and robust.

I added 1 Tbsp sugar and 12 oz tomato sauce (I like it a little thinner to dip my garlic bread in), simmered for only 15 minutes and the sauce was absolutely perfect!!! I made the tomato chicken parm and some angel hair spaghetti. I am making it again this Friday for some guests. Thanks so much!!

I rarely keep to the recipe thinking I can always make it better but put my ego aside and followed the directions just as they were. Wow! What a good sauce. I used it with the "Baked Ziti I" from this site and I am ready to make some more.
so easy and fresh tasting!  No need to buy jarred sauce from the store again.
Pretty good! Didn't change anything - may try it with red wine next time and add some more garlic.
Really enjoyed it.  Easy to make and a lot of fun

Great marinara sauce!  Exactly what I was looking for to use on my meatball subs.  I used 1 - 28 oz can of crushed tomatoes and skipped the step of blending it all together.  I also substituted chicken broth for the wine because I didn't have any.  Thanks!

Trusted the other reviews and made a triple batch of this  to freeze.  It is AMAZING!!  I'm so glad to have this recipe.  I used dried parsley instead of fresh (cut the amount in half) and diced the onion in the food processor so i didn't have to chop.  Massive 5 stars!!
I liked this sauce and would make it again.  But, I'm still on the lookout for the "Best Marinara Sauce EVER."  :-)
Excellent recipe! Absolutely delicious, my whole family loves it. I usually make this twice a month. I substitute with crushed tomatoes so that I don’t need to blend it. Moscato wine is best!
Delicous and simple to make.  Tastes better than the store bought sauces in jars.  Followed the recipe exactly as stated.

The title of this recipe says it all.  My Italian husband who is hard to impress, especially with Italian dishes, LOVED this sauce!!!  He now makes it quite often!  FYI- we use 2 cans of Aylmer Accents Original for the stewed tomatoes.
Quick, easy, and so much better tasting than a jar of store-bought sauce!
This was a really simple and easy sauce to make. I let mine simmer for a few hours and it wasn't bitter at all. I also used peeled plum tomatoes instead of stewed because that's all i had.
This sauce was so good. We loved it. The only thing I did a little different is I added 18 oz of tomato paste, because I was making this for pizza and I wanted it a little thicker. So good.
This is so easy and very tastey!!

This is a great sauce!  Not only is it delicious, it is super easy and fast to make.  I made this for my daughter's birthday, then again to top eggplant parmesan, and both times got good reviews.  So no matter what you use the sauce for, it works great!  Like others, I added some brown sugar to neutralize the acidity of all the tomato products, which I think is important.  And I upped the amount of garlic to 2 cloves the second time because the first time it seemed just a hair bland.  I will say though, this is the first, and only, sauce recipe I have ever made twice -- no others quite compare.  Very yummy and worth making over and over again!

This has become my stadard marinara sauce- the flavour is excellent and it is an excellent base to add to (roasted vegetables, grilled Italian sausages, sauteed beef, cream etc.). It is much lighter than many marinara sauces, probably because of the white wine, but the lightness does not compromise any of the flavour.  It's not our Italian grandmother's marinara sauce but is a more modern, fresh and versatile interpretation.
Excellent recipe; I felt like i was looking for one more seasoning/flavor to add though.

Over all, very tasty. This sauce was a little too sweet for me. I personally prefer marinara not sweet tasting. Next time I will use canned plum tomatoes to avoid that (I didn't realize stewed tomatoes had sugar in them).

5 stars for how easy this was to make and the taste is great!! I added about a tablespoon of salt and one clove of garlic. I used Pinot Gregio wine. I thought is was perfect buy my roommate thinks I should use a different wine next time or less of it. I think this is my staple marinara recipe from now on.
This recipe is the best I've tried so far. I followed this recipe but added pepperoni and ground seasonede cooked sirloin. Just Fabulous!

A really good, basic sauce. All my friends liked it a lot, but I did make the following changes:

Use:
4 cloves garlic, and saute them first
only 2 Tbs. olive oil
chicken broth if you don't have wine

Add:
dried basil
red pepper flakes
1 tsp. brown sugar

cook for one hour total

It definately would have been too acidic without the sugar, so add that if nothing else!

I make this all the time, and it is great!  I do make a few changes, but nothing that changes the nature of the recipe.  I don't use the parsley because I never have fresh parsley.  Instead of just oregano I do 1/2 tsp oregano and a 1/2 tsp basil.  I also add about 1/2 tsp red pepper flakes.  I use about 1/2 the olive oil and 1/2 the amount of wine as well.  We use this as is, or sometimes we add meat to it.  Either way, it is delicious.  No jarred sauce for us ever again!
Very flavourful and has a nice consistency.  I added basil, brown sugar, another clove of garlic and chili garlic sauce with good results.
Excellent sauce!  I will never use store bought sauce again!

Yum-yum.  I threw the tomatoes, tomatoe sauce and parsley in the blender to puree.  After I combined all the ingredients I put in my crock pot on low for about 2 hours until it was time to serve.  Everyone loved the taste -I loved that it could go together easily and was ready to go when it was time to eat.

Note to those out there, if substituting red for the white wine, use less than what is called for.  We are red wine drinkers and don't keep white in the house so I used what I had, a merlot...and while the sauce was good, it had a STRONG taste of red wine! Otherwise pretty yum, I made a lasagna with the sauce and it was good!
Liked it a lot.  Made it twice so far.  A keeper!

Yummy, Yummy - I made a couple of changes due to other reviews and what I had on hand. I used one 28oz can of crushed tomatoes, didn't use parsley, added a bay leaf, 1 TBS brown sugar, and fresh mushrooms which I sauteed with the onion and garlic. This sauce was amazing. I agree with others who said the sauce was even better the next day. Next time I make this I am going to AT LEAST double. Thanks so much for sharing Jackie!!

I love this sauce.  I made a few modifications. I added a tablespoon of coconut sugar, half of a carrot, half of a Zucchini, 2 cloves of garlic and a small piece of green bell pepper.  I also put  a splash of the  white wine . 
I put everything in the slow cooker and the following day I  blended it and poured it over cooked ground beef.
Delicious!

Perfect... very basic and easy.  The longer you let it simmer, the better.  I added a little basil and also used a little red wine when I ran out of white.  I also used slightly less oil than called for.  Yummy!

This recipe was the best.  I used another user's advice and used this recipe for baked ziti 1 and also used it in place of the alfredo sauce in the artichoke and spinach dip restaurant style. oh my what a great combination.  I've made this sauce twice this week. Thanks Jackie

Absolutely LOVED it!!!  I made it on a Monday and let it sit in the frig until Wednesday when we had it with pasta.  It was devine.  We tried different types of pasta with the leftover sauce.  The sauce froze well and is great for a quick meal.  We even put it in individual containers to grab for a light snack or for a couple of people.  Definitely a keeper!

Super!  Making with fresh herbs and tomatoes out of the garden I have peeled, chopped, and boiled down.  Plan on canning this over and over with a few changes.  I added 1 T worshishire sauce and omitted wine (I live in a dry county) and onion.  Smells and tastes yummy.

This is a simple yet wonderful sauce anyone can make.  Using quality stewed tomato products is the key to get rid of the acidic flavor you usually find with the cheaper brands of canned tomatoes.  The longer you cook it, the better it tastes.  HINT: This sauce is absolutely amazing and company-worthy if you use merlot instead of wine.  Thanks for sharing!
This is the best recipe for marinara yet!  With all of the different seasonings, it had wonderful flavor.  The longer you can cook it, the better!
My family did not care for the flavor at all.  I would not make this again.

It IS the best marinara sauce like the name says!  Only thing I changed was add basil.
UPDATE:  I made this again tonight and my husband kept on raving and raving about it!  I didn't even use fresh parsley this time and I also used 1 can of stewed tomatoes along with 1 can of crushed tomatoes.  BOY, it's delicious!  I would NEVER buy spaghetti sauce again!  Thank you!

I love this sauce.  Is very good as is, but I have experimented as well with adding more garlic, a bit of sugar, and a little less olive oil as it tends to be a bit much and I love olive oil!  I keep getting requests for this and will continue to make it again and again.  Thanks so much!

It's a great base recipe. I love to use it for a baked goat cheese appetizer. Fill a ramekin halfway with marinara, settle a disc of goat cheese on top and bake for 20-30 minutes at 350. Serve with bagel chips. The only change I've made is occasionally adding a few Tbs of brown sugar to offset the acidity and perhaps a pinch of red pepper flakes for the spicy crowd. Love this recipe!
Very easy to make and delicious.

This sauce was very good, but it was very acidic once it was finished so I ended up needing to add a little sugar and I thought it definitely needed more garlic.  However, this sauce is a great base and I can't wait to use it again, but make my own changes for my family's tastes.

This sauce has so much flavor.  The wine just added more great flavors & the aromas were just  divine.   I tweeked  it by sautéing the mushrooms with the onions, and  added Italian sausage to the sauce.  Lastly, I added 2 teaspoons of coconut sugar.   This marinara is a hit every time., and it is easy too.  I have made it many times.  Definitely a keeper.
This sauce was just "okay" to me. I didn't think it had that great of flavor, and would probably just buy jarred sauce rather than make this again.
Don't change a thing except maybe to throw in a few meatballs - excellent and sooo easy to make
Excellent, only added 1 tablespoon of sugar as mine was bitter. Best I have had ever!!!!!

Wonderful Taste, added a pinch of sugar, a pinch of red pepper flakes.and a pinch of basil. I grilled some Italian sausage and sauted green and red pepper and sweet onions. Added it to the sauce served over penne pasta. absolutly great!!!
An easy sauce to make with ingredients I already have on hand.  Needs a little kick - I had to add a little sugar.

I made this last night to go with my breaded shrimp. I tastes exactly like store-bought varities. I may try this again with fresh tomatoes, because the flavors of the stewed, canned tomatoes was somewhat flat.
Wonderful! I made extra to freeze and I'm sure it'll be even better once the seasonings have set over a couple days.
This is really good and easy. I love the thickness of it. I like to add meat and mushrooms and crushed red pepper flakes.
Absolutely the best sauce I have ever made and I have been working at the perfect sauce for years now.  Prepared exactly by the recipe and the family loved it.

The best sauce we have ever had! I will never buy sauce in a jar again. My 13 year old son raved about it. he is the spaghetti expert in the house. Of course I know a good sauce. Will use it for Lasagna, my eggplant, Ravioli , everything. Only think I added was a bay leaf , a pinch or two of chili flakes, dried Basil, and a few extra cloves of garlic. Simmered for 30 min.

Yum!  Really liked this recipe, and so did everyone in my family.  Added lots more garlic than what it called for.  Will probably add more onion next time, too.  I also used diced tomatoes with garlic, onion, and basil, as well as Italian flavored tomato paste.

Very good!!  I had to use crushed tomatoes because I didn't have stewed on hand - but will try it with stewed tomatoes next time.  And I added about a 1/2 teaspoon of brown sugar to even it out, and threw a few leaves of fresh basil into the food processor with everything else.  The fresh parsley makes such a difference - grab some at the store instead of using dried.  You'll be glad you did!  This was really good.  I'll be using it inside calzones tonight, and for dipping.  I will definitely be making it again...!!

I tried this to use in dipping with toasted ravioli (a St. Louis thing).  I would recommend cutting the olive oil to about 1/3 of what the recipe calls for and use more garlic and spices.  It was very good and easy to make.  My family really liked it.

Good Marinara sauce. But i added 2 cloves of garlic, 1 stalk of celery & saute the onions, garlic & celery with olive oil in pot first to bring out the flavors. I also added sugar, bay leaves & Italian Seasoning after the tomatoes. And i substituted red wine instead of white (U usually use red wine for red sauce). Cooked it for an hour. It turned out great!

This was DELICIOUS! I didn't have a food processor or blender so I followed the advice of another poster and used crushed tomatoes instead of stewed. It was a bit chunkier, but honestly I like sauce like that! I was so surprised at how delicious this was.

We really enjoyed this with Chef John's Italian meatballs and spaghetti. I sauteed the onions in just 2 T olive oil (I didn't think it needed 6) for a couple of mins, added the garlic (3 cloves instead of 1), then added about 1/4 teaspoon crushed chili peppers just for a few seconds. Stirred in diced tomatoes, tomato paste, and about 1/2 cup tomato sauce. Used about 1 Tablespoon dried parsley and didn't have white wine so I used dry sherry instead. Simmered for about 40 mins. Everything else I kept as written. Thanks for a great recipe!

A very good marinara sauce. This was easy for me to make and came out tasting fresh and delicious! Last night I roasted some roma tomatoes using, "Roasted Roma Tomatoes with Garlic," from this website. I also saved the natural sweet juices from the tomatoes to use in place of the canned stewed tomatoes called for in this recipe. This morning I smashed and crushed the tomatoes with my hands instead of using a blender. In the large skillet I add some olive oil, sauteed finely diced white onions. I added one garlic and let it cook. I then added the all of the tomatoes including its juices to the skillet. I added one (6 ounce) can tomato paste and the white wine with a handful of fresh chopped parsely and a little oregano. I sitrred to combine and let it simmer on low. I seasoned with a pinch of rock salt and some fresh ground black pepper. I also threw in some fresh chopped basil then a smidgen of brown sugar. I let the marinara sauce simmer for a while longer, stirring occasionally, then turned it off to cool. I like the consistency of the sauce, which is not too thick and not too thin. The taste of this homemade marina sauce was wonderful and full of fresh flavor. It was the fresh roasted tomatoes that put it over the top for me along with the fresh herbs and wine. I ended up with about 3 cups of marinara sauce. This recipe was perfect and I had enough sauce to layer in the, "Simple Spinach Lasagna," also from this website. easy and nice recipe, thank you for sharing.

I didn't have white wine on hand, so I tried champagne/sparkling white wine and it came out perfectly.  The second time around I decided to use regular white wine (as the recipe suggests) and it came out tasting sour.  I recommend using champagne and you won't need to use any sugar.

First time making Marinara Sauce. This Recipe was very easy. I do not use wine, so I used Apple Juice as a substitute. It was better than store bought Marinara. I liked it, but it wasn't over the Top. Would I make it again? Not sure.

This was excellent sauce.  I used a 28oz can of crushed tomatoes instead of the stewed tomatoes and a teaspoon of sugar but followed the rest of the recipe.  I served it with minced fresh basil generously sprinkled over the sauced pasta.  Everyone loved it.  Will make this again.

This is a very good mainara! I followed recipe as well as added 1 tbs. of brown sugar and waaaay more garlic. Also added one half of a jalapeno pepper from our garden for alittle kick;) Will have w/ thick spaghetti noodles, garden salad and Chianti as the wine. Nice....
Can't pinpoint what, but it was missing something.  Was still very tasty though.  Would make again, possibly adding more seasonings.

Fantastic recipe!  I make this quite often and have made only one consistent change....I always add fresh basil.  It adds so much more.  I sometimes add more garlic or substitute chicken broth (as someone suggested) when I don't have any white wine.  All in all this is just a great sauce and very flexible.  The only one my whole family loves!  thank you!
This recipe is fantastic. I use a sherry cooking wine to add to the flavor. My daughter would eat it every night if she could.

Quick and perfect! I eyeballed all the quantities because I was in a hurry. Used dried parsley. Sauteed green onions in butter instead of Olive oil since I had some left over from another recipe I wanted to use up. Used a hand immersion blender instead of a food processor and that made it all the easier. Finally, added about 1 TBS of brown sugar as suggested by other reviewers to balance the tartness. Didn't let it simmer the full 3O minutes, only as long as my other recipe was cooking. Still turned out fantastic. A very forgiving recipe and definitely a "Go-To" for a quick red sauce!
This is the best sauce.  It was a lifesaver for all the tomatoes in our garden last year.  The neighbors love me for it too!
Tastes homemade and is rather easy to pull together!
DELISH!!!   4 cloves garlic no wine 1 T brown sugar

My wife and I love this sauce.  I have found that we prefer to use red wines instead of White. A pinot noir when in the mood for a slightly sweet sauce, or a bold Cabernet sauvignon when in the mood for spicy.  This sauce also makes a great pizza sauce.

I have never reviewed a recipe before but felt that I must review this one.  Really great recipe - was a hit with the whole family.  I made this in the morning before leaving for work and put it all in the crock pot to cook on low all day.  Delicious and perfect consistency.  I doubled the recipe and there was plenty left over for another recipe.  I had been looking for a good marinara recipe and am so glad I tried this one.  this is a real keeper.

I read the recipe wrong and added White wine vinegar instead of White and it turned out great! I used half the amount of white wine vinegar and whole caned Tomatos ... we loved it some much Iadequate it again a few days later and tripled the recipe

will never buy another  jar of pasta again.  definitely use fresh parsley--it gave it such a great  earthy taste.  also don't like too strong of a garlic taste so I minced and sauteed it with the onions.
This was Very good!  I took this to a potluck and all enjoyed it.  I used crushed tomatoes though because it was what I had.  This may become a staple in our household.
Excellent, my family loved it.  Like one person said I replaced the wine with chicken broth and added a little ground sirloin.  Defiantly making it again.

Excellent sauce!!! It's the only one I make now and it's so easy. I add sugar and fresh basil and saute the onions in olive oil first. It's great with all kinds of pasta and on top of chicken parm. By adding extra spices you can use it for pizza sauce too. I love it!

This was delicious! I didn't blend everything together because I like a chunky sauce, but the recipe is very very good, I only made a few changes, I used some basil and other seasonings and some tomato sauce because I didn't blend everything. It turned out nicely.

I am not much of a cook and I would never consider making my own sauce.  But this was so easy and quick and the flavor beats any jar sauce you can buy.  I will keep these ingredients on hand at all times and I will never buy jar sauce again

This just isn't quite what I expected, but I can see where others may like it.  The consistency was great, and the sauce has potential, but to me the stewed tomatoes add way too much sweetness, so I may consider trying again with just plain whole tomatoes.  I was able to salvage by adding lots of other spices, but I will not make this again without a serious overhaul of the ingredients.
This ended up tasting great!  Followed recipe exactly but doubled it.  Used in the Chicken Parmigiana recipe found on this site.
This is fantastic!! I'm on a sodium restricted diet and I used no-salt stewed tomatoes and added just 1/2 tsp of salt to the sauce.
doubled the garlic and added a pinch of red pepper flakes, otherwise followed the recipe exactly and it was fantastic!
Delicious~!!! Best marinara.  I made it as is, and it was wonderful! Thanks.
We use this receipe every time we need a red sauce. Great texture and great flavors with out an overly strong tomato flavor.
I've made this sauce several times.  It is quick and easy.  I use less oil, add a little more garlic and use a chardonnay for the wine.  It is thick and delicious.  No more buying marinara again.
This recipe was good.It was not thick so if you are looking for a thick spaghetti sauce this is not it.  I added some chopped up carrots and sausage.  It was easy to make and tasted great.
Great. Added more garlic, achovy paste, capers, and a tbsp of sugar

Tried this tonight and it was a hit.  The stewed tomatoes are what makes this sauce different than the norm.  I have a terrible time getting my 16 month old to eat her veggies and I thought that the method of pureeing used in this recipe would be a great way to sneak in some veggies without her knowing it...and it worked! Once tender, I blended the veggies with the remaining ingredients.  Instead of doubling the oregano, I used 1 t. of dried oregano and 1 t. of italian herb seasoning (remember - I doubled the recipe).  Following the recommendation of another reviewer, I added 2 T. of brown sugar.  The result was perfect - it wasn't sweet, but the addition balanced out the acidity.  I served over whole wheat spaghetti with my homemade meatballs.  This sauce would be absolutely perfect with sausage, onions & peppers on a hoagie with melted provolone cheese. Thanks for this recipe...I am ecstatic that my daughter ate some veggies tonight and I love that it's so versatile.  I'll be using it for many different things.  P.S. I cut way back on the olive oil...used just enough to coat the bottom of the pan.

This recipe was a 3-4-star rating as written; however, the following changes upgrades recipe to 5-star. In addition to the ingredients already stated use:  (1) in lieu of Stewed Tomatoes, use Hunts(R) Oregano & Basil Diced Tomatoes, undrained (2) Add 1 tsp dried Basil, (3) Add 1 tsp Brown Sugar, (4) Add 1/4 tsp red pepper flakes, (5) Add 1 Bay Leaf, (6) Add 1 tsp Morton(R) Garlic Sea Salt.  Directions:  Simmer onions in olive oil until softened.  Add all ingredients, bring to a boil, and then simmer for 30 minutes.  Remove Bay Leaf and then use Immersion Blender to blend all ingredients for a lovely smooth, thickened texture.  Immersion blender is a must.  Very versatile recipe.  For a cream sauce, add 1/4 cup Half and Half(R) before using Immersion Blender.  There are better recipes, but this one is easy and will do well in a pinch.

Jackie's recipe is very aptly named as "Best" Marinara recipe. It's good not just for the fact that it's delicious, but also for the simplicity in preparation and the availability of the ingredients. 

I do think though that adding some seafood flavour will further enhance the recipe. Get a kilogram of raw mussels (still in shell). Scrub and clean them. Put them in a pot and pour the white wine (from the original recipe) into the pot and steam them until shells open.

Remove the mussel meat from the shell and set aside. Strain the cooking liquor (to remove the gritty bits at the bottom). At the end of cooking the tomato sauce, add the cooking liqour and the mussel meat.

Might take a little more time to shell the mussels, but well-worth the extra flavour.

Second, I use tomato sauce instead of paste because it is not so acidic (I simmer the sauce a little longer so that it reduces to the desired consistency). Finally, I use a hand blender to puree the entire sauce until it is as smooth/chunky as we need it (smooth for marinara dipping sauce, chunky for pizza sauce, chunkier for pasta sauce etc). I made this tonight for supper. The family all really loved it. I used mozzarella in place of swiss and I also substituted taco sauce for the sherry. It was great!
Very good! I didn't have any sherry, but other than that it went over perfectly with the family. I will try it with the sherry next time!

I was asked to make a swiss "gravy" for a baked potato bar and I used this recipe.  I made it as written (minus the sherry) at first, but then found that the swiss cheese was very stringy!  After some research, I realized the sherry is needed to "de-string" the cheese if you use a lot of swiss.  I added a little bit of lemon juice and it worked wonders to loosen the strings!  I also ended up adding a good bit more cheddar to even out the flavors, as well as some half-n-half for extra creaminess and thinning.   I added a package of tiny ham chunks and it went over really well.  Makes a great topping for a spud bar!
I just tried this on top of a breakfast egg bake in place of cheddaer and it was delicious. I will also try the fondue suggestion.

This was very good sauce however, I doubled the cheese which I think is necessary to achieve a thick rich sauce.  Without the extra cheese it was a bit bland and too runny.  Also the sherry adds a nice sophisticated touch!  Will use as my standby recipe for cheese sauce.  Very Tasty!  Thanks for the recipe!
Good stuff, brings back memories of my family's cheese sauce growing up...
This tasted too much of flour and too little of cheese.  Sorry.  I couldn't eat it.
WOW!!! I haven't even added the cheese yet but I snuck a taste already and it is YUMMY!!
Surprisingly yummy! I used it in a casserole that required a jar of cheese sauce and it was incredible! Thank you!
This sauce was wonderful! I left out the sherry because I didn't have any... I mixed it into a pot of noodles and left over ham from Thanksgiving!!! Thanks for sharing!! :o) I will use this again!!

This recipe is simple and great!!  I usually make my own thing but I tried something new.  I tossed in alot more cheddar cheese than called for.  I did not have any swiss cheese on hand.  But a success!!
My hubby liked the sauce, I thought it could use more of the seasonings. I also would use more cheese. I plan on perfecting this recipe and using it more often.
This was a really easy recipe.  I made it for my fiance to eat broccoli with.  I added "Mexican Cheese" to give it some kick..  Will make again!
Smooth and creamy, but not enough cheese flavor to suit me, even though I used double the amount of cheese.
This was really good. I added extra cheddar so it was  3/4 c each of cheddar and Swiss/needed a little more cheese to balance out all the sherry.....but only a minor tweak.
If you like Swiss Cheese, this recipe is excellent.  I actually added beer and used it as a fondue.

I really love this sauce, especially for broccoli and cheese baked potatoes. I've also used it to make mac & cheese, or added some hot sauce to make a tortilla dip. Wonderful! My only real change is I do usually add twice as much cheese as what it calls for.
I did not use sherry and cut the recipe down. Very easy to prepare and was still great after my amendments. I thought it went well over mixed vegetables and used it as a "fondue" as well.
This was very good, I left the salt out as another reviewer suggest - next time I will definately add the salt.
used 2 slices of American and about 1 cup grated Monterrey Jack because that was what I had in the fridge.  LOVED IT!

I made this recipe for our dinner tonight we had it over the broccoli...  I changed a few ingredients and left a couple out as well. I used half and half instead of milk, 1 cup shredded colby jack, instead of swiss and cheddar, I left out the sherry, and used garlic powder and onion powder in place of the mustard powder and the paprika. I used a bit more salt and pepper than called for (you should season to taste), and a sprinkle of chopped parsley just to be fun... It turned out pefrectly, and I must say it was delicious. Probably one of, if not, the best cheese sauce I've ever had.

This is a really easy recipe to make macaroni and cheese! I made a few changes, though. I left out the mustard powder, Swiss cheese, and sherry. I also added a lot of cheddar cheese (1 cup mild or 3/4 cup sharp.) I have made this many times (at least 5) for easy macoroni and cheese. Thanks for the great recipe!!

My family loves cheese sauce but we didn't care for this one. I followed the recipe accurately but we found that the sherry was overpowering and didn't go well with our steamed vegetables. Next time I will just add a little more milk.
Yummy. I used monterey jack instead of swiss and white wine instead of sherry - skipped the dry mustard. Very good!
pretty good...and super quick to make. I made 3 servings just for myself and it took 5 min.  I poured it over a potato/hamburger conncoction I made, and ate what was leftover with tortilla chips. Yum
We had this on brocolli.  It was wonderful!
I used this on some steak nachos.  It was good...but I think I would do all cheddar, or a different cheese than Swiss.  Was easy enough to make though, and no one complained!
We didn't like this sauce.

As others had said, I had to use 2 to 3 times as much cheese to get a thick consistancy. Next time I will probably just use the right amount of cheese and halve everything else because it ended up making a lot more then I needed. Also, next time I will use more cheddar and less swiss, but thats just a personal preference. Overall, it is a very good cheese sauce. I will definately make it again with the changes I mentioned.

I loved this over broccoli. But I wasn't paying attention to the amount it makes!! So after using it for the veggies I used on leftover taco meat for quick nachos and then I tried for mac and cheese. Really good basic gooey cheesy sauce. I did use an extra handfull of grated cheddar. And I sprinkled a little more cheese in the mac and cheese.

Loved this recipe!!! I found it to be very easy and not time consuming at all. Although first time trying I admit that I tweeked it a bit by adding a 1/3 cup more of sherry, 1 1/2 cup milk, 1/4 cup parmesan cheese and 2 cups Kraft finely shredded sharp cheddar cheese. Once butter is melted on low heat, I found that by turning the heat up to med./low you must stir and watch carefully after adding the initial ingredients and before adding cheeses as the mixture will lump up terribly. Should this happen don't dump and start over, simply stir a bit vigorously mashing out any lumps that have formed for about 5 min. once mixture is smooth again you can begin to add your cheeses and lower the heat some and continue to stir. I found that if you add too much cheese such as the cheddar it may be a bit too much taste wise, but adding some extra milk not too much will get it just right. Poured it over some steamed broccoli and it was simply "DELISH"...Thanks So Much Glen. Can't wait to try it again!!!
I made this sauce to serve over cauliflower for Thanksgiving and it was DELICIOUS! I did add more cheddar though, at least doubled, but you can make it as-is and then gradually add to taste.
Double the cheese.  Perfectly smooth, so easy to make.  I will definitely make this my go to cheese sauce recipe for soups and toppings.  Great on my pulled pork and broccoli baked potato.

Love, Love, Love it!  I have been making essentially this same sauce, minus the Sherry,  for years, I'm always experimenting with the cheeses, so I came here to look for ideas for different cheeses to try.  Adding the Sherry made all the difference!  I made my basic 60/40 Swiss/Cheddar blend and it was fabulous. It's a much more sophisticated flavor.   I'll (almost)never make my bechamel without the Sherry again.  I think even when a more subtle sauce is needed you can just adjust the amount of the Sherry.  Thank you Glen for helping me kick Grandmas green bean casserole up a notch!
I made only 4 servings and used on cheddar cheese and it was still very good!
Great simple cheese sauce.
Very good cheese sauce! I didn't add the sherry but it still came out very yummy. And I added a dash of nutmeg.

EXCELLENT! I used this sauce for a ham and scallop dish that guests raved about.  Didn't have sherry on hand and used about 3 c of mixed cheeses.  Turned out very creamy and delicious thank you for a great basic cheese sauce recipe.

This recipe is well done, with a more "gourmet" flavor than the typical cheese sauce.  The mustard, and particularly the Swiss cheese and sherry (I used dry sherry, not cooking sherry) all contributed to a more elegant sauce.  Still, this was not something we were particularly crazy for - not on our broccoli anyway.  Actually, this would be an excellent fondue with crostini or rye chips.

We really enjoyed this delicately-flavored sauce. I wanted a thicker sauce so doubled (or maybe 3x) the cheese.  Had to use all cheddar as my Swiss gruyere was frozen! I think the Swiss, combined with the sherry, would be really good too. Served over steamed cauliflower.  Thanks for the recipe, Glen.  I'll use this one again!

Glen's sauce was delicious made exactly as submitted, but the real joy of this dish is the ease of preparation.
Thanks Glen and Allrecipes
Just what I needed over rice pasta for my daughter.  My husband downed the leftovers!
Not cheesy enough for us! I'll likely use the recipe again, but add much more cheddar.
Needed to double cheese and add more seasonings

Yummy. I didn't have dry mustard so I just used regular mustard. I didn't have sherry so I used white wine. I wanted a cheesy cheddar sauce for broccoli on top of potatoes so I omitted the swiss and put 2 cups of shredded cheddar cheese. Delicious!

This recipe was excellent. The sauce was very creamy. I did use more cheddar than called for. I also added parmesan cheese. I love strong cheddar taste. I used it to make macaroni and cheese> Very quick and simple to prepare. Looks of flexibility as well with cheese varieties depending on what you have in the fridge.

I am the one who shared this recipe. I used the recipe for Meringue Two today and it was magnificent! It took my grandma's pie over the top! Just wanted to share that and I added a better picture than that years old one of my grandmother's!

I had this with vanilla flavored soy milk and it turned out great! It tastes just like I thought it would, I agree that the coffee taste is subtle but I didn't mind it at all. I left out the syrup and it was still sweet so it didn't need it in my opinion.

I've been treating myself to a banana/milk/coffee treat the past three weekends. This past weekend was inspired by the aztecs...cinnamon chili chocolate milk post workout replenishment in a cup. I really like this! I use Stumptown Cold Brew Coffee, and omit the simple syrup. I use very ripe bananas and don't need any extra sweetness. I've tried this with soymilk, coconut milk, and almond milk- all of which were great! Just make sure to blend the banana for enough time so you don't get any lumps  :)

The coffee flavor is very subtle which is fine with me.  I used soy milk, coffee ice cubes instead of regular ice cubes and I substituted 2 packets of Truvia for the simple syrup. Instead of pouring into 2 glasses, I poured it into 1 tall glass and drank it all myself!
I usually use 1 banana, 1/2 cups almond milk, 1/2 cups hot coffee and 2 tbsp ground oats. Do recommend!
YUMMY! YUMMY! YUMMY! This is the shot I ask for when it's not a tequila night. Naughty name, but I could have 'em all night.
Delicious! I served it as two mixed drinks over ice.
very good!
Sooooo good Karen!
These are awesome but can kick your butt cause they go down sooooo good ;)

Our family loves this cake. I double it for a 9x13 and omit the walnuts for the sake of one child. It benefits from a bit of salt and extra cinnamon. Cook a little longer if you are dealing with a gooey cake. A cream cheese frosting, whipped cream, or buttery sauce is the perfect finish.

I have made this recipe for years and its really good. I pour the boiling water over the oats and sugars and then add the rest of the ingredients in normal cake fashion. It's light and fluffy and rich.
This cake was gooey and did not have a good taste. I will not make this again.
Great recipe! I added shredded carrots, cranberries, chopped granny smith apple and a little more applesauce. I baked it in a sheet cake pan and cut into squares, it didn't last a day!

Great recipe!  If you're looking to save time, my beau discovered that they taste just as good made with instant mashed potatoes.  To add texture, he has put corn and diced onion on top of the potato mixture before rolling the tortillas up.  Fantastic!

These were very good. I came and read the reviews before I made this and I am very glad I did. I added a can of black beans, increased spices by a lot and used medium spicy enchilada sauce.
