Very good with the 10 minute sauce from this site.
These turned out very tasty.  My husband was skeptical but he loved them.  I thought they were just a touch too dry but it was nothing that cannot be adjusted.
I was skeptical at first, when I first made these I put to much potatoes in them and not enough cheese. The second time I put about half potatoes and half cheese making them even better.

Very tasty!  I followed other's advice and added extra cumin, chili powder and garlic.  I also threw in some onion for extra flavor. This sounded so good, I couldn't hardly wait to fix on New Years,it was terrible no one would eat this dish I had to throw it away. The potatoes was not a good idea for burritoes

I also had potatoes to use, so I tried to find something that could work as a filler with the chicken.  This did the job perfectly and it tasted wonderful!  The spices added a nice flavor to the potatoes.  I added few things I like such as fresh cilantro.  Just be sure that the potatoes are cooked all the way.  Mine were firm and I thought they would soften as they baked.  Not so.  Some of them ended up tasting uncooked.  This is a great way to add a filler or to use up potatoes, or just have a nice vegetarian burrito!

I have to say I was a bit skeptical about these, but I am so glad I gave them a try.  They were delicious and my whole family kept raving about them.  I did make a few changes per the other reviews. This recipe was great. they taste more like tamales instead of burritos but they are still very good.

Yummy AND vegetarian!  I used a smokey chili powder and it gave it a real good ol western Tex/Mex flavor.  Don't have kids to rate it, but my boyfriend LOVES it!

We liked these. I had to add a lot more cheese and more seasoning (extra chili powder and some fajita seasoning I had on hand)so it wasn't so bland. Next time I will use the whole can of enchilada sauce instead of the amount specified in the recipe.

YUM! We were looking for a filling vegetarian meal and these burritos were great! I added a can of fat free refried beans and an onion.  Used a whole can of enchilada sauce on top. Will definitely make this again!!

Made this one over the weekend. It was good but there are a few things I would change/add. First of all I used and HIGHLY recommend using the red enchillada sauce from this site. And last, I didn't think to do this until it was too late but next time I will definatley use some sour cream. Overall though, it was fantastic.

A little bland for my taste.  I boosted the cumin and chili powder and it was not as spicy as I'd like, so taste the potatoes before you roll them in the tortillas.  I added cooked chicken breast and corn to make it a main dish.

This is a good basic recipe that I have never even heard of before. It is a little carb-heavy, so I would definitely recommend adding other things to the potatoes. I added fresh spinach sauteed with garlic, and a can of black beans. I also, like another reviewer, made the "red enchilada sauce" from this website. It was all really good, but it makes a LOT of food! I took the extra leftovers to work the next day, and people were asking for the recipe! I think it would be especially good to use with leftover mashed potatoes, otherwise it is a little bit time consuming.
These were better than I thought they would be, but not sure if I like the combo of all the starch.

This was so good! Very tasty, and I usually don't like spicy things! The only thing is that it's really messy, and takes a while to make. And I think I'm gonna use more cheese in the mixture next time too. I love this recipe though! :)
Very good! Next time I will saute onions and add them to the potato mix. I used the homemade enchilada sauce from the website. Very heavy dish - you could very easily make half a recipe.
Not bad, a bit over potato.

I diced my potatoes but did not mash (they were pretty mashed after stirring anyway).  Added a regular can of mexi-corn and a regular can of black beans in addition to a whole diced onion. Added a packet of taco seasoning to potatoes (start with 3/4 and go from there).  Didn't use much enchilada sauce but topped mainly with green salsa verde taco sauce.  Yum!  Filling!  One was enough for me with some Spanish Rice!  I filled 8 tortillas but still have enough filling for at least 4 more - we'll be eating this for lunches, too.  Great for the budget and the stomach!
way too dry. definetly needs a whole lot more moisture to be able to eat more than half an enchalada
We used fat-free Cheddar so they came out a little spicy, but still delicious. Amazingly simple, but really great. Good job!

I definately suggest adding beans and/or some other vegetable for more flavor.  Great recipe to add your own flair to.  Rather bland by itself.

Delicious!  I made a couple of changes.  I added a small container of sour cream to the potatoes, because they seemed dry.  I used the entire can of enchilada sauce, and it could still probably have used more.
I added sauted seasoned chicken to this. It was delicious!

This was delicious, I changed a few things, and added a few things, I added some chopped onion, tabasco sauce, cheddar cheese and cliantro to the filling and also added some sour cream. I think next time I will also add a can of mexi-corn. Thanks, it was delicious.

These were tasty. My family wants them again. I added ground beef with taco seasoning.

I served these with a variety of other mexican dishes at my dinner party. This dish was a real hit..everyone loved it (even my kids)! Great dish even for "non" vegetarians!

I was very pleased with how these turned out. I think older kids may like them, but my 4 year old definitely did not. Suggestion: For the garlic-boil and mash 2 cloves of garlic with the potatoes-very tasty!
Just different.  My hubby liked and so did kiddo, but just so carby...
Definitely a winner...next time I will spice it up a bit with more onion and mild green chiles.

this recipe is a fine launching point for your own tastes and creativity.  i like a lot of cumin, cheese, and assorted peppers.  but both my hubby and enjoyed the potato base.  this is a quick, cheap, and easy dish-just waiting for your own flair.

This was really easy to make and very tasty!  I would maybe add chicken or steak to it next time.

Wonderful and so easy to make!! Kids love it!!

I really enjoyed these and so did my husband (much to my surprise.)  I added a dried red chile because I like spice. Also followed the other reviewers suggestions of adding chicken broth to the potatoes and used the entire 10 ounce can of enchilada sauce.

Yummy!!  Flavorful and easy.

Good recipe, but like other reviewers, it's missing directions.  Here's my changes: 1 1/4 cups warm water, 1 pkg active dry yeast, 1 tblsp sugar, 1 tsp thyme or Italian seasonings, 3 tblsp olive oil, 3+ cups of flour, 1 tsp salt. Mix water, yeast, sugar & oil in mixer bowl.  Then add flour & salt.  Mix-knead for 10-12 minutes, sprinkling with flour to keep from sticking to bowl.  Dough should be elastic & smooth. Place dough in oiled bowl, cover dough with oil, cover & let stand 1 hr at room temp. Then divide dough 2 equal parts roll into balls, cover with damp towel & let stand another 10 mins.  Use immediately.  Don't forget to poke holes into dough with fork once rolled onto pan to let steam escape while baking.

This pizza dough is BY FAR the BEST home made pizza dough that I have made to date. It baked up phenomenally, rolled out SO easy and tasted fantastic! I have been baking bread for many years and this is a wonderful recipe. One of the great things about this recipe is it versatility. I always like to try a recipe in its original form before I start tweaking and this one is good “as-is.” Honestly though everyone has their own idea about the perfect crust so of course I made my own changes to suit my tastes. To me the most important thing to this recipe is to proof the yeast in warm water with sugar before adding it to the flour mixture. To proof the yeast just add the 1 cup warm water and 1 tbsp. sugar and yeast in a bowl. Stir it and let it sit for about 5-10 min till it gets frothy. It is not a necessary step but it helps activate the yeast and develops flavor since it will not be going through a rising stage. After kneading I do like to let the dough sit for at least 5 minutes to let the gluten relax. It will help make the dough less elastic when you are ready to roll it out. The only other change I made was to add 3 tbsp. of olive oil rather than veg. oil. If you have the opportunity this crust cooks beautifully on a grill. It gets just enough char to make you think it was cooked in a wood fired pizza oven. Just lay it down directly on the hot well oiled grates. Cook till it is firm enough to flip. Repeat on the other side. When you get the amount of color you want brush both sides with olive oil, remove to a baking sheet, top how you like, and finish up in a 450° oven. Absolutely  delish. This one is a keeper.

I made this crust exactly as written. I am enjoying a delicious pizza right now.

I have been making my own pizza for a while, with my own sauce, I tried this recipe for the dough and it was pretty good.  But off hand from my own pizza making experiance, there is something that needs to be done that is not said in the recipe.  First is that after you combine the ingredients the dough needs to be kneaded for a minute or two, this is very important as it activated the glutten in the dough.  The dough needs to rise, it is very heavy if you do not and kneading is important to the texture of the dough.  Also I have always drizzled a little olive oil (not much!) after I put my sauce on this prevents the dough from drying out.  Overall the recipe is pretty good.

I used olive oil and  also added lots of dried herbs to the dry mix. This recipe also makes a really good garlic bread if you top it with olive oil, crushed garlic and parmesan cheese. I doesn't seem necessary to let the dough rise first, I didn't really notice any difference. Maybe our yeast is a bit different in NZ!

I rated this high for how easy it was to make and how great it turned out.I actually like how basic and simple it is. This recipe is exactly what I was looking for. Thank you so much!!! Wow, made this as is and Wow.  I usually make homemade pizza one time per week.  It has to be on Sundays because of the dough rising and kneading and rising again. simple, quick, easy - just like it advertises. Thanks!
Love the quickness and simplisity of this dough! Great in the oven or on the grill :)

This dough is really awesome! I had more time than most probably making this dough so I decided to put it in my bread machine for thorough mixing. I used the recipe as is except switched the oil for EVOO        (2 1/2 T). I also used bread flour in place of all purpose and 2 1/4 tsp yeast since I don't have packets. I then added some dried basil and garlic powder to the dough. I let my machine do the rest. When it was ready I floured a ziploc bag and put the dough in my fridge overnight. Next day I took the dough out and it had risen nicely. Left it out for about 1/2 hr then put 1/4 cup flour on my cutting board and shaped dough. I put my pizza stone in oven at 450. Let pizza stone get hot and took it out then put corn meal on it to prevent sticking. Transferred dough and shaped a little to fit. Baked the crust for 5 mins then put the sauce and other ingredients on it. Baked for about 15 mins then took out. Crust was hard when coming out but softened as it sat into really soft. It's the best I've tried so far! I think the idea is after it has come out of the machine not to manipulate it so much and you will end up with a nice dough!

Easy! Followed directions and ingredients as listed.  Used it for pan pizza and put it in the oven for almost 5 minutes to 'seal it off' before topping.  Was not bland, as some have suggested.  Will definitely used this recipe again.

given the ease and quickness of this recipe - perfect!  There's no excuse for homemade pizza anymore.

This recipe is perfect as is!  My wife and kids went to Grandpa's and my poker buddies and I outplayed the local pizza shop - needless to say, we needed something easy and FAST!!  No time to be creative, so we did it exactly as called for and it fed 5 "big boys".  I think it is better than anything offered by the national chains - not better than my local favorite pizzeria, but nobody would expect that!

For a quick & easy, no fuss crust for a pizza or calzone, this works great.  All these reviews saying "you need to let it rise," or "you have to proof the yeast exactly 10.3 minutes in a 72.9 degree room" - ignore them.

Follow the recipe, as written - toss the dry ingredients together, add the wet, mix it all up well, make a ball & roll or spread it out.  EXACTLY...AS...WRITTEN.  If you're looking for some fancy crust that you can spend 5 days making, this recipe doesn't claim to be that.  But if you've got a hankering for a quick pizza & it's the middle of the night & you've got all the topping but no crust?  This is going to do you just fine.  You can add some herbs, brush it with olive oil, or tweak it if you want - that's fine.  But you don't NEED to do any more than the instructions say in order to have a fully functional, perfectly acceptable, basic pizza crust.
works every time!

Great flavor and ridiculously easy. And I mean RIDICULOUSLY. I added garlic powder and basil; I also had to add some extra flour to help in binding the dough. I let the dough rise only as long as it took to preheat the oven. Made steam holes in a fork and baked the crust alone for about five minutes before topping. Note: the recipe says it yields one pizza. For those of you who like a more thin, cracker-like crust, I would suggest splitting one serving of dough into two pizzas. I used one batch per pizza and it came out a little too bread-like for me.

Our family loves this recipe and we have never had any of the issues that I've read in the comments. I agree with the 1st comment I read that this is meant to be easy and quick. Due to so many unsatisfied cooks I watched the video and saw a couple things. 1. The recipe says dry active yeast (she says that in the video) however dry active is little pellets and in the video she uses pizza dough yeast, which is ground up dry active yeast. This makes it so you don't have to "activate" the yeast pellets and wait for rising. 2. From making my own bread I've learned to mix the dry ingredients 1st, mix the water and oil in a separate container then mix them together. Honestly I don't know if this makes a difference for this recipe it is just one of the differences I saw I did.

Loved this pizza dough.  I made two batches and then divided the dough into personal pizzas, par baked them and then let my guests create their own pizza creations.  REALLY fantastic dough, many compliments and a great time with friends.

I made this dough tonight and it was perfect! I took the time to dissolve the yeast and sugar in the warm cup of water though and let the dough rise for 30 minutes. Then kneaded it lightly and let it rise again for 15 minutes. I feel the dough doesn't need to be flavored like others suggested; pizza sauce and toppings add all the flavor you need :) I made a huge deep dish pizza using all the dough in a 9x13 baking dish; piled high with cheese and toppings..the crust was thick, soft and moist just the way I love it!! Thanks for the recipe!
Perfect!  Use if for chicago style deep dish pizza in a casserole dish and it is wonderful!  I cover the dough with a moist cloth and let it rise for about 20 minutes.
Excellent Pizza Dough, good flavor, nice crust.  Held up well to my Ham and Pineapple pizza with bell peppers n onion toppings.  YUM!
i mixed the yeast with the warm water before mixing it with the rest of the dough. i would try this recipe again, because it was SO quick and easy.

excellent pizza dough. It was nice and elastic and very easy to work with. Good flavor and baked up crisp.Used it to make mini pizzas and garlic knots. Had some dough left and made 1 strombili. It worked for all of these recipes.

This is the recipe I have used for YEARS!!! I do knead it for 10 minutes and let it rise - just how I do it. After I seperate the dough and roll it onto my two pans, I do let it rise a bit more to thicken the crust. This is way better than Delivery!  The best sauce to use is Contadina pizza sauce, too! Try this several times - my dough never turns out the same way twice - sometimes the yeast makes a difference if it doesn't turn out!
This is mine and my family's favorite pizza dough recipe, we use it all the time.
We didn't find this very good, sorry.

Incredible recipe!  I've tried many dough recipes and have never been as satisfied as I am with this one.  Made it exactly and was thrilled with the ease of rolling it out - it was smooth as silk and didn't fight me at all.  Got it about 18" in diameter and my pan is about 15, so I cut strips of cheese and rolled it into the excess for a stuffed crust! BTW I sprinkled semolina in the pan generously, really added to the nice chew. When I make it again (maybe right now!) my only adjustment will be to up the salt by a pinch.  Thanks for providing this winner!

I dissolved the yeast in 1 1/2 cups warm water first, worked the dough and let it rise 45 mins, worked it again and let rise another 10 mins before rolling out 4 small crusts.  I made it a bit more diabetic friendly and healthier by using 1 cup of wheat flour, 1 1/4 cup of white flour and 3/4 cup of soy flour.  I also added a TBSP of oregano, 1 tsp of onion powder and a tsp of ground thyme to the flour mixture.
The kids loved it so much they had to make pizza again tonight!
I can successfully make a pizza now. Thank you! I will try out the "letting the yeast rise" methods sometime too, but quick and easy is definitely my style.

A great dough for home-made pizzas. The only big variation I would suggest is to just let it rise for about an hour and then use it. I tossed in a bit of basil into the dough and it gave it just a pinch of flavor, but I don't think the basil was even necessary. It's a good dough.

Edit: I cannot get this to come out the same way twice. Some times it'll be too sticky, Some times it'll be too powdery, Some times it won't spread, and other times it's like an oil slick. I've since abandoned this recipe and started buying the Jiffy brand packs. They cost 40 cents, they only need water, and they are consistent. We actually think the Jiffy packages are close to restaurant quality. Much less fuss and I know what I'm going to get out of it every single time so it's far less stressful.

I've tried a lot of pizza dough recipes and  this one is very good--best of all, the dough is easy to work with.  The only change I made was substituting olive oil for vegetable oil.  It isn't like the pizza dough at my favorite pizzeria but it is the best homemade pizza dough recipe I've come across.  I love how easy it is to make and use.  No need to let it rise.  It is a keeper!

Brilliant!  This easy and surprisingly good crust topped with pizza sauce 1 from this site and you can have a home made pizza in about 45 minutes made with common pantry staples and none of the scary ingredients found in a frozen pizza!  Thank you for sharing Gudny!

I love love love this super easy crowd-pleasing recipe! My only change was to make it with olive oil instead of vegetable oil and throw in some Italian spices! I've made it several times now and was wondering if anyone thinks it would be possible to make this recipe with wheat flour? Anyone tried it?
super easy and feeds my large family.

I'm not sure what I did wrong, but this didn't quite turn out like I expected. I did follow other's suggestions and let it rise for about an hour, and even pre-baked it for 8-10 minutes beforehand. The result is something like a foccacia bread instead of pizza dough - good, but not what I envisioned based on the pictures. I will keep searching for a good pizza dough recipe.

This is my standard pizza dough recipe. I have made this recipe two ways.  The first time I made it I let it rise first. My family didn't like it.  It was too thick and bread-like. The next time I did not let it rise first and my family liked it much better.  I cut the flour to 2 1/2 cups and cut the sugar to 1 tsp and that improved the recipe.  My bread making tip is to always proof the yeast first.  Add the yeast to the warm water and sugar and let sit for a few minutes until the yeast begins to foam.  Then add dry ingredients and oil.  This ensures that the yeast is still alive and will actually work in your recipe.

My family of six all loved this recipe.  The only changes I made were to use bread flour (just because I had some on hand) and I added some basil because we all love it.  Thanks for the easiest recipe ever.
This was my 1st time making pizza crust and it was not good at all.  I followed the recipe exactly and it turned out more like a biscuit.
Like other, I added some seasoning. But the recipe as is was awesome. I will definitely use this often.
Fast and  simple.  Just what I was looking for. Great recipe as is or change it up to suit your needs.  Will use this one often.  Thanks so much!
this recipe tastes just like pizza from a place i loved going to when i was growing up. this is definatly going to be a new meal in my house!

Very easy and delicious.  My dough only took 2 1/2 cups flour and was perfect.  I didn't do all of the extra steps that others did and it still came out delicious.  Whipped it up in the Kitchenaid, pressed it into a round pan, topped it, and baked.  So SIMPLE.

This was a quick and easy recipe. I did let the dough rise for about 30 minutes and used olive oil. I will double the recipe next time to make garlic knots, a calzone or stromboli. Thanks for a great recipe!

the best I've tried, and I've tried many different ones from the net and from books.

My way: I 'proof' the yeast, add it to the sugar water first, like another reviewer says. And I brush some butter on before adding sauce and toppings. I like to leave the dough in the refrig overnight; I think it improves the taste and how it works. Other than that, just like the rx says.

I've tried high gluten, low gluten, adding bread flour, pasta flour, different oils, different yeasts. Nothing works as well as this.
This recipe was awesome for making a quick pizza!  Thanks for sharing.

This recipe is fantastic if followed as is.  However, I did make some changes I feel improved the overall taste of the dish.  

Firstly, I proofed the active dry yeast in 110 degree water for ten minutes with the sugar.  Then added the flour (2 1/2 cup), two basil leaves from the garden, 1 clove minced garlic, and 2T olive oil and mixed for 5 minutes on speed 2 (KitchenAid) with the dough hook.  Then I added the salt and mixed for 1 more minute.  Let the dough rise in a warm place for 30 minutes.  Roll thin and bake for 5-7 minutes then topped with sauce leftover from The World's Greatest Lasagna (also from this site), cheese, and fresh basil from my garden.  

It was amazing!

Excellent!! It took about 5 min to gather ingredients, dump in my kitchenaid mixer, and viola. I used a regular sized pizza pan and hubby and I loved the thickness. Next time I might slide off on to oven rack for the last 5 min of baking to crisp up bottom. I love the fact you don't have to waite for it to rise, making this a perfect weeknight meal!

who knew somthing could taste so good and only take you about 5 min to make! I made a cheese pizza with it. Other pizza recipes call for leaving the dow in the fridge for hours to rise. well i don't have that kind of time! This was the best pizza i ever made. My whole family loved it and wants it every week instead of our "pizza hut" pizza night.
this was great! i really wanted a quick dough and this tasted wicked good :) i will definatly make this again. I made this just how it was and loved it.
very easy to make

Wake up, people!  This recipe is/was intended to be a FAST crust when you need pizza dough-  NOW.  It is not as good as one that has rested for three days, but it WILL make a darn good pissa, faster than you can get everything else ready.  It will work in a pan and it will work on a stone.  However, if you're using a stone, PLEASE use a lot of corn meal.  Baking parchment and a little corn meal is even better, but please slip-out the paper after 2-3-4 minutes in the oven and then continute baking on your stone.  As much as I like well-aged and flavored pizza doughs, this recipe works well for the "I need it NOW" pizza dough.  Double or triple batches are OK, if you have a strong mixer - and do not over-mix or machine-knead.  Divide as soon as mixing is done and let it rest as directed.  It may lack the flavor and texture of a mature dough, but it is a  site better than bought/delivered pizza, if you can wait 90 minutes.

Best pizza dough I have ever prepared for my family.  I found that after I topped it and let it set on the counter for 10 minutes it became much fluffier/thicker, or bake right away for a thinner crust.

Quick and easy.  I prefer thicker dough, but it tasted great.  It had a cracker type crust for me.  I rolled it with a rolling pin after I banged it into shape.  I also cooked it on 400 degrees for about 20 minutes.  I'm sure this affected the texture.  (Crispy)  I am giving 5 stars due to the fact that I didn't have to go to the store, (Had everything I needed.) and taste.  Now i can make pizza any time.  Awesome!

Delicious and quick. I had some extra time so I did let it rise for an hour: "1 1/4 cups warm water, 1 pkg active dry yeast, 1 tblsp sugar, 1 tsp thyme or Italian seasonings, 3 tblsp olive oil, 3+ cups of flour, 1 tsp salt. Mix water, yeast, sugar & oil in mixer bowl. Then add flour & salt. Mix-knead for 10-12 minutes, sprinkling with flour to keep from sticking to bowl. Dough should be elastic & smooth. Place dough in oiled bowl, cover dough with oil, cover & let stand 1 hr at room temp. Then divide dough 2 equal parts roll into balls, cover with damp towel & let stand another 10 mins. Use immediately. Don't forget to poke holes into dough with fork once rolled onto pan to let steam escape while baking. "

This recipe is perfect as is.  I might do like some other suggestions and pre bake it for a few minutes for a crispier crust then add my toppings.  The ways to flavor this or personalize it are endless, but it's also great just the way it is.
Great dough, really good considering the time it takes to make it.

This is a perfect recipe for me!  We do our own pizzas every Friday night and I have been looking for a good no-rise recipe that also is great grilled.  This one did not disappoint.  One batch yeilded 2 12" pizzas.  I love that the dough is easy to work with/shape (ie, not sticky and holds its shape).  I used 2 c white and 1 c whole wheat flour and proofed the yeast first, just because we like a crispier crust.  This is now my go-to recipe every Friday night!
Not the best crust, but definitely better than already made crusts. Quick and easy. Perfect for nights that I didn't plan to make pizza.

Followed the directions except added in a generous amount of onion powder, garlic powder, and Italian seasoning.  It turned out great!  I've used it three times so far, and everyone who tries it loves it!  I would recommend speading the dough over your pizza tray before prepping your other ingredients. Unless I'm feeling incredibly lazy, I will proably never by pizza again.  This was so good and truly easy!  And for those who don't use yeast packets, use 2 1/4 tsp of yeast.  To get the best results, put a little of your sugar in your warm water and add the yeast to that before mixing your other dry ingredients seperately.  It will let the yeast bubble up a bit, thus adding to the flavor.
This dough is super sticky at the beginning, but after letting it rise if you add some flour it's not hard to work with. Tastes good! I'd use it again just because it's so simple.

This was better than any delivery pizza. I added oregano and used olive oil the second time I made it, but the original recipe was excellent. It was so easy I will never order from a franchise again.

This was so easy to make. I shy away from doughs because while they are probably easy to do I haven't made them enough to feel comfortable with it. But I needed pizza dough and I came across this recipe. I will definitly keep this around for future use.

I followed the directions and the pizza dough turned out tough. Next time I'll try adjusting the ingredients. Easy though.

i made a well in the centre of the flour and put the yeast sugar and warm water in. then i added the oil making sure to withhold the salt. i then put all the flour on top of the well and put it on top of the warm oven. i left it til the top cracked and then i mixed it all in and gradully added the salt. i then kneaded the dough for a few minutes covered it in cling film and left it for about 1/2 an hour to an hour and came back kneaded it a lil bit more to get out the bubbles cut it in half and made two pizzas. i think the other people had problems cause they didnt let it rise at all. it was beautiful crust and it was nice and high.

This isn't my favorite pizza dough recipe, but it's nice because it's really quick and easy for weeknights. This recipe is super easy to make. I was able to make the dough , roll is out and bake it in less time than it takes for pizza to be delivered. And my family appreciated the effort to make them something special. Tastes great too!

Ok ... Is this the best pizza dough recipe ever?  Heck, no. That said, it was exactly what it says it is - quick, easy, and you've got decent pizza in no time. very tasty dough. my boys loved it. thanks!

I put the yeast in the warm water first like others said... This recipes was very easy to make and is great if your kids want to help. We really enjoyed this reciepe.

Also would like to add to the review from Kim, it helps to sprinkle your stone or pizza pan with a light coating of cornmeal to prevent burning and/or sticking :) My rating is based on my results with the suggested touchups!

Tasteless and WAY too dense. I even added some brushed on melted butter, herbs to the dough as it was being mized, and it still came out extremely bland. Plus, as was mentioned in most of the negative comments, the texture of it is just way off. I won't be making this again.

This recipe was just okay.  I made it exactly as stated and it was too thick and doughy - I wasn't able to get it to cook it all the way through without it being too tough because the dough was too thick.  Tastewise, it was good enough.

I also followed LADYMHARRIS's recipe and made two pizzas out of the dough. The second one tasted much better because it sat for closer to an hour per her recommendation. Great recipe!!!  No complaints.  If you have time it is better to allow to rise but still great if you don't have the time.

This is a very good and easy recipe.  I like it that the crust came out very nice and thin and crispy.  Although I did add a couple of extra ingredients to it like other reviewers suggested.  Add oregano, sugar, italian seasoning, parsley....
Super easy and tasted amazing!
This didnt turn out great for me, but it may have been my fault...  I think I made the pizza crusts way too think.
Awesome! My daughter said its better then the pizza shop.  I sprinkled the dough with garlic powder & Italian spices prior to adding toppings.
This was an awesome dough! I did reduce the flour to 2.5 cups and let it rest for 10-15 minutes. I then used the dough for grilled pizzas. The Family was happy and full!

Wonderful recipe, quick, easy and delicious! I used 2 cups whole grain flour and 1 cup bread flour, to make pizza pockets. They came out just wonderful! The BEST quick recipe for pizza dough I could hope to find!  I might try making bread sticks next...  A perfect solution for limited time and basic ingredients.

Perfect dough! Easy and quick. I did let it rise for 30 minutes just because it didnt look like there was much dough. I 30 minutes I had twice as much as I did when I started!  Great texture and taste. WIll use again. NO more buying dough from the store.

first time making homemade pizza! Made exactly as directed and the crust was soft, doughey with good texture! It was not crispy or thin (although I think that has everything to do with how flat you make it when forming the pie...) This is a keeper!

This is a tasty, easy, pizza dough!  It's also an amazing base for other things too....so far I've made cinnamon twists (added cinnamon and sugar to the dough and coated with the same), and breadsticks (added garlic powder, italian seasoning, and parmesan to the dough).
I'm sorry, but do not understand the rave reviews at all. Although very easy - tasted like eating pizza on a flavorless biscuit.

Actually, used this for Zeppolas "Fry Bread" take your pick of the name.  I let the yeast rise like the other reviews and then I let the dough sit for about an hour more after that. But the recipe, as is, deserves the full 5 stars.  You will never make pizza dough better than this with this little effort put forth.  Thanks for the FABULOUS recipe.  We will never order out again.

Easy and tasty.  Even better if you knead it and let it rise a little (I only did about 20 minutes).  I subbed 1/2 cup of whole wheat flour and added 1/4 cup honey and 2 tbsp of Italian seasoning.  Yummy!
quick, simple recipe that turns out great!  I love that I can make a pizza from scratch in less time than it takes to deliver one.

This was my 1st time making pizza. I followed the recipe exactly. It looked just like the pizza doughs I see at the bakeries. I added 1 egg and an egg yolk just because it seemed too dry; I addded as much extra flour as I needed for a workable dough. It was yuuuuuumy!!!!...I give this recipe more than 5 stars!!!.....at least 10 stars!!!!
Excelent recipe, easy, fast and very good taste. Try it as it is, and then, the next time, make the adjustments you consider necessary.   Thanx for this great recipe.
Best ever pizza dough....thanks
Not bad. Very easy to make.  I would suggest letting the dough rest for 30 minutes and increasing the oven temp.
I have used this dough recipe twice and I find it really quick and easy to make.

I have always been fearful when I need to bake anything with yeast. But now I'm a changed lady. This simple recipe made my day since the first try. An easy recipe for all...whether you are in hurry or just want to try something new.

Perfect every time and simple to make. I usually make a double batch and roll out half of them for bread sticks for a side. Truly worth a try if your making homemade pizza. this pizza crust is easy to make and easy to roll out for pizza or pizza rolls
great taste!
comes out perfect every time i use it and its soo quick and easy
we loved this. It was so quick and easy. Used olive oil instead of veggy, also after rolling it out, sprinkled with garlic powder, Italian seasoning and walnut oil.

Great recipe!!  For a better taste, I just added a pinch of garlic powder.

OMG!!! Possibly the easiest and best homemade dough recipe in the world! I loved the fact that I didn't have to wait for it to rise, then bake, then top, then bake again! My kids loved it because it was done super fast and they got to help :) 2 BIG thumbs up!!!

Very easy and versatile recipe that yields a tender, flatbread-like crust.  We added 2 cloves of crushed garlic, some basil, and an Italian Herbs mixture from Durkee. I love this recipe! It is so easy and tastes great!
great recipe! I did what the others suggested..cut the flour down and added basil and garlic.  I also let the dough rise.. delicious!
Good dough, although it seems to be temperamental. I can't always get it to turn out right. It always tastes good, though.

This was good for a quick, get-it-on-the-table meal. I made it and spread it out on my pizza stone. Then I let it rest for 30 minutes. I baked it for 15 minutes. Then I added my toppings and baked it for 10-15 more minutes. Perfect!

Tasted really good, and didn't make any changes other than prepping the yeast in the warm water and sugar before adding the rest of ingrediants and kneading for about 5 minutes. Really easy! Awesome...

My wife and I tried this for dinner and thought it worked out great.  We will be experimenting with some of the different versions, but overall, we were both pleased.

great recipe

I did not let the dough rise; I simply let it sit on the counter while I chopped my ingredients for the pizza.  I did not prebake the dough either.  Turned out great! This is a keeper!

Very good and so easy! Took advice of others and baked 10 min (mine was thick) then brushed with olive oil and Italian seasoning, topped with toppings and baked another 12 - 15 min. Tasted great and the kids loved it!

Great in Calzones but i have not tried pizza. I took some to school and they were great for lunch. My mom loved them alot and i have made them 3 times in the course of 2 weeks. It is great with oregano on top and with cheddar and parmesan cheese.

It is fast and easy.  I do dissolve the yeast and sugar in water like some of the other reviewers. I like this one for the quickness of the dough.  My house is too cold in the winter to really get dough to rise well.  I have added Italian spices and made calzones with this dough.

This is the absolute best pizza crust recipe!

asked for recipe. It's so fast and easy,too!!!

This is great!  As a treat, my mom would make fried dough for dinner.  Wanting to do the same for my kids, I was in search for a quick dough recipe.  Thanks!
Great quick and easy pizza dough recipe. We use it all the time at my house and we love it!

This was my first time making pizza and was a little nervous but thanks to the recipes being shown how to make it, I had no problem making it and will make it again! Just to see how I did for the first time I just made a simple cheese pizza, but since it turned out good I can go ahead and get creative like adding brocoli, mushrooms, and peppers.
Great recipe. A very easy fix. My family thanks you. This will not be a staple in my family.
The dough came out way too chewy for me.  I'm not sure if I kneaded it too much or not enough.  Either way, next time I'll try a more traditional dough recipe.

Fantastic...Fast Recipe!  With the exception of using Olive Oil instead of Vegetable Oil and adding more spices I followed the recipe to the T.  Easy, quick and yummy recipe, couldnt ask for more when your in a hurry!

Was my first attempt at home made pizza dough - everyone loved it.    I did split the ratio of flour to half white and half whole wheat, but that is just a personal choice - I am sure would have been just as good with all white flour.

Solid.  I added a tablespoon of minced garlic.  I think think that the fact you can add the spices that work for you without ruining dough makes this worthy of a five.

Great pizza dough.  Usually our pizza dough bubbles up like crazy.  This time we mixed the sugar, yeast, and water and let them sit for awhile before adding to the flour.  One the dough had risen, we made the pizza shape and put it on a pizza stone at 450 degrees for a few minutes till it hardened up a bit.  We then took it out and put the sauce and cheese on top, then put it back in the oven until the crust browned.  We've found otherwise that the cheese will be dark brown and the crust will still be a little raw in some spots if it all goes in at once.
We followed the recipe exactly! Turned out great!
Good "hand tossed" like crust. Perfect when you don't hive time to let one rise. Added Parmesan and herbs.

Thank you! Thank you! Thank you! We did this recipe for a Calzone recipe, and I was missing dough for this recipe. I never made dough before, and this recipe was easy  and the pizza dough was very good.
Quick, delicious, and husband approved! Thanks for sharing!

The second time I kneaded it and it turned out a lot better.  I had a little extra time also to let it rise a few min before I spread it out. I made this with calzones the second time, but the crust was too flat to use for them.  But it would of make a great pizza crust.  I will surely go to this recipe again when I need a pizza crust to whip up real fast. A little bland, but not bad. We let it rise an extra 15 min to fluff up.

I substituted one cup of flower with one cup of whole wheat flower, I think it gives it a bit better texture. I also sprayed the outer edge of the pie crust with butter flavored vegetable spray and sprinkled freshly grated Romano cheese on it before baking. I baked mine at 550 degrees for 15 minutes and it turned out perfect for my family’s likes.

This pizza dough is way better than average and more than qualifies as incentive enough to forget pizza delivery.  I made a double batch and used five cups of flour rather than six and it worked just fine.  I hand mixed the dough for a long time, following other reviewers recommendation of letting the dough sit for 30 minutes.  I'm glad I did.  The dough increased in size a LOT in the oven, so although I was concerned the pizza may be too thin, after rising in the oven, it was actually close to being too thick.  Just don't worry if it looks to thin when you put it in the oven - it will rise even more.  I used "Exquisite Pizza Sauce" which can be found on this website and flat out loaded my pizzas (I made two) with hamburger, canadian bacon, onion, pepperoni and cheese for a truly incredible meal.
The best!  Thanks!

No need to change anything. This is my go to for pizza dough. Quick, easy and delicious!  I have used it many times. Of course you can experiment with adding herbs and spices if you want but the basic recipe is great as is!  Thanks for sharing this.. My boys love homemade pizza night!

quick and easy to make!
This was a great recipe!! I make homemade pizza a lot but this time it was the best!!
This was easy to make and you can add so much other ingrediace to this dough. I had my 3 yr old son make his own pizza. it can be made just out of a bread. Very quick and easy. A must try.

Other things that went into the dough: subbed in olive oil, grated parmesan, chopped red onion, garlic, basil, rosemary and thyme (ALL INGREDIENTS FRESH). I, like others, cooked it for 5 minutes before adding toppings. If you're worried about the dough being too crispy, put some oil on the outter crust just before you throw it into the oven. It keeps it somewhat softer and is less likely to burn. But hands down, best dough I have had in a long, long while. Having read several reviews, I decided to follow the recipe exactly as written, especially since I was in a hurry.  I did use rapid rise yeast, since that was all I had.  I should have started with 2 1/2 cups of flour. The amount needed for a recipe does vary due to humidity.  Nevertheless, I used the full 3 cups, and the dough was quite dry.  I kneaded it until it was manageable, and then put the dough ball in the pan, flattened it out, and used a rolling pin to get it started.  It was quite stiff, but I managed to work it to the edges and up the sides of the pan. This brings me to a feature about this recipe that I really like.  When working with most yeast doughs, you end up with a lot of thickness around the edge of the pan, but with this dough, it stays put and does not continue to rise after you press it into place.  You don't end up with a thick ridge around the outside.   The directions are a little lacking, so I'm tempted to give this only 4 stars.  The end product is quite good, but not great.  Yesterday afternoon, though, when I was stressed out and in a hurry, this recipe came to my rescue.  Pizza dough this good, this fast, is worth 5 stars to me.

Added my homemade sauce and topping, it's just beautiful, smells great and tastes even better. Thanks for the original post and comments recommending the rising time. I love making pizza at home and have tried the pre-baked crusts and refrigerator roll-out crusts, but never tried homemade dough from scratch. I have found the pre-baked and refrigerator crusts to be disappointing and more difficult to work with (pre-baked crusts that are dry, crack, and fall apart, refrigerator crusts that do not roll well). This recipe was fantastic! I have made bread before so I began the same way by dissolving the sugar in 1 1/4 c warm water and sprinkled the yeast on top. I let it rise for a few minutes and added it to my flour, salt, and olive oil mixture.  My mixer's dough hook was perfect for the job; very quickly the hook evenly distributed all the ingredients. I lightly coated the ball of dough with olive oil and allowed it to rise about 10 min., covered, in a slightly warmed oven. I punched down the risen ball of dough, cut it into two balls, and rolled out two crusts using minimal flour to prevent sticking. The dough was not so elastic that it kept shrinking when I rolled it, but elastic enough to hold its shape.  After adding my desired toppings I baked two pizzas at a time on the top and bottom rack at 375° for 7 min., then switched them for another 7 min. They were perfect - light, soft, and lightly browned, not soggy or mushy. Roll the dough out more thinly for a crispier thin crust. This recipe is so easy and delicious that I would make it instead of buying a pre-made crust!

Tips for good rise.  DO NOT use tap water if your water is chlorinated, it will kill your yeast.  Make sure your water is also the correct temperature (too hot... kills yest, too cool, does not wake up yeast). 

BREAD MAKER:  this can be done in the bread maker for an even easier crust!
Place ingredients in the following order:
water, sugar, yeast, oil
Flour
Salt
Run your bread maker on the dough setting. When mixing is complete tip out onto lightly floured pizza stone and roll.

A few things I have figured out with pizza dough:
1. ALWAYS use bread flour to get the proper texture, other wise the dough will taste more like a biscuit.
2.  Handle the dough as little as possible.  This kind of applies to most doughs that need to be rolled out.  Just drop the sticky dough right onto a very floured counter top, then sift more flour on top.  I used a rolling pin to roll, then flip and flour, then roll, then flip, then flour.  The trick is using lots of flour.
4. Add some garlic to the dough, and put some melted butter on the crust.

This baked perfectly in about 18 minutes.  :)

Excellent crust, a snap to make. Had the pizza in the oven in 10 minutes...and that included sauteeing the veggies first. My family really enjoyed it -- thank you!
Great!!!!!!!! No complaints we don't even order pizza anymore!!!
Super easy and delicious!  Great when you decide to make pizza at the last minute!

This came out great. All I added was some fresh italian herbs for a fuller flavor. Thanks for the great recipe, no more delivery for me.
Totally awesome. No changes needed.

Very good pizza crust!  I did add 1 tsp italian seasoning and 1 tsp garlic powder after reading some other reviews - but would probably be just fine without it.  I let the dough rise 30 minutes before rolling out.  Brushing edge of crust with olive oil after baking helps with the presentation of the pizza - and also adds a little more flavor!

Instead of making a pizza out of this dough, I made rolls. What I did is let it rise, pat it down and let it rise again. Then I worked it for about 15 or 30 minutes. Then I baked it as normal in rolls. They where the best rolls I have ever eaten, and that is saying a lot! Great in a jiffy. Better if you have the time to let it proof.
wonderful, quick, simple and tasteful. I made oval shaped pizzas out of the dough, that looked like little gondolas. I topped them with ham, pineapple, mozzarella and tomatoe sauce.
Quick, easy, and just right size for my rectangle pizza baking stone!  No one will be disappointed with the flavor and crust stands up to lots of toppings!

Good flavor.  I did have to add extra flour b/c it was too moist. I also baked it for 5 minutes before putting toppings on b/c I like crisper crust. Next time I will either bake longer or use it for 2 sheets worth of pizza.
I made it this morning with my son and it came out perfect. He loved it, and believe me, if he approves it (he is so picky..) must be great! 5 stars!

I have tried this recipe twice as is. As RenaKS27 and Clare have mentioned: it is best to follow it as is for a nice quick pizza dough. Adding some dry herbs doesn't take too much more time. So the second time I did add some herbs to our liking. But overall, I love the ease of this pizza dough. You can make the entire pizza in less time than ordering in, and for about pennies to the dollar.
ok for quick
Excellent, used this recipe for a quick calzone, I added cheese, onions, and brocoli inside and folded the cirlce over like a calzone.  Worked out great.
No rising, no punching, quick and easy for when you need quick and easy dough! Five stars for the simplicity and no hassel of this dough. It's not gourmet but we don't always have time for that.

I think I have to agree with the previous commenter. People are missing the point of this recipe. It's supposed to be a last minute thing, and for what it is it's absolutely brilliant. The only thing I did differently was add some garlic powder and it turned out great. I agree that the extra steps do make a better dough in general, but for being a no-rise last minute recipe, it doesn't get better than this!

Loved it. Baked up nice and thick, but without having to mess with rise times! I added a dash of Italian seasoning. UPDATE: Made this again. This time I had to knead the dough to work in all the flour; once kneaded I divided the dough in half and rolled out two smaller circles. Prebaked for 8 minutes, then lowered the temp to 350 to cook the toppings and melt the cheese.
Awesome crust!   This is not a fancy crust but it is easy and fast.  That is what it's ment to be.  You do not need to alter the recipe.  Try it once as is and you will be sold!
really good dough, nice crust, perfect, pizza
Had fun at my sister's  brithday making mini pizza for doz girls ... so much fun and so yummy!

This is an easy pizza dough recipe. I recommend using a large pizza pan (14#) and really spreading out the dough to prevent the crust from being too thick. The 2nd time I made it I also spread olive oil on the crust which made it delicious!!
I prefer to add the yeast to warm water and wait for it to disolve, but that's just me. It is a good recipe though.

This dough is really easy. My kids loved it. I needed something quick and easy for dinner tonight. This fit the bill. I made 2 batches. The first I followed exactly. The second I used 1/2 cup less flour and added a bit of pizza seasonings. Both turned out great. I will definitely use this all the time. Even the kids can help make it.

I know this recipe by heart now.  Friday night is Pizza night at my house and I use this crust WITHOUT any modifications every Friday night without fail.  It is simple, easy to remember, and husband and kids love it!  I make my own sauce and we experiment with our toppings.  Love love love this crust.

I read some of the reviews and decided to take a little advice from a few of them, and it came out GREAT. Way better than I expected. Usually dough and I do not get along well at all...but this time it was perfect. So here's what  did.. 2 3/4 cup flour, 1 package active dry yeast, 2 tablespoons olive oil, 2 tsp salt, 1 tbsp white sugar, 1.5 tbsp garlic powder, 2 tsp dry oregano, and 1 cup hot water as hot as my sink gets.  I added all the dry ingredients and mixed, then oil, then water and mixed it up and attempted to knead it. It was a sticky mess and I thought Oh No! But I set it aside in a large bowl, covered it with a kitchen towel and left it alone for 30 minutes or so.   Preheated the oven to 400.. greased my pizza pan with olive oil, used the whole dough for one pizza, it fit perfectly. Then take a fork and make indentions all over the dough (so the crust does not bubble up anywhere) Then bake for 5 minutes, take out and continue on making your pizza.  That may just be the best crust in the world.  *My pizza was loaded with chicken and veggies and I cooked it at 400 for about 17 minutes and all of it cooked perfectly.

Wow! This is such a great recipe. I don't have any trouble with the 3 cups of flour but I generally dump in a little more olive oil than called for anyway. The first time I tried it, it turned out kind of dry and hard. The next time I let it rise for about 30 minutes and what a difference. It was fluffy and you could taste the heartiness of it. I usually double it and make one a pizza for the kids and the other I make calzones for me and my husband. I don't need to look any further for dough recipes, this is it!
needs directions. Yeast needs to be dissolved first.
It's ok, I think the taste is a little strong and not my favorite.  It's fast, though.

I HATE to cook and I LOVE this recipe!  I mix it in the bread machine.  I have also used this dough recipe to make pigs in blankets.  Who ever said it would result in a thin crisp crust has never actually MADE this recipe.  The dough is nice and soft.  I think it would also make good pretzels.  I've taken to throwing fresh oregano from my garden into the machine when mixing the ingredients, that's big time experimentation for me.  Thank you so much for this versatile recipe!
Fool proof.  I mixed wet ingredients and sugar with yeast and then flower and salt. Wasn't ready to use yet, so let rise 1.5 hrs.  Used for 4 calzones which we cooked at 350F for 35-40 min.

This is a great QUICK pizza dough.  I normally love a rich doughy taste with homemade breads but the exchange on this one is the time.  It's great when you want to make (or crave?!) pizza but don't have one, want to make pizza healthier or don't want to spend the money on a frozen one or delivery.  I've made this a handful of times now and the ingredient amounts have worked each time.  I haven't tweaked anything.  Will continue to make!  Thank you!
This is simple an ddelicious. I'm glad i found it. :D

I loved this recipe. It was tasty and so very simple. Great way to get dinner on the table in under an hour. The only thing I'd suggest is letting the dough rest for just 5 minutes or so. It makes it a little easier to work with

Okay, I was looking for cheap, easy pizza dough and this is perfect... It's just like school pizza! My almost four year old daughter (who has autism) helped me make the pizza and dough from start to finish, and she is eating lots of the pizza! Made a 9-13 inch pizza. Very simple, quick and tasty! Thanks! Will make again and again!

loved this! so quick and easy! make it for my boyfriend with mrs dash mixed into the dry ingredients and then stirred in crushed garlic into the wet. combined the two and made a delicious pepperoni pizza with a garlic bread taste!
Easy and delicious just as it is!!

Thanks Gudny for the recipe! Yes folks, there are many different styles of crust. If you are looking for one that has to be kneeded and rise and takes hours to prepare.... THIS IS NOT IT. What this is though, is a very good, simple, speedy recipe for crust that you can make and be eating in under an hour! I made as written, and yes, ALL the directions are there don't try to make this harder than it is people!! I coupled it with Easy Pizza Sauce III which is also terrific, and surprised the family with pizza in about 45 minutes. No more store bought dough, frozen or take and bakes at my house!!  This is way too easy  :)  Thanks again!
fantastic!!!! so easy to make, delicious. i made a smaller portion, only for me, and my mum ate a good part of it! fantastic. five stars. i'll make it again.

easy and tasty! I made the dough in the morning, oiled my 11x15 pan, rolled out the dough, covered with saran and let it rise in the fridge, when I got home I let it sit out while the oven was preheating, topped with meatballs, onions, peppers, mushrooms and Italian blend cheese, 25 minutes was perfect.

Great recipe, the only changes I made were to add 1 tsp of Italian seasoning and a little garlic salt to the dry ingredients and dissolved the yeast in the water before putting it in. I also used olive oil instead of veg. oil. I let it rise for about 20 min before making my pizza! It made a huge pizza and it came out awesome!!

This was the best thin crusted pizza crust that I have made.  I added garlic powder and basil and it was delicious.  I kept it in the refrigerator and used it for 3 days to make a small pizza each day.  The first day the dough was a little hard to deal with  and the pizza was a little thicker.  The 2nd day and 3rd day the dough was very easy to deal with and the pizza was cracker thin.  The only problem that I had, was after the basil and garlic sat for 3 days they became bitter.  Maybe it is not such a good idea to use the herbs unless you use the dough right away.

I also froze 3 pizza's with sauce and cheese for later.  I cooked the dough for 5 minutes before adding the toppings and the froze them.  I added fresh onions, tomatoes and green peppers before cooking on the grill and they were great.
great!

A wonderful recipe for pizza crust. After stirring everything together, I found that this dough really needed to be kneaded, and would not have worked without this step. After kneading for about 10 minutes, I oiled the dough and put into an oiled bowl, then covered and let rise in a warm place for about 30 minutes. After stretching to fit on a cookie sheet ( this dough is NOT elastic like traditional piazza dough) I parbaked it at 350 for about 5 minutes. Then I added my toppings and set in the oven to bake. The consistency of the cooked dough has a slightly crisp surface and soft inside. It almost reminded me of foccacia. DELICIOUS.

Super easy and really tasty. I mixed the yeast in the water, sugar, and oil first, stirred until dissolved, and then added the flour and salt. I also added some garlic powder, basil, and oregano. I let it rise while I was getting the toppings ready, rolled it out, brushed the edges with olive oil, sprinkled with garlic powder and salt, then baked it for about 20 mins and it was perfect!

Easy and simple to make.  This is a basic recipe and I can see where you can tweak this to make it what works best for you. I used this with the Unbelievably Awesome Barbeque Chicken Pizza from this site and it was very good. Thanks for sharing.
Perfect!  Thank you.  This is a very simple recipe that can be adjusted to anyone's tastes.  It was easy to follow and came out great.
Was okay, too doughy for my taste. My hubs liked it and it was quick, so I'd probably try it again when pinched for time. I proofed the yeast first and let it rise for about an hour.

I use this at least 2 times a week.  Sometimes I just roll out and use as flat bread for sandwiches. Adding sweet basil and powdered garlic makes for an excellent bread.
Easiest and fastest to bake on a Pizzaz.It's a cheap pizza baking machine that doesn't get the kitchen hot.  It comes out perfect in about 12 minutes.
This really is a GREAT pizza dough recipe! Only thing I added was some italian seasoning. PERFECT! So quick and easy! Will most def make it again! THANK YOU!.

for a quick, no rise dough this is very good. Super easy. Don't forget to put oil on your hands so the dough doesn't stick to you! I did use olive oil instead of veg. oil in the dough. I may try adding a little garlic to the crust next time I make it.

Wonderful! This is very fast and delicious, rolls or tosses out easily. I used EVOO instead of the vegetable oil, and added a few shakes of italian seasoning and garlic powder.  We've been using (and tremendously enjoying!) this dough for a while, and because I use a more liquid pasta sauce (pizza sauce can sometimes be rather sweet to our tastes) I find it helpful to bake the dough for 5-10 minutes before adding sauce and toppings. Thanks for this great recipe!

I have tried this recipe twice.  I did let it rise for about 1 hr both times.  In the mean time I got all the toppings ready to add to the pizza.  The first time I used the whole dough to make one pizza.  The second time I actually divided the dough into 2 parts and made to two pizza's.  This gave me a crisper shell, which I liked better.  I will definably make this again.
Really great soft pizza crust. We added some oregano and shredded sharp cheddar cheese to the crust and let it rise for about 30 minutes.

This did not turn out for me at all. I followed the recipe but my dough was soggy and the top of my pizza was way over done. The cheese was all brown. I don't know why it turned out so bad but I'm not making this one again.

I can say this is NOT the best. Nothing really can be perfect. But being quick and simple it is defiantly the best I prefer to use out of all I have tried simple or not.
I like to mix Garlic and union powder seasonings into this dough to add more flavor. When I cook it I have to go a full 25-30 minutes, or else it wont be cooked all the way since the first time I attempted this recipe was all messy going only 20 minutes. I also like to take Virgin Olive oil and rub it all over the dough once it has been formed into the pizza shape, square or round before adding sauce and toppings.
I have yet to try it without this, but defiantly easy and tasty with what I have experienced and very pleased with this recipe.
It is a very good one for someone new to making Pizza dough, to experiment with or try something new. (: Have fun!
Easy, Easy, Easy.  Instead of patting in a pan I made the dough ahead of time baked it off then let a bunch of 7 year olds make their own pizza's.

I love this recipe the only thing I would do is use bread flour instead of all purpose flour and spread some italian medley Mrs. Dash seasonsing blend salt-free. I suggest this because it makes you want to eat the crust as well. its an extra kick.

I subtituted 1 1/4 cups water and olive oil rather than veg oil like others had suggested. Overall it was a good crust! I make my pizzas on the bbq and this turned out crusty on the outside soft on the inside, a good combo.

This was a nice, simple recipe, but the pizza turned out a little doughy. Like many other reviewers, I had to add a little water to the recipe, but next time I will take the advice of others and dissolve the yeast and sugar in the warm cup of water, let the dough rise for 20 minutes, and pre-bake the dough for about 8 minutes before adding the toppings and cooking.
Great quick recipe!  I used 1 cup of wheat flour and 2 cups of regular.  It was very tasty and my 2 year old loved it!  I do recommend spraying your pizza pan a bit so that it wont stick.

I used this recipe tonight.  I made a pizza last week using my bread machine's recipe.  It was ok, but not great, so I came to allrecipes to find a better one.
I made this dough in my bread machine, which took about an hour.  It came out great.  Elastic, but malleable and not tough.

I will re-use it for certain.

Don't listen to any of the people who said the recipe didn't work or doesn't taste good. They obviously didn't make the recipe the right way!

I consider myself a good cook with a general knowledge of baking.  I've tried this twice.  It just didn't work for me.  It was flat, hard, bland (although a bit sweet), and just not good each time. I give it a two because it wasn't inedible and because I recognize that it is possible that I just missed something.

this is a real quick easy recipie, and it came out great the first time i made it. although many here suggest to let it rise for a little while first, it isn't needed. i put mine right on the pan and i still had a nice thick crust to work with.
Thank you for this recipe.  It is perfect just the way it is.  For those of you who want a more complicated and lengthy way to make pizza dough --go find another recipe.
This was bad. WHat is the point of adding yeast if the dough is not going to rise? It was dense, bready, cracker-like. why is this recipe getting good reviews?

What can I say other than WOW!
This was the first time I have ever made pizza, and the crust was excellent, and very easy! WONDERFUL!

Easy enough recipe, but as will all pizza crust recipes, it all depends on how you like your crust. As a Chicagoan, not all crusts are the same. This was easy to prepare and all, but it came out like bread sticks in consistency - soft. It didn't have any real chew to it and frankly, it was very bland. If you're looking for an edible carrier for your pizza, this works. I like a crispy thin crust with a definite chew so this had to receive only three stars.

Five stars for ease!  We've tried lots of pizza crusts - Boboli, Freschetta, a premade crust from an independent store, the Trader Joe's pizza dough that you roll out at home... None is quite right.  The Trader Joe's crust was especially frustrating, since it would always start shrinking back when we tried to roll it out.  I threw the ingredients for this crust together and had it rolled out in 15 minutes.  I did mix the yeast and warm water first and let it sit while I got the rest of the ingredients out.  I kneaded just enough to bring the ingredients together, and I was able to roll it out fairly thinly (the way we like it) to fill a cookie sheet with no snap-back problems.  I prebaked for 10 minutes at 400, put on toppings, then baked another 15 minutes.  It turned out crispy at the edges and chewy in the middle... just the way we like it!  My husband is VERY particular about his pizza, and he loved this crust.  Thanks for the recipe!
UPDATE: I've made this four times now and it's been just as easy every time.  Love it!!  I've been wondering if I need the yeast, since I don't allow the dough to rise at all.  Also, my daughter (7 months old) loves this pizza, and it makes a great teething biscuit (when prepared without salt) because it doesn't crumble in her mouth.  I usually use 1 c whole wheat flour and 2 c all-purpose and top with the sauce from World's Best Lasagna (on this site).
Tripled recipe and added garlic and basil as suggested.  That MADE it!  I let it rise for about an hour.

Excellent for the busy week night and you just HAVE to have pizza (okay maybe it's your 5 year old who HAS to have pizza :)  So fast & easy - beginning to the table about 40 minutes.  The only change I made was to add 1/4 more water - it was a little dry at first.  Thank you so much for sharing!

I'm giving this recipe 5 stars even though I changed it up a bit.  I did everthing the same except I used olive oil and added italian seasoning and I let the dough rise for a little while.  I didn't realize making pizza was this easy!  I'll be making my own pizza more often :)
Fast, easy and delicious. I couldn't have asked for more. Now we can have pizza any time without the hour long drive to pick it up.

it's a very simple basic dough. i used the recipe exactly as directed for the first time and it was delicious. i used a cookie sheet instead of a pizza pan. 

i'm looking forward to playing with spices and garlic.

Making this dough for the second time tonight.  Last time the whole pizza disappeared!  Crust is not too thin and not too thick.  I followed others' advice and added a tsp of garlic powder and 1/2 tsp italian seasoning before letting the dough rise in a warmed oven.  I also waited to add the salt until the dough had risen for 30 min.  Great recipe!
I don't get all the positive reviews, just couldn't get this to work out for me.  Crust came out dense, heavy, and raw-tasting.
great recipe.  i did let the dough rise for about an hour.  i got two good size pizzas out of this dough.
The pizza dough recipe was very fast and very easy. The only thing I did not like was the yeast taste. I think not letting it rise does that. But myself and my husband both liked it.

5 stars for quick! It was good enough for my seven year old son, my husband, and I! My son wanted to learn about how pizza is made and I didn't want to spend hours on the dough - this is a great recipe when you don't have a lot of time.

This is a good basic ingredient list. I have used it many many times and have added what my family has found to their liking and what I have in my pantry. I don't usually follow any recipe to the T but tweak it to my liking. I always refer back to this recipe for the ingredients etc which is why I give it 5 stars!  It has worked great for me.
I don't know what I did differently than other reviewers, but I did not care for this. Very tough and no flavor.  Followed the directions exactly.  Will not be making again.  Very disappointing.
You can't beat this for a QUICK pizza crust!
Very good and easy. I added garlic powder, oregano, and Italian seasoning.

So I followed some people's advice from here and added seasonings, as well as giving the yeast and then the dough some time to grow. Let me tell you, hands down the absolute best pizza dough recipe EVER! And so simple! 

I doubled the recipe and put it into these medium sized stone dishes, and they kind of became more like Pizza Cakes because the dough grew so much in the oven, so if you double the recipe, divide it so that you get three portions instead of two (or use a really big baking sheet so you could spread the dough out thinner.

Great job with this recipe and great advice from the other users!

My kids loved this recipe...I took some of the suggestions from others and let the yeast bloom in the water before adding to the flour mixture.  I also found that I needed a tad more than one cup.  Definitely something great for the kids to help with - they loved eating the pizza they made!
this is a good recipe. i did not change anything. it prove to be alright and popular among my housemate
Very good for being quick and easy.

This crust was a lifesaver! My kids were clamoring for pizza and I didn't have time to let my dough rise so ! tried this. I thought it was awesome for being so easy and it tasted good. Definitely not parlor crust but it passed here! 

Thanks!

I was really pleased with how this dough turned out. I used olive oil instead of vegetable oil, 2 tsp Italian seasoning, and 1 tsp garlic. I also ended up using a bit less than 3 cups of flour. I really love how quick and simple this is. I used a regular cookie sheet because I don't have a pizza pan, and it baked up beautifully!

My 11 year old son made his first pizza tonight & used this recipe for his crust.  He did it all by himself, with me just supervising.  It was AWESOME! We were all so proud of him & it was delicious, too.  We didn't even have to fake it.

I don't understand why anyone thinks this is good.  My pizzas have been in the oven for 30 min. already and the crust is so soft and undone but all the toppings are drying out and burning.  I will never use this recipe again.  I wouldn't give it any stars but I don't have that option.
This is so quick and easy!  It bakes great and tastes great.  The dough rises in the oven! I make this dough all the time.  It's a keeper.
I made this three times. 1st time as written...perfection. 2 & 3 time letting it rise and adding dry herbs to my dough... Perfection! Love this!
sorry to say that this was the worst pizza crust that i've ever made!  i had to serve it to my mother-in-law and it was an embarrasment!
quick and easy dough.  It needs no changes, no alterations.  Perfectly basic.  Those who are rating it low are forgetting that this is a basic recipe.

This is an awesome versatile recipe!  Its great how it is, and even better with different tweaks.  I actually use a cup of whole wheat flour and 2 cups white to make it a tad healthier and the taste is awesome.  I also include about a tablespoon of garlic powder and substitute unsweetened applesauce instead of oil.  I preheat the oven after I'm done mixing it, then set the dough in a covered dish on the oven so it has a few minutes to rise.  After the oven is preheated, I then make up the pizza and it comes out 13 minutes late absolutely delicious!  This is definitely a staple in my house!

Kids loved getting their hands in the dough and to stretch it and shape it up. And it came out great! Made two 12" pizzas and 4 pig-in-a-blanket with full size hot dogs. Kids wanted to eat them before even putting them in the oven. 
Oh, I messed up when reading the ingredients, and I added a spoon of apple cider (I have no idea how, where or why I saw that), but it turned out great even with this. Thanks for sharing! Will definitely make it again.

I've made this twice. Once using only whole wheat flour and one using a combo of regular and whole wheat. The mixture of the two turned out better than the entire whole wheat. I find that when I use whole wheat flour I have to add more water or it's too dry. I usually add garlic and onion powder to the mixture as well for some flavor. A super yummy crust that's super easy!!
This pizza was incredible!! My roommates couldn't believe I pulled off making my own crust.  We'll definitely make this whenever we have a pizza craving.

This is now our staple pizza dough recipe. I don't even want to bother with any others! I really enjoy the pizza it makes, I could eat it just about every night! I use 2 teaspoons of salt instead of 1, and sometimes add garlic powder and dried herbs to the dough. It also works well with a mixture of whole wheat flour - 2 cups whole wheat with 1 cup all purpose makes a very tasty crust.  Love it, thanks for sharing this!
quick and easy... made a lot of dough! could have made two pizzas :)

So far I've not had great success with pizza dough -- UNTIL NOW!!!  This recipe was great.  I've made it twice now, to prove that it wasn't just blind luck.  And to top it off, we used it on the grill!  It has great texture and flavor.  Once I added a little garlic powder and dried Italian seasonings to give it a little twist.  Another time I topped it with a little bbq sauce grilled chicken and a light sprinkling of cheddar cheese.  This will forever replace any other pizza crust for me.  Thanks for the recipe!

Excellent for easy pizza in a pinch! I used my bread maker on the dough cycle, for an hour instead of the 1 1/2 hour it usually runs. Added a Tbsp. of honey and Tsp. of Italian seasoning.  Really glad I tried this!
Absolutely delicious - light, quick, and easy to make!

I have made this recipe with the suggestions from LADYMHARRIS >10 times, and the pizza dough is perfect! I understand this particular recipe is meant to be simple, but it just doesn't produce the right texture. I highly recommend following LADYMHARRIS's suggestions. You will be very pleased with the results.

Thank you for sharing this receipe .I loved this dough.I thought it was awesome that it came out so well considering that I did not allow it time to rise.The only problem that I had is that it stuck to the bottom of the pizza pan so next time I will definitely need to spray the bottom of the pan with oil.
I've used the same pizza dough recipe for years.  My kids loved this one.  I guess it's time for me to change recipes.

I have used this recipes a few dozen times. I really like it and it's easy. That is the point. I like it thin and crispy. I parbake it first then load up my topping. Then I put it directly on the rack. Voila. Delicious. Gudny, you are on to something good...

This dough recipe is delicious and very easy to make. It works really well for making homemade "hot pockets" and filled braided breads. I mixed it in my bread machine on the dough setting so I didn't have to mess with it until I was ready to throw my pizza together.

Great recipe.  Like others, I used olive oil instead of vege oil, and reduced the water a little.  I always make ahead of time (in my bread machine on the dough cycle) and then refrigerate it for  a few hours.  It rolls out a lot better after resting in the fridge- it doen't "shrink" back when shaping it into the pizza.  I make two pizzas out of this recipe because I like a thinner crust.
For a quick and easy pizza dough, this recipe is great!

This pizza dough turned out thin for me because I mixed in the oil a bit late, but still everyone in my family enjoyed it. I always prefer though to add some dried basil, oregano and thyme or some Mrs. Dash Basil and Garlic and some garlic powder to the dry ingredients, for an extra measure of flavor. I don't have a large pizza pan, so divided this recipe in two and made 2, 12 in. pizzas.

Tried this today, and it's excellent.  I did add some garlic and onion powder to the mix, and did let it rise a bit before I spread it into a pan. Then let it sit for a while before I pre-baked it for 7 minutes.  I am sure it would be all right as written, thus the 5 stars.  I just had time to kill before dinner.  It is great tasting, and I will continue to use this recipe from now on.  Froze half of it too.
Great pizza dough recipe.  We ended up using this for calazones and got 4 good sized ones out of this recipe.  I will be using this again and again.  Thanks.
This was an amazing crust!  I spread the crust on a pizza stone and covered it with a melted butter/garlic mixture.  It really made me look like a chef!
good easy, quick dough. and you can add what you like!
Just add a tiny bit more sugar and flour, a pinch and it's great and easy.

I'd give this 5 stars because it definitely gets the proportions right, but as many have pointed out a simple "combine" direction isn't good. You should at least do the following (1) add warm water to yeast first (esp. if you refrigerate your yeast) and allow to dissolve (2) add sugar and let dissolve (3) add salt (more like 1.5 tsp for good flavor) and dissolve (4) add oil. This still only takes about a minute total but allows some proper yeast development. Then, add two cups of the flour and stir together in bowl. Put onto counter-top and knead in another 3/4 to 1 cup of flour and some herbs (oregano, basil, etc.). Then roll out after a couple minutes. In total your prep time is *still* ten minutes but you'll get a much, much better crust!

1 1/4 cups warm water, 1 pkg active dry yeast, 1 tblsp sugar, 1 tsp thyme or Italian seasonings, 3 tblsp olive oil, 3+ cups of flour, 1 tsp salt. Mix water, yeast, sugar & oil in mixer bowl. Then add flour & salt. Mix-knead for 10-12 minutes, sprinkling with flour to keep from sticking to bowl. Dough should be elastic & smooth. Place dough in oiled bowl, cover dough with oil, cover & let stand 1 hr at room temp. Then divide dough 2 equal parts roll into balls, cover with damp towel & let stand another 10 mins. Use immediately. Don't forget to poke holes into dough with fork once rolled onto pan to let steam escape while baking.

The pizza baked for 25 minutes & the toppings were cooked perfectly (cheese just a bit brown) and the dough had puffed up so that it was nice and fluffy, but the dough was not cooked all the way through.  I think that either I would have to spread the dough thinner (or use a larger pan), or else I would need to let it rise for a little while before baking. I wonder if I could use quick rise yeast. Also I thought that the dough did not have much flavor so next time I will add some spices etc.  Otherwise I think that this is great - very simple & relatively quick!  Update 5/25/09:  I made this recipe again a couple days ago and I found out what my problem was.  The water I was putting in was too hot and was killing the yeast, that's why the dough was too dense and not cooking all the way through.  I put in "lukewarm" water this time and it was perfect.  The dough was soft and plyable and rose to be very fluffy!
