I was excited to find a pizza dough that would be quick and easy... I made it exactly as the recipe says. I have experience making yeast dough and have made many of my own pizza doughs and this was by far the worst I have had. The dough would not cook through all of the way and I always parbake my crust. "Quick and easy" was not worth it.

This recipe was so good! Substitutions included- replacing coconut sugar for white sugar, I put the warm water and yeast in a separate cup while I prepared the other ingredients, and remember to poke little holes in the crust so that no bubbles form. Also, I cooked in oven for 10mins before adding any sauce or toppings so that it wasn't mushy. Then, I added the toppings and cooked for the remaining time.

My family is sold on this recipe, the only one I make now!! This dough is so easy!!!! Just as quick as delivery pizza, but soo much more tastier since we know exactly what is going on it and who has been touching it! Amazing home-made pizza in less than an hour!! I double the recipe and get three pizzas out of it. I also have added a little dried oregano and garlic powder to the dough on occasion and sprinkled on parmesan for breadsticks to go with Lasagna and spaghetti.  This recipe ROCKS!!!!!!!!!

Note the two steps.  Yes, it's pretty much that easy and makes a great pizza crust.  My first attempt yielded a pretty thin crust so I increased the ingredients by 25% and got a thickness that I liked better.  My daughter is vegan so I use this to make vegan pizza, which turns out great.  So good that I'm happy to eat it and I'm not vegan.

I altered the recipe some by adding oregano and garlic to the flour and activated my yeast beforehand with the water, sugar, and salt. Then let the dough sit overnight in the fridge (wasn't my original intention). It was probably one of me and my wife's favorite so far. It filled about an 18" pan with a hand-tossed fluffy dough, then the outer crust ended up really good too. Definitely keeping this one.
This is a great quick & easy recipe! I didn't modify a thing and mixed it all in the bread machine. Thank you for posting this!

The pizza dough was fairly easy to make.  i slowly added the water and oil (like one would do for any other kind of dough). however, i had troubles baking. the dough would still be white, and my cheese and the verge of burning. i suppose next time, i will pre bake the dough for 10-15 minutes and then add on the toppings. other than that, everything was super.
i have made several pizza doughs and i found this one to be very thick and tough though i hardly mixed it at all. we ate the pizza but won't be making this one again.

FAN-TAS-TIC.  I used exact ingredients, and added a little flour as needed.  Although this is a quick recipe and good as- is without allowing dough to rise, I was able to let it rise without prolonging the prep time anyway (which does add a little special something to the end product).  It turns out, if you mix the dough ingredients first knead dough and set it aside covered, you will likely have plenty of time to let it rise while you brown your meat and chop your other ingredients.  I also make my own sauce, so I did all of the topping prep while my dough sat covered, and it turned out soooooo good.  I did not bake the dough before adding toppings and used a large cookie sheet.  Perfect medium thickness crust.  It is not a hard dough, not crispy or thin, and did not get too big or tough, it was so perfect.  Don't hesitate to try this.

This dough has a great taste and easy to make too.
However for my needs I doubled the recipe to fill a large baking pan then put on the sauce cheese and topings. My family and I like a thick crust and due to the fact that I had loaded on two pounds of cheese and a pound of ground round we need the thicker crust to hold the weight.

Super recipe! I followed tips from other reviewers and let my dough rise 30 min.,puched down, kneaded, and let rise about 10 more minutes. It was so easy to roll the dough.I like a thin crust so I cut the recipe to 5 serving plus a little added flour and I easily rolled out a 16 inch thin crust pizza dough. Other than some added spices for taste the proportions are perfect!
Very quick, very simple & very good.   I added a bit more flour because I was out of cornmeal to keep it from sticking.  Fast and perfect!
Fantastic! Fantastic! Fantastic!
very good..bot is missing someting..

Made this last night for friends that came over. They loved it and talked me into making another pie! For never having made pizza dough before it came out quick, easy, and best of all great tasting! I did add the extra spices that others mentioned. Between pizzas and bread, I guess it's time for a baking stone!!

We love this recipe, we used Olive oil and 2 1/2c of flour, basil and black pepper.  Let dough rise for 30 mins, Cooked for 20 mins but next time we'll leave it in longer.  Otherwise AWESOME dough.  No more ordering in. Thanks.

Fantastically easy! I made this in the bread machine with 2 tbsp rapid rise yeast and a dash of Italian Seasoning. I substituted the all purpose flour with bread flour and the veggie oil with olive oil - just personal preferences. It tastes great, especially considering how quick it is to make. My boys loved it for lunch, we'll be making this quite frequently now! Thank you for sharing!!
Can I pre-make this dough and keep it in the fridge in a bag for a day or two before using it?
Very Good! But, if you are using a machine like i did to make this dough, add 1/2 cup of warm water to help it along. turned out amazing! best simosas ever!
It was quick and easy, but I found it lacking in flavor.

great dough!  probably the first time ever that every one ate up all of the crusty outer pieces first!  I proofed the yeast with the warm water and a couple pinches of sugar before adding - and I did let it rise a bit on top of the stove while the oven was warming.

Super quick and super easy. Took longer to find a quick and easy recipe than it did to actually make the pizza. Thanks again. I will tweak it a bit, adding some herbs and garlic next time... when I have more time!

Some of the reviews suggested making breadsticks with this recipe.. Don't even try that.. It was soft n soggy. As a quick pizza base, it's good n easy to make. Made a thin crust pizza n it tasted really good.

Tried this recipe tonight. Loved it!!
The pizza was amazing and soft and rise perfectly evenly. One thing I did, was poke a fork all around the rolled out dough. Best pizza dough recipe I have ever tried!
Great recipe, and super easy. I did knead it just to get the dough together properly. :)
fast, easy, tasty

excellent quick - spur of the moment pizza crust!!! Makes a nice crisp crust very quickly.  Thank you!  (note, this is not a deep dish, risen dough, that takes a little more time, and planning ahead.  We use Jay's recipe for that.  This is for those times when you want pizza in 30 minutes - excellent!!!!)

THIS WAS A MARVELOUS PIZZA DOUGH RECIPE. GREAT AND VERY QUICK AND SIMPLE TO MAKE.  IF YOUR WANTING MORE OUT OF THE DOUGH THEN IT WILL REQUIRE MORE TIME.  BUT THIS IS EXACTLY AS STATED QUICK! FOR THOSE WHO COMPLAINED REREAD THE RECIPE IT DOESN'T SAY TO ADD ALL EXTRA STEPS. THIS IS A QUICK BASIC PIZZA CRUST NOT A FANCY RECIPE.  THIS ONE IS A SURE FIRE KEEPER NOT TO DRY AND MADE EXACTLY AS THE RECIPE STATED.  THANKS FOR THE RECIPE....ITS A SURE WINNER!!!
This recipe is amazing and perfect!!!! I followed it exactly and in the last minute I added some garlic powder to the dough. It rose beautifully and tasted delicious! So soft and fluffy! Perfect!

I gave it two stars because it was edible and it was easy, but it really was dense, thick, and boring.  I rolled it out to about 1/6th of an inch and poked holes in the dough with a fork, and still it was thick and dense.  I would not make this again.  I think this would be a good crust for anyone who likes thick crusts.
Fast and tasty!

WOW!!!If I could rate this 10 stars I would!!! Make it exactly by the directions (well I used olive oil) and you wont be dissappointed!!!! SO easy and absolutely delicious!!! So simple, you can make a pizza faster than you can call and have one delivered! Ive never been so exited about making pizza! This is awesome, THANK YOU for sharing!

This recipe wasn't all that good. I ended up having to add a couple tblsp of milk when I was making it because the dough didn't want to cling.
Once cooked, it was a little soggy, and over all we really wern't impressed. Sorry

The best and easiest pizza dough recipe out there!  Anybody can make these, even a 2 year old.  I have followed the recipe to a tee with awesome results and have also let the dough rise multiple times and it doesn't make a big difference.  I always add a teaspoon of Italian seasoning & a 1/2 teaspoon of garlic salt to give it a little more flavor.  SO GOOD!!!!

This pizza dough was as advertised basic and quick!  I made it Saturday night and our pizza was ready in no time.  I completely appreciated how quickly our meal came together, however, I would try to flavour the dough somewhat the next time I make it with herbs or garlic as it was a bit on the bland side despite the numerous toppings we had on the pizza.  This is the reason I only gave it four stars. Great recipe and will be my go to for future pizzas!

I put it at 425 because I didn't have time to wait... the crust stuck to the bottom of the pan...not sure why...  I have to say pretty good though...   I'm thinking more salt not much flavor to the crust... I added garlic and spaghetti season to the crust.  We made two batches... and the one that we needed and let rise for a bit turned out way better.

To all those who feel it is needed to change a recipe that someone has spent the time to add it here, you should just put your own recipe in. A few hints are good, but changing it completely and telling the author it is not right, is not acceptable. If you do not like it, leave it at that.  I have used this recipe for what it is, SIMPLE & QUICK.
this was a good base recipe. I added one kiwi, and only half a lime. Plus about a quarter cup of sugar. I found after blending that I had to strain it  also. It's refreshing and very good. :)

I am drinking this right now!  I had to add 3 TBSP. of orange juice and 3 packets of splenda.  It made one glass (not a huge one, either), so I do not see how it is possible make this be four servings, but it is very good and refreshing and I will enjoy this often over the summer!  Thank you for sharing your recipe!

I just made this it was only enough for one serving! Maybe two small servings. I did add 1/2 cup of apple juice and a spoonful of honey. After I blended the original recipe. After the adjustments it was waaaayyyyy better!
I didn't think it could be that simple! I also added sugar but I guess it just depends on how sweet your oranges are.
this is yummy, but TART!!!!  we doubled the recipe and added a packet of stevia.  next time i'll double the orange-to-lime ratio.  definitely a true taste of summer!
AMAZING recipe i added more sugar though

This was a refreshing drink. I followed the other reviewer and did change it up a bit. There was no sweetener in it so I used 2 packs of Truvia. I tasted it without it and it was kind of sour. I had an orange in the freezer and cut it up and used that. I replaced the lime with a lemon also. I needed a liquid to get the mixture to blend in the blender. I added 1/4 cup of orange juice. I was able to get it to blend but it was very taxing on my mixer to break up 12 ice cubes and it is a quality blender. It was tasty, and reminded me of a drink version of an Italian ice, but after about 30 minutes it melted down to a glass of sweet orange juice with icy bits.

For as simple as this is, I really liked it! I liked the bit of sweetness and lightness of it. This would make a wonderful sandwich/burger spread, but I was dipping pretzels in it, and that was great too...I will def be making this again! Thanks for sharing. :)
simple, creamy and delicious!

Pretty decent tasting guacamole. I switched out the pepper for granulated garlic and added less mayo and more pepper sauce. I have a garden that is over run with tomatoes right now so I used up a small one. Good little snack, thanks for sharing.

lemon is a must in this for me...and cilantro also but I sometimes don't have i and find that adding some hot sauce makes it nice too. don't think the mayo is really necessary either. for me this isn't really guacamole but another type of avocado dip. guac needs lemon and cilantro
Dear Lord, thank you for this drink. Amen.

It is December and I have a ton of tangerines - this isn't just a summer time drink.  It is pretty good - it might be a little sour for some people but that is easily fixed by having some lemon - lime soda on hand for those that want it.
Made this for a backyard party and people LOVED it! I substituted mango juice for tangerine because I couldnt find that.  I had to make a second batch, it's going to be our summer drink!!

I did not care for this at all.  Tasted it after mixing and it was very sour, had to play around with adding different ingredients until it tasted okay so I wouldn't waste all the vodka.  Was able to salvage it, but won't be using this recipe again.

This was pretty good.  I did mess around with the recipe a bit to get the taste I wanted.  I didn't have tangerine juice, so I used orange.  I also halved the recipe to make a small pitcher.  Thanks for giving us a great punch idea to try!
I used a vegetarian chicken cube with 2 cups water and a little more than 1/4 cup flour. Thickness is great and very quick to make.

Well, yesterday was Thanksgiving so instead of 2 tablespoons of chicken drippings, I used turkey instead. I have the tendency to be gravy challenged but this turned out perfect for me. It was a little thinner than most but that is how I prefer it. I wasn't sure about the canned mushrooms but I was very pleased with the outcome. Fresh parsley really makes a difference in this one. I will be making this again today so that I have some for all of the leftovers.

I made it exactly as the recipe said with one exception. I added some vanilla pudding, as one reviewer suggested, to the cream mixture to make it more stable.  The flavor and texture were great.  However, if the yule log is not eaten by the day after it is made, the frosting loses its fluff.

I made different yule logs over the past few years, and they all came out too dry and tasted so-so.  I tried this one last year and it was a total hit.  I didn't use the liquor (kids) or the marmalade.. I just basically made the recipe that's on the wafer box.  It looked great and tasted so decadent.  I'll be making it again this year.  Thanks for the idea!  Edited to add: when I make whipped cream I usually add a little instant pudding mix.  Partly because it adds flavor and sweetness, but mostly because the gelatin stabilizes the whipped cream.

I made this for a Christmas party potluck at my boyfriend's parents house. Everyone loved it! They ate the entire thing! Even the kids loved it, which surprised me because I wasn't sure if they'd like the dark chocolate flavors for the cocoa or the orange marmalade.  I couldn't find chocolate wagers anywhere! I checked three different major grocery stores. I substituted with Nilla vanilla wafers and it worked out great!   I also loved how everyone thought that I put so much time and effort into forming the "cake" into a log. None of them had to know that they were actually eating Nilla wafer cookies and it only took about 30 minutes of prep time =)  Will definitely make again next year. Absolutely delicious!

We've been making this Bûche for the past 2 Christmas holidays. It's amazing how the flavors meld together when it rests! The wafers get soft and really incorporate themselves well. This log is nice and light-- not too sweet either. We use raspberry jam with a little liquor. The nonpareils and kisses are all extra stuff. 

Can't say enough positive about this one! :)
Outstanding and easy to make!
The alcohol was very strong for my family and I. It was difficult for me to  make, but I've never made a yule log before. Some directions were confusing for me as well.
it was tasty but othing special. probably wont make again
I liked this and it had the perfect amount of booze for us. Most call for more than one type which gets a little confusing. This blend was great!

This recipe is excellent!  I have been trying to find an easy, inexpensive recipe that is not just the bottle mix.  This was a great alternative to making a margarita with fresh lemons, limes and oranges.  It tastes the same, if not better, and is great when lemons, limes, and oranges are out of season or too expensive to use in a drink.  It also doesn't have that stomach upsetting sour taste.

My whole family loved it!  I plan on using this recipe again and again!
It's Great!!

I was skeptical about grapefruit flavored soda for a margarita, but I don't like mixes so I gave this a try and I am so glad I did -- it is fabulous!  I've made these three times in the last couple of weeks and all tasters loved them.  I used Fresca for the grapefruit soda -- nice to cut out a few calories in an adult drink, too.  Thanks for sharing!

Not bad, but a little too salty and sweet for my taste. A good tequila, 1800 Silver, and Triple Seq, 2 to 1, a quarter of squeezed of a soft lime, ice and stir makes a great margarita, without the salt and extra sugar. This mix is surprisingly smooth.

I wanted a lean option to explore cocktail options,  I did 1800 silver, triple sec, and fresh squeezed limes in lieu of sweetened lime juice.  I had orange seltzer, which was nice.  Good little cocktail,
I was really disappointed. Something was definitely missing.
Deee-Lish! Couldn't be easire & a nice, light, not-so-twangy version of a Rita! Thanks for sharing!
Finally found a truly tasty margarita!  Even my husband likes them.  No more stomach churning sour tasting margaritas for me!  Really enjoying this one and I did not change a thing.  Thanks so much!

Just finished making this recipe, and it was better than expected. Only Substitutions I made were 3 Habaneros vs 2 that were called for, used ground ginger instead of fresh, added a tablespoon of tomato paste and a few red pepper flakes for color. Absolutely delicious. This will be made again.
To sweet for us

We thought this was really different with the fruit puree and no tomato.  I pureed the fruit with a bit of mango juice and skipped the butter before covering the chicken with this yummy sauce.  Next time I would add the peppers a bit later in the cooking process to retain more kick and cut back the sugar and add a bit of vinegar for better balance.  Thanks for the awesome idea.
No changes at all needed. This sauce is awesome!!!
This sauce had awesome flavor would do it again but want enough of a kick, going to try 3 habeneros next time. Good recipe though
I agree with Naples.  Good fresh, pink lemonade at home!  I really enjoyed it. I'd be careful not to go overboard on rhubarb though!

Love love love this!! We made a batch last year and it was gone way too fast. I'm so excited to start making it again. It was delicious and refreshing and so easy to freeze the syrup to make for later. Can't wait to make up a bunch and freeze it!

It is very easy to make and it taste great.  A lemonade with a hint of rhubarb!  I am hoping to make a few batches and bottle them in mason jars to save for later, when the rhubarb is gone for the season.

I love this drink!  I gave it 4-stars, as written - straining the rhubarb.  It became a 5-star drink when I add the strained rhubarb back in the pot and use the immersion blender to mix it all together.  It is a nice combination of tart and sweet.  Because I tend to like things on the tart side, I will cut the sugar back to 2 1/2 cups, the next time. Luckily, I have access to plenty of rhubarb and use it for MANY recipes, this is definitely one of my favorite uses.

This is a brilliant way to use up a big rhubarb harvest! Super simple and inexpensive. I use bottled lemon juice. This recipe makes about 10 cups of syrup, which comes out to 40 cups of rhubarb lemonade once you add water to it.
I didn't find that this had much of a rhubarb taste.  I think it might be better if you use the pulp.  next time I'll try a slush recipe that uses pulp.
Great way to use all that rhubarb without added a lot to the waistline like the deserts do.
I used my immerson blender to puree the mixture in the pan. I also added a can of frozen concentrate Lemonade to the mixture after cooking.
This was a lot of work for what it was worth.  It needed more lemon juice.

I opted to use concentrated lemon juice from the shelf instead of fresh.  Perhaps frozen or fresh would make a better flavor, but I just couldn't get past that bottled lemon flavor.  If you do not like the bottled "real lemon" shelf flavor then I'd suggest to try something else or skip the recipe.   The rhubarb flavor was only slight. I also added another cup and a half when I made the recipe hoping it would stand out stronger.   It was something different but, I'll pass as I could of had 2 desserts or so with the amount of rhubarb needed to make one gallon of lemonade.

We loved it with the following changes.  We included some of the pulp; it seemed bland with just the juice.  Then we only thinned it with water 1:1.  Again, we wanted a stronger rhubarb taste.  We have taken it to a few gatherings and it's a huge hit this way!

Not bad, not bad!  Tasty and certainly refreshing, with just the slightest hint of rhubarb flavor.  I think that's a good thing, because really, who would want to drink rhubarb juice anyway?  It's just lightly pink, and the lemon is definitely prominent.  I simmered the rhubarb for several minutes to make sure the sieved juices would be thoroughyl infused with the rhubarb flavor.  Fun to try something different.

My husband and I absolutely love this drink! Since we enjoy pulp in our drinks, I followed one reviewers suggestion and used my immersion blender to blend it all together. You can see the pulp, but honestly I don't notice it much while drinking and this way you also save more of the rhubarb flavor and with less hassle. We are planning on freezing most of it. That way we can scoop out as much as we want for when we want it!

Yum!  My rhubarb plant is huge this year, so I was looking for different ways to use it.  Made this last night and it's delicious this morning.  Saved the pulp and hope to find a way to use it too.  Maybe a topping for ice cream...?

Absolutely wonderful.  It makes a great, tangy lemonade that everyone loved.  My rhubarb wasn't very red so I added a bit of food colouring just to give it that nice pinkish tint.  Almost no one guessed that there was rhubarb in it although everone loved the taste of it.  Some people told me how great they thought the strawberry lemonade was - they were quite surprised when they found out it was rhubarb.

It's a great way to use rhubarb from the garden, and since I freeze a lot of the rhubarb from my plant I'll be able to make this well into the winter if I want to!
This is a very good recipe it is also a good way to get rid of your extra rhubarb. And have something good to have  at the same time. LOVE IT!
Wonderful! Anybody that likes rhubarb, this is a keeper. Fresh, tangy and not to sweet. Tasted tested by 6 people, all 6 requested the recipe. A great way to use a surplus of rhubarb.

Love this fresh lemonade!  I put the concentrate in small jars and freeze them.  I double the recipe and get about 5 small jars.  With the excess pulp I decided it resembles banana mash for banana bread.  So I made a Rhubarb/Lemon bread using the "Banana Banana Bread" recipe from this site, substituting the bananas, and only used a 1/2 cup of brown sugar.  Very tasty as well!

A nice way to use up rhubarb. Next time I will double the lemon juice to add more zing. Also next time I'll use artificial swwetener & see how that will work out. Nice pink color, almost like pink lemonade!

This is great. It made 2 cups of liquid for me so I added 6 cups of water in a pitcher. Still, I cut it with ice and half water but it's awesome. And I saved all the stuff I strained out, and have used it as a topping on a biscuit, similar to strawberry shortcake. It's SO good. And so is this lemonade. Refreshing and different!

I followed the recipe as written however instead of a fine sieve I used my food mill. Not only did I end up with a tasty drink mix but some delicious rhubarb sauce as well. bonus!!! With less than a cup of waste for the compost pile.
it tastes Yummy I Had All of the cakes and rainbow treats in this web
This is an awesome cake . My 11yr old daughter an dI did this for her class whom adored it.. Thankx for sharing!!
Love it
This cake looks... AMAZING! Very nice job. This is defiently on my list!
I LOVE LOVE LOVE this recipe! I only had one egg on hand and changed the serving size, but this recipe saved the day! I use this exclusively for all my cakes now, thanks so much for sharing!
Someone took some classes :)

Fantastic!  I had to use bottled key lemon juice because it was all I had on hand.  Like another reviewer mentioned, it's like key lime/lemon pie but even creamier.  My avocados were so ripe, it was easy to mash them with a spoon.  I blended the first mixture, before adding the avocado, for awhile, 5 minutes or more, because I didn't know how thickened it should be and it set up beautifully overnight, nice and high but dense.  This was an experiment that instantly became a favorite!

This is fantastic!  I didn't sieve the avocado, just mashed it with a fork and then blended with the other ingredients.  The flavour and the colour are very nice.

Do not use a metal sieve or the avocado will go dark and have an odd taste.

I used key lime juice and rolled out a crust so I could bake the pie.  It tasted very much like a regular key lime pie but with a bit creamier texture.  Nobody would ever guess there was avocado in it!
The taste was quite good, sweet and limey. The only problem was the filling was pretty runny (like pudding).

I cooked the filling to avoid problems with the eggs and it worked just fine. Reminds us of a key lime pie, without using key limes.  Very smooth and great taste.  Everyone who tasted it really enjoyed the flavor.

This recipe was awesome. i did use butter instead of margerine for flavor purposes. i omited the savory simply because my grocer did not have it. after simmering for 20 minutes i blended it in batches, then added heavy cream instead of milk. topped with croutons and sour cream, this is a wonderful dish
Its a great recipe, but the ingredients are off.  I used 4 cups of Veg broth and it was great.  Also cooked with salt and pepper since I read the earlier reviews saying it needed it.
Really good with Italian bread and cheddar cheese sprinkled. I also added fresh chives, dill, marjoram and sliced mushrooms.
This was very good, had to omit the savory but it was fantastic without it too! Also very easy and quick to make, Thank you for submitting this recipe.

This is a good soup.  I think it needs salt and pepper, though.  Also, I pureed it after it was thoroughly cooked--it seems more palatable that way to me.  Don't forget the sour cream when serving.  It definitely "makes" the dish.

For a switch, instead of the sour cream, some cheese sprinkled over the top (cheddar?) might be good.

Great recipe. I added knorr® concentrated stock and 2 cups water instead of 1 cup chicken broth.  When done cooking used submersion blended to partially cream. I also added some spinach asiago cheese chicken sausages.  Fantastic.

I picked this recipe because it didn't have to be pureed.After making it I realized that this soup really needs it! Too many big chunks.Added a little curry to help with flavor.I've never given a bad review, but here it is.

This was a good base for Zucchini soup, but I found I had to enhance by adding salt, pepper and 1 shredded carrot for a bit of sweetness.  I also used a full 14oz can of low sodium chicken broth.   Again, a good base with lots of potential.
Tried this soup and I found it tasty.  I did not have but 2 zucchini but had everything else.  I will make it again the way it is.  I did add salt but that is personal taste.
Good soup, but I took some of the other reviewers’ recommendations and added more broth and milk, as well as some salt, pepper, and garlic powder.

I can't imagine making this kind of dish without altering the recipe.  It's begging to be interpreted by individual tastes (I used roasted garlic, tandoori spice - fantastic!).  The idea that the recipe gives is fantastic - thanks for posting.
Wonderful recipe, I halved the butter and added olive oil. I also added curry powder and celery salt to the oil at the begining. Worked great a main dish, very filling!

After tinkering with it, I liked this recipe. It's begging for salt and pepper and it definitely needs to be pureed. Extra milk doesn't hurt either. Couldn't believe it called for only 1 cup of chicken broth! I worried that it would burn before I ever got to add the fresh herbs. In place of savory, I used fresh thyme.

I don't know how this soup got 4 stars!!! This is the only bad review I've given on allrecipes. Usually I alter everything I make for personal preference, but this needed some major alterations.  Use the zucchini onions and potatoes and alter everything else: add ingredients, take out ingredients, more of this, little of that.

There is no way the measurments on this are correct... I had to alter everything. 1 c of chicken broth is supposed to make a pot of soup? Not so sure about that. I used a lot of different spices to add more to this... I also used 4 c. chicken broth and 2 c. milk... made plenty. I used red potatoes with the skin, and about 8 c. diced zicchini. This tasted wonderful, but I had to write all over the recipe to make it right... I'll make it again, but my own way.
my german friend insisted on following this recipe to a tee. i was not sure how it would come out, ( it sounded bland), however, i thought it was delicious!!!!

Good base recipe that can be tweaked to your taste. Sauteed the veggies in olive oil. I only had three zucchinis, and I used the herbs I had on hand - parsley, savory, and some fresh thyme. It does need salt and pepper, as others have mentioned, and I have no idea how this could be done with only 1 cup of chicken broth - I used the whole 32 oz box, and then just added a little milk at the end to give it a bit of creaminess. I also pureed it. Delish.
My husband and I did not care for this soup.  We will not be making it again.

Really quite tasty.  Nothing exotic, but nice.  Extremely quick and simple soup.  It is even surprisingly satisfying.  It really is even quick enough for a last minute soup and sandwich meal.  However, this is only as good as your zucchini.  If your zucchini was not watered well, you are in trouble.  Test your zucchini before preparing this soup - even if it is from the store.  Stores even have bitter zucchini at times.  If it is bitter, make some zucchini bread or something.......  But when you want a simple soup, this is really good.

I adapted this recipe for my daughter with milk and chicken allergies.  Olive oil for butter and vegetable stock replaced chicken nicely.  After pureeing (it is a must!), it didn't even need milk.  I also only had fresh basil, but that was just fine.  It was in the bland range of pureed soups, hence the 3 stars.  The kids loved it, however!

I baked this following the directions. I'm not a beginning baker but I didnt follow my gut either. I put a toothpick in and it came out clean after the recommended time. After letting it cool I flipped it over and after a bit it turned to mush with bits of cake. My kids ate it. They wanted me to make more but I didnt like it and the presentation was aweful.

I'm having a difficult time rating this cake.  The flavor was fantastic but the baking time is off.  I baked it in a round 9" pan and I started checking after 35 minutes. I have not made this recipe yet but I have an easy way to seed a pomegranate.  I carefully take off the top of the pomegranate without hitting the seeds.  With a very sharp knife I score the fruit into quarters again without cutting too deep.  In a  large deep bowl,  take the pomegranate and pull apart over the bowl.  Take each quarter and place it skin side up in one hand with your fingers open.  In your other hand, take a wooden spoon and whack the skin side of the pomegranate.  The seeds just fall out.  Don't be afraid to hit fairly hard.  You will be amazed how quickly the seeds fall out and the rind just stays on the skin.  You may have to still pick a few seeds out but this is so simple.  Have fun!!

I added a can of moist cat food in addition to the baby food, and flour enough to be able to roll out dough. Used small cookie cutter and baked for 20-25 minutes at 350. They love them!!

Not too bad.  The texture was nice for my cat's small teeth, but the flavor was lacking.  The wheat germ was a bit pricey, too.  Total cost of ingredients was $2.22 (compare to $1.50 for other recipes).  I put an egg/beef bullion glaze on these and my cat will eat them, but he prefers other kind.  I might try this again with a little tweaking.

We made a double batch of these, and found the wheat germ made it too dry to roll, so we added 3 beaten eggs (to a double batch) and a splash of broth to help things stick together. Since we have cats, we rolled smaller balls (marble sized) and cooked for 7 minutes.  All 5 of our cats ate them with enthusiasm, and my husband tried one (to be sure they were cooked through), and said they weren't bad.  They make nice gifts for folks that have cats and dogs.

One note: if you use broth, make sure it does NOT have onion or garlic or similar seasonings in it; they are toxic for animals, particularly for cats -- both can develop hemolytic anemia.

these cookies are kind of expensive to make, but my dog and cat both love them.  The dog wouldn't come out of the kitchen while they were baking.  It's like he knew they were for him.

I didn't have any baby food but I did have some wet dog food that I used instead.  Seriously, SOOO easy to make and the dogs loved them! Thank you!!

Lovely!! I used a bit too much jam and it spread all over the pastry. So, I advise following the amounts written to make sure they have that border. Otherwise, you'll need a knife and fork to eat them. Thank you for the recipe.

Since I have no bread machine, here is how I made the dough by hand. METHOD: Combine 1 1/2 cups flour, yeast, sugar and salt in a bowl. Mince garlic cloves with olive oil in mini food processor. Add lukewarm water (110 F) and oil/garlic mixture; mix until well blended. Add in the remaining 1/2 cup flour. Dough should form a ball and will be slightly sticky. Turn out on a floured surface, adding additional flour if you find it necessary (but not too much.) Knead until smooth and elastic. Grease a bowl with oil, put dough ball in bowl, turning it over to coat the whole ball with oil. Cover bowl with plastic wrap and place in warm place to rise for 30 mins. *TIP FOR RISING (can use with any yeast dough): Microwave a cup fill 1/4-1/2 with water till it is very hot, leave cup of water in microwave and place covered bowl inside, close the door. The steam provides a warm environment for the dough to rise. Works for me every time. After dough is finished rising, pat into pizza pan (using a bit more flour as necessary) and then I followed the recipe from step 3. MY REVIEW: I did not have bread flour so I used All Purpose flour, I used 3 large garlic cloves and it provided an okay amount of garlic flavour. Not overwhelming but not extremely detectable. I minced my garlic in my magic bullet with the olive oil so it would be more well incorporated. I used this as the base for Basic Beef Pizza (recipe on this site) and it was a delicious combination. Would make again. Thanks for sharing!

I would like to clarify some statements that were made in previous reviews about the terms "jam" and "jelly" and how they were improperly interchangable.  It is important to know the differences of the two in that jam is  a product that has physical pieces of fruit in the finished product, Jelly is merely a product which is "jelled" using strained fruit juice...NOT an actual fruit puree which yeilds a distinctly different "smoothie" kind of end product; Also the Juice, Fruit, Sugar, Pectin ratios are also different so be careful about interchanging these terms or you could quite possibly have a less than desired non-congealed end product. After reading tons of reviews on this jam, I have this to add:
1 - If you use RIPE strawberries (no white or green on the berries), then your jam will naturally be extra sweet.  If you don't like the extra sweetness, use the pink pectin box and follow the directions for low sugar (4 c. crushed berries with 3 c. sugar). When I used berries that had a little white and green on them, 4 c. sugar was needed. The lady at the strawberry farm told me berries with a little green/white on them actually help jam set up (and I believe her). 
2 - I like crushing the berries with a potato masher best. I think the chunkiness adds to making it a jam! (And you can use it for other things like smoothies and over ice cream.) 
3 - If your berries seem too runny after crushing, drain off most of the extra liquid before adding the pectin to the berries. This really makes the jam set up and seems to evenly distribute the berries throughout the jam. I like it thicker!
4 - Boiling the pectin/water mixture for 1 minute and then adding to the berries and stirring again for 3 minutes also seems to aid in the jam setting up with no sugary crystals. My jam seems to set up in less than 30 minutes.
5 - Since this is not the cooked method, I recommend letting the jam cool and then immediately refrigerating/freezing. I left a jar out once and forgot to give it to a friend. Two days later, I opened it and it didn't smell bad but had a metallic taste, so taste can be affected.   I HOPE THIS HELPS EVERYONE!

I would like to clarify a few things about this recipe: The blueberries can be strained out if you prefer just an infused simple syrup. I have found that a some of my children like the blueberries left in and some prefer not to have any, the choice is yours. The syrup will be thin and then depending on how you intend to use it, you can thicken it with a cornstarch + water combination. If you want to infuse a batter, then the original consistency should do fine (all things considered), however if you want to drizzle this over pancakes or waffles and want something closer to the consistency of pancake syrup then you should thicken this. Refrigerating this overnight will also help thicken the consistency slightly. A simple syrup by convention has equal parts sugar and water, however if this is too sweet for your intended use, and you make it again, don't forget to embrace the spirit of cooking and alter/add your own spin. Enjoy!

A KITCHEN DISASTER:

1. WARNING: PHOTO IS MISLEADING! A traditional, round pie is shown, but the recipe calls for a 9 X 13 inch baking dish. Without reading the recipe, I glanced at the photo and included a pre-packaged, deep-dish graham cracker pie crust on my shopping list. Sure enough, I had about 2 cups of extra filling leftover, which I stored in seperate containers to be eaten like pudding. Who cooks a "pie" in a 9 X 13 inch baking dish?

2. It gets worse: FILLING DID NOT SET! This after 24 hours refrigeration. Obviously there is too much of a liquid ingredient, which one I'm not sure. I was very careful with the measurements, careful to correctly translate the outdated listed quantities (evaporated milk and sweetened condensed milk are available today in 12 and 10 oz. cans, respectively, not 5 oz.). The mixture wasn't "firm" as stated. The end result was a gloopy mess, less set than pudding. The leftover filling I had reserved never set, either, after days of refrigeration. The taste was good, deepening the mystery of which ingredient was over-quantified.  So many cooks have had setting failure with this recipe that it should be removed from the site.

Quick & great for ur spouse who's not keen on being vegetarian. Used 2 8oz. cans of tomato sauce instead of diced tomatos. Definetly eased up on chilli powder. Used potato rolls, & it was amazing! Not too many changes like other recipes-so gave it 5 stars. Make about once a wk on busy nights

I made a simplified version of this: no carrots, celery, vinegar, or peppers and garlic powder instead of minced garlic.  I doubled the beans.  This cut the cooking time down to about 10 minutes.  It was VERY spicy, but my boyfriend (a non-vegetarian) and I loved it.  This is  definitely a keeper!!!
drain the can of tomatoes if they're stewed because it turned out more like soup i let it sit for a good 45 minutes to thicken and added cornstarch. overall very yummy with chedar cheese
Too spicy!
Very tasty. Serving size is exaggerated though. It says 8 servings, but it'll only serve 2 as a main dish.

made this just like the recipe stated, bought bagged onion/celery/carrot already chopped, this was super quick with pre-chopped veggies and my husband LOVED it, great recipe if your looking for hearty vegetarian meal that's quick and tasty.

I doubled this recipe. Instead of celery, I added zucchini, fresh tomatoes instead of canned, 2 1/2 tablespoon of vinegar, and only 1 1/2 tablespoon of chili powder(for a double recipe). I also added two masala veggie burgers for extra flavor.
Really enjoyed this recipe!  Even my carnivore sons said it was ok.

This was great.  A little to much chili powder for my taste, I would cut it back to 1 instead of 1 1/2.  My girlfriend and I used hoggie buns then topped it with shredded colbyjack cheese and tosted them at 450 for about 5 minutes to add a nice finish to them.

We absolutely Loved this dish! It was a great way to get my picky toddler to eat her veggies. However, I would recommend bringing the heat down if feeding it to a child. Though my little girl ate all of it, she also was gulping down water like there was no tomorrow.
These were great!!  Kids liked them.  We used half of each of the peppers and it was perfect.
Used crushed tomatoes... Had to add brown sugar to sweeten.

This was pretty good the night I made it, but very good the day after!  I guess it needs some time to sit.  I used the food processor to get the veggies chopped up pretty fine, and left out the peppers.  I also added some mustard, because that is how I always make sloppy joes.
pretty good but didn't taste much like sloppy joes more like chili.
I only used one tablespoon of chili powder, and it was still too much.  Too hot for the kids.  I would make this recipe again, but with less chili powder.
Taste great ! Yummy

These should definitely not be titled "unsloppy" haha they were fun to eat though! I also added red pepper as I read in a review, the cheese makes it stick together better, but I also think it's too juicy in the beginning I would drain the tomatoes and cook the carrots before anything else.  Balsamic vinegar instead of white really tastes amazing too!
This is just how I remember sloppy joes, minus the meat, of course.
Everyone loved this!  We are a vegan family and it is so wonderful to have a family friendly recipe that even the kids love.
I really liked this. We are trying to add more veggies to our diet and this recipe really kept us full for a long time. Plus we have a vegan sister-in-law and I will try this when she comes over.

"The best vegetarian food I have EVER tasted"..."A meat lover's perfect non-meat meal"... those were some of the wonderful things my boyfriend was saying as he was eating his. He was almost in shock at how great they were (he's a carnivore at heart). I thought they were spectacular as well... and being a vegetarian myself, I was able to appreciate them even more. I made a few alterations to the recipe though... my favorite alteration was using a red pepper instead of a green pepper. I think it added just a tiny bit of sweetness to an otherwise super-spicy dish. It also livened it up with more red color. I left out the celery because I didn't have any, but truthfully, I think it wouldn't have been as good with it. Since I didn't have any diced tomatoes, I added 2, 8oz cans of tomato sauce (which I think was a wonderful substitution). I also followed previous suggestions not to put in so much chili powder, so I put in 1 1/2 teaspoons instead of 1 1/2 tablespoons. This was absolutely the right decision. Even a drop more chili powder and it would have been way too spicy. The best part was that my boyfriend was complaining when he was done that he was too full. That is by far the biggest compliment of them all, because he's rarely full after eating a vegetarian meal. This is DEFINITELY becoming a staple in my diet. I couldn't be more pleased.

god, this is so good.  i, like other reviewers, halved the chili powder.  i also added a little bit more tomato paste.  this needs a liiittle bit of salt, but other than that, totally delicious and incredibly easy to make!
It was very tasty.  I prefer it over rice than on a bun, though.  Despite it's tastiness and health benefits, however, mine tasted nothing whatsoever like sloppy joes, hence the three stars.
I'd suggest cutting back on the tomato and adding some additional spices as it tasted a good deal like marinara after made.
This was great dinner. It will get into the weekly rotation of meals.
Even my meat eater liked this! It was easy to make and had a good little kick. Perfect for lunch or dinner.

I am super impressed with this recipe it was wonderful! Filling to eat and fast to make. I mistakenly grabbed a can of basil, garlic and oregano diced tomatoes but it still tastes great! I think I may use it every time. Also, my husband decided we should not scoop out our whole wheat rolls. A new recipe to use with out meat!! Thank you so much for sharing.

YUM! Based on reviews, I used 1 tablespoon of chili powder, a splash extra of vinegar, and a red pepper instead of green since I had that on hand. I also added about 1/2 teaspoon of Worcestershire, which I might add more of next time. Might also try it with the full amount of chili powder as it wasn't too spicy.

I had it over brown rice instead of buying rolls and that worked well!

It was DELICIOUS overall, especially as a cheap, quick,  vegetarian, healthy dish.. definitely making again. (Note we are not vegetarian and loved it!)
These were great! A really nice alternative to the normal meaty, messy Joe. I used red onion. The scooped out kaiser bread made a great bread pudding.
A little too spicy for my taste- but pretty good...will make again but with less pepper.
Not as good as I had hoped.  Maybe needs a spoonful of sugar added or some prepared barbeque sauce.
Tastes fine but more or less chili on a bun.

This is a great recipe!  I too "tweaked" it a little, added more garlic, used balsamic vinegar and a little less chili powder.  My husband, A huge meat eater LOVED it.  I took the left over mix and used it with spaghetti the next night and that was AWSOME!
this is a delicious recipe! me and my friend made it, and ended up just eating it by it's self it was so good. We added some fake meat to it, which added some of the traditional texture to it.

I was very disappointed in this recipe as written. The texture was great and I was excited to find a vegetarian recipe that didn't call for TVP but the flavor on this one just wasn't there. It basically tasted like tomato paste with a chili powder after taste. Once I added some BBQ sauce, the flavor greatly improved. The next time I make this, I'll use all of the same veggies but use BBQ sauce and catchup!

This is the best recipe I have used from allrecipes.  No doubt.  I rarely make it exactly to specifications because I just use what I have around.  It is still great every time!  I even made it for my non-vegetarian parents and they loved it!
The name is deceiving.  These don't taste anything like sloppy joes.  They taste more like stuffed pepper filling or a vegeterarian chili.  I threw the leftovers away.
we loved this recipe. My husband added cheese to his and said it was wonderful

We love this recipe!  The only things I change/add is to replace the tomato paste with a healthy squeeze of ketchup (just because I don't usually keep a tube of paste on hand for smaller amts) and I also add about 1 tsp salt.  I do cut down a little on the chili powder, but not much since I think it adds to the whole "sloppy joe" flavor of this dish.  We like to serve it with cheddar cheese and pickles on the buns...Mmmm! Super easy, super tasty, and healthy!

I made this recipe the other night.  It was okay for the hubby and I but my Kids did NOT enjoy it.  It would have been okay if I didn't use the pepper or chili pepper.  I even cut down the amount and it was still to much.  I think I could make this again for the fam if I take cut most of the pepper out.  The veggis add the flavor it needs as well as the vinegar... Overall it was good though!
Shredded all the veggies and added a can of refried beans for texture.  Made open face sandwiches with cheddar on top and broiled for 5 minutes.

I also gave this recipe 5 stars because it is hard to find a vegetarian dish that everyone in my family likes. I realized at the last minute I was out of chili powder so I substituted 1/4 t. cayenne pepper and 1/4 t. cumin.  Since regular sloppy joes have a sweet undertone I added 1T. honey. After cooking I felt it needed a little more sauce so I squeezed in 2T or so of catsup.  I spooned it on the rolls and put a slice of cheese on top and slide it under the broiler.  Thanks for the recipe!
Underwhelming.  Needs more seasoning and does not resemble the sloppy joe's I grew up eating, in taste.
Tastes nothing like a Sloppy Joe. Something seems to be missing.  Would not make again.

This recipe reminded me of the sloppy joes that my mother-in-law used to make. I thought it came out quite well. I followed the other reviewers recommendations and doubled the amount of onion, green pepper, carrots and garlic. I skipped the celery and added a red pepper for that. I also left the amount of kidney beans stay the same. I used 6 fresh roma tomatoes rather than canned. Finally, I used about 1.25 tablespoons of chili powder and cut the amount of black pepper to about 1/4 teaspoon. This is a very fast recipe to prepare and I will definitely make it again in the future. Thanks, KDCG for sharing it.
This recipe is amazing!  I love it - very easy to prepare and it tastes great - it's perfect for vegetarians!

I loved this recipe! I couldn't believe how close the sauce tasted to meaty sloppy joes, it was perfect! I used red wine vinegar instead of white vinegar, but that was the only change I made.  I would definitely use this recipe again and I highly recommend it.
This was a pretty good recipe.  We used only 1 tsp of the chili powder.  It would be great with melted cheddar on top.  It also works well on its own or with rice.
I added a little bit of salt to perk the chili flavor-I love spicy food! It was a simple and good meal.

This was absolutely delicious. I followed the recipe exactly except I only added in 1 tablespoon of chili. 1 1/2 would have been way too much. I will be making this again for sure!

Update: I had plenty of leftovers because I ended up eating this by myself; my boyfriend said it was no substitute for sloppyjoes (I disagreed) but that it might make a good spaghetti sauce. So today that is what I did with the left overs. I put them back on the stove in the pot and began reheating, added 1/3 cup of water, 2 tblsp of the tomato paste, 2 tblsp of olive oil, 1/2 tsp. each of garlic powder and oregano, and a large pinch each of ground thyme and parsley, then I put it over cooked pasta. I used egg noodles because that is all I had on hand at the time, but I think it would be even better on angel hair, or shells even as a form of goulash. To top it off I added parmesan cheese. My boyfriend was actually right about something! It came out really well.

I really liked these. My family thought they were just ok.  I added some ketchup, BBQ sauce, and a little mustard to mine to give it a kick since other reviewers said it was kind of boring.  Served it on whole wheat hamburger buns.

I wanted to like this more than I did, but gave it 4 stars b/c my MEAT eating husband thought it was good and that is always a big plus in my book! Again, the hubby liked it a lot, so I will be making it again. Thanks!

I really liked this! I agree with some of the other reviews, it's basically chili on a bun, but the flavor was more like a sloppy joe. I have made this probably five or six times since discovering this recipe a little while back.  This has to be one of my favorite vegetarian recipes ever.  I always double the recipe because everyone fights over the leftovers.  It is absolutely delicious.  The only thing I do different is to use a little less chili powder, since we don't like things too spicy.  I serve it with homemade bread bowls, sliced olives, shredded cheddar and a dollop of sour cream. Even my husband who insists every meal needs some sort of meat enjoys this.  Thanks for the great recipe!

It was SOOOO good, the very first time I made it.  Much better than meaty sloppy joes.
Really easy too. 
Having it again tonight. YUMM
Delicious! Lightly mashing the beans gave the mixture a nice meaty texture. I also added 1T Thai chili sauce to give a little sweet to the spicy. I will definitely make this again.

This recipe was delicious and very filling.  All the other vegetarian Sloppy Joe recipes I tried had TVP or veggie ground round, and they were too rich and not filling.  I think the 1 1/2 tablespoons of chili powder in the recipe was too much; next time I'll reduce it to 1 1/2 teaspoons. As many others have said, this recipe is absolutely delicious.  What I love the most about it is that it's so customizable to personal taste and you can pretty much make it any way you want, but works great as a general guideline.  Thanks for adding this recipe!
Huge hit at our house... sure does beat the normal sloppy joes.
Definitely needs cheese added to make it stick together a little better.  I added Monterrey Jack and that was a great finishing touch.  Otherwise, it ends up much like just putting chili on a bun.
It was really good but it was VERY spicy!  Next time I'm going to lighten up on the chili powder and pepper!
Loved it! Easy especially for a cooking-challenged person like myself. I loved them spicy, however, my family thought it was a bit too hot.
good.

My partner and I really enjoyed this recipe. He ate 3.5 sandwiches! We are always looking for good vegetarian recipes. I did decrease the amount of chili pepper to 1 tbsp. From reading the instructions, I plan to double the recipe next time so that I can freeze the leftovers.

This recipe was good, but nothing to write home to mom about.  I like that it is really simple to make, and I had all ingredients on hand, so it's a good pantry-ready recipe (hence the four stars). Not too bad as a vegetarian chili but definitely did not taste anything like Sloppy Joes to us.  I used half of the chili powder, as suggested by other members and it still ended up being overly spicy for our tastes.

One of my all time favorite vegetarian recipes.  I always make a double batch because it goes quickly, even with my husband, who normally despises vegetarian food.  The first time I made this recipe, the two of us ate it in one sitting.  I use a mild chili powder and 3/4 t pepper, otherwise it's way too spicy for our household.
This did not pass the test for myself and hubby and 3 kids. I think we all are used to the sloppy joes with meat and it just didn't come close to the texture or taste for us.
Really good. I omit the celery. We have these regularly for a fun supper.
Not bad but not one of my favorite recipes.  I think next time I'm going to add some veggie crumbles and omit the vinegar (I thought it put the flavors offa bit)

My fiance and I really enjoyed this... but I made some changes based on what other reviewers said.  First of all, I made 16 servings instead of 8 and froze half. It froze and reheated really well!  I would definitely recommend this.  It is so easy to go ahead and double the recipe, and a huge time-saver b/c of all the vegetables you have to chop.  Secondly, I added more vinegar to mine... I felt it gave the recipe more of the characteristic sloppy joes flavor.  I went ahead and added twice the amount.  I also only added 1/2 the amount of chili powder the recipe calls for, and 1/2 the amount of black pepper. Overall, this is really filling and even sort of fun to eat too, especially with the kaiser rolls!
next time i'm going to puree the beans so it goes better with the kids, otherwise a new favorite
Not bad, decent flavor and very filling have enjoyed it several times now! Thanks for recipe.

Used italian seasoning vinegar instead of white vinegar and increased it a bit. I didn't have tomato paste so I used same amount of tomato sauce. Simmered uncovered to reduce the amount of liquid. Turned out great, would recommend adding cheese as another reviewer suggested.
My husband loved these! They tasted very similar to Paula Deans meatloaf glaze (minus the brown sugar). Tasty!

As written, the recipe's flavor was not exactly what I like in a sloppy joe. The few changes I made took care of that. I increased the garlic to 2 cloves, decreased the chili powder to 1 TBS., increased the vinegar to 2 TBS., and added about 1 1/2 TBS. sugar. This took away some of the heat and acidity and created a slightly sweet and sour flavor.

People are afraid to eat my cooking, and rightly so.  This was so easy and looked good with some sharp cheddar topping.  Healthy, easy dish.  Also, I love spicy food, so the chili pepper was just right.  Could even have used more.
Quite good; a nice change from the usual sloppy Joes.
This recipe was good, but it would have been better with less chili powder.  I added mozzarella to the mix, which helped it stick together much better.
way too peppery and way too tomatoey. i had to throw this out and serve sandwiches
Better with ground turkey and I added water to make it more juicy. It came out dry the first time.
This was great!  Had a nice zip to it, and tasted wonderful!  My meat-eating boyfried loved it too!  I'm definately gonna have it again!
These were really good, however I wouldn't go into these thinking they will taste like sloppy joes.  They taste like vegetarian chili, but it was still a great recipe!

This recipe was easy and turned out pretty well. I love the vinegar in it, it definitely gives it a "meatier" flavor. I found it a little bit uninteresting in flavor, I think it needed a little salt (maybe if you use salted beans it works out?). Anyhow, that mostly just MY salt addiction talking! It was fine- a bit like a vinegary vegetarian chili.

I made a couple changes- out of necessity, I used canned black beans instead of kidney beans. I think the texture of kidney beans would have been better, but the black beans were nice, too.

A also reduced the amount of chili powder as many reviewers suggested- I wish I hadn't! I kept tasting and adding more and more. Different chili powders have different levels of heat! I used a blend of two types of chili powder, one that is incredibly mild with a nice chili flavor, and an ancho chile one that is spicier. My joe mix wasn't very spicy at all... I don't know of some of the reviewers are sensitive to spice or something, because I would have had to use a pretty hot chili powder to make it too spicy to enjoy. A teaspoon of black pepper also didn't really add much heat.

Anyhow, know your chili powder, and add the full amount if it is a milder one, or reduce the amount if you're using a hot powder. (And don't accidentally use Cayenne chili powder- that'll probably burn your mouth right off if you use much of it!)

I liked this a lot.  Was easy, inexpensive and the family ate every last bite.  I used French bread buns as that is what I had on hand.  reminded me of a chili bowl kinda thing...but since I love those too, this hit the spot on a cool October evening.  thank you for sharing....will be making this again.

I added a little bit of Worcester sauce to make these taste more sloppy-joe-ish; some liquid smoke might be good too.  Other than that, very delicious.  My boyfriend ate 3 before he noticed they were meatless!
This is one of the best veg recipes you can serve to a mixed crowd! Serve with corn chips and cole slaw and you have a great meal for young and old! This is one of my favorites!

This was one of my first attempts at a vegetarian dish. I really liked it.  I would suggest less chili powder but that is a personal perference.  I also added some mustard, a little Worcestershire sauce and a tad of ketchup.  Next time, I am going to try red bell peppers in addition to the green bell peppers.  Overall, a nice intro to vegetarian fare!

This was a great vegetarian recipe. I cut back to 1 tbls of the chili pepper and I used diced tomatoes with green chilis in them. I also added a little sugar to balance out the pepper. Great the next morning in an omlet.

I could eat this every day, twice a day. I love love this recipe, it's healthy, tasty and you can store some in the freezer for another day (or for dinner!). I made it pretty bare minimum, all the ingredients fresh but no vinegar, no tomato paste, and fresh raw tomatoes, not canned. It is so delicious.

This was NOT good as a sandwich.  It was very good when I had the leftovers the next day by itself with no bread.  I would make this again and serve it over rice.  I would not use the garlic.  Too much!

I followed the recipe exactly. It was quick and easy to make and tasted very good. I like that it uses everyday ingredients, nothing unusual that I wouldn't normally have on hand.  I served it open-faced on half a bun to cut back on bread. My husband liked it too so I'll will probably be making this again.

My dad couldn't put his finger on it, but he's never tasted anything quite like this stuff.  I'm surprised at how spicy it was-- usually I leave pepper and added salt out, but I was afraid this would be bland, so at t?e last minute I went ahead and added the black pepper.  Wooo-EEE! Right now I am eating the left overs over brown rice and topped with light cheddar cheese.  It's pretty good!

This recipe is a winner. My twin two-year-olds gobbled it down, and my husband asked that it be put into our weekly rotation. It was really easy, too! I added a bit of worchestershire sauce and some brown sugar to give it a more "authentic" taste (my mom used those ingredients in her sloppy joes). I also added a bit of cornstarch mixed with warm water at the end, to thicken it up and give it the right consistency. Really tasty!

We love this recipe! It's a great way to offer beans and veggies to kids and non-vegetarians, and it's super tasty!

I leave out the vinegar-- personal preferance-- but overall, this is an awesome meal which pops up in our menu on a regular basis. Thanks!

First time I've ever made sloppy joes, delicious and flavorful! And simple to make.

definitely a very yummy and healthy veg sloppy joe recipe! i have used veggie "meat" and manwich sauce in the past, but i think this is WAY better because you control the ingredients (especially the sodium, which can get so high with all prepackaged food!) and i love using fresh veggies and beans. i prepared dry kidney beans instead of using canned beans(again less sodium). i also greatly decreased the black & chili pepper amount, and kept adding vinegar until i liked the taste. i added a pinch of brown sugar too. it made a bunch, so i think i might try freezing half as another reviewer suggested. great recipe!

At first I thought this would just be an okay dish to try just for the heck of it...I had no idea it was going to be such a hit. I served this on "everything" topped buns with sliced jalapenos and sharp cheddar and OM it was soooo good. Check the seasoning as you go on this (as on every recipe really, everyone's tastes are different) and that will probably save you from over doing it.

I think this recipe is fab. I've made it for a few years now and it makes a great base - I put spices out and let everyone make it as spicy or hot as they want. Cheap, nutritious, filling. Great for a cold autumn or winter evening!

After a taste test I decided to add a bit of salt and two spoons of open pit bar-b-q sauce because I've always enjoyed the bold flavor bar-b-q sauce brings to sloppy joes. I didn't add the carrots either, but I doubled the other veggies to about a cup each. I confess that I did add a lb of ground beef so that way my husband would eat it. I also added a splash of worcestershire sauce, a tbsp of soy sauce and about a 1/2 cup of ketchup. That really gave it the sweetness that it needed and helped hold it together more. BTW - It was great the next morning with a fried egg and hashbrowns on top served open face. :) Will definitely make this again. Thanx!
This was terrible. I'll never make this again.  I had to throw it out, no one would eat it, myself included.
This recipe is really easy, tasty, and takes little time!  I decreased the chili powder to 2 tsp and it was perfect. Will make again!

I'm a really picky eater and didn't like this. But I'm also able to see what most people WOULD like and the other people who ate with me weren't picky eaters. To them, this was a decent recipe but nothing really special. They mentioned that they'd omitt the carrots. I probably won't be making this again.

We ate these open face on crusty rolls topped with shredded cheese and pickled jalapenos.

Great for the whole family!  I also think the serving size was exaggerated, I supposedly made 8, but it was more like 5.  After reading the other reviews, I cut the chili powder back to about 1 Tbsp.  I also added in a touch more vinegar, and about 1 Tbsp. brown sugar to cut the acidity.

Yum Yum Yum is all that I can say.  I followed the recipe to a "T".....the family loved these.  Also try Sloppy Sams on this website.....terrific as well!  Thank you for the recipe...it is definately a keeper.
These were very yummy! Even my carnivorous parents found them to be delicious. I will definitely make them again!
Absolutely delicious! Followed the recipe except for the suggestion to double the vinegar--that turned out to be a little too much for my tastes.

We didn't use this for sandwiches, but it made a great topping for baked potatoes! I lessened the chili powder and black pepper by 1/2 per other suggestions and used a mix of colors of peppers. The baked potatoes and a salad on the side made a very filling and nutritious meal.
Loved it!

this is good stuff and very quick and easy to make.
