This dip is fantastic! I used 20 caramels instead of 16, but it still wasn't quite caramely enough for me, so I'll increase them again next time. Overall, the texture was great, everybody loved it, and it was insanely easy. I will definitely be making this again!

Instead of the caramels, use peanut butter.  1 cup peanut butter.  1 cup brown sugar.  8 oz cream cheese and 1/4 cup milk.  I am addicted!  Its way easier and tastes better than using caramels.  Maybe a little more healthy too?
This was pretty good. It's really sweet, so I choose tart apples to dip. I also used 1/4 cup caramel ice cream topping to make the dip smoother than the wrapped caramels.

Sometimes simplicity is best! It was really great, not too sweet and not too thick. I served it at a college art reception and it went over really well with the students and parents. The one issue that I did have was that I didn't get the cream cheese super smooth before mixing in the caramel but i think that's a bigger issue with my patience than the recipe.
While I wasn't thrilled with this recipe (hence 4 stars instead of 5) it was a HIT at a fall party!  I still have friends asking for the recipe!  Thanks for sharing

You've got to try this!  So easy and so good!  Other reviewers are right- this dip stays soft, even after refrigeration.  Here's a variation:  add toasted pecan pieces, finely chopped apple (tossed in lemon juice) and Hershey's Cinnamon Chips.  Serve with graham crackers.  It just went from great to incredible.  I used Macintosh apples.  I was afraid the apples might get mushy, but was pleasantly surprised!  They didn't.  The dip was still good the next day.  Thanks for sharing this recipe!

I would have never though of this myself.  My mom brought me a whole bunch of apples, because she wanted me to "eat healthy" but I don't really like apples.  With this recipe... they disappeared from the fridge... my husband and I absolutely love it!!  Thanks Regina!!!  BTW... I usually only make half the recipe and 8 caramels with a splash of water melt perfectly in the microwave in 45 seconds... no need to dirty up the pots!
It's a good dip, I made it yesterday, it's got a nice taste and smooth and creamy. whatever you make this for,you'll be glad.

OMGGG!!! i added a splash of vanilla, and served it chilled (i'm not a fan of warm dip on my cold apples). i thought i died and went to heaven. my 2 yo ds keeps sneaking into the fridge for a fingerful. (and so does mom..)

I made this dip for my MOPS ( Mothers Of Preschoolers )Group. I was really nervous about making this dip. I had never worked with caramels before and I was really doubtful about cooking them in water. But the dip turned out really tastey!!! I only added half the sugar and it still tasted great, just a lighter color of brown/caramel color. One thing I noticed was that the dip was very "soupy" after I'd made it. So I left in my fridge,overnight, to see if it would set up better and it did. It was "spoonable" like yogurt.    
The dip was a great success at the MOPS meeting. I had a little left over so I brought it home and ate up the rest  in one sitting!!! I WILL make this a PERMANENT addition to my recipe box and   put it in my favorites recipe folder. Thank you Lori!!
Delicious dip!
I made this without additional sugar.  My husband thought it was gross, but I loved it.

Tastes just like what it's made of--cream cheese and caramel.  Yum!  I halved the sugar and it's still plenty sweet.  It definitely can be made ahead of time and served from the fridge--this makes the recipe much more appealing to me.
I made for guests that came over for Halloween.  Was the prettiest looking dip, but was very good. If they tried it, they liked it!
People raved over this dip!  When the apples were gone people were grabbing for closest thing- dipping even califlower in it?!  I will try it with a dash of vanilla next time..

I love this dip!!  I've made this a couple times & it is always delicious!  Everyone loves it- my cousin's three year old was trying to eat it with a spoon!  The only thing I do differently is use the whole package of caramels & make ahead & chill until time to serve. I also used low-fat cream cheese.  Great recipe I will be making again & again.
Easy and delish! My kind of recipe. I served it with sliced apples and pears. The children loved it.
very delicious. I did add about 10 extra carmels. I love this recipe. Only thing that I wanted to note is that it takes a little longer than 6 minutes to make. I would say more like 12 to 15 minutes

This stuff is SINFUL! So so good and so easy! I used a couple of heaping spoonfuls of caramel ice cream topping in place of melting the caramels - added to the easy factor - and I could eat the whole bowl myself. Mmmmm. Thanks for the great recipe!
Very creamy, extremely easy to make, I think the hardest thing was unwrapping the caramels.
In Canada we skip the brown sugar and add Skor bar chips (toffee chips like Heath bars) on the top of the dip for a great crunchy texture. Thanks for the recipe - it is a HIT whenever I make it.
delish! suprised at how easy it is to make!

Lori, this is AWSOME!  Thanks!  The carmel and cream cheese together.... mmmmm!  What a combination!  This is definately a keeper.  A great dip for fall parties and get togethers.  My picky 7 year old daughter went crazy over this one!

Great recipe!!! I followed the direction of another review and added vanilla. I served mine cold and stirred in crumbled up pieces of heath bar. It just gives it an extra crunch. It was great served with Granny Smith apples. This is a new fall favorite!
I make this a few times a year.. I now buy the bag of the little caramel pieces, they're tiny circles that melt sooo amazing and you don't have to unwrap anything!
To die for!  Perfect for afterschool snacks or parties!  Haven't given it to anyone who hasn't requested the recipe.  Thanks!

I did this but to serve one and omitted the actual caramels: 2 tablespoons cream cheese, 1 packed tablespoon brown sugar, microwave for 10 seconds, take out and add just a drop of vanilla, mix, and enjoy! That was enough for just 1 person and one sliced apple! Delicious!
Love it! I used 4oz of cream cheese and about 20 carmels.  It came out fantastic, my friends and family love it!  Def a family favorite!
Great 5 star Carmel Dip recipe!!! Loved it, didn't change a thing!

This is an easy and wonderfully rich dip to bring to parties. It doesn't look like it will make a lot but it does.  I used the caramel pellets/chips that they sell like chocolate chips. They were easy and there was no need for unwrapping.

I made this yesterday for Thanksgiving and only one person out of two families liked it. The only thing I did different was use Kraft caramel bits rather than caramel squares. My husband said it had a weird flavor. I thought it was because he doesn't like cream cheese (I didn't tell him it was in the recipe though), but my daughter who loves cream cheese said she didn't like it either. Glad I also made a yummy pumpkin dip. It was wiped out!
Good and easy.  Used 20 caramels.
So easy and a huge hit!
Very good, makes a lot and was a hit with sliced apples and pears.
Oh My Gosh...this is soooooo good.  I can't stop eating it.  I made it exactly as stated except for I tripled the recipe for a party!
This was very tasty!!!
Everyone LOVED this - they ate it with apples, vegetables, crackers! They just couldn't stop eatting it!
I LOVE this recipe. I make it as it and it's perfect every time. Thanks for such a good recipe =)

If I could give this more than five stars, I would. This was excellent, and a kid-friendly recipe as well. My eldest son and I had a blast making the dip together. I can see this one being made a lot in this house. TIP: I hollowed out a mini-pumpkin to hold the dip and my son arranged cut up apples around the pumpkin on a seasonal platter. Too cute!
This was a big hit! I used light cream cheese and added a few extra caramels. I made it the night before and it kept well for a couple of days. Will definitely make it again!

This was very good!  I did make a few changes because I was making it for children who do not like cream cheese very well.  I used a whole bag of caramel, 3/4 of low fat cream cheese, and added a bit of milk to the water to melt the caramel.  The kids loved it and so did the adults!!  Oh also added 1 tsp vanilla like other reviewers.  Yum!

Mmmmm! Like creamy caramel apples. I used less water and more caramels. I used Werther's- so easy to unwrap! They are really creamy too. Super easy to make for a party. My boyfriend made me make two batches- one for him to eat now!

OMG this was delicious!! SO simple to make! I used an 11 ounce bag of caramel bits since they are so much easier to melt. Make sure you soften the cream cheese first. I chilled the dip in the fridge for a little while before we ate it and was soooo good!
Over the top fabulous!

This Apple Dip is absolutely fabulous!!  I've made it several times for parties and get togethers and it is ALWAYS a hit, people can't get enough of it.  Instead of normal caramels, I've used Eclair Caramels from Cadbury, which are filled with chocolate. My final result is a chocolate-caramel dip. Hmmmmm!!!!
Yum!  I folded in the caramel mixture once it had cooled to room temperature.  Yum Yum!!
Fantastic! Easy to make. You definitely won't be disappointed.

It was very yummy and surprisingly not as sweet as I expected it to be!  I did add a little vanilla and a few more caramels as suggested by other members.  When it was all finished, I simply could not keep my fingers out of the bowl.  My daughter asked if she could eat it for breakfast!  Thanks for the recipe.  Will defintely be added to my "Recipe Box".
Great party dip! Everyone loved it. Served it with a fresh fruit platter. I made the dip in the morning and kept it in the fridge till that night. Still tasted great!
Amazing!! I brought it to a party and everyone LOVED it! One person even said anything would taste great dipped in it. :)

Scrumptious!  I love caramel apples but they can be a little hard to eat (not something you would serve at a party).  SOLUTION: the flavor of this recipe is very close to caramel apples, but it is easy to make and easy to serve to a group.   Suggestions:  1. add extra caramels for added caramel flavor.  2.  be sure to melt the caramels completely to avoid clumps.  3.  submerge apple slices in orange or lemon juice to prevent browning.  4.  I prefer to use tart apples, like Granny Smith to balance out the sweetness and enhance the caramel flavor.  5.  The dip refrigerates well.   Enjoy!  A perfect Autumn treat.
Yum!  I used about 24 caramels and it was fantastic.  I used the suggestion of putting the apples in water and lemon juice until serving time.
So simple and really yummy!  Will make again!
Great recipe! Even good when it has to be refirgerated when it's not all gone. Almost better when it was cold!
This was great!  I think I like it cooled better.

To make this even easier, instead of melting caramels, I put a layer of caramel ice cream topping on top of the cream cheese mixture (don't fold in) and then as an added bonus I sprinkle crushed skor bar on top.

Made for a Halloween party and was eaten up so quick I ended up making three batches! People were dipping pears, apples, even their fingers (onto their plates, not the serving bowl!!) into this luscious treat. I did add more caramels per other reviews, and it made it perfectly sweet and creamy. Today my husband and I are finishing off the leftovers...though that's only because I saved us some before it hit the appetizer table! The perfect fall dip!

I made this exactly as stated. Only I threw in about 5 more caramels! YUMMY!!! (very sweet - but not too sweet) I served with gala and granny smith apples, which by the way I learned a trick to keep from browning on my way to my destination and it worked WONDERFULLY! I cut apples under running water (read this somewhere - not sure if this step actually helped) and then placed the slices in Sprite - after cutting all apples - drained and put into gallon ziplock baggie and removed all air and zipped - hours later - my apples look like I just cut them!! :-)

I'm not sure what all the fuss is about.  I should have halved this batch, because no one at our house wanted to eat it.  It tasted neither like caramel or cream cheese.  I'm not really sure what it tasted like.  Personally, I thought it was good, but not as good as I expected.  It wasn't fantastic.
Love it's simplicity and flavor.  Great snack to cure those sweet cravings.

I've made this dip for several parties that I've had and people LOVE it! The bowl always goes empty...which my husband hates because he loves this dip too. I always get asked for the recipe. I think I will make a bunch of jars of this up and pass them out as Christmas gifts this year!
This is a delicious, creamy dip.  I've made it several times and I've discovered it's great on Ritz/Town House crackers if you run out of apples.
This dip is so very good. There is nothing to change about it. I love it.

This recipe is THE BEST! At first it tasted more like cream cheese than caramels, so I added 6 more caramels and it came out PERFECT!!  It makes eating apples ALOT easier!!  Awesome recipe!!!!  thanks!!!

WONDERFUL dip!  Great for encouraging kids to eat fruit.  I made this for my son's Pre-K Halloween party and everyone was asking for the recipe.  One of the teachers said "That's too good to give to children!"  It was a HUGE hit.  I made it just as the recipe was written.  Thanks for sharing!!

This is really good, better than I expected, in fact! I made it as a back-to-school treat for my boys and they gobbled it up and then asked for more apple slices so they could eat the last of it :) I followed the recipe exactly, no changes at all and none needed. this is a keeper!

Wow- I didn't realize I hadn't rated this yet!!! Serves 8?? Yeah, right! I usually divide this between 4 ramekins & sprinkle pecan chips over the top. SHOULD be enough for 4 large apples. I could eat this straight out of the bowl. I'll bet it would be great on ice cream or as a cake frosting!?!? Can't say enough about it. Used cored & sliced Fuji apples. Thanks Lori!
Excellent!!!  Didn't/wouldn't change a thing!
double caramel and water

Splendid, especially on a busy Halloween night. I paired this with Honey Crisp apples, one of the best apples available. The recipe approximates the taste of carameled apples, without the sticky mess and stick-to-your-teeth inconvenience. I highly recommend this easy-to-prepare recipe.
Really great, super easy! I'll never buy store-bought again! My husband even loved it, and he's not a big caramel fan. Thanks for sharing!!

I brought this dip to a family gathering and everyone loved it!  I also set out chopped pecans to sprinkle over the top.  I will definately make this one again and again.  Thanks for sharing your recipe, Lori!!
I like to bring this dip to parties and pair it up with green grapes, green apples, and animal crackers.  Everybody loves it!
Easy and sweet, good dip. Tastes just like a caramel apple would.

Outrageously delicious!!!  Took advice to add a little vanilla and a few extra caramels.  Melted the caramels in the microwave,  added to the cream cheese mixture, and it turned out wonderful!  Definitely a "keeper".

Ok, so I dont know for sure what went wrong, except that the "fold in the caramel mixture" step went bad. Dip was lumpy, like bad gravy. Maybe my cheese and sugar werent creamed enough, or mayb the fat free variety of cream cheese was the problem. I tried everything to fix it--from mashing out the cheese lumps by hand to putting it back on the stove in hopes that the cheese lumps would eventually melt. No luck.  It tasted ok, but texture and appearance ruined it for me.

Tasted like a 5 but gave it a 4 because of modifications - used 20 caramels and half the sugar as recommended.  Also used cream instead of water for richer flavor.  To avoid lumps (like yvetteski), make sure you soften cream cheese (20 seconds in the microwave is good), then whip it with the sugar and a sturdy whisk.  Kids loved it, me too!
People eat this stuff up.  I serve it with granny smith apples and graham crackers at get togethers.  I may have to try pretzels and bananas with it next.

SOOOO good!  Super easy, ready to eat right after making or right out of the fridge!  Great with apples, ginger snaps.  I used new Kraft caramel bits 1st time about 1 1/4 bags, 2nd time, doubled the recipe and used about 2 fulls bags of caramel squares (minus the few we ate during unwrapping).  The caramel bits melted easier.  While melting the caramel squares with water, I slightlt browned the bottom of caramel in the pan.  There was small darker brown bits in caramel, but no one even noticed, it tastes so good!
fairly good as long as you use craft carmels

simple and tasty!  only thing I did different was use a bag of caramel bits. made the night before, kept fine.
*UPDATE* I had leftovers because I ran out of apples. So I used it as a caramel sauce with brownie and ice cream. It was awesome!
This is good.

This was excellent!!  I took it to a party and nobody could stop eating it.  People were scooping so much dip that it covered the apple slices!  After I made it, I put it in the fridge and served it straight from the fridge.  It was still soft and easy to dip into.  I added extra caramels, but I don't think that it altered the recipe too much.  You will not be disappointed by this recipe, but don't make it is you're trying to cut back on calories! :)
I have made a caramel apple dip for years. I use cream cheese and caramel ice cream topping. Just soften cream cheese and add some topping to suit your taste. This is so much easier. Barb
Loved it! I used low fat cream cheese and it worked out great.

Absolutely splendid!!! Tried it with gala apples at first and it was much to sweet. Switched to Fuji and Granny Smith apples and couldn't get enough. My kids and I absolutely enjoyed this. It will definitely be made regularly. Thanks so much.
Super fast to make and wonderful!  I'll definitely try a little vanilla in there next time, too.
Excellent combination of flavors.Just the thing for dipping apples, graham crackers, bananas! We had some homemade granola bars to dip, yummy. Thanks Lori.
Dip was good but really can't take as carry in because even though I put lemon juice and water on the apples they turned dark.  Was hardly touched.
This is okay. Even though I love cream cheese, it had too much of a cream cheese taste and not enough of a caramel one, even after I added another 10 extra caramels. Probably won't make again

I served this dip with sliced apples at my son's birthday party, and it was delicious!  I used caramel ice cream topping instead of the caramels because I was in a hurry.  A nice change of pace from store bought dip.

I thought the dip was great!  The only thing I did differently was that I used 20 caramels instead of 16, based on some other reviews.  The cream cheese was not overpowering, but I still think I would use all the caramels next time - there's about 24 in the bag. (Werther's)
This was just ok.  Taste too much like cream cheese (and I love cream cheese!!!).  It was missing something, I'm just not sure what.
Just brought it to a party and it was a HIT! My friend and I are now known as the Caramel Girls! They loved it so much, they started playing keep-away with the bowl of sauce.

To make it even easier I buy the already made apple caramel dip found in the produce isle. I warm the cream cheese before mixing in the brown sugar and then warm the caramel and spread over the cheese mixture and for an added bonus put 3-4 chopped Skor chocolate bars on top. Never any leftover left at get togethers

This is so good!! I made it with 1/3-less-fat cream cheese and only half the brown sugar (1/4 cup).  Warm it was very creamy and had a definite but complimentary cream cheese flavor.  Chilled (my preference!) it kept its creamy dip-able consistency and had a more pronounced caramel flavor.  I also used 20 caramels instead of 16.  This recipe was easily doubled.  Thanks!!
very easy and quick. My son thought it was great. i did cut the sugar in half, and added more caramels. also added 2 tbsp of milk in to keep it easily spreadable and dippable.
Very quick and easy.  And yummy.
Absolutely delicious. Added a bit of vanilla to caramel mixture.

Oddly enough, my teenagers weren't really into this.  I, on the other hand, was taking to eating it right from the spoon.  Very yummy!  The best caramel dip I've ever tried.  What do teenagers know about eating anyway?  :)

Rated this recipe a five but actually give it a  10.  I questioned the cream cheese in this recipe but followed instructions and of course had to check it out before I gave it to the kids and OH MY GOSH!!!!  Hubby loved it too--WILL be making this often.  Already brain-storming ideas to incorporate it into other recipes.

This stuff is simple to make and omg is it good! kid's and adults alike love this one! Thnx for a great recipe!This will be my standard dip for fruit's.I also used splenda brown sugar and fat free cream cheese and added a touch of vanilla :)
What a hit!  Everyone loved this dip!  Make sure you remeber the water when heating the caramels (I forgot them the first time and had to start over :)

This dip is so yummy and easy we make it for every family gathering.  It is perfect as is, but I usually end up throwing in the whole bag of carmels becuase I dont know what I would do with a few leftover carmels in the cupboard.  I also top it with a chopped up Skor bar to make it look fancy.  Thanks for sharing such a fab-o recipe!
Easy and delicious!
Oh so good & oh so easy.  Stirred in some toffee chips at the end just before serving.  YUM!
VERY GOOD!!! Went very quickly.
such a delicious treat  not too sweet.. made it for halloween and my guests loved it

I think this tastes even better than the dip I used to but at the store.  I melted my caramels in the microwave stirring after ever 30 - 40 seconds.  Super easy, did not change a thing.  Will make this a lot.
So tasty. I'm definitely making this again!

This stuff is AWESOME!  And super easy too! I will use it for all my get togethers now.  Oh, one thing about the recipe though, it says to serve immediately, so I waited until the last minute to make it.  I now know though, that it keeps in the fridge for a day or two just fine, with no change in flavor or consistancy.
FANTASTIC!!  Easy to make and a hit with both the kids and adults.  I did add vanilla as suggested by a previous member.

This is the most delicious apple dip ever!  To make this dip even easier . . . instead of melting caramels, I use a plastic carton of caramel apple dip, sold in the produce section.  (Not to be confused with a jar of ice cream topping caramel.)  I also always top the dip with a king-sized Health or Score bar, chopped.  Beautiful presentation and even more irresistible!  I would never take this to a party without at least doubling the whole recipe.  It goes fast.  Oh, and make sure to slightly lemon or lime juice your apples to keep from browning.
Awesome! Added vanilla (about 2 tsp to the caramel mixture) as others suggested. Made a double batch the day before and left it in the fridge. Still perfect the next day and totally gone!

This recipe makes one bag of caramels go a long way and it taste great!  The only trouble I had was that it looked like peanut buter and everyone would try it.  Once I got the word out that it was caramel dip, they all ate it and loved it.  (I only had dark brown sugar, so maybe that's why it looked so much like peanut butter.)

This is an excellent dip! I was actually eating it straight from the bowl! I had a little bit of a time getting the caramels to melt in the water, but that could be something I did. Otherwise, it turned out perfectly
The whole family loved it! Will have to remember this one for the next party.
definitely one of my faves :) very addictive.
I served this at my last dinner party nd what a hit grown-up caramel apples. What a great idea!
Amazing! Very rich. The kind of dip where you like to eat more dip then fruit :)
This stuff is addicting. I found myself starting with apples, then moving onto graham crackers, then pretzels, then just anything I could find to dip in this stuff! It's great! Thank you.

OMG...this is the best! Wanted just half a batch, so I took reviewers advice - 16 caramels and cut everything else by half. Added 1/2 t. vanilla to recipe and served in individual dipping bowls sprinkled chopped walnuts - cut apple on the side.  Oldest son came back in kitchen and swiped the pan with finger to get the rest...no leftovers here!
Excellent! I did add more caramels by almost double, to make it taste a bit more like your basic caramel apple.

I used a whole package of the Kraft caramel bits, it saves the time of unwrapping all of the caramels.  I also softened the cream cheese a little in the microwave before mixing in the brown sugar and adding the melted caramel.  I actually made a double batch and it turned out great except for a few small lumps of brown sugar and cheese. I refrigerated it for the next day and I think the lumps will disappear if I stir it well before serving. Yummy!!

This was really good.  I was a little surprised that it was actually on the runny side... not too runny though.. it still coated the apples very well.... which actually probably made it easier to dip.  I made this for a party of 12 adults and 7 kids, so I doubled the recipe thinking that 8 servings would never be enough.... it was far more than enough!!  I could of made the single recipe and still had plenty for the 3 pound bag of apples I used.

I am making this tomorrow for my sons preschool snack however I just wanted to suggest, instead of using water to melt the caramels with, use 1-2 Tblsp. of whipping cream! It will be the creammiest caramel you have ever had!!
Thank you thank you thank you thank you! An old friend made something just like this when I was in college and I have gone ten years without it!  It is just wonderful!
This was great and so easy to make! Bananna's were great with it
Mmmm ... yummy.  Quick and easy to prepare.  The kids loved it!

This is good but if you think it going to be like having a affy tapple it's not.  That is my favorite and instead of looking for a substitute I would rather satisfy my craving and just eat a real affy tapple

This is delicious! It's not exactly the flavor of a caramel apple, but like a caramel apple cream sauce, maybe. I do think I'd prefer a different apple than the Granny Smiths I chose, because they sort of drown the caramel flavor out, but definitely a make-again recipe, thanks!
This is so yummy! I am making it again for Thanksgiving.

I made this recipe for a party and it wasn't a big hit.  I think it needed to be labeled because people weren't sure what kind of dip it was.  (Someone asked me if it had peanut butter in it.)  However, I thought it tasted very good, and it was easy to make, so I might try it again sometime.  I'll just be sure to let people know what it is.
This was way to sweet and the cream cheese flavor overwhelmed the caramel flavor.

Used the full bag of caramels-well, except the couple that we ate-and microwaved them. Next time, I will do in a double boiler, there were lumps of unmelted caramel. Absolutely delicious, and am planning on making again 5 days after the original try!

A perfect alternative to a Caramel Apple. Couldn't believe I actually got my son to eat a REAL apple. I was looking for a caramel apple recipe that was easy, ha-ha. This recipe was soooo easy compared to real caramel apples and really, the taste was to die for.

Use the whole bag of caramels, or the caramel flavor of the dip is overshadowed by the cream cheese flavor. Try adding a little vanilla. Dip apple slices in orange or lemon juice to prevent browning. Also good with pretzels and gingerbread man cookies.

Didn't change a thing and the dip turned out wonderfully.  We made this for my daughter to take as a treat to her classroom for her birthday party with sliced apples.  We didn't soften the cream cheese as others suggested and it whipped up nice and smooth after we mixed in the melted caramels.  Delicious.  Great recipe.  Thanks for the post.

Made this for our Fall festival event. While I thought it was a bit too sweet, lots of others loved it... especially the kids. Kind of reminded me of sweetened condensed milk with a tangy taste. I will give it four stars because it went over so well. If I were going to make it ever again, I'd start with 1/4 cup brown sugar and work from there.
Delicious! It doesn't even need the brown sugar - I made it without it, and it was PLENTY sweet enough.  I also used milk instead of water.
YUMMM! This was so good.  Both kids and adults loved it. Great for parties.
I found this while randomly browsing and decided to make this because of a sudden craving. THE best. Forget all about store bought caramel dip. This beats anything out of a container by far.

I think I was supposed to dip something in this instead of eating it by the spoonful!  Defintitely deserves more stars!  Cut the sugar in half, 20 carmels, and cooked on water & carmel stove top until carmels were melting then added cream cheese and sugar and whisk smooth.  I wonder what leftovers or cold would have tasted like?  LOL! Thank you for sharing!

Fabulous! I used fat free cream cheese, just to cut down a little on fat/calories, and I don't think it affected the taste at all. Took it to a youth group New Year's party and when it was gone I actually caught some of them scraping their fingers around the inside of the bowl to get the scraps!
A huge hit at the party I took it to.  I will definitely make this again.  It was so easy.  At first it seemed runny, but in the end the consistency was perfect. I followed the recipe exactly.

I absolutely loved this recipe.  I found the Kraft Caramel Bits which is wonderful. No unwrapping caramels forever. For those using these I called Kraft and was told 1 cups of bits = 25 caramels.    When I added just 1 cup of the caramel bits it was very watery.  I feared it would not firm up so since I love caramel anyway I added the whole bag. I put it in the fridge since we wasn't eating until the next couple days. It is a little thick but still good consistency for dipping.   I love this dip!! The cream cheese gave it a richer taste.  It certainly was hit!!

Wicked tasty!  Great recipe!  This takes caramel apples up about 5 notches.  I was very pleased with the outcome.  Okay, so slight changes to combine 2 recipes from this site but very minor.  I used heavy cream with the caramel, about 2 or 3 tbs.  A touch of vanilla and half the brown sugar in the cream cheese mixture.  No nuts here. Excellent!
My son loved it!  Will be making again!

LOVE this. I changed the recipe a little bit. I used 20 Wethers SOFT caramel chews, added a little bit of vanilla, used half the cream cheese and half the brown sugar (the Wethers caramels are extra sweet and rich) and added 1/4 teaspoon salt. My favorite thing to dip is pretzel sticks.
I doubled the caramels and followed the rest of the recipe. I put in blender to make it s-m-o-o-t-h. I could just eat it with a spoon.  Sooooo GOOD !!!

I made this as an extra dessert for a dinner party I gave a few weeks ago. Everyone LOVED it!! I made exactly as written, didn't change a thing. Hints & suggestions - Puff pastry at my local market comes frozen.  Plan ahead - place it in the fridge 24 hrs. before you need it (I did not try the "quick thaw" method so I cannot tell you if this dries it out.  It was just more convenient for me to put in the fridge 24 hrs. before I needed it).  I'd also suggest using only 1, maybe 1 1/2 loaves at the most of the multi-grain bread and at least 1 more 16 oz pkg. of seitan.  For our taste, it was simply too much stuffing and not enough seitan.  Plan ahead and use your food processor - place the bread in the processor and lay out on a jelly roll pan overnight. Then, place it in a storage bag until you're ready for it.  I omitted the margarine and put the carrots, celery, onion, and parsley together in the processor, then dumped it in an XL (read: very large) bowl with the bread and omitted cooking the veggies entirely.  Also, for the egg replacer, 5 1/2 tsp. is *almost* 2 Tbsp (1.8 Tbsp. to be exact).  I purchased 2 dried vegan gravy mixes at my local natural foods store (I could not find garbanzo bean gravy mix); next time, I'll make sure I'll have 4 envelopes, agreeing with a previous reviewer that gravy is the key. Dear textheavy,
Triple Sec is also known as an 'orange-flavored' liquor.

Equal parts of the triple-sec is way too much. A shot of vodka with about a thrid to a half shot of triple sec.A dash of fresh lime juice or Roses's lime should also be added. Very good! I added grounded beef, green beans and more tator tots and cheese. So I guess I turned it into a green bean cassarole, but very good none the less!

If you read a previous review under my "name"? That wasn't me. I have no idea how that got there. Anyway, I did really like this dish. Although, I'm not a fan of sour cream. This is a very creamy, cheesy casserole.  I really enjoyed it and it's incredibly easy to make.  Thank you.
You can't go wrong with tater tots.  This recipe made it legal to be the main dish.  Loved it.

We loved this! This was part of our make ahead menu for a weekend get-away to the PA mts. Our place has been winterized so no water for dirty dishes. i made this recipe for a party, everyone loved it!

This recipe is ok.  You really have to be careful with the taters or they will not be crispy enough.
Pretty delicious, although I prefer this type of casserole with hash browns.

I have been cutting back on eating meat and this recipe was a perfect non-meat recipe. My kids loved it. My daughter said it was the best thing she had ever eaten.  It was rich, but comfort food at its best.

This is a fast & delicious recipe that we really enjoyed.  Only change would be to add the french fried onions at the end, about 15 minutes before finished, as mine started to burn & I had to cover the dish with foil. Thought this was yummy!  I was looking for meatless recipes and this was really easy.  Not healthy, though, even though I used low-fat sour cream!
This was super easy and quick to prepare.  It smells wonderful and tastes fantastic.  The whole family loved it!

Prepared this for dinner lastnight along with steamed broccoli.

I can't wait to fry some up with some eggs later tonight.
Love it! So good, make it ALL the time! Hard not to eat it all ;) You gotta try it!!!

This gets rave reviews every time.
Very yummy dish, and great for leftovers!  It's not the healthiest thing I've ever cooked, but I continue to bake it when the craving arises!
Divine and easy1
My family LOVES this.  I only used the onions on about half, but both sides were very good.  My sister, who pretty much doesn't pay much attention to food unless it has beef, even raved about it.

Turned out so good!  I followed others advice and added a pound of hamburger and some green beens.  I also noticed there are no spices in the original recipe so i added salt, pepper and some garlic salt.  This is going in the recipe box. Yummmmm!
Very unsophisticated, but very very tasty. Easy to whip up after a long day and pleases even the picky ones (which would actually be me). A tad bit salty, though, so no need to add any. Yummy.
Well I followed the recipe the only change I made was to reduce sour cream per other reviews. I was glad I did. This tasted like sourcream and onion chips. Will not make again

This is a great base recipe for Tater Tot Casserole. The first time I made it as it is written, and it was a solid four stars. With some tweaking for taste, however, it quickly becomes five stars. I have added a pound of cooked hamburger, browned with the onions and other seasonings, and this gives the recipe a good balance. super good the  FF Onions  really  made it   so good

VERY teenage friendly!  I used cream of chicken soup instead and it was awesome!!  My husband & I liked it but it was my 3 teens that gobbled this down.  The ONLY problem I had was not "oiling" my casserole dish down as suggested and I used Pam spray instead.  Next time I'll use cooking oil.

and doubled the recommended amount (i love cheese!). i also bought the larger can of french fried onions and mixed 1/2 in with the soup, sc, and cheese mixture. once the mixture is spread over the tots, i sprinkled with garlic powder and finished it off with the last of the ff onions. super easy and heats up great for leftovers! yummmm....

This is a keeper! Thank you for sharing this recipe. Made tonight. My teens loved it! The only change I made was adding an extra cup of cheese. Yes, we are cheese heads. l think this will be a wonderful casserole to take to family functions. Again, thank you!
Anthony and Eoin both loved this recipe! Quick to assemble and inexpensive.  I added 2 cans green beans and 1 small package of boca burger ground meatless.
This was really good! The only thing I did differently, was to add some green beans just to have a little bit of vegetable. Will be making again.
Tasted really great, it was a bit greasy though and the tater tots fall apart, aside from that very tasty.
excellent the way it is or with modifacations, can't go wrong either way.

Like alot of other reviewers on here, I added a layer of hamburger meat.  To give some added flavor, I added an envelope of Lipton's Onion Soup Mix to my hamburger meat as it was cooking and it turned out delicious!!!!!

We love this recipe here!! I followed suggestions of some of the PPs and added a lb of ground beef and a dash of garlic powder. I also added a dash of pepper and used about 1.5 cups of cheese. Excellent!! Will definitely be one of our new regulars.
Oh my god, this was so good!!  Heart attack on a plate, but so good...

My family and I LOVED it, esp my kids!  I used sharp cheddar instead and doubled it (doubling it is necessary). Different, but really good.

With a little bit of ground beef, this dish is great. My boyfriend and best friend devoured it! The best part is that it is extremely filling so one serving goes a long way. Will use again- such a different, yummy recipe!
Very good recipe. I took the advice of other readers and added 1 lb. of ground hamburger, 1 can of green beans, 2 cups of shredded cheese and salt & pepper to taste. My family loved it!

This was a wonderful easy recipe.  Good comfort food.  I have made it a coule of times.

I recommend this to go with any main dish, or by itself.  Husband loved it also.

Thanks for sharing your recipe! :)
Pretty good.  Seemed a bit thick for me but overall very tasty.  The kids seemed to enjoy it, never thought about using the fried onions.  Gave it a good flavor!

This was wonderful - my whole family loved it (even the one who doesn't usually like things with sour cream : ). Sorry, but we didn't care for this at all.

French-fried onions were out of season so I had to make them myself which added to the prep time.  To make your OWN french-fried onions, thinly slice about 3-onions, dip in 1/2 cup milk mixed with 1 egg.  Then dig into gluten-free flour.  Fry in hot oil for about 5 minutes.  Drain on paper-towels.

I also added some sharp cheddar and broccoli.  I still thought it was a bit rich and would cut down on the sour cream next time.  The casserole didn't hold together too well until the next day when re-heated but then the fried-onions weren't as good.  Quite filling!
I know this isn't a very healthy meal but it was sooo good!  I doubled the cheese and cream of mush soup.  This will be something we make again!

i add ground turkey, mushrooms,onions.it's a big hit.

I added cooked ground turkey sausage to the recipe and towards the end of cooking I topped it with the french fried onions and covered the top with shredded cheddar cheese. This one of my most favorite recipes! It's so delicious!
This is great!  We are not big onion fans, so my husband recommended using crumbled bacon in its place next time I make it. Sounds like a good idea!
Pretty good. I doubled the cheese and didn't use as many french fried onions

I don't even like tater tots and I loved this casserole. I brought it to a graduation party and got lots of compliments on it.

This is dangerous and amazing. Dangerous because it's pretty unhealthy, but that will not stop me from eating it. Definitely worth the calories. I made it exactly as stated, but threw in a bag of frozen broccoli. Simply amazing.

delicious!

The best recipe ever!  I've made it for several occasions and bbq's.  Everyone loves this recipe.

The ultimate in comfort food! This dish brings me back to my childhood...even my college sorority cook made this. This version is definitely better. After finding this recipe and making this many, many times now, I make the following changes: brown a pound of 93/7 hamburger, seasoned with garlic powder, pepper, and half an onion; no grease to drain! I brown an entire bag of crispy crowns instead of regular tots. I layer the hamburger meat over the crispy crowns, then spread the soup mixture, which incorporates the top reviewer's suggestion to add more sharp cheddar than called for, some French fried onions, and I also season the mixture with additional spices to my liking (garlic & onion powders, a little paprika and pepper). I also use the Roasted Garlic Cream of Mushroom soup and the entire 16 oz container of sour cream. It's thick and creamy and using the back of a spoon, it spreads easier than you think. So what if the hamburger is mixed in? Top that with some additional cheese and bake 35-40 minutes at 350. 1-2 minutes before it's done, I sprinkle a few more French fried onions on the top and turn the oven to broil. After taking it out, let it sit for 10 minutes. Perfection! Now, if only my husband would let me add some green beans to the mix....

This was delicious. I used Philadelphia herb and garlic cream cheese and used fettuccine. Will make this again.

Made this tonight it was awesome. Added baked chicken and there you go. You have yourself and your family a healthy meal.

Fresh garlic and fresh spinach for a fresher, better taste!!! I also sautéed some shallot with the garlic. I probably used 4oz of cream cheese for a richer flavor. One of the BEST alfredo sauces I've ever had. My husband doesn't care for spinach and he LOVED it!

Recipe Group Selection 8/31/2013 -  Let me just say, thank goodness I have a gym membership.  I used the full 10 oz. package of chopped spinach which ended up being about 1 cup of chopped spinach.  It was very good and everyone enjoyed it but it's not something I would make too often.

Your recipe is pretty good! I basically add the same ingredients except the "cream cheese" due to the fat content but I suppose you could use low fat neufchatel instead. There are a couple things I do to maximize flavor; I prepare the chicken ahead of time, pierce it before marinating it in my tri-citrus marinade overnight using pineapple juice, slash of lemon & lime and even some orange juice with diced onion, green onion, red peppers, paprika, garlic and a bunch of other stuff (lol...salt, pepper..that sort of thing) to make it flavorful, juicy & tender....baste it while I bake it...Now you may think citrus chicken would clash with the alfredo sauce but it doesn't because it just adds a nice juiciness & flavor to it...then I tear it and toss it in with cooked homemade spaghetti (into which I have incorporated a little extra flavor by way of a pinch of salt, some parsley & garlic for push in flavor); then I added a heaping tbsp of my secret French ingredient...that's right...le mayonnaise! I throw in some mozzarella & parmesan cheese...Gives it another little boost (not too much mayo so that you can identify as an ingredient..just enough for flavor)! It turned out pretty good!! Thanks for sharing!

This is AWESOME.  Yes, I thawed and drained the frozen spinach before use.  I also added an extra tbs. of cream cheese.  When it was done I cooked some pasta.  While that was cooking I dipped pita chips in this, Delicious!!!  Then I had the pasta with this sauce on it.  Yes, I will make this again

My first time making home made Alfredo and this was a hit.  My family absolutely loved it.  I added sausage and mushrooms and seasoned to my taste but would have to conclude this we very simple to make, tastey and filling.

Incredibly good. Yum. Added baked  Costco chicken with lots of garlic. I almost forgot the noodles since they weren't on my grocery list.

Everyone loved it. Used fresh sauteed spinach and added cubed ham  from Sundays dinner. A little extra cream cheese ,served with linguine. Not a drop left.

Easy and delish! There's no beating that combo!
Actually followed recipe. Did add sauteed chicken and a little paprika. Rich, sweet and yummy.
Great and easy!  Added random left over veggies and it was great.

Absolutely amazing recipe for what we're calling "cheap" Alfredo.  Definitely read the comments and drain the spinach. We actually forgot to add the garlic powder for half the first serving....its a whole different meal which is also worthy of 5 stars.

Might be the best "easy" recipe on All Recipes.

So easy to make- and it came out so good! Can't wait to make it again! :)
Super easy to follow and make used canton noodles for a great fettuccine feel  would recommend!!!

I used fresh spinach and 2 minced garlic cloves, other than that,  I followed the recipe as written.  I tossed the sauce with rigatoni pasta and topped it off with slices of grilled chicken breasts.  Delicious!

So good! My husband and I both loved this.

Wow!  I normally just take recipes I find online and tweak them to my liking. No need here, I did use garlic salt instead of the garlic powder and salt, but . . . Wow. Perfect way to get my little guy to eat spinach!  This is a delicious creamy alfredo recipe that will be a keeper in my house.  Went perfect with a salad and breadsticks.

No changes and it turned out wonderful.  Great recipe!

Delicious recipe, just be sure to squeeze the water from the frozen spinach before putting spinach in the sauce.

Yummy and easy!  Pulled this together last minute when I realized I forgot to buy pasta sauce.   My only sub was 2% milk for cream, because thats all I had but my family still loved it.

Wonderful and easy!

Yum! I followed directions exactly except I added a pinch of red pepper flakes and paprika and sautéed some baby bell mushrooms in the butter before adding the spinach. This is a keeper!

Seriously better than Olive Garden! Don't look any further for the perfect Alfredo recipe. I did not use spinach and traded the garlic powder for 11/2 Tbl chopped garlic. I had to cook it for almost double the time in the recipe (about 20 min) for it to thicken but it coated the noodles beautifully and was so rich and creamy the extra time was absolutely worth it!

Soooo good! I used a little less spinach the first time I made it, and let me tell you, it was not all that great. When I used the recommended amount the second time, it was so fabulous that even my picky little sister ate it. Greatest spinach recipe ever!

very good -- I  use half and half cream, fresh spinach, fresh garlic( several cloves minced) -  it thicken  nicely  and I think a chicken breast - grilled and cut up,  would  go well  with this dish to  make it heartier , but  was very  good  as is and would make again --!
I cut the butter to 1/4 cup and used 4 oz. cream cheese. I will definitely make this again. Also, be sure to drain the spinach.

For a thicker sauce just use 3-4 tablespoons of cream cheese and 1/2 cup to 3/4 cup of half and half (or heavy whipping cream).  I do not use the butter, and I think it helps keep the sauce from running too thin (plus it's healthier). 

As I stir the cooked pasta, spinach & garlic, and the cream cheese, I splash half-half along the way to make sure my sauce doesn't get too thin. If it does get too thin, you can simmer it down by turning the heat on high and adding more cream cheese. Hope that helps :)

I made this recipe for the Allrecipes Canadian Allstars Spring Bling assignment.
I made the recipe as written except I halved it for a 9x9 pan and I omitted the topping because the pecans I had in the cupboard were MIA.
The batter was very wet, I had to add 3 tbsps more flour.
I used 2 small red delicious apples chopped finely.
Mine baked in 31 minutes.
This was like a snacking cake, very light and fluffy.
I found it a little too oily and sweet, when I make again I would halve the butter and sugars and then halve the topping and see how that works.
I lined my pan with parchment and cut into 9 pieces.
Thanks for a fast and tasty recipe!

Followed recipe. Worried it would be to mushy based on 2 reviews. Worked fine.  Was not sure how exact to measure the apple chunks.. Since I have lots of apples in need of a home, I mounded it up to to maybe 9 fluid ounces . Used 1.5% fat buttermilk most stores stock. Packed brown sugar hard in measuring cups.  Oven temp 350°F. Removed from oven at 40 minutes. Internal temp in center of cake was 205°F. Pan was glass 9" x 13".  Texture and taste both seem just right for me.  Thanks!

Didn´t look like the picture! Mine was a bit wetter rather than light and fluffy; the brown sugar seems to have sunk and formed a bit of caramelish jelly on the bottom. I really liked this soup. My modifications were to add a shallot, some white wine and a pinch of cayenne for a little spice. I think it would have been tasty even without the cream, but I couldn't resist.
Very much like potato soup in a low carb version. You should increase spices to taste. I like more garlic, spice blend, more leaks, etc.

This was delicious and I'll definately make it again. My only problem with it is it is a little soupy (not very thick) and I like soups with more substance. But since it is low carb it doesn't have starch from potatoes or flour to thicken it so it makes sense that it would be a little thin.

This recipe was wonderful!  I did follow the advice of others and used 6 cups of broth.  ( I used chicken broth, only because I had just boiled chicken and had the broth on hand.}  Otherwise, I pretty much followed the directions.  What a nice "comfort food" on a cool evening.  Thanks for the recipe!

INSTEAD OF VEG. BROTH I USED CHICKEN BOULION CUBES AND ENOUGH WATER TO MAKE BROTH, INSTEAD OF FRESH LEEKS I USED KNORR LEEK SOUP MIX. DID NOT ADD ANY MORE SALT. IT WAS EASY AND TASTY. A DEFINITE MAKE AGAIN!

I used roasted garlic and Better Than Bouillon brand vegetable broth. Instead of simmering the cauliflower 45 minutes, I roasted it at 425F for 15, while the rest of the soup ingredients simmered. Then I blended everything in the blender with 8oz tofu to make it creamy. Took about 25 mins start to end.   I'm sure I could get the same level of creaminess as regular potato & leek soup if I doubled the tofu next time. If you don't have a huge blender, you can do this in batches. I also think you can use onion powder if you don't have leeks or onion and it will be fine. Great recipe!

I used purple cauliflower because that's all I had...weird but okay. Be careful with the salt since the broth most likely has plenty. Next time I'll leave aside some boiled cauliflower and leeks and chop it up and add it in at the end to make the consistency more interesting (I'm not much of a smooth soup person).

I was blown away by how delicious this soup was. I did season it up a bit (added some onion powder, Rosemary , and red chilli flakes) as per other reviewers and roasted the cauliflower, but other than that I left it as is. It's a great soup to experiment with- will definitely make again!
I was looking for a soup to make and found this and it was wonderful. the only thing i added was some extra cauliflower florets to each serving to make it a little chunkier. fantastic recipe! thanks

I love the flavour and texture. I didn't have cream so used bits and pieces of cheeses I had left over in the fridge. Delicious!  Otherwise I stuck to the recipe. Looking forward to many delicious meals with artisan bread, salad and a gorgeous soup.

Excellent!  Normally, I avoid anything marked "low carb" like the plague, but gave this one a shot.  Every time I make this, I'm honour bound to bring some in to my staff, as they absolutely LOVE it.  If I don't have three leeks, I substitute an onion.  I also increased the garlic (well, doubled it, really) because I love garlic.  It's fantastic!!  Thank you for sharing the recipe!
Really good.  Here are my edits....  No butter, just 3/4 of (veg) broth,  add 1 can of white beans just before blending, add soy milk as needed after blending.
Was delicious.     , I baked the cauliflower , leeks. And garlic

Hello soup season!  I loved this.  I followed this recipe with the exception of using chicken broth instead of vegetable both and I didn't not feel the need to add the cream.  Wonderful texture, warmed the soul & healthy.  What a perfect soup on our first day of snow.
This was amazing!!  I added a little onion powder and some dill for flavor.  I have yet to find a better low carb recipe.

Just drizzle the bottom of the cookie sheet with the olive oil, place the cauliflower and garlic on top, then drizzle some more oil on top and broil until the garlic is a light brown color. Repeat the same steps throughout and enjoy!
I substituted chicken broth instead of vegetable broth. Added some half and half. It came out perfect . I will be making this again.

This was a wonderful soup. It diffently needs the cream, it really cut down the overwhelming flavor of the leeks in this soup. I will make this again with 1 less leek because mine were totally huge flintstone size, and I tasted more leek then califlower, but that's because of how big mine were. Other then that, I got my son to eat it and that made me giggle beyond belief because he doesn't like califlower. My family thoroughly enjoyed this very much and it made a great addition to my recipe box. Well done! Thank you.

This soup is outstanding!  I would recommend the broth sit a little above the vegetable mix - 6 cups should be enough.  I was generous with the leek and garlic, and also substituted some of the (vegetarian) broth for water to reduce the sodium.  Fantastic!
Loved the combination of cauliflower and leeks. The only change that I made was to purée a can of garbanzo beans instead of the cream. Will be making again.
AMAZING! I also used 6 cans of chicken broth and it had a perfect thick and creamy consistency. I omitted the butter entirely and no taste was sacrificed. I will make this again and again.
Absolutely delicious.  I used a small head of cauliflower, 6 cups of both, 1 cup of half and half, a few Tbl. of sherry, tarragon, thyme and tobasco.  Yum.

I make this often and love it. After making it so many times, I started to make my own little tweaks to suit my tastes. I usually roast the cauliflower to add a little more flavor and I use chicken broth instead of beef broth. I put in a blob of sour cream before eating.

This is an exceptional soup, very easy to makes, highly nutritious and extremely  tasty.

Highly recommended

What a wonderful soup!! After reading the reviews, I used only 6 cups of stock and found it to be just right. It wasn't bad without the cream, but I crave that velvety goodness of cream soups. Use a dusting of curry powder or not; delicious both ways.

What a great base!  I didn't have any leeks, so i used onions like another reviewer had mentioned.  After it was done, I added steamed veggies and rice.  It was delicious!  Tastes like a creamy soup and I didn't even have to use the cream!  Great healthy alternative!  Perfect for a cold day :)

This was surprisingly creamy. I substituted one of the leeks for a medium yellow onion. 
It's so easy and very tasty!!

WOW!!! This was awesome, My whole family couldn't get enough.  You could totally get away without adding cream for a healthier version.  It was even great chilled for a summer soup!  Needless to say it's a definate keeper

I reduced the broth to 4 cups (all I had on hand), increased the leeks (had 5), and used half-and-half instead.  My husband saw it cooking and asked me to serve it before blending it smooth.  Maybe I'll try roasting the cauliflower next time. Great soup... very elegant. Thanks!
Yummy and easy - I'm not a soup person normally but this was fantastic.

I’ve been on a soup kick lately.  Must be that time of year.  I deviated somewhat on this recipe by cutting the olive oil back to 1 T. and the butter back 2 T.  As others, I reduced the amount of broth to 5-3/4 cups (one 32 oz. box and one 14-1/2 oz. can) and used chicken broth instead of vegetable.  I also used white pepper instead of black.  This was just ok for us.  I thought it really needed some pizzaz.  We ended up adding Velveeta to the two servings we ate and the rest went to the freezer.  Maybe the leftovers will be better.  UPDATE 1/15/14:  Since writing this review we have had this two more times.  It definitely improves if you allow the flavors to meld.  Last night we added some sharp cheddar that I shredded myself and it was the best yet!  Now this is a five star recipe, not the three stars I originally gave it.
Absolutely delicious. I will use 6 cups of both instead of 8 next time to men it thicker. I added 6 cloves of garlic instead of 3. WIll do it again as everyone loved it.

Made a crockpot version of this, which came out nicely. I added some chopped shallots and sauteed them with the garlic, then put it in the crockpot with the cut-up leeks and cauliflower. Also reduced the cream by half, and it was still plenty rich. A great wintry soup for February nights!

Very good!  Creamy, flavorful, and comforting.  The cream really makes it taste more like potato but it was good without (if you don't have any on hand).  I will be adding this to my recipe rotation.  Thanks!

I think this soup is great. Super easy to make and a really good texture and flavour. A couple variations that I did were adding only 4 cups of veggie broth with a can of chichen broth and a can of onion soup. I also added four cloves of garlic rather than just three.  I would definately recommend this soup to anyone.

I roasted the cauliflower until lightly browned, used probably 3x the garlic (about half of which was roasted garlic), added some onion flakes, a little ground red pepper (be careful, it doesn't take much to make it really spicy) and 6 cups of chicken broth. Then I added a couple tablespoons of cornstarch to cold skim milk (about a cup?) before adding to the soup. Let it return to a boil and then removed from heat and blended.  Tried it tonight and it's awesome.  Can't wait to try it tomorrow after the flavors meld even more.  With the reduced broth and addition of corn starch it is quite thick and smooth.

Easy, excellent. I followed the directions exactly, did not add the optional cream, and it tasted delicious. Creamy, velvety texture, lovely flavor. And milk-free!

I would recommend drizzling some pumpkin seed oil on top, or sprinkling with freshly ground cracked pepper, but those are just suggestions as the soup tastes lovely the way it is.

On its own, this recipe was too bland for my taste. I added nutritional yeast (7 tbsp), smoked paprika (1/4 tsp), herbes de provence (1/4 tsp) and tumeric (1/4 tsp) in the soup itself and blended it in the Vitamix. The texture was great. I actually prefer the texture of this soup since it isn't as starchy as a potato and leek soup. When I served it, I added bacon bits, a spoonfull of sour cream and some chopped chives. (all vegan) The tweaked, final result was really good!

I got two HUGE leeks in my Farm Fresh to You CSA and had no idea how to use them! (a bit embarrassing) So I came digging at All Recipes for something tasty. And I found it!! Really enjoyed the simplicty of the recipe, for the beginner that I am. And it was so yummy.  I'm going to try to making "cashew cream" to replace the heavy cream that's optional in this one. I used the cream this time. It was lovely, but I'd like to reduce dairy even further from my diet. Thanks! I'll update on how the cashew cream turns out. :) Happy Eating!
I am so not a cook.  But this recipe was so easy - and so good.  I even got a call to make it for our family Thanksgiving dinner --- now that is a recommendation!! Didn't change a thing.

The first time I made this soup I was lazy and didn’t blend it. It was okay but obviously the texture was wonky. But I got an immersion blender and tried again. My husband semi-sort of remembered the first flopped attempt so he wasn’t psyched for a re-do. However the second attempt was a HUGE hit. Totally WOWed my hub AND discovered the joys of an immersion blender. Score!
It was easy to make, and quite tasty. Definitely a recipe I'll use again!

This soup is fabulous! I used crushed peppercorn to give it a nice kick and it did.  I also added one can of cannellini beans which added protein and a nice thickness so I didn't need to use the heavy cream or anything for that matter to get it to a nice thick, creamy consistency.
So easy and absolutely delish!  Even my fussy husband loved it.
I've made this several times and love it!

This recipe is AMAZING…..like the others who posted reviews, I used less broth.  I actually used just enough to cover the vegetables.  I cannot believe the great consistency (I did not use cream or milk).  I think the thickness is due to less broth (I used approximately 5 1/2 cups)…..I am going to try this and add some winter veggies.  I did need to add a bit of salt (the store bought broth was low sodium and it really did need a bit more - kosher salt).  The emersion blender is winner with this recipe! 
Don't hesitate to try this……it is so good!

I did not use any cream, etc. and cut back on the amount of broth (and I used chicken broth, it's more flavorful).  I also added an onion.  Was very good and didn't seem to have lacking in flavor for me!

I made this as directed and was so disappointed. I thought that it was bland and really needed some other seasonings in it. I also had to add a lot of salt to it because there was no taste. I was really looking forward to this but was disappointed.

This was very good!  I roasted the cauliflower with salt, pepper, and garlic oil prior to sauteeing and skipped the optional cream.  The end result was surprisingly filling and satisfying.  I resisted the urge to add additional herbs/spices to this dish, and I'm glad.  I think anything than salt & pepper may have overpowered the delicate leek/cauliflower flavor.

Both my partner and I thought this was excellent. I agree with the reviewers who have suggested cutting back the on the liquid. In fact, next time I will add 5 cups of broth. For those who are truly "low carbing," non need to cut back on the cream unless the calories are a concern. The cream helps make the dish really luxurious! For the reviewer who said she avoids low carb recipes "like the plague," I have to wonder why. Most LC recipes are very delicious, it's the low fat dishes that tend to lack flavor. True, there are some weird LC recipes out there (mock french toast made with pork rinds--it is seriously pretty tasty), but most LC recipes aren't strange--just short on starches and sugars.

Just happened to pick up leeks and cauliflower up at the farmers market this morn. It was their last day for the season. It was meant to be. I love these wonderful, simple, and easy recipes. Especially when they are music to your mouth!

I don't really measure when I cook, but I did follow recipe.
Made this soup tonight. My new favourite soup! Will definitely be making this again! I used chicken broth rather than vegetable but followed recipe as written. Perfectly delicious!

This was really good! I only had one leek so I added a yellow onion and some green onions. I also only used 6 cups of vegetable broth and more garlic than the recipe called for because I love garlic. Didn't need to add the cream it was the perfect consistency. Will definitely make again.

I love this soup and have it for lunch nearly every day. The texture is a bit more thin than a Potato and Leek Soup but that is to be expected in a low carb version and the flavor is outstanding. I now make it with 6 cups of broth instead of 8 but it's great either way. I also wanted to mention that if what you want is potato and leek soup then MAKE potato and leek soup and refrain from giving this recipe a low score because it isn't something that it never claimed to be. It's not rocket science people. Really. Thanks for the recipe!
Love love love this soup, as did the rest of my family.

This is a great low carb recipe.  I used others advice and used an onion instead of the 3 leeks and it turned out wonderful.  I also used 7 cups of vegetable broth instead of 8 (it was all that I had).  I will make it again.

This was awesome! I changed it up a tiny bit: added WAY more garlic and one sliced potato (skin on) and a little bit of braggs aminos instead of salt or pepper. SO GOOD, the recipe is enough for a small army so I have enough to feed myself at work the rest of the week!

I followed what the others did. I used 6 cups of water and added a can off garbonzo beans, drained, to the recipe. This is a keeper.  Delicious and healthy

New york

This was absolutely fabulous, and I can say that as a person who makes a lot of soup!   I was looking for a thick recipe that didn't require cream or starch and this is it. I cannot get over how simple and how good this is!

I just made this soup for the first time and my husband and I both loved it!  What a treat for us after having been on the low carb diet for a month.  It is a little thin but that's the trade off for being low carb.  Thanks so much for this recipe.

This came out absolutely delicious!!! I added about half the water and that was more than enough. Creamy and tasty.

Great hearty soup. Based on other reviews I roasted the cauliflower as it adds more depth and colour. I also added a can of Navy beans, which adds tons of fibre and protein. Lastly, I used old bay spice to bring out all the flavours. Really good!
I added a few spices to enhance the flavor.  Fantastic, definitely will make again and again!!

Added some cheese on top and stirred in a bit of Tabasco...so good...I did not even miss the potatoes!
Btw, I did NOT run it thru a blender...too messy...just mashed it a bit.
WOW what a tasty treat.  I roasted the cauliflower and garlic with olive oil and a sprinkle of salt and what a yummy nutty flavor that it added!!!  Will be making this on a regular basis.
add an onion (1/2 vidalia?) and celery salt and natures season. Only 3 cans veg broth. Ham would be good...or more solid veggies (peas, carrots, cooked cauliflower, etc - not blended in)
Wow this is delicious and very easy to make!

Very good.
Good, but seems to be lacking in something.

This was very good.  The only change I made was using home made chicken stock because I had some in the freezer.  I also didn't think there was a need to add salt (especially not if using canned stock)  I would eat this even if it were not healthy and will make it again.
this is the super most awesomest soup! We love it even without the heavy cream! it also freezes perfectly! We make it all the time now! Great job on this one!
A new family favorite! Subbed chicken broth for vegetable and added 1 whole chopped onion and 1/2 lb (10 strips) of bacon. Will definitely make again - and I don't really care for soup!!

I like the idea of the soup being low in carbs.  However, I found it lacking flavor even though I used only four cups of broth.  I diced up some jalapenos and added some cardamom and garam masala.  I would have added a medium onion as well if I had one on hand.  I did like a suggestion to use yogurt rather than heavy cream because this is a good way to add creaminess without adding a ton of calories.

No changes made to the existing recipe. With a minimum of ingredients and effort, you get a high end tasting soup. I excluded the cream but didn't miss it at all. Pureed in the Vitamix, it comes out silky smooth. It's pale green colour is very attractive as well. Absolutely delicious!

Yummy soup!!!!  I will make it again!!
This soup is awesome.. Way easy, low cost. Tastes like it came from a restaurant.. WOW!! Will easily impress any guest..

Decided to do a couple of vegetarian meals throughout the week, I'm so happy I went with this recipe. I followed it exactly, with the cream. Took me a while to make, but I'm always a distracted cook. I do not really care though,  because this soup is so good.

I made a couple of changes to this recipe, I made extra cauliflower and set aside some of it to add later so that there would be chunks (more satisfying), and we served it with a dollop of sour cream...........delicious!  Thanks for a great recipe.
WOW, served this soup with dinner and was told that it was one of the best soups ever.
i roast my cauliflower first and usually use chicken broth or stock because i always have it on hand.  it doesn't need much cream and i usually add gram marsala, cumin or curry for spice
We loved this soup.  I used half the cream because that is all I had.  It was creamy, flavorful, and filling.  I added ground dried thyme.
I used 6 cups of chicken broth instead of 8 cups of vegetable broth.  It was very tasty!
This was great! I added thyme and italian seasoning. Instead of cream I added some water to a can of cannelli beans and blended until smooth. This thickened the soup and added protein...perfect!

This soup is delicious, hearty and filling!! 
My sister (who does not like veggies by the way) fought me over the last bowl of this soup!

For my first time making soup (other than Top Ramen of course), this turned out fantastic. I halved the recipe to reduce to 6 servings, and based on the feedback of others, I made a few changes.  I roasted the cauliflower and garlic just enough to brown them before adding them to the pot. I also minced a shallot and sauteed it with the leeks, garlic, and cauliflower. For the broth, I used the full recommended amount of broth (4 cups for the halved recipe), but I used half vegetable and half chicken, both with lower than normal sodium. Once the broth was in, I also added one peeled and cubed potato.  Beyond the basic seasoning, I also added cayenne pepper, garlic powder, cumin, and a small amount of general Italian seasoning mix. The cumin went well with the roasted cauliflower and garlic, and while I may have added a wee bit too much cayenne, the soup was definitely not bland and I will make it again. It's also very filling, and a little bit of it goes a long way.

Excellent soup without adding in the merit of it also being low carb.  The thinner version works well as a chilled summer soup but by all means reduce liquid if you want something thicker.  I used half the browning fats & chicken stock/half vegie as it was what I had on hand.  Also used 1 cup evaporated WHOLE milk instead of heavy cream.  Easy to make, really easy to consume and a hit with my adult family.

I made this recipe today and now I wish I had doubled it. The taste was wonderful! My 4 year old and 11 year old tried some and loved it too (I didn't tell them it was cauliflower). Next time I make it I will set aside some chunks to add to the puree. Great recipe!

Followed directions with a few adjustments. I used two smaller heads of cauliflower that I roasted with olive oil and a few cloves of garlic. One head was blended up and the other added to the soup in smaller florets. I took the suggestions of a few other posters and added a touch of curry, paprika and garlic powder. Whoa .... So yummy!! I wish I had a dollop of sour cream for each bowl! A definite winner!!!
I loved and better yet, my kids loved it too. I roasted the cauliflower and some garlic as well.
A little salty with the broth...dont add salt. Used 2% milk istead of cream and it turned out just fine.
This is a simple, healthy go-to during cold months that my family loves. I don't use the cream - you simply don't need it.

Followed the recipe as is except that I added a little nutmeg and cornstarch. Needed a little pizzazz and some thickening. It was fabulous - the whole family loved it and the kids asked for it the next two nights!
A favorite at our house.
Really enjoyed the light taste of this, although I wish it had a little more seasoning.  Thanks to this recipe, though, I know use leeks much more often.  Delicious soup, and healthy too!

Awesome soup! I made a couple of changes.  I only used 4 cups of chicken stock (All I had) It was a think soup and more filling. It was even better the next day and the yogurt in it holds up to reheating without curdling.  Yummy!
I've made this twice now, it is so easy and delicious.  And it freezes well since there are no potatoes (which I find go mushy or grainy if frozen).   No changes to recommend.

This is a VERY delicious soup - especially for my husband who refuses to eat most vegetables. I varied the recipe slightly to make it healthier & because I didn't have vegetable stock. 

1) I used 6 cups of chicken stock and one can of cream of mushroom mixed with one can of water = 8 cups of stock. 

2) I also used Olivio Light for the butter. 

3) Instead of using heavy cream, I looked up substitutes and ended up using 1 cup of plain greek nonfat yogurt. You need to heat the yogurt up in a small pan on low heat until its hot and then whisk it into the soup to add creaminess. 

Each of these substitutions worked perfectly!!!
This was my first ever time making soup and it was amazing !!

This soup is a great light dinner, if it's for 1 or 2 people, there's plenty of leftovers to take to work for lunch! Low-carb, low-calorie, can be low fat depending on your use of heavy cream. I've made this twice, and I've made a few enhancements I think bring more flavor without adding anything unhealthy: -Roast the cauliflower in the oven - set the broiler to 500, break cauliflower into florets and place on baking sheet; spray with cooking spray and place on 2nd rack from the top. Roast until tips have a nice amount of browning (not burning!) and it's soft (doesn't need to be tender - it will finish cooking in the soup). Roasting enhances the final color of the soup as well. -Roast a thickly sliced shallot with the cauliflower, and add to the soup. -Add a yellow (can use sweet) onion to the pot when sauteeing leeks. -Saute some spices with the leeks/onions - I added fresh ground pepper, ground red pepper, and garam masala (an indian spice) for a bit of smokiness. Experiment! This soup BEGS for spices! -Try half&half or lowfat sour cream spooned over each serving. Tastes just as good. -Garnish each bowl with some thinly sliced chives and a thin drizzle of olive oil.  In all, a good soup, and my first time working with leeks - but use it as the foundation of introducing some spices or fresh herbs you particularly like - it's a little under-seasoned as-is.

This soup was absolutely delicious! I'm transitioning to a vegan diet, so I sauteed the vegetables in coconut oil and added coconut cream to the soup at the end instead of heavy cream. I served this at my Christmas dinner and it was a huge success! I'll definitely be making this recipe again!
Awesome! Easy to make and tasty.
This soup was great!  I am pre-diabetic & always looking for low carb recipes that have taste to them.  Very easy to make!
Easy to make and very tasty , I made it twice , once as is then again with less leeks and more cauliflower , both ways are good but I prefer less leeks. Really great recipe.

I omitted the butter.  Added chilli flakes. It was delicious!
This is so good!  My whole family loves it!

This was a hit! I did include the heavy cream. And it was delish!

Very good, and easy too! I did not saute my veggies, instead i made a rue with the butter and 3 tablespoons flour then poured in my chicken stock and just let the veggies cook a little longer. Rosemary is key here. Also I used pork stock from some ribs I grilled.

Wow, what great flavor for us low carb people! I agree with Hollyfae...this isn't potato soup, it has way more flavor!
I also cut broth back and added a bit more cream, yummy!!!
Love this recipe.  I had to make minor alternatives due to missing some items in the kitchen.  I've listed the changes below:

Pretty delicious! My only reservation is the salt - it was definitely over the top for me. Next time, in addition to cutting down the broth from 8 to 5 cups, I'll be sub-ing in some water for part of it. Also, I left out the cream - there's no need for it. Honest!
