I must say, this tasted better second day than it did when I did the spoon test immediately after making (as I said, just made for me...so put in the fridge after finishing for lunches)!  Looking forward to a few bowls leftover!

roasted the garlic and cauliflower w MONTREAL STK SEASONING, as i do w all my roasted veg + evoo for 10 mins at 400. used 1/2 large white onion (on hand) and 2 leeks w "fake butter." boiled w 6 cups mixed veg/chkn bullion. tasted after simmering and thought it was yum! continued on w greek yogurt instead of cream and finished product was amazing!!! had a bunch of other spices ready to add but didnt need them. love eating something great that is healthy;)
I followed the recipe, except I substituted low-fat sour cream for the heavy cream. It was delicious! I will definitely be making this again.

Made according to recipe except that I roasted the cauliflower.

Delicious as is.

I'm only rating this a 3* only because I think it either needs more cauliflower or less broth as it's really thin.  I think if it was a little thicker it would be a 4*. Next time I think I'm going to add carrots and use more cauliflower.
I made this without the cream and my family LOVED it!!! I used a bag of frozen cauliflower and it was great!
This soup was fantastic! I did however use half the amount of vegetable broth because I wanted a thick soup and it turn out great! Also used just a splash of cream.

I love potato and leek soup but have been low carbing it lately so this is a great alternative!  It's also nice because you can customize it to your own tastes and thickness of the soup.  It is a great tasting and comforting soup.
This is the second time I made this. I love it! Its so easy to make. The great thing about this recipe, I can start it early in the day and serve it when I am ready. I can't wait to do it again!!
I didn't have any watery issues with the amount recommended.  I used chicken stock instead of vegetable.  This was really good, but a bit bland so I just threw on some cumin and was good to go!
I made this several months ago, but I remember it was okay. I didn't use cream though. It might be good with it. Sorry if this doesn't help much.

Flavor was very good, soup was thin so next time I may add some flour to thicken it up and leave some chunks in it.  I also used chicken broth instead since I'm not a huge fan of veggie broth.  All in all a good, healthy recipe.

My first time using leeks and well worth the time.  I used approximately 6 cups of chicken broth and thickened slightly with flour instead of adding cream at the end.  The ideas submitted by everyone to enhance the flavor and heartiness will definitely be experimented with the next time.  I, however added finely chopped grilled chicken for a protein.
Creamy and delicious even without the cream.  Totally fooled the kids!!!

This soup is delicious! I'm on a low carb diet and this is just what the doctor ordered. I took the advice of some other reviewers and roasted the cauliflower with garlic and olive oil. I added extra garlic because I love garlic and reduced the vegetable broth to 7 cups. I also added the cream. Yum! Thank you :)

Loved the recipe, especially using chicken stock.  When using the chick stock I also added 1/2 tspn of dried Tarragon.  Gave the soup a wonderful aroma.  Once tried with some finely shredded Parmesan - that worked well too.
Love this... So easy to make and very delicious

I followed other reviews suggestions and only did 6 cups of broth, but next time I will use 4. I  added a lot of garlic and other spices to make it more flavorful. Otherwise it's a little bland. But a good soup for a cold winter night.

I am on a lowfat/lowcarb diet so I made the following alterations and it was super healthy and DELICIOUS!

-no butter
-no heavy cream
-just enough olive oil to coat bottom of the pan before adding in veggies
-added dried oregano & red pepper flakes & 1 extra clove of garlic
-used 5  cups (not 8) of low sodium chicken broth instead of veg broth
-roasted the cauliflower first in the oven (sprayed it with PAM so it didnt stick to baking sheet.

I found that all these changes made the soup thicker, creamier & quite flavorful with a bit of kick. Without the cream, butter & oil it has little to no fat.

Wow. This was soooo good! I made this for my stepdad who had surgery & needed light nutrition. I added keilbasa for protein, but it's good on its own. Also, my husband was freaked out that there was so much cauliflower (meat & potatoes guy!), and he inhaled it. A+++++ in my book!

I had some leeks I needed to use and some cauliflower, to this was perfect!  I added a bulb of fennel that I had also.  Cleaned out the veggie drawer.  The soup was fantastic, and I did not even add any cream.  It was delicious and had such a smooth creamy texture without adding it!
very tasty for a blended soup.
Used chicken broth added onion and a small potato
Very tasty!

I had my doubts about this one, but it turned out delicious!  I didn't see the comments about using less broth beforehand and I would use about a cup and a half or so less next time.  DO NOT ADD the cream- it is NOT needed!  I made half for my vegan family members without and it was fantastic, then added some cream to the second half, and it wasn't as good.  I also added a can of white beans for extra heartiness, I recommend that as well!

EXCELLENT soup!  I adjusted the following ingredients: 6 cups of chicken broth, two leeks, one yellow onion, and four cloves of garlic.  I added just a light sprinkling of paprika at the end.  No need to add any cream.  My husband said it was restaurant quality.  Plus, it was a cinch to make.  I'll double the recipe next time.

This soup blew me away! It has sooooo much flavor and is really really creamy w/ or w/out the milk! Yum Yum YUM! Can't wait to make again. I think I will chop up some ham next time, mmmm can't wait =)

I cooked, browned the leeks and cauliflower first. Deglazed with some wine. I did not use the cream. I did not put in the blender, just mashed the cauliflower with a fork. Added some cumin and all done! Yum
Delicious!!  Surprised I liked it so much!
We liked it!  Something different.  Only had chicken stock and used 6 cups of that.  Did not have any cream, but didn't need it.  Tasted good with some shredded cheese in it.  Would make again.

Wow, never thought I would be this excited about cauliflower soup.  I substituted the leeks with an onion and sprinkled in a little liquid smoke with a can of white beans for thickness and protein and used 4 cups of chicken broth.  Yummo. I'm full on just two small bowls. EASY to make, great and guilt free!  Thanks for the recipe!

I had lots of leeks in the house that I had to get rid of before they went bad.  This low carb recipe is a winner.  Many commenters said it was too watery so I took advice of others and used only 7 cups of broth (I used chicken).  It turned out thick.  You might want to even try it with only 6 cups of broth and add more broth at the end to get the consistency that you want.  Definitely use that cream!!!  Thanks submitter.

Have made this twice now (only recently discovered it) and the only changes I made were to use just 6 cups of broth, as many other reviewers noted, and I used chicken broth instead of vegetable (just personal preference). With the cream being optional, I used 1/2 cup cream in the first batch, but my vote is to not use it at all. Delicious!!

So delicious!   I omitted the butter and cream, and used plain nonfat greek yogurt instead - and it was fantastic, and guilt free!   Gave it the creamy texture without the added fat and calories of butter and cream.  So, so good.

This is a terrific recipe, I did however add paprika and cayenne pepper and I used fat free half n half. I also added 1/2 can of navy beans to it to add protein, since I often just eat soup for a meal with bread. A good rule of thumb for the liquid measurement, since every head of cauliflower is different, is to use just enough to cover the vegetables. It won't be too waterey then.
Made as directed by the recipe. I through some fresh spinach in to steam towards the end of cooking cauliflower though!  YUMMY!

SO easy and delicious!  Had a few changes due to what I had on hand.  Only used half head of cauliflower and didnt have broth so I poured about 5 cups of water with 5 small chicken bouillon cubes.  I did not add cream at the end and it did not need it at all.
Used a can of evaporated milk instead of cream and chicken broth instead of vegetable broth.  Even better the next day!

I made this soup today and found it to be quite delicious! I had only two leeks but when combined with the cauliflower and sautéed, the scent was really good.  When I finished the cooking and used my immersion blender and added the cream, it was just fabulous -- much better than I would have expected.  I didn't add any salt or pepper because I thought it was perfect just like it was.  I will definitely be making this one again and again!  Thank you, DRUMNWRITE, for sharing this delicious recipe.
Very good! I just had this for lunch and is very satisfying. Thanks for posting it!

Not bad!  To save cooking time, I cut up my cauliflower & leeks & pulsed them in the blender a few times before cooking.  Some of the veggies came out of the blender very finely chopped, while others were larger & more chunky.  I added extra garlic, & will definitely make this again!
I made it using chicken broth, and both my husband and i thought it was wonderful.
loved it!
As is I would give this 4 stars. I followed the advice of others and added Curry Powder and Paprika that really made a big difference.
LOVED this! Adding white wine and lemon is a must. I followed the advice of someone else and also pureed a can of cannellini beans to thicken it up. Absolutely delicious! And so so good for you!
I didn't use the cream and this soup was the best! My husband was skeptical of the leeks but he said this was the best soup I've made.
I've made this soup a few times a love it, my husband does too. I use milk or half & half instead of the cream and it's still great:)
I used 1 liter of chicken soup stalk, 1 liter of coconut milk, no cream. The rest of the recipe I left the same. I really love this soup! :)
I used white onions because I didn't have leeks or shallots on hand and this soup turned out great.

Just made this soup for the first time tonight and it was fabulous!  I did as others suggested and broiled the cauliflower & garlic with olive oil , salt & pepper until slightly golden.  I only used 5 cups of broth and boiled everything for only 20 minutes.  I did use the heavy cream in the end and I think this what put it over the top-delicious!

This is my favorite fall soup!  I make it exactly as the recipe calls for, but I don't add the cream.  It's a very forgiving recipe and super easy to make.  Sometimes my carnivorous husband likes to sprinkle bacon crumbles on the top, but I prefer mine with a little extra pepper.

I thought this was excellent.  I made it exactly as written..except I overlooked that garlic was on the list.  It looked very bland and I was thinking rapidly about what I was going to have to do to give it flavor.  I added salt and pepper and wow, yummy stuff!  I'm not sure why some found theirs watery unless they used small leeks or a small cauliflower.  The consistency was just right.  I used only 1/3 cup heavy cream (it's all I had on hand) and it was just enough creaminess.  I'd almost be afraid to use more.  Looking forward to the flavors tmw as others have said it only gets better.  It even had a buttery flavor from the saute step.  I may sprinkle some of the suggestions made by others in a couple servings to try that sound like they might add even more character:  curry, wine, bacon.  I'll be making this a lot.  Thank you for a wonderful easy and tasty low carb recipe.
This soup is simply amazing!  It has a warm comforting flavor and perfect for a low carb diet

I added a can of great northern beans, and mixed a little cornstarch into about 1/2 cup of 1% milk.  Added a little cayenne for a bit of a kick, and wow!  This soup was not only way better than I expected it to be, it was awesome!  Will definitely make again.  Thanks :)
Loved it.  I made it in a Le Creuset and this made it so nice and easy

I only used two ginormous leeks and organic chicken broth because that was what I had on hand. I sauteed two chopped zucchini with the garlic and leeks because I had to use them or lose them. I only pureed the cauliflower and chicken broth which meant I had to cook them seperate in another pot. It didn't take 45 minutes, more like 15. I gave it a taste without the milk and I thought it didn't need it, just a little more spice (onion powder, garlic powder, red pepper flake, rosemary). I threw in about a cup of chopped ham because I had some I needed to use. Really yummy. It totally makes you think you're having potato soup when you aren't. This is going to be a treat for me this week. Thank you for sharing! EDITED: And yes, this soup is even better the next day. It's totally like potato soup. It's fauxtato soup!

I love this soup.  I wasn't able to find leeks so I used half an onion.   I ended up adding a few carrots just because I had them in the house and   instead of heavy cream, I used 1/2 and 1/2 and it turned out very rich and creamy. I'll be making this again.  It was so good that I will double the recipe next time.
This is terrific! I used less broth and skipped the cream. I also added some herbs. I am on a strict low carb diet and thought this was even better than potato-leek soup. Thanks for a great recipe!

I agree that 8 cups of broth is too much - I prefer a thicker soup.  I also cut back on the fat by only using the olive oil, and instead of cream I blended in a package of silken tofu for texture and protein.  I also roasted the veggies for 30 minutes to add some depth of flavor.

This was very, very good!  I followed the recipe with the exception of using low sodium chicken broth as that is what I had on hand.  I also used the immersion blender and cream at the end.  Next time I will reduce the broth as the soup was pretty thin.  Thanks for sharing the recipe.

Great recipe. I must admit that while reading this recipe I had some doubts, but the finished product put them to rest. I took the advice of earlier reviewers and cut back the (chicken) broth to about 6 cups and thickened slightly with flour. I also reserved some of the cooked vegetables before using hand mixer and added them again after mixing. The whole family liked this, even my 12 year old,  who doesn't like cauliflower (we told him it was potato soup). This one's a keeper!
This soup was pretty good, husband didn't like it so next time I will 1/2 it.
This was quite good!  I used olive oil instead of butter to saute the veggies.  I didn't bother with the heavy cream, as once it was pureed it was quite thick and creamy by itself!
Delicious!!! Used only 6 cups of broth and added 2 Tbls cornstarch. Did not add heavy cream. Supper easy!! This has been added to my list of staple soups to have on hand :)

I made a half a recipe and was pleasantly surprised at how much flavor this soup had for being low carb and low calorie.  My soup turned out more brownish in color than the photos, almost looking like butternut squash soup.   The veggies were pretty brown after sauteeing for 10 minutes, already starting to caramelize and sweeten.  I used Kitchen Basics Vegetable Stock (only brand I use for boxed broths and stocks) which is deeper in color and richer in flavor than many others.  I think those two things made the appearance a little different than what you'd expect from cauliflower and leeks.  I did add just a little bit of cream but also added some FF plain yogurt, as well, which I think enhanced the flavor.   Thanks DRUMNWRITE , this is a keeper.

I didn't have vegetable stock, so I used chicken, and only 4 cups which just covered the vegetables.  Added whipping cream at the end....Delish!  My husband loved it and he hates cauliflower!  He didn't know that was one of the ingredients.

oh ...my...goodness.  I made this soup tonight exactly as it tells me here in the recipie and it is absolutely delicious.  Talk about a low carb, creamy treat!   I am thrilled to add this to my rotation! Thank you!

oh! just a thought- I cooked up some bacon extra crunchy and coarse chopped it as a garnish for the top. It made us feel like we were really, really cheating! YUM!

One word..Yummm!  Have to admit tweaking, but the base is great. I used chicken broth and reduced it to six cups, added a bit more garlic, one small hot chili pepper and one tsp curry paste. If you brown the veggies in the butter and oil before adding the broth, it will have a nice nutty, buttery taste. Once mixture was blended, I found it creamy enough without having to add the cream saving a few calories. Will definitely be making again, especially with winter around the corner!
Delicious!  I used 6 cups of the chicken broth I had on hand instead of 8 of veggie broth - perfect!

I ALWAYS modify recipes. I was looking for lo carb/sodium soup -- store bought is just way too high. I didn't notice that I using instructions for 12 servings-so I modified it--a lot of which was for the 6 servings directions. I added whole mushrooms, a stalk of celery and slices of onion roughly cut. For the broth I used only 1 heavily salted pkg of Goya chicken bouillon which is perfect for 4 cups of water which I prepared in the micro while the veggies were cooking.  I added the broth & cooked it for a 1/2 hr - which was too long ... I like a little crunch & next time (tomorrow?) I will cut this down to abt 15-20 mins.  I then added Cream of Mushroom soup with abt 3T of cornstarch.  Also mixed in few shakes of curry, pepper, mixed seasoning, along w abt 2 caps of cooking sherry. VERRRRY GOOD.

I am going to give this 4 stars because I couldn't imagine it being very good as written. 8 C. of broth just didnt seem right - I used HALF - 4 C. and just a tad of cream (1/4C?) and this was thick and filling. Overall, a good low carb option and I will make again.

This was a delicious soup idea though I altered the recipe a bit. I did not use butter or cream, but I did include a few shallots because I had them on hand. I made two versions: one with cumin and a touch of curry powder for a truly warming soup inside, and one with rosemary, time a basil for a savory soup. Both delish!

I just made this soup.  I reduced the broth to 6 cups, only had two leeks but they were huge, and did not add the cream.  I am on a very strict eating plan and can't have any salt or dairy, and nothing tastes good anymore.  But this soup was amazing!  I can only imagine that with the addition of salt and the cream it would be even more outstanding.  Thanks so much for the recipe!

We had this for dinner and although no one really liked it, everyone consumed their portion.  I used 7 cups of vegetable broth and thought that was too much, 6 would have been better.  That said, the vegetable broth is the main flavor, so make sure you really like the vegetable broth you use.  For our tastes, chicken broth would have been much better.  I used 3 leeks and could barely taste them as the vegetable broth and cauliflower really overwhelmed the leeks and garlic.   Although this was interesting to try, I doubt we will have this again.
Very yummy and healthy tasting! Definitely make again.

Great recipie.  I added coconut milk instead of cream and coconut oil instead of butter to make this a dairy free recipe.  Also added a bit more garlic! Delicious - my 11 year old daughter LOVES this soup!
I made this last night and it was pretty tasty. It was a little sweeter than I'd anticipated but otherwise it was very tasty. The only thing that was missing was a nice baguette!
No one could guess what was in it but EVERYONE loved it!!!

I just made this for the second time today! First time I didn't have any heavy cream and I blended it too long so it came out without any chunks. But the flavor was delicious and I knew the next time which is today I'd come more prepared. I added another whole cauliflower to thicken it up! You can't use too much of anything so I just throw as much flavor as I can when it comes to the leeks and garlic. It's good with fresh grate parm on top.
This is fast, easy and yummy! I like to top it off with some fresh ground nutmeg. You can float shredded cheese in it too.
I substituted skim milk for the heavy cream and it turned out great!

I have never cooked with leeks before, but was looking for a low carb soup.  This was awesome!
Because I am not vegetarian, I added leftover ham ( about 1 1/2 cups cubed) and can not believe how well it went together!   Thank you for a great recipe!

I've been on a low-carb diet for a few weeks and really felt the need for a good vegtable dish. This really hit the spot. I followed the directions to the T and it came out great. I highly recommend it.

This was a very good soup, I didn't modify it at all. Creamy and light. Mine was not a nice "white" color but that may have been because I made my own vegetable broth. I think my homemade vegetable broth added a different dimension to the soup, but really, I think it'd be hard to miss with this one. Good flavor and easy to make while you're preparing an entree. If you find that the soup is too watery, just cook it down a bit until the water has evaporated. This also improves the flavor.
I make this all the time. I usually leave out the heavy cream and just top with some sour cream and shredded cheese. Excellent, easy , healthy and kids love it.

I was eager to try this after so many people gave it such high scores.  I followed to recipe to the "t."  It didn't look at all like the picture (which isn't necessarily that big of a deal).  It had an average, subtle taste, but it wasn't absolutely delicious.  WORST OF ALL it was a full week until the cauliflower (quite similar to broccoli) smell diminished.  I had all the windows in my house open for an afternoon, had the fans running, sprayed Febreeze, lit candles, and used 6 plug-in air fresheners and it still took a week to subside. I liked it somewhat, it didn't taste bad; but the after-smell totally made it not worth it.
Delicious. I roasted my cauliflower. I think it was better before the cream though but it is still delicious.
This soup is great! I use the Campbell's low sodium chicken stock and also add a handful of lowfat cheddar cheese after pureeing the veggies and it tastes wonderful.

Fantastic flavor! I used only what I had on hand: 1/2 Cauliflower head, 2 cups Chicken Broth & 1 cup water, 4 garlic cloves, 2 Leeks, and 1 Tablespoon Low fat Evaporated Milk powder (creamier & no fat).  Thank you so much for this recipe. Happy cooking everyone.

Turned out pretty well and was a good recipe to use up a bunch of cauliflower I had. I use extra garlic and put in whole milk (instead of cream). I thickened it a bit with cornstarch. I also added two tiny potatoes that I had leftover.
This is pretty good stuff!  Although it says you can blend with a hand mixer, it doesn't work well. I added beans like one reviewer suggested. Very versatile recipe. Thanks for sharing!

I've never made even potato leek soup, but this soup is delicious! For ease, I used frozen "riced cauliflower" which made prep a lot faster! I lowered the amount of broth to 6 cups as other suggested. I sautéed half an onion with the leeks. I also added a cup of quinoa for a thicker consistency. And I used whole milk instead of cream. It's been a hit!
YUM! As suggested, I roasted the cauliflower and added a bit of onion. As an afterthough, I sauteed and added turkey kielbasa for a heartier soup. AMAZING, got rave reviews!
Will make again. Wonderful blend of flavor. Made it exactly as the recipe. I hope it freezes well.

I made the soup with just one leek, a full head of cauliflower and added a half head of cabbage.  Did not use  spices or milk, but came out good.  I use this as a health food and it helps to maintain or loss weight too.
Made this it was great. Actually started a recipe box because of this soup.  My husband really enjoyed it.

Made this for the first time yesterday.  What a great base soup recipe that you could tweak in so many ways.  Very rich tasting - I did not use any cream at all.  I did make some substitutions and additions - did not have vegetable broth, so used half chicken broth and half mushroom broth.  After tasting, I felt it needed some perking up and added some cumin, chili powder, smoked paprika and nutmeg.  You could really play with the seasoning in this recipe.  A great way to eat your veggies!

It came together very easily.  But, it was a big disappointment for me.  I took the advise from others and used 6 cups of vegetable stock I had made.  It was still way too thin.  Maybe I did something wrong, I don't know.

Delicious!  I'm on a 3-day green smoothie "cleanse" - ? not really sure it's a cleanse though, and am so sick of green smoothies.  
I made this recipe to get something more savory, with the following adjustments to keep it super low-carb / low-fat:
- no oil, no butter.  Just steamed the cauliflower and leeks in a bamboo steamer until ready
- no cream
- 3 c. veg broth
- forgot the garlic!  doh!
- added salt, pepper, cayenne
- after blending, added finely chopped parsley on top
Thanks!  Yummy!
This is a lovely soup that is very simple to make. I added original unsweetened almond milk in the place of cream and it was great. Will definitely make this again!
Delicious! Definitely roast the cauliflower first, doing so adds lots of flavour. This soup is even tastier the next day

Excellent!  Smooth, creamy and delicious!  I had my 15 year old God-daughter over, and she was a little reluctant to try this soup that had strange vegetables.  Once she did, she loved it and so did I!  It was amazing!  I will be making this one again!  It was the perfect soup on a chilly autumn evening.  Superb!

So. This was good-ish.

At my house: let's eat more healthy.

Also at my house: let's eat less meat and less carbs.

After making this soup, at my house: can you add some Italian Sausage?

Good soup. It is what you think it will be: cauliflower soup with leek.

One of our favorites. I reduce the amount of broth to 5 or 6 cups (we use chicken broth), add roasted garlic and a dash of white wine, throw in some Parmesan cheese before blending, and garnish with curry spice. It never lets us down!!

update: this is extremely easy with an immersion blender.  after making this soup many times, i did try to roast the cauliflower and garlic beforehand.  honestly it did nothing to enhance the flavor - the recipe is perfect as is!  subbed half and half for the heavy cream, otherwise followed exactly....yummy!  somehow i think bacon can only improve on the dish

I also suggest using less stock - this makes the soup creamier. I used just enough to barely cover the vegetables in the pot. I also did not include the butter to make it healthier, and I didn't miss it. I could not believe how delicious this soup was. Love that it is healthy and utilizes winter veggies that are in season right now. Potato soup is a guilty pleasure - this is a no-guilt, just-as-tasty and super healthy substitute.
This was the first soup I ever made and it is wonderful! Healthy, freezable... great comfort soup.

Low Calorie Cauliflower Leek Apple Soup:
Saute in medium saucepan - 
1 sliced leek
1 peeled diced small Granny Smith apple
some frozen cauliflower 
a few baby carrots
grated ginger 
diced garlic
black pepper
paprika
water to cover
a teaspoon or so of Better than Bouillon Organic Vegetable broth, which comes in a jar
Cook until tender, then use immersible blender
Yummy!  I served this with a dollop of sour cream, and a dash of Worcestershire, really good!

I roasted the cauliflower first. While it was roasting, I sauteed the leeks in the butter. I also threw in about 5 whole roasted garlic cloves that were left over rather than chopeed fresh. Finally, I used half chicken/half vegetable brother and tossed in some skim milk rather than cream at the end. A wonderful soup I'm definitely making again!
Great soup, and no carbs!

This was good. I was cooking for a vegan friend so I added tofu to thicken it and corn for more flavor. I guess that makes it higher in carbs, but it was delish. Next time I'll probably add kale as well.

I was rather unimpressed, although perhaps the positive reviews inflated my expectations.  I used only 1/2 a cup of cream; that almost made it less appetizing, surprisingly.  I think this recipe lacks spices and personality.

This recipe was outstanding! I followed the review of Matthew F from 2009 and added Garam Masala, the Indian spice, crushed red pepper too. I also broiled my cauliflower with a chopped shallot, and added a sweet onion to the leek mixture. With the salt, pepper, crushed pepper and garam masala, it was very flavorful and I possibly didn't need the cream, but....I ended up adding 1/3 to 1/2 a cup of Light cream and it definitely enhanced the end result. I even threw a few homemade croutons on top for garnish and still kept it low-carb. Fabulous recipe!
My husband and I found this a great low carb option to potato soup... somewhat bland but adding enough salt/pepper was a great help!!!  Def. a repeat!!!

Roasted the cauliflower, added 1 large shallot, a can of Great Northern White Beans, and about a cup less broth.  Tasted it before I added the half and half.  The cream really knocked it out of the park!!  Oh, and I also added a large teaspoon each of rosemary and thyme.  Will make again and again!!!

We are making this soup once a week now. My picky husband says it tastes like baked potato soup...and he's lost 15 pounds this month eating this for lunch most days.  I did substitue half and half for the cream and added 1/4 cup of shredded carrots and some cayenne pepper for zip.  Love it!
Good base recipe. I tweeked it. Added one potato, a tablespoon curry, five slices of bacon, and 1/2 cup cream. Blended lightly. Excellent. Well, no. Can't have it all. It is no longer low carb.
I actually put 5 leeks because it was going to be a little too watery and added some spices (garlic powder, basil) and it turned out good.  I would re-do again.

This recipe is yummy! I did modify according to some other posts - i added a little curry paste (i've done it both ways and it's delish either way) and I substituted the cream with greek yogurt. It freezes great too! AND tonight instead of giving them the same soup AGAIN I served it over white rice with some ground turkey (salt,pepper,chile powder, curry paste, cumin and ground ginger)and it was amazing!

So easy. So yummy.
I blended mine in the blender at the end, and peppered each bowl. This is tasty soup. Filling, slightly sweet and enjoyable with whole grain garlic toast.

A beautiful recipe...     As advised in the reviews I only used 6 cups of broth, this was the perfect amount.  I used extra leeks as I wanted to use them up.  And I didn't add salt as it was lovely without (and I usually add salt to EVERYTHING!)  I also added the cup of cream.  My boyfriend loved this soup so much he asked me for a straw so that he could eat it faster.  Easy to make and much faster than pumpkin soup as no peeling involved. Excellant! Thanks!!
Delicious...
So yummy!!  Just used a little less broth (6 cups vs. 8), and did use the cream.  I also used Better Than Bullion (chicken) for the "broth".  Turned out really amazing!

This is a staple in my house.  It's so easy, so delicious, and I haven't met anyone yet who doesn't love it.  I use less broth so it's a little thicker, more like 6 cups, and you only need light cream not heavy.  Wonderful.  If you want to shave some cheddar cheese on top before serving you can, but it doesn't need it!

I can't believe this is healthy ... to die for.  Only modification: We used half chicken stock, half vegetable stock because that's what we had available.  Used all 8 cups and we ground pepper into it.  New favourite!!!!!!!!!!!
An easy soup that will fill you up while helping you maintain your waistline.  I did add one hot pepper to the indredients which gave the soup a nice zip.
Was okay.  It needs something to add a bit more flavor.  Will probably serve the rest with crumbled bacon on top.
Delicious and healthy! Just made this today. Only used chicken bouillon since it was what I had. I definately will make it again. Thanks for sharing.

I really got a very good response from making this soup.  I did tweak it just a little bit by adding 1/8 of a purple onion and 1/8 of a white onion finely diced and i used this BEAUTIFUL purple cauliflower.  I added white pepper and 1/2 the salt in the cooking process.  I also forgot to cover it so i just added some more water.  Really tasty and really beautiful!

Will make this again and again!  My husband loved it and my Dad said he could eat it everyday!!  I used chicken broth instead of vegetable broth.  I did add a bit more salt, added some cayenne and garlic powder and swapped out the heavy cream for half & half.  It was delish!
I love home made soups   I got into it when I went to the Dominican Republic. Every day they had fresh soups. This one is absolutely fantastic  it is delicious. Thanks

This is a great soup. Everyone loved it. Just a couple of things I did differently from the recipe:  used chicken bouillion, left the vegetables chopped - did not blend them.

It's a favorite that will be made repeatedly.
Thanks for sharing.

What a wonderful, tasty soup, very easy to make and also good for you! I added a few garlic gloves, which I roasted off first to just enhance the flavour , and dropped the cream as it didn't really need it. Other than that, a simply good and easy recipe for a quick dinner or lunch.

WOW! This was absolutely delicious! I also used a half cauliflower and 6 cups of my homemade chicken bone broth and about 1/2 cup of cream. Superb flavor and creaminess. such a surprising velvity texture and taste! thank  you!
I loved this creamy soup.   Because I avoid dairy I substituted almond coconut milk for the heavy cream.

This is an ok, easy recipe.  I used chicken broth and fat free half and half.  No doubt it would have been better with cream but the old arteries can't take it.  Even though I mixed the soup with a hand mixer for a very long time and overcooked the vegetables the soup had a lot of texture and never truly became creamy.  Maybe my mixing skills are lacking.  To make the soup more enjoyable I added a dollop of sour cream and a sprinkling of feta cheese.

This soup is delicious. Better than potato leek in my opinion.
The only difference I used half and half that was all I had and it's great!

This is a five star with or without the heavy cream. I've made this recipe many times as written and then played with the ingredients as well. I recommend trying it as written. You won't be disappointed!
Wow!  This was great.  I followed recipe, except added a bit of sour cream for tang.  Very filling and satisfying.

I made this soup for dinner and followed the directions EXACTLY.  I did not substitute anything.  As is, this soup was AWESOME.  My husband loved it.  My 5 and 7 year old gobbled it up.  I'm definitely making this again.  Now I have leftovers for work tomorrow.  :)
I love this soup! I add crumbled bacon to it though.
Added a little curry powder, used fat free half&half instead of cream...really tasty, thanks!

Wonderful soup! My first time cooking with leeks! I don't usually make homemade soup and I found this to be very easy and delicious.  The only change I made was to use fat free half n half instead of the heavy cream but I tasted it before adding the half n half and it would have tasted just fine without it.  Thanks for the recipe.  I will definitely make this again.
An excellent, easy-to-make tasty soup. While the cream may be optional, it helps round it out.

This soup is incredible.  Thanks to the other reviewers, I made a couple modifications.  I cut the recipe in half using 3 3/4 cups vegetable broth AND half a can of cannellini beans.  After I blended the soup, there was no need for the cream.  My 9-year old is devouring a bowl now...She LOVES it! I made some changes, I only pureed half of the soup, left pieces of cauliflower & leeks and added 1/4 cup of white wine. Gave it a really nice flavour
Mmmm... so light but delicious.  Will definitely make again!

Tasty! Not our absolute favorite soup, but good lo-cal dinner. Served with chicken sausage and sourdough. Roasted the cauliflower and a clove of garlic at 400 for 40, 50 respectively. Since the cauliflower was mostly cooked, I didn't boil it in the broth for long. We can definitely taste the roasted garlic!! Used only 6 c of broth and a dash of thyme at the end.

Excellent! Taste just like potato soup. I tried it because I'm low carbing it. I'm really ppleased with the flavor. I didn't have any veggie broth so I used chicken broth. I will make it again for sure!

This recipe was really easy.  I didn't have any vegetable broth in the house, so I used chicken stock and it came out great.  I also mixed a few teaspoons of cornstarch in with the cream before adding it at the end.  It thickened up nicely and had a great consistancy.
I REALLY like this. We didn't use butter, pepper or cream, and we used low sodium chicken broth instead of vegitable broth. We used less broth to make it thicker.
Loved, loved loved this soup. It was tasty and filling. Only alterations I made were to use 6 cups of stock instead of 8 and 1/2 cup of cream. It was the perfect amount of liquid.
My kids who have never like a soup (and I have tried many) like this one!

Exceptional just as written with a loaf of homemade sourdough and a glass of french chardonnay.

Wonderful flavor that is rich and smooth. I added a couple tablespoons of dry milk solids instead of cream. And shredded spinach. Next time I may add mushrooms. But the base soup recipe is excellent if you need something light and nutritious.

Maybe I added a few more carbs, but like soup thick as it is more satisfying for my family.  Only used 6 C. broth, 2 cans of rinsed navy beans and two handfuls of Gluten Free Croutons to simmer. My son eats cheese so he melted a little grated cheddar cheese over the top.  Yum.
Love this soup! Freezes well!

This is a fabulous recipe that is healthy and EASY! I personally like a thicker soup so I add two heads of cauliflower instead of the one. I found this mellowed the flavor out a bit so next time I will also be adding six leeks instead of three because I enjoyed the intensity of the flavor with one cauliflower. Son and husband add bacon and cheese and it tastes just like baked potatoe soup! Love this, thank you so much for sharing.

OMG, this is delicious! Popatoes spike my blood sugar,  but i love popato leak soup. This is a simple and very delicious substitute.  I will be making this alot! Excellent soup!  Great flavor without the carbs of potatoes.  I used a smaller head of cauliflower and reduced the broth to prox. 5 cups and used 1/2 cup of half and half instead of heavy cream.

Very good.  I added three stalks of sauteed celery and used chicken broth instead of vegetable broth.  Tasted good even before the cream and I haven't added any seasonings yet.  I'm not a huge cauliflower fan but I had some leeks I needed to do something with from my Farm CSA, and this was great!  Since it's blended, I might even be able to get my three year old to try it!

Easy & delish!!!!!  Reduced stock to 6 cups and added well drained and rinsed cannelini beans.  The beans thickened the soup enough that I could easily have used 7 or 8 cups stock.  I also substituted non-fat greek (oikos) yogurt.  YUMMMY ;D  Thanks for sharing
loved it, used chicken broth instead. we have made this several times and have enjoyed it eacha nd every time. it is also a great crock pot recipe.

very refreshing drink, great for the summertime, or anytime.

The "old fashion" is a cocktail often ordered when waiting for one of those famous Midwest Friday Fish Frys.  I have been making Old Fashion mix for years.  Angostura Aromatic Bitters found in grocery or liquor stores.

1. The leisure suit is an old fashion.  The cocktail is called an "old fashionED."  

2.) This recipe incorporates two of the essential ingredients of an old fashioned--sugar and aromatic bitters.  However, to build on what another reviewer said, this mix is so simple it hardly seems worth the effort.  Just keep a little simple syrup and bitters on hand if that's your fancy.

For a variation, consider a mix that adds maraschino cherry juice and a little orange juice as well.  THAT particular concoction tends to pair best with a brandy old fashioned sweet, or a brandy old fashioned press, but can be just as tasty with the right whiskey or bourbon as well.

I love Old Fashions so I thought I would give this a whirl. I think it was way too heavy on the bitters so I would suggest cutting them down to suit your taste. That being said, I think making them from scratch is so easy I don't think I would make this again. Thanks for sharing!

this is the best recipe i've found for coffee liquor. i've made it several times now. it also makes great gifts, especially during the holidays.

Delicious!!!!  Following other reviewers I made a couple of changes.  Caramelized the white sugar (white sugar, water, and lemon juice) before adding apples and brown sugar.  I pureed the apples to make them more spreadable.  I didn't have enough granny smiths so I used a combination of granny smith, rome, and golden delicious (all great baking apples that retain their shape). I used the called for amount of pectin and increased the butter flavor (however it tasted just fine without it - so don't let this stop you from trying the recipe).  I also added some salt to cut down on the sweetness and because I like salted caramel.  Very very yummy.. It made 8 half pints.
Great recipe. Used Gala apples from our tree (can't wait until our Honeycrisp tree produces!) we did add 2 tablespoons of kosher salt - amazing.

I really loved the texture and the flavor (it tasted amazing on banana bread!). The only reason it didn't get a 5 star is because my husband and my father said they didn't like it because it was too much of a girly flavor - which they say about everything that is really sweet - so if you prefer a more mellow jam, this may not be the recipe for you.

Delicious with the apples we picked yesterday (Jonagold). It was quite sweet, I guess jam always is, so I added a bit of spice (cinnamon, cloves, and ginger) to add some depth. Also: I didn't have any butter flavoring, so I just stuck with the tablespoon of butter as above. I made 2 batches and only used one box of pectin in the second batch (the recipe calls for 1.5 boxes) -- turns out, one box works just fine.

I was looking for something a little different to do with apples, and came across this recipe. I made it yesterday & it was delicious!! My DH even put some over ice-cream. While I was processing them, I realized the instructions said to use 1 1/2 packages of 1.75 ounce pectin. I only saw the 1.75 ounces so I only used 1 package. However, the jam was still acceptable. A little soft, but that's the way we like our jam. I also should have chopped the apples smaller, so I used a stick blender briefly while it was cooking.

Absolutely wonderful! I had purchased some blemished/second picking apples to make applesauce and found I had many left over. I wanted to try something different and this sounded interesting. I'm so glad i tried it! I had read some of the other reviews and was concerned about the sweetness of the end product-especially since I didn't have tart Granny Smith apples. I went ahead and  used the required amount of sugar but I added 1 TB of lemon juice to balance it out. It's fantastic!
This turned out great!  I used half granny smith and half gala apples since my family doesn't love things that are really tart and it was super tasty!

Though it didn't really taste like caramel, this was a great alternative to the run of the mill apple jam. It has really been a hit in our house & has been used quite a bit on buttered English muffins. Thank you for this great recipe! :-)
Followed basic recipe using tart apples. Didn't have "caramel" flavor but I do like this jam.

This tastes heavenly! I was looking for ways to use up a lot of extra apples this year, and someone told me about this recipe. I also made a variation where I added in some rum when I stirred in the sugar.  Whichever way you do it, this recipe is sure to impress! Thanks for sharing it.

I was searching for a recipe for a black walnut bread roll like my grandmother used to make for the holidays. I found out what she made was actually a Walnut Poteca , when I discovered the recipe on here. I pared back the recipe to make a small amount since I had never done it before & it was a test. I still had a large amount of nut filling. It immediately reminded me of German Chocolate icing, which I looked up on Allrecipes & the only thing I had to do was add butter & cook to thicken my filling. It turned out very well, esp. Since I was using left overs. I would add some vanilla or coconut extract next time, but good recipe.
I like that I can use the egg whites and not the yolks since I have extra whites when I make certain pastries, I did still use the pecans because I don't like walnuts.
very nice, I did not have butter so used coconut oil, smelled heavenly!

I used a spice cake and butterscotch pudding combo and it was great , very moist but a bit heavy.. the sauce was amazing but way to sweet even for me.. I also used crushed walnut  and it was really good but I'd suggest cutting the recipe down by at least half as I have a ridiculous amount left over.. overall it was great

Chunky Italian Spaghetti Sauce Haiku: "This isn't 'chunky', would not cling to our noodles. Taste a '4', I guess." Maybe if it were tomato paste instead of tomato sauce, or stewed tomatoes instead of diced, it would've been more chunky, or if the recipe called for fresh chopped veggies such as onion, zucchini, mushroom, or dare I suggest, tomatoes, it would've been more chunky ... either way, this wasn't a chunky sauce BUT it was simple to make, and it tasted pretty good - ate ours w/ meatballs over spaghetti, but if I made it again it'd be drastically different and would no longer be this particular recipe.

Some reviews said it did not stick to the spaghetti so I left out 1 can of tomatoe sauce and added 1--  6 oz can of tomatoe paste.
Simmer  until reduced to your  desired thickness about 30 min.
P.S. I also added 1 can of sliced mushrooms.
Very rich and delicious. My husband enjoyed the meal. Used the recipe but added  a few other ingredients .

Just wanted a quick sauce with ingredients I had.  Always wondered how much garlic powder it would take for a good garlic flavor.  I made it pretty close to recipe.  Added 1 tblspn of onion powder, dash of red pepper and a splash of Worchester sauce.  l keep this close at hand.
Really simple, really easy and really delicious. Can't go wrong here. I used fresh basil and garlic though. Thanks Soulfood for your recipe.
Quick and easy! Made it in the time quoted. Added onion powder, ‘cause why not?

My new go-to sauce.  It is delicious and my husband and son loved it.  They loved the freshness of it and the chunky tomato bits.  The only thing I altered was using fresh basil and I sauted some vidalia onions to add.  Only because we are so onion crazy.  But this is really, really tasty, quick and easy.
quick and very flavorful....wouldn't change anything.

I used crushed tomatoes with basil in place of the diced tomatoes & the basil (it's what I had on hand) & I only added one can of tomato sauce as I prefer a thicker sauce.   I added homemade meatballs, simmered it about 30 minutes & it was delicious. My hubby & I both agreed it was the best spaghetti sauce I ever made & this is how I will make it from now on.   It wasn't chunky ...  
just thick, rich & delicious.  Thanks for sharing !!!

Made the recipe and used fresh basil, garlic, rosemary & parsley. Definitely wasn't what I would consider to be a chunky sauce but it had great flavor! I would follow another reviewer's suggestion of adding sliced mushrooms, chopped zucchini, etc next time to try and make it more chunky.

Very tasty! I used one 28oz can of crushed tomatoes, two 14.5oz petite diced tomatoes, and one 8oz can of tomato sauce and followed the rest of the recipe, except I added a little more of  the seasonings.  I substituted thyme for the basil, because I didn't have any, and I added about a tablespoon of cornstarch. I haven't made many homemade sauces, but this one  was the best one so far!
loved this,  i used yogurt instead of ice cream
Only thing I did different was use 1 cup coconut milk rather than 2 cups regular milk.  And I added five ice cubes.  OH SO YUMMYY!!!
this recipe would've tasted so much better without the bananna.

Extremely good and light. I tried it without ice-cream. My husband on the other hand prefers having it with a couple of spoons of plain yogurt - makes it bit thicker, than the milk-only version, but not as rich as ice-cream version. One of my favorites!

It's pretty good and healthy. And i hope Everybody in
my class would like it ( It is a project :)
I only used mango, this recipe was delicious!
Didn't use ice cream. Will use ice cream next time but it was magnificent.

Loved this - got to use an over-ripe mango and banana! Might need to strain the mango fibers. I like other's ideas to freeze the fruit first - or add some ice cubes - will try these variations next time!

I cut and froze my mango and banana the night before specifically for this smoothie. I used homemade frozen vanilla yogurt last night instead of ice cream and Truvia instead of sugar. Honestly, this had too much milk. I think it would have been much better had I cut the milk back by half, at least.
I left out the ice cream and nutmeg and changed the sugar for agave syrup and milk for almond milk, was lush!
I froze the banana and mango.
This is the best homemade milkshake I've ever had. Will defiantly recommend to my friends and make it again. Amazing recipe!!

This is just like its name...YUMMY!! :D I loved it and...I did use one whole mango (coz the it was a small mango) and 2 bananas (these were the small variety...alot more flavorful and very different from the normal bananas)....the only thing I skipped was sugar but that's coz I used a scoop of vanilla ice cream...this filled up 3 tall glasses....thanks for this recipe!
You can add a little bit of rose essence oil to it if you want to.

Hubs loves his breakfast drinks on weekends.  Whether you call them smoothies or milkshakes, whether they have yogurt or they don’t, no matter what fruit is added to them, he loves ‘em.  Me?  I really could take ‘em or leave ‘em, as I’ve never tasted one good enough to warrant all the calories and sugar, even if that sugar is just from the fruit.  Besides, after making them awhile, one began to taste pretty much the same as another anyway.  Not this time.  While I had plenty of berries on hand, both fresh and frozen, I was determined to find something different to try, and this was it.  Frozen mango came in handy, and because of that and the fact there was already quite a lot of milk in the drink, I chose not to add the optional ice cream.  I added the cinnamon but didn’t want to push it and take a chance with the nutmeg, so I left it out.  I handed this creamy, frothy milkshake to Hubs, then tried a little myself and thought, wow, this is awesome good!  Uniquely different and 5-stars for sure!  And even tho’ I didn’t expect Hubs would agree, he did!  So what was so different about this?  It wasn’t thick and gloppy, it was refreshingly light.  It wasn’t overly condensed with flavor, again refreshing.  It didn’t have the sour tang of yogurt. Most of all, it wasn’t your same old tired, berry smoothie.  If I had any criticism at all, it would be that I might have liked a little more mango, but that would just be overly picky.

This was really tasty. I left out the sugar since I used a bit of vanilla ice cream. Didn't use very much milk, but I like my smoothies/milkshakes really thick. 2 cups of milk would have made it really thin, IMO.

this is really good and refreshing, very fruity...i used a frozen banana and added about 5 ice cubes to make it thicker...anyways it was really sweet (so it doesnt need the extra sugar)and had that tang of mango...perfect for summer...
YUMMO! I also added some ice cubes and a little bit extra sugar and it was definitely worth it!! Thanks for the recipe!

This drink is kind of odd. It is like a mix between a milkshake, a smoothie, and a cold milk drink. I subbed the mango for peaches, just because I prefer it. I am not sure what the cinnamon or nutmeg did? I thought it left a weird after taste. I also couldn't understand how the ice cream, which is the main ingredient in a milk shake, was optional? I added a little more banana to get some more fruit in it and used Truvia for the sugar. The drink was room temperature, so I added 6 ice cubes for half the recipe. I also added a tad of vanilla extract for a little extra flavor. Not a shake I would make again, as it was missing that fruit flavor I get from smoothies, but it was something different to attempt anyway.
I tweaked it a bit by using instead... mango nectar,  evaporated milk and no sugar.  It was super delish!
I added a scoop of vanilla protein powder. You can't taste it, and it was a great after workout drink. Not too heavy. I would have liked to taste the mango more, but the mango I used wasn't the best.
This drink tastes just like something you'd get on the islands.  I used Dole Pineapple Orange Banana juice w/ Diet 7-Up.
Pretty tasty! You can't taste the rum at all. The pineapple juice gives it a distinct after-flavor.

Yummy - I put a little 
splash of grenadine in it.
This is an awesome drink. Super sweet and tropical!
Easy light flavor.  I will keep this one for a hot summers day.
Tasty and tropical! I halved the pineapple juice and added a splash of grenadine. Don't forget the little umbrellas!
Made this on our family beach vacation, did not care for it at all. Three people tried it and not one taker!! I think it was just too sweet for our taste.
low alcohol, but the "fizz" from the carbonated soda is a nice change for a drink.
Best drink ever!

Great Punch.  Made it for my niece's bridal shower last weekend and the guests loved it.  I touched it up with a bit of cranberry juice for color and made an ice block of pineapple and cranberry juice for the bowl.  Fill the container for freezing with 1/2 of one juice and when frozen fill the rest of the bowl with the other juice.
Sorry, too much like a bad bridal shower punch.  Much rather have bahama mama's.  Thanks anyhow.
Delish.  Used organic pineapple juice, the dash of grenadine is must add.

These were tasty and I would recommend using a clear glass because with my addition this drink looked great too.  I used 1 1/2 shots Captain Morgan, to only 2 shots pineapple juice.  Then I mixed and poured over ice.  I added the cup of lemon/lime soda, and poured that in the glass.  Finally, I added a dash of grenadine, which sinks to the bottom and comes up creating a sort of "sunset" look.  As a matter of fact, we're calling these "florida sunsets."  These had just the right amount of kick, but still went down smooth.
YUM!  Tastes like Hawaii.
This was great! Very refreshing!
yum.  this was excellent and went over with a bang at our bbq.  definitely add cherry juice or grenadine at bottom.  great summer coctail.  dont forget the umbrella!
We liked these drinks.
I didn't follow the recipe exactly, we just eyeballed the proportions.  We also added grenadine for color.  They were delicious!

While I agree with Tanya's sentiments, I only had heavy cream, no condensed milk...my problem wasn't with the taste (delicious), however; it was the grainy-ness.  Even after I strained the drink through a fine strainer, it still had a grainey texture.  I think whomever suggested whole spices might be right.

If you don't follow the recipe...then you are really rating a diferent recipe.  How is that helpfulto those interested in the rating for this one???  I followed the recipe and it actually turned out the way I think it was supposed to.  It was good if you like the spice.
good...its a nice change from regular hot chocolate

I just tried this tonight, and I thought it was just okay. I made it exactly as written, and it was fairly gritty, as other reviewers have already mentioned. I might make it again, and stir it a lot more, just to see if it improves any. It was, as advertised, pretty spicy, but since I'm not a big fan of nutmeg, it didn't wow me for that reason.

I probably shouldn't be rating this, just because I used regular whole milk chocolate milk and added the spices, but based on flavor, this was really good. The only thing I didn't like was that it was super grainy because of the cinnamon and nutmeg floating all around. Not good.

I appreciate the concept of this recipe, but with only a tiny bit of milk compared to the rest of the ingredients, it's really a dressed up hot chocolate.  We tried it hot, and didn't like the grainy texture.  I couldn't imagine how it would be cold. It was spicy, but the amount of spices (2 1/2 tsp of dry spices per serving) overpowered the hot chocolate mix and left a sludge in the bottom of the mug.  I'm sorry, but we wouldn't make this again.

I made this using regular milk instead of sweetened condensed and was conservative with the spices. It was extremely spicy and since the spices don't melt, VERY gritty. It was also bitter but perhaps that was because I didn't have the right milk on hand. My boyfriend and I took a few sips and had to dispose of the rest. If you make this, I'd suggest trying whole pieces of the spices so you can take them out after steeping in water or trying to strain them out. I, however, won't be adding this to my recipe box at home.
I didn't add the sweetened condensed milk (we were out). Way too much nutmeg. I  I added at least a cup of actual chocolate milk and it was drinkable, but still super bitter.

This is very good, but something is missing with the directions. The oven temperature should be adjusted to about 350° maximum of 375° after the eggplant has cooked the first time. Also, if it's meant to be in the oven for an hour at least cover it with foil so the cheese doesn't burn.
Use in fresh in soups, sautès, and even on sandwiches. Add to any dish where you want some added flavor. Also,  for convenience, freeze in ice trays to be used later. I hope you enjoy it.
Turned into a brown gloppy mess.  I had to pitch it.  I will try another recipe using powder.
i used a 2 inch piece of turmeric and i think i achieved a good paste
Great recipe! Thank you! I browned the tofu cubes first to avoid breaking them in the sturdier vegetables.  I also added bok choy and onions because I like them.

This was delicious! I used date sugar instead of brown sugar to make it a little healthier. I also used 4 carrots instead of 2, and substituted kale for spinach because we didn't have any spinach. Lastly, I used sesame oil instead of olive oil to give it more of an Asian flavor. It was so good! I will say, the pepper (we used cayenne) was a bit strong for the kids. I would probably leave that out next time and only add it to my own.
Used Sunflower Butter instead of Peanut Butter as my stepson has a peanut allergy, and it turned out great! Everyone loved it!
Delicious! Was a big hit. Use more srirracha sauce if you want it spicy. I drained the tofu in the fridge using paper towel and pressed between 2 plates. That method worked well.

This was incredibly good.  My ten year old wasn’t sure when she saw what I made for lunch but after tasted it, she said, “it was a lot better than I thought it would be”.  That’s a pretty good review from a kid. ;). I, personally, loved it.
Amazingly delicious
Added chopped cilantro and served over zucchini noodles or zoodles instead of to rice.  Pretty tasty

Ooh, this is good. I made it for a dressing for turkey meatloaf and I used jellied sauce (didn't have whole berry), but I can't wait to try it on day-after-Thanksgiving turkey sandwiches. OH! And I'm going to try it as a base for turkey salad too.
Easy, basic and delicious!

This is outstanding, and PERFECT for turkey sandwiches. I always loved mayo with cranberry sauce on sandwiches, but combining the two and adding poppy seeds makes such a difference. We ate this for days on our sandwiches, and I could see using this with chicken also. I made a half batch using Hellmann's mayo and a half batch with Miracle Whip, we loved both!  I can't wait to use this for a chicken salad or turkey salad, adding in some diced celery and onion. Thanks for sharing this wonderful, easy spread :)

I LOVE this! Perfect for Thanksgiving leftover turkey sandwiches!  So easy but tasty - the poppy seeds are a nice twist.  I made this with plain canned whole berry sauce and "Smart Beat" mayo-type spread.  I also think this would be fabulous with a little spice in it - like if you make homemade cranberries with a little jalapeno kick.  Great idea!  I will make this often!
great on turkey leftovers! I needed to put more cranberry to mayo ratio though....

Yummy!!! I always have my turkey sandwiches with mayo and cranberry sauce, I've never thought to mix the two together.  I was great, I got to mix some for me and the kids still got to eat their cranberry "jello".  I think the poppy seeds could easily be left out, but I added them for extra fun :-), thanks tahoegirl
This was amazing...I put it on "Becky's Chicken Salad". I made no changes to this cranberry sauce ...except used Chia seeds instead of poppy...couldn't find them.

Gosh, who would have thought?  I like mayo on turkey sammies, and I like cranberry while I am eating turkey, and DH loves every bite of turkey to have a bite of cranberry, so this was a hit!  I used lite Miracle Whip, a little more cranberry, and zero poppy seeds.  I also added a few dashes of chili sauce but I couldnt taste it and I didnt want to over do it on the first go.  Love this idea!  Thanks for sharing!
This was really good, and very straight-forward and easy to prepare. Had it over beef wellingtons and it was perfect. Thank you!
Really good, rich sauce!

I thought the sauce turned out great! I also decreased the butter to about 3/4 cup and clarified that, so probably ended up with about half a cup. The key to not having your sauce separate is to let the butter cool before you add it. Otherwise, the eggs will solidify, and you have a blend of butter and slightly solid eggs.
I found this recipe easy enough to make, but it had way too much of a vinegar taste.  The second time I made it I cut down on the vinegar and it was much better.

Very good...First time making Bearnaise for fish and it was good.  After reading the reviews I was afraid that the vinegar would be too strong so I reduced it by half.  Definately will make again.  Thanks for the post.

I made this on Christmas with Beef Tenderloin (recipe found here). The Bernaise sauce has too strong a vinegar taste and even though I did everything exactly as suggested, it still separated. Back to the drawing board for me. I'll seek another recipe that doesn't contain as much vinegar.

I halved the vinegar when I made it and it turned out absolutely PERFECT. To keep it from separating, though, Emeril Lagasse says to clarify the butter before adding it. I'll try that next time, since it was very hard to save the leftovers of this sauce :[
You will love this recipe. The flavor and the texture is just sublime!
This sauce is fantastic. I followed the directions as written. Great stuff.

This sauce tasted great, but the proportions seemed wrong.  There is way too much butter.  I ended up halfing it, and still had the sauce way too buttery.  Plus the consisitancy didn't seem right cuz the butter oil didn't mix with the rest of the ingrediants.  So on an aesthetic scale, it ranks low, but it still tasted great!  And we're used to having it in France, so that says a lot.  Thanks!

Great, easy recipe for a healthy and tasty pesto. I followed the recipe as written, though added a touch more parmesan.
This pesto is great on veggies, crackers, corn chips... and I will be using it as a sandwich spread tomorrow.

I've made a non-alcoholic version of this punch a couple of times for my daughters parties (birthday, New Years Eve) and it is so good!  I wish I could find an occasion to make it with some rum for me!

Terrfic on a hot day! I made for our Fourth of July celebration with great compliments. I did use the entire 16z can of cream of coconut, forgot to add the pineapple and lastly used the entire 750ml bottle of coconut rum.

Yummy!!
I made it without the rum and it was so great and easy to make!
This has become a favorite in my house! Great frozen drink for parties!!

This was a big hit over the 4th of July.  I followed the tips and put the crushed pineapple with the juice through the processer, used a whole 16oz can of coconut cream and the entire 750ml bottle of coconut rum, mixed it up and froze it overnight in two 1gal ice cream buckets.  I let it thaw about an hour then mashed it up with a meat fork and stirred for the slush consistancy.  Topped each glass with whipped cream & a cherry.  I got rave reviews from everyone who tried it.

This was fantastic!  I purchased 3 of those big reusable Glad plastic containers with lids and pulled one out of the freezer whenever the punch bowl was empty at a party.  The recipe yeilds a lot.  I was very happy I didn't double.  Yummy!
I made this for my friends bridal shower & everyone loved it & asked for copies of the recipe!

I made a regular and virgin pitcher for my son's graduation party. It was 90 degrees, so this was very refreshing. We used 3/4 of the 750ml Coconut Rum bottle. I did preblend the pineapple pieces in blender with the juice, and used coconut milk instead of cream.  This was soooo good.  Even my uncles  who don't like froo-froo drinks, loved it. I added a little bit of rum flavoring to the virgin pitcher.  Overall it was a big success.  Thanks soo much for sharing this recipe!!

Okay, check this out!  I had a group of ladies over and this recipe was a HUGE hit.  And let me add that if you have any leftovers, all you have to do is store it in the freezer and give it a stir when you're in the mood for a drink.  This is to-die-for!

Totally awesome punch! :)  I made it with a 16oz can of cream of coconut instead of putting chunky pineapple in it, and halved the recipe cause it was for a small party. It turned out great! :)  I left out the rum and made it virgin so if people wanted to add some rum in, they could. :) I'll definitely make this again during the summer.  Very refreshing and yummy! :9
This was awesome without any modifications.  I liked the chunks from the crush pineapple.  I make this recipe any time I have a party and it is a big hit.
We made this for our annual Luau and the people loved it! Using the coconuts as a glass was a festive hit! Bought those at a party place.
Delicious! It does make about 2 punch bowls at least.. but yes be careful about freezing it too long-- even with the rum it was a solid brick after i left it overnight..

Huge hit at our Luau celebration.   Recipe filled approx. two 3 quart pitchers.  I did purée the pineapple as suggested by others..and actually ended up using the blender to mix all the ingredients (except the soda).  After adding the soda I put in the freezer overnight.  If you do freeze overnight just make sure you have plenty of time for it to thaw the next day as it will be almost solid.

This is absolutely my favorite punch!  I used coconut milk and left out the rum and it was perfect!  I made sure to check it in the freezer, stirring every so often.  The result was a slushy pina colada!  Everyone raved!  Thanks for sharing, I will make over and over again!
Made for a personal bridal shower and everyone drank this punch right up! I did not use the rum and personally enjoyed the little pieces of pineapple.

This recipe was absolutely delicious!  It was gone in the first hour of our party because everyone loved it so much!  I made two slight alterations though.  I read the other reviews were people said they felt there were too many big pineapple chunks, so I threw the can of crushed pineapples into my food processor and blended it in to even smaller pieces.  So the punch still had texture, but you could drink it through a straw.  Also, I used coconut rum instead of regular rum, and I poured in the entire bottle (750 mL).  I froze the punch overnight and it was half frozen and very slushy once I broke it up and then just left it in the fridge all day.  I can't say enough how much everyone loved this drink.  Next time we have a party this size (about 30 people) I will make double!
The best pina colada punch ever.. I have made this many times over and everyone loves it...
AMAZING!!
This punch is fabulous!  I've had to start making two batches of punch because we always run out before the main meal.
I made this spiked punch for my Hawaiian Lula House Warming Party and all my guests just loved it! This is a punch that I be using at my next party. :)

Ooh la la, oh so good!  This punch is so good!  I followed the recipe as written and was very happy.  I did use the crushed pineapple, but processed the heck out of it with my food processor after reading other reviews not being happy with the "chunks".  It worked great while still adding a little bit of texture to the punch.  This does make a ton, so be prepared with a big bowl or pitcher.  Also, mine did not freeze to slushy consistency in 4 hours, it took much longer.

I made this for a ball wind up party. It was SO good. It was gone in 1/2 hour and everyone loved it!! The only thing was that it was so filling. Kind of left me feeling bloated. Tasted fantastic though.

Loved this recipe.  It was super easy and everyone loved it!  I made the whole batch, then put half in one bucket and half in the other.  I added alcohol to one half and left the other half with out.  Both turned out great!
This was definitely a crowd pleaser.  Everyone wanted the recipe.  I took the crushed pineapple and put it thru the blender first.  Which also made it a little thicker and much easier to drink.

I also used coconut milk and it worked just fine.  I also left out the rum so guests could just add it if they wished, but be careful not to leave in the freezer too long if you do this because it will freeze solid without alcohol.  To give you an idea of quantity - this makes 2 full punch bowls, so make sure you've got a couple of big containers available when mixing it up.  Everyone at the get together has requested the recipe.
I made this for a bridal shower and it was a hit!

Excellent for a summer barbecue.  I put the pineapple in the blender for a quick whir so it would be more of a puree and used coconut rum instead of regular (I also added more than the recipe specifies).  We had no leftovers and a lot of very "happy" guests.
i liked it ok, but my friends did not appreciate the "chunks."

This was so easy to make and was easier to drink!!  I did not use rum but I used 16 oz of coconut milk and not as much lemon lime drink.  Everyone loved it at a dinner party I attended.  I will make it over and over again.

This was a hit at our Halloween party. I did not blend the pineapple because the punch was "Poltergeist Puke", so the chunks worked nicely. I made it without rum and used both coconut milk and cream of coconut. Kids and adults loved it and repeatedly came back for more. It was not taken out of the freezer ahead of time, so I had to microwave it a little at a time, mash it with a knife and repeat until it was a thick slush. I then added the sprite. It was thick like a frozen daiquiri. YUM!

I made this punch for a baby shower yesterday and everyone loved it!  I omitted the rum and can of crushed pineapple.  I just mixed everything together and served it that way...without freezing it.  It was delicious and creamy.  I will make this again.
made this for a dinner party and am planning on using it for my summer wedding. the pineapple chunck aren't super-drinker friendly, so i'm thinking about substituting most of them with more juice.
FANTASTIC!
Substituted extra pineapple juice for the crushed pineapple after reading reviews about the drink being too chunky and it turned out good.

This was delicious! Minor changes: I made mine with 15 oz (a whole can) of coconut milk and 3 cups coconut rum. I didn't use pineapple chunks, just pineapple juice. I only used half of a 2 liter of soda, too. It was great. I think it would be wonderful if you followed the recipe as is, too. I placed it in the freezer about 6 hours before our party in a very large mixing bowl WITHOUT a lid (when it was covered it didn't seem to be setting), then took it out and stirred it to smooth it out a bit. The trick of Orange Juice is to use Valencia Oranges...Navel oranges just don't work for juice...don't worry about how they look...some can look terrible but they taste wonderful...Valencias are also called "juice oranges"...I get about 1/2cup juice out of 2 'regular' sized Valencias...I get about 1 cup of juice out of 3 large ones.
I use an electric juicer...but if you don't have one...you can juice any citrus with a fork: cut the fruit in half...use a knife to take out any seeds...Stick the fork into it and 'ream' it around to extract the juice, squeezing the fruit against the fork...you can also move the fork around...using a fork you will get more pulp out of the fruit...it's usually easy to 'fish out' any stray seeds...usually you won't have any seeds in limes.  Strain it if you don't want the pulp...that will also get rid of any seeds...but I always use it and never strain it.  Using a fork will also yield more juice - probably because of the extra pulp.  For any citrus fruit...the heavier the fruit...the more the juice...and the thinner the skin...the better it is...
