Served it up with some beer bread...Yummy!

Very good and very easy. Only thing I added were a few fresh muchrooms.
Will make again for sure!
Fast, easy, delicious-two thumbs up-Jan in NC

I made a couple of changes and let me explain why. The frozen veggie mix would work fast and fine I am sure but my opinion is that if you are going to take the time to chop fresh celery, potatoes, and onion then why not just use fresh broccoli, cauliflower, and carrots too? Again, it depends on what kind of time crunch you are in ( I would use frozen if in a hurry too) but as a rule of thumb, fresh is always better than frozen. Velveeta is very salty so if using the bouillon and water, I would recommend cutting back on the bouillon cubes. I chose to use 2 1/2 cups of low sodium chicken broth in place of the bouillon and it was still a little too salty so I cannot even imagine four cubes. With all of that said, I do think the soup could use some herbs. I ended up adding a little bit of dill and parsley. All in all this is a great soup, easy to make, and I will make again. Thanks for sharing!

This wasn't bad, but it was kind of like eating a cup of melted cheese with chunks of veggies.  I expected something a little richer.  My kids turned up their noses, which was a big bummer.  Thanks for the recipe though, it wasn't a waste of my time although I doubt we'll make it again.

This is one of my family favorites.  I had lost my recipe and was delighted to find it here in allrecipes.com.  I do not add the frozen mixed vegetables.  Instead, I just used carrots.   Everything else was the same.  Thank you Shirley for contributing this wonderful soup.

Wow!  This was just super!  I was concerned that there may be too many veggies in it, but it was perfect!  I added about 6 strips of cooked crisp bacon to it... and also, I didnt' cube the Velveeta.  I just put it in there whole and stirred it a lot.  Definitely a keeper!

This was an old family favorite and I had lost the recipe.  Now I can make it for my family.  Thanks.  I also add a bag of real bacon bits to it.  Instead of using celery, I add just a bit of celery salt.
Really good!  My kids liked it.
Ive made this soup a few times with several variations such as adding some leftover Bruschetta chicken or mashed potatoes to thicken it a bit. Its always a hit at our house!
What a decicious and simple recipe. It's a keeper in our house!

Stevia measurements differ from brand to brand, so I made mine according to how sweet I like my drinks. This hot chocolate was ok, but it was a little weak. Next time, I will add another teaspoon of the cacao powder to make it "chocolatier." This is a good base recipe for people to adjust according to their diet, perhaps using almond or soy milk. I did like the flavor the cinnamon gave to it.

Fantastic... my husband loves tom collins and I had to atempt it. Made it two nights in a row and my husband and I felt like we were on holiday. A movie on our tv, cheese and crackers, and tom collins.  The shaker caused a great refreshing froth at the top! I had a date with John and Tom.
I tried this recipe for the first time and have to admit, it is delicious and refreshing indeed. I used Perrier Sparkling L'Orange instead of Club Soda. I would also skip the Bitters. Perfection!!!!!
Round out with dash of blood orange bitters.

This is one of my favourite bar drinks.  Not too sweet, but not too sour either.  
Highly recommended.
Classic..very refreshing
First try followed exactly, felt the amount of lemon juice over powered the drink. Next try only used 1oz lemon juice, 1.5 simple syrup. Turned out great.
A very good tom collins recipe. At times I prefer lime juice to lemon, but it is all up to your own tastedbuds :)
Cut back a bit on lemon juice and added a bit of cherry juice. Was good.
I hate drinks that are too sweet but added just a bit more simple syrup to cut the tartness. This is light and refreshing. Perfect compliment to Gin's botanicals.
Live this summer time cooler... Yum!

This is soooo flippin' good. Like, could really REALLY get you in trouble good... Make it with the bitters if you can - a bottle isn't stupid expensive, and it just adds something indescribably delicious to the mix. Sometimes though, I cut back on the simple syrup just a touch, and add the tiniest splash of the juice from the maraschino cherries. Really good, too. Anyway, thanks, c-biskit! Your drink is fab!

Pretty Good!
I didn't have bitters on hand, so I left that out, but otherwise followed the recipe.  Enjoying one right now.  Light and refreshing.  Will probably make a 2nd one later...

A solid Tom Collins recipe.  Omit the bitters if you don't have them.  I use less lemon juice (1 ounce).  Fresh lemon juice is best, but bottled will work in a pinch.  If you want something light and refreshing, try this recipe!  If you're not a gin fan, substitue vodka for a Vodka Collins.
Great recipe, thanks! I added a little more simple syrup- perfection.
The flavor is great, a bit sweet, but offsets the savory bacon flavor of the coconut I used. Next time less liquid. After the maple syrup, the consistency was fine and didn't need the cream.

This frosting is just like the description says, it is a very sweet frosting. A little goes a long way. I wouldn't suggest piping on cupcakes like I did. I think this would be good smeared on top of cinnamon rolls.
I added a pinch of salt and used unsalted butter. It was perfect. Especially with chopped bacon!!

10.09.16 ~ Yum, Yum, Yum - I could have eaten this frosting with a spoon, but I didn't, I only licked the beaters. I didn't have any whipping cream on hand, so I used a little milk. It worked perfectly and gave me the texture I wanted to frost 'Grandpop's Special Chocolate Cake' from AR. Definitely will be using this one again.

Nice and easy. I had actually put this together without looking on here first except that I used milk because I had no cream. Tis very sweet frosting and as it was intended for a spice cake I added a bit of cinnamon to this recipe and to my taste lessened the sweetness and improved the frosting for the spice cake.
I didn't like this. Warm banana like this got runny and made a perfectly fine banana taste rotten.

The girls LOVED this for a treat after dinner tonight! Of course, I wasn't camping, so I just put everything on a plate and put it in the microwave for about a minute until everything was all melt-y and gooey. I also used mini chocolate chips b/c that's all I had on hand, which worked great. Perfect little treat that would satisfy any sweet tooth...a keeper~YUM! Thanks for sharing. :)
Banana boats are a great camping treat that is very fast and easy to make.

This is something my Mom used to make when I was little and had a cold - it brings back nice memories  :-)  She used a splash of red wine instead of rum.  Even without the alcohol it's a great hot drink w/ no caffeine.
Heated 2 cups of water in the microwave. Rolled a lemon & sliced it into my teapot. Poured water over lemon slices to steep. Added honey to mug of lemon tea. Yum!
this is a great recipes
Would like to try with maple syrup in place of honey!

This was perfect for my sore throat. I followed another reviewers suggestion and used 1 cup water, 1 tablespoon honey, and juice from a whole lemon. Very soothing. I will definitely be using this every time Im sick.
This was really good. I did use a bit less water, probably about 2 cups, just whatever fit into my small coffee cups.
this is also great for a cold works really well help soothe a sore throat and cough and tastes great
My mom always made this when I was sick. It's perfect for a sore throat.
I had to double the lemon juice and honey (too weak otherwise) but after I did, this was pretty tasty and really helped my husband's sore throat.

My Oma used to make this for me when I was a kid and nothing tastes better when your throat is sore and raw. I cut the amount of water down to one cup but kept the lemon the same. Very comforting Paula....

When I seen the title of this recipe I had to see if what it was that my mother too.Made us kid's the same thing but her's she used sugar,even if there was rum around I do believe she would've add just a tiny bit.But this the first for me to find  close to my mother's recipe.Thank's for sharing it.
I left the rum out. Very soothing and just what my upset tummy needed.

This is a really good alternative to the boxed neocitran... I however altered the recipe by using the 1 serving method, but keeping the lemon amount the same.  So therefore I used 1 cup of water, 1 tablespoon of honey and a full lemon, just because I love the taste of the lemon! Enjoy

I've been feeling cruddy today with a sore throat and swollen glands. I needed something to not only comfort but soothe.
My grandma used to make this for me when I was a kid and was sick. 

I made this for one, using half of a lemon and a little more honey. This is just what I needed.
I had a chill and this took it right away.  My husband had a full blown cold and said this was very comforting.  We used 2 cups of water as we wanted it nice and strong.
sub the rum for vodka!!! **delicious**
in my house when somebody get sick...we make some HOT LEMONADE...jajjaj...I thought that we were crazy
This recipe really soothed my throat, thanks!
Very good- soothing on the throat. Juice of 1 lemon is approximately 2-3 tablespoons of reconstituted bottled lemon juice.

I woke up feeling a bit under the weather--despite my efforts, looks like I'm getting bf's cold.  I decided to try this, and it is certainly helping soothe my throat.  I just boiled one cup of water and mixed it with the same amount of lemon and honey.  No rum for me--a little to early for that today!  Thanks for the recipe.

Well of COURSE it's not as good as ice cold lemonaid! This is a good alternative for either a sick child or someone who doesn't care for hot tea or that awful-tasting TheraFlu.  Another variation of this can be made with bottled lemon juice if you don't have a fresh lemon on hand and suger in lieu of honey.
I love lemonade but it just doesn't taste good hot.
Great when my kids were sick! I left out the rum though!
Excellent!  A great treat when you're not feeling well.
Really good cocktail to share with friends.  It is nice as an aperitif drink with little snacks, very festive.
I did not like it at all.  The raw garlic overpowered the basil.  I would saute the garlic in the olive oil first or use half as much.

I amgiving this recipe 5 stars simply because of the fact that it uses nutmeg!! That is a wonderful addition to any pesto sauce!!  I did modify it for other things however, I added lemon juice and parmesan cheese, and used pine nuts instead.  This is a great base however, and the nutmeg really does add an impressive taste!  Thanks for sharing!

I followed the recipe as written and it was delicious!
Everyone ate it and raved about how yummy it was!

Perfect!!!  I substituted the Almonds with unsalted Sunflower Seeds.  They're much closer in flavor to the traditional Pine Nuts at a fraction of the price of Almonds (about 30 cents from weigh-your-own aisle at the supermarket).
I was looking for a dairy-free pesto and found this. I also liked the fact that it called for almonds rather than pine nuts. The flavor was very good. Thanks!
We make this all the time to.  Good recipe.
I used pine nuts, and added parm. This was great!

I make basil pesto frequently but this time had TONS of basil to use (had to remove a garden bed) & the fact that this one used almonds intrigued me...I had an oversized can of mixed nuts leftover from a party & picked out the almonds. I love the fact that I can sub most any nut I have on hand (didn't need to add any salt) but this needed something so I added 1/4 cup parmesan & a quick squeeze of lemon & there it was!

I love this recipe! If I am feeling a little fiesty I'll throw a sun-dried tomato in it!! I pulse the dry ingredients before adding the olive oil- this way I can determine how wet/dry I want the pesto depending on how I am serving it! Delicious EVERY time!
Great recipe!  Very easy to make and tastes great!  The only thing I did differently was bake the almonds for 5 mins instead of 10.  Will be making this again.
best pesto quick and easy
Try with hemp hearts instead of almonds/pine nuts!
I did not know almond could make such a tasty pesto! I will make some more while basil is fresher and cheaper and freeze it to enjoy later.
quick and easy--my husband was uneasy b/c it isn't made with pine nuts, but he ended up really loving this on our pizza.

This is a great basic recipe for pesto. We were due for a hard freeze this week and I hated to waste all that lovely basil in my garden so I doubled the recipe.  If you do double this recipe, I wouldn't recommend increasing the amount of garlic.  Like others I made a few changes adding a little shredded Parmesan and lemon juice. Whatever you do, don't leave out the nutmeg!

I'm not a pesto connoisseur by any means and, in fact, this was my fist time trying to make it myself.  But I thought this recipe was incredible!  I followed the recipe with the following exceptions:  I added a few squirts of fresh lemon and about 1/4 cup parm/reg cheese.
Fabulous!!!! So easy and delicious. I added parsley cause that's what i had in the garden it was a great combo with the basil. Will become my most used pesto recipe.
it was ok, we tried it on pizza rather than pasta.

This sauce is fast, easy, and delicious! I love how quick it is to prepare and low-hassle. My husband and I ate 2-3 servings, it's so good! The only thing is that we add 2-3 cloves more garlic (personal preference), a squeeze of 1-2 limes, and threw in some grated parmesan (from a can) and it's great. You don't have to put those things in and it's still pretty good, but with it, it's a favorite in our home.

Worked for me!  With some homemade pasta, it was a great lunch.  But watch for browning of the sauce if you plan on pre-preparing it.  I had a 15 minute wait between making the sauce and eating it, and the top was already starting to brown.

Five stars!  Easy to make, tasty, and cheaper than buying it already prepared in the store or buying pine nuts. I followed PatiO's advice and decreased the oil and used a little water.  You can't tell there's less oil.  Also, ten minutes was too long for the almonds; the first batch ended up burned perhaps it was the toaster oven?  The second time, I baked the almonds for 6 minutes and they were perfect.  I think parmesan would be a nice addition but I don't need any more calories so I will wait and add it on top of my pasta.  This is a definite keeper.

My usual pesto recipe was packed away in a box so I was searching for a recipe to use up the basil in my garden. This was very good. I used pine nuts instead of almonds and I always add good parmesan to my pesto- with those minor changes  this was perfect for us.
Just made a batch with the basil from my garden! Love it! Love the idea of freezing it in ice cube trays! Ingenious!
This was so easy! My first pesto and it tastes so good. I will be adding sun-dried tomatoes to it next time for a little bling.

You score "5 stars" for an excellent basic recipe with the added originality of using almonds instead of pine nuts. It was wonderful, as is. However, I do prefer my pesto with added parmesan cheese (the real stuff, not processed) and a touch of lemon juice. Your recipe accepted these modifications with delightful results.

I made 48 servings worth of this recipe to have in the freezer for the year, but made it in 3 batches of 16 servings. I chopped the garlic and blended it with the almonds, added the oil (only 1 cup for the 16 servings), 1 tbsp of lemon juice, nutmeg and salt and pepper. After blending those I add the basil and mixed it with a spoon and then blend it while pouring about 1/3 cup of water into the blender. I froze the pesto into ice cube trays and silicone muffin cups. Will definitely make again.
Super on pasta.  I also had to make quite a bit more to fit im my "mixer".  I added olives, canned mushrooms and pecans(what I had on hand).  Kids and dad loved it.
I didn't care for this.  Maybe I just don't care for pesto in general though as it was my first time trying it.  It was easy though.

I've never made pesto before and was a bit intimated - now that I made this super easy pesto, I wish I had done it earlier! Three cloves of garlic definitely gives it a kick, but a good one! I love this recipe and am very unlikely to go searching for another one. I will be using this pesto tonight to make pesto-stuffed pork chops. yum!

This recipe really can be adjusted, and probably should be, depending on your taste.  We used about 1/2 a cup of toasted pine nuts, added a tbl of shaved parm., added a bit of mint and played with the olive oil till it was the right texture.  But this recipe shows you all the basic elements...adding sundried tomatos is fun too, or olvies.

Oh man...delicious!  I roasted a couple onions, 1/2 lb sliced mushrooms and misc other garden fresh veggies, boiled up a pound of pasta and combined.  We ate it hot for dinner.  I took the leftovers cold to a block party last night.  Fabulous.  One woman was trying to figure out what was chewy...it's the almonds.  What a great idea!

I kind of messed up with this recipe by doubling (!) the garlic.  I strongly suggest you do NOT do that!  6 cloves of  garlic was WAY too much!!!  SO, I then tried to dilute the garlic taste by adding more of the other stuff, therefore by the time I was done I had barely followed the recipe.  However ... I like pesto  with parm cheese in it, and this recipe didn't call for it.  Also, although I love pesto and was aware that pesto had oil in it, making this recipe myself with all that oil kind of grossed me out!  I'll never look at pesto the same way again!  SO, i'm going to keep looking for the perfect pesto recipe which to me would have parm cheese in it and, if possible, less oil.  Oh, the almonds did actally work okay, which surprised me.

I ended up making this for the first time and loosely followed the recipe, added Parmesan cheese, and omitted the nutmeg as I didn't have any. It turned out amazingly! I ended up adding a little more olive oil, as I had more basil I was using. I was using pre- crumbled almonds and toasted them, this made my prep time very short, and ended up with a finer result.

I made this with fresh basil from my garden and I had no Almonds so I used finely chopped black walnuts. OH YYYYYUUUUUUMMMMMM. I had enough to  use for two different meals. I made the first one a couple of weeks ago. Bruce liked it  and said he has to get used to the olive oil and I guess he better because I will make this every summer I have fresh Basil in the garden. Also I had some pork chops left over and boned them, sliced them very thin. Mixed them and the pesto and pasta together and what a delicious quick dish. Yum, yum, thank you for this recipe. I will make it over and over again.
This is so easy! I made up a bunch of it and froze some to use later. Oh and it tastes great too!
"Easy" is a great description!  This really helped me find a use for my abundance of basil!  Great on sandwiches and pasta.  I used my blender to make it and that worked just fine.
Pretty good, but better with about 1/4 cup Parmesan added in.

I love the ease!! This is also good on pizza to replace the red sauce. I did add Parmesan.
Thanks!!
Everyone loved it!  Nice twist with the almonds!
By itself it seemed a little dry. When mixed with bowtie pasta and shrimp, it was incredibly good. Wow. Great dish. I will be making this again!
This was my first time making pesto. It was really easy. I was worried that the blender would not blend it properly but once the oil was added, it worked fine. I froze this for later use.

I made this pesto along with the Pesto Pasta with Chicken recipe and it turned out really good.  My husband loved it and gave it 10 stars!  My daughter and I prefer a little more sauce and will try doubling the pesto recipe or adding more olive oil next time.  I also sauteed some mushrooms and added them.  Yummy Pesto Sauce and very simple.
Great "starter" recipe.  I added fresh parmesan and used a mixture of basils from my herb garden.  Will make again, but will try with pignoli nuts and a bit less garlic.

I made this exactly as the recipe stated and it was good. Not the best, but good for how easy it is. I must add though, that if you bake almonds at 450 for 10 minutes, you end up with black almonds. I made this mistake and I want spare others the same mistake. I had never toasted almonds in the oven before so I was just going by what the recipe said.
This made great pesto! Warning to the unwise (like myself) if you are using sliced almonds, only bake them for 3-4 minutes, and watch them closely. I almost burnt mine!

I've been making larger batches all summer using basil from our garden.  I freeze in ice cube trays and then place frozen cubes into a freezer bag.  I can then pull out the number of cubes needed for a recipe that calls for 'tub pesto' or add to other dishes as I choose!  Goes great with a variety of chicken dishes and/or pastas!

Very easy and delicious! I omitted the nutmeg, didn't have that on hand. I used closer to 2 cups of basil leaves, and would probably add the oil to the blender first, because the leaves and almonds made the blades stick. I used this recipe with "Pesto Pasta with Chicken" and it turned out great! I will make more of this in batches to freeze and thaw as needed. Super easy!
We loved this recipe, fresh, tasty and easy! It's a keeper.

This is the first time I've ever made Pesto, and I had high hopes of this recipe.  I followed it exactly, except I toasted the pine nuts in a skillet.  The result, for me, is OK, but not great (unlike the Pesto I have tasted when I eat out).  I will try a different Pesto recipe next time (I have lots of basil growing on my porch).

This was so easy and so delicious. Had it with bow tie pasta. Looked gorgeous and tasted great. I took someone's suggestion and blanched the basil and added Parmesan cheese. Other than that, stuck with the recipe and it didn't disappoint!

I made a double batch and it was just enough to fill one ice cube tray for freezing. Very good basic recipe, but I made some adjustments. First of all, can pesto NOT have Parmesan cheese? I added 1/2 c. to my double batch (1/4 c. for a single) and a Tablespoon of lemon juice (1/2 T. for a single batch). I used roasted salted almonds and didn't bother toasting them.

I just finished blending the pesto exactly as this recipe describes and I can hardly wait for tonights dinner! The smell and taste are intoxicatingly good. I have slices of tomato slow drying in the oven to toss into pasta tonight along with this little bit of heaven Mmmmm...
I loved this recipe!  Before putting in the basil, I dunked it in boiling salt water and then immediately cooled it in ice cold water.  This helps keep the bright green color of the basil.
I loved this recipe.  I never thought I could have pesto because I'm allergic to pine nuts.  I love the alternative with the almonds.  Tasted great and was super easy to make.
Very good! It's got a very fresh taste. I tossed it with cheese tortellini.
Wonderful!  I wasn't sure about using almonds, but I didn't have any pine nuts so I tried it.  Tastes great and very simple.  I'll use this recipe from now on.

I love basil and was looking for a good solid recipe to be able to make and freeze pesto to use up my herbs. I was really quite happy with this one except that the garlic was really overpowering...and I love garlic. I like that it used almonds as well, great thrifty alternative  to other nuts. I'll definitely be using this recipe as a base for the future, but tweaking slightly to suit my tastes. Excellent and easy recipe!!

I'm not much of a pesto person but had some basil from the CSA this week.  I LOVE roasted almonds so had those on hand.  Made as intended except I didn't have the real garlic so used powdered.  Good and easy.  My family even tried it and ate more than the obligatory "no thank you" bite.

Great pesto!  I loved the almonds (quickly toasted in a hot skillet) and added ~1/8 c fresh grated parmesan cheese.  I tried to go light on the oil, but ended up adding more to the pasta to get the right consistency - use the amount called for.  I'll be using this recipe frequently.

This is delicious and so simple to prepare. I doubled the recipe and froze most of the pesto. I did add some parmesan cheese since I had it on hand. I'll be making this again, I'm sure - I have an abundance of basil in the garden right now. Thanks for the recipe!
love the almonds. I think it might be even better with walnuts, since that's what I'm used to. Using with shrimp and pasta

Delicious!  I use fresh basil from my garden, I toasted the almonds the first time I made this, and it was great!  Since then I usually just use whole raw almonds and throw everything in the processer.  I have also used pinenuts, toasted first in the oven.

Excellent! Loved this one & easy to make too. One thing about the almonds that I really like instead of the pine nuts is the COST! The toasted almonds were very tasty & so much less $$. Also...a tip on toasting the nuts, don't bother with the oven, simply heat a (dry) non stick heavy skillet on the stove, and saute' the nuts until toasted with no butter or oil. They are super easy & quick to do this way. Great recipe!

My basil plants were going crazy, so I decided to make my first pesto. This recipe is yummy. I had so many leaves, I doubled the recipe, used 5 cloves of garlic (it was plenty)blended all in the blender. Poured it all into an ice cube tray and the double recipe filled it perfectly. Tastes great, thank you for submitting.

Loved this recipe, I will admit I did not measure everything exactly, but just by eye-balling it I know I was very close.  You don't need to change a thing, but I think I may try adding some grated parmesan next time and may switch up the nuts just for variety.  I will be making this often as a change from red sauce...and not to mention I now have a basil plant.
This is very good and easy to make. For those that don't like garlic you can substitute onions instead. I make mine that way. It is just as good.

This pesto recipe is very good! I've never made pesto before. It was super-easy with no fuss. The most difficult part for me was getting my food processor to work! I used it for a chicken and pasta recipe I was doing. The only thing I changed was not toasting the almonds. I didn't want to take the time to preheat my oven. I will definitely make this again!

This came out very well.  Following other reviewers' suggestions, I added an extra clove of garlic and a little lemon juice.  I used a pinch of black pepper and 1/2 tsp salt.  I also used closer to 1/2 cup almonds (it was the end of a bag).  If you're using a blender rather than a food processor, I recommend pulsing until it's the texture you want.
This was an awesome recipe! I added about 3 tbsp of parmesan cheese and used the pesto to make a cream sauce. I will make this again!
easy peasy. I didnot have the required nuts I just used plain peanuts and it was fine.
Very easy to prepare and it tasted absolutely great :)
Perfect!
I used 1 clove of garlic instead of 3, and added 1tbs of lemon juice and 1/4Cup of grated parmesan to bring this recipe up a few notches on the like scale......
This recipe was fair, but the garlic needed to be reduced, and about two cups of Parmesan cheese needs to be added. :P
Good lord this is amazing! I doubled the recipe and it filled one full ice cube tray.. This gal is going to have pesto all winter! Yummmmmmmm
I don't cook at all, but have recently become interested.  This is a wonderful, quick and easy recipe.  I cannot wait to spread it on some bread with cheese and tomatoes and toast it!  Yummy

I liked the recipe, especially using almonds in place of the pine nuts. It did make the texture of the pesto a little grainy, but it wasn't a problem for us. I recommend running the nuts through the food processor first, makes the texture better. I did add Parmesan and a hit of salt, and a squeeze of lemon juice.

As-is, I found it a little bland, but it was definitely VERY easy to make.  I added some parmesan, lemon juice, garlic salt (in addition to the 3 cloves) and a couple mint leaves, and then it had enough tang for me.  Also toasted the almonds on the stovetop instead of in the oven.
Pretty good, basic recipe.  I tried to toast the almonds and they ended up black (good thing I had extras), so I put in them in a dry frying pan and toasted them that way.
Very good!!  1st time making pesto and it came out great and it's very easy to make!!
The toasted almonds gave this pesto a little different taste than your normal pesto.   Will try with a little less olive oil the next time though.
I must have done something wrong here, because I wasn't thrilled with the outcome.  Highly unlikely that I will try this one again.
This was very easy to make.  Very tasty and I would make this again and again.

So super easy. 
I picked the basil from the garden and had all the other ingredients in house. I added some lemon juice and shredded parm. cheese too
I've never made pesto but needed some for another recipe. I think this pesto is what did it for the other recipe! Very good! Will be making this again!

Made the recipe according to the full serving directions. I was using a blender and ran into the problem of short blades. The problem was solved after adding about 1/2c to 1 cup of milk to increase the volume that could be reached by the blades. Also added more almonds (about 1/2 cup). Delicious and easy to make!

yum. this was great over pasta with barbequed grilled citrus chicken and some kebobs made with brussel sprouts and purple onion. i always toast my nuts in my nonstick skillet instead of bothering w/ the oven.
I tried this and it just didn't have enough zing.  I doubled the nutmeg, added about 1/2 tsp. of salt and 1 tsp. of lemon juice!  DELISH!
I really liked it but I would cut back on the garlic the next time.  It took away from the basil flavor
A great pesto!  Nutmeg added a nice flavor and I added 1/4 c parmesan so no extra salt was needed.  This will now be a staple in my house.
This is super easy and very good. I like that it uses almonds, which are cheaper and easier to find than pine nuts. This makes for a very easy meal when you toss with some linguine!

This is a good recipe, we doubled it for use in our cafe. I had to use peanuts because the pine nuts are almost impossible to find in Vietnam and...if you do find them, very expensive.

A good mild pesto, easy to make and great (average flavor).
Easy and taste.  Didn't like that needed to add salt for taste.

This is an excellent pesto recipe!!  You will save a lot of $$ by using almonds vs. pine nuts.  Don't bother cooking these in the oven, dry saute them on the stove top on a low heat- be careful, they burn easily!  And my most important recommendation: Add a Tbsp. or 2 (I did 3!) of finely grated Parmesan cheese - it adds a delicious creaminess that you don't get otherwise.
Very tasty...just used pine nuts instead of almonds, but turned out great!
EASY and excellent.  I used soy nuts that I had in the kitchen cabinet.  I just may make a bundle to give as gifts to mom, friends, sister-in-law. MMMMMMMM.

This is a good basic pesto recipe which can be tweaked to individual preferences. One suggestion, for those who had difficulty processing the pesto... Buy one of those mini-food processors for jobs like these, as they're better suited than the full size machines.
Good, but I might use a little less oil next time. It could be a bit thicker.
This is yummy. Next time I'll add some parmesan to it and might use walnuts instead of almonds.

USE THIS RECIPE!!!  This is the best pesto I've made so far.  I did add lemon juice, salt and pepper and didn't exactly measure, but this was the best!  I had never heard of using almonds before, but it was really good, and a lot cheaper.  This is great to make if you grow herbs and garlic in your garden.  I will make a much bigger batch next time!  Thanks for the recipe.

This reads so easy and with almonds. thats the good news.I will surely try it and come back with a review.
A simple tip on toasting nuts is to heat the oven on its higest temp.(250 degrees celsius) switch off the oven and place a tray of nuts.Forget about it.When the oven is cool (about 1/2 an hour) you will find the nuts beautifully toasted without the bother of checking for doneness or stirring every few minutes.
Fantastic! I went a tad bit heavier on the olive oil and omitted the nutmug.

This was my first attempt at making pesto.  Great base recipe.  I doubled the garlic, halved the oil and added lemon juice.  The garlic & oil are definitely personal flavor preferences but I think the lemon juice is essential.  I will use this recipe every year I expect.  Thanks.

Thought I would miss parmesan cheese and pine nuts, which are typically included in pesto recipes, but didn't miss them at all. This really seems to highlight the basil flavor, which is why you want pesto in the first place.  Be careful with the size of your garlic cloves:  The cloves I used were large (like bigger than an almond), and it was borderline too garlicky, even for a garlic-lover like me.  This recipe is easy.  I even made it a day ahead, covered and refrigerated it.  Next day, I brought it to room temp. and mixed it with pasta and chicken.  This is the recipe I'll use again.
Awesome!  So easy and tastes great-I used almonds instead of pinenuts.

I used a blender instead of my big food processor because I felt that I just had a little bit of ingredients and they would get lost in my processor.  My blender worked really well.  I blended the almonds first by themselves to get them chopped up really good then added the remaining ingredients.  The pesto was thick so I will thin it down.  Overall, good recipe.
Simple and easy, this was a good basic pesto.  The only thing I did different was to toast the almonds in a skillet.

Easy and great with almonds! I soaked slivered almonds in water for 10 minutes before toasting them on a dry, hot pan. I feel like this achieves the best flavor and texture. I also basically doubled the garlic because I didn't think it had enough for my tastes. I didn't have nutmeg either. Finally, I added some parmesan cheese to enhance the flavor.

Delicious. I didn't do exact measurement and the pesto still turned out really nicely. This recipes is very forgiving. I doubled the garlic and used 1/2 cup of pine nuts instead of almonds. My little toddler (17 months old) even likes it.
This was easy and tastes great! This is my first attempt but I will be saving this recipe. I did add Parmesan and a little more garlic based on my own taste.
Really easy to make and tasted good too.  I didn't have almonds so I just added almond meal.

Best non dairy pesto...hands down!  I used my mini chopper and toasted the almonds on the stovetop.  First batch I made I used large cloves of garlic and even for me it was too much (I love garlic!). So make sure to use small cloves and add more if needed. I tried it with added lemon juice and it was good but I don't think it needs it.  It's perfect as is! I was literally licking the bowl and spoon! Definitely a keeper!
FANTASTIC !!!!!!!!
Very simple, light, and pleasing to the palette.
Thank you so much for this recipe.  It's wonderful and delicious.  I can't wait to make it again.
easy! great!

I make this often with a few changes.  I use walnuts instead of almonds (just what I usually have on hand) and skip the toasting step.  I'm a working mom for goodness sake!  :)  I usually throw in some parmesan cheese as well.  I freeze this in ice cube trays for future use.  My favorite is a pesto chicken salad....shredded leftover chicken, chickpeas, celery, tomatoes, broccoli slaw, and a few cubes of pesto.  Great healthy lunch to bring to work.  Yum!

Definitely easy to make. I found the recipe as shown to be a little too oily so I reduced the amount of olive oil next time I did it and it turned out great.  I also added a generous helping of pepper as well.

This was very simple, and convenient and the taste was pretty good. A good everyday sort of recipe.  I needed to find a pesto sauce w/o parmesan, since I didn't have any on hand. However it was missed. If you find it kinda bland, add a tsp of lemon juice, that helped.

The entire family loves this recipe!  Tastes great with any nut (we use pine nuts, walnuts or pecans), and freezes wonderfully! I make a ton before the first frost and freeze it all in ice cube trays - love having this ready at any time. Careful on the timing when roasting the nuts - easy to burn them.
I've always loved Pesto, and once I found this recipe, I couldn't believe how simple it is to make. This is definitely a keeper!
Great on flavour and definitely easy to put together! I used a mix of cashews and almonds, added two tablespoons of Parmesan and forgot the nutmeg. A keep for sure.

I can't believe it was so easy and tasty!  I did toast the nuts on the stove top as suggested in earlier comment, and substituted walnuts (that's what I had) and it was great.  I've made it twice now...also great on little dry toasts/ italian bread or pasta and can adjust the amount oil used.  I used my homegrown basil, but found if you don't have the 1 1/2 c. basil, it is better to add basil from grocery, rather than reduce the recipe-the ratio is just right! Freezes well, just allow enough time to thaw before next use.
Wonderful recipe. I didn't have nutmeg, but I didn't miss it.  I used it in the Pesto Polenta Lasagna recipe on this site and it worked wonderfully!

Didn't have pine nuts so I halved and toasted almonds on skillet, covered for 10 mins on med-low flame. I do think more than 6 can be served with this recipe as is :-) I put some of this in mayo & it was so good! I also added this pesto to Allrecipe's Philly Pesto Pasta!!
This is the first time that I made pesto and it was way easier than I  expected and very good too.
Yum!! We used pine nuts instead of almonds, and we didn't quite have enough basil so it ended up being quite garlicky tasting, but we loved it and it tasted so fresh and delicious. Thanks!!
It was super easy.  I used pine nuts instead of almonds.  The taste was right on the money.  I even froze the extra in an ice cube tray so I have some ready to use next time.

This is a really fantastic dairy-free pesto recipe and it is super easy. You can substitute walnuts and pistachios with great results. For 2 cups basil I added 1.5tsp lemon juice and grated some lemon zest into it for brightness.
Quick, easy and delicious! I'll be making this one again for sure.
I didn't bake the slivered almonds, and I used the slap chop to get the texture I wanted, not a food processor. It turned out great.
LOVED this!  I don't like nuts in my pesto so I subbed parm-reg and it was wonderful!  THANKS!
did you use slivered or whole almonds?

A good basic pesto! Per others' reviews I added parmesan cheese, and since I had no almonds I subbed pecan pieces that I toasted in a skillet. Served over medium shell pasta with herbed chicken breast chunks and fresh tomato.  Family thought they were getting a gourmet dinner!   Leftovers today for lunch!  YUM!

Wonderful nutty, robust flavor. Great texture. It holds true its name,it was a snap to put together. I used 1 cup basil and 1/2 cup cilantro; it gave it a bit of zip which was delicious. I used 1/2 cup EVOO and an extra clove of garlic and tossed in grilled chicken tenderloins. I plan to use this one again and again!
This was way good! I did add some lemon juice for more flavor.  I made this for the creamy pesto shrimp pasta from this site....YUMMY!!

This was truly 'easy' pesto and it earned rave reviews from guests even though I skipped toasting the almonds. I did use the parmesan tip another member suggested, and added coarse ground pepper at the end. Three yums UP!

I loved this recipe!! its super easy and really yummy. I used pine nuts instead of almonds, but next time I will use almonds.... pine nuts are crazy expensive!! I also used parmesan cheese like other reviews suggested.

Followed the recipe as stated except I had no nutmeg and added in some Romano + parmasean cheese. I also added in some roasted cherry tomatoes and roasted red pepper. Btw, I'm a huge garlic lover and three garlic cloves was more then enough for me, so I wouldn't suggest adding more. Used seashell pasta. Pretty nice dish.
I am not a fan of pesto with almonds.

This is a great recipe. I had a lot of fresh basil from my own backyard and this recipe was so easy. I like the fact that it's almonds instead of pine nuts, which I'm not a big fan of. The only thing I changed was to add 1/4 cup of parmesan cheese, and I think it came out better this way.
This was YUM-MY!  I toasted the almonds in my toaster oven and loved loved loved this.  I think I'm going to put this on grilled eggplant for dinner tonight
I thought this recipe was good but a bit too nutty for me.

I appreciate having a pesto recipe with almonds as an alternative to the more expensive pine nuts.  Truth be told though, I thought it was pretty good - but would have likely been better with the pine nuts!  It is a good basic recipe to start from though.
Yum-  Made slight adjustments  Doubled recipe- 5 garlic cloves 1/2 c. almonds (toasted in pan on stove) 3 c. basil (or so) 1 c. olive oil 1/2 c. parm cheese dash salt & pepper dash nutmeg  PERFECT!
This will spice up your dinner and it is simple.
Very yummy recipe! I love the almonds!!

Fantastic recipe, however I feel that there was a bit too much olive oil. I found that 1/2 cup of olive oil left my pesto fairly runny. Still, the taste of the pesto is fantastic and I look forward to making it again.
I added parmasan cheese and neglected to add nuts and loved it.
Awful! Needs parmesan.

I'm not sure how to properly measure a cup of leaves, but I'm thinking they should be packed down after making this recipe. Seemed to have too much oil in it, so next time I'll pack the leaves down more.

Really tasty!!! Roasted my almonds in a pan instead of oven like other reviewers suggested which is so much faster. It was chunkier than what I expected (maybe due to my crappy food processor unable to fine grind the almonds) but delicious nonetheless. I used really good olive oil and it was perfection. Excited to try with parmesan next time.
Very easy to make and tasty. I added more garlic, but I always do. Thanks to those for the tip on just using a dry skillet to toast the almonds. Will use this recipe many more times. Thanks!

This was exactly what I was looking for. The basic instructions for creating pesto. This recipe was great. I used walnuts instead of toasted almonds and measured more by eye than exact measurements. It turned out great!  It was also very good with chicken. Thank you!
This is the best pesto I've ever eaten!  I did add 1/2t. salt, but we are salt lovers.  The hubs loved it too!
This was yummy and easy.  I made no changes to the recipe.  None were needed!

It's so very tasty! We made several batches of this last fall when we harvested huge piles of basil from our garden. We froze most of the pesto in pans lined with wax paper, then broke up the frozen sheets and stacked them in freezer bags. So any time of year I need the fresh pesto taste, I pull out a couple of chunks and let them thaw!

YUM! Loved this recipe cause it's so easy and the almonds are a nice change to the pine nuts which are hard to find & expensive in my small town. The second time I made it I added 1/2 tsp. cumin instead of nutmeg & the squeeze of one fresh lemon! I liked it even more this way!!!! (Note- be sure to use a good extra virgin olive oil for a better flavor). Thanks Rebecca!

I have never made Pesto before and honestly didn't know what it was until I made this and put it in a pasta dish,then voila! I realized the glob I dug out of the food processor was a familiar taste and made the pasta dish wonderfully delicious. I used raw almonds and did not toast them, and used dried basil instead of fresh leaves. I will definately make again and not sure I can make another pasta dish without it. Thank you!

Excellent recipe.  I used lots of basil from my garden and made two batches.  I placed the pesto in ice cube trays and froze then popped out and individually wrapped each cube and put all the cubes in a bag in the freezer.  I use these all fall and winter as single serving pesto, in sauces, or as spreads.
This was wonderful and easy.  The only nut I had on hand was walnuts.   I've never heard of anyone toasting walnuts......and didn't.  The pesto was delicious.  Thank you for sharing.

I would have never thought to use almonds instead of the pine nuts. I did have to stir some in at the end for looks. Tastes better then store brands and better then the ones at my farmers market! I will make over and over as I have basil coming out my ears in the garden. Just wish it could be canned!
Very easy to make.  I doubled the recipe using slightly less olive oil.  Added parmesan and pecans per others recommendations.  Delicious!

I tried halving this recipe and ran into difficulties.  In particular,
with half the material, after the initial blender pulse, all the material
-much more compact- now could lay beneath the blades.  Additional blending
didn't do anything.  I had to manually raise of the material and try to
blender again, but this achieved little because it quickly went below the
blades again, and in the end I was left with pesto with many practically
unchopped garlic and nuts.  This is posted here as an unrated review to
warn others that before reducing the size of the recipe, think about the
size, shape, and abilities of your food processor/blender.  (With more
material, I think that the convection in my blender would chop everything
without difficulty.)

great, easy recipe. the perfect way to use and preserve all the basil I had at the end of the summer. I made this in big batches, then froze it - then I grab a little as I need it. It's like it's summer all year long!

This pesto was delicious. Some suggestions for cooks: -My first batch of almonds burned. For the second batch of almonds, I put them on the lower shelf and cooked for only 5 minutes.  -I don't have a food processor (only blender), so I banged the almonds with a meat hammer and then added them to the blender. This worked well.

I tweaked this recipe a little to sit my fancy. Instead of adding toased almonds, I added toasted walnuts instead. (It was all I had on hand!) I also added 3-4 sundried tomato pieces that I had dried myself. They were hard and not canned in oil, so I chopped them first to help the food processor out. I also added about 5 cloves of garlic since I like it so much. With the tomatoes and extra garlic, however, I had to add a little more oil to get it to bind together. I used cinnamon basil rather than the traditional sweet basil which gave it an earthier taste. What I made was absolutely wonderful! It was also a very earthy color as the red from the tomatoes mixed with the green from the basil.
I really appreciated that this uses almonds vs. pine nuts.
Excellent and so easy! I had never  made pesto before--I was surprised at how much better it was than the store-bought kind. I added extra garlic and used pine nuts.
This has worked well for us.  I froze the extra we didn't use into ice cube trays for storage and has been quite handy in a pinch!
I did not like this recipe at all. The taste was unusual and not to my family's liking.

I had some fresh basil that I needed to use quickly, and this was the perfect way to do it!  As is, the recipe is fantastic, but I felt it was definitely missing a little something. A squeeze of lemon juice turned out to be exactly what it needed.  Perfect!

I chose this recipe because I had a bunch of basil that was going to go bad and I realized that my pine nuts had gone rancid. I added some parmesan cheese (probably about an ounce...i just cut off a chunk and threw it in) and replaced some of the oil with lemon juice to cut the fat a bit and heighten the flavor. SO YUM! We ate it with some roasted chicken.
This was nice and easy, I love it on spaghetti squash (which I sometimes use instead of pasta).

I liked the idea of it being made with almonds instead of pine nuts. I will definitely use this again, it was a nice change to pine. I used light OO. I didnt have fresh basil, so I used dried & was still good. Next time will try with fresh. I added this to cooked low carb ziti pasta and added fresh grated Romano cheese & grilled chicken. YUM!
This basic recipe was easy to build on. I used both basil and arugula, walnuts instead of almonds (untoasted) and I added some feta cheese. It turned out really well.

This was great! I did add Parm cheese and extra garlic. The cheese really gives it a much better flavor and adds a little something extra so the basil and nuts are not so over powering. I do like using almonds instead of pine nuts like some of the other recipes call for. :-)
Easy, turned out very good. Followed recipe exactly. (Except pan toasted Almonds) This will be my go to pesto recipe. I will try a double batch next time if I can grow enough basil.
Toasted the almonds over a gas stove burner In a heavy, dry pan. Almost skipped the nutmeg but it added a nice flavor level. Doubled the recipe and used the blender. Yum. Even the kids ate it.
Simple and easy to make.  I did the "Freezer trick" and froze a chunk, and then used it later.  It was like I'd just made it!  Fantastic recipe..thank you, Rebecca!
This is awesome!  I used pine nuts, but did not change anything else.  My husband and I both LOVED it!  Used it in the Penne with Chicken and Pesto recipe on here.  YUM!

I am a graduate Home Economist and have worked for two major food companies.  I was looking for an easy
quick recipe to use some of the basil growing in my yard.  This recipe, in my opinion, is incomplete and flawed.  It does not say what type of almonds to use - whole, slivered, chopped??  I had whole almonds with
skins on so I used them.  It says bake 10 min. at 450, I did 8 min. and they were close to too brown.  I used
1 garlic clove, not 3, and that would have been enough.  The result was a greenish brown sauce that we tried but it was largely uneatable.  I now know the almonds were the problem.  How hard would it be to list
the type of almonds to use?? Slivered, chopped, etc??  Very disappointing!

This was really good and very easy.  I usually have sliced almonds on hand, so I was glad the recipe included them instead of pine nuts.  I followed exactly except I added a handful of grated cheese to the mix. Very tasty!

This Pesto recipe was delicious! We made some adjestments, only used 2 garlic cloves, 1/4 cup of pinenuts, and 2 tbs of Parmesean cheese. Now we know what we will use the 20 basil plants in the garden for!! 

When storing pesto in the freezer, leave out any kind of cheese, Parmesan. If the pesto is frozen with it, the pesto will ferment.
This was really easy and taste great.  I made it to freeze for later.  Thanks for such a great recipe.
Awesome starter pesto! I did add 1/4,cup grated fresh Parmesan cheese and it was excellent! Even the kids enjoyed it!
YUM! It was delicious!  Did sub pine nuts for the walnuts and did throw in some parmesan...

This is a great basic pesto recipe- I use pine nuts and possibly any other nuts I have around (pecans). I also add parmesan cheese as I'm a big cheese fan. You can substitute water for some of the oil if you'd like a lower-fat version. Very versatile recipe!
I didn't even think I liked pesto...  Boy was I wrong.  This recipe was soooo tasty!  Will definitely be making this again!  I changed nothing in the recipe.

I tried using the oven to toast my almonds and that was a definite mistake.  My oven does not have a glass front on the door so I could not see how they were doing.  I am not sure if I over toasted the almonds or should have let them cool down more, but I could barely taste the basil when it all came together.  The toasted almonds took over the flavor.  Perhaps using pine nuts would be better because their flavor is not quite as strong.  Hopefully it will taste better after the flavors have had time to meld together.
Great recipe. I used it on Pesto Chicken Rolls. AMAZING!
I added a lot more garlic, a bit more olive oil, and a bit more salt and pepper. Put it on some French bread and toasted it. Came out great.

This was very easy to make and a good way to start using the basil from the herb garden I put in this year.  I liked it but the rest of the family was not impressed.  Maybe a little too much garlic for kids?  I made it and used it right away.  I wonder if the flavors would blend a bit more if next time I made it ahead of time.
Super Yummy! :)) I added a little 2 Tbsp of parmesean and it made it even better!

Very tasty.  My first time making pesto, so I chose the easiest recipe with the most basic ingredients. Even with all these variations, it tasted great and will I will make again, using this same base recipe.
This is the second pesto recipe I've tried on here and so far it's the best one yet.
Mmm super easy recipe!  Whenever I have leftovers, I put them in ice cube trays and freeze them.  That way, I can easily have pesto sauce anytime!
Great!  So ridiculously simple -- and I love how well almonds work in this recipe.  Will definitely make again!

This was really yummy Rebbecca.  Thanks!  I couldn't believe how fast it was and way cheaper and better tasting than the pre-made store bought stuff,  I wanted to make it lower in fat so I used 1/3 water to replace 2/3 the oil.  I suppose you could use lemon juice too but I loved it as made.  I served it over linguine with a bit of fresh shredded Parmesan cheese and some toasted pine nuts.  I made it twice.  It was better made with toasted pine nuts rather than almonds, although, both were great.
This was so easy and awesome!!!  Tossed with some fresh pasta, my whole family loved it and will be used often.

I have made this twice now and it is great. I've used it on pizza and pasta and it is fabulous and oh so easy. I usually double the recipe, but keep the oil amount the same and add additional oil as needed. Fabulous recipe!

This recipe was awesome.  The only change I would make is keep the oven at a lower temperature and watch your nuts!  They definitely don't take 10 minutes to toast, I had to throw the first batch out because they burned on me.   I also used one clove of garlic, I thought 3 would be a little overboard.
Super easy!  My husband loves pesto, and he said this was one of the best pestos he's ever eaten.

This was my second time making this in a short period of time as I currently have a plethora of fresh basil on my back deck. This recipe will be made again and again, as long as I have a basil crop.  Thanks again for this absolute winner.

This was so easy to put together.  I had to add some lemon basil because I didn't have enough of the regular.  It was great.  I would add more garlic and less oil next time. Thanks for a great recipe! Oh, I also added a little parmesean cheese 'cause I like it!

very good however: i used almonds already toasted form bj's, more than it says to.  more nutmeg than a pinch, some parm. cheese.  good if i have basil to use up. good over whole wheat spagetti, even matthew liked it (i didn't tell him what was in it) 7/09
It is true to its title - very easy! I think the garlic is a little much, so if you make that mistake and you find yours too garlicky, I added some lemon juice to cut the garlic flavor.
The pesto is great!  I loved the use of almonds instead of pine nuts, because that's what I had on hand.  I used the iron skillet to roast the almonds and that worked out fine.
The recipe was ok, but the nut taste is overpowering in this dish. Neither my husband or I enjoyed this. It was decent enough to eat because we already cooked it, but we would not make it again.

Awesome... I love something so simple and fresh tasting.  I put it in the "Pasta with pesto and scallops" from this site, (except I did portobellos and no scallops).  I ate so much I got a tummy ache. :)  I will never buy pesto sauce or paste again!

I had doubts about this at first. The aroma coming out of the food processor wasn't good. But once I added some extra garlic and lemon juice and made it into a cream sauce it was delicious. I would experiment with adding more things to the mix. I suspect this is meant to be a base recipe a cook can customize to his or her taste.
I'm not a pesto fan as a rule but needed it for a recipe. This was awesome! I did add about 2-3 tblspns of cheeses (fontinella) as others suggested. Would def make again!

I LOVE THIS!!  My only 2 strays from the recipe were that I toasted the almonds stove-top and added a bit of shaved parmesan cheese to the food processor.  The whole thing takes 10 minutes!  *FYI this recipe makes enough for 1 lb of pasta.  Thanks Rebecca for a keeper!!

I had a ton of basil that I needed to use up.  It doesn't tolerate cold at all, so it's streching it to keep it into October in Minnesota.  I was struggling to choose a recipe, so I decided to try three different pesto recipes from this site.  In A-typical allrecipes fashion I actually stuck exactly to each recipe so that we could truly judge them fairly.  The recipes were Easy Pesto by Rebecca Jane Thompson, Pesto Sauce by Sara, and Simple Garlic and Basil Pesto by FuzzyGreenMonkey.  My favorite was Easy Pesto.  It had a nice nutty flavor because of the toasted almonds.  It's also nice if you don't have much basil on hand because it uses half as much as the other recipes.  My husband liked Simple Garlic and Basil Pesto the best, it was my close second.  The parmesan cheese and pine nuts really make that recipe.  We both agreed that by far our least favorite was Pesto Sauce.  It was very bland compared to the other two.  I would attribute that to the 1 1/2 cups of walnuts.  I would not recommend that recipe at all.  It was a fun experiment and the other two recipes will go into my permanant file.
Great recipe! It´s super easy and delicious.
1st pesto I have made & it was fantastic!

I also added a couple of tablespoons parmesan simply because I love cheese and to cut down on the bite of the garlic. Excellent recipe!! I added 1/4 cup of parmesan cheese and it turned out FANTASTIC!  My guest and family LOVED it! I highly recommend this recipe for something quick,easy and healthy! Tastes great with the fresh basil from the farmer's Market.

Wow!  Do I like this recipe!  It's quick and yummy.   Just the thing to do with a handful of fresh basil straight from the farmer's market. I simply toasted slivered almonds on a hot, dry skillet until lightly toasted and fragrant.  Forget the oven!

Love this recipe!!!

Easy and delicious.  I prepared it according to recipe.  I tried to cut down the olive oil, but you need the full 1/2 cup to get the proper consistency.  After trying it, I did add some lemon juice, but it was still fantastic before I added it - the lemon juice just gave a little zing.

Wow, this is a great recipe!

This was the first time I have made pesto.  This recipe is easy to use and yeilds delicious results!  A must have for simple pasta dinners.

This is a very nice pesto! I have always used expensive pine nuts :(, but almonds and nutmeg really work! Yummy!!!! This is so very good. I took the other reviewers advice and just toasted the almonds in a dry skillet. Yummy!  This was the first pesto sauce that I've ever made and it turned out fabulous!  I thought that the nutty flavor of the almonds overpowered the basil and garlic, but it still tasted great.

Super easy super yummy pesto!!!
Great Pesto sauce but I did not toast the almonds.
Very good! I added a little bit of lemon juice and decreased the amount of olive oil.

This is the first time I ever made pesto and this was very good.  I liked that it did not require those expensive pine nuts.  Next time, more garlic!  I used three little guys; should have used three big guys.  Cloves that is, ha!  I used this over thin spaghetti tossed with shrimp & peas.  Yummy dinner!

Love that it uses Almonds instead of pinenutes. I doubled it and added a tablespoon and a half of parmesan cheese. Love it!  And so easy. I also toasted the almonds on a dry skillet on the stove top. Much easier then turning the oven on.  Enjoy!

This was very good, but I suggest to use 2 cloves of garlic instead of 3. I'm a garlic lover, but even this was too garlicky for me. I also added parmesan cheese and a small tomato for more flavor. Overall, this is a good pesto.
So easy and so good! I added a wee bit more salt but otherwise it was PERFECT!
For my first attempt at making pesto this recipe was a winner!  It was very easy.  I think I will take some of the suggestions from the others and try a new modification next time.

Really good! I used a whole box of bow-tie pasta and wasn't sure the sauce would cover it all but it did! I added a little water just to make sure. ot was very easy and quick to make.
