If you are making this for a "party" crowd, go ahead and use the 3:1 ratio, which would be 46 oz juice and 2 cups coconut rum.  For hard-core drinkers, just leave the cocunut rum bottle out and they can pour extra rum into their drink.  Delicious!
this has been my " drink" for years always just refer to it as malibu and pineapple though i don;t like coconut but love this
We call this drink a sponge bob and we add pineapple chunks and cherries very pretty and good (if you would like you can also add some 7-up like the previous review)
So good and super easy!  This has quickly become one of my favorite drinks!
I've made this several times but also add pineapple sherbet and mix it all in the blend.  Makes it into a nice frozen drink.

This was quick and easy. It is a great summer time punch. Always well received. My husband really enjoyed it. I actually like it better using a pineapple concentrate and then using sparkling water to reconstitute it.
Yummy. I used dried herbs instead of fresh. Good color & consistency. Nice basic sauce.

I made this with a few changes. I added 1 can of tomato sauce, decreased water to 1 and 1/2 cups, used olive oil instead of vegetable oil, added 1 clove of minced garlic, added dried basil. When sauce had thickened I added homemade meatballs. I poured the sauce over cooked rigatoni pasta, topped with grated pecorino/romano cheese, topped cheese with 3 slices of mozzarella cheese and baked for 20 minutes in 350 degree oven. This was delicious.

this was a great base recipe. I had already processed a bunch of tomatoes to wind up with about 4 cups of sauce so I followed this recipe to wind up with a tasty sauce. the only real difference I made was to toss in a quarter cup of red wine. No tomato paste, it thickened on its own.

Full rich bodied flavour, love it.   I did as other readers suggested and added oregano, cut down the water to 1.5 cups, added a carrot to cut down acidity  and added 1/4 tsp red pepper flakes.  I didn't have fresh basil so I used 1 tbsp. dried.  Didn't have any celery so I used 1/8 tsp celery seed. Awesome sauce.  Thank you for sharing!!!
Use half a tablespoon of sugar, olive oil, and one bay leaf
Very easy to make. Instead of vegetable oil, I used olive oil. I also had to add sugar to cut down on the acidity. Next time I'm going to add peppers and parsley for a change. Thanks for the receipe!
This was really easy to throw together and tasted great. I sauteed the garlic with the onion and added basil, oregano and a pinch of sugar. I also used 1/2 c. wine instead of some of the water.

I used extra virgin olive oil instead of vegetable oil.  I also saute minced garlic, celery, onion and carrots in oil before adding the rest of the ingredients.  I alway add a bay leaf while simmering (don't forget to remove before serving)!  I use this sauce at least once a week.  Somtimes I double the recipe and freeze what is left for the next dish.
Quick and easy sauce that tastes great!
Delicious sauce and very easy. I was surprised to find it had a lot of flavor. I used olive oil instead of vegetable, but followed the recipe exactly otherwise.
Just missing some mushrooms (I love them) but still perfect - what I was looking for!
This sauce was very good!  The only substitution that I made was olive oil instead of vegetable oil.
Excellent  recipe. Substituted beef broth for the water, also added fresh tyme.

Very delicious sauce. This was my first attempt at making homemade sauce and this was the perfect recipe. I took the advice of previous reviewers and used EVOO instead of vegetable oil, and I added probably 2Tbs of sugar to cut down on the acidity, I actually might add a bit more. It was perfection. I can't wait to make some stuffed shells to use this with.
Couldn't be much simpler to make and tastes fresh and delicious.  It is very like the sauce my late Italian mother in law used to make and she was a fantastic cook.

I just made this last night for dinner with Sweet Honey French Bread (from this site). It was SUPER easy which cannot be said for most spaghetti sauce recipes. I used oregano instead of bay leaves (didn't have any) and olive oil instead of vege oil (as per reviews). I also added a tablespoon of white sugar for the bitterness and simmered mine for about an hour and a half, covered. The recipe didn't yield much (I know, I let mine cook down A LOT) but it was yummy! It was a perfect, sweet, tomato sauce...so simple that you could really appreciate each flavor. Will make again in large quantities to freeze :)
This recipe is delicious exactly as written. I make it almost weekly during the winter. The sauce also makes a great base for additions. I especially enjoy adding hot italian sausage. Mmm.

This sauce is a snap to prepare and tastes great.  I added a little sugar and oregano.  I simmered it for about an hour, but would have cooked it even longer if I hadn't been so hungry.  The recipe made plenty of sauce for my family of five.  I'm sure it will be even better tomorrow!  I used it to top Three Cheese Manicotti.
Tastes like my mother's Sunday sauce!  I made it with Italian sausage, sliced and browned in the pan as the first step.  Awesome!
Very good basic recipe that can be altered to suit your tastes. I used only 1.5 cups water, which made it the perfect consistency for me.
I enjoyed this, but my boyfriend found it to be a bit bitter, so I added some sugar.

An excellent recipe, very easy to make and absolutely exquisite! We used extra virgin olive oil instead of the vegetable oil.
Thanks for the great recipe!
used on top of meatballs and pasta with grated cheese and it was lovely

This is a good, basic sauce.  Made some minor adjustments based on my taste:  Substituted extra virgin olive oil, and added a 1/2 tbsp brown sugar to cut acidity.  Also added about a tsp of dried oregano (I like the added flavor).

I had a lot of random ingredients in my pantry that I wanted to make a meal out of, and this was the perfect dish to make! 
I used vegetable oil. Added a pinch of sugar like some others suggested. Upped the salt from 1 tsp to 2 tsp. I also added in a 1/2 cup of chopped green pepper because it was going to go bad in the fridge, but it tastes great. Also, mixing parm in was a good call.
Will make again!

This sauce never fails. I do it almost every week and it is amazing how consistently good it remains. Follow the exact recipe with the same quantities and you are up to a very simple yet very delicious sauce. It is even better than what you usually get served in restaurants.

Great base recipe! I used canned whole roma tomatoes and crushed them with my hands. Make sure you use a good brand of tomatos, preferably imported from Italy--it makes a difference. I only used 1 cup of water. As many others did, I used olive oil, added oregano, red pepper flakes, fresh parsley and a whole carrot(removed at end).

I made this yesterday and was going to rate it four stars.  I served it over thin spaghetti and it was very good.  Today I took the leftover sauce, "smoothed" it in the processor, and served it over cheese ravioli.  WOW!  The flavors blended overnight, and the slight bite of the black pepper was even better than my favorite Italian restaurant.  My grandmother was northern Italian and grandfather was southern Italian, so I grew up with Italian cooking.  Definitely the key to this sauce is using fresh basil and fresh garlic and yes, I altered the recipe and used olive oil.  Easy, simple, delicious!  Great recipe!
Delicious! This recipe is great for a first time sauce maker. My Italian sorority sisters gave their seal of approval.

Very good. I agree it does need a bit of sugar. I felt I needed to remove the basil and garlic. Next time I'll finely chop them and leave them in. I will take the last reviewer's advice and use more basil next time.

I'm very excited I finally made spaghetti sauce and it was excellent, I did use olive oil instead of vegetable oil .My family loved this sauce, will definitely continue to use this recipe. Next time I will add mushrooms
Very good sauce, and easy.  I used Olive Oil instead, added basil and thyme to taste, and some crushed red pepper!!
Exactly what I was looking for.

Like the others, I used olive oil instead of vegetable oil, and I also added a tablespoon of sugar to cut the acidity.  I added small, uncooked pieces of stew beef, and some uncooked meatballs that I threw together.  I put the heat on extra low and let it cook for about 4 hours.  The sauce was great.  I think adding uncooked beef or sausage gives it an extra good flavor.

Made it this morning to use in a chili recipe later today.  Realized I was out of canned sauce and didn't want to drive to the grocery store.  Figured my grandmother didn't have that luxury, so I got innovative.  Fortunately I had most of the ingredients listed here ... and the Internet!  I took the suggestion of adding 2 carrots instead of sugar, and a dried bay leaf in place of fresh basil.  Excellent results.  Will make again if needed.  Fortunately this happened over a weekend, as I might have passed during the work week.

I thought this sauce tasted wonderful, but I couldn't find any basil or Parsley so I had to leave it with any real flavors. But I would cut down on the amount of water to just one cup, it came out more like a stew than a sauce. Another thing is that I didn't have a can of crushed tomatoes so I used about a kilo of fresh tomatoes, skinned but not seeded, I suggest to have more than a kilo, maybe about a kilo and a half, and put them in a blender for two or three seconds, so you have a smoother sauce.

This was very good. I don't eat meat so I needed a sauce that didn't use any bacon, pork, beef or chicken. I followed a tip offered in one of the other reviews and added 2 peeled and split carrots. This did cut the acidity.  I might  throw in a pinch of sugar but only because I like my sauce a little on the sweet side. I substituted 2 tbsp of olive oil for the vegetable oil. Thanks Mirella Cina this will be my sauce for life.
I used a couple of tips from other reviewers: used olive oil, added a bay leaf while cooking, added two carrots cut in half while cooking, used a bit less water. Turned out great!

I make this sauce quite similar. The difference in mine is I use extra virgin olive oil,I'm guessing about 1/2 tablespoon of oregano, and I use a bay leaf instead of basil leaves. I also cut 2 carrots cut in half and just throw them in the sauce. That cuts down on the acidity without having to add sugar and then you can easily remove them. Sometimes we throw in a hot red pepper to give it some heat. This sauce is the traditional sauce my mom and sisters have cooked for years that we've all carried on from my Nonna and we're all Italian. Thanks for this one.
Turned out great with just the right amount of spice. I added less water for a thicker sauce. A definate keeper.
Taste great and very easy to prepare

Very good sauce! I used all ingredients in the recipe and just added a tablespoon of oregano, 2 bay leaves, and a couple of carrots (for added sugar to cut acidity--took out at the end of cooking) and some red pepper flakes. The recipe is good just as it is though. I just felt like "playing" a little and was thrilled with the outcome.  A definite keeper! Thank you so very much!

Pretty good, this is what I did..I added more basil then asked for and also added some fresh parsley i didnt have a can of crushed tomatoes so i used chopped tomatoes and decided to run them through the blender since i dont really like chunks in my sauce. I added lots and lots of garlic powder, garlic salt, and crushed red peppers, and of course I added the sugar as well. I mixed this sauce with some ground beef over some angel hair pasta...yummy! My roommates ate it all up!
Very close to authentic Italian sauce, but you need to add lots of fresh basil and use ONLY olive oil.  A tiny bit of sugar is needed to cut down the acidity.
I used a 2 cans of paste because I doubled the recipe.  Great sauce!  I also added two tbs of sugar
simplicity at its best. just what i was looking for.

I, too, used extra virgin olive oil.  I also put in some carrots and celery.  I used white wine instead of the water.  I also added beef cubes and a couple of boneless pork chops.  I don't like my sauce with "chunks" of stuff in it, so I ran it through a seive - it came out delicious.  I usually make my own sauce using tomato puree.  This was a nice change of pace.  Thanks!

I made it with olive oil instead of vegetable oil, I doubled the garlic, added a pinch of sugar, used dried basil along with oregano, herbs de Provence, and 2 bay leaves. I sautéed the onions and garlic in a little extra olive oil (besides the 1/4 cup that goes into the sauce) and then put the onions and garlic along with all the rest of the ingredients in the crockpot along with 20 frozen meatballs from Costco. Cooked on low for 6 hours. Toward the end I put it on high and cracked the lid a little to thicken it up. I think I would do the same next time, although you could play around with using a little less water. It only took about a half an hour to thicken up and I cooked noodles in that time. Anyway, super delicious! I will not go back to sauce in a jar.
This is the best tomato sauce I have ever tasted! It is very rich and tasty.  For a more authentic taste, I added 3 tablespoons of balsamic vinegar and used olive oil as well.  It was lovely.
Great little sauce, used seasoning salt.
Great recipe! I use EVOO and much more fresh basil, and add a pinch of sugar and comes out perfect!

I've always wanted to make my own and this was really good sauce. My husband said it tastes so good, his Italian father (who has always made his gravy from scratch) would be proud. I did tweak it as suggested by Prendila, carrots, oregano and bay. Will definitely use this again, maybe adding sausage or meatballs for other flavors. Thanks!!!
I cooked for hours and hours on low and it was think and tasty!
i was looking for a simple sauce to serve with meatballs for my picky family. this was super easy and they loved it. i'll never buy jar sauce again!
Nice basic sauce

This recipe is great, but I made a few changes 

- I used Olive Oil instead of Vegetable Oil.
When I put the onions in to brown, I also put the garlic in at the same time to brown that as well.
Instead of using a can of crushed tomatoes, I used roughly 28 ounces of whole tomatoes. I peeled the tomato skins off and blended the tomatoes into a blender. 
I also grated a little bit of fresh Parmesan over the saucepan while the sauce was cooking, added a little bit of parsley, as well as a small amount of sugar to balance the flavors.
After the sauce was finished simmering, I took a mesh strainer and strained the sauce. 

This was my first attempt ever at making homemade sauce but it was very smooth and tasted amazing. Definitely going to be making it again. :)

Wonderful recipe to make and then freeze for use in the winter. I make several batches and after thawed and heating, add cooked sausage, mushrooms, etc. Vegetable stands will usually sell you their seconds(some bruises on them) at a cheap price and work perfectly for the sauce. I also add salt and pepper, oregano and thyme after the first two hours. Also, a tsp of sugar.
Nice flavor. Too thin
not for nothing but "the real thing" would be using the fresh grown roma tomatoes in my back yard.  now you've got the real thing.
I used tomato sauce instead of crushed tomatoes.  The sauce is a little tangy but if you are using it with a very cheesy dish that is fine.  I added more pepper to tone down the tanginess.
great recipe! I also used olive oil and added some fennel seed and added sugar. i may yry a carrot stick as someone mentioned. it was incredibly thick! loved it!
too much pepper although i did forget to add the water so i'll try again again and keep updated cause otherwise very good
I hate to give this a 3, but I can't say if it was really good or not because I used this in a recipe which was disgusting.  But it was easy.

I may just be spoiled by dining out and/or commercial sauces, but this recipe didn't do much for me. I used virgin olive oil, Tspn sugar, fresh crushed  roma tomatos, fresh basil leaves(cut up), 1.75 water, white onion, fresh ground pepper, & salt substitute. Even adding parm cheese & italian seasoning only improved it some. But, as others have said, its EASY to make.
I really like this recipe.  I also used olive oil in place of vegetable oil.  It is definitely better than the recipe I had been using.

I love this sauce. It is super easy and all the ingredients blend nicely together. I'm fairly picky about tomato sauce and I've never been able to find a recipe I truly like until now. My husband and kids love it too!
This was a simple and easy recipe to use i added some crushed red peppers to add a little bite to it.
I didn't add tomatoes because I hate them. I used tomato paste only. And I use olive oil rather than vegetable oil. Very good.
Made this the other day and used it for a salsa recipe.  Excellent but time consuming but well worth it!  Thank you for sharing it and will do it again!

I liked it.  Was in the mood for a new sauce and wanted it smooth, so after sautéing the onions and garlic (in olive oil), I threw them in the blender and back in the pan.  I also pureed the tomatoes before throwing them in with the onions.  I agree with others that it needed sugar and a lot more basil.  I also added a splash of balsamic and some sugar.  Came out great.  4 stars because of the needed modifications, but it really was good.
After trying so many recipes I found great luck with this one. Light and delicious...thanks

Simple and inexpensive to make. never buy jar sauce again.
Instead of frsh basil, I used 1 tbls of dried basil and 1/2 tsp pepper. It was to hot using 1 tsp of pepper. I also added a home made chopped red roasted pepper. in a day or 2 it will have the taste of a roasted  red pepper sauce.

It took me a couple of tries to get this right. I use 4 cloves of garlic instead of 2, omit the tomato paste and only use about 1/4 cup of water. I also use dried basil instead of fresh basil. This sauce has become a normal dinner dish in my house with a few tweeks.
Great recipe!  I added some sugar to cut some of the acidity and a little crushed red pepper along with a few more herbs.  This was one of those "CAN I HAVE EXTRA BREAD PLEASE" sauces!
Very easy and tasty.  I added fresh garlic and red pepper flakes for a little more kick.

This is a very good base for a sauce. You can add what you like depending on you and your family's taste! Put this over my tortellini. Sooooo yummy. 
I used olive oil instead of vegetable and dried basil leaves instead of fresh. I dropped in a bay leaf, added 1 or 2 tbsp sugar, 1/4 tsp Rosemary, 1/4 tsp thyme and  1/4 tsp garlic powder.

Delicious as is!  Next time I might use a little more salt, and perhaps a bit of sugar as it seemed to be missing just that little something.  That said, I could make it just the way it is again. My Italian Hubby loved it!
I love to make this sauce it's easy an great taste just like my grandmother's.

Easy to make and a nice basic tomato sauce. The flavor was really nice, although I used dried basil and did add about 1/4 cup grated parmesan cheese. Also, used extra virgin olive oil instead of vegetable oil...better flavor. The only thing I would change next time is to add a little less water because I prefer a slightly thicker sauce. All in all, really good!

Wonderful! I cooked mine with olive oil, a pound of beef, a couple of bay leaves, & Parmesan cheese. And I let it simmer in a slow cooker instead of on top of the stove. As soon as I added enough seasonings, it was just pperrfect!
So simple and a nice addition to a holiday party.  Also great in coffee.
It was as good as it looks, a big hit at the party!

If not for the candy cane, the drink would have lacked flavor and pizzazz.  I could barely detect any alcohol, much less the peppermint schnapps.  It was only when the candy cane started to melt in the glass that I could  taste peppermint.  Sure,  I could have added more schnapps, but I just couldn't get into it enough to start tweaking.
Delicious!  Don't use more than a splash of grenadine though.  Too much and it looks like pepto bismal.
I scaled it down to one, using a jigger each of the peppermint schnapps and creme de cacao and a splash of half-n-half and grenadine. Delicious!
Absolutely amazing! This was a big hit at a party. So yummy!

I made this recipe the first time and it came out ok.  I thought about it and read the other reviews and made it again with a couple of changes and it came out PERFECT!
I cooked the sugar/water/corn syrup mixture over low like it says, I stirred it CONSTANTLY until it reached 110 degrees. 
The second change I made was I melted my chocolate BEFORE I added it to the sugar  mixture and I reduced the almond extract to 3/4 tsp.
I then stirred the mixture until it cooled slightly to the consistancy I wanted to pour.
These changes gave me a smooth and shiny finished product that went over my tiny cakes beautifully.
When I use it on things bigger than petits fours I will first give my cakes a crumb coating of buttercream frosting.  This gives the fondant a smoother and prettier finish.

I love this recipe if you make sure to not overcook the chocolate, or it loses the shine a bit.  Overall though, if you just get it to a pourable consistency it works out just fine.  Can be a little hard to spread evenly though so try to pour over flat even surfaces and lay down a layer of frosting first to help even out the fondant and help it stick.
I have tried this recipe but it does not work..the fondant was thick but when i pour it on the cake it start to fall from sides...it does not stands on the cake and does not form a layer :/..

I'm actually wavering between three and four stars for this recipe.  I used a candy thermometer and was shocked at how far over 92 degrees I had to heat this fondant up.  Eventually though, it seemed ready and I used it to pour over my son's cake.  It looked fine until I noticed that a lot of it was clear with fine granules of chocolate in it, which gave the appearance, at first glance, of opacity.  Ultimately, I figured nobody was going to be examining the fondant that closely, so I didn't toss out the fondant or my cake.  The consistency and pourability was just great.  When I tasted it, though, I felt that there may have been some undissolved granules... I can't be sure, though, since I used some colored sugars on the cake also.  I'm not the most skilled at recipes like this, so the shortcomings in my success may be my own fault.
This works pretty well. I found that by waiting for the fondant to cool down a bit before pouring help with consistency.

Worked well the first time and served my purpose as a coating for some chocolate dessert bars. I didn't use a thermometer, but heated the mixture just barely enough to melt the chocolate and keep it pourable.
This is a great chocolate frosting - very easy and nice to pour over a double-layer cake.  It's very sweet, but also very delicious.  Thanks for sharing the recipe!

This fondant was not what I was expecting. Maybe I didn't get it to the right temp, but it was thick, and didn't pour. It also ended up crystalizing very quickly, and I had to throw the batch away! Maybe I need a new candy thermometer?
I used dark chocolate & it turned out perfectly! Thank you!

Did not taste like chocolate and was not smooth but chalky texture. I used a instant read thermometer with an alarm so I know the moment it got it to temp. Will be deleted from my my list. Used a chocolate mirror glaze perfect!
the chocolate doesn't ever melt so that it's uniformly brown, but rather white with brown speckles.  Tastes fine, but I won't use this again.

I use this recipe for petit fours and it works really well to coat the sides. The first time I made it I was careful with the temperature but now I just stir it until it gets to be the right consistency. It works just fine if you overheat it by a little bit but it won't dry with the same shine. Great recipe!
I found this to be a great recipe for covering a cake maybe, but for petit fours, I had to add some milk to it to thin it out a bit. I didn't find it thin enough to pour over petit fours.
This soup has a very smooth, unique, and delicious flavour! My husband and I loved it!

I made this the other day and it blew me away it was very simple but had incredible flavor. The only thing I would do is add 1/2 lb of bacon or small ham cubes to get a little more hardy and satisfying soup. this is going in my favorites immediately. :]

Decent recipe but is quite liquidy. I added more broccoli & cauliflower to thicken it up, along with quinoa. Also substituted the crushed peppers for a jalapeño to get some extra green in the soup without disturbing the heat.
As a lover of strong flavors I found this to be far too bland.  It had a nice texture but needs some work.
So, after everyone stopped complaining about having a dish with Cauliflower, everyone liked it. However, this recipe only yields four soup bowls about 3/4 full. But was a good dish. We'll do again.
Tasty soup. I changed things up a bit namely making way more than the original recipe (guessing on ingredient amounts) and omitting the cream. I will definitely be making this one again!
Fantastic.  Who knew these ingredients will combine so well.  I left out the cream as I am vegan and didn't miss it.  I will make it again and again.

I didn't bother with the cream and I added 2 small chopped sweet potatoes and some spicy peanut dressing, and dropped the cauliflower.  The added sweet potatoes recieved compliments.  Be careful not to cook the broccoli too long, as it will get mushy (still good though)
It is okay if you have some broccoli and cauliflower that you need to use for something.
This  soup is easy to make and beautiful to eat! Great with chopped up chicken in it too. My three year old loves it  too :)

I'm doing a Candida cleanse and this recipe is so far my fav of the 26 I pulled from my recipe box.  The only switches I made are almond butter, veg stock and coconut milk for the cream.  Amazing flavor.  Going to make a double recipe soon and add more red pepper flakes and perhaps a bit of curry?

I didn't have quite enough nut butter so I'm looking forward to making it again with the right amount! I didn't use the flour  because after the soup was finished I whizzed it all up with a hand blender, which made it very creamy and thick.
This is a lovely soup and is going in my rotation. Thank you for the recipe!
Also, I would like to say that I don't understand the mind set of someone who changes a recipe a lot and then gives it 3 stars. Seems petty to me. Why not make it as is  first? At least then your rating would be an honest one.

This soup doesn't sound like it would taste very good but because of the reviews, I tried. I've made this several times now and followed the recipe to the T (ok, except for the butter which I suspect the tsp is a typo) as well as made it with ingredients I have on hand. I think my favorite way was when I only used the broccoli and added carrots .  This soup is delicious. My husband is not a fan of soups and this one he had a bowl of of and liked!!

What a great soup.  I wouldn't have thought of broccoli and peanut butter together, but this really works.  The pepper flakes add just the right amount of flavor. I needed a tablespoon of butter rather than a teaspoon.

This was surprisingly good.  It was tasty, spicy, and lo-cal, a triple win.  I used 1 tbl of butter instead of tsp, I think that may be a typo.  Also, I skipped the cream and green onion.  I may try blending the soup next time to increase the "creamy" factor.
This was refreshing.  If serving to guests I recommend using white grape juice for a  better presentation.
I put this on meatballs, and it was fine. However, the amount of vinegar was too strong for us.
This is wonderful!  Not too sweet - not too rich - just right!  The recipe made just enough to frost 24 cupcakes.

Wow- how easy is this! I didn't use water, didn't need it. You could add strong coffee for a mocha flair though. I liked the fudgy texture and it isn't very sweet. If you need sweeter I would add a little sugar while melting the chocolate. For those who said it was bitter or not the right consistency, they need to read the label to make sure they are using sweetened condensed milk, NOT Evaporated milk. I think some people don't realize they are different. Evaporated milk is just that, thick milk, not sweetened. This is very good on brownies!
Totally delicious!  A bit time consuming with all the stirring, but worth it in the end.  Thick and fudgy, I'll definitely use this again.

A rich, less sweet, thick icing that is quick and easy, has a nice gloss to it and spreads beautifully. Don't freak if it looks awful the first few minutes you are cooking it. Mine looked like it was separating until about 4 minutes in.

I created an Allrecipes account just to comment on this.  This frosting is incredible, and I am insanely picky about my frostings.  Cook this until it is like a thick pudding, and it turns into the perfect cake-frosting consistency.  Tastes like a bar of Hershey's chocolate, it takes all of my willpower to refrain from eating it by itself.

Notes: I used twice the vanilla, and strong brewed coffee instead of water and it is divine.

Perfectly fudgey and rich, like ganache or chocolate fudge. I've made tis twice and it has come out fantastic both times. Set perfectly, you just need to follow directions and make sure you have the correct ingredients. I did make a few substitutions the second time around. I used fat free sweetened condensed milk and did not have any baking chocolate, so I added 6tbs cocoa powder, 6tbs sugar, and 2tbs butter as a replacement. It still came out perfectly.
Spreads nicely, not too sweet, just right.

While this "frosting" had a nice taste, not being too sweet like other sugar based frostings, I would not classify this as a "frosting" at all.  This is more like a sauce (and not even a glaze).  My cake tastes good, but it's now soaked.
I would consider making some significant adjustments to the quanitities of ingredients used if you're hoping for something thicker (like no water and doubling the chocolate).  Chilling overnight before using made little difference.

I've been making this frosting since the '60s as it was in my mother's [Good Housekeeping] cookbook. It is perfect every time, creamy, fudgy. I don't know how you could make a mistake, unless you don't know the difference between evaporated milk and condensed milk. And there are no instructions needed. It's the best frosting/fudge topping anywhere. never hardens always creamy!

This was fantastic and super easy.  I followed the recipe and it worked wonderfully, yummy & just the right thickness for frosting.  If you follow the directions, you won't have any trouble.  I did use hersheys unsweetened cocoa powder instead of squares, the measurements are on the back of the cocoa can for this common substitution.

I would definitely use this recipe again, but I feel it's more suited to bar cookies/brownies rather than a cake.  I put it on a home made butter cake and it was good, but not quite as soft as I would have liked.  I do believe it would be excellent on brownies!

I was looking for something that didn't require powdered sugar because I don't have any and didn't want to run to the store. This did the trick! Super easy and very tasty. The consistency isn't quite what you would expect for a frosting, but it's close enough and is perfect for my red velvet poke cake. Don't forget the salt...I tried it without and then added it, and it actually made a world of difference. Yummy...thanks.

In all fairness, I only made this once. I cooked it for 12 minutes, stirring frequently.  It has the consistancy of water. I didn't get to the point where one is suppose to add the water or the vanilla as I knew it was a bust.  I don't think I did anything incorrectly so I won't be trying to make this again. Sweetened condensed milk comes out of the can very thick, and when you cook it, it gets even thicker.   As you cook and stir it, the condensed milk starts sticking to the sides of the pan....keep stirring, and you will know when the consistency is right.  It took me about 7 minutes, but that is a bit variable depending on cookware, range temp, etc.  Adding the water at then end made the mixture smoother without watering it down.  What you are doing here is basically making a soft candy. The best part of this recipe is that you can spread it while it is warm (not hot) on to a warm cake, and it doesn't run.  For me, this made a very thick icing that I probably could have piped with had I let it cool all the way.  
**Because sweetened condensed milk is already thick and gooey when you open the can, reviews describing something being watery should be ignored.  Most likely those cooks used evaporated milk or tried to substitute regular milk, which is watery in the can.  There isn't any possible way to take a can of sweetened condensed milk and cook it until it is watery---there isn't any science behind that.

This Frosting is great. I have used this frosting for about 3 years now on my German Chocolate Cakes and it always turn out great. Here's what I do for the perfect frosting. 

First of all I use it on a 2 layer 9 inches round cake so I have to double the recipe because as it is written, it is not enough frosting for a 2 layer 9 inch cake.  I beat together the milk and egg yolks in medium saucepan, and then I stir in the sugar and butter. I stir with my whisk until the butter has melted, and then I put on my timer for 20 minutes. I continue to cook and stir my frosting over medium heat.  When the 20 minute timer goes off, I remove it from the heat and then I add my vanilla, coconuts and pecans.  Then I let the mixture rest for about 15 to 20 minutes before I try to spread it on my cake.  You will notice that when you take the frosting off the heat it will be a little runny but after you add the coconuts and pecans and let it rest it will thicken up.  If 20 minutes is not long enough for your frosting to thicken just let it rest until it gets to room temperature. You have to let the frosting rest for a while so it can thicken. Now you are ready to spread the frosting over the cake.  I hope this helps.

I didn't have yeas on hand to make my regular pizza dough, so I tried this one. It came out excellent and it's delicious!

Keeper! Very good!  After mixing up the dough, I let it rest wrapped in sprayed plastic wrap.  The dough rolled out so nice, I was able to roll it very thin, next time I would roll even thinner.   I heated the oven and a pizza stone to 450 for 30 minutes while making up the dough.   I placed the rolled out dough on parchment paper, did not pre-bake and topped with sauce, cheese and pepperoni.  Baked for 10 minutes at 450.  
This made one pizza, that was inhaled - next time I will double or triple the recipe.  Thanks for this quick and easy recipe.
Half the recipe to make a small one for myself. Very good, definitely will make again. I didn't prebake the crust, just added on the toppings and put in 400 degree oven.
I made this since it didn't call for yeast and I had the other ingredients. It's a pretty good pizza crust, but I had to add extra water since it was too dry to even stick together.
Love this crust after the additions of Parmesan cheese, garlic powder and oregano! This will be my pizza crust from now on!
This was amazing. Thin and crispy and incredibly easy, I'm 14 and this was quick and simple for me to make by myself!
I've made this several times and am so happy as to how it turned out! It's a great, quick pizza recipe and when rolled out thin makes for a perfect, crisp thin crust pizza. Thanks!

This recipe is great for thin crust as well as flat bread. The only change that I made was adding a little more flour when I rolled out the dough, because the dough is very sticky , even after rising. I also did add seasonings right before I threw it in the oven to bake off the crust , and then let it rest for about 15 minutes before I added the toppings. I made a lovely loaded potato pizza and the girlfriend loved it. I would definitely use this recipe again.
Great recipe.  We like a thin cracker type pizza crust and I think this one is great!
Turned out great as written!

This pizza dough was quick & easy. It was easy to roll out too. My husband liked it but thought it was a little too biscuit like in texture. I will use again because it is a good dough to use when you don't have a lot of time. I did add garlic & Italian seasoning to the dough mixture for flavor. Overall it made a good pizza in a short time. Thanks for sharing your recipe.
I loved this, super easy and taste perfect. I doubled the dough and had enough for another pizza. Thanks for the share.

I made this crust, I added garlic powder and Italian seasoning. Also used buttermilk. The crust was great  I had no trouble rolling it out. For the toppings I followed the recipe for hummus pizza on this site instead of using red sauce spread hummus on the crust. It tasted fantastic   Baked at 475 degrees for 10 minutes.  This a wonderful crust. I like that this recipe only calls for 1/12 cups of flour compared to others that are 3 or 4 cups. Who needs those extra calories.              Trixy

I used gluten free flour to make this.  I had to add a bit more milk to it and I should have added even more.  It was a tad dry.  Also, I found it did not make enough.  Double the recipe.  It is good though.  It just needed a bit of adjustment for me.  It could be due to the type of flour or that we live in FL.  We used the dough to make a simple stromboli.  I adjusted the cooking directions to just 1 time in the oven (with stuffing) at 375 degrees for 30 minutes.  It could have gone a few more minutes but was good.
Made it as last second bread sticks... It came out fantastic! Added Parmesan cheese and brushed garlic Parmesan butter and dill on top before baking... Will defiantly make again!
I really liked this crust, easy to make, was just slightly dry and biscuit like.   Thanks Missy!

Quick, easy, and works great when you decide at the last minute to make pizza for supper and don't have time to prepare yeast dough! I think could use a tad bit more salt, but otherwise a wonderful recipe.

This is by far the easiest and best no yeast pizza crust I have ever used!!  Follow the recipe for a no fail, light and soft/crisp crust.  I add Italian seasoning, garlic powder and greated parmesan cheese right into the flour mix.  If you do this you will want to add a Tbsp extra of milk.
My husband, nephew, sister-in-law and father-in-law loved this recipe! I added a teaspoon of garlic powder and Italian seasoning to the dough. We didn't have any left over.
VERY easy & delicious thin crust for pizza. I added some seasonings and brushed some garlic butter over the dough prior to baking. Turned out GrEaT!
This pizza crust was ideal because it was easy on short time and deliciously eaten up~!
No only is it great for pizza, but I made mozzarella sticks with it! Also if you add a little brown sugar to it, it makes a great pie crust! So yummy. Thank you for posting it!
quick and easy...i highly recommend the tip of baking it for a while before adding the toppings...did the trick!  thank you!
Really easy really tasty
It made a very tasty crust but even when I doubled the recipe, it was barely enough for one pizza...

Used this recipe to make a gluten free pizza crust; I used gluten free all purpose flour. This was a nice alternative to a yeast crust, and I was able to make it with ingredients I already had. Came out well. Will likely use again.

The only thing we changed up is the amount of olive oil.  We used a dash of olive oil, and mixed it with the remaining amount of melted coconut oil (so it wouldn't turn solid quickly), for healthier fats.  We also used stone-ground whole wheat pastry flour. It was delicious!  I'm so happy I can finally eat pizza now, since finding out I can't eat yeast!!  Yum!

Only change I made was omitting the salt (I have high blood pressure). Tasted fine for me, but I can see how it would be bland for others. One crust was perfect to share with my husband. Definitely will make this gain!

With the modifications I made this was a 5 star recipe. I tripled the recipe, used a little extra milk and olive oil as needed, added lots of extra salt and a lot of Italian seasoning. tasty and flavourful crust!

Very easy and good.  I too added some garlic powder to the crust before baking.  Rolled out beautifully with a little extra flour on the pizza stone and on the  rolling pin!  Definitely a keeper!  Thanks!!!
My husband and I love it!! I made them 2 days ago. It taste soooo good!!! It flat pizza.
I was looking for a pizza that is not so doughie. This was fast,easy,crispy and good.

Great base recipe for an easy, soft and sturdy crust that doesn't crumble or grow soggy under a generous helping of sauce. I'm thinking a little sugar might help it brown up better and some recipe-appropriate seasonings would be good, but quite usable as is. I avoid doing homemade pizza because of the time it takes to raise pizza dough, and this is easily a good enough substitute for yeast dough to allow me to do it more often.

To be totally honest, I did not have high hopes for this recipe at all but decided to give it a shot because I'm out of yeast. I'm so glad I tried it! My husband and I actually like this recipe better than our usual yeast dough (and it's awesome that it's so quick to whip up)! I ended up adding an extra splash of milk to my dough because it was a tad bit dry once I mixed it and like another reviewer suggested, I also threw in about a tablespoon of oregano and a clove of garlic to the dough mixture. To me, these additions really made this a great, quick weeknight recipe that we will be adding to our rotation!
Manchego Cheese, Chorizo, mushroom and crispy onion pizza!   Perfect!   I used cornmeal on my pizza stone also.

I made this recipe because I didn't have yeast one day and it was so fantastic made just as the recipe states. When I finally got yeast I made a different pizza dough recipe and both my husband and I prefer this one, so now it's our go to pizza dough. So easy and tasty!
Fantastic recipe! I used garlic salt instead of regular salt, and shaped these into heart shaped miniature pizzas.
awesome recipe..very easy..made a stuffed crust & baked it @ 425° for 12 min..came out great
amazing crust.  keeper for my family

We used this for calzones as suggested in another review.  The crust was just as it was supposed to be with the ingredients listed.  It was a little bland, but nothing some Italian seasoning, garlic and parmesan wouldn't help :)

I've made this a few times to make my homemade pizza. I've perfected the flavor and consistency over time. I use a full cup of milk because 1/3 is not enough for me, more salt, and olive oil, which I also spread lightly on the bottom of the pan. I use a round unperforated pizza pan and squash the dough down into the pan to take it's shape, making sure to spread out past the edges so I can roll the excess into a nice crust. Poke everywhere with a fork to keep it from puffing up all humpbacked in the oven.I bake it for 10 minutes at 350° and it makes a delicious deep dish pizza crust!

This is really good!  I made it 2 ways:  Method 1 Exactly as called-for in the recipe- creamy and delicious but not too sweet. it was just right.  Method 2.  I used the base recipe, but added a small pinch of cayenne to the mug and stirred well.  The added zip of flavor made it special.

I deliberately chose a fairly plain recipe so that I could "dress it up" occasionally.  Yummy both ways!

I cut this recipe back by half. I threw all the ingredients into large Ball Jar, slapped a lid on it and had my kid shake it until it was uniform in color. We all had a mug of this tonight--my kids thought it was good, my husband and I thought it was a little too milky, not enough chocolate. I am going to try to fiddle with it and see if adding more baking cocoa makes a difference. If I made this recipe again, I would cut back a bit on the nonfat milk powder.

This was good. I would scale back on the milk for a richer flavour. I added some hot pepper powder on top to give it a kick. When putting this together the powders make a pretty presentation. Definitely a gift idea.

Quite good! If you've never tried anything like this know it's not going to be just like cheese. But this was very tasty in our vegan nachos. I added about 1/4 cup of leftover vegan cheddar cheese shreds at the end but that probably didn't make too much flavor difference. Nice and easy!

For the 1.5 cups of salsa, i did 1C trader joes jarred red salsa and .5 cups of 505 Hatch green chile salsa. I also added another 1/4c of nutritional yeast with the salsa as I am a big fan.  Pretty spicy and very delicious.  Not only a really good dip but I see this as something to dress tacos or use as an enchilada sauce.  It's even good out of the fridge, not that I've stood there with a bag of chips eating it  with the fridge door open or anything...  I didn't have any margarine so I just used 2T olive oil.  I decreased the salt to .5t anticipating that the salsa would add plenty of salt and whatever I was eating this sauce on.

Really good!  My husband and I have recently starting eating a Vegan diet.  Cheese is one thing that I really miss. I am a cheese lover.  This recipe is really good and satisfies that queso craving.  I followed the recipe exactly, but next time I may add some finely chopped jalapeno.

Although I'm far from Vegan this one still piqued my interest and I had all of the ingredients on hand. This turned out surprisingly good. I would definitely make this again. A can of Ro*Tel diced tomatoes and green chilies works best with this. For those of you that are not familiar with  nutritional yeast it is quite good on it's own and has somewhat of a cheesy flavor. Shh, don't tell my carnivore friends that the last two recipes I made were vegetarian and they were quite good.
OMG I LOVED IT! It was a great hit, and all my friends want more!
i looooovvvvvvvveeeeeee  this milkshake i would soooooo make this again
Delicious! Super easy to make!

Red Velvet lovers, this is your recipe. It's so easy and awesome. God bless you for sharing this.  I was *supposed* to save this for a V-day treat. My DH said 'but honey, i love you every day' so I made it for the family without the frosting mixed in and piped a frosting heart on top. Everyone had sparkles in their eyes.
absolutely awesome!!!!!!!! my family are huge red velvet fans. this milkshake was something new and was a big hit!!!!!!!!
I couldn't bring myself to add frosting, but this shake definitely brings the boys to the yard

Oh my!  This is so good.  Love the slight texture and feel of the hot chocolate and the flavor it to die for.  I also tried this with ginger as suggested by another rater and yes, that is amazing too.  Both ways is a winner to me!
Now I've got a name to my concoction. I love this stuff!
I liked the spiciness of the hot chocolate and it is toe warming!!
I made it exactly as the recipe said and it is amazing.

Very good recipe! I made the servings for 2.  I only double the milk and cocoa mix (didn't use instant).  With 2 cups of milk; 6 tablespoons of cocoa... I used 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon and 1 pinch of cayenne pepper.  

It came out great.  It wasn't too much cinnamon and the right amount of pepper.  Me and roommate enjoyed.  I gave four stars for the amount of cinnamon recommended.  It should be 1/2 tsp of cinnamon.
I tried this for the first time and it was the best hot chocolate EVER! Thanks so much for letting me know such a delicious thing was possible.

The spices transform regular hot chocolate into a delicious drink with a nice kick. I enjoyed this different version and topped it with whipped cream. I'll definitely make this again. Thanks for the recipe!

This was a real treat! I used a tbsp of really good unsweetened cocoa powder and about 1 tsp superfine sugar in place of the prepared hot chocolate mix which made it even more delicious.  I even used skim milk and it was rich, creamy and satisfying, perfect for warming up after playing in the snow!  My daughter liked hers with just the cinnamon, and I probably went a little light on that in hers.
I use cocoa and sugar instead of a mix. I use 1/8 teaspoon of cayenne pepper. Mayan hot chocolate is the best hot chocolate I've ever tasted.

I used Starbucks dark hot chocolate and I prepared it by dissolving the hot cocoa in a shot of hot coffee and then added the cinnamon cayenne and a sprinkling of dryer ginger powder.i just eyeballed a the spices. I finished with some vanilla whipped cream. Amazing!! You'll be bored with regular packet hot cocoa for good!!
My entire family loved this. I was unsure at first but my hubby now believes this is his favorite hot drink. All three of the kids enjoyed it as well. It's a keeper. I made it just as recipe says.

I  added a shot of espresso. Too much cinnamon for me. More like a 1/4 teaspoon would be better.  I had some freshly opened cayenne so a pinch was nice and spicy. The older your pepper, the more you need. Don't recommend heating the milk to boiling point. It ruins the milk. I like to use almond milk for extra richness.

I thought the cinnamon was going to be overpowering but it was a really tasty, tongue-tingling drink.  Good blend of flavors!  Sure warms you up!  Had to ding a star for instant hot chocolate mix because it has additives and other stuff in it.
This is delicious!  I still like to add marshmallows, though.   =)
pretty good tho I'm not sure I'm sold all the way...

this burned my throat with every sip i took. i tried one of the reviews where they put 1 1/2 c. milk and 2 Tbs. of cocoa and 2 Tbs. of sugar and i added a splash of vanilla. then i saw my peppermint essential oil and i thought what the heck! i put one drop in and it smelled of candy cane hot choc! i tried it delicious! i like this recipe :) thanks for sharing your homemade easy recipe!
Delicious! Instead of instant cocoa I used 3 teaspoons regular cocoa and 3 teaspoons sugar, mixed in 1/2 dl of water.
I've hot cocoa just like this at my Mom's winter home in Mexico--delicious with and without spirits--thank you, That Grace

In the wintertime, I like to have a cup of hot chocolate before I go to bed at night. It's both warming and relaxing. I ran across this recipe and was apprehensive about the amount of cinnamon and the addition of cayenne. But I have seen so many cayenne/chocolate parings lately that I decided to try it. SO much better than plain hot chocolate! I WILL have this often -- thanks!
This was pretty good. I will make it again, but with changes. I will add more cinnamon and less cayenne pepper. Maybe my pinch is bigger than others, but it was just too much for me!
Wow! This is delicious! I added just a few drops of Vanilla and it was great!
Very tasty!
Don't let the cayenne scare you.  This hot chocolate tastes just like red hot cinnamon candy.  Or in my case, an Atomic Fire Ball because I use a BIG pinch of cayenne.

I just made this for small tea cup sized portions. I didn't have cocoa mix on hand so I used cocoa and sugar as follows (again this is for small china tea cups 1 serving) 1 full tea cup milk, 1 teaspoon cocoa powder, 1 pinch cinnamon, 1 pinch red chili powder heated on lowest setting over gas stove for about 2-3 minutes or until almost at a boil! It really does taste like some of the hot cocoa I had in Mexico... I tried abuelita expecting similar things and was disappointed, this is perfect.  It has a robust complex flavor and goes well with marshmallow cream if you want a little extra sweetness. Whipped cream if you have it will be more complimenting.
it was good, but I think I might've put in a liiitttllleee too much cayenne pepper so it was a bit too spicy for my taste....
I've  made this and have been drinking it since.

Yum!  I go to Mexico often and this is authentic!  I'd even suggest adding about 3 T boiling water to thin it out just a bit.  A real keeper.  I used Mexican cocoa instead of instant hot cocoa mix.  Tastes like it could ward off a cold, too!

I've been putting cayenne and cinnamon in my hot chocolate for years, but one other thing I add that makes it even more wonderful is about 1/8-1/4 tsp of ginger powder. Trust me...it's so delicious! Also, I don't use instant hot chocolate. I use about a cup and a half of milk, 2 tbls of cocoa powder and 2 tbls of sugar. I whisk it all together, along with the spices, over the stove. Just till blended and hot (don't boil it).
This is awesome!!!
I love this frosting as is, and half butter/half shortening! It colors so well, pipes easily, and spreads smoothly. Thank you for a great recipe!
Excellent, only change I made was 1 1/2 cups butter and 1/2 cup shortening.
OMG this was my first attempt at homemade frosting and it came out perfect. Taste just like the bakery icing you find in stores. Very easy to make

Sooooooooooo good. I made this for my sisters wedding cake. I had a ton of icing left over and it was a 3 tier cake! The only modifications I made were 1.5 cups shortening and 1/2 cup salted butter and omitted the salt. It really is the best frosting I have ever tasted. I took some of the leftovers into work and everyone raved how good the icing was. I even shared the recipe with a girl who is making cupcakes for her friends baby shower. :)

I tried it the first time as written and it was yummy but a too sweet for my taste. I would add 1 tsp butter extract for a buttercream taste and also use pure vanilla extract. It gives you just a bit of ivory instead of stark white icing which I prefer.  The consistency was kinda soft too. The second time I made it with the some other reviewers recommendations and Yummy Yummy YUM! I used 1 1/2C shortening and 1/2C butter and used only 5C sugar. I also used real vanilla extract.  It was very delicious, but quite soft. I also had an issue with melting. I think I would need to add a few cups of sugar and use less cream to actually make it useful for piping and being intricate with designs.  All in all its a good recipe because it tastes great (with the adjustments) and its adjustable. I'll have to play with it a bit more before I commit to only using this recipe.

This was pretty good frosting.  My mother-in-law pointed out the fact that it didn't taste like butter and I should've used butter flavored shortening... but all in all I thought it was tasty and it got compliments from other guests.
Excellent. Like other reviewers, I used 1 cup butter for part of the shortening. Fluffy, tasty, and plentiful, this is my frosting of choice. Terrific recipe--thanks!

I was making a cake for a  two year olds birthday party but did not want to use my meringue buttercream. I used half butter, half shortening and less cream. Everyone raved. It was easy to work with, and tastes great!

I am a huge fan of buttercream and this didn't do it.  I followed recomendations of using butter flavor crisco and half butter - really bad
!  I may try it with plain crisco next time.  I like buttercream recipe better

This was awesome.  I did something that probably not many of you have done and I used these on Clone of a Cinnabon from this site.  I used less sugar though, as the buns are pretty sugary already but everything else was the same.  I did not find this too greasy as it was, and neither did anyone else that tried these.  I gave some to my husband to try before I coated the rolls with them and he gave me that "This is really good stuff" look.  Also, I usually never do it, but i found myself trying the icing quite a bit, you know, to make sure its ok ;) lol.  It's those kinds of things that make you realize you found a winner of a recipe.  Thank you so much for sharing.

I tried this today and loved it. I did as others suggested and put 1 cup butter and 1 cup shortening, it was awesome. My husband even liked it, and he's pretty picky sometimes!  My only advice is to try not to let it get warm while you make it. I made the mistake of having the mixer sitting on top of the oven while my cake was cooking, and it softened a bit much, but was easily fixed.   This recipe made just a bit more than I needed, but my son didn't mind!
GREAT recipe that everyone will love! I substituted the shortening for butter and added a few tablespoons of cream cheese. This recipe was to die for!
My search for the perfect buttercream frosting has ended.  This was so wonderful, not too sweet and so fluffy - everyone thought my cupcakes were from a bakery!  Thanks for the wonderful recipie!

I've done it with half butter and half crisco and then I've done it with all crisco.  My family likes it either way, but there not as picky with their baked goods as they are with cooking.  But I will use this recipe from now on.  Easy and delish!
just a quick question that if someone can answer would be great ...do i whip the heavy cream before adding it in?

I gave this recipe 5 stars because it was perfectly delicious. I did make a minor change. I really don't enjoy the flavor of shortening based frostings so instead of using plain white shortening, I used the butter flavored shortening and a couple tablespoons of real butter.I could've used all butter in place of the shortening but I wanted to do some decorations so the shortening was necessary. I decided to make this a lemon buttercream so in place of the vanilla I used lemon extract and few teaspoons of lemon zest. My 80 year old grandmother who is the expert baker in my family asked me for the recipe. It was a hit.

Love it! I did 1c. Butter and 1c. Shortening and it was perfect for piping...it was the first time I made homemade frosting and this one is a keeper! I love the use of cream instead of milk! (I actually bought whipping cream by accident but worked great!) I also added the full amount of sugar if not more and I did not find it overly sweet at all. Thank you for the great recipe Rick!
Big hit. Awesome on my cookie cake. Thanks!

this was very easy to make. I used it for my sons birthday cake it turned out very nice. I used fondant to make the little green monster in Monsters Inc. and the butter cream frosting for the rest of the cake my entire family loved it
Too greasy.  I will find a frosting that does not call for shortening next time.  It does frost and freeze well though.

This a great recipe! I use it for cakes that I sell and never fail to get compliments. I do make two changes...I use only butter (shortening is an abomination) and I use REAL, high quality vanilla. My white frosting isn't necessarily brilliant white, but it's white enough that no one ever notices.
THE BEST!
Absolutely LOVE this recipe!!!! It has a great consistency for decorating and it not melting quick and running off the cake! Great taste and 5 stars in my book!
BEST FROSTING I ever made. I did substitute 1.5 cups butter and 1/2 cup shorting for 2 cups shorting and it turned out fantastic. Will use over and over again.  Thanks Rick
This is a great recipe, not too sweet and very fluffy if you beat shortening and sugar several minutes (I beat mine around 5 minutes). It tastes just like from a bakery. Try this, you will enjoy it!

I made this with the 1-1/2 cup shortening, 1/2 cup butter variation as suggested in some of the reviews. It came out perfectly! It really does make a lot though, so consider cutting the recipe in half.

This is the last buttercream recipe I will ever try.  I tried is with 3 parts shortening and 1 part butter.  It tasted exactly how I wanted to.  If you do all shortening, I think it would taste exactly like bakery icing.  If you want a more buttery taste, it's easy to adjust the ratio.
Everyone loved it!

It's delicious. If you are going to color the icing, dissolve the salt in the cream first. If you don't, you will get little white spots after the color sets.  Otherwise, it's not too sweet. I would advise to follow the recipe as is. Adding all the sugar gives it a good consistency. Believe it or not, it does not add to the sweetness. If you think it's too sweet after adding all the sugar, add a little salt to cut the sweetness. If you think it's too dry, add a little water in small amounts. A little goes a long way.

I am the kind of person who sits down to a piece of bakery cake and immediately removes the frosting. Icings are often too sweet or greasy for me, so I usually don't eat them. Today, I was looking for a frosting that would hold up in my first attempt to decorate a cake. The ratings and reviews  convinced me to try this, especially since so many reviewers found that it held up to decorating. I took reviewers' recommendations to cut down on the shortening and add some butter and to cut the sugar to avoid excessive sweetness. The reviews have been accurate in that this frosting went on well and made great decorations and writing. Unfortunately, it left a greasy taste in my mouth. I even used the whole 8 cups of sugar thinking that this would disguise the greasy mouth feel. No luck. The reviewers are right: this tastes just like a bakery frosting. The rating above reflects that; if bakery frosting is your thing, this recipe is great. If you don't like that sort of icing, you will not like this one.

Great recipe!  It tasted just like my favorite bakery. I used this to fill and frost two nine inch rounds adn I thought this might be a little too much for what I needed so I decided to cut the recipe in half. As it turns out, half was perfect!  We are a frosting loving family and I was able to be pretty generous.  Also, I could not find clear vanilla extract so I used the darker color that I had and it was still stark white.  I will absolutely use this recipe over and over.  Thanks for sharing!
WOW!! This is awesome, I used half regular veg. shortening and half unsalted butter. I also used whipping cream instead of heavy cream. This is a winner for sure. Thanks.

This was an ok basic recipe for frosting, but the shortening made it a funny texture and left a waxy feeling in my mouth! Maybe it's just personal preference, but next time I will use butter! If you needed to pipe the frosting, this would certainly be firm enough for that.
very good.  My consistancy was a little off but it may be because it was so hot in my house that day.

Great recipe, very forgiving for this momma who's never decorated a cake before!  I added 1/2 cup butter and 2 more cups of powdered sugar to this recipe.  It was a lot of frosting, but I was making a 2-tiered 8" cake and 24 cupcakes.  When decorating make sure frosting stays chilled, it's easier to work with...my hands kept warming up the piping bag.
Extra yummy!  We made pastel colors and decorated Easter cupcakes.  I think we have more icing than cupcake - however the girls would just eat the icing off the spoon and pass on the cupcake.
Yum Yum Yum. I used 1c butter and 1c shortening, and added an extra tsp of vanilla extract. This will definitely be my go-to white frosting.

After reading a ton of reviews, I made this frosting using the exact recipe.  The first time I must have done something wrong because it was very airy.  The second time, due to lack of sleep, I forgot to sift the powdered sugar, it turned out fantastic.  Great consistency, flavor and texture.  Will definately use this recipe again.

This recipe is the absolute best I've ever made.  Like others before me I made modifications due to personal taste & used 1 1/2 cup butter and 1/2 cup shortening, which yielded a great consistency & awesome taste.  One suggestion for those who have had issues w/ this recipe: Use a stand mixer and mix the ingredients for at least 10 minutes.  There's no such thing as overmixing with this recipe. I will continue to use this recipe as I haven't found one that even comes close to its quality.  No greasy after taste with this one.  Thanks Rick!
Compliments everytime. Not too sugary or waxy. Very easy to use.
Made a mess, but it was good.
definitely Im going to try this recipe it seems perfect for what Im looking for =)

This was my first attempt at a buttercream frosting.  It was wonderful!  I read several of the reviews and decided to go with 1 1/2 c. butter flavored crisco and 1/2 c. butter.  To save on money, I used about 1/2 can of 5 oz of cream instead of whipping cream.  I might should've used a little more to make it more spreadable.  I had made a cake for my 5 yr. old's b-day party.  I got RAVE reviews!  The icing made enough to frost 2 13x9 cakes.  I did not have enough left over to decorate...had to make another 1/2 batch.  I was so pleased with it.  Fantastic!
This frosting was fantastic! It turned out perfectly, the only adjustment I made was to make half of it (covered 24 cupcakes) and used half butter and half shortening, perfect mix!

Best I have ever made, very easy. I mess frosting up constantly , this came out great. I cringed when my son said he wanted homemade, I HATE baking, hate cake making. Even was going to go against his wishes and order one, but the woman that answered the phone was not helpful or friendly at all so I said ya know what forget it lady I will make it myself and thats that, will use again for sure if  I am ever forced to make another cake.
slightly too sweet for my taste; i used all butter and was perfect for pastry bag piping

Great frosting! I made some minor modifications:  
1. used butter flavored shortening
2. used almond milk instead of heavy cream.
I just let my mixer go for a while with the shortening, then after the powdered sugar, and then again after the other ingredients. It spread great, and the whole family thought it was the greatest frosting ever!

I'm a frosting fanatic--could skip the cake and just eat the frosting. I made this twice, once using half butter, the second time using 3/4 butter to 1/4 shortening. Both times, it came out terrific. I think it's a matter of personal taste, but something about the shortening definitely gives it that bakery flavor. I used real vanilla, and it didn't negatively impact the color of the frosting while significantly adding to the taste. Finally, the heavy cream gives it a wonderful texture. Thanks for a great recipe!
Love this frosting!

I took the advice of other reviewers, and used 1 1/2 cups shortening and 1/2 cup butter. This was Awesome! It was just like the frosting in the bakery! I needed a lot, so I made a second batch just in case. The recipe makes quite a bit, and I ended up with about 1/2 batch left over...but who's complaining. I'm sure it will get eaten!

I've been searching for a buttercream that is creamy, not too sweet and not greasy.  This is the perfect one.  I've been baking for a long time and this is the best buttercream I've ever tasted.  It pipes well too.  I did use 1/2 butter instead of all shortening.  I like that it makes a large amount too.  Thanks for sharing this wonderful, easy recipe.
Added 2 oz more whipping cream and butter instead of shortening.  Turned out great. Will be using again.

This frosting is fabulous!  I made it exactly as is, and it got rave reviews!  I've used it on both confetti and butter pecan cakes, and it complemented both very well.  I think this could be used on almost any cake or cupcake.  It piped well and was easy to color.

YES! This is exactly what I've been looking for. Kids were not in favor of cream cheese frosting, so I had to find another one to frost their Xmas cupcakes for class. They loved it! Thanks for such an easy, yet tasty recipe! Very versatile too!

I thought this was an amazing buttercream recipe, could be flavored very easily by adding extracts, I used butter extract as I just wanted a rich buttercream frosting- makes a ton of frosting though! Hale it and you will still have plenty for a large cake, or refrigerate the leftovers if you bake a lot.

i tried this recipe as written first and really disliked it. the taste of the shortening was just too artificial for me. i salvaged it with some butter and cream cheese but ended up with way more than i bargained for. the next time i used this, i used all butter instead of shortening, halved the recipe, added half a cup less sugar, and full tsp. salt. sooo much better. it was delicious! this will be my go to recipe from now on.

This is now my go to frosting. I do substitute butter for shortening because that is how I was raised. It does make a lot which is ok if you are doing some decorating. It also keeps well in the fridge. I am glad I found this recipe so I don't have to buy frosting in the store.

Great Frosting recipe!  I made this recipe for my daughter's sixth birthday party because I did not want to serve an artificially flavored frosting to young children.  As an American expat living in the UK, it was a bit of a challenge to find a Crisco alternative, but I managed.  Trex did the job, along with butter, to make this wonderful Buttercream Frosting.  Thank you for sharing this with the world!

I have been making this buttercream for a few times now.  This is a great recipe.  This weekend, I made it with 6 1oz choc squares (make sure to use the unsweetened-melt it in a double broiler, then add it to the batter in between the sugar additions) to get a choc buttercream to frost my choc cake.
YUMMY!   Thanks Rick!
Great frosting that comes out just right every time! Hubby's favorite by far.
Absolutely loved the frosting

Great texture and easy to pipe with, but not a lot of flavor since there is no butter. Would probably be a great base if you add extracts, crushed oreos, etc. I will probably make this again and add something to give it more flavor.
used unsalted butter.  frosting is really good.  will be using as my go-to frosting

I use this for all my cakes and cupcakes, I use all butter, sift the icing sugar and double the vanilla, usually I start with 1/4 cup of the cream then add as needed depending on the season,  great for decorating and frosting.
If I want a softer frosting I use half butter and half soy margarine.
Full batch frosted 75 cupcakes with 1M tip and had about 1 cup leftover.
Best frosting ever. I went with all butter and got rave reviews.  Consistency is perfect.  1/2 recipe for 24 cupcakes.

This recipe is everything you can ask for when looking for the perfect buttercream frosting. I halved the recipe and it was plenty to frost a 2-layer 9inch cake. I used butter flavored shortening ( that's what I had on hand), so it didn't stay perfectly white, but that's not the recipe's fault.  I have also added different flavors ( lemon and coconut are my favorite) and received plenty of compliments every time. I do add a couple of tbs. of light corn syrup so the frosting is smoother. This way it is easier to frost big areas of cake without any "bubbles/holes" and the surface becomes much smoother and prettier.  Will be making again!!

I scaled this to 18 servings and was able to generously frost 9 inch cake.  I used real vanilla extract, half unsalted butter and half butter flavored Crisco. I only used half of the ammount of salt it called for.  Anymore I thought would have been too much.  IT WAS AWESOME!  I cannot believe how much like a bakery this tasted. A+++++++++++++++++++++++

I made this with butter (in place of shortening) and heavy cream. Half and half also works just as well. This is hands down the best frosting recipe ever! I quartered the recipe (using 1 stick of butter, etc), to make just enough for one 13x9 cake (not much for tasting, however), and added 3 tablespoons of regular Hershey cocoa (it would be 12 tablespoons if you make the original quantity) for a chocolate version. My husband doesn't have a sweet tooth, but even he commented on how delicious this frosting was! Thanks for sharing, Rick!

This was VERY good and super easy.  It sure does make a lot - I easily covered over 50 cupcakes and still had enough for another 1/2 dozen.

I used it for my 2 daughters' birthday parties and got rave reviews - people thought I bought the cupcakes from a bakery.

Enjoyed it a lot and will be referring to it again in the future.  Thank you!

This recipe is the BOMB BABY!  I followed the advice of others..  I used 1 1/2 cup of butter and 1/2 cup of shorting.  I also added a little more salt to cut the sweetnees.  Now it was not wedding white, but I figure if you get that land o lakes white butter it may work.  I'm going to try it again.  I'm also going to try many other combo's with this.  

If you are looking for a creamy/whipped buttercream icing.  This is it.  It is nothing like Publix's, Ingles, Cubs, Sams, or Krogers (Krogers changed their recipe..theres used to be sweeter..now it is not)...whipped icing.  I'm from a place were icing is supped to be sweet or at least have a hint of sweetnees....and no grease...... THANK YOU RICK MAZZUCA... It is the best.
This is a great buttercream!!!!!! My new favorite.

Followed he recipe exactly and it turned out great!  I dont like frosting (unless its cream cheese) so I wont tell you what i thought of the taste.  Doesnt matter what i thought anyway, i used it on my daughters 12th bday cake and what matters is what SHE thought.  She LOVED it!!  I had a hard time getting all 8 cups of sugar mixed with the shortning, but i did add about 7.  The texture was a bit grainy so i added a bit more cream.  Let the Kitchen-aid do all the work for a good 8 min.  It was so easy to work with.  I will DEF use again!!
This is delicious everyone. Thanks for sharing this recipe! Did use 1/2 butter and 1/2 shortening and 1 cup less sugar!!!

Sweet and fluffy.  I used 1 stick butter and 1 stick butter flavored Crisco.  This may sound strange but as a compliment to a not so sweet cake the frosting was a little too sweet.  I think that on a sweeter cake it wouldn't have tasted so sweet.  The frosting itself; a five star recipe.

I could only give this 4 stars because I altered the recipe. I have a problem with a frosting being called "butter"cream when there isn't any butter used (and it doesn't remotely taste like buttercream - to me at least). I did what someone else did, I substituted 1 cup of butter for 1 cup of the shortening and it came out with the "butter" taste. Although I make real buttercream frosting, this is so easy and most wouldn't even know the difference, so this will be my frosting for everything except the specialties for which I will stick to my real buttercream recipe. Enjoy.  This is good with 1/2 shortening & 1/2 butter.
I did exactly as written. Best frosting. Thank you Rick for sharing the recipe!.
this frosting was sooo good!! very tasty with a lemon cake, or any cake!
I used 1 cup of shortening, 1 cup of butter. FABULOUS! Who needs cake?

I used half shortening and half butter in the recipe and it was still a bit greasy...only used about 3 ounces of cream but all of the sugar. I loved the sweetness of this frosting because I am a frosting person for sure :). I will try making it in the future using all shortening versus all butter to see which I and my family prefer.

Thought I would chime in because the reviews were old.  This recipe is great as written.  Butter always makes things better but the consistency is great.  If you are not a cake decorator or don't expect to make lots of cakes soon, 1/2 the recipe.  I used this for a "ho ho cake" a clone of the Hostess treat, to fill layers.  It was a hit! I replaced 1 tsp of vanilla with 1 tsp of almond extract just because I love the flavor. Also used 1/2 and 1/2 because that is what I had.  Awesome.

Yum Yum Yum!  This is so good!  I used 1/2 butter flavored shortening and 1/2 real butter and real vanilla extract, not the fake stuff.  It was so good!  I am very proud of myself and my fam was impressed.
Wow!!!This frosting is better than any I have tasted,including from the bakery...This is my new frosting.

This was perfect frosting. I made this to put on a baby shower cake and the response to it was great.  Better than bakery is what I was told.  I did follow the suggestion of switching out half the shortening for unsalted butter so I didn't follow it exactly but close enough for me to feel comfortable rating it 5 stars

I made this recipe twice before writing the review: once with regular shortening (actually half butter, half shortening), and once with butter-flavored Crisco. The butter flavor version was much tastier, but if color matters, it's not white. This is a very good recipe either way, and stays creamy (no hard "shell") over time. Thanks, this is in my permanent file.

I love this frosting!!! Hard to spread but pipes great. I made half a batch using 3/4 Crisco and 1/4 cup real unsalted butter.  I also used almond extract but you could use any kind to give it a different flavor.  It makes a lot of frosting. I would recommend doing half because it's easy to make more if you need it.

I made this frosting back in August for my grandsons 3rd birthday.  I made a train cake and used this frosting to decorate a 3-D Thomas train and a loaf and cupcakes.  It was easy to decorate with and the intricate details held up under the humidity.  The only negative about it was the taste.  I thought it tasted a little greasy, although everyone else thought it tasted good.  I used 1 1/2 cups shortening and 1/2 cup butter.  Next time I'll try 1/2 of each.

Fabulous!!! We switched out the shortening for butter, simply for personal taste preferences, but followed all measurements to a tee! Love this. Family favorite from now on!! We beat our butter for 10 mins, then beat the sugar & butter for another 15, then the sugar, butter, cream, etc for another 5.
DELICIOUS!  Perfect when prepared just as the recipe states. I prefer this over any professional frosting I've ever had!
Not bad, if you don't mind the taste that comes from all shortening and no butter.  Holds up really well in the heat, but I won't make it again...love real butter buttercream too much!
Substitute half butter
Came out wonderful! Will make again. :)
Awesome!  The only thing I did different was use half real butter in place of half the shortening and used regular vanilla instead of clear.  Very very good flavor, thanks for sharing!
This frosting was so quick and easy. I substituted butter for the shortening. It turned out perfect!

This was a pretty good frosting.  I dont really think it tasted like buttercream as much since it didnt have any butter flavor in it.  But it was very easy and I had the stuff on hand to make it.  I was really wanting to make it an almond flavor with some almond extract, but I ran out.  I put this on top of an almond wedding cake recipe on zaar.  I halved the recipe and it was well more than enough for a 9x13 cake.  I had a lot of extra even halving it.  I ended up having to use 6 oz. of the cream to make it nice and smooth.  Next time I make it I am definitely going to put in the almond extract.  If I wanted a real buttercream taste, than I would take others advice and use half butter or even all butter in place of the shortening.  Great frosting recipe!

I also rated this five stars, though I followed the advice of others and did half butter, half Crisco.  It is really tasty and stiff enough for piping.  The only thing I think I'd change is maybe next time cut back a bit on the Crisco and kick up the butter.  I don't like any kind of greasy after taste in my frosting, and Crisco seems to always do that.  If you cut it back a little, I'd imagine it'd be perfect!  Yum.
