I'm definitely going to continue to use this.
It really is that good!
This is an incredible frosting recipe.  Perfect for my daughters 3rd birthday cupcakes.  We made 48 cupcakes and doubling the recipe was plenty. Keeps very well in the fridge.  Thank you.

It's good, pretty frosting. Way better tasting than supermarket cake frosting. It does not get 5 stars though, because I am in love with the buttercream frosting from the Dutch Bakery in Victoria, Canada and I'm saving my 5 for one that tastes like that if I ever find it. This was a little too heavy and sweet to be perfect, yet it's wonderful to work with, beautiful and it is much tastier than anything store bought!
Fabulous buttercream!  Just enough sweetness to pair with any cake.
I'm a sugar junkie and this was the perfect frosting!
This was so easy to make and it tasted wonderful. I used half butter and half shortening. Will definitely be my goto recipe when I need frosting!!

Don't even think of trying another frosting recipe--this one is perfect!  Thanks to the hint of other reviewers I used half real butter and half shortening, and I think it's the addition of cream that makes this frosting tops.  This frosting handles beautifully, takes like a dream.  It DOES make a boatload, but it can be covered in an airtight container and the remainder used in a couple of days.  You won't want to waste this. I received tons of compliments on this and when paired with my favorite cakes, well just let me say, happiness abounds. The addition of butter and the use of real vanilla extract brings this from a bright white to an antique white color, but I much prefer the flavor.

Very good, 1 used 1c shortening and 1c butter.  Was not too sweet and not too bland, just right!  I frosted 3 layers and had enough extra to do a rosette border around the top and bottom, rosettes and dots all over the sides and still had over a cup of frosting left.  Perfect!

I made a huge birthday cake for 50 people yesterday and wanted to try a different buttercream recipe. I made 2 changes based on other reviews.  (1) I used 1 1/2 cups shortening and 1/2 cup butter. I didn't use more butter because of potential problems with softening/melting.  (2) I added 1 tsp Wilton's butter flavoring.  I left everything else the same.  What a great icing!  It was very spreadable and great when piping shell borders, rosettes and lettering.  It also tinted beautifully.  I did have to refrigerate the pastry bags after a minutes of use because the heat from my hands was too much and the icing became very soft.  At the birthday party, I had 4 guests who bake tell me that this was the best icing ever--that it was so buttery and not too sweet.  I will definitely use again.

I made this last night with the shortening and it was whey too greasy and it tasted awful. I read the reviews and substituted 1 and 1/2 cups of shortening for butter and only used 1/2 cup shortening. I added 1/2 tablespoon of real vanilla extract and it was much better. I am still on the search for that healthier no grease or butter buttercream frosting recipe.  Overall it piped well and decorated my cupcakes good, just don't keep it in your hands too long bc it begins to soften.
Used 1 cup shortening and 1 cup butter. Texture was stiff enough for rosettes on top of cake, but not so great for the sides. Taste was delicious!

I love this recipe. I did change a few things but the texture and flavoring of this frosting is much better than others I've tried. I substituted half the shortening for half (salted) butter and also added 1 tsp of butter flavor extract with 1/4 tsp of salt. I also added 1 tsp of meringue powder. It has just the right amount of sweetness to it without being sickening sweet! Thanks so much!

This is a wonderful frosting recipe! I used butter flavored shortening but otherwise followed the recipe exactly. Next time I will probably use half butter flavor shortening and half regular shortening as it was a little too buttery, but my guests said it was perfect as is...you be the judge.

I've made powdered sugar icing before and it's always turned out too thin and transparent. So, I had my doubts that this would turn out anything like what I'd seen in the pictures. I'm very glad to say that I couldn't have been more wrong. This was amazing. I made it exactly like the recipe calls for and used it to frost over 6 dozen sugar cookies, plus had enough to decorate them. My kids kept trying to eat it out of the bowls and piping bags! I will definately use this as my primary icing recipe. No more store bought icing in our house!
Wonderful frosting! Made it exactly as instructed (or close to, because I never use a measuring cup!) I frosted 50 cupcakes and still had a little left over! Will definitely use again and again!
This is a WAY good recipe!  I put it on my sisters cake and all I ate was the frosting!  I think that the frosting is the best when it is 1 day old!
I too used 1/2 butter and 1/2 crisco, and can't say enough about the unbelievable flavor of this frosting.  My favorite buttercream!!

This recipe makes a lot of frosting so if you need it just to decorate a 9 inch double or rectangle cake then i would suggest cutting it in half. This frosting is actually quite tasty and not too sweet like I thought it would be. It has has great texture and works perfect for decorating :) I had a bit of raspberry extract to mine for a nice flavor
Incredible! This is now my (and my family's) favorite buttercream frosting. I followed the video's possible substitution of 1 cup of butter for 1 of the cups of shortening and the flavor is amazing.
Great Frosting - just make sure that you follow the reviewers instructions and use half butter flavored crisco and half butter.

It tastes a lot like bakery frosting. It was very hard to mix if you follow the instructions because the powdered sugar and shortening (even softened) becomes to hard to mix with a beater. The first time I made the recipe it broke my hand held mixer so try the other reviewers suggestions. Overall, I like it.

WOW!!! This is THE best frosting I've ever made! My entire family loved it. You can totally use this recipe to decorate cakes.. you can play with the thickness by adding just a teaspoon more cream or vis-a-versa with the confectioners' sugar. I used this recipe to decorate both my daughters birthday cakes (used fondant on it, as well), and also created 16 cupcakes with it. I'm printing this one for my book so I can hand it down to my kids someday. :)  A+++

This was so easy to make and held up very well for piping even after it was warm from my hands. I made 1/2 a batch since I just wanted it for bordering a cake and only used 2 cups of sugar so it wasn't overly sweet. Since the sugar was cut I also cut the cream and it came out perfect. I will use this from now on when I need to decorate a cake or cupcakes
I have made this frosting 3 times now.  I did change it to 1 cup shortening and 1 cup butter, but everything else is the same.  It is easy to work with, and very yummy.

Wonderful recipe! I have been using this recipe for over 3yrs now and have never heard a complaint. I also add 2 TBS of Wilson Meringue to help stiffen the frosting for decorating. I will not use any other buttercream recipe..
Wow!  I also did half butter/half shortening, just a taste preference.  I used this to decorate an ice cream cake that I made.  It was amazing!

I took other reviewer's recommendations and used 1/2 shortening, 1/2 butter.  I also used pure vanilla extract, but used a little less than 2 teaspoons.  I used a little bit more salt and about 1 cup more confectioners' sugar than called for.  (It came out perfectly white, no problems).  Make sure you beat this for over 5 minutes.  Let me tell you, I am an icing junkie and this rates up there with the best!!  It tasted exactly like icing from the bakery.  Thank you for the recipe, I'll definitely be making this again!!!

This buttercream frosting is awesome, with some of my own changes.  As is the recipe works fine, but I prefer my buttercream frosting to actually use real butter, so that's what I did.  I substituted real, salted butter for the shortening and omitted the extra call for salt, although the adding it wouldn't have hurt.  I also used non-fat milk, but that was only because I didn't have any heavy cream in the fridge.    The key to making this, or any frosting, is to first cream your butter and then add the confectioners sugar slowly.  If you add it all it once, you'll end up with a big clumpy mess.  Adding the sugar slowly allows time for everything to come together.    Very smooth frosting and very tasty.  This is my go-to buttercream frosting recipe from now on!!!!!

There are a million recipes for buttercream...well not a million :)  I was attracted to this recipe because of the use of real cream.  I did however, use butter for 1/2 of the shortening.  The shortening gives a fluffy white texture (stuff inside a Hostess cake) but lets face it, shortening is not a real food.  It is a manufactured processed item that survives on the shelf forever.  Next time I make it I will try all butter and cream (hey!  thats what is in the name!) and see how it holds up.

People, this is an awesome recipe.  I did use 1/2 butter and 1/2 regular crisco.  I made three variations for a luau.  I added lemon zest and a tbsp of lemon juice, key lime zest and key lime juice, and coconut extract. Additionally some cupcakes were iced in vanilla.  All four flavors got great reviews from my guests.  This is my go-to frosting for evermore.  Love it!

I normally try not to deviate from a recipe if I plan to review it, but I couldn't resist on this one. I did not have shortening, but did have unsalted butter on hand, so I substituted that instead of the shortening. Other than that, I followed the recipe precisely. This was my first attempt at buttercream frosting and I think I need to look no further. I used it with the Simple White Cake also on allrecipes and it tasted just like a cake I would pick up at a grocery store bakery but since I made it myself, it was a fraction of the cost. I think from now on, I'll save my $20 and use these 2 recipes whenever an occasion comes up when I need a frosted cake. This frosting was so easy to make, easy to spread and easy to pipe on. Goodbye Betty Crocker frosting, it's time we parted ways.

If I could give this more than 5 stars I would. This stuff is to die for! I am so grateful to have come across it, I've been searching for that perfect buttercream and I have found it! It is a tad salty for some reason but otherwise, perfect.

On the up side, it took coloring fantastically!  I was making a ladybug cake and it actually came out red and black.  I don't know if it's just too big of a batch...  I couldn't fit it in the bowl for my stand mixer, and my hand mixer started smoking.  Maybe I should have added more cream, but it was a dry, dusty, smoking mess!  I may try it again and only make half at a time to go a little easier on my mixers.  It tasted fine, no compliments, no complaints.
Used half shortening and half butter - turned out simply yummy and perfect!

I subbed 1/2 cup salted butter and cut the shortening to 1.5 c. I also used only 6 C of powdered sugar.

I whipped the heavy cream first before adding any ingredients until still peaks formed (10 minutes), then I mixed the shortening/butter together in a different bowl before adding it all together.  The frosting is stiff, firm, yet smooth and flexible.  Absolutely amazing.  I personally think it's way too sweet, but my hubby says it's the best frosting he's ever tasted
used 1/2 shortening and 1/2 butter also added a bit of almond extract and added  milk slowly until whipped well. Great frosting!!!!

This is the best buttercream I think I've ever had.  I did substitute half butter, half shortening, but other than that I followed the recipe exactly.  8 cups of powdered sugar seems like it would make the icing sickly sweet, but once you add in the whipping cream and get it whipped up nice and stiff, the icing balances really well with the sweetness of the cake. I used it to ice cupcakes for work and it iced 30 cupcakes and I still have enough leftover for at least 10 more.  This will be going in my family recipes book.
Fantastic (and so easy)!
I did the 50/50 Shortening/Butter and it was a huge hit.  Hard not to eat it by itself!

This was a very easy to make recipe, and the texture was perfect. I thought it was way too sweet though!! If i were to make it again, i would probably only put 5 cups of confectioners sugar in. On the plus side, if you need a lot of frosting, this is the recipe. Since i found it too sweet, i only put a very light layer over my cake. I think i could have frosted two cakes fully with it.
Awesome! Perfect for decorating and flat-out yummy. The whole family loved it!

This is the first homemade buttercream recipe that I tried that turned out perfectly the first time.  I have used it on probably 50 projects throughout the past year and I could not ask for a better result each and every time.   Some days I have tweak the sugar/liquid ratio depending on the temperature in my house that day but it still works like a charm!

Made for a baby shower and turned out perfect following recipe exactly, except for extract flavor (1 1/2 tsp vanilla, 1/4 tsp coconut & almond). My mom made cakes for a living for many years and that was her "secret" to perfect icing. I also used butter flavored shortening because I was coloring the icing and did not need it white. Light, fluffy and smooth!!!

Easy and tasty! I didn't want the greasy taste & texture of just shortening, so I used half butter and half shortening. I also halved the recipe and it still made more than I needed. Easy to work with -

This is delicious, but I completely agree with other reviewers who have recommended to split the shortening half-and-half with butter (1 C. each). The consistency makes it much easier to work with and it doesn't taste so greasy. Yum!

::Update:: Just used this frosting again for an owl cake. It works fantastic in a frosting tube! I just bought a nordicware cupcake froster. The frosting flows right out of it. Wonderful!

This is a perfect decorating icing. I used butter flavored Crisco which I thought would make it taste even better but I have to say I think it would've been better using the plain, I subbed 1/2 c of shortening fo butter & I think the fake Crisco butter taste was just too much.  I used it to ice my son's birthday cake (oreo ice cream cake from this site which I doubled) & I still had a sandwich container of icing left over.
is recipe is the best. I made my grandson's 1st birthday cake with cupcakes and everyone loved it.
Great recipe! *Make sure you mix sugars in well. So you wont get a grainy texture!**
SOOOOO good!  I didn't have the heavy cream, but did have all natural coffee creamer, hazelnut flavoring, I left out the vanilla and used the 6 oz of cream, still turned out soo good!

Amazing! I used one cup of shortening and one cup of butter to make it an actual buttercream... I added a touch of peppermint extract and it was so light and fluffy with the whipping cream! this is just what I was looking for! I will use this recipe from now on! the second time I made it, I used 1/2 c shortening, 1/2 c butter and 8oz cream cheese. It was light and fluffy and not overly sweet. I would NOT use only shortening - that's just not right to call it buttercream...

Excellent!!!! 

Jeff
Perfect buttercream frosting
This is definitely the perfect recipe for consistency. I didn't have any regular shortening but did have the butter flavored shortening.  I thought it was a bit too rich but my family loved it!
I am new at cake decorating and wanted the fluffy whimsical look for a baby shower i found this recipe loved it the frosting was beautiful!!!

OMGI am not much of a baker but I used this recipe because of the reviews. It was so easy to make and use. Read the comment about using half butter so instead I used half Butter Crisco. I had so many people at my little girls party ask for recipe.

I was looking for a great buttercream recipe for my husband's birthday, and I think I found it!  I followed the other suggestions and used 1 1/2 C. butter and 1/2 C. shortening.  But, I did add more vanilla extract.  My only problem with this frosting was that it got gooey and warm really quickly. (and my kitchen was quite cool)  If you are using it to frost and decorate the cake, I suggest you put the frosted cake in the fridge while you are preparing the icing for decoration, i.e. tinting and placing in pastry bags.  I didn't keep the cake in the fridge and the icing practically melted off the cake as I served it. Otherwise, it was a wonderful recipe!
Very good for decorating!  I used the frosting to do some piping on a chocolate glazed mocha cake.  I took others advice and used half shortening and half butter.
Very Yummy, wouldn't change a thing!
Love this Buttercream!!!

I followed this recipe to frost my mom's birthday cake and I was worried it might turn out greasy. (She only gets the best!) It was better than I expected.  It's soft, fluffy, great for decorating and has a great flavor!  This is the first time I've made a buttercream frosting with cream and I was really impressed.  Usually she doesn't take all the cake home.. but she did this time.  I might use this to make an upcoming wedding cake for my sister.

This is the BEST buttercream frosting.  I halved the recipe and used half shortening (crisco butter flavored) and half unsalted butter.  It is so good, not greasy tasting and not too sweet, just the right amount of sweetness.  I did added alittle more heavy cream to thin it out alittle and 2 tablespoons of light corn syrup, this helps it soften more and gives it some shine, I will use this from now on, way better than the wwwaaayyy to sweet bakery icing.

This buttercream frosting is like the kind you get from bakeries; very light and fluffy and not too sweet.  It colors really nicely too.  When you mix the butter/shortening and icing sugar, it will look crumbly at first, but just keep blending and it eventually it becomes a thick paste to which you add the whipping cream and vanilla.  Believe me, the extra blending time is worth it!  Delicious.
I've been searching for years for the perfect buttercream frosting. This is it. The flavor stays wonderful, whether chilled or at room temperature.

It tastes VERY good but it doesn't hold its shape too well unless just out of the refrigerator. It does say that it's ideal for "frosting & borders" which it's great for so I gave it 5 stars + it's delicious. I agree with the others that you can sub. some of the shortening with butter (unsalted) and if you don't have cream you can sub. whole milk or half & half. It does taste pretty awesome, so if you're using it for a simple cake (or like we did, on a cookie "cake") it'll work perfectly & be yummy. It is definitely not a good "glue" nor stable enough for more intricate designs & detail.

Delicious!  I used it to ice sugar cookies.  I used all butter (no vegetable shortening) and replaced the cream with evaporated milk.  This made the frosting a little bit runny, which was what I wanted to glaze cookies.  I will definitely make this again!
Fantastic!  However, I followed another person's suggestion , to use 1 cup of butter in place of 1 of the cups of shortening, only 6 cups of icing sugar and 1/2 cup of evaporated milk.

This is an amazing recipe.  It does make a generous amount of frosting.  I substituted unsalted butter for the shortening.  I whipped the butter for 5 or more minutes in order for the butter to turn white.  I also added one package of white chocolate hot chocolate mix just for fun. I will definitely use this recipe again and have already recommended it to friends.

Followed the recipe somewhat, but only used a 2 lb bag of powdered sugar and 1.5 cups unsalted butter and 1/2 cup butter flavored shortening. Tasted pretty good, somewhat greasy but I think everyone will like it.

I like it better than others I've tried, I still don't care much for frosting but this one isn't bad and I used it to make a Barbie Wilton cake. :) (Oh 1/2 butter and 1/2 shortening with no other changes).

I first tried it with the half shortening/half butter option that many people were raving about, and it still left that icky film on the roof of our mouths.  Then I tried it with all butter and no shortening, and it didn't stand at all!  Granted, it was August, and hotter than Hades, but still, even after leaving the cake in the fridge all day, my meticulously piped stars ended up shapeless and bloated.  Maybe it would have held better with the shortening, but who wants to eat greasy frosting, no matter how beautiful it looks?

I;m not giving this recipe 5 stars because I did change some things with PHENOMENAL results!!! I used all real unsalted butter and real vanilla extract. It made some out of this world delicious buttercream! I also used only about half of the heavy cream so that the icing wouldn't get too soft for what I'm using it for (basketweave piping). It is perfect, rich, and melt-in-your-mouth. I suggest using butter and real vanilla. I could not stop licking the bowl :P I used this to fill and ice David's Yellow Cake (which is also scrumptious!).

Made this frosting this morning for a very special cake, my son's going away party (heading to Fort Benning, GA next week). After reading several reviews and personal preferrence I made a couple changes. I used sweet cream butter instead of shortening, omitted the salt, changed the sugar to 6 cups (my husband doesn't like super sweet frosting) and used between 5 & 6 ounces of heavy cream. WOW!!!! This is the best buttercream recipe I have come across, way better than anything I've had out of a bakery. I used about 1/2 cup of the frosting, thinned down with cream, to use as a crumb coat...worked perfectly. I know I changed the recipe, but I still give it 5 stars...was a great recipe to work with. =-)

This was a great frosting to work with!  I took the advise of a few other reviewers and used 1/2 cup butter and 1 1/2 cups shortening.  I also cut it in half to use to frost one double layer 9" cake...big mistake!!!  I did not have enough frosting.

I don't usually like regular buttercream. I usually make Swiss meringue buttercream because it's lighter and not as sweet. However, this buttercream frosting is perfect! It's fluffy and not TOO too sweet. I used butter flavored shortening.

I like the texture and how thick it is for decorating and frosting with tips, but it's a bit rich in my opinion.  I used butter flavored Crisco...don't know if that had much of an impact on that or not.  I will still use this again, but with a few tweaks (like a bit more sugar) next time.  Overall a good base frosting recipe.

This recipe turned out pretty good. I did, however, use real vanilla and butter instead of the imitation stuff. Turned out great. When I made it, I halved the recipe to frost a double layer 9-inch cake, and still had enough to decorate it. This is a great multi-use icing, and I would definitely make it again

I suggest using the Crisco butter flavor for this recipe.  Make sure to add the powdered sugar in slowly, it gets very thick before adding in the heavy cream to give it a frosting consistancy.  The Crisco butter flavor gives it at great buttercream flavor!!  This also holds frosting coloring very well, so you don't have to use as much!!!  Loved it!
It had a nice taste to it. I used half butter and half shortening. I did have some problems with it holding its shape, next time I will do all shortening for piping.

Great tasting. Simple to make. Easy to adjust measurements. My guests couldn't decide which they loved more, the cake or the frosting! This is my new favorite recipe. (One change, I used all butter...I couldn't envision it any other way. )
This is an excellent frosting...fluffy, creamy, sweet, but not too sweet. Smooth and spreadable, easy to work with (in piping bags etc).  Got rave reviews from all who tried.
I have to admit this was one of the best frosting I have made. It didn't taste like shortening and everyone loved it they thought it was store bought! Will make again.

This is the first layer cake I've frosted. I followed what some people said and used half butter (unsalted) and half shortening.  I also halved the recipe, but I should have made the whole thing.  I made 2 9" round cakes to layer, and had "barely" enough to do the middle, sides, and top.  

The frosting is really good. My husband is picky about frosting being "too sweet" and he liked it.  He is spoiled and picky, so that says something!

I liked that I didn't have to cook the frosting, to get a buttercream frosting.
Excellent frosting!  I used regular real vanilla (not clear) and it worked just fine.  I put the leftovers in the fridge, and it seemed to get even better the following days.  Thanks for the recipe!!

I made this recipe as written, but 4th it since I was only using it to top a pie (my version of a french apple pie).  It was delicious!  Nice stiff consistency...tastes like the buttercream used at the bakery.  Yum!

The BEST buttercream icing I have ever had! My mom & I are both professional bakers & have used the Wilton Buttercream frosting for years. On a whim, I decided to try something new and came across this recipe. I used 1 1/2 cup shortening & 1/2 cup butter instead of 2 cups shortening & used a total of 10 oz heavy cream to give it a thinner consistency. It was AMAZING and Everyone LOVED it. It turned out to be my best cake ever!!
One of the best buttercream frostings I have ever made.  The recipe was very easy to follow and came out great.  This is my new buttercream frosting recipe!
Delicious

Let me preface this review by saying that I am a butter girl.  I was very skeptical of and reluctant to use shortening in a frosting recipe, but since my last butter-only frosting was a bit disappointing, I decided to just try it.  Wow!  This recipe produces an incredibly fluffy, delicious frosting that rivals that from any bakery!  I used slightly less sugar (~7 cups) and this made  enough to frost 24 cupcakes with about 3 cups left over (in the freezer until next time!).  As with another reviewer, I kept "sampling" the frosting because I couldn't believe how good it was!  And it's not as sickly sweet and overwhelming as frosting made only with butter.  Try it, you will not be disappointed!

Wonderful!  I've made this twice in the last week.  First, for our neighborhood block party, where my cupcakes were a HUGE hit.  A teenage boy took the time to come over and personally compliment me on the cupcakes with the delicious frosting!  Made them again tonight for my son and his friends.  I only made one alteration - I used Butter flavored Crisco because I didn't have regular. While it didn't give me a perfect white frosting, it tastes perfect.  Thanks for the easy recipe!
Good consistency but tasted too much like lard for me.  I'm not a big fan of frosting in general, so it's probably just my personal taste.
This frosting is very good, I was a little nervous making it at first, but it came out great.  I would make it again.

This recipe tastes just like the buttercream frosting they use at bakeries and grocery store bakeries. Easy to make, delicious and PERFECT for decorating. I recently started a cake decorating business...this is my go-to recipe for icing for all of my cakes. Add some cocoa powder to make it chocolatey, or flavored oils to give it any flavor you like...orange, lemon, rasberry...YUM!
I used half butter, half shortening after reading reviews.  I also used half almond extract since I was pairing with an almond flavored cake.  Delish!

Fantastic recipe!!! I followed the advice of several other reviews and used half unsalted butter and half shortening (after making a small batch as the recipe is written, very good, but I liked the extra flavor the butter added!). I even ran out of unsalted butter when I was on the last of multiple batches, so I used salted and omitted the salt from the recipe. That turned out great also. Love the texture and flavor, it worked really well for a wedding cake I made. Lots of compliments on the frosting, and I even got a request to use it again for my dad’s birthday cake coming up. Thank you!
Always turns out great, especially when you use butter instead of shortening and REAL vanilla extract! I almost always use 1% milk instead of the heavy cream and it still turns out wonderful.

I just finished making this frosting. Literally, I am taking a break from washing out my mixing bowl to write this review. This is amazing! It is so creamy and fluffy and definitely not too sweet. I substituted 1/2 cup of butter and used shortening for the rest. I only had 1/2 tsp of clear vanilla left so I used it and 2 tsp of clear butter extract left and it is delicious! I can't wait to frost my daughter's birthday cake!
This frosting was ok. I used butter flavored crisco as my shortening, maybe that was a mistake. I liked the texture of the frosting, but not the flavor. It tasted a lot like crisco.

terrific, but I added two sticks of butter, more conf. sugar, and vanilla, and a bit more cream to make more frosting and give it a more buttery flavor, a more home made flavor, but the texture was CREAMY not gritty like usual, and i really liked it.
Can I use regular milk in place of heavy cream, to make buttercream frosting.

I just made a half batch for 2 dozen cupcakes and it was just enough for all of them.  I thought it was really easy and I put it in a pastry bag and it was the right consistency.  Perfect - will definitely use the recipe again.

This was my first attempt at buttercream frosting. I didn't have whip cream so I just used milk. That's probably why I was slightly disappointed with this. I was hoping for something with the taste and texture of the buttercream frosting from  Publix grocery store. If anyone knows of a recipe like that, please let me in on the secret!

this was PERFECT for frosting sugar cookies.  everyone LOVED it and wanted the recipe.  my only mistake was using butter flavor shortening which made the frosting yellower than i would have liked, but thats my error not the recipe!
Amazing
Easy to make and great consistency,  but I prefer a sweeter tasting buttercream.

Wonderful buttercream frosting only if you use unsalted butter and real vanilla extract (hence, the 4 stars).  I made 1/2 batch of frosting and had just enough to fill and frost a 9" layer cake, splitting both of the layers and filling.  Next time I may just cut down on the sugar so it's not as sweet.  Excellent frosting for your favorite chocolate cake.  Thanks for sharing!
Awesome! Made this to frost a shower cake and it turned out beautiful and delicious.  Used half shortening and half butter.  My new favorite frosting!

This was my first attempt at buttercream icing so I made this last night to icing two dozen cupcakes (Strawberry Cake from this site) and the Chocolate Cake II from this site.  To be honest I was skeptical in regards to using shortening as I thought the taste would be off but I was pleasantly surprised.  My son does not like cream cheese icing so I decided to give this one a whirl and he loved it!
Other than halve the ingredients (as I read all the reviews that said it makes tons) I did not change a thing and it was an easy recipe, great for piping, and great tasting.  I will be making this one again and I think I may take some reviewers suggestions and use half butter/half shortening to see how it changes the flavour.
perfect recipe!! i used a tiny bit less vanilla and added a dram of strawberry flavoring, it was amazing

Held its shape really good. Made an Easter Basket Weave Cake. ***UPDATE*** Used this to frost my husband's 43rd B-Day Crazy Cake. I used 1/2 shortening and 1/2 butter and the taste was much better than before. It had a sweeter and less Crisco taste. I'm not a big fan of buttercream but this was still good.
Creamy and delicious! I love this recipe and it works every time I need a good basic frosting for a homemade cake!

This recipe is awesome. The frosting is the perfect consistency for piping and spreading. It tastes amazing (except mine tasted a little bit salty, but I think that was my fault). I would highly recommend this recipe to anyone and this recipe goes amazing with this white cake: https://goo.gl/GNlMvR

I just iced my second wedding cake using this recipe.  The only change I made was adding half and half instead of heavy cream.  It was perfect and enough to ice a 16x16 inch square cake without decorations.

The best buttercream ever!!  I made it with all shortening, 1tsp of vanilla because I ran out and 1 tsp of Wilton's butter flavor.  It was for my son's 3rd birthday cake.  I iced the whole 9x13 cake, did top and bottom border and printed and still had left over icing.  I will try next time with half butter and half shortening just to see if it can get any better.  The cake was almost gone and I am going to have to get a bigger pan and make more next time.  This blow's Wilton's buttercream icing out of the water.  I did refrigerate my iced cake since the icing had heavy cream in it. Thanks!!!!! Awesome and I am recommending to a friend for her kids birthday cake!
I just made this for a party cake. It was amazing. Followed the recipe exactly. It tastes like a bakery frosting. I will sure to be using this one again.

Exceptional. I used it to do the fancy frosting swirls on top of cupcakes. I did the coconut cream pound cake as cupcakes and frosted with this but instead of vanilla extract in the frosting I used coconut extract and it was AMAZING.

AWESOME frosting!!  I have been trying all of them on this site lately and this has been my favorite!!  I did as some suggested and used 1 1/2 cup shortening and 1/2 cup of butter and used butter flavoring as well as vanilla.  So good and I got soooooo many compliments.  This recipe does make A LOT.  I had a lot to frost so it was great for me.  I was able to frost 33 cupcakes and 2 bundt cakes and I still had enough left over to do a few dozen sugar cookies. Please try this recipe, its great!!
I followed this recipe exactly as written and it is amazing!!! The most delicious buttercream frosting ever!  The recipe makes a large quantity.  Enough for frosting a layer cake plus decorations.

Delicious!  I have another frosting recipe that I normally use, but after reading all of the reviews for this one, I had to try it.  I am so glad I did - it mixes up beautifully and the texture is perfect.  If anything though, I may try all butter next time, since this is a buttercream... and I generally prefer to use butter instead of shortening if I can help it.  As is, this is a great recipe - I will definitely post an update if I try it again with the butter!

I made with 3/4 Crisco and 1/4 real butter and it's greasy. It left a film on the roof of my mouth and my tongue. I can't imagine how much worse it would be with 100% Crisco. I don't understand the rave reviews unless if they're by people that have not had truly good buttercream. I don't have time to make another frosting before our guests arrive and I'm truly embarrassed to have to serve this. 
The only positive thing I can say is that the texture is nice.

I give this a 2 stars only because it didn't really work on the cupcakes that I was making...which I think is actually my fault. I did use as suggested the 1 cup butter and 1 cup shortening and actually doubled the recipe, however it still turned out quite greasy. I also didn't add enough icing sugar (which was needed because I was making cupcakes for my 3 years pre-school class hence they were not sweet enough). Had I been baking a cake and needed to ice it or create borders, this icing would have been perfect, but I did not find it to be a good  cupcake topping. I was actually quite disjointed, but since I am not a baker, I lived and learned.

Wonderful Wonderful recipe...everything I hoped it would be. My boys compared it to tasting like cookie dough, which in this house is a huge complement!  I, too, substituted a little butter (1 stick).

I've tried a few other buttercream recipes and this one was by far the best. I made this for my daughters 4th of July ice cream cake and it was delicious! The only adjustment I made was used 1/2 cup of butter and 1 1/2 cups of shortening. My hubby even liked it and he doesn't even really like anything sweet. He told me not to change a thing about it. It's such a great & easy recipe that I'll never buy store bought frosting again. Thanks Rick!

This is by far the most exquisite buttercream I've ever worked with. I run a cake business from home and have researched and researched for a buttercream icing that i will find satisfactory. I didn't. so i've been working with swiss meringue buttercream for two years. the problem? it's expensive and time consuming. I'm so glad I found this recipe though because it's now going to be replacing my swiss meringue. To tell you a little about the icing, it's exactly as the reviewers have been saying it: it's light and fluffy and doesn't have an artificial flavor to it. I had no problem's icing my cakes and readying them for fondant. This recipe is very forgiving, I used 1.5 c. shortening and 0.5 c butter. I wouldn't have given it five stars with all shortening though. I also used a cup less sugar as I don't like my icing overly sweet and upped the vanilla by another tsp--so adjust to your liking basically. Try this recipe, you won't regret it. Thank you for posting this and changing my life!! I'm soo thankful.
Made a big batch of this recently and just wasn't thrilled with the taste.  I used shortening, but wonder if butter would have tasted better.
Best frosting I've made from scratch!
Smooth and perfect to work with. I had so many compliments on how great it tasted.
It reminded me of wedding cake frosting
It tasted fine the first day. The second day it tasted like crisco. I will never make this recipe again.
Great recipe. Easy and delicious

Definitely an amazing buttercream! Definitely taste like the local bakery. It did have an bit of a heavy shortening taste. I would follow another reviewer's advice and use half shortening and butter. I also only had 1/4 cup cream so I used milk and all was good!
I adore frosting. And liked the consistency of this frosting but did not like the flavor at all. Felt it was very bland and tasted greasy. Will not use again.
The best frosting!!!
This is the BEST frosting recipe i've found yet, thanks Rick!
I love this recipe. I added my own twist to it and it was amazing!!! thanks for this recipe!

great to work with, didn't have to add any extra cream.  After being chilled overnight in the fridge it didn't melt after 2 hours  in the heat of July for my son's birthday party, and I have had a lot of frostings melt off the cake!  I used regular vanilla extract, just makes it slightly off-white, but I colored it too.
Because of a few reviews I subbed 1/2 of the shortening with butter.  This was a great recipe, though maybe a little too sweet--I would add less powdered sugar.  Made a LOT of frosting.

Totally satisfied with this recipe although I did not follow the measurements or the ingredients..Ok, so I'm really satisfied with what I came up with..  I cut the measurement down to my needs and omitted the salt and cream and used margarine instead of lard... Beautiful!
Try with caramel extract instead of vanilla its amazing.

Totally idiot proof.  It looks wrong when you get done whipping in the sugar with the shortening but it comes out perfectly - you just have to trust it.  So good.  I did half the recipe and had more than enough to do a whole two layer cake - including the filling - with some left over.  I recomend it!

This really is the BEST Buttercream Frosting I have ever tasted! I don't like using shortening, so I used 1 1/2 cups of salted butter (did not use the 1/2 teaspoon of salt due to salted butter) and only 1/2 cup of shortening. This makes a TON of frosting, so I froze what I did not use. I couldn't stop tasting this...YUMMY!!!!!!!!!!!!
Absolutely a great recipe!  I did use butter instead of shortening and added a tad more cream, but really, you need look no further for a buttercream recipe!

Will definitely make this again! I did replace 1/4 cup of shortening with butter, just to give it a slightly buttery taste, but I don't think it was necessary.  I've always found buttercream icing made only with butter was too rich (even my sugar loving kids think so), and this was MUCH better!

I needed to make 200 cupcakes for Halloween carnival and this was simple and the taste was great, I added some hersheys chocolate at the middle of the batch and you talk about a treat. Can you tell I love chocolate.

This was the best frosting I have ever made! I did use 1 cup of butter in place of 1 of the cups of shortening. I also added 1 teaspoon each of vanilla, almond and butter extracts, which I highly recommend adding to any frosting recipe. It held up really well for piping (I actually did a basketweave pattern). It has great consistency and a wonderful taste. Everyone should try it!

Delicious!  I followed the recipe, except I subbed in some butter as others suggested.  It is creamy, buttery, not overwhelmingly sweet and holds together really well.  I have not tried adding any colouring to it, yet.

Oh wow!  This was spectacular!  This was the first time I have ever made frosting and I found it to be just perfect as is in the recipe.  Not too sweet, not too greasy, just perfect! I guess that I did not get the shortening creamed well enough before adding the sugar so I ended up having to add the remaining 3 cups after I put in the heavy cream but it was a HUGE hit!  I even have about a cup of frosting left over in the fridge!  Think I will make sugar cookies for it!  ;o)

I made this recipe to go with my champagne cupcakes. Using other reviews, I cut back the amount of confectioners sugar. I believe I only used about 4 1/2 cups and that suited my taste just well. I made 12 cupcakes and an 8x8 cake so there was plenty of icing to freeze. I can't wait to break it out in a while and try it on some different cupcakes.
Used half butter, half vegetable shortening and I added 3 teaspoons coconut extract and it was phenomenal. I added an extra ounce of cream which made mine VERY easily spreadable.

I'll definitely use this one again, and I'll likely give it 5 stars next time. The problem: the weather is too hot! I used all butter, and let it sit out to soften while I was at work. By the time I returned home, it was partially melted. I had to add extra sugar to get a decent consistency. I thought it was a tad on the sweet side but my siblings loved it (and considering it was a birthday cake for one of them, I think their opinion counts more anyway!).
yummmmmmmmmmy! I used this for my sisters birthday cake and i halfed the recipe and it was just perfect! it tasted like a bakery did it!
Sooooo good.  No changes made.

Okay, I made this just as it said too.... I definitely couldn't get it to combine with all that powdered sugar using a blender, so I mixed by hand and then added milk because it was still too thick for my project.  
Honestly..... the taste was terrible.  I'm a major lover of butter cream frosting.... Ridiculously so. Like, I love only the corner piece of cake, and I hate whipped cream frosting, so I was super disappointed by the taste!!!  Try all the suggestions people give in the other reviews because this does not taste anything like buttercream you get on delicious sheet cakes from your local grocery.

It was so sweet. I had to mix it w/ another recipe of whip cream and cream cheese just to cut the sweetness. I gave it a two star instead of one only because I was able to ice the cake as a base frosting- no decorating.
THIS IS THE BEST RECIPE FOR BUTTERCREAM FROSTING THAT I HAVE EVER MADE.  I LEFT EVERYTHING AS IS, EXCEPT IN PUT ORANGE OIL INSTEAD OF VANILLA EXTRACT.  IT WAS GREAT.

I really like this buttercream, though it isn't as sweet as I thought it would be.  It made a lot and I actually stored the remainder of it in my refrigerator for over a month and was still as good as the day I made it.
Half butter and shortening and didn't have cream so used milk...yummy!!

I gave my sister a surprise birthday party tonight and used the scratch strawberry cake recipe from allrecipes.com made in a 12 inch pan and this frosting recipe tinted pink. I used a French Vanilla cake too and cut the layer in half. I frosted the top of the vanilla layer, added some heavy whipped cream and sliced strawberries, then stacked the strawberry cake on this and repeated the frosting step. Topped the cake with the other vanilla layer and frosted the top and sides. It was sort of like a strawberry shortcake taste. The family raved about it. I've been doing cakes off and on for about 38 years and love doing them. I'll make a wedding cake for my youngest daughter's wedding reception next week-end. I love this frosting recipe.

I was looking for a chocolate buttercream recipe, and decided to customize this one.  I ran out of confectioner's sugar at the 4.5 Cup mark and added 2 cups cocoa powder for the chocolate.  I also used milk instead of cream since I didn't have cream on hand.  
I will say that with my modifications, all my  kids loved it, I found it to be the perfect sweet taste. If however I had followed the recipe as is, I think it would have been PERFECT.  So this recipe is now going to be my stand by recipe from now on.

great stuff! i subed 1/4 cup of butter for some of the crisco and uppped the vanilla a bit for flavor. the ability to decorate was great and the icing was tasty! DON'T try to double this recipe in a convential stand mixer, lol!! it's too  much!! I'll have to try butter flavored crisco next.

I rate it 5 stars with the exception that you use REAL salted butter. There is a reason is is called buttercream! The best frosting EVER. I have used it to decorate several cakes and it holds up nicely. I really was not a frosting person until this frosting found me! Not too sweet or waxy tasting (with the butter!) I get so many compliments on it. I like using coconut extract to flavor it...delish over chocolate cake layered with coconut pecan filling!

Tasted like sickly sweet shortening. I was looking for a true buttery flavor, but didn't have enough butter so I thought I could use this recipe instead. It doesn't taste like a buttercream at all. Tastes like the filling of a Suzy-Q.
This was my first time to make buttercream frosting. With this being my favorite frosting, this lived up to every expectation.

I was looking for something other than frosting out of a can for my sons birthday cake. Admittedly this is the first one I tried because the ingredients could not get any easier. Well, Im glad I did because this frosting was so fluffy and easy to spread and for piping, too. It was not too greasy either. Great frosting and it definitely goes into the recipe box. Thank you!

This was really good. Nice and creamy. I didn't use whipping cream, but instead I used hazelnut coffee creamer and it gave it a different flavor. Next time I'm going to use vanilla flavored coffee creamer and leave out the extract, too!
This frosting is absolutely wonderful! It tastes like fancy, bakery-style icing, yet it's SO simple! Thanks, Rick!
Spectacular consistancy, flavor,  coloring and everything. Just what I was looking for , and was eanough to frost a LARGE 3 tier tall cake :) new "go to" frosting recipe.
Great texture, needed to add a little more sugar to the recipe, but it tasted great!

I'm a rather novice cook and even less of a baker. I made this yesterday for my two-year old's birthday party. I halved the recipe to frost a 13 x 9 cake. I had about a cup of frosting leftover. I used other reviewer's advice and made it with half butter and half shortening. I cut down on the salt because I used salted butter.  

At first when the frosting was done it tasted a little greasy, but I decided to go ahead and use it anyway. I had to stick it in a fridge for an hour before I could frost the cake.  That must have helped because after I frosted the cake, it was delicious, light and sweet. I will definitely use this frosting from now on.
Perfect consistency, very very light!

I followed the recipe exactly, and am totally happy with the results! It tastes like my favorite whipped frosting from the bakery. The one unintended variation I made was to the flavoring: I ran out of vanilla and subbed almond extract for one teaspoon. It tastes great!

Had to laugh at the review that says this isn't buttercream because there's no butter. Tell me, how do YOU think butter is made?
holds well for cakes. i used it on my nieces bday cake. be careful to not add too much salt or the whole batch is ruined.

Didn't have enough shortening so i used butter for half and it turned out great. You can make it really light and fluffy by whipping it on high for a long time, it made it less sweet that way and was perfect on chocolate cupcakes!

This turned out beautifully.  Colors well, easy to make and work with, not too sweet.  Yum.  I modified the recipe to use 1/2 Crisco and 1/2 butter, and left out one cup of the powdered sugar.  I also added extra vanilla, but that was by accident.  This makes a LOT of frosting.  Enough for 3 boxes of store-bought cake mix.  Next time, I'll cut it in half.

I loved this frosting! The only substitution I made was I used butter extract in place of the vanilla. It didn't get 5 stars because it didn't yield as much frosting as it says in the recipe. I ended up having to make more to complete my project.
Variations that I chose between that work just as well: 1 cup shortening + 1 cup butter, 2 cups butter, 1 tsp almond + 1 tsp vanilla, 6fl oz milk/water
Very delicious and easy to work with.  This will be my go-to recipe...no need to look any further.  Thanks for sharing.
Very good, but I'm only giving 4 stars since I used a lot less sugar....I cut the recipe in fourth (I needed just a little to frost some cookies) but still only used 1/4 cup sugar.

I did not enjoy this frosting at all! I was really excited because of all the great reviews, but I did not care for it at all! I felt like I was eating pure Crisco! Maybe it would be better if was butter flavored Crisco? I I don't know it left a terrible taste in my mouth!

This was very delicious! I did want a little buttery taste, so I did alter the recipe by using 1 stick of butter (1/2 cup) and 1.5 cups shortening I made cupcakes for my daughters playgroup with this frosting, and they came out beautiful. It tints very easily, and also pipes well. comes together very fast---I used my stand mixer. It does yield a huge amount of frosting. More than I needed for 24 cupcakes. Definitely will make again---so much better than store bought frosting and so easy!

Woohooo! This is definitely the definitive buttercream icing. Texture is perfect and the taste is exactly what I have been looking for. I used half butter and half Crisco. I had no heavy cream, so I used half and half. This will be THE icing recipe I use from now on. Thank you, thank you!!!

I used my whipping attachment on my stand mixer. The results were a very fluffy, not to sweet, mildly chocolate buttercream. Lamb: I canola oiled my lamb mold with a paper towel, crisco'ed, floured with a sifter until NO bare spots, and chilled the pans in the freezer. Once the batter was ready, I filled him face down, to just under the rolled edge of the pan, and carefully used a spatula to fill the ears. I added a couple of toothpicks, laid across his ears, and a "cake pop" bamboo stick from his head to his neck (like making a letter T) to add structural support. I tied him tightly together with baking twine, and placed him on a cookie sheet for baking. My aluminum lamb mold only has one steam vent, am going to add one. It was hard to tell when he was done with only one whole to poke a straw into.  Laid him face down, steam vent side up, to cool. Cooled for 15 minutes, then took off the back "butt" side of the mold.  Cooled for another hour and a half, cut all around the edge with a sharp knife, and carefully took his face side out of the other half of the mold. Cut the bottom ridge of his belly off, so he would sit flat, brushed off his loose crumbs, frosted my cake plate for an adhesive, slathered him up with a solid coat of white, then added thin squiggles. No face. :) Picture added.

The 2nd batch I made was 1 1/2 c. shortening, 1/2 c butter and the rest of the ingrediants according to the recipe. This batch came out fabulous! If you're looking for the definitive buttercream recipe, then look no further. Here are a few reasons why this recipe rocks my world: 1) Consistancy: It's PERFECT. Not too gloopy or too stiff. Just right. EVERY time. 2) Flexibility [part 1]: You can easily adjust ingredients to suit tastes of the cake-eaters. Butter instead of shortening is unbelievably rich but a firm favourite for older eaters. The shortening-only version tastes a lot like bakery icing, so popular with a younger crowd. And a mixture of the two gives you the best of both worlds. 3) Flexibility [part 2]: Recipe here makes a shedload. Great if you need to ice cupcakes for a couple thousand of your closest friends, but proportions are such that it is easily halved (to ice one normal sized cake) without losing any flavour  or needing a degree in calculus to figure out what the measurements would be. Make it. You won't regret it.
