Awesome recipe!!! i decided to add some butter extract cause i missed that butter flavoring and with this addition i absolutely love it !!!

This really is a GREAT RECIPE however I STRONGLY recommend using half unsalted butter for half the shortening and only 5 cups sifted powdered sugar (otherwise it would be much too sweet).  I also used real vanilla powder (less color than extract).  With the heavy cream, it becomes a terrificly light, fluffy frosting that spreads beautifully.  You could beat in slightly more sugar to part of the finished frosting if you want to use it to pipe roses (but don't use that much sugar to cover the whole cake).

After searching for the perfect and easiest buttercream (not too sweet), I have finally found it right HERE!! I followed the modifications of another reviewer to use 1/2 butter, 1/2 shortening, 5 cups powdered sugar and 4 ozs heavy cream. I did add the salt. However, I used cake/icing shortening which gave a clean, non-greasy aftertaste as opposed to regular (crisco) shortening. The piping came out excellent! However, I will try to use 4-1/2 cups powdered sugar and 5 ozs heavy cream for a softer, less sweeter tasting buttercream filling for a cake roll. No need to take forever making Meringue buttercreams anymore. I think this recipe is way better!
I used 1 c butter, 1 c shortening to keep a solid consistancy w/o that gross shortening flavor.  Firms up nicely; is forgiving and smoothable.

I used this recipe to make the frosting for my kiddo's birthday cake - SO yummy.  I did use unsalted butter versus shortening; we don't use shortening for a whole lot, and I'd have to buy a big tub of it (we'd buy Spectrum's if we did buy some, and that's the only size they sell) - but everyone loved it just the same!
Wouldn't change a thing. I've used it a few times, and it's perfect as is!

I've always wanted to make  bakery-type frosting/icing and this is it. 
I made it exactly as directed but next time will use butter in place of some of the shortening as suggested by other reviewers.
Thanks for a wonderful recipe!

Okay.  First, let me say that the consistency, texture, and overall flexibility of this recipe gives it a 5-star rating.  What drops it down is the greasy aftertaste tha I cannot seem to get rid of.  I did read most of the reviews for this recipe and I tried it both ways.  Using all vegetable shortening, doesn't give me the rich buttercream flavor that I like, but it's great as it is.  I tried the recipe doing half vegetable shortening and half butter flavored shortening and I love the flavor, but not the greasy after taste.  I am hesitant to try all butter because I know it won't hold up as well as using shortening.  I haven't found the Alpine shortening, but I will keep looking.  So, the recipe is great, but it's not what I'm looking for.  I'll keep trying once I get the Alpine shortening and post a second review.

The perfect frosting recipe! I have even used it to make cream cheese frosting with this recipe as a guideline substituting half the butter for cream cheese(more if you want a stronger cream cheese taste).
Followed recipe exactly and while the texture is lovely, it tastes just like sweetened shortening.

This was my very first time making homemade frosting.  I followed the directions of some of the other reviews and did 1/2 shortening and 1/2 butter....I used only 5 or 6 cups of sugar...it turned out wonderful!! I made strawberry cupcakes with this icing for my hubbies bday and the icing piped out wonderfully....and it was very tastey...thank you so much

Just made this frosting...i made a half batch and it was plenty to fill and crumb coat a 3 layer 8" cake with some left over. As previous reviews suggested I used half shortening and half butter (i always make buttercream with just butter).   As a variation I used a 1/4 whipping cream and about 3-4 tablespoons Khalua to add a different flavour. it was very light and fluffy...but VERY sweet. I generally like sweet frostings but I found this a bit sweet still. Tastes very similar to "grocery store frostings" as many others said.

this was a really great frosting. though im still having a hard time finding the frosting that doesnt look like it separates. this broke and you could tell between the sugar and shortening and it wasnt even hot in my house. but it tasted great!

This recipe is the only icing recipe I'll be using from now on.  My husband who only likes store bought icing loved this recipe as did my brother-in-law who only likes homemade icing.  So, it's definitely a crowd pleaser!  I used both shortening and butter.

I tried to follow the other reviewers recommendation and follow the recipe exactly. My blender wasn't big enough to use 8 cups of sugar so I only used 4. Even though I cut the ingredients in half, it still made enough frosting for two cakes and I still threw some away. Taste was great though. Not too sweet and consistency was perfect for spreading. I will definitely use this recipe again.
I didn't care for this. I definitely tasted the shortening and did not like the texture in my mouth. The next time I made a buttercream frosting I opted for actual butter. It was so much better.
We use this recipe all the time.  It does have a bit of a shortening taste, but to me it makes it a little lighter tasting, not so sweet and heavy.

This was really great. And it made a TON! I made it to decorate a cake for my son's birthday, and I thought I might have to make a little extra. But it made more than enough for the whole job. Took color well also. This is going to be my new icing recipe. Oh, I used half butter, half shortening.
Most amazing buttercream EVER with a stick of butter added for 24 servings!

This recipe is terrific!  I have been skeptical of any recipes that call for crisco, but I substituted 3 parts butter and 1 part crisco, and it worked out great.  Any advice on how to store the frosting if I'm not going to use it for a few days?  Fridge, countertop?  How far in advance can I use it to make buttercream roses if I leave them in the fridge?  Thanks!!
Wowza was this sweet! After eating it I'm pretty sure I either have a cavity or diabetes. This does look very pretty when piped cupcakes.

This butterbream was absolutely fantastic. I did however substitute 1 cup of shortening with 1 cup of butter as per other reviews. My entire family loved it and all agreed it was the best buttercream I've ever made. This recipe is a keeper!!

I liked the consistency for this frosting, however, I did not like the after taste the cream had. After sitting for a while the flavors of the sugar, vanilla, and cream blended so it was good. I don't think I'll use cream again...I'll use whole milk instead.
I was hoping for a thicker, richer buttercream, like Trophy cupcakes or similar. This buttercream is a bit light and greasy. Tastes fine, but doesn't have the denser texture I wanted.

Holy cow!! This is the best frosting ever! It's so rich and so delicious. It just ramps up the tastiness of anything you put it on! It's so creamy and light.  Fabulous recipe. My new go-to frosting. I usually half the recipe though because I hardly ever need 7 1/2 cups of frosting...not that I mind having that much on hand. ;)

I used this recipe tonight at my cake decorating class, and it was a hit. 
Thanks Rick!
The frosting tasted like crisco, as many reviewers had said. Also the recipe will make a lot of frosting so be aware.

This is a really good frosting and the consistency was great, however, I used all shortening and I think next time I would try substituting maybe half of that with butter. Had a little bit of that taste to it where it coats your mouth (if you know what I mean) all in all though it was good and I would probably make it again.

This is my go-to frosting, I love it! It's very simple, but delicious, and complements a wide-range of sweets from dark chocolate cake to pumpkin ginger cupcakes. I made a few alterations to the recipe - I use 9 cups powdered sugar and 1 cup whipping cream. This just works a little bit better for my needs and taste, but to each his/her own! Thanks for sharing!

Easy to make and tasty.  I used .25 c butter to 1.75 c shortening... consitency was good for cupcakes and held up in Texas heat.  However, but not buttery enough for me.  Next time I will use more butter and less shortening.

At first I thought this would be gross, using Butter flavored crisco instead of butter.  However, the creaminess and flavor were awesome.  Didn't finish frosting cookies, put it in the fridge and frosting was just as great the next day!  I will never use a different frosting ever again!
Halved the recipe to frost 24 cupcakes.  1:1 ratio for butter and butter flavored shortening.

Just a cooking snob comment or observation, if you will.  But IMITATION VANILLA???  You would admit that in a public forum?  Get yourself some real vanilla. I'm not sure why they even sell the fake stuff.  Why buys it?  Oh that's right, you do!  LOL

I needed an eggnog flavored frosting, so I used this basic recipe substituting the heavy cream with eggnog.  It worked perfectly!  I did have quite a lot of frosting...enough to frost 2 two-layer cakes with a little left over.  This frosting is rather sweet, but if you are not havey handed with the fristing and your cake isn't too sweet it works well.

I've been looking for a new buttercream for awhile and I just love this one.  I followed the suggestion of others and use half butter and half shortening and just whip it for at least 15 mins.  It turns out great everytime and has a great flavor and consistency.

Good frosting. The closest to bakery frosting that I have made. Husband likes this frosting. I experimented and added cocoa powder. It was okay but a little dry so I added peanut butter. Really good! Also I divided the recipe in half because it makes so much. For a single layer cake this amount works best.
My kids & I LOVE this icing! It's a really smooth icing, and not way too sweet like most icings are nowadays (no upset tummies).

Great recipe.  I substituted Coco Lopez cream of coconut for the heavy whipping cream and even added some coconut oil and flakes to twist this into a truly INSANE coconut frosting. I want my frostings really light so I did an entire can of Coco Lopez and added almost a cup of heavy whipping cream as well. I have also replaced the vanilla extract with peppermint oil and created a sweet peppermint frosting that gives a great Christmas flavor to the frosting. This one goes in my permanent recipe stock!
AMAZING frosting! I have been looking for a recipe just like this that so perfectly mimics the ultra sweet velvety textured frosting that Sam's Club puts on their cakes.Thanks!

After reading several reviews and seeing all the changes everyone made to this recipe, I looked for the opinion of someone who actually followed the recipe.  I followed it exactly and it is the best frosting I've used.  Fluffy, easy to work with, delicious and a beautiful white color.  Thank you, Rick!!

This is a yummy frosting. I never made frosting before but it was better than the birthday you buy at the store. I sub 1/2 of the shortening for butter and use milk (that was all we had) instead of heavy cream. It was good. thanks.

This recipe makes a ton of frosting and is perfect for decorating since it holds it's shape.  I only made a small change, I added about 2 tsp of almond extract.  It gives it a richer flavor.  I also added about 1/4 extra of cream to make it less "oily" tasting.  Otherwise it's a fantastic decorating frosting recipe with a rich creamy flavor and texture.

It's a KEEPER!  Thank you Rick!  My husband and I have been watching Cupcake Wars and he decided he wanted to try and find the most moist chocolate cupcake recipe and the best frosting (that tastes like our favorite bakery).  This was the first time I ever made a cake or icing from scratch.  The chocolate cake turned out good and moist (my nanna's recipe), but could be a little more chocolatey -- we are still working on tweaking that, but the icing recipe my mom gave me (that was her sister's) flopped.  It was awful.  But, of course, it didn't come with all of the wonderful tips from reviewers to help assit me in my first 'from scratch' endeavor.  I was really skeptical but HOPEFUL when I found this recipe and all of the reviews.  I didn't want to make a huge batch in case it didn't work out, so I adjusted the servings to 18 and based on that and the reviews: I whipped the  out of 1/2 cup shortening, then added 1/2 cup SALTED butter, and continued to beat it like crazy while SIFTING 4 Cups Confectioner's Sugar and blending into the mix, then added 1 teaspoon clear Vanilla and 1/4 Cup + 2 Tablespoons Heavy Whipping Cream.  I blended it all and then turned the sucker on high.  I did add 1/4 oz more of the whipping cream.  I did not use salt since I used the salted butter.  It was still a little thick and could probably use more cream, but my husband couldn't wait to taste test it for me.  YUM, YUM, YUM!!!

I ADORE this frosting.  However, it didn't seem sweet enough for my family.  They said it tasted a little like cheap Wal Mart frosting, so the next time I made it, I did it with half butter and half shortening. Made all the difference.  Use lemon extract instead of vanilla, and yellow food coloring and you have a great lemon frosting for spring!

Well first off this recipe makes a LOT of frosting. Could make half of it to cover a normal cake. Second I had a bunch of issues with mixing the sugar and shortening together until "well blended". What a disaster. It was so hard and dry, so I just added the heavy cream before the sugar was blended and it turned out just great. This is the type of frosting that needs to sit a day to really enjoy the flavor. I love this recipe and plan on using it often....but hopefully no more disasters in the kitchen! lol
It was only okay..nothing to write home about. I could still taste the shortening.
I put my own twist on the frosting, rather than using all shortening, I used half the amount and the other half I used unsalted butter, it really made a nice frosting.
Everyone loved it... i did use 1/2 butter instead of all shortening.
I made this according to directions, I used it to decorate, it held up well! Tastes good, it does lack the soft butter taste, however, it did what I expected it to do. Thank you:)
Was very good. I used half butter and half shortening. It was great! Don't make what it calls for. 3/4 a recipe was to much for a double layer cake

This frosting was pretty good - I read the reviews so I di d some the changes used 1/2 cup of butter and 1/2 cup butter shortening - I used a lot of confectioners sugar to get this to be pretty stiff it was quite runny - I do wish I has more sugar bec I would have liked the frosting to have been a bit more stiff for the cakes I was decorating all in all it was pretty good.

I used 1 cup butter with 1 cup shortening, regular vanilla since I was coloring a 4-story tangerine ombre cake. It was fantastic. I didn't pipe although I did use a frosting comb. My go-to butter cream from now on. Thank you for the great recipe.
Excellent icing.  I think it tasted even better the day after it was made.

Fab-u-lous! Best buttercreanm recipe I've ever tried. Didn't change a thing and it came out perfect. Loved how eventhough the cake was refrigerated overnight once it was left at room temp. it softened up again. Will definitely keep onhand to use with other cakes. I used a vanilla bean paste and it didn't change the colour of the frosting, it just added little specks of vanilla thoughout which I like.

I made this on a chocolate bunt cake. The flavor was wonderful!! The only thing I didn't like was that after being on the cake for a day it began to get kinda greasy. I followed the recipe exactly. This was my first time at making frosting so I don't know enough about frosting's to keep this from happening. Or how to change the recipe up and use something else. I will keep looking for another recipe but this one does have a great flavor!!
It's a great recipe! I however will not let shorting into my house it's terrible stuff. So I just use real butter and it tastes just awesome without all the trans fat.

Very good recipe.  Nice and smooth presentation on a cake.  Recipe also makes a lot which is great.  One drawback is that you need to have heavy cream on hand.  I made the recipe as is the first time but found the following modifications perfect the recipe:  use 1/2 butter, 1/2 shortening; use 1 tsp vanilla and 1 tsp almond extract (cannot imagine buttercream without the almond extract, makes the recipe pop); and use no more than 6 oz of the cream for medium to thin consistency icing (the whole 8 oz was just too much, can't imagine anytime I would need to add that much).
Amazing!  Everybody at my daughter's birthday party raved about the frosting!  It's a bit labor intensive but DEFINITELY worth it!!!

This is my go to frosting for cakes and cupcakes!!!  You can't go wrong!  Perfect consistancy and easy to alter it so its the consistancy you're looking for!!  It tastes awesome!!  I have made it with half butter and half shortening and that tastes great too!!  We LOVE this frosting!!

I have been decorating for 10 years now and I always used the same buttercream recipe, it worked great with a type of shortening ment just for cake icing. We moved to a very rural area where all I can get is crisco now. I made this 3 times in the last 2 weeks, everyone loved it. I did make a few changes. I can't get clear vanilla here so I used 1t real vanilla and 1t imitation. I let it mix for about 10 minutes at the end. I made it with 1 1/2 cups shortening and 1/2 cup butter and it was firm enough to make flowers and ice cakes but I used fondant over the top. I haven't tried to decorate with it in any other way but when I do I will edit this review. All in all great buttercream icing. I will be using it from here on out.

Awesome, awesome, awesome.  Although this is not technically a "real Buttercream", the shortening makes this taste like a frosting you would get at a bakery.  It is also great for decorating - it has the perfect stiffness.  Everyone loved it when I used it for my 4-year-old's birthday cake.

OMG!! This is the best frosting ive ever had, very comparable to bakery frosting, and so easy. Made the night before, and it was just as good the next day. I did use 1/2 cup butter and 1 1/2 cups shortning.
All we could taste was the shortening. We had to scratch and start over with butter :(

I loved the texture of this frosting because it is great for decorating and it holds well in warm temperatures. However, the only thing that makes me not so crazy about this recipe is that is really has no flavor. Buttercream you need butter flavor so maybe adding a litttle butter extract would help. You can substitute half butter for the shortening but be aware that it will melt a lot faster.

Mm.. I made a few changes to make it a 5: used 1/4 butter and 3/4 shortening as other reviewers suggested, and i only used about 3/4 of the sugar amount stated and it was plenty sweet. I think i ended up adding more cream just because i was trying to frost the cake while it was still a little warm so i needed a softer consistency, but i'm sure i would have used less otherwise. Really good and easy!
Good stuff!

This frosting was wonderful!  I followed the advice of other reviewers and halved the recipe, I only ended up using about 3.5 c of powdered sugar.  I also used 1/2 butter flavored crisco and 1/2 butter for the fat.  I whipped it for about 3 minutes on high at the end and it was amazingly light and fluffy.  Great flavor, but I think next time I make it I will increase the butter a tiny bit more.
Used half butter, half butter-flavored shortening.  Outstanding texture and taste.  Will use this recipe from now on.
I did only use 6 cups of sugar, but it was plenty sweet.  Delicious
Texture was right but lacked the buttercream flavor I was looking for,
This is great, especially if it can sit for a day for the flavors to meld.  We used it to decorate a graduation cake.    It holds color beautifully, and holds up well even in humidity.
Absolutely the best buttercream frosting I've ever tried!

To me, this recipe is all form and no flavor. It is the ideal consistency for  a nice buttercream. But it tastes like . .  Crisco! A giant spoonful of Crisco with each bite. I definitely prefer a buttercream made with butter (or at least some combination of shortening and butter). Can't give it more than three stars.
easy to make and delicious. The only change I made was using half and half instead of heavy cream because I had none on hand.  It still turned out perfect though:-)
Had a great texture, but I could taste the shortening so I wouldn't use this recipe again.

1. Cut the recipe in half, and only used half of the sugar.
2. Use 3/4  of it as white frosting on top of the chocolate cake, add 1/2 TBSP coca powder to the left of 1/4 for the wording of the cake
3. The frosting is pretty good, but I'm not sure if the sugar I used is not good, will try different sugar next time
AWESOME recipe just as is!  You can also add a bit of butter flavoring and almond extract for a more bakery like taste.  Or cocoa powder to make it chocolate.  YUM YUM YUM!
Super easy recipe! Thick and creamy!

I wanted to eat the whole batch out of the bowl.  Screw the cake!  This was sooooo good.  I made this with a yellow cake for mothers day and got so many compliments.  It was the best cake they ever had.  It did make a lot, but next time if I make cake it'll be a double decker just so I can use more yummy icing on it!

I followed the recipe exactly as written.  It turned out wonderfully. I actually didn't get around to reading the reviews until after I was all ready finished with my project. I do have to agree with some of the other reviewers make sure to cream the shortening exceptionally well and when you add the other ingredients before the heavy cream make sure it's throughly mixed. Then after you add the heavy cream whip until it's nice and fluffy. I will definitely be making this frosting again.

This is fantastic and easy.  I did substitute and use 1 cup of butter and 1 cup of shortening.  I frosted 24 cupcakes and put the extra in the freezer.  I love that it made a lot.  My family loves this recipe.  Last night at bedtime my son said, "That frosting was really good, Mom!"  Awww.

When I took over the frosting making in my family, I was 12. I had watched my mum and all the neighbor ladies make it and did'nt know what the big deal was all about! Of course there were no measurements except for "2lg scoops of Crisco or "fluffo" beat it until it looks fluffy - then start sprinkling in some confec sugar then a little milk -more sugar, more milk until the box (1lb,) was empty. Now 2shakes of salt and 1-2caps (from tha vanilla bottle) of pure vanilla,and finally beat it some more. Choc frosting was made the same way except 2-3Tbsps of cocoa powder was added. Try this recipe as is, and add vanilla or choc. as you like. Thanks for the memories! (This was enough to frost the middle, top and sides of a 8-9in layer cake)

This frosting is amazing!!!  It tastes like frosting from the bakery with the perfect consistency for pipping.  At the recommendation of other reviewers, I took the shortening to 1.5 cups and .5 cup butter.  I did not use 8 cups of sugar, more like 7.  It turned out excellent.  This is my new go to frosting recipe.  One word of caution, it makes a LOT of frosting.  I made 24 cupcakes and still had about half the frosting left over.

Wow this is awesome!! This was my first attempt at making and decorating my kids birthday cake and this frosting not only tasted amazing, it was so easy to work with in regards to decorating with the wilton tips. I did use all butter, otherwise kept the recipe the same. I could only make 3/4 of the batch at once in my kitchenaid, it does make alot but it sure goes once the family gets a taste. I did find letting it mix for like 5 minutes made it much fluffier and even better.

This frosting is by far, the best!! I read the reviews about making with butter vs. shortening, and I made mine with butter flavored shortening!  I did not have any heavy cream so used half and half instead.  I also cut the recipe in half and half again since I only had 24 cupcakes to frost, and it was the perfect amount.  I used one box of powdered sugar (16 oz) and did have to use a little more cream.  Perfect consistency and also had a nice sheen to it.  Not too sweet either.  Will definitely be my go-to frosting from now on!

This was super easy to make!!!  The only changes I made was; 1 cup Crisco and 1 cup butter as suggested by others rating this recipe.  I did not add any additional salt due to the butter already being salted.

I love this frosting. When I served my it, everyone thouth that I had order the cake. I have made this recipe 3 times, and each time it turned out great! I know that I will be using this recipe over and over.
subbed milk for cream and it was still tasted good and worked well for decorating! hint-add liquid gradually to achieve desired consistancy.

Not quite perfect, but good.  I substituted 1/2 butter, 1/2 butter flavor shortening.  Otherwise, followed proportions to a T. Flavor is decent. I would agree that the shortning flavor is a little distracting in the background, but not awful. The consistency is excellent! The taste was a bit better after the cake was refrigerated a day or so. I think I'll try all butter next time because it's pretty good otherwise. Not at all gritty.

With some modifications, this is a very delicious recipe. I make this recipe with half-butter & half-shortening, 6 cups of icing sugar (instead of 8) and regular pure vanilla extract. Sure, the icing comes out kinda of cream-coloured instead of bright white, but it still tastes and looks delicious!
This reminds me of Safeways frosting. You can get it almost perfectly smooth on a cake, and it doesn't drive rock hard. Good flavor!

Great Frosting ! Try adding real vanilla bean (dried or fresh) instead of the extract. For those that like more than just a "sugar" flavor, this will be the ultimate real vanilla frosting then. The vanilla "dots" did bother me - very small.

This frosting will make you just go "yummm"! I made with half butter and half shortening for a cake, which was awesome, and 1-1/2 cup shortening and 1/2 cup butter for filled cupcakes with strawberry filling, where I did not want such a buttery taste and they came out tasting like zingers! I prefer less vanilla though, and will decrease it some next time. Definitely a keeper!

This was amazing! I took the advice of other reviewers, and I did half butter, half shortening. I made 2 half batches, because I wanted to make one chocolate. I used about 2/3 cup cocoa mixed with the powdered sugar to do that. Excellent! But it did take more cream than 1/4 cup to get it thin enough to decorate with. Each half batch made enough to frost about 24 cupcakes.

I liked this icing but i think i would have added a bit more of the sugar.  I only added six cups and although it was rich and delicious i just wish it was sweeter.  I have a sweet tooth so when i indulge...i like to indulge! It did ice my son's dinosaur cake very well and was easy to work with.
My daughter made this frosting for cupcakes on my birthday, and I must say I was really impressed. And I was a prof. cake dec. for 24 years. This was good icing.

The texture was great.  I should've read other people's reviews before making it; I assumed it was a great recipe.  It tasted like mildly-sweetened shortening.  Next time, I'll use half butter and half shortening, and see if it'll taste better
This is the real deal...I love this icing!
Very impressed, made my sons first birthday cake with this it turned out so nice and the everyone enjoyed it..
Very yummy
This recipe is very good as it is written to make it great, replace 1/2 of the shortening with butter and it is perfect.

I am dissapointed, considering the amount of ratings and good reviews this recipe has. I have noticed that buttercream that contain all Crisco or half Crisco and half butter will for sure have that Crisco Flavor and that greasy feel in your mouth once you taste it. So, like many other reviewers, I used 1 1/2 C unsalted butter + 1/2 C Crisco instead. This buttercream turned out TOO soft and TOO sweet. The buttercream looked good albeit sweet BEFORE the whipping cream but I thought I should follow through with the recipe. I added 1 oz of whipping cream and it became soft. Definitely not the recommended consistency if you're wanting to pipe with this buttercream.

I'd use less sugar (2-3 C less), and 1 TBSP of whipping cream, if not any at all.
A good, light frosting.

This frosting is fabulous.  I used another reviewer's suggestion for 3/4 c. butter, 1/4 c. shortening, 1 t. vanilla, & 3 tbsp heavy cream - turned out perfectly for my half a cake for my daughter's 6 month birthday. Thank you!

This frosting was the BEST frosting I ever made!  I made this frosting for my daughter's birthday party.  I gave each guest thier own little pastry bag full and put some differnt sprinkles on the table and let them deocorate cupcakes for themselves.  The 8 year olds asked if they could have the recipe because it was the best thing they'd ever tasted!!  I agree!  I followed the recipe to the T, and it came out perfect!

Only change I made was to use butter flavored shortening.  Absolutely fabulous frosting.  Just like the bakery and easy to make.  A half batch even gave me left overs when frosting cupcakes.  Just wondering about how long it can sit out with the whipping cream in it?

This is truly a perfect frosting not only for the taste but it was perfect for piping flowers etc! I made it for a birthday cake and received a ton of compliments! This will always be my "go to" when I make cake!

If your looking for the perfect frosting, you just found it! This fluffy frosting is superb! It can be put together within minutes, and can be used with almost any desert. I loved it and will definitely be making it again!!

I made it with 1/2 shortening, 1/2 butter. The taste is really yummy and it spreads very well. I found I could pipe many intricate details, but not those that had to hold themselves up. It would need to be a bit stiffer for that to be perfect. But for "frosting and borders" as described, it is spot-on.

this Buttercream icing was the best i had i ever tried, i love it soooooooo much, thank u for posting it. i had saw a lot of reviews about it and i decided to take a chance and make it on my sister's b-day since i have to make a cake on everyone's b-day, anyway it couldnt have been any better its the best
I made this just like the recipe said. " It was fantastic "

This is tastes just like the bakery frosting. Wow - Excellent!!   It was great to work with to decorate my Super Bowl XLIV Cake and I used disposable pastry bags.  I also tinted the frosting.  It held up well.  It is not necessary to refrigerate the cake after frosting.  Cover cake and store in a cool dry place works great.  I put fancy frill toothpicks so the clear wrap wouldn't touch the frosting to store.  Half of this recipe is enough to frost and decorate a 9x13 inch cake but if I was going to slice in half and fill I would of make the entire recipe.  Thanks Rick - been looking for a great frosting recipe for a long time - this is Definitely It!!
I used 1/2 cup shortening. 1 cup butter, 4 cups sugar, 1/2 tsp salt1 tsp real vanilla, 1/3 cup heavy cream. It probably would have been way too sweet for me if I had used the full amount of sugar.
This is an amazing frosting, it's easy and tastes great! I added some chocolate and peppermint to make it taste like a "Junior Mint". FANTASTIC! Doesn't get much better than this!

This was really good! I followed everyone's advice of using half butter and half shortening, and im glad i did so. even with a full cup of shortening AND a full cup of butter, the bowl still smelled greasy. the important part was that it didnt taste greasy, so definitely use half butter, half shortening. Also, DO NOT USE 8C SUGAR! i used 7 and it was too much, so i had to add more heavy cream. i'd advice using 5 and a half cups of sifted powdered sugar and then add to your personal taste. the clear imitation vanilla extract has too many unnecessary restrictions. my vanilla extract was alcohol free, meaning it had a thicker consistency and was dark brown-ish but my buttercream still came out snow white. i advise using pure vanilla extract. good luck! :)

I love this recipe.  I use it for every birthday cake I make.  It has a wonderful flavor and yet is thick enough to make directions.    My kids birthdays are all in the summer and I always leave the cake  in the freezer until party time though, as ti does have a tendency to melt some.
One of the best butter creams I've tasted. Nice and rich.

Used 1 1/2 cup shortening, 1/2 cup butter, and reduced sugar to 5 cup, otherwise kept true to the recipe. It's consistency is excellent, and the only complaint I have is knowing I can't assemble my 50 cupcakes ahead of time, because I just don't have the room in the fridge, and I'm topping with a little bit of fondant. I might take the chance if it were January....but it's August, so...last minute put-together it is.   The flavor is good too. Kids love it, and it will go in my box as THE buttercream recipe to use when I don't want to cook.
Great consistency and taste.  I use half butter, half shortening. Only frosting recipe I'll ever need :)
swap out butter for the shortening

I gave this recipe 5 stars even though I altered it, the texture is perfection.

For a 3 layer cake{Undecorated}I use 3/4 cup butter, 1/4 cup shortening, 4 cups pwd sugar, 1 Tbls. vanilla and 2-3 Tbls cream or half and half. I use this on Devils food and other super rich chocolate cakes, YUMMY. 

I rated this recipe because it was these proportions I used when changing to real butter as opposed to shortening, the ratio of fat to sugar is perfect and I added the bit of shortening just to make it silkier.

This is good, I did half butter and less sugar (6 cups).  The texture is exquisite, it is melt in your mouth smooth and creamy.  Literally melt in your mouth.  The taste is great at first with a not so great after taste.  I am going to let it sit overnight because some of these reviews say it's better the next day.  I think with all the sugar it says to use it would be too sweet for my family, but that is a very subjective opinion.  I would make this again.
Yummy!!! A little on the sweet tooth side but still very delicious. I made this recipe today for my chocolate cake but switched out the lard for butter and also cut the recipe in half. Thanks!!

Excellent! I made this for my daughter's bday cake. Used 1-1/2 c butter flavored crisco & 1/2 c butter. Tinted to a beautiful shade of blue! Guests raved about how light and delicious it was! Had enough icing for a small three layer cake and at least that much left over. I froze the leftover for future use. Thanks!!
VERY popular with all my friends on spice cake!  Not too sweet, juuust right!

It turned out REALLY nice, BUUUUUUT, THERE WAS WAAAAAAY too much confectioners sugar.  I ended up cutting the recipe in half. Ok. Fine. Then I added a half cup of confectioners sugar (icing sugar) and slowly started mixing and blending. Oh my goodness! What a workout! It was brutal trying to mix this. I ended up only putting in 2.5 cups of confectioners sugar, instead of 4, because I just couldn't stir it anymore. It was WAY too hard to stir. I also had to add 3 tablespoons of 10% cream (I didn't have "heavy" or whipping cream so I used what was on hand) and that made it the PERFECT consistency. 

Yeah, to be honest, WAY too much confectioners sugar. And mine turned out to be the perfect sweetness.

After reading all the reviews, I decided to take a chance and follow the recipe *exactly* - that's right, NO changes - and it was absolutely delicious! 5 Star all the way. I've taken the Wilton decorating classes, and I used to use their frosting, but from now on this will be my staple Buttercream recipe. I've been looking for a Bakery Frosting replica for years, and this is definitely it! Not only is the flavor wonderful, the texture is *perfect* for piping decorations! I made this with a hand held mixer, and my only tip is to REALLY beat the crisco to get it as light and fluffy as possible before adding the powdered sugar, and then beat it as much as possible after adding the sugar, and again after adding the remaining ingredients. If you're looking for a copy cat bakery frosting recipe, this is it! A+ (Exactly as written!)

This is by far the best buttercream frosting I have found! I have made it exactly as written which was very good and I have made it with a change of the recipe to fit my family's preferences. The change I made is to use 1 cup of shortening and 1 cup of butter. I feel so bad for the people who buy that yucky frosting out of a can from the grocery store. If only they knew about this recipe...

Followed recipe as written.  Very good.  I add unsweetened cocoa to a portion of the the frosting and that was even better!  It covered a two layered 8 inch round cake and 24 cupcakes and there was still leftovers.

im sorry but I didn't care for this recipe AT ALL! i thought it tasted too much like crisco and was really bland. if u added less crisco it would probably tase better. im really mad i made all that frosting... so to finish my cupcakes i made a different buttercream frosting which tasted SOO much better..

I have used this recipe multiple times.  Everyone in the family always asks for a piece to take home.  Do as users say 1/2 butter 1/2 shortening.  And there is a flavoring called WEDDING BOUQUET.  They call it the baker's secret.  And it is!!!  It makes cakes and frosting taste amazing!   ENJOY!!!!
Love this! It tastes amazing! Used on a wedding cake - very easy to work with and easy to color.

While this recipe is really good, it is definitely not for cakes to decorate in the Wilton fashion.  It is too soft to hold up intricate work.  Also, because of the cream, refrigeration is necessary.  Another reason to not use it on a large elaborate cake, unless you have a lot of room in your frig. But if you just want to frost a cake this is really delicious. I don't usually like to lick frosting, but this one is lickable.

LOVE LOVE LOVE this recipe!   
I do make some changes... If using shortening, I use butter flavored Crisco.  But usually I do this recipe using 1/2 butter flavored Crisco and 1/2 unsweetened butter.  I just whip the Crisco and butter together first until it is a very light color.  :)

My nephew asked me to make his birthday cake but he really wanted frosting like bakery cakes have. I used this recipe and he said this frosting is "much better" than bakery frosting! Definitely a recipe I'll use again!
It tastes amazing....but mine came out "gritty."
I made this frosting twice, 1st the way it is written, and the 2nd I used 1 cup of butter and 1 cup of shortening, and it was fantastic both ways.  THANKS!

This frosting was ah-mazing. It was the best homemade frosting I've had. I only used it for a layer cake, so I didn't do any piping or detail work, so I'm not sure how it would hold up to that. Using the clear vanilla left the frosting really, really white, and that made it really easy to add color to. This will definitely be my go to frosting from now on!

Excellent recipe!  I try a different frosting recipe every time I make cake but the search is over.  Even my anti-frosting really liked it.  Just added cocoa powder to make chocolate.  I also added one tsp of butter extract.  Otherwise I followed the recipe exactly.  Not overly sweet and not greasy in my mouth.

This is a fabulous recipe. It is not too sweet or heavy. I also used 1/2 shortening and 1/2 butter and only 5 cups of icing sugar. The consistency is excellent and very delicious. I will be throwing away my old recipe and replacing it with this one.

We are VEGAN here at my house, so I used 1 cup smart balance, 1 cup short., the rest was the same but the heavy cream. I replaced it with 4 ounces of Silk. Worked excellent- I even added key lime juice to one half and 4 TB of Peanut Butter to the other half to frost two types of cupcakes. :)

Pretty yummy frosting.  I halved the recipe & used half salted butter & half organic vegetable shortening.  I left out the additional salt.  I also used coconut extract instead of vanilla because I was making a coconut bunny cake for Easter.  The taste was great, not too sweet, but the texture was a little soft.  I may have to use less butter next time.  Will definitely make again.

I took a cake decorating course and one of the items we were taught to make was buttercream frosting which was very good, but I thought this was better.  I used 3 parts white crisco to 1 part butter and 7 cups confectioners sugar and it was excellent.  Will try different things based on other reviewers.
Excellent! Taste just like our local bakery.
Yum! Just perfect
FANTASTIC!!!  I opted to use just butter as it was for my daughters b.day cake and she loves butter...this is the best frosting I have not only ever made, but ever tasted.  Excellent!
I HAVE TRIED SEVERAL VARIOUS BUTTERCREAM RECIPES AND FOUND THIS ONE TO HAVE THE BEST OVERALL FLAVOR AND CONSISTANCY FOR MY CAKE DECORATING NEEDS.  IT IS DELICIOUS.
This was delicious. I used half butter and half shortening as other people had suggested.
So easy, so versatile, and delicious.
This is exactly the kind of buttercream I wanted - sugary and stiff, just like the bakery.  I substituted about 1/6 of the shortening with butter.  The frosting has a really good flavor.
Really yummy and easy to make. I made it by the recipe and put it on a yellow cake. It's delicious served chilled.
Made as written (only I halved the recipe) and it tastes awesome! Iced a two layer 9 inch cake very thinly - next time I'll make the whole recipe. :)  Thank you!!

I also used the suggestions for 1 cup butter and 1 cup shortening.  It turned out great.  I used it to make flowers and other decorations and it was fine. But I did put it in the refrigerator for 1 hour before decorating and it hardened up nicely.
all i have to say is....YUM!

I am giving this a 5 even though I think that I improved it by using half butter flavored shortening and half unsalted butter. I also used clear vanilla flavor since I needed white frosting. When I don't need white frosting, I use vanilla bean paste which is my secret ingredient. It takes it over the top in my opinion. My entire family thinks that I am the best baker, but all I am is a home baker that has some really great recipes and basic cooking skills.

I have one tip. Do not use butter flavored shortening! I thought I'd change up the recipe a bit and use butter flavored crisco. Mistake! I tossed the whole batch. All I tasted....was butter - and it was gross. I re-made it as-is and it was great! Yum.
I used this frosting for a cupcake in a jar project. Followed exactly
Great frosting. Not  as sweet as  typical buttercream.
Divine!  I have made this dozens of times, and everyone rants and raves about it.  The best part is how simple it is to make!  Thank you for a wonderful recipe!

This is a very functional recipe as I have been in the cake industry for some time.  The secret is to beat/beat/beat the frosting for at least 10 minutes to thorougly dissolve the powdered sugar.  You can use popcorn salt (finer ground) for the salt as this cuts back on the greasy taste.  Great Tasting
Excellent! I followed the recipe exactly and it came out wonderful. My family loved it!

Absolutly delightful! I hate,HATE,hate the Wilton buttercream frosting recipe. I was using another with all butter for a truly "buttercream" icing. It tastes wonderful but gets too soft for decorating details. This is the best of both worlds. I now have a buttercream recipe that I can say that I love! Also, the first batch I made was with the cream which is a great addition, the second batch I didn't have the cream so I made it with milk. It still came out perfect, although not quite as rich tasting. So, FYI, if you don't have the cream, still try this one with milk. You won't be sorry!

I made this buttercream in hopes that it would be great for decorating (as advertised) but it SUCKED. it went from really hard to running off the cupcake in a matter of one minute. Never making it again!

great recipe i added imitation rum flavoring to it and a few more tablespoons of powdered sugar to balance out the texture and keep the frosting stiff. tho next time i think i will try substituting some real unsalted butter for some of the shorting to give it a smoother flavor!

I made this with half butter, half shortening the night before a Memorial Day party--half of the recipe was still enough to frost a two-layer cake with fruit between the layers, with some left over.  The frosting did melt slightly in the 90-degree heat and un-air conditioned car, but in general held up quite well!  Absolutely delicious and was devoured on arrival.

I amade my daughter's birthday cake using this frosting and it was outstanding! I've been buy cakes instead of makeing them lately and wanted to try something different. This was perfect! It is a good size recipe, which is great, and even my leftover frosting disappeared. Excellent!
This was horrible!  It tasted like shortening. (we did half butter half shortening but it still tasted like shortening)  It was really a waste of ingridients and time!
Delicious frosting. Great choice for cupcakes.
I didn't have shortening so I made it with butter. It was a nice pale yellow which worked well on the banana cake and had a great flavour!

this was really great to work with and tasted good. I do like something with a little more flavor though so I would probaby use this again for decorations and boarders only but not as the main frosting.

Even following the suggestions of others - 1 1/2 shortening to 1/2 butter - I found this frosting to be rather greasy and soft, rather than buttery and capable of hcading a design.  Not very good at all.

FANTASTIC!  Wonderful basic recipe.  I doubled it to frost a 9" round layer cake and had some left over. Used 1/2 shortening and 1/2 butter for a richer flavor.  Also, because I was using this to frost the Lemon Chiffon Cake from this site, I used 1 1/2 teaspoons of lemon extract instead of vanilla.

This is my 'go to' frosting from now on. I did make some changes, based on other site reviews: 2 sticks margarine & 2 sticks butter, only 4 cups Confectioner's sugar, no salt, & 5 oz. heavy cream. My family loved it. It's creamy, not too sweet, and buttery goodness. We couldn't stop licking our fingers. The Sweet 16 Topsy Turvy Cake was a big success.
I followed the recipe exactly, but tested 6 servings ahead of time first.  It's delicious!  But VERY sweet. I'm going to try it with two cups less sugar instead.

I'm a beginner at baking.  I made it for my little girls 2nd birthday cupcakes.  This was super easy and everybody raved about how good it was!  I did tweak it a bit.  1/2 shortening 1/2 butter and 2/3 heavy cream and 1/3 sweetened condensed milk.  I just made it for a second time for my big daughter's 7th birthday.  I'll let you know how people like it.

I just made this for the first time and it is truly the BEST tasting and easiest recipe for Buttercream I've ever made.. You won't be disappointed. That said, I did replace 1 cup of the shortening with butter so it had the creamy buttery taste we've all grown to love. Enjoy!, and thanks for sharing.
Mmmmm.... Used this frosting as a filling and frosting for cupcakes. It was terrific. We are in a rather warm climate and I did keep them refrigerated after I made them. Thanks for the recipe!

This recipe was great!  The frosting was light and creamy, and my son won a cake bake-off with it!  I also substituted 1 1/2 cups shortening and 1/2 cup butter, and used orange extract instead of vanilla, it is a nice complement to chocolate cake!

I've made this a few times now, tweaking it a bit each time. The recipe is great, you can make it exactly as written, and rest assured you will have a great frosting for your cake. But I think substituting butter for the shortening was even better with a much richer flavour. I also tried cutting back on the icing sugar as well which was excellent as it produced a less sweet more buttery frosting. The best part about this recipe is how it can be tweaked to your individual tastes and still turn out to be a frosting that is delicious and easy to decorate with

Lovee this frosting! I cut the recipe into a third serving. Unfortuately the consistency wasnt think enough but other then that it was so yummy! I have tons left gotta go to the store and buy more cupcake mix!!!!

THE BEST FROSTING EVER!!!! I bake quite often and always like to test out new recipes and i saw all the reviews for this one an i said i HAVE to make cupcakes!!! I made vanilla cupcakes and cut this recipe in half delish!! This is my new frosting recipe permanently the search is over :)
I did half butter half Crisco like some other reviews said and it turned out perfect! A great frosting for piping and decorating cake.
The frosting was not to sweet and made plenty to frost a lot of cupcakes! Will make again!

This tastes absolutely amazing and  is an awesome way to build your upper arm muscles! Be prepared to whip the mix atleast half an hour to obtain the light fluffy texture perfect for topping cupcakes but the time is WELL WORTH IT!!

This frosting tastes so good!  And it was easy.  Seems almost fool proof.  I did the recommended 6 ounces of cream and the consistency is perfect.  Used 1.5 cups shortening and 1/2 cup butter as recommended by others.  I think next time I will try splitting the shortening/butter ratio to half and half.  But no complaints as is.  Used real vanilla so it's not pure white but I just cook for our family so I don't care.
I found this was a good recipe.  Next time I will add more vanilla though.

Wonderful! I use butter flavor crisco and I usually add unsweetened cocoa powder to make choc frosting and it helps eliminate a little of the sugary taste, so it isnt so overpowering. Don't understand why some people areg etting a greasy taste to this. There was NO greasy taste since i used butter flavored crisco.........best frosting recipe I have ever used. Everyone raves and asks me for the recipe!

I tried this recipe straight up, followed the directions to a tee, and without any ingredient alterations.  I LOVED the texture and how well this frosting stood up to all the piping I do.  This recipe makes A LOT of frosting, but it is ok.  The frosting gets better with time.  A week later I used the leftovers on some cookies, and it was AWESOME!!!  One change that I have made on my next batch was adding 1 tsp. of butter extract and it was even more scrumptious.  GREAT recipe!!!
This was so light, and fluffy, and soooo delicious! This is definetely a keeper. I can't wait to make it again! I used this to decorate "giant chocolate chip cookie" on this site. Thanks for sharing!
Easy to make and use.  Came out very good.  I didn't have clear imitation vanilla extract so I used what I had which was pure vanilla extract.  The frosting still came out nice and white.

Wonderful!!! I used half shortening and half unsalted butter. I used my Kitchenaid and whipped the heck out of it :) I also used regular vanilla extract, not clear, and my frosting was very white so I was glad I didn't make a special trip to the store for the clear :) Very delicious buttercream frosting and I will most definitely make this again!

this recipe was great! since i needed to cover 1 half-sheet, 1 quarter sheet, a 1 baby cake and make roses i changed the recipe to yield enough for 75 people. i started out with 2 cups pre-creamed shortening, 2cups unsalted butter, 1 tablespoon of vanilla,6 ox cream and by the time i added my second bag of sugar( 32oz each or 8cups) it was way too sweet! so i pulled out my cornstarch and began adding 1 tablespoon of shortening and 1 tablespoon of butter until it was just right. this was a very easy buttercream. it had to be easy since i was working with the bare essentials= a hand mixer, a bucket, a plastic serving knife and a scraper. *** side note pre-creamed shortening makes the frosting a little softer. thank you rick and everyone else who added their two cents!

I've tried so many recipes from this site but this my first comment, I just made this recipe & OMG is it GOOOD. the only thing I changed was I put 1/2 butter & 1 1/2 of shortening, I love butter!!! So I had to put some in. Great to work with & wonderful to eat!
Outstanding!

Although this was my first attempt at making buttercream decorations, I followed the advice of previous comments and replaced the 2 cups shortening with 1 1/2 cups shortening and 1/2 cup butter. I have to say, it kept its shape really well, even during its few hours outside of the fridge! It's delicious as well and I can't imagine what it would have been like without butter in it.
Good recipe.  Nice change from the Wilton Buttercream recipe I use.  I used 1/2 cup of butter and 1 1/2 cups of Crisco.
I always use half butter and half shortening and it always turns out amazing!

Oh My Gosh!  This is quite frankly the best frosting I've ever made.  I have a favorite standby thats a cream cheese frosting I lighten up with whipped cream.  I thought nothing could beat that, but this really does.  I only needed half so I used a stick of butter, half stick of the salted butter crisco sticks and omitted the salt.  It was light, fluffy, creamy and delicious.  I'd made other buttercreams in the past that got real firm after setting.  Not this one!  It really was awesome.  I'm so glad I found this and would encourage anyone looking for a new frosting to try it out!

Awesome Frosting!!  You have to make it with butter instead of shortening though!  It's so good you don't even need cake, I'll just eat it straight up!  Leave out the salt if you use salted butter.  I always add extra vanilla, but that's a matter of taste.  Let the mixer whip it for a long long time and it's the fluffiest creamiest frosting ever!
I used half shortening half butter other than that I followed the directions as they were.  This is a keeper for sure!  This icing was really easy to pipe and held up perfectly.
This was fantastic! I did use all butter instead of shortening just because i don't like using shortening. The cream really adds something great to this frosting...loved it!

I followed some suggestions and used 1/2 c. butter with 1 1/2 c. shortening. I probably could have added another cup of powdered sugar to make it a bit stiffer, but that's just being nit picky. I made the full recipe and it was more than plenty to ice a two layer nine inch round cake.

This has to be the best buttercream recipe I have ever tried, and I've  tried a lot of different recipes.  The texture of this frosting is great for decorating and frosting cakes.  My only recommendation would be to replace one cup of shortening with one cup of butter.  It tastes just as good as the buttercreams in the bakery!!

Awesome frosting and so versatile. I have used this for both cakes and cookies and licking off the spoon for girl time. I have used the heavy cream but have also substituted half&half as well as whole and 2% milk. So easy to play around with
Love, Love Love this frosting. I did 1/2 butter and 1/2 butter flavored shortening.  Not too sweet and wonderfully creamy.

I use this recipe for everything. LOVE IT. It holds decorations nicely. I also use it as my crumb coat, I just add regular milk to thin it down a bit. I have tried several other recipes and always come back to this one and everyone loves it.
just like from a bakery.
This recipe is great! I substituted butter for the shortening because that is what I had on hand. I used it on my daughters cake and EVERYONE loved it!
We used this buttercream to frost cupcakes.  It piped very well and didn't get to soft.  Tastes very good also.  Will use this frosting from now on.

This was really good!  I used it twice--once to make some cupcake frosting for some birthday cupcakes, and then again to put the inner layer of icing on a fondant cake for my son's birthday.  The first time I used milk because I had no cream, and it worked fine, but I had to use less to get the icing to hold its shape--it had the same flavor, though, and it was good!  Sweet and creamy and tasty, oh my!

mmm, taste-free frosting! groos, what a greasy mess. even with the alterations of extra vanilla and 1/2 butter 1/2 shortening, it was NOT the buttercream frosting i expected!had to go to the store for more sugar after this one wasted it all so i could make another recipe since i refused to serve my guests this hot mess.

Rick, you rock!  I made this frosting to go over a vegan chocolate cake for my daughter's first b-day, and got rave reviews.  So easy and yummy!  I split the shortening with butter, half and half.  I also put in only about 6 c. of the sugar.  So good I'll never buy frosting again. Thanks!

I used the 1/2 butter 1/2 shortening version of this recipe for a sculpted cake with a lot of detail.
I made sure I used a smooth knife dipped in cool water to spread the frosting and used many different decorating tips.  The frosting behaved very well for all uses and tasted great.  I beat the second batch at a higher speed for a slightly longer time, resulting in an even smoother texture.  I will use this recipe again.
Thank you so much for sharing this recipe!  I LOVE it!!!!!  :0}

I make this with butter rather than shortening, and it turns out very nice. I had to down-scale it a lot for my typical 9x13" cakes, but it does very well so thanks for sharing. A few spoons of cocoa powder make for a nice chocolate icing, and balances the sweetness very well. Sometimes I use instant coffee granules mixed with a very small amount of water instead of some of the heavy cream. That makes a very nice mocha flavor.
Fantastic!  Delicious!  It spreads wonderfully!!!

This is an amazing and very easy frosting.
I used half butter have half Crisco, but next i think i will use 3/4 butter and 1/4 Crisco. 
I also added 1 1/2 tsp vanilla and 1 1/2 tsp almond extract it was perfect. I can’t wait to make this again.
Amazing!

I lost my Wilton recipe for buttercream...I sure am glad that I did!  I used half butter and half shortening and it was absolutely magnificent.  It made the prettiest roses and without breaking!  Since Crisco changed its recipe, all of my roses have been breaking around the edges...not with this icing!  Thanks a bunch!
Awesome recipe! I followed it exactly and it was a big hit! Smooth, creamy, great for decorating! My new go-to frosting!

I don't think this recipe really needs another glowing review, but here it is.  This was wonderful, tasty and easy to make.  I used 1 cup of butter and 1 of shortening.  The color was creamy white and easy to spread.  This is a keeper.  I am not a Wilton cake maker so I need a frosting that is pretty and doesn't need special tools to make a pretty cake.

Okay, I have to admit I was a little weary of this recipe since it calls for shortening, but since I am a beginner I stuck for the recipe ;)  Oh, and I am glad I did!  I was amazing!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

I used this on a cake (also from this site) for coworker’s birthday.  Everyone loved it :)  I am so proud of myself (sorry beginner)!

This was sooo easy to make! I followed a previous suggestion and used 1/2 salted butter, 1/2 shortening, and omitted the salt. Not only did it taste terrific, but it held up to coloring, multiple layers, and lots of moving around. Thank you!

Loved this frosting! I used half butter and half Hi-Ratio shortening, you can buy this at cake decorating supply stores, it doesn't leave any greasy aftertaste. I used 6 cups powdered sugar and a butter vanilla flavoring. This came out really smooth and was so easy to work with.

This is the best frosting i have ever tasted and it is also the first time making buttercream frosting. I did not change anything the only thing that i did different was half the quatity and there was still lots to go round. This is the only one i will be making from now on.  Already given the recipe ti my sister.  Thank you so much my kids and friend loves it.

Excellent texture for decorating.  I used 1/2 shortening and 1/2 butter which gave a light butter color so could only use for colored decorations.  Next time will use all shortening and add butter extract to use for frosting.  Definitely better than Wilton recipe ... doesn't dry out and crack.  This is my new standard buttercream!

I used this recipe exactly as it was for my cousin's hot August outdoor wedding.  I made a three-tier wedding cake and tinted the buttercream for her cake.  It turned out fantastic.  I made it three days before her wedding and stored it tightly in containers for travel.  I frosted her cake the day of and put the cake parts back in the fridge in between...then added my gumpaste flowers.  It held up nicely in the hot August heat and of course, the most important part...it tasted delicious!  Everyone who ate it said it tasted like the professional bakers' secret recipes!  The key....let the mixer do all your work and walk away.  I let the shortening "fluff" for about 10 minutes and I let it fluff for a long time after each addition.
Great recipe. I use half butter and half shortening and it came out perfect.
Best icing recipe I have tried yet!!!!!

This is the best buttercream recipe I have ever tried before, but I read the reviews and substituted 1 and 1/2 cups of the shortening with butter (having made buttercream that tasted "greasy" before) and only added 1/2 a cup of shortening.  It was phenomenal!!  I froze the extra so that I can use it for any decorating needs in the future - perfect decorating consistency, but tasty also.  I also needed to make a lemon buttercream icing, so I substituted the vanilla with lemon extract.  I could not stop "taste-testing".  Didn't give it 5 stars just because if it was made as is with 2 cups of shortening, I do believe it would be too greasy-tasting.  This is a keeper!

Having read previous reviews and being of the younger crowd I thought this recipe sounded like exactly what I wanted.  I do think this recipe is fantastic, but it wasn't exactly what I wanted.  It was too buttery, not creamy enough, and a bit on the sweet side.  With that said, and with what other reviewers have posted, I am not scrapping this recipe but will try to alter it specifically to what I want.

Beware, I halved the recipe and it iced a cake and I have enough left over for at least three more cakes.  We shall see how well this stuff keeps.  :)

I have used this a few times now, I love it because it's not too sweet, and it has a great consistency... easy to adjust to your needs as well, add a little this or that or tweak it however.. its a keeper
This was one of the best if not the best buttercream frosting I have made....I recommend it to anyone...I used the exact amount of ingredients the receipe states and it was awsome!!
Stop calling frosting with no butter in it buttercream.
Made this exactly as stated in the recipe. Tasteless and bland, and way too soft for piping/decorations. Will look for another buttercream recipe.

Put a small dish in the freezer until it's cold, drop a puddle of your concoction on the dish and push it back with your finger - if there's a light skin on the top and the mixture slides back, it's done.  Mine turned out a little too thick when I put it in the fridge, but at room temperature the texture is perfect.  Instead of mincing the red peppers I used peeled/roasted red peppers and put them in a food processor.  Worked out perfectly - lovely red flecks of peppers mixed in with the carrot shreds.  Now here's the real orgasm... pour some jelly on top of chèvre (goat cheese) and serve it with crackers...  OMG!  That'll snap any silly cowgirl right on out of the blues!
