My boyfriend is from Staten Island. I made these for him and he said these are spot on. He is a spicy wimp and these are perfect for him. I used EVOO instead of corn oil, cut back a little on the salt, added about a tablespoon more tomato paste, and a bit more sugar. It depends on the onion you are using as to how you might want to add a little more of this and cut back a little bit on that. This is a fantastic recipe to adapt to your own personal taste without changing the main flavor. I have also used them to top hamburgers, Boudin sausage, and brauts. I would give it ten stars if I could.

I left out the black and cayenne pepper and added a teaspoon of brown sugar. I don't like food so hot that it feels like your mouth is on fire. These adjustments gave the recipe just the right amount of warmth for my taste. Thanks for this keeper!!!

Made this a long time ago when Lillian posted it on another site.  So good!  I have actually made them quite a bit since then cause I don't have a hot dog without them ;)  They are perfectly sweet with some zing from the mustard.  Thanks again!

This is a nice recipe in order to enhance the flavor of the onions, but these onions prepared as such is as a meal in itself with all of the extra condiments utilized. This is alright for a small helping, but to expand the size is to expand the luxurious ingredients with the addition of the lavish calories heaped upon a simple vegetable.

Pretty good!  I've never had onions from a NYC hot dog stand, so I have nothing to compare these to, but I'm confident Lillian hit the nail on the head. :)  I'm generally not a fan of grilled onions, but these weren't bad at all. My hubs commented that the spices added a nice kick. To add pizzaz to our weeknight dinner, I purchased poppyseed hot dog buns and Vienna all-beef hot dogs (the "official" Chicago dog of choice). Served with french fries on the side and cream sodas to cure the heartburn (lol), this was a fun, no fuss meal. Thanks Lillian! :-)

FANTASTIC! If I could give this 10 stars, I would! The flavors of these onions are awesome...spicy, tangy and sweet. A perfect compliment to a hot dog. Hubby said he's gonna ask for these every time I make hot dogs, lol. Made exactly as written. Definate keeper~YUM! Thanks for sharing. :)
Really liked the kick the seasoning gave the hot dog!

Though it's not a recipie I personally would try (a bit spicy for me) My husband LOVED these! He made an egg sandwich and put the hotdog onions ontop and said they are better than the family recipie for peppers! lol!

So good!  Next time I'll rough-chop the onion as I thought the slices where a bit challenging to eat, altho they look great on the hot dog.  I cut back on the salt, plus the hot sauce and cayenne as we are wimpy with hot foods altho we like spicy flavors. (05.20.12; 03.12.17)
I didn't know that I liked asparagus until I tried this sandwich!
Great simple sandwich!  I did saute the asparagus in a little olive oil instead of microwaving.  Nice!
Absolute love. Wouldn't have thought to do this, but will be repeating frequently. I used a chevre gouda instead of the Parm and it was terrific. Can't wait for tomorrow lunch with the leftovers.
I used leftover asparagus for this and my hubby was out of his mind thrilled. Very rare that he comes home from work and raves about the sandwiches I make him. Thanks!

This is a really good idea and as written we found it a little bland.  The second time we left off the butter, added lightly smashed avocado, quite a bit more pepper and a generous squeeze of fresh lime.  Excellent!

Yummy!  This was a great alternative for using asparagus.  I used sour dough bread and toasted it, placed the mayonnaise on one side and used green leaf lettuce with the steamed asparagus and parmesaen cheese and it was wonderful!  Will definitely use again - thanks for the recipe!
This might be my new favorite sandwich.  So good!!!!!!  I used sourdough french bread and lite miracle whip.  YUM!!!!!

Delicious! I used a sesame french bread cut on the diagonal, and lots of fresh shaved parmesean. The asparagus is crisp tender and this really is a great spring appetizer!
Thanks Dakotabear1 for submitting this recipe!
Tasty and easy. I ate this all the time while pregnant with my first.

This was really good!  I heated the asparagus for 2 minutes and added grilled red bell peppers.  I also toasted the bread first (we just used wheat bread).  Made one for lunch tomorrow, I hope it holds up well!
took this for lunch at a tennis match.  Food is important at these matches. Everyone raved.
Really yummy and quick sandwich.
This is one of my favorites now! This tasted much better than I thought it would. I think fresh sliced tomatoes will make it even better next time.
I halved the asparagus spears lengthways, then sliced them into thirds before cooking. I also used lite mayo, and a little more Parm. This was a nice sandwich. Thanks!
Yummy! I just became a vegetarian ( for the 3rd time in my life but hoping this time it will last the rest of my life) and have been looking for new "sandwich" meals w/o meat and this was so good!
This was ok but it didn't taste like the bahama mama I'm used to. What I'm used to: 1/2 oz each: 151, coconut rum, dark rum, coffee liqueur, 4 oz pineapple juice, juice of 1/2 fresh lemon.

The coffee liquor gave it an odd, "Off taste." I've never seen them made this way, but I had some Kaluha and decided to try it. I wish I'd not. I could not even finish it. Skip the coffee flavor for a more authentic taste.
This is great. I have coffee liqueur in my bar and it's nice to find drink recipes that include it.

I tried this recipe and it wasn't at all like
the drink I always get out at restaurants.  It
has a very odd flavor with coffee liqueur.

Anytime I go out for a drink, I order Bahama Mamas. I am also a bartender. Coffee-flavored liqueur IS NOT in any Bahama Mama I've ever had. Try using light rum (or 151), coconut rum, banana liqueur, orange juice, pineapple juice, and grenadine.

I made this recipe exactly as given and it was excellent. The only thing I changed was that I used brandy and more like 2-3 tbsp of mix for added thickness and flavor. The perfect warmer upper in the chilly days of winter.
This was ABSOLUTELY wonderful.  I followed the recipe exact. What a wonderful treat. My eggnog loving husband adored this and my kids had it sans whiskey and just drank it up.

My dad made homemade Tom & Jerry mix every Christmas.  Sorry dad, but this outshines your mix.  It is delicious.  I would omit the Cloves and Mace as I am not a fan of those spices.  If anything, I would add some cinnamon.

Tom and Jerry's have always been a winter treat since I was a young girl (of course back then it was always served sans liquor). My husband and I decided to try this recipe and we will never go back to store-bought again! It just doesn't compare to this. We had couldn't find the ground mace at the store we were at, so we grounded our own from whole nutmeg. Delicious!
This could be a 5 star rated drink mix, but, by increasing the spice from 1/4 teaspoon to 1/2 teaspoon each makes all the difference and brings it too a 5 star recipe.
The mix is great! The alcohol is a shame, recipe for this (20) adults 1c each dark rum, lite rum, brandy and lemon hart 151rum.  Add to empty booze bottle, Shake and pour 1.5 oz per 8oz drink.
Wonderfull! perfect consistancy and flavor. We didnt have a scale, but figured out the proper amounts through a little investigation.

As a Wisconsin native, warm winter drinks are a must. We have a local bakery that makes their own mix, they have been the mix of choice. I made this recipe for the first time today, and it is fantastic! Only note I'll make is that the directions mention adding rum, but the ingredients don't list any rum. I make my Tom & Jerry with 1/2 to 1 ounce each brandy and rum, about 2 1/2 tablespoons mix and about one cup of near boiling water. Mmmmmm. Sure to warn you up from the inside out!

I run a private club, The Fraternal Order of Eagles, Tom & Jerry's are our Christmas Eve tradition, this year, I was not able to get ahold of the mix, used this recipe..WOW...what a difference, our members LOVED it...thank you
EXCELLENT recipe!  Tom & Jerrys are a family tradition so this year I wanted to try and make it instead of buy it.  We add half brandy and half rum with ours and it is very good.

This exactly the quintessential Tom n Jerry Batter of my childhood and young adulthood! I grew in S.D.where there were family owned grocers used to sell their own version of this delicious Holiday beverage mix. So warm and spicy and comforting on cold Winter nights. Share this recipe with your Loved Ones this year and keep the Tradition going!

I make this dessert a lot over the summer, it's my kids' favorite dessert. I like to use the Hostess shortcake cups, if I can find them. This is also good with other berries, too, and even a mixture of strawberries and rhubarb or even berries and bananas, too. NOTE: I'm a little confused at the recipe's ingredient list calling for condensed milk but the directions don't explain on what to do with it. I've never used it in this recipe before but I'm interested to see if it makes it any better than without it.
Like the other reviewers....not sure what to do with the sweetened condensed milk, so I didn't use it. Otherwise, it's a nice simple "recipe". I used the sweetened whipped cream from this site.

I just made this with the condensed milk and it was awesome.I did add a little regular milk to the strawberry mix so it wasn't as thick and I added some blueberries as well.Thank you for the recipe :)

I LOVE strawberry shortcake! It is one of my favorite desserts. I was searching for a recipe to make it when I came across this one. It is very quick and easy! I skipped the condensed milk since I didn't know what to do with it. For the shortcake cups, I used the ones publix sells. Its usually next to the strawberries. I love this so much! Its like having  a short cut to one of my favorite desserts with 1/2 the wait time! I used heavy whipping cream and added in 2 tbsp of sugar when I was whipping it. Next time I think I'll use the whipped topping cream in a can and see how that turns out!
I had to make it for almost 80 people. But I would love to make it again

The milk can be used in two different ways. Chilled before using.
1. Stirred in with the strawberries after they have chilled for an hour then proceed as stated.
2. Poured over the shortcake after it has been assembled but, before the whipped topping goes on.
I love this. Not sure what to do with the condensed milk.  I also like mine with the strawberries sliced not mashed and cool whip.
I used a large can of crushed and a large can of diced tomatoes and reduced the recipe by 1 cup of water.  This was a great sauce with body and full flavor.  Will definitely make again.
Definitely use less water when making this recipe! I would say 3-4 cups and even that can be too much. Otherwise, this was a very good basic recipe.

This recipe needed some tweaking in my opinion.    First, the onion to seasoning ratio is alright but the garlic and sugar is off and there isn't enough sugar.    I followed this recipe and as most people found, it is hard to find tomatoes in a paste form already. I changed it as follows:   1. lg can of crushed Contadina Tomatoes  1. Lg can of diced Contadina Tomatoes  2. 12 oz cans of Contadina tom. Paste  1. 6 oz can of Contadina paste w/garlic (makes up for the lack of enough garlic in the orig recipe)  2. 1/4-1/3 cup of sugar.. I added to taste. I like my sauce sweeter   1. 1 tsp of salt    For the red wine, I suggest a sweet red. I used one called Campagna Di Romani but any sweet wine will do. The wine gave it some sweet to counteract the acid from the tomato.    After the changes, the sauce seems much better and has a lot more flavor to it.
First time to try a sauce like this. I started with fresh garden tomatoes then added about a tsp of salt and 1/3 cup of white sugar. Very good, I'm going to use this for pizza sauce!

A most definite keeper. Took my time with this one but added 1 tblsp salt, 1/2 tsp garlic salt and 2 bay leaves. Absolutely fantastic! Had even frozen half of it and seemed to taste even better afterwards. Go figure!
I have to agree with the other viewers - too watery.  I added salt because taste was a little bland.  Will not make again.

I have been adjusting spaghetti sauce for years. I cook if for 4 hours, and use spicy pork sausage with the ground beef. I use a very good Cabernet, $30 per bottle. The addition of mushrooms  is good too. Spices include bay leaf, fresh garlic, basil, oregano, hot red peppers, olive oil,  and anything else that looks good. Chopped tomatoes taste better than red sauce. Black olives are nice too. Then I watch a movie, make the husband grate Parmesan cheese for the sour dough bread. We zip the leftover wine. Then we open bottle # 2, pick out another movie. By this time we have 4 hours of simmering and a really happy husband.
I didnt even try putting all this water in this sauce. I put 3 cups in, but I used my own tomato sauce and tomatoes that I canned too. It was very good. And added more fresh garlic.

I had to increase the amount of garlic, decrease the amount of water, add extra ingredients (that were not used in the original recipe), and to thicken it up I added tomato paste. After all of the changes the sauce turned out pretty well.
Amazing...I only tweeked a little to make it spicer and I did add fresh oregano.  Great recipe!!!  I used San Marzano Tomatoes (D.O.P. certified)....made the difference!

This is a really good recipe. I used 1 1/4 cup of water instead of 7, because it's a ridiculous amount. Also I added 1/2 cup of Prego Roast garlic and herbs, cumin, oregano and a tbs of butter. I skipped the wine because I didn't had any and it was fantastic!

I thought the recipe came out great, but I made a couple of changes. I couldn't find peeled tomatoes in paste, so i just brought canned peeled whole tomatoes in juice/sauce, and brought an extra can of tomato paste. I added sautéed green peppers.I used NO water. For me, the juice from the cooked onions, green peppers, and canned tomatoes produced more than enough water. I put it it in my slow cooker on "low" for 5-6 hours. This was my own particular twist, but i added a small habanero pepper to give it an extra "kick" to it- you don't have to do this though. Ive been reading for years that once you make your own simple spaghetti sauce, you'll never go back to store brought spaghetti sauce again- now I know that to be true! Goodbye Prego and Ragu, its homemade sauce from now on!
Didn't care for this one, not saying it's a bad recipe, just wasn't to my taste.
This sauce is excellent  - reduced the water by 1/2 and increased tomato sauce

I also used home grown tomatoes and NO water.  I changed the recipe quite a bit.  Other than the basic cooking directions, I didn't really follow the recipe at all.  I also simmered for longer than this recipe called for.  My end result was absolutely delicious.  I would suggest following the very basics of this recipe, but not the recipe as a whole.

This came out wonderfully, but I'm at a loss as to why it needs to be simmered for more than 40 minutes.  I didn't have basil on hand, so I substituted with oregano and followed the directions to the letter otherwise, and I have to say, it came out divinely.  Very flavorful and rich without being too heavy.  It's now officially my favorite meatless sauce recipe.
Very good. I used less water.

I made some changes. I added a pound of ground pork, a garlic seasoning packet, Italian seasoning packet and 4 cups of water. No wine. I simmered it for 5 hours. It's perfecto. For my boyfriend who's extremely picky to like it. It's got to be good.  This one is a keeper.
Very Good.  I added a small green pepper and 1/2 lb of ground turkey and 1/2 lb of ground beef.

People are correct as to the water volume,thats a ridiculous amount. I used Tomatoes from our garden and about 4 cups of H2O with 3 cans of Tom. paste. It came out perfect. I added some other goodies from the garden as well. It was straight up Vege Sauce...
I cooked for 6 hours, added a teaspoon of salt and only 6 cups of water.  It was worth the wait:)

I thought that 7 C. of water seemed a bit much. I think it must be a typo! I used only 2 c. of water, and upped the amount of red wine to 1c. also added salt.  It might be that it's hard to find crushed tomatoes in PASTE and everyone is using crushed tomatoes in JUICE, the way that you find it in the stores. But I also added Parmesan cheese and meat. Came out okay. Just your basic tomato sauce. I'll keep looking- the one i'm looking for is thick and rich, not too chunky with a rich wine flavor.
Something is wrong with this recipe. It has way to much water. It doesnot thicken in the cooking process and is a very watery spaghetti sauce.
To  runny

I tweaked because I used what I had on hand. WONDERFUL SAUCE!! My husband and I both agreed it was our favorite: 1 chopped onion cooked til transparent, 4-5 cloved garlic chopped, 2-15 oz. cans petit diced tomatoes with garlic and olive oil added, 1-15 oz. can tomato sauce, 1 Tblsp. olive oil, 1 1/2 Tblsp. sugar, 1 tsp. salt, 1 tsp. course black pepper, 3 heaping Tblsp. Italian seasoning, 2 heaping Tblsp. basil. I had NO red pepper and NO wine, and I added NO water. That's what I had on hand and it was GREAT!

I had to cook for about 6 hours to get it to not be so watery, and the taste was worst then the cheapest canned store bought sauce in my opinion. Even with doctoring it up, it was bland yet spicy at the same time.

Yum!  I still have 2 hours of cooking time left and this is by far the best recipe for spaghetti sauce ever!  I used tomatoes from my garden and it is my first time cooking with fresh tomatoes instead of canned.  Now I can make batches of this until my tomatoes are gone and freeze it for later!!  Thanks Cathy!  My house smells great!

Very tasty and very simple to prepare.  I simmered it all day and it made the house smell wonderful.  It made a very large pot of sauce, much more than 6 servings as the recipe states.  I will definately make this again.

Just like some of the others warned, this was waaaaaaaay too watery.  If you follow the normal recipe, you might as well pull out a cup and straw 'cause you will end up with tomato water.  I had to cut the recipe by one cup of water and still had to add 3 extra 6 ounce cans of paste just for it to come out somewhat normal.  For added flavor, I put in 1.5 cups of parmesean cheese and 2 extra cloves of garlic.  Unless you are cooking for all of Rome, cut the number of servings as well.
This is exactly what I was looking for. I have a family recipe that always started with Prego as a base. Then we add the rest. Thank you!!

I made this recipe with fresh tomatoes and tomato sauce b/c that's what I had - it was AMAZING!  My kids kept walking by and eating a spoonful of it.  So good!  I actually quadrupled it twice and froze several batches - can't wait to try it in different Italian dishes.

This is a very watery Spaghetti Sauce recipe. I also prefer my sauce a little sweeter. I don't think I'll make this one again, unless I make some adjustments to the recipe listed.. Wish someone would correct/change the amount of water for this recipe for the sake of others making this in the future.

This sauce was fantastic! I let mine simmer in a crockpot on low for 8 hours for timesake and it worked great! The reason for 4 stars would be the way the recipe is written. I agree that 7C water is too much for my liking. I used 4 C water. My local stores do not carry ground tomatoes in paste- so I was forced to used Crushed tomatoes in puree. It seemed to work just fine for me. The flavor was very seasoned and delicious. Can't wait to eat the leftovers.
Its delicious. I completely omitted the water but used peeled whole tomatoes in tomato juice. Added salt and garlic powder to taste.
A little too red winey flavored for me, but I will keep this recipe and alter it slightly next time.

I thought that this recipe was WONDERFUL. I dont know why everyone is saying to not use so much water. I used the measurements, and I actually added some. I dont know if their not simmering it long enough or what, but I simmered mine longer then suggested because my husband was late from work, and because of that, I added a bit more water. My family is Italian, and this came close to my grandmothers sauce...except, when I was pouring the wine, a little extra spilled in, and it was a little more then my liking, but that was my fault. Take your time with this sauce, let it simmer a long time, and if you can put it in the fridge over night, reheat the next evening and serve. Sauce is always better the next day! Thanks for the recipe!
I made this recipe using REGULAR peeled ground tomatoes.  I added MORE garlic.  I also let it simmer for 7 hours.  It came out PERFECT!
This was a very tasty way to enjoy spaggheti sauce on a low fat/low salt diet.
This recipe was horrible i'm glad that i was smart enough to not add all the water.   But i'm thankful my children had nothing to complain about,  they will eat anything.
Question... im using fresh tomaoes from my garded. Do I peel the tomatoes before cooking them?
I turned it more into a baloney's, but it was good!

I have made a lot of versions of basic spaghetti sauce and this one worked the best. It had just the right amount of herbs and spices and was absolutely delicious. Best eaten the second day, and freezes like a dream.
Pretty good. Sauce is a little bit watery and a little bit bland, but it was a very good base for a basic spaghetti sauce. Now I can play with the seasoning until I get exactly what I want.  Thanks!
I agree about the water issue. Don't add any water at all and this recipe is fantastic.
This recipe was very very good and my husband really loved it.  He's not even a real spaghetti fan so I took that as a big do-over idea.
omg I loved it its amazing this recipe is great is you follow it the right way :9

I used this recipe to help save another sauce recipe  made with deer meat.  The red wine helped tone down some of the gaminess.  I too used less water and added bay leafs.   I will keep to use again!!!

This was surprisingly underwhelming!  It wasn't BAD, but it wasn't great.  I have a hard time getting excited about "OK" recipes.  I probably won't make this again unless I make some serious changes.  I'm looking for out-of-this world flavor and this recipe didn't even come close.
I must say this is an excellent recipe.  I added ground pork and ground beef to the sauce and I found it a bit too watery, so I will likely only use 4 cups of water next time.
easy recipe to use fresh grown tomatoes!very easy to prepare in a hurry!
Great refreshing flavor but so many seeds. Strain it would be my suggestion
I made this exactly as directed and it was wonderful and refreshing. Love it!! Thanks for posting.
This was excellent, especially after a day or two in the fridge.

This is really tasty, though a little strong and sweet for my taste - which is easy to adjust with water and/or less sugar. The mint and lemon together are great. If I was a drinking gal, vodka would be the sure way to go with this - total refresh and fall over. An extra cool thing about this recipe was, while I was digging through my utensils trying to find something to use as a muddler, I found ... a muddler! Magic! Who knew I had one? Thanks for the yummy drink and helping me find a muddler! :D
what a great use for peppermint, i've got a lot of it.  will try this, but will use real lemons to make my ade.
quite the drink! not much to it, but i really find it delicious! some of my favourite things are chocolate, lemons, and mint, so this is good for meeee!

I have used a similar technique using basil bouquet so I thought I would give the mint leaves a try too when I came across this today. I tried 2 new recipes today and liked this one best. However, I personally like to make fresh lemonade with around 6 lemons, then do a simple syrup with 1 part sugar, 1 part water and a bundle of the mint (or basil) leaves I boil it on high, remove the bouquet and add the syrup to the lemon juice and pour in 1 bottle of chilled pellegrino water and serve chilled with ice. It is not too sweet or too strong and the mint (or basil) tastes so delicate with the bubbly water. Plus its kid friendly. Enjoy!

This was a big hit at my Kentucky Derby party. I lightened it up by using 1 cup of Splenda and muddling the mint with 1/4 cup of sugar. I also added the juice of another lemon. I will use it again over the summer.
I made it for my little brother's graduation dinner and was very refreshing, my parents, siblings and sister in law loved it.Thank you for the recipe Debby!
This is excellent!
My favorite summer drink!

This was not as smooth as other Long Island recipes I've tried.  I added a bit more cola to make it more palatable, but it was still not my favorite (I did manage to finish it, though ;) ).  CHEERS, allrecipes!

I personally prefer mixing everything (except the coke and ice) in a shaker first and shaking it. I feel it mixes the liquors together better and helps enhance the flavor. It also helps diminish the strong alcohol flavor that comes from just dumping them all into the glass. It also makes the drink look a lot better. The mixture of all the liquors and the syrup becomes really think and beige like, so when you add the coke it really darkens up and actually looks very similar to iced tea.

Easy to make & spices make it standout from all others.
I did add some ground chipotle pepper to the mix & lowered sugar to 4 cups-
I cooked low & slow in crockpot for the 1 1/2 hours
Guess what everyone's getting for gifts now?!?!

This is the first time I have canned anything. I wish I had of read the reveiws before starting this recipe. I mad it as printed, however, I cooked it a lot longer than the 1.5 hours. It was like soup. I kept waiting and waiting and waiting for it to thicken. It seemed to take forever. Once it did get thick, it was then too thick. I don't know if this is an error on my part  having never canned before or not.
As for the taste, it is a little too sweet. The spices are great though.

This was my first time canning preserves. The recipe seemed simple and straight forward, so I prepared the peaches but I questioned the amount of sugar. So I started with only 2 cups of white sugar with the 10 peaches and it's was already too sweet. My wife and I decided it needed more peaches, so I added 5 more peaches to the mixture before I had it to the point of not tasteing too sweet. The cinnamon and cloves were just right.
I will definitely make this again. I didn't let it thicken too much because I wanted more of a topping. The spices are perfect! I think it would make a nice topping for waffles or pancakes.
Great taste but way too much sugar.. Added 5 cups and made the pot the consistency of soup.. I think I will start with 2-3 Cups next time.
Love them...

I cut the sugar with in half and added half with stevia sweetener. I loved the taste of how the cinnamon and ground cloves came through. Make sure the peaches are slightly on the ripe side. I wouldn't change a think about this recipe.

Yes this one does take some time to prepare, and has a very unusual ingredient for ice cream with the acorn squash! Very gentle flavour, with a very smooth and luxurious feel to the final product.  I made it as in the original recipe, but did add a dusting of cinnamon, not only for looks but it did complement the final taste.  None of your guests will guess the main ingredient, so interesting to serve to guests.  For me this one should be paired with some crisp spicy cookies or a slice of apple pie...

Kids and I decided to deviate from the usual smoothie today and instead made this.  I had leftover peach juice from a can of peaches that I used instead of buying peach nectar. Other than that, I followed the recipe, only doubling it because I knew my daughters would not want to share.  I was right - they wanted even more after they drank the first one.  Great refreshing drink that I am sure will get many requests in this house.
It's good. It reminds me of the bath tub punch that you make, then put sherbet in it.
This is the best non-alcoholic drink I've ever had! Definetley 5 stars!!
I followed the recipe exactly except substituted the saffron for just a pinch of tumeric. It was awful. I couldn't even eat it. It sounded delicious though.

This is a simple and absolutely delicious tomato soup. 
I doubled the recipe (glad I did, because the wife and I put away well over the original recipe's worth), left out the celery (only because I forgot it), added a bit more curry powder, and a touch of cayenne for just a little heat. 
I also added about a half a cup of milk to thin it a little and well...because I thought it would be tasty ;) 
We garnished with more cilantro and a dollop of sour cream. Fantastic!
Excellent!  I served this at my book club and everyone loved it!  The only complaint is that a double batch wasn't near enough!
I work as a chief, and the whole hotel LOVED this soup! I will be making it again!
This soup is amazing. The saffron really makes it delicious!

I roasted my own tomatoes as anything from a can lacks the texture and flavor of freshly made food. I also added just enough homemade chicken stock to get the right consistency, and once the tomatoes were finished, placed them with fresh basil in a bowl and loosely covered until cooled. This is not a bad recipe at all, but like with any food, can be tweaked and changed per "customer" :) 

I am only rating this as "OK" because I made changes that bettered the overall outcome. I'd still recommend trying it and keeping an open mind to new ideas that can be added. Tomatoes are SO versatile, so have fun!
Loved it!  I didn't have any saffron and added a pinch of turmeric like the previous reviewer.  I also doubled it and even so, it didn't yield a lot.

Very good! I did not blend it, added way more curry than called for, and basically tripled it. It was good, but not a lot. I also added garbanzo beans, which did nicely (I roasted them with the tomatoes.
Roasted home-grown plum tomatoes and added some milk at the end of the recipe to thin it out and increase the amount of soup. We really liked it and hubby said I could "make that again".
delcious and easy.. I adore saffron and was happy to find a recipe for soup with this  I reduced the oil and left out the butter  - i need to cut calories
I doubled the carrots and celery, lightly pureed the soup and it was SAVORY, chunky and fresh. I loved it!

AWESOME!  I had some frozen tomatoes left over from last summer and they worked beautifully.  Roasting the tomatoes is a must, it brings out the wonderful flavor of them.  I don't buy saffron because of the cost but substituted a pinch of tumeric.  Be warned about tumeric, just a pinch or your soup will be over-powered.

We adore this pesto. Used fresh ingredients from my garden. This pesto is a five star recipe. Just a tad of heat on the back of your tongue. Not too spicy so you could add more jalapenos if you like. I actually posted this recipe. I just wanted to point out that if you exchange the cheese with cottage cheese it will add a lot of moisture and will definitely make it too soft. You can replace the cheese with crumbled tofu and that works really well. Freeze the tofu first because it changes the texture a bit. Then make sure you squeeze out the excess liquid from the tofu before crumbling it and adding it to the recipe. Lastly I have since made this recipe by exchanging the oil for water (there's already enough fats from the nuts) and didn't really notice a difference. So that's a good option too.

I used a lot more onion and replaced about 1/2 cup shredded cheese with cottage cheese.  I also added the sauce after about 25min so it would cook longer.  I wouldn't cook it more than 40min next time, since it was a bit dry at 50min. Next I will try them in a tomato sauce.  Can't wait to make them again!!

I wanted a recipe for fresh pumpkin that was savory rather than sweet, and this seemed to fit the bill.  So glad I tried it! Very easy and very delicious.  After making it with fresh pumpkin, I can see how it would be very easy to use a can of solid pack pumpkin in place of the cubed pumpkin.  I served this with jasmine rice.

My substitutions/modifications: 
-instead of curry paste I used 2 tbsp curry powder and 2 tsp ground cumin, which is what I use every time I make curry
-substitued chick peas for the lima beans (glad I did, because the cooked pumpkin cubes are the exact texture of cooked lima beans...chick peas are firmer and added nice texture)
-used lite coconut milk
-chicken broth instead of water
-added 2 chopped garlic cloves
-added about 2 tbsp chopped candied ginger

While these changes seem excessive, they were based on my experience as a cook, what made sense to me, and what I had on hand. (Everyone is always giving me candied ginger as a gift...so I have figured out creative ways to use it up!)
All in all, a fantastic recipe...very quick, healthy, and delicious!

Easy to make.

Yummy. I did use the heavy cream,petite tomatoes and my own Italian spice. I also doubled the recipe. It worked like a charm.

Very Good.  My daughter requested it for days after... great for freezing and reheating for quick dinners too!
Outstanding.  I've used this sauce on everything from pork to chicken to gnocchi.  Simple and delicious, I will not be buying store made sauce ever again!

Caramelized my onions. Put this sauce over tortellini, spinach, and grilled chicken. Very, very, good.

Very good sauce and so easy to put together. I used half and half instead of cream because that's what I had and I increased the amount of garlic. I will make this often.

This was a hit with the fiance.  It works so well over penne pasta and is a wonderful cream based sauce.  Next time I will probably add some parmesan cheese to it to give it some cheesyness. I have made this nearly a dozen times already, and I keep meaning to review.  This is my favorite "last minute" sauce.

I love it, very tasty and delicious, I will make it again!

Wonderful sauce.  I like mine chunky. If I wanted it smooth is use tomato sauce instead of tomatoes. Also if u take out the CREAM and use skim of course it's going to be runny. Cream helps thicken it. But NEVER use flour. Blah it ruins the taste. Use cornstarch  makes a nice smooth thick sauce without sacrificing taste. I always use it in gravies, sauces.... Anything that calls for a thickener. I take out some of the sauce add the cornstarch till it's thick like icing. Then add a little bit at a time. Wait till it boils and see how much it thickens. Add more if necessary. But be careful not to add to much at a time or u will be adding more liquid. So much better then flour.

I learned the hard way the first time. And I also put in at least double, if not triple the garlic. You can never have too much garlic! :) All in all, a wonderful recipe.

So I have reduced the amount of sugar to no more then 2 or 3 tablespoons and I have added red pepper flakes to the onion and garlic as they sautee to add a bit of a kick.  I now use crushed tomatoes (28 ounce can) and add a 6 ounce can of tomato paste to thicken the sauce.

Wonderfully rich and creamy.  One hint to help thicken the sauce is to add a bit of grated parmesan cheese at the end if it isn't thick enough. That will thicken it without worrying about a "floury" taste.
I loved this recipe. I added chicken meatballs and I mashed the tomatos with a fork because I'm not a big fan of chunky tomatos. It turned out great :) I loved the sweet creamyness of it.
I was hesitant to make this at first because I used to HATE chunky sauces but I loved this! Amazing base recipe since I always add my own tweaks to tailor it for my family but jut awesome :-)
Yummy

So I realized I did not have cream after I started making this sauce. I used cream cheese in the place of it. I think it would have tasted better if I had not used salt at the beginning, because adding the cream cheese made it more salty. But it isn't bad! I think the sauce is a little too sweet for me though.

I only had stewed italian tomatoes, so I pureed at the end. Delicious! I also added 1/4 cup of parmesean cheese, 1/4 cup freshly chopped parsley, and a couple of sprinkles of Italian seasoning. I will definitly be adding this to the family recipes!!

Very good. Here are the changes I made(only 1 really).  Only 1 TBSP of olive oil to cook onions and garlic, after cooked them a little while I put all my spice in, drained the tomatoes and put them in the blender, then put them in with other stuff, cooked 5 minutes added cream and butter , cooked another 5 minutes...done.  It was great and not runny in the slightest.
I followed this recipe almost exactly, except that I added just a little bit more cream. This was delicious and everyone loved it! We served it with venison over egg noodles.
Absolutely delicious!  I followed recipe to a T except I used 2 green onions instead of a whole onion to make it less oniony.

Really fast and easy dinner from ingredients I already have on hand!  I doubled (ok maybe tripled the garlic) and I used half and half instead of heavy cream!  Also used a hand blender at the end to slightly puree it . I think it wouldn't be as good otherwise!  We gobbled this up with crumbled sausage and penne pasta! It only served 4 of us so I would definitely double this recipe for leftovers or seconds!

I've made this twice.  The first time I used 1% milk because I didn't have cream and added flour to thicken and it tasted good, and I'm sure the cream would make it just that much better!

The second time I made it, no one (including me) really liked it.  ???  It was really bland (which is weird because of all the spices).  I hate that I can't rate it higher, but I'm only giving it 3 stars.
This is very good.  I did, however, use evaporated milk in place of heavy cream.  I would definitely share this recipe with my friends.
Loved this recipe! Very easy to make. I added balsalmic vinaigrette at the end to give it some extra sweetness. Worked really well!
It tasted amazing. However I felt copious amounts of herbs to be able to actually taste taste the flavor.  I also didn't appreciate that the cream had a slightly grainy look and texture.

Quick, easy, and really tasty.  I use one Tbsp of Italian seasoning instead of the other 2 separately.  We use 1/2 and 1/2 to make it a little better for you.  Last time, my husband added some cooked italian sausage and it turned out great!  The only thing is...this recipe only makes enough for the 2 of us...there's never any for leftovers!

I read many of the commentaries before making this, and decided to blend it before adding the heavy cream and also added 4oz cream cheese and some asiago/parmesan shredded cheese.  It was nearly what I was looking for, but it lacked a little flavor.  I thought it was good, but my husband thought it was really bland.  Maybe more basil?  I'm not sure.... I do think I'll make it again...but it needs a little more kick.
Not a huge fan of this, tasted like it was missing something....but it was nice to try something new : )
This sauce was so  delicious!! I didn't change a thing and it turned out perfect!!  I made it to put on my potato gnocchi!!!!  Yummy!!
My kids loved this.  I omitted the sugar but otherwise made exactly.

I thought this recipe was amazing, but i  doubled the sauce and instead of using 2 cloves of garlic i used 4, and one large onion instead of 2..I used a little less than a box and a half of whole grain penne and the doubled sauce was just right for 5 people, and 2 servings left over for lunch the next day at work.  The other thing i would also recommend pureeing at least half of the sauce if you prefer a smoother sauce... This was an amazing recipe..I think next time I may add some grated parmigiano reggiano to the sauce next time... mmmmmmm

This was wonderful!

I added just under 1/4 cup onion because many reviews said it was too onion-y. That turned out to be about 1/3 onion rather than a whole. 
I also added 1/2 can tomato paste. 

It was perfect! Wanted to lick my plate.
It was ok, but not anywhere near as good as I hoped.  I wont be making it again.
Excellent sauce, I followed the directions to the letter.
Love this sauce. So easy to make

This was absolutely delicious.  I went to an italian restaurant and ordered chicken parmesan- the spaghetti had a different sauce on it than the chicken- and it stole the show! I found out that it was a tomato cream sauce and immediately went looking for a way to make something similar. I made this exactly as directed with some additional pepper (my personal taste). It was amazing. My only regret is that I did not make more! Definitely delicious!
Very easy!  I didn't change a thing.  Served over homemade pesto ravioli.  Yummm!
I changed it a little with adding garlic & onion powder. Also used fat free milk. Very nummy! I will make this again!

My very picky eaters loved this recipe...I used garlic diced tomatos and that really brought out the garlic flavor.  I even added some groud up italian sausage which one of my eaters loved, the other didn't like chunks in her food.  Would definitely make again.

This is a great sauce!   
I did add cooked crumbled bacon and sausage.
This will be a regular meal at our house.
My family loved this! Next time I will double the recipe. No need to puree -
Love this sauce.  I also used a tomato sauce as a substitute when I was out of diced tomato and added some parmesan cheese.  Absolutely wonderful!
This was very tasty, I didn't have heavy cream so i sub with low fat organic milk and cream cheese, with a half tablespoon of corn starch to thicken the sauce! Will use again and again. Thanks
Yum! Really easy and tasty sauce. I would make this again.

Beautiful sauce...easy to make.
I added a little touch at the end of nutmeg...

yumm! so easy! This recipe turned out great.I added italian stle pureed tomatioes instead of diced tomatoes then I tossed the sauce with penne pasta covered with a generous sprinkle of parmesean and baked an additional 20 minutes. Next time I will add turkey sausage, green peppers, purple onion, and maybe top with mozzarela. I will definetly be making this again!
My family loves this recipe! It's super quick & easy & absolutely delicious by itself, or with a little grilled chicken thrown in. A definite family favorite!
Puree the tomatoes, add cream cheese instead of heavy cream... Chicken and fancy cooked pasta... :-)

The whole family liked this recipe.  My two-year-old and five-year-old picked around the tomatoes, so I will run it through the food processor next time, as others have suggested.  I cooked some mild Italian sausage separately, added it during the last 5 minutes, added penne pasta when the sauce was finished, and stirred it all together.  My husband asked me if it was a different sauce from what I usually make (which comes from a jar), and I told him it was homemade.  He said it was really good, and then asked if I was serious about it being homemade.  He was impressed.  This recipe is definitely a keeper.  Bonus that I usually have all of the ingredients on hand.

So yummy & easy. Even my picky kids ate it. My husband thought it was a bit too sweet, so maybe I will cut down the sugar next time. I doubled it. I did not saute the garlic & onions. But I used a can of diced tomatoes with garlic & onion and another can with basil, oregano & garlic. I put a little olive oil in and blended it since my kids don't like chunks. Then I followed the recipe as directed. I really like this and will use it often!

This is extremely delicious and easy to make! I decided to add green peppers and more onion, garlic and cream than was mentioned. I also did not use the canned italian style diced tomatoes, but regular tomatoes. You can definitely change it around a bit to fit your taste. I served it over spinach fettuccine alongside fried chicken cutlets and some homemade bread. Everyone loved it! Don't use half and half instead of heavy cream. Some suggested it so I tried it and I was very disappointed!!

Very tasty! I used a 28oz can of crushed tomatoes and doubled the other ingredients (except for the onion), substituted fat free half, and cooked the sauce for a bit longer. I think I would also use a lot less basil next time.

This was quick easy and wonderful! I followed the directions to a T and it was delicious! I had all the ingredients on hand so this was perfect on top of homemade ravioli I was making for lunch.  I will definitely make this again. ^_^
This was so easy to make and it was delicious!!  The only thing I will do differently next time is double it. there was not enough sauce to go around.
I was worried it wouldn't be thick enough, but it was perfect! Added some cheddar cheese to it as well, really helped to pull it all together nicely. Also added a bit more cream, but yummy!

My boyfriend actually found this recipe one night we he cooked to surprise me.  This sauce has a lot of flavor is great with ravioli or any pasta you can think of.  I am thinking about trying to couple with pork in a chicken parmesan style dish. We shall see... This recipe has become a staple in our house!
DUDE!! This sauce was so good...I browned some ground beef and added it to the sauce to simmer, and it was perfect! Will definitely make it again.
This was really yummy!!!  I  had no cream so I didn't substitute anything else and it was SO good!!!
I made this today and it was way way to sweet will not make again I followed recipie exactly

Very good with some modifications.  I blended it before adding the cream to make it smoother as another reviewer suggested.  I also cut back the sugar to 1/4 teaspoon and used fresh basil and fresh tomatoes that I had on hand.  Will definately make again.

My husband and I both really like this sauce. It had a lot of flavor and wasn't bland at all. I was expecting a little bit more of a creamy sauce but this one was very good, just tomato-dominated. I also used my stick blender in the pot and made it almost completly smooth with just a little texture.

delish!  i did do a few changes...i added veggies, mushrooms, baby bells, and kale.  i did not have heavy cream, and did not feel like going to the store; so i used about half a cup of low fat sour cream, about half a cup of 1% milk, and about two Tbs of butter.  yum, yum, YUM!  my son does not usually like red sauces, this one he did!

This is a nice sauce that I served over Trader Joes ravioli.  I had some FF half and half that I needed to use up, so I substituted that for the heavy cream. I also sauteed two links of sliced tomato mozzarella basil chicken sausage, and added it to the sauce. I was quite satisfied with this recipe.
Easy, quick and really good. Not too heavy. Goes really good with chicken.
This is out of this world good!!  I have a larger family so I doubled it.

Amazing recipe.  My hubby loved it!!  I added red peppers, scallops and shrimps to make it a seafood pasta.  I put the scallops and shrimps when adding the cream so that they don't overcook.  Will definitely be making again.
this was good, not the best. i put the sauce in the blender to make it smooth.
Sadly, just ok.  I really wanted to like this but the spices just weren't right. I'll keep looking for a keeper recipe.

Great recipe!  I doubled the garlic (or more)  and added chicken. 
Quick,  easy and yummy!
Mmm so tasty.  This is going down as one of my favorites.

I tried this recipe two ways. Made half as written and the other half I made healthier by omitting the butter and using skim milk instead of cream. We preferred the healthier version but didn't love it either way. It might be better with more spice but will probably not make again.

I tried the recipe as written, but we didn't care for it.  However, this may be easily attributable to two things:  first, the recipe merely called for "one onion" (rather than specifying a specific size or amount of chopped onion) and I think the onion I used must have been about double the size of what was needed; second, the recipe stated a yield of 5 servings so I cooked a 5-serving amount of pasta to match but I think the sauce was stretched far too thin.  The overall result was a bland oniony glaze.  The next day I reheated the leftovers with a storebought can of spaghetti sauce and it was great - probably did benefit from the cream of the previous sauce.  Willing to try again but will reduce onion and alter ratio of sauce to pasta.

I blended the sauce as recommended by others, but it still had a strange consistency. My husband was a little skeptical, but it tasted much better than it looked and he gave it a thumbs up. I'll definitely try this again, but maybe puree longer..

Very good and also quick and easy!  Used half and half instead of the cream and thickened with cornstarch and water.  Left out the butter.  Even my super picky 5 year old daughter asked me to make this again.
It was excellent, I added about 1 tsp of crushed red chili peppers to spice it up a bit.

Excellent sauce! It complimented our spinach/kale raviolis perfectly! the only change I made, however, was to use a can of plain tomato sauce instead of the can of diced tomatoes...it still came out delicious!

Very good and very easy. I simmered it until almost all of the juices were gone, then used my hand blender to make it smoother before adding the cream. This made the texture perfect- creamy, not runny as some others reviewers mentioned.

I also pureed mine in the food processor to get a creamier sauce. The flavors taste more complex compared to how easy it is to make. I will switch it up and add shrimp or broccoli florets at times, whatever I have on hand. Very quick and impressive entree.
I chopped up about 5 fresh tomatoes instead of using canned. Delicious! Also, I put in blender to smooth the sauce. After blending, returned to pan and added sliced grilled hot Italian sausage.
This recipe is to die for.  I've spiced it up by adding Chili Peppers and sliced Red Peppers for a little bit of extra "zing".

Excellent recipe, easy to make and fast for last minute meals. A few additions or changes: I add extra garlic (about 3 cloves). Next, to make it sugar free, I use a sugar substitute (stevia) instead. I use regular diced tomatoes and I simmer longer than 5 min (about 15 min) making it thicker before adding the cream  and and butter to stretch this recipe because it does not make enough for 5. Doing this makes enough for about 3. If you need to feed more than double everything!!! Delicious and definitely restaurant quality!

Spectacularly easy and delicious.  The sauce would be good even before adding the cream and butter--and healthier too--but the cream and butter increase the richness by several notches.  My wife has a discriminating palate and she loved it; she had a second helping and rarely gets seconds on anything anymore.  We prefer a thicker sauce, so I mixed 1/2 cup of cream with a heaping teaspoon of cornstarch, stirring in a measuring cup until fully disolved, then added it to the rest of the mixture.  Doing it that way prevents lumps from forming.  This recipe combines great taste and ease of preparation.
It wasn't a hard sauce to make, but it was really sweet. I'm going to stick with my regular marinara sauce from now on.
Follow this recipe towards pasta sauce heaven!  I have cooked this many times now and my husband is a huge fan.  Tastes great tossed over pasta with italian sausage.
really good!

This is one of my favorite sauces I have ever made.  The flavor was amazing and I didn't know all those flavors were so easy to create.  Even without the cream base, the tomatoes after the seasonings were deliciouso.

This was great! It may become my new sauce for all pasta. I puréed the tomatoes because my husband won't eat pieces of cooked tomato. The tomatoes I used already had basil, oregano and garlic. I added a little more garlic, but that was it.
My husband added ground Italian sausage to some of the leftover sauce and put it over spaghetti. He thought that was great also.
Used the blender and it turned out amazing.  Will cut back on the basil next time

This Recipe was excellent and easy! im so glad i found this. I have been wanting to make a easy and tasteful pasta sauce for a while now and found it. The only adjustments i made is i added more garlic and oregano. I love the smell and taste of oregano and i added a small can of tomato Paste and sauce to give it extra flavor and color. Sauce came out great with some linguine and fresh Parmesan.

Very good and very like a sauce I already make.  I used 1/2 of a medium onion, 1, 14 oz can diced italian tomato's and 1 can of italian stewed tomato's.  I also used 3 garlic cloves, and about 1/2 tablespoon of italian seasoning. I had made a rump roast 2 nights before and added 2 large thick slices to the sauce.  My old italian mil used to make a roast in the sauce and the slices in the sauce reminded me of that.  Thanks! This was enough for me and my son and daughter in law, over ravaoli.
Too sweet .. ok otherwise.  Next time I'll omit the sugar and will use less onion (if any at all)

This was great. It is tomato season so I just used oven roasted roma-style tomatos from the garden. I omitted the sugar - not a big fan of sweet sauces and pureed it with an immersion blender. Turned out great.

Mmm, makes a nice creamy tomato sauce.  Mine ended up coming out a little spicy, but I tossed in a few red pepper flakes.  I will definitely make this recipe again, and I will play more with seasoning to tune it to my exact liking.  This a good foundation to play with.
Perfecto!  Very tasty and easy to make with no time at all.  The sauce was creamy and not too thin.  I made this recipe as a side dish in case it didn't work out.  Next time I'll add shrimp.

I had this souce for dinner tonight with home-made fettucine. My husband loved it, but it was just average for me. The sauce seemed a little bland but it might have been because I ate it over freshly-made pasta (which is much thicker than the store-bought dry noodles). Next time, I will try thickening the sauce with permesan cheese and maybe add more garlic for flavors.

Just made this for the first time with a few modifications.  I only had a can of fire-roasted tomatoes, so I used those - and they are delicious.  Also excluded the onion since I didn't have one and it was fine.  Used much more garlic; 3 cloves instead of four.  I used ground oregano and also added some rosemary - great idea.  Decreased the sugar per other reviewers suggestions; I did add about a tablespoon of flour and used half and half instead of whipping cream.  I like the "chunky" style so I did not run it through the blender.  Delicious and flavorful!  Exactly what I was hoping to have for dinner tonight!
Really good!

Wonderful!  I doubled the recipe for a large group.  Once the sauce was made pureed it with an immersion blender.  I added 1.75 pounds cooked diced chicken, 1.5 cups frozen peas and a pint of sliced baby portabello mushrooms.  Continue to simmer until heated through.  Then add 14.5 ozs of cooked farfalle pasta.  Stir and YUM!!  Served 6 plus leftovers.
added a little hot sauce and red pepper flakes, just cause.  Also, I used soy milk instead of cream, but only bc that's all I had.  SOOOOOO GOOD!

My husband loved this!  I put this sauce over 4 cheese ravioli.  I was nervous when I started making the sauce because my husband does not like onions or large chunks of tomatoes.  For my husband I after letting the onions, can of diced tomatoes and spices simmer together I threw them into a vita-mix blender and blended them, then added the cream and butter.  It turned out wonderful!  I gave the recipe 4 stars instead of 5 simply because my 2 daughters 8 and 22 mo. would not eat it, I think their taste buds might not be ready for this one just yet.  I will make it again for me and my husband though!  Great sauce!
Pureed half the tomatoes and added about 3/4 cup of shredded smoked gouda cheese to melt into sauce.  Also used fresh basil.  Very good!
Very delicious! I added shredded chicken and used evaporated milk instead of heavy cream because that's what I had on hand. Will definitely make again!
Absolutely amazing! I made it exact with just one change I used 1/2 and 1/2 cream. I also grilled chicken to add to it.  My husbands new favorite. This will be a staple in my kitchen for sure :)
I add shrimp to this sauce and it is the best!

Really great sauce - I did blend it quickly before adding the cream for a smoother sauce, and I also added one chili since I wanted a bit more spice, but other than that it was quick and easy with excellent results!
Only change I made was that I used fresh tomatoes from the garden chopped up. Worked really great!
Way too much onion. But good.
DELICIOUS!  The only change I made was to puree the sauce.
This sauce is wonderful and very fast and easy to make.  I did not add the sugar.  Heavy cream has enough sweetness for our taste.  Leftovers are wonderful! Make the sauce a day ahead!

This was a really good recipe. It was easy to make, and it turned out pretty good. I don't like my pasta sauces runny, so I let mine simmer until really all the water evaporated, and I also added some baby spinach to give add some green to the red. I opted to try using half and half cream, instead of heavy cream. I'm not quite sure what the difference will be in consistency, but I guess I'll find out eventually because I'll definitely make it again. :-)

Doubled the recipe
Added 1 lb. ground buffalo
Used Italian seasoning instead of dried basil & oregano
Used Spice World Minced Garlic instead of garlic cloves

Suggestion for next time:  ease up on sugar, add a bit more salt

Pretty much awesome!

This was really delicious, but it needed a bit longer than 20 minutes to cook to really let the flavors blend and mellow. I usually let my tomato sauces simmer for a minimum of 30 minutes, preferably more.
i think this is a delicious however personally i would add less sugar to it as i don't like the sweet taste, and i also didn't use oregano and i still tasted fabulous!

I'm in the middle of the mountains in Central America, and I wanted tomato cream pasta today. I ended up chopping up three fresh tomatoes in place of the canned ones, and I used a handful of powdered milk and a big squeeze of mantequilla in place of the heavy cream. I also added a dash of flour like some if the other reviewers said. It was so, so good. I'm making another batch tonight to take to school tomorrow.

This sauce wasn't bad, but it wasn't anything special.  I followed the recipe but replaced the heavy cream with evaporated milk (it was all I had).  The sauce had great consistency and wasn't thin at all.
Very simple to make, just what I was searching for!
A good, solid, and quick weeknight meal that pleased the whole family.  I did add a bit of red pepper flakes to spice it up.  Will certainly make again. Thanks for sharing the recipe!
absolutley delicioius! only the recipe didn't make quite enough. next time I will have to double

First time:  Really good. I used chopped fresh tomatoes. Like others, I used my immersion blender to blend everything before adding the cream. Once I added some grated mixed Italian cheese at the end, it elevated to 5 stars.
2nd/3rd times - Have also left it chunky which is good too!  At the end I added 2-3 big handfuls of fresh spinach, tossed it all with angel hair pasta, and it was amazing.
Awesome! A big hit with my husband and 3-year old!  I cooked with fresh Roma tomatoes from my garden instead of canned Italian-style tomatoes. I also omitted the oregano because I'm not a big fan :)

This recipe is great!  My whole family loves it, even my pickiest kid.  I like to use 4 cloves of garlic.  Purée with emulsion blender after adding cream to finish it off. I always double it for 6 - 8 servings.  Great over cheese ravioli or tortellini.
Love this recipe...simple and easy to prepare.  I did increase the amount of spices to my liking and will definitely make again!
Wow!  This was incredible!!  I added some cheese into the sauce and purred the tomatoes first but Yummy!
as previously stated, i added parm cheese and the family liked it...would go great in lasagna or on manicotti...tasted even better the following day

I thought it was really good! I used a combo of sun-dried tomatoes and fresh tomatoes as well as used flavored olive oil and it really turned out well.  I thought the texture was perfect for a pasta sauce.
The recipe does not say how much pasta this sauce will cover. I used 6 ounces of penne and it was just enough. Taste was good.

Absolutely delicious! I make this at least once a month, usually in a double batch so I can freeze half of it for later.  I omit the butter and sugar, and I use a little less olive oil than the recipe calls for.  It's fantastic!
Nice flavor, nothing spectacular.

This was awesome! I doubles the recipe and added a ck breast that I diced up really fine after it was cooked. I added it to the sauce and served over gnocchi. I added some crushed red peppers and a little extra sugar. Fantastic!

This is really good! It has become a staple in our kitchen.  I usually add something, cream cheese, bleu cheese crumbles, feta, whatever I have on hand, and the recipe tastes great with all of them. I've added chicken, beef, and seafood and have loved it every time.  This one is a keeper

I have always believed that, in cooking tomatoes, sugar is essential.  I actually use more than in the recipe.  
This is now a huge favourite with my wife for whom I cook!
  David
Made this and it was a great hit with my finicky husband and teenagers!! This is going to be a staple in our dinner menus

My husband likes white sauce, I prefer red. This is a perfect sauce for both of us to enjoy. I like to add sauteed mushrooms & green peppers and serve over spinach fettuccine. This recipe is a regular.
This is quick and easy and is a change to serving your average jar sauce.  i like to add sweet italian turkey sausage for a heartier dish.
I use fresh basil and half and half with a few tablespoons of fresh grated parmesan cheese, just add some sauteed hot Italian sausage for a complete meal.
Tis was great, my picky toddler loved it with cheese melted on top!

This is a really good pasta sauce...very easy to make.  I live in Mexico where canned tomatoes are not available except at Costco which is located 2.5 hours from where I live.  Not a problem.  I sauteed the onion and garlic for a few minutes. I cut up 3 fresh Roma tomatoes in small chunks and sauteed them with the onion .  I blended 4 Roma tomatoes to a lumpy consistency and added that to the sauteed onion, garlic and fresh tomatoes.  Once that was reduced a bit, I stirred in the cream and seasonings.  Skip the sugar!

My family really enjoyed this recipe.  I doubled it and made the dollowing changes: I used fresh tomatoes- peeled and diced and added Italian seasoning (had a lot of tomatoes from my farm co-op).  Pureed for smoother consistency.  Also subbed fat-free half and half for the heavy cream.  (Probably would have had a little better consistency had I not done this, but it was still excellent.). I'll make this again the same way, but I think I'll add some tomato paste to give it a little more density.  Highly recommend!
Very easy to make -- and very tasty to eat!  My husband said it was one of my better pasta dishes :).
amazingly great!!!
Delicious. Made it exactly as described but blended.

Delicious......used 2 (28 oz ) cans of chunky crushed tomatoes.....used fresh chopped basil instead of the dried.....way more garlic and fat free 1/2 and 1/2 instead of the heavy crream to cut fat and calories. Served over rigatoni pasta.....Easy and quick and very tasty...my family enjoyed this sauce. Thanks!

I prefer using fresh ingredients whenever I can. I used diced fresh Romano (plum) tomatoes & fresh basil -so much better!  I left out the onion & sugar.  I also substituted goat cheese for the cream & served the sauce over spaghetti squash. This healthy recipe is delish as a side or main dish!! P.S. Always add your fresh basil right before serving.

This was excellent. As I had been searching for something like this, but creamy so I made one change.  Before adding the cream and butter I put the tomato/onion base in my food processor and processed until creamy. I then returned it to the pan and added the cream and butter.  My husband LOVED it, as did my entire family.  I added fresh basil leaves and a dollop of goat cheese to each serving (over angel hair).  A keeper.
Lot of flavor.  The family thought it was outstanding.  Easy to make.

This is a great sauce!  It's always a hit when I serve it to people.  I always blend it in the blender after it's done to smooth it out and I usually use Italian style stewed tomatoes and extra garlic cloves.
Loved it.  Fast, great flavour and paired well with shrimp.  Made it exactly as per the recipe.
this was very very good and easy! it was a great change to the regular plain tomato sauce!

It was a good sauce! My variation subed the heavy cream for a can of cream of mushroom soup with about a half cup of milk because I didn't have the cream on-hand. I also added a can of mushrooms and fresh parsley, which really made a good, thick sauce. Then, I used it for the Chicken Parmigiana, found on the twenty for twenty list, which is served also tossed with whole grain linguine. It was awesome!

My husband and I loved this sauce. It was very easy and very tasty.  The only changes I made was to use fat free evaporated milk instead of cream and to put the sauce in the blender briefly to smooth out the tomato chunks. Neither of us missed the fat of the cream. Thanks so much for a great recipe!
eta: made this again for a spaghetti potluck and added cayenne pepper to taste. Very popular!
THIS WAS VERY GOOD. I ADDED SOME GARLIC POWDER AND ONION POWDER FOR EXTRA TASTE. BUT THIS REMINDS ME OF A RECIPE FROM AN ITALIAN RESTAURANT I USED TO WORK AT. GREAT FOR DIPPING BREAD IN. YUM!

This recipe was easy to follow.  Like a few others, I chose to puree the sauce in the blender as I prefer a smoother sauce.  Once this done I then added the cream and butter.  I tasted the sauce while making it and it was delicious.  I served this sauce over cheese ravioli along with roasted garlic bread also found in allrecipes.  I enjoyed eating the sauce the following day and found the the blend of spices set in overnight.   My family loved this recipe and it will definitely remain in our household.

Yum!  My husband and I were pleasantly suprised with this.  Tried it for the first time tonight and followed the directions for everything except the butter- omitted it, and the cream- used 2% milk instead.  A terrific and deilicious alternative to jar sauce- easy too!
Made it per recipe!  It was okay  but nothing special!  A little bland for our taste.

Wonderful! Family loved it. I used Fresh tomato, half and half and about 1/4 tbs butter. Plus used 1/4 tsp each: seasoning salt, Italian bread seasoning, and dried tomato pesto. I also used fresh basil. Will use again. So easy. I made this and added frozen meatballs before the cream and butter. Once cooked then I added the cream.

Second time I sauté one shallot and one onion. After a few minutes I reduced heat and added several whole partly smashed garlic. Cooked for a minute. Then added ingredients as suggested. I only used 1/4 tsp each: seasoning salt, Italian garlic bread seasoning, and dried tomato and garlic pesto seasoning.

Great sauce. I halved to use up leftover angel hair pasta.  I used fat free milk instead of heavy cream, 3 garlic cloves (if I did whole recipe I would have used 6 garlic cloves). I only had petite diced tomatoes so added in 1 tsp of italian seasoning, still using other seasoning as well. Like other reviewers I pureed the sauce then put back in pan with handful of mushrooms and then tossed in the left over pasta. I don't think we could ever go back to jar sauce.  So tasty and so easy to make.
This was great! Great flavor!
I didn't realize how sweet this sauce would be. It was like having syrup on pasta. Next time I make this, I'll use fresh herbs, more garlic, and no sugar.

i just made this cream sauce tonight and it was fantastic! i used a red onion and only had regular whipping cream, not heavy but it has a rich, tangy flavor and reminds me of a sauce i had in northern italy years ago...thanks kimber!

Pretty good! I added sauteed mushrooms and a bit more garlic, salt, and sugar. I also pureed it.

Next time I'll puree a little less (it wasn't chunky enough), use FRESH herbs, add more veggies (spinach?) and maybe add a bit more cream and/or parmesan cheese. Maybe pureeing in a little cottage cheese would be good:)

Overall, great tomato sauce recipe! I suggest doubling it and freezing the left overs.
it was awesome. i don't normally make new recipes before sharing with friends, but this turned excellent.

this was wonderful!  I did melt the butter in a separate pan and added an equal part flour to the butter to make a roux since some had said the sauce was a little on the thin side. I also added a splash of red wine. Loved this sauce!

I doubled recipe and added more seasonings per other reviewers.  Everything else was pretty much the same.  It was delicious and I'm making it again.  I was worried about teh chuncks of tomato in the sauce, because my hubs doesn't like chunky tomatos, however they became much smaller after cooking and simmering. Thanks for the recipe.  I will use this frequently.
Easy to make and taste great!
Added sauteed chicken strips and it turned out great.  I may try half and half next time to see if the heavy cream is worth the extra calories.

This is a very adaptable recipe, which I like: I didn't have any onion, so I amped the flavor with extra garlic (three cloves), which I sauteed before adding one can of regular, no added salt, diced tomatoes.  For seasoning I added 1 tsp of Italian seasoning, salt and pepper.  Instead of heavy creaming, I used half-and-half, since that's what I had on hand.  The sauce was a little thin, but very delicious!  I look forward to making it with the cream next time, but the seasonings were just right for us.  I served it with whole wheat cheese ravioli, with Italian cut green beans on the side.  Yum!
Excellent flavor! Just the right blend of tomato, cream and sugar. Made as written but added a few capers. I served it with homemade whole wheat pasta and everyone loved it.

This is an awesome recipe.  I puréed in a blender as recommended by others to have a smoother consistency.  I did this just before adding the cream.  I used fat free half and half and it worked great.  I also upped the garlic.
this tastes especially good with added mushrooms!
Quick, easy, and yummy. I don't add the sugar.  A little too sweet for my taste.
Delightful

I made this for my family the other night.  It will go in my Company's coming file.  It was fantastic!  I put it in the processor so there were no chunks.  Added a pound of shrimp and served it over tortallini. Fantastic and quick.  Easy to make on a weeknight.

This was delicious!  I used a little less sugar.  I used half and half since that's what I had.  Added a table spoon of flour.  And added Italian sausage,  since my husband needs some tyyof meat with his food.  It was great.  He asked for seconds and asked to have that for his birthday meal!
Made as is...perfect!

Good sauce!
I made a few alterations though.  I'm a fan of really creamy chunkless (is that an existing word?) sauce, so I started by pureeing(sp?) the garlic and onions, instead of just chopping them.  I did that before I cooked them, and in retro spect I probably should have cooked then pureed them, because it would have been easier to tell they were done.  Not to mention that I doubled the amount of garlic, because I like the extra kick.
Also, instead of using canned diced tomatoes, I used canned tomato sauce.  Because of this, the cream was unnecessary, because the sauce didn't need any more thinning.
And, last but not least, I added some pepper flakes and cayenne pepper to give it some spice, because I am a spicy food fiend.  I think Tobasco sauce would've worked out better, but I was fresh out.

I'll definitely make this again!  Took other reviewers advice and cut the sugar to 1/4 tsp, added 1/2 tsp of Italian spice (because my diced tomatoes were plain) and 3 cloves of garlic.  Delicious!  Thanks for this easy recipe.  Used it with Costco lobster raviolis.
This recipe is hands-down the BEST (tomato-based) pasta sauce I have ever made.  I made it as written, tripling the batch to feed my large family.
I made this recipe which I would give 4 stars.  I made some changes (added chicken, skipped the sugar, used two cans of tomatoes, and added chicken base.  It made several meals.  Fantastic.

I loved it! It was just not enough for my box of penne pasta. Next time I'll double the recipe! Love it though! Didn't change a thing which is unusual for me. I usually add something or change out an item. Just perfect!

I changed just a little bit to give it a stronger taste. 1/2 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp black pepper and 1/2 tsp crushed red pepper.  With parmesan on top of a bowl, it was amazing.  I also used fresh tomatoes (peeled and seeded) instead of canned.  5 medium tomatoes seemed to replace the can pretty well.

Definitely my favorite pasta recipe! If you use half and half instead of whipping cream be aware that it is a little sweet (at least the kind that I use) and so it may be best not to add sugar. My boyfriend loves this every time I make it. Thanks for sharing!

This sauce was a hit at my house! Husband, sister and her boyfriend all raved about it.  A million times tastier than the crappy packet mix ParmaRosa I used to make, ha ha ha.  I used twice the amount of tomatoes and twice the amount of cream (used half & half).  Oops, I also used margarine instead of butter.  Oops, and added four cloves of garlic and a sprinkle of freshly ground dehydrated garlic...and a generous amount of fresh pepper.  I found that the sauce didn't want to thicken up after the cooking time given but I ended up leaving it simmer for about 20 minutes and it did somewhat.  It was still a bit runny so I served it in shallow bowls to avoid spills.  What a delicious, economical, versatile recipe...the addition possibilities are endless--sausage, beef, chicken or just veggies.  Ohhh, how about as a sauce for lazy ravioli or lasagna!  I served it over pasta, of course, to which I added two stalks of chopped celery and half a chopped red pepper.  Sprinkled cheese over top.  Served with biscuits dipped in garlic butter before baking.  Thanks for sharing...I'll be making this often!

Excellent! I made it exactly as the recipe said and it was very tasty and surprisingly unique. I actually spread it out over about 6 servings and it was still fine. Could I have doubled it? Sure, but it was fine and flavorful if you want a finer coating as well.

This was a nice sauce.  I used half-and-half, adding it to the blender while I pureed the other ingredients.  This made a smoother sauce than the original recipe.  Note:  If you like generous portions of sauce on your pasta, this actually serves about 3-4.
I made sure I simmered the tomatoes for quite some time to thicken it up really nicely. I had this with beef ravioli and it was DIVINE!

This was the best!!!  I didn't even change a thing except I got diced tomatoes with jalepenos instead of italian (couldn't find them in the store)

I planning on sharing it with family and friends!
This one is definitely a keeper.  I didn't change anything at all, just added chicken and served over bowtie pasta.  Great dinner!

I adore this sauce.  The trick to getting it thick is just to let it simmer on low for a while.  I use extra garlic and lots of black pepper and add sugar to taste and serve it over any kind of cheese filled tortellini.  Thanks for a great recipe!

I made this recipe with fresh basil & fresh tomatoes (not the Italian style mentioned in the recipe).  It was pretty good although I think I would double the recipe next time for the amount of pasta I used.  Will make it again :)

definitely double the recipe.  I used half the onions and double the garlic and a little red pepper.  I also blended the mix before adding the cream and butter.  My only issue was it was a little watery...and it was fattening :)

I made this last night and I am still thinking about it. The dish was easy and wonderful. I omitted the sugar as the onions provided sweetness. I used stewed tomatoes and a squirt of tomato paste for richness. Otherwise just followed the recipe as written. The sauce had a lovely consistency...I did not use a blender for the sauce. My husband was blown away by the taste and presentation. One tip...I used FRESH fettucini from the dairy section of the grocery. This made the dish as it was delicate. The next time I make this (which will be soon) I may add lobster at the end. Thanks you for a great vegetarian recipe.
Better with fresh basil. No way it makes 5 servings unless you are a tiny eater. I double for  4 people.

Ok, I have made this twice now. I still don't love it. It is sweet in a disgusting way, and the texture is weird because of the chunky tomatoes and all the dried basil. Maybe I will spring for fresh next time! I am going to make it again, and try other reviews' suggestions to put it through the blender. I added probably 1.5 T of flour, which really helped thicken it and make it a great consistency, not runny. I like the flavor but must try it with these modifications, and without the sugar...

Bpth my children and my friends liked this dish. I diced real tomatoes and added Italian spices.  Like many other reviewers, I doubled the recipe, pureed it with a hand-held blender, and used half and half instead of cream.  It wss a bit runny and I will definitely add tomato paste next time.

I made this for my family the other night and everyone is still raving about it! For the most part I followed the directions, except I doubled the garlic and added tomato paste to help thicken it. I also added meat 1/2 pork 1/2 beef to make it a bolognese sauce.  You will not be disappointed. What are you waiting for, go make it! ??

I've made this sauce countless times since I found this recipe, and everyone in the house loves it! After the first time I've taken to using half and half in place of heavy cream, at least a little bit healthier and just as tasty!
So yummy!  I loved the flavor and and consistency of this sauce.  I will definitely make this again!!!
I have made this several times without changing anything. It is delicious!

So simple and absolutely delicious! We have an over abundance of tomatoes in the garden so I added some fresh tomatoes to the 14.5 oz of canned.  I used the light heavy cream which made no difference in the rich taste and also added some shrimp.  It made a perfect meal for my husband and I.  It was so good that I think I would serve it to company!  Karen S.      Melville, NY
Love it!! One of our favorites!! I could eat this once a week!

I love this recipe (and so does my fiance)!  I have made it several (hundred) times by now and I never deviate from the original recipe.
