I notice that a lot of people have an issue with the sweetness to the tomatoes, but I have a huge sweet tooth, so the sweetness didn't bother me as much.  As far as the "thin" consistency goes, I usually let mine set for a minute or two before serving, it thickens right up.

Really good sauce! I was trying to copy a similar sauce my husband and I tried at an Italian restaurant, and this is really close to it. The sauce in the restaurant was a little bit thicker, my guess is that they add flower in it. But, this sauce is also really, really good. We ate pasta with spinach, but would've worked even better with, like, cheese ravioli? Love it!

I used this sauce to replicate the Angelini di Mare I had at Macaroni Grill the previous night.  This sauce was WAY better!  I doubled the recipe (omitted the butter), pureed the canned tomatoes, added 3/4 lb. jumbo shrimp (cooked in the sauce), two 3 oz.pkg of Lump Crab meat, 1/2 C. fresh frozen green peas (blanched), and freshly shredded parmesan both in the sauce and as a garnish.  It was DELISH!!!!  It got rave review from my friends I cooked for.  I used 1 1/2 pkg of angel hair pasta, and it was plenty for three to have seconds, and still have 2 hefty servings left over.  Suffice to say doubling the recipe feeds 6-8 at $3/person!!  Definitely a keeper!
I'm sorry, but it tasted pretty much like regular pasta sauce. It was good sauce though. I was just looking for more.

LOVE LOVE LOVE IT!  Super easy to make.  I needed another reason to keep heavy cream in the house! :)

If you have a tomato hater like I do, you can substitute 1/2 jar sauce and let it cook down until thick.

This was a great base to start from. I pureed the tomatoes in the blender because I like a less chunky sauce. I also did not add cream, but substituted milk and it turned out just fine. I would probably add a few more spices next time, and omit the sugar.
I made this for my husband, and he really liked it.

Delicious!  I decided to make chicken Parmesan for dinner and decided to make homemade pasta sauce for it. Boy am I glad I did!  I followed advice from fellow cooks and only used half an onion.  I ran out of minced garlic, so I sauté the onion first and added garlic powder in with the rest of the ingredients. To cut down on calories, I used half-and-half. Double the recipe!  You won't be sorry!

I LOVED this recipe!  I made it exactly as-is except had to use a substitute for heavy cream (whole milk and butter) as I didn't have any in the house.  Husband said it tasted like a restaurant!  It was even better as leftovers the next day for lunch.  YUM!!!!!
I make this all the time because it is cheap, easy, versatile, efficient and fatty.  That's what I like.

I made the recipe exactly as written other than I pureed the ingredients in my food processor first.  After I tasted the sauce when it was ready to serve, I was disappointed.  I think maybe the basil was a little overpowering and it definitely needed more salt for my family.  I added a little more cream to tone it down some, salt and pepper and served it over grilled Italian sausage and bowtie pasta.  Probably won't make again.
Made as written - very good!
Easy and delicious.  Some reviewers complained that it was too thin, but I used crushed tomatoes, and turned out perfectly.

I enjoyed the ease of this recipe. I added some diced bell peppers and some left-over chicken and went a little heavy-handed with the spices the second time I made it. I think this is a great recipe, and it's easy to adjust to personal tastes.
Excellent. Simple and not too many calories! Although you would probably need to double the recipe to get 5 servings. Loved it. May have needed more salt though.
No extra explanation is needed, this recipe is ABSOLUTELY AMAZING.

Hard to believe a sauce this good is so easy.  Great flavor.  I did add a little anchovy paste and a few flakes of red pepper. I use Stevia instead of sugar. But the recipe needs no changes.  Love it over small penne pasta.  I think the consistency is perfect when made with cream.  This makes for a heavenly vegetarian meal.

This was an awesome sauce very tasty, made it just as recipe described no substitutions, I did use a hand blender to make it a bit smoother to hide the onion from my daughter, she loved it.  Served it over Penne Pasta was really great.

So good! I used about 1 TBL minced dried onions instead of 1 whole fresh onion.  I added one more can of diced tomatoes (which I pureed), 1 TBL Italian seasoning and a tiny bit more salt.  Left the amount of cream the same - delicious!
I think this is an excellent sauce.  I added meat to mine because I like meat sauce but it is definitely optional.

This sauce is delicious!!   Because I am a vegetarian , I like a chunkier textured sauce to compensate for the lack of meat so I added diced red and yellow peppers and chose to follow the recipe and not purée.   I did add a little flour as a thickening agent.   I also added crushed red pepper flakes and parsley along with the basil and  Oregano.  Served with penne pasta topped with Parmesan cheese.   Will be making this on a regular!!
Good, but messy to make.  I agree with others that you need to double the amount of sauce.
This was fantastic.  We put it through the blender and it was super creamy and smooth and delicious.
Loved it! I used diced tomatoes with green chilies instead of tomatoes alone and it was just a nice spicy zing to it.

This recipe was delicious!! This is the first time I tried it and was very surprised. However, I did make a few adjustments because I didn't have a few ingredients. I had to dice regular tomatoes and add tomato sauce and I also didn't have heavy cream so I just used whole milk instead. The dish tastes like it was missing something and the sauce didn't come out as think as I hoped but that was prob due to not having all the right ingredients. I would deff recommend this and make this again but the right way. Delicious tho!

Excellent. I triple this recipe to mix with angel hair pasta and top stuffed chicken breasts. I break up the tomatoes with a potato masher so it's not so chunky. I also substitute fat free evaporated milk for the 1/2 & 1/2.

I've been using a similar recipe for years... it uses evaporated milk in place of heavy cream... I suppose you could use fat free in place of it. I've always liked this as a simple, quick meal.  Can be on the table in less than 30-mins.
Easy and delicious!  We pureed at the end for the picky eaters amongst us.  Could use a little more bite...relatively mild flavors.

Great recipe, Kimber. I used 1/4 of an onion, 2 cloves garlic, fresh basil and oregano, and added 1/2 cup tomato puree. Threw it all in the blender before returning to heat and  adding in the cream and butter... also added 1/4 cup parmesan cheese. Served over 4 cheese tortellini, and boy, was it ever good! Thanks.
added a small amount of tomato paste, and little less sugar little more butter, turned out great.almost forgot i did blend ingredients before adding butter and cream
Added some frozen spinach just to have some veggies involved, and added a bit more salt. Puréed the sauce because my family prefers fewer chunks, and more sauciness. Topped with Parmesan.

Simple and wonderful recipe. I suggest using 2 cloves of garlic instead of 1. This recipe can also be modified to make a delicious vodka sauce: add half a cup of smoked mozzarella as you simmer the sauce, and add a shot of vodka.
This is delicious.  I read some reviews stating they couldn't get the sauce thick enough.  I substituted cream cheese for the heavy cream and it was perfect!
This was great. Served over pasta with some Chicken Apple Cherry Sausage. Used frozen garden tomatoes. Had left overs that I just added extra liquid to the next night. Just as good second night too!

Fantastic! I made it with half an onion and a large diced fresh tomato.  I used whole milk instead of cream, and added some tomato paste for a thicker texture.  The key is to puree it -- I used an immersion blender. Great as a sauce, and good enough on its own that I plan to eat it as soup tomorrow!
Reduced sugar to 1/2 tsp, used fat free half and half & puréed out a lot of the chunks.  Next time I will double the recipe.  No leftover sauce!

I really enjoyed making this recipe and it turned out wonderful. Instead of canned tomatoes, I used fresh Romas from my garden and also fresh basil and oregano as well as dried. I added garlic powder, onion powder, and used half and half because I didn't have any cream. WILL make again and again! Thanks!
I made it exactly as the recipe said.My husband and I  Loved it. I give it 5 stars.I will make it again. I did double the recipe and I am happy I did.

This is a winner.  Such an easy and rich sauce to make.  I loved the addition of cream; in my opinion it really takes it up a notch in flavour -- but I could imagine making it without the cream to save calories and fat. It would still taste good.  I added mini-fillets of chicken breast, sugar snap peas and mushrooms.  I used a roux of about 2T butter/2T flour so that it would be thick.  Shrimp would be good too. We used linguine pasta.  It's an easy recipe that tastes as though you worked for hours. It also is easy to adapt to your family's tastes.  We will make it again and again.
This was better than can sauce!! Is good with or without the cream :) A new favorite in our house!

This is a really tasty recipe.  Since it really only makes 3 servings, I added about 1/2 a green pepper and 1/2 cup of regular canned pasta sauce to help increase it to 4 small servings.  Also, to make it thicker just simmer it uncovered until it is a thick as you want it.  Stir often.

Fantastic recipe.  Followed recipe exactly as presented with the exception of using three garlic cloves, instead of one, and adding chicken.

I served it with penne pasta and a salad on the side.  I will add this to my keeper file!  Thanks for the recipe, Kimber!

This was wonderful.....I did add 1/4cup  more of whipping cream for more sauce ...i also put it in the blender to make it a smooth texture...my child really enjoyed it..since he had no idea that it had onions and tomatoes! you can also sneak in more veggies and the kid will never know!

I doubled the sauce, except only used 1/2 teaspoon sugar.  Sauteed mushrooms and chicken.  Used 4 cheese ravioli.  Me and my husband absolutely loved this recipe, and will definitely make again.  Would also be good with shrimp, or no meat.
This recipe might have been better if it weren't for the onion, maybe just a touch of onion salt or powder instead.

Agree with most of the other ones. I pureed the tomatoes as well. I agree this is a lot of onion if you use a regular sized yellow onion.  Also I agree this is not a lot of food but is probably enough for a small meal for 2. Also had no heavt whipping cream so used half and half, turned out good but probably would taste better with cream.  Overall good, but this is a recipe most people will probably modify to suit their preferences. I personally will add more seasoning next time, use half the onion and probably add some other veggies or meat so it's more of a meal.

This was fantastic!  It reminded me of vodka sauce minus the vodka but better than any store bought version.  My only changes were using half an onion and following the recommendations to put the sauce in a blender to puree before adding the cream and butter.  I'm not a fan of tomato chunks in pasta sauce so the blender worked perfectly to smooth them out.  I would've never guessed such a high quality tasting sauce could be made so easily!

What a great, quick and simple sauce to jazz up some plain pasta. The only thing I might do differently next time is add a splash or two of white wine. This is a definite keeper. Thanks so much Kimber.
I thought this recipe was pretty good.  I added about half the cream to make the pasta a bit less 'saucy' and added mushrooms and chicken.  Its great if you are looking for a simple tasty meal
A little too heavy on the onion. Probably won't make again.
My husband normally dslikes tomatoes, but he LOVES this sauce. I think next time I might used crushed tomatoes instead of diced, I like smaller chunks. Otherwise, easy and delicious recipe.

I think it is important to adhere to a recipe, but it is always fun to add you own zest to the recipe! Changes: I added more garlic  since I'm a garlic lover.  To bring a little more kick to the recipe, I added a tiny bit of red pepper flakes. I do not like added sugar to any kind of sauce I make, so I omitted that (probably why it wasn't too sweet like other people stated). I did not have Italian flavored diced tomatoes, so I used plain and added fresh basil (along with the dried basil).  I added more salt and pepper as well. For a protein boost, I added Italian seasoned grill chicken and served it over penne. My fiancé and I thought it was very yummy.  I will definitely make this again!
It was good, just too sweet for me, remove the sugar and it will be better
This was a great sauce to serve over Grandmas Gnocchi.  I will use it over pasta and also add some sea food as a variation.
A hit at my house. When I want to bump it up a bit I use Rotel.
Ok everybody don't hate me but one night when I needed something really fast I used a jar of premade sauce and added a dash of sugar, a dash of wine,  and the heavy cream! Super quick and super easy!
Very tasty and filling!  Good dish to eat with no meat.

Wonderful recipe - doubled it with ease. I had fresh basil on hand and it was delicious. I also blended it a bit as I don't like tomato chunks, so it was thinner than I anticipated. I think I would use rotini next time instead of spaghetti because the sauce will stick to rotini better. Definately a keeper.
This was an "ok" dish. The cream and butter made the dish very heavy.
Very easy and tasty recipe.  I added an 8oz. frozen spinach to the mix and I liked the color and taste balance.

It is a good base but adding your own is important. I always add crushed tomatoes and some tomato paste to make a richer sauce. Strange as it may be a couple oxo envelopes also add to flavor to my family's. (I am vegetarian.)
this was awesome!!!! my first pasta ever, and this was the PERFECT recipe:)
Will definitely make again.  Used a stick blender to make it less chunky. Made some meatballs and had this over them with garlic bread.  Didn't even need pasta.  Add a salad and you're done.  Yum!

This was amazing! I added a bit more salt as my DH love saltier than most. Even my picky 3yo boy gobbled it down. I made it w/ the quick gnocchi recipe on the site..side of texas toast and salad..Yum!

This is the best tasting sauce ever.  My body has a hard time digesting milk and cheese.  This recipe is perfect.. the heavy cream does not bother my stomach and there is no cheese in this but it tastes like there is some in it!  I will be making this for years to come.  A fav!!
tasted like soup

I made this on a whim so I wasn't able to shop for all the ingredients...however it turned out fabulous!  Probably our favorite sauce recipe yet!!  All I had on hand was a can of diced tomatoes with jalapenos (which was great because we love a good kick) and I didn't have heavy cream so I used cream cheese instead (all I had!)  I did everything else as listed.  It was phenomenal!  My husband about licked the bowl clean!  :)

Really fantastic. Just the right amount of tomato and cream. I used left over marinara sauce from scratch instead of the Italian-style diced tomatoes but other than that it was exactly the same. We ate it with three cheese tortellini. It's my hubby's new favorite sauce and my toddler loved it even when I put pureed sweet potatoes in his!
Really enjoyed this simple to prepare sauce. I used light cream, turned out just fine. I did lightly sprinkle a dusting of cornstarch over sauce to thicken at the end of the five minutes.

Very tasty recipe
Stands up to hearty pasta shapes
In response to other reviews, if it's too thin... Cook it a little longer, different canned tomatoes can have more water than others
Same thing with sugar, use as much or little depending on your tomatoes, sugar helps with the acid 
If your basil tastes funny, check the date on the bottle, it's probably  3 years old, or grow some in a bucket
My kids love it just like the recipe

Great recipe! Super easy. I followed the advice of other reviews and upped the amount of garlic. I didn't have any Italian diced tomatoes, so I just used plain diced, and it was still delish! I also doubled the sauce and tossed it with a box of spaghetti and some grilled chicken. It made plenty for my family of four, with some leftovers (although everyone was scraping their plates, so there wasn't as much left over as I was hoping for!).  Oh, and for the love, PLEASE don't use skim milk or any other kind of milk or half and half in this recipe - the heavy cream is what makes it so yummy. I tried subbing whole milk, and I was sorely disappointed.
Good sauce!  I had only some tomato sauce so used it instead.  I also substituted milk for heavy cream.  Add some shrimps into the sauce at the end and everyone loved the dish!

Oh so good. This is so delicious, easy to make and inexpensive. I took the advice of others and blended the sauce smooth. Because we have vegans in the home, I used non diary margerine and milk rather than buter and cream. Definitely a keeper.

I loved this recipe. I prepared the recipe as written except I added fresh chopped basil as a garnish on each serving. The consistency was just right and the flavor was fresh and light. Because I had leftover cream, I made it two nights in a row, but on the second night I used fire roasted tomatoes. I really couldn't tell much difference. On the first night, the dish was an entree and on the second evening it was a side served with chicken breast.
I used fresh herbs from my herb garden instead of dried and also added some red pepper flakes for some spice!

I used Pomi tomatoes instead of a product that comes in a can. That cut out the preservatives and extra salt. I had to add my own Italian seasoning , but as others have noted that works well.  I made it using my blender to make it smooth. The sauce tastes great.  It is not too sweet and can be used in anyway you want.
I altered it a little due to lack of ingredients, but it was very tasty. Will make again, thanks for such an easy recipe!

This recipe is a great starting point.  I add tons of extra veggies (zucchini, eggplant, mushrooms, spinach) then puree half in the blender, then add it back in to the sauce.  I also add a small can of tomato sauce.  Delicious way to sneak some extra vegetables onto my boys' plates.

This sauce is really delicious. I prepared chunky, with 1/2 the onion and added cooked, cubed chicken breast, broccoli and mushrooms (during saute phase) . With the addition of the vegges and meat the recipe does serve 5. Sauce can be runny, but it's nothing a little cornstarch can't fix! Yum!
Very good and easy to make.  The only change I made was to use more garlic.  I'll definitely be making this again.

Great recipe! My family loved it. I added some grated carrots, and increased the sugar to 1 tbls. I didn't add the butter because to my surprise I didn't have any but it still tasted great. Higly recommend this sauce. Thanks.
Wow! This taste like a restaurant sauce. I made it exactly as written and served it over 4 cheese ravoli. It was wonderful and it reminds me of LaMadaline's tomato basil soup.

Simply delicioso!  I love a creamy tomato sauce, and this recipe is a winner!  You can add more chopped onion, tomato, etc, to thicken it, and more milk to make it more creamy.  I will be making this again & again!  My Italian man raved!  Thank you!
Very Good! I used tons of extra garlic, only half of a red onion and added some extra fresh tomatoes w/ the canned tomatoes. Also added some hot pepper flakes to make it spicy. Will def make again!

I made this as a quick fix meal last night, and it was great! I doubled the recipe as other had suggested. I used one can oregano, garlic, and basil dicred tomatoes and one can petit deiced tomatoes. I also used 2 big cloves of garlic and only one diced onion. I would definitely make this again!
Easy, convenient on a busy night & tasty!
As others have stated, it is a great basic sauce that has room for versatility. I added parm cheese and sundried tomatoes. Very good :)
ehh... weird

Recipe is simple and tastes great. If you really want to take it to the next level without much effort, add sliced black olives, sliced mushrooms, and capers for authentic Italian flavor. The addition of the previous three ingredients really makes this dish taste shine. :)
Excellent for picky kids...they loved it.
Excellent.  Fast, easy, and delicious.  Can't get much better than that.
This is definitely a new favorite. I used fresh basil and sweet onion, plus added some sautéed mushrooms. It was so easy and absolutely delicious! Will be making this again and again.

Used this recipe as a base for a tomato and italian sausage cream sauce. Altered this by (1) using fresh roma tomatoes, (2) mixing italian sausageinto the onion/garlic mix, (3) adding chicken broth, and (4) adding 2 T tomato paste. Oh, and also sprinkled in some red pepper flakes. Delicious!

This recipe was fabulous!  My husband raved.  I followed one cook's recommendation to use 3 gloves garlic. Yes!  I also used fresh basil vs. dried, and sliced about 3 Tbs.  At the very end we added some chicken from a store bought rotisserie chicken. YUM.  It is in our keeper box. LOVE IT!

This sauce was very good.  I took the advice of another reviewer and pureed the tomatoes and onions but it was a little to runny so I added a tsp of cornstarch mixed with a sm. amount of creamer first so it would be smooth.  It lacked a little umph for us and had to add in a little crushed red pepper and a pinch of chile powder.  My husband said it needed sprinkled with Parmesan Cheese to make it perfect.

This was delicious! And it was really quick and easy, plus I made it healthier with a few adjustments.   I threw some spinach in after browning the garlic, cooked it for a minute before adding the rest. I also substituted a 10 oz can of tomato sauce (with basil and oregano and garlic) and a 4 oz can of tomato paste for the diced tomatos, since I too like a smoother sauce. I also substituted 1/4 cup fat free milk and 1/4 margarine for the whipping cream and butter.   It was amazing! Not too watery, not too sweet.

I peeled the shrimp and sprinkled weber Cajon seasoning on them.  Sautéed 5 crushed garlic cloves and 1/2 chopped onion in olive oil.  Then I deglaze  the pan with some white wine and added 2 tsp butter.  I cooked that for a minute or so and I added a can of diced tomatoes and fresh basil.  I cooked that down until thicker...then added the cream and shrimp.   So so good.

Great sauce! I followed a few of the others tips and it came out delicious! Both my kids are picky and they both ate this PLUS seconds! A winner for me!
I did 1/2 an onion, added 3 cloves of garlic & pureed the tomatoes for smooth texture..Perfect for my family!
Used a blender to make it a smooth sauce. Freezes well for later use!
This has great flavor!  Very rich.  It has become a favorite with my husband!

Very VERY good! Very VERY fast and simple to make! Perfect week night recipe if you want something tasty but fast. Followed the recipe as is and I didn't need to make any changes. I will make this again for sure!
This was very yummy. Hubby thinks it need something to make it pop more. But overall it was easy to make and delicious to eat!

Wow! my family loved this, I added a green and yellow pepper and served it with a breaded chicken patti and penne pasta topped with mozarella cheese.  I did double this since I have a large family.  I did use milk and 1/2 tablespoon of cornstarch because I didn't have heavy cream.  I also used regular diced tomatoes since that is all i had on hand.  But it was great.
I doubled it and the creaminess got thicker. I also served it with homemade noodles and added some bacon! The noodles are called gnocchi! Loved it! Definitely a winner and keeper!

We made this and my husband really liked it alot and he doesn't even eat tomatoes. I read a few posts about adding flour because it was "runny" you have to cook it until most of the liquid evaporates (which is more than 5 minutes). My husband is actually cooking this again tonight. We will be trying this sauce on different dishes.
I made this just the way the recipe said and served it over stuffed shells.  Amazing!!

This is a wonderful sauce.  Based on suggestions of others, I added hot pepper flakes, reduced onion (actually used Shallots) added sun-dried tomatoes and increased the amount of cream a bit.  Served with cheese filled tortillini.  Great reviews by all at the table.
It was so easy to make, my entire family loved it and I loved that it was quick to make.

My husband said that it tasted like it was from a restaurant....so we'll take that as a good thing. Very easy to make, but turned out a little soupy. I guess next time I'll have to let the liquid reduce longer. I also left out the onions because I didn't have any...I don't think it lacked any flavor without them...as a matter of fact, I don't think that I would have liked it with the onions.
This recipe was super simple.  The hardest part was chopping the onions!  Yummy!
Excellent, my new favorite sauce. I loved it.
So yummy!  I poured it over three-cheese tortellini.  Used diced tomatoes with basil.  Mashed a little with a potato masher.  Went back for seconds!

This is a really good recipe. I have made it several times and my husband would have me make it several times a week if he could! To make it more "hardy" I added about 1/2-1 cup of beef flavored TVP (I'm vegetarian)- tastes great!

This was overall pretty good. Blending it is a must, makes the consistency much better. I did not have a problem with it being too runny, I just let it boil a little longer than suggested. Would be FANTASTIC with some grilled chicken.
Added a bit more basil and sugar it was just superb. I love the sweetness it has. It's been a hit in my house for years!
Use crushed tomatoes instead of diced and don't substitute anything for the cream. doing it this way will give you a thicker sauce....no flour needed!
This was so easy and tasty!  I used red pepper as recommended, added some shrimp and served over rice.  I can't wait to try it with pasta.  One of my new favorites!!
I like my sauce smooth so I pureed this after cooking.  It was wonderful.

This was a home run for both my husband and myself.  My only addition to the recipe was some sauted mushrooms, which I made ahead of time, then set aside, while I prepared the sauce as directed.   Add the mushrooms just before serving. This will become a favorite sauce for us but, next time I plan on doubling the portion to have an extra portion to freeze.

This is by far my favourite pasta sauce! i followed the recipe with no modifications and thought it was delicious. My friends and family members also enjoyed it and thought it was delicious! I crave this every once in a while. Thanks!
Yes ,it was awesome and hubby loved it too.We had a green salad on the side.He raved about it so much I made it again and put in shrimp,still just as good.Will try others meats also

Perfect, thank you! I added organic yellow sunburst squash while cooking the onions, used fresh organic tomatoes, added marjoram and cilantro, and used organic black bean penne for the pasta. Delicious!
This needs NO changes it was SOOOO good. One of the best sauces I have ever had..mmmmm!!

This recipe is part of my regular rotation.  Absolutely love it!  The sugar is crucial, left it out once and it was a little bitter.  I sometimes pair it with chicken meatballs, which go nicely.  Thanks so much for such a great recipe!

This is perfect!!  I have made this several times...even forgot to add sugar once and it still tasted great!!  Of course, knowing that, I don't add sugar any longer.  This was exactly what I was looking for!

Very good recipe. I didn't have canned tomatoes or an onion, so I used fresh tomatoes and left the onion out. I also used my immersion blender to puree the tomato/spices before adding the cream and butter. Will definitely make this again.
This sauce is amazing, easier on the stomach for those of us red sauce usually upsets us. This is a big hit with my family.
Yummy!  I did stick the sauce in the blender after I cooked it.  I recommend doing this, especially for picky eaters.  Also, this is perfect for a 2 person main dish.

I really love this pasta sauce!  I add an extra half can of the tomatoes so that it goes a little further.  I add steamed peas, broccoli and chicken to some penne pasta, toss it all together with the sauce, and it's excellent!  My family loves it!
I used whole wheat penne and added italian sausage (breakfast sausage with italian seasonings mixed in). David and Allison loved it. I thought it was good.
I used this sauce for gnocchi.  Have a more substantial sauce was great.  I really enjoyed the taste - restaurant quality.  I used about half the butter.  Definately make this again!
I added diced chicken for a heartier meal and doubled the tomatoes.

I made this today  with minor modifications to suit personal preference and used it to make a delicious eggplant parmesan.   Per a few other reviewers' suggestions, I used a can of organic diced tomatoes (all I had in the pantry) and half-and-half instead of heavy cream, half a small red onion, two cloves garlic and fresh basil, since I had it on hand, half teaspoon sugar.  Added some dried oregano and Italian seasoning.  Pureed mixture in Magic Bullet.  Very tasty, silky texture, excellent for layering with sliced, baked eggplant and fresh mozzarella.  Yummy!

husband said it was restaurant quality.  I added two chicken breasts cut into bite size pieces for the last few minutes of simmering (chicken was cooked 95% of the way before adding it to sauce).  Very quick to make so a good go to recipe when in a hurry.
I love this recipe, it is so quick and easy.  It has become a family favorite.  Only thing I do different is use half and half instead of the heavy cream, it always turns out great.
Great sauce, although I used tomato puree instead of diced tomatoes and added italian seasoning to it. It was delicious!

Very good!  A winner in my book.  I substituted fat-free half and half for the cream,cut the butter a little and doubled the garlic. I also used my hand blender and smoothed it a little, so that it wasn't super chunky but still had texture.  Hubby loved it.  Served it over organic spinach fetuccini with spicy italian sausage sliced on top.  Beautiful meal!
This recipe is so easy and delicious! I could eat it every week and my two year loves it!

I had the pasta and needed a quick and easy recipe for sauce. This recipe saved the day. Super quick and easy to make.
From one of the reviews I caught that someone had pureed their tomato sauce in the end, I did the same with a hand blender and it turned out super! 
Most importantly,  my husband really enjoyed it. I added some chopped fried sausages in too at the end. I highly recommend this recipe.
Thank you!
This sauce is wonderful! I added one pound sweet Italian sausage. Everyone loved it. Thank you for submitting this.

I tried this recipe TWICE and it didn't turn out the way I expected; some flavors lacking, some flavors too bold, thin and runny BOTH times. My rating is on how the recipe turned out, NOT on taste or idea. The first time I did it, I did exactly as directed. It took alot longer than 5 minutes for the liquid to evaporate, and after about 10 minutes of waiting for the cream to thicken it up at the end, I added a little cornstarch and water.  Granted, it DOES taste good, but on a personal note, I'd reduce the basil by about 1/2 and add a little more garlic.  Though this recipe didn't make the grade, I am going to hang on to it because it has potential.  I think next time, I'll up the garlic and try using all fresh ingredients, puree them, and try it with about 1/4 of a cup of chicken stock instead of water.

For my tastes, this recipe used far too much onion, but I just added some more tomatoes, garlic, basil, and oregano to even it back out and put it in the blender. Based on advice in the other reviews, I also added a chopped red bell pepper and pureed the sauce before adding the heavy cream and butter. A big hit at my house!

Very good sauce. It's very versatile and easy to make your own. I used 1/2 an onion and 1 shallot. I also pureed mine. I didnt have heavy cream, so I just used whole milk. Im sure the cream would have been more decadant, but for those watching their weight, the milk was fine. I served mine over cheese and spinach stuffed shells at a dinner for the vegetarians. It was great. I might try it with some penne and feta. Great sauce. Thanks for sharing!

Excellent sauce. As suggested I used more garlic than the recipe stated and instead of the cream I substituted Marscapone (italian style cream cheese) which helped keep the sauce thick. Was very sucessful. We topped with sliced pan fried chicken breast and lots of shaved parmesan - Yum.

Was really really delicious. The only thing I noticed is that there was a lot of onion in the sauce which is fine with me, because I like onion but for others you might want to cut the onion a little. Also I used fresh basil instead of dried.
Easy! Tasty! Loved it!
Pretty good, but it is still missing something to make it amazing.

THIS IS SO GOOD!!!!!!!!!!!  I LOVE making pasta sauces with my homemade pasta (thanks, Kitchen aid attachment :)  and was looking for a vegetarian version to try.  Well, this beats all of the recipes with meat that I've ever tried too!  It is so rich, so creamy, so delectable.  East to make.  And my husband loved it too.
Great, flavorful recipe.  I used fresh basil and added a couple of splashes of white wine.  I think the wine made a great difference in the taste.

Great recipe ! I have used fresh tomatoes (pureed in the blender) and no sugar. Also i sauteed some mushrooms on the side and added them when the sauce was ready. Added some parmesan cheese to thicken the sauce !!!!!YUM

I made this pretty much exactly as written other than not actually measuring the ingredients and using just regular diced tomatoes.  This is the sauce I have been looking for! I always found homemade tomato sauces to be too acidic no matter what I added.  This was absolutely delicious.  My kids liked it as did my mother. I will definitely make this again. I can't see making any other ever again :)  Thanks Kimber!
I did not make any changes and it was delicious.  A keeper. Think I will try to add chicken next time.

Stunning presentation...Amazing Flavor!! Who would have thought a little addition of cream could make something go from "good" to "heavenly"!  I followed the recipe except I used fresh herbs and added mushroom and spinach to the finished product. I did not blend it like so many others as I thought it took away from the presentation. I will not change a thing WHEN I make it again. Buon!!

SO good! My husband loved this sauce...BUT,i did make a few changes. I substituted freshly chopped tomatoes for the italian diced ones that were called for. I also added sliced chicken sausages to add more texture and flavor. Oh, and i left out the butter, the cream was enough. Overall, delicious recipe, will be making it many many times to come. =)

I thought this was super easy and delicious. I didn't have any cream so I just used milk and a dollop of cream cheese (someone suggested it). I cooked up some linguine and grilled some chicken breast.  I will make it again. Thanks for the recipe.

Fantastic recipe! Like a previous poster suggested, I blended the sauce in the bullet and poured directly on the pasta. I also used 2 chopped up tomatoes instead of the can of Italian tomatoes and it still turned out great. I used this sauce over gnocchi and wow, what a meal!

I thought the flavor of this was very good.  I also blended it slightly to make the texture smoother.  If you are trying to make this less fattening - DO NOT substitute fat free half and half!  As soon as I added it to the sauce it separated and formed a solid, making the whole sauce really grainy.

I really like this recipe. I love italian tomato recipes so this was perfect for my pasta and chicken dish. I would recommend adding about a tablespoon of lemon juice to the sauce BEFORE adding the heavy cream and butter. I also doubled this recipe because i didn't have a 14.5 ounce can and only had a 29 ounce can. It worked out perfectly. I loved it!
After reading some of the comments, I adjusted the sugar (just used to taste) and added red bell pepper & mushrooms. Added some shrimp just before adding cream. It was delicious!!!
I made this with Gnocchi I from this site and it was absolutely delicious!  I didn't have dried basil on hand so I used Italian herbs.  Excellent recipe!

Very very good.  Extremely tasty.  I used only 1/2 onion and like 3 cloves garlic.  Then I used two cans of diced tomatoes(used the one flavored with basalmic vingar/basil-great extra taste), sugar, sea salt, pepper, red pepper flakes, and used italian seasoning to taste.  I doubled the cream and butter as well.  Will def make again and again.  THANKS!
I love this recipe.  It's one thing that I can whip up at a moment's notice.  Delish.
This is quite a simple recipe, and very good! I quickly mixed this together and threw it over some pasta in a pinch, and voila! Dinner is served.

This recipe is soooo good.  I didn't have heavy whipping cream so I used 1/2 and 1/2.  I don't think it needed the butter and I did add some hot pepper flakes and a dash of white wine to give it a bite.  I will be making this alot.  I feel it only serves 2 though so make sure you double it if you want left overs
This was a quick and tasty pasta sauce.  The heavy cream add a nice change from regular red sauce.  I topped this with parmesan cheese and leftover sliced grilled sausage.

This is a great recipe.  So simple, and so delicious.  Served it with store bought gnocchi (I was a little hesitant of that, but it was great) and had dinner in less than half an hour.  The only reason I'm giving it four stars is because the onion flavor was overpowering.  I read that in other reviews, so I used a small onion--which was probably less than half a cup.  Still, the onion overpowered everything else and was SO strong.  I think next time I make this I will start with 1/8 cup of onion and keep working with it until I get the right amount.  Other than that, it was great.  I added a few red pepper flakes which gave it a little kick, and will do that again next time.
Made sauce as written but omitted sugar and onions.  Added ground turkey w/onions.  Next time I will double the recipe.  Only served 3 as written.

I'm not good at experimenting but at the drop of a hat, when I had just a half hour to prepare dinner for 2, this recipe worked! Absolutely delicious. I  usedonly one-half of a small onion instead of a whole onion and I used 2 garlic cloves, not one.  I had all of the ingredients except the 14.5 oz can of diced tomatoes so I substituted what I had on hand: a one-quart container of fresh grape tomatoes, which I mashed in the pan when added, along with an 8 oz. can of tomato sauce. I used those two items instead of the large can of diced tomatoes. This sauce was perfect with a half-pound of macaroni. Added grated parmigiana & more fresh pepper to my plate. Delicious! (For those who thought the sauce was too liquid, they may have covered the sauce while it simmered. Don't cover it.)

Love this recipe!  Some changes that I made- were to add chopped baby spinich and shitake mushrooms sliced thinly to the sauce prior to adding the cream.  I fry salmon in a seperate pan and break it up then add it to the sauce over penne pasta.   Absolutely amazing!
It was alright, but not as amazing as I expected it to be based on the reviews.
This recipe was amazing! I added shrimp and diced chicken breast for a fantastic meal for my family!

This recipe is PHENOMENAL! I made the Tomato Pesto Bread Batter recipe from this site and I used the bread to scoop up this creamy, chunky sauce. I have to agree with other reviewers, though... I LOVE sauce with my pasta and this MIGHT be enough for two servings for me, but definitely not for 5. In actuality, I could eat all of this sauce, plain, all by myself. I would give this more stars, if I could.
Very delightful, very easy!!!!! I used half and half instead of cream.  Big hit at my house.
Love it, love it, love it!!!!!!!!!!
Would be best made a day ahead so flavors meld and would be thicker.

This sauce is really good.  I did double the recipe just for quantity sake. I also only used 1/2 small onion and 3 cloves garlic.  Just because we prefer garlic flavor over onion in our sauce.

**Just a note: To those who state the sauce is too thin, you probably didn't allow the sauce from the canned tomatoes to reduce.  You must bring it to a high boil and then reduce the heat to allow the liquid to boil off and thicken.  Also, this isn't meant to be a low fat recipe. If you substitute heavy cream for milk or even half and half plan on adding flour to your base otherwise you will not have the same thickness.
This was fantastic. I added some chucks of Mozarella Cheese, chicken and roasted pine nuts on top for a complete meal.  It was a hit!!
This recipe was great!! I found myself without any pasta sauce on hand and this turned out better than any store bought sauce! I wish I'd have doubled it, though, because it was SO delicious.

My husband made this last night and served on spinach ravioli.  It was a real treat.  It was extremely easy and tasted like it came from a fine Italian restaurant.  If you want to impress someone, do not hesitate to try this.

Loved it! This is my new favorite quick pasta sauce recipe. Instead of heavy cream, I used Neufchâtel cheese (like cream cheese, but healthier) and a little bit of milk for a richer flavor. I also puréed mine after cooking because I like a thinner texture. Next time I might only purée 3/4 to keep some of the tomatoes in the sauce.
Very Good. Thanks!

YUM! I love a good cream sauce, but hate the calories that go with them. Lightened this up considerably by using Fat-Free Sour Cream, and skipping the butter and sugar (it doesn't need the sugar). I also sauteed mushrooms to go in it...because...well...mushrooms just HAVE to go in a cream sauce!
I loved it. I used more garlic and blended it slightly. I also used 1% milk. Can't wait to make again
Ok, didnt really turn out like I wanted, had this at a restaurant and it was a lot better, this was maybe too chunky and not smooth and sweet enough?
Perfect and so easy.

OMG!!  I don't think I have ever commented on a recipe on here, but this one deserves it.  This was the best pasta I've ever tasted in my life.  I absolutely love the Olive Garden, but I could NEVER go there again, as long as I can make this!  I honestly think that my basil seasoning made the difference as it seemed to have some "hot" spice in it.  Not bad, just enough.  I used "Jane's Krazy Mixed Up Seasoning" (the "Mixed-Up Basil one) that is all natural.  I got it either at Ingle's or Food City in the spice section.  

This recipe has been moved up to my "keeper" list.

I was looking for something to put over whole wheat pasta. This was an excellent sauce. I didnt use heavy cream, used a low fat cream substitue and it was wonderful.  I will make this again and again.
I just add some sweet italian sausage and this is absolutely delish!!

Wow!  So easy...and so fabulous!   This is one of the best smelling dishes I ever made.   I fried up some turkey kielbasa with the onions, then when the tomatoes came to a boil, I added some tortellini and cooked until they softened.  After that, the cream and some shredded cheese.  Easy one pot meal that the family DEVOURED.   I felt pretty cool being able to say I made it from scratch instead of from a jar.  This is a serious WIN.

Easy, quick and yummy. I made four small changes here:  I used two garlic cloves, instead of one.  I followed other reviewers' suggestions and smoothed half my sauce in the blender, so it still had a little chunkiness but not too much. After I added the butter, I tasted it and thought the sauce needed a little more tomato taste, so I opened a can of tomato sauce I had on hand and added a few tablespoons to the cream sauce before the last simmering step. Last, I added perhaps a half tablespoon of flour to thicken the sauce a bit (I did not measure exactly; just eyeballed it).  Very pleased with this.
This sauce is fabulous.  We put it over crispy chicken and pasta and it is absolutly wonderful.
TRUE Italian NO SUGAR!!! More Basil!!

YUMMY! Made this last night and topped with grilled chicken. We left it chunky but would like to try it blended. I followed the tip about using skim milk instead of heavy cream and it was great. I also used a bit less butter. Super delish and will definitely make again.

Inspired by SunnyByrd's photo, I pulled this out of my recipe box and gave it a try tonight.  I've collected so many recipes that some of the best ones (like this one) often get overlooked.  This was absolutely wonderful - very easy to pull together and very filling.  I would definitely serve this to my dinner guests.  I followed SunnyByrd's lead and served this with shrimp over fettucine.  Only change I made was to increase the garlic to 3 cloves.  Simply scrumptious! Thank you so much for posting this recipe!

I'm giving this a 5 for super easy.  To make it with meat I topped off the pasta with Chicken Picatta from Sam's Club found in the frozen section. The chicken picatta comes with 2 trays so double the sauce recipe and freeze half. EASY & YUM!

For a quick pasta sauce this recipe is very good. I didn't have any heavy cream, so I just used milk instead. I also added around a teaspoon of fennel seeds. To thicken the sauce I used a teaspoon of cornstarch. One person said it only made about 3 servings. She must use 2/3 cup per serving. It made just a hair under 2 cups. I like making my recipes from scratch. This way I know what goes into them. Thanks for a great alternative recipe to my pasta sauce with meat. 
UPDATE-This can eaisly be made vegan by using almond milk instead of cream. It's delicious. It's my favorite sauce for pasta and many casseroles.

Very good and have been making something similar for many yrs.  Do not use Italian style tomatoes because we find them sweet - just add extra Italian herbs.  Also we do not blend it and at the end throw in some halved black olives.  They really give it some zing......
Way too much onion. It took over the sauce. I would definitely cut back next time I make it.

This was good. I was wanting a tomato-cream sauce for some Gnocchi.  I made the sauce as directed and it still did not have the taste I was looking for. It was good but not quite what I wanted.  So I added 4 oz of cream cheese and 1/4c parm. cheese.  It turned out to be exactly what I wanted.  It was REALLY yummy!

This is only the second homemade tomato sauce I have tried to make... it was amazing! Fiance isn't a fan of a lot of tomato and sometimes the texture but he loved it! The only change I made was after everything was cooked I pureed the sauce so it was a thicker, smoother sauce rather than chunky - definitely will be making this again!! (It's fabulous with Meatball Nirvana and we made them with Turkey this time)

added 3 garlic cloves, used diced tomatoes and just added italian seasoning, used skim milk 3/4 cup instead of cream, used only 1 tablespoon of smart balance spread instead of butter, used Truvia instead of sugar,  added 1/2 block of Tofu and Tomato paste to help thicken.  pureed it all with hand held blender. yum
The recipe was delicious!  It was not enough for a pound of pasta though so I would suggest to double it.
grade A+++
Very quick and easy to make...but, too much basil and not enough cream.

Oh my gosh, this is so good! This was my very first time making sauce from scratch, and this was so easy to prepare and came out perfect. I used half the onion, twice the garlic, subbed half and half for the heavy cream, and thickened it with a little flour...and it was perfect! I served it on manicotti (which I find rather bland with regular tomato sauce--I parboiled the manicotti shells, filled them, and baked them in the sauce, and the shells softened up nicely in the oven--I used 20 servings of the sauce for 1 box of manicotti), and it was absolutely delicious! I'll definitely be making this again.
First time trying this recipe. I had all the ingredients except for the heavy whipping cream. It was delicious!

This has become my staple sauce since I first discovered it on this site.  I have made it a countless number of times now, both as per recipe for a small scale, and slightly altered for a much larger scale.  Regardless, I always use more garlic than called for and always run the whole thing through the blender to smooth the sauce.  This is absolutely delicious and always receives rave reviews.  Quick, easy, and foolproof - what more could you ask for?

I followed Michael E's review and suggestions but I did add about 2 tsp organic sugar and used my basil and oregano essential oils to season, it was delicious. I added a can of the fire roasted diced tomatoes (because that's what I had), I probably won't use them next time. I have enough extra sauce to use it on baked ravioli that was suggested by another reviewer.
I used 3/4 c skim milk instead of heavy cream since that's what I had on hand. I put all ingredients in the blender and it was very good with Mushroom Ravioli.

My family (2 teens & husband) & I really like this. By accident, I used the big 28 oz can of tomatoes, and cooked it down for a while. I used less sugar, and 1/2 to 1 cup of half & half instead of cream. Since I had it on hand, I also added approx 2T of romano cheese. I sauteed & added to the sauce some chicken sun-dried tom.sausage, cooked a bag of tortellini, mixed it all together. It was plenty of food for 4! Yum!

I made this for my husband this Valentine's day.  We loved it!  Perfectly tangy and creamy.   
Thanks Kimber  = )

Good recipe! Unfortunately this wasn't quite enough for my family of 4 - and we aren't big eaters. I thought I had cream on hand when I started making this, but didn't. I ended up using milk as many suggested - not bad, but would have been better with cream. I also added some red pepper flakes for spice. Will do again with slight modifications.
Made it pretty much exactly as written.  Changes - only had 18% cream  and omitted butter as it seemed rich enough. Was very very good.
Flavorful and very easy.  Next time I think I will put it in the blender before I add the cream so my 10 year old can't pick all the "chunks" out!

This is a very nice sauce. I have made similar for many years. It is yummy over gnocchi. People are afraid of cream and butter. Don't be. Fat does not make you fat. Quite the opposite, it gives you energy and  keeps you satiated, but blend it into a creamy sauce. I have also made it with fresh tomatoes from the garden.

This was so delicious and very easy to make! I made this for my boyfriend and he loved it. I served this amazing sauce over fusilli pasta and served some parmesan roasted asparagus on side. I left out the sugar and pureed the tomatos in a food processer to make a smoother sauce. Next time I make this I am going to make a double recipe. Thanks for the great recipe!!!
Very easy to make and good flavor. I used reduce fat cream cheese (2oz) instead of the heavy cream and it came out well.
Super delicious!  Make this often in our house always turns out fantastic!
Very easy and tasty recipe.  Due to other reviews, i did use about 1 tbsp of flour to thicken it a little.  Also, I used fresh basil and oregano.  Turned out great served over spinach tortellini.

Awesome recipe. Easy and super good. I didn't have a can of diced tomatoes and ended up using a mixture of tomato paste and crushed tomatoes, which worked out very well. I just boiled the tomato sauce longer, probably about 15 minutes to remove most of the moisture before adding the cream.
Divine. Will definitely make again and again. I used diced tomatoes with chilies, so it was a bit spicy too. I loved it and it was good even the day after.
This was DEE-LISH!!!! I didn't have any heavy cream, so I used evaporated milk, YUMMY!!!! I will definitely make this again!

I don't know what to say about this except for the fact that I did not care for it. It wasn't very sauce like, the spice combo was just kinda 'meh' and i didn't find it very creamy. Overall it was bland.
I have three boys. They all loved it. I didn't change a thing. I will definitely be putting this in the dinner rotation!
Love it! Pureed my sauce in blender but other than that, followed exactly...just what i was looking for, and so simple!
Very easy and so delicious.  Not heavy like so many pasta sauces.   I might even turn it into a tomato soup.

This sauce was amazing! I don't know if I will ever buy store-bought sauce again. The sauce is even great before adding the cream.  I basically doubled everything but instead of using a second can of diced tomatoes, I used a can of tomato sauce, and I also added a generous splash of red cooking wine.

This recipe intrigued me so I tried it except I used fresh tomatoes and was quite disappointed with the overall result. It was bland, dull, flat. I had to then try to add some notable taste to it so added extra salt (no big help)then added crushed red pepper (eh, okay)fresh parsley, (better but still eh). It didn't need the sugar at all and I wish I didn't add that since the onions were sweet enough. I love the concept of a fresh tomato cream sauce so I will keep reworking this till I get it where I think the flavor should be at.

I followed the recipe exactly, and it was excellent! For next time I think I will cut the onion in half. The onions were very mild tasting, but there just seemed to be an excess amount. I served this with penne pasta (1/2 pound) and sliced chicken breasts. I mixed everything together and then served. This allowed the chicken and pasta to absorb some of the moisture and taste of the sauce. I also thought the amount of sauce was just right with the pasta and chicken (I don't like pastas slathered in tons of sauce), but think it serves closer to 4 people.

Simply delicious.  All I added was fresh spinach and cooked italian sausage.  Threw it all together with "Quick Gnocchi" from this site (a winner, too), in a casserole and baked it.  Fantabulous dinner and leftovers were wonderful, too.

This was great! I followed others' tips and pureed for our kids, and used 1% milk instead of cream to make it more healthy. I'm sure it would be creamier with the cream, but it was still rich enough with the milk. Great, easy sauce.
Made exactly as above, and is a frequent repeat at our table. When we had excess tomatoes this summer, I made and froze several batches for winter use!

I tried this recipe on a whim because I wanted something fresh that wouldn't take too long to cook...this came out great for me! I pretty much did exactly what the recipe said and pureed the tomatoes before adding the cream, based on other reviews. The flavors were perfect together, and it wasn't a heavy meal, which is what I was looking for. I will def add some sausage or chicken the next time I make it!
Very good.

My boyfriend and I loved this sauce! I didn't do the onions and garlic because we're not a fan of those flavors. I also put the tomato mixture in the food processor because I don't like chunky sauces. Thinking about adding mushrooms or other vegetables next time before I process it!
This recipe is wonderful.  My only adjustment was the onion (I only used half - personal preference).  Also, I added mushroom and chicken at then end.  It was a great meal for the middle of the week!
Will definitely reduce the amount of onions next time.

This was insanely amazing as a base to add your own kind of seasoning and make something really special.WARNING: this only makes enough sauce for about two people, so if you're cooking for a family adjust accordingly. When I made it, I added Cayenne pepper to kick it up a notch, and more black pepper (I'm a huge fan of spicy food!).
YUM!! Love it! I only used 1/2 an onion, added a tablespoon of Italian Seasoning and 1/4 cup of shredded parmesan. Then I pureed it in the food processor.
Very very tasty!! I didn't change a thing!!!  Well I did add chicken but thats it!
My family absolutely loved this recipe. Great tasting pasta sauce!!

This was wonderful. Just what I was craving. I put in a few dashes of red wine, (cause I was drinking it while makig!) and used half & half in place of heavy cream. I also added some canned tomato sauce (about 3/4 can) to thin it out a bit.I served with marinated grilled chicken breasts, salad and warm bread. I agree with the others that its not enough for 5, especially if you want dipping sauce.
Didn't really get to taste much of the sauce, put too much pasta :( Will definitely have to retry this!

This is a favorite recipe. I use half the onion, and no sugar, and I add about 1/2 tblsp. of red pepper flakes to the sauce. I also top this with feta cheese at the end and serve with breaded chicken.
I did not change a thing...I only added pepperoni.....DELICOUS.....JERRY...

This was easy and delicious!  It was a tad bit sweet, so I think I'll leave out the sugar next time.  I also used fresh oregano and basil.  (I added the basil at the very end.)  I smoothed it slightly with an immersion blender.  My husband thought it was awesome. 

Thanks!
amazing!!! but I didn't have any tomatoes so I used paste and still it was mind blowinnngggg
Didn't care for the consistency. Found it much too thin. Very tasty though
Easy and awesome
needs a little salt and some parm helps too.
Awesome!

OUTSTANDING! husband normally drenches his meals with parmesan, but this time, not one piece of cheese hit his plate! he "drank" all the extra sauce and licked his plate clean! as for me, i loved it as well :) will definately make the sauce over and over-maybe even for the italian in-laws!
I puréed the tomatoes.  Very yummy.

I thoroughly enjoyed this recipe!!  I did cut down on the onion quite a bit to maybe 1/4 cup.  The only other change I made was that after some of the liquid cooked off, I put the sauce into my food processor and pureed until smooth.  Then I transferred it back to the pan and added the butter and cream.  I served it along with cheese ravioli. YUM!!!
It tasted like I had gone to gourmet school!  Thank you for this wonderful recipe.

My 5 year old loved it even though I added chicken. It was pretty good, but after eating leftovers once, I wasn't up for eating it a third time. She ate it three times though. I used light sour cream instead of the heavy cream, which may have affected it for me.

My husband loved this! The first time I made it I thought it was too sweet, so the second time I added a little more salt and a little less sugar. Pureed in the blender and added shrimp and red pepper flakes.
Very very good and extremely easy to make! My family loved this! Served it over spinach gnocchi and it was a huge hit!

OMG, I just had this tonight and could not stop getting seconds! DELICIOUS! This was my 1st time making 'pink sauce' and I am very health conscious so I made some heart-healthy changes. I used 3/4 cup nonfat milk instead of 1/2 cup heavy cream (I never use heavy cream for anything), only 1 tab olive oil instead of 2, omitted the sugar and salt (as the can of diced tomatoes had enough sodium), and added a whole bag of fresh organic spinach. I served the sauce over fresh butternut squash ricotta ravioli. I think it's my new favorite dish!!! Will be making this as often as possible!

This was delicious! I doubled the recipe--except for the onion and dried herbs--to coat one-and-a-half pounds of pasta (medium shells) as a main course for my family and the proportions were just right. Made a ton, great next day leftovers. Despite using canned tomatoes, it still felt like a much elevated dish from the routine jar sauce, which I often will "upgrade" with the addition of some cream.

My 16 year old son loved this and even ate the leftover right out of the pan with bread.  It was really east and tasty.  I made minor adjustments.  I put in 1 cup of cream instead of half a cup and I added a 1/4 cup of shredded italian cheeses.  I like that this is a sauce that can be tailored making it a little different for the type of pasta or the type of eater.  I can take or leave meat but my boys are definitely carnivores.  So I can see adding some shrimp or chicken for them.  I sauce comments about the sauce being runny, it just takes longer than the 5 minutes stated in the recipe for the liquid to evaporate.  If you cook it for 10 minutes you will have almost not liquid when you add the cream.  Thanks for a great recipe.

This recipe is excellent as is. I did not find it runny at all. Just do not exceed by too much the cooking time that will make your sauce runny as the oils start separating even more with the heat. If you want to "cook more" your sauce only do this when cooking the tomatoes and add the time to the desired chunky or thickness by time lapses of 5 minutes. I also think that without the cream this makes for a good chunky tomato sauce for pasta. 
Someone suggested to omit the sugar. Well, the sugar is necessary for balancing the acidity of the tomatoes. When I cooked this sauce I rectified the salt.
Served over mojito lime pan seared shrimp. POW!

My husband liked it but I guess cream-tomato sauces are not my cup of tea, I've never really been impressed by them. After I told my husband how much cream was involved he decided maybe it wasn't worth it.
Incredible starter recipe!  I always double this as it is not nearly enough for my family, even doubled.  I also include a can of tomato sauce to make it more smooth and use less onion & more garlic.

My 11 year old granddaughter, Kortni, made this recipe today all by herself. She even chopped the onions and cooked the pasta by herself. It was quick and easy and it tasted great. She will definitely be making this again.
Need to cook veggies so they are soft

A solid sauce, but a little too sweet and creamy for me.  Though I modified as follows:  Fresh tomatoes instead of canned, added cayenne pepper, more garlic, salt and pepper and some fresh parmesan.  Also, I took out the oregano and reduced the cream some.  Oh, and added a few meatballs.  Next time, less onions, no sugar, and maybe puree the whole thing, at least a bit.
Super tasty sauce. The only thing I changed was that I skipped the sugar, added some Italian sausage, and threw in a can of tomato paste to make it thicker. Will definitely make this again.

Loved It! I added kielbasa, diced chicken breasts,black olives, fresh spinach, oregano, fennel seed and garlic powder. My kids asked for seconds, which they normally wouldn't with this kind of dish...a true hit! I also served over whole wheat pasta. Oh...I used 1/2 & 1/2 rather than heavy cream. I'll definitely be making again. Thanks for sharing!

Well, I was really excited to make this, but it just didn't turn out how I expected. I think one attributing factor is that I must have chosen too big of an onion. I think I will try this again, but definitely with less onion. It looks great in the picture, but what I ended up with was a very thin and oily sauce. I think I will run the leftover through my food processor and add some jarred sauce to it and it will be quite good.

DELIGHTFUL! It was grocery day and I somehow planned meals for the entire week except tonight...it was time to get creative! I didn't use any olive oil, instead I sauteed the onions in the butter and then added in about a tsp. or so of flour, whisked it with the butter and added the cream (used 1/2 c. cream and about 1.4 c. milk) until there were no lumps. Then I added in all the other ingredients. Simmered for about 15 minutes to get a good consistency. Then I pureed everything in the blender! Wonderful! I also added about a tbsp of vodka, extra pepper and 1/4 tsp of cayenne pepper for a little kick!  My fiance said it tasted just like the sauce on his seafood pasta at one of our favorite restaurant - he even said it tasted GOURMET. Score one for Allrecipes :)
I love this recipe. Huge hit with friends and family. I am current making some right now and using Hunt's fire roasted diced tomatoes w/garlic.

I DECIDED ON THE FLY TO CHECK PANTRY AND FRIDGE...FOUND I HAD EVERTHING! BUT, THE ROTEL WAS NOT MILD. NOW, I ATE IT WITH SPAGHETTI...HOT HOT BUT JUST COULD NOT EAT A LOT OF IT. I DID PUT, SOUR CREAM ON IT!

So good and so easy. This recipe will be used regularly. I have made it twice now. I used heirloom tomatoes instead of the canned tomatoes since that's what I had on hand. I used a handful of fresh basil since I had it. I also left out the sugar. It took more time to reduce the sauce since I used fresh tomatoes. I really like it! Thanks for sharing!
P.S. I agree with another reviewer, this recipe serves 3

Easy and delicious! I sauteed the onion and added crushed jarred garlic for the last minute. I didn't have Italian tomatoes on hand so I used petite regular (no-salt) tomatoes and added extra spices. Had a few tomatoes that were on the way out, so I chopped and added those also. Per a review I read, I transferred the mixture in a couple of batches to my mini-processor, and then added back to the pot. Also added a few tblsps tomato paste, a little white wine and about a tblsp of grated parmesan cheese. I subbed regular half-&-half for the heavy cream but fat-free would have been healthier! Look forward to having over pasta or ravioli! Seems better than store-bought sauce. Thanks Kimber!
I loved this recipe. I made the recipe as written except followed other commenters advice and added less sugar and thickened the sauce slightly with flour. Such a nice flavor yet easy and fast.
I found this just ok. I think I will add beef to make it more flavorful.

I didn't have any canned tomatoes so I sautéed about 5-6 medium tomatoes in oil for about 15 minutes with garlic and onion powder since I was out of onions. I blended it as suggested  and added all the spices and remaining ingredients and let simmer while making pasta. This only made about three servings and I did also add flour as others suggested.

I have made this recipe a few times.  However I cut back on the basil (1 Tsp, instead of 1 Tbls) , and I used rotel tomatoes to give it a little zip, and added cooked diced chicken breast to the sauce.  Its DELICIOUS!!

I made it almost exactly as listed but blended it like others said. To me, it was lacking flavor, so I added Italian seasoning. If I make this again I will use half an onion instead of a whole onion. It was way too much! And I will also omit the sugar. This had a weird sweet taste to it. I'm sure with these changes it will be a 4 or 5 star.
Nice change from regular pasta sauces.  My daughter really enjoyed this.  It doesn't make enough sauce - would recommend doubling or even tripling the amount.

Loved this simple recipe!   Didn't have cream on hand so used 3/4 nonfat milk and 2 tbs of butter and 1/4 cup sour cream. Added red pepper and Parmesan for a kick!   This came out amazing!   Hubby loved it!
Oh my goodness. I added Italian sausage. My hubby raved over this one. Wow. This sauce is that good!!!!!!! THis recipe is a definite keeper.
I love this cream sauce, it is my new go-to sauce for all pastas! It's easy to alter if you want to, and I added extra cloves of garlic, but it was easy and delicious!
This recipe is absolutely delicious! My husband and I agree this is now our favorite sauce! We used leaks instead of onion and it came out perfect.
I used this in a lasagna and got rave reviews from my dinner guests!
Yum yum yum, especially with some chopped jalapenos (seeds included if you like it hot).  Served with pasta and broccoli garnished with fresh basil, pine nuts, and cherry tomatoes cut like flowers.

My family did not care for this at all, in fact it got thrown out!  The sauting of the onions made it WAY too sweet, I even cut down on the amount of onion and sugar to start with.  The texture of the sauce was quite gross....I've had creamy tomato sauces before and LOVED them....this wasn't even close.  Will not use again.
This is a great fast recipe that everyone loves. I have played with this recipe a few different ways . Using milk , cream or half and half and it always comes out delicious.
This was a little too sweet for me but my Hubbie liked it. I did puree it to make it less chunky.

I made this about a week ago over Penne Pasta. I changed a few things and it came out amazinggg. Instead of using can tomatoes I used fresh and just added Italian Seasoning to the sauce. I used half the onion, double the garlic and FRESH basil all in the blender. I also used about 1/3 cup of tomato paste and added a little of white flower to thiken up the sauce a bit. Omitted the sugar. Again it was Delicious andnot hard to make. Will deffinetly do it again.
This sauce does have a great flavor to it. However, we did not care for the texture. I only used half an onion and fresh tomatoes and it was simply not the cream texture I was searching for.

I really liked this recipe and will be making it often, since I almost always have all of the ingredients in my pantry. I added mushrooms late (when reducing after adding the tomatoes) because I almost forgot them and totally misread that it called for 1 Tablespoon of basil and just used 1 teaspoon. I liked having the chunky tomatoes. I would maybe add a bit more cream and definitely double this recipe if I were cooking for more than just myself. It makes enough sauce for me to have a plate for dinner and a plate of leftovers. If I were a more normal person I could maybe stretch it to three, but there's no way this makes five normal person servings.
Just didn't like this,  Thought it needed something but I am not sure what.
This is a great sauce and easy to make.  I added more garlic than called for.  I also added some cooked chicken strips one night to the sauce and the family loved it.

I love this recipe! I did alter it a little the second time I made it by adding a can of tomato paste and a can of tomato sauce to give it a fuller tomato flavor. Either way, this is an EXCELLENT recipe (my dad gave his approval, and he grew up with authentic Italian cooking).
This is really yummy!  I used half and half in place of the heavy cream and a bit of Italian seasoning as well.  I don't think it really needs the sugar so I usually leave it out or just use a pinch.
Added some sauteed mushrooms and a bit of marjoram and it was delicious. Next time I'll use a little bit more diced tomatoes for some extra oomph.

Very good. I used a 28 ounce can of crushed tomatoes (all I had), 4 cloves of garlic, fresh basil, and a can of tomato paste to make it a bit thicker. It was delicious as well as easy to make on a night I had time restraints!

Excellent recipe! As written, it is gluten free. If you must substitute for heavy cream, has anyone tried using evaporated skimmed milk? This is an old standby alternative to add texture of heavy cream in sauces without fat that doesn't alter flavor. I haven't tried it in this but think I will for at least part of the heavy cream to see if it works. For those who don't like the chunky consistency, try crushed tomatoes & add the extra Italian seasoning. I like this recipe as is, though. I think any type of meat from chicken to Italian sausage could be added as well! This is a keeper!
The sauce is very good and pairs nicely with a glass of wine for dinner. I doubled the garlic and also used fresh tomatoes. Served over bow tie pasta with salad. It was delicious!

Agree, absolutely delicious!  Instead of canned tomatoes used diced garden tomatoes and garden fresh basil and oregano and a bit less onion and sugar..
Followed the spirit of the recipe, but simmered longer than five minutes until it thickened up.  Measured the cream and butter exactly, mixed it in and served with twist pasta.
Definitely a keeper recipe, and a good one to use when you get a lot of garden tomatoes at once (which usually happens :-)

This recipe is SO great!  I did blend my sauce as some other reviewers recommended, but other than that, I followed the recipe and it turned out wonderful.  I served the sauce over bowtie pasta with some chicken that I cubed and sauteed in a pan with olive oil and garlic salt, and then topped with fresh parmesan.  Yummy!  Thank you SO much for this recipe.  It was just what I was looking for!

I tried it per the recipe. Too sweet. I wish I hadn't added the sugar. After realizing it was too sweet, I did add fresh basil, more herbs, salt, pepper and a couple splashes of hot sauce.  I am glad I used a mix of crushed and pureed tomatoes because I think the consistency with the diced would have been too chunky.

this is one of our go-to recipes, the thinner consistency means  it's excellent over tortellini. (the heavy cream is what provides the body to this sause so if you are using a lighter fat option you may need to thicken it another way.) We add extra garlic and fresh herbs when we can but otherwise use this recipe as written.
Excellent! The only changes we made were to add a diced green pepper and Italian sausage. This was all cooked along with the onion. Wonderful!!

This was a tremendously rich and delicious sauce!  I also added some spicy italian sausage, however, the dish would have been superb without.  I used a spinache penne, a can of fire roasted and diced tomatoes and opted for fresh herbs.  Fantastic!  Thank you very much.  Also, I made the full fat version and I agree that one could probably get away with making some low fat substitutions i.e. half and half and still have a wonderful sauce. Thank you very much!!
Excellent! As per the other reviews, I tripled the garlic and added tom paste for thickness. Everyone loved it, including our toddlers and one picky preschooler.

Didn't have heavy cream but I did have reduced fat cream cheese.  Used 2 OZ cut into small slices and melted it in. Didn't have Italian style diced tomatoes so used regular diced tomatoes and added 2 T. fresh basil and 2 T. fresh oregano.  Added one more clove of garlic and just a pinch of sugar, left out the butter.  Followed other reviews and used my stick blender to smooth it out.  Sprinkled fresh parsley and Parmesan on top.  Absolutely delicious!
Pretty good.  good compliment side dish.

This was a very good sauce, though I did make a couple of changes: I omitted the sugar, used fresh basil, two garlic cloves, and 1% milk instead of cream. I served it over whole wheat penne with diced chicken, and it was delicious!

I used fresh basil and blended the finished sauce. Then I tossed it with bowtie pasta, and mushrooms, grilled chicken, and sun-dried tomatoes sauteed in olive oil/white wine. Topped it all with shredded Parmesan and more fresh minced basil. I am keeping this recipe. It was visually appealing and yummy enough to serve to company but quick and easy enough for a Sunday evening at home.

Nothing terribly special.  I had been really excited to try this one, too.  In the end I doctored it up a bunch just to try to get a better flavor.  I added some crushed red pepper, a little more sugar and butter, and some vodka, and got more of a vodka sauce flavor.  It ended up being better the next day for dipping with Easy Focaccia from this site.

Loved it!  Took another's advise and sautéed mushrooms with the onions and garlic.  Didn't have heavy cream so I used the milk/butter substitute and added shrimp to my pasta!  "Thats a 10!" said my husband!
Delicious!  Just can't seem to get the smooth consistency.  Always "gritty".  =[  Have tried blending it.  Any other tips?
My husband and I loved it! Not exactly good for you but it tastes great!
Good flavour. Easy to make with simple ingredients. Mine didnt thicken up very much even after adding the cream so I used 1 tbsp of tomato paste. Did the trick!

This was easy to make and delicious!  I added chicken (cut into small pieces).  And I prefer a saltier taste so next time Ill add more salt and probably omit the sugar.  But salt was something that can be added to your liking afterwards.  Great recipe!
Even the kids who normally don't like the sauce asked for more sauce, by itself.
This is really a great sauce! I did make a few changes out of personal preference. But as written it is very good. Definitely a keeper recipe!
I made it with chilli beans and ravioli it is amazing!!

I added a little more tomato sauce to get the color in it since the heavy cream washed it out. I also ended up adding a little more salt/pepper and red crushed pepper of course :-) 
Made with chicken. Finger-licking-good!

I have made this recipe twice now. Once, served over cheese tortellini, and last night, served with Penny pasta and cut up Italian sausage. I blended the sauce the first time, and didn’t the second time, and both ways were perfectly wonderful. This is such a good find. The addition of fresh basil at the end is really good, but I didn’t find it necessary. Still, it’s a great recipe to play with, but it’s wonderful just as is.

This was just how I like my recipes simple, fast, and good.   I used crushed tomatoes instead of diced.  It could have used a little more flavor so I gave it a 4.  Next time, I'm going to try some of the suggestions others have left.

Simply yum!  Simple and quick to make.  Tasty and filling; served over a mixture of orecchie and wild garlic fettuccine.   I only added a pinch of baking soda to cut the bitter tomato taste and I used San Marzano whole tomatoes and cut them up with the juice.  So flavorful - and the leftovers were even better as it gave the ingredients a chance to meld.

With some changes, this sauces is delicious.  I used Prego pasta sauce instead of dice tomatoes, fresh oregano and basil, half an onion, 3-4 cloves of garlic, a cup of heavy cream, a teaspoon of sugar, and 2 table spoon of chopped sun dried tomatoes halves.

Yum! I did use a little less basil and added parsley. I blended the sauce minus the heavy cream, then returned to the pan, added the cream and let it heat through on low until serving. We had it over whole wheat penne and it was delicious. Thanks! :)

I guess given the number of reviews, I expected a little better tasting sauce.  I did add one more clove of garlic and more sugar, as I thought the sauce was too tart.  Even after doing that, there was an unpleasant after-taste.  I might try again with crushed tomatoes, but I'll see.
I used 2% milk instead and it was delicious!

really loves this! simple yet tasty .. made it with fresh tomates and tomato puree because here in malaysia i can't find italian seasoned dice tomatoes. however the sauce that i got was delicious enough for us :)i also added dory fish cutlets.. nice. definitely a keeper

This was my first time making a tomato based sauce and I am truly impressed with how it turned out.  I made a few modifications to the seasonings, and it was great!  My husband and daughter loved the entire meal.
Delicious!  I doubled the recipe, pureed it in the blender and only used half an onion.  Served it with sautéed chicken breast on fettuccine.  Yummm!
