Absolutely delicious!! Best over penne pasta or cheese-filled ravioli. Even my picky toddler will eat this sauce!

Such a simple recipe has no right to taste this good!  Made as is, it is spectacular!  I occasionally add some fresh baby spinach or chopped mushrooms. I've used herbs d'Province, fresh herbs and Italian herb paste--you just cannot screw this up!  Thank you Kimber, for taking my limited Italian menu to a whole new level!

Tasty and definitely quick and easy....I added cut up fresh green beans and sun dried tomatoes to my fusilli while it was boiling so this ended up as a colourful interesting dish! It sounded wonderful, but I just didn't care for the combination's taste or texture, sorry.
This was really yummy.  The only reason I didn't give it 5 stars was because i prefer smoother sauces.  Next time I will put it in the blender and I think that will make even better.
i just made this recipe and its amazing!! thank u ! ure a life saver lol

Very good recipe to experiement with.  I grilled chicken and deglazed the pan with white wine, added rosemary, half bar of cream cheese, sauteed red bell pepper, ground italian suasage and a dash of basalmic.

Just made this sauce and it's soooo yummy! I pretty much followed the recipe as is and it turned out really good. I only had thick cream in my cupboard, so I only used about 1/4 c of that. great recipe!! perfect for busy nights...I added some half/half ground beef/pork and left out the cream in favor of a splash of white wine for a lighter dish.  It was awesome, my picky 7 yr old had thirds!!  thanks for sharing!
fantastic! Thank you!

my family loved this! we added a pound of ground beef seasoned with italian seasoning and it was a hit! loved the creamy flavor - it is going on the monthly dinner menu!

I actually replace the cream with Vanilla Soy Milk and the butter with a non-dairy spread and it is still wonderful!  I haven't tried to freeze it but I think it would even freeze and keep well.  It's SUPER easy to make and I recommend it to everyone!

I would have given this recipe only three stars, but my biggest problem with it may have been something I caused.  I thought it was too sweet.  However, I substituted fat-free half and half for the heavy cream (as suggested by other reviewers), and fat-free half and half is sweetened, so I'm guessing that was the problem.  I don't think I'll make this again, although I ate it all.  I'd recommend that people taste the sauce before adding sugar, especially when they make a substitution.
this was very yummy with tortellini

Very good! I pureed mine as well and served it over ravioli and it was absolutely delicious. I wanted spinach/chicken/cheese ravioli, but could only find 5 cheese. This would be good over tortellini too!
I use plain tomato sauce (I'm not big on tomatoes), heavey whipping cream and add shredded parmesean. Besides that follow the recipe to the t. Awe, tastes better than Carrabas.
Kinda bland, I'll have to do some tinkering with this one.
This has awesome flavor. I added 3 cloves of garlic and Italian seasoning. I also blended everything at the end for a smoother consistency. This was seriously amaze-balls.
Very nice.  No adjustments needed.

We really liked this one! I nice change as I usually just use canned sauce to make a quick meal. I served this over beef raviolis with a salad and bread. There was nothing left by the time we finished as we kept soaking the sauce up with the bread! This could easily pass for a fine resturaunt's meal and it was super easy. Most people have all the ingredients on hand, with the exception on the heavy cream, so that is a big plus in my book.

This sauce was absolutely amazing. So simple. My husband bought the wrong tomatoes so we used Italian style stewed tomatoes and it was still absolutely amazing!  Thank you so much, Kimber! This one is a keeper.
This sauce was great, easy to make, and tasted amazing.
love this sauce, serve over pasta, quick and easy
i made this for my boyfriend and he LOVED it. its a great sauce i would make it over and over again.

First off, I loved how easy this was to prepare. I had all of the ingredients on hand so it was a cheap recipe as well. The only change I made was substituting the heavy cream for fat free half and half to cut the calorie/fat content down.   My boyfriend and I both were knocked away at how wonderful this came out! We served it over gnocchi and the flavors were excellent. I felt like we were eating a gourmet dinner at home.   This one will definitely be made again!

This was good.  I stuck to the recipe with these changes ... I browned 1 lb hamburger (my family won't eat vegetarian), added more garlic, and a 15 oz sauce. Not great! Sorry but maybe it's missing something... didn't taste good at all and even the smell was off. I will not make this again.
An Outstanding dish and so easy to make! This will stay in the book for all easy recipes for years to come. You can use less cream if you want to.
I was missing a couple ingredients and made this last minute. I didn't have an onion and I substituted the fresh garlic for canned crushed garlic. It turned out great!
So delicious!!  We love this!

I've used a similar recipe in the past. The only differences I noticed are I don't use sugar, and I use fresh basil. I've added grilled chicken strips to the sauce before, and usually serve it tossed with a pasta dish, such as penne.
I love this recipe!  I add sautéed Italian sausage and some Arugula.  It's wonderful!
I didn't care for this texture or flavor.  Not very creamy.
Great, easy! Love it.
This sauce is so good.  My family loved it.  I would suggest you add flour to thicken it up.  Other than that it is good just the way it is.

I liked this sauce, but didn't love this sauce.  I was hoping it would measure up to a tomato/cream sauce I had last week while dining out...it didn't.  It was ok, but had too many onions for our liking.  I'll keep looking for a closer match to the restaurant sauce.

Thanks for an inspiring vegetarian dish!  I would improve it by removing the dairy and in its place use earth balance spread and coconut cream which is delicious and much healthier.   To get the cream, keep your can of coconut milk in fridge, 24 hrs minimum, the cream will rise to the top and you can scoop it off!
So easy, so quick and so good.  I added it to pene pasta with grilled chicken and my boys gobbled it up.

This is my "go to" for potlucks or big parties.  Easy, quick, cheap.  I serve over rigatoni and usually double the recipe and use 2 lbs of pasta.  I use my immersion blender to make the sauce smooth and creamy.  I also add parm after blending.  Once I added mushrooms after blending the sauce and it added a nice texture and flavor, but the original recipe is fantastic too.  Always a big hit, served with caser salad and garlic bread.  YUM!

This was a very good sauce, but I put more diced tomatoes (3/4 of a 28oz can)and I added a half a can of tomatoe paste to thicken it up and it turned out really great. Also next time I think I'll only put half an onion (a whole was was too much)and also maybe a little bit less basil. But still, this is really good and we will definatly make it again! Thanks!

This is a very solid basis for a simple, quickly-made cream sauce.  As other suggest, a puree would likely be best for most.  However, quick being key, I've had good results following the directions as-is, but sub-ing sun-dried tomatoes for canned/fresh and using finely chopped fresh basil.  A little flour helps to thicken the sauce just a bit.

This was pretty good - the only change was that I used plain diced tomatoes instead of italian style since I already had those in the cupboard and I pureed the tomatoes mixture. I found it to be a bit bland so I may play around with the spices a bit next time, but it could also have been because I used plain diced tomatoes.

Overall, this is a very good sauce. I added 4 oz of pancetta and changed the diced tomatoes to tomato sauce (personal preference). After that, I think it had WAY too much basil; it was overpowering. I will definitely reduce that to 1.5 teaspoons next time. With that change, I will definitely be making this again. Very easy.

I had two differant kinds of pasta i needed to use and some canned tomatoes. I came here as always.Glad i did!! I Fallowed the recipe to a "T" And it is sooo yummy!! Super simple,tasty and budget friendly.The best part my kids loved this and i do mean love it!!Thnx much will be making again and again.Next time i will throw in some zucchini & maybe spinach.This is so versatile and if u find it a little bland just up the herbs,ect according to your taste.Oh i did top mine with some shredded provolone that needed to be used up.Great Saturday lunch  or a quick week night dinner served with salad and some garlic roll's!! Yummy!!   *Side note* If you  do not have the cream no worries!!This sauce taste really good even before you put the cream and butter in.*UPDATE* I just finished making this again for lunch.This time i did throw in some chopped fresh spinach, grated carrot & Zuchini..Yum!! My kid's gobbled it right up and didnt even notice that the veggies were in there :))
Excellent and easy recipe! I make this all the time for my family and it's a favorite.
Absouletly delish!  Will make again!! LOVE this recipe, so easy and fresh tasting. I poured half of the sauce into the blender for a texture contrast and it was a rich creamy red color.

I really enjoyed this mixed with jumbo shrimp. I added fresh chopped parsley, more garlic, a few splashes of red wine and a can of tomato paste, as I found the tomato flavor a bit subdued. Definitely a keeper.
I tend to add a little more garlic and cream and then cook a little longer until the sauce is nice and thick.

I've been trying to duplicate the penne rosa recipe from Noodles and Company chain. This looked similar  to there ingredients and I followed the recipe exactly.It wasn't quite what I wanted but a good base for  future attempts. Next time I will puree it like several suggested and  it was lacking a little kick to me.
Sooo yummy ! Made it exactly as in the recipe!

Do not change anything about this! So good, I put red pepper flakes on the table for people that needed more spice. I doubled the sauce and it was the perfect amount for a box of pasta. I added sweet italian sausage to make it a filling meal. My guest loved it. Oops, forgot to say I threw the sauce in the blender to get rid of chunks.

The flavor of this sauce was good, but the texture was off.  First, it was much thinner than I expected it to be.  And second, I either used too big of an onion or I didn't cook it long enough- they were still crunchy and overwhelmed the dish.  Next time I'll add some tomato paste for thickening, and use less onion.

Tasted amazing! Me and my husband loved the flavor! I used the sauce over a spinach and cheese stuffed ravioli type pasta, and it was EXCELLENT. Tasted like a dish from a restaurant.

The onions had a delicious caramelized flavor which really added to the overall depth of the sauce. Also, since I only had extra thick double cream, I used less than the recipe called for and thinned it out with milk.

Definitely a sauce I'll use again, and will definitely try on an assortment of different pasta dishes!

yum! i love that i found this to make my own sauce. I do still buy the jars for days when i'm feeling lazy but there isnt much to getting this done so it's not a big deal to just throw things together. thank you for sharing .
Made as is. Added shredded chicken and pasta. It's amazing!!! Kids loved it.

Very Good, very simple but use less onions! I used 1/2 onion diced and it was still a little overwhelming. I ended up adding more tomatoes and some red pepper flakes. Next time I think I will add some red Bell pepper.

I really liked this sauce and it was extremely easy to make. I substituted half and half for the cream because that is what I had on hand. I also added red pepper flakes. I add that to all of my sauces because I like a little spice. I did think it was missing something though. Next time I will definitely add more garlic and maybe play around with spices a bit. It will be made again.
Absolutely delicious!  I didn't change a thing while making it!  I served it over beef-filled ravioli & sprinked parm cheese on top.
Super good. In pinches I have used crushed tomatoes, and cream cheese instead of cream.

This had a really good flavour! Scaled the recipe down to 3. Added 2 cloves of garlic, half a tomato and 2 tsp of tomato paste instead of what was called for. Also added more herbs. Will definitely make again.

Definitely spoon the sauce into a blender. It was delish!!! Also, I used fire roasted tomatoes 
(roasted them in the oven)

Doubled the recipe, tripled the garlic, subbed whole milk for cream, added garlic powder (1/2 teaspoon for doubled recipe), added parmesan cheese (1/2 cup for doubled recipe) and blended it.   Would add some Italian seasoning, red pepper flakes, and more milk next time for more fluid texture.  Looking for flavor profile of Bucca di Beppo's spicy tomato cream sauce.
I loved this sauce. My wife prepared it as a topping for a grouper filet that I pan fried in olive oil with a light flour and herb breading. The combination was excellent!

Congratulations!!  You nearly replicated the Spaghetti O in a can sauce.  It tastes nearly like it.  Cooked it exactly to spec.  The color is off, but still almost tastes like it.  Cooked it multiple times, Recommend it.

I thought this was pretty good.  I served over bow-tie pasta with some chunks of chicken mixed in.  I used my immersion blender at the end to make the sauce smoother.  Will probably make this again.  It might be good to mix in melted cream cheese in place of the heavy cream.

Amazing sauce! I now add chopped zucchini, squash, red pepper, sometimes asparagus! I've used all sorts of veggies to create a "no-meat" dish that is hearty and healthy. Also, I am a college student and this meal is perfect for any budget!

YUM!!!  I have never taken the time to sign up for a membership so that I could rate a recipe.  I found this recipe SO good that I just had to sign up so I could rate it.  I made it exactly as the recipe stated, and thought it was absolutely delicious.  I do, however, plan to experiment next time by doubling the recipe then adding maybe some shrimp or chicken and artichokes and black olives.

An excellent base sauce for pasta-especially ravioli. I like to boil my ravioli, then place it in an oven dish and smother with this sauce. Then I top it with asiago, mozzarella, panko and italian breadcrumbs and bake at 400 degrees for about half an hour. Scrumptious!
I love this recipe!  I didn't have any italian diced tomatoes so I used some petite diced tomatoes instead.  I also add some fried italian sausage.  So good!  One of my ultimate comfort foods!
Adding some sausage would be a great variation if you're looking to add some meat. Otherwise, the richness and pure indulgent feeling that the recipe provides is just right!
I made no changes to the recipe.  However, I added shrimp saute in butter to mine at the end.  Was very yummy!

I LOVE Tomato Cream Sauce, and this recipe is a godsend! It's SO delicious. I did throw it in the blender for a thicker consistency after following the recipe. For someone without a blender, perhaps substituting the diced tomato with canned tomato sauce and herbs would yield a similar result.

Awesome sauce, worthy of many repeats in our house! So easy to make, too! I didn't have any dried basil so, nor Italian seasoned canned tomatoes, so I just added Italian seasoning and some extra oregano to taste .  Family doesn't like tomato chunks so I took the immersion blender to it. I tripled the recipe, and it fed us 2 nights with the rest going to the freezer for a super-easy weeknight dinner. Served with fettuccine, grilled chicken breast slices and a side salad. YUM!
great easy sauce, and works with many different ingrediants.  One of my favorites now.

WOW!  What a great sauce!  So here's what I did...like another member, after cooking tomatoes, onion, garlic and spices in saucepan, I put mixture into blender and pureed.  Then I put back into saucepan, stirred in 3/4 cup nonfat milk (in place of heavy cream) and butter.  I left out sugar altogether.  Didn't need it.  I added a small amount of grated parmesan cheese to give it an extra kick.  What I got was a sauce that tasted like it was full of fat and calories, but it was actually almost fat free and very healthy!  Not to mention, it was EXTREMELY easy to make.  Definitely a keeper!
Nice light flavor! Did double the garlic but other than that stuck to the recipe.  This was a favorite with everyone here and we will be making it again.

I really liked this.  I would most definitely double or triple the sauce.  I cooked for 2 people and there was barely enough sauce and I followed the recipe exactly.  I bet mushrooms would be good in this also.
Very, very good ... easy to make. We cooked our chicken while sauteeing the onions & garlic.
Restaurant grade! Exceptional flavor and perfect consistency with pasta.  Really complimented the grilled chicken I added to the top, but would even go well with Veal Parmesean...
I have made this several times and love it. I never buy jar pasta sauce. I have added vodka to this sauce to make it a vodka sauce.
It was just ok.

I took the suggestion of another reviewer by adding a tsp. of Italian Seasoning to make up for the fact that I only had plain diced tomatoes. I must agree that this really only makes enough sauce for 3 entree sized servings, I will double next time. Really great flavor!
Tis is so good and easy to make. Doubled the recipe. Really tasty. Did recipe as is. You will miss out not trying this pasta sauce.
So easy and delicious.  I used 3/4 c. cream and added more quant. of herb.  I used about 2 TB of fresh basil.  Will make again and again....

Five star recipe as written when it comes to the flavor, but this recipe does result in a pasta sauce that is rather thin. The bf and I really enjoyed this one and I'll be making it often.  Thanks for the recipe!

I love it!! it was great easy recipe
I used fresh tomato instead of the caned one ,and brown sure instead of the white suger

This is the first pasta sauce I made from scratch... And it is amazing! Very easy to make. I only had half an onion, as it looked a lot bigger than usual. I make my own pasta from scratch, and now I have the perfect sauce to go with it.

My family loved this! When my toddler is asking for pasta, he's referring to this sauce over noodles! The only thing is I didn't have an onion on hand so I substituted onion powder, dried basil, and used already minced garlic instead of fresh. Again, what I had on hand. It still turned out awesome. I also doubled this recipe for we felt there just wasn't enough sauce and we wanted leftovers. Thanks so much for this recipe. This is definitely a delicious sauce we go for that takes so little time!

Quick and easy, also very good.  I did make a few additions: 1/3 cup roasted red peppers & 1/2 cup sliced mushrooms.  I didn't have any heavy cream, so I used 1/2 cup fat free half and half & 2 Tblsp. 1/3 fat cream cheese.  Will definitely make again and share the recipe with friends.

I'm not sure what I did wrong because I followed the recipe to a "T" but the sauce separated when I added the butter and cream and it wasn't very appealing looking.  Also, 1T of basil was WAAAAAY too much.  I should've trusted my instinct on that one.

I thought this was a great recipe!  I was looking for a way to use up some heavy whipping cream I had on hand and this worked out great and so easy and fast - black olives might be a nice addition to this sauce, but it's great as is.  Hubby liked it too!
Very good sauce. Especially when you're not quite feeling red or quite feeling white.
This was really good!  The only thing I did different was use fresh basil and fresh oregano.  I also used trecce del orto pasta. Delicious!!
reviewing this as I'm eating it. Excellent recipe. Diced my own tomatoes, used 3 cloves of garlic, skipped the butter, and used a hand blender at the end to make it creamy. so quick and easy!

Delicious recipe!! I added cubed chicken to the sauce.  Because of the chicken I had to increase all of the liquids. I added a little tomato paste, a pinch of flour to thicken the sauce, and some red pepper flakes to spice it up a bit.  It came out delicious! Everyone loves it!
I have made this sauce multiple times and it always turned out great! I always pair with pasta and panko crusted chicken.

Ill  definitely make it again. I used skim milk to reduce fat so I didn't get that creamy sauce as the picture shows (even after adding a little flour). Good but kinda bland at 1st. . I squeezed a whole lemon in the sauce and it made all the difference in the world. Even left the whole lemon sit in the sauce over night (in frig) and it was amazing!!!!

Super easy, Super yummy! Two thumbs up from hubby :-) The one thing I have to say is remove pan from the heat for at least 5 minutes before adding the cream. The first time I made this, I didn't take it off the heat long enough and the cream curdled when I added it.

Very, very delicious recipe!   And super easy.   The sauce was done before my pasta was finished.  For those who had found this to be too thin, be sure to do the step where you boil the liquid down off the tomatos, it will help the sauce not be runny.

Was very pleasantly surprised with this sauce. I followed to a tee (whipped up in the processor as one reviewer suggested), it was delicious over campanelle. It could be argued that it was a bit on the sweet side but not terribly. As another reviewer noted, this recipe would really suit 3 people rather than 5. Recommend it highly.
I doubled the recipe and blended it as suggested.  It tasted great and was easy to make.  My husband and four kids all gave it a thumbs-up so we'll be having it again soon.
I thought it was great, very tasty. My family suggested perhaps next time I could add some diced cooked Pancetta to the sauce with the butter and cream. I will try that.

I wanted something a little different and this really fit the bill. I didn't have diced tomatoes on hand so instead used tomato purée. Made the sauce a little thicker and there was no need to put it in the blender! Perfect consistency! I frankly like full fat in my meals (full flavor) so I put in both the cream and the butter. It was a family hit. Will definitely make it again!
We make this all the time and it's delicious.  The key is the tomatoes--the plain kind just don't cut it.

This was really good. However, the onion confused me.  It seemed like there was a lot of onion, and it made the sauce chunkier than I think cream sauces should be.  But then again, I'm really an amateur, so maybe I did something wrong? I mean...it's not like onions liquefy when you boil them in the sauce, right? Maybe I should try blending the whole thing before putting in the cream next time.  But it was really good.  Now I have way too much because there's just one of me! I used three cloves of garlic and put in a little bit of tarragon, and had it over gnocchi, which is basically the best pasta EVER.  It was very good. I might add a little chili oil next time.
This was a good tomato sauce, nothing special though.
This sauce is amazing! I follow the measurements loosely and it still turns out great!

There are only two of us, but I made this sauce for 6 servings (since a 14.5 oz can of diced tomatoes makes that amount) knowing if it was a good as the reviews that there'd be enough for use later in the week.  (Use the serving size calculator - very helpful)  Purchased chicken/cheese ravioli for use with this sauce and it was awesome...  Two nights later,  I gently reheated the sauce in the microwave, adding small amounts of leftover Heavy Cream to adjust refrigerated consistency.  This time paired with Ziti pasta.  (Raves were Equal to meal prepared earlier in the week from the Mrs..)  Next will try Linguine and perhaps add sliced mushrooms during the onion/garlic sautéing stage.  As my wife is a great fan of sauces that use tomatoes, she absolutely loved it and has asked for frequent inclusion in menu rotation.    BTW - with this sauce prepared ahead of time: Second meal prep time took 10 mins to boil the Ziti, you cannot beat that for a restaurant quality meal made at home.

Woww.. we were blown away by how good this is. I was craving a tomato cream sauce and this was better than I've ever tasted. I did follow another reviewers advice and put it the sauce in a blender to make it smooth and added some sweet italian sausage. MMMmmm...Thanks for the recipe!

This is similar to another recipe on this site:  Bow Ties w/ Sausage, Tomatoes and Cream.  While the other recipe is very good, I am not a huge meat (especially pork) eater and therefore this recipe is a good vegetarian option.  As with other reviewers, I added some additional veggies - in my case, mushrooms and red pepper strips.  I also added a full carton of cream (one cup rather than half a cup) just to ensure it got used up.  (Definitely more fattening, but I prefer that to waste!)  And I added an additional clove of garlic because my husband and I LOVE garlic.  Easy and flavourful, I'll be sure to put this one on the rotation.
Easy and tasty. I pureed as other reviewers suggested. Did not need flour as some other reviewers mentioned. Will DEFINITELY be making again!!
Not the most appetizing looking - but has a nice flavor. I would add more garlic next time.
One of my favorites recipes!! Love the sautéed garlic in olive oil.

This recipe was great. I sautéed the onions until they were soft then put the garlic in with the oregano salt sugar and pepper and let that cook for about a minute before I put in the tomatoes.  I also used 3 tablespoons of fresh basil instead of dried and put that in with the tomatoes. I will definitely make this again.

I made this for dinner last night after getting home from work, was looking for something quick and tasty and found this whilst at work. I used fresh tomatoes as I had them in the fridge with a little passata. Everything else I did the same just cut the recipe down a bit for 2 people. I didn't measure just added what felt right. This was lovely, fresh and tasty and made the house smell like I'd been cooking for hours it was gorgeous! And there were no complaints about a tomato cream sauce "I don't like tomato sauces" could have fooled me the plate was spotless nothing left at all. 30 min after walking in the door this was on the plates and shortly after it was gone. Will definately be making this one again. Thank you.

i've been searching for a tomato cream sauce that's like the one at my favorite restaurant. this looked promising & came close to my expectations. i followed the recipe exactly as written & had enough sauce to cover 3 servings of penne. fortunately, it was the right amount for what we needed. i suggest doubling this sauce to yield 5 healthy servings. note: be careful to only simmer & not boil your sauce after you stir in the heavy cream. thank you kimber!

I agree put less onions and more heavy cream.  I didn't have the Italian diced tomatoes so I just used regular diced tomatoes and it was still great.  I also added chicken and crushed red peppers and it was delicious.

"Mom, you can make this again. " To me,  that's the best compliment! I used low fat half and half instead of the cream.  I used an immersion  blender to smooth out the sauce.  Flavor was EXCELLENT! I grilled Italian sausage and garnished/placed one on the side for my teenaged boys. j
i followed this recipe exactly and it was really good! next time i make it, i might put it in the blender like others have suggested. either way, the flavor is great!

Excellent!  Made a few changes...added 8 oz. whipping cream, small can of tom. paste (with the oregano/spices), 2 TBSP of butter with all the org. ingredients, let sauce simmer for about 40 mins and.  We served it over penne pasta  and sauteed up some chicken-everyone liked it, including my very picky son!

Amazing! This was so good we made it two nights in a row.  I did make a couple changes - instead of using canned tomatoes, I diced two large vine tomatoes.  I also used garlic salt since I didn't have any garlic on hand, and threw in 2 chopped green onions.  The sauce turned out thick enough without any adjustments.  We also added cooked sweet Italian sausage and spinach the second time. Yum!
Yummy! My husband loves creamy marinara sauce and this one is really good. I'll make it again! Thanks so much for sharing!
A little thin. Will try to thicken it a little next time and add parmesan.

Such a great recipe!! The only changes I did was not to add the onions, garlic, and sugar. I did add a little bit of cooking white wine to the tomatoes, while they cook. The wine gives it a fresher taste, and my husband just loves it.

Simple, tasty and economical! I used half a medium onion and will definitely dice it the next time I make this meal. I used fat free half 'n half instead of the cream. My 3 year old loved it and my husband said I could make this every week and he'll eat it.
Even my son who doesn't like pasta very much liked this sauce.
Made this and used over tortellini, pretty mediocre,will not make again.Did not like the chunky mixture in cream.
Very good add mushrooms spinach sausage bacon
I added some white wine while sautéing the onions, and some Parmesan cheese, but it's a great base!
Excellent & Easy

Very delicious. I followed the recipe exactly except I doubled it & I used 1 cup of 18%table cream, 1/4 cup of butter & 2 tblsp of flour to thicken. Turned out great & didn't take away from the flavor. I also added mushrooms and diced chicken.  Will make this a regular dish when I want something different from a typical alfredo sauce.

Awesome!! Here are some additions to make it better.... 1 tablespoon FRESH (NOT DRIED) basil, mint and parsley, 1 full cup of heavy cream (instead of 1/2 a cup), 3 large garlic cloves MASHED and 2 tablespoons red wine. HOLY MOLY!!!!! WOW!!!!!

Very delicious!  The first time I made it as written and it was wonderful - not too thin at all when simmered as directed.  The second time I used a can of crushed tomatoes and substituted half and half for the heavy cream.  Equally delicious.  This was so quick and easy; I'll be making this often.
This was creamy and delicious. Left out the sugar and it was still wonderful.
The whole family loved this! Easy and super quick to prepare. Thanks!
I did not find this sauce to be anything special. I pureed it with a hand-held blender stick, and added more salt. It was okay but not great. Not sure if I'd make it again.
used minced onion and garlic powder, omitted olive oil.  Reg tomatoes with 1 tsp italian seasoning.  Omit salt and butter.
Delicious and easy.  My kids loved it

This is absolutely delicious, and so easy to put together. Even more so for me, as I used pre-minced garlic (a LOT more than was called for), and onion powder. Since so many reviews stated the sauce was thin, I did drain the tomatoes before adding. I  just brought all but the cream and butter to a boil, then cooked on medium for about 10 minutes to let the tomatoes simmer a bit longer for better flavor. I then reduced the heat, and added the cream and butter and cooked about 5 minutes as called for. I did not blend as others did, as I like little chunks of tomato. Sauce was a little bit thin, but not overly so once tossed with penne. The next day the consistency is perfect. Topped with shredded parmesan.
One of the few things that both my husband and I both really LOVE. Not overpowering, but very flavorful and delicious.

We loved this!  I served it over homemade fettucine pasta.  I added about a teaspoon of cayenne pepper, and used 3/4 cup half and half rather than whole cream.  I don't think it really makes 5 servings either, more like 3.  But we will make this recipe again!

Good and simple...a little too mild for our taste as written, but this is easily adaptable to accomodate for more heat or flavors, i.e. hot peppers, green peppers, cheese, etc. I also used fresh garden tomatoes rather than canned, so either will work. Great simple, basic recipe.

This was really easy and so cheap to make!  One recipe makes enough for 8 oz dry pasta, double it for a whole lb.  Like others, I pureed my sauce to make it smooth, but is also really good "chunky". I used half and half instead of cream (because that's what I had).  This sauce is also awesome as a base for a baked ziti - just sub ricotta for the cream, top with cheese and bake!  Here's a tip:  if you want to skip the pureeing step but like a smooth sauce, start out with a can of crushed tomatoes instead of diced.
This was good, took the advice of others and pureed the sauce....
This recipe has replaced the store-bought red sauce for me. Thanks!

LOVE this sauce. I made this cream sauce tonight, except I used 1 cup of Half & Half in place of the Heavy Cream then I pureed it in a blender and added another .5 cup of Half & Half brought it to a soft boil and served over Gnocchi. OUTSTANDING!!!

This just looked too easy to be any good but I had all the ingredients on hand so I gave it a whirl. I doubled the recipe, added a 6 oz can of tomato paste to thicken and subbed half and half for the cream  but followed the rest of the recipe to the letter. It started smelling amazing right away and only got better as it simmered. I doubt I will buy store sauce anymore. Thanks so much Kimber!!!
I doubled the garlic and added fresh parsley instead and it was delicious!  Plus I added chicken to it!
Made this today it was delicious
macaroni grill,watch out!!
Super Yummy

I love the tomato-cream sauce that is served at Carrabba's. I was hoping this would be just as good and it was. Carrabba's is still better but this was close. Really enjoyed this sauce. I did make a few tweaks because of taste preferences and ingredients that I had on hand. Amazing taste and very easy to prepare- used fresh tomatoes and herbs, flavor out of this world!
Very good!!!! I didn't use whip cream, I used fresh mozzarella instead, very smooth and creamy
This is much better with sundried tomatoes instead of the canned tomatoes. I very much dislike how canned tomatoes taste.
AMAZING!  But not so good reheated the next day.
I have been using this exact recipe for 6 years and it is always spot on perfect. Unless I get a little excited about the cream and add too much, but that's my own fault. It is spectacular !!!!

This is a great base for an amazing sauce. I made my own changes such as using twice as much garlic, adding celery with the garlic and onions, as well as adding some red wine and beer into the red sauce. It was really tasty and the entire family loved it. I used an immersion blender, so it would cling to the noodles more and so we could dip the garlic bread. Otherwise we stuck to the recipe and loved it!!

I made this tonight for dinner and I must say that this is one tasty dish.  I double the recipe for the sauce and added 7 cloves of garlic and 1 small sweet onion. i'll give it a five becasue it is so simple, easy, quick to make and my boyfriend loved it!. personally i thought it was kinda tangy but i'll try adding white wine next time.

this is a keeper.

My Independent Living class made this today - they loved it as well as the adults who were lucky enough to get some! We had Parmesan to sprinkle on top and I would definitely recommend adding it, Mozzarella would be good too.
great sauce! i added lobster to make a lobster cream sauce for raviolis !

This sauce is amazing & definitely my new favorite! Didn't have heavy cream si I substituted whole milk & it worked great. Poured this yummy stuff over angel hair pasta & topped with grated parmesan! Wow this is so easy too.
I loved this recipe!The only changes I made was I used two garlic gloves and puréed my sauce. I also topped mine with Parmesan cheese. Delicious!!

I tried this for the first time with company and was not disappointed! I looked for and couldn't find anyone else who had added peas, but I decided to add petite sweet green peas (frozen) and thought they were a nice touch. I was looking for a simple pasta sauce that was a little different.  This was a great recipe from which to start.  Since I didn't have enough basil, I added sweet marjoram to make up the difference. Thanks to Rachel for the idea about adding a thickening agent.  I didn't even think of that.

Any recipe that my kids will eat gets 5 *...I changed it up and used 3 med fresh tomatoes, chopped fine from the garden, a tablespoon of soya sauce, 1/4 cup wine, 3/4 half and half cream and fresh basil from the garden...the rest was the same...oh and a sprinkling of nutmeg and instead of olive oil I used olive oil I have garlic and rosemary sitting in and omitted the onion and garlic other than that and put garlic powder (as my kids won't eat a cooked onion). I really enjoyed this. I made sauce exactly as written and was very good. Since then i have made several times to suit my taste. It is excellent if you add chicken strips, peas or asparagus and lots and lots of garlic! YUM

This was a great pasta sauce for everyday dinners.  We made it with fat free half and half to cut calories, as well as, add a sprinkle of Wondra quick mixing flour while simmering to thicken it.  We were pleased with the flavor.  Also, it reheated great the next day for lunch!
I found this to be quite bland. Also, it was a very small amount of sauce. Maybe 2-3 servings, not 5.
This sauce is fabulous! I used it to make a baked cheese ziti, like Olive Gardens, only this was way better. Thanks

This took some tweaking, but I ended up with a very flavorful dish. I cooked the chicken separately (one pound of cubed chicken) in a little oil and 3/4 tsp salt, a generous amount of freshly cracked black pepper and about a tsp of garlic powder. I covered this and let it cook, stirring only occasionally. For the sauce, I doubled the amount of minced garlic, finely diced one onion and added 8 oz of sliced white mushrooms. Used about five ripe tomatoes for this. I added 3/4 tsp of salt and about 1/2 tsp freshly cracked black pepper. I let the tomatoes cook down and then took out the mushrooms; the remainder I pureed in the blender to get a smooth consistency (careful if you do this - it is very hot) and then put the puree back in the pot together with the mushrooms.  Added 1 1/2 tsp of Italian Seasoning, 1/2 tsp crushed red pepper flakes and 1/4 cup of chopped fresh basil to this. Don't forget the sugar - it will help cut the acid/tart taste of the tomatoes. At this point I added 1 cup of half and half and 2 tsp of cornstarch to thicken (since I didn't use the heavy cream). Chopped up the seasoned cooked chicken even further in the meantime and added it into the sauce. Served over penne pasta and it was delicious. Will definitely make this again.
love it! I added mushrooms cause I love mushrooms! some people say its too sweet but I like its level of sweetness, sometimes I even add a bit more sugar
SO GOOD. Added chicken, mushrooms, red peppers and put it over speghettini with fresh grated parm :)

Not too bad but not fantasic either. I was under-whelmed.

Delicious, served over mini penne pasta and shredded parmesan. Wish I had grilled chicken to go over top. One complaint: this really only made enough for 3 servings, no way 5 unless this was for a side dish. Thank you.

This was awesome! Only thing I did different was double the servings; and whisk a tablespoon of flour into sauce after butter & heavy cream. I served sauce over lump crab meat & noodles. My son said its one of the best things I've ever made!!! A keeper!
Great Sauce! The end result was a little too sweet for me, so I added another 1/4 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp pepper, and 1/2 tsp Italian seasoning to balance it out.

This was so delicious I almost ate the whole pan. The only difference was I only had a can of Fire Roasted Salsa Style tomatoes so I used that. It definitely gave it a kick, but I love spicy foods. Will make this again and again.
Very very good. I made it just as stated, though I doubled the recipe. Love it!
The grandsons loved it!  As other reviewers suggested, I used  my blender for a creamy sauce.  Definitely a keeper of a recipe - thank you Kimber.

Incredibly good and so easy to make!  I doubled the sauce and used half and half instead of cream. The only thing I added to thicken it was a 6 oz. can of tomato paste. I will make this again and again.  With recipes like this, there's no need to buy jarred sauces!
Really nice pasta sauce.  I pureed the sauce before adding the cream like many other reviewers suggested.
Added jar of medium salsa and jar of queso cheese dip, white wine,  no regular tomatoes.  Was yummy!

Thought this was the base for a very good sauce. I used tomato sauce instead of tomatoes since all the reviews stated that the chunks were gross. Omitted the sugar and oregano, I think the basil added enough sweetness.  I also added 2 small cooked diced chicken breasts and 1 teaspoon crushed red pepper although more could have been added. I poured it over rigatoni. Delicious! I know I altered the recipe quite a bit, but it's a good starting point to an even better sauce. I also think a few tablespoons vodka (making a vodka sauce) would be delicious! And use fat free half and half or regular whipping cream, heavy cream has way too much fat.
Yummy! Husband and I enjoyed.

I didn't make any changes to this recipe.. Contrary to what a lot of post said, I LOVED the chunky taste of the sauce, it was so different from all the other pasta sauce recipes. and a huge thank you to the person who posted about removing pan from heat before adding cream.. I am not a very experience cook and I am sure that saved  me.
Yummy!!!!! Made with whole wheat pasta, tasty and healthy!

This is a winner!  So easy and yummy!  I didn't have canned tomatoes so I used fresh grape tomatoes instead (their skins aren't tough like cherry tomatoes). I squashed them a bit once they were in the pan and then let them melt down while the sauce simmered.  It worked really well! I also didn't have heavy cream so I once again used what I had; some skim milk and a tablespoon of sour cream.  The sour cream added some nice tang.  I also added some dried italian seasoning and doubled the fresh garlic.  A few fresh basil leaves on top finished this off nicely.  Will make this again!  Thanks!
Fantastic! Don't change a thing! Goes great with Meatball Nirvana by lovestohost.

This was a good recipe. I didnt have everything on the list, so I used 5 fresh tomatos instead of canned, 2% milk instead of cream, an extra tsp. garlic, and double the salt and pepper. I also added 1/2 a tsp. of corn starch for a better thickness. I put this sauce on ravioli and topped with fresh basil and parmesan cheese. Easy and delicious. Tastes best hot!!:)

My husband is sometimes a picky eater, but let me just tell you he absolutely loves this!  The first time and every time after making this, I have used a Vidalia onion, partially because that's pretty much all we use.  I will have to try a "regular" yellow onion sometime just to see what the difference is. But the vidalias give it that much more sweetness to cut the amount of sugar added. I also use WAY more than one clove of garlic.  Ours is an Irish/Welsh household but you'd swear some weeks we were Italian!

I have a similar recipe & only made a few changes to this one. I used all of the following my homegrown: basil, oregano, parsely, tomatoes, & onion. I also add sausage to the sauce. I dumped pasta into a bowl & then the sauce & mixed together. Delicious!

Delicious and flexible! I didn't have cream, so I used 2% milk - cooked and reduced it by half - and it turned out wonderfully. I also love garlic, so after sauteing the onions a little I threw in 5 cloves of sliced garlic and cooked until soft. I didn't need more or less salt or spices. I served it over cheese tortellinis :) Yummmmm!

YUM!  I made this as directed with two minor exceptions. I doubled the entire recipe, but kept the onion at the single recipe quantity, and I used a large can of crushed tomatoes + 1 tsp Italian Seasoning as that was what I had on hand.  It turned out wonderfully.  Very yummy with chicken and using the crushed tomoates meant I did not need to hit it with an immersion blender to have a smoother consistency.  This will go into our rotation.  Thank you!
Extremely good!  I really, really liked this not only in taste but in ease to make.  Very suited to my palate.
Really really good! I added some sweet Italian sausage

So simple, and so good. I made a few alterations - like I used only and 8 oz. can of tomato sauce that cost about 50 cents.  I also used italian seasoning because i didnt have oregano.  No basil - but a little cilantro - which i couldn't really taste..
Delicious using fresh herbs.

This sauce wasn't much of a sauce--more like sautéed tomatoes and onion with cream over it. The flavor was okay but texturally was not great. I added 3 cloves of garlic and there still was no hint of garlic flavor. I also added Parmesan cheese at the end because I felt it was still lacking. And I didn't add the sugar because, do we really need sugar in everything these days? Blending it might help, but I still felt like it needed more depth of flavor.

The flavor of the dried herbs is too strong, and it needs more salt (I used fresh tomatoes) and for the sauce to be completely pureed.  I doubled the recipe to have enough sauce for 3/4 of a box of penne (but used just 1 onion, 4 medium-sized fresh tomatoes, 1 tsp garlic powder instead of fresh garlic, 1 T basil.  Everything else doubled.)

This was pretty good.  I doubled it and blended one of the cans of tomatoes.  Otherwise I followed the recipe pretty closely.  I put "some" butter in rather than measuring it and added six garlic cloves - that is the only variant.  I doubled it to toss with 5 mild sausages and 17 oz of pasta.  Pretty good.
Excellent and quick!
This is fantastic. Its kind of sweet so i add some red pepper flakes to it. I also throw some shrimp in at the last minute.  This is usually made twice during the monthly rotation.
loved the taste and easy to cook too...

My wife LOVES this, and asks me to make it regularly!

Even when I'm careless measuring, and substitute ingredients, it still comes out marvelous and she'll ask for it again.

I turned this recipe into a crock-pot dish with meatballs. It was a huge success at a pot-luck! Prepared as stated, only I didn't simmer off the liquid. Poured the whole thing into a crock, added pre-make/cooked meatballs and cooked til heated thru. Added cream and butter half hour before serving as I didn't know if the cream would curdle. It was fine!
Also, increased yield to serve 10.
I used what I had: mandarin orange, no lemon, ground cinnamon. It tasted good with a great aftertaste. Sweet and spicy!
This is very good! I did not simmer it for an hour though because all the alcohol would burn off.  Low for 10-15 minutes without it boiling still gives all the flavor.

I added the lemon extract, Candy Lady, thanks for adding that to the reviews (I was going to do that anyway, lol).  I frosted the top of a lemon pound cake and it was awesome.  I like the consistency of this frosting, it doesn't run yet it is firm enough for spreading.  I will definitely use this again with and without the pineapple juice.  In my opinion it's the right amount of each ingredient, for what I was looking for of course.  Thanks Candy Lady, after searching hours for a frosting I finally found something right for me.

I reduced the pineapple juice by about a tablespoon and added some pineapple puree. I made pineapple cupcakes with this frosting and a marichino cherry on top. It gave it a very "classic cupcake" look and tasted delicious. I made 24 of them and they were gone a day later. My family and friends gave so many compliments! Thanks for the recipe! I will be using it again! :)

Nice icing, very soft and spreadable...be careful!! Will spread more then expected if you don't watch it. I used this recipe to top lemon lime cupcakes. made a nice touch. Now will make this on some other cakes too.
This frosting was perfect.  It was not runny nor was it too thick.  Tasted really good.  Daughters loves it!!!!!!
I made to frost a pineapple cake and this was very good. I didn't want extra pineapple flavoring so I only used butter, cream cheese and a touch of vanilla extract  and it was perfect.

I made a 13 x 9 cake & knew as written it would be too much frosting, so  halved it. it came out nicely, a bit thicker than a glaze, but not one that could be swirled either. Which was fine w/me.   The only change I did was add a few drops of lemon extract to "brighten" the flavor. I used it on a carrot cake, to which I had added crushed pineapple. Very tasty together.

Pineapple was a great idea BUT I halved the butter and cheese, doubled the juice and kept adding sugar and beat/whipping the mixture in an electric mixer until I had a good consistency for a cake. Still tasted nicely of pineapple and was lighter than most cream cheese frostings. Used it on a  pineapple carrot cake and it was perfect. Think I will try it with other juices and matching cakes such as apple in the fall.
Given how much I changed, it hardly seems fair to review but the pineapple is such a great idea, maybe a high review will get others to try the idea.

For every pineapple lover out there.....this is THE recipe.  However, I did only add 2 C. powdered sugar along with 1/2 a can crushed pineapple (drained) and about 2-3 TBS. of the juice.   This is THE BEST EVER and I could have gotten a spoon and just pigged out!  Even better?  Coconut all over the cake....TRULY tropical.  THANKS for this simple yet so, so yummy recipe.  **by the way mine went on a smaller baked yellow cake with pineapple juice substituted for the water called for**
I forgot to add the 1 tsp lemon extract to this frosting
Good recipe for something just a little different.  Nice hint of flavor.

I use the juice from a can of crushed pineapple then I add some of the crushed pineapple.  This makes a wonderful textured frosting that EVERYONE will love!  I've used this recipe for years but this is the first time seeing it on Allrecipes.
Excellent!!  Didn't have lemon extract, so I used lemon juice instead, and it seems fine.  Makes a LOT of frosting, more than enough for a 9in layer cake.
This was very running and didn't have much flavor
I love this idea, I have used freeze dried fruit to flavor frostings with as well, it would add a lot more flavor than juice, and not thin the frosting as much...freeze dried strawberries is my fav.
Very easy to make and very tasty.  I used this on a pineapple cake (box).
Pretty good but very runny.  The pineapple is subtle in this recipe.  I would use it as a glaze (maybe a Jamaica Cake?) but definitely would not try to frost cupcakes with it again.
Oh good lord, yes! Make sure you sift!  And decorate with tidbits!
Yummy!  Doubled the pineapple juice!  Very faint flavor!
i would give this 6 stars out of 5 if i could. I dream about this dish every single night. My fantasies can never be pleased. I need this dish...

This couldn't be simpler. I even screwed up and added the pineapple juice last (rushing) and it still turned out great. I did NOT add lemon extract as suggested in the reviews. The pineapple flavor came through nicely without it. I halved the recipe and used this on Zucchini Cake II by Joan.  Thanks for a simply delicious recipe!

I made this to top Sam's Famous carrot cake which had pineapple in it.  The frosting had the perfect amount of sweetness and a subtle cream cheese flavor.  I really liked the pineapple kick.  Just wish it was even more pineapple-y!

This icing was so easy and quick to make. I didn't need the entire recipe as I just wanted to more or less drizzle on the Bundt cake. So I halved the recipe but added the entire 8 oz of Cream Cheese. I wanted a cream cheesy taste and I also added 4 TBLSP of Lemon Juice to cut back on the sweetness as I didn't have Lemon Extract on hand. It was the right consistency for drizzling, not too thin and not too thick and after I drizzled it on the cake, I added some crushed pineapple to give it some color. The flavor was just wonderful, not too sweet and not too pineappley.By the way, the cake itself, was Carrot Cake IV submitted by Cookie and the cake was superb also. I will use this frosting again.l
With pineapple mermelade and a little confectioners sugar perfect for cupcakes!
Great, simple, easy.......tasty !
You're going to need more orange juice! I did 1 cup confectioner's, about 1/2 teaspoon zest and 3 tablespoons juice.
perfect! Don't let anyone say differently!
Great drizzled on Angle food cake.

this glaze was used in a cake from this site called too much chocolate cake...(LOL No such thing as too much chocolate).Any way the combination of chocolate and orange flavors goes wayyyyyy back and this was a perfect topping. many have asked for this recipie and I always steer them here. Will make this again...and again...and again!
wow too good and easy.
Very good!!!! I used 3 tablespoons fresh "red" orange juice..used it to glaze a carrot cake,I prefer this to cream cheese frosting!!!
very easy and took the advice of Alia_26 and added the butter. thanks
This is such a simple, yet delicious glaze. Although I had to add more juice to make it, it was still a great recipe.
Yummy! I used tangerine juice instead of orange, and drizzled it over cranberry orange biscotti. Delicious!
Yummy! Followed and enjoyed! =)
I use it to put a filling in my cupcakes! Huge hit!
Quick and delicious!
sounded good, but failed to make a good impression on some good cookies.

This recipe is so easy and fast and it tastes good. 
Can't wait to put this glaze on my doughnuts.

Refreshing flavor! I added a bit of butter to make it a bit more creamy, and put it into a ziploc bag to pipe it on cranberry orange scones (from "simple scones" recipe on this site). Tomorrow, I'll be serving these to my daughter at breakfast...I already know she's gonna flip for 'em! :-)

Great easy recipe to have on hand.  I like a strong orange kick, so I added 1/2 teaspoon of finely grated rind.  Ended up having to add 2 tablespoons of orange juice.  Goes well on cranberry orange nut bread.
Matched with scones, this is perfect. I used 1 1/2 tbsp off juice instead to make it spread easier.
I put this icing over orange bread on this site, taste like they both would make good sweet rolls. Like cinnamon roll very good together.

The name of this recipe says it all--it's a simple, fresh orange glaze.  I made this to go on Big Soft Ginger Cookies (also on this site), and the combination was wonderful.  I had to use a bit more orange juice to get the right consistency for drizzling on cookies, but the results were perfect.  This is a nice glaze to have on hand for a variety of uses.
Perfect! I needed more liquid so I just added some water, and this did not seem to dull down the orange flavor at all. Thanks so much for sharing.

Just made this to go on Cranberry Scones from this site. Found this glaze to have a real orange kick, more so than I'd expect from one made with orange juice concentrate. Perfect sweetness to help the scones with their slight baking soda aftertaste.

Super simple like it says. Never made a citrus glaze before and wow! I will be making a lot more. I used blood oranges and also a tablespoon butter. Waited till my mandarin coffee cake from a box was almost completely cool. Spread it over the top of the 8x8 cake and got rave reviews!
I added about 4 tablespoons of fresh orange juice and 1/4 teaspoon more of orange zest. I used this to cover a Martha Stewart's orange yogurt cake and it was amazing!
This glaze was perfect on top of the butter snowflake cookies I baked.  It's very citrusy, which I love.  I had to use about 4 Tbsp of orange juice instead of 1, but it came out great.
The powder sugar came through a little too strongly for my taste, maybe a bit of butter as other reviewers suggested would help. Still tasty and hardened nicely!
Thanks, didn't have any zest, but good none the less. Used it on gingerbread Bundt cake.
Outstanding and perfect topper for pumpkin bread and cookies.  I too added the tbsp of butter and it hardens to a nice shiny glaze that tastes fresh.  Great simple recipe.  Thanks for sharing.

This Orange Glaze recipe is very good, very easy. I did add a tablespoon of melted butter to rid the chalky under tones as did ALIA_26. That made a huge difference! I used two tablespoons of orange juice and for added flavor - almost a tablespoon of grated orange rind.  I made an Orange Bundt Cake and everyone loved it! Thanks!

I had to add 2 extra tablespoons of oj to make it into a glaze. I also added more zest for it to have flavor. It did have a chalky taste. I'm sorry I didn't read the reviews before I made it and add butter. What I did was add a couple drops of orange extract to overcome that taste and it was good after that.

Delicious....an easy and very fresh way to dress up a cake. I used this on Buttermilk Pound Cake II from this site...the orange was a nice citrus compliment to the lemon flavor of the cake. Thanks for the recipe!

I have used this sooo many times.... and it is perfect.  Adjust the sugar or juice to make it as thin or thick as needed.  This time I replaced the orange zest and juice with lemon.  I have also done lime. Love it! Thanks for sharing!
A very flavorful glaze.  I followed other reviewer's advice and added a bit more juice.  This was great on the Beat and Bake Orange Cake on this site.  I'll use this again - on chocolate next?

Very simple and fresh tasting. I did add about a tablespoon of melted butter only because powdered sugar can have a chalky-like under tone with too few ingredients. This was perfect as a glaze over a deep chocolate cake.

The recipe is on to something but it needs work: The addition of butter is critical since without it the glaze lacks body. Plus, as stated above, much more juice is needed to achieve a glaze consistency.

I made this to put on cranberry pecan scones I made.  Worked great. I added a little bit more Orange Juice to flavor it more and thin it to me he right consistency. I wanted it thin enough to put on hot scones so it would run over and down the sides. It was perfect. And tasted just right.
4 stars as written.  I needed a bit more juice but, more importantly, the addition of just a little melted butter to reduce the chalkiness makes it 5 stars.

This glaze was wonderful. I used it for the Cranberry Nut Bread I on this site, great combination. I liked the glaze very much and would use it again for other things like cookies or breakfast rolls. Thanks so much!
Quick and easy ... I let it harden on my pumpkin cookies ... fun and they were a hit!

This is really good for a simple orange glaze - and it's all fresh and super easy to make! I ended up needing considerably more orange juice also, a little less than the juice from half of the orange I was using, to get the drizzly consistency I was looking for. But this was awesome!

I love how uber easy this recipe was to make and a great compliment to my cranberry-orange muffins!!! I will say 1tbsp of OJ is not enough, but it's such a good starting point to gage your preferred consistency. I used approx 2 1/2 tbsps of OJ, and was PERFECT! As it glided down the muffin top, it began to stiffen and left a beautifully glazed muffin. Though after seeing the results, I was disappointed I did not have scones on hand to glaze. I'll DEFINITELY be using this recipe again.
This is really yummy!!  I've had it on vanilla ice cream and loved it.  I could imagine putting it on waffles too.

Delish!

I probably had more rhubarb than the recipe called for -- in fact, I doubled the recipe, at the very least, and doubled the ingredients, but believe I had quite a bit more than twice the rhubarb.  Anyway, it is very tart and very delicious.  A great way for a single person to use up her rhubarb instead of a fattening pie.  

I also made homemade granola and so for breakfast I had the sauce with granola.  Tomorrow, going to pick up some vanilla low fat yogurt and make parfaits!

I added vanilla at the end of cooking as suggested by other reviews... vanilla makes any dessert sauce better!  A delicious (and quick!) spring dessert served over angel food cake with a whipped cream garnish...
Holy Sour, Batman! and no butter- rhubarb sauce doesn't have butter.  Added food coloring as my mother always did and doctored it with more sugar.

Great recipe!  My garden produced an overabundance of rhubarb this year.  Usually, I make strawberry rhubarb pie and strawberry rhubarb jam, but I had an angel food cake on hand and decided on the rhubarb sauce.  After reading the reviews, I decided to use a cup of bing cherries I also had on hand and a dash of red food coloring; I also added a bit of vanilla extract.  My mother used to make Rhubarb Sauce every summer, and it brought back memories.  I'm going to freeze the extra sauce for use throughout the year.
This is so delicious I could eat it by itself. But it's amazing over ice cream too. I followed the recipe except added some vanilla. Fantastic!
This recipe is awesome.  We love it over low-fat Vanilla ice cream.  I even us a little less sugar.

AWESOME!!!!! I haven't had rhubarb sauce since I was a kid and boy does this taste great.  My son is in love with this sauce.  The only change I made was I added a little more sugar and when it was done cooking, I added a little vanilla.  Great recipe.

As our family likes sauce to be pourable, I added 2T water per 4 cups rhubarb. Also added a splash of vanilla. Don't skimp on the butter...it makes it more sauce like. Great recipe! Just like my grandma used to make! Thanks!
I haven’t enjoyed Strawberry Rhubarb sauce in years. Tastes just like I remember. I didn’t change a thing. Will make this again! I used frozen rhubarb from my garden - turned out great!

I made this but would have preferred it be sweeter.  I will add strawberries next time.  Also, I took the advice given about not cutting fine because it will cook down.  I cut to 2-inch pieces.  Yes, it does cook down, but then it is more stringy, so I will chop it more fine next time. Just thought I'd share this for others.

SOOO good! I added about a cup of frozen cherries, used brown sugar instead of white, added a good pinch of cinnamon, and  about a a teaspoon of vanilla as it was cooling.  My son loved it on toast and I loved it with plain Greek yogurt.

Just made 2 batches.  Wonderful.  You could leave the butter out. But, usually it helps to eliminate the foam you get from cooking it down. so, I only used maybe a couple of teaspoons.  Was a nice consistency and flavor is super.
Have made for years tried less butter and added a little water, vanilla,  sugar, and cinnamon red hots (imperials). That way the candy gave the red color without using red food coloring.  Very good!
adjustments: used red currants a few tablespoons water corn starch to thicken  great w/ pancakes!
All of the recipes are wonderful…..checking out the rhubarb recipes tonite.
Very good!  Added in some ginger and used it on top of pumpkin pancakes.

I goofed it up and it still worked!  I'm generally pretty good at reading directions, but I threw everything in the pot and then read them!  It's ok, the rhubarb softened up and disintegrated as it was supposed to.  I love almond, so I threw a bit of almond extract in there.  Also, it makes it more appetizing if you throw a couple of drops of red food coloring in.  Delicious!
Yummy!  Can be made with less butter and sugar for the health-concious:)  Also don't worry too much about cutting the rhubarb - it will just boil down:)
I just tried this recipe and it is wonderful... the hubby approved too. I served it on top of vanilla ice cream
I loved this basic recipe. I added a 1/2 cup brown sugar and 1/8 of a cup of orange jucie and simmered until thick. Everyone loved it.

This was exactly what I was looking for,  my husband just wanted rhubarb.  Put over a little ice cream and it was GREAT.  Didn't serve 8 as it claimed, just enough for a couple nights dessert for the two of us.  Or maybe we were just being piggy.
Tasty!
This is such an amazing sauce for how easy it is to make. This is a great way to use rhubarb.
Just made it as is. Really good mixed in with my morning oatmeal!
Very good. Made as written. Next time will add tapioca to thicken and add flavor and thicken it up a bit.

I had never EVER cooked rhubarb before...but it was always in the house when I was growing up.  I'm not a huge fan, so I grated up a few gala apples (peel on) and what a lovely sweet/tart sauce!  Thanks!

This sauce was wonderful.  My husband really loved it.  It is great on homemade biscuits, toast or pound cake.  I also substituted a cup of cranberries for the rhubard and added a splash of vanilla at the end of cooking.
I randomly made this for a big waffle brunch we were hosting. We had over 40 people and many of them raved about the rhubarb "paste." I agree it was good!
I left out the butter, cooked down the rhubarb in a small bit of water. I made a bit bigger portion, 2.2lbs of rhubarb, 3/4 cup sugar.  Very nice. Thanks!
Awesome recipe!!  I grew up with rhubarb, but had never had sauce until tonight.  WOW!!  I could eat the entire batch!  I added a tiny bit of vanilla as other reviewers suggested.  Perfect!

Because of the previous reviewers' suggestion, I also put a squirt of vanilla in at the end.  In addition, I used 1/3 cup brown sugar instead of the white, and added a dash of cinnamon.  I also have made this substituting a cup of frozen cranberries for a cup of the rhubarb.  Yummmm!!!!!
I made this exactly as written; perfect sweet-tart blend. Used a mandolin to slice it thin, but may just rough chop it next time.

At $5.99 a pound all I could do was pray this was going to be good.It is fantastic..
Going to serve it with pork chops.
I tried this on pancakes, instead of maple syrup. I loved it!

This was really good.  Instead of butter, I just boiled a little water before adding the rhubarb!  We ate this on icecream and toast and it is delicious!  What is so great about it is that it's not too sweet!
Yum!  Added 1/4 tsp vanilla-great flavor
Substituted 1/2 of the rhubarb with frozen strawberries (because I was short on rhubarb).  Delicious recipe.  So good, I was cleaning out the skillet with a piece of bread.
Very good!
Easy but very tasty.  Added thinly sliced strawberries.

I made it and love it!  The changes I made were

8 cups of  2. Inch cut rhubarb
1/2 cup white sugar (yes for the 8 cups)
1/2 cut and scraped vanilla bean and bean.
1/2 cup unsalted butter.
I put it all in a big pot together and cooked over med-high heat for 12  minutes!
Excellent!

I was going to make a rhubarb pie for an elderly couple I take care of, however I discovered I only had brown sugar, and not enough butter! This recipe came to the rescue. It's SO good! Since it takes only a few minutes, I plan to make it often. I did add a bit of cinnamon and a touch of vanilla at the end, as suggested by others. To get a nice blush, I would have preferred to use berries, but didn't have any on hand. I "cheated" with red sugar from my cookie-decorating supplies. Just a few shakes, and the sauce blushed up nicely. Great, simple, tasty recipe!
Fantastic!
I love dis recipe but not my favourite!! I tried making it. My mum was da 1st 1 2 try it. She loved it so she asked me 2 bake it again!! Thanx Michele!!

Like rhubarb but rarely cook it due to need of lots of sugar.  With this recipe you can fell almost guilt free if you don't think about the butter. I will discontinue giving away rhubarb from my garden!
Made it just as the recipe stated.  Tasted wonderful!
I added about 1/4 cup more sugar and a tsp of vanilla, came out wonderful, eating it as I type! this made about 3 half pints.
Delicious in plain yogurt
This is very simple and yummy!!
This is really easy to make and I added strawberries too--I meant to serve it with yogurt or over ice cream but ended up spreading a lot on toast and it was really good!

The amount of sugar is about right, but I note that you don't need the butter, just cover the bottom of the pan with water, bring to a boil then cover and lower to a simmer for about 15-20 minutes. No need to stir.
Unlike other reviewers I didn't change a thing and it was PERFECT.  Tart and tangy.  And ideal with plain yogurt.
Real good!  Jam next.

I used this as a starting point.  Skipped the butter.  Used about 5 cups rhubarb, Splenda instead of sugar, and  a scant 1/2 C. water.  Simmered in a saucepan until all rhubarb was sauce consistency.   A real winner the way I made it.  Going to eat it as is, and top plain yogurt and oatmeal with the rest.  Will be making more tomorrow as it won't last!!!
I also added vanilla and an extra 1/2 c. sugar. Delicious!!!

This recipe is very tasty and so easy!  I also used 3 cups rhubarb and one cup frozen strawberries. Then reduced the sugar to 1/3 cup.  I used an immersion blender to make the mixture nice and smooth.

When I was young my aunt made delicious rhubarb jam.  I haven't had any for about 30 years so I bought some frozen rhubarb yesterday and found this recipe to try.  I love it!  Next I'm going to try it with fresh rhubarb, which I'm sure will be even better.  Thank you for such a simple, delicious recipe.
I like the addition of butter in this recipe.  Four cups of rhubarb is about 6 good-sized stalks.  Slice fresh rhubarb quickly and easily with a Mandoline Slicer.  Can also be cooked in a solar oven.
Very tastey!  I also added vanilla to the sauce and served it with a cream cheese pound cake.  Yummy!

This was wonderful! I rated it only 4 stars because I made several changes. I used a heaping 1/3 cup brown sugar and added some cinnamon and vanilla at the end. I also added some red food color since my rhubarb was pretty green. Delicious on angel food cake with whipped cream.
Very (very) fast and easy! We love it served with vanilla ice cream or just a bit of cream. Excellent either hot or cold--my go-to recipe for using up rhubarb!
Simple, terrific tasting and a seasonal delight.

SKIP THE BUTTER YOU DON'T NEED IT!  Used a little more than 4 cups rhubarb, and substituted splenda for the sugar (cut the calories down by like 800 or 900 calories!) My mom used to make a jello salad like this one that my husband tolerates so I was on the hunt for a better recipe.  I followed this recipe to the letter and it was waaaaay to sweet for me (all I could taste was sweetness!) and too much topping for my husband.  I decided to combine my mom's salad and this salad and I came up with, to me and my family, the perfect recipe.  Here's what I did:

Make the raspberry jello as the package instructs using the hot and cold water.  Add the crushed pineapple and about 2 cups thawed frozen blueberries.  (Note: the pineapple needs to be REALLY drained otherwise your jello won't set.  I mash mine through a metal strainer with a spoon.)  Put the jello/fruit in the fridge until set.  I didn't change the topping ingredients except to cut the volume in half.  Spread the topping over the set jello and chill until served.

We could taste the fruits in this version without being overpowered by sweetness.  Hope this helps someone!

The times I make two pies, I put the unused jello in a individual sized teddybear pan, so my toddlers can have a snack later w/o the fattening cream cheese mixture.  They love it!!  Anyway, I filled w/enough cream cheese topping to cover the bottom & sides of the pre-made crust. ...waited about 5-10 min. for the jello to cool from boiling (necessary), and then placed it on top until it reached the rim of the crust.  Be sure you're still able to carry it to the fridge w/o the blueberry mixture spilling over ...making the crust look not as presentable (speaking from experience). lol  The next morning, the texture was so nice, and there was a beautiful layer of cream cheese on the bottom.  Plenty of extra that I put in a Tupperware for those piggy's in my family to add more on top if they wanted.  I am always thrilled to show off this recipe, so thanks for the user who published it! Coated the bottom with sour cream/sauce mixture, laid down a layer of corn tortillas, then spinach, chicken, beans, rest of sour cream/sauce mixture, cheese (Mexican-style shredded 4 cheese blend), then more tortillas, sauce and cheese. These are yummy! You don't need to put the corn tortillas in hot oil in order to roll them. Just wrap in a barely damp paper towel and heat in the microwave till fairly warm. They will roll right up with no tearing.

I admire your use of "light" sour cream, but an even better choice, if you can find it, is "crema," a thin Mexican sour cream you can make yourself by putting yogurt culture (a tablespoon of plain will do) into milk and letting it sit for a few hours.  Also, as one of the reviewers complains that the corn tortillas tear and are hard to work with, I suggest that you "prep" the tortiallas in the traditional Mexican way: dip each one at a time into hot oil (canola is OK, though Mexicans would use lard), but only for a second or two, using tongs to dip in and out.  Then let them drain a bit on a cookie sheet covered with paper towels.  Another thing I admire is your use of *corn* tortillas, since no self-respecting Mexican -- or Texican for that matter -- would use flour tortillas.  These were introduced into the Mexican diet only recently and nobody down there uses them for enchiladas.  The very idea is totally abhorrent!

I love these and everyone at my party ate them up.  I used Trader Joes jarred Salsa Verde because that is my favorite salsa.  It was so good and so easy to make.

I have never reviewed a recipe but I couldn't pass up the opportunity this time.  This was sooooo good.  My dad and husband are huge meat eaters and they LOVED it. I will definitely be making this again.  The only change I made was layering it to make it easier.  I will probably add mushrooms and onions to it next time but it was great with out changes too!
The ingredients sounded great - but the tortillas  break apart -when you roll them -corn tortillas have to be softened in a sauce before you roll them -

I haven't tried this, but sound delicious.  I had trouble with corn tortillas & used to use the oil fry method, but am now married to a Latin.  After all these years & the extra calories all you have to do is put them over a hot burner & turn them until their warm...flexible & easy to work with...no more broken tortillas....

I have made this several times now and always add chicken. I also saute the spinach with garlic, olive oil & onion & season with salt & pepper before stuffing the enchiladas. 
I made this recipe Saturday evening, it was quick & turned out wonderful! The only thing I added was some shredded honey jalapeno rotisserie chicken I got from my local grocery store. I will say the flavor of the chicken added a wonderful touch to the dish. It tastes even better leftover - I have been eating it all week!
Loved it!  I did make more of the sauce (green salsa/sour cream combo)to pur over the top..Yum!

A simple dish that makes a surprisingly impressive weeknight meal!  I used both monterey jack and pepperjack cheeses and baked these seam side down in the baking dish (instead of messing with toothpicks).  I did use flour tortillas per our preferences.  This was on the table in 35 minutes and only required three dishes, 2 baking pans and 1 bowl, to prepare.  It doesn't get much easier than that!
Wonderful!  I made it for the first time and layered everything, kinda like a lasagna....so fast, easy and yummy.  I made it for a potluck.  Rave reviews.
Addes sauted onions a cumin.  Loved it!
This is how I make my enchiladas- so yummy! The only difference between this one and mine is that we use cheddar/jack mix and I actually buy the green enchilada sauce :) YUMMY!

Loved this recipe. To save time, I followed the advice of reviewers who layered the ingredients to make a casserole. I also added shredded chicken and black beans to my spinach and sour cream mixture. I cooked the shredded chicken by throwing a few boneless skinless chicken breasts in the crock pot with a little salsa and taco seasoning. It was ready to shred by the time I got home from work. We will be making this again!
I used quite a but more sauce than it called for. Slightly heated the tortillas (covered with wet paper towel) in microwave so they wouldn't break when rolling up. Delicious.

We loved these! I tried them out on some guests and they too were very impressed. Not to mention, I took them to work the next day and everyone was so impressed simply with the smell and I ended up emailing the recipe to the entire staff of the elementary school. Definitely a winner!
This was great with salsa verde from Trader Joe's and some mushrooms and peppers in the filling. Thanks for the simple recipe!
This was a great start!  I added black beans, corn & ground chicken.  I added some cumin & Mexican oregano.  It was good when i made it but so much better the next day.  Thank you for a great recipe!

Quick, easy and authentic. I used a tomatillo green salsa. This leans a little toward the tart side, but a little salt cuts this nicely. My only other thought would be to blanch or saute the spinach (go easy on the butter/oil) so you can fit more inside the tortillas.

This is really yummy.  I followed others' advice and sauteed onions, mushrooms, and frozen white corn.  I sprayed with non stick spray and layered corn tortillas, spread on some salsa/sour cream mix, spread some spinach, then the sauteed veggies and 1/2 of the cheese.  Made another layer of everything, ending with the cheese and baked.  Total winner, my two teenagers liked it and my husband said it was delicious.  Will certainly make again!

Great recipe. It has endless possibilities for anyone's taste preferences. I have been making enchiladas for years, so I added a few changes. I was taught by my Latin friend who learned it from her mom in Mexico that you are always suppose to cook the tortillas in a little bit of hot oil before filling them. The tortillas need to be soft before filling. I added shredded chicken, chopped zucchini, corn, and green chilies to my filling. I also added Mexican shredded cheese from Trader Joe's to the filling. My family really likes the cheese blend. It turned out great.

This was very good. Having said that, I did make some modifications. I created my own spinach filling - see below:  Spinach Filling:  10 oz package frozen spinach 4 tablespoons butter 1/4 finely chopped onion 2 cloves garlic, minced 1/3 cup heavy cream 1/4 teaspoon nutmeg Salt and pepper to taste To make spinach filling, cook spinach as directed on package. When the spinach is cooked, press to get all the liquid out. Melt butter in a skillet. Saute onion and garlic until soft. Add spinach and cook until all the butter is absorbed, about 4 to 5 minutes. Add heavy cream. Add nutmeg and salt and pepper to taste.   After that, I pretty much followed the recipe as written. I used tomatillo salsa which really gave it a very mild spice. The mix of salsa and sour cream was great - I had some left over and used it as a dip for chips. Also, I used homestyle (thick) corn tortillas and softened them in oil before pulling in the filling. All in all, a great recipe - will make again!
