Every restaurant I visit, I get extra honey mustard (to take home) because I never knew how to make it.  This is the PERFECT honey mustard, for all of you honey mustard lovers out there.  TGIF couldn't have done it better!  Thanks!
Thanks for this recipe! I used it to make dressing for the first time! I only used half of the lemon juice, though, as the first sample was too tart for my tastes. Wife loved it!
Easy and simple, just as a dressing should be!  I also used vinegar instead of lemon juice and it  was lovely.

I am not a fan of Honey Mustard dressing, but I even liked this recipe.  It is perfect for dipping chicken fingers.  I did decrease the mayo a little because I do not care for dressings with a strong mayo taste.

This was absolutely delicious.  I prepared this as written and found it was a little thick for a salad dressing (which is what I wanted it for), perfect for dipping.  So to thin I added about a tablespoon of apple cider vinegar, and a drizzle of water.  I also added a pinch of garlic powder, and S & P to taste.  So easy and good.  Thanks for sharing this recipe.
This recipe is super easy and tastes great! Tastes just as good, if not better, than the bottled dressing.  I tried it with regular mustard and dijon mustard and both tasted great.
This recipe was so easy and so good.  I used fat free mayo instead of regular mayo for a no-fat, low cal dressing and veggie dip.  Its now my favorite!
This was a very easy and tasty honey mustard for a salad or dipping sauce. I won't be buying store bought ever again.
Yummy!!
Thanks so much for this recipe!  It tastes great and it's really easy & fast to make.
i just eyeballed the measurements (and probably added double the honey) but it came out great!

WOW WHAT A TRIP!!  I HAD NO IDEA THE FLAVOR WOULD BE SO GREAT WITH JUST FOUR INGREDIENTS.  I used dijon mustard and light mayo and it was just fab.  I will never buy the store stuff ever again!  I put this on a wedge of lettace with carrots, mushrooms, cucumber and green peppers for my hubbys lunch.  I will see what he thinks when he eats it tomorrow.  My kids tried and they really liked it ***EDIT** I MADE THIS WITH THE PREPARED MUSTARD AND DID NOT THINK IT WAS NEAR AS GOOD AS WITH DIJON MUSTARD
Very good!  I made this last night and used Dijon mustard.  I served it on a ham and swiss bagel sandwich.  Loved it!
Easy and delicious.  We used it with chicken fingers and it was perfect.
I think a lil less mayo would be better but I still liked it on my fried pork chops!
I'm not a huge fan of mustard so next time I will cut that in half. But other than that this dressing tasted great on my chicken salad thanks.
Better than my other honey mustard dressing! I use this for a warm cabbage, mushroom, bacon and blue cheese salad. Yum!

Absolutely fabulous!  I swapped lime juice for the lemon juice and added just a spoonful for light mayo becasue I wanted to save a few calories.  Actually, I eyeballed all the measurements and it was fantastic!  Definitely a keeper ... and SO easy!!!
Yummy and simple!!!
This was wonderful and easy.  Perfect on a breaded chicken salad.  Yummy!! I will never buy honey mustard again.

WOW! I love this recipe. The only thing I changed was that I added maybe a teaspoon extra of mustard and honey, but that was it. This dressing is amazing! I have a hard time judging mayonnaise in recipes for some reason lol and I found that the proportions in this dressing are perfect!! Thank you so much for sharing this. I'm going to make this from now on! Very easy and simple.

Awesome dressing.  Only had about 1/8 cup of mayo left, so subbed non-fat plain Greek yogurt instead.  Very tasty!  Used 1/2 regular yellow mustard and 1/2 Dijon.  Thanks for a quick delicious dressing!
This is the best honey mustard dressing that I have ever made and tasted!  It goes well with almost any kind of salad.  I think this recipe is better than a store-bought dressing or in a restaurant.

This is so terrific! I have been searching in stores for the perfect "restaraunt-style" Honey Mustard dressing recipe to no avail--but this dressing is exactly what I've been after. :o) I played around with it a bit and found that using fat free mayo is just as yummy! Thanks for sharing!

This dressing is awesome. Perfect as is or add a little pepper. We live in Japan where a good dressing is hard to find. I served it as a dip with some chicken fingers and my husband loved it, just like we remember from our favorite restaurant back home.
Made this using brown mustard and plain yogurt in place of mayo (happened to be what we had on hand)... definitely making this one again. Anything to get the hubs to eat salad.
This is an awesome recipe!  Sooo easy and sooo GOOD! Thanks for sharing!

This honey mustard dressing is really really good.  I made it 2x's now with dijon mustard...love it.   I used it on baked chicken breast as well as on salads.  I also used it as a spread on a turkey sandwich.   There are many ways to use this dressing.  I even think it could make great potato salad.
pretty good, it wasn't the greatest but it was good
This is a great recipe! I add a little more honey, but overall it's all tasty.
Used 1/4 cup light mayo and 1/4 cup lowfat plain yogurt and doubled the remaining ingredients. Low cal and delicious!
I didn't have lemon, subbed apple cider vinegar. It was awesome, a great acid balancer.

Easy & breezy - done in 5 minutes or less.  I made this last night to marinate my homemade chicken fingers in replacement for egg wash and flour before I breaded them in panko.  I also made a separate dish of this for dipping.  This was awesome.  My picky 19 month old son shook his head (from the zing) and then began devouring it.  I will definitely be making a bigger batch to keep on hand.  Thank you Mary Ann for submitting this recipe.
Perfect!  Exactly what I was looking for. Did sub lime juice for lemon as I was out.  Delicious :)
Excellent!!  I added a little more honey and mustard to give it a little stronger flavoring.
Perfect.  I didn't change a thing.  We used this for dipping sauce with chicken fried chicken from this site.  Wonderful dinner.
SUPER FANTASTIC - no changes.  My son, who HATES mustard or anything like it, says this is better than Ranch!  I wish I could give it more than 5 stars!

Great stuff, I needed some honey mustard to use a spread to put on some mini Ham and Swiss cheese croissants for a potluck and it was perfect. I used low-cal "whipped dressing" (Miracle Whip), instead of mayo and it tastes just right!

THis was excellent!  Followed the recipe exactly and hubby loved it!  I can use this now instead of the store bought stuff with things I cannot read in there.  Hubby said it taste's better than any store bought or restaurant stuff!  GREAT dressing!  Thank you Mary Ann for sharing!!!

My daughter and I love honey mustard on just about everything, we always ask for extra at fast food to keep in fridge, as  we dont like ANY of the ones in the grocery store.  We can now have it anytime we want! Only personal adjustment: I add a little squeeze more honey and use dijon mustard. We us it as a dip or spread,  and for salad I add a few drops of red wine vinegar to the mix (Awesome!)
Love!!! Very basic, but pleasant. Just like the honey mustard you'll find at most all-American restaurants. So if you prefer the Dijon-style honey mustard, this is not the one for you.
I'm not a sweet-dressing fan, but my husband's teenage daughter is and this was a hit with her.
I will totally make this again. I used canola mayonnaise and a dark honey. Very good!

Was very tasty!  I liked it a lot, although next time I will make it with Dijon to see what that does to the flavor- I felt it was yummy, but will look for whatever it is that I want to give it a bit more depth- will try adding some spices as other reviewers have tried to see if that beefs up the flavor.  Thanks for the recipe, I'm not a sweet dressing lover tho the bf is- he loved it and you may have converted me!
This is a keeper! I made it with fat free mayo to make it a fat free dressing. Just wonderful!!!
I have been using this recipe for years. It is so good! I always add a just a little bit of fresh ground pepper to it and a little pinch of salt. This is a wonderful recipe. Thanks for sharing!
My husband & I loved this dip & will definitely be having again - it was great with Potato Wedges
I used this dressing over baked chicken and lots of greens.  It was easy and super yummy!!
DELICIOUS, just what I was looking for!

I used the recipe for a dipping sauce for my homemade Auntie Anne's Preztel kit and boy oh boy what a disaster I unfolded!  Be forwarned, DO NOT use the blender on the highest setting without a lid. I don't know why that wasn't mentioned in the recipe. I've had to hire a professional cleaning crew to scrape the delicious sauce off of my ceiling and walls. (one star deducted for cleaning crew) All in all it was delicious but I think in the future I'll stick to a recipe less dangerous.
This was fantastic! This tastes just like the honey mustard at all those popular restaurants. So easy to make, and so tasty. Thanks so much for this recipe.
Very good but I think I might perfer to use it as a sauce to barbeque with.  Jamie Lawson
Great, easy dressing made with ingredients you usually have on hand. I am looking forward to also trying it with plain greek yogurt instead of mayo.
Absolutely PERFECT!!
A little thick and added water to thin it out. Otherwise, great.
Excellent!  Restaurant quality and perfect with my homemade chicken tenders.

I am not crazy about honey mustard dressing, BUT i 
really, really like this one. Not only tastes great, it is so simple to make. You can't go wrong with this recipe it is sooo good!  thanks, Mary Ann

I wanted to make this low fat, so I took another reviewer's advice and used low fat yogurt instead. Only I didn't have plain yogurt so I used lemon and omitted the lemon juice. It is pretty good, I'm sure mayo would be better (but isn't everything that's fattening?) I added a little salt, pepper, parsley and white vinegar to cut the sweetness a little. I think this would be best with dijon or a spicy mustard, but that's just my preference. Overall, great recipe. I love when I can make something with ingredients on hand vs store-bought dressings.
This is very tasty. My daughter just loved it. I had made chicken nuggets from this site. The flavors blended well. We well be keeping this dip recipe forever
Simple  Quick  Delicious !
very good! didnt follow the measurements. of course added more honey, but really liked this. and extremely easy.

Thanks for the recipe. The proportions are helpful. However, for a more sophisticated taste, this recipe should be submitted again substituting dijon mustard for prepared mustard! The blend of honey and dijon has a more complex flavor than the yellow stuff. Even if you don't normally use dijon it is great in the dressing.
I just made this to go with baked chicken fingers.. its delicious!  Try it.. best honey mustard recipe I've found!!

I loved this! I used peach brandy instead of peach schnapps & cognac. The wine I used was a Riesling & it worked very well. I only used a bit of the ginger ale (I used Sprite) & then compensated for it by adding a little  sweetness w/ some simple syrup. I loved the orange & mango slices ... after we drank all the sangria I saved them to use as garnishes on mango ice cream.

such a fun, yummy sangria recipe!  I added raspberries as well thanks to other reviewers' suggestions.  
It is very sweet though, so if you don't have a taste for too sweet, you may not like this one!

I have tried several recipes for white sangria, including another from this site, and this is by far the best.  I only had frozen mango so I added some of this as well as a cut up fresh peach to the oranges.  Everyone loved it.

Made this for girls' nite and just myself and one other lady drank it - she definitely preferred it with the ginger ale. I followed the recipe and it was VERY strong and a tad too sweet. I used a sauvignon blanc, peach schnapps and ginger brandy. Used peaches, mangos and red raspberries. I also used super-fine sugar - definitely less than what was called for - and made it the night before. Boozy and maybe overly sweet drink, next time will ease up on the sugar and try club soda instead. But really good, pretty and easy.
The wine overpowered the fruit and liquor.  I added extra sugar and finally a full can of Old Orchard, passion fruit blend.
I made this for a cookout this weekend and got many compliments.  I also added fresh peaches to the fruit. and only used 3 bottles of wine (mostly because I ran out of space in my punch bowl).
Simple, refreshing, and delicious!  I didn't have any schnapps so I used frozen peaches, a little OJ, and a splash of dry sherry.  Thanks for sharing this recipe, Wifie!
Very tasty!  Served at a party and no one refused a refill.  Maybe one less orange, but otherwise perfect for a summer evening.
Very refreshing!  I followed other's suggestions and omitted the cognac and sugar.
This is absolutely the best!  It disappeared from my party and has been the hit of several of my sister's parties!!!!!!!!

This is the perfect light summer drink!  Served this at a cookout and it was gone in no time!!  I followed the recipe for ingredients, but when I made the batch I added everything but the ginger ale, and refrigerated for about 5 hours.  I added the ginger ale just before serving but I actually liked the flavor better as it sat for awhile.  Next time I will just add all ingredients and then refrigerate.  Delicious!!  Like others said, this has quite a kick so drink slowly!

Great recipe!  I leave out the cognac and the sugar and just soak the fruit in the schnapps, that way it's not too sweet.  I also use sliced firm nectarines, blueberries and green grapes, but you can use any kind of fruit you want.

I made this sangria and it is delicious! I used apples instead of mangoes because the store where I shopped didn't have a good selection of mangoes. It was a huge hit. My family loved it! I am definitely make this again. This is a keeip
This was drink was a big hit at my last party! I left out the cognac and sugar. Seems to taste very much like champagne.
Great! Guests loved it, I added more fruit than suggested.
Highly recommended.  Major hit at a dinner party.  Make extra because everyone will love it.  Also, make copies of the recipes for your guest because they will ask you for the recipe.

I made this for my friends 30th birthday party, I thought people would be mainly drinking beer and shots but the sangria was gone in an hour or so! I made a few changes, basically just added strawberries and raspberries and omitted the cognac because I didn't have any. I made it two days before and it was amazing! Will definitely make this again!

This Sangria was absolutely yummy!  I liked it better than the red whine sangria (and I'm a red wine drinker).  The mango is a really great complement!  This one is going in my recipe box to make in the future!

This is almost good. I made a few changes and it turned out great. I used Brandy instead of the cognac. I didn't have mangos so I used fresh peaches. It still needed more fruit so I added some grapes and apples. I also didn't have enough white wine so I used 1/2 white and 1/2 red. I also added 1-1/2 tsps of cinnamon. Yum Yum!!
I make this all summer but with the following changes, double the schnapps, no cognac, add frozen peaches, mango's and strawberries. Skip the oranges. I use pino grigio

Made this for a Shakespeare in the Glen picnic and it was a huge hit. I took the previous reviewers advice and omitted the white sugar entirely. I did add sliced strawberries as they were lovely and in peak season and I thought it made the sangria that much more beautiful but I guess it did make it not strictly "white" anymore.
The drink of my last four summer parties! I can't tell you how many people have asked for this recipe.  Be careful...it can sneak up on you!
I served this at a boat get together and it was well received. I'll be making this again.
I have made this for 3 parties recently and it went quickly at each!  I do add some orange liquor and doubled the peach schnapps because I like the flavor.

I make a similar sangria but use a full bottle of white wine, 1 cup rum, 1 cup mango vodka,  and 1 cup brandy. Add your favorite fruit, and dilute to taste with ginger ale or lemon lime soda. It's delish!
excellent!

Extremely good!  Used regular ginger ale and did not find it overly sweet.  Served it at a women's group and everyone raved.  May eliminate the mango next time, not because the flavor was bad--it was wonderful, but because it was not quite as pretty as I would have liked.
This is a great refreshing alcoholic beverage for the summer.  It's an easy recipe and had great reviews for my baseball tailgating party!

Big hit!!  have made it for 3 different parties so far.
and will taking it to one tomorrow.
I've got slices of mangoes, white peaches, strawberries, orange rasberries, kiwi and some rainier cherries.... in this one.  
a little gingerale into each glass poured.
Great summer sangria !!

I love this Sangria!  I do not like white wine, but I do now.  I have made this time and time again. I have used frozen Mangos and peaches...but grapes and apples in it..loved it!  This is a great recipe!
Yummy!  I am happy that I finally found a white sangria recipe that I will actually make again.  I did leave out the sugar, because the ginger ale added enough sweetness.
This is a fantastic recipe!  Served it at a bridal shower and it was a real hit.  I did add red raspberries just because they looked so pretty.  Next time I will make double!

I made this for a party and it was a hit..but I made some changes.  I only used two oranges - added frozen peaches and mangos and a few slices of apple.  Also..I only used one bottle of white wine.  It made a lot less sangria but the flavor was intense.  I thought only the girls would be drinking it but the guys were diving in too...and if you run out of ginger ale it tastes great with sprite too
This was wonderful. Served it at a Bridal shower. I made an ice ring to float on top and it was not only good but it looked good. Thanks for a new favorite party drink.
I made this for Father's day and it disappeared!  I didn't have Cognac so I added a little extra Peach Schnapps and my mostly non-drinking crowd devoured it and asked for more!  :)
This was soooo good!  I cut the recipe in 1/2 and it was gone in no time.  I will definitely be making this again.  I didn't have Cognac so I used triple sec and was still good.

I actually ended up adding a lot of fruits and letting it sit over night. Next time I will peel the citrus I used as I feel that the skin added a bitterness that I do not like. Other than that, it was very good.

Excellent drink!  I made this for a surprise 40th bbq and it was a hit.  I added more fruit...limes, apples, raspberries (at the end).  I also changed the cognac to brandy because it is a lot less expensive.  Thanks for the recipe.
This was a huge hit at my jewelry party! I was asked for the recipe and have already seen it at some of the other parties I've been too. I found that it's best served over a lot of ice. Delish!

Awesome!!  Have been making this recipe for years and always a hit. I use Vella box wines and switch between white or red with same recipe. Also, I have all ways made it all the way through with wine and ginger Ale and let sit refrigerated over-nite. It is better made the day before.  I will be taking this to the Derby party tomorrow.

This was so good. First white sangria I ever had, usually make red now my man likes it better than white and requests this one instead whenever I say I'm making sangria. great recipe, although... Should it be called plasma instead? lol
Made this for a BBQ and it was a huge hit!  Watch out though - people don't really notice how much alcohol they are drinking because it is so sweet and refreshing.

This was a hit at the party! Everybodu loved it! I doubled the schnapps, and doubled the brandy that I replaced the conac with. I soaked the fruit over night and added raspberries, kiwi, star fruit, lemons, and limes in addition to the oranges. It was gone in a heartbeat....I should have made more.

This is an absolute hit with all of my friends!!!!
It is always requested, and always delicious!!!
I would recommend this to for any bbq or mexican dinner party!

I made this for a party, and people liked it, but didnt' rave over it.  It was VERY sweet with the Ginger Ale.  I think I would have liked it a lot better without the Ginger Ale.  But, I think this is a good drink for people that like super sweet fruity drinks.

People go wild for this stuff. It's my go-to recipe for entertaining--and it's so good you'll see your guests' eyes roll to the backs of their heads on the first swirl. I have made it many times now, various ways. I use Pinot Grigio for the white wine version, and it works equally well with red wine such as Pinot noir. Experimenting with other variations,  I have skipped the cognac, doubled the peach schnapz, used Splenda instead of sugar, and made the ginger ale optional (just because I'm not supposed to drink carbonation). I have also used sugar free 7-up instead. I recommend fresh mango plus sliced peaches when in season, and feel free to add other fruits as well such as apple and orange slices when mango is out of season. You really can't mess up this recipe--it's so good. Thank you for a big keeper!

Holy cow! This recipe was amazing! Everyone raved about it. It is easy to adjust and use fruit you like. I will definitely do this again. I will most likely add more schnapps, cognac and sugar. In fact, I will probably double the amounts given. But it was still an awesome drink!
I use Sauvignon Blanc only because it's what I prefer.
I decided to try this as a new sangria recipe.  I did not care for it much and my friends didn't either.  I guess just not our taste!
Great recipe. People request it these days. But be sure to have a DD to take you home - more than one of these drinks, and you will be giggly!
This was a hit! I halved the recipe but doubled the amount of peach schnapps and used mango, peach and thinly sliced starfruit. Very refreshing and delicious!

Fantastic.  There were only 5 people who drank this at the cook out and the entire gallon was gone.  everyone loved it.  it does creep up on you.  

I used a bit less sugar, natural sugar cane, not white sugar, it was all i had.  I also used a LOT more fruit.

I used everything i had in the house, mangoes, apricots, plums, lemons and peaches.

FANTASTIC  I will make this ALL the time.

Thought i would update this.. i just made it a second time for a friend who had never heard of Sangria.  She left with the recipe.  She is hooked and has already made it for a friend.  FANTASTIC

This is a wonderful recipe. I did not add Cognac and it was still delicious. You can get creative with the fruit just don't add fruit that will get mushy. I like mangos, oranges, apples and frozen strawberries and pineapple since I already had them in the freezer. I did not need to add any sugar. I made this for a birthday party and it was gone very quickly. Luckily there was still fruit to eat!!

This was a very, very good sangria - numerous compliments from our guests.  The secret to any good sangria relies less on the ingredients than it does one very important factor - TIME!  When I make any sangria I usually make it the night before the party (or first thing the morning of).  The longer you allow the fruits and liquids sit the better flavor you have!  (Stir occasionally!)  Just remember your ginger ale (or whatever soda you add) is to be mixed in just before serving.  Time is one ingredient any good sangria simply cannot do without!

This is my go to recipie for sangria or adult punch for a crowd. Be careful it can sneak up on you!  I add lots of fruit...have also used apples, pear, pineapple, its no fun with only one slice of fruit in the glass. Try it with frozen fruit in place of ice to keep it chilled for a bridal shower, etc.  I use trader joes "2 buck chuck" .  The recipe gives you a lot of room to play with different flavored liquor (mango rum, flavored vodka in place of scnapps).  But definately a keeper the way it is, too.

Fantastic...I took the advice of a previous review and doubled the recipe and had some left-over...  (hurray for me!).  I've been adding more white wine, ginger ale and a splash of schnapps to the fruit and enjoying it for the last couple of days.

I have used this recipe atleast a dozen times so it's about time I leave a review. I always leave out the sugar and depending on the crowd I might also leave out the cognac. This is such a wonderful drink with a great presentation, so perfect for Bridal Showers or Baby Showers, women go crazy for this drink- you will run out!!!

This was my first time making Sangria - I wanted something lite and delicious - something perfect for an evening summertime party with the girls - well there wasn't a drop left of this.  It was delicious!  Even the people who didn't like Sangria drank this. Only thing I changed was the sugar - I made it superfine and I let it chill over night.

Easy, versatile and delicious! Only used peach schnapps (no cognac), bunch of cherries, oranges and apples (no measuring). Added ginger ale to top off the glass right before drinking. Fantastic summer drink!
the wine was a little pulpy with the oranges.  Next time I  might use mango and peaches.  I don't care for pulp.  Other than that the taste was great!!

12.21.16   I used skim milk, and although I had a container of malted milk powder on hand, it had been so long since I used it that it had completely hardened, so no malted milk was used.  If you're an egg nog lover, try this recipe...it's absolutely delicious!

I've made this several times, but obviously forgot to rate it...sorry, Mr. Infamous! This stuff is addicting - I need to buy jalapenos by the gallon now! I've always used and loved every ingredient listed (except fresh dill, which I never have, so use dry) and can't imagine why I never thought to put them together as a condiment on their own...It takes a Genius to "invent" simple stuff too, I guess! Thanks so much for thinking of us and posting this! PS to the reviewer that says it has "no taste of jalapenos" - I think you forgot to put them in OR your taste buds are shot.

This was a great addition to my turkey dog. I didnt have tequila so I didnt use it. I also ate this with a few blue corn tortilla chips and that was really good. Like another reviewer said, I bet this would be good with Frito Scoops as a dip.

A friend made this, and it was incredible. I immediately went home and made some. This relish is so versatile. Hotdogs and hamburgers become gourmet with this relish. Another friend put it into her salmon dip. It's good on eggs too. Have fun experimenting!

Good stuff to have around! It lasts forever in the fridge, and can be used a million ways. Dress up a boring turkey sanwich, burger, hot dog...add to tuna salad, or you can even add it to cream cheese/sour cream to make a spicy party dip to go with veggies and crackers.
Sounds great. I'm going to omit the tequila (non drinker). Would anyone who has tried this recipe recommend a substitute, or just leave it out?
I didn't have any garlic on hand so I just put in some garlic powder instead.  This is great for BBQ, thanks for sharing your recipe.

AWESOME! Super spicy, but super yuumy! Made as written aside from cutting the recipe down. Served this as a condiment for hot dogs. Hubby gave it two thumbs up, lol. I would make this again, for sure! Thanks for sharing. :)

This has been in my recipe box forever and I finally made some today. Wow is this ever good without even putting it on anything. I didn't have tequila and it still taste great. I'd like to try it with some tequila. I made some to give as gifts and the first batch was very hot, my jalapeños are Mt. Olive and quite spicy. So I kept that one for me and made one and half cup of pickles to the same amount of jalapeños. Used a sweet onion and dry dill. I'm sure this will get even better after it sits for a few days. Think this will be a staple in my fridge from now on...can't wait to have it on a burger or dog.

Delicious! Had it at a Fabulous party I went to ( Beach bash) LOL and even got to take some home. Spent the next 2 days putting it on everything I put in my mouth!  A bit spicy and tangy. Perfect:) Thank You Christopholofigus!
Not so good

Ay, caramba! Lol yea it's spicy alright. I followed everything except the dill. Updated Jan.11,2012: These became a staple at our house. Sometimes we add a little bit of pepperoncini's to it. We have used it for hot dogs, burgers, eggs, and even italian beef for sandwiches (AR).

I will always have this relish in hand! Made it for a cookout--it was a big hit. I didn't change anything, and I don't think I ever will. My son took quite a bit home with him, so maybe next time, I'll double the recipe. Thanks for a great relish!

This was FANTASTIC!  I made pretty close to as written w/the exception of using 1/2C less jalaps (my jar was only 12 oz I belatedly realized) and omitting the black pepper (I'm a freak who hates black pepper).  I even measured everything since I'd have no reference point for a jalapeno relish (and since it has so few reviews).  Awesome.  Just awesome.  I took it to a casual dinner party and we inhaled it both as is w/Scoops and atop grilled pork chops.  I can't wait to try it on grilled burgers and dogs and to mix it w/some sour cream to cut the heat for sissies for a nice spread/dip.  The possibilities are endless, but you NEED to try this!  Don't be intimidated at first bite; the heat hits you up front, yet is gone before you have time to swallow.  It's good stuff!  THANKS for sharing, Chrisopholofigus!
I've made this several times. My friends that like jalapenos love it and ask me to make more. I like to do 1/2 fresh jalapeno and 1/2 pickled jalapenos. Great stuff!

WOW!  What a hit this was at our cookout! Love, love, love it!  I was going to make a half batch (yes, the re-sizer is waaaay off so beware!) but I went ahead with the whole recipe and am SO glad I did!  There was only a little bit left and that was quickly used up when the kids made their school lunches with the leftover burgers.  It vanished!  GONE!  We really enjoyed this and it was requested that I keep a nice, big, jar of this on hand at all times!***update*** Our fridge is never without a big jar of this!  We do add more garlic than called for and just kinda splash the tequila in there - just might be a little more of that than called for in there too ;)
This is AWESOME!!    Served it with Oklahoma cheese grits, and both were gone before anything else on the table. Thanks so much for the recipe.   Make a double batch--one to serve and one to share!
There is no taste of jalepeno's in this relish, it just tastes like pickles!! Why isn't it just called a pickle relish???
One word: FABULOUS!!!!!

I had half a jar of jalapeno slices that I wanted to use up, so I made a half batch of this recipe.  We served this on burgers.  I will say that this was pretty hot, at least for us (and I wouldn't consider us spice wimps), so you'll definitely want to serve this on a bun with other condiments to cut the heat.

Oh wow...this is great!  I did double the onion and garlic because I could not help myself and it was perfect for us.  We had it on hot dogs but it will be good on so many things.  We will also, as others have stated, always have this on hand it is that good.
Good relish!  Served it on zippy burgers (from this site).  The only change I made was I added a little sugar.  But overall it tasted great on the burgers and I'm so glad I tried it.  DH loved it.

We liked this on burgers. We'll use the leftovers on hot dogs, maybe. My husband LOVED it, he's a huge jalapeno fan. Just an FYI to anyone else -- this recipe divider program does not divide in half correctly. When you switch the serving size to 24, it gives you equal amounts of jalapenos and pickles, instead of 2:1 as it should be. I'm sure they'll fix it at some point, but for right now, just be careful if you re-size this recipe or you could wind up wasting ingredients! Thanks for the recipe, Christopholofigus! EDIT: Adding that my husband did eat this on watermelon slices! He doesn't like watermelon, (but we eat it anyway, for health benefits), so he had nothing to lose by trying -- but he DID like the watermelon better with this on it :) Just adding that for anyone who's curious about trying it that way!
YUM!  Made just as written, and it FLEW off of the BBQ table!

This is good, but it is rather spicy, and I reversed the amount of jalapeno to pickle ratio (we don't do very spicy in this household).  That worked for us, so I think it just depends on your spicy tolerance.  If you like spicy, I'm sure you'll like it as is.  Because I was also making tartar sauce at the same time, I minced the pickles in the food processor, removed them, then minced the jalapenos in the food processor, then added to the rest of hte ingredients.  I don't have fresh onions so used dried minced onions.  Thanks for the recipe!
so simple, excellent relish for burgers, and recently tried some on baked fish-superb. I will be keeping a container of this in the fridge to spice up many dishes

I've been in the overflowing blueberry syrup situation before - & having homegrown, very juicy blueberries nearly ensures a mess - soooo to minimize, I used an 8x8 glass dish.  It was fine.  I added 2T cornstarch to the berries (very juicy ones) & reduced sugar in the cake part to 1/3c.  'Done in 35- 40 minutes.  Done = it bubbles five minutes.  The cake part reminded me of a sugar cookie.  It's crisp on top, but soft on the blueberry side.  A bit too much sugar.  'Not the prettiest dish, but you want to eat it, not just look at it.
This was easy and was a big hit at my spinning group.  I wish I read the first review, I didn't protect my oven and it over flowed.  Otherwise, I loved it and will make this again.
Tasty & easy but not much different than other fruit cobbler type recipes. No one jumped up for seconds.

this is quite good.  i was looking for a recipe to use the last of my blueberry crop and this fit the bill.  the only one thing i would change is to add a bit of cornstarch to the berries before putting in the pan.  it is a bit soupy when serving.  other than that, no complaints.  delicious, quick and easy to make.  thanks for the post yogurt4k, i will make again!

I have made this Mystery Cake 5 times in the last week and half! My husband loves it! I made it with blueberries the first two times, blueberries and blackberries the next two times, and right now it's in the over with peaches! It's really really good and really easy to make! most ingredients you would have in the house except maybe the fruit. It cooks up beautifully with a nice crust and I would consider this more of a cobbler type recipe than a cake. During the summer we have access to beautiful marion berries which will be wonderful with this recipe! I highly recommend this, have posted photos on FB and given the recipe out to several people already! It's going to be a staple dessert in my house!
We really liked this cake.  I would say it is more like a cake-like pie.  I guess my pan wasn't deep enough because it overflowed. . .thank goodness I had the pan on top of a cookie sheet.

To be fair, this is more of a cobbler than a cake.  But I can tell after making it once, I will be making this regularly.  I followed directions exactly, except I used my frozen berries from last year.  I can't wait to try it with blackberries and may even try strawberries.  :)

Thanks for the reviews!  Glad you are enjoying this family favorite!  If you are having issues with the pie pan overflowing (mine is really deep), feel free to make in a larger casserole dish.  I sometimes make in a casserole just to have a prettier dish to take to a party.

I made this for our church women's Thanksgiving dinner and it was a big hit.  Even the young children loved it.  I never made a cranberry relish with so much fruit in it, but that is what makes it so good.  I also used raspberry jello. Fabulous recipe!!!!!!!

I used orange juice instead of the oranges and for the jello i used one small box of strawberry jello and one of the raspberry jello...it turned out awesome! My Grandmother makes this recipe every Christmas...love it!!!
Loved it. Was messy for me to make, chopped cranberries in a blender! I also decreased the sugar.The end results were absolutely delish. Have made it 4 times over the holidays. My go to from now on.
Excellent taste! I have made this recipe 3 times this holiday season. It is a perfect cranberry dish!

The 5 stars rating is because DH and eldest daughter loved it with raspberry Jello.  Just as good the 2nd time with cherry Jello, but will do it raspberry next time.  Cut down the sugar to 2/3 cup and it was still too sweet with the jello. Will keep tweaking but its going to be a regular side dish for our special occasion meals.
This is very similar to a receipe I have used for years.  It is very good, but I use fresh cranberries in mine.
Really great!  I used Raspberry Jello instead of Strawberry.  I like the flavor better.  This recipe is great with chopped pecans too!
This is the best recipe for pickled okra I have ever tried, they turned out perfectly. My mother ate the first jar we opened almost completely by herself! Thanks for sharing such a great recipe.
Excellent recipe. Usu I'm not a big fan of okra but the smokiness of the paprika really brings out its best flavors. Madly rocks!

First Timer here. Never canned or jarred a thing in my life. Tried three different pickling recipes from this site and this recipe ROCKED! I couldn't find the schezuan peppercorns so I used 3 dried chili peppers per jar, waited the WHOLE week, my God they were good! Fear not! This was so simple and better than anything you pay $4 or $5 a jar for in the store. Thanks for the recipe and the confidence to try more!
this recipe says 1/4 cup of paprika. way to much. my liquid is red.....going to wait and try it anyway, but i don't have much hope

I made this but I think maybe 1/4 c paprika was a typo. I used about 1 1/2 Tablespoons and it was great! Also 1/4 c red pepper flakes was way too much for our tastes. I used 1 Tablespoon flakes and it was the perfect about of heat. My liquid was also very red like someone else commented but it was AWESOME! Will be using this every season.
Very good recipe, made with Apple Cider Vinegar.
Great recipe! Thats exactly how I make mine but I never thought of adding smoked paprika. I'm going to try that tomorrow. Thanks again! OH yeah, I also use toasted mustard seeds with the peppercorns.
This was so-so.  I really love smoked paprika, but it really does not complement the okra.  Next time I'll leave it out.
Easy and delicious ,liked the way the soda bought it all together!
Delicious.  My first "baking soda" red sauce.  I was careful to add no more than a level teaspoon and it cut the acidity nicely.  My Italian brother in law had seconds!
I love it ,make it  2 times a week

One of the best Italian sauces! So easy to make. I use Peeled San Marzano tomatoes and use my immersion blender to crush them while in the pot.  These tomatoes have the best flavor. I used less water than called for and did not use the baking soda. I added my uncooked Italian meatballs (1 lb each of veal, pork, beef) and cooked for four plus hours.

This recipe was easy to follow! I didn't read correctly to see it was 2 cans of 32 oz so I had 2 cans of 24 oz crushed tomatoes. The sauce still came out really good. I added way too much basil (dry not fresh) and I was a little worried. After simmering for over 2 hours it wasn't overpowering like I thought I would be. I added meatballs to the sauce for the last 20-30 minutes of simmering. This will be my go to for sauce from here on out!!
I made this for all our kids, used Marzano tomatoes. Delicious.?
This is a great sauce for being so simple.
Thank you! This simple, yet amazing, recipe made me a bona fide kitchen stud to my wife ... I now make it regularly and it's perfect everytime.
Amazing, and easy to make!  My fav sauce by far!

I do not like blue cheese but made this for my husband. He said it was good except that it could have used an herb or two but He didn't know which ones so you'll have to be the judge if you decide to add any.

I was so excited to try this Horchata smoothie but alas it did not meet my expectations. Against my better judgement, I included the mint leaves, making this smoothie taste more of mint than anything else.

I've looked all over for YEARS for the recipe for a Singapore Sling.  I was so pleased to run into this one while browsing the allrecipes site.....one of my favorite pastimes!   Will be making these wonderful fruity/sweet-tart drinks soon!  Thank you Home Happy hour

Your mouth will do the jetter bug with this nicely chilled drink in it !!! the fresh pineapple is a great touch to it ! But I also used the juice from the fresh pineapple instead of can pineapple juice, and that really made a huge differance. Go ahead and let your mouth do the jetter bug!   ^..^

I really enjoyed this. I subbed almond milk for the soy milk, and a handful of almonds in place of the flax seed meal. Other than those adjustments, I followed the recipe. Super yummy and filling. Will make again. Saved to my recipe box! Thanks.
I love this smoothie. The 2nd time I used half cup skim milk; half cup vanilla Greek yogurt; whole banana; and added 1 tablespoon chia seeds plus 1/4 cup oatmeal.

Yes, this recipe does work and tastes delicious when done correctly. No, it's not as easy as it sounds (as you can tell by the negative comments, here). So, why bother with this recipe? Well, learning to make this sauce helped me master all sorts of recipes that required caramelized sugar. With that being said, first, you need a little less water than a 1/2 cup: just enough to moisten the sugar. That's because all of that water has to evaporate before the hot sugar will caramelize (because the temperature of caramelization is 320-340F, which is higher than boiling - 212F). Second, and this is important, when the sugar starts to boil, drops will splash along the sides of the pot, the water will evaporate, and the sugar will crystallize there. If they fall back into the pot, they act as seed crystals, which can make the entire mixture harden (which has happened to some people who've tried this). For that reason, try not to splash the sugar mixture on the side of the pot when initially combining the water and sugar. To remedy this, dip a pastry brush in a cup of water and gently brush the sides of the pot to dissolve the sugary drops until they run back down into the pot.  You will only need to repeat that until the bubbles get larger and stop splashing. After that, it should be smooth sailing. My second time I forgot and found the cream cheese was denser than my first time. Test the firmness as directed at 45 min and every so often to get a melt in your mouth product. Heat sugar very slowly with just enough heat to melt the sugar plus a few degrees warmer so it does not solidify while you are tipping the pan to coat all the bottom. This melting process can get away from you quick and give it a smoke burnt tinge, so unless you like Scotch after taste, then take your time. I failed to do that the last one I made and it solidified in the middle sooner. Live and learn. Finding a 10 glass pan is difficult as some have mentioned, but 9.5" deep is do able but again the water bath is needed

Its kinda mild compared to lemon juice or red wine vinegar.  I added 1/2 teaspoon pink salt and a pinch each of garlic and onion powder.  Also, and this is key, I added 1 teaspoon or so of dijon mustard.  So I blended everything except oil in my BlendTec blender. till creamy. It was great! It was thinner than B*** F***s but perfect for blender mayo.  Check out my photo to see the results.  Very creamy, a little yellow, with flecks of pepper.  Herbs would be nice too for something special. (It's in a white crock in front of my blender on granite counter.)

I made this to go with pasta. Everyone loved it! I did leave out the garlic salt, & it was perfect.

LOVE LOVE LOVE this garlic butter!  I slather it over some texas toast or french bread and bake it until nice and crispy.  It gives the bread a nice flavor with the perfect amount of garlic!  This is the go to recipe if your making homemade garlic bread!
Fast and delicious!!!
I have used on garlic bread, steak,and fillet of fish. Gave the extra to a co-worker and her family loved it as well. Thanks for sharing.

AMAZING! I couldn't find garlic butter in the store so I made this. I will never buy garlic butter again!

Love this recipe! Ended up making it more like a sauce, and then put my rolls in the bowl. Basically, flavor was just what I was looking for. Only thing I'll do without next time is the paprika, mainly because of the color it made.

very good recipe.  has become a favorite with spaghetti!

I quadrupled this recipe for all of my family and it was great. I did what other reviewers said and substituted the garlic salt for garlic powder and it was great and salty enough without it. I will use this recipe for all time now ... THANKS DENYSE

Wonderful taste, really great on top of italian bread slices!
This recipe is delicous.  I used it on bread and also melted the butter and used it as a marinade for shrimp.
ummmm yummy!!!!!!!!!
Very very very very good.

This was great. Made it and put it on top of steaks. Once mixed, I formed it into a bar with parchment paper. Should get a few uses out of the one batch. Will definitely make again. The only thing I left out was the garlic salt.
I was looking for a simple way to dress up some fresh corn on the cob that I wasn't quite in season yet...easy and tasty!!! Thanks for the recipe!!
Quick, easy and great tasting. Thank you.
Good flavor, but way too salty.

I didn't use as much butter, and used 3 large garlic cloves sauteed in 1/3 of the butter, then added to the cooler butter and mash.  It was better than store bought and tasted great. Awesome!  This IS the stuff.  I too used garlic powder instead off garlic salt.  Perfect!
Yum! Yum! I made this and have put it on garlic bread, and also on a turkey cheese  tortilla wrap and browned it. Amazing recipie. Very versitile.

Very good on garlic bread. I'm not sure how it will taste on other foods. It seems very garlicy.

This makes great garlic bread.  I use margarine and then spread on store bought sub rolls which have been sliced lengthwise.  I close them and freeze for easy use. This butter is delicious! I had to bring butter to a party where the host was serving lasagna, searched recipes for garlic butter because I didn't want to bring just butter. Keep this in my fridge so is ready to use always.  Seems the flavors blend the more it sits too.

How could garlic + butter = anything other than wonderful!?

This  recipe has been passed along to all of the office crew, neighbors - you name it  !!!!!! Make a batch and freeze one in a log to slap on top of anything at the last minute for a real treat.  Thanks so much Denyse -- you have a winner here !!!!!!!!!

Wasn't bad, pretty much the typical garlic bread recipe but a little on the salty side so I cut down the salt by half (you can put more salt according to your own taste) and popped it in the broiler. As long as you cut down on the salt, it's delicious.
I reduced original to 4 and wow! Had all the stuff in my cupboard and wife & I both loved it. Thanks for the way to do it right! Yummy.

This flavorful butter goes with so many things it would be impossible to list them all.  I make up triple batches, making them into logs and freezing them.  That way they are on hand at a moments notice to put on fish, slip under the skin of chicken, or melt over a New York strip steak.

Made this the other night with a huge plate of pasta and some Italian bread - - let me add to the list that you can't find a better garlic butter than this.  Turns the same ole garlic bread into something so amazing.

Very good!

Incredible! I made a batch of this and melted it for dipping a homemade pizza into. Absolutely beats delivery garlic butter hands down! I will use this on just about everything from here on. This is so easy to make. I put it on everything from bread, to veggies to pasta. My family loves it.

Very good and flavorful! I will add a little more salt next time though.

Yummy!  We ate this with the breadsticks I made from this site and my husband said it should be illegal it was so good.

This mixture is DELICIOUS.

Edit: For those of you having trouble with curdling, it is key that the top of the double boiler be ABOVE (not sitting in) the simmering (not boiling) water to prevent overheating. I realized two things when I first made these brownies - these brownies need to be cooled for well over an hour before cutting and Jill's World-Famous Coffee Liqueur Brownies are some of the most delicious brownies to come out of my oven. Thanks, CAFN8ME, for the great recipe!

I used a different type of pan entirely, so while I can't necessarily speak for the accuracy of the baking time or temperature as written, I CAN say these are delicious, and well worth trying, regardless of what size pan you use - just bake them until the brownie looks set, starts to pull away from the sides, and a toothpick inserted in the center comes out ALMOST clean, but a few crumbs still remain on the toothpick. Any more than that and you'll surely overbake them.  In my case, I used the little 6-mold heart pan by Wilton. They're kind of shallow, and this recipe scaled down to 5 servings gave me just the amount I wanted for me and Hubs - four, good-sized brownies.  For those of you who have this specialty cake pan, I baked them at 350 degrees for about 21 minutes and let them cool about 10 minutes before I attempted to unmold them (and they were stubborn, even tho' I sprayed the pan with a flour-based cooking spray).  This recipe is all you'd want in a decadent chocolate brownie - rich and buttery, fudgy and pleasantly sweet.  The coffee liqueur taste is not obviously noticeable, however, I appreciated the way it livened up the flavor. They would have been just fine as is, but because I wanted to dress them up a bit I made a glaze (just winged the amounts) of powdered sugar, melted chocolate, butter, vanilla, a dribble of corn syrup, and Kahlua.

I've never before experienced a headache from sugar or chocolate...until this morning. I made these brownies last night and were too warm to sneak a bite so I had to wait until morning. Brownies are my BIGGEST weakness and wow, did these suckers win me over! I subbed cocoa powder and butter for the squares of chocolate (3T cocoa +1T butter for each ounce). I also omitted the nuts and chose to bake at 350 since that's where my oven was set. They baked in about 38 min. Sinfully rich and decadent. The lackluster top could've been prettied up with a very thin glaze, but it didn't need it and it was easier to pack/ship them without it. Good thing I mailed 95% of these off or I'd be hitting them gym til they close tonight... :)

Also I only used two cups of confectioners sugar since I don't happen to like a real sweet frosting. I made Sams Carrot Cake from this site (My favorite) and it is delish with this frosting!!!

I made this frosting to go with Sam's Famous Carrot Cake. I will absolutely use it with other recipes in the future because it is SO good. It was not overly sweet and the coconut was perfectly subtle. I ended up using about 3.5 cups confectioners sugar (because that was all I had), whole milk and used half the amount of coconut flavoring because I was afraid it might be too fake-coconut tasting. It turned out even better than I hoped. I was also hoping there would be enough left after icing my carrot cake to eat some at the end--there was. :) Great, great recipe, a definite keeper.

I made the cake exactly as  specified and it was wonderful - so moist and had great coconut flavor. I frosted it with coconut cream cheese frosting and covered it with shredded coconut. This cake is delicious. Thanks so much for the recipe.
Great starting point. I usually leave out the coconut and add much more powdered sugar to make the frosting thicker.
Delicious! Absolutely the best cake I have ever made.  3 cups of powdered sugar was enough sweetness for me.
Superb !!!!

I usually don't give 5 stars to recipes because there is almost always something that ends up needing to be adjusted based on previous reviews but this recipe is PERFECT.  The only change I mad was halve the recipe since one reviewer said that would be enough for a cake with filling and she was right!  I put it on the Heavenly White Cake and added some fresh raspberries to the filling and it was amazing!!
I left out the coconut; I just wanted the vanilla frosting.  It turned out great!  It also goes very well with fresh strawberries.
Delicious!  I omited the coconut.
Everyone at Easter dinner loved this frosting.  I used it with pineapple cake, making it a pina colada like cupcake.  DELICIOUS and great consistency.  Really good recipe - thanks!!!

Absolutely divine.  I had unsweetened coconut on hand an it was enough sweet for me (but I like things on the less sweet side).  I'm sure sweetened coconut is delicious too.  Used on some pineapple cupcakes.  It will be used on much more in the future.  Bravo!

This is an excellent recipe...everyone loved this cake and frosting...The only thing I changed was to put the coconut only on top of the frosting untoasted.  I used milk instead of cream and no salt.  I also spread the frosting on the center of the cake and spread a thin layer of my homemade strawberry jam on top of the frosting.
The coconut flavor is very subtle, which I did not mind.

I was charged with making a birthday cake for my sister-in-law this year for her 23rd. I've always been desperate to win over my in-laws, and this DID IT! The frosting was phenomenal! My husband's many siblings loved it, so much so that when I turned around to let the dog out they dove into the bowl and ate all of the extra in 3 minutes. If you ever need to impress, this is the frosting to try.
Easy to make and tasty. I doubled the batch to cover 36 cupcakes, because the serving size was for 20,  and I had way too much frosting left after generously frosting 36 cupcakes.

The flavor is awesome, but even after upping the powdered sugar to 7 cups, it was still too thin...it just ran right off the sides of my 8" 2-layer cake (which had been refrigerated for 24 hours).  Hmmm...I love the flavor, so Im going to experiment with this recipe to see if I can get a thicker, spreadable consistency.  It would be great for a 13 x 9" cake left in the pan, though, as it would be contained in the pan.

This was great, but I halved the amount of powdered sugar.  I also didn't need any cream to have the correct consistency with the absence of the sugar.  I like being able to taste the cream cheese, and since I added all of the optional sweetened coconut, it was plenty sweet.  I used this inside of a lemon sponge cake to make a jelly roll, and it was delicious.

Decadent! I used this to frost Hummingbirg Cake I from this site. It was a bundt cake, so I cut the icing recipe in half but probably used a total of 4 tbsp. half & half instead of the heavy cream to get more of a drizzling consistency. This frosting is DELICIOUS. Try it you will love it!
GREAT!

I don't understand all the high reviews, unless all these people like sickeningly sweet, runny frosting.  I doubled the cream cheese and left out the cream.  Then I put it in the fridge to see if it would thicken more.   I think there should be more extract and less powdered sugar- it's overpowering.

Followed the recipe and it turned out GREAT! Frosted a "Davids Yellow Cake" also found on this site. 
Toasted 2 cups coconut and pushed this into the frosting once the cake was frosted. Looked great and tasted great.
This was really just perfect for my Coconut Cake!!! Thank you for making my cake that much better!!

SO SO GOOD!  This frosting is perfect exactly the way the recipe is written.  I did not change anything, and had no problem with the consistency; I'm wondering if the writers of the reviews indicating it was runny had allowed the butter and cream cheese to get too soft before creaming them together.  I used this on white cupcakes (from the Cake Doctor cookbook), and they were just amazing.  Thank you for sharing, this one's a keeper!
Delicious! I made it to top SAMs famous carrot cake, and it was scrumptious. Everyone raved about it.

Kidlet says this is the best frosting I have ever made.  It's very sweet, a little thin (but easy enough to adjust), and the coconut extract/flavoring does WONDERS for this recipe.  Don't change a thing.
WOW amazing love this best ever

So very delicious!  Followed the recipe almost exactly - added extra powdered sugar to get to a buttercream-like consistency for a round cake.  Used a white cake and sprinkled the middle and top with shredded coconut and chocolate flakes.  Huge hit!

PERFECT cream cheese frosting measurements.  What more can I say?  It was super yummy.  I didn't add the coconut flakes this time around (only because I forgot) but added the exact measurements of all of the other ingredients, including the heavy cream.  This will definitely be my go to recipe for anything requiring cream cheese frosting.

Amazing! I've made this a few different times for cakes, cupcakes and a carrot cake. It's delicious and is always a huge hit! I've done several variations on it as well with and without the coconut and it's always good. When I include the coconut I usually double or triple the amount of flaked coconut.

I thought the frosting was very good. I did not have any coconut flavoring so I was surprised at how intense the coconut flavor was without it. I think shaved coconut would be better, texture wise as I used shredded (unsweetened, as it was all I had) and it seemed a bit chunky.  It was plenty sweet for us.

I made this last night to go on a coconut cake that I made and the frosting is really wonderful. The next time I will add a little more powdered sugar to make it a tad thicker (like suggested). Great recipe Lilster.
Excellent recipe and very easy to make. Not overly coconut tasting for those who are not fans of coconut....will definitely be making again!

I've made this before and saved it because I liked it. However, I never toasted the coconut before and the difference having the toasted coconut sprinkled on top of the frosting was phenomenal. I used 3 cups of confectioners sugar, and served on a simple white cake. Wonderful.

This frosting was really good. I used it on top of the Hawaiian Wedding Cake recipe from this site and it was a hit. I would definitely suggest adding the toasted coconut on top - it seems like a small touch but it really makes a difference in the level of coconut flavor that comes through.
Yummy!  I used 1 tsp. coconut rum & 1 tsp vanilla.
Loved this!  Fluffy and wondeful! It had lots of flavor and earned rave reviews on a banana cake.

I like others did not have any coconut flavoring.  I was mixing it up anyway for a yellow cake and when I tasted it, I thought it would be very good with chocolate.  I added 6 heaping teaspoons of baking cocoa and wow, it was amazing.  It tasted like chocolate cheesecake frosting...yum yum!

AMAZING RECIPE! Since I didn't have any coconut flavoring, I used some extra shredded coconut. Absolutely delicious! I use this on many cakes - carrot, white, yellow, coconut cake, coconut pound cake - everybody loves it! If you are looking for an all around good frosting that can be used on many cakes, this is the one! It is FABULOUS! You must try it.
easy to make but way too sweet and the consistency was not as thick as I would expect.  Would not make again
Great taste. Added a little more coconut and some lemon zest, which made it perfect!

i made this without all the coconut stuff as a cream cheese frosting for a red velvet cake. i did not like the consistency [i ended up using 4.5 cups of sugar but i stopped there because i felt i was losing too much of the cheese taste]; i would give that a 2. but the flavor is excellent, i would give that a 5. overall a good recipe.
toast coconut in oven @350 deg and sprinkle on top
Used this on the pineapple cake I recipe here (with a can of drained mandarin orange segments) on this site. Didn't have the coconut flavor but I did add some orange zest.  Delicious.

I'll never buy another container of frosting. EVERYONE who tastes it (on my lemon cake) raves about it and requests it, in advance, for all future  gatherings.  I usually substitute milk for cream and I use 1-1/2 cups of coconut instead of buying additional toasted coconut.  One batch is more than enough to frost a 9x13 double layer cake.  And I've never had a problem with the consistency or with it sticking to the sides the way it should.
this was just great. i used it on a carrot cake and it really added to it without overpowering the flavors of the cake. it was so good, though, that it would probably be delicious on anything!

LOVE!  I needed a simple cream cheese frosting for a red velvet cake but they are all so thick.  The heavy cream thins it out just enough to make it so smooth.  I just left out all the coconut ingredients and it made for the best plain cream cheese frosting!!!
I was craving coconut, so decided to use this recipe to top my vanilla cupcakes.  Loved it - don't skip the toasted coconut - it kicks these up a notch ( and smelled so good cooking).

My husband licked the bowl and commented any cake I make for him he wants this frosting on it. I did use the coconut flavor & it was perfect. I used it frost the coconut cake mix cake on this website-so did not add shred coconut. Great reviews from co-workers!
Great frosting! I used about a cup extra sugar.  I like it thicker and sweeter.  Otherwise I followed recipe exactly.

Great recipe.  However, I use only 1 2/3 cut powdered sugar and it's very sweet.  I cannot imagine using 4 cups.  No need for the cream.  I omit it each time.
I use this for carrot cake and add 3/4 cup shredded sweetened coconut.  It's great with 1/8 tsp of cinnamon and cayenne pepper (ground) also.
Would like to try it with a bit of lemon juice or extract.
As for the runny comments, I don't see how.  My guess is folks may be melting the butter or microwaving the stick which will release the oils.

This recipe is fantastic. Like many mentioned, I used a little less sugar. Instead of using heavy cream, I substituted the same amount of cream of coconut. I'll be completely honest - this frosting whipped up to a consistency that is very similar to that of store bought frosting. It's amazing. You could use some milk and another flavor - goodness - the millions of opportunities with this icing. This will now be my go-to recipe. It's fantastic.

This recipe was pretty good. I halved it to use on top of lemon cupcakes, and it was just right, not too sweet. I found I had to add a bit more sugar to get it thick enough to pipe onto a cupcake... so I would say in a half batch I used about 2 1/2 cups. 

I also omitted the salt (as I think the bagged shredded coconut is salty enough) and substituted the heavy cream for just plain milk because it's what I had and I didn't want to buy a whole container of heavy cream just to use two tbs.

This was excellent! I thought it could have used just a little more vinegar but hubby said he thought more vinegar might have overpowered the delicious flavor of the roasted peppers.  This was super fresh tasting and nothing like what you get out of a bottle. I highly recommend this recipe. Thanks for sharing!
used cumin instead of chili powder

Easy enough so that my young daughter could help me make it.  She's pretty picky when it comes to soups, but she really likes it!  I used just a pinch of sea salt and instead of cayenne pepper, we used red pepper.
I made this for dinner tonight. It was good. Next time tho, I will decrease the amount of chili powder because the soup was too spicy for my children.

This really was a hearty soup. If you're feeding a large family like mine, you would need to double it.  I served it with cornbread, and used cheddar cheese instead.  Wouldn't be opposed to using parmesean cheese in place of it.

I love this recipe. But I made a few modifactions; instead of cayenne I highly recommend either chipotle chili powder or a few chipotles in adobo [to taste; depending on the brand, really]. I also add 1/4 c diced bell pepper or a 4oz can green chilis, 1/2 t garlic powder AND  a bit of fresh or jarred garlic; again to taste.  And definetley use beef or even chicken broth boullion cubes.Disregard the salt requested in this recipe, the taste is much better with the salt from boullion.

This wasn't bad. I was out of corn, and I didn't have anything else I could throw in. I like the flavor of the soup, though. I had to use shredded cheddar cheese, and ketchup in place of the paste, but otherwise made as is. You'll have to crank the heat up to a low boil in order to properly melt the cheese. Then let it simmer for 5 - 10 minutes.

This was very easy and quick to make.  It turned out a lot better than i thought it would.  I added more chili and cayenne powder though and added some peas and carrots as well as some string beans.  My family loved it!
My family didn't care for this:(
My family loved it! Never made nor heard of hot dog soup but it came out fantastic! The only negative response i got about it was how spicy it was. Otherwise a real hit.
didn't care for this at all. The recipe tasted too acidic, salty and overly seasoning of spices and the cheese didn't bind well with the whole recipe. Won't make again. Sorry.
I love this! It is creamy comfort food at it's best. Enjoy!

Yes, it IS sweet---just as it was reported to be.  If you don't like sweet, you won't like this.  I do think I'd rather have it on the rocks, and just maybe I'll try it the next time without the simple syrup!  But you can't go wrong with these ingredients!  Thanks, cjm378!
omg...so good. i only had plain vodka but it was still yummy !
Super easy.  Family loved it.  I added a 1/4 cup cocoa powder to make it chocolate!  YUMMY!

Very easy to make.  I made my own pancake batter (without the wet ingredients), used the cherries I canned from last year,  and had to add a bit more milk than the recipe called for (maybe 2/3 c).  I also added a few drops of almond extract, because cherries should always accompany almonds.  ;)  It is in the oven, so we will see how we like it later! edit: This was fantastic!!
It is absolutely wonderful!!!

I doubled this recipe--tripled the cherries but just doubled the juice and the rest (because I love cherries)  and it was awesome!  Big hit -- did add sugar on top too.   Thanks--made it for my dad's 77th birthday party and he loved it!!!

Oh-So-Easy is right, and Oh-So-Good!!!! I had to cook it a bit longer so as to get the top a nice light brown, but that could be my oven. Made this for dessert last night and it was an empty dish that I found this morning. Will definitely be baking this up often... we love our cherries! Thanks, mzlizz!
I did not care for this recipe.

this recipe sounded so good, i had to try it. i bought sweet dark cherries packed in heavy syrpe by mistake. i bought jiffy buttermilk biscuit mix and measured out one cup of mix and followed this recipe. it was very thin. i topped with the cherries and slowly poured the syrpe mixture over top. this is when i said to myself how will this turn out, as it looked liked everything blended together. what a surprise when the crust formed on top and everything thickend up. it turned out fantanstic.  i didn't have icecream, but topped it with a little very vanilla soy milk. it was to die for. this super easy recipe will be one of my all time favorites. thankyou.

Great Idea.  I exchanged the cherries and sugar for Cherry Pie Filling and then used Bisquick instead of the Buttermilk mix and added 1/4 cup more milk.  My baking time was 40 minutes.  This was very good.  Thanks

I gave it 3 stars because the recipe was not very clear to me. Sweeten or unsweeten cherries? What is buttermilk baking mix? Bisquit???? Should the cherry juice be cooled before pouring over batter? I added 1/2 teaspoon good almond flavoring and 1/2 cup sliced almonds on top before baking. Baked 40 minutes. It was very good, but had to guess at all these questions.
I am absolutely crazy about cherries and as it is now the cherry season, this recipe falls well, that is it would if I knew what a buttermilk mix was.

Great recipe! Easy and very good. It only took me 5 minutes to make, which is a huge plus in my book. I followed the recipe exactly and don't think it really needs any improvement upon. Will also go well with a cup of coffee for breakfast. Thanks!

Great recipe!  I substitued real buttermilk for the milk and used fat free Bisquik.  I also added a bit of anise extract - which I feel is a requirement in any cherry dessert!   I have to admit - I was a little nervous after pouring all that cherry juice on top of the batter - looked more like I was making a jello mold!.....BUT  - it really did all absorb and turned out fantastic!!  I'm going to try this recipe with the same brand of canned blueberries next time!!

OK...so I made a couple of changes: increased pancake mix to 3/4 cups, increased milk to 1 cup, added 1 teaspoon almond extract tossed with the cherries, melted 1/4 cup of butter in 9 x13 " baking dish in the oven before pouring batter over.  Then proceeded with the recipe as written. Served warm with whipped cream....heavenly.
AWESOME! And so easy! I even substitute the cherries for other berries (blueberries) and it still holds true.... so delicious and easy, EASY, EASY!

I made this but made it easier! I poured 2 cans of cherry pie filling in a 9" x13" pan. I then sprinkled a box of WHITE cake mix on top, as evenly distributed as possible. Then, I cut up in small slices 1 & 1/2 sticks of real unsalted butter & arranged them all over the top of the cake mix.   I put the pan in a pre-heated 350• oven & baked it for 1 hr & 5 min. (Depends on how accurate ur oven temp is!)!  The white vs yellow cake makes ALL the difference! Makes for a crunchier more cobbler-like appearance & it just tastes GREAT!!
Easy to make and tasted good too. My boyfriend doesn't care for cherries and he even liked this. I had to cook mine a little longer to get the top to lightly brown. Will definitely make again.

As advertised, very easy recipe. Saw comment about it being too soft, so added a bit of melted butter to generously sprayed pan before adding batter. Cooked an extra 10 min. Came out perfect with crisp edges. Used 16oz bag of frozen cherries, heated in the microwave with the sugar, and it made lots of liquid. Didn't think it would gel without cornstarch, but it did. Could easily double the fruit next time. Could do the same with any fruit. Must have vanilla ice cream with it. Great with a splash of rum or red wine over the top.
Not enough fruit, trying it again with more to see if it is better.
Awesome, made just by the recipe.  Loved it!
this is so delicious and easy to make. i didnt have the cherries so i used frozen mixed berries with sugar.

Measured everything out as stated, opened the can of cherries and proceeded. Am very good at following directions to a 'T' and was very optimistic because of all the rave reviews but this recipe turned out to be a disaster and nothing even close to a cobbler. I don't remember ever giving such a bad review but guess there is always a first. Would give zero stars if possible. What a waste of precious food money

This recipe was great in a pinch.  I used 2 cans of tart pie cherries, halved both the sugar quantities and used 2 cups bisquick, and 1 cup milk.  I spilled about 1/4 cup of the cherry juice on the floor and the cobbler still turned out fine, in fact it was a little runny on the bottom.  Next time I may try a tablespoon of flour or cornstarch.   I baked it in a 9x13" at 350 for 25 min and then broiled it at 550 for 5 min and the top is nice and golden.   It was superb, will definitely make again.  Guests raved about it.  Thank you!

Really great!  I needed to make a quick dessert for a get-together and didn't have enough flour for a cherry pie.  So I came across this, had the Bisquick, and threw it together!  SO easy!  I actually doubled the recipe, baked it for about 15 minutes longer in a 9x13.  I also added some almond extract to the syrup mixture before pouring it on top of the batter and cherries.  Will definitely be making this again sometime!
Crust was a little soft...not crispy like I would like.  It was tasty, though!  Just a texture thing.
Very good.
I used tart frozen cherries, because that's what I had.  This was excellent. I also added cinnamon.

This was delicious!  I honestly wasn't expecting much from this recipe but it far surpassed my expectations.  Very, very good!  I served it with a little cream on top and it was just the perfect dessert! Thank you for sharing!

This was a really good, easy cherry dessert.  I doubled the recipe and baked it in a 9x13 pan, because of that it took about 15 more minutes to bake.  I also sprinkled a little sugar on top before I baked it.

Very yummy and satisfying to a sweet lover. However, I made these changes to the recipe, only because I had this on hand: I used a 1/2 of 16 oz bag of frozen, mixed berries (raspberries; blueberries; blackberries; strawberries,cut up)and sprinkled 1/4 cup sugar on the fruit before thawing in the microwave. This produced a syrup with the fruit. I combined a 1/4 cup of  sugar with 1/2 cup water to pour over the fruit. When I added the fruit to the batter, I poured the juice it made with it, also. Next time, I'm going to double the fruit and use Splenda and light Bisquick mix for the batter.
It came out perfectly despite using regular milk in place of buttermilk (confused by the directions), browned perfectly.  It definitely took real willpower to make it last 3 days.
This is an excellent low fat recipe and super easy to make.  Not overly sweet and very satisfying.

I doubled this to use in a 9x13. I had frozen cherries so I just sprinkled them with the sugar and defrosted them in the microwave. That made the syrup when they were finished thawing. The only other difference I made was to add a bit more sugar to the batter and to melt a stick of butter in the pan and then pour the batter on that followed by the fruit and syrup. My family loved this but my 7 year old son ADORED it, I ended up getting only 1 piece. Thanks for the recipe!
It came out extremely runny.
I tried this recioe for the first time and it was great.  I used bisquick and buttermilk and it was wonderful with frozen vanilla yogurt.

I made this for Bunco yesterday. It's super easy and very yummy, especially with whipped cream topping or Cool Whip!

I used Bisquick for the baking mix.  I cooked it in the microwave, about 8-9 minutes, just until it had a congealed look. Then, when I arrived at Bunco, we stuck it in the oven @350 to brown it, probably about 15 minutes.  It was delish!!

I would imagine it would work with any fruit. I plan to try it soon with peaches.
Good stuff!

This was SO simple and so, so good. All my Momma kept saying was how much it tasted like the cobbler her Mom made for her as a child.
I would recommend Bisquick instead of Pioneer buttermilk baking mix though. The Pioneer doesn't seem to rise as well

This was very easy and nice for a weeknight dessert.  The only problem I had was the recipe says it will bake in 25 to 30 minutes, mine took twice that long.  Other than that I had no problems and will make again.

have been using this for a long time, my mother-in-law calls it surprise pie, wokrs well with any fruit, especially great with peaches and apples. I use a good quality self-rising flour (saves a little  money) instead of the baking mix

This was a great beginner recipe for me since I just started baking.  My family enjoyed it but my dad said it didn't taste like his favorite one from Bob Evan's.  It's missing something.  Definitely would make again though!

Quick, easy and de-lish!

I made this last night to take to a friend's house for the 4th.  Excellent recipe!  So easy and everyone liked it.  I followed the recipe exactly.

Tasted good, and it's certainly easy to make. Too much liquid was left in the bottom after baking, but that might have been my mistake as I had a larger container of cherries and may have over estimated the amount of cherry juice. Served warm with whipped cream. Thanks!

An excellent recipe for what it is - a quick, easy and pretty darned tasty, comfort food dessert mixed up and poured into the pan in literally just a couple of minutes. Had I not made this myself I would have never known this cake/cobbler started with packaged baking mix.  As I assembled this I had my doubts that this could EVER work - it's a layer of batter, followed by a layer of cherries and finished by pouring a lot of juice over it all.  It looked strange. How it came to look like it did after it baked is beyond me, but it worked and it was good, warm or cold and particularly good topped with whipped cream.
Easy to make and followed the advice of one poster to use almond extract and Bisquick. Turned out awesome, will make again!
Loved it. Made it with lots of strawberries and it was amazing!

I absolutely loved it. I used frozen cherries a large bag. Defrosted in microwave with 1/2 cup sugar which created the juice I needed. Then strained and cooked juice as directed. I put cherries in a strainer and they drained some more. I doubled the recipe for the bisquick mix. I used regular not buttermilk. I added only 1/2 cup of sugar. Mixed as directed with a cup of 1% milk.  Spread batter in bottom of pan and arranged cherries over the top.  To the juice that drained from the cherries I added a tablespoon of cornstarch and mixed in with the microwaved juice and sugar. Poured over the top of batter and cherries. Baked for 35  minutes . It turned out perfect.  I was so surprised.  I thought it would be soupy because of all the juice.  But the cornstarch helped I figured.  Best cherry cobbler I ever made.
Delicious and easy! I added 1 tablespoon of lemon juice and 1/2 teaspoon of cinnamon for a little more flavor. Mmmmmmm good.
Pretty good first time cooking this one

Serving size should be more specific (i.e. volume).  16 servings makes roughly 25 ounces.  I don't know how many people consider a serving size to be over an ounce when dealing with a sauce this hot.  Be careful when you're sauteing over the stove, fumes will be noxious.  I did like everyone else and cut vinegar by 1/4 cup (so 3/4 vinegar), and added a bit of sugar (1/3 cup).  I also added a habanero and 3 serranos, along with a dash of liquid smoke.  In retrospect I probably could have omitted the extra peppers and it would be perfect.  It's got a heat that sticks to you pretty good.
