YUM!  I'll tinker with the consistancy as a dressing, but this was VERY TASTY & great as a dip (good with a vege tray)!  It really has a better flavor if you use the buttermilk, I've tried it both ways & the sour cream takes away from the flavor, it's still tasty, but better with the buttermilk.  This was great with the texas ranch chicken from this site.  Thanks Dawnia!
Hello Ranch Dressing II, my family loves this recipe. It was very very tasty and quick to make. Thank you for making our taste buds dance.
Good base recipe, used fresh herbs-parsley, chives and basil, skipped onion and garlic powder, added 1/2 cup milk to thin out as used for a pasta salad.
My staple dressing from now on.  Thanks.
I made this dressing for tossed greens last evening.  Made it as is, but seemed to need a bit more "tang" to it.  Added a splash of lemon juice, it was perfect.  Thanks for sharing this recipe.

This was very good... I will admit, I did add a rounded 1/4 tsp of garlic salt as well. For my liking, it needed a bit more salt/garlic. I served this to a serious ranch dressing lover and she LOVED it. Said it was better than the packet kind. Also, I used fresh chives (green of the green onion, about 1 1/2 Tbsp, not actual chives) because that is what I had on hand. I will be making this again. A for sure KEEPER!! Thanks Dawnia!

1st ranch I have tried to make and loved it! I did use vanilla yogurt instead of sour cream because it is what I had on hand. I think I will continue to make it that way it was so much BETTER than the store bought stuff!!!

I have been making this for a while as the recipe is written except for using buttermilk in place of sour cream or using 1/2 cup each of sour cream mayo and buttermilk.
Today I decided to use fresh garlic & onion both pressed in the garlic press and then fresh chives, basil (instead of parsley and increase salt. So basically, I have done what I hate when other people do and completely changed the recipe. But it is still is good. As it is written the recipe is good but it is also a great basic idea to play with.

WOW!!!! This is the BEST!!!!!!! I can honestly say that I will no longer be buying the bottled stuff... I made this tonight and used on the Bacon Ranch Pasta Salad from this site... I could eat this with a spoon (who needs the veggies) This is gonna be a must have in my refridge from now on... thanks so much for the TERRIFIC recipe......UPDATE>>> UPDATE>>>>> I would like to make a big batch of it to have when needed, but not sure without the additives if it would last long... Can anyone help, and let me know how long I should keep a batch???
Fantastic! Who thought homemade dressing could be so easy? Thanks for a great recipe, Dawnia!

This recipe was a good base. I found it to be too much mayo, so I added an additional 1/2 cup of sour cream, and about a tbsp. of white vinegar.  I didn't have parsley, chives or powdered onion, and used herbs de provence in its place. Nice consistency for a dip. I will make this again.

Made this exactly as written.  It's very thick, like a dip not a dressing, so I had to add a good amount of milk to thin it out.  It is good, but for my taste there is way too much dill in it.  Will make again but cut it to 1/4 teaspoon.  With those adjustments I think it would be a 4+ rating.

I have been living in Australia and missing my ranch dressing until now. This is the best and I will never buy packet or bottled dressing again! Using buttermilk would create a slightly thinner dressing if you prefer or add a couple tablespoons of milk to sour cream recipe if you would like. Cheers!
This is an excellent dressing and dip.  I use fresh herbs, rather than dried, whenever I have them.

This makes the best ranch dressing I have ever made.  I always use plain yogurt in the place of the mayonnaise and sour cream.  Excellent flavor.  I don't like store bought ranch, but I love this one.
Thicker than Hidden Valley out of a bottle. You can really taste the dill weed and can certainly tell it is mayo based. Overall I really like it and will certainly make it again!

This recipe was so easy and quick! And so much better than the bottle stuff. I changed a few things it improvise with what I had available in my pantry and fridge and it was fabulous. Added fresh crushed garlic, fresh green onions, didn't measure anything but used less sour cream and mayo and made my own buttermilk with milk and vinegar and added it to thin it out. Added the other dried herbs salt and pepper to taste. Perfecto!!! Never buying that bottle stuff again. Thank you!!

So good I'm not sure I'll ever buy Ranch dressing again!  The only thing I did differently was used fresh chives and parsley because I didn't have any dried.  Oh, I also used buttermilk instead of the sour cream like some others had suggested.  Fabulous!

Very delicious! I did take others advice and use 1/2 cup of each: mayo, sour cream and buttermilk. Was perfect, not too thick. It does have to sit in the fridge for a while so the flavors can meld. Tasted sooo good. Will use from now on! Thanks for sharing!
Great taste.

Very nice recipe for Ranch, and living in Australia you won't find a Ranch dressing on supermarket shelves that's anything like the Hidden Valley Ranch I remember from thirty years ago.
Following are the modifications I made:
I used 1/2 cup each of mayo, sour cream, and buttermilk.  Doubled the garlic powder and salt.  Added 1/4 tsp of paprika and 1/4 tsp. of Worcestershire sauce.  The remaining ingredients remained the same.

Absolutely delicious! Exactly what I like ranch to taste like. I worked in a four star restaurant where they made all their dressings from scratch. If you told me this was their recipe, I would believe it!

Great recipe for a basic dressing. You can easily add other spices to make new dressings/dips. Add our fave pepper sauce for a spicy tex/mex dip. Double the Dill for dill dressing (that may be good for a quick Cucumber salad). Best advice I can give, let it rest at least 30 min before you add flavors, the dry spices need to bloom and release flavors.
This is the easiest ranch dressing to make. I added a little bit of olive oil and 1 spoon of milk to give a smooth softer texture and it tastes awesome

Per other reviewers suggestions, I halved the amount of dill...and I used buttermilk rather than sour cream.  I thought this tasted just like the Hidden Valley Ranch packets...which is not necessarily a bad thing, I was just hoping for something more original.  Still very good though!  :)

This recipe hands down is the best I have come across. My daughter raves about it. For those of you who think the mayo will be too overpowering, I found after the herbs had a chance to "marry" for a few hours it tasted much better, and the next day its even better!  I like my ranch dressing a little thinner, so I added a few splashes of milk to mine. Great recipe!

We really liked this recipe.  I added a bit more salt than what is called for - not sure how much, just kept sprinkling in till we liked the taste.  I did increase the garlic powder to 1/2 tsp. too.  Also, I did the 1/2 cup mayonnaise, 1/2 cup sour cream, 1/2 cup buttermilk - as suggested by a previous reviewer. The longer it sat, the better it got.  Thanks for sharing!  I love being able to make things from scratch!
thick, delicious, and the best tasting ranch dressing I have ever found!
Very good dressing, I used fresh chives instead and it was perfect! Thanks for the recipe!
You might want to decrease the amount of dill just a bit, and I thinned it with a little whole milk.  Otherwise, I find this recipe excellent!!
Very good.  Rich and flavorful, not to mention easy.

This was ok, not what I was expecting.  I followed the recipe exactly but it is better as a dip then a salad dressing.  Next time I might try using buttermilk instead of sour cream.  I didn't use all the dill called for in the recipe either.
This is by far my favorite dressing to make, when I serve it as a dip I use sour cream, when I use it for a dressing I use buttermilk.  Everytime I make it I get lots of raves.Thanks
awesome.  i do 1/2 cup of light buttermilk, sour cream, and mayo.  i also up the spices a little.  really yummy with a bit of blue cheese as a dip for chicken wings and veggies.

This so so much better than the bottle version. I eat a lot more veggies and cabbage with this dip. It's flavor in burgers instead of mayonnaise is super and I use less cuz it's so full of flavor. I use it a lot.
Very good ranch dressing!
If you don't have mayo you can use milk instead it tastes just as good

By the other reviews, I thought this would be outstanding, but my husband and I thought it was a little blah.  I ended up doubling the dill and adding 1 tsp of lemon juice, and we ate it that way as a veggie dip.

This was great! I used 1/2 cup buttermilk instead of sour cream. You can't have ranch w/o buttermilk! I also halfed the dill, and upped each of the other spices just a bit for extra flavor. We are allergic to bland food around here! But you can't get an accurate taste right after you make it. You really need to let it sit in the fridge for a while to let the flavors combine. My hubby tasted it right after I made it & didn't like it. When he ate it w/ his chicken wings & carrots after it'd been in the fridge a couple hours, he loved it! So if you're not letting the flavors combine, yes, it tastes too much like mayonnaise. Otherwise, it's yummy! It is on the thick side. Not ideal for salad dressing, but was perfect as dip w/ our chicken wings. This will be my new go to recipe for ranch!

I made a low fat version by using light mayo and low fat buttermilk (I didn't have buttermilk in the house, so I made it by adding 1 1/2 tsp of lemon juice to 1/2 cup of 1% milk).  I also added some all-natural Mrs. Dash seasoning, which gave extra flavor and flecks of color.  In contrast to bottled low fat ranch dressing, which often tastes like glue, this recipe is simply delicious.
This is my first attempt to make ranch dressing and it's DElicous!  I love, love love this salad dressing!!!!  No more store bought dressing for me!
Wow. This is fantastic. Doubled all of the spices. Used a little milk to thin it some. Delish! Fresh veggies here I come.
I found the mayonnaise in this recipe to be overpowering. The dressing is also very thick, a little milk took care of that though. Over all it was ok.
This is my favorite ranch!!  I add a cup of milk to make it creamier and I let it sit for at least 24 hours before serving.  Great recipe!!

Very good. I followed the advice of others and used 1/2 cup each buttermilk, ranch, and mayo. Next time I will up the seasonings a bit. Even after a day in the fridge, it still isn't quite as seasoned as I would like, but still better than any bottled dressing you can find. With a little more tinkering, this will be the ranch dressing recipe for us. Thanks!
Very good, makes up thick, like a dip.
Really good I made a pasta salad with it. I threw in bacon, tomatoes elbow macaroni noodles and hard boiled eggs.

I love making home made ranch. First I use a 1:1 ratio of  mayo and 2% GREEK YOGURT. I also add PAPRIKA (a couple dashes/pinch for a half recipe used tonight). I ALSO ADD a couple dashes of LEMON JUICE; it thins the mayo and greek yogurt (or sour cream - I have used that in the past too) and adds the zest the ranch needs.

This is the best Ranch Dressing ever! It is not made with buttermilk, which I like, because buttermilk is not a staple in my house. My family loved it! I will never buy store bought Ranch Dressing again!
Straightforward with minimal prep and minimal cleanup.  I added a bit of sweet paprika to get a little color in the mix without seeming 'hot.'  Also, used frozen dill, which was a mistake.
Fantastic, I used creme fraiche instead of sour cream, doubled the garlic powder and added a dash of virgin olive oil.
Great recipe!  This tastes better than any of the store brands.

I made this for the first time, and made a few changes. First I used Greek yogurt instead of sour cream, I skipped out on the chives altogether, I ran out of dill so I used dill pickle juice but turned out great.

Why would anyone buy ranch when it tastes so much better making it like this.  I am glad it doesn't have buttermilk b/c I usually don't have any around, all other ingredients I do.  I like to dip everything in this ranch, like truly everything.

One day, all my husband and I had available for lunch was stuff for a salad. I wanted to spruce it up a bit, so I decided to look for some homemade ranch dressing, as we almost always bought ranch from the store. I really can't say enough how happy I am that I did...I now won't even buy store-bought stuff anymore. I got so spoiled on this stuff! It's AMAZING just as it is...however, over time, I made just a small change to make it a little more liquid-y (since we always have it on our salads)--I use a 1/4 cup sour cream and a 1/4 cup buttermilk, instead of the 1/2 cup sour cream. This makes it a little more spreadable, but we also do like the thickness, so the sour cream works out great. Thanks so much to whoever submitted this!
It does have all the preservatives in it because of the mayo.  :) Would use greek yogurt instead of sour cream as well.
Will definitely make again.  My wife is a ranch junkie and she absolutely loved it as is.  Will follow the advise of others and try buttermilk if I want it runnier for salads.
Not bad after  I doctored it up.
Very good recipe, this is the first salad dressing I made.  Just added canola oil for consistency as someone recommended in there review.
Delicious. Thanks for the recipe.

Thank you so much for this recipe.  I have been searching (without success) for a good from-scratch recipe for  ranch dressing for almost 10 years.  I don't know how I missed this one before, but I am so glad I found it now.  My preschooler came home asking for "dip" since he had tried it at school and liked it.  I won't bother looking any further now that I have found this great recipe, I can't wait to surprise my husband with salad tonight.  I only had about 1/2 cup mayonnaise, so I poured some buttermilk in the mayo bottle and shook it up to get the last bits out, and then added a little bit extra sour cream.  I didn't end up with quite 1 1/2 cups total, so I used slightly less of the spices than it called for.  I can't wait to try some of the variations other reviewers mentioned, this is so yummy!

Sooooo good! Love to crumble bacon in it for a more decadant dip.  Also can be made with light sour cream and mayo and thinned out with skim milk for a less fattening dip or dressing.  Thanks for the great combo of herbs and spices!

My family and I love this recipe; we have been using it for years.  I make it with sour cream or buttermilk (which ever I have on hand) and both are great.  Warning!  Once you start using this recipe there is no going back to store bought stuff.  I have tried a couple of times when I have been in a hurry and my family was full of complaints.

I found this recipe a while ago on this site when I did a search for Ranch dressing. I made it exactly as shown, and now it is the ONLY one I use! I use it as a dip for veggies, chips and pizza crust.
This is my go to ranch dressing. I use low fat mayo and low fat sour cream and extra pepper, it's perfect for salads, veggies and buffalo wings! Everyone will love this and want the recipe.

This was really good!! And so fast and easy!  I used light mayo and fat free sour cream and we still loved it. The flavor was definitely better after sitting overnight. I'm going to mix up a batch of the dried spices and store in a bag so I can make it in a hurry.  Thank you Dawnia!

I'm giving this a 4 as is, but really with the changes everyone suggested I'd give it a 5. Instead of the mayo/sour cream proportion, I used 1/3 cup light mayo, 1/3 cup light sour cream and 2/3 cup low fat buttermilk. I also doubled the spices and used fresh chives.
Whenever I make this, people want the recipe.  It is so easy and so great.  Thanks for sharing this one.
Dawnia....Job well done GIRLFRIEND! This recipe is naturally delicious TY!!!!

I,too, thought it was a bit too much dill-even though I love dill. Added sour cream and mayo to buttermilk and thinned with skim milk to make easier pouring for salad dressing. Very, very close to the real thing! Thanks for the recipe. I will cut back on the dill next time and add garlic, since I am a garlic fan!

This is great. I used 1/2 cup buttermilk, 1/2 cup mayo, 1/2 cup sour cream. The only other change I made was to add a little more garlic powder. Good stuff, and I'll be making this every time I need ranch dressing.

Absolutely great, it's as good as ranch gets. I doctored it a little bit for my purposes: decreased the mayo:sour cream ratio to make it lighter and (relatively) healthier and added a few teaspoons of milk to make it runnier for pouring over salads (it was too thick otherwise for that purpose). Great recipe though!
I´m gonna have to do this all over...frankly not the ranch dressing I was hoping for...not tasty or creamy...sorry, didn´t like it at all.

Yum! Served this tonight on our Cobb Salad, also from Allrecipes. It was the perfect compliment! I quit buying salad dressings this past year. They always taste too 'vinegary' and too salty to me. My family and I LOVE this recipe!!!! as is we use it for a dip, add a little milk and put it on a salad.
Love it!  To cut calories I used fat free sour cream and low fat mayo.  And didn't lose any flavor so that's a big plus in my book
I love the mix of flavors!!!
I half the recipe for the two of us. Will never buy ranch dressing again! Thanks so much for sharing this recipe.

I make HUGE amounts of the seasoning mix and store it in an air tight container.  Lasts forever. Use whatever combination of mayo, sour cream, buttermilk,  milk, etc. that you prefer.  Definitely a keeper!
Will never buy bottled ranch again!!!  This is great!  No wonder all those tastefully simple dips taste so good.
Very flavorful.  I served this dressing on a bbq chicken salad and my husband loved it.

Wow.....I was very skeptical about this..it was so good......the only change I made was to thin it w/about 2 tbs of milk.  Never thought I could make ranch dressing that would rival Hidden Valley.  (and I had all the ingredients in my cabinet!)  this was great!!!
Fabulous! I took the suggestion of using 1/2c mayo and 1/2c buttermilk and it was delicious!

So much better than packet ranch! I used half buttermilk and half sour cream and double the spices. Fantastic!
Very good.  I used 1/2 C of Mayo, Sour Cream and buttermilk.

This was amazing! I haven't been able to eat ranch dressing in so long. Absolutely.....
Positively.....
Delicious.....
:-) I use it as a dip for veggies, my daughter loves it!
Many Thanks

I just needed the flavoring in place of a packet of dry ranch dressing mix. It was for a corn salad and this was so much better! I used fresh chives, dill and parsley because the herb garden is really full and it tasted great!
very good, I tried it using sour cream , and then buttermilk.  Both were good, yet not exactly what I hoped for, but I will make it again.

I used this recipe to make a dip with blended cottage cheese and buttermilk, for nutritional purposes.  It is delicious!  I also added finely shredded sharp cheddar to dry up my dip texture and richen the taste, it is a great dip!
Perfect! The cooks where I used to work always made delicious ranch dressing and I always wondered how they made it. I think I found something even better with this recipe!
This had way too strong of a mayonnaise taste from me.

Great recipe, better than restaurant ranch. I like a thinner ranch, so I used 1/2 c sour cream, 1/2 c mayo, & 1/2 cup milk. Delicious! I used it right after I made it, and it was still great. Thank you for this recipe, I will never buy ranch again.

I tried this because I ran out of dressing and was to lazy to go to the store....Am I ever glad this was soooo soooo good... the only thing is I think I put to much salt in. I will never buy it again!

I have made this a dozen times now, and will continue to make this. I have found homemade dressings to be so much better then the store bought (and I can name all the ingredients) that I have no interest in store bought anymore
I made this with half plain yogurt and half low-fat mayo, then added milk to get the consistency I wanted. Simple and great.
The best!  Can't stand Hidden Valley Ranch.  This is what I've been searching for.  Did use only 1/2 c. Of mayo,sour cream and buttermilk.  That s the only change. Thanks soooo much.

This recipe is pretty bland.  I followed the recipe exactly the first time. The second time, I used 1/2 C mayo, 1/2 C sour cream and 1/2 C buttermilk per other reviews. It was still a little bland.  The search continues for a tangier ranch dressing.

OMG this is good! We added blue cheese chunks to it and it was to die for. Excellent with carrots, and absolutely amazing with onion rings. I love ranch, but man this is so much better than the bottled stuff.

It's ok for dipping veggies but way to thick for salad. I thought the dill weed was too strong, will change up the spices next time. I really happy that I have a dressing I can eat because all the store bought ones have vegatble gums in them and I'm allergic.  So anyone else allergic to gums will love this recipe!
I make this more as a dip then a dressing.  I do end up adding more then the amount listed in seasonings.  Always a hit.
An easy ranch dressing that uses ingredients I usually have on hand. I subbed Greek yogurt for the sour cream. It makes a great dip but needs to be thinned a bit for dressing.
Restaurant quality. I used 1% skim buttermilk.
Best Ranch Dressing ever. I will never buy bottled again.
Absolutely delicious!  I double the herbs and use fresh chives...I could eat it by the spoonful.  I omit the buttermile and use it mostly as a veggie dip.  Thanks for the recipe!

I have recently moved to Canada from the States and I cannot find packets of Hidden Valley Ranch mix anywhere..only the bottled stuff..I always liked ot make it homemade..I was so happy to come across this recipe...The only change I made was decreased the dill just a little and added a touch more garlic powder...sooo good... My husband, who is Canadian, never really ate that much ranch, but he thinks this is really good..Now I wont stress about having family send me the packets from home when I run out..

Great recipe to avoid the processed and preservative-laden store-bought kind.  I found the initial mix to be too thick (more dip-like), and so whisked in buttermilk until it got to the right consistency for us.
Very good.  I did add a few splashes of hot sauce and 2 tsp. of garlic seasoned rice vinegar.  Much better than store bought.
This is similar to a Ranch Dressing I created. The main difference is I add a piece of peeled, grated cucumber and use a small blender. The cucumber gives it the 'cool' ranch flavor.

Wonderful dressing. It's quite thick, so I had to keep thinning it down to get it out of the container!

It was ok. Definitely better for dipping vegetables vs. using on salad. My dressing was very thick. I also had to double all of the herbs to get the taste that I wanted.

Wonderful recipe. I did everything to the T except adding buttermilk to make it more liquidy. It smelt wonderful and looked just like ranch. It even tasted good before I put it in the fridge. Let's see how it is on my salad tomorrow. Thanks poster.
Delicious and simple! Easy ratios allow for smaller portions.

This is the ranch dressing recipe I've been looking for - herby not sweet and can be thinned with milk or kept thick for dipping. I was out of chives so I upped the onion powder to 1/2 tsp, upped the garlic to 1/2 tsp as well because we're garlic lovers and omitted the pepper due to dietary concerns. Still a very nice flavor profile. I halved the mayo and just thinned slightly with 2 Tbsp whole milk. Perfect!

I have bought my last bottle of Ranch dressing! Excellent! It was very thick, so I thinned it with milk. I skipped the dill, I didn't have any, and I used fresh chives. It is excellent on baked potatoes.

This was pretty tasty, but I like a real kick, I revised the ingredient amounts as follows, 1/2 Cup buttermilk, 1 Cup Mayo, 1/4 Cup Sour Cream, 1 1/2 t dried Chives, 1/2 t Parsley Flakes, 1 t Dill, 3/4 t Garlic Powder, 1/4 t Onion Powder, 1/8 t Salt, 1/4 t Pepper, 2 sprinkles Paprika.  So tangy, very thick.  Thank you for submitting such a GREAT base recipe, and one so easy to adjust according to taste!

I made this dressing for the first time this morning before I went to work.
I do not like mayonnaise whatsoever so I was sceptical about liking it, I put buttermilk in mine and slightly increased the garlic whisked it good and put it in the fridge, when I got home at lunch i put some on my salad, I can't say enough how awesome it was and I could not taste the mayo in it one bit. I totally love this dressing and its the only one I will make.
I would reccomend letting it sit a few hours for the full flavor to take over. Everyone who loves ranch dressing should try this one, you  won't be disappointed!!
This is a keeper!  The seasonings are just the right proportions, no overpowering garlic flavor. I used the suggestion to mix 1/2 cup each of mayo, sour cream and buttermilk.

I made a double-and-a-half recipe. I also used buttermilk to substitute sour cream. It wasn't as thin as I liked, so I added about 1/4 cup more buttermilk and 1/4 more water too.  It has turned out to be a great homemade dressing. If you want a ranch dip, then follow the recipe verbatim.

I rated this yesterday as 2 star...but today after the flavors had a chance to blend, it is so good! 30min is not enough. make the night before or early in the day if you have a chance. I used lowfat mayo and skim milk. My son said it was better than storebought.
Not even close in flavor to the packaged ranch dressings.  Nice try, but I'm back on the hunt for the real deal.

I made this twice, first time as is. I found the original recipe had too much dill and was too thick. The second time I made it, I used 1/2 C light sour cream, 1/2 cup light mayo, and 1/4 cup of fat free half and half to thin it. Measurements for spices stayed the same, EXCEPT reduced dill to 1/8 tsp. it was FABULOUS!!! Let this ranch sit for a few hours for the flavors to meld before reviewing. This is a great Ranch dressing, but with all recipes I adjust to my taste. Make this, then adjust to your liking!!

This dressing is fabulous!  I make with buttermilk as I like my dressing a little thinner. I make big batches of it and keep it in a large mason jar in fridge.  It doesn't stay around long at our house.

Really good.  I made it with buttermilk instead of sour cream and doubled the recipe.  Our family loves buttermilk dressing over slow-cooked green beans with ham.  I will definitely make this dressing again.  Thanks Dawnia for this great recipe.  Angela

I was looking for a recipe with no chemicals or MSG. This is very good. I made it with 1/2 cup Smart Balance Mayo, 1/2 cup fat free sour cream and 1/2 cup Buttermilk. I love the taste and consistency and to think it is only 25 calories per Tbsp. I will be making this from here on. My next thing to try is adding salsa. I love Salsa Ranch Dressing too.

I did as other reviewers suggested and used equal parts sour cream, buttermilk and mayo.  I also substituted and added a couple herbs, and it went for a whirl in the blender with two cloves of garlic and some leek because I thought it needed something else.  I thought it was fairly good, but my friends thought it was awesome.  I mixed the leftovers with mayo and celery salt and used it for pasta salad- in that form, it was probably the best pasta salad I've ever had!  So, 3 stars as salad dressing and 5 as sauce for pasta salad.  Oh and I like the Buttermilk Garlic dressing on this web site a lot more than this for salads.  Thanks for the recipe!
Absolutely love this recipe!

I did not make any change it was PERFECT the only thing I would like to know how long it keeps in the fridge
thanks for the awesome recipe

I make this all the time and it's wonderful!  I always have people asking me for the recipe. Made as is, is great, but I normally substitute seasoned salt for salt and also add cayenne pepper to taste.  I also like using fresh ground peppercorns for the pepper.
excellent. it is very thick so i just add buttermilk to it to make it more of a salad dressing. but the flavor is out of this world!

Great ranch dressing!  I don't keep dried chives in my kitchen, but it's great with out them.  I use this recipe all the time.  Great with buffalo chicken!  Also wonderful with carrots and celery sticks!!  Thank you.

My husband and I loved it. I am not sure I can ever go back to bottled dressing again. I agree with other reviewers that sourcream should be used for a dip and buttermilk for a dressing. The sourcream made a good, but thick dressing.
I did 1/4 c mayo & 1/4 c sour cream, no milk.  My was dip consistency.  All spices except Garlic and S&P, were 1/4 tsp.  Garlic was 1/2tsp and 1/8 of S&P.  My picky husband Loved it.  Great Recipe!
Didn't have chives - still tasted awesome!

Thank you, thank you, thank you!  My family is a bunch of "ranchaholics," I have spent a fortune on the little envelopes of the premixed stuff, until now!!!  You have saved me so much money already, wow!  This is a great recipe, the ranch dressing is fabulous.  I use 1 cup of buttermilk and 1 cup of mayo to make a dressing for salads.  This has a wonderful flavor and is quick and easy to do.  Try it, you won't be disappointed!  Thanks so much Dawnia.
This is the best ranch ever. I follow the recipe exactly (using mayonnaise for salads) and cannot stop drizzling it on and dipping things in the stuff. Quick and delicious!

This was too thick for a dressing, more of a dip. I thinned it with milk and that was fine. It was very mayonnaisey, which I didn't care for. Also, not much flavor till I doubled the spices and added salt and soy sauce, then it was  alright. Won't make again.

instead of using sourcream, i used plain greek yogurt.  i also used a little milk to thin it out.  dried parsley, oregeno, dried garlic, and cayenne pepper.  salt and pepper to taste.  i ended up eating the rest of it with raw veggies...yummy!
I've never made homemade dressings before, but I'm glad I gave it a try.  I like this better than the Hidden Valley pkg. kind.  This will definately be a staple in my fridge!

This is a great staple recipe! we made it exactly per recipe using homemade mayo and it was very good!  We ate it all in a few days!  recently, we made it with plain Greek yogurt in place of the sour cream, went heavy on the seasoning/herbs, and added about 1/8 tsp tarragon.   And this version was fabulous!!!

I made this as-is, but with twice the garlic powder and it was just OK (a little bland for my tastes honestly). After reading the reviews, I added 1/2 c. skim milk and a few dashes of worcestershire and it was perfect.  I used all reduced cal ingredients and it was a bit lumpy at first, but I got those out with an egg beater. The resulting dressing works for salads or as a dip.  Yum...

I'm from a part of the country where ranch is the 'house dressing' in most restaurants. This isn't it.  First, it was way too thick and needed some liquid to dilute it a bit (I used milk). Second, it was missing something in flavor. I finally realized it had no acid so I added some vinegar. Totally worked. I'll make this again, next time using buttermilk (since that's one of the key ingredients in ranch dressing). I also don't keep powdered garlic or onion so I added fresh, minced of both. The outcome, after modifications, was delicious. It the original recipe needs work.
Sooo Delicious!!! This is a staple in my house now.

I love this recipe!  the herbs make it taste so fresh! I am kind of a health nut, though, so I couldn't do the sour cream and mayo combo.  I combine equal parts mayo and Greek yogurt and that gives it a kick and keeps it more healthy.  If you don't have a taste for Greek yogurt you might not like it, it's more tangy, but very creamy!

Fantastic recipe. I make this recipe minus the may0 and sour cream, and up the servings to 72. I store this in a jar in my pantry to a ready to go quick spoon out the mixture and add to the mayo and sour cream for dressing ready to go when I am out of time. Great with just sour cream for a veggie dip, or thinned with buttermilk for a thinner salad dressing. My family likes it with less dill, but that is just personal preference. Thank you, Dawnia, for sharing.

Wow! This dressing is so good and so easy to make. Used it on the layered spinach salad from this site and it was divine. For a regular tossed salad, I would thin it a little with buttermilk. As is, it is perfect for dip and would work well as a sandwich spread too. Thanks!

BEST. RANCH. DRESSING. EVER.  I substituted a few fresh herbs because it's what I had but I think it will be just as good with the dried.  I will definitely be making this again.  It tasted like a house made dressing from a high end restaurant.

Great recipe. I am allergic to MSG (in most Ranches), but love ranch! This recipe has great flavor. The only reason I didn't give it 5 stars, is that I have yet to figure out how to keep it a consistency that befits a dressing.  It always congeals again to a dip consistency no matter how much milk I add. Maybe I'll try the buttermilk suggestion, next time.

This tastes so much better than the bottled version!  Like some other users, I also cut down the amount of dill. I used the suggestion of using buttermilk instead of sourcream, and it tasted delicious!
This was fast and easy to make.  Tastes great.
This dressing is restraunt quality. I omitted the dill and added enough buttermilk to make it a little runny for salad. Great on hot wings! My husband loved it.

This was so yummy and super fast.  The time it takes you to make this dressing is less than the time it takes you to go buy bottled ranch. It tastes so fresh and like the restaurant's ranch (it is a little bit thick, but not a problem with me). The dill gives it wonderful flavor. I will try it with buttermilk next time.

This dressing is awesome! even my husband who does not like mayonnaise could not tell that dressing had lots of mayo and found it great.
I made substitutions because of pantry issues: I used Greek style yogurt instead of the sour cream and omitted the onion powder and the dried chives. i added 1/2 t.of garlic powder instead, and still the recipe was wonderful. Next time I will try with all the right ingredients to see if there is a difference, but I cannot think that it can get any better that was I tasted with the substitutions. Thank you for a great recipe for home made Ranch dressing!
This is a great 'base' recipe for Ranch Dressing. You can easily change it up a bit to suit your tastes.
I received RAVE reviews for this dressing.  I tweaked it just a bit by adding fresh chives and some buttermilk to make it a bit more creamy.  This will become a staple in my house!  Thanks.
Tastes like ranch dressing should - nice blend of herbs, smooth and rich. Thanks for sharing

I rated it on the recipe as it's listed. This was a really good recipe! My only problem with it was it was more of a "dip" consistency.. very, very thick. It also tasted a lot like dill, which is okay, but it was just too much for my tastes.  So then I made it with buttermilk instead of sour cream, used half the dill and a little more onion powder and it was great! This is a very good base recipe-- I might try adding bleu cheese or minced onion next time!
If my son in-law could bath in ranch dressing he would that's how much he loves ranch.  Made this one night and he said this was the best he has ever had.
I am going to make this all the time! I don't know why  ranch in a bottle is never good but it isn't. I used grated onion because I didn't have onion powder and we all love it! Thank you!!!

This was a good recipe, but I did make some changes so I am reviewing as I made it, not as it is written.  I used equal parts of sour cream, mayo, and buttermilk in order to add the buttermilk flavour and make it pourable.  Lots of garlic and dill, I made this for a green salad at a family get together, and everyone loved it, a few even asked for the recipe.  Great flavour, even better the next day.

I rarely ever write negative reviews, but this is not what I expected after reading all of the reviews. I followed the recipe exactly and it tasted like seasoned mayo. Not good. Noone in my house liked it. Maybe with the buttermilk it would taste more like ranch and less like mayo?

THE BEST is the only way to rate this ranch dressing.  No more store bought for this family - no more questionable preservatives either!  I make it as stated except for doubling the dill - because we love the stronger dill taste.  As is, still delicious, and that is how I make it for a group.  Try adding a couple of tablespoons of salsa for a salsa ranch, or mix in the blender with some cilantro for another yummy variation!

Fantastic!  Doubled all the herbs and spices, used 1/2 cup mayo, 1/2 cup lite sour cream, and 1/2 cup fat-free buttermilk.  Added a bit more buttermilk to thin for salad dressing.  Absolutely delicious!
Made it with nonfat mayo and plain yogurt. Yummy!!
Better with equal parts mayo, sour cream and buttermilk plus extra seasoning. Fresh chives taste better than dried.

The taste/flavor of this dressing is fabulous, I love Dill! This recipe written with sour cream is definitely the consistency of a dip, I replaced the sour cream with buttermilk which is still a thick dressing, but the flavors seem to hold together better on lettuce when it's not so thick.
As a dip this gets 5 stars - perfect! For dressing on a salad, I added 1/4 c. milk as it is quite thick.
Very thick but good. Will use buttermilk next time
Pretty good. If you want a dip for cut veggies - use the sour cream. If you want a dressing to drizzle over salad - use buttermilk.

I really quite enjoyed this recipe.  As others suggested, I used a 1/2 cup each of (light) mayo, yogurt (instead of sour cream), and buttermilk.  Also didn't have onion powder, so I ommmited.  However I did add MAYBE a 1/4 t celery salt (eyeballed it).  I think the flavor from the dill, parsley, and garlic powder are what really make it, in additon to the wet ingrediants already mentioned.  Play with the additional spices to your liking.  It was really very, very  delicious.  I could understand other's complaint about the consistency being too thick for a dressing.  That's a personal prefernce of course.  It will easily be thinned with more buttermilk.  A keeper!

I made this tonight and cut the recipe in half since it's just me and my husband. It was fantastic! I didn't have any sour cream, so I 'made' some buttermilk with 1 tablespoon of fresh lemon juice and 1/2 cup of half and half. I also added another teaspoon of lemon juice, but other than that I followed the recipe exactly. It was GREAT! Pretty thick, still, but great!
way better than store bought

This by far is so much better than bottled dressing. My husband who doesn't normally use ranch but does oil and vinegar raved about how good it was.  I enjoyed it too and will make it again. Our daughter, sadly she likes the other kind. ( I am thinking may be the dill, will try again for her without it).  Based on earlier reviews I used mayo, s. cream, and homemade buttermilk substitute (milk and vinegar).  I served it as a drizzle on Buffalo Chicken lettuce wraps, I used the same spice mixtures of the ranch with a spoonful of sour cream on the boneless chicken cut up pieces as I sauteed them in olive oil. - it was amazing on the chicken, Can't wait to eat the leftovers tomorrow! I will definitely make this dressing again.

I ran out of ranch and decided to try this recipe.  Wow, this was better than I was expecting.  I didn't have any dill weed handy so I used Basil instead and it came out pretty tasty.  I'll be making this again.
Exactly what I was looking for....the longer it sits the better it gets. Great recipe. I changed nothing.

Used 1/2 cup each of buttermilk, sour cream and mayo.  Skipped the dill (really dislike) and added more garlic powder.  Chilled for 4 hours, and thinned with milk before adding to a tossed green salad.  Delish!

Just mixed this and already it's the best I've tasted. Can't wait to try it after the flavors have melded. I did 3/4 cups of mayo, and 1/4 cup 2% milk, with the 1/2 cup of sour cream, and added a lid full of red wine vinegar. No onion powder but 1/2 tsp of garlic powder. Can't wait to have it on oven fries tonight. Thanks, this is just what I was looking for!

I am very happy with this Ranch Dressing recipe use the dressing on a daily basis.  It lends itself well to slight alterations like using plain yogurt instead of sour cream.  I also add some milk to thin it a bit to make it more pourable.
Excellent!!

I made this as a dip for a party. I did'nt have all the ingredieints, but I made some quick changes to suit what I had on hand. I used dehydrated onions instead of the dried chives, and I was out of dill weed, so I used dill pickle juice! I let it chill in the fridge for about 4 hours before the party. When I served it, there was a line to the dip, and halfway through the party, the bowl was EMPTY! Everyone raved about how good it was! I will definitely keep this recipe!

This is one of the best Ranch dressing recipes I've eaten!! The only thing I did different was add some buttermilk.. AMAZING! I REALLY dislike bottled ranch so this is always on hand for me! Thank you!

This is such a blessing. I have missed eatting ranch dressing for years because I can no longer have the hidden valley ranch dressing due to the MSG they put in the mix. I get horrible migranes from the stuff. But this is just awesome! Tastes wonderful and I am eatting more veggies now because of this wonderful dressing! Thanks so much!!
This recipe got mixed reviews.  My sister loved it...my brother wasn't all that impressed.  I thought it was good, but will try it with buttermilk next time.

Excellent. Use 1/2-3/4 cup buttermilk w/o the sour cream for a dressing.  Only gave it a 4 since you need to double the spices to give it some taste.  Let it sit for a few hours before serving. Add 1/4 tsp of cayanne red pepper for a little kick.

Great recipe, great flavor. I live in Australia where I haven't found any good American style ranch dressing, so I'm very glad I can make it myself now! I added 1/2 cup of milk to make the consistency more like dressing and less like dip. I also added a little bit more salt and a dash of lemon juice, just according to my personal tastes. So happy I found this!!

This is wonderful, and the only way to eat this is to let it SIT IN THE FRIDGE AS SOON AS POSSIBLE FOR AS LONG AS POSSIBLE. AT LEAST overnight. 30 minutes wasn't enough in my opinion. It was wonderful though, the next night after I made it. I made it exactly as it instructed.
Easy, quick, and tasty!

I, like many, have been raised on Ranch salad dressing. My mother used to buy the bottles of Ranch when I was in school, and at some point she started making the stuff out of the packets sold at the grocery stores. I, too, have been buying the packets, and making my own salad dressing for years. I thought it was getting old, and not to mention expensive (those packets or jars add up). So, I thought I would look around for a Ranch mix, and I came across this recipe.  This is a good version of Hidden Valley Ranch. It is a little bit on the milder side, so I do recommend using 1/2 cup mayo,  1/2 cup sour cream, and 1/2 cup of buttermilk (or you can substitute as an alternative 1/2 Tablespoon of white vinegar or lemon in bottom of 1/2 cup and fill milk to the top of container, and wait 5 minutes like I did). Also, I tweaked it a little by adding another 1/8 tsp of herbs, salt and pepper.  I strongly suggest this recipe, because you can do so much with it. Also, it gets better over time!
Very good! I cut the recipe in half, and used fresh chives.

I love this recipe!  The store bought dressings are loaded with sodium and this is a fabulous alternative.  My daughter loves it and will ask, Mom, where's the recipe were short on dip.  I haven't tried it as a dressing yet.  Thank you, thank you, thank you.
Just okay. Had to tweak quite a bit more than I really wanted to get some flavor. I did use 1/2 mayo, 1/2 sour cream, and 1/2 buttermilk but the dressing tasted very "sour creamy"

Absolutely wonderful!! I have been on a lactose free diet, longing for the taste of real Ranch dressing...I found that I can use a sour cream substitute (Sour Supreme) instead of sour cream. The blend of the herbs is perfect!!
Delicious just the way it is!

So good and easy to make, love that I always have all the ingredients on hand. I don't like dressings that taste too much like mayo, so I used 1 cup sour cream and 1/2 cup mayo, and it turned out perfect! I used it to dip Boneless Buffalo Wings from this site, along with carrot sticks and bell pepper. Delicious!
This was good-we thought it was missing something though and you have to thin with buttermilk-too thick. We liked it better as a dip then a dressing.
Very yummy!!  Added a little milk to thin it out to how I like it.
Love this!!!!!

I had made a salad for my family and realized I was out of ranch!!So I found this recipe I was in a hurry I ended up  adding  some milk to thin it out I did not have any dill or chives on hand so I used a couple of  tablespoons of  chive and onion cream cheese it was really good thanks!!

I have been looking for a Ranch Dressing for years.  This recipe is as close as I have gotten to perfect.  I made a few changes though, for our own personal taste.  I doubled the spices, except for the dill, which I cut back to about half.  I also used half a cup each of mayo, sour cream, and buttermilk.  It's best after it sits for a few hours in the fridge.  My entire family loves it and even our picky teenager who doesn't want to try anything new.  I stopped buying the bottled stuff since this is so much healthier without all of the chemicals.  So he had no choice but to try it.  Now he loves it and doesn't ask for the bottled stuff anymore.  Thanks so much for a wonderful recipe!!!

I made this one, Great dressing for chips, I did add 1/2 cup buttermilk to thin it. Still pretty thick with the buttermilk added. Little more buttermilk help to pour it from a bottle. The best recipe I have made today. My family loves it. Making a double dose of this only last 3-4 days in our home. Salad's, Chips and Crackers are enjoyed with it.
Had dried shallots instead of chives and used plain Greek yogurt instead of sour cream. Hubby and I both loved it as a dip.
We love this recipe at home. Quick and easy to make. We don't usually put cloves in it because of lack of cloves but still awesome!
I love this Ranch. It's easy and delicious.

I halfed the recipe and followed it exactly. I used sour cream. With the sour cream, it would probably be good as a veggie dip, but way too thick and sour cream tasting for a salad dressing...Next time I'll use buttermilk. I'm sure that will help with the consistency and the flavor. The spices seemed right on though.

This was great! I cannot believe how inexpensive homemade ranch is. I had fresh parsley on hand, but no dried, so i chucked that in instead and my dressing was BRIGHT GREEN. Oops. Delicious, though, and my husband really liked it.
It's simply the best!

Quick. Easy. Delicious. We add a good dash of milk to thin it down but it has all the taste that we love in Ranch. Really good to use for a BLT salad. Adds a kick of flavor to that already yummy BLT taste. I can sit and dip veggies while watching TV and have no snack guilt feelings. :)

Pretty close match to the most popular brand of dressing mix.  After making it a few times, I decided to tweak it a bit.  I prefer more sour cream flavor & wanted to lighten it up.  So I make mine with either light sour cream/plain greek yogurt & lowfat buttermilk (if I want a dressing) with just a spoonful of mayo.  Yum, yum!  Tastes best if it has a few hours or overnight to sit in the fridge before using...

I mix up a larger batch of the dry ingredients to keep on hand, then make a veggie dip or salad dressing by adding it to buttermilk, yogurt, sour cream and mayo..whatever your tastes prefer.  Can also add some celery salt, seasoning salt or a bit of cayenne for some zip.  I find dried minced onion adds more flavour than powder.  Once it's mixed it helps to sit for a few hours to really bring out the flavour.

5 7 17 ... http://allrecipes.com/recipe/16131/ranch-dressing-ii/ ... This is good; closest yet.  I just finished making it, like just-just finished.  It's already good.  I have high hopes.  I replaced half the mayo for buttermilk.  Sour cream was fatfree.  So far, so yum!  :)
I think this is FAR to mayo tasting .   We added parm cheese and it was better.   Thankfully we made it for a dipping sauce for chicken tenders, it was ok for those.
Pretty good.  Not quite "it" but all in all everyone enjoyed.  I used less mayo and more sour cream/buttermilk to cut the overpowering flavor that mayo can have.
WOW! This was delicious! I have always made Hidden Valley ranch with the packets. I have found a new replacement. WOOT WOOT!!!

Yum! My kids love ranch with everything, but I hate buying the stuff at the store, because it's got all kinds of additives and preservatives.  This is a perfect replacement--better than the store-bought. The 1st time I made it, I did it w/ just the mayo and the sour cream.  It was wonderful, but thick like a veggie dip.  And, it definitely tasted better after a night in the fridge. The 2nd time, I did 1/2 cup each of mayo, sour cream, and buttermilk.  Dressing perfection achieved! :) The 2nd time, I did 1/2 tsp. of the garlic and onion powders (instead of 1/4 tsp.).  I liked it better that way (& it's easier for me to remember when it's 1/2 tsp. all around. Hahaha!).  Great recipe with all the right herbs and flavors!  Thank you!

This is a great recipe.  Very easy and nothing artificial.  I use 1/2 cup mayo, 1/2 cup plain yogurt, and 1/2 cup sour cream to lower the fat content and it turned out really well.  I make it all of the time.

This is what I have been looking for!!  We go through a lot of ranch in our household, and I have been trying to find a homemade mix that is as good as the packaged, preservative laden kind that I buy at the store.  This is so good!!  Thanks a million!!  I didn't have chives on hand, so i doubled the onion powder and it was very tasty.  I will be getting chives on my next shopping trip so i can try the recipe exactly as written.
not bad, seemed more of a dip than a dressing but thinned out its just as good.
My new go to ranch, will never buy store bought again! I used equal amounts sour cream and mayo and upped the buttermilk to thin it out a bit.

This dressing is that unobtainable "restaurant dressing" that until now, I've not been able to purchase in grocery stores.  It's just so creamy.  The key for me with this recipe was *no buttermilk* - that's the common taste of store-bought dressings.  This recipe has changed my life and the frequency with which I eat salads at home.

I have made this dressing multiple times now. It tastes great. Store bought ranch dressings contain a lot of unwanted ingredients (such as soybean or canola oil), but I can make this healthy from scratch. Thanks alot!
Just what I needed for a dry powder seasoning ranch recipe - I simply omitted the dairy products.

Excellent taste, I really love the flavor of all of the spices combined and it really does taste like ranch!  If you want dressing you need to replace at least half of the sour cream with buttermilk otherwise it's very thick and more like a dip. I have also made this recipe as a veggie dip but instead of using the mayo and sour cream I used plain Greek yogurt and it was amazing, just another way to prepare this recipe but as written this recipe is still great!
Awesomeness!!  Never again will a bottle of ranch be brought into my household.  This is absolutely amazing.  Thanks for sharing!!

Good recipe, I like to use fresh parsley, dill and chives.  I always add extra dill because I like it that way.

I quite like this recipe with a few changes of my own and from those of other reviewers.  First I decreased the sour cream to only 1/4 c. as I thought the sour cream flavor was a little overpowering.  I added 1/2 c. buttermilk to the mayo and used 1/8 tsp. seasoned salt in place of the regular salt, I also added 1/4 tsp. vinegar as had been suggested and upped the garlic powder to 1/2 tsp.  With these changes I gave it 5 stars.  Thanks for the recipe, it is wonderful!

I thought this was an excellent recipe with the sour cream as I don't care for buttermilk. The only thing I changed was the dill, I left it out. I put in a little extra garlic powder, and my grandson loved it!

The search continues for a HVR substitute.  I made this recipe twice.  The first time as directed and it tasted like mayo and not much else.  The second time I modified it based on suggestions of other reviewers and used 1/2c mayo, 1/2c buttermilk and 1/2c sour cream.  This balanced the mayo flavor out but it was extremely bland.  I doubled all spices and it helped alot but it isn't anywhere close to steakhouse ranch or the stuff in the bottle which is what I wanted.
made with buttermilk - delicious!

finding this recipe after realizing I'm lactose intollerent was a life saver.  I love ranch and cannot live with out it.  this recipe taste just like ranch with soy sour cream, I just had to add 1/4 cup soy milk to make the consistancy right.

Have been doing Creamy Ranch Dressing for many years.  The one I make has a 1/4cup of milk in it. It is the most delicious.  The consistency is not runny like the store bought type. It keeps very well for weeks.

I think this is a very tasty recipe, you may have to adjust it for a dip or dressing, but overall I can't find ranch in Japan and this recipe is a wonderful addition with the current ingredients! Try it with cream cheese for a different spin!

I unfortunately couldn't find chives, dried or fresh, but otherwise I made this as written.  This recipe definitely improves with time.  The first night I could only taste the mayonaisse, but in a day or two the flavors blended nicely.  I also mixed some of this with extra dill, black pepper, onion, celery and chicken to make a great chicken salad sandwich.
Excellent.  Made it as written and then refrigerated it until I was ready to use it.  I then added milk to make it the consisistancy I liked.  Mmm Mmm...

I stopped buying ranch dressing because this is so good.  My daughter-in-law is hooked on it now also.  I add more dill because my husband & I love the taste of dill other than that I haven't altered the recipe at all.  I am going to experiment with it next time.

Changes I made- First, I make the Whole Egg Mayo from this site, then I proceed with this recipe- I skip the sour cream and chives (because I never have those on hand) and I use fresh parsley. YUM! It's great as a veggie dip or salad dressing.
LOVE it!  Great response from when I take it to gatherings, too.  Thin it for dressing, thicken for dip :)
Having just made this recipe,  I am wickedly irritated that I have bought Ranch dressing for the last 20 years.   This recipe is stupid easy, and is positively FANTASTIC.
Awesome recipe. Thanks!

I have this one memorized. I always keep these ingredients on hand. People are amazed when you tell them you make your own ranch, and that it's so easy! Waaaaay better than anything on the shelf. Add chipotle gravy, (from the chipotle chili cans) and poof, chipotle ranch! I just made another batch for the taco salads later, and I had to review this recipe. Thanks for making me look like I know what I'm doing in the kitchen! Lol, all my friends and co workers are amazed:)

I have been using this recipe for several years now.  I haven't bought ranch dressing since.  I add extra onion and garlic powder.  Today when I made it, I took the suggestion of another reviewer and added just a dash of white vinegar and what a difference it made.  It adds that little something that seemed to be missing.

"HOW" incredible is this recipe? Let me tell you! 1) I hate "Ranch Dressing" with every fibre of my being! I grew up before the current "Ranch Dressing Craze" and never understood the attraction.
