This is excellent and very easy.  I would definitely make this again.  The only change I made was I used fresh chives rather than dried as I didn't have any dried chives on hand.

I was just put on a low carb/low salt diet and this is just perfect.  I traded the sour cream for buttermilk and left out the salt and FELL IN LOVE!

I wanted to drink the leftovers out of the jar.  :P

I have never made ranch before and was wondering what went into it.  I began making this in October.  I have not bought bottled ranch since then!  My 9 year old will not eat any other salad dressing now!
This ranch dressing is awesome. I used lite mayo, fat-free sour cream, and low fat buttermilk to thin it out a little bit. It was great! I also added some cayenne pepper for a little spice.
I followed the advice of others and used buttermilk to thin this.  Everyone loved it and it is now a staple in the house.  THANK YOU!!!!!
Love it, this is a staple recipe for me. 1C mayo 1/2C buttermilk. No changes necessary, it is perfect.

YUMMY! Made as written, subbing buttermilk for the sour cream to get a more of a dressing for salad. I did add more than 1/2 cup to get it to the consistency that I wanted. Great flavor and very easy to make w/ things I always have on hand. Super close in flavor to the packet mix. Will def make again! Thanks for sharing. :)

I didn't have have ranch in the fridge for the chicken salad i made. Then i got on here looking and wala! I didnt have parsley or dill weed and it still came out great! I used a little milk to thin it a bit because it was too thick to pour.Love it.
Would be good as a ranch dip.
Very good!  I make this if I'm making a large batch that I know I want to keep around a while.  That way I don't have to worry about fresh ingredients spoiling.

I've made this recipe exactly as written and I've made the buttermilk version suggested by many reviewers.  It was wonderful both ways.  When I used the butter milk version of the dressing I was cooking for 60 people and I needed a dressing that would pour easily.  It was great. This dressing will be a staple at our house. Thank you!
Great, quick recipe for a simple, healthy dressing. Recommend thinning out with 1/4-1/2 cup olive oil if you'd like to pour instead of dip.

Great dressing! I used buttermilk but doubled the amount as other reviews said the dressing was too thick as is. We enjoyed it in the "Warm chicken ranch wraps" from this site: perfect mix of herbs and spices!
yummy! I made this exactly as the recipe says and used it as a dip for cut up veggies. It was a huge hit at the party.
This was excellent.  I used buttermilk instead of sour cream. Added a little extra to thin it some. Will definitely make it again. YUM!
Hi, i tried this recipe and it is really good it is much better than the bottled stuff and uit is closer to the resturant dressing but it is still missing something but i just dont know what it is...

Because I have a son who will only eat Hidden Valley dressing, I have been trying many recipes for homemade. I made this yesterday, with the changes posted by one reviewer, using 1/2c buttermilk, 1/2 mayo and 1/2c sour cream and increasing garlic to 1/2 tsp and my son said "pretty good" which means great! Probably even better today, I'll let you all know. Guess what!! better when it sets!Imagine!  And for a southwest kick, add 1/2C spicy salsa for a nice change.
This is delicious! I do add more garlic and onion powder than the recipe calls for. I get compliments on this every time I make it. People are always asking me for the recipe.

I've made this dressing many times. Absolutely no changes whatsoever! Ranch dressing is my hubby's favorite, and comments how much he loves it every time! NOTE: I double the recipe and store in a Food Saver canister. I keeps fresh for a very long time.

This was delicious!  Very similar to the good thick dressings (that sell for $2.99) that you buy in jars in the fresh produce section of the grocery stores.  And this is much much cheaper---plus it's homemade.  This is going to part of our Christmas dinner.  A keeper!

I thought this was pretty good, and would probably be a five if I had all ingredients on-hand. I used sour cream but added a TB milk or so, plus about a tsp of lemon juice. I would caution that even if you love garlic like I do, using too much in this recipe might not be the best idea. I added more garlic powder to make up for the fact I didn't have onion powder on-hand and it was too garlic-tasting for me.
Made this tonight, used some of the suggestions made by others and added about 1/8th tsp of cayenne pepper. Perfect! Much better than bottled ranch.
I think the sour cream in this recipe is what messes things up, but this ranch taste very watered down and pretty tasteless.

This is BY FAR the BEST ranch dressing ever. I read reviews and the  thing I did differently  was ( at the suggestion of others) add  2% milk and vinegar because I didn't have the buttermilk. Some reviewers said they would never buy ranch from the store again and I'm with them. I taste it right after I made it and I said; This is delicious, so  I let my 9 year old taste and he said  this is better than delicious and better than Hidden Valley and I couldn't agree more. No more on the shelf ranch for us. I told my sister it's so good I may take it with me to restaurants if I know the ranch is not that great. If I could give it 10 stars I would!!!!

Thank you for this recipe. I've just eliminated buying the dressing. My family will only eat this now and it's encouraged them to take veggies to school too. What an incentive to make this. I did make some adjustments; reversed the ratio of sour cream to mayo, added some finely minced scallions and onion, increased the quantity of parsley and garlic powder. Definitely a great addition to my recipe box collection.
This was Excellent!!! Sooo much better than store bought. I couldnt believe that so few ingre. made such great dressing. Thank you!
since it's pretty thick, I'll add a splash of milk next time.  Wonderful flavor though!

Huge hit with the wife and kids (me too :-) ). It is definitely a ranch dip...swap the sour cream for buttermilk for a salad dressing. Also, I used the spices as purely a ratio guide between the spices and upped the qty for our family's taste (about 1.5x). Excellent base recipe.

This is a great basic recipe.  I made just as the recipe states and I found two huge flaws.  First off, it's more of a dip than a dressing.  It's thick.  And let me tell you, we normally like our dressing thicker than thin.  We found that this dressing was even too thick for us.  Next, it was really bland.  I will make this again but with play around with it until I can get it right.  More seasonings, less mayo and maybe add some milk to thin it just a bit.

I had gotten some free sour cream last week or so and wasn't about to let it go to waste, but didn't know what to do with it. I've never made homemade salad dressing before, but let me tell you I've never eaten my salad that fast! I used extra onion because I didn't have chives, made a few other to-taste adjustments of the final product, and it turned out great!
Ran out of the ranch mix, so threw this together in a pinch.  I didn't have dried chives, used 2 fresh chopped green onions instead.  Very good.
This was delicious!  I modified to fit what I had on hand and used light mayo and sour cream.  I used no chives, dil weed, or onion powder. I doubled the garlic powder and added paprika.
Too much dill flavor for me the first time I made it but easily adjusted to. Best flavor/consistency with buttermilk added!
A very good recipe that's easy to adjust to personal taste. I took the recommendations to use 1/2 mayo and 1/2 cup buttermilk. I thought it was great!

Based on other reviews, I used 1/2 cup sour cream, mayo and buttermilk. Increased salt to 1/4 tsp. I did not have dill weed and perhaps this explained the lack of "punch" but overall very good. Will continue to experiment to please the home crowd.

The recipe was good, but I also added a 1/2 cup of buttermilk. It seemed a little bland so I added a 1/2 tsp each of the spices and it still seemed a little bland. I then added some lemon pepper seasoning and that was exactly what it needed. A good base recipe, but since I had to add ingredients it only gets 4 stars.

I was looking for a home made ranch dressing recipe and this fit my needs perfectly.  I used low-fat buttermilk in place the the sour cream.  I didn't have garlic powder, so substituted garlic salt and omitted the salt.  I whipped this up in my food processor since I had it out.  I think that next time I may try to make this with home-made mayonnaise so that I can totally get rid of any preservatives in the mayo.  Thanks Dawnia for sharing!

Not a bad recipe.  I did adjust it a bit and used 1/2 cup each sour cream, mayo, and buttermilk.  It had a pretty good flavor, although I found the dill to be a bit too strong for my personal preference.  I would make it again though and reduce the dill and increase the garlic and onion powders.  Definitely a good base recipe for Ranch dressing that you can play around with and personalize to your own liking and so much better than the bottled stuff in the stores.

This recipe was great but I had many changes.  I had 3/4 c. mayonnaise instead of a full cup, I added an extra 1/4 c. of sour cream.  I added 1/2 c. buttermilk and 1 tsp. lemon juice.  I easily doubled or even tripled the amount of garlic.  The recipe could have used more salt and pepper to taste.  This recipe was a great starting point for a great ranch dressing.
The spice combination is excellent! Thanks for the dressing. Much nicer than store bought

I use this recipe for vegetable dip. We love it. To make it healthier I use 3/4 cup plain yogurt and 3/4 cup of sour cream instead of the mayo. Always turns out great. Best if it sits a night or two in the fridge.

I ran across this recipe when looking for a dressing to add to sliced cucumbers this summer. I did make it with buttermilk instead of sourcream and diced dried onions instead of onion powder. It was wonderful, and since have replaced my favorite bottled Ranch dressing with this. Thanks for the recipe!
to dilly tasting

I make a large batch of this and it keeps well in the fridge for a month.  This is very good.  Store bought salad dressings usually have additives so finding an easy, delicious and healthy recipe is very important to me.

I make this a lot, It's good as is but like everyone says you HAVE to thin this out with milk or buttermilk for it to be a dressing. After a while making it I also used more herbs like 1t. instead of 1/2 and I think I used 1t. of everything except the chives and SNP

I have been making this for about a year now and I no longer like the HVR bottled salad dressing that I LOVED for probably 25 years.  This recipe is delicious, I make it exactly as written.  It is so quick and easy and I always have all the ingredients on hand.  Perfection!  Thank you Dawnia!  10 stars plus!

Like many here, I altered this recipe a bit. For the base, I use 1 c mayo, 1/2 c buttermilk (lowfat is fine), and 1/4 c sour cream. (I did go 1/2 lite mayo and 1/2 c regular mayo to cut down on the fat and didn't notice a difference in taste from the 1 c whole mayo). For the herbs, I use fresh chives, dill, parsley, and crushed garlic in a jar rather than the dried herbs recommended in the recipe. I am very liberal with the dill and chives. I agree with others that it does taste better after some time in the fridge. I think time allows the oils in the herbs to leach out and blend with the base. I have been a ranch dressing fan my whole life, and have never been able to purchase or recreate the ranch found in many restaurants until now. Fantastic recipe :-)
The whole family loved this!

Simply awesome! I can choose between two different type of Sour Creams. The lighter(cheaper too) version which is also the more creamy, is the perfect one for this recipe. Otherwise I did everything exactly according to instruction. I love Parsley and Chive so much, therefor decided to doubled the amount on them. This Dip will from now on be the most of the time to find in our fridge. I just found a way to make a homemade  Mayonnaise. I think this will make this recipe even better. That's a 5 Star recipe for me. Simple, inexpensive and unbelievable good taste.

Fabulous!  I used the lowest fat mayonnaise available (with just 25 cal/Tbsp) and fat-free sour cream (just 25 cal/2 Tbsps).  I also used fresh dill, dried minced onion, and fresh minced garlic, all for stronger flavor.  I will never buy the bottled stuff again!
This was a hurricane Matthew snack! I've never made ranch but I love this recipe. The fam ate all the cheese fries I made and the cats finished up the ranch. All are full and happy!
Easy and delicious.  This will be my favorite homemade dressing and dip from now on.
This was excellent!  I used 1/2 c mayo, 1/2 c sour cream, fresh green onions, fresh parsley, fresh garlic and skipped the dill.
Perfect. Used 1/2 mayo 1/2 sour cream and 1/2 heavy cream because that is what I had. Next time I will use buttermilk but heavy cream worked fine. Also used 2tsp fresh chives. Yum!

I never thought I'd find a Ranch Dressing recipe that beat every store bought dressing hand down!
This is the one!  So good it should be illegal!!!  Thank You!
This recipe tastes authentic. It was fresh and delicious. I would recommend letting it refrigerate for at least 4 hours though and definitely use buttermilk. Excellent!
LOVE this flavor.  Just a hint of dill.  Family loved it!  Thinned it with a touch of half and half.

Bottled dressings aren't even close to hanging with this homemade version! I loved it! I used buttermilk and also used fresh chives. It is imperative to let it chill in the fridge for a while. Just after making it, I tried it and it tasted "mayonnaisey." But after three hours it just tasted great! Thanks for the recipe, it is definetly a keeper.

While not the best Ranch dressing I've ever had, this was pretty decent nonetheless. On the contrary, my parents liked this a LOT! Every time I invite my parents over for dinner, I try to serve a fresh salad on the side - and try a new dressing to go with it. My dad has never been a "greens" fan, but due to his health, he's on a heart-restrictive diet. If I can show him that healthy foods can be flavorful, I've made a stride in the right direction. :) This really doesn't taste like Ranch at all, IMHO. It's very sweet compared to most Ranch dressings I've tried (store-bought / restaurants). Perhaps it was the generic brand mayonnaise I bought or the substitution of buttermilk for sour cream??? Next time I'll stick with my gut and make what jumps out at me first. Sarah Jo's no-guilt zesy Ranch dip / dressing sounds far more interesting and now I know why.... Thanks anyways, Dawn. :)

This is great.  I used buttermilk instead of the sour cream and left out the chives as I didn't have any.  I also substituted tarragon for the dill weed (I didn't have any of that either.  Still was great.
Perfect!  I'll never buy the bottled dressing or the powdered mix again!
YUM. I'll eat my veggies now!! I hate store bought ranch that maintains the shape of the dish it's sitting in, and doesn't dilute with water added to it--freaks me out a bit. This stuff---excellent!

I was excited to make this recipe as I love ranch dressing & making it at home without all the preservatives is always appealing. I just got done with it, and of course, I had to taste it before I put it in the fridge. I didn't want a thick veggie dip, so I followed someone elses advice and used 1/2 cup mayo, 1/2 cup milk, and 1/2 cup sour cream. It ended up like ranch water! VERY runny, so I added in a little more mayo. It doesn't have the taste I was hoping for. The aftertaste tastes more like ranch than when you first put it in your mouth. Maybe I should have used buttermilk, and I will try it again that way. But as for the way it is now, I will not be making it like that again. It's pretty though!!!!
Awesome recipe, I made my own buttermilk and used that instead of sourcream.
It was tasty and easy to make

This ranch has a really good flavor. I'm not really a dill fan, so I'll cut down on that next time, and it was a little too thick for me, so, as another reviewer suggested, I will replace the sour cream with buttermilk in the future. A really nice change from other Ranch dressings though.
it is good.

I have never tried to make homemade ranch dressing before and I don't know why, not only was it easy but delicious. My granddaughter who is the ranch snob absolutely loved this...so did everyone else.
This dressing is great.  I will never buy another bottle of Ranch dressing again.  And so simple to prepare!

I have finally found the perfect ranch dressing! The ones purchased at grocery stores or eaten at restaurants are never the same - too sour, too much vinegar, too sweet, too creamy, etc. However this recipe is consistent and delicious every time I make it. It does get better a couple hours in the fridge. Thanks for the recipe!

I substituted buttermilk I had leftover from making butter and all fresh herbs from the garden.  GREAT! Very easy recipe and I will never buy ranch dressing ever again!  (I added some horseradish one night for a little extra kick, which also came out pretty good)  The next night I added cilantro to some of the ranch and used it as a taco topping.  This made for the best tacos ever!

Awesome recipe! 
Wife took the salad dressing to work with her, so I had to improvise, never made it before.. Dang was this gooooood.. I did not have dill weed, and it was still good without it! Made it like the recipe, just thinned it with milk to consistency I wanted.. Without thinning it would be great dip! Saving this for the future, way better than store bought.

I stopped buying store bought ranch a while ago due to the added MSG. My kids and I have missed it. So I found this recipe, made it, and it is delicious. I added some extra chives, onion and garlic powder for our tastes, and it is so yummy! This will be a staple in our fridge from now on.
I had high hopes for this but even after letting it sit in the fridge for a couple of days it still tasted way to much like mayo.

This is a quick & easy recipe, and very tasty. I agree that fresh herbs prob'ly make it better, but there's nothing wrong with using dried. I've been cooking for 45 years and I'm here to tell you there isn't that much difference, if the dressing is allowed an hour in the fridge to marry the flavors. I think the mixture of mayo & sour cream is a good one, because a lot of people don't have fresh buttermilk on hand every day.

Love it! I found this recipe when I got tired of the greek and  raspberries salad dressings (found also here).
 I added double the dill, and used fresh parsley (besides the dry) and green onions (didn't have the chives). After trying it out once I ran to get buttermilk, and used 1/2 sour cream 1/2 buttermilk. Yummm, husband loves it.

Oh my, this is a really wonderful recipe.  To cut the fat I used light Best Foods mayo & light sour cream.  I also added a squirt of extra virgin olive oil and red wine vinegar - everyone loved it and were amazed that it was lowfat.

This dressing is awesome!  I don't have any onion powder, so I double up the garlic powder.  The dill really gives it a wonderful taste.  I also used this dressing to dip carrots and make Ranch chicken with.  Dip your chicken in, roll in bread crumbs, and bake!  It's excellent!  Thanks for a great recipe!
So much better than the bottled stuff! Thanks for sharing!
I added a 1/4 cup of nonfat milk. Delicious recipe. Will definitely make again!

Awesome! I'm never buying a bottle of ranch again! The first time I made this I followed the recipe as is and it is thick but full of flavor. The next time I made it I followed the suggestion of some other reviewers and added 1 tbsp lemon juice to thin it out just a little and it is perfect! Thank you for this amazing recipe=)
I really liked this recipe.  I made it out of desperation when I found I didn't have any bottled dressing but ended up liking it so much that I still haven't bought another bottle of dressing.
Love it.  I changed the 1/2 C of sour cream to 1/3 C, and added 1/3 buttermilk.  Also added 1/4 teaspoon of tarragon, a little cayenne, and Worcestershire.
Good stuff! Substituted red for black pepper to add a little extra kick.

I make a healthier version with 1 cup non-fat yogurt and 2 tbs mayo, and I replace the onion powder with fresh grated onion (which prevents it from tasting yogurty).  Any time I make this dressing, I end up stuffing myself with so much of it on top of raw veggies that I end up losing a pound or two from not being able to consume much else -- it's that good.

I didn't like this dip when I first mixed it up, but after it set overnight and took on the flavours of the herbs, it was awesome! I had it with celery sticks and also dipped baked potato fries in it. Yum! Thanks!
My husband and I did not find this dressing to be very tasty, I tried adding more spices and still did not find it to have much flavor. We won't be making this one again.

I prepared this with the dried herbs as listed using lowfat mayo and nonfat sour cream.  After letting it sit for a few hours I did a taste test and choose to up the pepper, chives and dill based on personal tastes.  This one will be a keeper for my family, it's great!
It was pretty good. I didn't have sour cream, so I used plain yogurt and thinned it out with milk. My daughter loved it.
I made as is with a little white vinegar for some bite.  Excellent!

I've been looking for a simple ranch recipe, and this fit the bill. I made it with buttermilk instead of sour cream, and substituted 1 tbsp fresh herbs for the dried. A few hours after I made it, it was good. The next day, it was awesome. Definitely let it sit overnight.

This rach dressing was really good, but it was quite thick, more like a dip then a salad dressing.  the next time I make it I think I will modify it a bit and use buttermilk to make it thinner.  The spices were perfect.  I will definitly use this recipe again.

I thought this recipe was very good with a minor change--I used 1/2 cup of each low fat mayonaise, low fat sour cream and low fat buttermilk.....DH love it!  I no longer will be buying bottled stuff.....thank you!
everybody at church loved it.  i originally made it for my fried pickles that we served, but someone made a veggie tray so it got used for that too.

Great recipe...unbelievably better than the Ranch you get in the supermarket...and really easy. Have tried it with non-fat sour cream as well as reduced-fat. Both were good. Also tried it with reduced fat mayo and no mayo. Same results...very tasty. Best to let it rest for an hour or so before serving. Very very good...thanks!

I love, love, love this recipe for Ranch dressing! I cannot stand to eat the stores' shelf varieties anymore after having this. Thank you for sharing a great recipe! (I do use half mayo and half sour cream per my own liking)

Pretty good...I took others advice and used a mixture of sour cream, buttermilk and mayo...along with a tsp of veg. oil for consistency.  Iused the same measurments of spices but I think for next time I would use a little less dill, it was a bit over powering.
We LOVE this dressing.  It is VERY good on a vegetable salad topped with chicken and shredded cheese!  We make this a lot.

I use buttermilk instead of sour cream and use fresh parsley and chives from my garden, a dill seasoning blend instead of dill, garlic and onion powder because the blend has all three.  My husband was never a big ranch dressing fan until I started making this recipe.  I've used it on salads and as the "sauce" for pasta salad with fresh cucumber and cherry tomatoes.  Delicious!

I made this recipe vegetarian by substituting the sour cream with tofu, blended it in the food processor and served it with assorted veggies during the holidays. Everyone loved it, even the kids! I didn't get to it soon enough to try it and had to scrape the bottom of the bowl just to get a taste.
Overall very good.... did add a bit of extra garlic for a little more flavor.
Very good, I make it a lot! I put a dash of rice wine vinegar in, give it a touch more zing!
I used 1/2 c sour cream, 1/2 cup buttermilk, and 1/2 cup mayo, and a bit more dill than it called for, and it was a lovely, fresh alternative to bottled dressing.  Thanks!
was looking for a recipe to make closer to natural....this was very good.  I used plain yogurt instead of the sour cream and a more healthy mayo with flax.  This one's a keeper!
Delicious.  My daughter tried it and wanted the recipe, also.  Thank you for sharing!  I did use buttermilk instead of sour cream for the dressing, will use sour cream in a dip.  Yummy!

Love, Love, Love! As written this is the best ranch dressing I have tried! I usually make a double batch for parties and serve with veggies and chips, and it's never enough. I used fresh parsley and fresh green onions (instead of chives) from the garden and sometimes make it lighter by adding Greek yogurt. Had to write a review as this is my favorite dipping ranch and salad dressing (thin down with a little milk or water for salads) and I make it quite often. Best part about making it from home is that there is no MSG!

I gave this recipe 4 stars because of the modification I made, but the result was the best ranch dressing I've ever tasted. I considered the modifications of other members and used the following:
Added 1 tsp Olive Oil
Added 1/4 cup grated parmesan
Added 1 TSP white wine vinegar (it was flat without this addition)
Doubled the herbs and spices
Used 1/2 cup each mayo, sour cream, buttermilk
Added 1TBSP lemon juice

With these modification, the dressing was wonderful. I won't use store bought again.

really good! i am in europe so it is often hard for me to find your typical american dressings and sauces. i made this one, even though i couldnt find all of the spices, and it still turned out great. thanks!
This is a quick and simple recipe with ingredients you normally have in the kitchen.  I use it just the way posted for dips and then out some with milk, buttermilk for a pourable dressing.  Try it!

Living in England I found my self "stocking up" on Hidden Valley packages when coming home on Holiday.  Never again.  This recipe is Fab.  A bit thick for my liking but a little milk did the trick.  My family loved it and it was soon gone.
Goes great with cold Salmon and cucumber
great basic recipe. I use fresh herbs when I have them, and usually do equal mayo and sour cream.
Fabulous was out of Ranch Dressing, the family favorite and made this.  They all loved it.  Great Recipe to have around.

Holy cow!!! I am so impressed. I was out of chives and it was still fantastic! It's pretty thick so it makes a great dip for potato skins or cheese fries. For salads, just add buttermilk until desired consistency. Great recipe!

In a pinch, I will make this recipe again because it contains all the ingredients I already have in my pantry.  Flavor is good but it's a little too thick for salad.  You may need to thin it out....not sure how yet. :)  It works best as a dip...wings, carrots, etc.  Thank you Dawnia.

I just mixed up this dressing, and it's fine, there's no problem with it. But the description states "...no sharp notes in this buttermilk and mayonnaise dressing", except there's no BUTTERMILK in it! It's fairly thick with just mayo and sour cream, so I might thin it with some buttermilk, but I'm wondering if perhaps the buttermilk was accidentally left out of this recipe?

I have made this several times and I we love it!  I use Plain Greek yogurt in stead of Sour Cream and reduce the mayo slightly (I am a trial and error cook (why I don't bake).  I also add a teaspoon of Dijon Mustard and a 1/2 teaspoon of olive oil and a splash of apple-cider vinegar.  Double the recipe so you can store it in the coldest part of your refrigerator (good on steamed veggies too)!

Excellent recipe! I subbed buttermilk for the sour cream and did have to add a bit extra to get a consistency I liked. I didn't have chives so instead used green onions and as per another reviewer's suggestion, I added about 1/4 tsp of olive oil to make it a little smoother. We've also taken to adding a couple tsps of fresh Parmesan.

I gave it 4 stars because I tweaked the recipe for consistency. I found it was too thick , so I use less mayo and add some buttermilk.  The herb blend is delicious mixed into a bar of cream cheese and a little milk -1 tbls. It makes a great spread for crackers, Leftovers, if there are any, would be great on a fluffy baked potato.

Thanks for sharing.

I don't buy ranch dressing anymore!  This is a great recipe.   I've made it using 1c buttermilk (or 1 TBSP white vinegar and enough milk to make 1 cup) to it to make it thinner, and it turned out great.
This was a great Ranch dressing!  One of the best I've tried.  I halved the sour cream and made up the difference with buttermilk.  The buttermilk made it into a dressing instead of a dip.

Great. I didn't have sour cream, so I used nonfat plain yogurt. To bring up the "zing" I added some dried buttermilk powder. I also didn't have any dried parsley, so I used dried cilantro (which is REALLY bland, not like fresh) and it mimicked parsley quite well.
Very good ranch dressing.  Using other reviewer's tips, I used 1/2 c. mayo, 1/2 c. sour cream, & 1/2 c. buttermilk.  Perfect consistency.

Excellent recipe and a giant leap from the funky, chemical taste of bottled dressing. I used the 1/2 c. mayo, 1/2 c. s.cream, 1/2 c. buttermilk formula that other reviewers had success with and it was still a little on the thick side for salad dressing but the perfect dip consistency (think Buffalo wings & celery!). Of course, it can be thinned with add'l buttermilk or olive oil. I used it as part of the Rosemary Ranch Chicken Kabob recipe posted on this site as well as on a garden salad and it was wonderful for both. Thanks!!!

I followed the recipe using the adjustments Christy E. had suggested.  I didn't have onion powder so finely chopped a teaspoon of onions instead. The dressing was good but lacked something.  I'm not sure what but will make it again with onion powder and a dash of hot sauce to give it more umph.
Dawnia - this ranch dressing is awesome!  Thanks.
i like it!! tasty

This was good - but not the bottled Ranch. I did substitute milk for the sour cream, so it wouldn't be too thick. It made for a nice change, and a very light tasting dressing, but don't make this if you are wanting "Ranch" dressing.
I am a die hard Ranch Dressing fanatic.  This is by far the BEST ranch dressing I have ever had.  I don't like to eat the bottled stuff anymore.  This is AWESOME!!!
used fresh dill.
Excellent replacement for the powdered packets. It's much cheaper and there's no preservatives or garbage going into it. I used this to make beer dip and it came out fantastic.

This is the only recipe I use for ranch. I don't buy store-ranch anymore. What I do slightly different is use 2 cups mayo, 3/4 cups sour cream, 1/4 cup water then double the seasonings. Makes a good family-size amount (salads, tacos, dip for fries, veggies and chicken strips, etc.).

This is outstanding. Never again will I buy Hidden Valley Ranch. It tastes just like it, only better, fresher, and of course, cheaper! I didn't have any dried chives or onion powder. I didn't think the amount of dill was overpowering at all, as some other reviewers have suggested. I only used about 3/4 cup mayo, and added about 1/2 cup buttermilk which thinned it down to a consistency suitable for a salad dressing and gave it delicious flavor. Wonderful recipe, Dawnia!
Good stuff.  A little too much dill for my taste, so I added more chive and garlic.
This recipe is wonderful!  I never have to buy store made ranch dressing again!

This is delicious and easy!  Turned out nice and thick and not "vinegar" tasting like so many are.  The only thing I changed is that I added 1Tb. lemon juice to thin it out a little.  If you want to use it as a pour-on dressing, you might want to add a little milk to thin it out more but if you mix the salad in a bowl before serving, I found that the moisture from the salad itself automatically  dilutes it to the right consistency.  The dressing actually clings to the salad and doesn't end up at the bottom of the bowl!
Used as is for dip, was fantastic (changes: cut mayo in 1/2, didn't have any chives, put in an extra shake of garlic). Will thin with buttermilk for salad dressing tomorrow.  Can't wait!
Very easy to make usually I don't keep buttermilk but this dressing doesn't use it...Love it and so have others that I've made it for.
Delicious tasting as is, but is way too thick. I added about a 1/2-2/3 cup milk to thin it out enough to pour and it was still very thick. Also added about a tablespoon of red wine vinegar.

I made this to go with some buffalo wings and it turned out pretty great!  I didn't have any buttermilk or sour cream so I used 1/4th cup of half and half with a table spoon of softened butter and 1 tsp of white vinegar. I also upped the salt, garlic and onion powder for more flavor. The consistency is creamy and tastes just like restaurant style ranch!! I will definitely make it again in the future!

An excellent ranch dressing. I personally found the dill flavor to be overpowering (and I really like dill). It was so strong in proportion to the other seasonings that I could taste little else. For those who claim to have made buttermilk from scratch adding a lemon juice or vinegar to milk does not make buttermilk. It makes sour milk. It is a fine substitute for buttermilk. It is not buttermilk though.

 To make buttermilk from scratch you have to make butter and then use the remaining liquid. That is what buttermilk is. The milk left after making butter. Hence the name buttermilk.

I used about 1/4 cup each of mayo, sour cream & buttermilk and decreased the spices, also. It was so good!! Will def make this again & again as it was not difficult at all!!
was ok but too thick to put on a salad

Thank you for this recipe. I'm going to a dinner party tonight at some new friends house. I was asked to bring a garden salad. I want to make a good impression. I replaced the sour cream with buttermilk, and added 1/2 teaspoon of vegetable oil. I doubled the recipe and it taste perfect.
Delicious! I no longer by the bottled stuff. Thank you for sharing the recipe.
Very good ranch recipe.  As recommended by Christy, I substituted the 1 cup mayo with 1/2 cup mayo & 1/2 cup buttermilk.

I realized after mixing 1 cup may and 1 cup buttermilk that I couldnt find the ranch dressing mix I had bought so I found this recipe and put the spices together and added it to my mayo/buttermilk and it turned out awesome!  I will be using this from now on.

This was very easy to make and far superior to any brand of bottled ranch I've ever tried.  I used 1/2 cup of regular mayo, 1/2 cup of low-fat buttermilk, and 1/2 cup of sour cream.  As a matter of personal preference, I also reduced the dill slightly.  I'll be using this recipe again.
We love this dressing.  Served it at our party last night and it was a hit.

VERY Good. My standard is "O'Charley's"  Ranch dressing, and this comes pretty close. ( I did substitute the sour cream with buttermilk). Certainly less expensive! Will now make my own ranch dressing!!
Consistency was great, I just thought the dill was a little overpowering (and I like dill).  Next time I'll reduce it.  I added about 1/3 cup of buttermilk.
This is very nice. I always use the buttermilk instead of the sour cream.

There is another clone that I took some advice from, and that's to add a little accent or msg. The flavor seems to fade after a day or 2. Although, its pretty darn close to what we are all looking for, and I think its Hidden Valley. I keep the dry ingredients mixed and ready. Certainly saves you $$. Those packets are expensive! NOTE: I think I'll cut down on the dill and up the garlic and onion powder. Thanks for the recipe, defintite keeper.

I was making hotwings and celery and needed a dipping sauce/dressing. How clever this recipe ... no need for buttermilk! I didn't have dehydrated chives, nor sour cream. I substituted with a tiny bit of chopped red onion and full fat Greek yogurt.  Tangy and full flavored. Great recipe!
Made it s few times as is and it is perfect. This time I added some buttermilk to thin it out a little bit and it turned out great!

I've been using this for months. This is great stuff. You won't buy bottled ranch ever again. Made the recipe exactly as written. The longer it sits the more the flavors blend. I highly recommend this recipe.

One of the most satisfying things about this recipe is when someone says, "That's homemade, isn't it?"  Even if you look at it as a bunch of dried spices, it doesn't taste like it came out of a bottle, or one of those little packets.  Yea!
Was very good. Taste more like a dip than a dressing. I will make it again, but it will not replace my bottled Ranch.
Super easy and good!

I am still tweaking to perfection, but this is a major find!  All of the bottled ranch dressings without MSG taste horrible.  This is yummy, yummy, yummy and easy!  No chopping, just mixing.  Thank you!
I made this in place of Ranch dressing. I LOVED it, it had a much  better taste, and my kids even loved it with their pizza rolls.

Just what I was looking for!  All 3 of my kids gave it "thumbs up".  So good.  I did change a few things according to other reviewers.  Doubled the recipe and used 1 cup light Mayo, 1 cup buttermilk and 1 cup sour cream.  Added more garlic powder than 1/2 tsp, probably a full teaspoon. Used minced onion instead of chives and left out the dill weed.  Used my hand blender to mix.  If I would have known it was this easy I would have been making it long before now!

Quick, easy and delicious.  Clean fresh taste. Great base recipe to make variations of  different salad dressings and/or taste. Most important, my kids are crazy about it and ask for salads so they can have the ranch salad dressing.

This was my first attempt at homemade ranch. It was great! I could not believe how easy it was and tasted just like the "official" packaged stuff, better-fresh.  I did not have chives, didn't miss them. I added a drop of lemon juice to help preserve it in the fridge. Good recipe!!!

I won't buy bottle dressing again (if I can help it!)  This has wonderful flavor.  I did as others suggested and made with buttermilk.  Other than that, the recipe can stand on its own.  I'm going to try to keep ingredients in the house so I can make this regularly - Thank you Dawnia!

I used lowfat sour cream and mixed lowfat and regular mayo to make one cup.  Without all the salt found in packaged mixes, the flavor of the dressing really comes through.  This is delicious both as a dressing and a dip.  Edit:  I now make this with all fresh herbs as a dip and it is over the top delicious.

My daughter and I have been searching for a simple basic ranch dressing and this was fantastic!  The consistency was more like a vegetable dip but by adding a little milk or buttermilk, you can thin it out enough for salad dressing.  I like to have this on hand for a healthy veggie dip snack and will only thin out some for salads on an as-needed basis.  Thank you so much for this recipe!!!!

I used for Sue's Taco Salad on this site. I wanted to use what I had on hand as well as make it healthier. I didn't need to make so much so I used 1/4 c light mayo, 1/4 c Fage Greek yogurt and 1/4 cup homemade Kefir milk. Adding to this 1/4 t garlic powder and dill weed. Good flavor and made a nice topping for the taco salad.
Great recipe!, i did do 1/2 c mayo and 1/2 c buttermilk for our east texas taste buds and it was fantastic!

I'm not a ranch person, so we never have it on hand. My husband wanted some last night when he was making fried chicken, and I found this recipe. Super easy, and he said that it was "legit," and I could serve it in a restaurant. Since he has probably ordered ranch at every restaurant he's ever been to, I think I'll keep this recipe on hand! Thank you so much for sharing!

Took Christy's advice with the spices but didn't add any buttermilk not oil as i wanted it to be more of a ranch dip vs. dressing.   also, substituted  miracle whip for the mayo and used fresh chives.  turned out amazing! took it to a potluck and was being asked left and right for the recipe.  THANKS!!

Finally a junk free (say anything I can’t pronounce) homemade ranch dip/dressing (depending if you’d like to add a bit of milk/buttermilk) that is just amazing! I’m letting my daughters all know about this one. YUM!
loved better than store bought ddressing.

Just when I had given up hope of ever finding a ranch dressing that doesn't contain MSG I find this! (May I suggest everyone research MSG-it's awful for our bodies) Thank you soooo much for sharing this recipe!!! I'm so excited!!
This recipe was incredible.  I substituted the sour cream for buttermilk, and it was delicious.  It was still thick enough to dip vegetables in, and I think it would also work as a salad dressing.

I never ever considered making my own ranch dressing until this site. I somehow stumbled upon this recipe and decided to give it a try for my party last night. We used this for fried chicken wings and a veggie platter. It was a hit. Everyone was surprised that I made it from scratch. I really, really enjoyed this recipe. This one is a keeper. Thanks!
Very good flavor and super easy.  This would be a great dip.  I added a little milk to thin a bit to make a dressing.

I know I may be beating a dead horse, but this ranch dressing is fantastic! I mixed about 8 batches worth of seasoning together and added about 3 teaspoons of the finished seasoning with the cup of mayo and 1/2 cup of buttermilk. I knew this dressing was delicious when I had to go out and immediately purchase veggies just to dip in it, but I had no idea I would be polishing off the whole batch in one weekend. I usually only purchase Hidden Valley Ranch, but this dressing is like a gourmet restaurant ranch and is far superior. I even tried to use up the rest of the HVR I had in the fridge after finishing this and almost gagged at the taste of that bottled stuff. I definitely recommend letting this dressing sit overnight as to allow the flavors to mingle and the dried herbs to reconsitute (if you can let it sit that long!) Truly addicting!!!

I'm giving this 3 stars, not because it wasn't good, but because I don't believe that this tastes like a true ranch dressing.  The dill overpowers the other flavors but that is just my opinion.  I did enjoy using the recipe as a dip for chips and pretzels.  I will try it again with less dill next time to see if it's the flavor that I associate with ranch.  Thanks!
Great to replace the chemical filled bottles that go by the name of Ranch Dressing.  Took 2 minutes in the blender - I used kefir instead of sour cream.  Yummy

For someone who doesn't even like Ranch Dressing, this recipe has changed my mind.  It was so good.  I didn't change anything to this recipe.  Made it as is.  Since I was going to mix in into a salad and serve, I didn't add the milk to loosen the consistency.  However, when I had left overs and need it to be more "pourable" I added milk as needed (1T at a time) and it did the trick.  This dressing is a big hit and would definitely make you STOP buying store bought.

This is amazing! I used buttermilk to make dressing rather than dip. It's delicious, the kids loved it, my husband loved it, I loved it. Will definitely make this again.

Only one "gripe", this is the only food I've ever encountered that LOSES flavor with time. I put it in the fridge overnight, thinking the flavor would intensify, but nope, when I took it out the next day, it tasted kinda bland. So be prepared to season some more the next day.
It was delicious. Substituted sour cream for mayo, and didn't have chives so substituted dried onions instead.
Awesome recipe!  So simple!  I made this exactly to the directions (with sour cream), and I wouldn't change a single thing!  I used this to dip chips and buffalo wings.
Overall yummy - I added a dash of worcheschire sauce for a little kick,and it was good.  A little too thick, so I will add buttermilk or milk to thin out to pour, but very easy and good.

I had to improvise and mix milk with cream of tartar in place of sour cream/buttermilk. The mayo tasted strong, but I think that was my doing. I'm definitely going to use this recipe again. It's perfect consistency and was very good as a dip for the fried mushrooms I made.

I don't really like ranch, but LOVE this recipe.  I like that I can make dressing fresh and without all the  that goes into commercial dressings.  I even modified it for my son who is lactose intolerant, using veganaise and Tofutti sour cream.  Came out GREAT!!

I substitute 2/3 c milk + 1 T lemon juice for the sour cream. This adds a brightness to the flavor that I prefer over buttermilk and/or vinegar, and it's more pourable. Let this mixture stand for a few minutes before adding anything else. I increased the pepper and dill a bit, too. The family loves it. Thanks!
All my kids loved this!
Very good recipe!  I think next time I will use buttermilk to make it more the way that I love but this was a great dressing.  My husband loved it!  Thanks!

We have been searching for a "secret" ranch dressing recipe. This is as close as it gets. After much experimenting we finally figured out that ingredient! The garlic! Increase the garlic to 2 TB fresh garlic. I also add 1/8 cup water because we like it a little more runny than creamy. I also added fresh green onions instead of dried chives. Delicious!!!
This was great!!!! Followed recipe to the T with a bit more salt and let sit for 24hrs (by accident). The flavor was extraordinary. It is thick so a little goes a long way.
this is really tasty. I used 1/4 cup half and half and 1/4 cup sour cream and green onion in place of dried chives.

I will never buy bottled dressing again. This simple recipe tastes better than any ranch dressing I have purchased....even those expensive refrigerated versions in the produce section. I had all the ingredients in my cupboard. I used frozen parsley and chives that were in my freezer from last summer that I had harvested from my garden instead of the dried stuff. i also omitted the dill because i did not have it. otherwise, I followed the directions exactly and the dressing came out perfect. I had made wings and chopped the celery and realized I had no ranch. I immediately went to allrecipes and knew I would find a perfect replacement for the bottled stuff and I did. Awesome site. Thanks so much!!!!!!!

I have been trying to find a good ranch dip/dressing.  This was fantastic.  I made it for a family get together and had to make more!  Everyone loved it.  I have not heard so many ahhs and oohs before.  It was gone before I knew it.  Maybe I need to triple the recipe.

I followed the recipes exactly as directed.  I've made it a few times & find increasing ALL the herbs/spices a bit (heavier handed on the garlic & onion powder) & the addition of celery salt makes it superb! I also add a little milk to thin it out a little, so it pours easiler.

This recipe uses the right amounts of each seasoning.  It's a great recipe as-is, and you can easily tweak it to suit your own taste.  After reading the reviews here, I opted to use buttermilk instead of the sour cream to make it a little thinner.  There was a little something off or missing in the overall flavor, so I also added a few squeezes of lemon juice to brighten it up.  Perfect!

I made for this for a party and everyone loved it. I did make a couple of adjustments because i did not have all the ingredients on hand but it still came out delicious. Instead of chives, i used a table spoon of chopped white onion, and one garlic clove. I threw in the black pepper, salt, dried parsley and left out the dill weed because i did not have it. It was AMAZING! My wife asks me to make this instead of buying the stuff from the supermarket because it has so much more flavor and freshness!
The flavors are so fresh and wonderful! I made it as stated then tried it. It was very thick and would have made a perfect dip. Then I added 1/4 cup of buttermilk to thin it out. Perfect for salad.
Very good.  I used real mayonnaise - you know egg yolks and oil beaten together.  Didn't have any problems.  Salt and pepper is a matter of personal taste.

This is excellent, but the only reason I didn't give it 5 stars is that I feel like it's more of a dip -- and is in fact delicious with raw veggies.  While it is good on a salad, I think it would be even better with a bit of tang in it, like lemon juice maybe, or some buttermilk.
This was yummy!

Five stars, with a few changes.  I used 1/2 cup mayonnaise, 1/2 cup sour cream, and closer to a cup of buttermilk (I was going for dressing consistency).  I fried up a couple of pieces of good bacon and crumbled it really tiny into the dressing.  It also got better the longer it sat.  By day two you could taste the bacon in every bite.  It was fantastic and now I get to figure out how to do it again.

I only put in about 2 tbs. mayonaisse and about 1-2 cups sour cream (depending on how much I need) as well as about 3 tbs buttermilk powder, then season to taste. It is absolutely delicious! The only ranch I eat anymore and I use it all the time!

My family and I  LOVE this recipe! This has become our go to recipe instead of buying store bought/processed/GMO ranch. I love that it takes no time at all to make! We buy the Just Mayo since organic is hard to find where we live. I do add milk to thin it out. I just add enough to make the consistency I like. I have made this for family before and they were shocked that I made this and it didn't come from a bottle!
I just tried this. Very good!. Next time I will try Ranch Dressing 1 so I can compare them.
It's the genuine article--Thanks!
Loved it!
Skipping the wet ingredients, this worked well in place of half a packet of ranch dressing mix which I did not have on hand.
I used this ranch recipe to make rosemary ranch chicken kabobs (recipe also on this site), and I died and went to heaven! A++!!!!
I also have a soy allergic little boy, and it is darn near impossible to find a ranch dressing without soybean oil in the store.  Thank you so much!!!!!

I have a hard time with reviews that include people who change the recipe then complain about the outcome.  They're really just complaining about their own recipe.  

This was simple and awesome. Follow the recipe and it works great.  If you change it up and it sucks, then don't complain.
This dressing was quick and easy to make. I used plain yogurt instead of sour cream and I skipped the chives because I did not have any on hand. It turned out great.

I've made this a number of times now, and everyone always compliments it.  Based on earlier reviews, I use 1/2 cup each of mayo, sour cream, and buttermilk, but otherwise leave the recipe unchanged.  It is a thicker dressing (even with the buttermilk modification), perfect for dips, but also compliments salads nicely, sticking to the salad and not gathering uselessly in the bottom of the bowl.  As others have mentioned, the flavors blend together much better after a day or two.  Have I found my Ranch Nirvana?  Not yet, but this is as close as anything else I've tried!  Thanks, Dawnia!

Delicious!  This is the only ranch that will be in our house from now.  I halved the recipe, just in case. Didn't have sour cream, so I subbed 1/3 c. buttermilk.  Also instead of 1/4 t. dried parsley, I only used 1/8 t.  Thank you.

This was brilliant, the only thing I changed was fresh parsley and chives.  This was so good I am 100% sure I will not buy bottled ranch ever again.  I used this on the Cobb Salad from this site and the two go together brilliantly.

This is the perfect ranch recipe!!!  I did change it just a little... I used buttermilk instead of sour cream, but added about 1/2 cup to make it a little runnier.  I also left out the onion powder, but added 1/2 tsp. season salt, and we didn't have any dill, so I put about 1/8-1/4 cup of dill pickle juice straight from the jar- and Oh My Goodness!  It is DELICIOUS!!!  Thank you so much!!  No more Hidden Valley for me!

Excellent Recipe!  I did adjust a little based upon personal preference after the first batch, but did enjoy as written as well.  My 2nd batch I used equal 1/2 cup measures of Mayo, Sour Cream and Buttermilk to make it a little thinner, and less dill weed (1/4 teaspoon) and more garlic powder (1/2 teaspoon) and added a teaspoon of Johnny’s Garlic Bread Seasoning (mostly more garlic and parmesan).  My taste preference is more garlicky and a little less dill.  This was a great home made alternative to the yucky bottled stuff or the expensive seasoning packets (Hidden Valley, etc.) that have stuff like MSG, and other chemical, preservative, fillers, etc.  I won’t be buying store bought / premade seasoning ranch dressing again.
Easy, delicious and MSG free!! THANK YOU SO MUCH for this recipe!!
So far this recipe has come very close to a restaurant recipe I have been trying to figure out. Very refreshing. However, do not be lazy like me and throw it in the blender. It will come out runny.
This is a nice base for homemade ranch.  I did add fresh garlic as i felt it was a little bland.  I have also added a teaspoon of taco seasoning and some salsa for a taco salad dressing.
Great dressing! Simple and tastes great. I used it for the loaded cauliflower since I did not have the dry mix.
I didin't think there was any flavor.  Instead of wastin the batch I mixed in pre-made ranch dressing powder.

Even without sitting to allow the flavors to blend, this recipe is wonderful. I was sceptical, but not anymore! Used 1/2 cup each homemade mayonnaise, homemade Greek yogurt, and milk curdled with vinegar for the base. Seasoning and consistency perfect.
All I can say is....YUM!

Super yummy! I have just gotten back to making everything from scratch because of health issues. I can use vegan mayonnaise, and no one in my household can tell the difference. In fact, it tastes super fresh! Love it!
This is delicious and so quick and easy to make.  Immediately upon finishing it you can use it instead of waiting for the flavors to blend. I am certain it will be even better tomorrow.  Thanks!

Exactly what I was hoping for as a veggie dip! I used one 5.3 oz container of plain nonfat Greek yogurt, and an equal amount of mayo. I didn't have dill the first time I made it, so I subbed an extra 1/2 tsp of chives. I love garlic so I generally add more than called for, and it's simply perfect!

This is the best homemade ranch dip/dressing I've tasted. I made it as a dip for veggies and crackers and it's perfect! As a dressing, you would probably need to thin it just a bit. The ONLY thing I did differently was use 1 cup sour cream to 1/2 cup mayo. Actually, I ran 1/4 short on the sour cream and added plain yogurt in to make up the difference. This is truly a wonderful tasting dip (or dressing if you use it that way).

Fantastic ranch dressing!  I followed other reviewers's advice, and decreased the amount of dill.  Living in the UK, I cannot find ranch dressing, and, even if I could, I won't be going back to bottled dressing now!  Thanks!

I'm a chef in Southern, CA, and 27 years old...best 'simple' recipe for ranch/house dressing that I've ever made in a pinch. I had suprise guests come over, and my buddy loves my cobb salad. I left my recipes at work, and needed to make a good blue cheese dressing. I looked up this recipe and then added a tsp. of worstechire sauce, and gorgonzola cheese to make the blue cheese dressing and it was great. I saved half of the original ranch dressiing and had it woth some buffalo wings, carrot, and celery the next night, and by then it had developed a fantastic flavor. GREAT RECIPE.

Chef Dave
I used low fat mayonaise with this and it still turned out great!

Thanks DAWNIA for this recipe! I never knew it was so easy to make ranch, and all with stuff I always keep in my kitchen! I made wedge salads for lunch, and it was a hit. Better than any I have ever bought, I will say. I made this recipe to the exact way written the first time and added a little more chives and dill to my taste the second. I know TAST IS SUBJECTIVE, SO I SAY TRY THIS ONE, it worked great for a group of picky eaters.
Very good, but a little salty as is.
SO MUCH BETTER than normal ranch. I used buttermilk instead of sour cream.

A truely great base recipe... It makes a great ranch veggie dip... you can adjust it to fit your likings... for me that is less mayonnaise and more sour cream... if you want to make it into a dressing just thin it down with milk... for a ranch dip it is a great place to start
Qiuick, easy and very good! So simple especially when you have your children bring a couple of friends over for dinner  unexpected. Great dressing!
Instead of mayo and sour cream, I used silken tofu, lemon juice and a splash of unsweetened soymilk. Vegan, low fat, creamy and has protein. Fabulous!

I used fresh herbs from the garden, and even so, there was something missing for me, no matter how good it already was!  I put about 1/2 teaspoon aged white wine vinegar and got the taste I was looking for.  It gave it a little more depth....
This is just how ranch dressing should taste! I used 1/2 cup mayo, 1/2 cup sour cream, and 1/2 cup buttermilk. Don't leave out any of the spices. Delicious!
This recipe has helped cure my homesick cravings for ranch dressing. I personally like to double the garlic and black pepper, but it's wonderful as written too.
Love this recipe

I read the reviews before I tried this.  I used 1/2 c Mayo, 1/2 c buttermilk, 1/2 c light sour cream, and the spices as listed in the recipe. I think I will cut the dill in half next time, but my son absolutely loves this!  He even suggested adding a bit of BBQ sauce to it and using it as a base sauce for BBQ chicken pizza.  I am not sure how that would bake up, but this dressing was great with to dip our BBQ chicken pizza in!
I've been looking for a ranch without MSG (or hidden MSG) in the ingrediants.  This one is great !  Thank you - Jeannie
Perfect!  Exactly what I was looking for.  Thank you so much Dawnia!

This is a very tasty recipe for ranch! I followed it except for substituting the following:

Dried chives: chopped fresh green onions
Onion Powder: 1 tbs dried onion flakes
Up garlic powder from 1/4tsp to 1/2tsp
(Left out the parsley)
Best after it sits a day.
YUM!
Very good and very easy. I used buttermilk, less dill, and added one clove of chopped fresh garlic.
I halved recipe then added 1/4 cup skim milk and 1/2 tsp white vinegar (making my own buttermilk).   Excellent!

This is delicious! It tastes better the longer it sits. We didn't care too much for it the day we made it, but loved it the next day.  I used 1/2c fat free sour cream, 1/2c low fat buttermilk and 1/2c fat free greek yogurt as a sub for the mayo - very point friendly for those on Weight Watchers!
This tasted EXACTLY like the bottled ranches, which I hate.
This is a great base recipe, followed as written using all fresh ingredients rather than powder. Turned out wonderful.

This is the best Ranch EVER! We are against preservatives and this one is so good. I switch around the sour cream and mayo, we like more sour cream taste. I also add a little milk for salads. My friends and family are addicted too.

Loved this dressing.  I did follow the advice of others and used 1/2 cup each of mayo, sour cream and buttermilk.  I added a little extra garlic and dill.  Very tasty.  Will definately make this again!
My family loved this recipe so much they don't want me to buy ranch dressing ever again. If you go back to store bought ranch you will taste all of the preservatives.
Wow, what a delicious dressing!  Since I love buttermilk, I substituted part of the mayonnaise and sour cream.  I will never buy ranch dressing again!
This is excellent! I'm just sorry I've spent so much money on bottled dressing. Easy & delicious.
Taste like dill dip and not ranch. I still like it, however, disappointing as I was hoping for the ranch taste.

I'm glad I "listened" to the reviews that stated to use the buttermilk if you want this for a dressing.  Thanks to Melissa I did and it's still very rich and thick but suitable as a dressing.  I used low fat mayo and low fat buttermilk and I still absolutely love this dressing.  The seasoning is perfect for me.  Just remember if you want a dip the sour cream will be ok I'm sure - I even had to add a bit more buttermilk to get the right consistency. I do think there should be a better description of the use of sour cream vs. buttermilk - only reason I did not give this a 5 also.

I made this recipe with the mayo/buttermilk for salad dressing and it did have a strong dill flavor as others said. Luckily I love dill, but it was not the ranch flavor I was looking for. Still delicious!
Followed the recipe exactly the first time and it was really just like a vegetable dip. The second time I reduced the dill by half and used buttermilk instead of sour cream...perfection!
This was a great base. We added some garlic pepper seasoning instead of regular pepper and a dash of chili powder, left out the parsley and chives.
Wonderful!  It was a little thick so I added about 1/2 c milk to make it thinner.  Loved it!

This is the first ranch recipe i've ever tried. It tastes pretty close to restaurant ranch, but I'm new to cooking so I don't know how to give it that fattening taste. I used buttermilk. Next time I will try it with half buttermilk and half mayo. Definitely good for dipping. Not sure if it's salad dressing status yet but it's definitely a keeper. Thanks for submitting!

I have a recipe that calls for Ranch dressing that I've been wanting to try. So my husband and I were at the store reading all the Ranch dressing labels. They all contain MSG (monosodium glutamate), which I can't have since I'm severely allergic to it. I found your recipe and tried it and - oh my goodness - this must be one of the best dressings we've ever had! I love using it as a veggie dip, too. I did follow someone else's advice and used 1/2 cup each of mayo, sour cream and buttermilk. I don't think it tasted too "dilly" at all (of course, I like dill). Thanks for a great recipe!! You ROCK!

This is a very good ranch dressing. I used a 1/2 cup each of mayo, sour cream, and buttermilk, and all fresh herbs in place of powder and dried. I added fresh garlic, black pepper and hawaiian sea salt to season the dressing. I let it marinate for half an hour before tasting. It is a thicker salad dressing even with the 1% buttermilk but you can doctor it up some more to the consistency you want.  This is perfect for dips, compliments toss salads nicely and is also great as marinades. This is fresh tasting, creamy and I love the flavors of the herbs in the dressing. My reccomendation is to use fresh herbs whenever possible because it really does makes a world of difference in taste! Best part of this recipe is you can adjust the seasonings to suit your tastes. Today I used this as a marinade for, "Rosemary Ranch Chicken Kabobs," also from this website. I also plan on using this recipe again for salads in the near future.

I have been on a three-year quest to find the perfect ranch dressing recipe, and I finally found it!  This is great!  I did make modifications to suit our Texas taste buds (ranch dressing is a condiment here!), but this is a wonderful start.  My modifications are to 1) Change the mayo/sour cream/buttermilk to 1/2 cup mayo, 1/2 cup sour cream, 1/2 cup buttermilk, 2)Increase the garlic to 1/2 tsp., and 3) Add 1/2 tsp. vegetable oil (for consistency).  Thanks Dawnia!
I wish I could give this recipe more stars. It goes together quick with ingredients I always have. Thanks so much for sharing! It's fabulous!
We love this ranch! Always make it using buttermilk. So good! You will never eat ranch from a bottle again.
Very yummy!  Getting ready to eat it with some carrots now :)  Didn't have onion powder so I made it without.

YUM!  I just whipped up a half a batch to give it a try. Tastes just like the dry package mix that is the taste we all identify with.  Also tastes just like what you get in a restaurant.  I did use fresh green onion (minced) and fresh parsley (fine).  I didn't have the dried chives on hand and needed to use up my fresh parsley.  Also added water a 1/2 TBLS at a time until I came up with the dressing consistence I was looking for.  It comes up very thick as written, more of a dip. I'll try with the dried next time to see how it works that way. We'll see if it rates a 5 that way =)
