I love this little casserole.  Someone said the buns were soggy, but mine weren't soggy at all. But toasting them a little while pre-heating the oven isn't a bad idea. I made it once slicing the hot dogs to make 2 long pcs, and another cutting up the hot dogs. I think i prefer cutting them up. No need to use canned Tex. chili though.  Just cook up your ground meat (I use turkey) and add chili spices, or even a taco seasoning mix (love Trader Joe's). You can use a little tom. sauce or just add a little water after adding the spices to the cooked meat. But easy, sort of fun dish... and delicious!! I make it in a 9" x 9" baking dish... just cooking for 1 here, so it's probably 4 meals. Oh, and I use Mexican style shredded cheddar.
really fun for the kids.  followed recipe exactly and didn't have any soggy bread - make sure you cover the buns completely with hot dogs.  used only 6 buns per other reviews.
This was pretty good! Easy, Fast, Tasty and Inexpensive! Definately needs 2 cans chili. My husband, a chili dog lover, says he likes them better this way! We'll be making this again!
Good, quick and filling.  It was a hit!
If you love chili dogs you can't go wrong with this recipe.  My whole family loved it.  A keeper!!
very good, different. Kids would like it.
Dana, what did you use to make the little faces?? Thanks.

I was a little skeptical, but this was really good.  I didn't know what to expect with the buns since there were conflicting reports.  I think the type of chili used might make a difference.  I used two cans of Hormel chili with beans and the buns did not get soggy.  In fact they came out like they had been toasted.
This was a pretty good recipe.  Like other reviewers have said, it definitely needs two cans of chili.  This is a great potluck recipe.

this recipe was amazing! It was super easy and taste. I don't buy canned chill but I had some of my homemade chill in the freezer so I used that instead. I also omitted the onion and mustard because my chill has enough flavour already.
This was great..
So easy that the kids did most of the work. Made one with onion & one without. :) I used chili with no beans, but that's personal preference. :)

This is the easiest thing in the world. My kids love helping me make it. Takes about 10 mins to make and then you are done. The  kids love eating this for leftovers at the end of the week which is also a plus.
I cannot believe how easy this recipe is.  I was worried the hot dog buns would be soggy but they were very crisp and delicious.  Thanks.
This was good- something different for us.

I agree with the tip to broil your buns, get a little outside crisp on them before you start layering, yum. I  also altered my hotdogs a bit for Halloween, I made little "dead men" out of them and put them on top. I posted a pic. for you :)
This was pretty good.  I think the hot dogs I used were gross.  I think they were Sugardale.  I would use a different brand next time.

I really wanted to like this recipe. My kids love hot dogs, so I was looking for something else to do with the and found this recipe. unfortunately it was a big salty mess. I I put the rolls down on the bottom, cut up the hot dogs and put them on top, 8 hot dogs cut up got lost on the bread, just didn't seem like enough, so I used 16 hot dogs. one can of chili didn't cover the dish, so I used 2. even the kids didn't like it, they just picked out the hot dog pieces.

Something went askue in this recipe with the proportions!  The flavor was just ok....8 hot dog buns in a 9x13 pan need 3 CANS of chili, not one 15 oz.  One 15 oz. was barely enough to spread a smear over the top.  This then will feed a football team!  So if you're looking for around 4 servings, use 4 hd buns, 4 weiners, and one can of chili in an 8x8 dish.  For little kids or really hungry boys, this might be an ok recipe - but for myself, husband, and 13 year old daughter - we'll pass and buy a chili dog at Weinerschnitzel!!

I spread the mustard on the buns first and I didnt tear them up my buns were day old so no chance they would get soggy. I cut the cheese in half because its so pricey right now. This was a good weeknight dinner with a salad. Thanks

My husband, daughter (3 yrs old) and I loved this.  I used five buns and five dogs instead of the eight so I wouldn't have tons of leftovers.  Kept the chili, onion, mustard, and cheese the same.  Also used all veggie chili once instead of regular, still turned out great.

My family is very picky about what they eat, so I was hesitant to try anything new.  But this is just perfect, and it really is like eating a really big chili dog.  I loved it, will definitely make again!

This was surprisingly good (: I wanted to use up some left-over chili.. and what a great way to do so. This casserole is quick and easy to put together..and hardly takes any time to bake. Thanks for sharing this recipe!
I really like this one. I used my dad's homemade chili because he always makes a ton at a time. Cheap and filling :)

It was easy and quick I made it before I went to work and put it in the fridge so that when my fiance got home he just had to put it in the oven.  I came home and everything tasted great.  My fiance ate about 4 serving sizes He loved it too.

This was excellent - a huge hit with everyone!  I followed the recipe closely, but the actual items you use can affect the flavor. We use Hebrew National hot dogs, the 97% fat free, and the spicy beanless chili by Hormel (DH will not eat beans), oh and two cans of it.  For the buns I tried making my own using the Buttermilk Wheat Bread recipe that I make hamburger rolls from - they were a bit dense this time but that actually worked perfectly in this, they didn't get soggy and the bottoms got a little crispy which I really liked.  For the cheese - although I love cheddar, I had some Montery Jack to use up so I used half that and half sharp cheddar.  I did add the onion & mustard too, that's how I like my chili dogs anyway :) Everyone really loved this and we'll have this again!

I made this using the suggestions in Deana Manfredi's review (first one below the recipe itself). Nice recipe for a busy-day supper and I made it when our three grandchildren were visiting. I think, however, that it would have been better if I had either A) used the hot dog buns, or B) used only one package of Jiffy mix. There was too much bread and too little meat mixture. Whether you decide to with the cornbread mix or the buns, do use at least two cans of chili, and do add cheese. I think adding some chopped dill pickles would have added something as well. Still, my grandkids liked and it was easy for me, so I'll probably make it again.
We loved it!  I made it for  Saturday lunch.  I halved the recipe as it is just my husband and I.  I used Castleberry's Hot Dog Chili Sauce.  It was a perfect blend of spicy and saucy!

I agree with another reviewer on this recipe.  Seemed like a LOT of work for what tasted just like a chili dog.  Easier to make chili dogs and let each individual add their own ingredients to their liking...having said that....this recipe calls for WAY too much bread!  I used almost twice as many hot dogs just to make up the difference, and then I used 2 cans of chili.  Was good, but..it's still a chili dog! LOL  It's probably a good recipe to use for a football party or something then you don't have a whole bunch of individual bowls with condiments and then you have more space on your table for other foods.
yummy I used with tater tots
This was great.  So tasty and so easy to make.  This is a winner.  Thanks

My 5,4 & 1yo & hubby loved this dish. All of them had more then one serving. I made it with fritos instead of buns and served it with California Salad Bowl (from this site). I didn't like it at all, but chili dogs aren't my thing either. Good kids dish I think.
This recipe is wonderful !! So easy and tasty. I also use 2 cans of chili tho.  Picky husband loves it !!! thanks for this one :)

I have to say this was just "ok". My husband and 7 yr old liked it, my 3 yr old barely ate any.  it  Followed the recipie, but toasted the buns first. Great idea, but it seemed to be missing something.
I thought this recipe was great and EASY!  I halved the recipe, but still used 1 can of chili.  I will definitely make this again...THANK YOU Dana!

pretty good for a quick meal!! made with tater tots. I made less, 4 buns and 5 beef hot dogs, chili, onions and cheese, no mustard.  I was worried about the buns being soggy, but they were fine.  I will make this one again!

Thank you very much for the recipe - my family loved it!!!  I made a couple of changes to it. I omitted the mustard and buns. Added about 1/2 cup whipping cream to the chili before pouring it on the hotdogs, and sprinkled the whole dish w/ breadcrumbs and then the cheese. We served it w/ rice -- YUMMY!!!!!!
Oh, this is a good one!  I followed previous advice and used two cans of Hormel chili and skipped the mustard.  This was awesome with ketchup drizzled on top when served.

I have always ment to rate this casserole, and never did. Today I am going to rate it. This is the 3rd or 4th time I've made this dish...........Every time it has been.........GREAT.  A hit with the whole family. It really does taste like a chili dog. It is a dish my family get a craving for and will ask for it. Very good. I have also passed it on to my sister-in-law. Her family loves it too........Good Job.....I also grew up in Flint, Michigan...Home to the Original Angelo's Coney Island......this casserole reminds me of eating coney's at Angelo's back when I was growing up and living and working in Flint......Try this casseroll....if you like coney's this is the casserole for you!!!!!
Husband approved:) Thank you.
My whole family loved this recipe. I used a suggestion from another review and used Fritos instead of hot dog buns. It was a big hit!!Easy and quick to make.
This just didn't work for us...  the bread was soggy. We would have liked it better if we jut used the ingredients for hot dogs...  :( sorry.

My husband and son loved this. The whole pan was gone by the end of the night. We thought the only change we might make next time is to add a little more chili. We used 1 can hormel chili w/ beans and it could have used 2. The bread did not turn out soggy at all, in fact it seemed to toast up a bit. Very fun and easy!
Love it!!!  Whenever my husband makes his chili, I always make sure he makes extra so we can have this recipe the next day.

I give it a 3 and the kids give it a 5. I knew they would. I subbed the hot dog buns with tatter tots. (everyone loves tatter tots) And the rest I did as said. It's def a kid pleaser and a fun meal. Will prob only make once or twice a year since it's not healthy at all!!!! But it's nice to throw the rules out the window once and a while.

This is a great and quick kids meal.  I break the buns up into very small pieces and let the whole thing sit for a while so the chili will soak into the bread.  I also give the kids ketchup to add to their plate because a couple of them REALLY like it that way.  
Letting the kids help make this recipe is probably what made it a hit- when they figured out it actually was hot dogs, just mixed up- they really liked it.
I tried it today...and my kid did not even like it. The buns on the bottom became ROCK HARD...and the rest of it was just GROSS...I would NEVER make this dish again.
I have got to say this was easy and very good.  I toasted the buns first and used double the amount of chili.  Served it with onions and mustard on the side.  Yummy. I will make this again.

This is an awesome idea, however I think the soggy bread turned my son "the chili dog lover" off.  I used my own chili (I omitted the onion because it was in my chili), and used half bun half frito on the bottom.  I agree with other reviews that I should have just used the fritos.  Next time I'll go for the chili cheese fritos to add some kick!  Thanks for the idea Dana & Donna!!
Yup, tastes just like a chili dog!

I am not a fan of canned chili therefore I used brick chili.  Canned chili to me is very runny.  And I used the hog dogs whole not cut up.  Nothing left in the pan.  Everybody loved it.  I have one grandson who doesn't like onion's so maybe next time I will make 2 one with onion's and one without.  Also used Pepper Jack Cheese for a little kick.  Will make many more times.  Nancy
My bread got soggy, next time I will toast it first!
Something very easy to make, the guys love it, just add some jalapenos and sour cream and your good to go.
This is a really good kid-friendly recipe. If you use whole grain buns, low-fat cheese, low-fat chili it also can be pretty healthy. Thanks! And it's easy to make - always a plus!

This was better then I expected! I left out the mustard cause my husband doesn't like it. It needs 2 cans of chili one is definitely not enough. I also froze a head of time, thawed, then cooked & it still turned out good.

This was pretty tasty and I'm not a huge fan of hot dogs. I almost left off the mustard as it seemed odd, but I trusted the advice of other reviews and left it. I'm glad I did; it gave it an extra kick! This was an easy low cost meal that will get added into my rotation.
It was ok. I don't think I will make this again though.
Toasted buns with butter and used a family size can of Hormel chili.  Excellent recipe, will make again and again.
If you like chili dogs, you'll love this. It's great because you really dont need to follow a recipe for it, just put whatever you like on a chili dog in a casserole dish and voila. So easy!
Great recipe. My husband loved it. The only change I made, is I added cooked hashbrown cubes on top of the buns. Will make again!!!

Here is what I did based on reviews:  I only used 4 hot dogs and buns and a smaller baking dish.  I used 1 can of chili, 1 tbsp. dried diced onions, and 1 cup cheese.  I left off the mustard due to personal preference.  I opened up the hot dog buns with the crust side up, per another reviewers suggestion.  Turned out pretty good!  Even one of my picky sons ate it.

Made this for a Superbowl party.  It was okay.  Not the greatest and not a lot of flavor surprisingly.  I made it with the cornbread instead of the buns and doubled the amount of hotdogs the recipe calls for.  Didn't make anyone go "MMMMMM!" It was just okay.  The cornbread was lacking something.  I think next time I'll add chili powder and cumin in the cornbread for more flavor and maybe more mustard in the chili.  We love chili dogs, so this would be a great recipe if I could just figure out how to give it more "oomph!"
MY KIDS LOVE IT
This recipe is so easy to make & the kids just loved it!!!
I will definately make this one again.  It was a huge hit with my family and I had all the ingredients in my kitchen on hand!!

This recipe was pretty good. I didn't like it with the hot dog buns so next time I make it I am going to try Fritos as some have mentioned. Also not really a big onion fan but they weren't too bad in this recipe. This is a great quick fixer meal.
This is so easy and quick to make.  I made it for lunch the other day.  I must have put the ingrediants together in under 2 minutes.  It is a very satisfying meal.

Definately not lowfat but my whole family liked it, even the picky eaters.  I followed previous suggestions and used two cans of chili.  I also made half with hot dog buns and half with fritos.  Both were good.  So easy my 10 year old son could make it. Even my brother-in-law liked the leftovers the next day.

We thought this recipe was great!  I made chili the day before and we just used the leftovers.  I didn't put any mustard in (because I don't like it on my chili dogs), but my husband added some while he was eating it.  It was the same great taste as a chili dog without all the mess on your fingers!
The Best. This is comfort food. I did toast the hot dog buns and chopped the onion really fine. So good. Can't wait to make again. Even the picky eaters ate it.

This was sooooo good!  Changes I made: 2 cans 99% fat free Wolf brand turkey chili, fat free turkey dogs, 2% cheddar cheese, and I only used 6 of the hotdog buns (ran out of room).  Great low fat version.  Will definitely make again!  Thanks!
It is the easiest and everyone loves it!

This was good, and a nice way to change up coneys. To cut calories, I used only 5 buns, 97% fat free hot dogs, and only 1 cup of cheese. All mixed together, you really couldn't tell that I used lighter ingredients.
I used an extra can of hot dog chilli sauce, and it came out ok. My son liked it so-so, but my hubby loved it.

This is super easy and quick to prepare!  It tastes just like a chili dog, but without the mess!  Like other people, I added 2 cans of chili but will probably use 3 cans next time.  I used about a cup of chopped onions and omitted the mustard. I thought there was a bit too much bun for me, so I'll use a little less next time.  I can't wait to make this one again!
My kids love this!  And surprisingly, my hubby and myself actually liked it.  Quick easy dinner.  My boys request this often.

I made this for my husband and I.  By the next day it was all gone.  The only thing I did different was used 19oz. of chili and covered the top with cheese until I could not see anything under the cheese.  I will be making this again soon.
     Reviewed by: H. Chandler
Toasted the buns while the oven was preheating. Used only four buns, four hot dogs and two cans of chili. This was a great tasting, easy dish to make with ingredients already on hand.

Great recipe.  Not as messy as eating an actual chili dog.  Easy to throw into tupperware for lunch at work.  I didn't mind that the bread got soggy.   Used two cans of chili.  My son ate it as leftovers two or three times, which he rarely eats leftowovers at all.
This one is not for me.  I'd rather have a regular Chili Dog.

This is a WONDERFUL recipe! My family really enjoyed it and I look forward to making it again.  For those of you having trouble with soggy bread, you might want to reverse the layering of the ingredients like I did:  Chili first, then hotdogs, followed by onions, mustard, cheese, and bread last.  The moisture stays on the bottom, and the bread bakes up golden brown and delicious.
Quick and easy!! Husband loved it! Would make it again!
I made this using hotdogs that were already cooked and it was a hit!!!  I did use two cans of chili.  A keeper and would be great for potlucks!
Not only was this very quick and easy, there was none left!  The kids gobbled it up. It was a wonderful alternative to messy chili dogs. Thanks for this one. It will be used again and again.
Great for a cookout.

My family and I thought this was just o.k.  Even though I toasted the buns ahead of time, they still got soggy during baking.  Perhaps that is because I used my own chili instead of the canned, which tends to be more pasty.  We will probably just make regular chili dogs in the future.
I thought that this was really good.  My husband wasn't all that impressed.

Halfed the recipe, used 3 toasted hot dog buns and 5 hot dogs. I tore the hot dog buns after toasting them and placed the crust side up according to the suggestions. Also i just added chopped onion to half because my husband is not a fan of onion. I did use the mustard and it tasted great. The recipe was ok. Next time i need to make some adjsutments because the bread was chewy and kind of hard. maybe just bake the hotsdogs an chili with mustard onions and cheese and serve with a piece of french bread or something. Or maybe just not toast the hotdog buns. Either way i will try it again sometime or another! Tahnks for sharing!!!
My 17mo didn't complain, but my husband & I didn't love it.  I followed the directions exactly and the buns got too crunchy.
Loved the recipe, but would take out the mustard.  Didn't really do anything for the recipe, just the random bite, and then you taste it.  I really like the way that the crispy buns tasted!

I was looking to change up the basic chili dinner and the concept of this casserole did not disappoint. I used homemade chili and instead of hot dog rolls, I made corn bread. I prepared the corn bread and baked it in a cast iron skillet until just before it was set. I then added the hot dogs (that I grilled), the condiments, the chili, and the cheese. I cooked the casserole until the cheese was melted and bubbling. The whole family loved it.

This was a great recipe!  I loved it!  I only put onions on half b/c my kids don't like onions.  I also toasted the buns to cut down on soggyness.  My husband is not much of a hot dog eater, but to my surprise, he liked this.  The one thing he wants me to change is to save some of the toasted buns so he can use them separately to spoon it on.  And my oldests son requested more hot dogs to be put in next time.  All in all, very good.  Thanks for sharing!
My kids are the pickiest I've ever seen and this is the first thing I've made that they all loved! I added another can of chili to cover completely and it turned out great!

This is good, but I think some of the quantities are off.  Four buns covered the bottom of my pan, so I stopped there; I think 8 would have been way too many.  I also thought one can of chili didn't cover it enough, so I ended up adding another can.  I did make sure all the bun pieces were crust-side up, and they had a nice texture--slightly crispy on bottom, soft (but not soggy) elsewhere.
awe I guess I only made this because I had so many hotdogs to use up. I really didnt like it.

We were very disappointed with this recipe. I expected it to be great since there were so many good reviews and all the ingredients we like. The taste wasn't that great and all I can really say about it is that it seemed like it was "too much". One or two mouthfuls is all I could handle. Maybe it was just too rich. I would not discourage anyone from trying it though, we just didn't like it ourselves.
Loved it. Made it like KELLYGOFF said.  We added Franks hot sauce to it on out plates. I'll make again.

I was VERY surprised but this was really, really good.  My husband agreed.  The only change I made was turning the whole buns crust side up and toasting them a bit before I put the chili mixture on top.  I used Castleberry hotdog chili which isn't too great on its own but in this recipes was good.  I left off the mustard because I was skeptical but ended up adding it before serving...it really made the dish.

This recipe was horrible! My kids wouldn't eat it and they generally are good eaters. I doubled the chili because it looked too dry;that didn't help. I think if I was to make this again I would omit the buns entirely add salsa. The existing recipe was WAY too dry.
I love this recipe and it is often on the menu!
ehhh, just okay for us.

This was really pretty good.  I didn't think one can of chili was enough, I used a beanless, so I added a can of light red kidney beans.  All I had on hand, chili beans would have been nice too, but it was still chili enough.  The juice from the beans, when added to the chili, made it easy to distribute over the casserole.  I opted against the mustard.  Chili dogs are so messy and you end up eating it with a fork anyways, so this is a good solution.  This was quick and easy and everyone liked it.

My kids liked this one a lot.  I think I prefer the traditional way of making a chili dog myself.  It's not like this recie makes it any easier to make a chili dog.  I gave this a try because I made a big pot of chili for dinner a few nights before and I wanted to use up the left-overs and this sounded like a good way to do it.  Not  horrible but not an all time favorite either.  Might make it again if my kids request it.
This was so easy and tasted great!  I used a large can of chili instead of the 15 oz and piled on extra cheese.  We will fix this again!
great a family fav. quick easy

This was very good (for a easy/quick dish).  I used one can of Hormel Chili with no beans and two cans of Tony Packos hot dog sauce, mixed togther with the mustard.  I also used Deli style hot dogs (large and juicy) which are much better for this recipe than typical hotdogs.  Handcut and homemade french fries, with malt vinegar were a nice sidedish, reminding me of fairs and baseball games.

My boyfriend loved this casserole.  I liked it, but wouldn't be able to eat it once a week, and definitely wouldn't be able to eat it left over, the bread was like moosh. Like everyone else I used 2 cans of chili, and used 6 buns, 8 would have been too much.  If you're making this recipe for 3 or less people I recommend  halfing the recipe and putting it in a smaller dish, because it's definitely not something you'd like to eat left over.  This dish would be good to make a bunch of guys watching a football game or something.  It was a super easy recipe.
This was really good but I add the larger can of chili and next time will add 2 cans. This would be good for camping
This is a great idea.  Easy to make and tasty too.

WOW!!  what a crowd pleaser.  i can't say that i got to taste this recipe, because the 5 kids i made it for ate every single bite.   i made two casseroles and the kids couldn't get enough. thank you for sharing this.
it was ok but i would have to say it was not a hit on my husbands list, I thought it was going to be more then it was, and was really looking forward of it being a hit with my husband.
I made this for teenage boys, they loved it, I think next time i will toast the buns slightly before putting it together, a little crunch in there might be nice, thanks for sharing

This was good.  My 17 month old ate it without blinking.  I put my buns in the oven when I turned it one to preheat.  By the time the oven was hot, my buns were toasted perfectly.  I only made 1/2 a recipe.  I didn't think there was enough chili though and ended up using 2 10 oz cans of Hot Dog Chili.  It tasted pretty just like you would expect.  Next time I may preheat my chili though.  I found some of the center of my casserole didn't get very hot.  I also didn't think the buns got any soggier than if I was making a regular chili dog.  I will keep this recipe in mind for nights I need a quick meal.

4 stars because I modified it, using the instructions/modifications that Deana Manfredi listed below.  The kids LOVED it...the cornbread topping really gave it something special.  I don't think they/we would have liked it with any type of bread or buns on the bottom.  Thanks for the great idea though, never had thought of doing it in a casserole.  I also added a sprinkling of shredded cheese on top of the cornbread.

This is the best and tastiest way to use leftovers!  I used hot dogs from a barbecue and old hot dog buns.  I left the hot dog buns sit overnight (they became stale) and I used Castleberry's Hot Dog Chili which is low cal but tasty.  My brother-in-law, a former Army Cook, prefers potato buns versus hot dog buns.  Either way, this is a great recipe.  Eye ball the ingredients and use more versus less hot dog chili.  This is a keeper!!!!

My family and I love this recipe. The only thing we do differently now is, instead of buns on the bottom, We fry some french- fries. Its awesome this way. You get chili dogs and chili cheese fries at the same time. Yummy!

I really enjoyed this but I made a few changes. I used prepared chicken stuffing on the bottom instead of hot dog buns. I used 6 oz but I would double that next time. I only used 4 turkey hot dogs and 1 1/2  cups of cheese. I used a 15 oz can of chilli which seemed like the perfect amount so if you use the original recipe, I would use more chilli. I also sprinkled garlic powder and garlic salt when it came out of the oven. My husband added red pepper flakes to his dish. All in all it was a really good dish.

I just came across this and realized I never rated it over a month ago when I made it.  I had a large party where we had lots of leftover buns & hot dogs and this was perfect!  The kids really enjoyed this meal.  I did toast the buns for a bit in the oven before pouring on 2 cans of the hormel brand chili but otherwise followed the recipe.  It's not something I'd make frequently but we did enjoy it!
My fiance LOVEs this recipe! i dont make a whole lot of changes to the recipe but i do add bbq sauce to it and also more chopped onion!
This was good but the buns were soggy.  To improve, next time I will tear the buns apart and mix the pieces in at the time the dish is served.  Kids loved it
My kids want me to cook this at least once a week. I leave the mustard and onions out of it. I usually end up using a whole package of weanies. Delicious!!
Wasn't impressed, basically just a chopped up chili dog...not horrible but don't see the point in a casserole.
We all liked this very much!!!  Definately easy after a long day.  Next time I think I will try cornbread instead of buns and maybe a little more chili.  Very good though, thank you.

This was good and really easy. My youngest had 2 helpings so I was very pleased. This is great for those "I don't have time to cook" nights and it's cheaper (and simpler) than going to the drive-through.
This was an ok recipe--I am not a huge fan of chili dogs but my husband is, and he wasn't really impressed.  However, it is quick and easy to make.
I followed one reviewer's advice and toasted the buns in the oven before adding the rest of the stuff and it did not come out soggy. It was pretty good.

This is a very tasty recipe. I used Hormel turkey chili, and turkey franks. Next time, I'll try lining the pan with toasted split buns instead of tearing them into pieces. I'll also thin the chili slightly to make it easier to spread uniformly.
Great idea. I would have gave it 5 stars but it was a little dry. Next time I will use 2 cans of chilli.

Five stars for flavor alone!  I made this with 2 cans of chili and that was just right.  I also browned the hot dogs in a hot skillet for extra flavor.  The only thing about this recipe is that it really should only be an occasional treat because it's a high fat/cal dish.  Worth the try and will make again (in a few months)!
wow !

My husband and I loved this.  My son turned his nose up at it though.  Since I was only making it for 3 people, I used 3 hot dog buns and kept the other indgredients the same, except I used a little less cheese.  Will make again!

I thought this was excellent.  Followed the advice of a previous reviewer and put the buns in the oven while it was preheating and that toasted them nicely.  They didn't get soggy either, but then I used quite a dry chili (I am vegetarian so I used a lentil-based vegetarian chili and vegetarian hot dogs).  I also left out the onions as there were already onions in the chili.  A really easy and scrumptious dinner!

Well, many times we end up eating part of our chili dogs with a fork so why not just make a casserole?!  I found this recipe and decided to try it because we had 1 leftover hamburger bun, a couple hot dog buns, and about 6 hot dogs and 2 brats.  I made this in an 8x8 pan because I was using leftovers and a smaller amount of buns than recommended.  I only had chili with no beans on hand so I used it with a can of chili beans for more filling.  My buns weren't soggy either.  They were soft on the chili side and firmer, almost crispy on the pan side.  I did warm up the hot dogs and leftover brats in the microwave before adding to the casserole dish and glad I did because I'm not sure they would have heated thoroughly enough for my liking.  I agree with other reviewers that if making in a 9x13 pan, more chili would be better.  It wasn't the prettiest of meals on the plate, but what do you expect from a chili dog casserole?

Wonderful teen (and husband) pleasing recipe, inexpensive, easy to throw together for a crowd, (when adjusted)and our kids can make it themselves! I added an extra can chili beans with the chili so it wouldn't be dry and cut the buns to just cover bottom of the pan I was using.

Simple, cheap, and my boyfriend thought this was awesome (he LOVES hot dogs, for whatever reason, I'm not sure). :) I didn't have any hotdog buns, so I used 3 whole wheat hamburger buns. Split them in half, left each side whole instead of tearing them up, and layed them in a casserole dish, stuck them under the broiler for about 5 minutes, flipped them over and broiled for another 5 or so. They were nice and crispy after this and held the crispiness even after the chili was added. I used 1 can of Hormel Chili that had Tabasco in it and spooned that onto each hamburger bun, covered with cheese and baked for 25 minutes, then added another layer of cheese for the last 5 minutes. Omitted the mustard and onion since my boyfriend isn't a fan of either, but the Tabasco in the chili made up for any lack of flavor. The hamburger buns worked perfectly because it designated portion size. My boyfriend thought this was great 'man-food', so I'll add it to my recipe box. Thanks!

I've made this casserole 5-6 times now and my fiance and I love it.  The mustard really makes this dish.  It's perfect for sports get-togethers or just a night when you don't feel like cooking anything extravagant.  It couldn't be much easier!  Only thing I recommend is toasting the hot dog buns before layering them in the dish--helps them hold up a bit better after the chili covers them.
Oh wow was this good! Great comfort food. The only thing I did different was use 2 cans of chili. (1 with beans and one without.)
We enjoyed this recipe very much! Just be sure to toast the buns first.

Made this for a church potluck.  I used a full pack of buns and hotdogs, didn't want leftovers.  I thought it was a bit dry, will add more chili if I make it again.  Everyone seemed to like it.  I will probably make it again.

I tried this recipe for the first time last night.  It turned out really good.  I took some advice from other reviews and tried them out.  I toasted my hot dog buns while preheating the oven, which seemed to really help out.  I also went on some other advice and used two cans of chili instead of one.  That gave the casserole better coverage.  I used Hormel chili.  It was a really easy recipe overall.  Quick and easy to prepare, not too long cook time, and was very tasty.  I'm sure I'll do this one again.
for something a little different, i replaced the hot dog buns with tater tots i had precooked in the oved, it was awesome!!! definately going in my recipe box, good for when you are short on time!!
We love chili dogs so this was a great new discovery!I used Turkey dogs and instead of canned chili i used leftover turkey chili i had made in the crock pot. This really tasty.

my hubby and twins loved this. i liked it myself, quite a compliment considering i'm not too big on hot dogs. it was easy and all in one dish. seems less messy than the traditional chili dog. i tore up the buns into chunks, and added sliced jalapenos to one side of the dish. yum!
This is sooo good and sooo easy.  Thanks for a great, fun recipe.

This recipe is very easy to make and the kids enjoyed it. After reading some of the previous reviews I decided to toast the buns before I put them in the dish so they would not get soggy and I addded 3 cans of chili.

I made this a long time ago, and was going through my recipe box and though it had a 1 star rating, it said I hadn't ever written a review.  I remember this dish DISTINCTLY ...I made it for myself and my friend who are BOTH chili dog lovers.  I made it with my own homemade chili, NUTS what a waste...the buns were soggy, and I have an aversion to soggy food anyway, but the overall dish left much to be desired.  The mustard made it taste even stranger.  I thought that this would be a pretty decent recipe given the high reviews and the ease of preparation, boy I was sadly mistaken.  I will not make this again.

This tasted just like a chili dog.  My husband and I both enjoyed it. It was easy to make and quick.  I also took the advice of readers though and toasted the buns, otherwise they get a little soggy. Good recipe.

Everyone I have shared this with LOVED IT ! Great for my picky hubby too!
I do change it up a little... I cut the hot dogs and fry them in a pan for a few minutes to give them a little more texture, and use 6 buns. I cook it a little longer for really crispy buns! Love it !

I made this today and the kids loved it.  I tweaked it a little bit.  I sautéed hot dogs in a skillet until browned and added diced onion to hot dogs and sautéed a little longer.  I doubled the chili as well.  I served ketchup,mustard, sour cream and diced pickles on the side for toppings of choice.  This is a keeper.
my family had this halloween evening before trick or treating . we loved it !! this is right up my husbands alley !  thanks for the great idea !

We made this last night for the Super Bowl.  Instead of hot dog buns, our bottom layer was crispy tater tots (crispy so they'd soak up some of the chili).  And, based on other reviews we used 2 cans of chili, one with beans and one without.  It was a hit and we only had one serving left over!  Thanks!
This is good for a quick and easy meal.  It was easy for my toddler to eat on his own.

I liked the convenience but way too much buns, 4 buns covered the bottom of my 9 x 13, I had 2 cans of chili and ended up needing both for a full layer of chili and felt it needed more. The flavor was ok, not like a real chili dog.  The buns got soggy which I liked and the onions stayed almost raw, another plus in my book but don't think I'll make again. I am glad I tried though, thanks.
COULD USE 2 CANS OF CHILI INSTEAD OF 1
this was realy good ,i used 2 cans of chili.will make again.thank you
Very good!  Only one problem it gave me the worst heartburn!

i made this out of desperation one night and now my husband won't stop obsessing.  since it has zero redeeming nutritional qualities i make it only once in awhile. i use half the amount of buns, dogs but entire can of chili - otherwise not enough chili to cover the top.

Very easy. We doubled the amount of chili on it, but we like 'em sloppy. Another trick to avoid soggy hot dog buns is to pop it under the broiler to quickly toast the buns before adding the chili and cheese.
good recipe .. i cut up 2 packages of biscuts and put on the bottom instead of hotdog buns.
Great Recipie!!  Tasty, quick and fun....My 1.5 year old loves it!!!

This has become a staple in our house! Whenever I make chili I always make a pan of this with the leftovers. I've never added the onions or mustard, just use the chili as is. I also omit the hotdog buns and replace with a layer of Bisquick biscuits on the top, finished with some extra sprinkled cheese! Just great!
Definitely needs 2 cans of chili. The more cheese the better!
This was a good idea..I did use the other reviewers suggestions and toasted the buns first..I think next time I will use the chips or my husband suggested cooked tator tots in the bottom
This was pretty tasty.  I took the advice of others and added more chili.  Would make it again
This recipe was really good and really easy. Definitely a keeper. If you like chili dogs you'll like this recipe.

Well my kids are not easy pleased when it comes to dinner time until now i have found this super easy lovely recipe.This was a winner with all of my children and thats a great result when i have such picky eaters.Thank you so much for this quick easy recipe

This was good I toasted the buns first made my own chili and used more hot dogs but next time I will just use 8.  The onions were a bit crunchy will leave off next time and put in a bowl on the table.

I substituted corn chips for the hotdog buns. 
I found this much better for reheating the leftovers (If any). The Kids liked the "crunch" in every bite!

This is as close as you're going to get without making individual chili dogs. The bread nearest the bottom gets a little crunchy making a nice crust. I usually double the dogs and the chili. One package of buns is enough to carry it. We all like it. I would suggest however to reserve some "home made" chili and not using canned. It's a taste thing....

HA HA HA, I made this last night and my husband said I can never make this again because he nearly ate the entire 9 x 11 pan. I used 4 (buttered and toasted in the broiler) hot dog buns cut into bite size pieces, 8 deli dogs cut up into bite size pieces, 1- 38 oz. can of Stagg chili. I followed the directions as written and well it was really good. Needless to say I will make this again : )

Very easy recipe to personalize.  I cut up a bagette into chunks, browned in butter, chopped up 2 large all beef franks and sauted to crisp up, used homemade chili, the rest as the recipe said.  Very well received by adults.
I added an extra can of chili; the whole family enjoyed.
This was an intersting meal.  I served the mustard and onion on the side since my son will not touch the stuff.  It was ok,  I will not try this one again.

My kids liked this but my hubby and I thought it was just okay. I think the mustard ruined it for me. I usually like all this on my hot dogs but in the casserole it just tasted off. Weird huh? Maybe I will try again w/out mustard. It's a nice idea though.

These were really good.   We did what other suggested and toasted the buns a bit first and we omitted the onions.  They weren't as good the next day as leftovers (maybe cause the buns got soggy over night).  Thanks for the recipe
I wasnt sure what to think when i made this, but was very pleasantly surprised. The torn up hot dog buns got a little crisp which was quite nice. I would make this again.
Easy to make and the dish was empty so I guess it gets a 5!  I didn't have hot dog buns so used bread and added an extra can of chili.
I liked this because it was pretty easy to make after work one night.  It was less messy for my kids too.  I will probably make it again sometime.

This was not a hit at my house, my family asked me to never make this again, my kids could not even finish a serving.  The bread became soggy(I even toasted it before hand), the taste was dead on though.

I followed another review and changed the recipe a little.  I place 2 cans of chili on the bottom of a casserole dish, followed by a layer of hot dogs, a layer of cheddar cheese, then 2 packages of jiffy corn bread, finally finish with some additional cheese on top.  It is a really simple, quick Saturday lunch and my kids love it!

When I accidently left out the mustard in preparation, it was decided that might be
for the better as it could then be added by each individual's taste.

This is very economical and a real "kid pleaser".

My kids love this dish so much, I promised them I would serve it at my wedding.  Needless to say, it was a big hit!  I even attached the recipe to the thank you cards so everyone could enjoy it at home.  I enhanced the recipe by also adding crumbled corn chips on the top.  I have only two words for this recipe, mmm mmm!!!

This was pretty tasty.  Used all 10 hot dogs from the package and probably more chili (used homemade).  Forgot the mustard.  Had request for the recipe from a potluck, so that tells you it's a good one!
Great for using up leftover Chili!  My toddlers and I just had it for lunch.  Did nothing special, but my bread came out crispy on the bottom.  Great and Simple Idea.

Made this for dinner tonight and the husband LOVED it.  I used the revised recipe with corn muffin mix instead of hot dog buns and it turned out really good.  It was especially yummy topped with ketchup and mustard.

If you feel like hot dogs, this is it! Tastes just like a chili dog you eat with a fork! I didn't put in the onions until after so that everyone could put however much they wanted. I toasted the buns before I added everything else and they didn't get soggy. Plus I had Fritos at the table as well. Definately, make this again!
Big hit with 12 year old and hubby.  Both went back for seconds!  The buns to get a little crispy, but everyone seemed to like it.  I left off the mustard, not big mustard fans at my house.

I like this recipe because it is cheap and very easy.  Due to what other reviewers said, I chose not to put the hot dog buns in the casserole because I didn't want to eat soggy bread.  Instead, after I cooked the casserole, I served it in hot dog buns.  I also cut the cheese in half because I didn't think so much was necessary.
REALLY GOOD AND EASY TO MAKE.

THIS RECIPE IS SO SIMPLE, YET MY WHOLE FAMILY JUST LOVED IT. YOU THINK THAT YOU CAN ANTICIPATE WHAT IT WILL TASTE LIKE, BUT IT IS VERY DIFFERANT FROM WHAT YOU EXPECT.  I ALSO USED MORE CHILI THAN WAAS CALLED FOR.

WHOA!  This recipe ROCKS!  Couple of suggestions:  I agree with the corn chip substitution and the two cans of chili.  I browned my hot dog pieces in butter with the onion then added the chili, some black beans and mustard and mixed together and heated through then poured it over the fritos.  Then topped off with the cheese.  WHOA!  NOT lowfat!  WHO CARES?

I made this for a 4th of July party and everyone loved it - to my surprise. I tore up the buns into bite sized pieces so that people didn't have to worry about cutting at all - also browned them a bit before putting hotdogs on top (on broil.) I added the mustard and it really added a nice tang. Instead of putting onions in (which I'll do next time) I served diced red onions for people to sprinkle on top. Will definitely make again - serves a lot of people and VERY easy to make.

took this to a 4th of july bbq and it was a huge hit! everyone was asking for the recipe... best part was it is very kid friendly which is a major plus for family events.  i skipped out on using the buns and just used the fritos as suggested by other reviewers.  i also recommend using two cans of chili as well.  on top i sprinkled a mexican/taco blend of shredded cheese instead of the plain cheddar... sooo good!!!

Really easy fun dish for the kids.  I did not have the sogginess that some other reviewers had.  Used Hormel chili w/o beans, and did not toast the bread beforehand.  Hubby loved it, so did the little ones!  Really good!

Unsurprisingly, the key to this recipe is the dogs and chili you use. While I prefer this recipe to Chili Dog Casserole II, I didn't like the cheese weiners I used here as much as the smokey franks I used previously. Also, I didn't realize that the chili I bought for CDCI had beans in it, which I also didn't much care for. I will definitely make this again (so quick, cheap, easy and tasty) but I'll check out the Hormel chili that seems so popular with other reviewers. Thanks, Dana!

We decided to try this recipe because we had some leftover hot dog buns from our Memorial Day BBQ. This was very tasty and in my opinion, better than a chili dog because of the toasty buns and it was easier to eat with a fork. It was easy to make, quick and inexpensive. I used 5 hot dog buns, 5 hot dogs and 2 cans of Wolf brand chili w/o beans. I left out the mustard though because hubby doesn't like it. I used part colby jack and part sharp cheddar cheese. I didn't tear up the buns, but did slice the hot dogs up. Also, like some others suggested I put the buns crust side up and it wasn't soggy at all. We both really liked this recipe and will definitely make it again.
Chililicious!  I made this for my kids, but especially for my 80 year old father who loves hot dogs. They all had one complaint...there was none left over for the next day!!

Great for a quick meal that's easy to put together. Does it show off expert cunlinary skills? Um, no. Is it a heart healthy meal? Definitely not. But after a long work day and late arrival home, I needed something I could get in the oven in minutes. My family ate it, and oldest DD proclaimed "I really like this!" I chopped up a whole package of hot dogs, tore up 6 buns, used 3 cans of chili and no onions (didn't feel like messing with it). I didn't measure the mustard, just squirted it on and then topped everything with the cheese. It baked for about 1/2 hour and was ready to eat! Definitely will be using this recipe again. Want to try it with leftover homemeade chili.

1. What a great way to use stale hot dog buns!
2. Omitted the onions (onions turn my kids off).
3. I used a combination of jack & chedder cheese.
4. Used my own home made chili and I'm sure I had more than the called for amount.
5. Made this with my two finicky eaters and my friends two finicky eaters.  My daughter and her two sons had seconds - than never happens!  My four year old son had 4 helpings!  Incredible!!!

Great job Dana!

I made this last night for my boyfriend, but used tator tots instead of buns! It was fantastic and will definately make it again. I cooked tator tots until slightly browned and then added the rest of the ingredients as directed.I also used 8x8 instead of 13x9 and it was fine.

It was delicious! I made a few changes to make it healthier and tastier, as per several user reviews. I used whole wheat bread instead of hotdog buns, and I toasted them approximately halfway through before placing them in the casserole dish. I used five pieces of bread (four whole pieces and one torn apart to fill-in any remaining gaps in the casserole dish). I also used vegetarian chili, doubled the chili, used turkey dogs, and excluded onions.
I made this for my daughter she is 4 and she loved it, I did not put mustard on as stated and it still came out pretty good. Real easy to whip  together. :)
needs 2 cans of chilli. use all the bread even if it looks like a lot. =]
This turned out great. I didn't use the onions or mustard and all my picky eaters asked for more.
This was a wonderful recipe! My entire family loved it. It was simple to make, and was perfect  as a lunch dish.

I made this for my son and my husband last night.  They both loved it.  I halved the recipe and used an 8x8 pan - still needed a 15oz can of chili.  Mine was not soggy at all - I sliced the hotdog rolls on a slight diagonal and layed them in the bottom of the pan.  I then put a scant 1/2 c. colby jack shredded cheese mixture over the bread.  I used good quality Hebrew National all beef hotdogs and Denison chili.  Will add this to my "family favorites" list - thanks so much!

I really enjoyed this recipe and so did my family. May take a little improvising at first (need more cheese or chili) to fit how you like it. 2009 UPDATE: We have now been making this for years, it has become a regular meal at our house, so much so that I think I am completely burnt out :-) Hubby insists that we have this once a month and we've just had our first of at least three children so I've got a while before I can retire this recipe :-) I've give this recipe to many coworkers who have now all incorporated it in their regular meals. WE LOVE THIS RECIPE!!!!
I first downloaded this recipe in 2001, and have used it too many times too count, and given the recipe to a lot of friends.  This is one of my favorite "comfort" food casseroles.  Thank you!
great for kids and its nice and quick to make

This casserole was great!!  I made it without the onions and mustard and with two cans of Hormel chili.  My hot dog buns did not get soggy as some of the other reviews said.  It was a really quick and simple meal and everyone in my family loved it!
Great, my son and husband request it atleast onece a week..

This was hearty and yummy! Next time I'll add more chili (I used turkey chili) and I'll leave off the onions, they were too crunchy for me. I may also put a layer of chili under the buns since I think I would like the buns softer. But I will definitely make this again and again.
Great way of changing up regular chili dogs.
I used a larger can of Hormel chili and a few more hot dogs and onions. My husband and I liked it but it wasn't a hit with the kids.
Very good and easy!  I would agree that it is better with 2 cans of chili.
YUM, YUM, YUM!  Very easy to make and very tasty.  Will add this to our "regular" dishes at home.

I took some of the other reviewers advice and added more chili.  I think I overdid it because it was VERY soupy.  If I were to make it again I would definitely only use maybe a little more than the recipe calls for.
This is a great recipe for the kids...my husband liked it too, and he can be pretty picky.  Not very good the next day though!! Soggy bread...gross.

This was awesome!  I did use two cans of Hormel turkey chili with beans.  My sister-in-law laughed at me and said, "Why not just eat the chili dog??"  My three-year-old who will not eat chili dogs, gobbled this down and loved it.  I will definitely make this again.  Just had it leftover for lunch!  If you use stale hot dog buns, they don't get soggy.  :)  Thanks for the recipe!
This was edible. I don't know about these "American" casseroles

I used whole wheat buns, kosher dogs, two cups of the Big Game Day Chili that I made the day before and used a 2% sharp cheddar. I didn't have any of it but my boys got a kick out of it. They loved that it was a new way to eat chili dogs. NOTE: This was so cheap to make that it should be illegal. I bought the hot dog buns off the clearance rack and everything else I already had on hand. Great for families who are stretching their food budget.

My entire family loved this recipe! I did add another can of Chili,and as others suggested,I made one half with corn chips and the other half with buns.My family all agreed that next time we will make it with just the corn chips.Very tasty alternative to chili dogs!
I loved this one, I also thought it had the right amount of chili. If you like soggy bread you might add more chili. But I liked some of the bread cruncy. Thanks I will be making this again.
My husband absolutely loved this recipe!  I used Fritos instead of buns and omitted the mustard (by mistake).  It turned out excellent and was so easy to make.
Toast your buns in the oven prior to making casserole to prevent soggy bread!!!  Delicious quick easy meal!

VERY EASY!!! My children including my biggest child (my husband) LOVED this!!
I used 10 hotdog buns and 10 hot dogs, I also used 3 cups of cheese instead of 2. My husband even took this for lunch the following day!
Kids loved it.  It was exactly like cut up chili dogs...

Delicious & fun dinner idea!  My husband and I really enjoyed this. My children (11 & 5 yrs.) had mixed reviews.  They ate it, but their biggest criticism was the bread.  I guess they're purists (hot dogs ON buns, not the other way around, etc.).  I did use Hormel's low-fat Turkey Chili, and found that two cans would have been better than the one that I used.  Next time, instead of hot dog buns, I think I'll try using a prepared cornbread stuffing mix which would be crispier than the cut-up buns (although, I did lightly butter and toast them before adding the rest of the ingredients, but they still absorbed too much moisture from the chili than my kids liked).  Thanks for the idea, and I will be making this again. UPDATE ON 6/28/06:  WE HAVE TWEAKED THIS CHILI DOG CASSEROLE TO EVERYONE'S LIKING...LAYERED IN THIS ORDER:  2 OR 3 CANS OF HORMEL TURKEY CHILI W/O BEANS; 1 PACKAGE OF LOW FAT OR FAT FREE BEEF FRANKS CUT UP, DICED ONIONS, 1/2 PACKAGE LOW FAT SHREDDED CHEDDAR/MONTERAY JACK; 2 PREPARED PACKAGES OF JIFFY CORNBREAD MUFFIN BATTER SPREAD ON TOP, THEN FINISH W/ REMAINING CHEESE AND BAKE.  EVERYONE LOVES THIS, AND I THANK YOU FOR INSPIRING ME!  GREAT RECIPE IDEA!

This was fantastic!!! My husband and I gobbled this up.  We followed other suggestions and used 2 cans of Hormel (hot) Chili.  I also doubled the onions.  Putting the hot dog buns crust side up definitely kept them from getting soggy (they got pretty crisp on the underside).  Great recipe!!

I left out the onions, used 2 cans of chili, and mixed the mustard in with the chili, to distribute it more evenly.  I also substituted corn chips for the buns, as another reviewer had suggested.  Everyone who likes chili dogs will like this!

This was good.  Exactly what I expected.  I used more hotdogs than called for, 2 cans of chili, and only half the amount of bread.  And I put the mustard on the hot dog buns.  Not gourmet fare, but tasty.  I will make this again.
My family loves this.  Whenever I ask my 4 children and husband what they want for dinner, this is the answer.

Quick and easy and tastes good too!  I didn't make any changes.  I used Hormel chili with no beans.  The bottom of my casserole was crispy not soggy like I expected.  It was very good.  As I put it together I thought it was gonna need another can of chili but it was fine as is.
This was fast, easy & good.  It was a little something different from the same old thing.  We will eat this again.

Chili dog you eat with a fork. Yum! This was okay and made for some savory hotdogs. I did make one change though I did not cut up the buns and hot dogs. I just filled the buns w/ the hot dogs and chili as you would any regular hot dog. Then I added additional chili on top, some onions, some shredded cheese and crumbed bacon. I put this all in the oven and baked and it was really good. I topped it all off with mustard.

My husband just loved this! Toasting the bread seemed to work quite well as it wasn't soppy at all. Chili dogs have always been a favorite of my husbands and mine so we were just thrilled with this recipe! Thank you so very much for a new favorite! :)
my kids loved this. very easy & quick. will definately be making it again.

A 5-star when it came to how quick and easy, and a 5-star about how my 4 kids (ages 2-16) all LOVED it! I did put the open up the buns and put them crust side up in the pan and I did use two can's of chili.  I am the one who hates anything soggy and I have no complaint about this recipe-it rocks!   I told a few friends about it and had to make them copies of the recipe.  I am going to try to make it with chili with no beans, next time since that is the only part he didn't like.  Thank you so much for the recipe!
Good but not overly special. Needs extra chili. Kids would enjoy this probably.
We loved it.  It was cheap and super easy.  Thanx for a fun and easy casserole dish...

This is a great recipe!  Everyone I have made it for has loved it!  It also works great to make a batch and freeze it.  To cook from frozen, I first thawed it and then cooked it per the directions.  Excellent!

Wow, this recipe surprised me. I wasn't sure how well it would go over, but the family really enjoyed it. Next time I will definitely make with corn chips...it needs a crunch. But a great recipe for kids.

Nothing fancy but my husband who was dissapointed to hear what we were having for dinner (he doesn't like hot dogs) ate seconds because the bread and the chili kind of make the rest ok. 18 month year old liked it too. We just used some bread that was nearing its end intsead of hot dog buns.
Eh... Nothing special. It's basically chilli dogs cut up in a bowl for a toddler.  Niot bad for a last minute dinner requiring no effort.
This was a great recipe and simple. I belive that we will make the traditional chili dogs from now on but this was a nice idea.
This recipe is so easy and hearty! My fiance loved and it and asks me to make it repeatedly!

This is a great, quick weeknight recipe.  Not very healthy, unfortunately, but you can make it a little better for you by using fat-free franks and turkey chili.  I only used half the bread called for, and added two tablespoons of ketchup, which I drizzled over the top with the mustard.  I used colby/jack cheese because I didn't have any cheddar.  This was excellent and my family, hubby included, loved it.  I think I'll leave out the mustard over half the casserole next time to suit my picky six year old -- when she saw the mustard, she didn't want to eat anymore.  My 10 year old maintains that it's the best casserole she ever ate.

I made this last night and it was pretty good. This is the same ingredients that I use when making chili dogs, so its great to incorporate it into a casserole dish. Next time I will toast my buns first. They got a little soggy after baking. Also if you can get skyline brand(Cincinnati style) chili where you live, I highly recommend it for this. And dont use the canned, use the frozen, or make it yourself! The canned always leaves the chili with a tin flavor, yuck. Overall this was a super fast and easy meal. This can be very versatile by adding different ingredients to it. I think next time it would be good to add in some rotel tomatoes! Oh yeh, by the way, I added chili cheese fritos on top to give it some crunch.  They made the whole recipe!  I will make again for sure, thanks!

This was a great quick supper idea!  My family loved it.  I used chili w/out beans, and cooked the hot dogs first.  There was enough chil left over in the pan to make chili cheese fries!  Will put in the make again file.
This was very much a "kid friendly" meal.  It is what it says it is...in a big glop.  Taste...it tasted like a chili dog.
Super easy. Super cheap. Best when made with leftover homemade chili. The family really enjoys this with fritos crumbled on top for crunch. Thanks Dana...

This was great. I made it for a large group of people as part of a brunch and it went over well. I would definitely make it again. It was an easy and affordable dish to create and something that noone had tried before. A keeper! Thanks!

This recipe is fantastic!!!  AND I have a couple tips to make it a little easier and less messy to make.  The final product for this recipe is just as good if not better than the stuff you get at the grocery store, but after making it twice, I discovered a couple things that really help the mixing process.  

First, the suggested serving size in this recipe is about 1T, and I'm not aware of anyone who doesn't put at least 2T in each glass they make, so consider that when estimating the serving number you want to make (and remember, the batter is fantastic kept frozen, so go ahead and make extra!).  I used the serving size calculator to adjust it to 45 servings (and there are only 3 people in our home).  This # of servings allows you to use an entire 2lb bag of powdered sugar so there's less mess - no measuring needed. At 45 svgs, it then calls for 7.5 eggs - I used 6 large eggs, and 2 small ones to make that work.  The completed batch nicely fills a 1/2 gallon container which I keep in the freezer during Christmastime.  For mixing, you will find much less mess if you mix egg whites, and mix the yolks.  Then add yolks to butter, plus vanilla, then add the whites, and THEN add the sugar.  After all mixed, add spices at the end.  This eliminates the cloud of powdered sugar floating around your kitchen, as there is more liquid to help soak it all up.  I'm sure there may be a reason for the suggested order, but I've found this sequence a much less messy process.  :-) 

Enjoy!!

I've given you three stars as how a man makes his martini is a very personal thing; however, that for me is not the way you make a gin martini. 

Winston Churchill: "The way to make the perfect Martini is to pour an ice cold gin, drop an olive in it and bow in the direction of France". This is almost definitely a misquote. 

Winston is correct about the vermouth though, if he may be exaggerating slightly. The way I make one is to fill a shaker with ice, pour in about the same measure or vermouth as you have there, but, shake with just the vermouth so that the ice gets a covering, then pour the liquid away.

I then pour in the gin gin gently as to not bruise it and stir it rather than shake it to retain the flavour. Always Noilly Prat dry vermouth and always a top shelf gin.

Stuffed olive or flamed lemon rind is fine, dirtyness is to your own discretion

If you want, you can add baby pickled onions on a pick instead of an olive, in which case it is called a Gibson martini.
