One of my favorite adult beverages! This one is absolutely PERFECT! Thanks for sharing!
A pitcher of these is great on a Friday night!
Yummy!  My husband suggested a dash of nutmeg on the top, and it really pulled it together (not to mention making the presentation a little nicer -- brown like a deer!)

This was a great idea, a little bit strong for us, but so cute.  I even put chocolate milk in martini glasses for the kids and garnished with the cherry and cinnamon sticks.  Thanks for sharing this creative recipe

Wow! Really strong!  I made them with lesser volumes of the alcohol and added the nutmeg as suggested by another person on here.  The nutmeg really does finish off the drink so I definitely recommend that.

I loved the presentation so much but had to change the recipe to suit the crowd. Thanks for the heads up that the ingredients as written were too strong.
I made it with equal amounts of vodka, Frangelico and Baileys.
It was great!
Brilliant!
I thought it was good but my guests felt like this was very strong!  The kids idea with chocolate milk was a hit.  Make sure you use a very shallow glass so the antlers stand up.
This is an adorable holiday drink and everyone got a kick out of it.  I followed other reviewers' suggestion and used half the amount of vodka which worked out well for us.
Tacky and disgusting

I love the idea of this drink and really wanted it to be a hit, but sadly, it wasn't. We're used to drinking martinis, but we all agreed that this was very strong, even for us. I feel like this drink is missing some sort of mixer that would cut the alcohol a little and add some color. In addition, for the Rudolph thing to work, you either have to use very small martini glasses without a lot of depth, or very long  cinnamon sticks - and I bought the only ones at my grocery store in standard length. Therefore, they barely stick up from the glass, and you lose the effect.
The presentation is cute, but the flavor just didn't appeal to me.  It's not bad, just not a favorite.
Really good, but a bit too strong (and I am a big martini drinker!).  Just cut the vodka by half and the recipe is perfect.

I was looking for a recipe close to one my Mamma use to make, and this one hit the pickle!  Mamma's pickles always got the blue ribbon at the county fair, and once I finally let theses set up they sure were close to her blue ribbon.  Thank you for bringing back such a great memory.  I did add a little sprig of fresh dill into each jar, just like Mamma did. ??
It was too salty, I would cut the salt at least by half if I made again.
Way to salty. Won't use this again.

This tasted great, even after one a couple of days in the jar. I'm sure it would have been better after a couple of weeks. I did use garlic powder because it turned out my garlic was spoiled.  Next time I would use less onion because the ratio of onion to cucumbers was not like I liked. I also used powdered cloves because my whole cloves were not to be found. I sliced celery instead of celery seed because the store was out.  My 5-year old granddaughter loved it so much I sent a couple of jars home with her. Changes or not it was excellent. I made another batch with fewer onions and plan on making more this summer.
Wish I had processed these so that I could enjoy them longer. I really prefer that vinegar bite. Thought this recipe was a prefect balance between sweet and tart. Will definitely make these again.

Nice pickles, thanks!  I canned them, which is why I'm just now reviewing them.  We still have tons of pickles from last summer's canning sessions!  I enjoy these, and they aren't too difficult, but I have to say that our house prefers Bread and Butter Pickles II on this site to these.   I think it may be the addition of peppers to the others as well as the different spices that makes it for us, but we still enjoy these a lot.  Very sweet, good pickles for sandwiches or burgers.  The onions in these are pretty good too.  Thanks for the recipe!
I didn't use any salt. Didn't have any turmeric....other than those minor adjustments, turned out good.
Didnt like these, sorry. I dont know if its too much vinegar or ? but they came out way too tart. The vinegar flavor was too overpowering..
Yummy...yummy...yummy is all I can say as my mouth is full of sweet pickle goodness!

Well I just canned these it was an easy recipe however I changed it just a bit.  Couldn't find some of the spices it called for so I used pickling spice and then followed the recipe. Then I used the larger mason jars (1liter) so when filling only 1/2 the jar with vinegar mixture then topping off with hot water.... And I will wait an additional 2 wk or so before tasting

I really liked the tangy flavor. The only thing I changed was the amount of salt.The first batch was way to salty for my family. I cut the salt in half and it was great. We really liked the flavor the tumeric added.
I loved this recipe I will plan on trying it with rose water soon but I strongly suggest this recipe to any one who is looking for a spring/summer refreshment!
This makes a delicious hot tea also!  I have been looking for recipes with rose water and fleurs d'oranger.  Thanks for a lovely tea!

Oh my god. This is good. I expected this to have a stronger flavor when I made it, but I love how subtle the flavors are. And I bet you can make it with less water if you do want a stronger tea. I made it with blood oranges and squeezed a bit of the juice in which gave it a beautiful color.

Update--I've made this countless times in the last month, and it's always a hit when I serve it. One thing to watch out for though, don't steep the tea excessively or it leaves a slightly bitter aftertaste.

This was ok, I didn't care for the rose water in it and it was too sweet for my tastes. I probably wouldn't make it again unless I just put a slice of orange into some unsweetened ice tea. Thanks for submitting this recipe, it was definitely worth a try!

Like a lot of us, I don't drink enough water and for me that is directly related to the fact that I'm just not a plain water fan.  So in an effort to drink more water I've been trying a number of creative ways to flavor it - and this caught my eye. It is mild and delicate enough to drink with meals as you would water, but still has enough flavor and interest to drink in its own right as a refreshing beverage. I only steeped the tea bag for three minutes, not wanting the slightest bit of bitterness, and used Splenda rather than sugar. I found the orange to be a nice contrast to the lemon one would typically expect. The rose water was an interesting and pleasant addition and the one teaspoon was just the right amount. I was happy to find another use for the bottle of it I have in the cupboard! In addition to being delicious, refreshing and a great way to up my water intake, this is quite pretty too, especially served in a clear glass pitcher. No reason at all to limit this "Springtime Citrus Cooler" to springtime.  I plan to have this in the fridge regularly!

It took a little while for this to grow on me. I made it exactly as written, even using the optional rose water (I found this recipe mainly because I had some I needed to use up). My big addition, though, is that this needs time to develop. Maybe there should even be a step 2, to let it sit for 12 hours, or a day, or even more. I had my first glass almost immediately after making a batch, and thought it weak, with a prominent rose flavor. Plus the fact that it wasn't chilled didn't help much. That pitcherful lasted for 4 days, I think, and the last couple of glasses tasted great, with much more orange flavor. (I'm not enough of a tea connoisseur to care much about the Earl Grey flavors.) A bonus is that after the liquid is all gone, the orange slices make nice dessert-time snacks.
I have another batch of this in the fridge as I write....

I made this minus the rose water and subbing Splenda for the sugar. As a tea, I wouldn't give this many stars. As a flavored water, it would get 5 stars. The tea flavor isn't very strong, but it is a pleasant way to get more water in. I definitely plan to make this again adding the rose water to see the difference.

Three words...Simple, subtle, sublime...  This is wonderful! I bought rose water and wanted to try different recipes with it. The only thing I did differently was to substitute artificial sweetener for the sugar. It's light, but not too watery. It doesn't taste like Earl Grey, yet it doesn't taste like orange either. You'll just *have* to try it! The rose water is so fragrant and really adds to it. Thank you for this great recipe!
Lovely, light, and refreshing.  The rose water adds a lot to the drink, so don't leave it out if you're able to get your hands on it!  I used half of the sugar because my orange was extremely sweet.

This is a light, refreshing drink that would pair well with any food. To avoid the possibilty of bitternessfrom the tea, I added a pinch of baking soda,a tip from the recipe for amooth sweet tea also on allrecipes. I found it much tastier the next day than  when freshly made, as the orange had more time to infuse into the liquid, making the rosewater less dominant. I will definitely be using this recipe over the summer months as a way to stay hydrated. Thanks for the different recipe!

If you are used to eating sugar-free or someone who has to avoid sugar due to health reasons, this might be for you. I couldn't get past the after-taste that this leaves in  your mouth, and I ended up adding some regular powdered sugar along with a bit of heavy cream, to get it to the point where I could eat it.

This tasted suprisingly descent to me. I am not a big fan of frosting as I find it mostly way too sweet. This was only lightly sweet tasting. The texture was fine too with the addition of the cornstarch. I find vanilla bean a bit pricey. So, I just did a couple of drops of real vanilla extract. I tested the recipe with making half. I am a fan of chocolate, so I added 2 Tblsp of baking cocoa for half the recipe. Ty

I'm sorry to say that I didn't care for this sauce. I never got to make it thick enough, and believe me, I tried. The orange flavor doesn't make it spectacular for me. I think the amount of butter is too much.
I really loved this! I made it for Asparagus and can't wait to make it again for salmon and Eggs Benedict.  Once you start on the double boiler,  it needs full attention until done.
This was delicious. I'm glad I made it. It seemed to me that the directions weren't  correct concerning the egg whites. I didn't put the egg whites in the cheese cake
Light and tangy in a perfect mix. Note: don't take a shortcut and use packaged 'egg whites' for the meringue. A day later and the meringue has disintegrated about 50% Everything else is PERFECT!

made just like the  recipe , was very good 
will make again
I added lime zest to the cheesecake as i didn't have lemons

I don't make cheesecakes that often but I have to say this one is near perfect. I love that it didn't need a waterbath too. Mine did take longer to bake and I think I may have jiggled it too much when trying to figure out if it was done and it fell a bit. With the lemon curd and meringue you would never know though ;) I did use a jar lemon curd but in the future I would make my own instead of being lazy. My meringue was perfectly cooked, I took it out at 9-10 minutes. I did have crust issues but, I was attempting a gluten free crust and sometimes cookie crusts can be tricky. In the future I would use my go-to graham cracker crust.

This is a good cheesecake, if somewhat time consuming to make. The cheesecake itself is probably the best part for me, and I might just make the cheesecake portion in the future and leave off the curd and meringue.  (Just a tip--if you make homemade curd, don't use a metal bowl! It will leave the curd with metallic taste---use a glass bowl. No plastic either!) I'm really fond of the fact that this cheesecake wasn't baked with a water bath. It gives it a nicer, denser texture--which I really prefer. I baked the meringue for about 12 minutes, and it was browned, but the middle was still kind of soft. It could of probably baked  a little longer, but I was afraid of the peaks burning. Overall, I would make it again with a few minor changes. It was a learning experience for me lol.

Haven't made this yet, but it is very appealing sounding, hence my 5-star rating! I think the recipe should state "4 eggs, separated", as it seems the yolks would go into the cheesecake batter and the whites would be used for the meringue. Just saying....
I added 2 scoops of ice cream and then pour the soda and grenadine. over the ice cream. Grand Kids loved it!

This is a great summer treat and so different than a normal ice cream float!   The cherry flavor from the grenadine worked so well with the vanilla ice cream.  I made with two scoops of ice cream, but, otherwise made exactly as the recipe stated.

Rating it for my daughters who absolutely loved this yummy float. It's tasty, sweet, and pretty. Adjust the sweetness and taste by adding more or less grenadine. 

I added scoops of ice cream to a small cup, mixed the 7-up and grenadine in a different cup, then poured it slowly over the ice cream. Adding whipped cream and a cherry make it even more special. Thank you for sharing this delightful treat.
A fun twist on a Coke float.

The above recipe, on its own, is bland.  I added salt/pepper, garlic and dill.  That made it pop!
Will make again!

This was good! I opted to use this as a dip for tortilla chips, and that worked very well. I did add some salt, but that was my preference and my only change. This is on the thicker side, so to use it as a dressing you may have to thin it out a bit more. Thanks for sharing. :)
Its delicious, While i used more milk and chocolate chip icecream instead, it tasted awesome. Odd texture and hard to blend, but very good.
It's delicious, though not nutritious. :D sorry bad rhyming there. I love the idea of chocolate chips! Picture helps a lot, and yummy yum yum! Thanks for the AWESOME recipe!
try half cup of milk instead. thinner shake but mixes well.

I made this for one this morning, adding a tablespoon of instant coffee granules.
Reminds me of the Big Train coffee drinks that I love so much here from my favorite coffee stand. God bless you for posting this recipe. TIP: Next time I'm thinking of adding smushed Oreo cookies to make it more like a Cookies and Cream Big Train.
noone was eating the icecream in the fridge so I decided to make this. I added  1 1/2 scoops of icecream, more milk. My sister really liked the chocolate chips in the shake
Awesome ... i loved it :D
I love chocolate milkshakes. Not so fond of the chocolate chips though. The pieces kind of froze and were crunchy. It might be because of my blender though?
it was great. i just added some chocolate chips to the top of the shake after pouring it into the cup. twice the chocolate!! YUM

This recipe was awesome. If you like chocolate then you'll like this. I don't suggest that you put chocolate chips in. Also, I only got 1 serving out f it instead of 2. But other than that,it's a favorite!

There's not enough liquid in this recipe to "mix", at least not when I put all the ingredients in the mixer.  Everything just kind of stood there and I had to use a spoon to shuffle the contents, then I had to add more milk (about 1/2 cup?) just to get things moving on a consistent basis.  Last, there were 2-3 large chunks of ice leftover in the shake, and I had the blender on the next to highest speed.  Taste was finally ok, but would probably leave out about 1/2 the chocolate syrup.  For me, just too much modification to the recipe for it to be complete and work in the blender.
Good recipe...does not make as much as it says it will make should be doubled. It tasted amazing. Use miniature chocolate chips.
It's like drinking cake batter; not at all like a milkshake. It was tasty, but I am NOT impressed!
Oh, my kids were excited about this one.  Chocolate, blended with more chocolate, and then more chocolate on top of that.  Huge hit!
WOW!!! This is such a good recipe.  It tastes awesome with whipped cream on top.  Thanks so much Melanie

Whoa, this should be named death by chocolate shake! There was no way my mixer was going to budge, and I have a strong one, with 2 tsp of milk. I ended up using 3 Tblsp. and it worked. For the chocolate drink mix I used Ovaltine, as it didn't specify. The only other change I made was using low fat dairy products and sugar free chocolate syrup, which I do all the time. It was just too much chocolate for me with chocolate ice cream, chocolate malt, chocolate syrup, and chocolate chips. The ingredients increased their richness together. I could drink about 1/2 of the half a cup or so serving. I also had picked this one for the lowest of the calories, per shake, but now I am starting to wonder about the accuracy of the numbers considering all the ingredients. The other person did finish off their drink no problem though.
I used hot chocolate drink mix instead of chocolate drink mix, but otherwise made exactly according to the recipe and it was so good! I will be making this often!

This recipe is good but needs a few changes, first it was delicious but a bit chocolaty so i added a scoop of vanilla icecream also, it didn't make that much so i would double the amounts that the recipe gives you.  Also it turns out very good but the ice might not blend as well and might make it a bit chunky, but the good thing is ice is water so it can melt!  Overall this is a very good recipe and I would reccomend it to everyone!

Great tasting recipe.  I used the 10 oz. package of frozen spinach and the loaf of frozen bread, but halved the rest of the ingredients, and ended up with just a large amount to fill the 8 pieces of dough.  The dough was easy enough that my seven year old granddaughter rolled out the eight pieces of dough.  She really enjoyed herself and was very proud that she was able to do it.  Thanks.
Good, but not unbelievable.

This was pretty good. I added fresh garlic and used low fat ricotta as well as refrigerated pizza crust. I made 4 good size calzones from this and still had a lot of filling left over (which I froze).  I wasn't crazy about the pizza dough so I think next time I will make my own dough, something that has a little more flavor.  We did dip in spaghetti sauce.  Delicious.

I loved these, however not all of my kids would eat them.  These are better than the ones I used to buy at the deli.  I will keep this recipe for a long time and make them from time to time, definitely a keep recipe.
Its a good recipe overall but I would prefer a little less spinach. I will be making this again with some minor alterations.

This was a very good filling.  The changes I made were to sauté Italian sausage, drain and cool.  Next I mixed the ricotta, mozzarella and parmesan with a wooden spoon in a bowl, next added the eggs.  I mixed this well and added half of a head of fresh spinach.  I found the frozen to be too watery.
Once the sausage was cool I spread it to the bottom of the calzone then covered it with the cheese mixture.  Next I sealed the calzone and proceeded with the cooking instructions,  I covered it with Chef John's tomato sauce and it was delicious!

Fantastic - family loved it.  I used whole wheat dough from the bakery at the supermarket (healthier).  I substitued green peppers for spinach on my daughter's request.  I would like to try to spinach next time.  I served heated sauce on the side to dip cut up pieces in.  Yum, yum :)

This was very good. I cut the recipe in half and it made 4 good-sized calzones. I think there's a typo with the amount of Italian seasoning to use.  I used 1 teaspoon and it was just right.  I also used the Pillsbury pizza crust (in the dairy section) and it worked great.

REVISED: I made these once before and my husband wasn't crazy about them; he said they tasted too much like ricotta cheese.  However, I made them again for myself and the kids and whaddya know, they were delicious!  All four kids gobbled them up!  I made them just as the recipe stated with the addition of sauteed onion and garlic. Turns out it's just my husband who's crazy.

These were very good - and so much easier than I thought a calzone would be.  I made half with the spinach and the other half by using diced pepparoni, onion, and green pepper.  Served with marinara sauce for dipping.  Also, like another reviewer, I used the refridgerated pizza dough.  Very good and would make again for a quick Italian dinner during the week.

I was out of ricotta so I used large curd cottage cheese & when they were nearly done baking they burst & spilled out on the pan (but that crispy, cheesey stuff was tastey!).  Brushed them with garlic butter & coarse salt prior to baking & we dipped ours in jarred spaghetti sauce thickened with 2 TBs of tomato paste, WOW!  fast dinner, fattening & tastey.

Being a poor college student, I made some substitutions and they still turned out incredibly delicious! I put in one package of softened cream cheese instead of ricotta, which I know is no proper substitution, but it made the mix creamy like it needed to be, and it turned out yummy! Also, I used powdered parmesan, which works if you don't have the grate-able stuff on hand. And then I added the garlic salt and onion powder as well as cooked, cubed chicken. I brushed the outside with butter and sprinkled with parmesan, as someone else said. My husband told me we need to make these again really soon!
I really liked these calzones, but instead of bread I used crescent rolls so it wouldn't be so much bread to eat.  It turned out great.  I also added pesto to the mix. Will make again.

I didn't realize the recipe called for 2 lbs of dough; I had only bought 1 lb, but everything still came out fine. I made one long (log) calzone, and the top/middle was busting at the seams, but of course it didn't change the taste and just made it look that more appealing. I also added garlic powder to the filling but that would be optional to someone else.

We loved these versatile calzones.  I added black olives and canadian bacon, but the options are endless.  The filling oozed out of mine.  Maybe I filled them too full, or didn't seal the edges enough.  They were still fabulous.  I used my favorite pizza dough recipe and we dipped them in pizza sauce.

very good recipe- i did make a slight adjustment adding sausage and using a refrigerated pizza roll, but followed everything else as stated. after some effort, was able to coax a 5 year old to try it despite the "green stuff" and it disappeared within minutes. used excess dough to make breadsticks. served with a cucumber & tomato salad. delish :)

Delicious! I followed the recipe except for the dough. I used Pillsbury Refridgerated Pizza Dough (one roll made 4 square calzones). It was really yummy & since I didn't have to roll out dough, it was really a quick meal to put together. Near the end of the cook time (it was definitely less than 30 minutes) I brushed egg white on the top to give it that glazed texture.
I will definitely make this again.
These were really tasty, but be sure to flip them 1/2 way through - otherwise you'll end up with 1 doughy side!
Yum!!  Prepared exactly as written.  We topped them with Ragu Traditional Pizza sauce.  May try adding different ingredients next time.

I have made these at least 30 times with a few additions to the filling. I add 10 button mushrooms and cook then dice 3 chicken breasts. I place all the ingredients into my food processor and pulse it for about a minute. It ends up being a double batch, but I make 2 batches of pizza dough from my bread machine and after baking it all, I toss the leftovers into the freezer for another meal. I control how big I want them to be.  I once served them as an appetizer, making them really small (although somewhat tedious) but everyone raved. My hubby likes these served with pizza sauce, my kids prefer ranch dressing.  REALLY YUMMY!

These were wonderful and very quick to mix up.  I used pizza dough as some suggested.  I've always added a pinch of nutmeg to ricotta mixtures, so did so in this case as well.  Lovely.  Will try some of the variations suggested.

These were really great!  My whole family liked them.  I used refrigerated pizza dough and I used 3T fresh mixture of oregano, basil, garlic chives and thyme and 1T dried Italian seasoning and I thought that was right on with the spices.  I also cut up a spicy brat and added that to the mix which was really good. And I added 1/2T mayo and a dash of hot pepper sauce like other reviewers suggested. I like pizza dough spread really thin on these, otherwise they seem to bready to me.
I really liked this dish.  I followed the directions exactly and they came out great.  My boyfriend wasn't crazy about them but I knew that he wouldn't be.  At least he ate the whole thing.
We did not care for this.  if you use the new dough that says just to roll it out it was very very very difficult to do that.  nobody like this.
These were great and it's an easy recipe to follow. I did use a can of frozen pizza dough because I didn't have frozen bread dough and they were delicious.
Not very tasty.  Will not make again.
YUMMY!  I made these for my Bunko girls and they loved them (Hubby did too)!  I also added mushrooms and garlic and used canned pizza dough as recommended by previous reviewers.  DELISH!

I make something pretty similar to this, but have a few additions that really make it pop.  1) Decrease the Italian seasoning or skip it completely.  Instead, brush some pesto onto the inside of the dough before you roll it up (store bought Progresso works- cheap and easy).  2) Instead of frozen bread dough, you can buy fresh pizza dough in the cheese or deli section of most grocery stores.  Tastes amazing.  3) Ricotta is optional.  Just the spinach and mozzarella combo with the spinach works great as long as you serve it warm.
I topped the calzones with some tomato-mushroom sauce!  MMmmm...it turned out delicious, but be sure to top them with the sauce.

I made this great, super simple recipe for dinner last night. Like other reviewers, to make it even easier I used the Pillsbury Pizza Dough in a can. I also added sauted garlic & onion, crushed red pepper seasoning & pepperoni pieces to the recipe. Served it with salad & warm sauce. Absolutely excellent! Definately a keeper!
Good recipe. I added extras to my spinach mix. I included garlic salt,extra parmesan cheese,mozzarella cheese and fresh parsley& basil.
Very bland
Delicious! Thank you for the recipe! I will definately make it again and again. :)
So delicious.  Worth the time.

I made this with a pizza dough recipe.  I added chopped red bell pepper and cooked chicken to the filling - I only made 1/2 the filling recipe and it made 5 calzones.  Turned out very nice.  Will definitely use this one again - very amenable to tweaking.
Will add some sausage or bacon next time for my husband's preference. But we all enjoyed them very much
I made my own pizza dough, but other than that, followed the recipe. My family LOVED them, and the kids even ate the spinach!

Love this recipe. I did cut the italian seasoning down by half.
Try making with cottage cheese because Hailey doesn't like ricotta cheese.
I also bought the pizza dough in the dairy isle at P&C

My kids (age 5,7) actually made these with a little help! We forgot the parmesan cheese and only had 1 TBS italian seasoning left and they still came fanstastic. I would probably stick with the 1 TBS seasoning as any more might have been too much. Great way to sneak little spinach in their diet! We added pepperoni to half of them and we sprayed the tops with a little butter spray about 10 min before they were done. Next time will try with sausage and mushrooms.

My husband and I LOVE these calzones!!  I was nervous about making them for dinner as my husband is a meat-guy but he really enjoyed them.  I added a bit of Italian seasonings and used Pilsbury pizza crust.  I brushed the tops of the calzones with melted butter mixed with garlic with gave an extra touch.  The recipe made four huge calzones with extra filling.  I froze the leftover fillings and then used them later stuffed into pasta shells and topped with spagetti sauce (baked covered about 20 min - made enough for 3 people).  This was amazing!!
I added feta cheese so I could call it a four cheese calzone. It was a big hit.
It was just ok... i won't make it again I'll be trying new recipies. I followed it exactly as written. Very bland tasting.

This was pretty good, at least the men in my family liked it a lot. I made my own dough, used low fat ricotta and only used one scant tablepoon of Italian seasoning which we felt was plenty for us.  Good recipe!

My boyfriend LOVED this.  I used the pizza dough, onions, and garlic powder as suggested.  I also added chicken since he won't eat something without meat.  It was a huge hit.  Only made 4 with the pillsbury pizza dough, so I have a lot of the filling left.  I'd recommend cutting the recipe down to 4  or 5 servings if you end up using the dough, or just buying two tubes.
These were delicious and so easy to make.  Next time I will make a little less filling, though.  Sauce on the side for dipping is a must!
My huband and I loved this recipe, I made a nice italian red sauce for dipping, top notch!

I halved the recipe (just 2 people at home)but did use all the spinach and added soem diced pepperoni.  I used homemade whole wheat bread dough, and brushed them with an egg white wash before baking.  They were crispy and delicious!!  I will definately make these again!
My family loves this recipe!

After reading other reviews, I made a few changes to this recipe and it turned out great (meaning my kids actually liked it) and it was pretty fast.  First, I cut the recipe in half.  Instead of buying different cheeses, I skipped the ricotta and just used a 2 cup package of shredded Italian cheeses.  I also added some sauteed onions, garlic, and red pepper to the spinach mixture.  I used way less of the Italian seasoning.  Finally, I bought Pillsbury's thin crust pizza dough instead of bread dough.  I realized that if I unrolled the dough and held it by the edges, it would stretch out on its own.  Then I cut it into rectangles, filled half the rectangle, and folded over.  My calzones weren't in the traditional form, but no one cared.  I brushed the top with olive oil and added a bit of parmesan.  Be careful with the baking time.  My calzones only took about 15 minutes.
I didn't have any frozen white bread dough so I used pillsbury crescent rolls (if you choose to use these be warned that they will cook in only 11 minutes). Yummy!
I followed the recipe except that I added a cup of feta and used pizza dough instead of bread dough. This was good but a work in progress...

I actually used Pillsberry crescents instead of white bread! It worked great! It only cooked for about 20 minutes!  You should cook it until the tops are a deeper brown, that way the bottoms get done perfectly! We actually paired this with a homeade fettucini! Delicious!
Pretty good!  I didn't have bread dough, so I ended up using Grands biscuits and it turned out good for being in a pinch!

I made these calzones for dinner last night and my husband and I both thought they were pretty good. To the filling, I added chopped salami and pepperoni, some red pepper flakes, and I decreased the Italian seasoning by half. Overall, this wasn't one of my favorite calzone fillings(which is too bad, since I had a lot of filling left over), so I probably won't make it again, but I'm glad I gave it a try at least.
Made these using pizza crust made in the bread machine. Added one large clove garlic. They were delish!!!

This recipe was delicious but the white bread dough was very difficult to work with. I'm not sure if it was the brand I bought or what. But the outcome was really tasty. Instead of ricotta I used cottage cheese for a lighter alternative, and it didn't seem to take away from the calzones at all. The second night when we ate the leftovers, my husband thought it was "too much spinach" but he still ate it all. They need to be dipped in marinara for the best flavor.

spinach mixture was great.  we even personalized a few for the kiddos (turkey pepperoni, sausage, feta - etc) - the issue is with the dough.  very thick as it is a bread - so if you can't get it rolled thin enough - you end up wasting most of the finished product to get to the good stuff.  would be best with home made dough - but all in all good concept - not an easy throw together weekday dinner.  this one takes some prep and good amount of clean up (dough, flour, etc).
Definitely needs more bread, less filling, and more flavor.

I don't think this recipe deserves 5 stars as written, but modified it was great! Here's what I did based on other's imput and my own tastes: First of all, I used frozen pizza dough (I just don't like the fakey taste or texture from the Pillsbury refrig. kind). Then for the cheese mixture I cut back and didn't use all of the container of ricotta (others have complained about too much), I added 3 sauteed cloves of chopped garlic that had been sauteed in a bit of olive oil, some chopped up turkey pepperoni (surprisingly good) and 2 Tablespoons of Kraft mayo. I know you're thinking that the mayo sounds gross, but I saw it from another reviewer and it brought to mind a fabulous pizza recipe from the Pampered Chef that contains a little mayo. I cut a small vent/slit on the tops & brushed with olive oil and baked on a pizza stone. They looked beautiful and tasted delicious dipped in pasta sauce (Bertolli's Tomato Basil, my fave). Give this a try - It is great to gather everyone's wisdom & with modifications, this makes a great calzone.

These were pretty good.  I agree with other reviewers that they were a bit bland and could use some garlic and onion salt.  Instead of the frozen bread dough, I used jiffy pizza crust mix (I box for 2 calzones).  I also added pepperoni.  Even after brushing the calzones with olive oil, the crusts got crunchy, so I would suggest being very generous with the application.

My kids had "build your own calzone" night. I too used pizza crust and brushed egg over the top. I also used fresh spinach which I sautéed in olive oil and garlic. I found some organic (chicken) Italian sausage and pan fried that to go in the calzones. I followed the recipe for the cheese filling and had my kids help mix it. This was a really fun and easy dinner to make!

mmmmmmm, i made these delicious calzones as written with the exception of adding a small sauteed onion to the ricotta mixture. homemade whole wheat pizza dough compliments this recipe even more. thanks wheatfields!
These are delicious. I used fresh mozzarella and they came out great. Next time, maybe stuff them little less as most of the calzones leaked while baking.

My DH made these calzones for dinner tonight and they were fabulous...but he did change some things.  Here is what he did: added about 3 Tbsp of miracle whip, 1 tsp chili powder (could have used more), 1/2-1 tsp each garlic and onion powder, salt and pepper.  We also used "light" ricotta and part skim mozarella, but we both felt as though the amount of all three cheeses could have been reduced a lot.  Lastly, we used pillsbury pizza dough instead of frozen bread dough.  The end result was really, really yummy...but we had A LOT of spinach filling left over because we only made 4 calzones, but this filling would be really good for homeade ravioli or manicotti, so I froze half of the filling for later use.
These were good. The hardest part is working with the dough. The dough needs to be at room temp, it is so much easier to work with when it's not cold.

This recipe is a keeper! Very tasty, even the kids enjoyed them. I used fresh spinach and added 1TBL. minced garlic to the mixture. For the dough I used Jiffy Pizza Crust Mix (4-boxes). Also served them with little cups of pizza sauce for dipping as suggested.
Really solid recipe for how quick and easy it is. I made it for dinner and had the leftovers the next day on a plane trip. They were still great room temp. This would be a successful lunch box item.
Really Yummy- I used Pillsbury Pizza Dough and that was great! Everyone loved it when I made it on a football Sunday. I added meatballs and pepperoni to some.

Yummy recipe!  I made my own pizza dough and used fresh spinach sauteed in a little bit of olive oil with mushrooms, garlic and red onion.  Added some pepperonis in a few of them.  My family loved them!
Delicious! I added a few pepperoni to a few. They were so good and I will totally make them again!

These were FANTASTIC! I made them with the "Amazing Whole Wheat Pizza Crust" from this site. I can't believe how many I ate... These are now my favourite calzones. The recipe makes a huge amount of filling. I had almost half left over, so DARN! - I had to make more the next day. So delicious!
Pretty good made following the recipe (somewhat dry), but it was way better the second time I made it--added more cheese (mixture of chedder/jack, and extra mozzarella) and a package of cream cheese.
These were very easy to  make.  I used the refrigerated pizza dough for the crust and added a good measure of garlic powder to the spinach/cheese mix.  Very tasty.  Thanks.
Very yummy and easy! We used Pillsbury thin crust pizza dough (2 tubes) for the crust and had enough for 4 people to eat two meals.
I followed the recipe and found the bread to be too much. I will defin9try these again with pizza dough like others have suggested.

I think this recipe is a good base for a great calzone.  I served with generic pasta sauce from Supertarget and it was really good overall.  I halved the recipe since it's only the hubby and me and made the recipe almost exactly as written, except I added pepperoni to add more flavor.  With that said, next time I'll reduce the amount of italian seasoning a bit (thought it was really strong), reduce the amount of ricotta cheese and add more mozarella cheese.  I will also add a clove a garlic, dice up the pepperoni and add some onions and/or mushrooms. Great recipe though to alter and adapt to your own personal preferences!!
My 9 year old son made this for a Mother's Day menu @ Daycare with the other kids. This dish was their Main Dish for the luncheon and it was a hit! Have to try this myself!

My family and I love this recipe.  The only change I made is using two pre-made pizza crusts instead of the bread dough.  I have made this recipe several times and you can halve the recipe by halfing the cheeses.  We top them with warm spaghetti sauce right before eating.  They have tuened out great every time for me.
I thought this was okay but my kids loved it.
The cheese blend is excellent! It gets a little intense when it's in too big of chunks, but when we added Italian sausage, onions, and mushrooms, the flavors came out in a very pleasing combination.

delicious!  I used the stuffing to make stromboli.  I put it in the middle of Pillsbury can french bread.  then folded it (fold in thirds)..   a little corn meal and garlic powder on top and its good to go!
Too much Italian seasoning for us. If I use this recipe again I will half the seasoning.
One of our favorites!  Amke it again and again.  Served with spagetti sauce on top or on the side.

I really waned to like these, but I found them nothing special. I made them using the whole wheat and honey pizza dough recipe from this site instead of the canned dough the recipe calls for, but I doubt it made that much difference. I don't think I'll make these again.
I thought these are too doughy. I prefer filo dough or more of a crusty dough.
4 and a half stars!  Very good and easy to vary for different tastes.  I had the recipe as is, but made my kids ones with pepperoni in them (and no spinach).  Everyone loved them!

I made these into bite-sized calzones.  I had about half of the mixture leftover, so I would suggest doubling the amount of white bread dough to use all of it.  I also baked it for half of the time.  Add some marinara for dipping and you're good to go!
These were pretty good. Used the refrig pizza dough, brushed w/ egg whites, definitely serve w/ your fav marinara - needs the extra flavor.
These were pretty good.  I used fresh spinach and sauteed it in just a little olive oil with mushrooms, garlic, and onion.
These were Great! I ended up using pizza dough. My wife loved them! Even my 8 year old who "wont eat green stuff" loved them. I forgot to mention to him ther was spinach in there.

Wow! Great Recipe guys!! Nice one for the Recipe of the Week! Now, I have made these a few times and I found that they were even BETTER when you added about half a tablespoon of Mayo mixed with a sprinkle of chili powder and chives. TRUST me, It may sound wierd but you WON'T be dissapointed.
I'll make it again, but needs a dipping sauce or something.
One of my family's favorites now! I like using the fresh bread dough and not the frozen as I found the frozen one rises too much and made the calzones to thick.

I made this for me and my bf, I ended up with a lot of extra filling so I baked it in a custard dish.  I made my own pizza dough from scratch  Mix 1 packet of yeast 1 teaspoon of sugar 1 cup of water (let sit for 10 min)  1 Tablespoon of olive oil 1 teaspoon of salt 3 cups of flour  Let rise for 1 hour then follow the recipe as above.  Turned out great.  I also had a can of diced tomatoes simmer for the baking time and added some oregano and basil for dipping.  I was out of canned marinara.

Very good, very easy-my kind of cooking. ;o) Tried the pizza crust and it worked perfectly. The elasticity of the dough let it stretch easily without tearing. Thank you, Wheatfields, for the delicious filling. Thank you, reviewers, for the pizza crust suggestion.

Wonderful.  My hubby gave it a 'thumbs up'.  My kids (twin 6 year olds, 4 year old &18 monthold) all ateevery bite.  The flavor was perfect for our taste.  We used a marinara sauce for dipping.  It did require plenty of planning ahead- it took all day for the frozen loaf to rise- next time I may try the premade pizza crust.  The kids were all amazed to see a rolling pin in action.  It was a family affair for this dinner.  I brushed the calzones with a beaten egg- they looked beautiful when done.  I can't wait to make it for guests.
Loved these!  I made the recipe and froze most of them to take out individually and bake.  My three year old and I can pretty much share one for dinner!  Thanks!
So good I made it with home made pizza dough and an egg wash is highly suggested.

Yum! What a quick, easy recipe! I incorporated the suggestions of others  adding mayo, chili powder and fresh garlic to the spinach mixture and brushing the tops with butter and garlic. I also used pillsbury biscuts, which tasted great but did not hold much stuffing and tended to unwrap. Thanks for the great tips everyone!
Add broccoli, mushrooms and sausage. Made dough from Real Italian Calzones recipe.

These were good - I think that they would be better with the addition of some garlic to the filling. Pretty easy if you don't mind rolling out the dough. Next time I will make sure that I have some marinara sauce on hand, I think that would make them even better!

This was average.  My husband didn't like it at all.  I thought it was okay, but a bit bland, even when served with marinara sauce.  If I made it again, I would definitely add garlic and perhaps some sauteed onion and/ or bell peppers.

I just made these tonight, and the family loved them.  A few changes I made were using homemade pizza dough, adding some garlic salt, oregano, and cut-up pepperoni.  I also put some shallow slits on the top, and brushed the tops with olive oil and sprinkled with a little sea salt.  Will be making again soon!

At first taste they are pretty good, but after a while the spinach are ricotta gets to you.  I would like to try this recipe again with a smaller filling-to-dough ratio.  Also, maybe with something to add to the filling such as pepperoni or bacon bits.

i LOVE this recipe !!!  i make it exact. all 5 of my kids and my husband actualy loved it too(wich never happens) my 5 yr old has even requests it for dinner. anything to get them eating their vegies gets an A+ in my book :) THANKS for the AWESOME recipe.
Awesome recipe!  Everyone in the family just loves it.  It does take quite a bit of prep time, but well worth it.  I made a double batch and froze them; making it an easy after school meal.

I'm not sure if they were unbelievable, but they were very tasty indeed.  I used frozen pizza dough, my pizza spice grinder instead of the Italian seasoning and 1 1/2 tbs mayo, like another reviewer suggested.  I also sauteed some mushrooms in butter and a dash of garlic powder.  Brushed the tops with melted butter. I did have a difficult time shaping the pizza dough, so they weren't a beautiful presentation, but delicious anyway!  I was able to get 12 calzones out of the filling.  Dipped in homemade spaghetti sauce.  We will definately be putting this recipes into rotation- my kids LOVED it, my husband loved it and I really enjoyed it too.  very easy for a busy night, if you have everything frozen ahead of time.

Delicious!  I also used pizza crust because I had some in the fridge.  I didn't use spinach, but used pepperoni, mushrooms, green pepper and onions.  These were delicious!  Ranch is also an excellent dipping sauce!!!

Extremely good and recommended.  I have never made calzones before, and this was really easy.  I took the suggestion, and added artichoke hearts as suggested by another.  Also great leftover.  Will make again.
These were tasteless and unedible. After spending hours making them I ended up trowing the whole batch in the trash.
Make sure to roll out the dough pretty thin. Otherwise, there is a lot of dough in each calzone.
These are so good. One of the few recipes you don't need to change anything. They are truly unbelievable!! Thanks for the great recipe!

Yummy! First time making calzones and it went well. I added some hot italian sausage, yellow squash, mushrooms and it was excellent. I like the ease with the premade dough but I had a hard time rolling it out. Maybe it was me but everytime I rolled the dough out it would bounce right back to it's tiny little shape. I also did not need to cut into 8 pieces only 4.  Just for fun, I put marinara sauce in one calzone. It was good with and without it. Also I brushed some buttery garlic on top before baking. YUMMMMMMMY!

My entire family, aged 18 months to 29+ loved this recipe.  I used canned pizza dough and fresh spinach instead of frozen.  This was easy and delicious.  An earlier reviewer suggested brushing egg whites on top, and it did add a nice shiny glaze to the calzone.  This one is a great master recipe for a calzone.  I can't wait to make it again.

This makes a lot of filling--maybe too much.  I added 1 T of Italian seasoning and 3 cloves of garlic to the filling.  I brushed an olive oil, salt, Italian seasoning, onion powder, and garlic powder combo onto the tops of the calzones, and then sprinkled parmeasan cheese over it.  Baked them on a pizza stone. 4.5 stars.

I did not have frozen dough so I used Pillsbery pizza dough which was quick and easy.  I covered the calzones with tin foil for the first 15 min so that they would not get too brown and I cooked Italian pork sausage with chopped onion and then added it to the stuffing for more flavor.  I served them with spaghetti sauce on the side for dipping and they were a hit!

I used pre-made pizza dough, which made it super easy and they were yummy!  I would probably coat the top with butter as another reviewer suggested since they do turn out a bit hard on top.  Definitely didn't need 30 minutes cook time; as it was, the cheese was running out... So good though!

I made 4 large calzones instead of 8. They turned out gigantic and yummy. Two things I would do differently next time is make sure I had some red sauce/marinara for dipping and I would definitely add mushrooms and onions to the mixture. I will also stick to the recipe about making 8 as no one could finish the jumbo versions. This recipe could easily be altered to anyones preference.
Scrumptious!!!   1 egg yolk (used the white for brushing) extra fresh spinach, sauteed with onion and garlic Homemade pizza dough
We didn't care much for these. If I made them again, I would add something more to the filling. Proscuitto, Ham, or Chicken for example. I think this filling is better off in a pasta shell.
Filling was delicious!  Dough was very bland.  Maybe next time I'll sprinkle salt and parmesan cheeese on top before baking it.
Easy to make. I melted butter and garlic to make a dipping sause.  It was a lil dry.  Maybe next time i will add an egg to the cheese .

Our local "pizza guy" is going to be very upset because he just lost my family's standing order for no fewer than 10 of his calzones each and every week. I made these last night for dinner, following the recipe exactly (except I brushed the tops with olive oil and adjusted the fillings to accommodate family member preferences: I like spinach, my husband likes ham, my boys pepperoni and my daughter requested sausage; I will definitely experiment with other stuffings in the future). In my family, it's all about the cheese, and the proportions indicated here were near PERFECT for our purposes. Slitting the tops before baking was a great suggestion, and made for an attractive presentation. In addition, I was VERY (and most pleasantly) surprised when I compared my cost to make these vs. the price we USED to pay to have them delivered (less than $25 vs. approx. $75 -- when you include taxes and tip). I always thought calzones should be easy to make, but for some reason, it never crossed my mind they could be baked in anything but a pizza oven. My infrawave oven cooked 2 at a time in 22 minute "sessions" so I simply reheated the 4 I had cooked first in my microwave before serving (with cups of marinara sauce, ranch and blue cheese dressings as side accompaniments). A real keeper of a recipe. I believe I will be making these AT LEAST once a week from now on.
my mother loved this recepie and so did my son, he does not like spinch
I added vegetables to the filling and made some bread dough in my bread machine and this was excellent. A great way to sneak spinach into the family.

Very forgiving recipe!  I lessened the ricotta cheese because I hate ricotta, and doubled the parmesan and mozarella.  I also sauteed an onion and a carton of mushrooms and added that into the filling.  I ran out of pizza dough and so I filled squares of refrigerated crescent dough.  Also a couple slits in the top will keep the calzones from bursting.  My husband loved this!

Unbelievably Good! I actually made a huge mistake, which thank goodness turned out great. I read the ingredients in the morning and decided to make this for dinner. I didn't see the word "dough" — duh! I thought it said "bread"! So, when it came time to make dinner, I forged ahead with my slices of whole wheat "bread". I rolled each piece out as thin as I could get it. I brushed the edges with an egg wash (added salt & pepper) and filled as per the directions. I placed them on my cookie sheet and brushed each calzone with more egg wash. It turned out great!!! I will definitely make this again, but I will have to decide if I should make the same mistake twice.

I'll admit I changed this up a lot to suit our personal tastes, but the results were great!  Added meat and onions, and omitted some of the cheese.  Brushed the top with garlic butter for some added flavor.. We'll make this again and again!
These are unbelievable, indeed. I like to sprinkle cornmeal on the pan. Top with a ladle of warm spaghetti sauce.

I had a couple friends over for dinner and I decided to use this as a base recipe (with the exception of using pizza dough). I ended up adding some onion and garlic powder in with the mixture as well as chicken and bacon. I also brushed the tops with egg whites when it was close to being done and sprinkled garlic salt on top. And because I'm not the biggest fan of marinara sauce, I provided the choice of marinara or alfredo sauce to dip it in. It was AMAZING! My only complaint was after I added the bacon and chicken, there was far too much. My 2 friends and I each had a large calzone and then I ended up bringing the left overs to my sisters house for a dinner party the next night and we made mini calzones for appetizers. I would say we made at least 20 three inch calzones before running out of pizza dough and I still had quite a bit of filling left. I don't usually cook so I didn't realize how much 3 chicken breasts and some bacon would add to the total amount of filling.
these were not as easy to make as the recipe makes it sound, but they tasted great.
The cheese filling is terrific.  I used the left over for Manicotti.
Yummy. I used whole wheat frozen bread and it was ok, next time I'll try my pizza dough around it. Definately needs extra garlic!
This recipe was so easy to do.  The kids loved it and so did I.  I used refrigeraged pizza dough. Very good.

This is a really good recipe!  I added chicken to it.  I only added about 1/2 of the ricotta cheese.  I also separated the dough into smaller rectangles because when I have made calzones in the past with the dough just cut in half it seemed to be too much dough.  This way turned out perfect.
eh, these were ok. I think it would be simpler without the ricotta and egg, but thanks for the idea!

This recipe is simply delicious. I did end up using pizza dough (the thick crust kind)  thanks to the tips of other. Before serving I poured marinara sauce on top and it was so tasty. Next time I think that I will use less Italian seasoning because it was quite strong. The cooking time was only about 20 minutes.

Quite good - also bought Pillsbury pizza crust (which was ok - a little like crescent rolls so might try another one next time). Forgot the parmesan and felt really stupid.  This needs some dipping sauce - I had leftover spaghetti sauce and that really elevated this recipe from great to incredible.

I doubled the recipe so we could freeze one calzone for later enjoyment.  Otherwise, I followed the recipe to a "T".  Well, almost.  I used frozen pizza dough instead of white bread dough, and made a tomato sauce dipping sauce to accompany the calzone.  Based on other reviewers who said it needed garlic, I added a lot of garlic in the dipping sauce.  Next time, I'll add the garlic to the spinach and ricotta mixture.

Okay.  I made them with pizza dough and added crushed red pepper.  They were satisfying and fairly no-hassle to prepare, so I'll probably make them again, but may try adding some more ingredients next time.  Seems like a recipe kids would love.

So good!  I didn't have any ricotta cheese on hand so I unfortunately had to omit it.  I added a little crushed red pepper and some cooked mild italian sausage (for my meat eating men) and used fresh pizza dough the first time I made these.  The second time I used Pillsbury pizza dough as suggested by a few other reviewers.  It was easier, but I didn't like it as much.  Great recipe!
This recipe was great!  And easy.

I've never made calzones before.. so, I was nervous going in. I added a tablespoon of chopped garlic. The calzones turned out lovely. Looked very presentable. My boyfriend suggested adding Italian sausage. Along with another reviewer, I think adding mushrooms would be phenomenal. Just need to find your own taste preference. Overall, I loved this recipe and will definitely be making it again.

These were great, I've made them twice in the past week. I used cottage cheese because I like the taste better, pre-made pizza dough, a lot of fresh spinach and I brushed the calzones with egg whites before baking them. I froze a couple unbaked to have for later and they turned out just as good.
These calzones were pretty easy to make and tasted good.  Mine needed less bake time (the tops got too hard and brown for my liking) and next time I'll add meat/other toppings to the filling.
this recipe is very easy.  I made homemade white bread dough instead of the refridgerated dough pkg.  I think the filling could us a bit more...maybe artichoke hears, or chicken pieces.

I followed the recipe with a few minor modifications.  I used Pillsbury Pizza Dough.  I wanted to make small    ones, so I cut out 5 inch circles and was able to get 6 or 7 from each roll of dough. I scaled the recipe to make 12 servings and used 1 and half rolls of dough and still had a bunch of filling leftover.  I brushed the tops with an egg wash and sprinkled with Parmesan Cheese   before baking.  They came out great, although when I make then again I will probably add some garlic powder and some additional seasonings. I also made Quick Sausage and Pepper Calzones from this site and served with warmed spaghetti sauce.

Very good!  I followed the recipe quite closely and it turned out great for my first time trying Calzones.  I'm glad I read the other reviews because 20 minutes was definately enough and the brush with garlic butter kept it from getting hard. This is a keeper!
Yummy.... used prego parmesean romano sauce to dip!

This is such an easy recipe! I agree it needed some extra spice: I used more Italian seasoning and some garlic salt. I saved one egg white and brushed it and extra garlic salt on the tops of the calzones before baking. Great recipe to share with my vegetarian roommate!

I made these with frozen bread dough, sauteed fresh spinach and added 4 cloves fresh garlic and a small onion sauteed. Tossed in some red pepper flakes and crumbled italian turkey sausage. Left out the ricotta cause I didn't have it handy, then wrapped each one with a few sliced roasted hot peppers. Yum gave it a four because I altered it so much.

Good! I added 8 oz sauteed mini bella mushrooms to this and used low fat cottage cheese in place of the ricotta.  I also put some turkey pepperoni in some of the calzones.  Before baking, brush with olive oil and sprinkle some fresh crushed garlic on top for a delicious garlic flavor!

We tried this the other night.  I used the breadmaker to make whole wheat pizza dough for the bread part.  They were great!  I was estimating the spinach and the ricotta because the containers I bought were larger than the recipe called for.  It seemed it could've used a bit more spinach.  Other than that it was great!
The basic idea of this is good. I didn't like the spinach so I am going to try it with other things mixed in (ham, green peppers and pineapple).
thought these were just ok. I like ricotta but didnt think it went well in a calzone.
The filling was tasty, but I really killed it with trying to make my own bread dough.

These were wonderfully delicious! I made them, exactly as stated in the recipe, to take to a homebound family, and they raved about them.  Couldn't wait to get the recipe!  I did have some leftover filling, so the next night I used the Pillsbury Pizza Dough as per Ellie's review from 3/07, and my husband loved them also.  I'll definitely use the refrigerated pizza dough next time, as the only hard part for me was rolling out the bread dough with my arthritic hands.

I used pie dough but it worked out well.  I also used only shredded chicken, spinach, riccota, and a touch of evo, as traditional calzones do not have sauce inside.  I will try again but next time with a different dough.
Great!  Husband and I loved it!

I'm not a big fan of calzones (I usually find the bread too much) but I am a big fan of spinach. I'm giving this a 5 because I discovered it is just as wonderful WITHOUT any bread. I didn't have crescent rolls or frozen bread dough on hand, so used pizza dough instead. I also didn't resize the dough, just added more filling and cut them in half for 2 servings. I did add extra spinach (did I mention I love spinach?) Had some filling left over so put serving sizes into custard cups, cover loosely with foil and baked along with the others.  Perfect! My brother loved it with the bread - I loved it without!
This recipe was ok but it was nothing to rave about. Followed the recipe except for using pizza crust. Dipping them in spaghetti sauce made them better.
Didn't think it was all that special. My husband couldn't even eat his, but he's kinda picky. Good for one dinner, but probably will not be making again.

Overall pretty good. The amount of italian seasoning called for is a bit much. I added chopped chicken as someone suggested, which was a good addition. I also used 2 cans of pizza dough, which cuts down prep time. I only baked for 25 min.
These were pretty good, but nothing spectacular.  It was a great way to use up some spinach and get the flavor I was craving without going through all the time lasagna requires.
this was an excellent recipe. i goes well with pasta sauce on the side.

I too used the pizza crust which made 4 calzones and cooked in about 20 minutes.  I halfed everything except the spinach and seasonings and added lots of garlic and some diced cooked chicken (because my husband won't eat anything without meat).  It was quick and easy and really good served with some marinara on the side.
The filling on these did not have much flavor.  Probably will not try again.
The flavor was good, but it was a big mess.   Probably won't make it again.

My family loved this recipe! Especially my kids. My daughter actually went back for seconds, which she never does! The only thing I did different was use fresh chopped spinach. Thanks for a wonderful recipe and great way to get the kids to eat a green veggie.

A great recipe - loved it. I added 1/3 cup of feta cheese to the filling and reduced the same amount of ricotta. A local bakery sells frozen pizza dough (about 24 ounces each). I defrosted one, and cut it into 6 pieces - it was a delicious crust for the calzone. It sealed well (I crimped the edges with a fork) and it wasn't too ' bready.' I used  about 1/2 cup of filling on each calzone - I still have quite a bit left over - I'm going to use it to make turnovers with some phyllo dough leftover from another recipe.

I modified this a little bit to get a pretty good dinner set up. I made my own dough in the breadmaker, added onion and garlic powder, as well as an egg yolk to the cheese mixture, and used drained, canned spinach instead of frozen. I liked how these tasted, although I think I might like some meat in them next time.

5 stars for this one because it's extremely simple to make and tastes great. Simplicity is one of my biggest factors when it comes to cooking dinner. We ate this with Ragu sauce. Next time I will cook these a little longer, as mine were doughey in spots.

These are so delectable! to be creative, I added 1 teaspoon of cinnamon, and a teaspoon of cocoa powder. WOW. It was even better than the original! it sounds pretty weird, I know, but trust me and try it!

These were really easy to make and tasted very good. I used my pizza dough recipe for my bread machine to make the dough.  My husband thinks they would be even better with chicken - although we enjoyed them as they were!
Good, but a little too much ricotta cheese.  Kids didn't like it at all because of the spinach.

Just made these for dinner tonight.  YUMMY!  Made exactly as the recipe stated except used sausage and pepperoni instead of spinach (didn't have any).  Added a side of pizza sauce topped w/cheese on the side for dipping.  My family loved every bit of it!!
We loved it! Just added a little bacon to make it perfect

Love it! The only alteration I made was using jarred Classico Pesto for extra flavoring - about 1/4 or so. Makes it real good. We also top with sphagetti sauce.
Thanks, great recipe.
Great recipe ! I followed it as written.

My husband and I loved this recipe.  We're big fans of calzones and we love spinach puffs at Greek restaurants, so I figured we'd like these.  I made my own pizza dough and added 3 cloves of garlic.  Then I put a jar of Ragu with some red wine on to simmer while they baked.  They were an excellent dipped in red sauce.  It was a great Sunday night meal that also fed my husband Monday and Tuesday while I was out.
Yum, I made these the other day!  Easy and delicious.
Good, but filling not spectacular.  Bread dough a nice and easy way to make calzones.
I me and my family just finshed eating it was great.

This was a good starter recipe.  I was worried that it wouldn't be flavorful enough so I added sauteed garlic, mushrooms and onions to the mixture.  I also used regular fresh pizza dough.  I brushed the calzones with egg and garlic powder for extra flavor.  I will make these again.

I loved this recipe except that I like a home made dough.  So, I used one from another recipe..combined the 2 and am more than satisfied!  These are so great because you can vary the filling to whatever you are craving!  thanks

Im sorry, but this dish wasn't that good. Everyone in my family disliked this meal. It was took much trouble to make this dish, and then finding out it, that this dish wasn't even that good. I forced myself to eat this dish so that my mom didn't get up about wasting good. I was begging for dish to be finished already. My mom even tried putting ham in it and it still wasn't very tasty. I'm kinda of a vegetable lover and I do like spinach, but this meal was nasty and hard to make.

Really tasty!  I used 2 tubes of ready made pizza dough and baked for 25 min.  Next time I would use more spinach, less ricotta and only 1 egg.  It was a little too quiche like for me.  My guys loved them!

These were soo good! Instead of using frozen bread dough I made Emeril's deep dish pizza dough...which you can find on foodtv.com. I made them for dinner last night for some of my friends and they devoured them! Next time I'm going to add some artichoke hearts and some sun-dried tomatoes!

Excellent recipe! I used two packages of spinach and only one egg, my usual garlic/onion powders and Pillsbury pizza dough in the tube instead of the bread dough. It rolled out so nicely too. I brushed the top with egg white and sprinkled with parm and garlic powder. Marinara sauce on the side completed this very pretty picture. Family loved it and thanks!

delicious!  I did an egg wash on top and sprinkled with kosher salt and a little shredded parm.  Ours were perfectly done after 26 minutes.  For dipping, I made a sauce by pureeing 1 small sized can of plum tomatoes with a clove of garlic and some italian seasoning, then simmered while the calzones cooked.  Delicious!

Nice basic recipe to get you started in the right direction.  I used a can of pizza dough as another reviewer suggested.  I also added cooked chicken, marinara sauce and sauteed mushrooms and onion.  It was the additions to the recipe that made my family love it.
My kids ate them! I would have liked if they had a little more flavor. But, I will still make them again. I love how easy they are!

Giving this four instead of five b/c I doctored up the filling a bit. I added sauteed garlic, onions, mushrooms, and pepperoni to the spinach and cheese mixture. Used Pillsbury's frozen pizza dough, per another reviewer's recommendation. Brushed an egg wash over the calzones before popping them in the oven for about 20 minutes. They looked and tasted great. Really easy, fun, tasty dish.

I used homemade pizza dough ("Pizza Dough II"), and in this case, the less-browned ones were better than the well-browned ones. I think the freshness of people's Italian seasoning makes a difference-- I opened a fresh bottle and 1 and 1/2 tbsp. of seasoning was plenty to me.
Yummy. Used extra moz and pizza dough. Served with homemade marinara. Had waaaaay too much filling leftover, so we made a spinach pizza--it was delicious too!

Very good recipe! I used Pillsbury refrigerated pizza crust instead of the frozen bread dough and I like the texture that you end up with. Other additions that I recommend would be a dash of garlic powder (to taste) and any other good additions to the filling that you have around (black olives, mushrooms, etc). Very good meal to pull together rather quickly when you want something filling and comforting.

Loved this! I went a little easy on the mozza and Parm cheeses to make it more healthy, but I'm sure it would be even better if I hadn't. I added 2 chopped roma tomatoes and a cup or so of chopped fresh mushrooms. I also used one egg instead of two and didn't miss anything. Needs just a pinch of salt. My hubby and toddler went to town on this! Thanks so much for the recipe!

I thought this was a very quick and easy recipe. I only made 2 small modifications. I used 2 cans of Pillsbury pizza dough instead of making my own dough. I also added a layer of Canadian bacon slices on top of the spinach/ ricotta mixture. My husband loved this one.

This is the fistrecipe I cooked , easy too make ,tasty  I took the suggestion and I used easy pizza dough (pillbury)
I did enjoy cooking this
Added some mushrooms, garlic, and onion.  Thanks for the easy and tasty recipe!

These were ok, a little bland, next time I will add garlic or nutmeg to the filling. I do love the taste of the spinach. I made my own pizza dough and there was just enough filling for 8 calzones. Nothing really exciting and I am not sure if I would make again. Used all fresh cheeses.

This was ok.  My husband loved them.  I followed other reviews and used pillsbury pizza crust, that was good.  I did not like the filling.  I also followed other reviews and added saute'd onion and garlic, I thought that was very strange in a calzone, next time I will just add onion and garlic spice.  I  would also use less ricotta and more mozzerella.
BLAND.  I even added garlic and onions it was still tasteless.

Filling is a little bland but a good, flavorful dipping sauce helps.  Next time I'll try adding some red pepper flakes to it. Also recommend brushing them with olive oil before baking for a nice brown crust.

Not very good, unless you LOVE the taste of "dried Italian Seasoning".  I would reduce that spice by at least 50% and add anything else....garlic, onion, pepperoni.  Tomato sauce for dipping was a must because it had very little taste. Also, there was way too much filling for the amount of bread dough the recipe called for.
These were pretty good, the filling had a great taste, enjoyed them very much.
With a few minor changes this recipe is AWESOME. I used canned pizza dough, cut the cheeses way down & added more veggies (bell pepper, mushroom, onion) and spices to the mix. Very hearty & yummy.

These were amazing!  I added a little bit of cut up pepperoni, because I was feeling a little carnivorous.  I made a meal of these calzones, the "Cheesiest Potato Soup," and Faccacio (spelling?) bread (all from this site).  The Calzones were the best thing involved.  I had a little trouble flattening out the white bread dough, but next time I'll have purchased a rolling pin, and hopefully that will help me.  The recipe makes a LOT of stuffing.  I froze the rest of my stuffing to make more calzones in a few days, I hope it holds up okay in the freezer!
I thought the Italian seasoning was overwhelming.  I'd only use 1 T the next time I make these.  My kids loved them!
This was so good!  I ate it with warmed pizza sauce... yum!

I made one as stated in the recipe so that I could review it honestly (except using a can of Pizza Dough). The rest we had "build your own Calzone" night. I had sauteed mushrooms, canadian bacon, and Italian sausage. For us the meat one was better. I have enough of everything to make myself lunch tomorrow. I will spread the top with garlic butter next time before cooking (the top was hard & dry). Also, mine did not need the whole cooking time. Really easy quick supper.

Makes too much filling.  Egg once mixed with cheeses does not store well in a fridge for any length of time so if using the egg, mix it as a 2nd mixing stage once you know how much filling you're actually going to use.

Stock recipe sorta bland, this is one to really get creative on, but is a solid base point for making something that when cooked should look awfully similar to a calzone.

Ideas:  Dill? Salt? Gouda? Colby-Jack?  Meats? buttered garlic?  Add just about anything you wanna add into the mix to add an edge to it (The cheeses are mild aka bland) would be my recommendation for other people cooking it.
We loved these! I added chopped tomato to some of them. Wouldn't recommend it as the liquid would allow the dough to seal.

Excellent.....used 1 tube of Pillsbury pizza crust, rolled it out and cut into 4 rectangles. Used 1 box of spinach, 3 small cloves of garlic and 1/4 chopped onion (which I sauteed in olive oil, a little nutmeg, 1 c. ricotta, dried basil and oregano, 1 egg and a handful of parm. Filled the four rectangles perfectly with no leftover and then added mozz. cheese to the top of the spinach mixture. Folded over and crimped edges and lightly brushed with olive oil and baked on a silpat on my cookie sheet. Served with my homemade marinara sauce with lots of fresh basil. Family loved these. Also made Giada's recipe for Spicy Tomato Soup on Foodnetwork on the side. Yummy dinner. Great calzones...will try again with real pizza dough and different fillings. Thanks for a great recipe that you can make to taste!

Didn't like the frozen bread dough. It was flat and not fluffy like I'd hoped for. Added pepperoni but could've used a little more flavor. Garlic,onion,other veggies would've been nice.I did like the mixture though, it just need "more".
This is a great recipe. Did not have spinach so I subbed it with broccoli. Very good. Will make again with pepperoni and cheese and get pizza sauce for dipping. Thanks for the great recipe.
VERY VERY GOOD, I like others used pizza dough which speeds up the cook time
Made it last night - huge hit!  I could add more spices, but the simplicity of this recipe means it will be easy to alter and add whatever I want!  Thanks :)
Something needs to be done to improve the dough.  The filling is excellent.  These keep well.
Except it was a pain dealing with the pizza crust I used - too stretchy.  I had way too much filling also.

I'll give this five stars because my children (ages 5 and 12) both thought they were "yummy" and ate a whole calzone dipped in sauce. That's a green vegy and a red vegy!! As a mom I'm thrilled to get them to eat vegetagles without complaint. I made my own pizza dough in the bread machine, so I had my oven temp on at 375 (400 sounded too high for my oven and I thought the dough would burn). They turned out great. I'll add a bit of fresh garlic next time, too. Does anyone know if these freeze well either prepared but not baked or after they have been baked? Thank you for the recipe!!

I gave it 2 stars because they were vey nice looking, but the taste was very bad. The cheeses were too bland and the overpowering flavor was the italian seasoning - way overpowering flavor. I used the freezer bread dough like the recipe called for and you really have to seal the edges good or they'll pop open while cooking. I would recommend doing an egg white wash on the tops before baking. The filling just wasn't good.

Very good. I made a few exceptions. I only used one egg and added a lot of fresh basil. Instead of using frozen spinach, I used fresh, chopped spinach. Added 4 large cloves of garlic. To assemble, put a spoon of sauce on the dough, heaping pile of fresh spinach and two scoops of cheese mixture. Will definitely make again!!

These came out delicious.  I followed the recipe exact, except for the dough.  I made my own pizza dough but next time to save time I will buy the store bought dough.  They were really tasty and I even ate the calzone cold for lunch and was really good.  will make again!
I was not blown away as I was expecting, but these were still good!

The filling makes a big batch, so you can use it for a party or freeze what you don't use. We've turned calzone night into a party, everybody rolls out their own dough, adds their own ingredients and we hang out while they're baking. Makes for fun conversation and personality-typing!

My husband and I loved this!  I did make some modifications. I scaled this recipe to four servings and with my additions below I had enough filling for 8 servings. Additions: 1/2 tsp. each of garlic powder and onion powder, 2 handfuls of fresh sliced mushrooms, and 1 (2.25oz) can of sliced black olives. I used a (13.5)can of Pillsbury pizza,but should have used two cans because I had a quart of filling leftover. Used an ice cream scooper to dish the filling onto 4 inch circles of dough. I did brush each calzone with olive oil and sprinkled Parmesan cheese on top.  Served with pureed marinara sauce.  Very Yummy!

A friend of mine made these. I asked him for the recipe, he sent me here, and I'm giving it five stars! They had just the right balance of cheese and spinach. My friend made whole wheat dough instead of buy something prepared, and they were fantastic.

These were pretty good.  I halved the filling and used 1 thawed loaf of frozen white bread dough (make sure it is room temperature, so it's easy to work with).  I only used about 0.5 tsp of Italian seasoning (could have omitted it totally), and added some garlic powder.    It was just perfect to make 4 calzones.  We thought the balance of spinach/cheese was just right.  Made great leftovers, too!

These are really easy and fast.  I'm giving it a four only because I felt it needed more flavor and added more seasoning than the recipe called for, but thats a personal preference thing and I will definitely be making these again! Thanks :)
I made these a couple years ago for a friend's baby shower & forgot to review.  They are amazing!  Absolutely delicious and I didn't change anything.
These are FABULOUS!

Recipe after recipe, I've failed at creating the perfect cake/cupcake. And seeing how this recipe only had 4 reviews, I was hesitant to try. But boy am I glad to have taken that leap of faith. They were a huge hit with the crowd when I brought them to a July 4th BBQ party. Granted, I didn't use the entire recipe and tweaked the cake part of the recipe based on what I had on hand. But the result was scrumptious.

SUBSTITUTIONS:
- Vanilla instant pudding mix
- orange juice instead of lemon (not as strong a flavor, but figured put it in there so the amount of liquid is consistent)
- frosting: strawberry frosting from All About Cupcakes
- 18 minutes in a convection oven

RESULTS:
- could be more moist
- a little bit on the sweet side, so next time I'll probably cut the sugar by some
- Overall: 5 stars :)

Delicious! They are more work than your average cupcake recipe, but the extra touches like the cream filling and interesting flavors make them perfect for a special occasion. I made these for my friend's bridal shower and copied the decorating from the picture posted by another reivewr and they turned out great. Everyone thought I had bought them from a fancy bakery.
great recipe! directions for the cake part were confusing at parts. overall this cupcake was delicious

I prepared everything except the frosting the night before I went to a family breakfast. When I opened the carrier the next morning to put on the frosting, I swear, the smell was like a little bit of heaven. 

The fresh lemon in the recipe just kicks the taste of the cupcakes into overdrive. The combination of flavors mingles pleasantly and yes, it is reminiscent of raspberry iced tea.
