I then made it again, but this time no real measuring, just using up the remaining of what I had, and it was still excellent.  Even my 2 year old kept asking for more.  Her cousin also 2 years old had three bowls of it and then couldn't eat the turkey! LOL

I served this soup for an Oktober Fest party and everyone loved it!  I roasted the sqaush on a sheet in the oven (cut in half and roast cut side down) for about 45 minutes at 375 because roasting brings out the flavor better. (Plus it is a lot easier than cutting an uncooked squash).  I used butter because I never use margarine, and I added slightly more cayenne than called for.  Everyone wanted the recipe.  It was fabulous!

Yummy and rich! Perfect for a cold day when you need some comfort food. I took previous suggestions of roasting the butternut squash first and that helped a lot to make it easier to cut. I als used 1/4 of the cream cheese and it was still plenty rich and hearty!

roasted the squash at 375 for 45 mins. (as was  suggested by others), didn't use any cream cheese but did add a generous splash of whipping cream and apple cider. This soup was amazing! My husband (the critic) declared it the "best he'd ever tasted".

This soup is just fantastic!  I usually process the squash and freeze it so I will be able to make this soup on almost a  moment's notice.  After cooking the squash, I strain the cooking stock and freeze it in an ice cube tray and put the cubes in another freezer bag.  When I later thaw and add cream cheese to the previously cooked squash, I add some "ice" cubes and/or half-and-half, heavy cream or just water to thin it out a little.
Very good soup. I exchanged 2 T of onion for some fresh garlic to add some more flavor. Just make sure that you leave plenty of time to actually cut the squash (it's very hard!).

If you make this soup and don't like it, you shouldn't be cooking (eat out!) I don't like squash and think this is one of the best soups I have ever made.  I used canned broth and 1/2 the cream cheese.  Have used different spices each time I make it but love it every time!

A neighbor gave me a squash from her garden and I had never tried one before! This was easy to do and made my house smell great! (I love that) it tasted even better than it smelled!! yum! I did add a little extra pepper bur, this is great as is!
Smooth and wonderful soup! Great on a cold winter's day. Add sliced, roasted almonds for a little texture and flavor.

Love this recipe. I've made it a few times now, first time I followed a reviewer's suggestion and added half the cream cheese but everything else the same. Turned out great. This last time I was not feeling like peeling and cubing the butternut squash, so I cut in half and roasted in the oven, until it was tender. I also had a head of cauliflower so I roasted that too, and when I mixed the cooked vegetables along with the other ingredients, I used an immersion blender. And, I left the cream cheese out to cut some calories. Still turned out delicious and the cauliflower addition made it a more "meatier" soup.
This soup is SO good. I used this same basic recipe to make cream of broccoli soup too.

I did this two nights before Thanksgiving and it was well received with my dinner:)  I had some two days after and thought the flavor was even better!  I sliced the butternut squash in half and rubbed olive oil, garlic and salt and pepper and backed in the oven as recommended.  I only used half of the cream cheese too.  Yummy:)
I didn't care for it but my daughter loved it!  It tasted like I should add brown sugar to it so may try that if I make it again.

I loved this soup!  The most difficult part was peeling the squash (I used 2).  In the future I may bake it and scoop out the insides.  I also made a few other changes.  I used 2 cans chicken broth, only 8 oz of cream cheese, and allspice in place of the marjoram.  Even with my slight changes, the soup was fantastic.  It will become a staple around here.

I was looking for a recipe for butternut squash sauce for ravioli, a favorite of mine at a local italian place.  I used this recipe as the base, blended everything well and topped with parmesan cheese.  We certainly enjoyed it.
I used thyme instead of marjoram.  Only used 1/4 of cream cheese. Yummy
Very good and creamy, I only used half the cream cheese.  Fairly simple as well, I made in between baking and mixing Christmas cookies. Kids and hubby liked it as well.

if i could've given this 4.5 stars, i would have.  very good and easy soup.  great with ham or turkey sandwiches.  my kids licked it up too, which is what is really important.  i only added one 8 oz. cream cheese after alot of the reviewers said this was the way to go.  i didnt think the soup was too rich or had too much cream cheese - just right!  the reason why i didnt give it 5 stars is because although it was very good, it didnt "pop".  seems like there was something missing and i am not that great of a chef to figure it out.  maybe it would help to add a little garlic.  i didnt add the suggested cayenne amount cos i was worried it would be too much for my kids, so maybe that was the kick that was missing??(but i dont think so)  overall it is a great fall recipe!  thank you.
Rich and creamy and fairly easy to make. Delicious.

I thought this recipe was great.  It was very easy to make and it was very tasty.  I did roast the squash in the oven for 50 minutes at 350, and I only used a 1/2 a package of cream cheese, but it turned out wonderful!! This is a soup I will make again and again. Thank you

This soup is amazing; a common dinner request from friends. I always add a couple of sweet potatoes, which makes the soup a bit sweeter and the texture more creamy. I also season with garlic powder and sea salt, and use real butter instead of margarine.

SOOOO Good!  I experimented with this soup with my mom and my husband and we all indulged in just 3/4 cup each and it was not only delicious but was very rich and filling!  We all kept rolling it around in our mouths and commenting on the flavors.  The red pepper leaves a slight spice in the back of your throat, but it is great.  I followed the recipe exactly and made no changes.  It is a pretty soup that can be garnished with many things like green onion, bacon bits, or thyme.  I've never used Marjoram before, but now I will be trying it in other dishes since it was so good.  My mom hates butternut squash, but loved this soup!  We all agree that this would be a good starter soup to a pork, turkey or roast.  It's very rich, so you only need to serve about 1/2 to 3/4 cup per person.
Followed directions to a T, substituting chicken broth for bouillon.  Delicious.  Was a huge hit at a luncheon I took it to.
AWESOME!! I used only 1 packet of the nuefchatel cream cheese and it was great!!
I tested 3 different squash soup recipes before deciding which to serve for Thanksgiving. This was so delicious and so easy to make.
This is my go to fall soup recipie! It's so easy! I used 3 cups of low sodium chicken broth instead of water/bouilons. Love it!
LOVE it!  I took the advice of baking the squash and using 1/2 of the cream cheese.  It turned out very yummy!  I can't wait to make this easy impressive dish again~
superb!!
So and easy and absolutely divine !  It is better to bake the squashes before. Added both packages of cream cheese and it was great, I was running low on soup and all I did was add more water !

My friends and family realy enjoyes this soup.  I did make a few alterations however.  I left out the cream cheese ( greatly reduces fat content),  added in one pear ( or an apple can be used), and one potato ( a weight watchers trick,  gives soup the illusion of being more creamy).  I also broke up some spagettini into one inch bits and added this during the last 8 minutes of cooking.  Gives a different texture,  really great soup!!!!!
I think I'm just not a fan of butternut squash soup, but my husband loved it!
Loved this recipe! The only change I made was to 1/2 the amount of cream cheese.
Really, really good!  Just a little overpowering.  Eat with toast...  I am going to make it again!!

Amazing, awesome recipe.  By far the best Butternut Squash soup I've ever had.  Blows away so many gourmet restaurant soups as well.  I've made this soup for the past 4 years every Thanksgiving and always get rave reviews.  I used to get the whole butternut squash gourds at the supermarket and roast it in oven and cut and peel it like another reviewer suggested.  But now I pick up the pre-cut cubed butternut squash from Costco, way easier than peeling and cutting on my own.  Going to try roasting the cubes this year, think it does add to the overall flavor.  Two thumbs up, thanks so much for sharing this gem! :)

Never made squash soup before but someone brought me a ton from their garden and thought I'd give it a try. This is an awesome recipe because you can't hardly mess it up. I've made it with one cream cheese, I've used light cream cheese, I've frozen the squash, I've experimented with the spice amounts (love the cayenne)and all batches have turned out wonderful. Baking the squash first is super easy and more tasty compared to boiling. If you don't have anything against pureed soups, try it!
Cut cream cheese in half, very good but still very very rich.
I love this recipe. It's delicious and perfect for cold fall and winter days.
Simple & great tasting. This is on the menu for Thanksgiving dinner this year.

Loved it!!! . . . But like most cooks I did slightly alter the recipe. My alterations were: I added approximately 3 to 4 more cups of squash, kept the peels on, 1 more cup water, deleted the marjoram, used butter instead of margarine, used ground red pepper instead of cayenne, and cut half a cube of the cream cheese off the recipe. I also added a little extra salt-and-pepper and this concoction was freaking delicious!

This recipe is absolutely wonderful.  I did change it a little. Roasted the butternut first - cut in 1/2, scoop pulp, oil w/ olive oil, salt & pepper. 350 for approx 45 minutes.  I used chicken broth vs. water & bouillon.  I also took the recommendation of others and cut the amount of cream cheese down to 4 oz.  Perfect!!!

Without a doubt, the BEST soup recipe I've had from this site.  As suggested by others, I roasted the squash and cut the cream cheese back to 1 (8 oz)package.  We devoured this, with a small bowl left over for my husbands lunch.
Only half a container of cream cheese

This recipe is fantastic!  I have made this soup twice, and everyone who tries it loves it!  I must admit that I made a few changes.  I roast the squash first, and I add in extra cayenne pepper and some curry powder (I like mine with a little kick).  But my biggest change is that I cut down the cream cheese significantly - I only use 4 oz (half of a block), and it comes out perfect.  Smooth, creamy, and delicious.
Great recipe!

Flavor is excellent...I would thin I out a bit more since I was very thick.  Has anyone froze the leftovers and reheated successfully? Two packages of cream cheese is a lot of dairy and wasn't sure it would freeze well.
This was absolutely delicious. I used half the cream cheese recommended and it was perfect!
I served this as an option on a birthday buffet at church and everyone loved it, in fact it was so creamy that some people thought that it was a dip to go with the crackers I set out with it.
I added this pureed soup to homemade potato soup and served it to my son's future in-laws who are vegetarians. It was a hit! I'll make this recipe again.

Amazing.  It won rave reviews at home, and rave reviews when I took some leftovers to my parents.  Will definitely cut down the amount of cream cheese and use neufchatel next time, as it was very rich (but still very good).

Great soup for a cold winter day!  If you live near a Wegmans do yourself a favor and opt for their precut family size package of butternut squash which is 3lbs total.  I used almost the whole 3lbs and only one block of the cream cheese then added a little Lawry's seasoning salt at the end for some extra flavor.

Delicious was to use squash that my whole family loved!  (Even the 4 year old!)  I don't have a food processor, and my blender died on this meal, so I used a hand mixer and it did a great job puree-ing the squash.  Will definitely pull this out again as the weather turns cold!!

Wow!  On a scale of 1 to 5, this recipe is a 10.  I've been using this recipe now for years and it is a staple recipe in our household.  I only use 1/2 package cream cheese and it's still wonderfully creamy.  For ease, I also skip the onions and butter and just add 1 tsp onion powder.
I'm sorry, but I thought this soup was horrible. I hated the texture and cream cheese taste.
Wow.

This was a very easy recipe. I brought it to work for a function and had to hand out the recipe to a few people as well.  Listening to the other reviews, I cut the squash in half and put a little butter on it then baked it on a flat sheet with a little water in the bottom for an hour at 350 and it came out perfectly.  I also halved the cream cheese as one package was plenty and it turnes out really creamy.  Last change I made wasnt intentional. When I went shopping I forgot the broth, luckily I had some beef buillion at home and thought id give it a shot using that instead of chicken.  I havent made the original so I dont know if it was an improvement or not but it was amazing. Will definitely make this again. The cayenne gave it just the perfect touch.
EXCELLENT  SOUP FOR HOLIDAYS OR ANY WINTER DAY! WILL MAKE IT ALL THE TIME.
too sour. :(
I followed this recipe exactly, and it was delicious! So creamy and rich... a little bit too rich. I tried using light cream cheese, but still had to half the amount. Still, delicious!
This soup is fabulous!!! It gets rave reviews every time I have served it.  I only made 2 small changes.  I only added 1 8-oz. package cream cheese and I added a scant teaspoonful of Turmeric.

This is excellent.  I DID roast the squash in the oven and cooked the onion in broth (rather than sauteeing); I only had enough ingredients to make a half-batch and only used 4 oz. of cream cheese.  However, as other reviewers have stated, it would be delicious withOUT the cream cheese!  It's a simple recipe, but the results are phenomenal.  Thanks, Mary!

Great recipe! I changed it up a bit ... Used no soy gluten free butter and only just a spoon of cream cheese and sprinkled goat cheese. The cayenne pepper is a must. It gives a nutty creamy soup with a good kick (cayenne).

Loved the taste but I changed it up the recipe a little. I used butternut and acorn squash. But kept everything else the same. Soooo good. Oh and also forgot to put in the blender tried mixer but next time I will use the blender. But still turned out great.
Never knew I liked squash 'til I made this!  I followed the other reviewers' advice and cut the cream cheese in half.  I also didn't have marjoram, so I substituted curry and it was delicious.

Absolutely delicious!  I baked the squash in the oven as others suggested and that was wonderful and easy.  I did not measure my onions, just chopped up two smallish onions, so I'm sure I had more than 6 T, but I like savory soups, so I did that on purpose.  I also only added a couple ounces of Neufchatel cheese - a little less fattening than cream cheese.  I added just enough to change the color of the soup and pureed it all together.  It was not sweet at all (may have been with all the cream cheese) - it was nice and savory, the way I like it.  The cayenne was delicious in it.  I make soup from summer squash pretty regularly, but I liked this even better.  My husband raved and my kids even liked it - I just added a little milk to their bowl to bring down the spice a bit (they are 3 and 5), but a little dab of sour cream would have been great for a garnish for them too, if I'd had some.  I will definitely make this many more times...thank you for the recipe!
I made this but skipped the cream cheese.  Loved it, quick easy and tastes like something that simmered for much longer.
Thank you!! This recipe was excellent!!

I followed the recipe exactly!  I did, however, use an immersion hand held blender to combine all the ingredients right in the soup pot.  Thin the soup with the simple addition of additional chicken broth.  Delicious !

What a hearty, rich and creamy soup!!! This will certainly be a winter staple this season.  I used a 32oz package of chicken broth instead of the bullion cubes and water and it tastes like a dream!!!!
Made it just as the recipe called for; sprinkled some pumpkin seeds on top.  It was amazing!!!!
I tried this recipe using Philadelphia cooking creme sauce instead of cream cheese and basil instead of marjoram and it was wonderful!  I plan to prepare it for my next dinner party.
DEELISH!  Followed advice from others, halved the cream cheese, bumped up the red pepper, added a little garlic powder and ground ginger.  Perfect!

Amazing! I went back for thirds!  I put a little more squash then the recipe called for so my soup was really thick and I used a bit of basil instead of the marjoram.  I also substituted half and half for the cream cheese.  I will be making this often.  Thanks for the recipe!!
I did everything  except I used 3 cups of low sodium chicken stock and only 8 oz. of 1/3 less fat cream cheese.  EXCELLENT RECIPE!  Thank you!!
A sprinkle of nutmeg after serving topped it off.
Fantastic!  I cut the squash in quarters, rubbed with butter and sprinkled with cinnamon/nutmeg before roasting it.

Pure. Autumn. Heaven.  This is OH SO GOOD...I've made it several times and have passed the recipe on to friends per their request.  I like roasting the cubed squash to get it carmelized and only use half the called for cream cheese.  The cayenne gives it that little extra something! Thanks!
This is one of my very favorite recipes! I add a clove or two of garlic to the onion, cut the cream cheese in half and substitute heavy cream for the rest. I always get rave reviews! Thanks!
This is delicous!!!!!

This soup is very good, but I did make a few changes. Like many other reviewers, I roasted the butternut squash in the oven instead, and blended in just one 8 oz package of reduced fat cream cheese and the soup was plenty creamy.  I also minced two cloves of garlic and about a tsp of fresh ginger to give the soup a little extra kick.
Fantastic! I made this for Thanksgiving and people were practically licking their bowls - even the one who claims to hate squash. I also roasted the squash and used 1 pkg of neufchatel cream cheese.
I have absolutely loved it! It is better than the one I had in a 5 star restaurant. Highly recommend it! I made it exactly like the recipe calls for .
Perfect as is, but be forewarned - it's rich. Small portions will do.
I made this for Thanksgiving this year for my husbands family.  I couldn't keep my father inlaw out of the pan.  What a great soup for the rainy day we had.
Very bland. I would not make this again.

This was a really good soup & for Halloween festiveness I put it in a pumpkin to serve. My family thought it was great! I made 2 batches, 1 with regular cream cheese & 1 with non dairy cream cheese. My husband thought the regular cream cheese one was AWESOME!

Excellent!  The changes I made were to roast the squash, onion and 4 cloves of garlic together, then sub 1 cup of apple juice for broth and use 4 oz. crm cheese. Sweet from the roasted veggies, great for kids!  Will make often.

This was pretty good, but we made a few changes. We thought the cream cheese was awfully fattening, so we cut that out and replaced it with 3/4 cup of milk. It was still very creamy. After tasting, we added some red pepper flakes and some cumin.

I thought that this soup was AMAZING!!!  Perfect for a cold evening and complete comfort food!  It was really quick and easy as well!  I only used one package of cream cheese.  I'm sure it would have been creamier with two, but it was cheaper and healthier to cut it in half, and I wasn't disappointed.  I also added some "Better Than Bouillon" to it to add flavor and some garlic.  Very happy with the results!

This was wonderful.  I roasted the squash with some Olive Oil, Cinnamon, and Coriander for about 60 minutes.  I added a diced potato to the soup mix to thicken a little.  We just added a spoon full of cream cheese to our bowl and it was perfect.  I will be making this recipe a lot :).

I added a carrot, chopped, and 1 stalk of celery, sliced with the onions when I sauteed them after seeing another butternut soup recipe.  I also used only 1 pkg of cream cheese as someone else had suggested.  It was very creamy with that one and I think would have been too rich with 2 pkgs.    I also roasted the squash pieces with some smashed garlic cloves as another person suggested.  Then everything went into the crock pot and simmered for about 3 hours.  Delicious!  I will definitely make this again.
Delicious good flavor however we preferred only 6oz cream cheese

So Good! I also roasted the squash ahead of time.  So easy, but tastes time consuming.  I'm making it the night before Thanksgiving, and I know that the flavors will only get better by tomorrow! Thanks so much!
Very good - make sure to cut the cream cheese in half.  Added carrots & sweet potatoes in with the squash.  Yummo!
Fantastic - But I found no need for 2 pckgs of cream chesse. I only had one package and it didn't need anymore. A GREAT recipe - a hug hit last weekend at (Canadian) Thanksgiving dinner!! Thank you!!
It is possible that I don't like squash soup, but I wanted it to be more flavorful.  I even added some apple.  Perhaps will try something with more spices next time.

This recipe is pretty good.  The only kind of squash I've ever had before was fried squash and it was less than tasty.  I give 4 stars because I think it needs to have something in it...I added a little more cayenne pepper and salt and pepper to taste when i was finished cooking it.  Also, I added a can of kidney beans (well rinsed)-I think this soup would also be a good base for a chowder or creamy stew.  Its also very good for dipping a crusty french or sourdough bread.  Overall pretty good-just may need to do some tweaking based on your own tastes.
Much too rich.

Delicious!  I microwaved the butternut squash first to make it easier to cut, added a potato, and only use a bit of the cream cheese (and froze without the cream cheese as another reviewer suggested).  I didn't have marjoram, so used oregano.  And used homemade broth instead of water & bouillon!  Delish!

Loved the base of this soup, but I also adjusted for our tastes.  I roasted the cubed squash tossed in olive oil and salt & pepper. Used 4 oz low fat cream cheese.  I added fresh ginger and used Ancho chili pepper as it complements the sweet flavor of the squash.  After pureeing, I finished the soup w/ a swirl of FF half and half in the bowl.  Pretty, Yummy and really easy!!!
fantastic. can't wait to try with other squashes. Made for a local homeless shelter - servings increase easily.

This was incredible!!!  I've never made anything with butternut squash before so I did take some of the other reviewer's suggestions.  I halved the squash, brushed it with olive oil and then roasted it.  It was super easy to peel after that.  I added some garlic to the onion, used half the amount of cream cheese and left out the cayenne pepper.  It was perfect.

This soup was delicious.  I chopped each butternut squash into large chunks, coated with a little bit of olive oil and seasoned with salt and pepper.  Roasted at 375F for about 1.5 hours until the squash had caramelized and became very soft.  The squash was so sweet and almost buttery when it came out of the oven - so good!  Sauteed the onion and 1/2 of a cortland apple and then added that, the butternut squash and the stock to the blender in batches and pureed until smooth.  Heated it gently in the stock pot with 4 ounces of neufetchel (1/3 less fat) cream cheese.  Added a little more cayenne than the recipe called for and adjusted salt & pepper to taste.  

Some things I may try when reheating leftovers: 
Add just a dash of nutmeg and/or cinnamon.  
Adding just a bit of very finely minced fresh sage from the garden.  
Saved the seeds from the squash and may make some spicy toasted seeds and top the soup with it.
Made it for potluck.   Huge hit

Sorry, but I didn't like this dish. The cream cheese gave the soup an odd "tangy" flavor, which neither my husband or I enjoyed. Also, and maybe it was the butternut squash I used, but the soup came out "yellow", not orange and the color was unappealing.
I made it exactly as the recipe states and it was perfect!  Really, very nice!

We loved this soup!! So creamy and so easy to make.
The hardest part was peeling all the acorns.  I took like the recipe said and cooked the squash for 20 min, but I put a lid on it even though the recipe didn't say to do so.  I would serve it at a dinner party
As an appetizer it was so good. We dipped homemade bread in it and my husband ate 3 bowl fulls.

This is a really good recipe.  It would probably have been fine as is, but we cooks love to tinker!  I roasted the squash with butter, salt, pepper & brown sugar for 40 minutes at 350.  I sauted onion, garlic and 1 small apple in the butter and then added almost a cup of apple cidar (all I had left) and 2 cups water to the onion mixture.  I added chicken boullion, @ 2 cups of leftover chicken, oregano, red pepper, salt & black pepper.  I used only 1 package of cream cheese and only had 1 medium squash, so blended it and added it.  I also like to chew my soup so threw in some leftover brown rice.  The consistency was just right, but a little sweet.  Maybe I'll leave out the cidar next time.  Everyone liked it very much.  Thank you for the recipe.

I used "not chicken chicken broth" sounds funny,to keep it vegetarian. I also used less cream cheese after reading reviews. And according to the poster. Glad i did because i think more and i would have lost to much of the butternut taste.  Thanks am going to make it for thanksgiving

Made this for lunch and was excellent! I didn't have marjoram so put in a little thyme instead. Also threw in a few carrots for sweetness. Tossed all ing. in a covered stoneware and cooked in the microwave until all veggies were soft and then blended. Definate do-again!

Okay, I'll admit I cheated by using the frozen cubed butternut squash. Very tasty with the spices but I think I may have been a little heavy handed with the red pepper but my hubby likes a bit of fire. I didn't have any regular cream cheese but some pumpkin flavored and used  about half the container as it looked really thick after using my handheld blender. Will definitely make again!

If youre trying to be a little bit healthier when making this just omit the cream cheese and milk all together and add about 3 cups of chicken broth, this is for six servings. I swear it pretty much taste identical just a few hundred calories less, and you might prefer not to use as much salt bc there's usually salt in the broth. Hope this helped!

Just made this tonight and it was super yummy!  I had to downsize because I had a smaller squash, so my measurements were estimates.  It was pretty good as written but I tasted it before serving and decided not to add the other half of the cream cheese and to add salt and cinnamon.

I loved this recipe.  After reading many of the reviews, I made a few changes too.  3 Acorn Squash, that I cut in half and baked in the oven for 40 minutes at 375; chopped three shallots and four carrots and sautéed both in a stick of butter,  Once soft, I transferred to by Slow Cooker/Pressure cooker; added 4 cups of chicken base, 1 tbsp. of ground ginger, 2 tbsp. of brown sugar, salt and pepper.  Took the squash from the oven and scooped all into the slow cooker.  Cooked slow for 2 1/2 hours and them blended all in the cooker, finally added 8 oz of whipped cream cheese, blended that in and covered slow cooker for another 1 1/2 hours.  Husband loved it, so I dared to bring a pint to my Mother...Received two thumbs up from her.
Thanks to all for weighing in on the great recipe.

I did tweak this recipe a bit-  I used only 1 block of cream cheese, added 3/4-1 cup heavy cream, 1 tsp. more marjoram, 1 tsp. savory and I used cxn stock instead of water.  I also roasted the squash first as others suggested.  It was delish!  Very thick and definitely for a cold day!

Excellent! Only modification I made was I used only 1.5 bricks of cream cheese and they were 1/3 reduced fat. Still very creamy and rich, but slightly more figure friendly! Excellent cozy soup for those brisk fall days.

very good, with some of the adaptations suggested by fellow reviewers:  I roasted the squash, used chicken stock & real butter of course, and half the cream cheese.  However, the suggested amount of cayenne was enough--if not too much--for my family.  My five-year-old wanted to know why the top of her mouth felt "sour" (she still mixes up spicy with sour).  This would be really excellent with French bread or bread sticks to dip.
Terrific, though that's way too much cream cheese.  Using one package is fine.  Also I'm good with two or three bouillon cubes instead of four.
Really creamy even w/fat free cream cheese.  I added garlic powder ands nutmeg.  Roasted the squash first.  So tasty.

FANTASTIC recipe!  We had this with Easter dinner, and it turned out perfectly.  Minor changes to the recipe:  2 medium sized onions, butter vice margarine, chicken broth in replacement of the water, and 2 cubes chicken bouillon.  Sooo good, we had nothing left... Thank you!!!
Yummy, creamy fall soup!
Very good, definitely a keeper. I used half the amount of cream cheese as other reviewers suggested. Also used oregano instead of marjoram as that is what I have on hand.

Absolutely stellar!  And I didn't have chicken stock, or marjoram....played with measurements, as am genetically predisposed to resist any accuracy or patience with measuring, and it was a massive hit. An absolute favourite, thank you very much.  Should add that I have used water or vegetable broth for the  liquid without a problem, and definitely used only 1 brick of cream cheese--more than enough!  The touch of cayenne just sets it off perfectly.

I didn't have cream cheese on hand so I used 4 cups of half and half.  It was delicious!  Next time I will try only 2 cups because of the fat content.  I also added about a teaspoon of garlic to the onion mixture (because I'm a garlic nut) and I used 1 Tbsp of butter instead of 4 Tbsp of margarine.

For the most part, we loved this soup. I just now read the past review suggesting putting the butternut squash in the oven to help with the peeling process. I highly recommend that. I had a very hard time peeling that thing! 

The soup had fantastic flavor. Our only complaint was that it was pretty rich. I'm not sure how to remedy that problem, because, frankly, rich isn't always a bad thing. However, we all left a little hungry because we didn't eat as much as we might have if it wasn't so rich. 

With that being said, I would still recommend making this soup for a nice cool Autumn day.
Perfect Holiday treat! The whole family liked it. Followed the recipe. Thank you.

Don't change a thing!! (except only use 1 bar of cream cheese) Have made this many times as it's so easy and the taste is superb, so good you'll wish you could glug it right from the pan... but use some restraint, serve in bowls (especially tasty topped with some homemade seasoned croutons), and you'll wish you had made a double batch.  Some reviewers prefer to bake the squash, but in early fall when the weather is still so warm I would rather not heat up the oven so the stovetop works for me! Thanks so much, this one is definitely a keeper!
Did I mess up?? I tasted the soup before I added the cream cheese and it was fine. After adding the cheese it was too thick and just not good.

I have made this recipe several times to bring to harvest parties...everyone loves it!  Like other people I have cut the cream cheese in half ( using only one block). I also roast the squash in the oven with a little bit of olive oil and I use butter instead of margarine.  Otherwise, the original recipe stays the same!  Thanks for a super easy, wonderful tasting soup!

I just made this soup and I literally can NOT stop eating it!  I am so impressed with how easy it was to make yet it tastes like a gourmet soup.  I used 1 pkg. of cream cheese and 2 chicken bouillon cubes (because that's all I had).
Easy, and tasted great!  Definitely a keeper.

So darn yummy!  I didn't use oregano because I don't like it. I substituted it with Sage and parsley. I think next time I will only do half the cream cheese just to save on calories. I didn't use the blender, instead I used a blender stick. So much less fuss. Didn't have to do batches just did it right in the pot. This is totally worth the chopping and stirring!

Fantastic.
I made it according to the recipe, but I found that the cream cheese made it a little too thick for my liking, so I added about a 1/2 cup of milk. Also, it is an excellent dip when could, very good with cooked broccoli.

I made this for a get together with some girl friends and everyone enjoyed it. I made some changes.
use about 3 lbs butternut squash. 
32oz fl of chicken stock. 
1/3 of 8oz of cream cheese. 
2 cloves of minced garlic. 
1 tart apple.
i didn't have any marjoram, i sub for pumpkin pie spice. 
i used olive oil instead margarine. 
and salt to taste.
much more flavorful!!!
Next time i will added some apple cider!!
Just a little bit of cream cheese makes the soup.  I used 4 oz. and it was perfect.  Love the spiciness, too.
Great recipe! I used only half the cream cheese to reduce the number of calories and it still turned out very tasty.
EXCELLENT soup! I roasted the squash first though...as did many others who left comments. Great recipe and easy.

excellent!!!!!!! wonderful!! what a refreshing soup to have on a cool october night. i took the advice of others and baked my squash with olive oil. i added garlic to my onions as they sauted and also added half of a granny smith apple to add some zip. it turned out very good. this soup is easy enough to make and the presentation is excellent. we are also going to add some spinach ravioli for a more filling soup. thanx for the recipe
Might add shrimp or crab

After reading several of the earlier reviews, I cut the squash in half, put it cut side down on parchment paper in the microwave and cooked it for 8 minutes.  It had to cool briefly before I could handle it but it was then very easy to scoop out.  Although already cooked, I put it in the pan with the onion and butter and cooked it longer, then used a potato masher before I put it in the food processor.   I also used chicken broth rather than water and bouillon cubes and used less than half of the cream cheese.  We've just come from a cruise where I always love the soups they offer  -- as someone else said, even my husband likes this and now I plan to serve it for Thanksgiving.   :>)
Delicious!!

I made this tonight and can't wait to share it with friends tomorrow.  It's fabulous as is, but I made some changes to suit my own tastes.  I roasted the peeled and diced squash, along with an acorn squash and 2 sweet potatoes, tossed in olive oil, garlic powder, poultry seasoning, sea salt and black pepper for 45 minutes.  With an immersion blender I pureed the vegetables with 48 oz chicken broth, 1 pkg. cream cheese and 1.5 cups skim milk.  I substituted red pepper flakes for the cayenne that I didn't have.  This is a wonderful, velvety recipe!  An easy way to peel the squash is with a vegetable peeler.  It didn't take any longer than a potato.

Made this 3 times in the last two weeks... Thanksgiving everyone loved it so thank you! Made it again for my girlfriends family and once more for a holiday party this past weekend. People were asking for the scoop on how to make it. 

Followed the ingredients aside from water and bouillon, I used free range low sodium chicken broth, which was a nice touch. And the 2nd time I decided to try a low fat Philly cream cheese and I used about 15 oz the taste was not even really noticably different. So for the health concience thats something to keep in mind. 

third time I made it for double the serving about 14 people, doubled the squash and the broth kept the cream cheese at 16 oz for the double servings and it was still 2/3 fat Philly cream cheese and yet again it was a hit. 

Also, I used one of my favotite ingredients, Tumeric, eyeballed it as I do everyting else but it was about 1/8 Tablespoon for the smaller pot and about 1/2 tablespoon for the double recipe, adds some really nice floral notes and helps wo compliment with a nice white wine of your choice. 

I also doubled the Cayenne... Yum 

Hope this helped someone.
The only thing I did different was roast the squash in the oven. Absolutely delicious! This is a keeper!
Delicious
Reduced the chicken broth to make it thicker. A delicious autumn soup/

The first time I followed the recipe exactly and it was good. I've made it several more times since then. Roast the squash with olive oil salt and pepper. It will be more flavorful and easy to scoop out of the skin. I sautéed the onion and spices in butter and added them to the soup. In my opinion, only one package on cream cheese is necessary. Chicken stock rather than bouillon and water will enhance the flavor.  An immersion blender makes quick work to purée.

The soup is one of the soups where after you taste the final result, you say outloud, "I made this??" It is delicious! I did use 1/2 the cream cheese, used some nutmeg bc/ I didn't have any cayenne pepper, and used 1/2 apple cider instead of water.
Sounds great but will use vegetable boullion instead of chicken.
This is a wonderful soup for the holidays. I made a huge pot of it for my christmas dinner guests and they raved! Dont change a thing it is wonderful the way the recipe says.

This is the first time I've ever made Butternut Squash Soup and it was fantastic! I followed a few tips from other reviewers and it was perfection. I roasted my squash first which made peeling easier. I used 4 Cups of chicken broth and added 1sp. of curry powder, a cinnamon stick and a bayleaf for some extra flavor. I omitted the marjoram which I didn't have. I didn't have cream cheese either so added 1/2 and 1/2 before serving, plus some brown sugar, which made the soup sweet at first, followed up by the heat from the cayenne and curry. AMAZING!

This is one of our favorite soup recipes!  I added minced garlic and 1/2 cup of white wine to the butter & onions.  I used half of the cream cheese this time, but would probably use more next time since we like it thicker & richer.  I also reserve a cup or more of the cooked squash and add it to the blended soup for interest and texture.  I garnish each bowl with shredded sharp cheddar and a dollop of cream cheese.  Even my picky 2 year old likes this soup, especially when I add some cooked brown rice to his bowl.
The flavor was to die for.  Guests returned for more and asked for the recipe.  I roasted the squash for almost an hour.  Very easy to make.
Love this quick and easy recipe for delicious soup :) I found half the cream cheese plenty.
Took the common advice of baking the squash first. But the problem is this recipe has way too much cream cheese - might try with 1/2 next time.

Made with 7 cups squash and 4 cups of homemade chicken broth- came out wonderful!  Very easy- My husband said, "I'm digging this soup- kept going back for seconds!  I like a garnish on a smooth soup- any suggestions?

I used potatoes instead of cream cheese (don't like cream cheese), then purée the soup, it was great without the processed cream cheese. Didn't change anything else. I am giving it three stars because I tweaked it.
Yum!  We really enjoyed this.
Used reduced fat cream cheese (one 8-oz box only).  Excellent!
I used a mixture of acorn and butternut squash.  It was wonderful! I only used 8 oz. of cream cheese and it was great!

This soup was delicious!! I used frozen precooked squash because I didn't have time to roast the squash myself, but it still turned out amazing. I also threw in some pine nuts and dried cranberries right before serving to add a color pop and a little bit of a mix into the flavor. Got great reviews from my guests. Will be making this again!
Tasty, easy to prepare, very good.
Excellent soup!  Really easy and fast, and best of all the family loved it.  Thanks
My husband who normally doesn't like butternut squash really liked it.

This was quick and healthy comfort food. I used non fat plain Greek yogurt instead of cream cheese to lower fat content and boosting protein. Using real butter gave enough creaminess. Purreeing with an immersion blender made it super quick! Using frozen squash cubes made it even faster yet still tasty.

I actually want to give this 4.5 stars, but that's not an option.  Loved it!  Bake the squash first and then peel it.  Also, try using low-fat cream cheese to make it healthier.  One package is all that is needed.  Up the cayenne if you like some heat.  You really can't go wrong with it.

This was tasty, but I think next time I will use less cream cheese. I used the same proportions of ingredients, but I used one bag of peeled and cubed butternut squash from Trader Joe's and microwaved it, in the bag, for the recommended 5 1/2 minutes. It made this soup super quick and easy.

OH wow, this is a super yummy recipe. Followed the full recipe, put in all the cream cheese. Very creamy and delicious. But I think next time I can do with just half of the cream cheese or maybe even just a quarter. Try the recipe! It's definitely worthy of all these positive reviews.
Absolutely amazing. Very rich, with a wonderful flavor.

I used 1/2 of the cream cheese and added 1/4 tsp nutmeg.  For my husband's sake I added 3 chicken breasts to cook with the squash.  I took the chicken out before putting the soup in the blender and then added chunks of chicken to the blended finale. OH MY GOSH!!!  It was FANTASTIC!!!  I was licking the bowl!  The nutmeg gave it a sweet Christmas-y taste and the cayenne peper gave it just the right kick.

Love this soup. Amazing flavor a true comfort soup. Served it before main course at Thanksgiving they really loved it. The only thing I  did different was I also added paprika and a dash of lemon pepper. Doubled the batch and canned 5 jars.

AMAZING!  I used butter instead of margarine, and chicken broth, cut the cream cheese to 1, 8oz pack, and added some roasted red pepper to the mix, blew my office staff away. I plan to make this for a Thanksgiving course.
Delish!!!
I was craving butternut squash soup and came accross this recipe, it was nice and easy, but i added some maple syrup while puree, and it turns out to be nice and sweet but not overly sweet.
I LOVE this soup the only change is not Marjoram and 1/2 the cream cheese. I puree squash and onion which makes is real smooth.

I prepared this soup along with several other recipes from this site for a couple on Valentine's Day.  It was mind-blowing.  The couple is still telling everyone about this soup and the Almond Mandarin Salad (another big hit).
So good! The only change I made is I used half the amount of cream cheese. This was plenty. I will definitely make it again.
Turned out grainy and tasted mostly like cream cheese. I don't think I'll be making this again.

I thorougly enjoyed this soup. I did cut the sour cream in half and also used non-fat (couldn't taste the difference!) My wife thought that it was a little bland, mainly because she prefers soups with a chunkier texture. I may try adding some cubes (cooked) squash before serving. I highly recommend this tasty soup!
AMAZING!!!!!
I love this soup.  Quick, easy and very flavorful.  I add some curry powder for some extra zing.

Tasty winter soup.  I used only one 8 ounce package of cream cheese instead of two to cut down on fat and it was very good, and still creamy.  I used less cayenne, too, just to make this more toddler-friendly.
Just tried this recipe last night!!! It was so delicious and so easy to make. I used chicken broth and all the cream cheese and I came out perfect!!!  Thanks for the great recipe (:

very good and easy to make.  I will make again.  I loved it but my husband thought it was just ok (that's why I gave it 4 stars).  But if you love squash, you will love this soup.  Thanks for the recipe!!
Very good soup. I did roast the squash in the oven.
Like others, I cut out some of the cream cheese, I used less than one block.  We serve this as a yummy lighter meal in the fall with a side of sliced apples, cheeses, and water crackers.
Wish I would have read reviewed first....definitely 1/2 the cream cheese.  Otherwise was great!  Pretty easy to make too.

I made this according the recipe, and that was far too much cream cheese. I added another cup of water with bouillon cube and that helped, but I'll probably still throw a lot of this away. I have some squash left over, so I'll try it again according to another reviewer who eliminated the cream cheese.
FANTASTIC! :)  My whole family loves this recipe!  Easy and fast...will make it over and over!  Great for fall!
Amazing soup! Worth the effort. I used turkey stock and added more water than it called for. Recipe makes a large kettle of soup. Excellent!

This was really rich: a great fall/winter time soup.  I enjoyed the buttery flavor.  I roasted the squash and it worked great that way.  I also used a very small amount of light cream cheese to make it healthier.
This recipe has been adopted as a family favorite in our house. My only variation is to halve the cream cheese. Creamy, sweet, and a little spicy, it is fall-time perfection!

Ok, maybe I did something entirely wrong, but I tried to follow the recipe exactly. There was definitely way too much cream cheese.  I would recommend anyone making this to half the amount of cream cheese.  I'm slightly surprised by all the great reviews.

I veganized this soup.  It was a little thick so next time I will add more liquid.  I used a low sodium vegetarian bouillon and vegan cream cheese.   Absolutely delicious.  Such a treat that I can invite my vegan friends over for butternut squash soup.  I used a mixture of butternut squash, turnip and yam believe it or not and is wonderful.  I got this at Trader Joes and tried the soup.  It's a real winner.
I make a lot of soup and this one is now on my top ten list.  Absolutely fabulous!  I used half the cream cheese and two cans of chicken broth. Can't wait to make it again. Thanks for sharing it.
I've made this several times.  It's delicious!  Like the others, I only made this receipe using 1 cream cheese and that was plenty.  We love this soup!

My husband and I had this at a friend's house for Thanksgiving and HAD to have 
the recipe!  It was absolutely delicious and would be perfect for a Fall or Winter 
meal along with a loaf of homemade bread.... absolutely the best soup I have 
ever tasted!!
Only added 1/4 the amount of cream cheese.  Perfect!!  I've made this soup many times, and it freezes/reheats WONDERFULLY!
This soup was simply outstanding.  I roasted the squash before cooking and added some freshly grated nutmeg.  The taste was so good and my Thanksgiving guests loved it.
I thought this was delicious.  I roasted the squash for 45 min in a 375 degree oven.  It was a great dinner with a loaf of sourdough and a nice salad.  would definately make again.

Been eyeballing this one for a while and finally had some free time to make it yesterday before a ball game, Let me tell you that this was just delicious! If my picky eating son, says its yummy; then it is a great day!!! I only modified slightly: Coconut oil instead of margarine, about 1/2 tsp on all the spices and used 1.5 boxes of chicken stock with one bullion cube thrown in, and we like onions so I diced up a whole sweet vidalia and let it sweat for a while, and only one thing of fat free cream cheese... So nothing crazy just a few minor tweaks to our preference BUT was a fantastic soup and garnished with some chive and a pinch of Mozz!
Made this for a starter for Thanksgiving dinner and it was a hit!  I can't wait to make it again.
Used only 1 (8 0z.) package of cream cheese.  I really can't imagine using TWO as it was rich and thick with one package!  Will definitely make it again!  YUMM-O!

I thought this recipe was fantastic, but I too made some changes.   I roasted a 3 lb squash with a peeled granny smith apple for 45 mins at 375.  I sautéed 1 medium onion chopped, 1 peeled chopped carrot, and 1 Yukon gold potato, 2 cloves of minced garlic in the 4T butter.  I used 4 c low sodium chicken broth, added the the chopped up roasted squash and apple, added 1/2 t marjoram, 1/4 t cayenne pepper, 1/4 t rubbed sage, and pepper.  Simmer for 10 mins.  Added salt to taste.  Puréed in the blender w/ only 4 oz of cream cheese.  Was delicious, but I wanted a bit more bite so I added 1 T of apple cider vinegar.  Truly spectacular.  It is a thick soup, but I like it that way!
I used home made chicken stock and used 4 oz of cream cheese instead of 8 and left out the onions and this was fantastic! My new favourite soup!
Too rich for my taste.
absolutely amazing!  it was my first experience ever using butternut squash- definitely a keeper!

Followed this recipe to the tee. Not all that impressed. I might try it again, but it needs major tweaking. 4 boullion cubes is too much! It makes the soup very salty. I'll follow the advice of others and use chicken stock, and may try baking the pumpkin first.
Was very tasty but I should've used less cream cheese like reccommended, the cream cheese overpowered the flavor of the squash. Otherwise, not a bad recipe.

I LOVE this soup.  I used half the amount of cream cheese and used reduced fat.  I cooked my chicken in it while the squash cooked and it was fabulous.  It makes a good sauce for chicken and pasta too.  My 13 year old though it was 'ok' which is high praise for a vegetable from him.
I did not make any changes. I like trying out recipes as the chef recommends . I am glad I did not. it was delicious!!! it has become my go to butt squash soup recipe! thanks for the share!

Spectacular! Ok, per other member's suggestions, I added garlic and celery. I used only one package of cream cheese. When it was done, the flavor was great, but it was WAY too rich. I added milk until it became soupy enough for me. Next time I will add broccoli.

Really Good!! Roasted the squash in the oven on 350 for about an hour. Added 3 pears. Tasted it without the cream cheese and it felt like it was missing something. Added 1 block as suggested by other reviewers and the flavor was delicious! I will definitely add this to my soup collection during the fall/winter. Thanks.

Very good- although I completely agree that you really only need maybe 2oz of cream cheese, if any.  I put in 4oz, and I thought that was even a bit much.  I roasted the squash in the oven with olive oil, garlic, salt & pepper, then followed the other reviewer's advice about adding a bit of apple cider and nutmeg while cooking it down on the stove with the 3c water, chicken bouillon and spices.  I also made "spiced pumpkin seeds" from the squash seeds to top the soup with, and those were fantastic!!
This recipe is very simple and delicious.  I opted for one block of cream cheese and that worked for our taste.  My husband practically licked his bowl!  We will definitely make this soup again.
My whole family loved this.  I added a couple carrots, 2 potatoes and an apple.  Yum!
Yup! 5 stars!  So creamy and flavorful.   I'm tossing my old recipe and replacing it with this!

This was a great and hearty recipe.  Make sure you roast the squash first until it can easily be removed from its skin.  I omitted the cream cheese and added 1/2c of light cream instead.  I also added pinches of nutmeg and cinamon to really bring out the flavour.  It makes a lot so it's great for dinner parties or to freeze.  Enjoy!

Even better the next day!!! I coated in olive oil and roasted the squash and 5 cloves of garlic in the oven face down at 350 for one hour. I used half the cream cheese as many have mentioned.. Added a bay leaf and the roasted garlic and simmered all ingredients for 30 minutes. strained out solids and served hot!!! So good. A real crowd pleaser. Used sodium free stock. Total winner!
I loooved this soup! I added more cayenne to kick it up, I love spicy!   I added some bouillon cubes to the stock also, had LOTS of flavor.

I really liked this soup, used 1/2 the cream cheese even though I love cream cheese. It was very rich, but I served it with a baguette. My boyfriend didn't care for this at all, I guess you either like butternut squash or you don't!
Very easy and delicious!

So delicious!  I used dried oregano because I didn't have any marjoram. I also halved the cream cheese and it was plenty rich.  I made a double recipe so we had leftovers the next day, and I was still wishing I had more!

very rich and fantastic!  ETA: I've made this a few times and always roast the squash. I even served it as part of Christams dinner and my Mother loved it even though she hates squash. The cream cheese is what sets this recipe apart so don't skip it. I use the 1/3 lass fat kind to cut fat but not flavor.

I am someone that has never tasted Butternut Squash Soup in my life. I tried this just as written ( but only used 2oz. of the Creamed Cheese ), and I liked it ! Super easy to make, smooth and rich. I will make it again and freeze for later this winter. 
Thank you for a Super Basic Recipe !!
This was a very easy recipe and my toddler even loved it.  She is such a picky eater!  We will have this soup often during the winter months.

I did not enjoy this recipe at all. I am not too fond of squash to begin with so take it with that understanding. The texture of the soup was unpleasant and the over all flavor too bland for my liking.
I didn't have marjoram so left it out. It was amazing! I'm not sure I ever want to try it with. Only used 4 oz. sour cream...still rich and creamy! My family loved it too. I called it Halloween soup!
It is so easy and so good.  It is as good using sour cream instead of all the cream cheese.  Love it.
It was delicious!  We used just one bar of cream cheese and it was plenty rich for us.  There are only three of us in our family and there were barely any leftovers.  I think that speaks for itself!

What a great way to eat squash!  I love soups in general, but frankly, this was one of the best soups I've ever made!!  My 17 month old loved it which is pretty amazing since I served him cubed butternut squash the day before and he was spitting it out.  As a modification, I cooked the squash in the microwave, only put in 1 tub (8 oz) of light cream cheese (I couldn't imagine putting in 2!), used canned chicken broth and pureed with a hand mixer right in the microwave bowl.  Like others have mentionned, the only time consuming task was peeling and cubing the squash, but it is soooo worth it!
easy to make and was delicious.

This turned out way better than I had expected! I used two small squashes, and it made exactly 6 cubed cups. I used a hand blender to blend directly in the pot, and then decided to only use one block of cream cheese. It was PERFECT with just that.

Absolutely delicous.  This will become a new, but low fat comfort food for me.  It tastes much more caloric than it is.  Roasting the squash is a must as it gives a fuller flavor, and the skin peels off so easily!  As did many others I used real chicken broth, 4 cups, (organic & low sodium due to high blood pressure) and I think that also adds to the rich flavor.  I also doubled the cayenne pepper and used only 8 ounces low fat cream cheese.  Was glad to read reviews that this freezes well.

Though this is a very easy recipe, the results do not warrant making this again.  The kids would not eat anymore after the first bite.  Even my husband (who will eat anything!) didn't really care for it.  Personally I thought it was OK.  It does need more water however, it was too thick with just 3 cups.  I'd like to add that I always use the highest quality ingredients and still this recipe lacks appeal.  Sorry, I know I am a minority on this.

I've been craving butternut squash soup and this was a delicious recipe.  I roasted my squash in the oven and then added it to the rest of the ingredients.  The only thing I did not care for was the large amount of cream cheese--I only used half a package and it was still a little too much for my liking.  I think 1/4 of a package would be perfect.  Thanks for a wonderful recipe!

Didn't change anything and loved this creamy creation.  Yes it is a pain to peel the squash but so worth the effort.  I garnished with fresh chives, bacon and sour cream.  I made a double batch.  Gave 2 containers to a friend, 2 containers went into the freezer and we ate the remaining soup.  (I got 10 cups of veggies from one squash and got 13 cups from a bigger squash so I froze the remaining 6 packages of unused squash for later.)  Thank you!

I made this soup last week. As suggested by other reviewers I roasted the squash first and used 8oz of light cream cheese. I also used vegetable boullion instead of chicken to make it suitable for vegetarians. It was easy, creamy and delicious. Great recipe!

I have made this soup once a week for the past 4 weeks. The girls from work love it. I have to admit I have changed it a bit.  1. Roasted butternut squash (cut in half, clean out seeds, rub with olive oil, place face down on cookie sheet, roast 350 degrees for 30-40 min or until easily pierced with a fork.  2. At the same time I roasted a whole clove of garlic and added it to the soup. ( cut top off with knife, sprinkle with olive oil, wrap in foil. roast same temp and time as squash) 3. I used chicken broth not bouillion. 4. Used half the cream cheese. 5.  Added garnishes... green onions, bacon, and grated cheese. 6. Used a immersion hand blender in the same pot!!   Feel free to add in this recipe. I have used apples and white wine too!!  This recipe is a must try and share with friends!!
It's ok, but not great.  I really think the apples make the dish to apple sauce like.

MMMMM!! Will make again!!! I used 1 butternut squash, and half a bar of cream cheese because that was all I had. I added a teaspoon of garlic when sauteeing the onions. I put the squash in the microwave and used a hand mixer to blend in the pot. It was actually quite messy that way but left the soup a little lumpy which I enjoyed!! I used chicken stock and doubled the cayanne because I love soup with a kick!!! My 18 month old and 3 Year old both loved it too!!
Awesome!  I only used one pkg of cream cheese and added about a quarter head of cabbage to add more substance and stretch the recipe.

This was unusual. This was my first time cooking and eating butternut squash, so I didn't really know what to expect it to taste like. I followed the advice of others by: 1) cutting the squash in half, drizzling it with olive oil, sprinkling salt and pepper and roasting it. 2) I also roasted a head of garlic at the same time and threw that in later on. 3) I then picked up with the recipe and used homemade chicken broth instead of water & bouillon. And 4) I used half of the cream cheese called for - definately enough! I found it did need a little extra salt and seasoning in the end. It was also a little tart, so I added some sugar to taste.  Okay, but I doubt I will make it again.

Tweaked a touch w/ a splash of Dry Sherry, dash of freshly grated nutmeg and 1/2 of the cream cheese.  Served in shot glasses w/ drizzle of balsamic vinegar (reduction) and creme fraiche as a "shooter" at a cocktail party.  It was a hit!

*ALL* my kids loved this one, event the picky 3yo.  I made this completely in my electric pressure cooker.  After saute-ing onions, cooked for 5 min on high.  Then used my hand stick blender to puree the cream cheese (used low-fat).  One pot perfection.  Garnished with small dollop of Mexican sour cream (creamier than sour cream) and dash of paprika.  Looked as good as it tasted.  Served with oatmeal bread to dip.  Very thick and hearty.  Thanks for a fabulous recipe!
I have made this numerous times.  I do not add the philly due to calories, fat and vegan friends.  Everyone seems to love it.  They don't know it could be better!
Excellent.  Per the advice of others, I cut way back on the cream cheese.  The consistency was still perfect.

This was INCREDIBLE.  Like others that have reviewed this recipe, I used chicken broth instead of the water and bouillon.  I roasted the butternut (halved, brushed with olive oil, flesh side down) and then pureed it with my food processor.  I used two cans of chicken broth and a cup of apple cider.  Everything else, was the same, except I used more cayenne.  Again, INCREDIBLE.  Love this.

This was delicious - however I did reduce the cream cheese to 8 oz. and added an extra cup of broth. I have hesitated to make this soup because I find cutting up the squash to be very tedious, and baking it first makes double work. I like FAST. But I discovered Trader Joe's sells a bag of diced butternut squash for $4.99, hooray!! I will definitely make this again!
Very tasty, little too much time to prepare, very rich.  Very tasty.
i only added 1/2 the recommended cream cheese, the soup was white and frothy. not a fan.

I made this just like the recipe and family loved it.  Very easy. Next time I would increase the cayenne pepper to 1/4 tsp I think.  Will try freezing it also as I have a lot of squash in my garden this year.
Delicious!  I skipped the cream cheese because of the fat.  I used chicken broth instead of water and bouillon cubes.    YUM!!!

Oh so yummy!  My whole family loved it and I didn't change a thing.  I will definitely make it again.  For those who say butternut squash is hard to peel, I found it peels quite easily using a sturdy potato peeler!  I also roasted the squash before making the soup.

SO SO SO darn good!  A friend made this for me first and I was skeptical because I hadn't had good experiences with this type of soup in the past.  But it was so good.  I got the recipe from her and then found it here.  I did much the same as others have already mentioned: I baked the squash in the oven versus boiling it.  I used one medium onion and sauteed it in olive oil versus butter.  I cut the water in half, but used all the chicken broth.  I didn't add the cayenne pepper, but did extra basil and seasonings.  I also only did one package of cream cheese.  Turned out great.  Great flavor and not too squash-y!

However you make this soup you should save all the seeds and scrapings.  While the squash is cooking,  saute 2 or 3 minced shallots in some butter or oil for a few mins. till soft, then add the seeds and scrapings  and saute a couple mins. more ,  add 4-6 cups of water ,and bring to a boil, then simmer covered for 30 mins.  , strain out the seeds and add this broth to your finished soup before pureeing.  It will give it a lot of extra flavor.

Just tried this one.  My hubs who hates squash loved it.  As well as the toddler.  It's a forgiving recipe.  Went a touch light on the cream cheese, accidentally doubled the bouillon, and used sage instead of the marjoram that I didn't have.  Absolutely will make this again... with a touch less bouillon (that made it taste a little veggie-dip-ish).
I make this every year at thanksgiving- my entire family loves it! I always use just one package of cream cheese.

I made no alterations to this recipe when I prepared it, and it turned out great! Expect to spend a lot of time peeling the butternut squash... next time I make it I may go ahead and roast or steam it first to help soften it. Very easy to make, not many ingredients required, and it turns out fantastic. Good recipe all around! Make extra and freeze or can it for later!
We love this soup!  I did add a touch of garlic.  We will be making this often!

The cream cheese in this soup is too overwhelming.I changed it up after tasting it,To tone the cream cheese taste down, I made up half the recipe again minus any cream cheese and added this to the 1st batch.
I followed up with 1 tsp of nutmeg and 2 tablespoons of brown sugar create a savory taste.
This is the best butternut squash soup I have ever had.  I used one 8oz package of the cream cheese and real butter.

As written I think it tasted way too rich. I cut the cream cheese in half, used chicken stock, added a pinch of ground ginger, nutmeg, and cinnamon along with some minced garlic and an apple. I added tons of salt to bring up the flavor and about 2T. of honey. After all those changes I love it. The way it is written it should just be called cream cheese soup!

Meh. Made this as written, and didn't really care for it, even after adding more spices. It was just too bland and meh. Husband also said "soup is all right," which is pretty accurate. It wasn't bad, just not terribly good, either.
Used half the cream cheese and roasted the squash in the oven like others suggested and it came out gread. Had good simple flavor. Will make it again.

A very good soup!  I roasted the butternut squash before making the soup which gave it a wonderful flavor.  I used veggie broth and only about 4 oz of cream cheese.  In the future, I'll just use milk or cream; the cream cheese was ok but it kind of left a few little pieces floating around that looked a bit like curdled milk.  I loved the cayenne-it added a GREAT zing to the soup.  I really loved that this soup was not sweet as most butternut squash soups are.  Wonderful and a definite keeper.  Thank you!
WOW! This soup turned out amazing! I followed the recipe EXACTLY! I highly recommend you try this recipe!
I made this soup with half cream cheese, it turned out okay. Won't make it again.
I used Herbs de Province and 1/2 the cream cheese. We love this soup. Thank you.

This recipe is great ALTHOUGH here are some hints to make it better. Bake the squash in the oven first for about 40 minutes 350 so it is easier to work with, and use only one package of cream cheese and use real butter of course.....
I used 1 cream cheese as per the request of other reviews and it was delicious!  Very rich and the leftovers freeze well!
I used leftover buttercup & butternut squash that had melted butter already in it.  Used a sweet onion and less marjoram than called for. Didn't need the cream cheese. Perfect~!!
Heavenly good

This soup is delicious, and pretty easy to make, but VERY creamy.  I even followed the suggestion of others and only used one package of light cream cheese, and was still VERY rich!!  In the future I'll only use a spoonful of cream cheese!  I also added a lot more cayenne (maybe a 1/2 a teaspoon), and the cayenne flavor was strong (yet delicious).  I also baked the squash for maybe 45 minutes before, makes it easier to peel & cut.  Will do it again, with modifications.

I sauteed the onions in margarine and white wine, then added them to the food processor with the squash and blended them also. It's best to roast the squash on a cookie sheet in the oven for 45 mins. at 375. I also added a little brown sugar in with the squash puree just for some extra flavor.
This soup is easy and so delicious! I make this once a year and we freeze it to eat it all year long. Very filling. You'll need about a 2 1/2 - 3lb squash for 6 cups.
Only change was I roasted the squash. We loved it including my 7 & 8 y/o grandkids.

This is a great base recipe for those of us who need a starting point.  For a delicious twist, substitute the marjoram and cayenne with a bay leaf and curry to taste.  I'm making a pot right now using a hubbard squash I inherited.
Comfort Food

Roasted the squash, added a sliced apple to the stove top with the mixture before pureeing.  Added a dash of nutmeg, cinnamon, and ground ginger as well.  This was really good.  Added pumpkin seeds and a dollop of sour cream when serving.
Not really me, but I actually liked it. I really liked it with Wheat Thins chips. My mother begged me to make it again.
Great!  Half the amount of cream cheese was even better.

It is a winner I used coconut oil to cook the onion ( I aded a clove a garlic)  and coconut milk to thin a bit.  Roasted squash, chicken broth, and seasoning; could it be easier?  I tried cream cheese as a topping and also sour cream it didn't need either. Tasty.
Following it to the letter is pretty bland. It's a good base to start running with but I will need to doctor it up alot the next time.

One brick of cream cheese was enough to make this soup thick and creamy. I tripled the marjoram. I also tripled the black pepper and cayenne for added heat to the back of the soup. I garnished with green onion and served with sour dough toast and roasted leg of lamb. Delicious!
Wonderful recipe.  I did use whipped cream cheese, and about 1/2 the amount called for, and also roasted the squash.  Great soup for a chilly fall night.

I made the terrible mistake of forgetting about the reviewers' advice by the time I made this soup, and ended up dumping it down the disposal. This is cream cheese soup with butternut squash coloring, and I'm usually a girl who can eat cream cheese by the spoonful. If I ever attempt any butternut squash soup recipe again, I will use one that doesn't even have cream cheese in the ingredients list. Thanks for the opportunity to try it, though. Shame on me for not following the great advice!

Yum, yum!  If you don't like rich foods, this is not the soup for you, as it is very thick and VERY rich.  This soup converted someone who thought they didn't like squash.  I will definitely make this recipe again.

Modifications: Doubled all spices, used vegetable broth, and halved cream cheese.

The flavor is excellent!  Now on menu for housewarming. Not sure about the texture. Seemed a little mealy. I'm a squash novice, so maybe that's just the way squash is.  How the heck are you supposed to peel these things? Took me forever. My adaptations: 1/8 + teaspoons cayenne pepper, 2 beef boullion cubes and one chicken, pureed the onions too.
This was awesome! I love it and have made about 5 batches in 3 weeks. Thank you!!
it was okay, very creamcheesey, I would start with 1 pkg of creamcheese

I was so dissapointed in the final result of this soup because it really was like baby food in consistency- so much so that we had to throw it out.  And I also cut down on the cream cheese.  Before I added the cream cheese and pureed it,  I kept tasting the broth and thought it was very good, so I anticipated a great soup.  Then it was a huge pain to puree in batches, and we couldn't even eat the final soup!  I might attempt this again, but will not puree.  Also, what made it much easier was buying the pre-packaged cut p butternut squash our supermarket sells.  You just throw it in- no cutting involved.  Anyhow, the broth tastes good, so it is a good base.
yummmm!  cut the crm chz in half & added more cyanne.  also cut in half & cooked squash in microwave first.
LOVE THIS SOUP!!! Have made it several times now. Even those who are opposed to squash that I have made it for really like it.
I did NOT tweak hardly at all except that I used sour cream instead of cream cheese and I added bacon and chives as a garnish.  We loved it!

I am 52 years old and this is the first time I ever cooked a butternut squash and I have to say I had my doubts. My husband and I were blown away with the savory flavors. I must have used a very big squash because it was like mashed potatoes but we loved it anyway!
Favorite comfort food recipe!!! Love it.  I made it the same as the recipe except I use Italian seasoning (that has marjoram in it) instead of just Marjoram because that's what I had on hand.  Yum!

I loved this soup!  Even my boyfriend that doesn't like butternut squash soup liked this one.  I did use chicken stock instead of the water and chicken boulion.  I will be making this recipe many times.  Thank you for sharing.
Creamy, flavorful and wonderful!

The "TASTE" of this soup is 5 STARS but I found it WAY too thick to give it an overall 5 stars. I made the soup for a 2nd time today and am extremely pleased with the results!  I used 5 cups of chicken stock in place of the 3 cups of water and boullion cubes and also added 1 clove minced garlic along with the squash. I omitted the cream cheese all together this time & don't miss it a single bit. The soup still has an incredibly rich, creamy flavour without all that extra fat and calories. The flavour of the squash shines a bit more this way too.  Would definitely make my altered version again.

So SO YUMMY!!!  I have never made Butternut squash soup before-or even cooked a butternut squash.  But this recipe was so EASY and so YUMMY!  I did as others had and roasted the butternut squash before and I also only used one package of cream cheese.  Thank you so much for this recipe!

added a 1/2 block of cr. cheese/1-2 c sour cream... added to butternut squash: 3 potatoes, 1 lg. sw. potato, roasted garlic,chic. stock, 3 sm. apples, extra onion and 1 c hvy. wh. cream. Fresh mint on top would be nice!  NOTE: leave part of this (maybe 1/4 of it) unpureed...or at least just partially pureed. We liked having some small chunks/texture with each bite. Top w/ nutmeg!

This recipe isn't excellent, but it's good.  I was alittle disappointed given all the great ratings.  I followed the recipe except I did bake the squash instead of cutting it into little pieces.  Butternut squash is extremely hard, so cutting it into small pieces would have been a nightmare. I sliced it long ways, placed it cut side down in a pyrex, put alittle water and covered with foil -- baked at 350 for 40 min or so.  It was very easy to scoop out at that point and continue the recipe.  If your going to make this, I suggest you prepare the squash the same way.  Like I said, it's worth a try, but I really don't think I'll make it again.
Very good. Made exactly as the recipe called for EXCEPT used 1/2 the cream cheese (8 oz total). Will make this again.

Great soup!! I roasted (one squash since I didn't measure) with salt, pepper, olive oil and a sprinkle of nutmeg for about an hour. I took out the seeds and cut it in about 8 pieces. Then there's no need to boil the squash once you add it to the onion since it's already cooked! There's absolutely no reason to add 2 packages of cream cheese. I only added half of one package and it's so creamy!!! I also added a pinch of all spice and nutmeg to the soup, and like another reviewer went a little heavier on the cayenne. This soup is one of my first and it's FANTASTIC! Thanks for the great recipe!

This soup was ok, I thought it was bland. I used 4 ounces of cream cheese and baked the squash in the oven before scooping it out.  It would have been very hard to cut.  The soup did not have much flavor, it needs more spices.

With over 300 reviews and a 5 star rating, this recipe does not really need my review too...but, everyone who has ever tasted this LOVES it.  I've been making it for over three years now and have passed the recipe on to many of my friends and family.  The only change I made was to cut the cream cheese down to one package.
Tip: microwave the squash for three minutes to make it easier to peel.
Followed what another reviewers suggested and roasted the squash first.  It was absolutley fantastic.  I did add a little salt to finish it off.  Very hearty for a squash soup.
The soup was really good and creamy. I like my soups a little less creamy so I will be adding more veggie broth next time. My husband loved it.

This soup has incredible texture.  The taste is mild (kid friendly).  I only had 5 cups of squash and 1/2 c of cream cheese.  Instead of chicken bouillon and water I used one can of condensed broth and one can of water.  I will definitely make again, I'm rating this a 4 because I think there is way too much cream cheese as written.
Awesome!!!!!!!!!
SOOO good.  I agree with most people - only use one package of cream cheese, though.
soooo good, even my husband ate it!  Also added just a pinch of nutmeg. good call!
I used low-sodium chicken broth instead of the bullion cubes and fat-free cream cheese. Still tasted delicious and cut the calories and sodium in half.

Delicious! I used real butter instead of margarine.  I halfed the cream cheese, as suggested. Also, I did not use chick boullion or water--instead, I used 3 cups of vegetable stock.  I added some extra cayenne pepper.  The soup was creamy and sweet with a hint of heat (from the cayenne).  Everyone loved it and wanted the recipe.

Yummy! My husband and I loved it. I only used 1 package of cream cheese, but i think next time I will use even less. It was a bit to creamy for me still. oh yeah, and only 3 cubes of bouillon is really necessary for my taste.

I have made this many times now. My husband calls it restaurant quality and always asks me to make it when we have company he wants to impress, LOL. More importantly, even my mother-in-law was impressed!  I do only use 1/4 of the cream cheese called for though, otherwise it is WAY to cream-cheesy.
Here's what I do: Cut squash in half and bake for 1 hour at 350 (cut side down on tin foil). Let cool while sauteeing onions and some garlic. (Sometimes I cook the squash the day before). Add one peeled/cored apple. Scoop out squash into pot. Depending on how ripe/soft the squash is, it's sometimes easier to cut the squash into strips and slice the skin off. I actually do this more often than not. Add broth. Add seasoning (marjoram, nutmeg - 1/2tsp, cinnamon - 1 tsp, dash of cloves, S&P, garlic powder). Simmer for an hour or so, then drop in the cream cheese for a few mins to soften before blending with a hand immersion blender. Done!

This soup is perfect for the fall and absolutely delicious!! :-) I substituted marjoram for dried oregano & red pepper flakes for cayenne pepper. I cut the cream cheese in half and it was a nice balance, not too rich.

I really enjoyed making this, it was very easy and very good.  I also took the advice of other reviewers.  I made the recipe with 2 large butternut squash, I used 2 small onions, and chicken stock in stead of bouillon.  I roasted the Squash for 45 min at 400 degrees let it cool a little then peeled it.  For the two big squash I doubled the recipe but only put one 8oz pkg of Neufchatel cheese (its cream cheese just reduced fat).  It came out amazing!
Amazing, this is one of my favorite soups to make in the fall. The flavor is off the charts and I give most of the credit to the cream cheese. It really makes this a super rich and creamy meal.

Yum!  

The only 2 changes to this recipe were as follows:
1. I used just 1 pkg of cream cheese (1 pkg seemed to be plenty, and I used 1/3 less fat).
2. I baked my butternut squash whole (with a few fork pokes) at 400 for 1 hr and 20 mins.  I used a rather large squash, so if you decide to bake yours, you should adjust your baking time accordingly.

This will definitely be on my list of favorites.  Thanks for sharing!
I loved it it is very delicious my only advice would to lessen on the cream cheese for it is very rich
I roasted the squash in the oven  for 45 minutes first. Then instead of cream cheese I used a cup of plain Greek yogurt. Delicious!

this was outstanding. my favorite part was tasting the levels of flavor in this soup. from the onions to the pepper it was a delightful eating experience
