my husband is not a squash lover, but he is now. He tells me he wants me to make it more often.
Excellent ~ The only thing I did different was I used Chicken stock instead of water (extra flavor) And at the end before serving the soup I added some fresh nutmeg.

YUM! My husband and mother-in-law don't even like squash, but they both thought this was really good, too. I cut the fat a little bit by using 2 Tbs. of butter instead of 4, and using 1 package of low-fat cream cheese, rather than 2. SO good.

I LOVE this soup, and I don't even like squash!  I did cut the cream cheese in half as suggested by many other posters, and it was plenty.  I like a nice thick puree, so I reserved a little of the liquid before blending and was glad I did;  you can always add it back in if you like yours a little thinner.  I found that my trusty stick blender was WAY easier than the food processor too. I also followed the lead of many other posters and microwaved the squash to make it easier to peel and cube (quarter it and scoop out the seeds, meat side down for 5 minutes).  It has a little kick to it because of the pepper & cayenne, but my guests and I didn't think it was too much.  If you have a sensitive stomach you might want to cut back on them and then taste.  ENJOY!!

This soup is absolutely delicious!  I used butter instead of margarine, and chicken broth instead of water.  I also roasted red pepper and garlic, and put all the ingredients into the blender.  This is definitely one of my favorites and what you would expect from a fine restaurant.  Thanks for the great recipe!

I got this huge tub of peeled and cubed butternut squash at Costco and came across this recipe when trying to decide what to do with it. When I told my husband what I was making for dinner he said "yuck" but said he'd try and ended up eating 3 bowls... I guess he liked.. I loved and so did my little one.  I used all the cream cheese (light) amount but added more squash and water and a little ginger, added the cayenne but used sparingly and put on the table for me to add a little to the finished product, used the blender on the stove method..awesome idea and theres only a bowl left for my lunch tommorow... thanks will make again!!
Delicious soup! My husband can't follow directions and also added 1/8 tsp. ginger and used half the cream cheese. It was great and even my toddler liked it!

STUPENDOUS, INCREDIBLE, FILLING SOUP.  I PRESSURE COOKED THE SQUASH AND BABY CARROTS, AND USED IN PAN BLENDER AND A POTATOE MASHER TO MAKE IT INTO A SOUP.  THE SKIN FELL OFF, SO IT WAS SO EASY TO FIX, IF ON A BUDJET, THIS SOUP WILL FILL TEENAGERS AND PUT THEM TO BED.  IT IS RICH AND OH SO FILLING.  I ADDED CREAM, AS WELL AS THE PHILADELPHIA CREAM CHEESE. IT BELONGS IN A 5 STAR RESTAURANT.

My husband and I love this recipe. It can be served as a main dish as it is very filling.  My husband was a tad concerned about how much cream cheese must have been in the soup to give it such a delicious, rich and creamy taste, but I actually only used 1/8 of the cream cheese called for! He was very pleasantly surprised as something in life that tasted so good is also healthy!!
amazing! thank you for sharing
Used chicken stock, 8 oz. low fat cream cheese and the soup was thick, creamy and filling.  The soup could use a little extra spicing.

So rich and such a hit! In Chile, we could only find Hubbard squash to use, and it was fantastic. We'll find out this Thanksgiving how it's different w/ butternut squash. I cut down the cream cheese and add peeled  chunks of red pepper after it's all mixed.  Also, sometimes we save some broth for a thiner soup.

I love butternut squash soup!  Why cream cheese? It is so fattening. Any milk would suffice. If you must have the cream I would go for whipping cream over cream cheese. The only spices I used was salt, pepper and paprika. I also used chicken stock and not chicken broth.Yummm!!!

My husband who likes neither squash nor soup said this was his new favorite soup!  This was great for a snowy, cold night next to the fire.  
I roasted the squash like others suggested and cut the cream cheese down to about 1/5 of one 8 oz package.  I can't imagine how yummy it is with the full amount.  I also cut the cayenne out because I didn't like the spice last time I made it, subbed about a 1/4 cup of brown sugar.

I used one cup of water and one cup of half and half (That's what I had in the house),  and no chicken bullion.   I baked the squash whole (with some serving sized fork holes stuck in it) for an hour. Let it cool and scraped the skin off. It was so easy. I added some salt. I will add some kick to it later. Since I changed it I felt I should only give it a 4 star.
This is sooo delicious!! Easy to make too!!

A good start, but falls short. With some tweaking, however, it can be excellent. For starters, maybe 1/4 of the cream cheese and about 1/4 cup of half and half. Also, more squash and cayenne with the addition of nutmeg. I included more onion too. Squash was overpowered by the richness of the cream cheese.

Used puréed acorn squash that I need to use up and homemade chicken stock (Chef John's recipe from this site).  The soup was so delicious that I could have drunk it with a straw.  It is great leftover and reheated as well.
This soup is awesome - we've been making it for years!  We now substitute frozen butternut squash.  It's so much easier and you can't taste the difference.

Made it as is but went a little lighter on the cream cheese but not much. A bit heavier on the ceyenne. I roast the squash covered after peeling and dicing. Also add salt salt to taste.  There's another recipe I've done with apple but I do like this one as is for something different. I sprinkle fresh parmesean on top and also use homemade broth.
Very easy recipe, great taste.  Reduce cream cheese portion as it was too creamy.

I love this recipe, but I never use butternut squash, I use a hearty winter squash. In the Fall I buy several large squash, cook them and freeze them in 3 cup amounts in ziplocks. Then its easy to throw this together. I also use 1/2 regular cream cheese and 1/2 nonfat and double the pepper. It has become my favorite soup. Thanks for sharing!

This is an excellect soup!  I follow the recipe to the letter and it comes out perfect every time.  The only improvement I've made is that I blend the cream cheese right in the pot.  I cut it into cubes, dump it in the pot with the cooked squash and puree with my stick blender.  Much easier than trying to pour hot soup into a standard mixer.

Tastes like creamy cheesy potato soup!  Only needs one package of cream cheese (never had it with two... neufactel at that).  Would be great base for cheesy broccoli soup or good with carrots added.  Followed another's suggestion and cooked squash first in microwave about 10 min (cut in half & place insides down).

A huge success at our New Years party!! Definitely roast your squash!! I roasted them for about an hour at 350 degrees brushed with olive oil, garlic, salt, and pepper.  I also sauteed the onion, and substituted chicken stock instead of water. I Doubled the recipe and omitted one pkg of cream cheese (used 3 instead of 4pks.)  Amazing and addicting!!
I liked this recipe but you definitely need to cut back the cream cheese.
Yummy!

I use papaya peach squash, it is slightly sweeter than butternut.  I also use lowfat sour cream and about 1/2 cup canned milk in place of the cream cheese and it is simply fantastic.  My daughter even likes it!
So easy and so good! I used only 4 oz low-fat cream cheese, and that was plenty.

LOVE, LOVE, LOVE this.  So does my 5 year old.  I had this soup at a friends house and had to make it myself for last Christmas.  It was a huge hit.  I have made it several times since.  Everyone asks for the recipe.  I cut the squash in half and roast for about an hour.  I use canned chicken broth.  I do not change the amount of cream cheese.  It's great the way it is.  Try it.  You will be glad you did.
My very first time making soup. Holy cow is this stuff amazing. I had ordered butternut squash soup at a restaurant last week and this recipe blows the restaurant soup out of the water! mmm mmm mmm
I love this soup!  I would recommend only using 4oz of the cream cheese, makes it to rich if you use more.
Delicious and easy!! Definitely a crowd pleaser.

This soup was good, but I was surprised by how cheesy it was, even with only half the called for cream cheese.  I followed others' suggestions about roasting the squash first, instead of trying to cut a hard squash into little cubes.  Simply sliced it in half lengthwise, and put on greased pan in oven at 375 degrees for 45 minutes.  Other than that, I followed the recipe as written except only using one (8oz) package of cream cheese, being a tad scant on my pepper measurements (for the kids' sake), and using base instead of bouillon cubes. The kids liked it (which was a nice surprise,) but the overwhelming flavor was cheese, not squash.  I think this recipe should be called Cheesy Butternut squash soup.  I can't even imagine how cheesy it would have been with two bricks of cream cheese!  Anyway, overall this soup was good, but just not what I was expecting.
My husband and I love, love this soup and he hates squash! It tastes more like a light and creamy mushroom soup. I only used 1 package of reduced fat cream cheese and I think it's perfect.
Mmmmmm. This was sooooo good.  I used half the cream cheese and a hand blender as suggested and it turned out great!  Will make again.
This soup was scrumptious and hit the spot on our first snow day! Might try less cream cheese next time only because it was really rich and I'm slightly lactose intolerant.  So good though!

I just tried this for the first time and it was a success. I used organic chicken broth and only one package of cream cheese. Texture is great, has good flavor. I sprinkled bacon bits on top as a finisher. I'd like to try experimenting with different flavors and toppings, but overall it's quite good the way it is!
A big hit at Thanksgiving.  This soup is simple but delicious.  A roasted the squash and it had a wonderful flavor.

This soup was great. It was my first time cooking with butternut squash. I roasted it prior to adding it to the soup for a bit more flavour. In the end, it was super thick and I had to add LOTS of milk to thin it out. This may because I never measure anything and likely had too much squash (consequently I also added way too much cayenne - opps!). I also didn't have enough cream cheese (i.e. only half), but it still tasted great. I will make this again.

It's a good recipe but 16oz of cream cheese is way too much. I only used 12oz and it was still to heavy. Next time I'll try 8. I didn't have enough squash so I subbed the remainder with carrots and that was fine. For the broth I used homemade chicken stock. My daughter loved it but agreed that it needed less cream cheese.

This recipe really was amazing. I added two chicken bouillons because it was all I had and a the rest in vegetable broth. I also have a five pound butternut squash that I roasted and then used 3/4 of. Had no marjorm so skipped that, and use about 5 ounces of cream cheese instead of 8. 

It came out amazing! If my boyfriend doesn't get down on one knee after tasting this then he's crazy.

A good solid soup. I made it as the recipe stands and I think it maybe a tad too salty and too cream cheesey. I think next time I will reduce the number of bouillon cubes and use half and half instead of cream cheese and see how it turns out. Tastes excellent with saltine bits broken up into it.
Delicious, even better if u add some heavy sipping cream ,

This was fabulous!  I would say the best I have tasted so far.  I used leftover squash that I had cubed and roasted in the oven the night before with brown sugar.  I sauted onion and added a clove of minced garlic until tender, then started adding chicken stock, then the left over squash until it was all cooked through.  I pureed in food processor with cream cheese, then just heated it through again right before we ate.   Taking into consideration other comments on the cream cheese, definataly add the cream cheese about 3 or 4 ounces at a time, that way you can get to the richness that you prefer before you have taken it too far.  I added less than half the recipe called for.  Lovely!!

This was my first time cooking with butternut squash. I was afraid that after all that work making it that I would not like it. I loved it! I used butter, one block neufchatel, 4 cups broth and added some salt.
I did not care for this dish.

Not even sure how I came upon this recipe, I'm not a big squash fan.  But I'm glad I did!  The only changes I made: I used 4 cups of chicken stock for the water and I only used 1 package of cream cheese.  We both really enjoyed this soup.  Will make again.  Thanks!
I eliminated the cream cheese and instead pureed it w/a couple spoonfuls of non-fat plain yogurt.  Great taste - can't wait to make it again.

Easy soup.  I used 4 oz. of cream cheese (that's all I had in the house).  It was delicious.  To save time buy a squash that is already cut into pieces.  Playing with the spices can make a big difference.  The cayenne really made the flavors POP!  A great and comforting soup for the fall.  It goes well with raking leaves and apples.

YUM!  Thanks for an easy and fun recipe!  Made this according to direction (OK, I'll admit I used chicken broth instead of water + bullion because I was out of bullion ;-)).  Next time -- will stay with the chicken broth plan (unless I'm out then will do the bullion/water plan), cut the cream cheese in half, and probably just nuke the squash instead of cutting, peeling, cubing.  Good recipe - thanks for posting!
absolutely amazing,i want to make this everyday
Very rich, but delicious.

Very good soup.  I only added 6 ounces of cream cheese and it was still great.  Also, instead of pureeing the soup in batches, I just stuck my hand-held blender right into the pot and pureed the whole thing in a few seconds.

This is just amazing to taste.  I had no idea it would be so very good.  I had to make it again the next day.  And I ended up having a small amount left over that thickened in the fridge.  The next day family was using it as a dip with pumpernichel bread....and the thickened soup was perfect for that too.  It is a great recipe.
I have made this many times and my whole family and most friends love it.  When fall comes around, it's the first soup I make!
Great recipe!  I used 1/2 of the amount of cream cheese and extra chili powder.

Thought it was delicious and easy to make!
My modifications:
I quartered the squash and microwaved face down for 8 minutes before peeling.
Thought it was too salty with 4 cubes, so added only 3 (same amount of water).
Added 1 T fresh minced garlic to onions.
Omitted the marjoram (only bc I didn't have it).
Used 4 oz of cream cheese.
Still creamy, smooth and amazing!!!
Love it "as is"

I would give this recipe five stars, but I changed it slightly, so I can't give it a true review. I also roasted the squash first as others had. I used three medium sized squash and that was just enough. I also used only one 8oz package of cream cheese and it was plenty creamy. I cannot imagine using two - it would be way too rich, in my opinion. I also used real butter and low fat cheese and chicken stock, rather than bouillon. It was perfect for fall and squash season.
This was GREAT!  I used 8 oz of Neufchatel and it was just right.  I also used a hand blender instead of a full size blender which was easier to clean-up and worked very well.
Absolutely perfect!  Exactly what I was looking for!  (and I also only used 1/2 the cream cheese)
I only use a single block of cream cheese, but it still turns out fantastic. The liquid should not quite cover the squash for a thick soup.

I used others advice to roast the squash first, then only use 8ox of cream cheese and it was looking good and smelling good until i added the marjoram, it totally ruined this for me. Next time i think i will only add a little bit of brown sugar and salt and pepper, then i think this would be great!
I loved it!!! I cooked for lunch today and It was a hit!!! thanks!!!!

Fantastic!  As others have suggested, I first roasted the squash on the oven at 375 degrees for 45 minutes.  That helped a lot.  I put twice the amount of cayenne pepper and it was JUST spicy enough.  Delicious!
This is one of the best butternut soup recipes I have made.  I use less than one package of cream cheese and replace some broth with some apple juice or cider.

Delish!!! Wonderful recipe! OK, for my conscience, I cut out 4 oz. cream cheese, but just tasted it after making it to exact specs, other than that (hate it when people change recipe and rate), IT IS FABULOUS!!!! Beautiful color, silky texture and aroma-wonderful taste.
Just picked some butternut squash from the garden and came across your recipe-THANK YOU for posting it!!!!

Wow!  This soup was incredible!  I followed others advice and roasted the squash and used a hand emersion blender to break down the clumps.  My husband is a meat and potatoes guy, so I served it with toasted beef sandwiches, but it was hearty enough for me to eat as a meal.  (I used the 2 pkgs of cream cheese which made it thick and very creamy) 
Thanks so much for sharing this great recipe!   

I also tried this recipe with canned pumpkin instead of squash and it turned out great!  I added a little bit of brown sugar, some ginger and cinnamon and it was a huge hit!  The pumpkin made a slightly thinner soup, but could have also been because of light cream cheese.  Either way it was delicious!!   Thanks for sharing the recipe!!!

I put the squash/onion/broth mix into the food processor and gave it a try before adding any cream cheese. It was beyond amazing. It's really hard to believe that something so simple could be so delicious. I was afraid, however, that by not adding the cream cheese I'd be missing out on something. I added less than half of the amount listed in the recipe, but even that small amount was enough to kind of ruin the recipe. It's delicious enough before adding any cream cheese, so just leave it out. Cheers to our health!
Butternut squash is a favorite and I love soups. This was ok, but I've tried better recipes for this. Not thrilled with the cream cheese.

Just made this recipe - it was REALLY easy.  I tweaked it slightly in that I had to use some items I had on hand.  I used red onion, I used cajun seasoning instead of cayenne, I used butter instead of margarine.  I only used 4 ounces of cream cheese (that seemed to be enough).  To top it off I put a swirl of Agave nectar and Tapatio for a sweet and salty kick.  Very good.  Would probably add a little garlic and more salt and pepper next time. :)

I just made this and... wow.  It was a huge hit.  I did make some changes.  I only used about 6 oz. cream cheese.  I used sage instead of marjoram (b/c sage and butternut squash were made to go together) and I used more like 1 1/2 tsp.  I used a bit extra black and cayenne pepper.  AND I used about 1/4 cup parmesan which added a nice extra flavor.  I boiled the squash before working with it to soften it up.  So I cut the stovetop cooking time down to 15 minutes. 

This was so easy and so decadent.  I'll definitely make again. But it is FILLING!

Amazing! After tasting this recipe, I don't think I'll ever make butternut squash in the oven again. I am going to make it to bring to my mother-in-laws for Thanksgiving next week...THAT'S how much I like it.  Lol!

I made this soup tonight but replaced the butternut squash with pumpkin. It turned out amazing! Very simple and tasty!I only used half of the recommended cream cheese, but that wasn't any problem as it turned out very creamy.

We love this soup but I made several changes. 1)Used homemade chicken broth instead of bullion cubes. 2)Rubbed a sprinkle of dry oregano and parsley into it instead of marjoram. 3)Added a small sweet potato and a couple of small carrots. 4)Used just one package cream cheese. 5)Used a submersion blender right in the pot to blend instead of messing with regular blender, much easier!
I used a good neufchatel cheese to make this.....it was GREAT! really rich flavor. I roasted the squash in the oven with onions and brown sugar

I have made this soup with both frozen cooked squash and fresh roasted squash.  a friend who made this soup gave me the recipe. It is a simple soup that gets wows everytime it is made.  I have also made without using the cayenne pepper. very good. Will continue to make.

This turned out Really good! I did not put margarine--I put butter. Instead of 2 pkg's of cream cheese I put 1 1/4 and was still very creamy. I used a food processor but it needs a blender to get it finely pureed. I added more cayenne to be spicier. Very delish!
Waaaaaaay too much cream cheese. It was very thick and it seemed like a velveeta cheese dip. I would reduce cream cheese by at least half or more.

This soup is EXCELLENT! I am pregnant and have had an extremely hard time eating food; so I have been quite wary of trying new recipes. This recipe had so many great reviews (and soup sounded so comforting) that I thought I should try it. I decided to follow the advice to use half as much cream cheese and it tasted TERRIFIC! I had a horrible time trying to put the extra soup away. Even though I was stuffed to the brim I still wanted to keep eating it because it is so delicious! This has already been added to my personal favorite recipe book that holds only the best recipes I have ever found. (I'm sure I'll soon have the recipe memorized and won't need the recipe at all.) I love it! Thank you so much for helping me enjoy eating again, Mary!

delicious! I did make some changes: 1. roast the squash with 4 cloves of garlic and a drizzle of olive oil at 350 for an hour 2. cut the margarine to 2 tbsp 3. you really only need 1 package of cream cheese and use the 1/3 fat version I had never used a butternut squash before.
I don't know...it was ok.
I  loved it!!!!!  I did add 1/2 cup of roasted red peppers to the puree though.  It wasn't needed.  It was just something I decided to add for more nutrition.  Delicious!!
I have made this soup several times and everyone always loves it.  It is very rich though so I would recommend either serving it as a meal in and of itself or in small portions with dinner.
The family loved it ! I added a dollop of sour cream and swirled it before serving. Then I garnished it with a pinch of paprika.

Great basic recipe.  I also roasted my squash as other reviewers suggested - those suckers are a pain to peel!  I added about a cup of really good apple juice in addition to the chicken stock and only used 4oz of cream cheese - it was plenty creamy!  The girls at work went ga-ga over it.

Thank you for sharing this amazing recipe, Mary! My family loved it. We've never had squash soup before now... This is going in the recipe hall of fame- one of my favorite soups ever! I only used one package of cream cheese and it was great- garnished with a sprinkle of crispy bacon pieces and a little dollop of sour cream.... Amazing!!

I followed other reviewer's suggestions by roasting the squash first, using 8 oz of cream cheese, adding a golden delicious apple, some sage leaves, and using chicken stock instead of bouillon. It was a little spicy for my mother's taste, but she's kind of a wimp about spice :) I thought it was great! Thanks for a great recipe!
Great soup, quick to make. I substituted greek yogurt for the cream cheese and it worked out wonderfully.
Delicious but I did roast the squash first and only used 1 pkg of cream cheese..otherwise it would have been way to rich and thick for my liking.

This is a good start - but totally agree with many other reviewers who halved the cream cheese the recipe called for. I doubled this recipe and still only used 8 oz of cream cheese and it turned out really nice. Adding fresh grated ginger also compliments the squash. Gives it a nice vibrant kick - which the recipe needed if prepared as is.
Definitely a great recipe! The only thing I would do next time is only use one package of cream cheese instead of two. It kind of overpowered the taste of the squash.

Very good soup. I kicked the spices up a notch because I was craving spicy - used black pepper, cayenne, mild curry powder & a pinch of nutmeg. I used 1/2 the cream cheese called for, but still noticed that the soup smelled really... cheesy. Didn't taste too cheesy, but the aroma was affected. I think next time I'll go with heavy cream instead. Getting the warm pulp out of a squash that's been roasted or in the microwave without burning your fingers is hard enough, I am not even going to attempt to peel those suckers raw!
Really Yummy!!! I didn't use cream cheese, no need for it the soup it's already thick and creamy as it is.Also I omited the cayenne. Everything else the same. A keeper for sure.
Simple & Delicious, used 1 package of cream cheese, plenty good.

So good!  I roasted the squash, added apple, salt, and nutmeg per others' review.  Used only one block of cream cheese.  I wanted it a little more thick so I added a bit of cornstarch slurry.  Delicious!
Very easy recipe!  I used homemade chicken broth that was full of spices and very flavorful.  I also only added 1 pkg of cream cheese.  I found it very yummy for a cold day!!  Thanks!
This was really good, but so rich!  I also thought it should have been a little creamier- mine seemed a bit watery.  Anyway, I got a lot of compliments and it looks beautiful!

WONDERFUL---Easy to make, and the flavor is WOW. I followed the recipe exactly. There are suggestions here that one can take or leave. I am def. going to try roasting the squash for even more flavor, sure maybe less cream cheese is fine. I am thinking adding some shredded carrot next time and I believe this would be fantastic adding some crab too. That's whats great about this kind of recipe. Good as is, or have fun.
delicious!  used light cream cheese and only 1 stick.  also, used chili powder instead of cayenne.  if you want to taste some heat use more!

This was a very easy soup to put together, like others I too roasted the squash prior to assembly. I only used half the suggested amount of cream cheese, and I think a person could omit it entirely if they didn't have it on hand. I added a teaspoon of curry powder to the soup as well, as I like the added heat and thought it balanced the richness a little better. Overall a really great and rewarding recipe

This was excellent, however, I did alter the preparation a bit. As others did, I roasted the squash and only used 1 pkg of cream cheese. I forgot the squash while it was cooking so it roasted for about an hour and 15 minutes, but it didn't burn and seemed to give a better texture. I used a can of chicken broth and added 2 Tbsp of nutmeg. I didn't have the time to mix in a blender so I just put eveything in a large pot and used a hand-held mini-blender to mix. I think it definitely helped in the texture although it was still a little "grainy", not that we minded. It was still a little rich, but excellent. However, when it was reheated for lunch the next day, it was not very good...way to sweet and the taste seemed to have altered a bit. Maybe the ingredients had a chance to "meld" together and alter the flavor. Overall, I great recipe. Thanks!

Oh my goodness, this is by far the BEST butternut squash soup I have ever had.  I love the taste of cayenne pepper in it.  I doubled the marjoram and my squash was huge so I don't know how that affected the taste all I know is that my husband and I loved it.  I also added only about 4oz of cream cheese.  This will the only butternut squash soup I will be making!  Really, really amazing!

only changes I made was to slice the squash in half and bake in the oven first (350 for about an hour). Also used butter instead of margarine (and about 1T instead of 4T). Didn't have marjoram so I used oregano. Also used only 6 oz of low-fat cream cheese (can't imagine using 2 whole packages!) It was still VERY thick and creamy. Delicious!

My husband loved it(and he normally doesn't like soup) but I, a soup lover, did not love it.  It was a little rich and too smooth for my taste.  I would prefer something else in there for more texture and zing.  Just personal preference.

i like this soup, but do think it has something missing. i added some nutmeg and cinnamon per other posters, and it livened up a little.  and be careful with the onion, i its flavor almost overpowers the soup. however, i think some flavored, herb bread dipped in it will be perfect!!   but certianly a beautiful soup because of the deep orange color. add some sour cream swirls and some greenery, and you have  beautiful dish!!
this soup is just divine! I roasted the squash and  added just a touch of ginger and cinnamon. I also went with 1/2 the cream cheese (reduced fat). I will be making this many more times!
I'm not a soup-person but gave this a try and everyone was pleasantly surprised.  Great for the cool/cold fall months coming in fast.
I used 1/2 the cream cheese and a little red pepper since I didn't have cayenne and it turned out great!

I made this today for thanksgiving and it was so easy for one I bought the squash already cube so all i had to do was follow direction. Great soup, never had this type of squash before and it will not be my last. Didnt have marjoram and only use one pack of cream cheese.

This soup was very delicious loved the smooth texture and the rich taste. My family enjoyed it also. I did not however, enjoy the preparation of cutting the butternut squash it proved to be very difficult this would have been the perfect recipes if suggestions for cut and peal were mentioned.
I did not care for this recipe.  Definitely way too much cream cheese.  Will try to find another recipe that's lighter.

I have to admit I did what a few people suggested and put the apple cider and granny smith apple in this recipe that was the only thing I changed. And it was absolutely horrible to sour and the flavors did not blend at all together. I was very disappointed in this soup. I wish I hadn't have wasted the Delicious 2 butternut squash on this recipe, I'm sorry but this gets no stars.
Can't beat it for a cold winter warm up.

This is was so yummy.  I roasted the butternut like others suggested with butter, salt and pepper at 350 for 1 hr.  I also used 4 cups chicken broth instead of water/bullion cubes.  I also only did one cream cheese, and I added a couple of dashes of nutmeg.  So good.!

This didn't have much taste to me aside from the cream cheese. I used less than half the required amount because I had tasted the soup prior to blending it with cream cheese and was concerned that the whole thing would just taste like cream cheese if I used it all.  I also added much more of the recommended spices towards the end of cooking the squash because it didn't taste like much.  Perhaps my squash wasn't fresh enough to add good flavor?  Not sure. I might try it again and re-rate, but for now it's a 2.

Our dinner party was raving about this! We had some tasty bread to dip in the soup, but honestly it seemed like it took away from the amazing flavor! Changes we made: We used butter instead of margarine, chicken broth instead of water & boullion, and neufchatel instead of cream cheese. We microwaved the squash before cutting it into small peices and throwing it into the pot. After we added all the ingredients, I smashed the squash with one of those potato mashers (still in the pot). We added the cheese directly to the pot, and it melted right in. We also added some orange peel for flavor. Definitely will be making this again, many times!
Awesome! I didn't add the second block of cream cheese and definitely wouldn't recommend doing that. I can imagine the soup would taste too cream-cheesy.
I make about 3 batches of this each fall. It is so delicious. I also cut the cream cheese amount in about half. I look forward to it every year.
Excellent.  Do use chicken broth in place of water and 1 pkg. instead of 2.  So quick, easy and delicious.

This soup is addicting!  Very creamy, full of flavor, and so easy to make!  I took the advice of other reviews and only used 1 package of cream cheese.  Next time I make it, I think I will add more water and bouillon to make it a litte thinner; just as a personal preference.  Thanks for sharing this great recipe!

Hey folks this is SO easy to make if you don't cube and peel the squash first. Just cut a half inch hole in the squash (to avoid explosions) and microwave it whole until tender when poked with a fork, about 15 minutes. Turn a few times during nuking. Then just cut it in half, scoop out the seeds, and scoop out the cooked squash from the peel. VERY easy!
I halved the recipe, and used onion powder and garlic powder and no marjoram, 1 T of butter and 3 oz cream cheese. I just dumped the cooked squash and other ingredients into a blender and it was done. Excellent, rich and tasty!
Hard to please everyone at the table right? Wrong! Easy to make and easy to please. Thrilled to have found this. I agree, baking the squash first is a great hint.

AWESOME! I roasted the squash with olive oil, s,p, and garlic for about 1:15 at about 375. Only used 1 block cream cheese, 1/3 less fat cream cheese. And used 2 cups water, 3 cubes bouillion. Used 1 squash.
This is delicious even without the cream cheese.
Great, but I cut down on the cream cheese

Coming from a young amateur chef, this soup was fantastic. It's only the second soup I've attempted and it came out wonderfully. I added fresh parsley and a dollop of sour cream at the end which made it aesthetically pleasing.
Used chicken broth instead, roasted squash first, added garlic powder and curry powder as seasoning. YUM! Favorite at our house!
sooo good- used 1 pkg of creme cheese and it was a big hit.  didn't have cayanne so i used red pepper flakes ground up.  i will make it again and again.
I used 4 oz of cream cheese instead of the 2 blocks of cream cheese, and it was excellent.  I make this quite a bit, love it every time!

I have rated this before but I have now made this many,many times and it is requested often. I use one whole squash (large) and only one cream cheese. The cayenne is what I love, we love the kick this gives.
When making ahead , remember to add some more broth or water as this thickens up quite a bit.
This is a healthy and delicious soup!
just delicious the way it is :>

Made this tonight - very delicious! I used 3/8 tsp cayenne and 1/4 tsp cinnamon. I also substituted oregano because I didn't have marjoram. I used 8oz. Cream cheese but will probably cut it to 4oz. next time. The soup got a bit thick toward the end of a bowl. Also we crushed plenty of Ritz crackers into it. So yummy!

My husband HATES all squash. I made this for him and he LOVED it, that fact only desveres 5 stars, I made it with 1/3 reduced fat cream cheese and next time I am goignto try Fat free just to see if we can make it healthier without losing any of this awesome flavor. I am also going to roast the squash, I just love the roasted veggie taste it really adds alot to dishes. But all in all it is great without any changes! TY Mary!

This is better than most brands I have bought in the store. I know I am strange, but I decided to make this sweet and add brown sugar to it. I also left in the cayenne and it had a sweet/spicy taste that I love.

I'm rating it a 4 because I liked it but my kids didn't. Its a very rich soup and I only added half the cream cheese. I also didn't have cayenne pepper so I did not add any. I cooked the squash the day before and just added everything together just before lunch. I will make this again however I will add a little more chicken stock and less if any cream cheese. I hope it freezes well. Thanks for sharing.
This soup was awesome!

Yum!  I definitely cut the cream cheese in 1/2, though.  And used 1 pkg frozen squash instead of fresh.  All I had on hand.  =).  Don't overdo the cayenne, either.  It adds quite a kick.  A VERY impressive starter for an elegant dinner.  I served it in clear bowls with parsley sprinkled on top.  Beautiful!  And tasty. Thanks!

Super yummy!  After following the recipe, more or less, I thought it was a little bland then added too much black pepper.  Too much for my little guys, but I still loved it.  Next time will let people add their own add'l seasoning.

FABULOUS with only a few minor changes.....definitely decrease cream cheese to 8oz. and use neufchâtel for healthier version. I added just a dash of nutmeg and about 1/3 c canned pumpkin (leftover from baking!). It is so good!!!

I only made a couple of changes and it only made it easier.  Instead of bouillon i used LowFat, Low Sodium Chicken Stock and reduced the amount of cream cheese to 12 oz. using Low Fat Cream Cheese. Added a little parsley on top and it was delicious.  I'm enjoying a mug of it right now!!!!

I did a couple of things different as per other reviews. I roasted the squash and only used 1 package of cream cheese. It was divine. Making it again for my family Christmas get together. Thanks for the recipe and helpful hints.

This is yummy! If you have a Trader Joe's in your area, you can buy bagged, diced butternut squash.  It's a perfect-sized bag for this recipe and a huge time-saver. Just pop the squash into the broth (with the cooked onions) and simmer for about 20 min.

I made this just as directed except I only used the amount of butter I felt I needed to saute the onions and I halved the cream cheese as Mary suggested & it was very, very good. This soup has a good seasoning while not masking the squash.
I followed the recipe except i added chicken stock and water and substituted the cheese with one cup of heavy cream.it turned out delicious.

I followed the recipe essentially as written. I did start the squash in the oven to roast for 45 min but then ended up cutting it up and cooking it in my Instant Pot. It did help giving it a start in the oven. While it was hot to touch, it made peeling it easier. Next time I will cook it in the Instant Pot entirely and then make it into soup.

But I digress... following the recipe as written except for only adding one brick of cream cheese instead of two. I also added some apple cider, based upon a previous reviewer's suggestion. This made it good but it seemed bland. I ended up adding some powdered ginger and then some french seasoning from Penzey's. That took it to a new level, can't wait to have it for lunch tomorrow! Thanks for the recipe!

Made this kind of soup for the first time and I would say I'm not very good in the kitchen. I followed the directions but did reduce the cream cheese as suggested. I found it really easy to make and everyone loved it! I will absolutely make this again.
My roommate and I are in LOVE with this recipe! It's so easy to make and perfect for cold winter nights. I'm so ready to start making it again this fall!
We only used one bar of cream cheese and it was plenty - two bars may have been too much.  Good recipe overall!
Loved this. I only used one package of cream cheese, and added half a can of coconut milk.
Jeepers! So easy and so delicious! I used thyme instead of marjoram and didn't quite add as much cream cheese, but realy, it is a recipe I'll be sharing and making again!

I always use this as a base recipe, turns out fantastic every time!  In addition to kick it up a little, I add:
1/2 tsp cinnamon
1/2 tsp nutmeg
1/2 tsp ginger
1/4 tsp all spice
1/4 c maple syrup
Then I substitute a large apple for the onion.  Only because I don't like onions.

I used 4 oz of low fat cream cheese and it was still rich, but great!  I didn't use quite as much better as called for.  I roasted the squash for about an hour at 350 with some olive oil, garlic powder, and pepper.  About 2# squash needed
ETA:  made with less cream cheese and it was not as good, and pepper really took over.  Would stick with my above review.

Great recipe! I used two medium-sized butternut squashes, halved them, and roasted them for 35min in 350F, cut side down, with chopped garlic, salt, and pepper. I also eliminated the marjoram, used 4c chicken stock, and added only 4oz fat-free cream cheese. I tried it without the cream cheese and it was just as good. Since the butternut was already pretty tender from the oven, I only brought to a boil for a few minutes, then used an immersion blender to blend it all. Finally, I added the cream cheese at the end so it wouldn't curdle. Overall, very good. It was missing just a little something though...I wonder what it'd be like with a little sharp cheddar...I'll report back :)
I hate rating a recipe that I tweaked.  But I appreciated and followed the suggestions to bake the squash first and to cut the cream cheese in half.  Served this for my friends and they loved it.
love it, it was easy and fast to do.

This is fantastic. I cook the squash in the microwave first. Just split it, remove the seeds and cook cut side down in a half inch of water for about 15 minutes. Then it just has to be scraped out of the shell. Much easier than peeling and cutting up. I also think this is great without the cream cheese if you want to cut down on some calories.

I made this for my family the other day, however I only had acorn squash on hand and it worked just as well.  I used half the cream cheese to start and it was perfect. My whole family enjoyed the soup.  I may add some more Cayenne pepper next time for a little more of a kick.  I will be trying a few other ideas that the previous posters shared as well. All in all...it is on my "cook again" list.

This soup is awesome; I've made it twice now, once for me and once for Christmas dinner.  It went over real well and had many requests for the recipe.  As many others suggested, I only used 1 block of cream cheese and it is definately creamy enough.  Thanks for the great recipe!

Wow! This is really good. Like others, I used one package of cream cheese and a little more cayenne pepper. I didn't have majoram on hand, but basil works wonderfully in this. I also had no chicken bouillon cubes so I used vegetable stock. This is easy to make and is now on my list of favorites.
I loved this soup! I only used 1/2 brick of cream cheese and it was still plenty rich and tasty.
absolutely amazing and so easy to make - served this as a starter during one of my Christmas meals and EVERYONE was asking for the recipe!
I used vegetable bouillon to keep it vegetarian. I added a litlle too much cayenne and it tasted funny. Next time I will use more broth to make it thinner because it was very thick.

Simple and delicious!! I did make a few changes. I used 1 cup of cheddar cheese and 1/4 cup of cream because that was what I had on hand. Roasting the squash makes things a lot easiest and gives the soup a great flavor. The cayenne pepper is a surprising "must add"! :)

This is a huge hit with my family both at TG and Christmas. I peel, core and cube my squash, toss it in EVOO, sprinkle with salt and roast about 45 minutes in 350 for a deeper flavor. I chop a large Vidalia onion and mince up 4 cloves garlic and saute in EVOO. Add 4 to 5 cups veg stock (Instead of water) and leave the spices the same. I add in my squash + a peeled and chopped honey crisp apple and bring to a boil for a minute or two. I omit the cream cheese altogether. Blend in small batches and be sure to always cover top of blender with hand towel to prevent getting burned. I pour from blender to crock pot for parties. I've made this soup 3 days in advance and it only gets better. I also use it as a sauce over cheese ravioli and it's AMAZING! I'm a vegetarian and just love good recipes that don't call for artificial ingredients.
my picky two year old ate it all up- and that says a lot!

This soup was so yummy!  When I had planned to make this for dinner my husband told me that he does not like squash, so I told him he could heat up leftovers from the previous night.  He decided that he would eat the soup and he loved it!  The cream cheese is the key ingredient.  I used reduced fat and only one package...very creamy and thick.  I did not have marjoram, so my husband looked up on the internet and found oregano as a substitution.  Looking forward to eating for lunch tomorrow!
To say that this is incredible is an understatement. Super easy, inexpensive and a taste that will knock your socks off.

I added basil and cumin instead of the spices listed, and only used 1/2 of the cream cheese.
Excellent recipie - definate crowd pleaser :)
       Janinne - university student and soup lover
Great!  I used a little oregeno instead of the Marjoram.  I also added a chopped up apple and a little ginger.  It's a stick to your ribs fall/winter kind of thing.
This is a great recipe, even my husband who does not like squash soup loved it! I did use a little less cream cheese, since it is added at the end, easy to adjust to your liking.

This was a great recipe I did follow some others and I roasted the squash onions and garlic with olive oil salt and fresh cracked pepper I only used half the cream cheese I did not use the marjoram I used Curry for a twist and it was AMAZING made so much took it to the office and everyone that tried it loved it ...this is a keeper

It was ok, but my husband and I didn't care too much for this soup. It needed to be more savory or more sweet. It was edible for me, but my husband wouldn't even finish his. I think next time I'll just stick to eating my squash roasted.

This is a great starter recipe. I really enjoyed making it. I did make some modifications. I roasted the butternut with olive oil, fresh garlic, S&P. I only used half of the cream cheese as I didn't want the cheese to over power the squash. Added extra cayenne, 2 cans of chicken broth and 1 cup of water.

This is really good. I also cooked the squash in the oven first.  It is so much easier peeling and cubing.  Also, I only used one package of cream cheese.  I think the 2nd package would have made it to creamy and overpowered the squash.  I did still use the same measures of all other ingredients. The family loved it.  My dad asked for the recipe to make for friends!  I will make this again and again.

This has been my go-to comfort soup ever since I discovered it this past fall trying to find ideas to use the squash that I received in my CSA share!

A couple of tips: 1)Only 1 bar of cream cheese & go for the reduced fat version (neufchatel cheese) to cut calories out... you will not taste a difference! 2) Definitely bake the squash at 350 deg for at least 45 min with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, pepper and lil bit of crushed garlic.. you will taste a slight raw squash after-taste if you don't since I've tried it both ways. 3) I like to add slightly more cayenne pepper (1/2 tsp total for a kick) and reduce the chicken boullion cubes to 2. 4) Costco sells the butternut squash already skinned and pre-cut in a 2 lb package for $5 (which is all this recipe needs). Slightly more costly, but saves a TON of time prepping. 

Enjoy :)

Delicious!! I used 4 cups of water instead of 3, a bit more marjoram, 1/4 tsp cayenne, and 1/2 package of 1/3 less fat cream cheese. And butter instead of margarine. It is sooo good! I might even use a little less cream cheese next time or a little less better. As I saw in another review, 6 cups of butternut squash is roughly equal to 2 lbs.

I needed soup in a hurry so I used cartons of organic butternut squash soup. I used 3 of these and 4 cups chicken broth. I added italian turkey sausage and browed it with my onion and garlic first. I couldn't resist adding 1/4 of sherry. I added everything else and used only 8oz of the cream cheese. It was heavenly and took only minutes to prepare. Now I crave this soup!

This recipe is delicious and easy to make.  It's a regular in the rotation at our house.  I use oregano instead of marjoram (half of the recipe amount for marjoram), 1 bar of cream cheese and chicken broth instead of water.

this soup was amazing I made it for my baby shower and everyone loved it! I did however make three changes to it 1) I did not puree the squash and onion mix I just mashed it 2) I only used one 8 oz pack of cream cheese 3) I added cubed butternut squash at the end.
best soup ever!!
Super easy to make and very good.

This is my favorite squash soup. I've made several times with and without the cream cheese (prefer without), with stock and 1 added boullion cube instead of water, and increased the cayenne b/c we like heat. It's a nice change from the brown sugar/cinnamon flavors you usually get with squash. Thanks for sharing!
My daughter made this for our Thanksgiving dinner and it is delicious!!  Thanks!!  She only used one cream cheese and it ended up thick, almost puddingish, but really, really yummy.
We just didn't care for it.
has become a Thanksgiving staple....
Very good.  Roasted 2 smallish butternut squashes cut in half at 375 for about an hour. Didn't use nearly as much cream cheese, maybe 6 ounces.
I made this soup..minus half the cream cheese and 1/2 c. Less water. I used an immersion blender to cream everything together after the squash was cooked.  It was absolutely amazing. .
Sooooo good. Wouldn't change a thing

Excellent soup. I've made it twice during dinner parties. Leftovers reheat surprisingly well. I used half the cream cheese, like many other reviewers, and followed the rest of the instructions to the letter. It's a favourite now. Cheers.

Great recipe, though I did alter it a bit. The first time I made this soup it was too thick and much too rich, so I added a cup more chicken stock. I also used only half the cream cheese. Additionally, I love onions, so I used an entire medium sweet onion. 

Great for a cold evening!
Very good- I added an apple to the mix and it was fabulous!
I added a ton of pumpkin pie spices and used light sour cream instead of cream cheese, cutting the amount in half. It gave a nice zip to the soup. It was DELICIOUS!!!
Very good.
I loved it

My first time making butternut squash soup. Loved this soup! Thank you for the recipe and reviews to help me twig it the way I know I would like it. I sprayed a tinfoil lined pan with olive oil and roasted a small butternut squash (open side down/scoop out the seeds)and 2 cloves of garlic (put them under the hole where the seeds were) at 350 degrees for 45 min. Let it cool down. While it was cooling I sauteed 2T butter with finely chopped onion until soft. I added 1C of the chicken stock. I scooped out the squash with an icecream scoop and added it to the pot along with 2 more cups of the chicken stock, a pinch of  five spice (I didn't have cloves so this worked), black pepper to taste. Then I put it all in the blender and mixed it up.I heated it back up in the pot, then added a dollup of sour cream and mixed it in.(I did not use any cream cheese) I spooned it into bowls and grated parmesan cheese in the middle and added a pinch of parsley flakes.  Mmmm so good! Makes 4-5 bowls
Made recipe as listed.  Very good.  Remember to choose a ripe squash, which is indicated by the flesh being darker orange.  Much more tasty when ripe.  Add curry if you'd like.

This soup was not good.  I cut the cream cheese in half as others recommended and roasted my squash.  I don't know if it was because I had a really large squash or what but it turned out so thick you could eat it as a dip.  And I found it still too rich with the amount of cream cheese.

Just made this soup tonight!  Perfect night for it since it's pouring rain here.  I used butternut squash from my garden (which worked out well since I didn't know what to do with it!!).  I also only used about 1/4th of the cream cheese and it was perfect!  My husband said this is the best soup he has ever had!!
My young boys LOVE this soup.  They don't even know there's squash in it.  They call it cheese soup and ask for seconds.  I definitely recommend cutting the cream cheese in half.
I use herb de provence  instead of marjoram. Also cut cream cheese in half.

This was a real keeper.  I too used real butter (unsalted due to the bouillon.)  I also only used one block of cream cheese. I finished it off with toasted pine nuts.  Delicious!  And so easy.  Definitely better and quicker to roast the squash and scoop it out.

Only gave it 4 stars because of the 16 oz of cream cheese.  I used 8 oz and could have even used a little less.  I also added roasted yellow peppers and turmeric.  This is a very good base soup to play around with.  Husband loved it.

I like to roast the squash in halves, peel the skin off after it's tender. I used one butternut squash, one 8oz cream cheese, and only 3 vege bouillon cubes instead of four. Otherwise kept the directions as is. Perfection!

It is quite spicy.  And, I like spicy stuff. I only had one small-medium squash so I used it, 1 large sweet potato and the rest of the ingredients. I only used 1/4 block of cream cheese, 2 chicken cubes and 3 cups of water.  I def need to cut back on the cayenne next time...yikes!!!  It's tasty, I like it but my husband was a so-so.

Outstanding! This was a wonderful soup that didn't last long around here. I would agree to 1/2 the cream cheese. I also added 1/2 apple, nutmeg, cinnamin and a little brown suger. It worked well with acorn squash too. Next time I'll try a little milk to thin it out a bit. It is really thick and creamy. A definate keeper! Try it.

I have been making this recipie for years and I have finally perfected it!!! I made a few tweaks with trial and error over the years but this soup is amazing if you do the following:

Use 3 butternut squash, halved and roasted in the oven with crushed garlic and evoo at 350 until soft. Let cool and refrigerate over night only because I'm lazy.

Sautee 1/4c onion, add squash, 1 large peeled Granny Smith Apple and 4c water. Boil, then purée with immersion blender.  I get about 10-12c squash out of the 3 I use. Add 5 bullion cubes, add more water as I go to desired consistency. Add 1 brick of cream cheese, 1tbs marojam, 1tsp cyanne, fresh pepper and some fresh salt. Let simmer stirring occasionally for an hour to marry the flavors.

Roast the squash seeds in olive oil, a dash of salt and some lowerys seasoning salt... Just a smudge! Use this to top the soup!!! Soooooo good! 

Serve with crusty bread and cyanne powder. Mind blown!
I added a healthy dose of garlic to this and used only half the cheese (reduced fat, at that) and it was very good. I felt it was too thick, but my husband, who loves thick, creamy soups, loved it.
This was good, I only had half the cream cheese, and no cayanne, but I added butter and milk, paprika and a a few ounces of vegatable cream cheese. It was very tasty!

Great recipe. 
I followed some of the changes and added my own and my boyfriend said it is his all time favorite soup and he doesn't even like butternut squash. 

First, I cut two butternut squash in half, put some EVOO and salt/pepper on them and cut side down roasted them at 375 for 45 min. 

Towards the end of the squash cooking time, I sautéed the onions in the butter with two cloves of garlic until translucent. 

I used only two chicken bouillon cubes, added the rest of the ingredients to the pot, including the scooped out squash. Oh and I almost forgot, I added one chopped up and peeled apple to the pot. 

Added that all to a blender and since I only had half a block of cream cheese, used that. 
Tasted PHENOMENAL. 
I topped each bowl with some fresh steamed corn since I had a bunch and wanted to use it and some chopped chives. 

Delish.
This soup is GREAT!! but there is no need for that much cream cheese at a couple of tablespoons at a time you really don't need any more than 2T

This recipe is awesome.  Even people who say they don't like squash love it.  It's so creamy.  I only use block of cream cheese (which is plenty), and I cook the squash in the microwave and scoop out the pulp into the soup.  It is much faster, and I'll do anything to avoid peeling and cubing raw squash!  Yum!

Weeknight suggestion: If you put the whole squash wrapped in tinfoil in the slow cooker then the only thing you need to do when you get home from work is wait for it to cool, purée the ingredients and reheat. So quick and yummy!

This soup makes me feel like I'm eating in a restaurant each time I make it. I prefer using pre-cut squash to save time. 2LBs is about 6 cups. I add an apple, and use 2 - 14.5oz cans of low sodium, fat free broth. I also reduce the cream cheese to 4-6 ounces. My kids don't like spicy, my 1st born likes nutmeg in his, and DH likes Hot Madras Curry in his, so I put those and cayenne on the side. I serve with French bread (tried sourdough, and we feel it's too tangy for this soup). Thanks for the keeper!
Very good! I only used half the cream cheese. I also did not purée, whisking it til soup was slightly chunky.

I followed the advice of using only 1/2 the cream cheese, and it still turned out very creamy and cheesy.  I think next time I will use only 1/4 of the cream cheese, and perhaps add a bit of milk.  Also, I think i will try a bit of allspice.  I also followed the advice of baking the squash for 40 minutes before dicing, that made it very easy to blend.  I will definitely make this again.  Yummy!
I cut the amount of cream cheese in half, and worked out perfect for my family!

OMG....this SO good! Rich and creamy. I followed the suggestion of others to roast the squash first. I also used 4 cups of chicken broth instead of bouillon and water. I used only 1 package of 1/3 less fat cream cheese and it was plenty. I also added a little garlic powder and sage to the other seasonings. This is super simple and tastes like restaurant quality. Thanks for the fantastic recipe. I will make this over and over again.

This was delicious!  I used chicken stock (not broth) and 1 package of cream cheese was plenty.  My hand-held blender was perfect for this recipe, the end result was creamy and smooth and no blender was required.  Will make again!

Loved this soup! I roasted the squash with some olive oil and minced garlic first, then blended it together with the rest of the ingredients. I opted out of the cream cheese and instead substituted 2 cups water and 1 cup half & half instead of 3 cups water. I added a chipotle pepper and a bit more Cayenne pepper. It had a little extra kick and a smokey flavor! My husband isn't a huge squash fan- but he loved this soup!
This came out great the first time. The only deviation was that I used 1 pack of 8 oz cream cheese advised by other reviewers. My 7 year old even gave me a thumbs up!

This is our family's all-time favorite allrecipes.com recipe--we've eaten it frequently since first discovering it (and allrecipes.com) more than 2 years ago. The only change we've made was to make it the way our friend first fixed it for us: a block of low-fat cream cheese and a block of silken tofu instead of the 2 blocks of cream cheese. It doesn't alter the taste, but adds a little extra protein. My toddler LOVES this soup and requests it often. Peeling and cubing the squash is time consuming, but the soup freezes well before the addition of the cheese, so I often devote an afternoon to the beloved butternut!

I loved this recipe!  I opted not to add cream cheese and instead scooped in a tablespoon of low fat sour cream.  I also added a sweet potatoe.  To speed up cooking time, I cut the squash lengthwise and cut up the sweet potatoe and microwaved it for 15 mins on high in a small dish with about 1 cm of water in it.  It comes out soft.  I just peeled it and used a potatoe masher in the pot to mash it all up.  It was amazing!! Even my kids gobbled it up:)

Roast squash in olive oil, salt, and pepper face side down instead of the skillet idea. Till tender of course. The skin should peel off very easily when it's done roasting. Oven temp around 375 to 350. Depending on how much time you have. Also only one package of cream cheese should be used. Two is way to much. Also add some nutmeg into the mix it creates a much more complex pallet. And much more delicious. Since this recipe is so creamy I added fresh cooked bacon bits to add a little diversity in texture and some chopped chives as a garnish. It helps to keep you interested in eating. The guy loved it.
Omit cream cheese altogether.  I used 1 knorr vegetable bouillon cube and 2 cups water but used only half of the resulting stock. Add some milk. Salt to taste.YUM

The best!!!!!!! What an incredible soup.  I am always so glad that I read the reviews before preparing because I also used only 1/2 an 8oz cream cheese and the soup was still just perfect.  Fat free cream cheese will be super next time I make it (just didn't have it on hand today).  Thanks for this super recipe.  I will be making it all winter!

My new favorite soup!  the addition of the cream cheese is key in this recipe, although after the first time I only use 1/2 to 1 block of light cream cheese and that definitely does the trick.  I've made this recipe a few times, and once I did get a slightly mealy texture...I think it must have been the squash since everything else was the same.  Judging from my experience and a lot of the other reviewers, this soup is pretty versatile and can be altered and varied quite a bit with fab results, just don't forget the cream cheese!!!

I just wish I had found this recipe sooner! I used half of the cream cheese that the recipe called for, and it was still very rich. I would do the same, or possibly use even less in the future. The flavor profile is perfect, it could be a bit spicier if you like spicy food, but is great as is. We will definitely be making this again.

I think I just found a piece of heaven in the form of soup!  So easy and so delicious!  I used butter instead of margarine and add a bit of garlicwhile frying the onions.  I used chicken broth in place of water and bouillon and I omitted cayenne pepper as well.  I only used about 1/4 of the cream cheeseas I found it just perfect without it.
Real easy but loved by all. For the record, six cups of squash is about 2lb.of squash.
Just finished making this soup...deeelish! I followed as Mary says in her intro....I used more broth and less cream cheese....PERFECT! ty

Made this for a work lunch today. It was a fabulous hit! I followed the recipe as it said- 1 LG. squash, 4 c low sodium chicken broth (one container is 4 cups) and used butter and hot sauce instead of margarine and Cheyenne. I made it last night and was a little thick today, so I added 1 cup water to the bowl and rinsed the container/diluted. I only used 1 pkg cream cheese and it was still it was rich. Excellent! Will now be a staple on our menu!

I made this recipe but with a few tweaks...I used half the cream cheese,another tablespoon of onion,and an extra half a tablespoon of butter (I can't believe it's not butter).I followed the seasoning to a tea but added bacon salt to the equation.ABSOLUTELY AMAZING!

I think this soup is wonderful! I have never before had butternut squash, this was my first time and I have to say I am glad i tried it, making this soup! I did however omit one of the cream cheese like others suggested;)

I can't stop eating this!!!! I did change the spices to fresh basil and rosemary  because they are my favorite and I added a dash of cumin because that's what I had in the house and now I can't stop eating it! AND.... I forgot to remove the calories so I'm in trouble now :)
Perfect as is but I halved the cream cheese to reduce the fat a bit.

Excellent recipe. Used Pacific chicken broth instead of bouillon which allowed me to salt the final product to my liking. One package of cream cheese was plenty. Opting for a milder version, used thyme instead of the cayenne. Sliced up cold, sweet Fuji apples and generously garnished the soup with the apple chunks and a dollop of sour cream in the center just before serving. Perfect!

Very good and very easy to make.  I took the advice of many other reviews and I only put one block of cream cheese in and I was great.  I might even put a little less in next time but it turned out very well.

This stuff is fantastic!  I get cravings for it.  I cut the cream cheese in half and it's still too rich to eat plain, but I use it as a dip for sourdough bread and it's perfect.  My husband, who dislikes squash, eats this willingly because the cream cheese covers up the squash taste.  One warning: you have to use a good squash or the recipe is ruined!  Out of the many times I made this, it has come out all wrong once (strangely sweet) and I had to throw it out.  I'm pretty sure the squash was at fault.

This is one of my "healthy" eats when I'm trying to lose weight. Why? Because this is soooo good even if you leave the cream cheese out. To dress it up for friends, I also add some diced carrots to give it a bit of texture without extra calories.

because of having a very large meal i decided to omit 8 ounces of cream cheese, leaving only one package in the soup. I tell you, that this is an amazing recipie! I never stay fully true to any recipie so although i added my own twist to it, this soup is amazing and really good!

I'll keep it short.  Super soup.  I only used 8oz of cream cheese and used the 1/3 fat version.  I only used 2 1/2 cups water.  I used about 1/4 tsp cayenne, maybe a tad more because I like a little more spice.  I roasted it with EVOO and Salt and Pepper (350 for 45min).  I also added extra fresh ground pepper at the end...Superb.

DELICIOUS! Same changes as others suggested... roasting the squash (drizzled with olive oil and black pepper) in the oven first. They were perfect at 425 degrees for 45 minutes. I also only added one pkg of cream cheese. Best if served with a fresh loaf of bread.

Once you make this soup there won't be a need for another roasted butternut squash soup recipe; this is hands down the best!  I tweek mine ever so slightly.  I don't put the cream cheese in mine.  Instead I put heavy cream in the blender because it is the ideal consistency in about 30 seconds.  I might add a bit more stock depending on how much butternut squash I added because I usually add a bit more to get a thicker soup.  I put a big dollop of heavy cream on the top of the soup with a sprinkle of the course red sea salt and some homemade croutons (sourdough bread, butter, olive oil and parmesan cheese and kosher salt).  I use the biggest stock pan I have and we seldom have any leftovers.  The roasted butternut squash makes this recipe a real winner!
Very creamy and delicious, but almost TOO creamy. The two packages of cream cheese make it incredibly rich; almost too rich to finish a whole bowl.

This is a very good choice for first course on Thanksgiving!  If you're making it for a lot of people though, it is quite an undertaking.  I highly recommend the roasting of the squash beforehand and only using 1/2 the cream cheese.  I also used lite cream cheese and it still had a very creamy consistency.  I'm so glad I have leftovers!

Roasted 2 medium sized squash for about 45  minutes at 425 (30 minutes in I cut the squash in half). Put them in a large purex dish, added the liquid like suggested then added 1 package of reduced fat cream cheese. Using a hand blender I pureed right in the dish. It is delicious!

I used this  as a base recipe ---one thing I changed was to use only 2 Tbsp of cream cheese --- and added  can evap milk about 1 cup  --- used 1 cup applejuice  fresh and 1 pear  and lots of spices -- cumin- red pepper - ginger ,nutmeg and thyme & marjoram----I added  a little at time and  kept tasting until  just enough  --I  cooked  about 1/2 cup onion  and  2 cloves of  garlic and blended  altogether- it is delicous--- served  with pumpkin seeds and a dollop of sour cream  on top - yummy!

My family LOVES this recipe.  I've made it several times and usually double it.  I do only a couple of things differently.  First off I don't ever use margarine, so I used butter instead.  Also, before blending I leave out a couple of handfuls of cubed squash and add it to the soup for some texture.  I have used low fat cream cheese on occasion and it doesn't seem to make a difference.  Either way, with or without my changes this soup is amazing!
i used 1 package of Cream cheese and halved the cayenne pepper. I also roasted the squash in the oven instead. turned out fantastic

Two words: Comfort food. It was a chilly autumn night when I made this, and the perfect way to end the day. My husband cringed at the sight of it, but as promised with all my cooking he did try it and loved it after all! I used vanialla yogurt instead of cream cheese and it was still creamy and delicious!
My husband loved it, it was a little too rich for me and the kids.

Really delicious! would definitely make again. only used 1 bar of cream cheese and it was plenty rich. my friends told me this soup tastes like something they would expect from a very fancy restaurant. it's so rich you can only eat a little but outstanding! wouldn't freeze again, doesn't taste the same the second time around

Butternut soup is good and nutritious. Here is a easy way to up the ntrition and reduce the fat and dairy; just change half or all the cream cheese with silken tofu - it cost about the same and adds the same consistacy.

I love butternut squash soup but can never get it to come out just right. This one was easy but I changed it to fit my tastes. I don't like spicy- I prefer sweet, so I skipped the spices and added brown sugar while the squash was boiling. Being vegetarian I changed the chicken bullion to veggie broth. When the squash was real soft I put a few ladles full in a bowl with a package of cream cheese & blended with a hand mixer. I kept adding ladles full of squash until all was blended then put it back in the pot and cooked on low for about 15 minutes. SO SWEET and GOOD!! The cream cheese was what I've been missing all these years!
I've made this recipe several times, usually following the review of SLJ6. This time I added 1/2 tsp ginger and 1 tsp cinnamon. My fav recipe for butternut squash soup!
The recipe tastes great, but warning: If you have never cut a squash it is time cosuming and difficult. I watched a video on youtube that was helpful in how to cut the squash.

This is my first time making this soup.  I was hesitant to try it because my daughter hates squash of any kind.  It's almost finished warming up and she tasted it saying it was 'delicious!'   Thanks for a great and simple recipe!

I enjoyed this easy recipe very much! I definitely did not add in all the cream cheese, however, as it would have been way too rich. I only added 2 tablespoons for the whole batch. I also added 1 cup of apple cider to the soup and used chicken broth. Before serving, I sprinkled some ground cloves on top for garnish. It was delicious and I froze the leftovers. Thanks for sharing!

I used this recipe as a base.  
My version:  
. Substitute marjoram with basil
. Increase cayenne pepper to 1/4 tsp
. Reduced cream cheese to 1-8oz package

Easy and delicious!  I baked the squash first, and used 1/2 the cream cheese as others suggested.  I also used oregano instead of marjoram, and a blend of onion, garlic, and shallots (pre-diced from Trader Joe's).  It was quite tasty!  I think you could tweak the spices easily to suit your own taste.

I also roasted my squash first, so much easier. And instead of a blender or processor, I used my immersion blender and it worked like a charm, and less clean up! My husband, not a big soup fan, went back for seconds! Said it was excellent! Thanks!
This soup is just so absolutely delicious...we all fight over the leftovers!
This the best soup.  My in-laws want it for Christmas instead of a gift.  I make it and put in canning jars and give away for Birthdays, and Christmas..  So easy and inexpensive to make.

So good, so good!  I did deviate on the preparation, but I used all the ingredients, except for the cayenne pepper (not my fave).  I only used 2 T of marjarine to saute the onions, roasted the squash with olive oil, and cut the cream cheese by four.  I only pureed half of the squash with the cream cheese and then mashed the other half with a potato masher.  I like to chew a little bit of something in my soup.  This was the best.  I had a pumpkin soup similar to this ten years ago and LOVED it.  I have been searching for the recipe ever since.  Now that I have this one, I will try it with pumpkin next.  Yummy, yummy!!

PS. When making this another time, I found out to NOT use fat free cream cheese.  DOES NOT blend well.

Everyone loved this when I made it. I used 2 whole butternut squashes and when it came time to add in the block of cream cheese it worked well with the blending, but because it wasn't a thick enough soup for me, I tried to add more cream cheese, this time the container kind. I ended up with chunks of white speckles. But it was still phenomenal.

Cut the cream cheese in half, double the cayenne pepper, and viola! You have an absolutely delicious soup!

P.S. 6 cups equals about 2 lbs, or one regular size butternut squash

This soup is so wonderful and creamy.  I didnt alter the recipe at all!  It has a nice spicy kick to it.  I happen to love spicy food, however, if spicy food isnt your thing, I would suggest using a little less pepper.

The kids and I really loved this soup and I had never tried Butternut Squash before.  It was rich,creamy,and just the right amount of sweetness for a hearty and healthy soup.  My hubby didnt really care for it but he's not much of a soup person.  This recipe is a definite keeper for the cool winter months.  Thank you!
Loved this soup. I cut back the cream cheese by half and was still incredibly rich. I puréed cooked bacon for the base and it turned out awesome.

EXCELLENT, you can use about 1/2 of the amount of cream cheese and inrease the water to make it healthier and less filling.  I find it plenty rich with only 1/2 the amount of cream cheese.   Also, I cut the amount of Cayenne in 1/2 so that my 2 year old will ask for seconds, and thirds!  Excellent recipe!!

Ok. . .just made this recipe for the first time and it is amazing! I did cut the cream cheese down to just one 8 oz. and can't imagine having used 2, it's great with one! I wasn't sure if I was supposed to purée the onions with the squash as well, so I have small onions in my soup(which I don't really mind). I suppose next time I will try to purée it all together or possibly just strain out the extra particles from the onion and spices. Very good recipe, I will be making this again!
This is delicious!!!!!!  I used 1-1/2 pkg. of cream cheese.  I didn't have marjoram, so I used thyme and oregano instead.  I will be making this again! (oh it was super easy too!!!)

This was very simple to make.  I made a few changes.  No Marjoram, so used Garham Marsala, and used Chipolte powder instead of cayenne.  Also roasted cut side down brushed with olive oil for an hour.  Fabulous soup, hubby loved it too!
Everyone loves this soup! We make it a meal with some fresh sourdough bread. Definitely roast the squash to make peeling and cubing possible.

Terrible.  Two-8 oz blocks of cream cheese is just too much, so I used 1 1/2 blocks--still way too much.  Also, it was so terribly salty-four bouillon cubes is probably way too many.  Maybe I should have read more of the comments too, because if I had roasted the squash, maybe this soup wouldn't have tasted so bland.  I won't be trying this again.

Loved it and so did my guest. 

My changes.
1. Time: I let the veggies cook in butter for 15min (mixing often), not 5min. 
2. Added: 1 clove of minced garlic, 1/2 teaspon of cinnamon and 1/2 teaspoon of nutmeg
3. Substituted: 1 of the 2 potatos with a sweet potato

Just wonderful.  I followed the advice of others...baked the squash.  I used something other than butternut.  I used 1/4 the cream cheese.  I put everything in the blender except the broth.  Let it chill over night, then thinned with the chicken broth as I reheated it for quests.  They were scraping the pot for every last drop!

This was delicious. I made it as-is, except I added some chopped up kale for extra nutrition and color (I added it along with the squash at the beginning so it would cook down). I would love to experiment with adding mushrooms, beer and/or broccoli to the mix also!!

I loved it this soup. I will be making this soup for my dinner parties until I find another to love. I tweaked it a little, I used one package of cream cheese and substituted the 3 cups of original soy milk instead of water too keep up with the creamy flavor. I did not have marjoram so I used oregano and thyme instead. Thank you for such a yummy recipe.
Tasty! Almost too much cream cheese though  - I added some curry powder for kick and everyone thought it improved it.
Easy and wonderful!  I did put a little
I made this with what I had on hand - only 4 oz cream cheese.  I can't imagine if I had used all of it.  You wouldn't be able to taste the squash.  All in all, a good soup though.
This was delicious.  I don't think I've ever had anything better.  I followed other reviewers' advice and roasted the butternut squash and halved the cream cheese.  It was sooo good.

Fantastic!
Whips up great, if possible use chicken broth or stock instead of bouillon cubes. 
It's very thick, I made mine the night before, and the warmed it up on the stove the next night.  I garnished with fresh parsley and paprika. 
A big hit..
It's become a Thanksgiving tradition in my house.  Great with half the called for cream cheese!
Excellent recipe!!  It's soooooo good!  One package of cream cheese is definitely plenty.
It was wonderful.  It had a sweet and spicy taste.  I only used 1 package of cream cheese.  I will make this again.
Great  soup, have made this numerous times, always good and gets rave reviews from guests. Did change recipe by roasting  the squash in the oven for 45 minutes .  Great recipe!
Absolutely fantastic!  4 stars because it is definately better when you roast the squash.  Don't like Margoram, so I used Thyme, and used 1/4 of the amount of cream cheese.  Thank you!
YUM!!! This was incredible!!!

I was surprised and pleased by this recipe.  I love squash, but am not a huge fan of butternut squash.  However, this recipe was a definite winner with me.  The soup was creamy but not too rich.  I did have a little difficulty pureeing everything after I cooked it, because I had to use a ladle to transfer the soup to a blender, which was a messy process.  I also added about half the cream cheese, and used low fat to decrease the calories.  It still had fantastic flavor.  One thing I would recommend that really helps cut down on the prep time is if you buy the butternut squash already diced, then just cook it with the chicken broth.  I've found it pre-diced at Trader Joe's.
I followed the recipe and the soup had a paste-like consistency and a very strange, sweet flavor.  I expected it to have a a smooth, rich flavor.  It was inedible.  What did I do wrong?

I followed the recipe exactly. I love butternut squash soup very much, but not sure I'll make this version again. If I do I will follow advice of others and maybe try using just one package of cream cheese. We found this made a lot of soup, so great for a crowd!

I did not puree all of the ingredients, I saved some of the cooked ingredients for a little texture.  I added the cream cheese at the end until it was melted in. LOVED this soup, base and have added or deleted new ingredients or spices that I love.  Make it your own be adventuresome.
