I used 4 oz cream cheese, which seemed ample and  also baked the squash.  Soup-hating husband loved the recipe.  It was even better 2 days later.
Absolutely delicious...I added an apple to the mix for a little somethin' somethin'.  Incredibly YUMMY!  Thanks for the recipe!!!

Excellent!!  This recipe was so easy to make.  The hardest part was peeling the squash, which I found easiest by using a paring knife.  The cayenne gave a nice kick.  I used half the amount of cream cheese because that is all I had at the time, but was glad because any more would have made it too rich.
Quite good, but a little spicy.  It makes a lot of soup and, as there are just two of us, I freeze half of it to enjoy later.
Good with cumin!

Wow this was wonderful :) For those concerned about using the cream cheese, just use fat free or low fat. I used just one of the Philadelphia cream cheese round 250 gram containers, 95% fat free. I did not have any apple cider but I did have apple butter and I used about a cup of that, plus half an apple. I used one butternut squash and I also did what another reviewed recommended and put olive oil, salt, pepper, and smashed garlic cloves on the squash. I baked it for an hour at 375 (I have a very old oven :). I sauteed the onion, added in water, chicken bouillon, apple butter, and spices (except for marjoram which I did not have. I added 1/2 tsp nutmeg which was nice. Also I used crushed red pepper in place of cayenne and it still gave it some nice heat). I pureed the squash and garlic cloves with the cream cheese in small batches as recommended. I then added the pureed squash and cream cheese mixture to the soup on the stove and let it simmer at low heat, stirring until it was all nice and mixed up. I won't add any salt at all next time as it was perhaps a tad too salty. And I think next time I may add apple cider or more apple for a bit more sweetness but overall it was soooo good! :)

Found the secret missing ingredient!! More on that below. This was delicious and easy! :) I followed the recommendation of many other reviewers and baked the squash first (halved and put face-down on a cookie sheet, 375 for 50 minutes), cut up an onion, and used 5 c. chicken broth instead of bouillon and water. Cut the cream cheese in half to one block.

GINGER! I added the spices as it called for, which was yummy, but a teaspoon of ginger added such a rich, delicious fullness to it that totally complemented the other flavors already present. I added a dollop of sour cream once it was in my bowl. Sooooo good! I will make this again and again.
I only use about 2 OUNCES of cream cheese. I've made this soup about 6 times in the last 3 months. Every time I make it, someone asks for the recipe.

Giving a 4 star only because I did NOT use the cream cheese and though i'm sure it's rich and delicious, I wanted to keep it lower in fat.  I did roast the squash in the oven for 30 minutes at 375 degrees and it was then easy to peel the skin and add to my pot.  I added the chicken broth, seasonings/saute'd onions and 1 cup of half and half.  It still gave it a creamy texture and it was GREAT.  thank you!

I give this 5 stars, because it was absolutely delicious and super easy to make. I also split the squash in half, scooped out the seeds, and roasted the pieces at 350 until tender (about 35 minutes since I used 2 smaller squash). Once that was finished and scooped out of the skins, it took barely any time to put the soup together. I added a little more than 1/8 tsp of cayenne, thinking it wouldn't make a huge difference and I love cayenne pepper.. but it was quite spicy. I still found it enjoyable, but next time I think I'll stick to the recipe on that one for the sake of others eating it.

I used the recipe as a rough guideline. I added 2 soft apples that would have been thrown out to the sauteing onions and used fresh oregano instead of dried marjoram (didn't have any).  I roasted 2 medium butternut squash.  I added a bit of salt at the end to taste and used about 6oz of cream cheese.  It was great.  I think this is one of those recipes you can tweak to fit the ingredients you have on hand.

I made a few changes that several people mentioned: I roasted the squash for 45 minutes on 350 before adding it to the soup, I added 1 cup of apple cider, and I used only half of the cream cheese. The result was a rich, elegant, satisfying soup that got rave reviews from our fifteen holiday guests.  The only thing I'll do different next time is to make it early, because it's gotten even better over the last three days.

This soup is awesome. I roasted the squash as per suggestions, also threw in 3/4 can of leftover pureed pumpkin. The flavors worked well together. I only had 1 pkg of cream cheese, but seemed plenty smooth and creamy for my taste after putting soup through the blender. DELISH!
This recipe is a great base. I've made it a few times now, making little changes along the way. The last batch was definitely the best. If you're interested in trying my tweaks:

This soup is absolutely delicious.  Just as good as you would expect with all the 5-star reviews.  I followed suggestions from some other cooks & added an apple to the soup, and only one 8 oz. pkg of cream cheese.  I used Neufchatel (light cream cheese) and chicken broth instead of water & boullion.  Also, I used oregano instead of marjoram because that's what I had on hand.  I started to give it only 4 stars because my husband wasn't as crazy about it as I am.  But as far as I'm concerned it's over the top good!  You must try it!
Half the cream cheese was plenty but I had so many compliments on this dish it was amazing! Very very rich but amazingly good.

I doubled the recipe because I had a large squash and wanted to use the whole thing.  I didn't double the cream cheese.  I only used the cream cheese that the original recipe called for.  This was an absolutely delicious soup.  My family loved it.

This soup is absolutely delicious.  I pretty much followed the instructions, but found it slightly bland, so I increased the marjoram to 1 tsp, and added about 1/2 tsp. of onion salt.  I also found that 1 & 1/2 pkgs. of cream cheese was enough.  A great consistency, and wonderful flavor.  Can't wait to eat dinner tonight :)

This was a huge surprize.  My husband and most of my kids don't like squash so when they heard what was for dinner I got a lot of flack.  They all loved it!  It was so amazing!  Now another wonderful way to use up my bumper crop of butternut squash that they will all eat!
Delicious! I used 1 block of cream cheese, roasted the squash(2 med-lg)and pureed in the blender.

WOW!  This was a huge hit.  Most people turned their nose up when I said butternut squash but after tasting, the group talked about it the rest of the night.  Dynomite recipe.  Very warm and cozy for those chilling evenings.  TRY THIS, YOU WILL LIKE!

I modified this recipe based on the reviews and what I had on hand. I roasted the squash. I included a potato to thicken the soup a bit as I didn't have the cream cheese. I included a bit of cream at the end (probably somewhere around 2/3 and 1 c).  Delicious!
Delicious.  I used 1/2 the cream cheese and I thought it was still a bit too rich.  Next time I'll cut the butter down some.
Really tasty. Nice texture. Simple. Will make again.

I tried this last night and have to say like many others, I did add/change it. First, I cut out half the cream cheese (I'm not sure how I could it eat with two!) 
I also did not cook it the way it said to start. I cut thick slices of the squash and baked them with a little EV olive oil and sprinkled with garlic, cinnamon and cayenne. 

I used butter and not margarine (next I won't use so much either). Then I added low sodium chicken broth (about 3 cups but I should have added more because it felt a little thick). I think it depends in the size of the squash but mine was from the garden and huge! I used it all. 

Then I realized I didn't have marjoram so I just threw in whatever sounded good. More cayenne, cinnamon, a pinch of nutmeg and ginger and black pepper. 

The only other thing that I would do is chop the onions finer or blend them with the squash. It doesn't bother me but I know my mother wouldn't like onion chunks. 

Overall, this was so good and my first attempt was a hit with the hubby!
Everyone loved this soup.. However, I did half the amount of margerine used!

I made it as requested except I substituted 3 cups of Chicken broth for the water and bullion. We enjoyed it, but I think I would double the amount of squash next time. I think it's a choice between creamy and squashy. I think adding some more squash would be a good balance. P.S. I took someone's suggestion and roasted it in the oven for 45 minutes at 375. It scooped out so easily.

This soup is so incredible! I had no idea how delicious and naturally sweet butternut squash is. I roasted squash in oven for 45 min at 345. Used chicken stock instead of water and boiled a peeled and cut up pear w stock and onions.  Cut butter significantly and used less than half cream cheese.  Could have even used less. Used 1% organic milk to thin and perfection! I'm hooked!
De Lish!!  Can't wait to serve it to my lunch guests and tell them I made it!! So easy.
Really enjoyed this a lot and it was fairly easy to make.
I only cut back in the cream cheese by 1 pkg and it was by far one of the best we've had. I liked the plain simpleness of the flavor.
I used one half of one package of cream cheesy and that was more than enough...can't imagine using the full amount.
Terrific as a first course for any meal!  Great flavor and consistency.
This was delicious!! I only used 1 brick of creanm cheese and it was plenty creamy. Also roasted the squash for 40 mins in the oven first to make it easier to cube. Tastes great the next day too

This soup was insanely rich, but still pretty good.  I only used 1 8oz. cube of cream cheese.  I think next time I will add a tiny bit (a couple tablespoons maybe) of cream cheese or may even omit it entirely.  I think the flavor was wonderful without it.
This soup is so rich and creamy it hits the spot on a cold day. I served this soup at a birthday party and received rave reviews from my guest's.

We loved this soup, and don't ordinarily love squash.  I followed the lead of some others and roasted the squash.  I used two squashes, sliced in halves.  I splashed with olive oil and coarse ground pepper and kosher salt.  Roasted cut side down for 45 minutes.  The flesh was super easy to scoop out and use.   I used vegetable buillion to make it a vegetarian soup.  I used 1/2 the amount of cream cheese to make it a bit more calorie friendly.   I didn't have cayenne, so I used about 1/2 t. hot pepper sauce.   I will surely make this again.

Yes, as others have said this soup is scrumptuous!  Like others, I modified it, but only slightly.  This is soup is so good, it would be hard to mess it up.  My modification was a) use only half the cream cheese.  I really think it would be too rich to use 16oz.  b) I added some fresh sauteed red pepper.  I think the red pepper was a delicious addition; I'll use even more red pepper next time I make it.  Incidentally, butternut squash makes terrific "pumpkin" bread, too.  Search for recipes!

I made this for friends and there were lots of moans and groans while they ate. Said it was the best butternut squash soup they ever tasted. The second time I halved the cream cheese and it was much more balanced. I haven't tried roasting the squash first but am looking forward to that.

Very good. I used chicken broth instead of water/bullion. I adjusted the serving size to fit 4 people and I also used only 1 pkg of cream cheese.  It was DELISH! I think the cayenne pepper and marjoram added great flavoring which is sometimes lacking in other soups!

I liked this recipe but I thought that it tasted better before the cream cheese and I only used 1 package. I also roasted the squash in the oven first and I processed the squash with its skin which tasted fine to me. I added a sweet potato for fun it made the recipe sweeter!
recipe is better WITHOUT the cream cheese.  I would use half of 1 package, or none at all!  I wished I hadnt put any in.

Excellent!Both my husband and I loved it.
However, I am glad I tested the soup after I added 12 oz of cream cheese. Its incredibly rich. I would suggest starting with half a rectangle (4oz) and add incrementally to make sure your soup fits your desired richness. I agree with some of the reviewers that the soup would be great even without any cream cheese, rather a dash of cream. I will definitely be making this again.
The soup was so good and my family loved it! I only used half the amount of cream cheese and I still thought it was too heavy. Next time I’m just going to use quarter the amount.

I did not care for this soup at all.  I followed the directions exactly except for using half the cream cheese, as other users had suggested.  I did not like the texture or the taste.  Won't make it again.

So easy and delicious! 

Used cream cheese substitute for a dairy allergy - Tofutti, about 4 oz - so good.

Otherwise I followed the recipe exactly.

My husband and I are always competing to see who is the best cook, well, needless to say, I won the day I made this.  He even brags about it to other people!!! I followed the receipe exactly and thought it was fine as is.

Was really good and I'll make it again.  I made a couple of minor changes:  I used chicken stock instead of bouillon cubes.  I added only 1/2 of one block of cream cheese.  I was trying to cut back on the fat but I think next time I'll add the entire block.  However, I did use real butter b/c I don't use margerine.  There goes the "lower fat" thing -  I know!   I had a bit of the grainy texture to my soup, as someone else mentioned. I used the immersion blender and think next time I'll try the blender.  Overall, I will definitely keep this as an easy, go-to butternut squash recipe.
This soup is amazing!   Simple, inexpensive to make and very yummy!  (I used one package of light cream cheese instead of the 2 that the recipe called for.)
If you love butternut squash soup.... This is so easy and so delicious. Will make it again.  It's a repeater according to my entire family

Absolutely DELISH!!! As other reviewers suggested, I halved the squash, added olive oil, salt and pepper and put the cut side down on a baking sheet and cooked at 375 for 40 minutes. I also only used one 8 ounce cream cheese. AMAZING!!!
Very rich and tasty. Has the appearance of a cheese sauce. We dipped lightly steamed broccoli in it - yum! Used half the cream cheese - both blocks would have definitely been too much!
Delicious.  Reduce the cream cheese and replace with milk.

This soup is absolutely amazing!! I didn't roast the squash like some suggest, just peeled it and cut it up. I didn't have any marjoram or cayenne so I didn't add it, but I did add some salt and parsley. I also added a cubed potato and 2 cut up carrots. I also made it once where I added a zucchini. It was very delicious and I only used about 3 tablespoons of light cream cheese- still nice and creamy (but it also tastes good without any cream cheese at all). You could probably cut up and add other vegetables too, like red peppers, and it would taste great! One tip though: you can use other varieties of squash other than butternut, but choosing one with a smooth skin, rather than grooved or bumpy skin, makes it much easier to peel. Thanks Mary!

I had butternut squash soup n an upscale restaurant this fall and I have been craving it ever since.  This recipe came really close.  I used it as a base and following the lead of other reviewers, tweaked it a bit.  I roasted the squash with olive oil and dusted it with cinnamon.  I scooped out the tender flesh after it roasted about an hour.  It smelled great baking.  While it was baking, I sautéed onion, garlic, and fresh ginger in margerne.  I added chicken broth and then added the squash.  As far as seasoning, I added 1/2 tsp of curry, 1/4 tsp of cayenne pepper and black pepper.  I then used a submersion stick blender and blended the mixture in the pot.  I then added 1/2 a block of cream cheese and blended it as well.  It was super creamy and smooth, but was missing a little something. So I added a about 1/4 cup of cheap beer and about 2 tbsp of brown sugar.  This brought it over the top!  This was great!
Oh my! Roasted the squash and used 1 tub of  light cream cheese. Soooo yummy!
I? actually used an acorn squash with this because it’s what we had on hand, but it was still delicious!

This was AWESOME, loved it. I used skim milk instead of water for a creamier texture and it probably didn't need to. The only bad thing is this is a very fattening recipe so use half the cream cheese or use low fat cream cheese. Non fat cream cheese, I just think tastes nasty but haven't tried it on this recipe. This is definitely a "comfort" food.

Excellent, smooth and creamy soup...but I had to use only half of the cream cheese that was recommended.  To make it slighly healthier, I used 1/3 less fat cream cheese and it was delicious!  I made homemade flatbread seasoned with the marjoram and cayenne to complement the flavor of the soup.
Made this as directed. Minus one small adjustment. Used only one package of cream cheese.  Made it like 5 times since 1st part of November.  Yummy!
I've made this several times and really love the cayenne pepper. I now cut the cream cheese in half and use 8 oz, not 16. Healthier and I can't tell the difference.

I decided to make this soup at the last minute for Thanksgiving. So glad I did. It was EXCELLENT in taste however, I could see as I was adding the cream cheese that it was getting to be thicker than I would prefer it  to be so I cut back about 4 ounces. Other than that, I can say it was a great choice for a holiday or any day day soup.
I reduced the cream cheese to 3 oz. and tripled the cayenne pepper. I also added a dash of orange juice.
Too creamy.  I think this could be a much lighter soup.  I would enjoy it more if it had a lighter flavor, too.  I wouldn't make it again.

Yummy!  I've made this several times and loved it each time!  I have used leeks instead of onions, and that's good, too.  I usually double the recipe but only use approx 12 oz of cream cheese (1 1/2 blocks - the doubled recipe calls for 4 blocks).   I also use chicken broth in place of the water/boullion.  Can add a little more chx broth if the cheese you add makes too thick.

This is part of my regular rotation of soups. I love the slight zip you get from the cayenne. I use only one package of cream cheese and find that's plenty to make it creamy.  I also slice & bake the squash, then scoop it out and cook with the rest of the ingredients. I get an allergic reaction to touching the squash that makes it hard to peel and slice. But baking seems to work as well without changing the flavor.

This is delicious, though I agree with others, you can easily half the cream cheese. Next time I make it I might even quarter it. Otherwise followed the recipe, and added some paprika and bits of applewood bacon to it. Mm.

The spice and thickness of this soup was really good. I didn't add any salt or pepper, and I doubled everything (2 squash, 2 carrots, 1 onion, twice the stock, twice the spices), and only used 1 package of cream cheese. I also baked the squash for 40 min at 350 after poking a few holes in them. Really yummy- would have given it 5 if already included my changes :).
I followed the suggestions of toasting the squash. & I only used 1.5 bricks if cream cheese. Very good.

The soup was very good, but I thought it was a little heavy on the cream cheese. Next time we'll only use one brick.  I used one butternut and one acorn squash and baked them first (I didn't notice they would be boiled in the recipe) and then blended them with the cream cheese and added that to the broth.  It came out incredibly creamy.
Wonderful!  The kids even liked it. I cooked the squash first then pureed with broth and it was just fine.

I used four boxes of frozen squash instead of fresh and it was delicious! I thawed the frozen squash in the microwave for four minutes, stirred and added six bouillon cubes and water and microwaved for four more minutes. Then followed recipe as directed from step two. I did add a tsp of salt. Absolutely delicious! Everyone LOVED it! Will definitely make again using frozen squash.

Ever since I had Butternut Squash Soup on Thanksgiving, I've been on a real tear to find a recipe for this rich soup.. This recipe and the reviews makes me believe that I found the right recipe.. The only real snag for me is that I've been put on doctor mandated weight loss program, and this recipe calls for cream cheese.. My solution? NOT-FAT half & half! Land of Lakes makes it, and I'm going to give it a shot.. I'll report back the results, but I anticipate, it'll be delicious!
This soup is outstanding. I've made it  a dozen times.
This has become a staple in our household. I do like to add cinnamon and sometimes a little cayenne pepper!

I've made this three times so far and it's been wonderful every time.  I've always used real butter.  I've never added the marjoram - we just don't have any.  The first two times I only used one cream cheese, but I cubed the squash as instructed. The third time I used two packages of cream cheese and baked the squash, and it was much better-tasting.  Each time I've used Better Than Bouillon instead of bouillon cubes.  I've always used my blender and the texture comes out very nice.  My nine-month-old loves it!
Also good with carrots.  One of our favorites.  No need to scrimp on the dill.

This recipe has WAY too much cream cheese.  I am surprised that so many people gave it 5 stars and then commented that they cut the cream cheese in half.  After seeing all the 5 star reviews, I made it exactly as the recipe instructed (without reading the reviews).  It would have been more helpful to me if people gave the review less stars so that people would read the explanations/suggestions before attempting the recipe.
this was great, i just tweaked it a bit and it came out perfect for me. what i did was i fried some pancetta in the pan before adding the puree back into it.
Quite simply, one of the most delicious soups I've ever had.  I cooked the squash in the microwave first, and used only 1 package of cream cheese as others suggested.  It was absolutely fantastic!!!
This was delicious and so easy!!!! I also only used half of the cream cheese, and I used real butter, of course. Could hardly stop eating it!
Amazing. I didn't have marjoram or cayenne pepper, and instead of butternut squash, I used yellow squash. I only used 1 package of cream cheese.  It was soooo yummy.
I wanted to add Apple Cider but I didn't have any.  So I added some Steven's Apple Cider mix instead.  It was fun to use my Butternut Squash from my garden.  I will probably make it again.
I used lite cream cheese and it was still good.  The soup is very thick and creamy it is a meal in itself.
make sure to follow the directions and this is great!

My wife loves this recipe, it's so easy. the only thing she did different was when she sautéed the onions in butter she added the black pepper, marjoram, cayenne pepper at that time. For more of a kick she also added a dash of white pepper.

I made this soup but with changes, I used only can milk and squash, salt and pepper because I did not want all the fat from cream cheese, it was thick and delicious and the best part, my husband loved it also!

I saved time by using dried minced onion, and just adding a Tbsp of butter to the squash at the beginning.  I didn't have marjoram, so I used nutmeg, and added a packet of stevia for sweetness.  Having said that, I loved this soup.  Perfect thing for a cold autumn night.

One of the best soups I have ever made. I have made it so many times. I keep the ingredients the same, but don't measure any of it.  I used one package of cream cheese and it came out perfect.  I even threw in a bag of frozen butternut squash one time along with the fresh and it came out tasting perfect.  Best soup ever!

This soup is easy and delicious. I did roast the butternut squash in the oven first, which tastes great. The only ingredient change I made was to reduce the cream cheese. I made it once before with two blocks of cream cheese and it was WAY to rich and creamy. I couldn't taste the squash. So, I quartered the amount of cream cheese this time (using only 4 oz or half of a block). It is perfect this way!

I followed the recipe with two modifications. I used butter instead of margarine and substitued Not Chik'n cubes for the chicken bouillon. It was excellent - I will definitely use this (slightly modified) recipe again!

Kids love it!  I used only one package of cream cheese and just a sprinkle of ground ginger in addition to the restof the spices the recipe calls for.  Only minor changes...  This is a great base recipe for your own modifications.
A very easy and elegant cream soup to serve either hot or cold

The only changes I made to the recipe were using chicken broth instead of water and I used a little more onions than they called for ( because I love onions!)...it is scrumptious!!! Definitely will remake this again! Amazing recipe!
this soup was delicious!  I did double the marjoram and added a tbsp of Jamaican curry powder. I also cut the cream cheese by half and used reduced fat version.  Definitely a make again recipe.

As the recipe stands, I thought this soup was only okay. It had a beautiful texture, and a good basic flavor, but wasn't anything special. I took other reviewers' advice and only used half the suggested amount of cream cheese. I tweaked it by adding 1 tsp. of cinnamon for depth of flavor, 1 cup of good grated parmesan, 2/3 cup sour cream, and equal amounts of milk and chicken broth to thin it down to my desired consistency. With these changes I thought it was pretty good, but will continue to play with this recipe until I get it just right.

I tasted the soup prior to adding the cream cheese.Fantastic (and low cal.). I than added only half of the requested cream cheese and I thought it was way too rich. Next time I'll just stick to a little light cream.

This recipe was had to rate. First, it's an easy soup to make, other than peeling the squash which was a pain. I sliced it into rings and the cut off the sides. I just feel, for me, the taste is way too rich and the consistency is off putting (too thick like baby food). Although I can see the appeal and it is highly rated by others, it wasn't for me.
This is delicious.
Very good recipe. It was very thick even with only one cream cheese so I ended up thinning it out with some milk. I also added 1/2 tsp cayenne pepper for a little more spice.
I made this for thanksgiving and people went crazy for it. I filled a large punch bowl with this soup and there wasnt a sip left after. Really easy to make and so worth it.

this is really fabulous! I halved the cream cheese, which was plenty. The only addition i made was a little white wine before blending the hot soup. It "lifts" the flavors a bit, i thought. Also, the 6 cups of squash turned out to be 3 pounds almost exactly after i roasted and cubed it. We will be adding this to our Thanksgiving menu.

I loved this soup, although my family didn't eat it! But that's o.k. - I've been having it for lunch woth croutons on top. I used a homemade chicken stock I had in the freezer in place of the water. Also, I only used about 1/2 brick of cream cheese. (i know the recipe called for two - I thought it had only called for one and saw other comments about using less cream cheese. I will mkae again.

I Looove this soup!!! I made it for Thanksgiving last year and it was a favorite! I have made it several times since, and now it's my favorite! It's one of those soups that you just can't foul up, turns out beautifuly every time. Sometimes you don't have enough cream cheese, or cream... no problem with this recipe. I like to change up the flavor sometimes with curry powder, roasted garlic, or cilantro. Y-U-M!!!!!

This turned out really well. I was surprised. I didn't have a blender to use at the moment nor a food processor, so I used a stand mixer. It wasn't as smooth as I would have liked but it was still delicious!

I always add 1 tsp. of garam masala (not spicy) curry and 1/2 tsp of regular (spicy) curry to the onions just in the last 2 or 3 minutes.  It's just spicy enough for me and the kids. I also occasionally throw in 10-13 cheese ravioli's, just to make it go a little further.  Def. in the heavy rotation!

I'll tell you what is missing from this recipe to give it ALL STARS... as I have been making it for over 21 years when it was published in a Kraft recipe booklet (for the cream cheese that is used).   To take this recipe over the top as originally written you puree roasted red pepper in a food processor and dollop it onto the finished soup.  Using a toothpick you can swizzle and make elegant designs with the pepper and then add chopped basil.  I also love adding thyme while the squash is simmering.  Taste as you go along.  This has been my winter Squash soup for over 20 years and you can tweak it to your liking.....but honestly, garnishing this with the pureed roasted red pepper and  chopped basil as originally written by Kraft truly makes this  eye candy, and a WOW for your friends and family

My first Butternut Squash Soup!  Turned out awesome!  I did follow the advice from another reviewer and added only 4 oz. cream cheese - 1/3 fat.  It was really thick!  Used chicken bouillon too and a dash of curry.  Didn't have marjoram either but it still tasted delicious!  Next time I will try the soup with heavy cream instead of cream cheese to make the soup thinner.  I will experiment with other spices and herbs too I think it needs a little more flavor. My 8 month old loves the soup too so it's a winner at our house!  Thanks for sharing!
It was very tasty and I also used this as a base for squash soup with maple-apple flavored chicken sausage as part of a new recipe

Absolutely delicious! I got rave reviews. The spices in the recipe are just right. It was very rich with just one package of cream cheese as others have suggested, and roasting the squash was definitely the right way to go. It's a pretty time consuming recipe, but worth every second. I also added a small dollop of sour cream and a sprinkle of paprika on the top of each bowl, for flavor and presentation. I'll be making this soup for years to come.

i roasted the butternut squash and pretty much followed the recipe, but this isn't as great as everyone has said it is...it's a bit too creamy for my liking. it's also missing something, but i can't quite put my finger on it...i added some ground ginger in it and it helped but i don't think i'll be making this again.

This is a must-have in our kitchen these days! I've tweaked the recipe and added the Italian Seasoned Philly Creme Cheese cooking creme; I've added celery to the sauteed onion step; all variations have been a huge success! Thanks for making me feel like a chef- this one impresses!

This is a yummy very creamy squash soup.    I made it to recipe except that I agree with a lot of other reviewers-  Half the cream cheese was plenty!!    It was probably still a little too rich.  I too quartered the squash and then roasted it cut sides down in the oven as other reviewers suggested.   More flavorful and easier to peel the squash.  But still a great recipe.
This is a favourite of mine. Wonderful with fresh bread. This also freezes really well.
WOW!  Very rich and delicious.  I thought it was a bit of work...but totally worth it after I tasted!

4 out of 5 only because I made modifications... I roasted for 45 minutes.  I also added into the mixture 1-8oz block of fat free cream cheese.  I grilled chicken & apple sausages and threw those in as well.  Spices used: Cinnamon, nutmeg, and curry.  Also, added baby spinach at the end for a nice contrast in color - and swirled at the top of my bowl a little maple syrup.  Oh. my this was heavenly.  Will do again, but next time will add chopped apple as well.

Great soup, Mary.  The consistency was a little thick and I would suggest adding more broth to the original mix to give it a more "soupy" consistency:  that cream cheese (only half, of course, use only 8oz) really thickens it up!
I added a little nutmeg and only 1 pkg of cream cheese and that was plenty! Very good!

Fabulous soup!  I did as others suggested and roasted the squash for about 40 minutes in a 350 degree oven.  I used about 2/3 the cream cheese called for and doubled the cayenne.  It gave it just enough kick to notice it was there.  Everyone, even the picky guys thought it was fantastic.  I will definitely be making this again.  Thanks for the great recipe!
Delicious!!! Even my son who’s 5 ate it and loved it

This was an absolutely WONDERFUL dish! I made a fan out of my oldest who hates squash normally! TYSM to teh poster for sharing this wonderful recipe! I did make a couple of minor adjustments but other than that its wonderful! First I onion used 1 package of cream cheese and I subbed the water & bouillon with 4 cups of chicken broth. Was absolutely to die for! YUMM-O!

I precooked the squash and the onion in the oven, I only used 10 ounces
of the cream cheese, and I used two cans of chicken broth instead of the 
bouillon cubes and water.  I used a 'stick blender' to puree the soup.  I think 
that this soup is great eventhough I have never had squash soup before.  
Thank you, Mary, for sharing this recipe.

I was really hesitant about making this soup but was glad I did after! Thick and great flavor. I followed the recipe exactly as far as the ingredients go but did roast the squash for 45 min on 375. I did add it all in the pot and boiled for about 10 minutes to infuse the flavors. I will make this many more times!

We love this soup.  I have shared it with many friends who also rave about it.  I made it exactly as the recipe was written and will continue to make it again and again.  It's rich so we top it with oyster crackers.....GREAT

So rich and delicious, maybe it should be outlawed!  I cut back on the cream cheese, and it was still very rich.  I wish I had followed a suggestion below and roasted the squash first for easy handling....not only is it difficult to peel, but it's like trying to chop wood.  Still, a great recipe!
I love this recipe! I added some garlic. One of my favorite fall dishes.

I made this soup and pureed everything except the cream cheese the day before.  Before serving I pureed the soup base with the cream cheese and reheated.  It was great.  For fewer calories this soup tasted great even before the cream cheese was added.  Although if you aren't watching your waistline the cream cheese really put it over the top.
This was good, but I agree it was a little too rich -- it is rich enough to be the entire meal with just a small salad on the side.

I worked with what I had and this recipe came out ammmmazing.  I roasted in 2 squash for about 45 minutes at 350 in the oven.  Meanwhile I did the onion and butter, added the squash and 4 cups of chicken stock when the squash came out of the oven (I used 1 1/2 squash).  Pureed in my little kitchen aide with the cream cheese! Awesome.  Oh, and I didn't have any marjoram and it was still fantastic!

This soup tasted great but was way too creamy and I only used half of the cream cheese called for! When I make this again I will omit the cream cheese and maybe just add a little half and half for creaminess.

I bought pre cut squash cubes which I roasted in a 400 degree over with the onion and a little bit of carrot and celery.  I used a homemade very flavorful vegetable broth.   My husband loved it.  As much as I love roasted vegetables I will not roast the vegetables next time.  I may rate it higher when I actually follow the directions.

a wonderful soup on a cool fall night. it has a wonderful sweet yet spicy taste, that go so well together. i used half of the cream cheese as did the other viewers. i used chicken broth instead of cubes, taste more authentic. i sauted some onions, celery, carrots and potatoes and added them to the mixture. i blended only half of the mixture in the blender and lightly smashed the other in the pot to give it a little something to grab on to. it turned out wonderful. i would highly recommend this soup.
I love the little kick from the cayenne pepper.

This Christmas season I made it twice.  I don't have marjoram so I used nutmeg instead.  I also added a little jot of cinnamon.  Otherwise everything according to the recipe.  This soup gave me the "need" to purchase an immersion blender and I am surely glad I did!  The recipe is really delightful!

Great soup w a few adjustments. I followed some other suggestions, baked the squash first, used less than 1/2 the cream cheese as made it too sweet and rich, added a bit of milk, 1 tsp ginger , 1/2tsp dill and about 1/4 tsp crushed red peppers.(I didn't have any cayenne pepper or marjoram)) It was delicious!
Delicious!  I used only 1/4 of the cream cheese, and added 1/8 tsp of cinnamon.

I made this with only 1 package of cream cheese as several other reviewers suggested and it was still very thick. It was very tasty and I even enjoyed it cold. However I did find it a bit time consuming to make and I think one might try adding some nutmeg or brown sugar to make it a bit sweeter.

This is a great recipe for squash soup.  I also cooked my squash in the oven for about 45 before preparing.  I also added a little extra squash than what the recipe called for.  I would recommend also that you cut the amount of cream cheese in half, one package is plenty.  This soup was a hit in my house!
Delicious and so easy to make.  I did use canned chicken broth and precut butternut squash. One brick of cream cheese was plenty.  I also added a few dashes of nutmeg.  I would make this again.

I loved it have always wanted to make . I did make some changes. Instead of boiling squash i roasted mined flavor is bolder and sweeter when roasted. I added 1/3 cup of heavy cream and added the low sodium chicken broth a little at a time until I got the consistency I wanted. This is a keeper . Thanks
Wonderful recipe.  I did add roasted red peppers and sour cream.  Delicious!  Add a tbsp of sour cream right on top of your soup to enjoy!

A really good, fall soup but we all agreed the cream cheese was a bit overwhelming.  Wish I would have read the reviews ahead of time, as I usually do, because I think I would try this soup again but cut the amount of cream cheese in 1/2.  My 11 yr. old thought chunks of chicken would be a good addition also.
This soup was very good!  I didn't have any marjoram, and I only had one package of cream cheese.  I went ahead anyway and I'm glad I did.  Very good!

I make this rich creamy soup many times each fall & winter since I found it on this website. Last year it was a very impressive first course for our Thanksgiving meal.
I have used half the amount of cream cheese, it is very rich and half the amount is fine.
Really delicious and easy. The only hard part is cutting up the hard squash, but it's worth it.
My sister took a crockpot full to a party and it was empty in no time.
A winner!
A little "oniony" for my taste, but still very good.  I also used only one package of cream cheese as many other reviewers stated and it was plenty creamy.

I read this recipe and then read of few of the reviews and made some changes.  I baked the butternut squash with olive oil, salt, pepper and crushed garlic for 1 hour @ 350 degrees.  I added 1/2 sliced apple.  I used 32 oz. of chicken broth because I knew if I didn't use the entire package for this recipe it would end up going to waste.  I blended the soup with a hand blender (easy!) I didn't have any cayenne pepper so I used extra ground pepper and a little bit of ginger.  I also left out the cream cheese because it was creamy enough and the butter (I used butter instead of margarine) added enough calories and fat.  Next time, I will try olive oil instead of butter.  It was sooo good!!!
I loved the flavor & texture of this soup.  I added some ginger & brown sugar as a personal preference.
Absolutely Fabulous!  Good to the last drop!

While I did tweak the recipe a bit, it definitely deserves all 5 stars.  I didn't have a problem peeling the squash with a potato peeler.  For spices, I used a curry masala and pepper.  I also only used one package of cream cheese.  I will definitely be making this recipe again.  It was a huge hit with my family, who, typically are not squash fans.

This came out really delicious! I added 3/4 head of cauliflower, and only 3/4 of 1 block of cream cheese. Next time I would only use about 1/2 block, it was on the rich side for me.  (I feel like 2 whole blocks would make it inedible!) I took the advice of others and roasted the squash in the oven for 45 minutes. I cooked the cauliflower in the spiced broth for about 15 minutes, then added the squash and simmered for another 10. 
Sprinkled some fresh mint leaves on top and some whole wheat naan on the side for dipping. Yummy!
I used half the amount of cream cheese as others had suggested.  This was ok, but it was a bit bland.
My favorite soup!!
just ok... bland.

I have never made butternut squash soup before, but had a squash sitting around, so I decided to give it a whirl.  I was not terribly impressed while eating it...until I looked around online and found that some people add balsamic vinegar to theirs.  So I put a dash in my bowl and a miracle occurred!

In short - balsamic vinegar will take this soup from okay to great!
such a great simple recipe for hearty, yet not heavy, fall soup. definitely a repeat

Served this as first course for Thanksgiving dinner -- everyone rated it 10 stars!  I only put 1/2 the cream cheese as per the other reviews plus shallots instead of onions and real butter (we don't use margarine) with packaged chicken stock.  It came out creamy and delicious.  Everyone was scraping their bowls to get the very last drop.  Fabulous recipe, Mary, thanks!

what a fantastic recipe!i made it for thanksgiving (canadian) as an appetizer and everyone was asking for seconds! i only used half a bar of cream cheese and also used a little spoon of sour cream when serving.it will be a family favourite.
Wonderful - thks for sharing.

At long last!  I've been looking for a great squash soup recipe and this is what I've been searching for.  As others have mentioned, definately cut back on the cream cheese.  I used a single block and still found this to be a VERY thick soup.  I will start with a half block next time and add more, as desired, while blending.  Great flavours!
I will make this again, I used chicken broth instead of water and bouillon.
I have been making this for a few years now and really like it.  I only use 1 package of cream cheese and replace the margarine with butter.  It's rich and delicious.
I made this for the first time today and it was fantastic. And very easy to make too! I'll be making it whenever I can get my hands on a good butternut squash, that's for sure.

I don't alter it a whole lot like so many other people did. It's a great soup with only half of the cream cheese as she stated though. Tips for moms of picky eaters: I will often prepare this under the guise of it being fondue and have veggies and crusty bread to dip in it and they eat it! Not real fondue, of course, but they don't know.

This recipe is the best!  I, too, only used 1 stick of cream cheese, but the soup is still so rich and flavorful.  I have made this 3 times already this fall and haven't tired of it yet!  Plus, each time I've made it I get tons of requests for the recipe and I am almost ashamed to show it to them because it is so easy yet the soup tastes so elegant.  Definite winner for anyone who likes this type of rich and hearty soup!!  You won't be disappointed!!!

This was my first attempt at making Butternut Squash Soup.  I didn't have any Marjoram so I left it out.  I also only used two VEGETABLE bullion cubes.  And instead of cream cheese I used half a pint of organic heavy whipping cream.  I also doubled the onion, subed coconut oil for the butter and added 2 cloves of garlic.  And I also added a lot more red and black pepper.

Oh yeah, and the squash only took about 5-10 minutes to cook.

I have done the butternut squash soup recipe. I used vegetable broth, A vegan brand of cream cheese, and vegan margarine, and topped it with a spoonful of vegan sour cream. delicious, an excellent recipe.

I loved this soup, but like the others, I also roasted the squash in the oven for about 40 minutes at 350 to make it sweeter.  I also added nutmeg and cut the cream cheese in half.  Oh, and based on personal taste, I cut out the cayenne pepper completely.  It's delish.  Highly recommend.

NASTY!!  The cream cheese completely ruined it.  I though it would complement the flavor, but it was just sweet soup with a horrible cream cheese tang fighting the flavor of the squash.  We flat out could not eat this.
I used chicken broth, and only 1 block of cream cheese, as suggested.  It was pretty good.
We loved this.  Made a few changes by adding potatoes, carrots & celery....still puréed it all together. One package of cream cheese worked fine for us.  Delicious & easy!
Great recipe.  I used a package of pre-cut squash, and threw a few carrots in for good measure.  I thought the soup was rich enough with just one package of cream cheese.

Very good.  Only four stars because I cannot even imagine what it would have tasted like with 2 packages of cream cheese.  I used only 4 ounces and still though it was too much.  Next time I will use less, or use none, and just garnish each bowl with a dollop of cream cheese.
Spicy and delicious.... definitely cut back on the cream cheese - great with sour dough crusty bread!
This was wonderful!! I used vegggie broth (6c) instead of water and cubes and olive oil instead of butter. I also used 8oz whipped cream cheese. This was unbelievable! :)

Amazing! I followed all instructions to a T, except I used 1/4 of the cream cheese called for, since we have family members that need to avoid fat where possible.   I also found that 2 squash made 12 cups cubed, maybe I just had large squash. It was a good thing though, because I doubled the recipe and ran out immediately!! Everyone gobbled it up and I had to send out several emails post-thanksgiving with the recipe.  P.S. - By accident, I added 1 whole tsp of cayenne pepper, and it was DELICIOUS!! For those of us who like spicy foods, of course. I don't recommend that much cayenne for the average person.  I would give this recipe a 6th star, but they won't let me.
Made this for Thanksgiving.... found it to sweet for my taste.
This was only okay and we didn't like the cream cheese texture.  It really wasn't very flavorful.  I have had much better butternut soups.
This was yummy.  Used greek yogurt instead of cream cheese and added cumin and corriander for some spice.

I used three cups of chicken stock in place of water and bouillon.  At mealtime, I found it needed seasoning and heat, so added salt and Tabasco sauce.  Next time I make it, I'll use a full teaspoon of cayenne.

This is one of the best soups I have ever made; DELICIOUS!  I cooked a med sized squash in the crock pot, and peeled it.  I cooked 1/4 of a  onion chopped and 2 chopped celery stocks in 1 T butter. I added 1 diced clove garlic at the end and then  I added 2 C water and 2 t chicken base, a couple of pinches  of cayenne, and of black pepper and added squash.  Boil for a short time, and then blend with immersion blender.  I then stirred in 4 oz of cream cheese, cooked until melted, and then used immersion blender again.  Really AMAZING!!  MY husband loved it and he does not like squash!

I follow this recipe pretty much exactly (other than roasting my squash before hand so I don't have to peel and chop it when it's hard). It is a HUGE family favourite and a big treat when I make it. I did try it recently with just 1 package of cream cheese and my husband and I couldn't tell the difference.
We like a thick soup so I followed this recipe exactly. It was delicious! Next time I might try it with steamed cauliflower added before serving.

We liked it but did make a few changes after reading reviews. I cut, seeded and microwaved the squash sprinkled with garlic powder until tender then scooped out. I made 1-1/2 batches and used only 2 bricks of cream cheese. I used slightly less cayenne pepper for our taste. I would make again.

The best!!  I substituted 1 can of coconut cream from Trader Joes in place of the second 8oz of cream cheese(low fat).  Used 1 whole large chopped onion, didn't measure. Also I had no marjoram so I used some Thyme and Basil and used low sodium chicken broth in place of the water and bouillon. Came out wonderful, creamy and perfectly sweet.  I will try this recipe with cauliflower and broccoli.
My family didnt like this soup very much.I think it was the texture and bland taste.
This soup was so creamy, yet not so rich that you couldn't finish the bowl. My husband loved it. I would make it again.
This soup is delicious! I cut the cream cheese in half like others suggested and used vegetarian bouillon. Will definitely make again!

I followed this receipe to the letter.  The soup came out delicious but was a little thick and cheesy.  I would recommend reducing the amount of cream cheese by half.  I added about a 1/4 white wine a 1/2 cup water to thin it out a little and it was perfect.
Awesome flavor!!  I also roasted the squash first.  Added minced garlic.
Made this the day after Thanksgiving & used the turkey stock I made from the bird, instead of the water and bouillon cubes. Delicious!
Good as is . . . . . but try adding some grated cucumber near the end of cook time, and snipping some fresh dill on top.  It gives it a subtle fresh flavor.

I've made this 3 times now, and this was the best versioin yet.  I use 1/2 the cream cheese called for, and I used 2 cans of broth (veggie and/or chicken depending on what I have on hand) and its fantastic.    Even my husband likes this and he hates squash.  The cream cheese and the cayenne pepper give it a good flavor!

Everyone seems to love this but I didn't care for it. I think the cream cheese may have been its downfall. I roasted the squash first for 40 minutes at 375. Had no marjoram so used poultry seasoning instead which is primarily marjoram. It smelled fabulous while cooking. I only added half the cream cheese but it was still very overpowering and the soup was way too thick and too sweet for my taste. Without the cream cheese it may have been quite good, I'd suggest pureeing and sample first before adding it.

i only used 1/3rd of the original amount of cream cheese called for in this recipe, and i still found it to be very rich. it was very flavorful, but not exactly my style. i don't think i'll be making it again.
Was better than I thought. We all ate it, but wasn't a super favorite. Was easy to make with frozen cubed squash

I toss it in a regular oven for an hour until fork tender. Peel comes right off and it's easy to cut- and then your soup is done lickety-split too. 

Like others I've kinda combined other recipes in to this one. I sautée carrot celery and onion, add (homemade but  I've used low sodium broth too) chicken stock, sweet potato or pumpkin purée (I had neither on hand this time so I baked a sweet potato along with the squash- also unpeeled and voila!). I add a few globs of cream cheese, applesauce, honey, cinnamon and for a little kick since I can't do curry I add ginger. Salt and pepper to taste. I add roasted veggies to sautéed veggies in the stock pot, simmer a bit and use my immersion blender.
I used the broth and omitted cream cheese completely .  added 1/2 cup of heavy cream.

I make this every fall.  As soon as the weather turns cold, the kids (now teens) start asking for it.  It helps a lot that Costco sells the squash peeled and cubed, ready to use!  The only change I make is to use the organic bouillon paste instead of the little dry cubes.  And sometimes, my husband sneaks in a bit more cayenne.  I've given this recipe to so many people.  Just love it!
Yum!  I used chicken stock and baked the squash at 400 for 1/2 hour to soften.  Great recipe!

This recipe is fantastic!  Very easy too.  I used two regular sized butternut squash, baked them at 425 for 35 minutes.  I also used 3 cups chicken broth and 1 package neufchatel cheese.  It all fit in my blender perfectly so I only had to puree one batch.

I HATE squash and last year our pastor's wife gave me a sample of the soup.  I did not have the heart to tell her I would not eat it because I hate squash so I took it and put it in my freezer with no plans to eat it.  Then one day, out of groceries and needing a lunch for work, I packed it.  I heated it up at lunch making faces at the soup and then tasted it.  It was SOOOOOO YUMMY!!!!  This seriously is now one of my all time favorite soups and I HATE SQUASH!!!  I only use 1 block of reduced fat cream cheese and 3 TBL of butter instead of the margarine but it turns out perfect every time!!!  Highly recommend this recipe!!!!

Delicious! I used a bit extra squash and only half the cream cheese and it was amazing! I planned on using the whole amount of cream cheese but realized it would have been too rich if I had. Can't wait to share this recipe with friends! I think next time I'll add an acorn squash or a yam for extra flavor.   (Due to other suggestions I roasted the squash for about 45 minutes at 350 degrees)
I don't think I like the cinnamon in the soup.  My husband and I like butternut squash so I will try another soup.

Yummo!  I have never had or made butternut squash anything and this was very very good. I only used about a 1/4 of the cream cheese and tiny bit more cayenne and it was delish! Even my son who doesn't like any kind of squash liked it.

It was alright, if I use this recipe again, there will be a lot of modifying.  First, I cut the cream cheese to about a 1/2 of what was state.  Also, I used vegetable soup stock instead of water, and about twice what was recommended, as the soup was way too thick.

I don't like the flavor that cream cheese gave the soup - use milk or half& half or yogurst instead - definitely cream cheese though.
Amazing and so easy to make

This is the second time I have made butternut squash soup. I must say that this version is much more appealing to be me than the cinnamon, ginger, clove, etc. version. I used neufchatel cheese instead of regular cream cheese to cut down on fat and it is still wonderful. I used 4 c. of chicken broth and the soup is a little thinner than I would like (but still delicious!) so I will cut down to 3 c. next time.
Used borth instead of cubes and used 1- 8oz. block of light cream cheese.  Stick to your ribs soup!

Absolutely wonderful! I used one Honey Crisp apple as one user suggested for a little sweetness. I also used one pkg of cream cheese as others suggested. My husband folded sauted veggies into a couple of spoonfuls of leftover soup to make a veggie omelet. It was very good. We also used the leftovers poured over a baked potato. It's all good!

Love this recipe but I did make a few changes: I made it a butternut squash/ pumpkin soup. I just split the amount of squash and pumpkin. I also shredded some fresh ginger in after putting it through the food processor. Yummy!
I am a soup guy I like anything cream based never tried a squash but after this I will be trying more of it. Big thumbs up..

I am putting 4 vs 5 stars because I slightly altered the recipe. My butternut squash was 4 cups worth so I decided to reduce the quantities accordingly. I also had to substitute oregano because I didn't have the marjoram on hand (its in the same family just a little stronger so reduced amount to 1/4 tsp). I also used reduced fat cream cheese and instead of cayenne pepper I had a smokey hot pepper meade that I thought would add good flavor instead. Then I tried it and thought it still needed something. I added some cooked broccoli florets and cubeds some baked chicken. Yep thats what it needed to make it fabulous in my book and I shall continue to do so going forward. :) -Thanks for the recipe!

Delicious soup.  I added some ground cooked sausage to help fill my teenage sons. They loved it and it went to school is thermoses.   Numerous requests by everyone to make it again.  Thank you for this great recipe
Amazing! Definitely cut the cream cheese in half otherwise it would be ridiculously too rich. Otherwise it was perfect!!
Really good.  However, I broiled the butternut squash to make it easier and for more flavor as other reviewers suggested.  I also halved the amount of cream cheese called for.
This soup is delicious!

This was incredible! I even got a family member who refuses to eat veggies to think it was "cheese soup" til he got too suspicious of me. I replaced the regular cream cheese with fat free and honestly didn't even notice! Normally you can really notice the taste. I served this as a starter at Thanksgiving dinner with my huge left over squash from holiday decor. No joke! Was fantastic!
I love it...simple, very easy to make but exceptional!

Great beginning of a recipe.  Like others I cut the cream cheese in half and this was plenty.  I also used chicken stock instead of bouillon cubes and water.  I add fresh grated garlic salt and Tony Chachere's creole seasoning.  The soup was a big hit.  For a more hearty meal you can cook some small noodles in chicken stock and butternut squash puree and add it with chicken to the soup.  My husband loved this addition. Serve with corn bread and you have a complete meal.

I can’t do anything right in my mother-in-laws eyes but she lapped up this stuff up and went for seconds.  I think it irked her that I concocted something she liked.  My wife is crazy about this soup and I’ve made it for her 3 times now.  I only use around 5 oz (little more than a half a cube) of the light cream cheese. It is naturally rich so don’t see the need to dump in a bunch of fat. I use caned chicken broth for the base.  I don’t dig it as much as my wife but she is absolutely nuts-o about it.
Yum!

I didn't like it much as a soup - way too much cream cheese. I wish I had read the reviews prior saying to only add half of it. Don't get me wrong, it was delicious to dip bread in, but as a soup I've definitely had better butternut squash soup. This was more like a cream cheese soup with butternut squash flavoring.
Have made this recipe numerous times. It's a family favorite! Our daughter even requested it when she visited recently even though it was 90 degrees outside!

Love this recipe as is and always get great compliments. Did try a different twist for the summer by omitting the marjoram, cayenne and cream cheese and adding a dollop of coconut oil and pinch of nutmeg. It was equally as good!

This is a great little starter recipe--provides the basics for how to make butternut squash soup and can be tweaked in many ways.

I baked my squash first, with cinnamon, cloves, brown sugar and a little butter before adding to the sauteed onions and spices.

I then used neufchatel cheese to cut down the fat and calories, and half as much as called for.  I used a mix of half and half and skim milk to help thin it out and find rich, but smooth consistency.

I'm looking forward to making it again this winter and playing with the proportions and spices again!

This soup is sooo good!!!  I followed advice of others by using only 1 pkg of cream cheese and it was wonderful!  Only problem was I didn't realize how filling this would be and prepared an entire meal with it!  We would have been fine with just the soup & fresh bread!  KEEPER - Thanks Mary!

I used to make a version of this when I lived in the BAsque country in Spain.  Instead of onions, I used a couple of chopped leeks, sauteed until soft, then added cubes of squash or pumpkin and the chicken stock.  Let it cook until soft, throw in ONE, not two lower fat cream cheese packages and used an immersion blender to make a smooth, rich, almost puree-like soup.

This was SO SO yummy! Like others, we did cut the cream cheese to about 7oz (Instead of 16oz) and we used 3 cups chicken broth instead of the water/cubes. I also roasted the squash first. It was absolutely delicious and will definitely make this again!

Very rich and delicious! I followed the recipe but to save on some calories I halved the butter and cream cheese. I think you could almost quarter the cream cheese and have an excellent soup... maybe even taste more of the squash. I was surprised how filling it was being a bisque, a coffee cup full filled me up more than enough.
YUM!  I did take the suggestions of adding a little more cayenne pepper and 16 oz of cream cheese!  Loved it.  I know I know what to do with all the squash in my garden!

anytime I've had butternut squash soup it always had a hint of sweetness to it which I don't really care for. This recipe is savory and for that I'm absolutely in love. Instead of marjoram are used a quarter teaspoon of dried rosemary and half a teaspoon of fresh sage. I'm definitely saving this recipe so that I can make it again and again.

This was very good.  I followed the suggestion of other reviewers, and pre-baked the squash.  After sauteeing the onions, I added the boullion cubes, seasonings, and only one cup of water to the pan, then added only one package of non-fat cream cheese, to warm.  Then, I pureed it in the food processor, and returned to the pan.  The pre-baked squash was pureed in the food processor, with the remaining 2 cups of water, then also added to the pan to warm.  Be sure not to boil the mixture after the cream cheese is added, or it will separate.  This is a lovely, rich tasting soup, with very little fat, if you reduce the butter and use fat-free cream cheese.  Yum!

What a nice comforting soup for a day when our high temperature was 10.  I did change the method while keeping the ingredients the same.  Having never worked with butternut squash before, I took some other reviewers' recommendations and roasted it first.  Then I put the squash and cooked onion with some of the broth into the blender.  I put all of the blended squash in my slow cooker and added 1/2 the cream cheese.  The cheese melted right in, and I let the soup cook on low for about 6 hours.  It was fabulous - rich and creamy and delicious.

Yum!  Yum!  Y-u-m!  Y-U-M!!!  y-U-m!  Y-U-m!!!  
In other words. . . YUM!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
Love this soup! Its a fall and winter staple in our house.

Amazing soup!  Helpful tip-if you make it too spicey (I was trying to double the recipe and added a little to much of both peppers) just add 1 teaspoon of lemon juice and it cools it right off!  Whew!
It was very good.  I didn't use as much cream cheese as called for...
Really good - I had to scale down as I didn't have enough squash so didn't have measurements down quite right.  But really creamy & good flavor.

I read the top reviews so I tried the recipe first without the cream cheese (or half n half as another reviewer suggested).  I have to admit that I liked this best without the cheese.   I liked it ok with a touch of cream, but just a tiny amount.  also, since I had it in my csa box, I substituted a leek for an onion.  I added a half of celeriac and a small fennel bulb and two peeled apples.  It was glorious.  I didn't taste the fennel since it was such a small amount.  The celeriac made it really creamy.  this soup is really filling.  I made a lot of it and it will freeze well (without the cheese or cream).  Awesome recipe.  I'm glad I tried it. 5 stars even with the changes, since I might have passed on this if it didn't get such high reviews.

I was looking for an easy recipe for squash soup. I always look at the ingredients to see if I have most of them in my cabinets.  I couldn't believe this was so easy to make.  Not only did I think is was wonderful...my husband..who by the way...does not like squash thought it was absolutely delicious!  I served it for lunch with my friends and the next time I will have to make a double bach!  Thanks to Mary for a wonderful and easy recipe.

awesome. I used a little garlic with the onion.  I baked the squash after cutting it in half and placing on a cookie sheet brushed with olive oil.  Used much less cream cheese and much less red pepper (the 1st time I made this it came out way too spicy even using 1/2 the amount of red pepper).  I blended in my Vitamix and it is sooo creamy.

This soup is easy and delicious. I've fixed it twice now and both times a big hit.  The first time we went by the recipe and it was a little too rich for us so the second time I baked the squash in the oven for 45 min at 350 degrees, used chicken broth instead of the water and boullion cubes and used only 1 pkg of cream cheese .  I have passed this recipe on to numerous people who enjoyed it just as much as we did!  Thanks!

Just finished making and eating this. Wow, there's a reason for so many amazing reviews! I followed other suggestions and only added 3 oz of cream cheese. The soup was so thick that I ended up adding some skim milk to thin it out. So incredibly delicious!!

I like texture in my soup, so I blended the squash and the cream cheese (only 8 oz) then added it to the onion mixture, then added the broth and spices.  I really enjoyed this soup, but still tasted cheese more than squash, I may use even less cream cheese next time.
great sweet soup.  changed it up: roasted the squash with olive oil, salt & pepper. Then added only 3/4 of a package of cream cheese - was extremely rich so could likely cut to 1/2.

This is my new favourite soup! It's quick and easy and makes 
an absolutely scrumptious lunch served along with Dee's Health Bread 
and Jamie's Cranberry and Spinach Salad. I only used half the cream cheese
and it was creamy and delicious. Two pkgs. of cream cheese would have
been much too fatty and rich for my liking. Great recipe!
Love this recipe. I've found the soup actually tastes richer after overnight storage in the fridge and reheating.

Have made this recipe many many times but I have only made it with cream cheese once and only 1 package not two.  I generally use about a cup a whole milk or evaporated milk in place of the cream cheese as I prefer it not to be quite so rich.   The blend of spices is very nice.  This soup has excellent flavour!

This soup is excellent! I have never even had butternut squash before, but fixed this for my elderly father who has to have all of his teeth pulled. I was surprised how tasty it is. I followed the advice of other reviewers by roasting the squash and only using one package of cream cheese. I also a whole medium sized onion. Will definitely be making this for myself in the future.

So delicious... I LOVE this in the fall!  Try it with "Downeast Maine Pumpkin Bread."  I double the recipe, use three large butternut squash, real butter and only two packages of cream cheese.  I have always roasted the squash in the oven first but it's such a pain to scoop the flesh out afterwards I'm going to try it next time boiling them as the recipe states.
love this recipe!!! I do agree with other reviews about not putting so much cream cheese. also I put some curry in it I find it just goes with the taste of this soup :)
I LOVE THIS SOUP!  It is delicious and very easy to make.

This soup is fantastic.  I deviated from the recipe a bit.  These are my changes: substitued 1/2 cup white wine for 1/2 cup of the water; added a diced celery rib when sauteing onion, and omitted the marjoram since I don't have any.  Oh, and I used 1/2 pgk of lowfat cream cheese.

I am doing this review so I can remember my recipe.  I boiled the squash, onion, and carrots in chicken broth.  I took all and did the puree.  Added garlic salt, heavy cream, nutmeg, and cayenne.  This was the best batch I have ever made.  I have tried a few times but this time was the best.  Don't use water...

DELICIOUS, DELICIOUS DELICIOUS.  You will not be disappointed with this soup.  I did use other's advice, and baked the squash in the oven, then hollowed out the pulp.  I made this recipe with one 3-lb butternut squash.  I only added 1/2 of ONE block cream cheese, and it turned out AWESOME!  I can hardly wait for my family to try this.  Thanks so much for sharing.  This is a KEEPER!
I never thought butternut squash soup could taste so good. Made ahead of time to serve with crusty bread Christmas Eve Lunch. From what I tasted off the spoon, this soup is delish!

Such a simple, yummy recipe.  I substituted about 1/2 a can of condensed milk for the cream cheese, since I didn't have any on hand.  Added a potato and doubled the cayenne as suggested by other reviews.
This is the best soup I have ever had, although I only used half the cream cheese and it was enough.

I made this soup for the family and everyone loved it. It really needs a bit more salt and we added a dash of cinnamon which gave it a kind of "harvest" taste. All in all, a great recipe for a smooth delicious cold weather soup.

I am pleasantly surprised.  I've never had butternut squash before at all, but decided to be adventurous.  This was yummy.  I roasted the squash in the oven and used about 4 oz. of cream cheese.  My kids will probably even eat it!!  :)

LOVED it - my family is watching cholesterol though, so i made a few changes: i didn't have marjoram, so we used a rosemary/garlic spice mix (the kind you can get for dipping bread in!) we used 8 oz. neufchatel cheese instead of cream cheese, and we got it to the consistency we needed (ours was rich and thick thick THICK) by adding skim milk. we topped ours off with a dollop of fat-free sour cream (so cool and creamy against the warm sweet/spicy soup) and had fresh-baked bread on the side.

My sister-in-law made butternut squash soup a few years ago for the holidays and I loved it so much I asked for the recipe.  She conveniently kept "forgetting" to give it to me so I searched on-line for recipes.  I tried a few over the years and there was always "something" missing - they all tasted good but not quite GREAT.  

She made it again last month and that time I noted the flavours.  I thought the missing ingredient was possibly some kind of cheese so when I found this recipe calling for cream cheese, I thought I'd give it a try.

BINGO, I'd found the missing ingredient!!

I basically combined my previous favourite recipe I'd found along with this one to come up with my final product.  I roasted the butternut squash; left out the marjoram (didn't have any); used only half the cream cheese; and added 1/2 head of garlic, a medium carrot and a stalk of celery for added depth of flavour.  I have to say, it turned out even better than hers!

Wow, this was definitely a keeper.  To make it easier, I split the squash and baked it ahead of time.  Also, after sauteing the onion, I just threw the rest in the crock pot and mixed it up with the hand blender.  I really liked the bite the cayenne gave it, but will use less next time because it was a bit too spicy for my little kids.  Also used a little less cream cheese than called for, but probably wouldn't do without it entirely.  The texture was still nice without, but the taste was greatly improved by adding cream cheese (of course, I think EVERYTHING is better with a little cream cheese). Really great comfort food and easy too!

I am not a big fan of creamy soups, so I cut down on the cream cheese as suggested.  I make it for one and I only use 1 ounce of cream cheese.  I've been making it with pumpkin, and it is so tasty.  I've made it 3 times in the past 2 weeks, so maybe I should rescale it again to make more!

This is the best butternut squash soup I have ever had--perfect for Thanksgiving, or any chilly Fall night!  Rich, creamy & relatively easy to make.  I roasted the squash, and actually used the meat from 1 1/2 squash in the soup.  Based on the reviews I read I used only 8 ounces of light cream cheese (neufchatel) and it was still sinful!  I also substituted chicken broth, oregano & red pepper flakes, for the bouillion, marjoram and cayenne, respectively, and it is incredible.  Impressive for guests.  Beautiful color--I garnished with finely minced red pepper and flat leaf parsley flakes, and it was gorgeous!  I'm so grateful I have leftovers!
Love this stuff! Could eat it everyday. More cream cheese or less..it is all good. Simply perfect, Thanks for sharing.

I have yet to meet someone who DOESN'T want the recipe for this!  If you don't have butternut squash, pumpkin is equally fantastic.  I agree with others- 4 oz. of cream cheese is plenty- my husband loves Philly and even he said it was too rich to use the full amount!
This is delicious!

So delicious!! I had never had a squash soup before, not being a squash lover, but i thought this was very flavorful! I used half a block of cream cheese instead of the half and half and canned pears instead of fresh and it was still very good!
Oh man.  Even my dad who doesn't like squash at all loved this.  I had to share it with friends and family.  Awesome stuff!!
So delicious! My family raved about it at Thanksgiving. I used only one package of cream cheese and a tablespoon of sugar at the end.

This is one of my favorite recipes of any type.  This soup was SO good!  I followed the recipe exactly, but I would do 2 things differently next time:  (1) As recommended by many others, I would cut the cream cheese in half; and (2) I will try roasting in the oven rather than trying to cut it first and then cook it on the stovetop from raw.
Can use less cream cheese and some heavy cream to get right consistancy
I liked the flavor, but this soup was really thick even though I only added 1 of the 2 packages of cream cheese. Probably just needs a bit more broth.

I have made this soup multiple times and it's always delicious. I speed up the process by cutting the squash in half and microwaving it for about 5 minutes to make cutting the squash much easier. Enjoy!!

This recipe is good, but I think it calls for too much cream cheese.  When I was in the final stages of prep, I was thinking, wow, I LOVE creamy things - I mean I make my morning coffee as a heavy whip misto - but I thought I'd start small with half the amount of cream cheese - and it was still very heavy.  When I make again, I think I will do with 1/4 the amount.  I have to imagine that this is a typo, because I feel like this recipe is for butternut squash flavored cream cheese.  

Other than this - the recipe is quite fantastic!  I used real butter, add some garlic and extra cayenne, and also added salt as I use homemade stock that does not have any.
This was delicious!  We loved the cream cheese.  Didn't change a thing.  Thanks for sharing!

This was so delicious! few changes however. I only put in 1/2 package of cream cheese...it really doesn't need more than that! i also added a little more onion and doubled the cayenne pepper. the only thing i would do for next time would be to buy butternut squash that is already cubed just to save time. i get home from work real late and also wanted to make a salad and bread. im a new cooker too so i was amazed how well this turned out knowing im no expert!
Can't imagine anything better.

Only use one pack of cream cheese (or none!) I added a couple of carrots and some Cajun seasoning and it tastes good but two packages of cream cheese overtakes taste-wise and consistency-wise. I added some more chicken stock at the end to try and thin it out and it worked to a small degree but I wouldn't make this recipe again without alterations.

Fall Yummies! I made this soup yesterday.  I had two good sized butternut squash.  I used another reviewer's suggestion and halved them lengthwise and roasted them cut side down on a large cookie sheet in the oven for 45 minutes at 350.  This was perfect for scooping out the pulp.  I sauteed the onion in olive oil and a little butter.  I added 3 cloves of roasted garlic to that. Another reviewer used chicken stock/broth in place of the water. I did this also and it lent a richer flavor. I used about 4 cups of broth because I had more than six cups of squash and the soup was still very thick and hearty. I used only 3 boullion cubes.  I took the advise of several other reviewers and used only one 8oz. pkg. of cream cheese and I'm glad I did this because it would have seemed more like a cheese dip with another block of cream cheese in there.  I also added a couple of dashes of curry powder and that along with the cayenne gave this soup a robust flavor.  This was perfect for a fall afternoon pre/dinner appetizer. This is being added to my recipe box for sure.
This recipe is amazing! It was my first attempt cooking butternut squash and now I want to make this every week. I did omit the cream cheese because it tasted fantastic without it.

This soup had one of the strangest tastes/consistencies we've ever eaten.   Our 1 year old ate it the best, however, she gets butternut squash baby food on a regular basis.  As a side note, neither my husband or I had ever had squash soup so I'm not sure what we were expecting.  I added cheese ravioli to give it a little texture.  This just wasn't for us.
Easy and delicious!
I used 1/2 the cream cheese and added a dozen uncooked shrimp (21-25) to the completed batch.  Simmered on low for 5 minutes and served.

I have made this recipe 3 times now and have finall figured out how I like it... I found a 2# container of cubed butternut squash at costco so that simplifies the recipe exponentially.  Because it's more squash (I found 2# = 9c. squash,) i just increase the rest of the recipe 1.5x.  I don't have dried majoram and found that I can sub with less oregano.  Also you could probably cut down the butter (who uses margarine??) so it's more calorie friendly... I don't have chicken buillon and used chicken stock instead (add in salt to taste if you do this!)  I also followed suit and cut the cream cheese and added in a little (light) sour cream!  Lastly, i only use a dash of cayenne and monitored the black pepper cuz I've found it can be overwhelmingly peppery otherwise.  For added spice, i use my best friend Tapatio to taste :)  the soup is thin, so i followed the directions on the side of the corn starch box on how to thicken my soup (though still a delicious thinner soup!)  I make this every other week since it freezes well, so i split the soup over 2weeks and freeze half of it. Super delicious!
Delicious! Will make it again, easy and great flavor.
Followed directions exactly, it was pretty thick.  I think one brick of cream cheese would have been plenty.
This was absolutely amazing!  I roasted the squash first and it pureed very easily.   Everyone LOVED it!  Thank you for this easy and delicious recipe.  It's a keeper!
Very tasty, but as written, the recipe does have too much cheese.  A little extra broth and half the cheese, as suggested, is where you should start if you're making this.

Highly recommended. I halved the amount of cream cheese and omitted the cayenne pepper. For us, I'd also reduce the amount of pepper, but I'm not a fan of black pepper. Very creamy, sort of frothy, delicious!

I actually made this for my kids since my youngest (8 mos) is transitioning from baby food to table food.  I made as directed but omitted the spices.
