They enjoyed it, but it's really heavy on the cream cheese.  I wish I had read some of the other suggestions prior to making, because this soup is very rich.  I felt full after tasting it!

This soup was absolutely delicious!  Because of previous reviewer suggestions, I used only 4 ounces of cream cheese and it was still very creamy.  I will definitely make this again and again - next time I think I will saute a little carrot and red bell pepper with the onion.  Yum!
This tasted too much like chicken stock and was quite salty.  I couldn't even taste any hint of the butternut squash.
So easy and quick to make.  I used fat-free cream cheese to cut calories and fat.  Still excellent.
This is so good!  I used 1-1/2 cups heavy cream in place of the cream cheese.  YUM,YUM!

This soup tastes great. I love the spices. However, the amount of cream cheese this recipe calls for is WAY over the top. I started adding the cheese slowly and had to stop at about 3 ounces. Even the 3 ounces I found was too much. I ended up cooking up approx another cup of squash and added 1/2 cup more water. This thinned it out enough so it wasn't so thick and rich.

I tried this recipe this weekend. I didn't change anything in the recipe except I did not have cayenne pepper so I used red crushed pepper. I brought the soup to work today & 3 other people also liked it & asked for the recipe. This is one recipe that I will continue to use over & over! Thanks Carolyn G, California.
This soup is so wonderful.  I used only 1 pkg cream cheese.  This is my second time making this great soup.  Really hits the spot on cold, windy day!

Thank you Mary!  This was the most wonderful soup I've ever made!  I used the prepared chicken broth, which cut down on preparation.  I also wanted to cut down on the fat, so I used about 3 oz of cream cheese, and 1½ cups of low fat cream. I think next time I'll even leave the cream cheese out altogether.  The flavour was outstanding and the texture was perfect.  My 2 yr old even loved it.  This will definitely be a recipe that my family will continue seeing at the dinner table in the years to come.
The cream cheese seemed out of place. I think I'd like it substituting some regular cream.

This was fabulous!  Also roasted squash and used 1/2 the cream cheese (used fat free).  Made for a vegetarian friend so omitted the chicken stuff for water, Mrs. Dash and extra spices.  Couldn't find the marjoram in my spice cabinet so used italian seasonings instead.  Used a whole onion sauted in butter and crushed a few garlic cloves too.  Added a bit of salt at the end.  I will be making this all winter!!
Excellent as written.  You don't have to like squash to love this soup!

A few added details make this recipe superb! Roasting lots of garlic before hand and then adding it to the batch to blend later. Using half the cream cheese and buying broth instead of those super salty cubes. We had this for dinner all week (our squash was huge!) To  jazz it up we used croutons and pumpkin seeds. Yummy.
Best Squash soup I have ever made

This fall soup is fantastic!  Make sure you roast the squash for at least on hour.  After the squash is roasted, let cool and scoop out into kettle.  Invest in a and held mixer--you can puree the squash right on the stove.

Yummy! Made a few alterations based on other reviewers' suggestions. Oven roasted squash first, cut in half, olive oil, garlic powder @ 350 for 50 mins. Increased chopped onion to 9 tbsp & added 3 cloves minced garlic. Used olive oil instead of margarine (healthier). My whole squash was more like 5 cups but it still worked. Used 3 cups organic vegetable broth, no chicken bullion & only 1 8oz pkg of cream cheese. WOW! So yummy!

YUM! I tweaked it a tad using oregano and basil because that's what I had and the blizzard outside didn't look too inviting for a trip to the market. I roasted the squash and roasted 7 or 8 cloves of garlic with it and added it all in. Also, I substituted chicken stock for water since I am vegetarian. I used one cream cheese, fat free and I sautéed the onions with the barest spray of oil and let them soften with low heat and their own moisture.  So very good and creamy and calorie friendly! Thanks for the recipe!

Delicious!!!  So easy to make, too!  I bought the butternut squash at Costco already peeled and cubed which made it all the more simple.  I only added 1 1/2 packages of the cream cheese and it was still great. Probably could have used just one 8 oz. package and it would have still been very good.
This is one of the best soups I've ever made.  No need to add all the cream cheese either.  I roasted the squash first, I think it gives a much deeper flavor.

Wow! Super easy, fast and oh so yummy! Better than any I've had at restaurants. Made just as recipe with exception of used butter instead of margarine, reduced fat Cream Cheese, and  added a dash more cayenne.  I used my FAVORITE kitchen tool, my immersion blender & simply pureed it in the pan I cooked it in. Will be a "regular" on my menu rotation. Thanks for submitting it!

I roasted the squash with a little salt and pepper   45 min at 350 for easier peeling, used half the cream cheese, 1/4 tsp cayenne. Added a little salt and a dash of sugar and cinnamon (I like just a hint of sweet with a little kick). So good!!!

Absolutely wonderful flavor. I only used 1/2 the cream cheese and it was excellent. I took the suggestion of microwaving the squash and don't think I will do that again. Too hot to handle and  messy. Maybe if I did it ahead and allowed it to cool before scooping out? Anyway a definite soup favorite in this house. Thank Mary.

I am sitting here on a Autumn Sunday afternoon eating this soup, and it couldn't be more perfect. I too took some suggestions from others experiences.  I only use 1/4 of 8oz pkg of cream cheese since I find any more makes it too rich.  I first roasted the squash which made prep work so much easier.  I also find the soup a little thick, so I add about 3/4 c of additional chicken stock at the end.  Just enough to thin it a bit. My favorite soup!  Hope you enjoy.
Very tasty.  I used about 1/3 of the cream cheese called for and added a carrot and a bit of sage.  Also, I roasted the vegetables with a little oil at 375 until tender.
I took it in for a dinner party and EVERYONE loved it.

On my third time making this! Very good!After making this recipe once, I cut the cream cheese down to 1/3 and let a small amont of sour cream melt in the middle of each hot bowl of soup served.This was the first butternut squash soup recipe I've tried and I feel the need to look no further for something better. Thanks!

I made this for my family and they went out of their gourds over it. However I omitted one of the cream cheeses and added about 1/2 cup of half-and-half instead. I also baked my squash halves (open-side down 350 for 1 hour)instead of peeling and saute-ing. Much easier to scoop out the cooked squash mush than to peel and dice and I think the roasted flavor adds to the richness. Definitely will make this one again!!!

You really don't need any cream cheese at all in a butternut squash soup, so unless you are trying to fatten up starving wilderness survivors, I'd leave it out!  The suggestion of apple cider or juice in another review is a good one as a fruity variation.  Personally I like it savory with prebaked squash and garlic. If you have time to make your own vegetable or chicken stock, it's a huge improvement on chicken cubes. Isn't butternut squash an absolutely wonderful rewarding vegetable to cook with?!!!
My favorite soup and I don't like soup.  My husband doesn't like butternut squash---UNTIL WE TRIED THIS RECIPE!  It's wonderful.  Thanks so much.

I substituted Thyme for Marjoram (because I had none.) I also roasted the squash as did a lot of other reviewers and only found I needed one package of cream cheese! YUMMY soup.  It was completely gone and now I'm sad I have no leftovers for tomorrows lunch.

In a word, INCRERDIBLE.  I made this the first time, with home made chicken stock (no salt, better flavour) and only one pkg cream cheese, 3x the amount of cayenne (we like a little spice).  It was to DIE for.  Used a hand blender to puree, turned out perfect, can't understand how anybody could have grainy soup, unless squash is 'old', which can happen this time of year...we found 1 pkg cream cheese was plenty with the proportion of stock listed.   The next day, was even BETTER, mellowed out, but seemed thicker-so we used (skim) milk to thin own a tad.  Next time I  made it, I doubled the stock, and added 2 pkg cream cheese.  Still outstanding!!  For me, a nice bowl of this and fresh sourdough bread is a comforting meal.  Used light cream cheese, worked out just fine.  Not to mentiuon this was SOOOOOOOOO easy!!!!! We will make this again...and again...and again....
FANTASTIC!!!! Only thing I changed was pre-baking the squash, and I only used one carton of cream cheese to cut back on the fat/calories. Soooo good.

After reading all the great reviews i was disappointed in this soup. I usually like butternut squash soup but this did come out well for me. A little too spicy which is odd become a prefer spicy food.
Fabulous!! Everyone loved it. I'm shopping now and making a lot ! I used the tweaked version. Super easy and a huge hit
Fab..1st time i have tried it & it was lovely..i didnt add any spices (only pepper) and only 1 pack of 8oz cream cheese...was really good, the family loved it..will do again very soon
Great soup! 1 pkg cream cheese is definitely enough. Everybody loved it
YUM!  Used only 4 oz of cream cheese & feel that was plenty :)  Liked it before even adding that much... plus healthier!

SO GOOD! I used this recipe for my first time ever making butternut squash soup and it was great!  At the suggestion of a friend I baked the squash in a 400 degree oven for about 45 minutes to make them easier to peel and cut. I also used chicken stock instead of water and chicken bullion. It was so good, I had 3 friends ask for the recipe!
Easy to make (I baked the squash in advance), but I used only half the cream cheese. IMO, it was still too much and I like cream cheese!

Delicious!  This soup has such a wonderful mild flavor, and it's so rich and creamy.  I made mine using about 12 oz of cream cheese rather than 16 oz, and it was just perfect.  My husband already wants to know when I am going to make it again.  Spectacular!

OMG! This was fabulous! Like something in an expensive restaurant where you wish you could have a second helping (but, alas, you can!). I used homemade chicken stock I had just made and like others I only used one package of cream cheese (couldn't bear the thought of all those calories). I also used a precut package of squash, so it was really easy. It was perfect.

Way too much cream cheese! I cut the cream cheese in half and it was still too rich for me. I could barely taste the squash anymore.

I find it frustrating that so many reviews omitted the cream cheese but then give five stars. It's not really reviewing the original recipe anymore, as the cream cheese changes it so greatly.
One brick of cream cheese, I use just chicken broth instead of water and bouillon.  YUM

DELISH!!  The only thing I did differently was to roast the squash, use oregano instead of marjoram (that's all I had), and add 1/4 of the amount of cream cheese stated.  I served this at a dinner party and everyone kept asking me where I bought the soup from!

This recipe was delicious!!!  I used half the cream cheese like other readers suggested.  I think the amount the recipe calls for would have been too much. I slow roasted the squash in the oven after brushing it with olive oil.  It smelled yummy!  Nuking it in the microwave would have been faster, but the microwave is known to zap some of the vitamins and minerals out of food, so I opted for the longer process.  I added ~ 1 1/2 tablespoons of minced garlic, 1 teaspoon of cinnamon, 1/4 teaspoon of ginger, and 1/4 teaspoon of nutmeg to give it more flavor.  It came out a little too thick for what I'd call soup, so I thinned it with lowfat milk.  It was just the bomb!  My picky family asked for seconds!

Yum LOVED this!  I added some salt (because I salt everything) and added a tiny bit more cayenne pepper.  It was amazing.  This is my first experience with butternut squash and what a good experience it was.  I also roasted my squash in a buttered casserole dish for and hour and then peeled the skin and cut into cubes the night before.  It was really quick to throw the ingredients together and heat everything through the next night.  It was really rich and I probably wouldn't serve with a heavy meal. I had mine alongside the black bean veggie burger from this site.

This is the 3rd time I'm making this and I have to double the batch because my sons friends love this. I also cut the squash in half and roast it for about a half an hour and I substitute butter as I dislike margarine. The squash is so much easier to cut and definitely more flavorful. I added a little more cayenne as well. De-Lish!!!
This wasnt seasoned enough for my family.  I added sage, white pepper, ginger and italian sausage.  Came out a winner.

I made this last Christmas for my entire family (in-laws, parents, etc.). My father, who is very traditional, did not want any but agreed to have a taste. He went back for a full bowl. My father-in-law only agreed to a bowl so he would not hurt my feelings and went back for seconds. I think I may have halved the cream cheese but otherwise followed the directions! This is wonderful.

A great fall soup and it's fun to cook something different like this.  A great way to kick off the fall season. Also feels good to introduce new vegetables to the kids and discover that they like it too!

This is a pretty good soup. As others have suggested, I roasted the squash ahead of time and cut the cream cheese in half and was pleased with the results. I also doubled the amount of cayenne pepper as some suggested. I enjoyed the final flavor but there's no doubt it was a little hot.

My 10 month old just finished pureed food & moved onto finger foods. i had a fridge full of pureed squash i needed to use. what a great recipe! i've never made a squash soup before. this was pretty tasty!
I'm not a big soup fan, but everyone loved this.  I did cut down on the cream cheese as others suggested.  The boyfriend thinks I need to make this often.  Thanks for the recipe.

This is the best soup for Thanksgiving! Love the sweetness with the spice of the cayenne.  I use chicken stock instead of the water and boullian cubes.  Instead of 2 cream cheeses, I use one plus add some fat free half and half and a bit of sherry at the end.  I also kick it up a bit with a little more cayenne.  Like to serve it in demitasse cups as an appetizer, passing it among guests.
I followed many suggestions and used half the cream cheese.  However, I think it was still a little too cheesy.  I may try it again, but with 1/4 of the cream cheese, or maybe none at all.
I could not believe how good this soup was!  I've made it 4 times now and it's always great!
Perfect with only one 8oz container of cream cheese. Two would have been too much!
Too rich with the amount of cream cheese in the recipe.
I roasted the squash & I feel it gave it a very rich flavor.  Easy to prepare. Received excellent reviews from my hearty eaters.  Fantastic  football day food.  A definite recommend!!!!

This was good.  My family liked though they thought they wouldn't.  They said it tasted like cheese soup.  I halved the recipe and it was almost too creamy, so like others, next time I would cut down the cream cheese a bit.
This was my first experience with butternut squash.  I loved this recipe. Will surely make it again and again.

This is the first time I have made butternut squash and the soup was amazing! I added one cup of organic apple juice and only used 1/2 the cream cheese.  I also baked the squash (brushed with EVOO) for 30 min in the oven to help with cook time. It was so good that even my 2 year old ate it.  I will only use 1/4 the cream cheese next time.  GREAT RECIPE!!
added cinammon and used a little less cream cheese but that's all i changed and it turned out so flavourful and delicious. the perfect soup for fall!
Just made this today.  I am a soup freak and it was absolutely awesome.  Only thing is that next time I will bake the squash to make it easier to cut.  Delicious as is.
Sensational! I added a teaspoon of raw ginger to the squash & boiled it together; it gives a "mysterious "  taste that everyone was trying to decipher...
AMAZING.
Very good flavor. I added similarly seasoned navy beans for protein and used one 8oz package of fat free cream cheese.

As suggested, I roasted my squash first and used butter instead of margarine. I also switched the broth out for stock since I think it has way more flavor and cut the cream cheese in half to avoid it being too rich.  Overall, small little changes to a FABULOUS RECIPE!  Will definitely be making this again! Thank you for sharing :)

Pathetically easy and yummy. Feel free to play a little with this recipe. Or just keep it simple. I used the already peeled and sliced squash. Once the squash was soft and squishy, I threw in half a bar of cream cheese (4oz) and about 1 C of light cream. Too rich? Maybe but it was tasty! Also, use a really good hand-held wand mixer. Works like magic!

This is a real comfprt food and hard to mess up!  I have already made it twice since finding the recipe a week ago.  It is smooh and creamy and very satisfying.  I used only one package of cream cheese because I thought I would loose the taste of the squash.  One package was more than enough.  The cayenne pepper makes it a little hot for those who don't like any heat.  (You may want to leave it out.)  For those who like heat, you will bearly notice it and want to add more.  (Like my husband.)   Personally, I thought it was just right.

Yummy soup for a cool autumn evening... and so easy!I roasted the onions and squash first,intensfied the flavor immensely. No majoram in my cupboard so added powdered ginger and thyme...and only a 1/3 of the cream cheese(low fat). I can't imagine 16 oz of cream cheese in this soup!!! Also made my own stock last month and it made the soup that much better. A GREAT soup, so rich it makes a meal with a green salad and some bread.
I did really like this soup.  I cut the cream cheese in half and it was still really thick so I added more water but overall great flavor, I have already made it twice
This recipe is to die for!!  The only suggestion I would have is to cut it with milk because it is too thick just by itself.
I've served this for a dinner party and it was a huge hit!  Rich, but absolutely delicious.

I had squash left over in the fridge and didn't know what to do with it.  I scanned the site
for a fast and easy reciepe and stumbled upon this one.  I am so glad I did, my kids loved it!
We don't really care too much for squash on its own but I can see this soup becoming a 
weekly "must-have".  I took it to work and everyone raved about it as well. THANKS!!!

Really, really wonderful soup.  I made it with half the cream cheese and without the cream cheese.  Both taste wonderful.  Very easy to make, the hardest part is peeling the squash. A lady at the market said to microwave the squash for 3 min and then peel - much easier.

I've made this soup twice now. The first time, exactly as specified. It was good, but I felt like there could've been another layer of flavor added. Tonight, I tweaked it a little and WOW! What a difference. My husband loved it so much, there wasn't any left over to freeze this time.
First of all, let me say that I halved the recipe as there are only two of us - it still comes out beautifully.
Here's what I did:
After sauteeing the onions in (real) butter, deglaze the pot with 1/2c. white wine. I substituted Herbs de Provenc for the marjoram and I roasted the squash.
The biggest difference is that I added about 2Tbl honey to the soup after it was blended. It adds a subtle sweetness that compliments the soup without making it sweet, and I grated fresh nutmeg over the top of the bowls before serving.     
What a lovely soup on a cold, rainy fall day. I will definately make this again.

My husband was very impressed with this recipe...which, in turn, impressed me! The only change we made was adding garlic. It was delicious, but a little bit goes a long way because it is so rich and flavorful. I wouldn't serve this as an entree, but rather in small bowls for a starter so you don't get burned out on it half way through your meal.

I gave it only 3 stars because the cream cheeze is a lot for this recipe and the amount of water. the first time i made it it was too creamy. the next time i used 1/2 the ingredients and a quarter of the cream cheeze, half of the water i used was homemade chicken broth. I added a sprinkle of ginger powder and a teaspoon of crushed fresh ginger. This other batch was alot better than the first one when i folowed the exact recipe.
This was absolutely best soup I've ever had in my life.  I too used only half the cream cheese and half the butter. I added garlic and oregano instead of marjoram.

This was exce llent!  and I've ruined a good butternut before!  I did bake the squash in the oven cut side up (reversed from what I tried last time) and just salt and peppered it.  I used 2 cans of chicken broth (my squash was a bit small) and only about 3 oz of cream cheese.  DELISH!
Oh my gosh.....I made this soup exactly according to directions.  It was restaurant worthy!!  Absolutely delicious.  I served it with a little Paprika and bacon bits on top.  Definitely recommend.
Loved this! It has become a household favorite. All I changed was halving the cream cheese as others suggested and because i am a vegetarian , I used vegetable broth.
Made it for Christmas dinner and it was raved about.

This is delicious - of course a couple of differences.  I did roast the squash along with an onion and a couple pieces of garlic at 375 degrees for 40 minutes as others mentioned.  I diced the roasted onion and sauteed it in the butter and then added the squash.  I used 2 squash so for spices I did 1/2 tsp white pepper and just a tiny bit less than a 1/4 tsp of cayenne and 1 tbsp brown sugar.  I used the immersion blender and added non-fat half and half.  It is SO GOOD.  Will make this again very soon.
Just wonderful!

Delicious! Along with everyone else, I agree that one block of cream cheese was plenty.  I will probably use 4 oz next time. I  used 3 c. chicken stock with an additional large bullion cube.  I think it could have used more liquid since I prefer my soup to be a little less thick.  Seasonings were just right
This is a great recipe!  My husband loves it.  I roasted the butternut squash along with a whole head of garlic and then cleaned and mashed them together.
Delicious! I've made it twice so far. Next time, I think I'll use less cream cheese and more squash. Very tasty!
Did not like. Maybe a lot less cream cheese would be better but don't want to waste my time trying. Sorry

This recipe is just delicious. I used the chicken stock and one 8 oz. cube of cream cheese and it came out creamy and GOOD! I could even use this soup for a nice sit down dinner if I wanted and it fixes up so quickly!

Delicious and super easy to make!  Only a few modifications - I used an acorn squash instead of a butternut (it's what I had on hand), and roasted it in a 350 oven - cut side down - on a baking sheet for 45 minutes.  I increased the cayenne pepper to 1/4 t. and added a dash of nutmeg.

Its a delicious soup, so fitting during the fall season...The only changes I made was adding a granny smith apple and I roasted the squash as well as the onion in the oven with garlic, salt pepper, and olive oil....very good! My husband raved about it and my 9 month old ate it all up!
I really liked it, but my wife didn't. I cut the cream cheese by 1/4 the amount, and should've done more as the soup is more squash flavored cream cheese, than squash soup.
The is wonderful!  Prepared just as written, my family thought it was the best soup I have ever made!

Absolutely awesome! The first time made it with a fresh squash from my friend's garden. The second time, used six cups of frozen butternut squash cubes (in the freezer section) and it tasted the same and took a quarter of the time! An absolute winner whether you choose the long road or the short road.

WARNING!!  THIS SOUP IS HABIT FORMING.  This recipe is incredible.  I as many, roasted the squash in the oven first.  I also used only half the cream cheese.  While I was making it, my 12 year old son kept saying, "I won't like it".  He now says it is the best thing I have ever made, after my burgers of course.  Also, don't think of this recipe as only a soup.  We have found it makes an excellent sauce also.  Use the leftovers to pour over other items.  I made omlettes the day after the soup and my wife immediately poured some soup over it.  It was quite delicious.  

I have now made it 3 weeks running.  And the family still wants more.  Use it for Eggs Benedict in place of the Hollandaise.  Delicious

Delicious soup!  But like the others, I only added 8 oz. of cream cheese and that was PLENTY.  I can't imagine what it would be like with 16 oz!  I didn't add the cayenne because I wanted my girls to eat it, so I had that on the side for hubby.  I did add something different that made it even more delicious:  I sliced and chopped fresh ginger root (about a tablespoon) and added that to the onions as they were cooking in the butter.  This added a nice taste to the squash and I highly recommend it!
Very good recipe. I will use less than 1/8 cayenne pepper next time to give it less punch.

This is the best butternut squash soup I've ever had.  A true taste of gourmet at home.  It's  creamy, velvety, comforting and all around yum!  Changes - used 3 cups of chicken stock instead of water.  Blended in our Ninja.
This soup turned out amazing! I used veggie bouillon cubes and added a little bit of brown sugar near the end, but this turned out really fabulous! Highly recommended!

Yummy!  Truly restaurant worthy.  I roasted the squash the night before, seasoned in salt, pepper and cinnamon.  This cut down on the cooking time the next day, and added a nice twist to the flavor.  I also only used half a bar of cream cheese, and it was plenty rich. Thanks for the great fall recipe!
Excellent soup! I used a hard shell squash and my friend used a Hubbard (?) squash and they both turned out great. We did cut the cream cheese down to one package. Thanks for the recipe

WOW! I changed this a little, less cream cheese, different spices, but it was so good! I added canned chicken,bacon bits and croutons to give it some substance.I thought I would taste it in advance because I wasn't sure about it and I ended up eating 2 bowls! Try it, it is sooo good!

This soup was fantastic. The only thing I varied was the cream cheese - used 1 pkg (half of the standard recipe amount). I added more black and cayenne pepper than suggested - just a matter of taste - started with the recipe amounts and just added a bit at a time until it was just right. I tasted the soup to make sure it was OK and I just couldn't stop! Everyone at our Thanksgiving table loved it - even the guys who didn't think they wanted to try it. It is pretty easy too - a bit of a pain to pour into the blender, mix, pour back into pan - but overall it's easy and quick and DELICIOUS. Enjoy!!
Excellent!
It tastes awesome but definitely not a soup. It's more of a dip.
This recipe is fantastic.  I have made it countless times this winter. The only change I made is to add chopped garlic and celery in with the onion to saute. Thanks for the keeper!
I added a can of white kidney beans for protein, served with crusty bread, even my toddler loved it!
Really liked the taste, but it was a bit too thick. Will use smaller squash next time.
First time making this and it was very easy and delicious. I went easy on the chili pepper because of my MIL and even with that, she loved it.

I made the mistake of using 2 packages of cream cheese in this recipe-- WAY TOO RICH AND THICK!  Even so, the flavor was great, so I will definitely try it again with 1 or even 1/2 a package of cream cheese.  Very, very easy.

Smooth and delicious. I had only one butternut squash and two acorn squash, but it turned out great. I also only used about 1/2 of a bar of low-fat cream cheese, which was plenty! Wonderful fall soup with a hint of spiciness from the cayenne pepper.
OMG is this Delish! I only used on package of cream cheese and it did not affect the consistency. Super easy and a great fall soup!
Yummy!
This soup was a great hit with my family! It was so tasty! My recommendation would be to forgo the bouillon cubes & water and go with the chicken broth instead.
We all loved this soup. I followed the suggestions to cut down the cheese(i only used about 3 ounces) and it was still creamy and delicious!

I would have given this 5 stars if I based it on the soup after I made the recommended changes.  It was a very tasty soup.  I roasted the squash (350 for 45 minutes), added a bit of garlic and only used 1 block of fat-free cream cheese.  So good!
Very tasty and super easy!

I've been making this for Thanksgiving for the past few years and it's wonderful.  I only use 1 cream cheese and it's perfect.  Everyone always asks "You're making the squash soup, right?".  Thanks Mary!!!
Fantastic flavor.  I wish I would have cut back on the cream cheese though because I had a hard time keeping it warm (without lumping up) while the rest of my dinner came together.

roasted 6 cups cubed squash with garlic, salt & pepper at 350 for about 20-30 min.  Sauteed onion and small apple in butter.  Added 3 cups chicken stock and 1 cupp apple juice.  simmered for do min.  Later reheated and used immersion blender.

This wasn't a total fail. First I used Neufchâtel cheese instead. It just gives it an extra layer of flavor. But 2 8oz were too many. I woul recommend 12 oz and maybe 2 butternut squash. But as far as seasoning this needed a lot more. I used cayenne and chilli powders and a roasted garlic in with the onions. 
I live the base for the soup though.
I love this soup. Good for you and tastes great. I cut the cream cheese in half and add more squash and onion. Very tasty.

I am not sure if something went horribly wrong or what, but while the taste of this soup wasn't bad, I found the texture of it to be too much.  I think this would be good as a sort of appetizer dip but I thought I'd gag when I attempted to eat a whole bowl of soup.

My wife and I found this recipe easy to follow and to prepare!  We followed the advice of other reviewers and cut the cream cheese serving down to just one 8oz package and also used the light version.  The consistency is quite thick and I think adding a bit more water to the cooking process would help (1 cup water to 1 bouillon cube which is normal).  I will definitely be making this soup again!
Fantabulous!
Really liked the flavor of this soup.  I followed directions exactly, and thought it a little too creamy.  Next time I will only do 1 block of cream cheese.

This was really good !
I also tossed the peeled and cut up butternut squash with olive oil and some garlic powder and roasted in the oven for 40 minutes. I think this process gives more flavor ! Then sauteed with onions, few fresh garlic cloves and couple slices of fresh ginger. Pureed everything together. Used only one cream cheese block. I did add more freshly grind black pepper and cayenne pepper at the end. HEARTY AND HEAVENLY !
PERFECT! This is the absolute best soup I've ever had, much less made! It's hearty, perfect for cold weather, savory, and spicy all at the same time. I love love love this recipe!

I made this twice now and my family loves it. The first time, I made it just like the recipe which was still pretty good. The second time, I changed it up. I used chicken stock instead of bouillon. I used rosemary and parsley instead of marjoram and cayenne pepper but I kept the black pepper. I caramelized the onions which added to the sweetness of the butternut squash. I also added a little bit of maple smoked bacon to add more flavor to complement the squash. My family inhaled the second batch. I had no leftovers to put into the fridge.

I pre-cooked the squash in the oven and scooped it out of the skins.  I also substituted coconut oil for the margarine, same quantity.  Lastly, I restrained the cream cheese amount to one 8 ounce brick.  (Otherwise the original recipe was closely followed.)  

The results were terrific.  (I think using 16 ounces of cream cheese would have been too rich for my taste.)

This was my first time ever making butternut squash soup. It was so easy and turned out amazing. My family loved it. I made it the night before and didn't purée it until I was ready to serve it. I softened the cream cheese in the microwave for 20 and it blended so nicely in with the purée . Definitely a repeater.

This soup was wonderful! I only used 4 ozs. of cream cheese and it was as good and as rich. I had never eaten butternut squash soup and was looking to try something new. This is great for starters. Thank you

I make this soup all the time. It's always a hit and freezes well. I like to serve it with fish or pork. I have tried this recipe as is and it was great. After a few times I started adding a roasted red pepper as well as roasting the squash. It brings out the the flavours. As far as the cream cheese, it really dose ad a great dimension but the things that are bad for us always do. The soup stands on its own without it but I think the cream cheese is worth the calories, after all it's a starter not a meal.

This is my favorite Butternut Squash Soup recipe!  Made some modifications that I picked up from reading the comments here.  The soup turned out great!  Check out my pictures here at my blog, Forever Comfy

Another amazing review for this amazing soup!  I can't believe how fast, easy and forgiving this recipe was.  I just roasted the left over squash from thanksgiving in the oven for 40 minutes, dumped it on top of sauteed onion and garlic, used oregano since I didn't have majoram handy, used a combo of 1% milk and chicken broth and let it simmer for about 20 minutes.  Added 2 oz of reduced fat cream cheese, pureed in the blender and voila!  My four year old wants to have this "every single dinner"...success!

Great, easy recipe.  I know the squash can make the soup sweet, so I added 2 cloves of garlic to the onions.  I also added a red chili for a little kick and instead of cream cheese, added half and half after I pureed the soup.  Delicious.

I made this for a pot-luck and this was the first dish to go and 5 people asked for the recipe. No one could believe it was squash! Un-chicken broth was used to make it veggie friendly. Definitely a keeper!
This soup was excellent. I only used an 8oz package of cream cheese and it was still super creamy.  I added cashews as well to give the soup texture.  I highly recommend.

I added a couple cloves of garlic and used vegetable bollion cubes instead of chicken cubes, and didn't use the cream cheese it was so savory and flavorful without it! May use a little whipping cream if it comes out too thick.

It was fast and easy using pre-cut, cubed squash from the grocery and frozen diced onion. I also added some nutmeg and a big dollop of organic applesauce for sweetness. I only used 6 oz. of cream cheese. Delicious!

This recipe is really good but my husband and I like heartier soups so I added potatoes and zucchini and it was great.  I also added a tablespoon of hot sauce.  My husband said it is way better as left overs as well.

We made this recipe after visiting our local farmers market and acquiring a nice butternut squash. Delicious!! The only changes we made were reducing the cream cheese to one 8 ounce package, and using butter and chicken stock. Thank you to the reviewer who noted that a two pound squash was the same as six cups of peeled and cubed squash. Also, our thanks to Mary -

Great fall soup! I only used one pack of cream cheese, and; it came out perfectly, still thick and very flavorful. I served with grilled basil and mozzarella sandwiches and it was a perfect Sunday lunch.

This recipe is simple, but delicious.  Having made it twice, I've found this a hearty, tasty soup.  However, the first time I made the soup, I used canned low sodium chicken stock which I found preferable to bouillon cubes and hot water.  I did increase the spices as well as add 1/2 tsp ground cloves which works nicely.

This soup is excellent. I did however added 4 cloves of finely chopped garlic with the onions. I couldn't stop eating the soup!

Thanks for sharing.
April
This was a easy and delicious soup. I served it last night at a dinner party and my guests raved about it. Served with a fall salad and monkey bread that I purchased at Trader Joes.
Really excellent, fast and simple. Practically impossible to screw up. I will never make butternut squash soup another way again.
I also added a little nutmeg.

This was really yummy. I used italian seasoning instead of marjoram. I halfed it. I used the cream cheese, which gave it a richness. (The cream cheese was frozen and I just defrosted it in the microwave on defrost). I did yucky rolls baked in bread pan and cut into slices and then buttered, seasoned with parmesan, rosmary, thyme, and light garlic salt, and broiled.

We loved it! I  I roasted the squash first along with a couple of whole garlic heads.  (Cut the squash and scooped out seeds, cut the garlic in half then brushed olive oil across tops of squash and garlic, sprinkled a bit of salt and pepper, put cut side down in a pan and baked at 350 degrees for about 45 minutes). The roasting of garlic and squash was from a different recipe. I had them roasting when I found this recipe.  I only used one 8 oz package of reduced fat cream cheese.  I added a little bit of non fat sour cream when serving and then enjoyed!  Oh so good!  Husband loved it too!
Great tasting soup.  I topped each serving with a dash of nutmeg
Excellent and creamy, but only needs 1 package of cream cheese.
So easy and yummy. Only thing I would do differently is reduce the amount of cream cheese. Maybe even down to 1 8oz. The soup is good, but you can definitely taste more of the cream cheese.

This recipe is pretty wonderful, but for me I think the proportions of cream cheese is just too much.  I only used half the amount and it was still way to creamy, and tasted so fattening!  I added 2-3 times the onions that the recipe called for and loved the results.  In conclusion, next time I may just make this soup without the blender or cream cheese.  It's delicious even without step 2. Thanks!
I made bread bowls to go with this soup and the two went together perfectly.  I loved this soup, and my husband thought it was good.  However, it was not a big hit with the kids.
I used one medium sized squash (4c) and alternated the recipe slightly to fit the difference. It was amazing!

Loved this recipe!!!! Great meal to start off the fall season. I really got a lot of information from the other reviews and followed along. I used skim milk riccota cheese instead of cream cheese..still had the full richness without the extra fat from butter and cream cheese. Will make this again!
Really good recipe.  I took the advice of others and used only 1 container of cream cheese.  I also roasted the squash in the oven.  Def. puree in blender and strain.

This was very good, but next time I will cut down a little on the butter (I use butter instead of margarine). I added minced garlic & used 1/2 & 1/2 instead of cream cheese (sour cream would probably also work).  This is a good basic recipe & one that you can easily customize to your own tastes.  I will definitely try again.

Ohhhh my goodness, this is the best soup I think I have ever eaten. I did make a couple changes but minor ones. I used fat free cream cheese and I can't believe its not butter to cut down on the fat and calorie count since I am dieting. I also added a tad more black and cayene pepper. Yummmyyy

OUTSTANDING!!  I had an excess of spaghetti squash from the garden and used that instead of butternut.  I think any winter squash would produce an excellent soup with this recipe.  The only variance from the recipe was using just 1 package of cream cheese as others suggested....and it was the reduced fat version.  It was still very creamy and very flavorful for so few ingredients.  This is better than restaurant quality!
This was too spicy for me & my family.  Next time I will omit the cayenne.  I used only 1 brick of cream cheese & that seemed to be fine for thickening the soup.

AWESOME. I substitute plain fat free yogurt instead of the cream cheese and use cooking spray instead of margarine when sauteeing onions and this is still fabulous plus it falls into the WW Core Plan if you're dieting. I love it and could eat it every day.

I have made butternut squash soup before and wanted to try another recipe. The amount of cream cheese seemed like too much so I only put in about 6 oz of cream cheese. I have to agree with other reviews that the cream cheese ruins this. It adds a tang that butternut squash can't compete with. Might have been better with just a splash of cream or half and half. It was also too thick. Cannot recommend this.

Made a few changes, added 2 carrots, 1 large or two small garnet yams and some celery. Roasted the squash, yams and carrots in the oven to carmelize. Sauted the celery with the onions. Used white instead of black pepper, added a good splash of cream sherry and used only 6 oz of fat free cream cheese. AMAZING! I also have made this using a little fat free half and half because I didn't have enough cream cheese, same results.
Delicious!

My favorite all season soup! I use a potato peeler on the squash and then cut into pieces. After browning the onions, and adding a little fresh garlic (our preference), I add the chicken bouillon broth , the squash chunks and the seasoning and cook a little before transferring to a crockpot, when the soup is cooked, I add the cream cheese, adjusting to the size of the squash soup, heat up and serve. This soup is great reheated too.
Too thick and creamy.  next time would use only 1/2 block of cream cheese and more than 2 cans of chicken stock.
Very good.  Very easy!
I think the cream cheese over powered the soup.  It was pretty rich for our tastes.

I've never made butternut squash soup before, but I took the advice of others and also cut the cream cheese down to 4 ounces, and used neufchatel instead to cut some additional fat. 

I roasted the squash -- cut in half lengthwise, sprayed the cut side with PAM and roasted it, cut side down, on a baking sheet at 375 degrees for 45 minutes. This cut the boiling time in half and I think added some great flavor. Next time, I might try adding an apple to blend with it -- this is a very forgiving recipe. Even my husband, a very picky eater who doesn't like "adventurous" foods loved this and asked for seconds!! Even better as leftovers. Definitely a keeper!

Delicious! I halved this recipe because I didn't know how well it would turn out. I took the advice of some others by roasting the squash first (1 med. size squash was plenty)and only used about 3 ozs. of cream cheese. This is a keeper for me.
This has amazing taste BUT I should have used half of the cream cheese as mentioned because this was way too rich for my taste..

This is a fantastic recipe!  Just to make it a little easier, I used one 32 oz. carton of Wolfgang Puck's chicken stock and upped the squash to 7 cups.  I increased the spices just a smidge to compensate for changing up the other ingredients. It had a wonderfully sweet flavor that I don't ever remember coming from squash I had eaten previously. I will definitely make this one of my favorite fall recipes. Thanks for sharing!
This was really good! I used chicken stock instead of bouillon and water.
I am going to make it for the weekend

I made this recipe in October 2013 at the beginning of our kitchen remodel - in order to have quick, yummy meals that could be warmed on a hotplate or microwaved.  I found a bag today in March 2014 in the back of the fridge - I reheated on the stove and it was as good as the first day I made it.
I used vegetable broth (my daughter is vegetarian) and only one pkg of cream cheese and this was a huge hit. There were no leftovers which is a shame since I wanted it again the next day. Excellent.

Yum!  I love butternut squash soup, and this was really good.  I used less cream cheese than was called for, and I think that helped.  It was rich and flavorful, with only half the cream cheese.  Will definitely make again!
Good but a little too thick for me... will add some chicken stock next time

This wasn't any more time consuming than any other homemade soup,and came out really nice. I used only one package of reduced fat cream cheese, which was plenty creamy, and veggie broth instead of chicken. I gave it five stars since both my kids, ages 5 and 14 months, loved it!
I just made this for Christmas dinner and it was a smash hit! People were literally licking their bowls. I used chicken broth instead of the boullion. Extremely easy to make and so delicious. WOW!!!!
Absolutely delicious and easy to follow-directions.  I add a bit of cinnamon to the top of mine but it's such a yummy soup for fall!

This soup is VERY creamy, pudding-like texture! I made 6 people proportion, and found that 18oz of cream cheese was a overkill. That's is the secret why this soup stands out from the rest. You put cream cheese on grass and it will taste good! 8oz ( 6 portions)is just right, won't sacrifice the taste nor the texture . 
:advice:
1. Roast two halves cut side down @ 350f for 45min
2. Add some butter in squash pan (use some of the butter ,easy for this recipe, it will all comeback into the pan)

3. Take all the juices from the squash pan, collect it with some broth, in the pot it goes

I gave it 4stars for the calorie fat. I am a sucker for healthy, looking for more thing good and healthy

I have made this soup 4 different times with slight variations each time. Amazing! Although I never have used the full amount of cream cheese, it is perfect. I have boiled and roasted the squash switched types of squash and once subbed half ricotta for center cheese. Amazing everytime and quick and easy! Only 4 stars because of crm cheese quantity.

This soup was amazing! The only reason I only gave it 4 stars was because I did make some changes. I cut two squashes in half, drizzled with olive oil and rubbed with 8 cloves of minced garlic and sprinkled with salt. Baked in the oven at 350 for 50 minutes and scooped out the squash, added the cooked onion, water, bouillon, & spices and brought to a boil. I then added the cream cheese to make it easier to blend. Once that had melted I added everything to the blender in batches. I also used only 1 1/2 packages of cream cheese but I would only add one if I made this again.
This soup is very mild and cheesy; it's a perfect lunch for a cold and windy October day!  I only used one pack of cream cheese and it was plenty.
This soup is absolutely fantastic!  I will definately be making this again and again.  I did use half the cream cheese and it was perfect!  Thanks for sharing!

This soup is DELICIOUS!  My family loved it. The cayenne pepper gives it a great zing.  It's really creamy and filling, and leftovers reheat well in the microwave. 
 
I didn't change the recipe, but I AM a shortcut taker...  I used three 12-oz boxes of frozen butternut squash--it's already cooked and pureed, so I heated it in the pot with the other ingredients until the squash wasn't frozen anymore then brought it to a boil, and eliminated the additional 20 minutes cooking time.  I tossed the cream cheese in and blended with an immersion blender right in the cooking pot so I didn't have to transfer the soup back and forth.  

The flavor is wonderful. Just for variety I'm going to add cilantro and curry next time as it seems it would make a good Indian-style soup as well.  I'm sure there are many possible variations, but try this soup as-is first!

This soup was the hit of our Thanksgiving dinner! Roasting the squash was the best tip - careful not to burn it like I did, though - and only half the amount of cream cheese was needed. Next time I will cut out the cayenne and serve hot sauce on the side. Delicious.
Great soup!!! Halved the cream cheese, otherwise no changes.

This soup is amazing. I made it exactly to the recipe, but added a bit more cayenne pepper. I was concerned that the pound of cream cheese would be too much, but after I let it set overnight, it was fabulous. This will become a fall and winter staple! Thanks again all recipes!
I have a tendancy to stay away from bullion so I use organic free range chicken broth, 3 cups and use a packet of Crocks Spicy Soup mix and remove the onions prior to puree. No cream cheese needed.
My guests asked to take some home!

Delicious! I was hesitant, since being in the fall season I was on pumpkin/squash overload. But the cream cheese made it! I only had one package of cream cheese and it made it very rich and creamy. Perfect! It did change the taste a little bit, but in a good way (I was tired of the squash taste) I used only one squash and it made enough for 4 people with leftovers. Served with these little turkey meatloaf stacks from Trader Joes. I would make this again

This was excellent!  I added about a 1/2 teaspoon of nutmeg and left out the cayenne pepper.  My whole family loved it (including my 2-year-old).  Very easy.  You can roast the squash in the oven first or cut into smaller pieces and put it in the microwave for about 5 minutes to make it easier to peel and cube.

My whole house is in love with this soup. For a rich treat - every now and then - I leave the portion of cream cheese as is. I always add extra onion - lots of it - it helps give a boost of flavor. I always also add an extra cube of the chicken bouillon and add a little extra cayenne to give it some kick. Everyone I've made this for loves it - even friends who don't eat veggies! This is a keeper, I've also told lots of friends about it.

I made this with blue Hubbard squash....OHHHHH  it was delicious.   I used butter instead of margarine and chicken broth instead of bouillon cubes and water.   It was so wonderful!   I licked the bowl!!!  I added nutmeg and cinnamon and a bay leaf.   Wonderful!
Excellent soup very savory and thick. Will definitely make this again.

Butternut squash soup is so versatile it's hard to mess up, but here are my suggestions after many, many times using this recipe. Halve and roast the squash with the 1/2 onion (quartered), 1 carrot (1/2 inch slides), 1 apple (peeled/cored/quartered) and 2 garlic cloves for 45 min. Use chicken broth (reduced sodium) instead of water/bouillon, cut cream cheese to about 4 oz. Add a few pinches each of ground curry and ground ginger with the chicken broth. Stir in 1/2 c.  half and half or milk just before serving.
I use a hand blender to blend everything in the pot. Easy, delicious, and comforting!

I followed previous reviewers advice and 1) roasted the squash cubes first (with olive oil, s&p) and 2) used less cream cheese (4oz instead of 16oz).  Soup was slightly sweet with a strange consistency - it reminded me of liquid sweet potato pie.

OMG, this is SO GOOD!  Like many others, I roasted the squash first - the day before I made it - then peeled and cut the squash up when cooled and kept in the fridge overnight. When I came home from work the next day, it was short work to throw everything together for dinner.  I also used one pkg of cream cheese, and my own chicken stock instead of water/bouillon - otherwise no changes.  Yum, yum!
I did roast my squash in the oven first. 375, with garlic oil salt/pepper one hour.  Followed the rest of directions except used 1.5x the red pepper.  I think it has a great taste.

I didn't have any of the seasonings so I used Curry and pepper only. I also did what others suggested by baking my squash in the oven first then putting it in the blender. I only used 4oz. of weight watchers cream cheese. This soup was so good. I at the leftovers the next day. I also served it with garlic bread. My husband said I did a fantastic job for my first soup!
GREAT! A really delicious soup. Easy to make and tasty to the last spoonful. This will be made again and often.

This recipe was VERY good...however, I would give it 5 stars with the following revisions. I like my soup a little more on the sweet side. I added 1 Tbsp. of Nutmeg, a dash of ginger and about 1/2 cup of Apple Cidar. I also added about 1/4 cup of brown sugar. OMGoodness!!

I prepared this as a "soup de jour" for Thanksgiving, so I made it the day before and let the flavors "merry" together in the fridge overnight and warmed the next day!! Holy Cow this was awesome! My family gave rave reviews over this one!

I also only added 1 pkg. cream cheese and I roasted my butternut squash in the oven for approximately 50 minutes on 450.

If you want a really good, rustic, fall recipe...try this one! You won't regret it!!

I wish I could give this 4.5 stars - even people who started out with, "Ewwww" liked the soup. Following other suggestions, I roasted the squash first and did only use 1 block of cream cheese. We like food spicy so I added some cajun seasonings and other personal spices to add some kick. My immersion blender worked great to blend everything. Thanks for the recipe!

I followed the recipe to the T and all I could taste was the cream cheese.  I prefer to taste the butternut squash in my soup.  If I make this soup again I would definitely cut down on the cream cheese.
This was delicious with a loaf of crusty bread. I used chicken stock and one package of cream cheese and it was perfect. Will definately make again.
I tried this and was really disappointed. I'm not quite sure if it was because I've never tried butternut squash before but I did not like it. It had an odd flavor to me.
I think it needed more spices and less cream cheese.

This is my go-to butternut squash soup!  Sometimes I use sour cream instead of cream cheese and it's just as good but with fewer calories.  I've also served with pumpkin seeds which gave it a wonderful crunchy texture.  Lately I've only been blending just a few scoops of the squash so there are still delightful chunks of squash left to chew on.  I've also made it with a potato added it and that was a nice addition.
This was absolutly delicious. But for sure, only add one block of cream cheese or even half of a block. Other than that, it was amazing. My mother in-law even approved. Yummy!!!

This soup was excellent.  I modified it a little since I only had frozen squash and cut the recipe in half and used 4 T. cream instead of cream cheese and substituted marjoram for a 1/4 t. pumpkin pie spice. Very quick, no pureeing needed.
I made this exactly as directed (except for subbing veggie stock). The flavor was good but the consistency was a little goopy. If I were to make it again, I would do half cream cheese and half milk.

I was skeptical of a soup that used bouillon instead of broth, but this was delicious.  I used butter instead of margarine and only 4oz. of cream cheese, and my husband and  2 and 4 year olds loved it.

I thought this recipe was great! Perfect with homemade bread on a chilly fall night. I did take some suggestions from other users and omitted the cream cheese, used only 2 tablespoons of butter (not margarine), used chicken broth instead of bouillon cubes, added a dash of nutmeg, a cup of apple cider, and one granny smith apple. I also roasted the squash in the oven first, with EVOO, salt and pepper, and garlic cloves. My husband and daughter thought it was a tad too thick - but they tend to be picky eaters. Regardless, it was enjoyable :)

I made this exact recipe the first time and felt it was too cheesy so the next time I halved the cheese and it was much better.  My favorite was when I made the soup without cream cheese and put a dollop of sour cream on top of each serving.  Looks pretty and tastes great.

This recipe was not bad, but it's probably not my most favorite soup. I added everything that was already stated except the marjoram and cayenne pepper simply because I didn't have it. I used just regular pepper instead. I also didn't use cream cheese and instead using corn starch to thicken the soup. I also used a mixture of papaya and squash instead of just squash because I was short. I also added just a bit of heavy cream. Overall the soup wasn't bad!

I recently had my wisdom teeth pulled, so I have been limited to a liquid only diet. I saw this recipe and went for it. I halved the recipe for less servings, but it still turned out well. My dad loves it.  Looks like I will be making this soup again.

Great recipe, very rich and creamy. My husband loves the little kick the spices give it. To cook my butternut squash, I cut it in half lengthwise, turn the halves face-down in a glass baking dish, fill the dish with about an inch of water, and bake in the oven at 375 for about 40 minutes. After it cools a little, you can just scoop the butternut squash out.
I made this soup last weekend, and it was wonderful and very easy.  Also,even one of my teenagers liked it.
Good with 1/4 of the cream cheese, better with 4 oz fresh goat cheese.  This is a very rich soup, a little too rich for a main course in my family.  Serve with crusty bread and greens.

Absolutely the best...easy to make and tastes wonderful........I'm making it again tonight....we love it.............I also baked the squash beforehand and only used 8 oz of cream cheese..it's very yummy...............

Love this soup. Added a pear this time and used 1/4 the cream cheese. 
It's amazing.
Excellent but thick. Cut cream cheese in half at least.

DELICIOUS!  I make this all the time!  It really is so delicious!  If I have the cream cheese, I put it in, but if I don't, I use milk when I blend it.  I also roast the squash with some garlic and olive oil instead of boiling it with the broth.  Depending on who is eating it, I sometimes throw in more cayenne pepper (kids don't like it too spicy) and I eat it with whole grain crackers.  I LOVE this recipe!  Bravo to the creator!

I followed the advice of one reviewer who shared she cut the butternut squash in half and microwaved the the squash for 5 minutes. It was easy to peel and cooked somewhat. It saved some time also. My family really enjoyed this. I followed the recipe as written otherwise.

I have made this dish using all sorts of squash but butternut and pepper are the best!  I half the squash first, drizzle each with olive oil and rub coarse salt, freshly ground black pepper and minced garlic over each half.  Then I wrap each one in aluminum foil and bake at 350 for 30- 40 minutes (depending on size of squash).  I also half the amount of cream cheese.  Great for autumn picnics.  Loved by all!
Awesome

My neighbor gifted me a butternut squash that was close to 2 1/2 lbs, so I decided to give this a try.  I halved, de-seeded and roasted the squash at 350 for about 40 minutes.  After roasting I could easily scoop the flesh out into the soup pot.  I added 3 1/2 cups of chicken broth rather than the bouillon/water, along with the remaining ingredients and simmered for 20 minutes to meld the flavors.  I pureed the soup with my emersion blender right in the pot.  After tasting the soup I decided to skip the cream cheese altogether.  I thought it tasted great without it.
Has a nice kick with cheyenne spice and pepper.
Easy and flavorful...made as written.
Added a bit of fresh ground sage .... loved it!!!
Warm, creamy, and tasty with a little kick. I used half the cream cheese and served it as a side to broiled garlic chicken, along with some crusty loaf. Delicious!

This is the creamiest, richest, most delicious and flavorful soup ever.  What made this extra nice to make was the peeled and cubed squash that was available at Costco during Thanksgiving and Christmas.  Not only did that save money and time, I'm pretty sure it saved a few of my fingertips and the launching of numerous obscenities.
I did bake the squash for a little while to make it easier to cut.
I used less cream cheese to cut the richness a little.  Otherwise a very good soup.
It was easy, quick and amazing.  Very delicious. Followed recipe except used butter vs margarine.  Took one butternut squash to get the 6 cups and used 1/3 cup for the onions.
Delicious!  One package of cream cheese was great.

Overall very good soup, but I did make some adjustments.  First, I roasted my squash is the oven brushing it lightly with olive oil and the sprinkling it with salt and pepper.  I only used one half of one cream cheese block, 4oz I guess.  It was still very rich and creamy.  I can't imagine liking it if I used the orignal two cream cheese blocks that the recipe calls for.  Sometimes less is more.  Also, I used chicken broth and omitted the bouillion.  I loved the kick the cayanne pepper lends to this soup.  Delicious.
Even without the cream cheese, this soup came out fantastic!

This soup is SOOOOO good.  I have been making it for years and am finally leaving a review.  The only thing I would add that makes it so rick and yummy is that I roast the butternut squash....I cut it in half. drizzle my pan with olive oil and roast at 400ish until I can easily poke a fork into the butternut.  I let it cool then just scoop out the squash into my pot.  It adds a whole new dimension to the soup!

This soup was awesome. I followed others advice and baked the squash in the oven. It is much easier that way. I also increased the cayenne pepper a little. Cayenne pepper is very potent so be careful not to add too much at a time. All of my family loved this soup, for 5 kids and one husband I'd say that deserves 5 stars!

Wow, this soup was AMAZING. We roasted the squash first (cut in half, open side down on a cookie sheet, 45 min at 375), only used half the cream cheese, real butter, and also added some asparagus that needed to be used. It was a beautiful color and perfect consistency.
Fantastic as written but also excellent with half the cream cheese. As a variation, I make mine with shallots instead of onions.
Will make this soup again.
This soup was awesome!!! I too halfed the cream cheese and rosted the squash in the oven for about and hour. Delish!!!!

OMG!!! Delicous!!! I've never made a squash soup before and the hubby HATES squash. I made this for the family and the ATE IT UP! This was absolutly amazing. I did however add a little more bouillon to take away some of the sweet taste and only used 1 package of reduced fate cream cheese..... I WILL MAKE THIS OVER AND OVER AGAIN!

Good soup but came out too sweet for my taste.  I added 1 granny smith apple to onion saute and 1/2 cup apple juice as one reader suggested.  Could have been why it tasted so sweet!  Definitely recommend oven roasting the squash, it really brings out the flavor.

Like many people suggested, I did tweek the recipe .  I halved the squash ( used one squash) rubbed it with olive oil salt and pepper then baked face down 350 for 1hr not covered. After I removed the skin cubed it and placed it in the pot with real chicken broth mixture ( softened onions and celery). I halved the amount of regular cream cheese and added a pinch more of cayenne. Used my immersion blender  and voila. Served it last night for thanksgiving dinner at friends,,,everyone loved it! I served it with herb buns ,,,,sooooo goooood!

I used 1/3 amount of cream cheese and added some almond milk instead. This made it a bit more watery than probably intended but was necessary to bring down some of the heat of the pepper and cayenne that was probably relying on the extra cream cheese to neutralize it. Delicious!

I accidently added more cayanne pepper (my shaker broke as I was using it), but decided to take it to a dinner party anyway.  The extra spice was a welcomed surprised and everyone asked what ingredient gave the soup that extra kick.  The only person who went home with an empty dish was me!

I absolutely love this dish. the first time I made it, t was with zucchini squash because it was thanksgiving and they were out of butternut. Both ways are absolutely wonderful. I garnished with bacon and parmesan cheese. THANKS!

My husband and I don't particularly like squash or soup but oh my, this was delicious.  This recipe is one of the best I've tried from this site.  I used kabocha squash, which has a milder flavor than butternut and is supposed to be excellent for soup.  I roasted the squash before finding this recipe so I didn't follow the recipe exactly.  I added the frozen pureed squash and let it simmer until it thawed.  I whipped the cream cheese on its own and then whisked it into the soup.  I also used veggie bullion to make it vegetarian.
I tried with only 8 oz cream cheese and it was great!  Might try to see with 2 pkgs.  Great recipe!!

Maybe using butternut squash is the key. I used an heirloom squash, crookneck, and it was very bland, so I used a suggestion from another squash recipe and added alspice, nutmeg and ginger. It needed a lot of salt too. It helped a lot. I liked it fine, but my husband who is not fond of squash, didn't care for it and he is not a picky eater.
This soup was very good. I only used 1 pkg of cr cheese and it was very creamy. Can't imagine what 2 pkgs would have done. Will make again!!

Good. Half the cream cheese...
Roast butternut in oven..
perfect as is - have made this for years - good recipe
The perfect recipe: fast, easy, delicious!  I have several friends who claim to hate squash, but love this soup.  Yellow squash can also be substituted.

I love the soup! I am down to making it without measuring anything. Blend everything then add the cream cheese on high for about 30 mins. I personally believe that it is better slow cooked. I have also make it with an apple cinnamon version. I boil 1 apple and a cinnamon stick with the broth from the soup for about 30 mins, blend and then add. Gives it a totally different experience! Sometimes I add cooked ground sausage and peppers in the middle to again add a different taste and it actually goes well with the soup! Women tend to love this soup, men not as much :/
Great recipe, flavorful and thickened up as it sat.

Everyone raves about this soup.  I only use 1/2 of one package of cream cheese, otherwise its way too rich for my taste.  The other secret is to DEFINITELY roast the lightly oiled squash (cut in half) placed over some garlic cloves until soft.  Your house will smell like heaven and it makes it makes it taste so much better.  This is a new family recipe that will be at every Thanksgiving from now on.

This is super good. I did up the cayenne pepper a bit and added some nutmeg and cinnamon. And as recommended by others only used half the cream cheese. I also tried to just use the hand mixer to blend it, it was too clumpy or grainy so I did put it in the blender for about 5 minutes.  My husband loved it!!
Absolutely fabulous!  Very rich without the second package of cream cheese.  Easy!

I love this.... though, I only use 8 ounces of FAT FREE cream cheese.  It is also great with sweet potatoes, instead of the squash.  I've made it with and without the cayenne.  I like it both ways, but be sure to use the marjoram, that flavor really so good with the mellowness of the squash.
Wow, this was the best butternut squash soup I've ever made. Rich and delicious. Definitely adding it to the rotation.
FANTABULOUS!!!   A little spicy, I will put in a little less cayenne, but easy to make and delicious!!

Think it's great! I used chicken stock instead of water + bouillon cubes and halved the cream cheese. I think I added too much cayenne, but still yummy with the extra heat. The soup thickens quickly once it sets.
I hate butternut squash, so I didn't care for this, but my family LOVED it. So if you like squash this is for you, but it's very squash-y tasting.
First time ever eating butternut squash, and loved this. I did use half the cream cheese, added steamed mushrooms after and garnished with dill for a little extra sum'n. Very nice :)
the only thing i added.. is one cut up peeled, cored granny smith apple... very good... and 1/2 cream cheese and a tablesp. sour cream.. 1 t. cinnamon  1/4 teas nutmeg

guess im going to have to agree with the other satisfied customers, this soup is great! fast and easy added garlic and lessend the amt of cream cheese. but next time i think i will use 8oz and a half of cream cheese, my mom loved it also...

Great way to use up excess squash, but it was a little bland IMO.  Once it was finished I added garlic powder and a bit more cayenne, which I think helped.  I would try this again with maybe some extra seasoning/spice.  I did half the amount of cream cheese, I think it would have been the dominant flavor had I not
I love this! But I only used 1 package of cream cheese and it is already creamy with just 1 package.

This is an incredibly rich tasting soup.  Wonderful, interesting flavour with the cream cheese.  I only used 1/2 of an 8 oz. block of cream cheese and will try 1/4 or 1/3 next time as I still found it too rich for me.  I also cut the 
butternut squash in half lengthwise and roasted it at 375 F for 45 min. so that I wouldn't have to go through the trouble of peeling and chopping raw butternut squash.

I followed some of the other recommendations and roasted the squash first - makes it much easier.  I used half and half in place of cream cheese.  Making another batch of it today and I am going to try creme fraiche instead.  My daughter loved the soup the first time I made it and is looking forward to having it today on Thanksgiving.

This was VERY good!! I only used 1 package of the cream cheese and I did add about a cup of some mashed potatoes that I had left over in the fridge.  I used a hand held blender and it was so flavorful.  Great to have on hand during Lent for Friday lunch.  Thanks!

Delicious.  I did bake the squash in the oven and I had to use a little Oregeno instead of Marjoram (I was out).  My suggestion is to use a stick blender (they are totally worth it) to blend everything together.  That way you don't have to pour hot soup into or out of anything other than your bowl.

Delicious!!  The only thing I did differently was to add a half cup of cilantro to the onions and squash as it was cooking and eliminate the cayenne because I didn't have any.  My entire family ate it and that is saying something.  My husband, who hates soup, turned the pot upside down to scrape the last of it into his bowl.  Definitely making again.

Delicious soup! My husband dislikes squash of any kinds prepared any way. When he asked what I was making, I stated "Soup...would you like to try?" He took a small spoonful and said "That is really good." I did not change the recipe other than using only one 8oz cream cheese.

Ahmazing.  I've never done a squash soup before, and don't have a food processor, so I was a bit worried.  I shouldn't have been, a blender works fine.  This recipe was super easy!  I added some garlic with the onions, used coriander because I didn't have any marjoram and doubled the black pepper, so it definitely has a kick.  I also used less than 4 ounces of cream cheese and it's plenty creamy!    I try to only eat meat a couple of times a week, so this will quickly become one of my filling winter staples!
My family of 5 loved this.  I made it with butter and only 8 oz of cream cheese and it was perfect.

So disappointed with this soup after reading all the reviews.  I followed the advise of others and cut down to 1 package of cream cheese.  It tastes like butternut squash flavored cream cheese.  All I could taste is cream cheese.  If you're not a big fan of cheese, this is definitely not the soup for you.  I've had much better butternut squash soup elsewhere.

I just made this to go with a fall fish fry and it was a hit. I only used 1 pkg of cream cheese and added 1 cup of heavy whipping cream.  I also used about 3 cups of broth and some water and one whole onion, roasted all the onion and squash as suggested in other reviews.  I added chives and a little extra cream to top it off.
My wife absolutely loved this soup during the final trimester of her pregnancy last winter - can't wait to start making it again when all the squash start coming in.

This recipe was great! I ended up only adding one package of cream cheese instead of two and it was still quite good. The soup was still delicious days later as well! I will definitely make this recipe again.
used 1 1/2 bars of cream cheese.. would use only 1 next time (very rich)..... made it extra spicy for the adults... omitted cayenne and the kids loved it!!
Really yummy and quick to do! I like spicy, but I might have out too much cayenne in cuz it seems to have a bit of kick, but tasty!
Awesome. That is all there is to it!!!

At the advice of the other reviewers, I used 1/2 the cream cheese (and even used low fat) and it was WAY too rich.  I guess it's a preference, but for those of you looking for a fresh, lighter soup... this is definitely not the right recipe.
This soup was amazing! You could definitely use less cream cheese to make it a little healthier, but this will definitely be on rotation at our house!

So delicious it almost tastes like a dessert. And it is really filling. All I had was a bowl of salad and a bowl of soup and I was completely satisfied, and I'm training for a marathon so I'm always really hungry!

I tried to make this recipe exactly as it is, except that I did roast the squash ahead of time because it was a beast just to cut in half, and I scaled down some of the measurements because I was just going to use half of a squash.

I brushed on olive oil and rosemary on the faces of the cut-in-half squash, baked them face-down for 1 hour on 375, then scooped out the seeds, peeled them with a potato peeler, and cubed. Meanwhile, I was leaving the cream cheese out to soften. By this point the squash was already really mushy, but I went ahead and boiled it with the onions and other spices. Since the squash had already baked an hour in the oven, it was still really hot, so after I pureed everything in the blender, I just put it in bowls and served. My mother-in-law wanted her bowl heated, but she's the kind who likes things to be scalding. I ate a salad first and my soup was still a good temperature when I moved on to it.

For timing, I put the squash in the oven at 4:15, took out at 5:15, and let them cool, then started peeling at 5:30, did everything else and was ready to serve it by just a little after 6.

This was my first time cooking with butternut squash.  This was a good beginning.  I read many reviews before making it.  I roasted my squash in the oven, salted with olive oil.  I sauteed my onions in part butter and part coconut oil. Like many I only used one package of cream cheese.  I put in two 32 oz cartons of chicken broth.  Maybe that' why mine didn't come out too thick.  It probably could have been a little thicker.  So next time I'll use slightly less chicken broth, but definitely more than the 5 cups of broth that I was going to use per one reviewer's suggestion. I didn't have marjoram. So I used oregano and thyme as one reviewer did.  I used one-fourth teaspoon of cayenne instead of the one-eighth called for and it wasn't too spicy.  I will definitely make this again.

Soup came out delicious. I would've rated it 5 stars, but even though I only used 6 ounces of cream cheese, it was a little too much. Could be I didn't use 6 cups of butternut squash. Would help if recipe told you how many butternut squashes it takes to make 6 cups. Anyway, it was pretty easy. The toughest part was cutting up the butternut squash. I may go with the precut stuff next time instead.

This was not good at all. The flavor of the cream cheese, which I had cut down to just one block, was entirely too overwhelming.  It had a sickly sweet aftertaste. I will attempt to make this again without the cream cheese and without butter (I had used some butter to saute the onions).

The absolutely best soup my family and I have ever had!!!  We had friends for dinner, and I sent home, reluctantly, the bottom of the pot of soup with them.  Will make it time and again.  I also used half the cream cheese (lite).  As far as peeling the squash, I found peeled and cubed squash at the local grocery store and (although a little more expensive), used it instead!
Far too creamy with the listed amount of cream cheese.  Cut down by at least half.
Served this at a party and everyone loved it, even the people who claimed to "hate" squash.  I agree with only using half the cream cheese.
ummm weird soup

Love this soup we had it as an appetizer for our Christmas dinner and it was my favourite part of the meal.  We choose to use one package of cream cheese and it worked out perfectly. I am however intrigued at how deliciously rich the soup could taste with two packs.  Either our a dish to remember!!
Unbelievably sample and delicious!  Only used  8oz cream cheese and it was wonderful--cant imagine how rich 16 oz would be!

Great tasting recipe! Since I'm vegan I used vegetable broth instead of chicken bouillon. I left out the onion and used Italian seasoning (so I wouldn't have to buy the marjoram). I blended the sour cream into the mixture one tablespoon at a time until I got the creamy taste that was right for me. Delicious!!! Did not take long for the butternut squash to soften when boiled.
At first my boyfriend thought this would not be good. Now he cant get enough of it. I added curry and nutmeg and heavy whipping cream. Skipped the celery

What a fantastic recipe! I halved the cream cheese, which uncovered the cayenne. As for baking the squash first - I'm the world's slowest vegetable peeler/chopper but I had no difficulty at all peeling/chopping from 'raw'. The next time I make this soup (which will probably be in the next couple of weeks!) I'll try them baked to experiment with the flavours.
LOVE this soup - have made it 5 times this winter.  I use 2 squash roasted in the oven - 40 min at 400 - and one block of cream cheese.

Yummmmy!  I did modify the original recipe a little bit.  I substituted green onion for the onion, fresh cayenne peppers (3 seeded and chopped) for the ground cayenne pepper.  I sauteed the green onion, chopped cayenne peppers and two gloves of fresh garlic in about 2 T of butter until tender.  I roasted the squash in a 375 oven as others had suggested prior to adding it to the pan with the sauteed onion mixture and 3 cups of chicken broth.  I had to simmer the mixture about 10 minutes so that the squash was the right consistency to blend with my hand blender (right in the pan).  I also added a little salt and fresh ginger. I blended in about 4 ounces of reduced fat cream cheese as the last step. My boyfriend raved about the soup!  This soup will find its way to our table a lot during the upcoming cooler months!  Delicious!
So easy and super delicious!

I didn't make any modifications except to roast the squash first for about 50 minutes at 425 degrees; then scoop out the squash and add to pot with the rest of the ingredients.
