I used a handheld blender to blend the soup right in the pot, and it was very creamy, no lumps. The cream cheese makes it extra yummy. I added more cayenne pepper and some nutmeg. I also sauteed some garlic along with the onion. Delicious!

Made homemade broth with a rotisserie chicken carcass.  Gave this soup the most deepest rich flavor.  I only used 1 pkg. of cream cheese and it was plenty.  Silk smooth texture, LOVED this soup and very happy how well it turned out.
I used 8-oz cream cheese.  It was GREAT--especially with crumbled saltines.  Both my young kids loved it, as did I.  I'd definately make it again.
I sauteed the onions in olive oil, then used frozen, cubed butternut squash, liquid chicken bouillon and 1 tub of roasted red pepper cream cheese, which gave it a nice kick. It turned out great!

Definitely too much cream cheese in here. I think half the quanitiy would be better. Sorry about the low star rating but I think the overall average of 5 stars is misleading as the recipe needs to be altered to taste nice. After making it with the original quanities we used the soup as a sauce over broccoli and it was delicious.
This was fantastic!  I added a bit more pepper.  I like it spicy!  I also roasted the squash by cutting it in half and spraying it with garlic flavored PAM.  It took about 30 min on 350.  Thanks!

I've made this wonderful soup several times but this time I only used half the cream cheese as so many reported that it was just as good...I disagree.  Although still very good,  it just doesn't  measure up to the original version.

I have made this soup for the last three Thanksgiving's and is now my staple signature dish!  I use 8oz fat free cream cheese, to make it more healthy, and it still tastes wonderfully rich and creamy!  Thanks so much for an easy and tasty recipe.
Baked squash in 350 oven 45 minutes prior to adding to onion and soup mixture.  Did use more cayenne and real butter.

Delicious. I used two small pumpkins instead of the butternut squash, roasted them in the oven at 375 for an hour. I sauteed the onion and one clove of minced garlic in 1 TBS olive oil instead of the margarine. I brought all the other ingredients (3 cubes vegetable bouillon instead of chicken) up to a boil, then added the scooped out roasted pumpkin, brought back to a boil, let simmer for about 5 minutes, then added the neufchatel, which I halved per the other reviewers' comments. Next time I will go a bit less still...I think 6 oz will be about perfect. I did add a touch more cayenne and black pepper after I tasted it. It was delicious. I really agree with everyone else: I can't imagine this with the full amount of the cream cheese, which is why I gave it 4 stars. But it was a hearty and satisfying meal with some salad and french bread. Will definitely be making it again.
This is great.
I do use the same recipe, but I only use 1/2 of a bar a cream cheese and it is wonderful!
What can I say, we just love it and I follow the recipe to the dot except for halving the cream cheese. Thanks for putting up this delicious recipe.
I'm not a huge squash fan, but this will make a lover of the most skeptic squash eater. Love the creamy texture and the sweet flavor balanced out by the cayenne pepper.

This is a great start for butternut squash soup.  I roasted the squash until it was tender (roasting adds much more flavor than boiling it and makes it much easier to cut and peel).  I used oregano instead of marjoram just because I didn't have the marjoram and it was a good substitute.  I used one package of cream cheese and thought it was very creamy.  My husband (who HATES all types of squash) was even impressed by this recipe.  If you have an immersion blender, use it!  Much easier and faster.

This was very good... I was looking for an easy to prepare butternut squash soup and this fit the bill.  It does help to roast the squash first, makes the skin come off much easier... I followed the advice of using chicken stock and half the cream cheese and it was wonderful... I used my emusion blender to puree and this was ready in no time at all...
Very Rich and Tasty.  Leaves you wanting for more.

this was amazing.  My husband refuses to eat soup of any form, and he licked the bowl clean. Then ate the left overs before i could get to them.  I threw a bit more of the spices in it as well as some cream.
Terrific! Great flavor and consistency. So easy too! The majority of my time was spent peeling and cutting up the squash, but after that, the recipe goes very quickly!

everyone loved it even my dad who turns up his nose at most things very filling and worth the effort pot gone in hrs I rosted the butternut in foil first though with a wee bit of salt and pepper oil and honey this made it easier to cut and peel.
I am not a squash fan, or a soup fan, but I tried this recipe and LOVED it!  I've made it several times now and it has changed my mind about squash!
Excellent consistency and perfect for the cold fall and winter months. I boiled the squash in water for apx. 15 minutes prior to cutting it to make it easier to skin and cube.
Wonderful soup! I found that 8 ounces of cream cheese (half of the recipe) was still too much, so next time I'll try 4 ounces. Definately microwave the squash before peeling- it's so much easier.
Pretty rich.

As a soup lover, this was absolutely amazing! I made a few changes as some other reviews suggested. I roasted the squash beforehand, sauteed 3 celery stalks and 2 cloves garlic with the onion and also used half the cream cheese. I used whipped cream cheese but I'm not sure if that mattered much. I didn't have any marjoram and added turmeric then topped the soup with fresh chives when I was ready to serve it. Delicious!!
I found this soup waaay to rich with all the cream cheese in it.  Instead I double the amount of squash used and only used 8 oz of cream cheese and it's just perfect.

I baked the cubed squash for almost an hour before I put it in the pan with the other ingredients. I used only one bar of cream cheese. I substituted chicken broth for the water and boullion. I believe it could have used four cups of broth instead of three. We really liked it. Nice enough to serve to guests.

I have tried this recipe and others probably experienced that peel and cutting a butternut squash is a pain unless u have a very very sharp knife I found it easier to pierce the squash and place it in the over at 400 degrees until it can be pierced with a fork smoothly then I let it cool and cutting it is a breeze and all you have to do is peel the tought skin off.

I have to agree with others on this site when they say to roast the squash first. The recipe is So very tasty as written. I just used an immersion blender to puree everything right in the pot!! Mmmm super tasty

I LOVE, LOVE, LOVE this recipe and I am NOT a big soup fan.  I thought it would be nice to have a soup with christmas - it was easy to make once you get the squash cubed (which no small feat!).  My husband thought it was too rich (I used 2 packages cream cheese) so maybe next time I will use only 1.  It did taste amazing with only 1 package I just wanted to increase the volume so I added the second. Thanks for this amazing soup recipe!
Everyone that tried this just loved it, just the right kick.  Didn't use as much cream cheese as the recipe called for.

Tweaked the recipe (for my own tastes)
- Skinned the squash before roasting it per SLJ6's review as I used most of their tweaks as well, made for easier handling.
- Cubed the squash instead of quartering it.
- Tripled the garlic, we love garlic.
- 6 cups equals approx 1 squash FYI
- Substituted Veggie broth for Chicken
- Sauted the onions in butter instead of margarine
- Halved the cream cheese

Great soup! Warm, comforting, and freezes wonderfully. Vegetarian family loved it and meatatarian DBF tolerated it. Very heavy and filling, and I can eat a lot so with a salad could be a meal in and of itself.
I make this every year at Christmas time. It comes in very handy when overnight guests are here and you don't need such a large meal. Ham sandwiches go great with this.

Wow, this soup was delicious! I disagree with the reviews claiming it was bland, I thought it had the perfect amount of seasoning--more would have obscured the delicate squash flavor. The only changes I made was 1/2 the cream cheese as many have suggested, butter instead of margarine, and broth instead of bullion cubes. I made part of it with vegetable broth to accommodate my vegetarian sister and the difference was barely detectable. I took this soup to a party and received lots of compliments on it, and I will definitely make it again--a very cozy soup!
This was a hit with the whole family.  I followed some other suggestions, 1/2 the cream cheese and roasted the squash.
I think this is a great base soup but use several of the same substitutions as previous reviewers.
This soup was amazing!
I'm so happy to come across this recipe!  It made the house smell wonderful, preparation time was resonable and the taste was supperb. It deserves the 5 stars for sure!

I would have never thought to put cream cheese in butternut squash soup, but this was one of the best butternut squash recipes I've ever tried!  The only difference I made was to use sage instead of the marjoram.  I made this for my book club last night and everyone raved and asked for the recipe.  Definitely a keeper!

I roasted the squash separately, then just scooped it into the saucepan with the sauteed onion, poured the chicken broth over and added the spices, and voila, a soup in 5 min flat! I added 2 T cream cheese last minute and it lumped...maybe because it wasn't room temperature. Anyway, I'll leave it out next time or add milk instead. A pinch of sugar or drizzle of honey really makes the squash flavor shine. A quick, easy favorite.

Love this soup! It is easy to prepare and freezes well. I use cut up squash (organic from Costco). Since it is seasonal, I make several batches and freeze in Mason Jars. I put everything in the pot except the cream cheese and the milk that I add instead of so much cream cheese (I cut the cream cheese in half and add a cup of milk per batch). Once it is cooked, I put it in my food processor and then back to the stove to add the milk and cream cheese. Once it's blended, cool and into the jars...so easy! Great recipe!!!
I left out the cream cheese and added pureed apple. It was amazing!  Sprinkled cinnamon too when I served. I roasted the squash in the oven.
YUMMY!!!! I roasted the squash for 1 hour as others had suggested.  This is definately a keeper!!

I doctored some.  Used 6 tsp liquid beef bouillon and omitted the marjoram but used curry instead; I also added 2 peeled and chopped granny smith apples. After boiling etc. I pureed all and in the last puree batch (which was mostly liquid) I added 1/2 of one container of light cream cheese.  The potato and apples really thickened the soup - EXCELLENT

This soup is so yummy.  I changed a couple of things. I used one whole squash and only used 1 package of cream  cheese and felt that made it plenty rich.  I also added an extra cup of water since I used the entire squash.

Our family did not like this very much. I roasted the butternut squash first, as other had suggested.  Was it  was rich? Yes!!! Was it bland? Yes.  I make a lot of homemade soups because my family loves soup, but I will not be making this one again, sorry.
Wonderful!!! I used veg broth and lower fat cream cheese, made it vegetarian and a little more figure friendly :)
Nice and creamy. Very satisfying. I found it was a little bit bland though. A bit of extra salt helped intensify the flavor.

This one of the very best squash soup recipes I've tried.  I did cut down on the cream cheese and only used 8oz's which I feel was just right.  I even served it one time using small pumpkins as dishes, which went over very big with my guests.
Have made it several times and use 1 pkg of lite cream cheese, not 2.  Love it.
Delicious!  Used the 1 potatoe idea and only 1 pkg cream cheese and 4 cups chicken broth. Loved it and so did the family

fabulous soup considering everyone else's alterations--less creamcheese, etc. I also used some zucchini since didn't have a full 6 c. of winter squash. Don't need to dirty an extra pan to fry onions first, either, just boiled them with the squash. Used butter instead of margarine...better flavor.
Enjoyed by all!  Only sub was veg broth instead of chicken, used one pkg of cream cheese, wonderful, thanks for recipe!
Yummy delish!  I only used half the cream cheese and low fat at that.  It was fantastic with a hearty, crusty bread.

I've made this soup twice this season. Delicious fall flavor. I used organic chicken broth and only 1 8oz package cream cheese. It does take quiet a bit of time to peel and cut up this hard squash, I do think baking the squash would cut down on the prep time greatly.
Delicious soup. It does work great with just 8 oz of cream cheese. Also I used chicken broth.
Love this recipe! A lady from my church grows butter nut squash and is always willing to share so we go for this each time!

I am lactose intolerant so I was worried that without the cream cheese the recipe would be a flop, however it was absolutely delicious - I didn't have any marjoram as it is not a spice I use often and I used coriander instead which was great!

I used only have the cream cheese (8oz) and I had no marjoram so I substituted Italian seasoning (oregano and thyme) and it turned out great.  A nice kick from the cayenne counteracts the sweetness of the squash and the cream cheese makes it nice and thick.

Great flavor, made this for a friend who is undergoing radiation.  Roasted the squash, used two butternut's, could have used three of them.  Added carrots, used fat free Swanson's chicken broth, 6 oz of light cream cheese, and non fat yogurt starting with 1/2 cup but adding more in the blender to decrease the thickness.  Took awhile to make but will make again.
Very simple and delicious, everyone wanted some.
I have been using this recipe for years and it always pleases.  I try to eat healthy so I only use 1/4 the cream cheese which i think is plenty! I also use butter instead of margarine.

The recipe for this soup intrigued me when I first read it but the reviews convinced me that perhaps I needed to give this soup recipe a shot.  I have made this soup twice now and, in my opinion, it is absolutely delicious.  Everyone must try this recipe atleast a few times and I guarantee, you won't give it up.  Good recommendations were made to use chicken stock and 1/2 the cream cheese listed in the original recipe.  My soup ended up very rich and thick so I thinned it out a bit with low-fat milk.  Then, it was absolutely perfect.  I also froze a portion of it and used it another time - it was just as good if not better.  You will truly enjoy this soup, especially on a cold, winter day.  Please try it!
Yummy.  I only used one cream cheese, too.  It was thick and creamy and awesome!
This is one of my favorite! Rich & creamy meal. Every time I make this to share I preprint the recipe because I know people are going to ask for it.

Delicious!  I made this for some friends this past fall and it turned out really good.  I ended up trying to cut the squash while it was raw.... a bad idea.  It was really difficult and took a long time.  I should have taken the advice of the other comments and cooked it first before trying to cut it.

I used this recipe as a base and added to it. Like a lot of reviewers I cut the cream cheese in half, I used butter instead of margarine, and home made chicken stock instead of bullion and water. I added two small granny smith apples, garlic, cinnamon, nutmeg, and ground clove. I just eyeballed the amounts based on what I like. I added a little cream to thin it out but I think I'll add a little more stock, it's getting lot thicker as it cools. I was really surprised at all the flavor. My husband doesn't like butternut squash and he liked this !
Easy and very good. Opted for one bx. cream cheese.

Ok...I have to say that I tweeked this recipe big time. I used this recipe in addition to another butternut squash soup recipe. First of all, I used 2 squashes..cleaned and cut into 8 pieces..roasted them with olive oil, salt,and pepper and smashed garlic cloves for an hour in the oven..350. I then removed them from their skins..sauteed the onion and added 1 c. apple cider in addition to the chicken broth...and one peeled, chopped granny smith apple...and nutmeg, salt and pepper. I also have to say that I didnt use any of the cream cheese...the puree was perfect without..but I think I will add a small amount of 1/2 and 1/2 for a little richness. Excellent soup...thick, creamy and rewarding even if you dont use the cream cheese...way to calorie concious. Puree' in small batches in the food processor...be careful if its too hot!
Great recipe idea.  I changed the recipe and added some carrots and celery. I also cut back on the cream cheese.  It was a great soup.

I have used this recipe time and time again, and it keeps getting better.  Everytime I walk through my office, people stop me and ask "when are you going to make the soup again?".  One thing I did do diffrent was used an entire Walla Walla onion the last time and due to it being a sweet onion made a great flavor in the soup.  Also im sure I use a little more cream cheese then what is required.  but everyone seems to like the richness.

Fairly easy to make.  We added a cooked apple to the recipe and roasted pecans on top.  It had an overpowering taste of cream cheese which I didn't care for.  I think next time we will eliminate that ingrediant altogether and it will taste more like I expected.
This soup was awesome. My picky eaters even loved it. Very flavorful. Next time I would blend it a little less. A keeper!

I baked the squash at 350 for about an hour, scooped it out of the skin into a bowl added the cream cheese and whipped with a beater until it was smooth. then I boiled 4 cups of water with 6 table spoons of margarine added the bouillon. added the rest to the pot and let simmer..then like another viewer suggested..added apple cider!!! yummy!! to die for!
Excellent soup!  Very easy to make.  Everyone liked it at my Thanksgiving dinner.

While making this, I was going to add the amount of creme cheese and thought it was way way too much.  I ended up adding only 1/2 and it was great.  Next time I will even add less.  I would like to tase the squash more instead of the cheese.

Made a couple minor modifications, but it make this soup delicious! Here are the changes I made:

-cut squash into 6 pieces, coated with oil, salt, pepper & minced garlic & roasted at 350 degrees Fahrenheit for one hour
-added a chopped Apple & sautéed with onions
-added 3 sage leaves whole simmering & removed before blending
-used chicken broth plus 1 tsp Better Than Bouillon instead of water & bouillon 
-only used 4oz cream cheese
-garnished with Mexican crema & crumbled bacon
slow down on the cream cheese and only add as much as you need...I usually only use 1/2 a pack (1/4 of what is recommended)
thought it was very good, I did decrease the amount of cream cheese plus I used low sodium chicken broth to decrease the salt.. very good.. thanks

I love this recipe. I started making it for my son when he was 2 and now at 5 he still loves it especially when he gets to help make it. I add some ground cloves, all spice and nutmeg for added flavoring. This is a great recipe for everyone.
This soups is so thick and creamy Love it.

I used 1 pack of cream cheese and it was more than enough.  I'd suggest using 6 oz or just add heavy cream.  I poked holes every 2 inches going around the squash and stuck in microwave for 2 min.  Easier to cut that way, but that was the hardest part.  This soup was very creamy, rich and tasted like a very good restaurant's version.  Husband loves it, but I'm giving it 4 stars because of too much cream cheese.  Also used extra dashes of cayenne and nutmeg.
I loved this recipe!  The only thing I would do diffrently is use less cream cheese.
Turned out great! I love this soup. I add a pint of homemade canned carrots, and I use 1/2 the amount of cream cheese.

omigoodness so good!I tweaked the recipe a little bit...the first time i made this recipe i used the full amount of cream cheese and found that it was way too thick, so the second time i scaled way back and used a dollop of plain yogurt instead.  I also used chicken stock, real butter as well as ginger and nutmeg..it was so good! a real hit at the party i hosted.
thanks!
this recipe was awesome. Made it just as recipe called for and plan on doubling the recipe and freezing batches to have on hand.  Lom     P.s. used ready made chicken broth instead of bouillon
I have been using this recipe for two years. My family loves this soup! The cayenne pepper gives just enough kick. Great for a cold fall day.
I used roasted squash and half cream cheese and half butter.  best soup I ever made.  Yum.

First, thanks to all of those reviewers that said to use only 1/2 of cream cheese.  I can't imagine you would be able to taste the squash if you used the amount listed in the recipe.  This was good but I couldn't give it 5 stars because I could easily taste the cream cheese.  I prefer recipes that are the sum of their parts.
This soup was easy to make and delicious!  It tastes like a dessert.
The whole family loves this.  Delicious and very filling for a soup.  The kids didn't even know they were eating vegetables until I made the mistake of letting them watch me make it.

Outstanding. My inlaws rave about this soup - and I make it just for myself. The only hard part is cutting up the squash (I peel it first too); after that it's very easy. And soooo delicious. I've always made it with just the 8 oz. cream cheese, and it would still be delicious with less.

FANTASTIC!!!  But I docked it a star because as almost every other reviewer noted it calls for entirely too much cream cheese... I just did one brick.  Pre-Roasted the squash as others did and this made it so much easier to peel and slice.  Made with vegetable base and needed more liquids, but I think my squash was more than 6 cups (it was around 6 pounds).  Tried to "cheat" and just use a hand mixer in the pot, but that wasn't cutting it so I did have to blend in batches as directed which was somewhat labor intensive and MESSY.  Will definitely make again and experiment with making it further ahead of time, and even freezing it.  My mom suggested tweaking it with curry, which would be a very nice acompaniment to an Indian meal.  Next time I'll serve it with a swirl of sour cream or creme fraische and drops of herbed oil like they do at fancy restaurants =)

This was an excellent soup.  The cayenne pepper gave it a little extra kick.  I changed the recipe a little, I used a small cooking pumpkin and also a squash called sweet dumpling.  I baked both squashes in the oven for an hour until very soft then followed the recipe after that.  I also used 11oz of cream cheese instead of 16oz and it was just as creamy.  I will definitley make this recipe again, very, very good!
Very good, but only as an appetizer.  It's too rich for a meal.

I made this froze it. Pulled it out as a 1st course for my inlaws & got rave reviews! Added sour cream as a pretting squiggly topping (put sour cream in a baggie & cut a corner to pipe out in a swirle on top of soup). AMAZINGLY good. Restaurant quality.

This was very rich but tasty. I can only eat a small amount at a time. I used one squash which I cooked in the oven at 375 degrees for 45 minutes. I sauted an onion with the margerine, added 2 cups of water, 1 cup of apple cider, a peeled/chopped granny smith, salt/pepper/cayenne, 6 oz cream cheese. I then used my blender to mix small batches with the squash.

It was good.  The amount of cream cheese was definitely overkill.  I have made butternut squash soup before and it was much sweeter and less heavy without the creamcheese.  I would definitely make it again but I will cut out the cream cheese in this receipe and I'll use chicken broth instead of bouillon.
Tripled the cayenne and halved the cream cheese.  YUM
I was surprised to find I loved it, even with only about 3 oz. cream cheese (I tried to keep it healthy).  Love the sweet, spicy flavors and the creamy texture.

Honestly I think this produces a better soup, with less hassle, than roasting the squash first. Shocking I know. But it works well for me. I use real butter and 1/8th of the cream cheese called for. Honestly I would not add more than 4 oz of it and it is still velvety smooth. A go-to for us!

This was really good! Probably the best soup I've ever made! I did make a bit of a change with the cream cheese though: I replaced one of the packages with a can of beans (navy beans) to make it a bit healthier, and it still turned out amazing!
Easy and Very YUMMY!  After reading the reviews, I only used one block of cream cheese (and I used light!) and it came out just fine.  Also substituded chicken stock for water.  Everyone loved it.

This soup was the hit of my thanksgiving dinner!  I made it just as the recipe suggests, and we loved it.  I didn't expect it to be so spicy, but it was great!  The recipe makes a lot of leftovers, but we're looking forward to them.

Beautiful!!!  I did add a bit more water to thin it out a little and LOTS of cayenne pepper, its really good spicy.  My husband is from Nigeria and eveything is very spicy~!!!  Thanks for another great recipe for a very new cook!!!
Very creamy and delicious. Easy to change for your own preferences. Will definitely make this again. Thanks so much for sharing this scrumptious recipe. :)
Excellent soup! My first try at a squash soup! I left out the cream cheese, and I roasted the squash with evoo and garlic! Awesome!!
This was very delicious. Made it exactly like the recipe, except I didn't have marjoram on hand. Very simple to make as well.

Overall a great recipe! However I did make some changes.  I only used 1 pkg. of cream cheese and still found that it was still overpowering.  I added a dash of cumin and salt.  Only used 1 chicken bouillon and it was more than enough.  I have a picky mother, which I thought was not going to touch it, but she enjoyed it very much!
This was great.  Made it with pumpkin from my garden, also cut the cream cheese to 12 ozs. and doubled the onions.  I used a stick blender.
An easy and 100% delicious recipe which can be served as a light supper for a large crowd. It can easily be dressed up with a sprinkling of chives and croutons for visual effect.

Really delicious soup.  I used 1 eight oz package of cream cheese (lowfat even) and it was still very rich and creamy.  An immersion blender is much easier than transferring to a blender in batches.  I will definitely make this recipe again - I could barely stop sneaking spoonfuls before I served it!
I used a red curry squash for this. My husbad loved it and has been asking for me to make more.

I halfed this recipe because I had only one squash which yielded about 3 cups.  I didn't have marjoram so I did a Google search and discovered that oregano is a stronger cousin so I used that instead. The only other thing that I added was about two cloves of chopped garlic and about 1/2 tsp. of salt to balance the sweetness.  I used 4 oz. of reduced fat cream cheese and it was just right.  I will make this again since it was super easy and went together quickly since I pre-cooked the squash in the microwave.
so yummy
This is so good. I think I used about half the recommended amount of cream cheese and it was still very thick and creamy. Also, like many other reviewers, I roasted the squash first.

I couldn't figure out why all the recipes for butternut squash soup on here instructed to just chop the squash and boil while EVERY review said to roast first! I did both, doing the other steps exactly the same... the roasted squash soup is REMARKABLY better! More flavor, better flavor. Not roasting it first makes it an 'ok' but rather bland bowl of pureed orange mush. Roast your squash people!

This is one of my favorite soups to make. I used REAL BUTTER, instead of the margarine. I also as other reviewers have stated used less Cream Cheese. I use about   a little less than 8 ounces. This is a thick and hearty soup. I also added some milk to thin it a bit. My 13 yr.old daughter who said Yuck (at first) decided this was good. I didn't put any marjoram in the soup either.
Update on this review  Still good soup!!! BUT I was short on time so when I was at Trader Joe's they had cubed squash. Sometimes it is Butternut and sometimes it is Acorn. This is a HUGE time saver for me and the soupd comes out wonderful. I even have cut down the Cream Cheese even further. I use the Veg/Chicken stock combo and it is flavorful!!! :)

Absolutely delicious! Although I sort of used this recipe as a base and used what I had on hand at home. Here's what I did:

Sauteed the onions in about 3 TB of olive oil. Once they are soft, added in some minced garlic. Then throw in the squash (I used two bags of pre-cut, cubed from Trader Joe's) and a can of chicken broth. Add salt, pepper and fresh thyme (about 1 tablespoon; dried would probably work fine). Cooked for about 25 mins until the squash is tender. Take off stove and added about half a package of cream cheese. I used whipped because that's what we had. Taste for seasoning; add more salt if needed. Put all in blender and serve!
I am obsessed with this soup. I cut the cream cheese amount in half and add some grated parmesan and sharp white cheddar. Holy monkeys...this is the best! I've made it four times in the last month.
This soup was EXCELLENT!  The flavor was so creamy and delicious and very easy to make.  I will definitely be adding this to my fall recipe collection!

Had a nice taste with the changes I made.  I used chicken stock versus bouillon and water.  I added 2 sliced apples.  Since I didn't have morjoram I used allspice.  And used 1 8 ounce package of low fat cream cheese.  Soup was good.  But I used the leftovers as a sauce over rigatoni pasta and that was DELICIOUS!  Thanks for sharing.

This is the best soup I've ever had. I roasted my squash, only used 1/2 the cream cheese, added 1 peeled and chopped apple, and added about 1/2 cup of half and half in the end. Wow! I couldn't stop eating it! The family loved it too. I'll definitely be adding this recipe to my Thanksgiving spread this year.
The soup was nice and warmed the family up on a cold night.  It was o.k.  I used less cream cheese than it called for.  It could use more seasoning or spice for flavor.  The kids liked it.

Excellent! I sliced the squash in half, brushed with olive oil, added S &P, then roasted. I took the advice of others and only added one pkg. of cream cheese. The whole family enjoyed this. Next time I'll try adding the apple and cider as well. A little more sweetness would totally work in this recipe. Thanks Mary!

SO yummy.  I accidentally used cumin instead of cinnamon, realized my mistake and added some cinnamon before serving.  It was outstanding, so I think I will use the cumin again!  Sounds strange to me, but it totally worked!

Yummy! As per other reviewers suggestion, I cut the squash in half lengthwise, scooped out seeds, drizzled olive oil, salt & pepper and roasted for 45 mins. at 350. I peeled the skin off before pureeing. Next time I might try the microwave for mid-week cooking. I also used chicken broth instead of bouillon. Didn't have the cayenne pepper so I added just a dash of chili powder. As others have suggested, I used one package of cream cheese & it came out splendid.
Delicious!!!! I added a good squirt of Sriracha to heat it up and it was awesome. Next time i think i'll try using less cream cheese to make it a little less rich.
This is awesome!!!  The only change i made was to use only one stick of cream cheese.  Nice and thick, didn't even need the rest of my dinner!

I was really skeptical. It looked really wierd,a nd the ingredients seems kinda strange. I'd herd good things but didnt know how the "at home" version would be, but i made it anyway, and boy am i glad! This was soo good. Choping up the squash was the most difficult, i had to google a video on how to do that part. Everyone has GOT to try this!
The best soup ever! I had never made squash soup before, and my husband was very skeptical, but he was crazy about it. I only added one pkg of cream cheese, and it was rich and delicious.

One of my new favorite soups - wow! I baked the squash ahead of time to soften it up, used fat free cream cheese and no sodium boullion. 

My only suggestion is that I will probably use half the boullion next time - the "chicken-y" flavor overpowered the spices and squash a little.
Did NOT put in the apple cider vinegar! All else is great!

im eating it right now!i followed alot of the advice of other reviewers... and it deff needed the tbs of brown sugar I put in!! also im a cream cheese/ thick soup lover, and I put less than half the cc, and it is still almost too thick! but delicious!

I never write a review, but this recipe deserves one!!  This soup is so hearty and DELICIOUS!!  Leftovers freeze well, but let's be honest, there won't be any leftovers.  I always roast the squash in the oven with some olive oil and sea salt to bring out the flavor.  I have found that 1 package cream cheese usually works and makes the soup super creamy!!  Is it bad to crave squash soup??  mmmmmmmm :)

Yum! Perfect creaminess and the cayenne gives it a nice little kick. I am not a spicy fan, so this is just perfect. I didn't have any cream cheese, so I used whole milk instead. I would imagine it would be even better with cream cheese!

My tween daughter loves this (surprisingly) and actually puts in requests for it!  One package of cream cheese is plenty.  The squash is a pain to deal with, but when I roasted it, my family found it to be too sweet.  May try to microwave and see if that eases the prep.
I only used one container of cream cheese and it was still creamy and delicious.

This is not what I was looking for. I thought it was on the sweet side rather than the hearty side. My family liked it ok but I will look for another recipe. I even halved the cream cheese and added haf and half.

very very good as suggested by some of the other reviews I roasted the squash  in the oven then scoop out the inside and add to chicken stock and just followed the recipe from there on....all in all a keeper for the winter months ahead

Oh my GOD this is AMAZING!!!!  I never thought I'd like butternut squash soup, but one of my students gave me a butternut squash and I have been looking for something to do with it that didn't involve sugar.  So I figured I'd give this recipe a shot.  And now I think I'm hooked!  I'm a vegetarian, so I used vegetable bullion instead of chicken and I only used half the cream cheese, but it was delish!

I prepared this according to the recipe and exact instructions (unlike many reviewers), and thought it was awesome. The only thing I'd be sure to change is to skip the nasty synthetic margarine and use real food...butter. Using a stick blender to smooth the soup is easier and safer than using a food processor.
I roasted the squash as well as onion and garlic.  I use broth instead of water/bouillon. (Can use chicken broth or vegetable broth - I've made it both ways). Tastes even better the second day.

Excellent flavor - with the chayenne. It seemed like it was missing something so I sprinkled crountons on it and it added a wonderful zesty crunch to it. Didnt really need the cream cheese but added 3oz any way. Looks spectacular!

This is a yummy fall and winter soup.  Nice and hearty.  It is very rich with the 16 oz. of cream cheese, and works better with the 8 oz....better "squash" flavor without losing anything.  My company (and I) loved it!
This is good, but like another reviewer mentioned. I only added about two tablespoons of cream cheese. And I used 3cups of chicken broth instead of bullion.
I made this soup with yellow squash and it came out delicious! I didn't add the marjoram (didn't have any) or cayenne and I used 4 oz of cream cheese.
A super rich and creamy soup.  Will use again!!

I thought this tasted like a mix between pumpkin and carrot soup. I really enjoy the flavors and only used 1/3 of the cheese that was asked for. I used laughing cow cheese instead of cream cheese. Also, I used my immersion blender twice. First to puree the squash after I cooked it in the oven. Second, after I added the cheese and let it melt. It really helped to give this a smooth consistency.
Fantastic soup! This is delicious and easy, this recipe is definately a keeper. Followed recipe, only change was to use 1 T butter  in place of margarine.
Absolutely amazing.

This has been the best tasting soup ever! I took the advice of one of the other reviews by cutting the butternut squash in half, spread oil with salt and pepper to the inside, and baked it in the over for 45 minutes.  You might even want to  consider doing this a day before you plan on making this soup since it takes so long.  This has been one of the best recipes I've tried yet.
Incredible.  Served with dried apple chips on top and sourdough bread for dipping.  Was very rich and hearty (and I used low-fat cream cheese).  Great for a cold night.
Anyone who I serve this soup to, loves it and wants the recipe. Sometimes I add a littleless cream cheese to thin it up a little. It is delicious.
Use half as much cream cheese

I just made this and it was so simple. I followed other reviewers advice and roasted the squash first, then followed the recipe as directed. I didnt have any marjoram, so I used a little oregano. Its a very good, rich soup. I am not too crazy about the cayenne flavor, but other than that, I will be making this again. Thanks!
Very tasty, very popular.

I am sure the original recipe is awesome, but I altered it with what I had on hand. I used one large butternut squash baked and scooped out, three cups of vegetable broth, one pouch of cream cheese, and doubled the cayenne pepper. It was awesome! They cayenne pepper gives it a warm taste after that made my nose run, I loved it.
Made it the second time tonight and it is even better than the first.  Only change was the amount of cream cheese (1/2 the amount per the suggestion of many).

I had to convert this to metric (because I am in Italy) and I think I added too much water, so it was a bit liquidy. I halved the cream cheese as the recipe suggested as an option, and it was great. Follow th recipe exactly, because all the other suggestions are just personal preferences and won't really improve anything.

It was amazing! Amazing! My husband, who doesn't really like to eat any of the American soup I make even gave his approval. 

So In all, I don't think the proportions I used were dead on, but I can't wait to try again! Perfectly toasty for a cold winter night. I also may add some broccoli next time just to see how it turns out.
I really enjoyed this soup!! The children were less impressed but i will try it with them again another time as Tastes change!! Certainly worth a try!! xxxx
Fast, easy, and delicious. I added some roasted red pepper to the mix and pureed it all together and it is soooo good.
I was dubious as to what this would turn out like as it seems so simple.  But this was absolutely delicious.  I roasted the squash and only added half a block of cream cheese.
If I make this again, I would only use one package of  cream cheese. I didn't not care for the texture, which is unusual for me. The flavor was good. My husband seemed to like it more than me.
I LOVE this! ... my family HATES it.  I even had them try it with different amounts of cream cheese.  No luck ... so I'm writing off the family and keeping this recipe!  :)
This is a great recipe so don't ruin it by using vegetable oil spread, yuck! Only real butter please... By the way water comes from the tap not a bottle made by Nestles!
This soup was excellent!!! Will make again for sure. (Didn't have marjoram so I left it out).

Absolutely the best Butternut Squash soup I've had anywhere!  The ONLY change I made was reduced the cream cheese by half and used Neufachatel instead of full fat cream cheese.  SO easy and SO delicious.
Used 1/2&1/2 instead of the cream cheese
Excellently creamy and surprisingly tasty!  Melt some crumbled blue cheese in it, and you won't be disappointed.

Delicious! My teenagers loved it. I used 1/2 the amount of cream cheese and it was plenty rich and creamy. I'd use a bit more water or stock next time as this soup was fairly thick. I also used fresh marjoram--1 Tablespoon--with wonderful results.

I only used one package of cream cheese, and I pre-roasted the squash as others suggested; I thought this soup was bland and too thick, though the smell was deceptively delicious! Probably won't make this one again.

Bland, added 1 teaspoon pink salt, doubled the oregano that I used instead of marjoram, and doubled the cayenne.  I also used a little less cream cheese. The extra salt may not have been necessary if I would have used the boullion instead of the low sodium chicken broth.  Served with homemade garlic butter croutons and toasted Italian bread.
Great soup

pretty simple, but this recipe calls for ALOT of cream cheese.. in the end, the soup came out less sweet than expected, couldn't really taste the full flavor of the squash. Will make it again, but try a different recipe.

SO CREAMY!  I used a stick blender right in the pot to puree the cooked squash and the onion.  Added only 1 package of cream cheese (it was plenty) and used the stick blender again....smooth as silk!  I also added a touch of nutmeg then sprinkled just a tad of cinnamon & sugar as a garnish.  So quick and definitely delicious.

This recipe was great but I think it calls for WAY too much cream cheese.  I started adding it and it was really thick so I stopped.  I ended up with about 3/4 of one container of cream cheese and it called for two.  I think it would have been way too rich thick with all of that cream cheese.  I also used butter because margarine is awful.

We loved this soup!!! My boyfriend requested that I make it every night, and then threatened to run to the grocery store to get another squash!! I used the microwave trick and scooped out the squash with my ice cream scooper. I did only use 1 thing of cream cheese and lots of salt and it turned out great!! As for blending, I made the mistake a long time ago of not letting it cool long enough - splattered boiling soup all over myself! Pour a batch in the blender and the rest in a large bowl (I use my quart sized measuring cup) until heat isn't actively rising from either bowls (It won't create a pressure when you have the lid of the blender on). Start the blender off at the slowest speed and work your way up to puree, while keeping a towel over the top.

This makes a wonderful soup! Excellent for cold fall & winter days.

To make it more smooth, I'll sometimes substitute the cream cheese with some whipping cream or canned milk. I also like to put fresh spices into a cheesecloth that I can take out at the end. This makes the soup more uniform in color and flavor. When I serve it, I like to save some of the cream/milk and give the soup an artistic swirl.

I roasted the squash (pierced with fork, on cookie sheet in 400 oven for 1hr), pulled off skin, scooped out seeds, and then put the "meat" in the blender with all the other ingredients but just 4oz cream cheese. Delicious! Everyone raved about it. I highly recommend it.

This soup is fantastic.  I have craved it ever since the last time I made it about a month ago and plan to make it again this evening.  I followed other reviewers suggestions to roast the squash first as well as to add apple and nutmeg while cutting the amount of cream cheese down to half a package.  I also added ground ginger.  Even though I made several changes, I am rating this at five stars because I think the addition of cream cheese is absolutely brilliant.
I don't like any soup but I LOVE this one!!!

My husband and I made this tonight to use up a butternut squash that came in our weekly box of organic veggies. We did make a few modifications to the recipe. We cut the squash in half, seasoned with salt and pepper, rubbed with a little olive oil and roasted it, cut side down, in a 375 degree oven for 45 minutes.  Since there was no marjoram or cayenne pepper in the pantry, we subbed in a tiny bit of hot chilli powder for heat and flavor. Also, we cut down the bouillon to two cubes as ours is not sodium-free and it seemed that 4 cubes would make the soup too salty. It tasted beautifully rich as it was so we decided not to add any cream cheese, which cut down the fat.  We did thin the soup with some 2% milk before serving as the texture was a little thick - everyone in the family loved it. Great recipe - will definitely make again, especially in the wintertime!
Family loved it!!
This recipe is very yummy, however I wish I would have taken other reviewers advice and reduce the cream cheese dramatically. 4oz should be enough. It was good but very very heavy.

So delicious! I added chicken stock instead of water and put in only one bouillon cube. I did not have marjoram so I left it out. I used half of a brick of cream cheese and the result was still creamy and dreamy. Yum!

I love this soup! I have made it five times and it was the star of two large parties.  I use the precut squash which is exactly the 6 cups required and is a huge time saver.  I use Better than Boullion. I like the soup without the cream cheese.  Instead I use a small spoonful of sour cream on each bowl.

This is one of my favorite Fall recipes, but I do tweak it quite a bit. First, I roast the squash. I also add a chopped, peeled apple or two and cut the cream cheese quantity in half. I use vegetable broth instead of water. 
My son made this recently and followed the recipe precisely, and we all agreed that it was much, much too rich (too much cream cheese) and not "squashy" enough.
This is the best soup I've made so far.  Absolutely excellent.
This recipe has become a staple in our household. We are on to our second batch this fall! Try with half the cream cheese. That's all you'll need. YUM!
Wonderful fall soup.  Tastes like you spent hours on it.  I only used 1pkg of the cream cheese and used chicken broth instead of bullion.  I also added ginger and put toasted crushed walnuts on top.

I have made this soup several times, using one average butternut squash and only one package of cream cheese.  I also added 2 cloves of garlic and about one tbsp of fresh ginger root while cooking the squash.  Very good and easy.
GREAT great great but very very very filling.

Yummmmmm!

I followed the recipe exactly (only thing was my squash was already pureed as it was leftover from when I was making a pumpkin pie last week).  So i didn't bother pureeing the soup, just let the onions be a bit chunky.  SUCH good flavor, and I used about a third of the cream cheese.  Try it!

Delish..along with roasting the squash, I also roasted an onion and a few garlic cloves blended all together with half a block of nuefchatel cheese and it was AMAZING! Always have to roast the veggies!!

I like many reviewers roasted the squash in the oven first. Cut in half and roasted with cut side down on a greased baking sheet for about 40 min at 375. Cut down the cream cheese. I've added red peppers (sauteed with the onions) to the soup as well.

I also oven roasted the squash before hand.  Made it much quicker to put together.  My 9 year old daughter loved this.  I added the called for cream cheese and I thought it was fine, very rich and creamy. Needed a little salt but otherwise great recipe that will go in our do-over file.  Oh, I just made half a batch.

Husband and I loved this - but with a few modifications.  I didn't have marjoram so skipped, used only 1 block of light cream cheese, used 1 box chicken broth instead of water and bouillion. Also because I love flavor of green apple with butternut squash I added 2 peeled, cored and chopped Granny Smith apples when I added the squash. Also I didn't measure the squash - I just used what I got from 2 medium sized squashes.

I only added 2 T butter, about 5 T cream cheese, added two heaping T. of brown sugar and one PEAR......AMAZING!  Thanks for the recipe after trying so many other butternut squash soup recipes that I did not like! :)))

I made this recipe according to the directions until, like other reviewers, it came to the cream cheese. I put in one box, half the proposed amount, and I still found the cream cheese taste to be really overpowering. I wish I would have put in 1/4 of the amount and then added more to taste. Also, like others mentioned, the finished soup was extremely thick, like a dip. I probably added another 3 or 4 cups of chicken stock to thin it. All in all, I would make the recipe again because it's really easy, but I will make some major tweaks. Oh, and here's a note for the other beginner cooks out there: one butternut squash is more than enough to make the soup. You do not need to purchase multiple squash. 6 cups sounds like a lot, but a squash goes a long way.
Good stuff,but too peppery. Will cut in half next time. Adding cooked broccoli at the end would be good.

Pretty good! A little mild in taste, but with a nice little kick! I roasted the squash since I had extra time on my hands. I only came up with 4 cups but it worked out fine.  I thought that much cream cheese was far too much. I only added 1/4 of one package (2oz) and that was perfect! More than that would have been too rich and would have drowned out the other flavors. I used the leftover cream cheese to make the "Cucumber Sandwiches III" on this site. Made for a great lunch!

MY FAVORITE SOUP! I bake my butternut squash whole and then cut it in half and pull the peel right off, put it in the blender to puree. I bought a bunch from a local farm market so I can freeze 6 cup bags so I am ready to make this all year long.

Like the other reviewers, I roasted the squash first.  Then, I added it to the broth to simmer and, after 20 minutes, I was able to easily mash it with a potato masher/ricer in the pot, which I think was easier and less messy than using a blender/food processor.  I realized at the last minute that I did not have marjoram, so I substituted thyme and a little cumin, which I thought tasted great with the cayenne.  Really rich, creamy, lets the great taste of the squash shine through.

Great soup! I roasted the squash as recommended by others. Since I was roasting the squash, I roasted a garlic bulb as well and put it in the soup with the squash. Used good quality chicken stock and only one package of cream cheese and it was phenomenal! I'm embarrassed to admit that I made it two days in a row.

FANTASTIC! Used two butternuts from my garden... Like many others, I roasted the squash in the oven for about 45 mins at 350.  I ran out of time, and stored the cooked squash overnight in the fridge. The next day, I sauteed the onions in a dutch oven then put them in a large bowl with the squash and all its juices, and the bouillon (I used Emeril's, as I love it). I used a hand blender to puree. I then added only ONE package of whipped cream cheese. I returned everything to the dutch oven and seasoned with black pepper and a few grates of fresh nutmeg. Did not use cayenne - personal preference. It was rich, thick and delish - loved by all, and reheated beautifully. Thanks for this recipe - I will make this many, many times in the days ahead!
Forgot to buy another cream cheese so I subbed 8oz sour cream. It turned out great!
I accidentally planted butternut squash instead of summer squash. So I had 10 squash to use :). Made a double batch of this soup and I'm glad I did. It is soo good. Will make again.

All four of the adults at the table raved about this soup. My three kids decided in advance that they weren't going to like it, but two of them changed their mind after trying it. Success! I love making soup on a cold fall afternoon, so thanks for the recipe.  I'll make it again. Oh, and I did follow the advice of fellow reviewers who used half of the recommended amount of cream cheese. It was plenty.

This tasted great but it was a pain to make.  Peeling a raw butternut squash is just not a great idea, so I boiled it whole and then peeled it and chopped it, then added it to the onions and water.  I ended up having to add at least double the water and bouillon because the mixture was too thick for me to puree.  As a final product, the soup was very good, but it's not fun to make and the broth amount in the ingredients needs to be doubled, or the squash and cream cheese halved.
Over X-mas, this soup was our starter before our Turkey Dinner, it was so delicious, we almost made it our meal.
DELICIOUS! Our spring weather suddenly turned chilly but this soup warmed our souls! Very rich, eat in moderation.
Very easy to make.  Although I'm not a soup person, my husband and son loved it.

I didn't use all the cream cheese (about 3/4s) and used vegetable broth instead of chicken broth.... very good!  Garnished with some slices of  butternut squash roasted with salt, rosemary and tuscan infused olive oil.

This turned out WAY too thick for our tastes.  Definitely use half or less of the cream cheese.

UPDATE: I decided to give it another try and I made it according to the suggestions that @SLJ6 gave in their review.  It helped, but the soup still ended up being meh.  I added in a generous amount of brown sugar which seemed to help, but it still seems like it's missing something.  I've seen another recipe for a butternut soup with crab meat, and I think that might give this soup the counterpoint of taste that it needs to be really good.
Wonderful!

I added half the cream cheese with a little bit of light sour cream and it was perfect. I used light cream cheese. I actually cant imagine the recipe with the full amnt of c.c. I think it would be too rich! I also added garlic powder and dried rosemary.
YUM!!  EVERYONE LOVED IT

I made this the first time following the recipe to a tee. This time, I too tweaked it. I roasted the squash, but differently from other reviews that I have read. I cut off the top and bottom, sliced it lengthwise, scooped out the seeds, sprinkled with sea salt, ground pepper and dotted with butter. Then I put the squash in a baking dish, cut side up, put 1/4 inch of water into the dish, covered loosely with foil, and cooked for 45 minutes in a preheated 325 degree oven. When done, I kept whatever butter melted and put it in the stock. I added garlic powder to the onions, doubled the cayenne pepper and used half of the cream cheese. My hubby just told me that he thinks this is very delicious. It has a rustic flavor instead of an overly sweet, rich taste.

This was delicious, I also halved the cream cheese make it a bit healthier and it was still very creamy.  You could play around with adding other vegetables very easily.  Veggie stock makes it vegetarian :)
My husband loved it but I didn't as much. Maybe because it was too thick. I would need to double the liquid next time.
Skip the cream cheese and add an apple!  Delicious!
Saute squash with onions and garlic for a few min. before addding spices and vegetable broth.

This 5-star rating is more for the rejuvenated recipe I created, of course using advice from a ton of other reviewers. I used the same ingredients as this one, except I cut out all but 1/4 of the cream cheese and used 2 cans of chicken broth instead of bouillon.  Other additions included 2 peeled and diced summer zucchini (if you don't have enough BNS), a celery stalk (diced), one granny smith apple (cubed and peeled), nutmeg and about 1 tbsp of light whipping cream. To prepare it, I roasted the butternut squash in the oven for 1 hr at 400 F with salt, ground black pepper, and crushed garlic on top. Once it was done, I sauteed the onions, celery, apples and zucchini for 10 minutes.  After that I added the butternut squash and let it cook in the pan for a few minutes too, since it wasn't completely cooked in the oven. Then I poured in the chicken broth, marjoram, cayenne pepper and nutmeg. I let that all come to a boil and simmer for about 20 minutes.  Finally, I added the cream cheese and whipping cream and blended it up. So delicious, my new favorite dish!
This soup was so very delicious.  Better than ANY I've ever purchased!!!

This soup was so good. My husband loved it too.  It was however, very rich. I used some leftover marscapone cheese and heavy cream (about half of what the recipe calls for in cream cheese). It turned out very well. I think I will use cream cheese next time but definitely only 8oz. Even without adding cream the soup was great...a more healthy option if you are looking for a lowfat recipe.

This soup was amazing! I did tweek it a little bit though. What I changed from the original recipe was I added carrots, celery and a potato to it as well. I also baked the squash first as others recommended, and I only used 1 package of cream cheese. So good!

This was a huge hit for our family from our 5 year old to my husband.  I did make some changes after reading reviews.  I used about 4 cups of Chicken Broth instead of the boullion and water.  I also diced up 6 small red potatoes and boiled in the broth.  I used 2 butternut squashed, halved them sprayed with olive oil then roasted upside down with a clove of garlic under each half for 30 minutes at 400 degrees.  I added the roasted squash to the broth and boiled just until everything was tender.  I also used Neufchatel instead of regular cream cheese.  I will make this again and again.
This is SO good!! I made it for Thanksgiving one year and ate so much before it made it to the table, that we barely had enough!

OUTSTANDING! Tip - Definitely use only 1 package of cream cheese as others suggested. I made it exactly according to the recipe, except for that one adjustment, and family and friends could not get enough of it! I could eat this stuff daily.
This was great!!! but I used vegetable stock instead and low fat cream cheese was fantastic.

Of all the courses I served for Thanksgiving, this was the one everyone raved about the most, even the non-soup eaters.  They were lucky there was enough since my family and I ate so much of it before they came.  Thanks to other reviewers, I also cut the cream cheese in half. Thanks for the tips
I've made this many times and have even prepared this for guests. Everyone loves it. I use cumin to flavor the soup and cut the cream cheese way back - about 1/2 a package to the full recipe.

Great Recipe, I normally make Squash soup all the time with the basic but wanted to try this recipe, while I slightly deviated it was still great. I added only about 2 Tbs spoon of cream cheese, and also added heavy whipping cream. I chopped about 2 tbls spoon worth of fresh chicken in small bits with half a handful of pasta. This allowed the soup to thicken real nicely. The chicken bouillon was reduced slightly to reduce the sodium content. The soup was rich and creamy with small bits of chicken, and the occasosional penne pasta bit.

Like many others, I roasted my butternut squash first.  I only used 1 block of cream cheese....which I think is enough.  flowed the recipe exactly, and I added freshly grated ginger -- because I love fresh ginger in butternut squash soup.  This is the first time I've made

I put 1/2 cream cheese in and I added an extra cup of chicken broth.  
Delicious!

This is a very rich and creamy soup.  Everyone in our family initially raved over it so I have made it several times since.  It is very easy to make.  I prefer to place the cleaned squash face down in a roasting pan and add 1 c of water and cover with foil.  Then I prepare the rest of the meal while it is baking in the oven.
I made it with half the cream cheese because I forgot to buy another package, really loved it and would make it exactly the same again

I made this recipe w/the extra squash from the garden...took me about 10 minutes to prepare and 30 minutes to cook.  A WONDERFUL soup that is easy and quick.  I'm not sure how kids would like it.  I modified the recipe for only 4 cups of squash, and only used about 5oz cream cheese, and it was excellent!  Everyone that tried it raves!
I added diced potatoes to make it more chowder-like, and it was great!

I like this recipe because you can whip up a wonderfully rich flavored pot of soup in no time. I'm sure all the provided tweaks add to the flavor, but if you want something great from the get go, try this recipe. You won't be disappointed.

This is SO Yummy just as written!!! I made it a second time with an extra acorn squash I had, So I figured I would tweaked it big time... I boiled & smashed one butternut & one acorn together, added about 2 teaspoons of cayenne, about 1 tablespoon garlic, one whole onion, 2 packs cream cheese, 3 cups chicken stock... blended it all together... Mmmm it was thick & delish...

Made on December 10/15 used 2 pkg. frozen squash thawed, roast for 20minutes with olive oil . Sauté onions and minced garlic, then add one sliced apple then ad squash, chicken broth (4cups) and spices including 2Tbsp. Brown sugar, 1 tsp nutmeg.  Simmer for 1 hour then drop 1pkg cream cheese to soften for few minutes, when tender cool abit then put in small batches into nutribullet. YUMMY!!!!

Amazing!  I'm not even a soup fan, but I found this wonderful.  My husband I I both agreed that it was a little rich with the 2 packages of cream cheese (we used the fat free kind), so I think next time we will only use 1 package. But we will ceretainly make this again!
I used 8 oz of cream cheese and 2 cans of low sodium chicken broth.

This soup has a really nice flavor. I only used 1/4 the amount of cream cheese (half of one block), and it's still very creamy and rich. I only used one butternut squash, medium size, which obviously isn't 6 cups worth -- but still carried the nutty/sweet squash flavor nicely. (I roasted it in the oven for 1/2 hr, as other reviews suggested). Next time I'd use a larger squash just to give it a little more thickness, and a slightly fuller flavor.
Very VERY rich when using 2 pkgs of cream cheese.  I tried substituting the second pkg of cream cheese with milk (or use 1/2 & 1/2)
Used 1/4 of the cream cheese because that's all I had. Superb!

I only had 4 cups of butternut squash, so put in 1 cup of acorn squash and 1 cup of spaghetti squash.  I also added 1 1/2 cans of pure pumpkin.  Like one other review, I too roasted the squashes to bring out the full flavour!  I used 2 boxes of Campbell's chicken broth instead of bouillon.  I used butter instead of margarine to saute the onion.  I also added about 1 tsp of fresh ginger and an additional 1/4 tsp of cayenne pepper.  The cream cheese is this recipe makes the recipe if you ask me!

I would make this again, it was very good.  I only made a couple of adjustments, roasted butternut squash for 45 minutes, used 2 more cups of broth in the blender, and only used 4oz of cream cheese (it was very creamy). Gave it 4 stars because I tweaked it with added broth and cream cheese.  Flavor was very good.

I didn't enjoy this recipe at all.  I found the final result to be the consistancy of baby food and to have lost the great flavor of the squash altogether.  Perhaps I did something incorrectly when making it...

I love this recipe!  At the suggestion of some reviewers, I reduced the amount of cream cheese. I used 1/2 of an 8-oz pkg, and it was very thick and creamy.  The cayenne pepper gives it just the right bit of heat.  This is definitely a keeper!
One of my new favorites!  I roasted the squash in the oven at 400 for about 30 minutes and then added it to the other ingredients in the crock pot and cooked it for about 2 hours...PERFECT!
I loved this soup and so did my husband!  The cayenne pepper gives it a nice kick.
So simple and so yummy! Didn't add the cayenne or marjoram but who cares? My husband wants it again this weekend. I also threw in 1/2 cup salsa from my garden before blending.

Everyone in my family loved this soup!  It was creamy and delicious...the flavor and consistency reminded me of a broccoli cheddar soup.  I tried a separate recipe version as well and the only thing I liked better about that version was the addition of chopped carrots before I blended it using an immersion blender.  When I make this recipe again, I'll experiment with adding in some carrots.
This is good as a side dish, but a little overpowering to be the main course.  Half the called for cheese is definitely the way to go.  A very good cold weather soup.

I loved this recipe.  But I cooked the squash whole in my crock pot on low for 8 hours. It was super easy to peel and completely cooked. I also used neufchatel cheese instead of cream cheese to lower the fat and calories. I think it would be just as good with half the cheese as well.
Awesome Soup!  I too used only 1 package of cream cheese but followed the rest of the recipe to a tee.

Good base, left out a package of cream cheese and added about half cup of sourcream instead.  Glad I did otherwise the soup would have been so rich there's no way it would have been suitable for as a main dish, great as a starter though.  Thank you for the recipe!

This was absolutely delicious!  I roasted the butternut squash in the oven at 375 for 45 minutes because I wasn't sure how to peel a squash.  This was my first attempt at this.  I also only added 1 block of reduced fat cream cheese.  I was fully prepared to add the second, but the consistency was what I was looking for after only 1, so figured I'd skip the calories.  It was amazing, amazing, amazing!  All of my children (4, 6, 9, 11) ate a whole bowl too!  That was what sold me!!!  Make this…you will NOT be disappointed!!!

This was fantastic! I followed some of the other reviewers comments and roast the squash first,  only added one 8 oz pkg of cream cheese, still amazing! I also didn't have marjoram, so I used Italian seasoning, MMMMM!
So good. I used only about 1/2 of the cream cheese called for. I ate it all in 2 days

This is the best butternut squash soup we've ever had!  I use about half the water and half the amount of cream cheese plus I use light cream cheese. It's still VERY creamy and we like the thicker consistancy.  Also, if you have one of those single hand mixers they are GREAT for putting straight into the pot to mix the soup so you don't have to transer the hot liquid through the blender.
Fantastic soup. I'm a very amateur cook and the instructions were great. Thanks Mary!
Even if you are leary about eating "squash soup" you'll love this.  It is very rich with 8 oz. of cream cheese; I can't imagine it with twice that!
Very yummy after I deluded the soup with 1 1/2 C of water. Too thick for me. Next time I will half the amount of cream cheese. But after I deluded it, it was fantastic!

Awesome!  I used chicken broth instead of bouillon and to make this a little thinner I used four cups instead of three.  Absolutely fantastic.  By using more broth I got a soup that was thick but not like gravy.  Everyone enjoyed it.

I followed the advice of others and baked the squash first. I added 1 1/2 cans of chicken broth instead of water and boullion and only one package of cream cheese. It turned out great! Just wish I had doubled the recipe, as it didn't make enough for too many leftovers. And definitely some homemade bread to go with it is great!
Loved this! Followed the recipe. Only change was I cut the squash in half, coated with olive oil and salt and pepper, then roasted for 45 minutes.

Wonderful recipe, went over huge w/my guests. Here's my little changes... Used chicken broth instead of water and broth cubes, cooked squash in oven in about an inch of water/cut in half for about 30 min. first. Added a bit of garlic and tiny amount of ginger for zip to the onions. And only used 1/2 of the cream cheese. Served with a dallop of sour cream and a couple dashes of tobasco. YUM!!!

I haven't had or made this soup before so I wasn't sure what to expect, but the boyfriend was happy with it and so was I. I roasted the butternut squash with olive oil, salt, pepper, and garlic as some of the other readers had suggested. I also used half of a granny smith apple and, instead of cream cheese, just a bit of heavy cream did the trick. I regretted using the apple at frst because the soup was too sweet, but you can use something acidic to balance that out - I threw a little splash of balsamic vinegar in and it balanced it well. I also added more spices then the recipe called for.
I ROASTED THE SQUASH & USE 8 OZ CREAM CHEESE & IT WAS GREAT.  IT IS A KEEPER FOR SURE.

FANTASTIC!! I read through the other reviews so made a few very minor changes (1/2 the cream cheese and used reduced fat and I roasted the squash before cooking) and this is sooooo good!! I just warmed some up at work and everyone is asking what I am eating for lunch!! LOL!!
pretty simple. very tasty.  Thank you!

Very Good, I only added 1/2 of the cream cheese,I used  low sodium chicken stock instead of water which is probably why it needed quite a bit of salt, I would say 1 teaspoon at least, I also added 1 tablespoon of tarragon vinegar right before serving. Would make a great first course for Thanksgiving dinner, Oh, I also used acorn instead of butternut squash...
This is absolutely delicious.  It's rich and creamy and easy to make.  I prebaked my squash and just scooped it out and pureed with the cream cheese to make it easy.

Loved it!  It's rich yet still light somehow.  I think I put a little too much onion in it the first time.  Also using a hand blender makes life a lot easier than using a food processesor.  And I added a few tablespoons of cream just to make it a smidge richer.

This soup doesn't really need another review.  Obviously many people think it's outstanding!  I agree!!  It's wonderful.  My daughters and my husband love it as well.  I have used half the amount of cream cheese, it's still fantastic!

Made this dairy-free using room temperature coconut butter (not coconut oil, but the butter made from the whole coconut flesh), and tahini at a 4:1 oz ratio. It turned out amazing!! And because the coconut butter was room temp, the soup didn't require reheating after pureeing it. I just stirred it thoroughly in the still warm sauce pan. Delish and simple recipe!

One of my favorite comfort foods, this soup takes some time (mostly to peel and cut up the squash, but it's worth it. I usually get one large or two small squashes and make a big batch. Sometime I add a dollop of homemade pesto instead of the herbs. Once I adapted it into lobster butternut bisque by coking the squash in stock made from lobster shells instead of chicken broth. And eight ounces of cream cheese is plenty.
Just finished the taste test. Awesome!!!!
Delicious soup! I followed the recipe all the way up to the cream cheese.  One 8-ounce package seemed to be plenty creamy.  Would make again and again.
I made this wonderful soup with vegetable broth.  Best butternut soup recipe I've tried thus far.
Soup was wonderful and all I added was a 1/2 teas of ginger and a smidge of nutmeg.  Enjoy
I love this soup! I've made it at least six times. I roast the  squash for 20-25 minutes first and halve the cream cheese. I'm thinking it'll make a nice Thanksgiving day soup.

I am rating it a 4 because I only added one pkg. cream cheese and it was way more than enough for the soup.  I think two pkgs. would make the cheese overpower the squash flavor.  Very delicious! This is our new favorite.

I thought this tasted pretty good before I added the cream cheese...and I used only 1 package of it.  The cream cheese was still overpowering.  I baked the squash first for 40 min. and then scooped it out.  I might try again without the cream cheese.
I didnt like it but my wife loved it.
Made this with 1 less cream cheese.  It was delicious!

I made this as-is and it's absolutely DELICIOUS...

What a heavenly soup!  I paired it with King's brand Honey Wheat dinner rolls and that was an excellent combination.  In the future I think I'll serve this with some roasted vegetables (probably winter squash, potatoes, carrots, stuff like that) and I think the combination will be great.

This soup is pretty filling and a bit thick, which is what I prefer anyway.

Definitely a wonderful cool-weather recipe!  I can see making this all winter long...
Excellent warm-me-up dinner with salad and crackers.  My husband loves it and I've served it for company with much ooohing and awwwwing.  Thanks .... Carol Hill
Simply outstanding. I used 1/2 the cream cheese and did not miss the fat or calories in this great soup.

Serve with hot Parmesan rolls or garlic bread sticks (homemade of course)
8oz of cream cheese is PLENTY! 4C chicken stock is just right. Can add some mashed potato flakes if soup is too thin. (Don't over do it..it takes a minute for the potato to absorb the moisture) Use a stick blender to puree right in the pot. (No burned fingers or lid exploding like in blender) Puree is a must for creamy texture. You can substitute any kind of winter squash or pumpkin

good , easy , and delicious i boiled the squash in chicken stock also i liked it better before i added the cream cheese and i only used half.  i also  added more pepper and next time im just gonna add a splash of heavy cream and completely leave out the cream cheese but sooo tasty :)
This is very good but I would suggest using only 1 package of cream cheese.
Simple and very tasty; goes well with French bread for dunking.  Definitely recommend using less cream cheese than it calls for though, it came out quite thick.  Or, thin it out with milk.
This is delicious! I made it exactly as the recipe says and it is perfect. The richness and taste are just want I was looking for so my whole family can enjoy it!

I only used one package of cream cheese, I felt two would've been overkill. This needed more flavor, garlic, more onions, maybe cilantro? I will try the other butternut squash soup recipes in an attempt to find the perfect recipe!

Very easy to make, especially after following the advice of other cooks on here to roast the halved squash in the oven first for an hour at 350 degrees. I only used 4 ounces of cream cheese, and it was plenty. I did not have cayenne pepper on hand so I substituted chili powder and a little bit of crushed red pepper. I added some porcini mushroomand thyme ravilois after cooking and it was so yummy!

This is a really good recipe.  I cut the creme cheese in 1/2 and will probably cut a little more next time (but it still tasted wonderful).  I also roasted the squash (brushed with olive oil, fresh roasted garlic, pepper, marjoram & cumin).  I sauteed onion and red bell pepper (cut fine). Used hand blender and warmed.  The consistency is fantastic.  I will play with flavor a little more, but will definitely make again and again.

Delicious and Healthy! I used less butter (only 1 1/2 T.) and used fat free cream cheese. I thought the taste was great, although next time I will experiment with different spices because I thought the majoram was a little strong. The only other thing I did was add more water, because it seemed almost like mashed potatoes instead of soup when I blended it. I will definitely make it again though!

my family loves this recipe. I made many of the changes that previous people stated. I used only 8 oz of low fat cream cheese. Since squash has risen in  price I purchased frozen winter squash in the frozen vege section and works well. I add minced garlic, a couple of apples and a little juice if I have some. Then I puree with my stick blender. Tonight I even added a can of pumpkin and some frozen squash and it is just as yummy!

I didn't change a thing the first time. It came out perfect. The 2nd time I added 1/2 of an acorn squash and it was just as good just a little sweeter. Either way everybody loves it so much I grew my own squash this year. Thanks.
Added a sweet potatoes and a few other veggies but otherwise stuck to it- sour cream with it is delish.
This was great! We cut the cream cheese in half and still found the soup plenty rich. We'll actually try cutting it back a little further next time.
This recipe is fabulous! Very good I followed it exact but left out cayenne pepper. It's one of my favorite soups.

As other reviewers have suggested, I only used 1 package of cream cheese.  I found it interesting that the soup smelled savory, but actually tasted quite sweet (with a little spicy kick!)  Not something I'd do frequently, especially since the kids didn't care for it, but my husband loved it!

I have made this twice.  Both were amazing.  Second time was easier because I simply baked the squash (cut open, remove seeds and place flesh-side down on aluminum foiled pan) for an hour.  I sauteed onion, boiled the water then combined all with the squash and seasonings.   I pureed with little hand-held blender.   So easy!  The flavor is incredible; I added heavy cream because I am out of cream cheese.
Excellent!  As other reviewers noted, 1/2 of the cream cheese is plenty, and I thinned the soup down a bit with more chicken stock.  It was a HUGE hit!
Delicious!  I cut out the cream cheese completely and added 1 cup of fat free yogurt.  I also added 1 potato and 1 apple to increase the consistency and cut down the fat!  Awesome recipe!  Thank you!

I just made this today and we loved it! I followed advice from others to bake the squash because it brings out the flavor and makes it easy to work with. I softened the onions in butter then added the water and bouillon cubes with the spices. I used rubbed sage because I didn't have marjoram and added a pinch of nutmeg. Also upped the cayenne just a bit to our taste. Then I scooped out the baked squash and added to the mix w/ the cream cheese. I used my hand blender to puree it altogether. Excellent recipe! To make a beautiful presentation you could swirl a tsp. of cream around the top of the soup. If you love squash this is a must try. Thanks for the great soup recipe.

I made this soup for my best friend's birthday dinner and it was delicious! The best tips I picked up on this website were to cook the squash, halves face down, in a cake pan with an inch of water at 350 for 1 hour. I then used an ice cream scooper to scoop the squash out and added it to the blender with the cream cheese and chicken broth. I was already sauteing the onion in butter in a saucepan and so it was easy to puree the squash mixture in the blender and then pour it into the pot with the onions and heat through. This reminded me of a soup I used to order at Wolfgang Puck! I highly recommend this one on a cold fall night!
Delicious!!! I took the suggestion of one of the reviewers and added a pear and potato and blended it together. I also added more cayenne pepper and only a couple tablespoons of creams cheese.
Thaks Mary!  I put it all in a 7qt crock pot, and had a ladies lunch! 29 out of 30 ate all of it, and wanted the recipe!  The one who didnt eat it, well, she is wierd anyway! :)
Added 2T pure maple syrup and 1/2 t dried marjoram.  Delicious!

This is a great soup and love making it in the fall.  I peel and cube the squash and place in a crockpot with all ingredients except the cream cheese.  After squash is cooked I add the cream cheese, melt it and use a blender since I don't have a food processor. Yummy!
