Changed the prep. a little.  Roasted a large squash and two med. onions with about half a head of garlic until the squash was tender.  Then pureed all in the food processor.  Doubled all the spices and added a 1/4 t. of Allspice and a bay leaf.  Dropped in chunks of one 8oz. pkg. of cream cheese while simmering on the stovetop.  We all LOVED it.  Had some kick, but not enough to knock you over.  Next time might use a hand mixer or a blender to see if I can get it even smoother.

Delicious absolutely amazing and easy. I used half the cream cheese and cut the squash in half placing it face down on a lightly oiled baking sheet for 20 mins at 375 first then boiled it for 5 mins and then pureed. It was a just a tad lumpy but so darn good. Ive been asked to make it for everyone again next week.

I only used 6 oz. of cream cheese and it was perfect. Very creamy and thick, but the taste was not too strong. I roasted the squash in the oven and it made it easier to work with. Next time I will leave out the cayenne or put an even smaller amount, but it was too spicy. Good soup otherwise.
Fabulous soup - couldn't be easier.  I roasted the squash in the oven with some macintosh apples first and cut down the cream cheese.
Have made this twice in the last week and what a hit!  I did not puree' but left some chunkiness to it, also used only one package of cream cheese and added a can of chicken broth...yummy!
My favorite butternut squash recipe! Delicious & easy!!!

Very good.  I did use some of the suggestions of others ie: bake the squash, garlic, celery, more onion, more cayanne pepper.  I also used FAGE Green fat free Yogurt (Costco, TJ's) Better than Bullion chicken in a jar (Wal-Mart) and blended it all with my Braun hand mixer.  I don't know how I ever made soup without my hand blender.  You can put it in a boiling pot of puree.  So much easier than putting batches in a blender.  Thank you for the recipe.  We love it.

This is a delicious soup, especially because it is a little bit different from other butternut squash soup recipes.  I'm a vegetarian, so I made it with vegetable broth, and that worked well.  As others have mentioned, I used less cream cheese, actually only about 1/4 of a block of neufchatel.  I would recommend only using about this much when you initially blend the soup.  You can always put it back in the blender again with a bit more cream cheese if you decide you want more, but you can't take out the cream cheese once you've blended it in.  Also, I found the soup a little bit thick, so I added a little bit more vegetable broth (about 3/4 cup) to the soup once it was entirely done and blended.  That thinned it out, and it was great!

This recipe is wonderful!  I made it for my extended family and everyone asked for the recipe.  I only used 3-4 oz of cream cheese and roasted the squash first.  I also used a little more cayenne as a personal preference.  Thanks for sharing a  great recipe.

Fabulous!  As others suggested I roasted the squash first, did chicken stock instead of water/cubes and added 1/2 the amount of light cream cheese.  I also drizzled honey on the bowls and would've added a bit of granola w/ cinnamon in the bowl but didn't have any on hand.

This soup is unbelievable!  I have never eaten squash soup, but after reading all of the great reviews, I thought I'd try it!  I did follow some of the other suggestions and cut the squash in half, sprayed with Pam and baked for 40 minutes before cutting and peeling it.  I used 5 boullion cubes and I only used 8 oz. of cream cheese and that was plenty creamy!  My husband kept on going back for more!  Thank you for a great recipe!
YUM- Tho I totally skipped the cream cheese!
Fantastic! Added butter.

This is wonderful altho I was skeptical about squash soup do begin with.  This is a winner.  I have halved it and double it and it is consistantly delicious.  Everyone gives it an A+.  Thanks for the recipe!!
I used less cream cheese but it was still totally unbelievable!  Loved it.    Thanks for the recipe.  Harvest Kitchen Sisters
You can also substitute coconut milk for Philly cheese, roast the cubed butternut squash beforehand and puree only half of it and also add lentils - delicious

Substituted the low-fat cream cheese and also cut back by half a package for half a cup of half-and-half. Bit more onion and when my spice rack took a fall I forgot to add the chicken bullion! But the family didn't notice, and loved it all the same! Amazing, and wish I had more butternut to keep this soup in stock for the winter!
Delicious just the way it is!!!! Can't go wrong with this when teenage boys devour it!

Great soup! Perfect for a chilly autumn day. Used some suggestions and roasted 2 lg. butternut and a lg. onion for about an hour, until I could see the squash start to brown. In a blender pureed squash, onion, cream cheese along with 4 tablespoons butter, and a 48oz can of chicken stock. By the way, 1 package of cream cheese was enough to make it thick and creamy. I was a little heavy handed with the peppers but I do like it spicey.. :-) Made 8 qts and sent some to Mom, sis and the neighbors.  All agreed it hit the spot. Made it twice before writing the review.  Thanks and enjoy.

Delicious recipe.  Made a slight variation to the recipe. I added white asaparus and chives.  Garnished with a beautiful flower.  Quick and easy.  The only time consuming part was cutting and preparing the squash.

This soup has a very subtle, but delicious flavor. I was a little apprehensive about the cream cheese, given I'm not usually a big fan. But it made the soup nice and creamy. My fiancee and I loved it!
Awesome soup.  I did bake the squash first and cut the cream cheese in half.  LOVE IT.

Good recipe - I rated a 4 instead of a 5 because I cannot imagine how thick it would be if I had followed it exactly and used a pound of cream cheese!!!  I had a couple cups extra of squash, so adjusted the amounts as necessary.  It was quite thick even before I added the cream cheese - about the consistency of heavily whipped potatoes.  So I just went with 4 ounces, and still had to add about a cup of water to thin it out.  I generally like a thick and hearty soup, but it was just too thick.  Good flavor, though!  I think next time I may try adding some buttermilk instead of the cream cheese to get the tangy taste.
I did the roasting of the butternut squash and halved the cream cheese and it came out great! I would even use a bit less cream cheese. Added a bit of cumin too- delicious!
Fantastic. Hubby and I agree it is the best soup we have ever had. I made it just like the recipe except used 1 brick of cream cheese (Neufchatel for 1/3 the fat) instead of 2.
so good! Like many others, I used less than half the amount of cream cheese called for and substituted with neufchatel cheese, which is lower in fat. Great recipe, a real keeper!

This soup is easy to make and was delicious!  I am going to take some other readers suggestions on reducing the cream cheese, it was very rich.  Otherwise, I could not get enough of this soup.  This recipe is fabulous.  Thanks!!!!!

This was pretty good, but I wouldn't make it for guests. I only used one pkg of cream cheese because I tried it after one, and it already tasted cream cheesy. Also, I didn't have marjoram, so I used herbes de provence.
Great! Nice flavor.
So yummy! I'd already made 30 trips to the store this weekend, and was out of cream cheese... so I used the Laughing Cow cream cheese flavored wedges and it was still DELICIOUS! And super simple. (:
Used more onion than recipe called for and I used Grreek yogurt and cream cheese combo.  It was amazing...

This soup was really good BUT definitely need to halve the cream cheese - was overpowering. Also, I cooked the squash in the oven to soften it up before scooping it out (cut in half, cut side down in a bit of water in pan).
It was good but it tasted more like potato soup to me.
This recipe is delicious. Since I made the recipe for two I cut everything in half (only used 3/4 of one block of a low-fat cream cheese). My hubby loved it too.

I thought it was delicious but the rest of the family are not big on squash .. I used chicken broth instead of the water and bullion cubes and left out the margoram .. will save the recipe and maybe try again

I baked and seasoned the squash prior. More work, but was worth the flavour payoff. 

Definitely do not use all the cream cheese. 

This soup was delicious however after 2 days it got that grainy texture and I had to throw out.
I made the recipe with the half as much cream cheese.  It was still too much!
Love this soup. I add 1 large potato and the whole family loves it.

This was delicious!  For me, the hardest part was peeling and chopping the squash but once that was done, the rest was a cinch.  I didn't use nearly as much cream cheese as was written; I only used 2/3 of one bar and the full flavor of the squash came through while still being creamy.
used some low sodium canned chicken broth and only one package cream cheese. Very good soup!
I left out the cream cheese and added a spoonfull of fresh Chevre when serving

This always get rave reviews.  Here is how I have chaned the recipe based on trial and error as well as other recommendations:  Cut in 1/2, remove seeds and spray with EVOO. Roast Squash in oven before pealing at 375 for 45 min. OR microwave 1/2 at a time meat side down for 8-10 min.  sub butter for margerine; sub parsley for marjoram; sub all spice for cayenne; add garlic; reduce cream cheese by 1/2; use inverted blender stick.

My family loved it, I substituted 1 package of Neufchatel cheese for the 2 packages of cream cheese.  My family all agreed it was cheesy enough with 1/3 less fat of the cream cheese.  Definitely will cook this one again!
I did not find this to have enough squash flavor. Next time I will follow some of the other reviews, more spices, less cream cheese, and maybe add an apple. Too much cream cheese for my taste.
The cream cheese flavor dominated the taste of the squash, however, it was still very good.
Delicious! So rich and creamy - I added a couple carrots and celery to the sauted mix. My husband is even deeper in love with me after this meal. (:

I substituted the potatoes with one large sweet potato.  I  also added one tablespoon of brown sugar and a tablespoon of ground ginger.  Oh, and one Granny Smith Apple. I made a roux with the butter (I used a whole stick) the onions, celery, brown sugar, ginger, salt and pepper.  The rest I followed as directed.  It is soooooo good!
Made this for the first time on Xmas Eve for a group of 10.  Needless to say I had 10 requests for the recipe.

SO GOOD!! This recipe is awesome! I don't use all the cream cheese, about 1 1/2 packages is perfect. I also love to serve it with a dollop of sour cream (the warm soup and the cold sour cream are great together) and spinkle it with cinnamon... try it next time!
*UPDATE: Still making this recipe after 2 years... still love it!

I made the following changes: Turned out FANTASTIC!
1) Sautéed 1 serrano pepper along with the onion for a little spicy zing. 
2) 1 cup of diced pears (and so used 1 cup less of the squash) 
3) Used only used 1 pk creme cheese
4) Replaced marjoram with sage

First time ever trying butternut squash and wow did this recipe deliver.  The little bit of cayenne really hit the spot, even my 8 year old boy loved it.. we had it with garlic bread. The next day,(today)off the bus, the kids ate it cold and used it as a kind of dip for a sandwich before church. Definitely this recipe will now be on regular rotation. One extra is that we roasted the squash in the oven beforehand, if you do this be prepared for extra time for it. We also doubled the cream cheese, but since we aren't an exact measurement family we probably used more squash also. Yummy!

Killer!!!  I made this with a carton of chicken broth and recommended amt of squash.  I kicked up the pepper, and used only 4 oz of cream cheese-  sauteed the onion in 1 T. olive oil-  definitely will make again for MYSELF as a treat!

I have made this recipe dozens of times for soup suppers at church during Lent, and it is my most requested recipe. I am a vegetarian, so used a Kosher "chicken" cube which contains neither meat nor gluten. (I've never asked what IS in it!) I only use half the cream cheese and have also found roasting the squash beforehand does make life a lot easier.

Awesome!  I roasted the Butternut for 1 hr. at 425.  I also halved the butter, added 1/2-1 c. more water, omitted Cayenne & Marjoram (didn't have) and only did 1 pgk. cream cheese. Super flavorful and creamy!

I have this recipe in my recipe box at home--it's the ONLY one I use! This soup is so good and so addictive!  I didn't change a thing.  Bought 2 large butternut squash today & will be making this soup tonight.  DEFINITELY, prepare your squash by slicing down the middle, turning cut side down on a sprayed pan and BAKE for an hour at 350 until fully roasted.  I can just taste it now. .  . :-)  Yummy and so good for you!
So yum! Half the cream cheese is MORE THAN enough (And I love cream cheese!) I added a bit more salt and pepper and a dash of nutmeg.
This soup is really good! It is easy to prepare and it tastes amazing! I used vegetable broth instead of chicken broth, and I added paprika and a little bit of cream before serving.

I will give 5 stars because this recipe is always my base but I don't follow it word for word, as is 3 stars. As you will see with many of the other reviews. This morning I decided I will never 'cut up' butternut  raw again because my hand is still sore. My husband got a 4.5 pound squash - 2 pounds is about six cups. Cook in the oven before... Taste better and so much easier. 
You must LOVE cream cheese to add that much. You can also substitute heavy cream, milk, potatoes, or a milk/flour/butter thickener. 
This soup is simple and tasty - great for a cold Wisconsin winter.
I added more crushed red pepper for a kick. Yummy soup - very easy to make. Can't wait to make it again!

I thought it was a very tasty soup. I used a food processor (since I didn't have a blender handy), and I thought it added too much air to the soup. Next time, I will use a food mill. Substituted rosemary for the marjoram.
a wonderful recipe! Tried making this soup for the first time- I think it's my new favorite !

delish. I followed other peoples recommendations and reduced the cream cheese to 1 block and added a little cumin at the end. I also put it in the blender rather then food processor, just be sure to loosen top a little to allow steam to escape. My husband loved it and hates butternut squash. Did I mention how much he hates it.

Don't get me wrong, the taste of this soup is fantastic but it needs a little tweeking.  If you follow the recipe perfectly, you'll find (as did I) that this soup is way, way, way too thick.  If this soup is the only thing you'll have for dinner, then it's okay.  If you plan to use it as an appetizer, add some more chicken broth to get it to the consistency that you'll prefer.  You can also get by using only one cream cheese.  Everyone enjoyed the soup but agreed it was too rich.  Good flavor just too thick!

Loved it but definitely made some tweaks. ..if you want a bit of a healthy twist on it......try substituting coconut oil for butter.  Also the recommendations of cinnamon, garlic and nutmeg is a must! I also left out the potato as I like my squash soup to have mostly that squash  flavour
I made this last night with 1/2 the cream cheese, very good.   I warmed up left-over for lunch today and topped it with grated cheese and oven dried cherry tomatoes.  Nice!

I really like this soup, the only thing I changed was the amount of cream cheese, I only used one.  Everything else stayed the same.
My family really liked it.  Thank you, will make again !!

I agree with many of the comments that it needs a little something extra.  I added ginger, chili powder and garlic.  I could not imagine putting two bricks of cream cheese in though.  It was plenty thick with one.
so easy!  soo soo good.  i only used one package of the cream cheese and cannot imagine it any creamier.
Wow, lots of suggestions which I read quite a few. Used only one cream cheese. This recipe is defintely a keeper. You can have many variations and still create an incredible tasting soup. Thanks.
Loved it!
I also used only one package of cream cheese.  A very tasty and very rich soup.
I made this for a wine dinner I hosted. It went beautifully with Chardonnay!

Savory, creamy, rich and complex.  This soup is very good and very easy.  I had some left over chunked butternut squash that I used for a different soup recipe (we did not like that one!) so I was looking for something that I could do with it, with other ingredients that I had on hand.  I had already boiled the butternut squash, so followed the recipe, except I did not cook it all together for 20 minutes.  I just put it all together, carefully measuring out the right measurements of squash and water.  I put it all in the blender and had wonderful soup in about a minute.  This is seriously like a five star restaurant soup recipe, it would be wonderful served in demitasse cups as a starter to a meal.  Thanks for posting, I will use this recipe again and again!
Absolutely delicious! Added one large carrot, 4 stalks of celery and used fat free cream cheese.

I away make this soup for thanksgiving and Christmas and special occasion, everyone loves it and will continue to make it. The kids like it as well. I add a bit more cayenne pepper slightly more and it perfect.

This was one of the tastiest soups I've made. If this had've been served to me at a high-end restaurant I would've been super pleased! I made very few changes: I used shallots instead of regular onions; used only 1/2 a block of cream cheese instead of the 2; used olive oil rather than butter and finally, used veg stock. I also baked squash for 45mins for ease of peeling. This was creamy and very flavorful!
Delish!! 1 pkg cream cheese is definately enough. I like to add about 1/2 tsp curry powder just to add a little depth to the flavour. I was asked to plant more butternut squash next year!
Love this recipe!!!

This was absolutely delicious. I've never made this type of soup before. But I had bought the cubed, ready to use box of butternut squash from Costco and needed to use it up. I read through the reviews and based upon the majority of the reviews, I used only one package of cream cheese and used chicken stock instead of bouillion. I also added a couple of turns of freshly grated nutmeg at the end. I used my immersion blender because frankly, I hate the whole process of moving from one container to the other. I also cooked it longer, more like 30 minutes, before adding the cream cheese. I think this soup is adaptable in many ways, using an apple, white wine etc. I'd give this recipe a 4 1/2 stars if I could. Give it a try!
The only thing I did different was cut the cream cheese in half. It was plenty thick with just 8 ounces. Everyone loved it

To Die For!!! I made this last fall, and twice in the last week. Everyone raves over this soup. So good and rich. Smooth and creamy. Warms you up on fall nights. I follow the recipe exactly as written. I always use all the cream cheese. I plan on making this as a vegetarian option at my Halloween chili party this year. I will be making a double batch though, because I will guarantee you every non-veggie will want it too!! I use an immersion blender and blend it right in the pot. Velvety smooth. :)

This soup is absolutely delicious. 
I only added about 1/2 a package cream cheese and I thought it was more than enough. 
I will definitely make this soup again!
This was easy and delicious. The cayenne added a nice warmth to it.  I used dried sage instead of marjoram and used half the cream cheese. I will definitely make this again.

I wish I’d only put in one package of cream cheese. As it was it more like squash-flavoured cream cheese soup rather than creamy squash soup. It took a lot of doctoring but I finally got it to a great soup despite the cream cheese.
I used half the cream cheese but followed the recipe otherwise.  We loved it.  Made it 5 times now.

This was lovely!  I had leftover squash from another recipe and was pleased to see that I had all the other ingredients on hand as well.  This was simple, quick and delicious!  I am sure I will make it again, although I think I will only use 1/2 the cream cheese next time.
Yummy!

Excellent recipe!  Prebake the squash and 1/2 the cream cheese though.  I also tried another suggestion which was to add a few tablespoons of balsamic vinegar when blending the cream cheese. It was delicious and definately gave the soup a different flavor.  I asked my guests to taste test it with and without the vinegar and they chose with!
Excellent.  FYI - we use 1/2 the cream cheese and everyone likes it even better.

I loved this.  I too used 1/2 to 3/4 of just one cream cheese.  And I added 2 fresh garlic gloves.  And I too put the squash in the oven after I chopped it up for about 15 min.  It was very good.  I can't wait to make it again.

I found using the ingredients asked for, and the amounts.  The end result was too bland for my taste.  Two packages of cream cheese, this favour seemed to dominate the result. Also using the amounts asked for I have way more then six servings.  I hope it freezes.  Will not try this again.

This is a yummy soup.  I have made it with and without the cream cheese.  Both were good, my boyfriend prefers it less creamy w/out the cheese added.  I like it a little thicker with the cheese.  Will try half the amount next time.  A very tasty soup either way.
Instead of using less cream cheese I added about 2 cups more water, Also I had a large Butternut Squash, almost 2 cups more than the recipe called for. Soup was very good!

I made this for Thanksgiving last year and my guests have been raving about it ever since (and insisting that I make it again this year). I roasted the squash beforehand and used just 1/2 a block of light cream cheese and it turned out just right. I have a newfound appreciation for squash!!

This is really good soup. I used about 150g of cream cheese and it was very creamy and delicious. Dh said it could do with a little more cream cheese, but I didn't think so. The cream cheese gives it a slightly sweet, very faint abstract taste that suits it well. I baked the squash with two cloves of garlic. The only problem was, this recipe took ages from start to finish. I made strawberry jam in about half the time. I gave this recipe 4 stars for the taste, though, not on timing as it was my choice to roast the 2 squash I had. I have tasted a better soup at a restaurant that I'm still trying to mimic. Thankyou for the recipe. Even my kids ate it!

Great stuff, the squash flavor was still a little too strong.  So I added a pinch more pepper (I omitted the cayenne-usually have bad results with the kids when I add that).  A pinch of garlic and onion powder and a half pinch of thyme.
PERFECT!
Amazing!  I added spinach to the soup and let it cook for the last 8 minutes and used half the amount of cream cheese.  Delicious!!

That is delicious.  Simple flavors that blended well together.  And much easier to make than I thought it would be.  I did add a bit more squash and only used one 8 oz. package of cream cheese.  And as a warning- it makes rather more than I suspected it would.  More than my husband and I could put down in 2 meals.
I would say about 45 minutes for prep if the squash has to be peeled, but other wise it was perfect!!
JUST PERFECT!!!!!YUMMMMMYYYYY
Very rich. Next time I'll cut the cream cheese in half. The taste was very good

I didn't read the comments of others to first roast the squash until after I had it cubed.  So I went with the original recipe, except I used butter instead of margarine.  Also, I didn't have marjoram, so I substituted 1 tsp coriander, 1 Tbsp curry powder, and 1/2 tsp nutmeg.  I also used only one (8 oz.) package cream cheese instead of 2 as the recipe called for.  It was very tasty!  Although I think next time I will try only 4 oz. cream cheese.  This recipe is simple, forgiving, and can easily be tweeked and experimented with to suite personal taste.
Delicious

I'm a vegetarian, so I used vegetable bouillon, plus I doubled the cayenne.  Other than those changes, I followed the recipe as it read.  Even the picky eater in the house liked it!  We're planning on having it for Thanksgiving.

YUMMY.  Like so many others, I tweaked this recipe quite a bit.  Because of time limitations, I baked the squash in a pan of 1 inch of water, skin side up - yesterday.  I also added 1 large sweet potato that I cooked in advance as well.  Today I melted the butter added the onion - 1 whole - and besides adding the marjoram, I added about 2 teaspoons of curry powder.  I only used about 3/4 of a package (6 oz.) of cream cheese. Which gave it a rich, but not overpowering taste.  It needed a little salt, and is so incredibly tasty.  I was making it in advance for a party but I like it so much I know I'm going to have to make another batch.
LOVE IT! :)
Mouth watering.
Very good, made a few suggested changes so rated 4 stars.

I roasted the squash and then put the soft meat into the dutch oven with the onions and sauteed. This is so good. I added some Louisiana hot sauce instead of the cayenne pepper and was able to control the heat and could add more at the table. Surprisingly filling.
ok but not great...a bit bland.  Might make again but with some extras.

This soup is very good !   I roasted the squash for about 45 minutes at 350 and then chopped it and saute'd it in the skillett before blending it with the cream cheese.  I also used about half the cream cheese as called for.
 Note: When decreasing the cream cheese you will need to decrease the water some and then add as needed while cooking the soup. If the soup is too runny, just cook until it thickens to desired consistency.
This dish is a little time consuming, but very worthwhile.  I served it as a first course for Thanksgiving and everyone loved it!  This is a keeper.
Very nice. Tastes better with a splash of cream sherry in with the butter and real chicken in it too.

Everyone absolutely love this recipe.  I entertain a group that tends to be picky about the sides that I serve but tends to enjoy my main course.  Today, almost everyone asked for a second portion of the soup, and no one didn't complete the first portion.  I followed the recipe as listed, but only used one 8oz. pack of cream cheese after reading some of the other reviews.  It was VERY creamy with just the one, and I would consider tasting the soup first if you plan to add the second.  This is an all around winner!

This was good  I made it for my husband who was coming down with a bad head cold - he loved it but I have to admitt it needed something - maybe a good shot of wine wouldve hit the spot. I'll make it again.
Amazing!  And no one knew that they were eating squash!

The reviews were unanimous: waaaay too thick!  I used the full 2 blocks of cream cheese and it was overkill.  My son actually compared this *soup* to mashed potatoes!  That said, hubby and I agreed that it may be worth trying again with a whole lot less cream cheese and maybe a little extra spice.

I made this yesterday and it turned out great!  I made a few changes, I added garlic, used vegetable stock, used rosemary instead of marjoram, omitted the cayenne.  I also used only 1pkg of cream cheese. I served this in individual french onion soup bowls with pastry crust over the top.  Delicious, just like at a dinner we were at a few weeks ago. A perfect appetizer!

OMG, this was SO good!  I made it as written, but cut it in half for just hubby and me.  I did reduce the cream cheese by half (I used 4 oz. for half the recipe) and it was plenty rich.  I'm glad I didn't use any more.  Hubby was skeptical when I told him what I was making for dinner (he's not a big squash fan) but he really liked it!  I wish I'd made a full batch.  The cayenne gave it a nice tang; really added to the flavor.  Thanks for sharing!
Definitely only needs 1/2 the cream cheese.  I made the recipe as is and that is the only change I would make for next time.
only 8 oz of cream cheese..roasted squash w olive oil and garlic and added half and half

I loved this recipe but as always tweeked it a bit by adding some curry powder, salt, nutmeg and about a cup of Greek yogurt...the yogurt gives it a zing because I felt it was just too smooth and I wanted a contrast to the sweet of the squash.  I plan on changing this recipe a little each time just to see what progresses...maybe next time with beets and spinach?

I roasted the squash in the oven like other reviewers had suggested and it was super easy to skin and cube up to add to the soup. I also used vegetable stock to make it vegetarian and only added one package of cream cheese. (And some garlic. I put garlic in just about everything.) The first night it was kind of bland, so next time I'll either add more spices or simmer spices in the vegetable stock while the squash roasts. I also felt like it was a bit too thick, so next time I'll halve the cream cheese. Or make it ahead of time. ANYWAY. The second day it was awesome! I added about a cup more broth and it's fantastic.

This was amazing!  Relatively easy to make and so darn good.  I used only 1 1/2 cream cheese squares and did not measure the cayenne so may have added more than it called for.  It had a spicy kick at the end but not the kind of hot where you drink endless amounts of water while eating  it.   Next time I will add more water as it got a little thick as it cooled.  Will definitely make this again.  My kids even liked it!  Such a nice fall/winter meal.
Great soup, very filling and rich.  Used a little extra cayenne, substituted oregano for marjoram and one pack of cream cheese.

Wow!  Wow!!  Wow!!!  I used one block of cream cheese (1/3 lower fat) and it was wonderful!  My 2 year old got a taste and came running back to me saying, "Mommy, I neeeeed moooore soup."  Go figure, my husband said it was ok, but the rest of us loved it.  I halved the squash, seeded it,  and nuked it for 4 minutes to soften it.  It was much easier to peel and cube then.
This was not bad but the cayenne pepper was not good in it, sorry. Had I left that I think it would have been a little better
This is the kind of recipe that makes people fall in love with you when you make it for them.

This soup is delicious! I did give it 4 stars because I made some changes.   First, I baked the squash at 375 for about half an hour. This made it much easier to cut! I also only had 2cups chicken broth so I added 2 cups water and a lot of spices. I also added 1 sliced jalapeño pepper to spice it up. Following reviewer suggestions, I only added about half the cream cheese and I'm glad for that. It would have been too rich if I used the full amount.   Delicious soup I do recommend the added jalapeño! As a side note, I the soup is grainy try blending for longer.

I just made this mostly following the directions exactly(I roasted the squash first) and it tastes pretty good to me! I may have thrown in more cayenne and I didn't measure the squash, but I made a half recipe bc I read that one squash is about 3 cups. I'll try other people's suggestions in the future. This was my fist time cooking butternut squash and I can honestly say I'll do it again! I gave it 4 stars because while I think it's delicious, in sure there is room for improvement.
This is one of the best soups I have ever eaten! Creamy, comforting and delicious... I only used 1 tub of cream cheese and it was plenty enough.
The cream cheese makes this taste like a cheese soup, and reminds me of a broccoli and cheese soup. Which I'm personally not a fan of.
I am drinking a cup of this wonderful soup as I type this review. Excellent! It's 40 degrees & cloudy out here in Ct. This warms me right up. Will definitely make this many more times, thanks Mary.

This is a really good butternut squash recipe, although I think the restaurant versions are better. I doubled the recipe and added some sherry (I peeked at other recipes!). The butternut squash is a real pain to cut so I took the advice of another reviewer and baked it in the over for 45 minutes. Turned out terrific, but just took a long time. I can't wait to do this soup again for my family at Thanksgiving!

this was the First time I have ever made soup with butternut squash, I made some changes, I used fatfree cream cheese and i used a can of chicken broth inst.  This was Very Good :) and my family loved it

Yum! I roasted the squash and scooped it out. Used sauted onion and garlic, also pepper and tumeric. Skipped the cream cheese. Don't want all that saturated fat! Pureed with chicken stock to desired consistency. Looking forward to squash season next year! I think I'll plant some just so I can make plenty of this soup!

This is a great recipe.  I only add about 1/3 of cream cheese, a dash of heavy cream, 1 celery stick and about 5 baby carrots. If yiu don't have marjoram, a sprinke of oregano or basil, a pinch of salt.
Absolutely delicious!!!  My husband loved it so much and said it tasted like something you would find at a gourmet restaurant.  I also roasted the squash at 400 for 45 minutes before adding it in.

Unbelievably good! I too baked my squash in the oven first. I used butter instead of margarine, 2 cans of chicken broth and cut the cream cheese in half. I didn't bother getting out the blender and all of the parts, I simply used my immersion blender right in the pot. Next time I will cut down on the cream cheese a bit more or try reduced fat cream cheese. This is now one of my favorite soups recipes and will be great during my Michigan winters.

I prefer to use the broth and no water, 1/2 the cream cheese and 2 diced pears added to the saute'.  Either way a wonderful fall/winter soup that everyone loves.  Can add a small dollop of sour cream on top when served.
This has got to be the most delicious soup I have ever made. The cream cheese gives it the most creamy texture and taste. Just wonderful!
This soup tastes great!

This is the best butternut squash soup I have ever tasted - way better than most restaurants'.  I did bake the squash at 395 for about 30-40 minutes just until I can pierce the skin with a fork.  I then cut and cubed.  I did not use any cream cheese and the soup was still so delicious.  I used real butter rather than margarine, and seasoned with black pepper and nutmeg, and added a dollop of sour cream at serving.  Cannot wait to make more throughout the season!
Takes a bit of time to cook, but it tastes awesome. My boyfriend, who says he hates squash, thought it was the best soup I've ever made. Definitely a winner.
I've made many times.  We love every spoonful!  I changed a few things, using ideas from other reviewers.

I love this soup! I've made it many many times without altering a thing. It's creamy and flavorful. I'd suggest following the recipe as written before following the changes made by other reviewers. You'll find the changes to be unnecessary. Also, peeling a butternut squash isn't hard with a good vegetable peeler. Hope you give it a try :)

Great recipe but I made several changes. Butter instead of margarine, almost doubled the squash, used half the cream cheese, chicken broth instead of water/chicken boullion and added more cayenne, pepper, marjoram and a pich of salt. My family loved it.
Wonderful recipe, however I would recommend that you not use all of the bouillon cubes.  I've found that 1 or 2 do just fine.
tasted like nothing but cream cheese and came out baby food consistency.  I added some apples and apple cider vinegar which only had the effect of making it taste like sour cream cheese baby food.
This was the best soup!  I have always been heistant to try squash soup, but this was great!  I only used 1 package of cream cheese.  LOVED IT!  Will make again! Thanks for sharing

Sorry, but I just didn't think this soup was very flavorful.  Maybe my squash was not up to par...I measured everything carefully and didn't stray from the recipe (except to only use 1 block of cream cheese instead of 2, and to use chicken broth instead of water & bouillon).  I sprinkled a little cinnamon sugar on top of my bowl and that was a big improvement.  But, it was very easy to make, and maybe I'll try making it again with a better squash!  Thanks Mary for sharing.

Excellent. My husband and son who said you are making what? loved it!  I used 3 cups of chicken broth instead of boullion.  Only (1) package of cream cheese and I cooked the squash in the oven first for 40 minutes at 350.  Good winter meal with biscuits.  Thanks for sharing I will definately make again.
My husband even loves this soup! I usually cut down to one block of cream cheese and it is still so yummy.

I made this for the first time and doubled it for our family of five.  I did not make any alterations to the recipe, but wish I had!  Way too much cream cheese!  One 8oz.  Package would have been plenty!  It overpowered the soup and we couldn't taste the squash.  I would like to try it again sometime but with half the cream cheese.
Excellent soup!  I made it with the one block on cream cheese and suggested and it was fabulous.  I will definitley be making this again.
I made this for me and my husband, we both loved it, very tasty.

I liked it a lot, the rest of the family thought it tasted too much like cream cheese.  Lovely texture.  Froze the leftovers as individual servings and those came out a little thicker, a little spicier, maybe even better than the original servings.  If frozen, reheat very slowly - don't let it boil!

EXCELLENT! Made this for my family - even my 12 y/o daughter loved this! Based on the previous reviews I decided to add one package of cream cheese and taste before adding the other...this was a good idea because it was perfect with just one cream cheese package! I would highly recommend using only one cream cheese! I also baked the squash first at 350 for 40 minutes. It's just easy to work with this way. This soup was delicious and satisfying and I will make it again!
It could maybe use some more spice, depending on your tastes, but it was really good, hearty, and flavorful.

Tons of different variations to this soup. This recipe works well w/o cream cheese and marjoram.  I also followed other reviews and baked the butternut (brushed with olive oil/garlic) for an hour at 350. Serve with some homemade toasted bread. Great warm meal for a cold fall night!
This was fantastic!  I added a little less of the stock than what it called for. It thickened it up. Thanks for the great recipe!
Really good as is. It tastes quite rich and has a lovely flavor.

I was not sure I would like this but decided to try it since I had a butternut squash and only 1 8oz cream cheese -low fat. I roasted the squash by halving it and baking face down for about 40 min at 375. It was almost soft when I took it out but was able to peel and cube. I then continued and cooked it on stove for about 20 more min to blend flavors. Then I used my vitamix and put in cream cheese and soup. From there I poured it back in the pot  and It sat on my stove most of the afternoon. I just reheated for dinner....yum! Better than I thought! I also used quart of chicken broth instead of water and chicken bouillon.

Very good!  Didn't have an onion so I put the butter in with the chicken base (never use bullion cubes!).  Also only used one 8oz. cream cheese.  Replaced marjoram with thyme as it was all I had.  Very creamy, very sweet.  All 3 of my boys, ages 1/5/10, ate 2 bowls!  A great keeper for chilly fall days!

Great soup.  I only added one package of cream cheese and it was MORE than enough.  You could easily cut that to half and it would still be yummy.  I also used fresh marjoram which made my kitchen smell wonderful.

My husband made this and it came out delicious tasting but runny, maybe because he only used 4 oz of the cream cheese?  I think it had enough cream cheese, it didn't overpower the squash.  My husband did a few things differently:  like I said less cream cheese, he roasted a whole onion and the butternut squash, he also roasted a whole head of garlic and used that, he used 3 cups of chicken broth instead of the water/bouillon combo, and he added some nutmeg.  Like I said, the flavor was excellent, we just need to work on the consistency the next time we make it.  It's definitely a side soup type of thing, not hardy.
Tasty, but, if you ask me, even tastier without the cream cheese!

Awesome!  My husband, "the chef" modified this, by adding celery, garlic, honey, nutmeg, cinnamon, and some sugar.  He advised me to adjust to taste buds, turned out great!  I agree with other reviewers only need 1 8oz package of cream cheese.  I used fat free, I could not tell a difference.  Lots of flavor and creaminess.  Used two huge squash and made a gallon of soup.  Also, a lot of reviewers roasted the squash first, but I followed the recipe and boiled until I had a great stock base with flavor and the squash was rtender enough to puree.  Will make again definitely!
I have made this recipe twice now and everyone loved it.  This one is a keeper!

I used a Fuji apple with the onion, sauteed in mirco... then added everything, this was ready in 15 min's! I had already roasted my squash. I did not add cream cheese, I only added a small amount of half and half. Delicious. Served with day old bread, to dip! WOW! Kids loved it too! Thank you!
Great soup! Better then I expected. I did also cut the cream cheese in half. It was super creamy with just 1 bar.

DON'T use that much cream cheese! 3 stars as is, but probably 5 stars with less. The best bites were right after it left the stove, when it was not as thick as it turned out, after it cooled down. I wish I had read the suggestions before cooking it.
So delicious!  I left out the cayenne pepper though and it was perfectly spicy for me.

This is the easiest and best soup!  The only thing I did differently was to bake the squash at 350 degrees for 30-40 minutes with a little olive oil/salt/pepper.  Amazing!  Thanks so much for the recipe.  It's going to get a lot of use this fall.
Excellent, very rich and creamy!  We made it over the holidays for a small get together, everyone truly enjoyed it! Fat City!
Absolutely delicious. I did use broth instead of water and reduced the amount of cream cheese to 3 tablespoons.

I made a few minor changes to this recipe and have made it for several occasions. Everyone always wants the recipe. I cut my squash into halves, drizzled with olive oil, and roasted on 375 for 40 minutes before moving on with the recipe. I used 4 cups chicken broth in place of the water/bouillon, a combination of cumin and oregano in place of the marjoram, and only 1 8oz block of reduced fat cream cheese. This soup is hearty enough to be served with some good chunky bread as a meal all on its own.

Okay, so with all the rave reviews, I had to include this on my very first full-out Thanksgiving day menu for my family of 16!  As a newlywed, I was eager to use all the new China and Silverware.  Anyway, I made this soup the day before, and found it to be only average; I personally didn't care too much for the taste.  However, my Aunt and my sister raved about it, and took all the leftovers home!  To each his own, I suppose.  I just couldn't eat more than a couple spoonfuls of this, as the taste is just so...rich.  I did convert this from its original 6 serving recipe to a 15 serving recipe, and only used 2 of the 5 packets of cream cheese it originally called for.
i didnt use as much cream cheese, can imagine it with as much because its such a rich soup. Great soup, very rich.

This was very simple to make & was a perfect side to smoked pork chops!
I gave this 4 instead of 5 simply because, like quite a few other reviewers, I made some changes to the written recipe.
I, too, roasted the squash in the oven.  IMO this not only adds flavor but adds to the ease in preparation.
I'm doing WW so I reduced some of the fat & calories by using fat free cream cheese and only half of the called for amount.  I also used fat free margerine.
I thought the soup was very rich & creamy.  I believe using the full amount of cream cheese in the recipe may have overwhelmed the mellow flavor of the squash.  
With these simple changes, this recipe came in at only 3 points per serving according to the WW recipe builder.  Def. a keeper for my winter soup recipe box!

My favorite squash soup recipe! Followed the recipe and really liked it! Modified later by adding 1/4 tsp nutmeg and substituting 1/4 cup half and half for the cream cheese and loved it even more! Easier to just roast the squash whole then cut in half & scrape out insides  rather than peeling & cubing. I make this all the time in the fall & winter months, it's a hearty soup that tastes great!Thanks for sharing!
My husband and I both really enjoyed this soup.  I baked the squash for 30 minutes before adding to the recipe.  YUM
I absolutely loved this delicious squash soup.  I can't wait to make it again.  Thank you!!

I have to say this soup came out delicous. I also baked the squash first. The only problem i had is when it says to add the squash and cream cheese in the blender, do you add the broth also? and if you bake the sqaush do you boi; the rest of the ingrediants seperate while the squash is baking? Anyway I did use the two blocks of cream cheese- reduced fat- and it came out great. Thanks for the recipe.
My family loved this.  The only change I made was instead of pealing the squash I roasted in the oven and the peel came off.
I used half the amount of cream cheese. It's not the easiest thing to make, but boy does it taste like heaven! I've made it 3 times in the past 2 months! Well worth the effort!

Wow! I had to create an account just to comment on this recipe. I have been eating a great butternut squash soup at a restaurant for years, but I think I like this one better! And it's so easy to make! I just halved and microwaved my squash face down for 10 minutes or so until it was easily scooped out. Then I just added the squash, sauteed onion, and other ingredients right into the blender, instead of into a pot. I also added a little extra cayenne pepper just because I like a little extra spice. And less than half the cream cheese, but it was still a very rich and creamy soup. Will be eating this all winter!
I made this recipe for Thanksgiving and it was a hit.  I had never had Butternut squash soup before, but it will be a staple at my dinner table.

This was AMAZING !! I roasted my squash in the oven and used butter for cooking onions ..  So yummy .. I did not have bouillon cube and  used low sodium broth .. Added salt and pepper  to taste ... . Husband said it was the best he had .. This is a keeper!

This soup was fantastic! I used one block of cream cheese but that is because I increased the servings a bit. I ended up using two good size butternut squashes, roasted in the oven cut side up in two baking dishes with a quarter inch of water and covered with foil. I sprayed them with butter spray and sprinkled on kosher salt, pepper and garlic powder. Roasted at 400 for an hour until tender. I used 3 cans of roasted garlic flavored chicken broth. Next time I won't even need to bother with the onions and butter and saved calories to boot. The flavored chicken broth gives it plenty of good flavor. It was excellent and everyone at the party I took it too really enjoyed it.

This is absolutely the best butternut squash soup recipe, EVER.  I did modify this recipe just a tad.  As another viewer recommended roasting the squash with olive oil, salt, pepper and garlic for 1 hour @ 350.  This was absolutely the key in making this soup stand out from all the others.  I also only used one 8 oz package of cream cheese.  Once I added the 1st package I really didn't see the need for the second one.  I also ommitted the cayenne pepper, only because I don't like it, the garlic from roasting the squash gave this recipe the kick that it needed.    

I do not have a food processor so I used my hand held wand blender, worked perfectly.  I don't recommend using low fat or fat free cream cheese only because I think it will take away from the purpose of using it in the soup.  Sometimes a recipe needs that fat to make all the other flavors combine.  

If I could give this recipe more than 5 stars I would.  Hands down, just awesome!!!! I can't wait to share it with friends and family.
I followed the directions exactly and the result had no taste at all.  Just tasted like you blended up a squash.  What a waste of ingredients!

This was my first time eating butternut squash soup (and I think butternut squash in general) and I found out it just wasn't for me! Too sweet or something I think. However, my boyfriend gives this recipe 5 stars and ate his portion as well as the rest of mine :)

I followed some of the other reviews and used 1/2 the cream cheese (plenty!) and used 4 cups of vegetable broth instead of water and boullion.  It turned out great - even my father, who won't touch most butternut squash recipes because he doesn't like his veggies "sweet," loves this one.
This was really delicious & easy.  I used an immersion blender which made it even easier.  You can add more spices or more onion or garlic to spice it up if you want.  Great recipe!
It only took 1 butternut squash to get the six cups needed.  I wish I had known that going into it- since I cooked two.  Good taste, but it kind of looks like nacho cheese.
Very delicious easy to make
This soup is by far the best butternut squash soup I've had in my life! I'm amazed I even made this! It's probably the best soup Ice ever had, even my husband agrees!!!

This was exquisite. I oven-roasted all of the vegetables together with a couple of cloves of garlic and an apple, then put them in the food processor and into a sauce pan to simmer. I used only a dollop of cream cheese, but the soup was still very rich. To finish, I toasted some pumpkin seeds with a bit of roasted garlic and olive oil and sprinkled them over the bowls of soup, then drizzled over a bit of boiled apple cider mixed with water. One of the best recipes I have tried from Allrecipes!

It was really yummy and had great flavor. It was way too think with 16 total ounces of the cream cheese. Next time I make this I am going to only add 8 ounces. With how thick it is, it makes a great chip dip!

Delicious!  And not only that, but it is SO easy, as well.  I took previous reviewers advice and baked the squash for about an hour beforehand.  I also only used one 8 oz. package of cream cheese and it was plenty. I also salted it to taste, which ended up being about 1/2 - 1 teaspoon.  I was surprised salt isn't in the original recipe, as it truly enhances the flavor.  I will most definitely be making this again and again.  And again!

This is a definite 5* recipe!  So good and so simple.  I also only used 1 pkg cream cheese and may use even less next time as it was still very rich.  There were no leftovers!  Thanks for a new way to use squash!

Husband and 4 year old son love it!  I have also made this in the crock pot.  Let cook on low for 6-8 hours until squash is tender.  Puree with immersion blender.  Add cream cheese and let the hot soup soften it for 5 minutes.  Puree again with immersion blender to blend cream cheese.  I freeze leftovers in muffin tins for perfect individual serving sizes.  Freezes and reheats well.

The best soup I've ever made! I used chicken stock instead of bouillon and used half (even less than half, actually) of the cream cheese this called for. I also roasted the squash before I added it. I couldn't get enough of it and will make it all fall and winter! Wonderful, wonderful recipe!
I also tweaked this recipe a bit-I added a small apple, a couple cloves of garlic, some thyme, & greatly increased the amount of cayenne pepper.  It turned out great-the family loved it!

This was excellent!   I have tried many other butternut squash soup recipes and most have apples or curry, which I am not fond of.  This was great, however, I did use only ONE cream cheese, as was suggested by many.  Two would definitely be too much!  I put a bit too much cayenne in it though and it's a bit "hot" even for me.  I'll measure it next time!!!   Now I'll have something good to do with the millions of squash we grew last summer.
We will make this every fall for sure! Definitely use chicken broth instead and half the cream cheese as suggested.
Great recipe  Very flavorful and easy.  I too cut back on cream cheese to 6 oz.

This soup was so good I had to comment!  I bought two smaller squashes, and microwaved them for 3 minutes to soften the skin.  It was easy to peel and cube them after that.  I substituted butter for margarine, used chicken broth instead of water and bullion cubes, added a little garlic, doubled the cayenne, and used half the cream cheese.  The result was heavenly!!
Really creamy and tasteful! Maybe I would drop one of the chicken bouillon and only use 3 as I found it gave almost "too much" flavour :-)

This is good, but not a show stopper so only four stars. The squashy creaminess is a pleasant flavor. I doubled the cayenne pepper and didn't have marjoram so used a Tbls. of dried parsley. Only used one package of cream cheese and it seems plenty thick and rich.

I'm so glad I took others advice and cut the cream cheese by 1/4.  It was great but if you use the entire 16 oz of cream cheese, I think it would over power the squash.  We also cooked the squash in the oven to make it easier to peel and cube.  Glad we did.  Thanks to all with the great advice.

I only used 1/2 the cream cheese and cooked the squash ahead of time in the oven so it didn't have to simmer so long on the stove. I also doubled the amount of spices and added salt, but I like my food with a lot of zing. I can't give this recipe five stars since I made changes, but I loved what I ended up with.
THIS WAS NO GOOD...REALLY THICK WILL NOT MAKE AGAIN**
Easy to make! Roasted squash 375 deg oven for 45 mins. Squash was tender and easy to scoop out. Added a bit more cayenne. I will definitely make this recipe again!

I used one pkg of cream cheese, added 1/4 tsp of ground nutmeg and ground ginger plus a pinch of ground cloves.  I used chicken stock instead of water.  Served it for an early thanksgiving meal with a large group and everyone loved it.

My family and I didn't expect to like this soup at all. We have never been lovers of butternut squash or thick soups but were willing to give it a try. We were very happy we did. I can't say that it is the best thing I have ever eaten which is why I am giving it a 4 star rating but is close. Everyone should try it, maybe it will be a 5 with you.

Very yummy, but I also tweaked it a bit. -I roasted the squash, cut side down for 45 minutes. -I only used about 1/2 a block of fat free cream cheese. -I added "most of" a can of vegetable broth to the finished soup, as I found it to be too thick. -I laced it with fat free half & half before serving. -And I served it with garlic cheddar biscuits... delicious! Next time, I'm going to use Vegetable Stock instead of the chicken broth for a vegetarian version.

Love this Recipe!  My husband will tell you its the reason he asked me out.  I do some things different.  I cut the squash in half, rub it with olive oil and roast it until it's tender.  I use chicken stalk in place of bouillon and water, real butter, 1 teaspoon of cayenne and only 1 package of cream cheese.  I make this soup every fall.
Great recipe!  As previous reviewers have recommended, I used half of the cream cheese.  I also added some salt and garlic powder at the end.  Came out perfect!!!

This soup was wonderful.  I tweaked it a little.  I used 1 squash, quartered and roasted for 45 min at 350. Then I cooled it, skined and chopped it. Added it to a pan with about 2 1/2 cup chicken broth, 4 T butter, 1/2 t pepper, 1/4 t nutmeg, 1/8 t cayenne, and dash salt.  I also added half of a diced granny smith apple.  I let that all cook for a while, then used the potato masher, and let it cook a while more.  I cooled it then pureed it in the blender.  Back to the stove, added maybe 1/2 c cream and heated back up.  YUMMY!!  Even DH who swears he hates squash said he would eat again.

Yana-you're a genius. This was so delicious that I even liked it and I hate soup! (I make soup I just don't usually eat it.)
Thanks so much for the recipe!
I followed suggestions: microwaved squash, doubled the cayenne, lessened the cream cheese by 1/3 and used 1/3 less fat.  I ADDED 1 T sugar.  Excellent!!!

I love finding and trying new soups and this one will be a repeat! Easy to make, tasty and a great way to have squash! I did substitute the cream cheese for a small carton of whipped cream. I loved it and so did my picky family!

I loved this soup and so did my family. I did make some changes after reading some of the reviews.  I used 2 tablespoons of butter I don't like margarine, 3/4 of the cream cheese ( I thought 2 pkg was too much)and I did not use chicken bouillon instead I used 32oz of chicken broth from the box or you can use the cans. I peeled the butternut cut in pieces and put in the oven in a cookie sheet to roast. You can adjust the consistency of your soup by adding water or you can add half and half. Since I did not use 2 packages of cream cheese I did add some half and half. If your soup looks great and taste wonderful then you made a delicious soup. Very good on these cold days. :)

yummy!  Reminds me of the pumpkin soup I had in Australia.  I used a whole butternut squash, an acorn squash, and some leftover canned pumpkin I had on hand.  Only added 1/2 of one block of cream cheese...still very rich and smooth!  Would be excellent served chicken enchilada soup-style- just add some cumin, cooked chicken, and top with cheddar cheese and tortilla chips.  Mmmmm!!!
Delicious, just as is!

Is wonderful.  Best way to describe it is creamy yet frothy, butterly delicious.  I only made a few minor changes because of what I had on hand and taste preferences.  Like everyone else, I roasted the butternut squash ahead of time to make it soft and easier to work with.  I roasted 2 butternut squash and 5 carrots.  I only used 1 package of cream cheese, and I used the fat free kind to make the recipe a little more healthy.  And I added about a tbsp. of garlic when sautéing the onions.  Wonderful recipe though.  Perfect for a cool fall day!

Just made this and love it! I read the reviews and made some minor adjustments. First, I made 3 times as much so I can freeze some for later. I also used veggie broth instead of chicken and added about 1/2 cup half and half to make it a creamier texture. Also added about a tablespoon of brown sugar. At first I thought it wouldn't be thick or creamy enough, until I put it in the blender, then it came out perfect! Yum.

I didn't have time to puree the soup, so I just mashed it with a potato masher. Obviously, it was chunky rather than smooth, but the flavor was great!  I couldn't convince my non-soup and non-squash-eating husband and children to taste, but I will definitely pass this recipe along to others!
I added 1 8 oz pkg. cream cheese, 2 teaspoons of curry and I used sweet potatoes instead of regular potatoes and left out the celery and it was delicious!!!!!! yuuummy!
Yummy, Yummy, Yummy!!  I also used just one block of cream cheese and used 4 cups chicken broth.  Even my five year old asked for more!

This was really delicious!  I took the suggestions and halved the cream cheese an used chicken broth.  I like things with a little spice so I kicked up the peppers just a smidge.  I also added about 4 cloves of roasted garlic which gave the soup a little depth.  Very good.  Served at dinner party and there was not a drop left by the end!

I found 4 boullion cubes was too much.  It was very salty.   Next time I would start with 2 and then maybe a 3rd.  Also should have taken advice of person who only used 1 cream cheese.  Too much cream cheese takes away the flavor of the squash.  I also baked the squash ahead of time as one person suggested which was a great idea.  375 for 45 minutes was perfect.

My favorite soup by far! Couple of notes: you can use oregano if you don't have marjoram. One block of cream cheese is plenty. 

I'm going to sprinkle bacon and sour cream on top next time. Should go together so well!

I never hadbutterut squash soup before.I'm wondering why!!!  It is so good!  My hubby HATES savory soups, but loves savory sauces...don't ask....anyway- I made it and put it on chicken as a sauce he loved it...and was shocked when I told him it was soup!  Thanks for the great recipe!

I didn't even know I liked butternut squash!  Roasting the squash first is a bit better.  I used some extra seasonings that I picked up from another recipe: 1/2 t. curry powder, 1/4 t. each of celery salt and nutmeg, and a little more than a table spoon of brown sugar.  I also used only one cream cheese.  This is SO good!  I'll be growing butternuts again next year for sure!

I give this 5 stars, but only with how I tweaked it.  To make it less labor intensive, I microwaved the squash (after piercing it with a fork) for 10 minutes, turning every couple of minutes.  This softened the skin to make it easier to use a knife to peel off the skin.  I could have halved it, microwaved it longer, and scooped out the insides instead since this is how I "roast" butternut squash, but I didn't think about that until I was halfway done with cutting it in chunks.  I used one whole small onion and 4 small cloves of garlic (my husband loves garlic and onion), sauteed them and then I added a dash or two of each (ground):  sage, ginger, nutmeg, coriander, celery seed, and cloves.  Then followed the rest of the recipe.  I also used only 1 package of Neufchatel.  Mine turned out creamier than any other butternut squash soup I've ever tasted.  I never understood why people blame the texture of their creations on the lack of fat in neufchatel since its essentially the same as full fat cream cheese.  I've never had that problem (even with my award-winning cheesecake).   If you want a thicker soup, reserve about a cup of the cooking liquid while you're pureeing the chunks of squash with the cream cheese.  That way, you can judge how thick its going to turn out.  I ended up pureeing and adding the rest of the liquid in the end.  If it didn't turn out creamy enough, you need to either cook the squash longer or puree it longer.  This would make a great sauce on cheese raviol
Delish!  Used this as a guide.  Did add crumbled cooked sweet Italian sausage in the end to add some savoriness.  Made it a meal!  Freezing some leftovers, we will see how if that is successful.

Thanks so much for sharing this recipe!  It was DIVINE.  I took the advice of other reviewers and used one package of cream cheese and baked the squash.  It was very easy and tasted simply amazing.  I will make this again and again.

My husband gave it 5 stars, I gave it 4.  I used one package of lower fat cream cheese.  I think two packages would have lost the flavor of the butternut squash.  It was rich and creamy with just the one pkg.  I also used 4 cups of chicken broth instead of the water and bouillon.  It was easier than trying to pick the pieces of wrapper off the bouillon that always sticks! :)
very good
I did add diced celery and diced green apples and cut the cream cheese in half turned out amazing
Excellent!
Great stuff.  I went a little easy on the cream cheese and it tastes just as good.  Highly recommend this one!!!
great soup, I cooked the butternut squash in the oven as suggested and it was briliant, will definately cook this again

Very delicious soup.  I followed some advice to bake the squash that way it will be easier to cut in pieces.  I used less than half of cream cheese of an 8 oz package.  Also used some curry powder, very tasting, a new favorite...

some of you changed it so much..just add your own ! You rated your own soup in the end.
Sorry Mary, your soup was fine as is, and if I changed anything, I guess I would add my own version undermy own title.

This soup was ok for a little while but then couldn't keep eating it because it is so rich.  The flavour just became overwhelming.  Too much fat even though I cut down on the cream cheese like others suggested.  I'll stick to my regular pumpkin soup next time.
Heavenly.  I used 1/2 the amount of cream cheese as recommended in other ratings & was still rich and creamy.  My 11 month old couldn't get enough of it!!!
LOVE this soup, made it twice, once with butternut and once with hubbard.  Excellent taste, easy to make and easy on the budget too!  I made it as written and wouldn't change a thing!

One word: WOW! This recipe meets all of my criteria for 5 stars: easy, healthy, and delicious. I took some suggestions of other reviewers - I roasted the squash first (much easier that way), added less cream cheese (I didn't have the full amount on hand), and added more cayenne (love a little spice). I used a hand blender to puree. Thanks, Mary, this recipe rocks!!!
Insanely good. We love it as a side for sausage, and we crumble up some Ritz for that crouton crunch.  2 bricks of cream cheese really is insane, though. I used 3/4 of one and it was perfect for us.
A wonderful, comforting and delicious butternut squash soup.  Followed the recipe as written and will definitely make again.  Thanks, Mary!
1 package of cream cheese

I found that 2 packages of cream cheese was way to much for my taste - not only was it to creamy but it overpowered the butternut squash. That said the consistency was nice, but if I ever make this again I will be using only 1/4 of the suggested amount of cream cheese.
Loved this soup! Have made it several times!

I made this recipe AS DIRECTED, no changes.  It's easy and very tasty.  I use the pre-peeled butternut squash halves from the store, saves so much time.  My kids love it & have no idea how good it is for them.  I'd like to try the Butternut Squash Soup II on this site as well, it looks great.
I found the basic recipe very good!!

WOW, I can't get enough of this soup!  What a great texture and flavor.  I could have used a little less crushed red pepper especially for the timid palette.  I used only one cream cheese and it came out incredibly rich.  Used 2 small butternut squash.  I'll make this again and it is a real keeper.  Thanks

A quick and easy way to prepare this dish is to cut the squash in half, place each half face down on a plate, and microwave for about 8 to 10 minutes.  Then just scoop out the prepared squash and puree with the rest of the ingredients.  Half the cream cheese was plenty.

I've been wanting to try this one forever!  I baked two squash (cut into quarters) at 400 for 45 minutes.  Way easier than trying to peel those monsters.  I only used 4 oz cream cheese and thought it was perfect.  My regular blender is broken so I just pureed it right in the pot with a hand blender and it was so easy!
Amazing! Have made many times! I only use one block (8 ounces) of cream cheese though.

I made this soup tonight... I'm 35 weeks pregnant and was craving butternut squash soup! I changed the following: I baked the squash in the over for 30 min. first, then cubed and cooked it according to the recipe for 10 min. I also added a bit of powdered ginger and cut the cream cheese in 1/4. (I used 4 oz. total) I thought the outcome was terrrific!! I will definitely make this recipe again!
Added a few more spices . Did not use 2 cream cheese . One was plenty . Dollop of sour cream to serve delicious.
Made this for the first time today for Thanksgiving dinner. Huge hit with the family.
WOW! I roasted the squash in the oven 400F until tender. I also used 8oz Neufchatel cream cheese and was just right.  YUM!
very delicious and simple to prepare.

Loved it!  Used 1/2 the cream cheese (forgot to buy two) and it was PERFECT! I ate two small bowls after dinner as I was "putting the leftovers away"! Don't think I can freeze it so I will just keep eating it until it is gone. Lucky me!
Very delicious! I omitted the cayenne. The cream cheese makes it awesome! I will definitely make this again.
Delicious recipe - and quick to make.

When I received an immersion blender as a gift for my birthday, the first recipe I tried was this one, and all of the rave reviews are true... this is an amazing soup.  The first time I tried it, I used one 8 oz package (it was too rich)  The second time (I must admit, a few days later), I used half of a package (4 oz) and it turned out much better.  I can't even imagine trying it with the two!  Second admission.. I licked the bowl! It's that good.

One thing of note: after the first try, I now always leave out the onion/butter step.  I didn't like finding little pieces of onion in an otherwise smooth soup.

This is a winner!Q My husband said it was about the best soup he ever ate (and he's been around a long time). I used 2 pkgs of peeled and cut squash from Wegmans net wt 20 oz each and adjusted the broth proportionately to about 4 1/2 cups  used 1 cream cheese, blended everything w/ an immersion blender and seasoned to taste
Thanks, Mary

I have made some modifications to this recipe and it is a regular for my family in the fall.  My children request this soup and it is my daughters favorite.  

I use only about 1/2 of a package of cream cheese rather than 2 whole packages.  I omit the cayenne and black pepper, which is my personal preferance, my husband adds the pepper in his bowl.  This soup freezes well, and when I don't have access to fresh local butternut, I use two bags of frozen squash, although it does result in a thinner soup.  

Thank you so much for this recipe!
This recipe was not for us.
I used 1/4 of the cream cheese and that was plenty.  I would review some of the other comments before making again and try some of their tweaks.  Needs more flavor.
This was so yummy!  Prepared almost exactly as written (didn't add cayenne and only used 8 oz. cream cheese) and it was perfect!!  Thanks for a great soup recipe!!

Because this soup is rather "bland" in the sense that there isn't a mix of vegetables or beans in it, I choose to serve it over white rice. It is an easy way of making it a hearty soup :)

I have had butternut squash soup before that was MUCH sweeter and better tasting. While the consistency was great, the taste wasn't on par for me. I added brown sugar and cinnamon to help compensate for the lack of taste but it still wasn't the same...still searching for a good butternut squash soup recipe :(

Oh, and one pack of cream cheese is plenty! Richness was fine.
This is a very nice soup, but I tasted it after one cream cheese and it was more than enough.  Any more and it would be cream cheese soup.
We loved this soup.  It was very easy and delicious.  We buttered and toasted deli baguettes to accompany the soup and was even better.  This recipe is a definite keeper.
Great soup. Just spicy enough. Very tasty.

I make this delicious soup every Thanksgiving, and it always receives rave reviews and recipe requests.  As others have suggested, I roast the squash before adding, and cut the cream cheese in half, at least.  I use 4-6oz, and find that to be plenty!  I add 2 cloves of garlic in with the onions, and love that added flavor.  This is a wonderful cold weather soup.  You will not be disappointed!

Just made this soup because I had some butternut squash from my CSA this week......it has to be the BEST butternut squash soup I've ever had and i've had a lot!!!!  Will no longer make it any other way.....I did use only one 8 oz. pkg. of cream cheese and herbes de provence instead of marjoram because that's what I had.....excellent.....try it!

I omitted the cream cheese, didn't have quite enough butternut squash to make 6 cups so added a sweet potato.  Also, didn't have marjoram and substituted Thyme.  Otherwise, the recipe was the same.  It had good flavor and was very filling.  Served it with a dollop of sour cream and a side of green salad with apples and cumin cheese with a Walla Walla poppyseed dressing that was a nice, sweet offset to the savory flavor of the soup...oh, and a nice baguette completed dinner.
Excellent recipe! My guests can't get enough each time I make it...
This recipe was great! I used only about 5 oz of cream cheese and I think it was plenty. I will definitely make this soup again.

Truly delicious! Definitely use chicken stock and 1 cream cheese. Tried the hand mixer but the mixture wasn't creamy enough for me so I put it in the blender and it was perfect. A must try and a new staple in our home.

This is my first time making butternut squash soup, but my first time having it was at Panera Bread. I didn't expect this recipe to turn out like theirs, and it didn't, but it was delicious nonetheless.
I added an apple and potato - it was great.  Love the philly cream cheese idea - never tried that before but will again!

Wonderful soup! I just roasted the squash in the oven first for 45 mins, the followed the recipe. I reduced the cream cheese a little, but think it would be good either way. I added cooked bacon and sour cream on top. YUMMMYYYY!!! This is a keeper!
I loved this recipe.  Didn't have cream cheese so used half&half.  Delicious!!!
Want five stars?   ADD A POUND OF FRIED ITALIAN SAUSAGE.  DO IT.  So good!   Also, use real butter, real chicken stock, and half as much cream cheese.  AND DO NOT OMIT THE CAYENNE PEPPER!!!!
My first time making the, an it was very easy to make! My husband love it!!!!

Everyone raves about this soup when I make it.  I have found it difficult to cut up the squash  so I just cut it in half pop it in the oven until it is teneder enough to scoop out the flesh and then follow the recipe as is.

I combined 2 Butternut Squash Soup recipes. Roasted 2 medium squash with 2 cloves garlic for about 45 minutes.  Meanwhile sautéed small onion, a carrot, a stalk celery in about 2 TB butter. Add salt. Let that sauté on low for about 15 minutes. Peeled and sliced thinly a potato and an apple. Added to veggies. Scooped the squash into pot along with roasted garlic. Then added chicken stock to cover plus about 1/2 cup apple cider. Brought to a boil and simmered for about 1/2 hour. Added little nutmeg and cayenne.  Added about 2 ounces lite cream cheese. Stirred till melted. Used immersion blender till smooth and creamy. Correct seasonings. I ended up adding about another 1/3 cup apple cider and little salt.
Great taste!  Used only 1/4 of the cream cheese and was plenty for us!

This is a good savory butternut squash soup! Used 2 squash and baked them first to soften them up. Only one package of cream cheese was needed, that made it plenty creamy enough. Instead of water used broth for added flavor.

I took a large butternut squash, quartered it, and put it in the oven with a few potatoes and a few large carrots(washed but not peeled).I sprinkled on some olive oil, added about 1-2 tsp kosher salt and 4-5 whole cloves of garlic. Then I stuck it in the oven at 350 until the veggies were soft. After the veggies were cool enough to touch I peeled them and added any juices at the bottom of the casserole to a large pot along with the veggies. Then I added the broth, and other ingredients in the original recipe. I also added the slightest amount of clove to add a bit of kick.
Now this is GREAT soup - I used 4 oz of cream cheese and 1/2 cup fat free yogurt, but I'd love to try the 2 8 oz pkgs of cream cheese - but my waistline said no! (Though I may do it next time!!)
I don't like butternut squash all that much, but this soup was amazingly rich and creamy.  Yum!
....just added a 1/4 teaspoon nutmeg and 1/2 the cream cheese. Must say out of this world good.
I like this recipe. I tried it out for the first time today and it was easy to make. I added a bit more cayenne pepper than the recipe called for to give it a spicy kick. My girlfriend loved it.
Awesome.  Lots of flavor.  I added a whole chili pepper and extra cilantro.  Very good.

Now I have never once had butternut soup- so I don't have a baseline.  I had many butternuts in the garden this fall- and was looking for a way to use them.  I used 8oz of reduced fat cream cheese and found that it is still very thick and rich- could probably use only 4oz. I also had some opened chicken stock to use instead of bouillon. I also used a pinch of oregano since I did not have any marjoram. Next time- I will be roasting the squash first in order to make cutting it easier- I think I bruised my hand with the knife!

This was my 1st time ever making butternut squah soup so I was alittle nervous. Followed this recipe exactly and I must say it was easy and extremely delish.  Best part was was my 2 year old and 7 year old eating in all up without asking what it is. Loved it!!

Delicious!!  I cut my squash in half and roasted for 45min at 375 degrees as others suggested, then just scooped out the inside and threw it in the pot with the onions. I only used 1 package of low-fat cream cheese and it was still REALLY creamy and sooo yummy.  This recipe is a keeper!!

Great soup to use up my abundance of garden butternut squash!  I roasted the squash with olive oil as others did and I feel this adds greatly to the soups flavor.  I added 3 cloves of garlic in with the onions and a couple stalks of celery.  I had no marjoram, so I substituted sage, which adds a surprisingly good taste.  Left out the cayenne altogether. I did as others and used 3/4 of a pack of cream cheese (1/3 fat).  As the squash was well roasted, it fell apart in the cooking process, so I did not puree it, so it had more texture.  As a vegetarian I also used vegi broth.  Next day the flavors melded wonderfully when we had it as leftovers.  This is a keeper.

This soup is delicious.  Make it on a crisp fall day when squash are plentiful and hot soup would surely warm you up!  I used only 1 8oz. cream cheese as suggested and the flavor was wonderful.  I also used my hand blender and pureed the soup right in the pot instead of pouring it into my blender a little at a time because hot liquids expand in a blender once it's turned on.  Less dishes to wash!
Complete delicious!

Yum!!!  This was sooooo good!  I did do a few things different as many other reviewers suggested.  I roasted the squash at 375 degrees with olive oil brushed on each half until soft (about an hour).  I carmelized the onion in olive oil.  Then pureed it with the squash and cream cheese.  I didn't have marjoram so left it out.  I did use a little curry powder and used only 1/2 block of cream cheese (4 oz).  I'll make this again and again!
I did the tweak the one of the reviews did. Apples, cider.  And a chopped apple.Wonderful.

I also followed others suggestions. I baked the squash first. Then I only used one 8 oz cream cheese. It was still very rich and creamy. I have a hard time with my blender so I used a hand emulsifier to make it creamy. Watch out for splashing. This soup was awesome eaten right after it's made. But as someone said, even better the next day.
This was my first time making a squash soup. This recipe is very easy & delicious. Very creamy and it seemed to be even better the second day. I made it just as instructed.
Made it for Thanksgiving. Super easy to make and everybody loved it.
