Try adding Boursin or herb and garlic cream cheese....very complimentary to the sweetness of the squash.....very gourmet!

I tried this soup today, with a few mods...  I put a whole small yellow onion in the food processor to chop it pretty fine and added all of it.  I didn't want to hassle with cooking a whole squash, so I used a frozen pkg of cooked squash that was 14 oz cube from Safeway.  I used a single can of chicken broth, also 14oz.  Only used 1 tsp of chicken bouillon granules, skipped the marjoram and cayenne but did add a dash of nutmeg and garlic.  I only added half an 8oz pkg of cream cheese since my batch was so much smaller.  Pureed in blender until smooth and served with a dollup of (not Daisy) sour cream.  It is very good.  Along the lines of other creamy soups like tomato.  Would be very good with grilled cheese sandwiches.

I was skeptical when i read this recipe but decided to try it anyway.  So glad I did, this is my new favorite soup.  My only complaint?  It is almost impossible to stop eating it! I roasted the squash 1st (also toasted the seeds for a snack) and added a couple shakes of nutmeg.  Have given the recipe to friends and they too loveit.

Delicious!  I used only 4 0z cream cheese as I am counting calories.  I added a touch of nutmeg and orange zest.  I used boxed chicken broth with low sodium.  I felt I did not sacrifice flavor to make it a bit healthier.
Excellent!  I followed the directions as in the original recipe....  I did bake my squash in the oven first.

This recipe is so wonderful, definitely a favorite, definitely a keeper.  I have made it several times and find I prefer it without the cayenne. I use white pepper instead of black, add a teaspoon of brown sugar, and use fat-free cream cheese (not nearly as rich, so you can use the full amount).  I then sprinkle on a little dried parsley for color, top it with a dollop of fat-free plain yogurt (a mild brand like Dannon), and not only does it taste incredible, it is gorgeous soup to look at  - and healthy as well.  Everyone LOVES it, even people who hate the sound of the word "squash"!

I just made a few changes - used 3 cups of bone broth instead of bouillon and water.  2 packages cream cheese seemed like a lot so I only used 1 and it was just right. The soup was very tasty with a good amount of seasoning and lots of flavor!

I've made this many times. The nice thing about this recipe is, the measurments don't have to be exact.  One nice size squash equals about 4 cups.  I use 3 cups of broth and only 4oz of cream cheese.  I like to season mine with nutmeg, curry powder, white pepper and thyme. It took me a few times to figure out why mine was grainey. I have found that blending in a blender, in small batches rather than a food processer will make a smooth (not grainy) soup.

Surprisingly excellent!  And the reason I say "surprisingly" is that I usually don't like creamy soups.  I picked this recipe because it was a soup and it had butternut squash, and it was rated 5 stars by at least 200 or 300 people.  Then halfway through making it, I realized that this was a creamy soup!  I followed the optional advice and used only 1 package of cream cheese.  Delicious!!!  And I love the little kick from the cayenne pepper!
Love this...great Fall recipe!  Only added 1 package of lowfat cream cheese.

Loved it!!!  I made a few changes, as most cooks do.  I roasted the squash in the oven instead of boiling.  I also used 1/2 the cream cheese the recipe called for and added 1 more cup of water.  Scrumdillyicious!!!
Amazing and pretty easy to make
This was the first time I've ever made anything with Butternut Squash and it was great.  My friends loved it.  I will be making this again soon.
It was easier than I thought to make.  I used canned chicken broth instead of bouillon and water.  I also substituted heavy whip cream for the cream cheese (it was all I had on hand).

Amazing recipe! This was the first time I've had butternut squash soup and it was absolutely delicious. I modified it a bit based on everyone's suggestions. I changed the margarine to butter, used only one 8 oz package of cream cheese instead of 2, used 4 cups of chicken stock instead of the water and bullion, and added one clove of crushed garlic. I'll add a bit more cayenne pepper next time to give it an extra zip!
I followed the recipes except limited the cream cheese to one package.  It was thick and delicious. I'll make this again!
I love butternut squash soup, and I really like this version.  I used only one container of cream cheese.  Wonderful!
It was WAY too rich with that much cream cheese. I will only be using half a pack of cream next time.

Love this soup!!! I've made this many times now for friends and family and get rave reviews. The flavor is amazing. Only a couple of minor alterations - I use half of the cream cheese (fat free). Try adding a little nutmeg and sprinkle of sugar (I used Stevia). WOW!

Should have stuck to the original recipe but tried the healthy version with apple cider as another reviewer suggested.  What a disaster that was!  Thanksgiving supper and the soup tasted like vinegar broth!  "1 c." is 1 cup right?... I only used a half a cup and it was embarassing to serve it to my guests who kindly said it wasn't that bad.  I don't understand why people just don't write their own recipe instead of making so many adjustments to the original.  Also, how can you rate a recipe when you changed it so much?  I will try this recipe again as is and give it a proper review/rating.

I really don't want to be negative but I have to admit this soup tasted too much like a velveta cheese soup with a hint of squash.  I only added 1 package of cream cheese and that was too much.  I wouldn't use cream cheese at all.  I added about 2 cups of heavy cream, a dash of nutmeg and a dash of cinnamon to "fix" it.

I made this last night, and was just a little disappointed. I used one package of cream cheese, but I used the Neufchatel cheese instead of full-fat cream cheese, and the soup isn't as creamy or rich as I was hoping for. Next time I'll just go for the fat. :)It WAS really easy to make, though, which was great. I roasted the squash in the oven for a while before peeling it and cutting it up, which made it easier. Thanks for the recipe!

I followed others' advice and cut cream cheese in half. I added the first half a package to blender, but forgot the other half. So I ended up only using 1/4 of the cream cheese called for. My husband loved it and said to leave it that way.
truly a fantastic soup! It's one of my favorites.
This soup was DELICIOUS!!! (and I'm not really a soup eater!)  Quick to fix and soo-o-o-o creamy.
SO tasty. Followed recipe to a T except I only used 1 brick of cream cheese...Still amazingly tasty. I also roasted the squash beforehand.
I liked it.  Too spicy for the kids.

THIS IS SO SO GOOD!!!  I roasted the squash like the others said to and then separately boiled the water, boullion, onions, black pepper, cayene pepper, and some salt in a sauce pan.  I scooped out the squash and put it in the blender, added the cream cheese, and then poured the boiling ingredients over top in the blender and puree'ed it.  I didnt add margerine because I forgot and I didnt add marjoram because I dont have any.  lol  It was absolutely fine without both.  I find that this could also be used as a fondue!!  AWESOME!!!  Oh and my husband and I are on Weight Watchers and this is only 2 points per serving!!!  YAY!!!

I loved this soup! My family really loved it, too. My son said it was the best soup ever! I did change a few things because of other reviewers' comments including roasting the squash for an hour, cutting back to 1/2 package of cream cheese (a little less would be even better), skipping the marjoram, and adding fresh nutmeg. A keeper for sure!

I've been making this recipe for about 2 years now, and it's a fall/winter favorite!  I usually only put 1 block of cream cheese in (it thickens as you refrigerate it and seems to be thicker next time you reheat it).  I also use chicken broth instead of the cubes and water.  Thanks for sharing your recipe!
Very filling and delicious. I highly recommend halfing the cream cheese and doubling the cayenne. I love a rich soup but two 8oz packages of cream cheese would have been to much.

This recipe is fabulous!  I was looking for a savory butternut squash soup and this recipe fit the bill.  I will say the marjoram is a must as it adds a subtle taste that should not be missed.  I make a vegetarian version using vegetable broth - one 32 oz container - and I do not use the chicken boullion cubes and I do not add the water that the recipe calls for.  This soup always gets rave reviews.  As with other reviewers, I find it easier to roast the squash first, then scoop out the pulp for this soup.  I also do not use more than 4 oz cream cheese and I use an immersion blender at the end to make a velvety smooth soup.  Thanks, Mary, for a fabulous soup I have made many times now.

Excellent, hearty soup!   I only had 1/2 of a squash, so I added two carrots and one potato, and used just one packet of cream cheese.  The cayenne pepper added just enough kick to the soup, but don't add more than the recommended amount.   This is so easy to make and even my 89 & 86 year old parents, and their 88 yr old friend, loved it!   I'll be making this again soon.
i roasted a whole onion, some garlic and the butternut squash, then pureed it. also, i did not add the marjoram, and only used 4 oz cheese. it was rich, creamy and delicious.
I really liked this recipe and have made it several times.  I only use about 6 oz of light cream cheese and I double the cayenne.  This is a good one IMO!

I made this in my vitamix - delicious and easy!! I roasted the halved squash face-down as others suggested. To make it all in my 8 cup blender pitcher I: used onion powder (a little over a tablespoon), 3 cups organic chicken broth, and only one package of cream cheese. I can see myself roasting the squash and having everything in the pitcher ready to go when we are entertaining.

I have to say - did SLJ6 ever make the recipe according to the printed recipe or is he/she just using this page to SHOW OFF?  Post your own recipe and let people rate your recipe.  Honestly, not sure how you can even fit your ego-swollen head into your kitchen.  THIS RECIPE by Mary is fabulous!  Thanks for sharing it with us!!!
Great Holiday Soup. Goes well with a Turkey meal
This soup was very good, but way too much cream cheese, it was very rich with all the cream cheese, family still enjoyed it, but next time i will half the cream cheese at the least.

Not sure what all the fuss was about.  I found this recipe to be very average.  The squash didn't seem to have a strong enough flavor to carry the recipe, and I added a small portion of the cream cheese, and it overpowered the flavor of the soup.  I'll eat it, but I won't make it again.

This was perfect to make on a cold rainy day. I sautéed the onions with about two tablespoons of butter. I roasted the squash and then brought all the ingredients (besides the cream cheese) to a boil then I just shut it off and let it sit for about 15 minutes. I blended the squash and one block of cream cheese in the blender.  Mixed it back in with the other liquid. I think two blocks of cream cheese would have been too much. It's a great fall recipe!

The only thing I did that was a "cheat" is I bought pre-cubed squash.  Otherwise I made it just as the recipe called for and everyone loved it!  I also made this around the Holidays and I added a dash of ground clove and a dash of ground cinnamon.

Ii took the suggestions of others by roasting squash, onions, garlic and an apple in oven for an hour (drizzled olive oil and seasoned with salt and pepper) sautéed the onions in butter, added roasted vegetables and added 4 c water with 4 heaping tsps of Epicures chicken bouillon, marjoram, 1/4 tsp cayenne, 1/4 tsp nutmeg. Heat until warm and purée small portions in blender, return to pot and heat to serving temperature. I did not use any of the cream cheese...it was amazing without the extra fat.
I made this with leftover sweet potatoes instead of squash and it was excellent.  Very rich flavor.
I give it 5 stars, but I only used ONE 8oz pkg of cream cheese.  I think if I had used 2 it would not have been as good.  It's plenty cheesy with one pkg.  YUMMY!
I used half the cream cheese. This is a new family favorite!

Excellent, but only 4 stars since I made some changes: used chix broth instead of water and bullion, one package of cream cheese instead of 2, butter instead of margarine and then added some nutmeg, oregano and some cinnamon and sugar
Extremely easy and delicious.  My only addition was 1/2 cup of brown sugar.  I felt this was needed to balance the cayenne pepper.
Only used 1/2 of the cream cheese and I roasted the squash.  I thought that it was a yummy soup, but my hubbie and daughter did not hence the 3 star rating.

I followed it exactly except i roasted 2 squash at 375 for 45 minutes. Very tasty! Next time, I am cutting down the cream cheese because it was overpowering and kind of a weird taste... so next time just one package. Otherwise, very very good!
I love this recipe! It's one of our family favorites. I made a couple of changes - I bake the squash at 350 for 35 minutes and I add a pinch of nutmeg. Thanks for the recipe!

Wow, this soup is amazing! I made some changes: I didn't add any cream cheese at all. I added a sweet potato and 4 carrots. In the spice category i added nutmeg, allspice, red pepper, and cinnamon. I also didn't puree it because i am a lazy cook so i just mashed everything together in the pot (more like a stew) and it was still very good!

I roasted the squash meat side down like another reviewer recommended and it was so easy to work with and had a great flavor.  I also used 1/3 less fat cream cheese and it was very rich!  If you used fresh ground black pepper you won't need to increase the cayanne.  I'm from Texas and my tongue is used to some heat - trust me.  Enjoy!  This might be our new Christmas soup.

i only used 1/2 the cream cheese and still thought it was too...cream cheese tasting for me. but the squash flavor was amazing. my squash was a little over 2 lbs - i cut it in 1/2 , drizzled olive oil, salt, and pepper, and baked in over at 350 for 30 minutes, then preceded with the recipe as written. the hardest part was getting the skin off of it. next time i may skin before baking. once everything was sauteed together in the pan and just before blending with cream cheese, i tasted the squash and it was AMAZING. it was so good i almost didn't want to make it into soup! i'd like to try a slightly healthier/less rich version that didn't involve cream cheese or at least not so much of it...

I have been using allrecipes for years and this is the first time I have stopped in my tracks to come back and review an item. This is the best tasting soup I have ever made!!!

Thank you!!
I cooked the squash before i made it. The soup was delicious! Next time I will use half as much cream cheese.
Great! Creamy soup with a kick of spice. The whole family loves it.

I didn't have any onion so I just left it out.  I cut one butternut squash in half and drizzled it with olive oil, salt and pepper then laid each half cut side down on a cookie sheet and baked for 20 minutes at 375.  I dissolved 3 cubes of chicken bouillon in 2 cups water then added the peeled and cut up squash, nutmeg (didn't have any marjoram), and cayenne pepper.  I boiled this for a minute or two then scooped out the squash into the blender, using some of the liquid from the pan.  I blended this with 3/4 of 1 package cream cheese.  My mom and I loved it!  Sweet, creamy and just a little spicy.  I plan to freeze it to enjoy later.  Thanks for the recipe!
This was wonderful.  I took everyone else's advice and cut the cream cheese in half, and it was still super rich!  Nice and thick.
Perfect!  I didn't want to make a heavy soup with cream or cream cheese so this recipe fit the bill.  My family all loved it!  Added an apple and some apple juice for the perfect touch! Thanks!
excellent! I used 1pkg of cream cheese and a little light cream. My famly loved it, especially during this blizzard we are having

I have made this over and over and over, we love it that much!!! I too use only half the amount of cream cheese and it is perfect!!  I leave out the marjoram (hubby doesn't like it) and add in garlic, basil, oregano and parsley. I always make a double batch so we can have leftovers for lunch the next day. YUM!!
This soup was AWESOME!!  Simple, fast, delicious!

Wonderful.  A few changes:  Used one butternut and one acorn squash.   Poked cloves in squash ...Halved and baked in oven for an hour..

Added 3 apples to onions...Lots of grated nutmeg.

Make some homemade croutons and add pepper flakes to croutons!!!
i changed it based on other people's reviews
This soup is crazy good! The second time that I made it I used a little less cream cheese, but this is a great recipe.
Wonderful soup!  Most people that reluctantly tried this soup loved it!  I add 1/2 or less of the cream cheese.

This was the first time I made squash soup, and I love butternut squash but this was very bland.  The texture was nice but just not a good taste.  No one in my family liked it.  Maybe we just don't like squash soup.

I've made A LOT of recipes from this site and most of them have been very good and worth making again but this recipe actually inspired me join up just so I could rate it!  What more can I say when a husband with a cold (i.e., grumpy), a 6 year old, a 4 year old, and a 2 year old all love dinner!  I've never been a butternut squash person but this was yummerific!!  (I did follow others' advice, though and add an additional 2 cups of water.)  It was good!
Very delicouis!  We loved it.  Was a little too rich for my 9 yr old. I highly recommend 6-8 oz cream cheese.

WOW!  This was delicious!  The only change I made was I cut the squash in half (lengthwise) and placed each half cut side down on a buttered cookie sheet and then baked it for 40 min in the oven at 375 degrees.  This really brought out the flavor and made it simple to scoop away from the skin.  I then followed the receipe as instructed.  Also I only used 1/2 the suggested cream cheese - for my family that was perfect. Yum!

My husband is willing to try anything, but is very selective with his feedback.  He literally said, "this is the best soup I have ever tasted," after the first few bites.    I followed recipe for the most part but used only about 6 oz of cream cheese (rather than 16 oz), and substituted a vegetable bouillon (without MSG or other preservatives) for the chicken bouillon.  The VitaMix blender was awesome to puree, and all I can say is that it was phenomenal.  Thanks for the great recipe.
A really delicious soup!  I only used 1/2 of 1 package rather than 2 packages and it was thick enough.
My family thought this was really bland.  I went back and added 3 times as much cayenne pepper and it helped a little, but not much.
We add a dash of yellow curry... even the kids love this soup!
It really doesn't taste like butternut squash AT ALL. And the soup is not orange.  I followed it as written otherwise.  It is an okay soup with a little kick.
This recipe is fabulous!  This was the first time I have ever made butternut squash soup and definitely a keeper!

The marjoram wasn't a hit at all - use freshly grated nutmeg and plenty of garlic! Leave out the cream cheese too...if you must have a creamier soup (not necessary in this case!) drizzle fresh cream in a swirl over the top of each bowl.
I halved the cream cheese (thanks for suggestions!) and it still turned out wonderfully. Tasty and perfect for a cold winters' day.

This recipe is great! I made it directly as instructed the first time but the second time I made a few changes that I think make this outstanding! Instead of peeling and cubing the squash I just baked it with butter at 350 for about 45 min, it was much easier to cut the squash in half (or quarters depending on the size) than to peel and cube! Then I used only 8 oz of cream cheese and a little more water-probably because of my elevation. But these changes were wonderful! It was still creamy and delicious but not too creamy and thick like before, with 16 oz of cheese it tasted mostly like cream cheese, but with 8 it was much more balanced.
Excellent recipe, very smooth and creamy. Will make often.
I served it for Christmas dinner.  I loved it, but most of it went down the drain.  It is an aquired taste.
I thought this recipe had a lot of flavor. I had a little extra bouillion cube and I did cut down on the cream cheese. I think I will try milk next time instead of cream cheese. It was plenty thick.

Amazing! My husband said " it tastes like Fall". I too roasted the squash before. Also I added a grated clove of garlic with the sauteed onions, 1/2 tsp of Cayenne, 2 dashes of cinnamon and 1 dash of ground cloves. I also put in half of the cream cheese as was recommended. It was awesome!

This was a perfect soup for a cold snowy day. I added garlic to the sautéed onions, a pinch of hot pepper flakes, and half the cream cheese. I used an immersion blender to get it nice and creamy. Then I topped each serving with a tablespoon of crumbled bacon. It was delicious and beautiful. This is a recipe I'll definitely keep in my recipe box.

Yummo!  This was a huge hit with my guests!  I did roast the squash first and then pureed it in my food processor.  I only used 2 pkgs. cream cheese and it was still creamy and loved by all!  It's a keeper.
I've made it twice and the second time I cut the peppers in half (just my family's preference), but other than that, it's perfect as written!
This was oh so yummy.  I took the advise and only put in one stick of cream cheese.  I'll be looking to try to reduce the fat in future batches.
Simple and tasty, can't get any better than that!
I used only about 4 ounces of cream cheese to cut down on the calories. Easy and delicious!

Similar to the other reviews, I also thought this recipe was a good foundation.  I used reduced fat cream cheese and also only used 8oz.  I had to thin the soup with a little milk at the end it was so thick. I added nutmeg and a small amount of cooking sherry wine.  I thought this was good and will definitely make again.
Fantastic! This is better, in my opinion, as an appetizer soup. It is rich and dense, and we couldn't really do a whole soup bowl of it.

Absolutely delectable!  A balance of sweet & spicy made this soup a winner.  I like chunky soup so I scooped out the squash with a spoon and put it right into the soup to cook and left it at that.  Wonderful!  Thanks for the recipe.

Absolutely outstanding. I do use about 48 ounces of chicken broth and only one package of cream cheese, because otherwise it's WAY too thick. This has become a huge favorite in my family, and requested every fall and winter. Everyone loves the pepper! To make it super easy and quick, I pick up four packages of the cubed, peeled butternut squash in the salad section of Trader Joe's. Very yummy, and very filling!

Absolutely will make this again. Just delicious. I made 1.5 of this recipe, used a half cup more of the substituted chicken broth (to use up 3 full cans instead of 2.5) in addition to the bullion, not in place of, and used the two cream cheese as called for in the original recipe (not 1.5). I had no problem cutting up the squash-cut it in rings of about 1.5" wide, then peeled it around like you would an apple, then chopped. It was very flavorful and just a smidge on the salty side and not as thick as the picture, which was fine. Next time I will just double the recipe and use only half of the bullion. Still, first attempt was a smash hit! I almost put cubed ham in it, but wanted to taste the recipe as is, so I put the ham on our salads instead-paired very well with the soup. So good.

I'm a huge fan of butternut squash soup and had never tried one with cream cheese. I LOVE cream cheese and was really excited about this recipe. It was just ok..not worth the extra calories imo. Oddly bland. I agree with other reviewers re: tweaks (roast squash, throw in a pear or apple, use half the cream cheese, alter spices, etc.) Before you add the cream cheese, puree it and get yourself a cupful..swirl in a spoonful of plain yogurt. It add awesome depth and creaminess.

This is just plain fantastic. To address complaints of grittiness, I don't know if I read it here or elsewhere online, but I'd recently learned it can have something to do with the age of the squash. I myself have made this three times now, and one attempt was perfectly smooth with almost no texture outside of smooth and creamy. The other two did have a bit of grittiness. I couldn't figure out for the life of me what was different, so I researched and learned the younger the squash, the more tender. (No different than zucchini.) So they're more likely to blend down smoother.

Either way the flavor is PHENOMENAL. I've also used this as a base for a pasta sauce with chicken apple sausage, with great success. So happy to have found this!

Awesome soup, thanks Mary. Second time I made this soup I added an additional cup of stock and also added 2 potatoes and recuced cream cheese to 1 package - was excellent. As others have recommended I also pre-roasted the squash for 40 minutes at 350. I will make this again!
Great recipe! Best one I've found for this soup. I agree with other reviews....I used half the cream cheese and it was just perfect.

I used one reviewers suggestions by roasting two squashes sliced in half at 375 for 45 min - I also used more cayenne, and only 1 package of cream cheese (although probably should have used 1/2 of a package).  I used Smart Balance instead of margarine.  Delicious!

This soup was delicious.  Like many others, I also only used half 
of the cream cheese.  I also used butter (1 1/2 tablespoons), instead 
of the margarine. Instead of using a food processor to puree it, I just
added the cream cheese to the pot, and blended it with my hand blender.
It worked perfectly.

A perfect soup on a cold night! I followed the advice in previous reviews and added extra onions and garlic and an apple, and used only 4 oz of cream cheese, which was more than enough! The taste of the cream cheese would be way too strong otherwise! I also kicked up the spices a bit and added some dried coriander powder.
I found that the amount of cream cheese was too much. I will try it again and cut it by 3/4. Honestly. It's so thick. I'll have to add chicken stock to loosen it up.

Wonderful recipe.  I did tweak it a bit to feed my family of 7.  I took 2 butternut squash's, split them in half, took out the seeds, and microwaved each 1/2 for about 8-10 minutes each, then peeled off the skin in order to get to the meat of the squash.  I also used about 8 cups of water and 8 bouillon cubes.  I also doubled the spices and included salt.  I kept the cream cheese at 2, 8 oz. pkgs.  I found that this helped to keep the soups creamier.  Other than these changes, I followed the recipe the same.  Next time I think I might add some garlic to the onions.  W topped off the soup with some sour cream, bacon bits, and shredded cheese.  I will definitely be making this recipe again.

Yummy soup!!  I took the advise of one review here and used a potato instead of cream cheese, added a little bit of milk during blending process, and a little extra cayenne pepper due to my family's preference!!  Soup was a big hit!

Absolutely amazing!!  Very filling and wonderful with some crusty bread.  I'm usually not a fan of spicy foods, but this had just the right kick to it.  It's so easy also...  can't really mess this one up.  It also saves wonderfully in the freezer for easy reheating later.  Only change I made was to reduce the cream cheese to only 8oz...  the other 8oz definitely aren't needed.  Love love love this!  Several people asked me for the recipe! Thanks so much.

Delicious soup. My blender with the glass jar kicked the bucket, so I got out the potato masher instead and mashed it in the pot, then added the cream cheese. I've had this recipe 'blendered' before, and mashing did not detract from the overall soup at all. It came out fairly smooth. I used homemade chicken stock, and one package of light cream cheese, and it was just right. I also didn't have any marjoram, so I substituted with oregano and a smidgen of thyme and sage (dried leafy, not powdered). Great soup, will definitely make again.
Great recipe!  I have been looking for a squash soup and this one is good and very quick and easy to make.  I added some curry powder and it added some spice to the soup if you like that.
This is delicious. I only use half the cream cheese. Great soup.

Freshly grated NUTMEG is a very tasty addition to this delicious soup. Wow.....what a great recipe. 

For an EASY WAY TO CUT THE BUTTERNUT SQUASH: microwave the squash for 2-3 minutes. That softens it.

 After that, cut off each end and set upright and peel downward. Cut it in half. Cube the top 1/2, then scoop out the bottom 1/2 and cube it.

I cut the recipe in 1/2, making 3 servings.
We fixed this soup this afternoon and it is delicious! I substituted chicken broth for the bouillon as per the Allrecipes.com cookbook and will definitely be making this again real soon.
The only changes I made was to add a bit more [of this and that] as I had more than 6 cups squash.  I also added a bay leaf.  This recipe is SO GOOD AND EASY! Definitely my new favorite.
Its to rich, After a cup it didn't taste so nice. I don't think I'll make this again.

I followed the directions as they were provided and people raved about the soup.  One comment was that it was the best Butternut Squash soup they had ever had.  I made it for Canadian Thanksgiving this past weekend and since I bought extra squash, I'm making another batch tonight when I get home.  Amazing!
Favorite soup ever. So many ways to dress it up. For a more substantial meal, pour it over spaghetti Noddles and add bacon and parmesian...yummm!!!

This was GREAT!!!  I wanted a Squash Soup and this filled the craving and then some!  It was easy and inexpensive.  I will make this again.  I am starting WW and figured that I could actually use either reduced fat or fat free cream cheese (although I don't know about fat free as sometimes that has a funny flavor), and use minimal points.  HIGHLY RECOMEND!!

Again, I don't know if it's truly fair to rate this 5 stars when I adjust the recipe per other people's comments (love that aspect on this website!), but I absolutely love this soup! I roast the squash prior to cubing it (split in half, remove seeds, spray cut face w/ non-stick spray and lay face down on cookie sheet, roast in 375 degree oven for about 45 minutes-- makes peeling and cutting so much easier, plus it brings out the flavor of the squash). I also OMIT THE CHEESE altogether (made it both ways and decided I liked it better w/out it). Very tasty and great for those fall afternoons!

Tasty, did as one other reader suggested and baked the squash in the oven with s & p, and minced garlic....used cream instead of Philadelphia because that was what I had....a lovely starter!! Thank you for recipe!!! A keeper!
I tried this recipe this weekend and it was a hit. I've been requested to make this for Thanksgiving as well!! Thanks for this wonderful recipe. I have never ever used butternut squash until now.

Like other reviewers, I used only 8 oz of cream cheese. Other than that small modification -- this recipe was absolutely perfect. It was sooooo delicious! As good or better than anything I've had in restaurants. 5 stars, for sure! I'm using this recipe when I want to impress someone!

Creamy, flavorful, delicious!
I did make a couple of changes to mine.
I used one butternut squash and added a 
15 oz can of pumpkin after squash was tender. I used only three bouillon cubes and 12 oz cream cheese. My 18 mo. old, who tends to be a finicky eater, loved it.

I loved it.  I used chicken broth instead of boullion.  I warmed it up and it was even better.  In fact, I had my third day of soup for lunch COLD.  I was surprised how much I enjoyed it COLD, TOO!   I will make this one again.
I love this soup!  It's spicy and creamy and just plain delicious.  I wish butternut squash came pre-cut - the only downside to this recipe is all the chopping.

I used my own chicken stock, a small squash, and 2 ounces cream cheese.  I baked the squash in the oven before blending with remaining ingredients.  Results were delicious.  Thank you Mary for sharing your recipe.

I've made 3 soups with butternut squash this year and this was BY FAR the best tasting. Like other reviewers, I roasted the squash first and used 6oz of cream cheese (which I still think was and oz or two too much). I also put a tad more cayenne pepper. Overall, if you're looking to make an easy and very tasty butternut squash soup this is the one.

I roast my squash for about 45 min at 400 degrees after brushing it with melted butter and adding salt and pepper to get that sweet and nutty flavor out of the flesh.  I kept everything else the same but only used 8 ounces of cream cheese, not 16, I felt it was going to be way to rich if I used it all.  Also, a side note, if you roast the squash, you only need to simmer it with the rest of the ingredients for about 5-10 minutes since it's already been cooked.  Enjoy!
Good, creamy a little spicy, but other recipe was a little better

I used 4 C. of vegetable broth, and  did not measure the squash and onions exactly, just sauteed what I had in butter.  I added a pear and used whipped cream cheese...perhaps 3/4 cup.  I think the pear lighten it up.  Served with croutons.  Very good!  Will definitely make again.
I used some leftover cooked squash from the night before and it cooked up almost immediately. Very tasty :)

I loved this soup I brought it over for a girls night :)  I made a few changes.. I followed the advice of everyone only using half the desired amount of cream cheese as it was very creamy and thick with just one brick.  I also didn't have any marjoram so I added a few fall spices to mine to make it flavourful.  I added quite a lot of cinnamon,  a pinch of ground ginger,  a pinch of ground Clive's and also a few pinches of nutmeg I put them in all to taste,  but the Cinnamon is the most important so if you are going to add anything I would say Cinnamon is the game changer!  It was awesome and really easy to make!  Highly recommend this lovely soup!

This was awful. It ended up looking and tasting just like nacho cheese you find at a ballpark. I had to dump it down the drain. If I was doing it again, I'd play with much less cream cheese.  I'd start with about a half of one package, blend it in, see what it tasted like, and go from there.

I microwaved the squash to cut down on the cooking time and only added one package of cream cheese and it was excellent.  My husband loathes onions so I left those out too.  I think two packages of cream cheese would be too overpowering.

Doctored up and it was delicious!! Rich but delicious! I took bits and pieces of other reviewers suggestions when I made this.  I used one medium squash and one sweet potato.  Both which I baked @ 375 for about an hour with olive oil, salt, garlic and about an inch of water in the pan. The rest was according to the recipe except I did use only one cream cheese package.  It has a richness that made me only want one bowl but very soothing on a rainy fall day!
I forgot the bouillon cubes so I added chicken broth. Other than that I used everything that the recipe ordered. I added a sprinkle of cinnamon on top and my soup is so tasty.
DELICIOUS!!! I am a vegetarian so I changed it to vegetable boullion and 1 1/2 package of cream cheese. Could even use less because it is so rich.
Fabulous soup.  Everyone liked it at Thanksgiving.  I will definitely make it again for my family meals.

Excellent recipe!! I put the squash in the oven at 400 for about 30 mins to soften it up a bit. Then I put it in the food processor to chop it up before putting it in the pan with the onions.  I had no marjarom, so I substituted it with oregano. I only used half the recommended amount of cream cheese.  I thought it was a really tasty and easy recipe and I will definitley make this again!
excellent!  I used two pkgs of frozen squash and added about 2 cups of skim milk in place of one of the cream cheese.  So good!

Great soup - I halved the cream cheese, and used lite instead of full-fat.  It was still incredibly rich.  I also used chicken stock from a can, which was easy and delicious.  I'll definitely make this again.

It's my first time cooking with butternut squash and I have to say that I joined just so I can write this review! It was wonderful! My fiance loved it! I cut the squash in half and scraped out the seeds, drizzled some olive oil and sprinkled some salt, then baked them, upside down for 45 mins at 180°C. I added just 3 bouillon cubes since the ones we get here seem large, and 1.5 of the cream cheese and 1/4 t of cayenne.  Next time, I plan to use 1 package of cream cheese, and 2 bouillon cubes. I plan on including this into my Thanksgiving menu this year!

Great soup, after a few modifications. Leave out the spices and cream cheese, and roast the squash for better flavout. Instead of the recommended spices, add the following, for a really flavourful, rich soup:

1-1.5 Tbsp Thai Yellow Curry Paste
1 Tbsp. brown sugar
1/2 can coconut milk
1 tsp. Thai Fish sauce
juice of 1 lime

Adjust spice to taste, and enjoy!
I totally agree that roasting the squash works better. I also put a bottle of wit beer in the soup to add a slightly fruity flavor.  Love the soup!

Have made this recipe several times and my friends can't get enough of it.  Didn't have cayenne pepper the first time so used crushed pepper.  Went back to using the crushed pepper really had a nice bite to it. My thanks to Mary.

Like many others here I edited the recipe slightly.. I used 3/4 the cream cheese called for, alittle more stock to make it less dense, and I added a pinch of pumpkin pie spice per 6 servings.  Big hit at Thanksgiving.. many friends have asked for the recipe or by request for parties I attend.
I'm NUTS about this butternut squash soup.
This soup is amazing. I've made it over and over again anyone who's tried it has loved it.
Make this every year at thanksgiving.  It's my mom's favorite soup.  This recipe is PERFECT.
Easy, simple and delicious.  I substituted chicken broth for water and bouillon.  This is a go-r

Yum. Good base recipe. I took the advice of others and roasted the squash in the oven with garlic cloves. I used an immersion blender to puree everything in the pan and it worked a lot better than the blender method. The soup wasn't nearly as gritty as the first time I made it.

I really like this recipe. I make it on those cold, midwest, winter nights to warm us up from the inside out. It fills you up rather well, which most soups don't do. My husband appreciates that, as then he's not hungry for food again in 15 minutes.

Yum!  However I did take the recommendations of several others.  I roasted the squash...reduced the cream cheese...and added milk.  Then.....I added some garlic and roasted chicken...the chicken really finsihed it off!!!  Definitely a wonderful combination of flavors....so creamy and delicious!!!
Great recipe!!! I used about 1/2-1/3 of the cream cheese, but in fact it's very nice without any creamcheese at all.
This was excellent!  I added more butternut squash the second time we made it so it wasn't so rich.

I only needed 1 squash, because that was give or take 5.5 cups. I peeled it then hollowed it out with a grapefruit spoon like I would a pumpkin, even taking an extra layer off of the stringy part. Then I chopped it into 2 or 3 inch pieces. But, since it's being boiled I definitely think it should be chopped smaller. Really though, the bigger pieces didn't make a difference.  I followed the recipe to a T, boiling everything (but cheese) for 20 min. Then I put half in the processor with 8oz of cream for about 2 min. Moved it to a side container and did the same with the other half.   It had way too much cream cheese! I really only used 1.75 containers, because my instinct said it would be too much cream cheese. It really overpowers the squash.  This recipe may be worth trying again someday if I cut the cream cheese by 1/4, and maybe add more from there.
Great flavor & wonderful texture! My squash-shy husband really enjoyed this soup.
Really tasty soup, for an extra kick I double the cayenne. For a richer flavor I use bone broth instead of water and butter instead of margarine as well.

This recipe is wonderful, i did change it up a little and it came amazing!!! I've made this soup now about 10 times and i think i got it just right, everyone raves about it and asks for the recipe! I use 2 1/2 lbs squash, 4oz cream cheese, 32oz chicken stock and 1 (the secret) beef boullion cube! every thing else I do the same but by mistake I used a beef boullion cube once and it turned out even better!!!!
Love this! The second time I made this I used only one package of cream cheese and a leftover zucchini that I wanted to do something with. Everyone who has tried this loves it!

The basic recipe is ok but it was a little bland.  I added brown sugar, cloves, cinnamon, and nutmeg to taste.  Also followed other reviewers comments Andes an apple and apple juice (no cider n hand).  I only added 4 oz of cream cheese.   This is an essential ingredient as it adds a new layer of flavor but I think the full amount called for in the recipe is over the top.

I cut the cream cheese down to 6 ounces and added some heavy whipping cream(about 1/4 cup but I didn't measure) to make this the flavor texture I liked.  Used chicken broth instead of the chicken cubes and water. Also added cinnamon to sweeten it a bit, and for garnish when serving.  If you are not crazy about onions you can cut that back a bit too, but I used the six tablespoons called for.

I have to say I was a bit intimidated as I have never tried butternut squash!  
I did use the broth instead of water. 

This recipe was easy to follow and a hit with my family!!  I'll definitely be making ahead and freezing for the winter!!

I made this soup on the spur-of-the-moment with fabulous results. I've been asked for an encore, so you know it's good. I read the reviews and did limit the cream cheese to one package (I figured I could always add another, but didn't need to.), and I roasted my squash instead of boiling (old habits). Otherwise, I followed the directions with rave reviews. Thanks

Quick & easy:  I sautéed everything in a pot while squash was in oven roasting.  When cooled, I put cooked squash pieces in the pot and mashed with a potato masher.  Then added cream cheese and again mashed with potato masher.   Done! One pot soup, easy clean up!

Used only 8 oz. cream cheese and added more cayenne. Color and texture were fine. Flavor a bit bland. Pureed  jarred roasted red peppers and swirled (separately)  on top with sour cream. Added a bit of flavor and great presantation.

EASY EASY AND QUICK! I agree only one cream cheese, the soup loses that great squash flavor if you add more. I used boullion cubes, and next time I'll use butter instead of margarine. This is one of my favorite squash soups ever....
awesome recipe!  the kids loved it, even the picky one.

Roasted the squash split lengthwise face down at 375 for 45 minutes first; makes the skin easy to peel and the squash easy to scoop. And cuts the boiling time down to only about 5 minutes once you add to the chicken broth. I cut the cream cheese in half, I used three cans of chicken broth. PHENOMENAL. I made this for a potluck dinner last month and it was the only soup that was really touched out of four choices - everyone loved it. Roommates and friends have requested it 4 other times since. Super easy to make (about 30 minutes after roasting) and VERY delicious.
I've been making this for several years and it's a hit every time!  I baked the squash first, then scoop it out into the chicken broth.  I only use half the cream cheese.
The best!
Very good.  I used 1/2 the (light) cream cheese and extra cayenne.  My squash was out of season, so I had to add a couple of tablespoons of sugar.  That made it perfect.
This recipe is amazing!  I only used 1 box of cream cheese and it's still SO rich.  I also added a bit more cayenne to give it a delicious kick!  Thank you, thank you for this recipe!!

This was a very thick soup, and it was very rich. It was a little too rich to be a soup, but it made an AWESOME gravy! To cut the fat back, I used fat-free cream cheese. To make the fat I put in it healthier, I used EVOO instead of butter.

YUK! WHY IN THE WORLD I WOULD EVEN BOTHER TO MAKE THIS TO BEGIN WITH, IS BEYOND ME----DON'T KNOW WHAT I WAS THINKING. I GUESS SEEING ALL THE "RAVE REVIEWS" MOST LIKELY. SQUASH IS AN OK VEGGIE & THESE "TRENDY" SOUPS SOMETIMES SURPRISE YOU. HOWEVER, IT WAS PRETTY TASTELESS, & NOT MUCH DIFFERENT TASTING THAN IF YOU JUST EAT SQUASH ON A PLATE  TO BEGIN WITH! I AM AN AVID COOK,& GOURMAND----WHY ALL THE RAVINGS OVER THIS IS BEYOND ME. JUST THICK, TASTELESS SQUASH. SORRY, GOTTA BE HONEST.

I made this for my fiance and she LOVED it.  I tweaked the recipe much like someone else who commented.  I didn't use any cream cheese.  I halved and seeded two butternut squash.  I roasted them for a hour at 350 degrees with olive oil, garlic, salt, and pepper.  After the squash was finished roasting I sauteed the onion, and I used chicken stock instead of water.  I also added 1 cup of apple cider and a granny smith apple.  I added slightly more cayenne pepper because we like the spice.  I'll definitely make this soup again!

I halved this recipe--I only had 1/2 a 2.25 lb. butternut squash, so I used half of everything specified, and used organic chicken broth instead of water and bullion. It turned out delightfully. This is the first recipe I've awarded 5 stars. Also, I used fat free cream cheese without any adverse impact on the recipe. This soup is comfort food, with a subtle sweetness and velvety texture. I agree with other reviewers--roast the squash in the oven so the peel comes off easily.

This soup is to die for! My husband muttered "YUM!" after every spoonful. I didn't change a thing and it served us two nights with crusty bread or rolls on the side.  Thanks for posting, this is a keeper for sure!
Way too much cream cheese. Thank goodness I read the reviews first and didn't use the amount in the recipe.

This recipe is amazing. I've made it many times and EVERYONE asks for the recipe. I roast the squash face-down in a 350 degree oven until it's soft enough to be poked with a fork. Then I let it cook and peel. It's much easier this way and the flavor is more intense! I also add a few chopped cloves of garlic when sautéing the onions, double all the spices, and use only 1 package cream cheese. This is a winner every time!

This recipe is very good and very easy.  I did halve the cream cheese.  To lighten the fat I used lowfat cream cheese.  This is now a favorite in our house.  I'm not a big fan of sweet squash recipes so this is great for me!

MADE ADJUSTMENTS! This is a five for sure, although I'd probably make some adjustments to cut the fat if this was going to be in the regular rotation.   If just making a couple times a year, it's perfect like this....  Bake the squash at 350-375 for 40 minutes or so, just till it is easy to scoop from skin. Do the onions with butter of course, I will use only 2 tbsp next time. I doubled the spices and halved the cream cheese. I simmered the onion, water, chicken cubes, and spices for 15 minutes, then added the already baked squash for 5-7 minutes to get the flavors together. Then blended with cc.  Excellent.  Would be a wonderful cup of heavy soup for an appetizer (small cup as it is THICK)

Devin made it.  YUM!  I'm working on my second cup.
He used real butter instead of margarine, red onion, and I added about a teaspoon of sea salt to the pot.   I suggested the immersion blender instead of what they recommended.
AND I think you could cut the cream cheese by half and you would still have a thick and rich soup.
I wanted to add some sausage -maybe next time.
Tasty, thick, soup for a cold winter evening.
Excellent!  I did cut the cream cheese in 1/2 but 16oz probably tastes out of this world.  This is definitely a keeper.
So good! Next time I won't use as much cream cheese and will roast the squash for more flavor!

Other than cutting up the squash the soup was super easy to make.  My husband had one bowl and was filled!  (This never happens with soup)  I made garlic biscuits to go with it and put some chives on top with a swirl of cream and it looked like it came from a five star restaurant!
The cayenne pepper makes this dish.  I also used just one block of cream cheese and it was just as good.
Super easy. Great for Thanksgiving.

This has been my favorite soup recipe for years.  Use half of the cream cheese that the recipe calls for (and substitute with Neufchatel cheese to reduce the fat content,) and double the cayenne to create a perfect balance of sweet, savory, spicy.

I like this recipe but I omitted the curry powder and substituted cinnamon. I think I needed to add more than the 1/2 teaspoon I used. Perhaps a whole teaspoon for half the recipe.  I also left the skin on the apples and the squash and only had small infrequent chunks remaining after liquefying in the blender. More fiber can't hurt for a healthier diet.

Awesome recipe.  I've been making it for years.  Freezes well.  The only thing I changed is that I use half of the  cream cheese that the recipe calls for and I also use the neufchatel and not the full fat version of cream cheese.

Fantastic!!!  I've never made soup before and I must say that this recipe was easy.  I baked the squash beforehand like so many people have suggested and I used chicken broth.  You must try this soup; it's just like in the restaurants.
I loved this recipe.  I made two changes which was only using 1 package of cream cheese and adding carrots to the recipe and it turned out great.
AWESOME!!!
Cut the cream cheese in half.  I used oregano instead of marjoram.
I followed the recipe but used butter and only 4 oz of cream cheese (that's all I had) and it tasted great. It might be better with more cream cheese but it's not necessary.

THIS WAS AWFUL! WE LIKE BUTTERNUT SQUASH,BUT THIS WASN'T EVEN EDIBLE. I REALLY HAD HIGH HOPES SINCE MOST OF THE REVIEWS WERE EXCELLANT. DO NOT WASTE YOUR TIME. I HAD SEVERAL PEOPLE TRY IT AND THEY HATED IT.
A little too much cream cheese
I followed this recipe exactly as stated. It was too creamy. Next time I would only use 8 oz. cream cheese. Nevertheless, my husband still LOVED it.  I will try again.

Very good!  Gave it 4 stars because I followed all the suggested revisions:  only 1/2 block of cream cheese (2 blocks would have totally ruined it), added a pinch of cinnamon, nutmeg and garlic powder.  Served topped with pumpkin seeds.

This was really fantastic!!!
I made it with one package of cream cheese instead of two - one seemed like it was plenty.  Also I put crumbled bacon on top right before serving.  wonderful!
Made the recipe with half the cream cheese but next time I will eliminate it completely. It gave the soup an odd flavor and soup is creamy enough without it.

Excellent.  I loved the addition of cayenne pepper (I used a scant 1/8 tsp., which was plenty).  I also used 2 butternut squashes (probably medium sized) to make the 6 cups.  I just used 1 block of cream cheese and that was plenty- I might even decrease it a bit next time.

This was the first time I'd tried butternut squash soup and both my husband and I loved it.  Rich and creamy; great flavor.  Would be a nice soup to serve as the first course for an elegant dinner with friends.
Very smooth, rich soup, I only used 1 pkg. of cream cheese and as others suggested I roasted the squash first and added a granny smith apple.
In full disclosure I also added 1/4 tsp. white pepper and 1/8 tsp nutmeg while reducing cream cheese by half. Wonderful!

Soup is delicious.  I used onion  powder instead of onions because I have a friend who is allergic to raw ones.   Also, I roasted the squash in the oven with olive oil and salt and pepper.   I used chicken broth (two kinds---Better Than Boullion and Watkins).  I also added about 6 cups of water.   I only used one  8-oz. package of cream cheese, and I did not purée the mixture, I mashed the squash and stirred in the cream cheese.    Very yummy on a cold winter day!

i made quite a bit of modifications. in the end, this is what i did (using this recipie as a guide)   4-5 servings:  I roasted one medium butternut squash in the oven for about 45 minutes.  I seasoned it with salt, pepper and olive oil before i put it in the oven. I did this the night before and scraped the flesh out of the butternut squash and put it in the fridge overnight for easy prep the next day.  In a medium pot, i browned 1 med. onion.  Added  2 carrots, 2 celery, 1 large sweet potato. Let that cook down for 5-7 minutes.  added enough chicken broth to cover the veggies.  Bring to a boil and simmer for 40 minutes.  Using a hand blender, i blended the soup in the pot and added more chicken broth until i got the consistency i wanted.  I threw in salt, pepper, cinnamon, all spice, groud cloves, and ground cayenne pepper.  Sour cream to garnish.   such a versitile soup that you can modify to your taste!
My family enjoyed this one.  I added half of a largely chopped cauliflower and doubled 1/8 teaspoon of cayene.  I served with chopped fresh chives.

My entire famiy loves this soup! I did change a few things, I had roasted buttercup and butter cream squashes. I used about 6 cups loosly packed of the squash.I added a half of red sweet pepper to the onions whie I was sauteing them.I used broth and added a sprinkling extra of the cayenne pepper. Instead of warming after processing I put it in a crock pot to hold while everyone gets together for dinner. a salad and crusty bread and it was a great meal.

This soup is fantastic! Especially after it's a day or two old. I took other recommendations and cut two large butternut squash in half, placed them face down and baked on 375 for 30 min... scooped out the inside and blended it in a blender with the cream cheese in batches. I seasoned just as recommended and it really didn't need anything extra. I've been eating the left overs for two days now with rolls. It gets better the longer it sits. I will definitely make this again!!!

Delicious!
I changed it up by using low-fat cream cheese and only 1 package of it.
Additionally, I cooked my squash in the microwave (ten minutes, cut in half with 1/4 inch of water) while I prepared the other ingredients. I also put the liquids in my sauce pan after lightly sauteing the onions. Then scraped out the squash with a spoon and everything went into my Vita-mix blender and I blended for one minute.

Fabulous consistency: creamy, rich and smooth. For my portion I added a couple extra dashes of cayenne, as I like it on the spicy side.

This is one of the best soups I've ever had!!  I served it to friends who all wanted the recipe.  Even a man who doesn't like squash loved this soup.  I used only 12 oz. of cream cheese, doubled the pepper.  I baked the squash in the oven first, and then used my hand mixer to blend in the cheese.  YUMMY!!

Best squash soup I've ever made! Halved the recipe, using 3 c. butternut squash, and wild onions. Definitely the easiest way to make this it to halve the squash, put in Pyrex with butter and 1/2 c. water and bake until tender, then add other ingredients and blend. Since I only used 3 c. of the cooked squash, I made pumpkin bread with the rest. Very good recipe!!!
we LOVE this soup!

Good recipe. Like others I only used half the amount of cream cheese, any more and you;d run the risk of this being squash-fondue. I'd also suggest being careful the water does not boil off and making sure there is enough liquids when you begin blending, or else it comes out too thick. I also doubled the amount of cayenne pepper, because I like the added kick.

This soup is fantastic!!!!!!!!!!!!!!  Very creamy and easy to make.  I did not add the 16 ounces of cream cheese.  I only added 4 ounces and it was still very creamy!!!!  My 6 year old wanted seconds!!!!  Definitely a keeper!
Really yummy. Loved the consistency. I did put too much cayenne pepper (didn't follow the recipe on that one). I'll do it again with less pepper so my boyfriend can eat it!

I read through many other reviews of the recipe and decided to go with just one pack of cream cheese. however when I finally got to the recipe after a long day of cooking, I realized I only had 5 ounces of cream cheese and it was plenty and probably the bare minimum needed. I used veggie broth from a carton instead of chicken stock or bullion cubes. Also- it took some head scratching to figure this one out- 6 cups is roughly 2 pounds - which is roughly two small sized squashed. It was a great hit and really nice that it was so easy! and oh yeah- I didn't even use butter, used olive oil out of habit and didn't even notice the difference.
Very good. i have a 3 year old and a 4 year old. both had seconds. my daughter had 3rds! Lol. only suggestion-salt.

I made this soup today and it was fabulous!  I looked over the reviews and made the following changes: butter instead of marg, used half the cream cheese, added a pinch of nutmeg, instead of bouillon, I used a product called, "Better than bouillon chicken base".  Thank you for sharing your recipe!

Excellent recipe! These are the adjustments that I made: I used canned chicken broth instead of the boullion cubes and water and, as another reviewer said, 4 oz of cream cheese is just fine!
Thank you!
I loved this! I didn't use nearly as much cream cheese though, but still great!

Really good basic recipe, except I made a few changes.  I roasted the butternut squash, cut side down with a little olive oil, at 350 for 45 minutes.  I also roasted 2 cloves of garlic at 350 for 20 minutes.  I carmelized the onion in a saucepan.  After the squash and garlic were done, I peeled and cut the squash into large cubes.    I disolved the boullion cubes in hot water.  Then I put roasted squash, roasted garlic, carmelized onion, and 1/2 cup heavy whipping cream and pureed, adding boullion water slowly.  I poured the puree into a stock pot on the stovetop and simmered while I seasoned with salt, pepper, cayenne, pinch of thyme, pinch of cinnamon and a dash of nutmeg.    I served with grilled chicken and swiss sandwiches for a warm meal on a snowy night.  My husband and son loved it!

loved it! i've made it numerous times. took the suggestions of other reviews. chopped up some celery, carrots, a granny smith apple and sauteed it with the onion. only added 4 oz of cream cheese and put in a little coconut milk. so soothing on a cold winter day.
So So good!  I only used one package of cream cheese and it was plenty creamy!
I look forward to autumn so I can make this soup!  I use 1/2 the amount of cream cheese and real chicken broth.  This is a wonderful recipe and the soup freezes and reheats wonderfully.

This soup is awesome.  I usually add a couple of pears or apples and some ginger, and cut way back on the cream cheese (1/4 to 1/2 what the recipe states).  If I'm out of cream cheese, I just add milk instead.  It freezes well, too, just add the cream cheese or milk after reheating.  For an easy garnish, you can toast the cleaned squash seeds in a 350 degree oven with 1 tbsp of olive oil and some salt and cinnamon until they start to brown.
I found the cream cheese really took away from the butternut squash flavour (and I cut the amount in half). Perhaps with less cream cheese (or no cream cheese) this might be a keeper.
Wonderful, rich soup!  Cook the squash (halved) before you try to peel and cube it.  You can bake, boil or microwave it.

This was not for me. There was way too much cream cheese, It actually overpowered the flavor of the squash. My boyfriend said it reminded him of the texture of nacho cheese, which it did. I would bypass this recipe if I were you.
Add cinnamon, nutmeg, and allspice.

Love love live this soup!! I've made it several times and husband and I love it. I only use 1 package of cream cheese. I run it thru the blender to smooth it out. Yum. Can't wait for fall and then I'll make it again.

Very easy and delicious recipe! I usually love cream cheese but this recipe does call for a lot. I halved the amount as suggested and it was plenty. I also used reduced sodium chicken broth. I love spice but this was a bit too spicy for my 9 and 5 year old. So I'll probably cut the amount of cayenne next time. Added Crema Mexicana as a garnish which went very well with this soup. 
I was also able to add the entire mixture to the blender at once with no issues.
I think grilled ham and cheese would go great with this soup!
I roasted my squash cause it's way too much trouble to cut.  My family liked it, but it didn't quite make the favorite category - probably because nobody is a butternut squash fan.
Very tasty. I also did a lot less cream cheese, and added these seasonings which were nice: poultry seasoning 2T, ginger 1t, lime juice 3T. This had more breadth and hint more tang.
So good - I didn't have cayenne pepper so I added a few red pepper flakes and it still came out awesome.  I served it with toasted french bread.

Great recipe with a few tweaks.  As other reviews suggested, I cut the squash in half, de-seeded, and roasted (cut side down with skin on) in a pan with some olive oil and salt/pepper for 45 minutes at 350 degrees.  I then let the squash cool and peeled/cubed it.  I think roasting really brings out the flavor.  I also made it vegetarian and substituted the water/bouillon for 3 cups of vegetable broth and double the cayenne pepper.  It was delicious!  Very rich so if you like thinner soup, I would suggest using half the amount of cream cheese.
Absolutely "DELICIOUS".  Will be making it again and again.  Cutting down on the cream cheese was a great idea with no loss of taste.
This soup is delicious. I have made it exactly as described, but I prefer it with half the cream cheese and try substituting the cayenne pepper for curry powder! Delicious!

This recipe was very good, i just changed a couple of things. I added both ginger and nutmeg in addition to the other spices.I used Oregeno instead of majoram.I used 3 sliced cloves of garlic and instead of the cubes and water i used 3 small cans of chicken stock. I did not use any cream cheese, instead i used 1/4 cup of skim milk. Great healthy recipe!!
This great recipe was easy to prepare. Next time I make it, I will cut the cream cheese to 8 ounces and maybe add a little more onions.  Sorry Kraft!

Wow - this was much better than I expected, and much easier.  I used a quart of chicken broth rather than the water/cubes.  I also peeled and chopped an apple to add, and went heavy on the spices (except the cayenne).  I used only 1/2 the cream cheese (low fat), and I just used my little hand mixer, removed from heat after 20 minutes and mixed 8 oz of cream cheese in.  I can only imagine how rich and wonderful this would be had I used all the cream cheese.  Definitely a keeper and good enough for company.
Quick and tasty.  I sauteed the cubed squash for about 5 minutes (after the onions were soft).  Added a bay leaf with other seasonings.  Used half and half and about 4 oz. cream cheese.

I am a cream cheese addict so I thought I would love this recipe.  I cut the cream cheese in half like others suggested and it was still way too creamy.  We had to add milk to make it thinner.  It still was too thick and creamy for me.  I added the fresh ginger as a few people had suggested and it added such a fresh, yummy taste.

Tastes like heaven, and it doesn't hurt that it looks like nacho cheese sauces."  14 yr old daughter's comment.  "Mom, you should makeke this EVERY night!"  11 yr old daughter's comment.    LOL, thought I'd get this all to myself!!  I did roast 2 butternut squash, unseasoned, and only used 1/2 of an 8oz brick of Neufchatel cheese, otherwise made recipe as written (oh, except used only about 1 tbsp butter to saute onions).  Delish!

I thought this was a surprise hit!  It is still a pain to cook butternut sqaush, it takes so long in the oven, and that is the way I do it.  Plan ahead on that one.  I cut the cream cheese down to about 4 ounces and I can't imagine going any richer-- it's a heavy soup, but very flavorful!

I made this soup Saturday.  I didn't add any spices due to personal preference, just salt to taste.  I used 4 cups chicken stock and one 8 oz package cream cheese.  I blended it using my immersion blender.  My husband and I just loved this soup!  I think I will make a big batch to serve on Thanksgiving!

Just made this for 30 people at a 75th birthday party for my mother.  It was a hit.  I did change just a bit to add a little sugar.  It was a nice compliment to the cayenne pepper and turned out great!

Very scrum-de-licous soup!!!!  I did as others and roasted the squash with some oil, minced garlic, salt and pepper.  Only used one package of cream cheese and substituted red pepper for cayenne pepper.  Just a pinch of cinnamon and nutmeg and you have yourself a tasty little soup.  This soup tastes great as is but I think I will add some broccoli and chicken or cooked bacon to spice it up a bit for my husband.

This soup was wonderful! I used the suggestion to use chicken broth instead of boullion and reduce the cream cheese. I also added a teeny bit of allspice and crumbled a table spoon of bacon. Oh Yum! It was wonderful. And I must admit today for lunch it's even better. The only thing I will change next time is, I will definitely make a double batch.

This had a good flavor, but it was sooooo thick and rich, even after I cut the amount of cream cheese in half!! I cannot imagine using the whole 16 ounces. I will probably find a different recipe if I want to make butternut squash soup again.
I loved it, kids thought it was too spicy with the Cayenne Pepper (oh well I thought it was great!). I might do a batch someday without it....just white pepper instead.
Awesome flavor!
Perfect combo of sweet, savory, creamy, and spicy. This is the BEST fall soup.

Wow! I recently discovered butternut squash soup when I visited South Africa and couldn't wait to come home and make my own. I roast the squash first as several reviews say and add some ground cloves and cinnamon. I also cut the cream cheese all the way down to only 1/2 of one 8 oz bar and control the thickness by adding chicken broth a little at a time. Great recipe!

My  friend served a squash soup at her wedding as an appetizer, and I was hoping to relive the experience, but this wasn't quite the flavor I was hoping for. I did halve the cream cheese, which I think was a good suggestion, but still not "the best" in my opinion.
Mary, your recipe is awesome!  As you recommended, we halved the cream cheese. It was OUT of this world!!!  Thank you SO much for sharing!  It is the BEST soup my husband and I have ever had!!!

AMAZING recipe, thank you!!!  I only had half the amount of cream cheese recommended and it was perfect. I didn't have cayenne OR marjoram; I added chili powder and rosemary. I roasted the squash first as some suggested.
I made this soup at my job and got raves.

I also baked the squash in the shell for an hour, with olive oil, salt, pepper, and garlic powder. And then scooped it out-easy!  And I used only one block of cream cheese.  I only added some ginger to flavor it.  And it was really, really, good!!
This was amazing.  Even my college-age son loved it.  I used half the amount of cream cheese called for and found that it was more than rich enough.

this is a terrific soup!  super easy and everyone who tries it loves it!  i always cut my squash in 1/2 and seed then roast in the oven.  i find that 1 lg package of  1/3 less fat cream cheese is plenty.  i made this for the teachers at my kids school last year and this year they requested it and a great # wanted the recipe.  thanks for a great recipe, Mary!

This is delicious!  I do not normally like squash but love this soup. Fantastic! Used butter, chicken stock, less cream cheese (only 4 oz.), and baked the squash. Easy. Best soup recipe I have. Thanks!
My family and friends love this soup. Even people that don't like squash like this soup.

Disappointing!  You have to like thick, creamy soups that have the consistency of baby food to really enjoy this soup.  I did not like it at all, and I thought that the cream cheese (even though I put half of what the recipe called for) made the soup too creamy.  I had to throw it out!
Amazing soup, added a few tbsp of maple syrup, and it was perfect.
Great recipe. The cayenne pepper adds a great kick. I like to toss in a few dried cranberries, walnuts and a sprinkle of fresh parsley to make it feel extra classy.

The was excellent!  Because I am trying to eat  healthier, I used only one fourth of the cream cheese and it was still very tasty.  I always cut my butternut squash in half and wrap with foil and bake until soft.
Used only 1 package of cream cheese (light) it was plenty rich enough without adding the second one.

I had never made butternut squash soup before and I used this recipe as a starting point. I ended up making many alterations though, and I think they were definitely worth mention:

- roasted the squash for 45 minutes, cut side up, with a light brushing of olive oil
- used 1/2 a red onion, sauteed in *butter* then added 1/2 t marjoram, 1/4 t black pepper, 1/4 t cayenne, pinch of fresh ground nutmeg, and pinch of cinnamon, as well as four sage leaves
- chopped up a honey crisp apple and added that with 3 c water + 2 T chicken stock
- simmered this while the squash roasted
- added squash when it was finished and simmered for maybe 15 minutes longer (take out sage leaves before pureeing)
- pureed everything in a blender with only 8 oz cream cheese instead of 16 oz
- left on heat for 15 minutes longer to marry the flavors
- served with a dollop of cream cheese

My boyfriend is a professional cook and he declared this to be the best butternut squash soup he's ever had! He even bragged about it to his coworkers the next day. The added cayenne gave it a bit more kick, which we really loved, and the apple added another layer of flavor.
I did not care for this.
Super easy to make and tastes great!!  I would probably use just slightly less cayenne pepper next time but other than that it was great!!

Added some carrots and celery to the squash and roasted in oven at 400 for approx 40 min. Also used a whole onion and chicken stock (from a box.) Used 1/2 the cream cheese and added extra chicken stock until I got the desired thickness. IT WAS DELICIOUS!

Perfect for these bitter Canadian winters. I used vegetable bouillion instead of chicken so that I could share it with a vegetarian friend. The cream cheese does wonders for the texture, whether you use a little or a lot. I also tried a batch with a couple of skinned pears pureed into it, which sounds a bit bizarre but adds a lovely subtle flavour. Thanks so much!
I substituted chicken broth for water and chicken boullion.  No other changes and it was delicious!
Very tasty!!  Based on other reviews I roasted the squash first, cut the cream cheese in half and used twice as much cayenne.
Whoa. Yum. Very rich but so good. I used butter instead of margarine and Swanson broth rather than cubes. Try it!
YUM! Took other reviewers advice and only used half the cream cheese. First time cooking with butternut squash and this is a keeper!

Yummy!   Very easy to make and I didn't even need to tweak the receipe.  The aroma of the soup cooking brought the kids out of their rooms to find out what smellled so delicious!   We will definitely keep this one!  THANK YOU!
Half the cream cheese and add a cup od half and half for a better soup...

This recipe is all about comfort. I cut my squash in half length wise, coated it in olive oil, salt and pepper and roasted cut side down on baking sheet at 375 for 45 minutes for a small one and added 15 minutes longer for a large squash. Let cool until easy to handle then scoop out flesh (trying not eat much). I used canned chicken broth. I increased the cayenne to 1/4 tsp and it leaves a nice little after heat. Bring everything up to a simmer then add squash. I used a stick blender to puree soup and when smooth as I wanted it I added 4 oz. room temperature cream cheese cut into cubes. Bring soup back up to simmer then serve. The small amount of cream cheese adds thickness and creaminess without being identifiable. Left overs will have to be thinned as the soup thickens as it cools. Great recipe.
Great winter soup!
I LOVE THIS RECIPE!  I did reduce the amount of cream cheese, other than that, I followed all the other instructions.  OMG!  This is soooo good!
A great recipe! I add sour cream instead of cream cheese and it's delicious!
Steve grunted alot eating this soup.  Make it again and again and again
Amazing!  I have been asked by my father to can it for him to freeze.  He asks me to make it all the time.  Everyone that tastes it loves it!  So easy too!
Fast easy and delicious

I added to much onion but this dish still came out rather good. I think it could almost go without the onion and bacon. My daughter loved it and ate most of it which is impressive because she is 2 years old and usually hates stuff like this. I almost wanted to add creamcheese instead of more flour to the base of the soup but I decided not too. I almost wanted to also add some brown sugar because I think that would have really added a punch of flavor. For this recipe I baked the buttnut squash with butter and brown sugar in the middle of the squash and to cut the squash I did as one reviewer suggested and microwaved the squash for five minutes in water before cutting overall great recipe!
Outstanding. I've been making this for years from this recipe and still love it! I add an apple, a little vanilla, cinnamin and brown sugar. It is amazing!
Tremendous recipe, I altered based on other reviewers; microwave the squash and half the cream cheese.  I'll try alternate next time. but this is a delicious, very easy to make recipe.
This is such an easy recipe. I baked my squash. Came out yummy. I'm making this again.
So good just as it is.  All my friends wanted the recipe!
Yummy, Yummy, Yum.  The richness, smoothness, and taste of this recipe has dazzled my family.  It has been requested every Thanksgiving since I found the recipe 3 years ago.
Instead of water, I substituted chicken broth.
LOVE IT! Used lowfat cream cheese and only half the amount.

I made this for our neighborhood pot luck.....where it recieved rave reviews.  I made it per the recipe and it was terrific.  Next time, I will try to cut some of the cream cheese for a healthier version as others have suggested.  This is a delicious soup!

Used one package of reduced fat cream cheese...  didn't have any onions or butter!  YEEKS!  Used ideas of other reviews of roasting the squash at 375 for 45 min...  Used dried minced onions and used poultry gravy mix...  (I know I need to go to the store!lol)  This was SOOOO good!  Oh my!

This was great.  I baked the squash instead of cutting it into cubes first, didn't saute the onions (so didn't use the butter), and only used half the cream cheese - that cut about 120 grams of fat from the recipe.  I also threw a couple of cloves of garlic into the puree.
I made this in my electric pressure cooker. Came out great!
Don't forget to add garlic!
This was yummy!! It was like a thick cheese soup and I dipped some artisan tostitos in it!

For my taste it was far too creamy, and the cream cheese took away too much of the squash flavor. The recipe's author does mention, though, cutting down the cream cheese if it's too rich. And I took her alternative suggestion and used chicken broth instead of bullion and water.

This soupd was too rich for me with 2 bars of cream cheese, so the next time I made it I used only one 8 ounce reduced fat cream cheese, and used 7 cups of butternut squash and it was the best butternut squash soup I have had.  A friend suggested toasting some pecans and coconut and sprinkling them over the top for decoration and a little crunch.  This made it even better.  Yummmm.

I halved the squash and microwaved until soft like I always do. I scooped out the squash and added about 1 & 1/2 cups of water to puree. I also added 1 tart apple (peeled and cored) to the squash when pureeing. I used vegetable bouillon instead of chicken,  only 1 - 8oz package of lower fat cream cheese, 1/4 tsp of nutmeg and topped at table with chopped chives.
This was delicious...I used 1 pkg of cream cheese and cut the cayenne pepper in half.

Excellent.  I loved this soup.  I took the advice of others and only used one package of cream cheese.  I think it would be too thick if you used two.  I also put the cubes of squash in the oven for about 20 minutes while preparing the other ingredients.  I'm not sure if that made a difference, but the flavor of the soup was excellent.  Thanks for sharing.

I have never made anything like this, and it was not only easy, but wonderful!   I roasted the squash first for about 50 minutes, then scooped it into my other ingredients.  I used chicken broth (made with powder and water) and cut down the cream cheese to only one package.  It was delicious and everybody raved about this fantastic soup.   Thanks for sharing, Mary!!  :)

My whole family loved this soup the first time I made.  I only used one package of cream cheese and added some cinnamon and nutmeg.  I also roasted the squash in the oven before adding it to the stock.  I will make this recipe over and over again.
Great soup. Family love it.

Quite good, although I altered the recipe somewhat, so I'm not sure if it still counts as the same recipe... Like many other commenters, I roasted the squash rather than boiling it. I also used 8 oz. of some homemade herbed cream cheese I had. It had thyme in it, so I let that stand in for the marjoram. Basically, any combo of squash, broth, and cream put through the blender is going to be pretty tasty though. :-)

I served this for a dinner for 20.  It was a huge hit. My family was very pleased I had leftovers. I modified it slightly by using chicken broth, using only 2 packages of cream cheese and substituted hot sauce for the cayenne.
If I was a making a quantity for 6 I don't wouldn't put in any cream cheese.  It would still be perfect.

This is so good!  I picked up a bag of already peeled and cut squash at Costco that yielded exactly 6 cups.  I used chicken stock in lieu of cubes and water, I also added 1/2 cup of apple cider.  I only used one package of cream cheese and found that to be plenty.
Roasted squash, added some sherry, and used low fat sour cream 1/2 cup instead of cream cheese or cream. Nice recipe, would recommend!

I've made different variations of this recipe for years. I never have put cream cheese in any of them... and after tasting this soup I never will again. The soup was very rich. My advice is find another recipe...
