First time to even eat butternut squash soup.  Loved it!  Sweet and hearty with a slight bite.  I did take the advice of many and went with half the cream cheese.  It was almost too rich with 1 package, I can't imagine 2 packages.  Edit/add: After making this multiple times now, I think the key is making sure you have enough liquid to start, and to make sure you catch it at the right time.  You want to boil the squash until it's breaking down, but not turning into a paste.
Xcellent!!! It has great flavor...not sure if that squash from the local farmer made much of a difference but I'm sold on the farmer and the soup.

This was very easy to prepare after I fought the squash to cut into chunks.  I did not have marjoram so I did not use it & I used crushed jalapeño instead of cayenne pepper.  I thought it was delicious, but very rich.  Next time I'll use less cream cheese.   This was my first time ever to cook butternut squash.

Great recipe!  My family, which includes a 5 and 9 year old, absolutely loved this soup.  I chose to roast the squash first and included  seasoned sauteed chicken diced.  We had it for Sunday dinner and it was a hit.

Took the advice from others and changed it a little. Mostly because I didn't have cream cheese and I did not want to go to the store. Roasted it for 40min face down, then 15 face up with butter and garlic. Then did what others suggested. I also added finely chopped apples to give it a crunch. It was a big hit.

I can't say if this is the best recipe because I followed the advice of previous reviews.  So I would give the reviewers 5 stars!!  I roasted the squash, which made it much easier to cut up.  I used a mixture of bouillion, chicken broth and Better Than Bouillion because I didn't have enough of any of them.  I skipped the cream cheese, added a little garlic and some sherry.  It was plenty thick enough and very tasty.  I will try it again and add a smidge of cream cheese to see how it tastes, but I didn't need the extra calories this time.
Amazingly good, easy to make using simple ingredients.

Replace the water with vegetable broth. Great soup to start the holiday meal.
Place squash in the microwave for a minute and it will be easier to cut.

This recipe was awesome with two minor changes.  I used butter instead of margarine (yuck) and I used chicken broth instead of water and bouillon cubes.  With these changes, this was the best Butternut squash soup I ever had!
one of my favorites.  i leave out the cream cheese entirely and add some thyme.

This recipe is AMAZING!
The cream cheese really gives a beautiful texture. However I modified this a bit. I used 1 package of cream cheese and 1 wedge of smoked Gouda. It have the soup an amazing, rich smoky flavor. Highly recommend making this! It was a huge hit and I will be using this recipe again

I made this soup for the first time as the first course for our Thanksgiving dinner. It was absolutely delicious! Rich, creamy, with a little heat from the cayenne pepper. My guests nearly licked their bowls clean!

I only used one and a half blocks of cream cheese, though, due to the suggestions of reviewers here. I thought it came out fine!

Thanks for the recipe, Mary!
Delicious, and oh-so-easy! Substituted a greek yogurt based cream cheese for the regular. Smooth and creamy with the classic butternut flavor. Yum! This will be a regular.
very yummy!  My spice adverse family didn't like the pepper though.  Next time I'll try it without it. Also I only used 1 package of cream cheese

This was certainly a tasty (and a guilty) soup.  I don't know if it needed the whole pound of cream cheese, but it made it delicious.  When the weather gets cold and the days get shorter, this will lift your spirits for a bit!

This is my daughter's favourite soup. She takes it to school for lunch throughout the fall and winter months. I replace the water and chicken boullion with vegetable broth. I also roast the squash in the oven first. (Cut in half,  vegetable side down in about a 1/2 inch of water at about 375 degrees for 40 mins)  With 20 mins left in roasting the squash, I put in 2 peeled, cored and quartered MacIntosh apples. Once the squash is roasted (fork should easily pierce the skin), I remove the skins and throw the squash along with the apples in the pot with the rest of the simmering soup base. At the very end I use the hand blender to smooth out the lumps. This is so delicious. I have served it as an appetizer for Christmas dinner as well. As a helpful hint - I once bought frozen cubed squash thinking I was saving time. DO NOT do this, it really lacked flavour. It was the only time my daughter did not finish the batch. There is a wonderful taste that comes from the roasted squash.

AWESOME!!  I followed the other suggestions and added less cream cheese...also I baked the squash first then used my hand blender in the pot to mix.  Big hit!  I have to say it was better with the squash from our garden rather than the supermarket.
Delicious!  Definitely half or quarter the amount of cream cheese you add.  Also, I tried making it with acorn squash.  Not quite as good, but not a bad option.
Best soup I've ever made! Used half the cream cheese, but plenty rich. Just called my mother & told her she must make this!

This recipe is excellent!  It's tastes like it takes hours to make but of course it doesn't!  I think I only had about 4 cups of squash so I only included 1/2 pkg of LIGHT cream cheese.  The richness still seems so sinful!  I chopped the squash into small cubes, to help with cooking and the later pureeing.  I also cubed the cream cheese before adding to the blender.  I will be memorizing this one!  Thanks, Mary!

I really liked this soup, but I too put half a block of cream cheese and I think next time I would put a little bit less, too rich for me. I would definitly baked the squash, just easier to cut. I will definitly make that soup again.

This recipie was super easy and really delicious.  I made a few changes...veggie broth for my vegetarian daughter and only 1/2 the cream cheese plus it was lite cream cheese.  It was still super rich, might try 1/2ing again the cream cheese.  The next day I added in more veggie broth to thin it out.

Very tasty soup - restaurant quality! I will be serving this for Thanksgiving as I think it has universal appeal. Thick and Creamy and Filling. 
I did have a problem though, with the squash itself. It is impossible to cut thru with a knife, I ended up scrabling up a way to peel and cube it and had to microwave it to soften it up. Once it was cubed, everything else was easy.
Fantastic!!! Easy to make and it is always a hit.

This is a very pretty dish. I really wish I liked it more. I cut back the cream cheese, but the resulting soup reminded me of baby food. I think the cream cheese just makes it too thick. I wonder if leaving out the cheese and adding a little half and half or whole milk would improve the consistency.
WISH I COULD GIVE THIS A 10!!! This soup is soooo good!

Thanks for sharing such a great recipe! Per reviews, I roasted the squash (and garlic) first, to make the squash easier to peel. The only substitutions I made were: bacon fat instead of margarine for sauteing the onion and plain yogurt instead of cream cheese (because I had it already). 

We had mixed reviews over this in our house... I loved it. It has a gorgeous color, a smooth texture, and an uncomplicated flavor with a bit of a kick. This is quite a spicy soup. It was too 'hot' for my three year old & I ended up making something else for her. Next time, I'll keep that in mind. My squash-hating husband didn't like it, but said I should make this at Thanksgiving (though I'm guessing he meant so he'd only have to eat it once a year! *laugh*).
I just made this soup tonight and it is wonderful!  I only used 1 package of cream cheese and it was still really rich.  I also added roasted red peppers.  I will definitely make this again!
I loved this recipe. Easy, quick and a crowd pleaser.

You can make this recipe more exciting by adding a can of corn and some roasted russet potatoes. I diced my potatoes and drizzled them with olive oil with a little salt and pepper before roasting them in the oven. Add the corn and potatoes as while you heat the soup after it's been blended. Makes it heartier and SO good! P.S. My son loved it with CHEEZITS on top!
One of my favorite recipes!  I use half the cream cheese and substitute the other half with soft tofu to throw in some protein.  This is an exceptional recipe!

A couple of variations that I did with this recipe:
It takes a little longer, but the night before I cooked the soup, I roasted the squash in the oven until they are soft.  This makes it easier to get the "meat" out when you're ready to make the soup and it gives the soup a fabulous nutty roasted flavor.
Also, instead of adding cream cheese, I added heavy cream, it makes the soup much lighter, and If you have family members that are slightly lactose intolerant, they can usually handle the heavy cream over the cream cheese (or add Lactaid, which works very well).
But this soup recipe was very easy to make and very delicious. It is my new favorite soup.  Thank you for submitting it!

This is amazing! By the way 2 butternut squashes equals around 12 cups (oops!) so I had to double the recipe, however, I kept the same amount of cream cheese (2 pkgs). I baked the squash at 375F for 45 minutes, next time I'll bake it a little less because they were a pain in the butt to peel! Also, I used homemade chicken stock and butter. However, this was SO much work because I didn't have an immersion blender.. I had to throw it in the food processor in batches and it got really, really messy. So beware. Other than that, this is definitely a keeper and I'll definitely make it for company some time.
This was delicious.  I wouldn't change a thing.

Absolutely delicious soup. I roasted the squash in the oven and only used 1 package of cream cheese and it was so good. I loved the little bite you get from the cayenne pepper, maybe add a dash more. Oh, i also simmered the broth with 2 bay leaves. I am going to start growing squash in my garden from now on just so i can make this soup.

This soup is terrific!!! Made it exactly per the recipe and even my girls, ages 8 and 2 loved it. It's filling, so definitely can have as a meal. I tried a little nutmeg sprinkled on it before serving. Very good.  Thanks!
Super easy to throw together and always a crowd pleaser. I like to make it the day before and let the flavor develop....mmmm.

This soup was a hit at thanksgiving dinner after I made a couple of changes.  The first time I made it I followed the recipe exactly and found it too salty and way to rich with the full amount of cream cheese.  So instead of adding chicken boullion cubes I made the water into chicken stock and only put in 1/4 of the cream cheese called for in the recipe.  I also used light cream cheese.  The result was a yummy creamy soup great for a cold winters day.

I’ve made this recipe several times with success.  Since I dislike cutting the squash, I bake it in the oven for 1 hour at 350 degrees along with one head of garlic – sprinkled with olive oil.  (roasted garlic)

I’ve used vegetable broth as well as chicken broth.  One package of the cream cheese instead of the two.  I’ve also skipped the seasoning other than a pinch of the cayenne pepper.

I've taken this to 2 soup festivals and it is always the first soup to disappear! I halved the cream cheese, used chicken stock instead of bouillan and water and added more cayenne. Mmmmmmm...Excellent!!!!!

I LOVE THIS SOUP!!!  I have made this now four times in the last two months.  The reason I only gave it 4 stars is because I did make a few changes.  As another reviewer suggested I have been adding 1-2 apples (depending on size) & 1 cup apple cider.  Also, the cream cheese is not at all necessary for either taste or texture.  I've never submitted a review before but I just made my fourth batch tonight and discovered something that I had to share:  USE CHICKEN BROTH INSTEAD OF BOUILLON!  I've been using broth just because I had so much on hand but decided I'd try it with bouillon tonight and it just is not the same.  I even ended up adding the cream cheese this time in an attempt to improve the flavor.  Broth is definitely the way to go!

I've made this several times and it always comes out wonderfully. It's very forgiving to little adjustments per your taste. I've tried roasting the squash, scooping it out, and burning my fingers (since I'm too impatient to wait for it to cool) and I've peeled it, bruising my knuckles on the cutting board a few times, and honestly, either way, it tastes just great, so whichever seems easier for you. I like the addition of nutmeg to the spices and I definitely use broth (chicken or vegetable). It also works well with the addition of other squash like Delicata, Kabocha, Carnival, etc. Enjoy!

It was really very easy to make and quite tasty. I followed suggestions from a lot of the other reviewers by roasting the squash ahead of time to make it easier to cut and peel and shorten the cooking time. I only added 1 package of cream cheese, used chicken stock instead of water, and added a little red curry powder.  The results were fantastic, my husband who doesn't like squash or curry really liked it! I will for sure make this again to use up garden squash.
I loved this!  The only change I made was that I roasted the squash in the oven first... YUM!
All we tasted was the cream cheese.  I would not make this again.

This soup was absolutely FABULOUS!!!!  I couldn't believe that I made something that tasted like it came from a 5 star restaurant!  It is super easy.  I didn't have any marjoram handy so I just substituted a little cinnamon and nutmeg...not much.  I am so glad I found this.  I will be making it for years to come.  My extended family thought it was outa this world, and coming from my dad, being a restaurant owner, that is a big thing!!
I bought a butternut squash at the grocery store.  The cashier kept talking about this soup that she had.  So, I decided to try it.  I was not really impressed.  Very flavorful, but way too thick.

Very good recipe! I grilled the butternut squash cubes (gives it the awesome smokey flavor!) Oh, and I highly suggest adding some chicken and crumbled bacon or turkey bacon in this soup! :D Thanks for the awesome recipe!
This is one of the tastiest soups I've ever made.  I roasted my butternut squash as others suggested and used only 1 package of cream cheese.  Outstanding.

Was not disappointed!  I did reduce butter and cream cheese by 1/2 and used Neufchatel cheese in place of cream cheese (1/3 less fat).  Changed marjoram to thyme.   Added garlic croutons and a little pepper when served...delish!
EXCELLENT soup! Very easy to make! Big hit with my family!

This soup is awesome! I only used 1-1/2 packages of low fat cream cheese and it was quite rich. And, I added some steamed broccoli and baked chicken to zip it up a little. Yum! 
Thanks Mary!!

With an overabundance of butternut squash, I decided to try this because it sounded different.  I am so glad I did and even more so, glad I read the reviews first. I too also used 1/2 the amount of cream cheese and might use even less next time. I let everyone choose the amount of cayenne pepper they prefer. Next time I will try and leave it a bit chunky for some texture.

Oh, this was wonderful! I made it for company and it got rave reviews...one guest said it was "gourmet restaurant quality"! I served it with a 1/4 canned pear in the middle, and tossed a bit of fresh parsley over it. I only used 1 cream cheese, but used half and half cream to get the consistency I wanted, and I used butter and 1 whole med onion (just because we love them)and about 10C of squash, as we needed the quantity.

This is true quality!! You will NOT be disappointed in this recipe...I've already sent it out to two couples from last night! ENJOY!

So satisfying.  I followed other reviewers and used about half the suggested cream cheese.  I also added an apple, cinnamon, and nutmeg.  Before serving I drizzled with cream and toasted coconut...YUM to say the least, thanks!

This soup is absolutely delicious. Like a lot of the people who commented, I halved the cream cheese and baked my squash instead. I also subbed oregano for the marjoram, and threw in a new potato because I wasn't sure if I had enough squash.

This was delicious!  I was faithful to the spirit of this recipe, but I made it in the crock pot by adding all the ingredients to the crock, cooking on low for 6 hours, pureeing with an immersion blender, adding cheese, pureeing again.  I used one LARGE butternut squash (I think the squash was around 5 lbs whole, and yielded 10 cups of cubed squash).  I also increased the onion to one whole onion, chopped, and substituted 16 oz Philadelphia Lite Cream Cheese for the 16 oz cream cheese called for.
Our catering company at work makes the best butternut squash soup, but this one is right there with it.  It was super (souper) tasty.  The only thing I added was a dash of cinnamon.

This soup is rich and delicious even using only 4 ounces of cream cheese.  I made a big pot of it and froze it in quart zip-lock bags BEFORE adding the cream cheese.  When I defrost it, I add the cream cheese just before serving.  It is a huge hit with my 13-yr old daughter too.

This was incredibly good.  Just as good as any 5-star restaurant.  I used 1/2 the cream cheese (could have actually cut down just a bit more), added about 1/2T of brown sugar (probably didn't even need it), and added a bit more cayenne pepper, and about 1/8 tsp of nutmeg.  Yum!!  And, so easy!!  Oh, I also used pre-cut butternut squash (thank you Whole Foods) and roasted it instead of boiling it.

In an attempt to eat more fresh produce this year I bought 2lbs of peeled and chopped butternut squash from Sam's Club and decided to try something new. I scaled the recipe down to 4 servings and ended up with 6 - 1cup servings. I didn't have marjoram so I subbed oregeno. I also roasted the squash for 25 minutes in the oven, per the suggestion of others. The first night the soup was just okay, but after a couple of days the soup was amazing. I had it for lunch everyday for a week, and the 1 cup was just enough to really satisfy me. I will definitely make it again, and let it sit for a day or two before I plan to eat it. Thanks!

Really good. Rich, creamy goodness. I followed other reviewers and roasted the squash before and used just 1 package of cream cheese. I also added comice  pears. Soooo good. And really easy as a weeknight meal.
I did not have cream cheese, so this review is for the recipe with a yogurt substitute.  It was so delicious.  My kids gobbled it up!

Very Yummy! I doubled the cayenne, may even use more next time. Didn't have enough squash, so I substituted about half the amount with boiled baby carrots. I also used half the cream cheese. Will definitely make again!

I actually was looking for a recipe to use for some butternut squash that was sitting in my freezer. I just tossed the squash into the chicken stock and cooked! I did not have marjoram on hand so I did add a touch of cumin (which gave it a smoky southwestern style flavor)and dill (which always tastes good on vegetables). My kids had seconds and wanted it for lunch the next day! Mmmmmmmmm!
I really liked this recipe,but just a little too mild for my taste -   I doubled the spice quantities & it was fantastic.
Made it to original recipe - but roasted the squash for 45 minutes.  Used 2 low fat cream cheese packages.  You could hear the "mmmmmmm"s around the table during our Thanksgiving meal.
I've never had squash before and decided to take a gamble after watching a chef make it on TV. I am not dissapointed. This is really good...you won't be sorry.
Amazing - everyone LOVES this recipe!  It's so rich, I can't eat more than a cup at a time, but thats fine because then it just lasts longer.
This is incredible!!!  The second time making it, only used 3 chicken bouillon cubes.  Gave it more of a squash flavor, but admit it was best with 4 cubes.

This soup was so delicious, everyone loved it! I did change the recipe a little. I used one large squash. I roasted it in the oven 350 degree for 1hour , cut in half, face side down in a cake pan with water in it to keep the edges from burning. I added a dash of cinnamon, 8 ounces of milk and used 2 cups of water instead of three and one cup of chicken stock.
Decreased cream cheese to just 3/4 of 1 package. Used broth instead of water/bouillon. Fantastic - eating it as I type!

Followed the recommendation to cut the cream cheese in half; otherwise made no alterations.  The soup is really good but I think 4oz is still too much cream cheese.  I'll make it again but try adding carrots and cinnamon.
This soup is very rich, creamy and delicious!  I followed some of the other suggestions and roasted the squash,added some celery and I also doubled the cayenne.Easy and tasty!
Amazing ! I baked the squash first. This is our new favorite soup!
DEFINITELY only need 1 brick of cream cheese. Other than that, it was YUUUMMMMY!!!!!!!!
Add more spice!
Very yummy.  I would use only I cream cheese block.  I made it both ways and yu lose the squash flavor with 2.
easy to make and even people who hate squash (me!) will love this.  I toasted some hazel nuts and chopped them up and sprinkled them on top as a garnish.  mmmmmmmm
Yum! Roasted quartered butternut (drizzled with olive oil and sprinkled with salt and pepper), peeled and added as directed. Cooked for ~10 min with broth before pureeing.

Called for WAY to much cream cheese!  Made it more like a sauce than a soup.  Had to cut it with more broth.  On the up side...I did like the seasoning choices and have go on to use them in my own recipe for Butternut Squash soup.

This soup is delicious!! My family loved it so I will definitely be making it again as the weather gets colder. I only used 1 package of cream cheese as other people had mentioned on their review and it was just enough to give the right amount of cream cheese flavor.
This is absolutely delicious!!! Used one container of spreadable cream cheese, and nutmeg instead of coriander.

I used SLJ6's suggestions and roasted the squash and used apple cider and an apple in the mix.  Added some fat free half and half at the end.  Didn't use the marjoram or cream cheese, but did use the cayenne and black pepper.  Turned out great!!
I made 1 1/2 recipes and used 2 8 oz fat free cream cheese. I also added nutmeg and extra cayenne pepper.  It was good and creamy and my family wants to know when we can have it again.

This soup is ok.  It definetly needs more spices in it and less then half the cream cheese.  I used one 8 oz package and I felt like I was eating melted cream cheese with a zing.  I did add chicken and top it with tortilla chips, this help cut back the heaviness a little.  It was easy to do, just not my personal favorite recipe.
I thought this soup was just OK.  It just didn't seem to have the flavor I was looking for.  I've had other butternut squash soups before and this receipe lacked what I was looking for.

VEGETARIAN VERSION
I served this for a dinner party and it got high raves. Two people emailed me the next day for the recipe. 
However, I made one small change; I used vegetarian bullion instead of chicken. Trust me.....no one missed the chicken stock!
Oh my god, this was so delicious and almost  perfect...maybe a bit too thick but that's easy to fix.

I love this easy recipe. I make it often and yes roast the squash first. I also half the cream cheese and use broth, Sometimes I add an acid like cooking sherry or a couple tablespoons balsamic vinegar. The original recipe was perfect the way it is though, I just like to experiment.

This was delicious! To make it even easier, cut the squash in half, and place it cut side down in a baking pan with about an inch of water.  Cover and bake at 350 F for about an hour or hour and a half. This will make it so much easier than trying to peel it!  When cool, scoop the insides out into a blender or food processor and combine with the cream cheese to puree.  Add this to the other ingredients and heat through. I  used chicken broth instead of water and boullion and used a little crushed red pepper instead of cayenne. I also used only one package of light cream cheese. This was quite easy and truly delicious!
Delicious!  We chose to use only one pack of cream cheese and add an extra cup of water.  The original recipe is very thick and rich.

Great Recipe! Thank you so much!
This was easy, quick and delicious.  Like so many others, I did alter the recipe some based on the many reviews I read.  The alterations I made that I would do again: Add butter instead of margarine, buy pre pealed and precut fresh squash then boil in store bought chicken broth, add cinnamon, nutmeg about 1/8 cup of fresh parsley and doubled the cayenne for a little extra kick!  Flavor was amazing! Didt not need ANY salt.. love that!

If you have one, try it.  I love the rice cooker because its easy and fool proof.  Sometimes rice can be a pain, so if you are looking to impress, take no chances...just don't eat the thin, scorched layer on the bottom! If you do prefer the stove, here are some tips. 1. Your rice is NOT going to "puff" while being sauteed.  I don't know why it said that.  Rice will puff, or cook rather, when its completely submerged in liquid. Instead, the first step is meant to give it a more golden color in the end. 2. If you find your rice more "wet" than you'd like, leave on simmer but take off the cover.  It will evaporate the extra liquid. 3. To make rice soft: Don't take off the cover while cooking, let your rice stand for about 10 minutes after cooking, then fluff with a wooden spoon, and let stand again for 5 more minutes. 4. If its still not soft enough to eat after cooking, re-cover and cook another 5-10 minutes and refer back to #3.  Hope this helps!

The only things I did different were I added the onion to the skillet first and sautéed just until they were opaque, then added the rice. I added a little more tomato sauce since I just added the whole can (it was a small can), so it was probably about 3/4 cup instead of the 1/2 cup that the recipe calls for and I added a whole tsp. of Cumin. LOVE.THIS.RICE.  Sooooo great.  Don't let the simplicity of the ingredients fool you....this has TONS of flavor if you do it right!  DO NOT use a rice cooker, either!  You must remember to sautee the spices as you brown/toast the rice so the flavors absorb into the rice. So important!  Add some fresh garlic, too!  The toasting of the rice gives it a nutty depth. very easy to make

Very bland.  Will look for a better recipe.

This is my go-to mexican rice recipie using a few alterations after reading the reviews! 

I sautee about 2 cloves garlice with 1/4 chopped red onion, 1tbs olive oil and the cumin for a few minutes. This was just O.K. for us.  It was somewhat bland, needed quite a bit more flavor to win the hearts of this family.  As with other reviewers, ours never got past the "slightly underdone" texture either.
Amazing!!  I will never make Mexican rice another way.  I think I could get by with less oil though, so next time I will try cutting back a bit.
Could taste a bit bland but for a side dish it is very tasty and satisfactory. Easy to make and all the ingredients will usually be at hand in the cupboard.

This is a simple, very tasty Mexican rice dish. It compliments my (typically very spicy) Mexican dishes well!  I followed the recipe exactly except adding about a teaspoon of fresh garlic along with the garlic salt & cumin. 
Two thumbs up!
Tastes just like what is served at our local Mexican joint.  YUM!  I made no changes and follow the recipe as directed.  Turns out perfectly!

Pretty good.  Tastes authentic enough for me!  It was good with my tacos and my son really liked it, which is a miracle!
Sooo good and easy!
This was okay, nothing special. It's good accompanied with refried beans.
This is wonderful! It is restraunt quality!

Hey...this is my Mom's recipe :) This is exactly how my mom cooker her rice with only one change. She added minced garlic (instead of garlic salt)at the same time she added the onion. Readers, you will be able to tell the delicious difference fresh garlic will add to this dish! This is a totally authentic mexican rice recipe...TWO THUMBS UP!

I cooked this according to the exact ingredients and directions and it came out very good.  My boyfriend told me it tasted great just like the mexican rice we often get when eating out at mexican restaurants.  I thought it was pretty good also.  Will definitely use this recipe again.

It makes a big difference in the brand of rice. I know.  I use Mathatma long grain rice, sometimes I place a whole jalapeño when adding liquid. Sometimes I use Pace Picante salsa. Use your imagination.

Great.  I forgot to add the salt but just sprinkled it on afterwards and stirred really well.  Turned out great.  Will keep for all my mexican nights.  (which are very often my husband loves mexican).  Never buy premade rice again.

this is delicious.  We make it with uncle ben's brown rice and it turns out so that even my fiance who dislikes brown rice loves it.  We make it exactly as the recipes states although next time I might try adding in some beans

Really good recipe! I tried this for our "build your own burrito" night. Everyone was really impressed by how authentic the rice tasted. And as leftovers, when people smelled the rice they asked which restaurant I got it from.
This recipe is so easy and turns out perfect every time.  No need to try it out ahead of guest.  You can trust this recipe!
Awesome recipe--I did have to spice it up with "taco seasoning I" from this site, but that was the only change I had to make.

Omigosh!!!  This is incredible!  I followed one reviewer's advice and used 1 pint of homecanned tomatoes instead of the tomato sauce...added 1/2 jalapeno (cause we like it spicy) and this has to be the best rice we've ever had!  What flavor!!!
Excellent! i doubled the recipe and added corn. i also had to add extra red sauce. will make again.

I have never made Mexican rice before and made it for a work function.  It turned out really good. This recipe is awesome! It has some tomato flavor, but not  too much which I love! Highly recommend this recipe.
Needs a bit more cumin and garlic- This recipe was good (and I know good mexican food- I'm from San Antonio) but could use some improvement.

the best recipe for mexican rice i've tried yet!
Always good!

LOVE this rice! My son loved it so much I had to make it the next day. The do use 1/2 the oil though. 3 Tbsp made it too greasy. I also use some adobe seasoning along with the garlic salt and cumin. It's great!!!!

I made this tonight.  The only thing I changed was to add a little bit of mixed vegetables because that is how they serve it my favorite Mexican restaurants.  This is excellent! I'll make again next time we make burritos/fajitas and use this as a topper.  Thanks!
Followed the recipe but I added Rotel with green chilies..it adds a little spice and great flavor...wil make again...my family loved it!
This was good, but I thought it came out a bit dry and could use a little something extra to spice it up.

This was wonderful. It was fast and easy and tasted so much better than I expected. Usually I end up tweaking a recipe along the way but this I made as instructed and it came out perfect. Followed the recipe exactly and this turned out really well! I will be making this with all my Mexican meals now....much better than anything out of a packet. We loved it!
Awesome recipe! I will never buy boxed mexican rice again. The only thing I changed from the recipe was using a can of rotel instead of just the tomato sauce.

I loved this came out perfect with my chicken flautas, I will make this with my next mexican dish. It was easy to make and tasted wonderfull!

Very good side dish for tacos, I add a few dash's of garlic powder along with the garlic salt.

This was the best Mexican rice we had ever tasted, even compared to the rice we eat at Mexican restaurants! great flavor!  I added the taco seasoning like someone suggested and used petite dieced tomatoes instead of the tomato sauce.  i'll make this again.

This was fantastic.  I made it with brown rice and it was wonderful.  It did take longer to cook than I expected, but the flavor was amazing.  I'll definitely be making this again.
good basic recipe

Fantastic! I made this rice to go with a mexican feast of enchiladas and tacos, which were superb, but this was MY favorite part of the meal! It tastes JUST like the rice they serve at my favorite authentic Mexican restaurant. Delicious. My search for the perfect Mexican rice is over.

really yummy!  I added some garlic as always, and the outcome was fantastic! Has a mild spice to it and tastes very authentic

This recipe is perfect! My family loved it and I loved how simple it was to make. This has become a new staple in my kitchen.
Very good.  I followed the recipe exactly.  Went well with the fish tacos I made for cinco de mayo

This rice was excellent!! The only thing I did different was reduce to  1 1/2 cups of chicken broth and 1/2 cup tomato sauce (about half an 8 ounce can). I also added 1 chopped roma tomato. The liquid should not exceed twice the rice amount or the rice will be too mushy and liquid will not be properly absorbed. Instead of broth one can use water and 2 bouillon cubes. The rice came out perfect with those modification and feel free to view the photo. Thank you for the recipe!!

GREAT MEXICAN RICE!!!!  I have tried so many horrible recipes and now I have finally tried the one I will stick with!  My only suggestion would be to add the garlic salt and cumin to the rice right before it is browned because otherwise it gets kinda burnt tasting.  Also one of my favorite local mexican restaurants adds corn, carrots and peas to theirs and I really like that so I will be throwing those into this recipe as well.  Thank you so much for the fabulous recipe!  Also this goes great with the South Texas Carne Guisada recipe posted on this site - super yummy!

This rice was very good! I'm giving it 4 stars, I did think that 3 Tablespoons was too much oil. I used all three but I will try two next time, as the rice was very oily. I was out of tomato sauce so I used 1/2 cup of medium salsa instead and it actually added great flavor! I think I will always use salsa in it from now on. Thanks for a great recipe!

I prepared this recipe as-is. No substitutions or additions added. Upon completion of this recipe, I have found this recipe unsatisfactory. Tweaking is very much needed in this recipe adding salsa, peppers,and garlic will definitely improve the taste. 3-stars for effort.

We liked this rice much more than any of that store bought stuff.  We have not been able to find anything that tastes halfway decent.  The only reason I am giving this 4 stars is that my liquid did not completely evaporate and it left the rice kinda mushy...I followed the recipe almost exactly except I added some garlic as I was browning the rice.  Next time I will add less  broth. Served in Tacos made w/ the Taco Seasoning I as suggested by another reviewer.  Tasted fantastic together. 

I have since made this again to use in burritos and I reduced the amount of liquid, took off the lid once the rice was no longer hard and let the rest of the liquid evaporate.  I also used diced tomatoes instead of tomato sauce (we liked this much better) and upped the broth  to about 3/4 of a cup.  The rice was great and it tasted even better the second day.But, since I had to make the changes I still can only give it 4 stars....It really tastes authentic w/ the changes and I have made this about once a week.  Used to live in Los Angeles and moved to Colorado...have not been able to find anything, even in restaurants that tastes half as good.  Our rule is "Never Mexican restaurants while in Colorado"

I really enjoyed this rice.  It was surprisingly easy, and I've never cooked rice before, but this turned out great.  I didn't use long grain rice, but a Japanese medium grain, but it worked well.  I used olive oil instead of vegetable oil, and I added some minced garlic before I put the rice in.  I also used half of a a chopped white onion, a whole tomato(diced), and a jalapeno(also diced).  Instead of tomato sauce, I used a small can of tomato paste.  I also added fresh cilantro at the end.

After living in the central valley area of California for some years and enjoying the many Mexican restaurants frequented, this Mexican Rice recipe brought me right back to the restaurants I've so enjoyed.  Thank you so much.

I just made this today and I have to say, this was pretty good. I had to substitute some things though. Instead of garlic salt, I just added a finely chopped garlic clove and a pinch of salt. And instead of regular tomato sauce, I used "El Pato" tomato sauce. It has a blend of spices and chilies that gave this rice a nice edge. And since I didn't have any chicken broth, I made my own using a chicken bullion cube and boiling it in in 3 cups water. I decided to use a bit more water when I read other reviews about the rice not being fully cooked.
I was looking for something more than just plain rice and came across this recipe.  It did the trick and it had such a wonderful taste.  Definately a keeper.  I wouldn't change a thing!!!

I  made his rice exactly as the recipe says to, and it came out very very bland. It didn't taste like anything. I think next time I'd be better off making white rice with some salsa added to it, it would have more flavor than this!
I've made this a coupla times now and think it's great. I use fresh garlic cloves instead of garlic salt, and chipotle salsa instead of tomato sauce for extra flavour.

This is the best I've tried so far. After trying it as written, which was really good, I've made a few changes. Instead of tomato sauce I use enchilada sauce and I also add 1/2 tsp of chili powder and a pinch or two of red pepper or flakes. And my family don't like onions so I just use powder in place of it. On occasion I have sub chicken broth for beef. Its so good either way and the original way. U can't go wrong with this recipe in my opinion. I've made it over 30 times soooo good!!

I had never made Mexican rice before, I guess I was intimidated by the dish, even though I grew up in Mexico. But this was phenomenal! The only changes I made were adding green onions and a whole garlic and instead of 2 cups of broth, I used two cups of water a 1 chicken bouillon cube. Delicious! Can't wait for dinner to eat with taquitos.
I used basmati white rice and canned diced tomatoes (since that's what I had on hand).  This rice was very good.

This is awesome authentic tasting mexican rice.  The only changes I made:  used 1 cup of canned chicken broth and 1 cup broth from chicken breasts that I boiled for "Poblano Chile Enchiladas a la Gringa" from this site. (awesome by the way!).  Then instead of just throwing in salt and cumin, I used "Taco Seasoning I" from this site as well. My Mexican friends snarfed this stuff up! Yummy!!

I really wanted this to be PERFECT.  And it wasn't bad....it was just ok.  Maybe some taco seasoning instead of just cumin?  The consistency wasn't quite there either, and I made it exactly as written (except for the use of veggie broth instead of chicken, I don't eat meat.)  Like I said, not bad, but I think I'll keep looking.

This is as good as is found in most restaurants; however, there is still something missing.  Instead of the salt and cumin, I substituted an equal amount of Taco Seasoning I from this site.   In the end I needed more salt and black pepper.  This is definitely a keeper, but I'm not finished tinkering.
Wonderful. I didn't change it 1 bit.

This is a great starter recipe. After the first time making this I made the following changes. I like the rice sautéd in butter, added fresh minced garlic and the chopped onions once the rice start turning brown.  Put unsalted chicken stock in a large bowl, added petite diced tomatoes, cumin, fresh or dried cilantro, salt and pepper. Stir to mix all the ingredients then add to the rice, let simmer 20/25 minutes.

All I can say is YUM!!! I have Mexican rice in restaurants and it has always been just OK; an OK side to the meal. And I have tried the boxed Mexican rice from the store and that was boring. So we tried this and it was great! My 3 year old loved it and he has to be the pickiest eater on the planet!!! Followed the recipe exactly, except I had jasmine rice, so I used that. It never fluffed up, but still amazing.
I used freshly made tomato sauce and I don't know if that was the problem.  I felt like it needed some tomato paste.
I've made this probably 20 times and every time it turns out amazing. This time I used salsa for tomato sauce and bone broth for chicken broth. Better than restaurant quality.

Very authentic. My husband loved it! And he is my authority on authenticity :) His sister has a version that involves making your own tomato sauce, but as I am pressed for time most nights, this recipe works out great. Definitely a keeper.
Delicious! I thoroughly enjoyed this--very flavourful. I added just a pinch more of garlic salt than was called for. I can't wait to make this again.
It was okay.  I followed it exactly, but next time I will add some chili peppers and more garlic.  Still tasty as is, especially as a bed for the Salsa Chicken!
Full of flavor!!! This recipe is delicious. Can be used as a side to any mexican dish.

Very good recipe! I did modify it a bit due to not having Chicken Broth and tomato sauce though. I used Jasmine rice, a can of regular Rotel (drained) and "Better than Bouillon" Chicken Broth mix. This gave it a slightly saltier (just a little) and spicier (jalapeno's in the Rotel) taste. Next time I may go with mild Rotel, but either way it was delicious. Like other reviews, if the rice doesn't puff much when cooking in the veg. oil, the broth will certainly puff it up and make it perfect.
We have tried several of the recipes for mexican rice, and we all liked this one the best. Thanks for a great recipe and ending my quest for the best mexican rice.

It was really good, instead of regular tomato sauce I used one from the Mexican section called El Pato (Mexican hot style)and it was spicy and delicious, I just used the whole can 7 3/4 ounces, I thought it was 4 ounces, guess I should have worn my reading glasses but it was still really good. It was definately spicy which I like but if your family doesn't just use regular tomato sauce. I will make this again especially with a great soup I recently had in Dallas. Put rice in a bowl, add shredded chicken some tortilla chips, pico de gallo, Monterey Jack cheese, a few slices of avacado and top off with peppery chicken broth and some cilantro, yummmm, this rice is perfect for this.
This is the best rice.  Everyone I've made it for has to have the recipe.
This is wonderful!  The best mexican rice recipe that I found.  I will be making this from now on.

Love this recipe!! I make it almost exactly as written, with just a few changes to my liking ( I have made it as written too, just as good). The only things I do differently are: 1) instead of tomato sauce, I puree a can of mexican stewed tomatoes and use a full cup of that and 1 1/2 cups of chicken broth, 2) After the rice is done cooking in the pot, I will throw it in a skillet pan and toast it up a bit. So delicious!

Great recipe! I added a teaspoon of Cajun seasoning to it and changed the tomato sauce and chicken broth to 1 cup. DH found it a little bland and added some hot sauce to his which did improve it. I added chicken and sausage to the leftovers for lunch the next day and it was very good.
We liked this.  There is nothing overwhelming about the flavor, which meant that all my kids enjoyed it equally.  I'll definitely make it again.
Exactly what I was looking for. This is more like what you find in the Mexican restaurants.
Absolutely wonderful! I use vegetable broth instead of chicken broth (we're vegetarian), and it works great. Also, I use 2 tablespoons of oil instead of one. Thank you for a great recipe!
rice was good but it was kind of mushy. will make again.
Our go-to rice for Mexican meals!
Yum. Nice side dish with Mexican meals, I mix it with Mexican seasoned beef or chicken and top a Taco Salad.
This rice was awesome and matched well with Salsa Chicken
I make this exactly the way the recipe says to.It's awesome.We like to add a little sour cream and a jalepeno or two to the top.
excellent and easy to make!
I followed this recipe exactly and it lacked flavor.  Maybe  like some other reviewers mentioned that using stock instead of broth and fresh garlic may help increase the flavor.

I'm mexican/puerto rican and this is just how my mom and dad make it, minus the chicken broth and ground cumin. Usually my parents just use water and fresh cloves of garlic, onion and tomato sauce.   I found this recipe to be a bit too salty though for my taste. Way more salty than what Ive come across in Mexican restaurants as well.   I like the addition of broth, it definitely adds more flavor. I wouldn't change anything in this recipe except maybe using fresh minced garlic instead of garlic salt and salting to taste if needed.    Thanks!

This was my first time making mexican rice.  I added fresh garlic instead of garlic salt, used vegetable broth, a little chili powder, and jasmine rice.  I was worried about it tasting to tomatoy, but it had good flavor.  My friend helped me make it, and while I was dicing the onion and garlic she was browning the rice.  She starting freaking out when it started to puff.  It was really funny and we enjoyed making it.

Cooked the rice in oil then added a large minced shallot to soften, plus 1/2 tsp salt. Bloomed the cumin and 1/2 tsp garlic powder in the rice mixture before adding 1/2 cup of red enchilada sauce (since I was making chicken enchiladas). Used chicken stock instead of water and reduced the amount to 1.5 cups (2 cups made this rice too mushy). The garlicky shallot + enchilada sauce in place of tomato sauce really kicked up the flavors of this tasty side dish. Delish!

My wife and kids love rice.  This recipe made the grade.  They asked for it the next night.  This one will be sure to make the table on a regular basis.  I only made one change, I add El Pato Salsa Brand tomato sauce.  It kicks it up a notch.  Everyone loves it with spicier tomato sauce.
Very good. Husband said I must make this instead of my other Mexican Rice Recipe.

I love this recipe so much. I found it on this site about 7 years ago and have used it every time I make enchiladas or fajitas. I have gotten so many compliments on it. The only thing I do differently is use salsa in place of the tomato sauce.

Very good and easy! I made this with Jasmine rice, and I added 1tsp chili powder. As other reviewers have said, the rice doesn't puff but does brown. I will try this next time with brown rice (I am currently on a health food kick!)

Very fast prep and effortless to cook. I made the lime fish tacos with it, and the combo was great and coordinated well with the prep of the ingredients. I added a little extra onion and hot sauce to give a little extra zing. A crowd pleaser for kids too!
We LOVE this recipe!!!  I've made it several times and it smells great cooking and tastes even better!  Thanks Mommyto2 for an awesome and easy recipe!

This is just like typical mexican restaurant rice. I've been searching for a recipe like it for years! Thank you!! It's definitely not a main dish or show stopper, but a great side to some spicy chili rellenoes or enciladas.
excellent!
I've been looking for a recipe that resembles the rice at Mexican restaurants and this one does it!
as easy as it gets

A great easy and quick basic mexican rice. My kids enjoyed it.    
When having company over, ill be reaching for my more authentic recipe with more ingredients and a few more steps.  But for a good side dish quick this was good
Loved it, it was exactly what I was looking for! I added and cooked up a fresh tomato to the mix. I will make this for all my Mexican dinners. Thank you!:)
This recipe was delicious! Followed it exactly, didnt feel it needed anything else added or changed. I will definitly use this again!

Very tasty rice.  One suggestion:  When cooking the rice in oil, cook it by itself until you get it golden brown and puffed.  THEN add the cumin and garlic salt.  If you add the cumin too early, it darkens the rice and you can't tell when it's done.
Followed the recipe almost exactly, but substituted Vegetable Broth to make it vegetarian friendly.  Very easy to make and pretty close to an authentic Tex-Mex restaurant flavor.

I’m an “authentic” Tex-Mexican from south Texas and in my opinion this recipe is 100% authentic. I alter my recipe a bit depending on my audience’s taste preferences. For example, I might use 1/4c bell pepper or 2 tomatoes, or ½ c tomato sauce if I don’t have fresh tomatoes, or even ½ tsp garlic salt if I don’t have fresh garlic.  Sometimes, I even omit the jalapenos or chicken bouillon. I recommend following the exact recipe and then altering to your taste preferences or dietary needs/restrictions.

I modified this as well. It is an excellent base and as close to authentic Mexican rice as one can get.  I personally took out the cumin and garlic salt and replaced the tomato sauce w/ diced tomatoes. My rice did not "puff" during the browning process.  First I browned the rice, added onion, added chopped garlic cloves. Next I added the tomatoes stirred and cooked for a min then added liquids (water and chicken broth), then added salt for taste.  I prefer salt and garlic cloves instead of garlic salt, but if I didn't have cloves I would have added the garlic salt.  Family and friends love this and ask me to make it all the time.

Also hint...once you add everything and stir let it sit, maybe stir once to prevent buring right after you turn the burner off, but leave rice alone it needs to rest.
I thought this was rather bland- it needs more flavor or spice (and I don't even like spicy food).
I was out of tomato sauce so I used a can of Herdez salsa instead. Substituted water and a vegetable bullion cube for chicken broth.  Turned out spicy but delicious.

This recipe isn't as great as I thought it was gonna be.  I think there was a little too much garlic salt for my taste and it looked more brown than the traditional orange-ish mexican rice.  Next time, I'll add 1/4 cup more rice and see if that helps.

This was good and pretty easy to prepare.  I did find it a little bland, mushy and lacking texture.  It needs more garlic salt and cumin.  I also added a can of corn at the end that worked very well.  Goes well with Salsa Chicken.
This is my go to recipe for Mexican Rice....its delicious!!!!!!

Excellent!  I didn't change a thing!  I did use an authentic Mexican tomato sauce (from Walmart, small carton for like 40 cents).   Being married to a Mexican, I'm always trying to make him things along this line that he'll love, but until now my rice has always been 'meh'.  Thank you for giving me the rice recipe I've been searching for!  Now to figure out what I'm doing wrong with my refried beans! ;)

I decided to try this recipe since it had cumin in it--and I like cumin.  My rice did not puff either, but I just kept going with the recipe, and the rice did cook perfectly.  However, I couldn't taste the cumin and found the dish rather bland.  My husband's remedy for any dish not reaching par is to add a big tablespoon of butter.  This I did and it helped.
Good starter recipe.
this recipe was perfect for me because I was making it for a family who was not big into very spicy food. I just doubled it and it turned out well.

Ummmmmmm delicious!!!!!! I did add a few more spices after I made it exactly like the recipe says. I just like a little more flavor and spice. A little more cumin, some chili and cayenne pepper to taste.

I decrease the Liquid by 1/4 cup, and exchange 1/2 cup of the chicken broth with seasoned bean juice (as I always make seasoned refried beans when I make this rice) otherwise I follow the recipe. Turns out great every time and we love it!
This rice was just NOT for us.  It took waaaayyy longer than 25 minutes for it to not be totally watery & the only thing I could really taste was SALT.
This is delish! Didn't change a thing.
I used Sazon and a little cumin and I though it had good flavor. Good basic recipe for you to make your own.....

Only rice I had was medium grain but it worked very well. I liked this rice better than the rice I get at mexican restaurants. It was definitely more flavorful without taking away from the rest of the dish.
Instead of using the skillet, I just threw all the ingredients in my rice cooker and it turned out wonderful (and only took 3-4 minutes to prep). Very easy, very yummy.
I will cut down on the oil, but the flavor was great.
Very nice recipe!

I've been looking for a good mexican rice recipe and I have found it!  Per someone else's suggestion, I used the Taco Seasoning I recipe from this sight and it turned out great!  Left overs were just as good the next day!
My family loved the rice!!  Did use enchilada sauce instead of tomato!  I agree with the others.....use garlic salt...it is needed!  Will make this again and again!
This is great, and similar to what you'd get at a lot of Tex-Mex restaurants.  I like to add a little bell pepper and jalapeno, leftover from whatever Mexican dish I'm making this with.

I always make this rice as a side for our Mexican dinners.  I add a 1/4 cup frozen corn, 1 can rinsed, black beans, and a handful of green onions in the last 5 min of cooking.  It adds some color as well as flavor!  Excellant!

I thought this was a solid side dish, but it doesn't really stand out in the taste department for me.  I eat Mexican occasionally, and just came back from a trip there, and whatever it is that they do to the rice makes it more flavorful.
This recipe was perfect as a side dish. My husband couldn't believed I made it from scratch!

This was good...but not great.  Even after substituting salsa for the tomato sauce and adding chili powder....it was still lacking something.  Maybe next time I'll try using taco seasoning as others have suggested.

I used really liked the base of this.  I  I doubled the recipe .  Tip and time saver is to blend the onion, tomatoe  sauce and a few garlic cloves in the blender with the stock.   Add extra chicken powder to the blended mixture  for real flavor and pour into the sautéed  rice  and cook as directed.  I omitted the cumin as my other dish had  a fair amount in it.   This base  is easy and delicious!

I doubled the batch and added 1/4 cup of Penzey's Taco Mix (equivalent of one packet).  Because of this, I omitted the salt.  The rice was a bit mushy but my daughter loved it.  It did need a little more salt but that was my fault.
This was rather bland.  I expected stronger flavours.  I added some chili powder and that helped a little.  The saving grace was spooning sauce from our Mexican Chicken recipe over it.

This is my go to recipe every time I make Mexican rice. Being Puertorrican, I instinctively make rice 'our' way' which uses a slightly different technique and will render a rice that is not the traditional Mexican texture. This was the recipe I've been searching for. The rice was just like you get in a restaurant. I had to do one thing different then as called. I did not have cumin and read in my betty crocker cook book you can substitute it with chili powder. I would never recamend doing this.

This is the best Mexican rice I've ever had! Instead of tomato sauce I used Rotel tomatoes and chicken broth to equal the amount of liquid needed for the rice and I added some chopped Poblano chilis and a can of chopped green chilis. My family will never eat packaged Spanish rice mix again. Everyone even commented on how pretty it looked.
Pretty good stuff- realized after I'd started cooking it that I was out of canned chicken broth, so I substituted a Ramen packet and a couple of bullion cubes, which gave it a pretty good flavor.
It was good.  Just needed something to make it perfect.  I will read all of your suggestions.

There are many different styles of Mexican rice. This one is similar to one that a Mexican relative of mine makes. I like it because isn't dry. The tomato flavor really comes through, but it isn't overpowering.
very good. it's not spicy at all, so if you need to add some spice. Otherwise very simple and mild.
a little greasy

This recipe is easy and delicious. Instead of 1/2 cup tomato sauce, I added 1 small can of Rotel tomatoes (we like hot). Rice is moist and does not stick together. Don't worry about "puffing " rice, just slightly cook in oil.

The last time we had tacos for dinner my husband insisted we have Mexican rice with it.  So in a pinch I went out and bought the packaged stuff.  It was so gross that I vowed that I would NEVER again buy that stuff!  I am still having bad dreams about it ;)
So, I set out to find a quick and easy recipe and came across this one.  I made a few subs: chopped some fresh garlic and added it with the onion.  Used about 2 tsp. taco seasoning instead of the cumin and salt, and subbed veggie broth since we are vegan.  It was really good!  Hubs kept commenting on how good the rice was.  I even got my little ones to try(which is a huge feat!)  This one's a keeper for sure!
This is very good mexican rice. My husband is Mexican and so I made him this rice and he loved it!! Thanks for the recipe
It looked the restaurant rice, but all I could taste was the cumin.
MMMM... very yummy! great mexican side dish!
Made this as written, the whole family loved it!
Good and easy but for my family could use a bit more flavor
perfect; i used mild rotel so my son could eat it. if that's what you're going for too, cut the chili powder in half. thanks for the great recipe!
Great rice! We just like a lot more spice. I added taco seasoning more cumin and used salsa instead of tomato sauce.
Thought this was very good!  Almost as good as a Mexican restaraunt!

Wow!  Fixed this with Grilled Chicken Breast with Pablano Pepper Sauce, what a GREAT compliment.  Followed the recipe exactly, so simple, yet so very tasty.  The only change that I made was to add a couple of cloves of fresh chopped garlic with the onions.  This was delish and I'll definitely make it again!
Constant staple of every Mexican night at our house. Wife uses brown rice just has to cook it longer to make the rice tender. Best out of all the ones we have tried. Thanks!

I had never cooked "real" rice before, but it definitely takes longer than 20-25 minutes. It took over an hour for the rice to cook. I was surprised at how good this simple recipe is!  Very easy and makes great Mex rice.

This was great. I have made it twice. 1) Followed recipe to a T, pretty good. 2) Improvised & customised: I had a spare packet of taco sauce & taco seasoning from a taco kit, so I used the taco sauce in place of tomato sauce and half a packet of taco seasoning in place of cumin. I also added red & green bell peppers, corn, a rasher of bacon minced and 1/2 lime juiced. Needless to say I got RAVE reviews! My friends said it was restaurant quality, I aim to please :)
I made this as directed and it turned out perfectly. I browned the rice and then added the finely chopped onion to cook a bit. I wouldn't change a thing.

I used brown rice which took forever to cook, plus I thought I had garlic salt but didn't so I just used salt...big mistake! It turned out way too salty, but overall it had a wonderful authentic flavor.  I would make this again, but correctly next time!

Rave reviews at our dinner table, just the right blend of spices and flavors. This recipes tastes exactly like our favorite restaurant's version.  The directions are super easy to follow, could probably cut back on oil if desired, but we thought it was delicious just as it is written.

As a very proud Mexican, I have cooked all kinds of Mexican dishes with ease but could never master making really good arroz. Thank you so much for posting this recipe. This is honestly the only fool proof recipe I have found and I have made it 5 plus times and it always comes out perfect. Always a hit and everyone loves it.

Minor alterations... I use fresh minced garlic a little extra tomato sauce and additional onions. But this is more for personal taste. 

Amazing!!!
Pretty good.
Great recipe!!! I have looked for a long time for a good mexican rice recipe!!! Found It!!! Thank You

I really like this rice and my husband especially loves this rice. I have made this several times it has turned out great every time. I used 1/2 tsp garlic powder and 1/2 tsp salt because i didn't have garlic salt but it turns out well that way so i won't even try the garlic salt. Also, I think it only needs 2 Tbs of oil, sometimes it seems too oily with three. I don't think my rice puffs before adding the broth and tomato sauce, but it does brown. I add the onions at the same time as the rice because they have to be completely soft for my husband to eat them and they are done at the same time the rice is if you don't cook it at too high of a temp. Thanks for this great recipe, I wont go back to the boxed kind.
Great little recipe! I substitute 1/2 of salsa for the 1/2 of tomato sauce...yummy with any mexican dish!

This is tasty and simple.  I must agree that the second time I made it I added a few teaspoons of Taco seasoning instead of the Cumin.  And a couple of pickled Jalapeno pepper slices to give it a little kick.

We're getting there slowly.  I'm on the quest of finding the perfect, fluffy mexican rice for my DH who is Mexican-American.  His grandmother made the "best rice he's ever had" (of course!) and I'm trying to find something similar.  This one was fluffier than others and had great flavor (which from what I understand is supposed to be on the mild side, not strongly flavored).  I had no problem getting my rice to brown and puff.  I think some people are expecting it to puff like popcorn, and that's not the case.  What it does is swell slightly and go from being kind of clear-ish looking to being kind of pearly looking.  Good recipe and hubby is getting happier!

great recipe, thanks! The first time I made this I only had brown rice and it was ok, but the flavor and texture of the rice was just too present. Tried again last night with regular ol' mahatma long grain, and it was perfect! light and fluffy, so easy, and delicious!
I thought this was very good.Ty 4 sharing.
This works!
My husband LOVED LOVED LOVED this recipe. great job. It had a truely athentic mexican flavor.
Wonderful.  Throw in some protein and this is a meal  by itself.

This is a delicious rice recipe.   Something different than the usual fried rice type of side dish.   It is also very versatile as I used a seasoned pizza sauce in place of the tomato sauce and it was still great!
This taste just like our favorite mexican resturant makes!!!!

Just what I was looking for, a recipe similar to mine that makes a smaller batch. This recipe yielded tender fluffy rice, better than my other recipe. I omitted the garlic salt and used 3 cloves of fresh minced garlic and added sea salt. I also added in black pepper, a pinch of sugar, frozen peas & carrots, and fresh chopped cilantro. I agree with the reviewer who said that Mexican rice is a side dish meant to accompany the spicier entree and it is supposed to be a little blander, this was what Mexican rice is supposed to be! Thanks for the keeper recipe. I am making it from now on and it is easier than my old recipe too!

This just might be my new recipe for mexican rice.  It has a fantastic flavor.  I made it exactly as written, except I added a little bit of chopped green pepper. Thanks for the great recipe!
Very good!  I made this exactly as written and it turned out great.
i thought this was delicious. i used salsa in place of the tomato sauce because that's what i had. i might add some chopped mild green chiles next time. much better than the boxed mixes.
Overall, this is a very good recipe. I think the cumin flavor was a little strong for me, so next time I will maybe cut back on it or omit it all together. Thanks!

I just made this tonight, and man is it good! Thanks so much no more boxed rice for me! I did add some coriander, a pinch of mexican oregano, and a couple cloves of garlic.  Delicious! Don't let the name intimidate you.  I am a chef at heart not by trade.  I am of Mexican heritage and was the only one of 5 girls to learn to cook like Mama.  This recipe is very close to what I learned to make from my mother.  Slight differences are that we add a little less onion about 1/8 of a cup and we add about the same amount of chopped bell pepper that is added with the onions about half way through the sauteeing of the rice.  Instead of garlic salt we use granulated garlic or fresh garlic which will add a little more flavor.  We also add a dash of black pepper.  If you don't have fresh chicken broth that is already salted, we use 2 cups water and about 1 1/2  Tblsp powdered chicken boullion by Knorr Suiza found on the Hispanic aisle which has lots of salt in it, no need for extra salt. I'm not sure about adding taco seasoning as other reviewers have suggested, this makes me think of Fast Food Bell rice.  Homemade Mexican rice is not supposed to be over flavored, the main dish should have the flavor and or the salsa that you serve should be as spicy as you desire.  These flavors should not be expected to be in the rice.  I'd say this is a darn good recipe for anyone wanting to make homemade Mexican rice!  My chef hat off to Mommyto2!

The first batch made a nice, semi-firm cheese, but with only about a 1/4 tsp of salt in the mix, it wasn't overly flavorful. Not bad, but not exciting. this recipe makes wonderful, versatile soft cheese!  i think the other reviewers had a problem because of the temperature of the milk when they added the juice.  also, lemons vary in size, so measure the juice (or white vinegar works, too). to a gallon of milk, heated to 190 degrees, 1/4 c vinegar or lemon juice should work. and please, use a thermometer!  don't rely on "bubbles" which could form at a much lower temperature depending on your altitude! also, let it sit for a full 10 minutes to let the curds fully form!  i use 4 layers of cheesecloth (it usually comes folded in half in the packages i buy, so i fold that in half again) so no curds slip through.  strain your whey into a container and if it is not yellow, but WHITE, heat the milk and do it all again... the white means there are still milk solids (cheese) contained in the whey that you can extract.  when it is through dripping whey out of the cheesecloth (an hour or two) unwrap it and put it in a container in the fridge.  i usually make ricotta out of it by sticking the curds in the blender, adding a little milk and blending until smooth.  i have made the BEST lasagna with it... VERY creamy mouthfeel and melts delightfully!  next, i'm going to try making tangier cream cheese by mixing it with plain, lightly salted  yogurt cheese (recipe from this site, but leave out the garlic and black pepper) which is much smoother! Meanwhile, pour 2 cups of buttermilk in a large bowl and add the salt.  Pour hot milk over buttermilk and stir gently.  Pour 3 Tablespoons of white vinegar into bowl and stir gently. Only 5 stars if you do it right. This is the same as a basic ricotta cheese recipe. Heat slowly and be patient. The milk should not boil. People, read the reviews on this one!  The advice by another poster helped me make perfect cheese the very first time with this recipe.  Make sure you measure your lemon juice (1/4 cup to a gallon of milk) and use a thermometer. Letting it rest the full ten minutes is important.

Also, every time I have made this (and I now use this recipe all the time to make ricotta cheese but also to make syrnyky and blintzes) I have had to reheat the milk mixture to get the full amount of cheese.  

Remember, until you only see yellow whey left behind, you still have milk solids that, if reheated, will become cheese!  Strain it once and if your liquid is still milky white, reheat and add more lemon juice and it will all turn into cheese.

The syrup is always added first in the glass because if you add milk first, you can't tell how much syrup you are adding. This makes portion control impossible in a restaurant. My problem with this receipt is the use of the term "cup". If you put selzer in a cup, then chill it, it becomes flat. Traditionally there is only one acceptable syrup for an egg-cream. That is "U-Bet" syrup. The key to a good egg cream is to have highly carbonated selzer, well-chilled milk and a well mixed combination befgore the selzer is added. The amount of milk here is a bit much. You need a higher selzer to milk ratio for the best egg-cream. There are two parts to adding the selzer. First you add and stir till the mixture bubbles to the top. Then stop. Then add more selzer. The best egg-creams have a froth of chocolate bulles on the top. It is difficult to make a good egg cream without a seltzer bottle. Not impossible, but difficult. You can also make vanilla egg-creams. The best glass for an egg cream is the coca-cola soda-fountain glass with the bell-shaped top.
