Very good. I didn't actually measure anything, just eye balled it. I didn't ahve any grenidine, so I left that part out. I added some club soda to ad a little fizz, which I think is a fun addition. Anyway, good stuff! Very refreshing
Fun and light. Wife loved it.
Very yummy! I bit on the over-sweet side.  Also nice with orange juice.
Tried these yesterday and they were yummy! I had them shaken and poured over ice, but I'm sure they'd be just as good served straight up. They're pretty sweet, but just perfect for a hot summer day!

Basic mixed drink, nothing fancy in my opinion.  I will admit I make a lot of mixed drinks using "The Little Black Book of Bartending" so I'm probably not the best person to rate a drink like this one.  Doubtful I will ever make again.
Fruity!  This was great.  Very "beachy".
Loved it... I'll be making it again!
yuuuuuummmyy delicious drink. It's a keeper.
I found it a wee bit strong strong and sweet so I added some club soda. It was awesome!
Very nice drink, although I used pineapple/mango juice instead. Only because our store had a special sale on it.
Not bad! Basically tastes like spruced up pineapple juice, but it's a great way to get lots of fruit into your day. Used Splenda instead of sugar with no problems.

This was quite tasty. Very light, very exotic, and it scaled very well. It also made lots of room for adjustments--I didn't have as much pineapple juice as called for, and I used a frozen banana, and it still tasted very good. My father loved it.
Very yummy! It's the perfect treat to end your day, or a perfect breakfast drink. Will definately make again! Thanks for the great recipe!
It was very yummy. I didn't totally follow the recipe, but chose to wing it with the ingrediants. It still worked.
Very Yummy!  I added 1 oz of rum and a slice of pineapple on top.  I've never been to Hawaii but this was close.  Thanks.
Tasty!  I doubled the coconut milk because the pineapple overpowered it a bit.  Added a some ice cubes as well.

Mmmmmmm. I wish I was still sipping this... I reduced the amount of pineapple juice to about 10 ounces, otherwise the taste of pineapple would have dominated the drink. I also added 12 ice cubes to give it a more smoothie-ish feel. I used one frozen and one fresh banana. It was grrrrrreat! :)
omit sugar

This was a great drink, but we tried it a second time and we froze the pineapple juice with rum in it. We also froze the banana in chunks.  Then we whirred all the ingredients in the blender and it was creamy smooth.  The only thing missing was the coconut shell glass and the umbrella garnish.
A little weird. I added rum, which made it a bit better.
My kids thought this one was just ok.  I thought it was ok as well.  It was a nice refreshing change from the usual.

Delightful!!  We used cream of coconut in lieu  of the coconut milk and sugar; also added pineapple sherbet and ice to give it a smoothie texture.  (I probably wouldn't have used the ice if I had time to freeze the banana.)  Add rum or spiced rum for a grown-up version.  Will definitely serve this again and again!
Creamy and delish.

I mixed and matched this recipe and made it rather my own. I used less pineapple juice, more coconut, added some ice, and added a bit more banana / sugar. (The bananas weren't very ripe, so it was a little bitter.)  Delicious! And easy. =) Thanks for sharing.
Add 2 tablespoons vanilla yogurt for a little change.

Too much pineapple juice.  I doubled the coconut milk and could still barely taste the coconut.  I also like a thicker drink so I added ice.  I will also add yogurt next time to make it more smoothie like.

Very good! I doubled up on the coconut milk, replaced the sugar w/ simple syrup (upped it to 2 tbp.) & hit it w/ a lg. shot of white rum (although this particular drink may benefit from a rum taste so next time I will try Bacardi Gold instead). I garnished w/ a marashino cherry & pineapple wedge.
I did not have coconut milk, but I did have coconut flavoring. I used whole milk and just a little coconut flavoring. I used frozen bananas, too, to make a thicker smoothie. It was okay.
We used fresh pineapple. recommend adding more coconut. Not bad, but wasn't perfect. Not sure what else I would add though.

ALOOOOHA!!! This is delicious! Melt in your mouth creamy tasty drink! You really do feel like you are in hawaii! my girls love it! My little 5 year old went and put on her hula skirt and flowers because i offered them HAWAII smoothies! she loves it and asks me to make it all the time now!
Have had better.
the kids loved this one....and i thought it was pretty good with a little spiced rum!
If you like a refreshing drink for a party, if you also lemon punch it tastes the same.

I used Diet Ginger Ale and I made homemade lemonade using a recipe from this site that used Truvia instead of sugar. I did NOT add the additional sugar. My kids enjoyed this as is but my husband made these into a makeshift Lynchburg Lemonade by adding a jigger of whiskey. I'll make this again.

Thank you Martha for such a yummy recipe.  I made a cup of this for myself just to taste it using crystal light and diet ginger ale.  Rather than adding ice I added frozen raspberries which added an additional layer of flavor.
This is easy to make and very tasty. I used "Newman's Lemonade" which has a very low sugar content and diet ginger ale. Delicious and refreshing!
I must have used the wrong ginger ale or lemonade becuase it was EXTREMELY sweet! It probably would have been perfect if no sugar was added. We ended using a lot more ginger ale and lemonade.

I have made this recipe at least three times for family and friends and everyone loves it. They often ask for the recipe. It's such a pleasure for me that it's very simple to make and it doesn't include 50 ingredients.
I used Splenda instead of sugar, but otherwise followed the stated amounts in the recipe. This was a nice refreshing drink for the first warm day of the year in Columbus! Thanks, Martha!
I made myself a drink- using 12oz diet ginger ale, 6 oz light lemonade, & 1/4 c. Splenda. No ice- just used chilled ingredients. VERY YUMMY!!! And so easy & virtually no calories- wow.
This was way too sweet. I had to double the amount of lemonade because it just tasted like overly sweetened ginger ale. Next time I will leave the sugar out all together.
I used store bought lemonade and left out the sugar.  Great for serving at a party!

10.18.17  Like the combination of ingredients in this smoothie, that little bit of grated ginger adds another very interesting layer of flavor, and the lemon juice brightens it up.  Found this very thick, so I did add more vanilla almond milk, but everybody has a different preference for smoothie texture.  Very nice smoothie.
Really good! I made mine with Tonic instead of Soda and I was pleasantly surprised!
Haven’t had a Tom Collins in years, and it was refreshing.  Don’t think it’ll ever be my favorite, but it still was good.
Really good!

Oh, YUM!  This is a great drink!  I used Chambord, a common substitute for creme de cassis.  Everything else is just as written.  One ounce equals two tablespoons.  You can decorate your drink with the orange slice and maraschino cherries as you wish---leaves you open for a little artistry!  Thanks for the drink, Chris!  Skol!
So tasty! No need for the addition of salt though. Other than that this is perfect as written!

This is absolutly the best punch receipe I have ever had!!! I wouldn't change a thing about it. It is perfect just the way it is! I had been looking for a VERY simple punch receipe for a large gathering (200+ people). When I found this one I was a little skeptical because it was only 3 ingredients and you just mix it all in the punch bowl. No prep work! So I tried it out and had my sisters taste test it. They loved it!! I ended up making TEN batches of this receipe and by the end of the night the punch was gone and the coffee was hardley touched! It was a hit!!! Would highly recomend it. One reviewer suggested lime sherbet and frozen limeade...I think I will try that for the next party!!

This was wonderful!  Everyone loved it, I did make sure to thaw the ice cream for a half hour before making it.  I also used pineapple-orange juice frozen concentrate and 1/4 gallon vanilla and 1/4 gallon sherbert as suggested by others!  Will definitely make again, so easy!
This is Awesome~but instead of 1/2 gallon orange sherbert--I used half orange sherbert and half light vanilla ice cream~AWESOME!
I have used this recipe often and everyone loves it. I recently tried it with lime sherbet and concentrated Limeade and it was wonderful.
This is the best ever, easy, fast and simple.  I use sherbet/vanilla ice cream mix it's much better this way.
Big hit at my grand daughters birthday party. Made a double batch,  followed  as per recipe except I used 2 liters of ginger ale and 2 liters of cream soda. Dream cream punch!!
Love it! Very refreshing and always a hit at a party it potluck. Perfect for the summer

Really tasty  but may not be visually appealing - the sherbert and ginger ale make a weird looking foam. 

I would probably put less sherbert and more ginger ale next time. It was a bit too creamy for my liking.

I personally cannot tell you if I liked it or not because I served it at a party and it was gone before I even had a chance to try any!  I gave it a 5 because it is clearly a crowd-pleaser. I am plan on making this for my next event and I will be sure to try it before everyone gets there.

This was excellent!  I had just bought an antique punch bowl from a junk shop and just had to use it right away.  But it's so big I had to double the recipe, which came out perfect!  After the kids went to bed, the adults added a little vodka to the punch and nothing went to waste!!

I doubled this recipe for 12 girls at our daughter's birthday party and it ran out not even half way through. Every 7-8 year old girl LOVED IT!!! Thank you so much for an awesome party punch. Didn't change a thing.
This is a great punch to serve at wedding showers, bridal showers, etc.  Very refreshing.
Used half vanilla ice cream and half ornge sherbert, mind blowingly good!

I recently made this for a Halloween party I hosted! I called it "Witches Brew"! It was a HUGE hit, there wasn't a drop left!! I used a sherbert ice cream that had vanilla in it, it was perfect! I'm going to make it again for my son's 1st birthday party.
This mix is wonderful! I used lemon sorbet, frozen lemon concentrate, and ginger ale and it turns out great! Lots of great compliments!
Simple and delicious
This is much better than the fruit punch that normally gets served at showers.  I agree that it is best if you get the orange sherbet that is swirled with vanilla ice cream!

This punch is absolutely the best! I found this while searching the internet for punch recipes for my in-law's 50th Anniversary party. I could not keep the punch bowl filled! Everyone loved it. I will be serving this again!

If you like orange dreamsicles, you'll LOVE this! I made it for the kids at our New Year's Eve party and the adults loved it just as much (if not more!). Of the half gallon, I used a 2/3 orange sherbet and 1/3 vanilla ice cream. It was beautiful and frothy.
Easy as pie..or punch. My kids put it together in a matter of minutes and it was delicious!
I made this for our school bridal/baby showers that we have had a lot of recently, and everyone really loved it! It is easy and not too expensive to make.
Pretty...but way, way, WAY too sweet...and I have a sweet tooth!  I will be trying to figure out a way to cut the sweetness as it does have potential.
So good! I was looking for a recipes similar to one my step mom used to make. I substituted rainbow sherbet and it was amazing! Just what I was looking for!
Great and easy punch! Everyone wanted seconds and after shower they all wanted the recipe!

Made this for ladies night and they loved it!! They got the last drop out of the punch bowel. I did use sherbet and vanilla mix, and I added alcohol Smirnoff vodka and triple sec loved it will make again.

I made this punch, altering a little. I used 2 Great Value Orange Sherbets (49 oz each) & 2 Blue Bunny vanilla ice creams (49 oz each).  One 12oz. can of frozen orange juice.  Let them soften and add three 2 liter bottles of Canada Dry Ginger Ale.  Be sure to have a big bucket to make this in or cut recipe in half.

I made two batches for a 80th birthday party with about 100 of people in attendance.  We had other beverage options too, but everyone kept coming back for more punch.  I'll definitely make it again.

I used a beverage dispenser and ended up with a lot of froth after the punch was depleted.  Don't try adding ginger ale to the froth, it will not make more punch.  Dump it out and add more punch that has been mixed up with the above ingredients.
Served this at my son's 1st birthday party and everyone loved it! It was so simple and tasted wonderful.
This punch was a hit!  I figured with everything else there was to drink, I'd have some left over - no such luck - it was gone halfway through the party!

I was asked to make an orange punch for Christmas and found this recipe. I thought it was going to be a little creamier than it was, so I would mix the ice cream in well with the orange juice first. I had to double the recipe to get it to fit in my large glass spout container. Everyone liked it. Thank you!

Super easy to make and absolutely delicious. 
I used Breyers Creamsicle ( orange plus vanilla) as suggested by many reviewers. The punch was big hit with kids and adults alike. The adults enjoyed it with a dash of bacardi as well. I let the icecream and frozen juice thaw completely before carefully adding the gingerale, but it frothed up a lot initially and had me all worried.  Within half an hour though, the froth settled a bit and all was good. I will have to figure out a way to mix the gingerale in without it frothing so much.  I had some frozen sliced oranges that I wanted to add for visual appeal, but skipped it due to the froth. 
Definitely making this again, this ones a keeper.

This is now my go to punch for showers, receptions, and birthday parties. I even made a small batch one hot afternoon and my grandkids loved it as a refreshing break during a swim party.  They ask for it all the time!

This is a fabulous-tasting and super easy punch that I served at my daughter's wedding and a friend's bridal shower.  The regular orange sherbet is definitely better than the orange sherbet/vanilla swirl ice cream.
super, super, easy, yummy, add some sliced oranges on top with a sprig of mint , just for looks. Barb

I made this recipe, used half orange sherbet and half vanilla ice cream, for a military retirement party and it was a huge hit. Everyone kept saying it was the best punch they'd ever had, and it was!  Thanks so much for this recipe.

I used vanilla ice cream with sherbert in it.  poured in a can or evaporated milk and a few cups of a citrus drink that was in the fridge, just to fill up the punch bowl.  It was great.  tasted just like anorange push up ice cream.  rave reviews

I used 50/50 Orange Sherbet and Vanilla Ice Cream. Before adding the Ginger Ale, I microwaved the mix just until it started to melt/soften. Then I mashed it with a potato masher. Finally, I added the soda. It was perfect!!
This is fabulous punch!  I made this for 75 people and they drank it all!  They were coming back for 2nd, 3rd and 4th helpings.  My only suggestion is to make twice as much for a crowd of 150.
I make this punch for a baby shower...and I ran out! It was a hit! Just be sure to let the sherbet sit out a while before making the punch.

I wanted to make this a little more healthy and a little less orangey, so I used 1/2 gallon pineapple sherbert, 1/2 gallon sugar free, fat free vanilla ice cream, a can of frozen OJ, and 2, 2 liters of diet sprite, makes a big batch.  Made it for a party in my punch bowl and everyone loved it! :)  SOOOOO Good!  Lotsa compliments!  Could not tell this was healthy!
This punch was a HIT!  I made this for a wedding shower at work.  Word spread like wildfire about the fantastic punch!  People couldn't get enough!

This is really a yummy punch!  I'm willing to bet that the person who said it tasted just like orange juice, used a full 12 oz can and didn't notice that it only calls for a 6 oz can.  I almost did that, as I only had 12 oz cans of frozen OJ in my freezer but than double checked the recipe and it turned out wonderful!! :)

Tastes just like an orange creamsicle!  I used orange sherbet/vanilla ice cream.  Kids and adults loved it.  No leftovers.  Make sure the orange juice and sherbet/ice cream is well softened before adding gingerale so it does not clump up too much.

This was sooooo good!  I took it to a pot luck and didn't bring any home.  
I did add vanilla ice cream to "soften" the orange taste.  OH yum!
Made w art of ice cream and art of orange sherbet w Gingerale.  Frothy, sweet,rich.
Excellent!!!! Made this for thanksgiving and people went crazy over it!!
what can i say, i thought it was too simple to be THAT good, but everyone at my daughter's first bday party kept asking me for the recipe. It was really really really good and so easy its a sin
This was too sweet for me.

I'm a huge fan of the old fashioned sherbet/ginger ale punch, and adding the OJ concentrate is a great addition! I doubled the batch for a large gathering and every drop was gone. Decorated with sliced frozen oranges to keep it cool.
I make this punch every year at Xmas & it's a great beverage with no alcohol that everyone enjoys.  Highly recommend it!

Made this for a bright orange and pink themed baby shower.  Floated a rubber ducky on top of it.  Made the recipe exactly as written.  Had to make 2 batches.  Even though there were plenty of other beverages there, this punch went very fast and everyone commented how good it was.

Wow, this was delicious!  I made a double batch for my 13 old daughter's Christmas party and it was all gone before the party was over.  I even had 13 old boys asking for the recipe :)  I did as others suggested and only used 1/2 the sherbert and added vanilla ice cream too!

I read the other reviews and used 1/2 sherbet and 1/2 vanilla ice cream...incredible!  Everyone loved it and it was gone in minutes.  It was super easy and made a very pretty presentation too.  Thanks!
I'm making this for the 4th of July but I'm making an adult version with orange jubilee madd dog, I'm sure it will be a hit!!!!!

I give this recipe 5 stars for taste but 3 stars for appearance. The ginger ale kept separating from the range cream mixture and it was kinda embarrassing serving it to people when they had to use spoons to keep stirring to keep it mixed. Somehow i will learn how to fix this problem. I also used orange creamsicle ice cream instead of the sherbet.
Huge hit with the young and old at easter brunch!

I made this for my daughters baby shower. I made two punch bowls full and it was gone in a blink of an eye. It was a big hit. She asked me for the receipe a year later  to make at the baby's first birthday party. Everyone loved it.

Everyone enjoyed this quite a bit. It was a bit sweet (to me) but tasted great. I've made it with ginger ale and 7-Up and both work great. I like using the rainbow sherbet more than just the orange, but either way it's yummy.
Delicious and refreshing

I made this for a baby shower yesterday and it was very good!  I used orange sherbert and vanilla ice cream like another person had said.  Everybody liked it and mine was really good with a little vodka in it! :)

I made this for my 3 year old twins birthday party. We had a packed house, 10 kids, 20 adults and this was loved by all. I followed the advice of another reviewer and used half orange sherbert and half vanilla. It really was a dream punch!

Fabulous!  Made according to recipe, and it was perfect.  Luckily, I purchased extra ingredients, as I had to make a second batch... the first batch was consumed in minutes.  May try variations next time, as others mentioned in the other reviews.
This punch was real easy and fast to make.  It taste more like orange juice than a punch.  Next time I will mix 1/2 sherbet with 1/2 vanilla ice cream and try that.

The recipe as-is is really more of a float than a punch. However, after a couple small adjustments everyone was raving about it! As many other reviews said, I used half sherbet, half vanilla ice cream. Instead of frozen orange juice, I used pineapple orange juice to keep it from being too orange-y. Then, It was too thick to come out of the dispenser, so I doubled the ginger ale, which also helped to balance out the flavors. I made four batches of it during the graduation party, and it was great and easy to refill. If you want to add alcohol, I would definitely suggest any rum or Malibu.
Made this for my daughter's baby shower and added that new whipped cream vodka to it.  It was such a huge hit, we had to make 4 batches of it!!  DELICIOUS!!!
num num num
This really is the yummiest tastiest jello salad!!!! Love it!

This was very good and very easy to make.  I subbed strawberry pie filling for the raspberry because I didn't want to pay the ridiculous price they had on the raspberry.  It was really good and was a big hit at our Thanksgiving table, even from some doubters that thought they wouldn't like it.  Thanks for sharing this recipe!
This is delicious!  The only change I made was I put in some broken up fresh raspberries instead of the crush pineapple since my kids don't care for pineapple.  It was great.
I had a 12 ounce can of raspberry cake and pastry filling which I used for this recipe.  I also used strawberry Jello.  The salad is very good.  I will make it again.

New family favorite! It is a Tabasco style hot sauce, not a chili salsa. I used rice vinegar because it is mild and allows the serrano flavor to shine through. The heat was not overwhelming and was a forward heat that didn't linger. 
This one's a keeper.

It didn't dawn on me until after I was done making the recipe that basically all you are doing here is flavoring the vinegar and making your own green pepper sauce such as Tobasco.  There isn't anything wrong with that but I just didn't realize that at first and thought I'd mention for those making it next.  I plan on saving an empty shaker bottle and keeping this in my fridge at all times.

This is pretty good with the blackberry brandy, but it's even better with any one of the puckers. I like to double up on the pucker for a stronger drink. TIP: Float some frozen berries in this drink and pour them in flutes for a more elegant look, like for a baby shower or wedding shower.
I used homemade blackberry brandy and this was really good. I'll have to admit that I do prefer the pucker as another reviewer mentioned. Still good though and a nice treat!
This is good, but I like Zima with a shot of Chambord, just about the same thing.  Unfortunately for all of us they have ceased production of Zima as of October 20, 2008.
Finally! A good mixer for Blackberry Brandy! You won't be disapointed :)
Quick and Tasty -  Try some midori if you don't have blackberry brandy!!
i mix Razmataz with mine. Zima is starting to be hard to find lately.
Unbelievably easy!! I did a trial run for Thanksgiving.  I used gluten free puff pastry (Nicole Hunn's recipe) and ginger sugar.
So easy, so pretty, so delicious!

Awesome and EASY!  I didn't have any sherry.  I used frozen cauliflower (2 bags) but fresh potatoes and carrots. I made the equivilent of 1.5x the recipe to serve 9.  I also added 3 slices of lite swiss cheese and used evaporated skim milk. The cheese and evap milk added protein and reduced fat and carbs.

amazing! I changed a bunch of things though: added the stems of some broccoli heads, put 1/4 tsp nutmeg (not 1/8), used baby carrots instead of regular carrots, used 2 cloves fresh minced garlic, did not add salt, and instead of chicken broth I used one chicken bouillon square.  At the end I added sharp cheddar cheese to taste.  Don't worry too much about chopping  up the veggies, just throw them in and let them boil/soften.  Before I blended the soup, I took out some of the cauli florets so that they could add a bit of texture to the soup.I didn't have sherry, but I thought it still tasted very good! def'ly will make again.
Really delicious! I have made this several times. I use olive oil instead of butter, omit the dry sherry, and use dried parsley instead but it always still takstes great!

This makes a delicious, low-fat but creamy soup.  I forgot to add the sherry, so I assume it's even better with the sherry added.  The addition of potatoes gives it a nice texture, although it did remind me a bit of vichysoisse (although we love vichysoisse, so that's not a problem).  I may try roasting the cauliflower next time to increase the cauliflower flavor.  We'll definitely be having this soup again!

Though I made some slight revisions, I really enjoyed this soup and so did 2 out of 3 of my teenage sons! First off, I doubled the recipe {note previous mention of three teenage boys}. My youngest loves leftover soup for breakfast and I like it for lunch the next day so I always make A LOT! I made the recipe vegan by substituting Earth Balance, organic vegetable broth and non dairy milk. I left out only the dry sherry because I didn't have any and I added about 1/8 teaspoon ground cayenne pepper with the nutmeg because some reviews mentioned the soup was a little bland. I also only pureed about half the batch because we like some chunks in our soup. Even though my kids won't touch raw cauliflower with a ten foot pole they loved it in this soup! It was even better the next day and I plan to make it again, but next time I'll skip the puree step all together. Great recipe!
This is FANTASTIC! It doesnt look like your average white, creamy cauliflower soup, but WOW.  We will definately be making this again!

Great soup, I made it twice, I didn't add sherry because I didn't have any. The fist time followed directions and it was great. The second time I make soup I added spinach. After I blended, I split soup in half and added a a cup of evaporated milk to half. My husband likes cream soup and I like low fat. Both were great.

I made this yesterday, it is wonderful. I added one cup frozen spinach, and 1 tbs of tomato/chicken boulion(dry)did not mash or blend, it is our new favorite soup, yummmmy. Also used one half cup canned evaporated milk.

This is AMAZING! I followed it as close to the recipe as possible. I didn't have carrots or sherry, but it was still delicious! 
I have tried a few cauliflower soup recipes but lost my usual one. This has now become my hands-down favorite recipe for cauliflower soup. I just have to make sure I never lose this recipe.
Sorry, this one did not do it for me.  I made a roasted cauliflower soup earlier this fall that was 100% better.  Followed the recipe to a T.

Dang.  This soup is fire.  I will definitely be making this again and I can't wait to try it with broccoli and maybe asparagus.  I bet it's going to be even better tomorrow after it sits in the fridge for a bit.  THANK YOU
I realy enjoyed this soup. it was the first time I had it with potatoes.Because I don't like nutmeg,I omited that and the sherry and I added heavy cream with 1% milk.It was creamy and delicious.

I'm not a fan of cauliflower, but it was SO cheap I couldn't resist! I went on my quest to find an alternative cooking method and found this soup recipe.  It was new and different for me, and as it turns out, a great choice. I made it following the recipe as close as possible. My changes (based on what I had availabe) were using water and better than bouillion stuff; also, 4 skinny old carrots that lurked in the bottom of the vegetable drawer, nonfat milk, about 10 tiny white potates scrubbed and skins left on, and only 1 teaspoon of sherry (I've done sherry in soup before and thought it overwhelmed it, so opted for just a HINT of it in this soup).  This soup is a very tasty use for cauliflower.  I really like it.

This soup is awesome! I've made it 3 times so far, and it was perfect every time. Sometimes I substitute the milk for heavy cream, just to add to the taste, and add a 2 teaspoons of curry. But even following the recipe it's great.
Delicious!! I used only three garlic cloves and left out the sherry, but followed everything else. The flavors are excellent. Thanks!
I used almond/coconut milk instead of dairy milk and half chicken broth/half water and it turned out delicious!
Recipe was great, even without the milk and the nutmeg.  Just a simple delicious soup!

Another winner in my quest for good soups for someone on a pureed diet.  This tastes really good, but I'm afraid the 2 potatoes infringes a bit too much on the cauliflower flavor.  Almost tastes like potato soup.  A good potato soup, but that's not what I was looking for.  After a partial blend with the stick blender, I took out half for those that like a chunkier soup, then blended the rest until completely pureed.  BOTH were very tasty.  Next time I may try it with just 1 potato (and there will be a next time).  Cheese would work with this too.  Might even try a little swiss.
Ooh this turned out so good.  At the last minute, had to Substitute instant mashed potatoes because my potatoes were bad :( ... But it was fabulous. The nutmeg and sherry give such a nice flavor.
Wonderful soup.  Omitted chicken broth to avoid msg and added a little more salt.  Did have the sherry and it was still wonderful.
I used almond milk and unpeeled baby potatoes.  Yummy.

This was a quick and easy soup to make in a short time! As most I added my twist to it. Before I blended the veggies I took some pieces of cauliflower out and added them back in with some sharp cheddar cheese and a touch of cream after it was pureed. It was awesome! One of those soups that makes you feel good on a cold winters day......it's home.

Delicious!  I left out the sherry because it was so good without it I couldn't imagine it improving it any and was afraid it would distract.  My son, who would never eat a bowl of cauliflower, carrots and potatoes, gobbled this up - great way to get those veggies in.  Thanks for a delicious and healthy recipe.

Very good.  Used pkg. of frozen cauliflower as I did not have fresh available.  Instead of milk, added a bit of half and half and topped with a bit of cheese before serving.  Thanks for  a good recipe and will definitely make again.  To make it very decadent (fatteninging) - might add bacon bits next time.

Absolutely amazing and simple!!
This was my second time preparing this soup...instead of diced potatoes, I had some leftover mashed potatoes from the evening before...worked out beautifully.
I also substituted broccoli for the cauliflower.  When serving I topped the soup with grated cheddar and a few dashes of cayenne pepper...Oooo La La

This soup was easy to make and turned out great, hubby loved it! I myself thought it needed a bit extra flavour, even though I added the nutmeg, I also added dried mustard powder. I did not have sherry or parsley to add. I used 10% cream and pureed most of it, only leaving some chopped vegetables. Makes a very large pot full.
This turned out excellent.

Awesome soup! My kids both loved it...I only made 2 small changes. I omitted the sherry only because I didnt have any, and I added a dash of cayenne pepper just to kick it up a bit. It is very good and full of flavor!
The recipe makes a nice creamy soup without a lot of added calories.

This was very yummy untill I put the nutmeg in.  It was too strong for me.  Very good other wise.  I will just have to scale back the nutmeg a bit for my tasting.   I love the uses of cauliflower.  My favorite is alfredo sauce, use blended cauliflower instead of dairy products.  I did not add the milk cause I thought it would be just as creamy with out it.
So good and easy! I am vegetarian so I used 2 vegetable bullion cubes in 30 ounces of boiling water instead of the chicken broth. It turned out wonderful- light and low calorie!

This is the best basic cauliflower soup recipe I've ever tried! I did tweak it to my taste, but it was great the first time I tried. Not, next time I'll do this instead. It also made me realize that this is the base for a Irish potato soup that one of my local taverns serves. Just use potato instead of cauli and lots more butter!
Yum.  I added 6 ounces of sharp cheddar cheese.

This was wonderful.   I added a stock of lemon grass while cooking and removed it before blending.  The lemongrass gave it a nice Thai-punch.  I also left some chunks of cauliflower for texture. It is going to be one of our favorites!  Thank you.
Really enjoyed this soup. Easy to make and tasty!

Really LOVED this one!!  I kept some cauliflower pieces whole and added at the end for texture as other reviewers suggested.  I also added just a dash of dried oregano for a little color and flavor.  Definite keeper - thank you!!
Excellent soup ... like the idea of using potatoes instead of cream.  Added grated cheddar cheese ... will make it again
Very tasty soup. I used fat free half and half instead of milk. Also, it makes all the difference to reserve some of the veggies instead of pureeing the whole thing.

My family loved this soup!!
Very easy to make and has great flavour

Absolutely outstanding...the best cream soup I have tried. The flavor is full, and it can be enjoyed on its own just as much as it can with cheese. I did try a few times with parsley added with the califlower as one reviewer noted, and enjoy it a bit more that way.

This is a delicious soup! Perfect for even the main course. I omitted the garlic, sherry, and nutmeg  but added shredded cheddar cheese as a topping while serving. Also I used a handful of baby carrots instead of the two large carrots. This recipe is very easy to follow or get creative!
Super yummy, but a pain to make!
I liked this soup.  It was very tasty.  The sherry added a distinct flavor that was very good!
Our family really enjoyed this recipe, even our 8 and 11 year olds. It was perfect for a chilly January evening.
Can add more milk to make it more soupy but I left it exactly as the recipe called and it turned out like a bisque.  So good!!
Found this to be just ok. Nothing great.

Really enjoyed this soup! The key is to make sure you cook the garlic onions and potatoes long enough to give it the depth of flavour it needs. I added alittle cream to this thick soup the first day and served with toasted baguette rubbed with a little more garlic. The second day I thinned it with some stock and served with grilled cheese for lunch. Yummy!

I think this was just okay.  I didn't add the sour cream or cheese so when I warm it up for the next meal I'll add it then hopefully will like it more.  The nutmeg is a bit overwhelming.  This made a lot of soup.
The soup was very good, my family forgot they were eating cauliflower! I would definitely make this again.

I found this to be very bland even with an extra clove of garlic. I won't be making this again but will try more sherry and nutmeg in the leftovers. Seems a lot of the people rating this so high added cheese so maybe that would make it better.

Delicious!  Quick, simple, easy recipe that tastes wonderful pureed or left rustic.  Followed recipe to the letter but had to use dried parsley.  Will make again buy may sub half-n-half for the milk next time.  Makes about 8 cups,
Delicious - set aside some of the veggies before pureeing, skipped the sherry, used 1/2 & 1/2 instead of milk, and added the non-pureed veggies back in before serving.  It is a keeper!
Really good - I didn't even use chicken broth...just bullion cubes.
This was a delicious soup!  I'm looking forward to making it a second time for guests!  The sherry complemented the recipe and the potatoes was a great way to cut down on the fat!
Wonderful feel-good soup!  I added a bit of curry powder to put a little zip into the taste and left out the sherry.
This was a great hide-the-veggie recipe!  We have trouble finding ways to use cauliflower, and this soup had a very subtle cauliflower flavor, so it was just what we were looking for.

Dang this is some good soup!  I followed all the instructions with the following modifications: 7 cloves of garlic, 1 large sweet potato/yam instead of russet potatoes.  I added a yellow squash at the same time I added the potatoes and and carrots.  I used vegetable broth and cream instead of milk.   I also used himalayan pink salt, cracked pepper and cinnamon.  I only pureed about 1/2 of the vegetables and left the the other half whole.  So so so good!  Had two bowls :)  Can't wait for the flavors to marinate and have some more tomorrow!  Great Recipe!
Delicious and fun to play around with.

I made a few changes to the recipe -- I omitted carrots, because I like my carrots better raw than cooked, and I did not want my cauliflower soup to come out orange!  I liked this recipe's idea of using potatoes to thicken the soup, but I had 2 servings worth (2/3 cup dry) of 4 cheese instant mashed potatoes that needed to get used up, so that went in together with the one quart of broth, in place of the 2 potatoes the recipe calls for.  I used 6 oz of 2% milk, plus 2 oz half and half, in place of the 1 cup milk -- which now that I've eaten the soup I don't think was needed; it would have been creamy enough with one cup of 2% milk and no half and half.  Instead of black pepper and nutmeg, I used the idea of tarragon, thyme and white pepper from a different cauliflower soup recipe on this site (Cream of Cauliflower soup I).  And finally, I omitted the parsley and simply topped each bowl of finished soup with a few grinds of fresh black pepper, for its color as well as flavor.  I put shredded swiss cheese into each bowl, and let the hot soup soften the cheese. Delicious!
I used broccoflower and added sharp cheddar.  I didn't care for the sherry taste, but other than that I really enjoyed it!
Creamy and delish! Not a super strong taste (if you do not over do the nutmeg, that is :)) but that is perfect-my fiance and I do not like it too spicy or too plain..this soup is right in-between!

Surprisingly great flavor, yet very mild at the same time. An immersion blender (boat motor) is a must! Between that and the soft texture of the potatoes and cauliflower, the soup has a great velvety texture!

This is a really tasty soup...comes together quickly, too.  I used one good sized head of cauliflower and together with the other veggies, it made quite a lot of soup.  I used Vegetable stock, that I had on hand - turned out great!  And good for you too!

This was a wonderful recipe.  I made it exactly as written and really enjoyed it.  I picked it because I was looking for something to do with a head of cauliflower and really liked that this had very little added fat. Thanks for a great recipe.

This soup is great and simple too. I sauteed the onion, garlic and grated carrot for a few minutes then, added the broth, cauli and 2 small diced potatoes and covered. Simmered on low as I prepared dinner. Added skim milk and a small slice of valvetta. Used my stick blender. I didn't use the sherry. Just the ingredients I mentioned plus salt and pepper. Excellent soup.

Selected this because of its relative simplicity.  Somewhat bland; my wife and I simply were not impressed with this, made per ingredients and directions.  I ended up with 1/2 tsp nutmeg, adding some dashes of ground red pepper and two more T dry sherry. but, even then concluded that my quest for a simple cauliflower soup will march on.
We really liked this soup.  I added just a little seasoning to give it a little spice.  The sherry was a good idea also.

This was a very satisfying and yummy soup.  Simple to make and easy to modify.  I cut back a bit on the cauliflower and added some broccoli, also added some grated sharp cheddar,parmesan and some cream cheese.  Also, very important not to puree the entire soup, leave a couple cups of the vegys whole.  Thanx Vivien.

This soup is very easy to make. Everyone loved it, my mom who is 71 and my youngest daughter, 2.5 years old. There is no need to extra salt pepper or anything. I didn't use canned chicken broth. I made about 3 1/2 cups water with 1/3 cup chicken base. Absolutely perfect.

I found this soup very thick. I had a huge cauliflower so I used half of it and the carrots were large maybe thats why but I had to add a lot more broth and milk than called for. The carrots make this soup a pale orange color so it does not look like cauliflower soup. The other vegetables also change the taste not exactly a cauliflower soup really more of a vegetable soup really.  I thought it was okay but nothing spectacular.  I make a lot of soups and this is not one of my best
Delicious!  Even my cauliflower-hating husband loved it!

Awesome soup.
I made it with chicken broth instead of vegetable broth and added some curry powder.
Mmmmmmm
Will definitely make it again.
Made the recipe exactly as written but no sherry. Absolutely delicious!  My whole family loved it.
This is a delicious and simple soup. I'm usually too lazy to get out the blender, so I just mash everything in the pot with a potato masher. Thanks for the recipe!

I am vegan. I absolutely LOVE THIS SOUP AND SO DOES MY ENTIRE FAMILY! I love coming home from church on sundays and making this soup! It takes about an hour if you take your sweet time as I do and it’s delicious. I don’t use all the (vegan) butter it calls for at the beginning, I add all the veggies, veggie broth paste, a tiny bit of almond milk at the end if I feel like it’s needed, and omit the sherry and garnish. With homemade bread boy this fills the belly and is very very healthy!! (Without the animal fats) I usually have two huge bowls haha. Thanks for sharing :)
I make this frequently. It's super easy and my kids ask for it. Thanks!
Good, light and smooth soup.  Could use a perk up in flavor. Maybe a bit of grated parmesan on top or a splash of vinegar stirred in just before serving.
No taste.  This was just so-so.  Will try another recipe.  Wont make this again.

Yum! The day turned cold, so I decided not to grill steaks and steam cauliflower. This soup was easy to prepare and perfectly delicious. I added the fresh parsley (along with a little fresh rosemary & oregano) when I added the cauliflower. Served topped with cheddar cheese and bacon bits and a side of crusty bread. Husband and I enjoyed this simple meal while watching Game 6 of the World Series. Go, Astros)
I used veggie broth instead of chicken, added about a tsp of cumin, and sprinkled grated cheese on top of each bowl of soup.  Very tasty.
Very good soup - I blended most of it.. left some vegetable chunks -didn't have sherry on hand used a splash of dry red wine. Very good soup - will make again!
This was fantastic. It was the best soup I have ever made. I followed the recipe exactly except I didn't have fresh parsley so I used dried.
Just OK. Left out the sherry.

I made this with a gigantic farmer's market cauliflower and it turned out great.  It would be nice on a cold winter night.  I didn't have time to puree right after it cooked, so I left it in the fridge in the pot until the next evening.  Pureed well.
extremely good, I love puree soups and this one definitely hits the spot. I made it as is and we loved it, we now buy cauliflower more often just for this soup.
Very flavorful and light. This recipe is a good replication of my favrotie soup at a local Italian restaurant. I used a little less nutmeg (a pinch).

This was a great BASIC cream soup. I found that I didnt need the milk as it was already pretty thick. I also added baby spinach into the blender and when I put the soup back on the stove to simmer, added the salt and pepper along with curry, indian masala, tumeric and garlic oil I made myself. Delish!

I roasted the vegies for more flavor(425 for 30 minutes or so  with olive oil ,salt and pepper). Like otheres used vegt broth. pureed a bunch of parsley with soup. Added 1/3 cup half and half. for vegans would be fine without any dairy.

Great soup! We all loved it, including my 2.5 year old. Personally, I would cut down on the garlic, but my husband liked it as it was. I just used water and a bit of instant vegetable soup powder instead of the broth, and marsala instead of the sherry.
Very good.  I used 1/2 and 1/2 instead of milk and added gruyere cheese.  Delicious!

Really good soup! I had to add more salt to make it to our taste.  You can always add salt but you just can't take it away. I told my kids it was potato soup and they ate it up. One of the kids gave it 5 stars and the other gave it 4. I told them afterward what it was. This is a great way to hide veggies that may be hard to get kids to eat.
Used an immersion blender but it did not come out as smooth as in the photo, it was a little gritty. Flavor was good.

This is a fantastic soup! I pureed all but one cup of the veggies and mixed those back in at the end. I topped mine off with a little shredded Monteray Jack cheese. My 2 year old liked it a lot too. This recipe is a keeper, quick to make and very satifying.
Exactly what I was looking for, had some cauliflower and carrots to use up.  I think the spices need to be adjust a bit (add more pepper), overall good healthy soup.  Thanks for sharing!
Loved it, the potatoes really made it that perfect thickness!

Tried this recipe for the first time and we loved the soup.  It was easy to make but prepping the vegetables takes the most time.  I used only 3 cloves of garlic and substituted 1 cup of 18% cream for the milk.  I thought that the cream would add more flavour than the skim milk I had on hand.  The only comment is that the soup tastes more of potato than cauliflower.  But overall, this recipe is a keeper!

This soup was surprisingly yummy!  I just happened to have a whole head of cauliflower and wanted  a soup recipe, so this worked great.  But the head so large, I had to double the milk (I used skim).  I also did not have chicken broth, so I used 3 bouillon cubes and doubled the spices but skipped the sherry!  I guess I really customized it, but it came out delicious anyhow!  Tastes better than it looks!  :-)
Curry powder adds some oomph. Reserve about 1-2 c veggies before blending. Before serving, sprinkle with sharp cheddar. Excellent over grilled chicken.

I used 2 sweet potatos, baby carrots, and my cauliflower was gigantic so I used twice the milk, sherry, nutmeg, etc. This was really great for a lazy Sunday night paired with a spinach salad with feta, dried cranberries, sliced almonds, and balsamic vinagrette. Delicious, easy, and will definitely make again.
I didn't have any sherry so I left it out.  Even without it this was absolutely the best cauliflower soup I have ever made.

I love soups and this is one I will add to my go-to list. I only used 2 cloves of garlic (I didn't want an overpowering garlic taste), and I also only used 2/3 cup of milk. Next time I may use cream instead as I felt like it could have been just a tad bit creamier. I found my emulsion blender really came in handy so that I did not have to transfer batches over to the food processor, and also like some of the previous posters mentioned, I left out a cup of the veggies so as to add a bit to the texture in the end. I topped it with monterey jack shredded cheese instead of the parsley. Very good, and will make again.

Really good and very yummy - left the sherry out as didn't have any. I know this will be consumed very quickly today and toddler loves it. Thanks Also left the milk out as forgot that also and will still very nice.

This is a good cauliflower soup and enjoyed by everyone in our household. HOWEVER, if you are looking for the pure white, creamy cauliflower soup typically served in restaurants, this is not the recipe for you.

This soup was extremely disappointing. I thought the carrots completely overpowered the flavor. I omitted the brandy. The end product was very bland despite adding cayenne, crushed red pepper and doubling up on the garlic.  Needless to say I will never make this again.

I added 4 more cloves of garlic (on account that I looooove garlic) and an extra couple of carrots. I also left out the sherry (didn't have any in stock). But this soup turned out AMAZING!! 
Thanks Vivien for sharing this recipe.
This was delicious. Used light cream instead of milk bc I had it, and used shredded parmesan and croutons for garnish.

I left out the onions and used onion powder instead.  I also used vegetable broth instead of chicken to keep it vegetarian tonight.  May make again.  My two year old did spit out his candy for more bites of my soup though so that's always a plus!
This is the best cauliflower soup I've ever made. It's simple and delicious. I didn't change anything except substitute vanilla for the sherry.

Very delicious and simple to make. I also substituted heavy cream for the milk. As tempting as it is to not bother picking up fresh parsley, the garnish really adds a nice fresh flavour to the soup.
Great recipe. I kept out at least 2 cups of steamed veg's to add in last. Also added more parsley, and a bit more mutneg for flavour. Over all, was a hit here, and will be making again.

Yummy!  Even my two-year-old was scraping his bowl.  It was just that good.  We followed the recipe exactly, but we added about 1 cup of shredded cheddar at the end.

This was so easy and so good. I did make minor changes to suit personal taste. I added celery and added extra carrots (trying to pack in the veggies) and therefore added a bit more chicken broth. Wonderful recipe !  Used margarine instead of butter, 2% milk and Mrs. Dash Salt-free original seasoning blend.  Added dry parsley with rest of seasoning. Had no sherry so just left it out.  
Great taste !   This is a keeper for sure!  Thank you!

I altered just a bit by adding 1 more carrot, 3 celery, a little more pepper, NO milk, NO sherry or NO nutmeg - but I did add and eye-ball of rosemary!  Yum, definitely easy and a keeper - plus a good share! Thank you

This is one of my husbands (and my) favorite soups! I don't add the sherry (because I don't have it) and I add about a cup of grated cheddar cheese at the end. Otherwise I follow the recipe exactly.

I love that there's no cream, and I used low-fat milk - this is a LOW FAT soup. The only thing I left out was the parsley - we tried it and I don't think it's needed - and it's something my kids don't like so easy to skip it.
Love this soup! I prefer to leave some chunks of cauliflower and I use a little more than 1/8 tsp of nutmeg. Serve with crusty roll.
Okay, so I exchanged the milk for heavy cream.  Other than that, I followed the recipe to the letter...the sherry and fresh nutmeg are what make it stand out! Thanks for sharing!
lovely soup made it exactly to the recipe but kept one cup of veggies unpureed as suggested. REally tasty
This soup was awesome. I added heavy cream instead of milk and cut back on the potatoes. Overall very good recipe.

I started to make rice for dinner and then changed my mind to soup so I just added the rice after it was all done. It tasted awesome and gave it some texture. Lots of flavor. I will definitely be making it again.
Easy & delicious!
This soup is OK but not wonderful. It does not taste like cauliflower soup. There just are other recipes that are more flavorful than this one.
AMAZING!! Just brilliant the way it is :o) Thanks so much for this recipe

This recipe needed some tweaking.  There is so little fat in this recipe (which is awesome!!) that is does fall a bit short on flavor as written.  Things I did differently:  1) Roasted my cauliflower 1st with olive oil, salt, pepper, and garlic in a 400 degree oven, which gave it more depth...mmmm!  2) Left the skin on my potatoes, which is easier and healthy for you.  3) Added broccoli and celery that needed to be used up (and it pumped up the flavor).  4)  left some of the veggies chunky for texture, and didn't puree the entire batch, like other did.  5) Added more garlic than the recipe called for. 6) I even added thyme and a bay leaf.  7) Served with shredded cheddar on top.    After the modifications, it was yummy and satisfying.  I should mention that I had no sherry or nutmeg, which could be another reason it needed the modifications.

This is an excellent recipe. I had an usually large head of cauliflower so I had to adjust the broth and seasonings but I wouldn't make any changes.  Like the fact that it is relatively low calorie/fat. I will definitely try this with other vegetables. Thanks for the recipe.
First time I have ever made soup and it worked out great.
Very good. I will add this to my list of keepers.
Used white pepper instead of black for a spicier flavor, doubled the amount of sherry for a smoother flavor and omitted the parsley for garnish because I didn't have any!  Very good.

Freezing day here, so decided to make this soup. I was not disappointed, soup hit the spot! I decided to not purée the soup totally, leaving some of the vegetables intact. Served with a fresh baguette, yummy!! Will definitely make this  again!
very good and easy to make.

This soup is an awesome addition to a cold winters day! I added lots of shredded cheddar before serving with french garlic bread.
I also added a few very small florets of cauliflower and simmered at the end for extra added texture. This is a keeper!

This is really good.  The reason I didn't rate it 5 stars is that the first time I made it, I followed the recipe exactly -- the onion was way too much and overpowered the soup.  I made it a second time with very little onion and thought it was delicious.

it tasted good, but it kind of looked like baby food. next time i won't even puree it and just keep it as chunky potato/veggie soup. Cauliflower was expensive when I went to the store, so I used broccoli instead. Added some parm cheese on the top. Also- this made WAY more than 6 servings.
Excellent. Only change I made was a bit more salt (1.5 teaspoon instead of 1) and after letting it simmer, I put in some pieces of cauliflower so there would be some bigger chunks.
Made to recipe except left out sherry (did not have).  Everyone enjoyed and I will definitely make again.  Thank you for sharing.

I loved this recipe and so did everybody that I served it to. Even my picky 3 year old who normally refuses veggies. the only thing I did differently was I did not add the sherry or the parsley. I will make this again for sure!!
Very easy, very good! thank you!
The recipe is good!!! but u can reduce the amt of salt .=D
I tweaked this just a bit.  I used fat free half & half instead of milk, I threw in a couple slices of boiled ham, and I added some water as it seemed too thick without it.  It came out very tasty!
Wonderful recipe--easy, delicious.  I like that it uses potatoes to thicken it.  My family wanted seconds, and I will definitely put this on my make-again list.
This soup was pretty good though I felt it was a little light on seasoning. It tasted better the next day once the flavors had a chance to set.
GREAT , I am a new cook , and followed the plan to a T . My reward was in the smiles all around . Loved it and will keep it in my favorites file . Thanks . Lyle

I'm giving this recipe four stars primarily because I changed a lot of things, and I don't think it's fair to rate a recipe lower than that unless you stay true to it.  That said, all of my changes were either suggested in the intro to the recipe itself (adding more/different veggies), or out of necessity.  The soup we ended up with was good, not spectacular, but I thought there were some problems with the recipe itself.  The biggest one is that there didn't seem to be enough liquid.  That could be because I had a mutant head of cauliflower (I only used half, but did add a cup or so of broccoli florets and a little leftover frozen spinach), or because my idea of a "large" potato or onion is bigger than Vivien's.  Either way, I had to add an extra two cups of water, and the still veggies weren't close to covered.  Also, maybe she was using salted stock -- mine was unsalted -- but I had to add far, far more salt than 1 tsp; could have been the extra water, but I still don't think one tsp would do it for all of those veg.  The nutmeg and pepper disappeared until I added more.  All of that being said, this was a decent base recipe, and will be useful for making cream of leftover veggie soup, but I'll probably keep my eye out for another in the meantime.  Thanks, anyway!

Made this last night and brought some to work today for my lunch. Yum! I let the potatoes and carrots simmer twice as long as called for (40 minutes) to make sure they were tender when I used the immersion blender. I also reserved about 1-2 cups of veggies before blending. I highly recommend eating this with big, crunchy croutons. My husband thinks it tastes more like a gravy so, why not! we plan on serving the rest of this over grilled chicken breasts for dinner tomorrow night.
Great recipe for helping me to use up all of my CSA cauliflower.  Mmmm, will defintely be making this again next year.

The soup was great until I added the pepper. I followed the recipe exactly and the kids said it was too hot to eat. I will make it again without the pepper because I have a lot of soup to eat by myself before I can make it again.
Very tasty!!!! the creamy texture made it very fulfilling as well, highly recommended!!!!

This was great! I didn't have chicken broth, so just used water + a little salt. Didn't have carrots, so omitted them. Added more milk and seasonings than it called for plus a little sour cream at the end. Topped with parmesean. Yum!

Geez, this is good!!!Did not use sherry, did not have any, used a hand blender, and left small bits of veggies, added celery, cause I had it. You can leave the salt out, broth has enough, but do use the nutmeg. Add more or less milk depending on taste. Really great soup, next day even better.
What a great tasting soup.  Nothing to change.  I've already been asked for the recipe
I liked it but the rest of the family thought it was boring.

I made this for my husband who loves cauliflower and he raved about it! I added a half moon size of amish swiss cheese when the soup was done and just let it melt in. It wasn't a strong cheese flavor but really enhanced this soup! I HIGHLY recommend trying it this way!! ENJOY!

Incredible recipe. My son had two big bowls and wants all the leftovers to himself. I was generous with the garlic (6 large cloves) and skipped the sherry and parsley. I added 2 bay leaves to the oil before adding the onions and garlic and kept everything else the same. Garnished with parmesan flakes. This is a keeper!

Great recipe!  The only changes I made were omitting the sherry (didnt have any), and I added 2 tsp grated fresh ginger while simmering.  When I served it, I topped it with some finely shredded swiss cheese.  It got rave reviews from my hubby and guests.

Made this recipe the way it was written and used my immersion blender. Instead of using milk, I used fat free evaporated milk (1 can) and 1 tbls Marsala Wine, because that's what I had on hand. Don't love parsley, so I used 1 tblsp. of dry tarragon. It was perfect. Thanks for this recipe.

This recipe is simple and very tasty. I used 1/2 milk and 1/2 Half and Half (simply to use up the Half and Half) and omitted the sherry because I didn't have any. It is quite tasty. I think some shredded cheddar cheese on top will be fantastic.
This a great tasting soup.  It's quick and easy to make.  Sometimes I mash it with a potato masher and leave it chunky and it's delicious that way as well.
My husband and I both thought this was missing something but we couldn't figure out what it was.  Maybe milk or cream?
Just made this soup...awesome recipe.  So easy to make.  Also put aside 1 cup of vegees and added it back into the puree soup...and top it off with any shredded sharp tasting cheese!

This is a good, mild flavored soup. Serve with shredded cheese on the side for those who prefer the more common cheese cauliflower soup and oyster crackers or saltines. I think the soup is at it's best with some vegetable chucks left in the puree.

While not the most appealing soup to look at, it tastes amazing! Lots of flavor. I skipped the sherry and used vegetable broth, along with adding cheese and celery to this soup and it was perfection. Will be making this again.
Great ingredients.  Nice, thick soup.  Unfortunately, there's just no incredible flavor.  Topped each of my servings with lots of shredded Sharp Cheddar Cheese plus Paprika and it was pretty good.
Very good and pretty easy.

Delicious, easy to make too, thanks!

I have made cauliflower soup before but prefer this recipe because it doesn't call for any cream, but tastes sooo creamy!

This soup tastes good.  I did use hazelnut liqueur instead of sherry.  I also just used a potato masher instead of a blender which left the soup a bit more chunky. Made exactly as written (no nutmeg, don't like it).  Great light soup, family loved it.

This was easy to make and pretty tasty. I tried my new immersion blender (instead of using a normal blender)- it worked beautifully on the soup and was easier to clean up. The only bad thing about the soup was that it made the kitchen stink for two days.. Not so sure how that happened!

I thought this was a great recipe! I have never made a cauliflower soup before and was surprised at how flavorful and creamy this came out. I did make a couple small changes. So easy and so good!  I did change a few things, like using heavy cream in place of milk (3/4 c.) since I had some I needed to get rid of.  Honestly, if I was in a bind, and had neither, I thought the soup would have been fine  without any dairy or extra liquid added (based on both flavor and thickness of the soup).  Depends on your own personal tastes.  I also added an extra carrot, used an eyeballed amount of fresh grated nutmeg, skipped the sherry altogether and added 2-3 tbsp. of parsley to the soup instead of using it as a garnish.  I added it at the same time as the cauliflower.  Finally, I followed others advice and held back a bit of the veggies to add back to the puree. I was so pleased with the versatility of this recipe, that I think I will be using it for a very long time to come.

[Edit: I wrote this review in 2008 and it's now 2014. I'm still making this soup with a few other alterations. I don't bother blending or pureeing this soup at all anymore. I find that I like having a more rustic feel, with bits and chunks from using a potato masher (just mashing until I get a consistency I like). I still skip the dairy completely and I never used the sherry (you just don't really need either of those ingredients, especially the way I make it). I still add the parsley into the soup (nice handful finely chopped, no measuring needed) and also add a medium sized sweet potato (sliced thinly for faster cooking). The sweetness pairs well with the fresh grated nutmeg I use.]

I do a lot of canning.  I mashed the papaya up by pulsing the food processor after I peeled the fruit. Also, I have Amish cookbooks and they recommend using jello in place of pectin; it's cheaper and adds a pretty color.  If you do this, be aware that the color jello you use will affect the results.  Use 'orange' for this recipe, not lime.  If you use the jello, for 5 cups of sugar, I'd recommend taking about 1/2 cup out because the jello has sugar in it and it will be a little too sweet otherwise. Leave the OJ out.  Also, I noticed some c/o the jam being a little runny.  The Amish book I have recommends freezing fruit before use. Has something to do with the pectin levels (better consistency).  Also, for you that have papaya trees and are running over in fruit, my suggestion is "have you ever made homemade wine"?  I started making it due to an over abundance of fruit from when I lived in the Apple Valley in Washington.  I gave the recipe 4 stars.  It was ok, but if I would have lessened the sugar, I think it would have been better (I did not lessen to 4.5 cups & jello has sugar). The flavor was ok, but not as good as I'd like; however, the person on here that suggested habanero peppers..not a bad idea. Kicking it up a notch in that way would be an added punch to regular pepper jelly; if you haven't tried it, do.  Nice holiday gift with cream cheese & crackers. Habanero are hot, so if you don't like it really hot try serrano &/or jalapeno. Serrano have really good flavor.

I love this jam! We have had a ton of papaya from our tree and so glad I found a recipe I can use for all of them! Tried it with orange juice and just used only 1 package of pectin. It came out perfect. I'm going to try lemon juice on the next batch!
Papaya does not need pectin.it contains natural pectin already.i made this recipe with only the other 3 ingredients: papaya , orange juice and sugar.

This was yummy.  Mine did not set quite as well as i would have liked, however it was my first time making Jam.  I used only one package of pectin per another users review, maybe that is where, I went wrong?  I don't know.  It was still a yummy and a fun way to use a bunch of papayas that my neighbor gave me from her tree

yummy!  The only change i made (because we like sweet and spicy) was to add 2 habeneros.  It came out so good.  I had got a bunch of papayas from the local food bank and had no idea what to do with them.  By happy chance, my grandmother had just given me a bunch of old canning jars. so now i have several batches of Delicious Habenero-Papaya jam and a few batches of regular will be made up tomorrow.  It didn't take too long, because i had 3 little helpers to mash the papayas for me.  This recipe is definately a keeper
The Best EVER!
It didn't gel like it should have. I needed more pectin. However I will make it again with the extra pectin because it tastes delicious!!! It worked really good as it was as a sauce on ice-cream.

This is a great jam. However, it can be improved upon. I like my jam with a little more zestiness. So, instead of using orange juice I have used lilikoi juice (which is a Hawaiian passionfruit). That is fabulous. People keep telling me to eat papaya with lime juice, so I just tried that - substituting the orange juice with lime juice. Also great. Both make the jam 'pop'. yum.

Excellent taste very easy to make. i am a novice at this jelly thing and i found it so easy to make. i changed it up alittle bit though, i added some pineapple puree to it and about 10 whole habaneros with excellent results

I made this jam 3 days ago.  It was very easy and the only change I made was that I squeezed juice from half a lemon to balance out the sweetness.  It tasted wonderful but like the previous comments it didn't set up firm enough.

Nice jam!  I had some fresh tangerines on hand so I squeezed a couple of them in instead of orange juice... delicious.  A great way to take advantage of the giant papayas that go on sale in the Mexican market.  The color is gorgeous.
have 3 trees  this very good

this jam came out great i have a papaya tree in my back yard and this was my first time making any kind of jam it was so easy the only change i made was i diddnt have pectin so i substituted arrowroot starch it worked like a charm i tried the plate in the freezer trick and it instantly jelled up we tried the papaya as it is in fruit form but my husband diddnt care for it this way so i first made a papaya bread wich came out great and then i tried this jam im so glad i did now i can make several different variations and try new flavors !

I have made this rub many times now. I made a few changes. I reduced cayenne pepper to 1 tsp as I don't like too much heat. I reduced salt to 1 tbsp because I also use a bbq sauce to finish at the end. I also added a bit of cumin just because. I marinate ribs overnight with the rub, applied freely. I fully cook the ribs slowly in the oven (I have a steam/convection combination). At the end, I remove ribs and brush on bbq sauce and put back in oven on high heat for just 10 minutes, or throw on grill. I have been told these are the best ribs someone has ever tasted, including restaurants.

Thank you for this recipe. I made it my own, but I started with this.
Loved it! I also added about 1/4 C. ground coffee & made a rub for ribs!
My family loves this rub on pork or chicken. It can get a bit spicy. Use only half of the cayenne pepper. Looks dry on the outside but seals the flavors and juices into the meat.  Excellent rub.
Great easy recipe used dried onion flakes instead of onion powder and reduced the cayenne pepper to cut the heat for the kids but overall very happy with recipe

This was a delicious way to incorporate a lot of fresh ingredients into a meal! After reading other reviews I used 6 romas & added a 6oz can of tomato paste (and about 2tbsp water to dilute that). I also added a can of chopped basil & oregano tomatoes just because I had it in the pantry; will try without next time. Served over whole wheat pasta.. DELICIOUS! I am convinced that I'll never buy pasta sauce again because this recipe is a great base to add-on to and make my own healthier and homemade version!

I tried this and it was AMAZING. I made a few changes I'd seen suggested beforehand and a threw in a few of my own. Because my mother in law has a garden with about a billion more tomatoes than she needs, I added in quite a few more than the recipe called for... about 12 cups! I also added a third cup of mushrooms, a can of tomato sauce, 2 tbs garlic, 3 cups bell peppers, and 4 sliced sausages (since I can't do without meat). Then I let it simmer for 45 mins to let all the flavors blend nicely. It was a hit with my family and even though there was so much sauce, it all got eaten. My husband says he now forbids me to buy any canned spaghetti sauce EVER. Thanks so much!
Loved this! The onions cooked down nicely. I did add a smidge of tomato sauce to thicken it a bit more.
Very good. I substituted crimini mushrooms and used tomato paste instead of wedges (2tbsps paste+1/2 cup water at high altitude). I put the ragout over baked polenta topped with goat cheese. Delish!
Great sauce! I froze it in silicone muffin cups. Just the right size for 1 person. Thanks for sharing!

This was very nice over whole wheat pasta.  I did add 2 minced cloves of garlic with the onions to suit our taste, but I think it would still be good without it.  Thanks for sharing an easy, tasty pasta topper.

This recipe was simple and delicious! I added minced garlic and a can of tomato paste, as well as some italian seasoning, and a dash of chili powder. I sometimes make a variation of your recipe with chicken breast strips instead of mushrooms, and we love that too. Thanks for the great idea!
fast & easy. i added two cloves of garlic to the onions and it turned out great. not extraordinary, but a decent quick pasta topping.
Cooked this tonight and really enjoyed it. Great taste, quick & easy to make. Thanks :)

This is excellent, nice and simple but still hearty and delicious. I used a pint of halved cherry tomatoes, because I had them on hand, and dried basil as I had no fresh but it was still really great served over creamy polenta. Thanks for the recipe!
Added a little garlic and a dash of cayenne for a little heat since I was out of red pepper flakes. Served over egg noodles . So awesome and simple. Thanks for a great recipe.

Love this recipe! I'm a huge kombucha addict, but it gets expensive and I haven't ventured into making the real thing yet.  This is a super tasty shortcut recipe that really does taste like the real thing! I'm not a huge fan of powdered ginger, so was a little conservative with the amount at first, but I ended up adding the full amount.  Next time I might try with a slice of fresh ginger. The blueberries give it a nice pink color. I think I will omit the lemon juice, or halve the amount from now on, just a personal preference.   Such a refreshing drink for the summer! I can't wait to experiment with flavored La Croix waters and different fruits. Thanks for the awesome recipe!

07.10.17 ~ As soon as I saw a review from LilSnoo, I knew I had to try this recipe. My DH loves the expensive version of this drink. He thought this version was 'ok' and I liked it better than the store bought version, but still can't love it, yet. I love the taste of vinegar, but have a hard time getting past the taste in the drink. I did buy a flavored seltzer water so I'm going to try this again. I'm still giving this 4-stars and going to work on perfecting it for my DH taste. Love the cost of this version, much better!

This needed major doctoring in order to be drinkable for my taste. I did use lime juice, rather than lemon juice, as the submitter said it was an okay substitution in the recipe and I had fresh squeezed lime juice readily available. I found it way to "boozey" and even bitter tasting. To doctor it up, I added some frozen peaches and some sugar. Blended it in my Vitamix, and then served it with a bit of 7-up. Made it drinkable, but not something I'd make again. Sorry!

I love most things pumpkin, so I was intrigued by this recipe.  The first time I made it with pure pumpkin - don't make that mistake, it was horrible.  The recipe should have emphasized to buy the pumpkin pie mix.  I add 2T of fat free half and half and sprinkle cinnamon on top of the whipped cream, and it is quite nice!  You could add cinnamon sticks if you are entertaining.
I did not care for this recipe.

SUPER YUMMY!It is very rich though, so if you don't like rich things you won't like it...I do though so it was amazing!Just like pumpkin pie!The only thing I changed is we couldn't find any maple liquour so we used caramel creme liqour...Still super super yummy!

Went to Salem, MA myself and this is what I used when I got home. Follow directions on can of pumpkin and bake for 15 minutes. Let cool and blend really well. Fill shaker with ice and add 1 scoop of pumpkin 1 shot of Goldschlager 3 shots of Baily's 2 shots of Captain Morgan 1 squirt of whipped cream and a drop of milk. Rim glass with crushed up graham crackers!!
Great Pumpkin-tini. I used heavy whipping cream and maple extract because that's what I had. Other than that I followed the recipe.  I like being able to drink my 'pumpkin pie'!
Not good.

Good basic formula, doesn't go wrong.  I prefer the stronger flavor of apple-cider vinegar instead of basic white, although it's more expensive.

I use more raspberry (preserves) than this recipe calls for -- about three times as much.  I'm looking for real raspberry flavor, and less doesn't seem to do it.
i tried this receipe and loved it. but I used malt vinegar  and a teaspoon of djon mustard. I used it on to of a spinach and strawberry salad. was to die for
easy and yummy!
This is soooo much better than store-bought. I didn't change a thing in it.  Thanks for sharing!!
Thrs sounds good.

I reduced the amount of ingredients to make a 1/4 cup of the dressing. With the modifications I made, I would rate this vinaigrette dressing with 5 stars.
Loved this recipe.  The portions of each ingredient are perfect.  I used blackberry jelly instead for a new and exciting flavor
This was easy & wonderful!I had no raspberry jam, so I used blackberry jam instead. It was great.
Excellent taste

Yes. I made changes and will make it again and again indefinitely. I changed it a lot because it needs a lot of help. But I give five stars because I rave how simple and inexpensive it is to make. Firstly, I found that it needs much more raspberry jam than the meager amount the recipe calls for, and also it needs typical vinaigrette spices, as I put in ground mustard and a bit of jarred chopped garlic and a bit of dried thyme. The mustard is integral to the flavor that's fantastic! It's better than Ken's Raspberry Walnut! And much healthier for you! I'm a triple the ingredients up to fill up the whole Ken's plastic jar, that I emptied the contents of to have a bottle I can shake it in.
I liked this recipe as it was very easy. I did add 1 tsp. Dijon mustard because it was a bit sweet, and without a distinct taste.

8.13.16 ~ Made this delicious salad dressing as part of a salad bar for a birthday dinner with friends. Of course, when I asked the other couples what their favorite dressing was, all four of them had a different 'favorite'. No problem, I just made everyone's favorite. This raspberry dressing was very easy to make with 4 simple ingredients. I put the jam, vinegar and olive oil in my Magic Bullet® and let it whip together this dressing. I stirred in the salt and pepper to taste.  It has a slightly tart taste and a thickness to the dressing. Our friend who requested this type of dressing and my husband really enjoyed it

Ow...way to tart for my tastes as written.  I should have used half the amount of vinegar.  I didn't taste until it was all mixed so I doubled the jam and added a teaspoon of sugar, too.  I will be using it tomorrow so will see what happens to the flavor as it stands.  

Fortunately, the ingredients and mixture is incredibly easy so if I doctored it too much, I can always make more!
Easy, quick!

Fabulous vinaigrette! Easy to make, yet tastes better than anything you'd get in a bottle. I love it when a few simple ingredients you have around the house come together to create something so good. Poppyseeds would be a great addition, but this was fine as is and was perfect over mixed salad greens with thin sliced red onion, Granny Smith apple, toasted walnuts, dried cranberries and a bit of feta cheese sprinkled over top - YUM!
So good! Although I changed it since it was a bit too vinegar-y for me...and I only had blackberry jam.
I was out of jam so I used 1/2 cup of raspberries with sweetener. We loved it. This is going into regular rotation!
Fabulous!!  Kids, neighbor...we all loved it.  Soo simple.  If you don't have rasberry...any jam will work!  YUMMY!!!
I didn't think I would like this but decided to give it a day in court and made the recipe as stated.  Wow --tasty!  And dead easy to make!  This is definitely a keeper!

I cut this recipe in half to try it.  I used seedless/sugar free raspberry preserves and no salt.  This had the right amount of tangy-ness.  Went great with my grilled chicken salad.  Now I'm making another batch for lunch tomorrow.  It does start to separate so really mix well before serving.
Good recipe and simple.  I added half teaspoon of Dijon mustard  and another teaspoon of jam to emulsify the mix
Simply delicious. Very easy to make. I'll definitely will keep making it. It's a keeper!

Excellent vinaigrette recipe! I did change it a bit by using white balsamic vinegar and adding 1/2 tsp of dijon mustard to emulsify the dressing. I used it for a pear, gorgonzola, cranberry and candied walnut salad. The combo was delicious. Brought it to my daughter's kindergarten graduation pot luck and it was gone quickly. Very easy to make, which is the best part.

A very simple salad dressing to make.  If you already make raspberry jam it's even easier!  It is not sweet like you would think, but a tad bit tart, which is fine with me.  If you like tart and you like raspberry it's a good dressing to try.

It is probably not fair to rate this recipe because I did not make it as is.
