Very good. I substituted a can of rotell for the fresh tomatoes and green peppers and added some cumin. Didn't fry in oil, just sprayed a nonstick pan with olive oil spray and cooked for a minute on each side.

This is SUCH a good idea! Who would have put these two together!? We make it ALL the timenow, my husband LOVES these, its a meal too! Like a bean burrito and a cheese quesadilla. SO SO SO good, definitely try this one. I did it a little different, mainly using the idea, i just make a quesadilla cheese and smear refried beans in it. Fry it in a little butter on the skillet and put sour cream and salt and pepper all over it. Thats how we do it, its yummy!

My family LOVES this recipe. I make it even easier by using Rotel tomatoes which also add some spice. I usually add a combo of beans, black and pintos. Sometimes add refried beans. I assemble the quesadillas and just microwave them to melt the cheese. Very easy and great meal to get some  healthy food into a picky eater.
Good and easy to make, but it needs some seasoning.  I added salt but would also suggest adding a little taco seasoning or red pepper flakes.

This is delicious! Frying it is a great idea - the crispy tortilla is to die for. When I made this, instead of chopping up tomatoes, I just poured in some Newman's Own salsa into the pan. This added a bit more flavor.

I can't get enough of these. I made them as directed, substituting olive oil for the vegetable oil. Also cooked then on my panini press and topped with salsa when done. Will be keeping the mixture in the fridge for any time I feel like throwing one together for a quick meal.
It was a good recipe, but a little bland.  Next time, we need to add seasoning to it to give it some flavor.  Otherwise, it was a great recipe.  Needs some tweaking.
Awesome!!  My wife is Costa Rican and loved the black beans.  Very easy and quick to make - I've made this a couple of times this month and I'm sure I'll continue to do so

I'm always on the lookout for ways to prepare vegetables for my very picky family.  Both my husband and 3-year old boy gobbled these down and asked for more.  Couldn't have been easier to make and allows for inclusion of all different vegetables depending on the season.  This is a winner that I'll make repeatedly!

This was even yummier than I thought it would be.  Soooo good!  I followed the recipe exactly and we really enjoyed it.  Both my husband and I probably would have liked it a little spicier, but I wanted to give little bites to our 10 month olds (they loved it as well!) so I didn't substitute anything spicy.  I found this recipe just to use up a large can of black beans that I opened yesterday and didn't use much of, and I expected to like it but not love it.  Well, we were pleasantly surprised...this is certainly a recipe where the whole is more than the sum of the parts!  I garnished with additional tomato, green onions, sour cream, and some extra filling.  Quite delicious, thanks!

I made these for me and a friend, and we both loved them. I had some leftover filling, and they are just as good (maybe even better!) the next day. To avoid the mess I also found it easier to use one tortilla folded in half. Also, after my disaster frying them in a skillet, I tried brushing a indoor grill with oil, and cooking them on there (which also avoided the hassel of flipping!)- it worked perfectly!

Philly LIKED it! I have a picky hubby with lots of health considerations. It isn't easy feeding Philly and keeping him healthy. This recipe is one that will help. We used whole wheat tortillas and it was satisfying and fun to eat. No scrunchy faces on this one! I will be keeping this recipe in my menus, and that is saying a LOT!
REALLY good. Be careful when flipping the quesadillas, and make sure the oil is not too hot (as mine was- burned myself). My kids loved this and we will add it to our regular rotation!
MMM  this was sooo delicious! I used vegan cheese in it :]

I agree with other readers that it is a little bland as it stands BUT it is so versatile so do what you want. Kids love it and it is filling. I put it on a griddle pan but like to see that some have put it in the oven. I think I'd like it that way, too.
I added chicken to mine.  Yummy.
I, who hate beans, LOVE this recipe.  I topped it with low fat sour cream and salsa!!  We will eat this over and over again!  Thank you
These were delicious.  I used whole wheat tortillas, yum!

My foods and nutrition students loved this!  I have since made it for lunch several times.  It's quick and easy to put together.  I would recommend using much less oil in order to fry the quesadillas.

Another delicious way to have a quesadilla!  I made the recipe exactly as written and I wouldn't change a thing about it.  We enjoyed ours with olives, pico de gallo and sour cream.  Thanks for the awesome recipe.
Good, but trying to flip the quesadillas was a real pain. Alot of the filling spilled out. Tasted good could use a little more spice.

My husband and I really liked the versatile mixture. We are going to try the leftovers in breakfast burritos tomorrow morning. I also baked the quesadilla's in the oven and they came out perfect. Super quick and easy for the nights your just not in the mood to be in the kitchen for a long time. Will defiantly be making this one again...LOVED IT!
Pretty good. I used a cast iron pan which made it crisp. We dipped slices into picante sauce.
Yum!! We loved these, I used a red pepper, I had it instead of green.  I served with salsa and sour cream on the side.  I will make these again for sure.

I baked these, which was easier and healthier than frying them. Due to a tomato snafu, I replaced the tomato with spinach and tomato paste (long story). They turned out well, if a little messy! I added some spices (chili powder and red pepper) too.

This was great! I found the veggie mixture a little bland, so added 1 tbsp chili powder and 1 tsp ground cumin. I covered half of the tortillas with filling, topped with cheese and cilantro, then folded them in half and broiled them for a few minutes per side, without olive oil. I served them with sour cream, guacamole and salsa. They received rave reviews from adults and kids alike! An easy, tasty, satisfying and nutritious vegetarian weeknight meal. Thanks for a keeper!
First try at something like this.  Both hubby and I loved it.

I looooove this recipe!  It is my go-to for days I want a quick and easy meal.  I usually sub most of the ingredients with the can of Herdez Salsa, can of black beans, and some corn....super easy and delicious!!
Couldn't get black beans so substituted with kidney beans. Very tasty would make again on one of our meat free nights

The filling was very good but there was too much of it. Besides that my family enjoyed it tho it was difficult to flip in the pan. next time i make it I will probably just make the filling and add meat.

Easy and fun to make. I used the smaller 6" tortillas. I placed the tortilla in my pan, added toppings to one side, and folded the tortilla in half. This is much easier than the traditional method and less messy. This recipe is not spicy at all, so if you like some heat, add hot peppers or dip into spicy salsa. I'll definitely make these again!

To me this recipe is a good start. The flavors work well together but some items were a little out of proportion. For instance, 1 cup of cheese (if you're making 6) is way too little. Also, you'll note that many other reviewers were adding other things. That's because on it's own it lacks character. Next time I'm going to add some jalepenos or crushed red pepper. As far as the frying, I don't see why it was necessary. I spritzed the pan with some olive oil before putting the tortilla in the pan and it worked phenomenally well. Nice, golden and crunchy. Forget a quarter cup and just squirt some olive oil into the pan before each quesadilla goes in. Like I said, a very good start and I will make this again with a number of revisions.
I made these and cut them up in small wedges and served for a party.  Everyone LOVED them and I will most defintely make these again!

This was really good but like a lot of people I did modify the recipe because it was a little bit simple.  I added diced jalapeno peppers to the mixture and tossed in a bit of seasoning: cayenne pepper, paprika, and cumin added quite a bit of flavor.  It was hard to flip the flour tortilla, though.
Tasty.  Although I had to add more cheese, 1c. is not enough!  Chicken would be a nice addition next time.

Very tasty!  After reading numerous reviews, I made the following changes:  while sautéing onions and garlic I added 1 tsp. Chili powder and cumin, 1/4 to 1/2 tsp. Chili flakes, 1/2 tsp. salt and pepper.  I then added chopped pepper and sautéed a few minutes before adding other ingredients.   My personal preference there wasn't enough cheese.  I used 2 1/2 cups of shredded cheddar and placed a bit on the tortilla before the vegetable mixture then added the rest on top.  Lightly brushed with olive oil and baked at 400 for 15 minutes on baking sheets.  Thanks for the recipe!
I will try to make fold the tortillas instead of putting one on top of the other.  Delicious easy meal!

These are awesome! I did use a can of diced tomatoes with green chiles instead of the tomatoes. I also added more garlic and a little chili powder. We put them on a cookie sheet in the oven at 400 degrees for about 15 minutes and didn't even need to flip them.

My advice is to invest $20.00 at Target for a quesadilla maker.  It makes perfect 10" quesadillas in 3 minutes without the mess.  This is the first recipe that we tried and we loved it.  It was a little soupy from the tomatoes, so we drained it. The entire family loved it and came back for more.  I doubled the recipe and froze some for a 5 minute dinner in the near future.
Very tasty.  Added cumin and chili powder.  Baked at 350 for 10-15 minutes.
Fantastic.
Delicious and easy, no need to place quesadillas in skillet, stick 'em right in the oven!
I folded mine in half and baked in the oven. Tastes great.
As noted added cumin, chili pepper and red pepper flakes

I used corn tortillas instead of flour to give the quesadilla a deeper flavor and they turned out awesome!  Also changed up the cheeses by sprinkling mild cheddar on the bottom tortilla before adding the bean mixture, and topping it with white Mexican cheese mix.  Will definitely make these again, yum!

I love quesadillas and I didn't like these much.  If I were to do it again, I would use roasted peppers and omit the corn.  The super-chunky/crunchy texture was a little too much for my taste.  They could use some spice as well, so I added cumin.

What a great meal we had for dinner tonight! I followed the recipe until the very end. I tasted it and like some others have noted, it was rather bland, hence the 4 stars instead of 5 I would give for the final product. I added sea salt, cumin, and chili powder, a little at a time until I liked it. I served it with Mexican Rice I by Michele O'Sullivan (made with brown and wild rice) and guacamole by Bob Cody. Back to the quesadillas, I folded each one in half and spread a little butter on one side of the outside. I put on a big spoonful of beans and topped with shredded cheese (much more than the recipe called for). I cooked them on the electric grill until browned on each side. Topped with sour cream. Delicious! Thank you!
Super fast and easy. I added dashes salt, pepper, cayenne pepper and cilantro for more flavor. It was a hit!
So good! The only thing I changed was that I baked them for about 5 mins!
I added chille powder and cumin for extra flavor.

This was a very easy, tasty recipe.  I added some red peppers to it and it made a very colorful dish.  I also folded the tortilla in half  instead of putting a second on top.  This made it easier to flip.  This is definitely a recipe to make again.
These are great quesadillas...even good cold.  They make a great snack or a nice dinner with the addition of some rice, lettuce, tomato and sour cream on the side.
Will make it again. Added 1 tbsp cumin and chili

You know, this came out really well for bean quesadillas, but the next time I wanted to make these, I forgot the tortillas, green pepper, and cheese.  I panicked for a minute and then remembered I had Fritos scoop chips.  I decided to turn the bean quesadilla filling into a dip base. I used a 4 oz can of chopped chili peppers stirred while heating the vegetables.  I also added a 1/4 cup of lime juice and sprinkled in about a tablespoon of dried cilantro for an extra kick.  YUM YUM YUM!
Really delicious! I added shrimp to the mix, and nicked the bell peppers. I also used vintage cheddar directly from the Cheddar Gorge in the UK. Excellent dinner.

Easy and everyone ate it. I didn't have any green peppers or tomatoes but threw in a little salsa instead. I put a little cheese on the bottom, then some of the bean mixture and then some more cheese to seal it; hence less spillage when flipping. Baked 350 on non-stick cookie sheet for 10 min, flipped and then baked for 5min more.

Excellent, easy recipe, and if you watch the amount of oil and use wheat tortillas, this is an incredibly healthy dish! My kids loved it, even the picky ones! I've made it four or five times and it's always a hit.
These have become a staple at my house AND at some of my friend's houses. So good and easy.

Loved these!! Will probably add some jalapeños next time for a little flair. The flavors worked well together. Also I will bake them next time because although they were delicious fried, they will be healthier baked. I saved the veggies and beans in the fridge overnight and it was even better in the morning! Thanks for sharing, I really enjoyed these!!!!
I added a jar of salsa as we prefer our food saucy.  I also used mixed beans and didn't add any corn
Very yummy!!!
I really liked how simple this recipe was and that there wasn't a ton of ingredients.  But even so, the taste was really good.  And not unhealthy!  Easy, quick and ideal for one person or many.

These are good with the addition of chili powder and cumin.  Without I think they would be lacking in flavor.  Also for the tomatoes, I added a 15 oz can of diced tomatoes with green chili's.  Didn't fry them--seemed like an unnecessary step since the tortilla crisp nicely in a 400 oven when brushed lightly with some olive oil.

This was good, but needed a little more flavor. I added lots of lemon and cumin, but next time I will also add jalapeno, and cilantro. I used corn tortillas instead of flour and added some chicken. It also works good just eating it like a taco with melted cheese on top. Thanks for sharing!!
Great ingredients. Added salsa. How in the world are you supposed to flip this thing?  I can't even get it out of the pan.

This is a wonderful tasty dish, however, I think it makes 6-8 servings, instead of just four. It is great to have the leftovers though. One important observation, use a griddle instead of a skillet. I started using a large skillet as in the directions and when I attempted to flip the quesadilla, I started a small fire!! All the filling and oil went everywhere. I quickly started using a griddle and didn't have a problem.
Yummy, healthy and easy!
This turned out good as written. It does thicken up quick after you take it off the heat so move fast.

Absolutely delicious! We took a salad to a dinner group tonight, and everyone loved it. A friend said she makes a very similar dressing with a tablespoon of orange juice. I might try that next time too. I followed the recipe, except I added some raspberry flavored vinegar to the vinegar measurement. The onion really adds the perfect kick to the dressing. I'll be making this regularly.

Loved this! I used about 1/4 cup chopped green onions and put them in the food processor (it did turn my dressing kind of green, but it didn't matter when I mixed it in). Instead of a cup of oil, I used 1/2 cup extra light olive oil. I used this dressing on spinach, peaches, blue cheese, and toasted pecans. Delicious!
I love this... I put blue cheese and toasted almonds on spring greens and add this dressing.  I could eat it all day.
Oh, WOW! This is so delicious. Every time I've taken salad with this dressing to a potluck, everyone asks me for the recipe. They keep coming back for more salad until the bowl is empty.
Perfect dressing for any salad with fruit or berries.
Wonderful dressing, made this to go over a Spinach salad with Peaches and Pecans by Robin on this website. I will make this my staple poppy seed dressing from now on. Thanks Paula for the recipe.

I needed a basic recipe for Poppyseed dressing, but wanted to do something healthier than white sugar an vegetable oil, so these were my substitutes: Instead of white sugar, agave nectar. Instead of white vinegar, red wine vinegar. Omit the dry mustard. Instead of vegetable oil, extra virgin olive oil. My husband loved it.
Awesome, fast, and EASY!!! Love it! Packs the flavor!
Amazing on a spinach, craisin, pecan, feta cheese salad.
This is the best recipe.  I have used it on my green salads for years!  LOVE, LOVE, LOVE IT
Love this recipe...I use one tablespoon of Sweet Leaf Stevia in place of sugar...everyone loves this recipe!
Delicious with chopped romaine lettuce, apples, pears, toasted almonds, cranraisons, chunked blue cheese, and some fresh lemon juice...even my teenage boys devoured it!!!
We really love this dressing on tropical fruit.  Especially fresh pineapple.
This is a yummy dressing...!!  changes/substitutes I made......agave, fig balsamic Vinagre, Blend of Olive Oil and Walnut Oil,  2 tablespoons water to lighten it up.....not so oil heavy!
Very nice.  A keeper.

Excellent! At first I wasn't sure it had much flavor but after about a half an hour the flavors really came through. We enjoyed it on a spinach salad with mandarin oranges, sweet onion, and slivered almonds. Thanks for sharing :)

Loved it!  Also cut the oil in half and it tasted great.  We have made this several times now and made several variations of it depending on what we have on hand and all turned out well.  We have also made the original recipe and it was also really good.  Some variations were using onion powder in place of grated onion, olive oil in place of vegetable oil, half the oil, stevia in place of sugar, regular mustard in place of dry mustard, and omitted poppyseeds, added pepper.  It's great no matter what.  It seems like every time we go to make it we don't have everything and hand and have to substitute something.
Loved it! Used coconut oil instead of vegetable oil to add a subtle tropical flavor. Added a tablespoon of orange juice and it came out perfect. Light, healthy and flavorful.
Loved it! Very tasty and simple to make.

Fabulous!  I used Orange Muscat Champagne Vinegar from Trader Joe's, used a little more onion, and a little less olive oil.  Used on a salad of spinach, pecans, and raspberries.  I did make the mistake of halving the recipe...should have just made the whole lot of it!  Yummers!

I made this with my cooking class (5 6-8 yr olds) and it was amazing. The student that requested this recipe said it was so much better than the store-bought version she normally eats. Next time I will cut the vinegar back 1/4 and sub lemon juice and a little lemon zest-I can't wait!
It was okay, basically.  I think it needed either more sugar or less vinegar or both!
This is my favorite! I tried using olive oil instead of vegetable oil once, it was not as good.  Good stuff if you follow the recipe though.
Very good dressing. I used white wine vinegar and cut the sugar to two tablespoons sugar and two tablespoons honey.
I thought it was delicious!

Sweet and tart. I made this by hand using a wire whisk, white wine vinegar, corn oil, and powdered onion instead of fresh grated. This was fantastic on my roasted peach spinach salad. I liked the onion flavor and how easy this was to adapt to only 2 servings. Thanks Paula for a wonderful salad dressing.
This was very easy to make and tasted great.  I cut the oil in half because I like to cook light and it was fine.  I also used white wine vinegar since I was out of plain.

My favorite dressing on a fruit covered green salad with nuts (toasted Walnuts or Pecans).  A little goat cheese or feta is a nice touch as well.  Super good.  One can add more sugar if they like the dressing sweeter.  And it stores in fridge for several weeks.  Can microwave it to bring up to temperature to make it easier to pour.

Excellent-I added about 2 T more sugar after mixing just to adjust it to my personal taste but other than that followed the recipe as is. This is going to be one of my dressing staples-love that I can make it out of stuff I always have on hand.
I enjoyed this dressing very much, but am looking for a lighter version.
Quite delicious -- the best I've ever had the pleasure of making in my kitchen. Thanks for a wonderful recipe!
I found it to be far too vinegary and runny.
This was very easy to put together although I used red-wine vinegar and also onion powder instead of grated onion.  Will make again!
Very easy.  Very tasty.  I just love this recipe
I tried this recipe but it keeps separting when I put it in the frig.
Very good dressing - has a little kick to it - used on green salad.

Pretty good recipe, I just made a couple changes. I didn't put the onion in since I'm not a fan of raw onion and used regular yellow mustard instead of dry. I also used a little less vinegar and added some mayo to give it a more creamy color. Because I didn't need to process the onions I just made the dressing in a glass shaker bottle. It worked great!
Easy and delicious.  used splenda instead of sugar, dried minced onion, and half the oil and it turned out great.  will make again.

I cook for a pre-school, and the kids all loved this! I made a few changes to make it more kid-friendly. I used lemon juice instead of vinegar (I added a few tablespoons later to give it more zing). I didn't have mustard powder on hand to I used prepared yellow mustard (French's) instead. I also added 2 cloves of garlic and substituted Italian seasoning for poppy seeds. It has become a staff and student favorite!

Loved this recipe. I needed to make a salad dressing in a hurry. This was the first recipe I came to and I thought I would give it a try since I had all the ingredients on hand. Made it just as it is and my husband loved it. Most poppyseed dressings we have bought are very sweet and this one is on the slightly tangy side and not so supper sweet, which is why my husband loved it so much. I will make this again. Thanks!
Very good!  However, I used rice vinegar instead of white, and substituted regular mustard instead of dry.  It was delicious!
My families favorite Summer dressing
This salad dressing was delicious!  I made it just the way it is, everyone loved it.  My daughter asked my "mom, can you make it again"?

I did a couple changes based on other reviews and it was AWESOME.  For the vinegar, I used 1/4C white vinegar and 1/4C Cider vinegar.  Skipped the grated onion and added a half tsp of onion powder.  Blended it and it was AWESOME to supplement a prepackaged Kale Salad.  Next time I will toss their poppyseed dressing and use only this.
I have made this many times.  Tried it with homemade raspberry vinegar in place of white and used it on a spinach salad with strawberry and red onion.  Straight to yumville!
Very good recipe for fennel, rucola and carrot salad.  Thanks for sharing.
Good...but not as good as Renee's salad dressing...still looking for the winner!
I needed a little pzazz and wasn't getting it quite from the dressing so I added a small amount of Red Raspberry dressing and it was perfect!
Excellent easy sweet vinaigrette that uses ingredients I always have on hand.  I've made it with and without the poppyseeds.
Perfect for a strawberry salad!  It was a hit!
Amazing!  The only thing I did a little differently is used 1/2 olive & 1/2 veggie oil and 1/4 white wine and 1/4 white vinegar.  The best poppyseed recipe ever!
The only changes I made were I used half the salt and onion powder. It is terrific. Poured it over a salad made of romaine lettuce, strawberries, blueberries, mandarin oranges and pecans.
OMG.. Yum! My husband raved about this dressing!

Awesome and easy!  I made a spinach salad with mandarin oranges and candied pecans.  Went to reach for the pre-made poppyseed dressing (I like Kraft) and lo and behold--all gone!  Came over here and snagged this one.  EXCELLENT!  For the person who said it separated---it will!  Just shake before pouring on dressing!
Very good!  I used raspberry vinegar instead of white vinegar (highly recommend it!).  Half (or even a fourth) of this recipe is plenty.  Thanks for sharing it!
love it, so easy and flavorful~
Loved it!!

Excellent recipe! I didn't have poppy seeds so I used chia seeds, giving it a bit of a nutritional boost. They thicken it a bit too, so if you don't want it too creamy, add a bit more vinegar. The flavours are even better the next day.
I used this dressing to top a simple romaine side salad on the side of teiyaki chicken and rice. Very much like the little side salad Teriyaki restaurants serve. Delicious:)
I found the vinegar flavor very strong and will be cutting that in half and adding more oil.

This was delicious.  I, too, used it on the spinach, pecan, and peach salad.  I ate it three days in a row.  I tried decreasing the sugar content, but ended up using only a bit less than the recommended amount.  The sugar is necessary.

After trying a creamy poppyseed dressing on a strawberry spinach salad at a friend's house, I loved it so much that I had to try making my own! Although this dressing was a little different than the one I had tried, I liked it even better. Even the really picky eaters in my family liked this dressing! I used it on a strawberry, spinach, and pecan salad, and the taste was so simple, yet so yummy! I used dry minced onion in the recipe, as I wasn't quite sure what the grated onion that was called for was. Thanks for sharing, I will definitely make this again!
We love this dressing.  We use it on the Spinach, Peaches and Pecans recipe on this website and it is our favorite salad.  Because we avoid sugar, I substituted Splenda and it was marvelous.
The recipe is absolutely perfect with spinach, chicken, almonds, goat cheese and strawberries/blackberries.   I've also substituted Chia seeds for poppy seeds for a hit of protein.   Delicious.

Only tried the dressing from the grocery store before, but in my neck of the woods it's not easy getting hold of "american specialties" like poppyseed dressing in the store, this stuff did the trick, it's easy to make and tasty!

I made this dressing on the weekend with the watermelon, raspberry ,grape and spinach salad .It was excellent 
Can I rate it higher than 5 stars  ? :)
Delicious!

This is delicious I actually did not have white vinegar so I had to use a combination of apple cider and red wine vinegar, the taste was still a bit more tangy so I added about 2 more tbs of sugar. I also added a pinch of cardamom for another dimension of flavor although I tasted it before the addition and it was still quite yummy.
This was excellent. Easy to decrease the size of the recipe too -- I made it for 5 servings. Used Apple Vinegar and it was excellent. Emulsified perfectly.
I used 1/4 cup apple cider vinegar and 1/4 cup white wine vinegar (because it was what I had around) and it was wonderful.
BEST POPPY SEED DRESSING EVER! I don't grate the onion. I just throw a piece about teaspoon size and throw it in the blender with the rest. The blender does the work. Thank you for sharing!
Made this dressing tonight for our salad. I used Truvia in lieu of the sugar and it turned out great. Perfect balance of flavors for our spinach salad!
This is the best poppyseed dressing recipe I have ever made. Like a previous person stated, I too used only 1/2 of the oil and it turned out great.
Very tasty.  It had an odd color though.

Delightful, sweet, light dressing... I added an extra tbsp of sugar because I wanted it a little sweeter, and used a 1/2 tsp dijon mustard since I was out of dry mustard. also substituted white wine vinegar to add a bit more depth. wonderful!
This was the first dressing I've ever made and I was afraid but it is so good!

In a word--excellent.  Pungent is an appropriate word when describing this dressing.  I'm used to Albert's style Poppyseed dressing, a company that has it's roots in Omaha.  Albert's style is milder than this version, which is a bit wild.  Like another reviewer, I used white wine vinegar.  I highly recommend this recipe.  It's quick and easy to throw together and your family and friends will be impressed.
Made as written and loved it.  Made it for company and they loved it as well.  Served with baby spinach, strawberries and sliced almonds.

This dressing was very good on a shredded kale/brussel sprout/radicchio salad. I will make again but with some changes.  I used champagne vinegar this go round and think i'll experiment with other vinegars.  I would also use olive oil next time and a little less than recipe indicates.  Overall a good starting point and I recommend trying this one.
Very sweet and tastes exactly how I remember poppyseed dressing tasting.  Yes.  I haven't had it in a long long time!
Very good.  Husband also liked it.
This is so good my family is actually eating Kale now!

Tried it with White Wine vinegar like others suggested.  Much too vinegar-ey.  This would have been the case with white vinegar also I'm sure.  I added more sugar and a little water to make it less pungent.  Will keep looking for a copy-cat of my favorite poppyseed dressing in a bottle.

My mom's been making this since I was a little girl. It was found in a Mennonite cookbook. She gave the recipe to me and I've been making it for several years now. It's my husband's very favorite dressing and he asks for it all the time. I always have this in the frig! Thanks for posting it! :o)

I've made this dressing a few times.  We use it on fruit or green salads or for veggie dippers.  I tend to use less salt, but that's because our family uses less salt in general.  I use a mini food processor to put it all together.  It takes just a few minutes and tastes a million times better than the bottled stuff.
Excellent dressing, just enough sweetness and tartness... I wouldn't adjust a thing!
No more store bought poppy seed dressing with way too many scary sounding ingredients for me.My husband said it tasted better  than the one he got at an expensive chain restaurant the day before.

This is just the right combination of sweet and tangy.  I used prepared Beaver Hot Mustard for the dry mustard and put it on a bed of fresh spinach, strawberries, raspberries, blueberries and slivered almonds.  Nice combo!
I also used raspberry vinegar. It was delish!

I made this to the T.  I doubled the recipe to take some to a church picnic, and  to have some at home.  I used it for the peach and spinach salad on all recipes.  It was gone from the picnic. They wiped it out.  Of course fresh peaches are in season, so it looked pretty stellar on the table.  This dressing is fabulous.  I will use it for several fruit and lettuce type salads in the future.
Used Pomegranate Infused Balsamic vinegar & reduced oil to 3/4 cup.  Poured over mix of shredded cabbage and Craisins.  Nummy
I used half EV olive oil and half vegetable oil and apple cider vinegar. Delish!

Poppyseed dressings in my experience have been hit or miss. This is definitely a hit and I was happy that there was just the right amount of onion. I halved the recipe and used slightly less oil than the recipe called for as I like things a bit on the tangy side. Great recipe.

I made this for a salad I was taking to a pot luck church picnic.  My salad called for "Mango PoppySeed dressing.  I KNEW I was not going to find it in my area, so looked up this recipe. my grand kids love this sauce on there french toast and pancakes and I caught my hubby using it to after he ssaid it wasn't for him he loves it to great saucegive it a try really easy to make

YUMMY!! I NEEDED A BLUEBERRY SAUCE TO SAVE MY JELLY ROLL CAKE THAT WAS DRY!! THIS FIT THE BILL!! I DID SKIP THE ALMOND EXTRACT MY FAMILY DOESNT CARE FOR IT I JUST USED VANILLA EXCELLENT! I CANT WAITE TO TRY THIS SAUCE OVER WAFFLES NEXT SUNDAY!! THANK YOU FOR THIS WONDERFUL RECIPE!!

followed recipe as written...yum!!!

Husbands quote" wow!  This is amazing! " and my 6 year old licked his plate clean. I think it's a winner.
This was good, but I thought the almond extract flavor was too pronounced; next time I'll omit it.  Served with Cheese Blintzes recipe from this site.

I love the almond, orange, and cinnamon flavors in this! And my breakfast guests always love it, too. Great on whole wheat pancakes.   I don't add quite as much sugar as called for, though, and added a pinch of nutmeg.

This is a wonderful recipe.  I adjusted the sugar to 3/4 c. plus 2 tbsp. Splenda Sugar Blend because my husband is a diabetic.  I agree with others this taste even better the second day.  We love   blueberries and will be making this on a regular basis.

All other ingredient measurements remained the same.  I first brought the blueberries, sugar, orange juice, and water to a boil.  I then strained the juice, placed the juice back on the pot, added the water/cornstarch mixture to the pot.  I allowed the sauce to thicken.  Removed the pot from the heat, added the vanilla and cinnamon.  Next time I don't think I would add the cinnamon or I would add less cinnamon.
I love this recipe. I have many pounds of frozen berries and can them in a 10 minute hot water bath
has anyone tried to freeze this sauce with success??
This sauce is delicious for pancakes, ice cream and with a little corn starch added it make a great filling for cookies.

YUM! I changed a lot, maybe I need to make my own recipe and post it on here. Family loved this! Thanks for the idea!

I took into consideration the other reviews that said to leave the sauce for a few hours to let the flavors settle.I made it the night before and served it at room temperature the following morning with waffles and whipped cream. This sauce was absolutely amazing! I did not make any modifications. Love. Love. Love. Will definitely use again.
This was delicious and very hard to mess up.  i estimated lots of the amounts and it still tasted great on waffles =]
Awesome recipe!  I did it as written but waited an hour to eat it.  It helps it blend the flavors and it turns out exceptional!  Thanks for sharing!

This is a very simple recipe. I followed recipe as written and per reviewer suggestions let it rest for roughly 2 hours before reheating and serving over french toast and topped with whipped cream. Thanks for the recipe!
Love this sauce and it is so versatile. It's good with french toast, pancakes, waffles, and ice cream. And it is better when you make it ahead and let it chill and then reheat.

This was fantastic and easy. Added a tiny bit of freshly squeezed lemon juice and let it sit and cool for about an hour. Really really good. Can't wait to try it on some pancakes!
Very easy to make!  Will definitely use less cornstarch next time ~ it was very thick. Didn't actually taste yet as others said it was better after a day or two. Looking forward to trying it!
Yum, yum, yum! Quick and easy to make with frozen blueberries. I had to use vanilla as I had no almond extract. Loved the addition of cinnamon. Next time I'd use only two tablespoons of cornstarch.

I'm not crazy about almond, so I substituted vanilla. It was GREAT over pancakes. Next time I'll put whipped cream on top, too. MMMMmmmm!
This was pretty tasty, but I don't think the almond extract added to it.  Next time I'll try it with vanilla, or just without any extract.

Okay, I originally rated this a 4 but when I tasted it 2 days later it was amazing. Very orangy in the beginning but flavors really blended. Used frozen blueberries, strawberries, and rasberries. I have enough to feed an army right now but I will freeze and use next month for family reunion.

Soooo good! Thank you for the recipe!
Wonderful! Don't be afraid to try this. Made this morning for french toast topping....In a word, delectable.
Best the day after

Delicious! Only change I made was vanilla extract instead of almond and it was fabulous! Served on top of angel food cake for dessert! Yummy!

What a great way to make use of blueberries.  This recipe was followed exactly and great served over ice cream, waffles, pancakes, or a cheesecake.  I've even ventured to eat it solo.  Anyone else have any other serving suggestions ?

I loved it, my husband was only so-so about it.  As mentioned by others, the flavor does develop more after a day in the fridge.  I used 1/3 c. sugar and 1/3 c Splenda, and it was plenty sweet for me.  Good alternative to sugary syrups!

I have made this many times and it is wonderful!  Several times I substituted a berry mix for the blueberries and that is good too, but my favorite is with the blueberries. I get rave reviews whenever I serve it.

I bought blueberries at the Farmer's Market and tried this though halved the recipe.  It is excellent.  Had it on waffles this morning.  I will make this again and will use frozen during the winter months.

Even better with grape juice instead of orange.  I love this recipe!
Loved, loved, loved.   Used with dessert crepes perfect consistency.  Easy!

Yum yum!  I made just as written and it was delicious over blueberry pancakes. Thank you for posting this great combination of blueberries & orange juice.
Very easy, tasted great!  Used it to serve over angel food cake.
I LOVE this sauce! Had it on pancakes tonight, and my 4 yr old son loved it too. Can't wait to try it on leftovers tomorrow

FANTASTIC! I had some on my waffles and it was so great I'm making a cheesecake later this week just so I have something to eat the leftovers with!

This is delicious over pancakes or as an ice cream topping!

Awesome. Everyone loved it.

Everyone loves this! I brought it over to friends house for dessert to put on top of angel food cake. They loved it, and said we should use the rest on top of vanilla ice cream!

Oh My Goodness! This was amazing! We had it on top of waffles!  Definatley a keeper! Thanks so much!

Decreased to 4 servings and made as is. great taste but I did add some more water because the sauce got too thick for me. Served with "Whole Grain Waffles." Next time, I would like to try them on pancakes.

This recipe is fantastic! I read the other reviews and did make a few changes. I used 1/2 cup OJ and the rest water to perserve the taste of the fresh blueberries. I did not add the almond extract.
