I just made 18 oz of this to try it before busting out 9 pints and it is the most delicious recipe I have EVER made from this site. We tried some Hot Pepper Mustard we bought in a store in Helen, GA over the weekend and we ran out in a day with Ham Sandwiches, Pretzels, and Brats.. I used Half a Jar of Hot pepper rings and a few Jalapenos instead of slicing myself. Also, I too had a problem with the flour water ratio but stirred until my arm almost fell off and they were barely noticeable. FANTASTIC!! Gonna make a larger batch this weekend.

I labeled my jars as Jalapeño Honey Mustard because though it is hot, it is sweet.  Per another reviewer's suggestion, I mixed it to taste with sour cream.  This mixture is great for making tuna fish salad.

My pepper plant gave off almost 200 peppers this year.  The type of pepper is "longhorn".  Some are super hot and some aren't.  Even so, I used almost 50 peppers, seeds and all, for the recipe.  I also decreased the sugar by about a cup.  Additionally, I used .75 cups "clear gel" instead of flour since it's an approved thickener for canning (flour isn't). I was feeling pretty paranoid about using the flour but I know a lot of people use it without a problem.  Clear Gel can be found on Amazon. The recipe has been a huge hit with my friends.  I highly recommend it!!!

Found a great price on banana peppers at a  local produce market, so I decided to give this a try and use as give-aways to friends and family.  As recommended by another reviewer, I added a couple red mini bell peppers which gave the mustard just a bit of color (with no effect on flavor).  I bought the inexpensive store brand of mustard which made this even more affordable.  Made half a recipe, used 4-oz canning jars, and ended up with a lot of nice little homemade gifts.  This will be a nice change from the traditional jams and preserves that we all give away so often.  This should be absolutely delicious with one of the soft pretzel recipes on AR. UPDATE 4.12.12  Mixed this into some sour cream and served over freshly-steamed asparagus last night, and it was delicious.  Also, mixed some of the mustard into mayonnaise for a really nice potato salad dressing.

I have made this a couple of times and along the way adjusted the sugars to my own taste.  My friends & family beg for more when their jar is empty !! The only thing I do differently is I let the mixture cool before adding the flour/water mixture and then heat it back up to thicken. I did this because I could not keep it from lumping when the mixture was at it's hottest.  My way comes at smooth as can be !!!

I've made this recipe for 2 summers now and let me tell you, I can't keep enough around to enjoy myself!  I now have friends asking me when I will be making it again.  I adjusted the recipe a bit by cutting out the sugar altogether and using Splenda Blend instead so a diabetic friend could try it. The back of the bag says if a recipe calls for 1 cup of sugar, use 1/2 cup of Splenda Blend.  I cut the amount of sugar down to 4 cups in the original recipe so I use 2 cups of the Splenda Blend when making a full recipe and it is perfect, with just enough sweetness. And I have also thrown in whatever kind of hot peppers we have on hand, even habaneros which gave the mustard a good kick.  Last year when I made this was my first attempt at canning too and now you can't stop me!  I just canned 6 half-pints of hot pepper relish yesterday!

Can I just say, "yum" ?  I cut this recipe by 4 to use the peppers I was able to get off my one plant.  Next year I'm planting 10 plants and gifting jars of this.  Didn't change a thing, though next time I may cut the sugar slightly.  Eating it with pretzels and find it to be absolutely delicious.  Did have some problems getting the flour smooth and I also don't have a food processor or blender so my banana peppers are just very finely chopped.  Still super good.  WILL MAKE AGAIN.
Great taste used less flour 2nd time had no lumps that way

I'm on my second batch this week......The first batch went so fast I don't know what happened.  I'm doubling the next batch, processing it in half-pint jars then decorating the jars and giving it to our "adult" trick-or-treaters!
This tastes wonderful but most defiantly not as easy as it sounds
Really great, easy recipe for gift giving. My family loves it as a snack.

Excellent recipe...thanks! Followed recipe and had no issue. I did use a hand blender before hot water processing to make sure all lumps out as other users had said lumps had occurred but really did not see a problem with that. Loving this recipe!

excellent!  we used it as a pretzel dip and on ham sandwiches.  definitely puts use to the peppers coming out of our garden!  i'm going to be making this recipe with some hotter peppers next time for those that think they can handle it!
I got this same recipe from my nana. We give it as presents. The boys eat it in everything. They use it as chip dip, on hotdogs and hamburgers, with pretzels, everything.

ok so i just made this entire recipe in my blender! i needed a quick pretzel dip and came across this. i used all the ingredients listed but didnt cook it cause i was going to use it right away. delicious! the only thing i did differently was added a handful of jalapenos i still had in the garden.

All in all, a success. Made this yesterday for Christmas gifts. My peppers were on average, longer than 5 inches so I ended up with more than the recipe says so I started filling up whatever mason jars I could find. Generally, banana peppers aren't terribly hot so I didn't bother with gloves when I was cleaning and prepping the peppers. When I started food processing the peppers, however, I started having a very intense reaction - sneezing and couldn't have my face near the chopped peppers without a face mask. Then after finishing, when my hands felt on fire, I realized I had what felt like a chemical burn on my hands. I never knew before yesterday that capsaicin burn was even a thing. It still hurts the next day when I put pressure on them or get them wet. So if you end up with a batch of super hot peppers like we did, wear gloves and perhaps be prepared for some consequences. The mustard is pretty good - but quite spicy. I would have preferred to use a more mild batch of peppers.

Way too sweet for me. I followed the recipe as written but if I made this again I would cut the sugar by at least half and maybe even add a dash of hot sauce. The sweetness totally overwhelmed the spiciness.
Everyone loves this. My daughter's boyfriend go through so much of this that she claims he drinks it through a straw, lol.
Very good.  Next time, I will add less sugar and maybe a habanero or two to kick up the heat a bit.

I canned several pints for my neighbors using hot banana peppers, 3 jalapenos 2 with seeds, re-pureed ALOT in my blender after cooking, and added a red pepper for color as suggested. The reviews are in and my neighbors are RAVING! I even subbed the sugar for equal...but no one needs to know that:) My buddys bringing me another 10lbs of peppers in return for a few more jars. My most successful canning recipe yet, thank you so much for it!!!!

Very good, husband loved it better then gourmet mustard be buy.  I did use a mix of 5 different peppers because we like more heat! In addition to the banana peppers, I used a chili pepper, Hungarian wax pepper, jalapeño pepper and a habanero pepper. A definite keeper! Thanks for sharing !
This recipe is delicious and very flexible. I have used a variety of peppers and it has turned out great every time. I have had problems with lumps of the thickening developing.

The first batch my wonderful husband and me made was going good until we added the flour/water, which turned into dumplings.  The second time we mixed the flour with cold water and slowly added it as he vigorously wisked it for me.  The second batch we also substituted some brown sugar for white.  It turned out great.

Can I just say.....LOVE IT!!! I see some mentioned the flour not blending in. I added a little at a time, wisked it in, and then added more. That seemed to help with the blending. Great recipie, thanks!!
Great recipe! Tastes great and is easy to make!

All in all, a good and easy to make recipe. 

I did a half batch.  I used a variety of different peppers that I foraged from my friends garden and added some Sriracha because I didn't find it spicy enough. I would have left some of the jalapeno ribs in had I known, but c'est la vie. In the future I think I would cut back on the amount of sugar as others had noted and I wish I had taken this advice initially. 

I also agree about the flour: make sure you add hot water and some of the cooking liquid into it to make a nice smooth paste. I found mine to be a bit more lumpy than I had wanted, so I threw it into the blender to smooth it out. 

Enjoy!

My friend and I made 3 (1/2 batches) of this recipe, with modifications to the last 2 just to experiment. All are wonderful but the favorite hands down was our 3rd half batch. Here are our modifications: 10 banana peppers we processed until smoothish while the other 10 we coarse chopped, along with 1 jalapeno, and 1 red bell pepper, 1 cup white sugar, 1 cup brown sugar, and 1 cup honey, also in this batch we used 6 TBL corn starch and 3/4 cup water instead of the flour and water. The rest of the ingredients are the same as the recipe (by half of course, since we were making 1/2 batches) We like the smoothness and lightness that the corn starch gave the recipe and the coarse chopped peppers give it a pretty look.

I have not tried this recipe yet, but will be.  However, in reading over the reviews I am seeing that ALOT of people have no idea how to make a thickener even for basic gravy apparently!  Put your flour and water mixture in a gravy shaker (Pampered Chef or any other cheaper brand even) and shake till the mix is smooth.  There will be no lumps!!!  Or you can whisk vigorously in a jar or small bowl for the same results.  NO NEED TO ADD MORE WATER TO THIS RECIPE!  I am rating this 5 because I am quite sure I will like it (and because you can't post anything on here without clicking the stars!)

Delicious.  If you are a beginner, make a half recipe the first time.  To avoid lumps, use warm water to stir into the flour, and also add some of the hot liquid to the flour mixture before stirring into the mustard mixture. I use sweet banana peppers for the most part, with only a few hot thrown in...we like it low heat mixed with sweet.

I left all seeds in the peppers for some heat. Overall it turned out better than expected. i use it on hot dogs, hamburgers, and as chip dip. I would say if you like franks red hot you could tolerate the taste of leaving the seeds in.

I've just finished a half batch of this mustard.  I've taken a star off for the flour/water ratio...you absolutely need more water than flour in order to get a smooth mixture to stir into the hot liquid.  I ended up putting the ugly glob in my food processor and added half again as much water.  
Another thing, the food processor wasn't making a smooth enough job of the peppers on their own so I added in some of the sugar and mustard and that really made a much better job of it.  Even though it's still hot, the taste is pretty darned good.  I might add just a bit more sugar next time but I'll wait until I taste the cooled product before making that decision. By the way, a half recipe made exactly 6 pints of mustard.

I've made this several times so far.  My banana peppers must be very mild because my first two batches ended up basically (delicious) sweet mustard.  Third batch I added a few Jalapenos, it ended up a little hotter, but not much.  Have a batch on the stove now using about half and half  Banana peppers and Jalapenos, all with their seeds.  Hoping it will take it to the level I want it.  As for a couple problems others have had, use some of the vinegar in the blender when processing the peppers, works great!  For the clumping flour problem, do the same thing, adding some of the mustard mix with the flour and water (and I use a little more water).  It is then a better temp to add to the rest.  If you still have clumps,  just put it all through the blender (after cooling some), re-heat it and finish.  I also cut the sugar by half.

Well, after reading many of the reviews I had to just try this for myself.  I took all the suggestions from everyone, and also purchased at the Farmers Market sweet and spicy banana peppers.  I made 1/2 a batch  thinking that I have nothing to loose if it didn't turn out.  
I added 4 Jalapeño peppers, 4 cloves of garlic, 1 red pepper, half reg sugar and half brown sugar.  When I did add the flour, it still clumped on me, but I used my sauce small blender in the pot and it was all good.  
This turned out to be the best mustard and I am looking forward to making more this coming weekend- foot ball season is around the corner and I can't wait to serve it up- thank you to everyone and all their suggestions. !!
AWESOME & easy.
Loved it, fixed it exactly as stated but tempered the flour water mixture. Next time I would cut back on the sugar a little maybe by a cup.

A honey mustard with a zesty semi spicy finish. I cut recipe in 1/4 and added a baby jalapeno (1") and 2 salsa peppers (still green), removing all seeds. Delish!! My daughter claims it's the very best mustard she has ever tasted! Can't wait to give some to friends, if it lasts that long!
This is absolutely amazing!  Don't change a thing

I don't think I've ever had so many compliments from something I've made.  Back on here today to copy the recipe for someone a whole state away!  I had more compliments when I added extra jalepenos the second go round.

I made this last night, and let me tell you, it is absolutely amazing!  I had no trouble with any lumps, clumps or any other issues. I have already shared several jars and they want to buy some from me! The thing about this you can kick it up if you want or have it mild, your choice.  I would not change a thing!  Thanks peachypie for sharing this wonderful recipe!

Great recipe!  I did make changes for dietary purposes (gluten free and sugar free household).

I used 4 cups of Sucralose (TM Splenda) in place of the sugar to minimize the glycemic impact.  I also substituted a 1/2 cup of cornstarch in place of flour because we are a gluten-free household.  Finally, I used two cups of agave nectar in place of the honey (again, the glycemic index factor) and one of the cups of sugar.  I heated the agave nectar up and mixed the cornstarch into it before  pouring it into the pot, thus eliminating the cup of water.  
 
It was a little sweet to me - I'd prefer more of a bite of pepper/mustard - but the rest of my family and friends like it the way it is.  In the future, I'd probably cut out some of the sucralose.  Considering it was my first time making this recipe and making the dietary modifications on the fly and people really like it as it is, I'll call it a success.

Delicious! Doubled the recipe for the whole family and it was a hit. Love it. I did add a bit more spices than what was called for.

Made it exactly like the recipe was given. Have never had spaghetti squash before so it was a trip cooking it. That being said We Loved it.  My brother said this was a keeper.. Just wish the nutritional info was available.

I put olive oil on the squash before cooking it. Family LOVED it. Also used turkey Italian sausage.

My wife loved this.  I used quartered grape tomatoes instead of slicing a regular tomato as I think they hold up a little better during cooking. I misjudged the squash and over cooked it so the texture was a little soft but the flavor was fine.  I will definitely make this again.
Everyone loved it! We have made it a couple of times now. Next time, I'm going to add some black sliced olives on top.

Have made this twice. Changed up some of the veggies will make again. Hubby love this one

Made this delicious recipe as written with the exceptions of cooking the spaghetti squash in the microwave for 12 minutes and I adding a few sliced green olives at the end when heating the entire dish. This is my go-to dinner for when I want something that tastes fresh, is easy to make, and will be just as good a day or so later. I use seasoned chicken/turkey sausage and an additional zucchini. Makes great leftovers, hot or cold!

10.11.16   I used garlic naan bread, mild Italian sausage, and my homemade marinara sauce.  I must say that the ricotta in the cheese base really does make this taste a bit like lasagna. Delicious! And pink - perfect for girl's night!

Perfect cocktail  for our Cinco de Mayo dinner!  Made exactly as written with a little less tequila . Nothing but fresh ingredients. So much better than the mix in a bottle!

Fantastic margarita! I was initially put off by the amount of sugar but you don't pour all of it. Excellent drink!  Just follow the recipe exactly, and you won't be sorry!  Thanks, BloodyGerry!
I love a good margarita and this is the best I have ever made. Used recipe just as written. Perfection!

Loved this AFTER my change of 3 oz tequila toned down to 2 oz. Everything else I followed exactly as described. I too have been looking for the right balance of tart and smooth and am especially glad to get away from the store mix. This is my keeper margarita recipe for sure!

OK, I'm giving two stars for the ingredients EXCEPT for the tequila choice.  Jose Cuervo Gold??  Really?  Invest in something just a tiny bit more expensive and get 100% agave tequila.  Jose Cuervo Gold is NOT top shelf tequila.
I've had my share of margaritas but this is my favorite.

I have been making this recipe for the past several years and it remains the most requested breakfast dish whenever family or friends are coming over.  Actually, they request it and invite themselves over, but regardless...it's everybody's favorite. Even the pickiest of eaters never complain

The only changes I make are using butter instead of margarine, whole milk instead of skimmed and I use multi- grain French bread.
I love fixing this on weekends, and since I fix it the night before I can sleep in! My kids (4 and 6) love this; my husband and I both love bread pudding, so we like the consistency

It was great and a big hit at my party.  It turns into more of a sweet bread pudding which was great.  I actually made challah bread instead of using store bought french bread and it added an extra special and extra tasty element.
Made it exactly as written.  Coworkers loved it.  3 people asked for recipe.

I made this recipie for my daughters slumber party.  I was very busy with the girls and forgot to make it the night before.  I assembled it a couple of hours before breakfast.  Then baked it.  It turned out great.  The girls loved it.  I did not make the sauce, I was too tired...I just used maple syrup.  It did stick to the pan, next time I will spray it.

I made a half recipe, subbing a handful of raisins for one apple.  Put the raisins under the apple slices to keep them from burning. I also cut back on the sugar by about half, and it was still sweet enough without the sauce. For French toast, I would cut the sugar and sauce out completely and serve with syrup. As it is, it makes a lovely bread pudding: dessert, not breakfast.

Made as directed.  I was weary of the caramel sauce.  I thought it would be too sticky sweet.  But the sauce was really good!  The dish was much better with the caramel sauce vs. maple syrup.  Next time I will try using large cubes of french bread and tossing the apples in the spice/sugar mix before topping so that all of the apples get some of the spice/sugar. Kids really didn't care for this. Also, the toast stuck to the bottom on the dish. Won't be having this too often.
Yummy but very sweet!

I took it to a bridal shower and it was gone pretty fast.
Excellent! I will make again for sure!

This was easy and good... I used whole wheat french bread, it gave it a nuttier taste, went well with the apples.  You could easily change out the fruit to pears, or pineapple and change the sauce up a bit.  We loved it... easy and it tasted great!

This recipe was great, even with the changes I made . . . didn't have any apples and also halved the quantity, but still delicious! My mother-in-law even went back for seconds, so it must be good! It's a keeper!

This recipe was ok.  I do love breakfast recipes with apples, andI've made several others that I prefer.  For those of you that have not made this recipe, let me offer a few suggestions.  The apples do taste great, but I expected them to end up more like pie filling.  They were spiced apples on top of french toast.  The caramel sauce is delicious, but it is just that, caramel sauce.  If you do not want a caramel sauce on your french toast, syrup works just as well. The directions for making the sauce are vague.  Cook on medium until it starts to boil, then put on medium-low and let simmer until it thickens. Also, check the bottom of your french toast after about 45 minutes.  I cooked mine almost an hour and the bottom did not stick to the pan, but it was overcooked.  I did like the taste of the french toast without the apples, but the combination of the apples, toast and caramel sauce was a little much for our family.  It may work well for others though.
The recipe was not at all what I expected.  The apples did not get soft and it was more like a bread pudding than french toast.
Terrific even without the apples.  Just to save time - after it's done baking, I drizzle it with melted butter and syrup!  It's now a family staple!

Loved this recipe for a extra special breakfast treat.  I used about 1/2 of a large Italian bread loaf since that was what I had, and butter for the caramel sauce. Also, I only had about 1 1/2 apples, though I would've liked a bit more, I can't imagine using 6.  Really enjoyed this recipe and it paired deliciously with trader joes smoked Apple Chardonnay chicken sausage!

I really liked these, and they were a big hit at our Thanksgiving party last week, but I plan on making a few changes next time.  I'll probably slice half of the apples into rings, and the other half into cubes.  I'll toss the apples with the spices instead sprinkling them too.  Then, instead of slicing the baguette into 1 1/2 inch slices, I'll probably slice them a lot thinner to make two layers of bread that I can sandwich the apple-rings between and then top with the cubes.  I'm still thinking of a way to make this more like fried french-toast instead of bread-pudding.
Huge hit with all the whole family this Christmas Day!!!!
Delicious! The sauce really does pull it all together.  My husband, who is not a big fan of apples, still loved this recipe.

so easy and delicious!  I substituted 1/2 c. whipping cream for part of the milk.  not as healthy i know but yummy!  I loved that I could make it after my daughter went to sleep.  Then just pop it in the oven the next morning, while we got ready for the brunch.

This is Wonderful!  Got this recipe from a co-worker to make Christmas morning. She often brings it for staff functions. The base bread and egg mixture look to be very versatile. We will be trying different fruit toppings like apples with nuts or raisins; bananas and strawberries; and blueberries, all with less or different sauce.
I made this for a baby shower brunch.  It was a huge hit!  The sauce was better than syrup.

Overall, I would say this is a good recipe.  Like others, even with buttering the pan beforehand, it did stick a bit to the bottom.  I made half of the recipe and used a 9x9 glass dish.  I also sliced up some whole wheat baguettes which worked well.  Didn't come out soggy and the caramel sauce was much easier to make than I expected.  I used Golden Delicious apples and it wasn't too sweet.  I will try it again with different types of bread.

I brought this to a family brunch.  It was a big hit. I made it as stated in the recipe, except only used 2 apples.  I spooned the delicious caramel sauce over the top before serving.   Had requests for the recipe and I will be making this again.
This was very good! I made it for my daughter and her friend who stayed the night.  It was very easy to make.  I would not skimp on the apples.

I enjoied this however it was more like Bread pudding than french toast.
I did make it with sugar twin on the bread adn served the apples on the side, since my Mother-in-law is a diabetic.

My family LOVED this. I did it exactly as the directions said. The caramel sauce was incredible!
This was delicious! I substituted canned apples to shorten the prep time. The sauce is AMAZING! DO NOT LEAVE IT OUT!

This is the best baked french toast recipe I've tried yet.  Maybe since I used Challah bread, mine was a bit drier and less like bread pudding (which I preferred).  Too often I've ended up with a soggy bread, eggy mess.  This actaully looked like french toast slices I had cooked in a pan.  When I poured on the egg mixture the bread immediately soaked it up (and there were a few dry spots so I even added a couple more eggs) maybe that is the secret.  I didn't do the apples (but will certainly try that) since I was also serving a crockpot oatmeal with apples and raisins.  Instead, after baking, I arragned the slices on a platter, topped with fresh sliced bananas, and then drizzled the caramel sauce over them - delish!!! and quite an impressive presentation, too. You could even add walnuts or pecans!

Outstanding!! Everyone loved it and I loved the sliced apples on top. I sliced up french bread before it got too hard and froze in a ziploc bag. Then I just pulled out the slices and made this recipe as is, except I did add one extra egg. The pan fed 5 and would likely have fed 6, but not 12. I made the yummy caramel sauce (and also added chopped walnuts on top), but I think maple syrup sounds like a great alternative as well. I used whole milk and some leftover cream, but will go lowfat next time with 1% milk. 3 apples is plenty  on top. Wonderful for serving guests. Thanks for sharing, I will definitely make this one again!

Made exactly as directed and did not care for at all. My husband liked the super sweet sauce ok, but the french toast itself was not to our liking.  He ate 1 piece, I ate 1/2 piece.

I mixed the cinnamon/nutmeg/sugar together then tossed in the apples so everything would be coated.  I then placed the apples on top of the bread and let it sit over night. My kids are still young enough that they won't try anything like this, but it's beautiful to look at and taste. Thanks!
This was so good. The sauce was very tasty. I would just make the sauce and serve it over ice cream. I made this Hawaiian Bread II, and it was a good choice.

I am NOT a good cook by any means, but this recipe turned out DELICIOUS! I found it was very easy to make, even though you had to prepare the night before.

This french toast is a combination of rich french toast and delicious baked apple ~ covered in a deliciously light carmel sauce.  It tastes as good as it smells.  I double the ingredients and enjoy the meal twice!  Everyone in the family loved it!
Very sweet, but truly yummy.  It worked for me without marinating the bread overnight.

ABSOLUTELY loved this recipe!! I had to adapt it for a gluten free diet and made the following changes : Lined the bottom of a greased 9x13 inch pan with Udi's whole grain GF bread. Mixed 4 eggs, 1/2 cup milk, 1 tsp cinnamon, 1 tsp vanilla, and 1/3 cup sugar.  Pour over the bread.  I let it sit for about 30 minutes then flipped the bread over.  I used canned apples slices (I sliced them a little to make them thinner and to make them go farther), and placed them on the bread.  I sprinkled with coarsely chopped pecans and brown sugar.  I refrigerated over night. In the morning I put the glass pan in a COLD oven at 400 degrees.  I baked for 40 minutes.  It REALLY crisped up nicely! I warmed up some store bought caramel sausce and drizzled over each piece when serving.  This was so amzingly good!!!
I did not care for this recipe, half the bread was to dry the other half to soggy. The caramel topping was thick.  Will not make again.

I did not make the caramel sauce, though I'm sure it would be amazing too. I just topped it with maple syrup. So yummy!

I made this for a group of family members and they all enjoyed it.  I used buttermilk bread from Trader Joes and broke it up in 1-2" square pieces.  mixed the bread in the bowl with the batter until saturated then poured it all into the casserole dish.  I baked 40 minutes covered with foil and 20 minutes without.  The top was toasted and the bottom was like pudding.  It was delicious.  I didn't have time to make the sauce and only had one apple around the house.  I would prefer a little more sweetness but perhaps if I had more apples and made the sauce it would be 5 stars.  I really liked the moistness and texture.

I made this recipe once for a work putluck breakfast, since I could make it the night before and just bake it while getting ready in the morning.  Well, once was all it took and I have not been able to make anything else for all potlucks after that.  This is so delicious for for a group breakfast or brunch.  I have even out it together and wrapped it up for my brother's family for Christmas morning breakfast.  They just popped it in the oven while opening presents and reheated the sauce.    Over the years of making this, I have discovered a few tips that I now use.  I bake it for at least an hour and 15 minutes.  I like a drier french toast and this seems to gift it the golden brown the recipe calls for.  I use Granny Smith apples.  The tartness with the sweetness of the sauce helps balance the flavor.  Also, to slice the apples, if you have a mandolin or easy slicer, it goes so much faster and then you don't have to peel or core the apples.  To lighten it up, I always use egg substitute.  Even the harshest critics will never know the difference.  Will continue to make this recipe for years to come.  PS.This recipe title should be "Caramel Apple Baked French Toast" much more true to the dish.
My family loved this recipe. It was very simple to make but very YUMMY!!

T made this for Christmas Breakfast, and it was AMAZING!  I will be more inclined to make for dessert in the future; tasting more like Bread Pudding than French Toast.  I will double the cinnamon and vanilla, and add toasted Pecans.  Still a 5 star just the way it is!
oops, I rated the wrong recipe. I haven't tried this one yet. :) looks yummy!

I made that the night before to, then just heated in the microwave the next morning and topped the toast.  I also used a can of apple pie filling instead of peeling and cutting apples- worked very well.  Will make again, thanks!
I made this for Christmas morning. The bread was soggy on the bottom and too crunchy on the top.  The flavours were good, but I don't think I'd make it again.

Delicious!  Halved the brown sugar as suggested and was a hit!  Will try with other seasonal fruit.

Not too good, I'm afraid.  Nothing like French Toast.
This was one of the "best" recipes I have ever made.  It was a sure hit at a family breakfast get together.

This is so good! I used Texas toast instead of french bread and I cut the bread into big chunks and mixed the apples in with the bread instead of just adding them on top. Loved the caramel sauce as well. I will make again.

I thought this was great!  Would make it again. I didn't have time to refrigerate it overnight.  So, put it in the refrigerator for 1 hour. Also, cut pieces of bread into small chunks instead of slices.  Worked out great.
this is rich and yummy!
Great recipe, 2nd time around I decreased sauce , since there was way too much left over.

Absolutely DELICIOUS! I wanted it be richer so I used 1/2 cup heavy cream and 1  cup of milk. I also used whole milk in the sauce. Since I was making it for guests, no worries about calories but next time I will use only skim milk. The entire dish disappeared real quick! A keeper!
This is a great recipe that I have made several times over the years.The apples should be sliced thin and the bread should not be fresh or it will get mushy.
I fixed this for our family for Christmas breakfast and it was a hit!  So easy and so good!

I made this for breakfast on Fri. and let me say OMG!  I didn't let it set over night but regardless it came out so yummy! I'll be making it again and again and again!  The sauce that went on top was just amazing! Highly recommended!
I serve this with homemade hot vanilla pudding as well as the sauce.
Yum!  I am not a great cook, but I followed the instructions and got rave reviews!  Thanks for a great, simple, yummy recipe!  The leftovers are even good re-heated.
I've made it twice. Fantastic, easy and huge hit!! It's the new favorite holiday go to breakfast!
I made this recipe at fishing camp for some friends, they loved it. I will make this more often.
I just served this to a large group and my guest loved it!  It was the hit of my brunch.  The carmel sauce maked this dish very special

I made this for Saturday breakfast for my family and everyone loved it!!!! My husband is already asking when I'm going to make it again. I made it just how the recipe called except I used whole milk. Since i prepared it the night before it was super easy and the sauce really did pull it all together.
This is a very good french toast bake. I even like the simple caramel recipe. I have made it with out the apples also and it is still very good.

Absolutely delicious!  I sprayed the bottom with Pam and it still stuck!  However the taste is worth the mess you are left with.  I added chopped pecans to the top and the caramel sauce is worth the extra effort.
As Ned Flanders would say Scrump-diddily-umptious!!!1
I love this recipe and have used it to feed 50 people.  They love it.  It's easy and the syrup is divine!

I made this for dessert (with vanilla ice cream) and it was a big hit.  Used the recipe as directed, but I only refrigerated it for 3 hours before baking.  I wasn't sure whether it should be baked covered or uncovered, so I left if covered with aluminum foil for 35 minutes, and baked uncovered for the last 25.  That worked well.  Also appreciated the tip about boiling the caramel sauce then reducing the heat.  Thanks for sharing!

I made this last night for breakfast today and it was like dessert for brealfast. My husband blurted out after his first bite..."Wow! This doesn't suck!" I got a good giggle and a decadent french toast to start my day!

Though you must prepare this the night before, it is such a sweet delight. I actually gave some to my friends and they had smiles on their faces the next time I saw them wanting more. Wonderful!!! Thanks!
These are soooo yummy! I followed the recipe exactly and all 3 of my toddlers LOVED these muffins! Even my husband raved about them, thank you. :)

My 1 year old LOVES these muffins. I bake them as mini muffins and he eats 3 to 4 at a sitting. When he's teething, they provide great relief when they are frozen. To help increase his protein intake, I've substituted a jar of turkey and vegetables baby food for the squash - I couldn't even tell the difference! Going to try with a jar of chicken and broth and see what happens.

Followed the recipe as is (HATE it when I read reviews of things people added, deleted or changed!  Its not the same recipe so they shouldn't review it...I digress...).  My 18 month old is SUPER picky and I'm so happy he likes these muffins.  Sneaky way to get in some veggies!  Even I like them and I hate squash and carrots!  Might try it with organic sweet potato baby food instead of the squash next time.

this was great! i did change somethings due to ingredients i had. i used 1/4 coconut oil instead of the butter and i used grated zucchini instead of the baby squash. used WWflour and halved the oat bran with flaxseed. added baking powder and vanilla. there were out of the oven 10 minutes ago and they are almost gone!! ill be making these often!! thanks!

Great recipe!  I used ground flax instead of  oat bran because its what I had on hand, and used 1/4 cup instead of 1/2.   Very moist, and my two year old and I really like them.   My husband says they don't have a lot of flavor though.  I would have given five stars except for his comment.

I made this twice and it turned out great each time. The only thing I changed was I used oatmeal instead of oat bran because I didn't have any. (Oh, and the second time I used part oatmeal, part flax seed, but I think I liked the plain oatmeal better.) The first time, I used paper cupcake liners, but that didn't work very well because the bottom of the muffins came out too soggy. The next time I just greased the muffin tin with great results. I think you could definitely cut down on the sugar, especially if your bananas are ripe. I froze the second batch of these, and they freeze and reheat great. Perfect for a quick morning breakfast.

These muffins are great!  I added 1 tsp. of vanilla and 1 tsp. of baking powder as I noticed others suggesting in previous reviews.  I cannot believe how awesome these are!  My picky toddler will love them!  Thanks for posting this recipe!
OMG

Ehhh...I tried this recipe only substituting canned pumpkin for the squash. The mini muffins didn't really have any flavor. The butter and banana were really the only things I could taste, and even then still kind of bland. 

For fun, I tried a second batch using 1/2 c. applesauce instead of butter, 1/2c. turbinado sugar instead of brown sugar, still used canned pumpkin, 2 T. flaxseed meal, and did half the batch with craisins and half without. Thought the ones without craisins were just as bland and the ones with craisins were overpowered by the craisins. 

So, this recipe is not a keeper for me. I really like the morning glory muffins from this website. Some similar ingredients and I like the way they taste.

Substituted oatmeal for oat bran and grated a whole small zucchini in place of baby food. Turned out well and made 24 mini muffins, and 6 small regular muffins! My 2 year old announced "cake!" And ate one right away!
Made recipe as is, they turned out greasy from too much butter.

These are amazing!! A few changes due to what I had on hand; mixed veggies instead of squash baby food, used oats instead of oat bran, and added some raisins. They are so yummy and all those veggies in there makes me feel good about giving a second one to my 3 year old. She is quite picky and ate them up.  I was even thinking adding a cream cheese frosting and sprinkles to this for a birthday treat or holiday treat. Great recipe! Thank you Lori!

I went by the recipe exactly, and these turned out really well. Sort of a cross between pumpkin and banana bread. Can't taste the veggies at all. My cooking time was more like 10-12 minutes for the mini muffin pan... and it made closer to 42 mini muffins rather than 24. (Score!) I will for sure be making these again.

Just made these as we have a potlach at daycare tomorrow - substituted canned baby blueberry dessert (blueberries and some brown suger) for the squash. They turned out delicious - moist & tasty! I think the kiddos will love them!!
Delicious.  Kids loved them.

My two year old granddaughter and I have made these twice.  She is an extremely fussy eater and LOVES these.  It might be that I let her help me mix them, but she asks for more!!!  Incredible!  I admit to using quinoa instead of bran and squashed fresh peach instead of squash.  Great recipe!

These were moist and fluffy -- but too salty for my liking.  I think the salt could easily be halved in this recipe.  I used 6oz of pureed squash and about a cup of chopped steamed carrots (I was using up our existing stash of freezer baby food) with mashed bananas.  Baby boy was interested for a few minutes, so that's always a win.
My year old daughter absolutely loves these.
Turned out great!!!

I found this recipe and promptly went to the kitchen. My 11month old has become a picky eater already (though I don't blame him being sick of "baby mush"). The only thing he will consume is smoothies, and I really wanted him to eat something "solid" again. These yummy muffins, which yielded 3 dozen mini muffins for me, did the trick! I didn't have any squash, so I substituted a 128ml packet of HEINZ baby food in "pear green bean mango" flavor in order to still pack in the veggie matter. I also had no oat bran, so replaced that with toasted milled flax. They still turned out delicious and moist. Thank you for sharing!

Pretty tasty and I feel great about cutting small pieces of this to give to my 10 month old as he's eating finger foods! A side note, this recipe made 48 mini muffins for me, not 24 like the recipe says.  Oh well - more for the freezer!
These were muffins were delicious . I followed the recipe and they great! Thanks
So good! Everyone loved them and could feel good about munching them down quickly. I even made a bread loaf out of it.. but cooked it for about 50-55 minutes. Yumm!

Fantastic recipe!
I have made these over and over again for my 1 year-old.  My older kids love them too.  They are terrific without any changes, but I have substituted many times according to what I had on hand, and they always turn out perfectly.  A few subs I've made: for the bananas/squash/carrots- any equivalent quantity of boiled and mashed carrots/butternut squash, for the oat bran- wheat bran.

These are so good! I just made a batch for our road trip tomorrow. The baby is asleep and my husband and I just scarfed down three of these lol. I tried another kid-friendly muffin on this site and it was way too sweet and greasy. But these were awesome! Thanks for a great recipe for my little one (and me)!

I added cocoa powder, a handful of chocolate chips, some agave syrup, only one banana, 1 container of babyhood squash, 1 container of babyhood green veggies, and 1/3c of ground carrots and spinach and it really tasted good.  If it is at all bland, I dab a bit of butter on the warm muffin and everyone eats them up. Next time I will try pumpkin and/or peanut butter as well as a ton of veggies.

I was quite impressed on how good they were and it has become our regular afternoon snack.One of my picky, picky eaters said he LOVED them. He does not noramly say that about my cooking. So Thank You. :)

I made this recipe for my very picky toddler and she loves them. She thinks they are cupcakes and eats them easily, licking her fingers even. Note that they are very soft when they come out of the oven (may be different if using oat bran, I only had wheat bran on hand and used that) and taste the best if kept in the refrigerator and eaten the next day.

Everyone in my house from hubby, 15 year old, to 11 month old gave these a thumbs up! I used wheat bran in place of oat bran and pureed baby sweet potatoes in place of the squash since that's what I had and otherwise followed recipe exactly. These are awesome! My husband, son, and I almost ate half of these fresh out of the oven... oops. I put half of what was left in the freezer, and saved the rest out for everyone to enjoy. My daughter ate one of these up with her dinner and really seemed to enjoy it!
Amazing! only thing I changed was less brown sugar and oatmeal because I couldn't find out bran. Kids and adults alike loved these.
Pretty tasty, even for grownups.  Nice texture, too.  I added more spice, as I do with most muffin or other recipes, especially when they are healthy and relatively low sugar.
My one year old daughter loved them! I cut the recipe in half because I used a mini muffin pan and it was the perfect amount. I will definitely be making these again.
These muffins are absolutely delicious and so healthy for adults and kiddos. My son loves these!
These were easy to make and a quick breakfast choice.  It is also a great base recipe to play with other vegetable and fruit choices.
Oh my gracious!  You should call this something else so Everyone will want to try it!  It's too good just to give to little ones only!  Thanks for the recipe!

My 14-month-old loves these! I used muffin cups, which was a bit of a mistake since the muffins don't have enough fat in them to peel off of the paper. I also substituted a container of applesauce for one of the bananas since I only had one banana and they still turned out well.
Very very good!  I made for a non veggie eating 16 month old.  She didn't hesitate to eat it and as a  adult I liked it too.

These are fantastic, moist and hearty. Not only did our baby gobble them up, but so did picky older siblings. It's a breakfast or snack I can feel good about offering. I also enjoyed one (ok, 3!) myself with a cup of coffee.

Love these muffins!  I've been making them since my son was 2 and he loves them.  They were a big hit at our playgroup and my husband and I are also huge fans.  I use whole wheat flour and they turn out great!

My 4-year old daughter and I have been making these muffins for a couple of years now. They are so good and simple enough that she can help out with the bonus of being semi healthy. We've followed the recipe exactly, exchanged out the bananas and squash for applesauce, pumpkin, sweet potato, etc, used flax meal or oatmeal instead of oat bran, and replaced butter with coconut oil....all with good results. We tend to add an additional 1/2 tsp or so of cinnamon and about a tsp of vanilla just out of personal preference. Thank you for this household staple!
These were ok. I will make again b/c it's something easy I can give my daughter for lunch or snack.  Was hoping my other kids would enjoy these but no go.
Great muffins! Easy way to sneak veggies into food. I also used oatmeal instead of oat bran.
Followed the recipe. Tastes like banana bread to me, which is OK, but wanted more than banana flavor. Next time ill only use 1 banana and more of the carrots and squash.

Very good, baby wasn't too interested yet but my husband loved them and requested I make them again! Only substitutions were oatmeal instead of oat bran and cinnamon for the pumpkin pie spice because that is what I had.
My picky toddlers approve! Very moist and tasty. Froze them and reheated in microwave for about 30 seconds and tasted like they just came out of the oven. Used wheat germ, in place if oat bran.
I liked these a lot. Follow the recipe, and grease muffin tins! I use cupcake liners, and they stuck to them like glue.  :(
Wow!  The best!  I have made these twice now and the second time I doubled the recipe.  My two year old loves them, but so do I!  Very moist and just downright yummy!

My twin one-year olds eat these yummy muffins every single morning. I expect muffin to be among their first words. I use canned pumpkin instead of baby food squash, ground old fashioned oatmeal instead of oat bran, and I cut the butter in half and replace with 1/4 cup of applesauce.

Made this two weeks ago. My entire family LOVED these muffins. They tasted like banana bread! Will be making more to stock in the freezer! Thanks for the great and healthy recipe. I plan on trying half whole wheat flour the next time I make these just to see if it's noticeable.
I make these all the time!  I sub different kinds of baby food and add more cinnamin... Everyone at our playdates enjoys them!

This is a simple and quick recipe that my toddler loved helping me make and eat! All I had was baby carrots so I measured out 2/3 cup grated and it was perfect. I didn't have pumpkin pie spice so I substituted cinnamon. They tasted great, but I do want to try them with the pumpkin flavor.
My 22 month old LOVED these.  I did too :)  great recipe

I love this recipe! I use it with my one year-old who hates to eat vegetables. They usually end up on the floor. I change this recipe a little bit by adding shredded zucchini and walnuts and raisins and substituting half whole wheat flour for regular flour. What I love about this recipe is that it's versatile and you can add things or take away and see how it works! My one and four-year-old both love them and I think they're pretty good too :-)
this is a great idea, but I was wondering about the oat bran.  Where do you get that? Is it similar to wheat germ?
Very kid friendly and mom friendly since it has vegetables! Not the prettiest to look at, but very yummy. I also substituted oatmeal for the bran
Wow! My six year old helped me make these and says he can't stop eating them because they are so good! Made exactly as written except with quick oats instead of oat bran.

My 2-yr old VERY picky eater loved these!  I did make a few changes.  I replaced 1 of the bananas with a 4oz. jar of spinach baby food, cut back the sugar a bit, and I couldn't find oat bran so I used Wheat Germ.  I used baby carrots, and just guessed the amount...I think I used a lot because I ended up with 48 mini muffins.  But they were great!  Baked them for about 16 min, and they turned out perfect.

I know some people don't like when people review a recipe if they didn't follow it exactly.  But I like seeing what people did and how they turned out.

I need to "sneak" a few vegetables and fruits into my own diet.  These muffins do the trick!  I have made them several times and even sent a batch to work with my husband. Didn't use the squash as I didn't have any in hand. Added another carrot and used All Bran instead of oat bran.
