Didn't look so good to me, but my three year old devoured them

i'm sure these will be great! i'll be making them soon but i think i only have pumpkin puree on hand that should work well instead of the baby food.
yum!

Hi, these are delicious... The only differences I made were using coconut oil in place of the butter, rolled oats instead of oat bran, baby carrots instead of regular carrots, and pear/mango canned baby food because I didn't have squash. They are so moist and definitely deserve a 5 star rating! Thanks for the recipe

Very tasty but could definitely cut back on the sugar by half at least. Also would consider avocado instead of butter for this recipe in the future to make it healthier. Little one will love these I'm sure!
Awesome recipe!  Followed as is and the kids in daycare loved it!

These were awesome!  The only change I made was that I used fresh pureed butternut squash instead of the jar of baby food. I also added 2 TBS of milled flax seed. They were so moist it was amazing.  My 2 year old loved them and kept asking for more "cupcakes" because they were so tasty.  The only problem I had was that I liked them so much too I kept going back to eat more!  I am going to make them again today and expand it a bit more by adding some zucchini as well.

Delicious! Added some flaxseed for omega 3 fat and used grated zucchini instead of baby food squash because I had fresh zucchini to use. Even our picky teenager said these were great (high praise). Thanks!
My kids LOVE these. I make mini muffins all the time and these are their favorite.

My 4 year old daughter will not eat veggies at all. This recipe was an excellent idea to help her get her veggies intake for the day. She eats them like they are candy. I also have been playing around with the recipe and have added some vanilla extract and some shredded zucchini. When I don't have bananas I have also added pureed pears or apple sauce. I also decided to try it with 3/4 cup wheat flower with 1/4 white. 3 out of 4 of my kids LOVE these. Thanks for the recipe!!

These were REALLY REALLY good! So moist and delicious.  My kids really enjoyed them for breakfast with a glass of milk or kefir. And they didn't even suspect there was anything "yucky" (i.e. healthy) in them.  : )  My husband and I liked them too.
Great recipe!

These are so amazing! My two year old gobbles them up along with the rest of the family. A much healthier alternative than store bought muffins that are loaded with sugar and other chemicals. I make these often so thank you for sharing!
Substituted canned pumpkin as I didn't have baby food.  Very nice, subtle flavours.  All of the kids enjoyed them.

If I could rate it 10 STARS I would. I make double batches of these almost weekly. Hubby LOVES...LOVES...LOVES these muffins.
Only thing I do is add more carrots to it, more fiber one original cereal & more bananas and I have to add pecans and or English walnuts Some times I add both types of nuts together.

Thank you for this recipe...
Everyone LOVES them in our family & that includes Friends
If my Brother loves them that would be a miracle. He has to have icing & all the ooey gooey bad sugary stuff to it NOT THESE. YEA !!!

THANK YOU !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
I have two picky eaters that don't like to eat vegetables. They loved these muffins!

A hit in my house hold, I also tried it with the pumpkin instead of the squash and it is just much better with the squash they kids eat them faster when it is squash, thank you for helping me hide those great things my little guy will not eat.

Great recipe! Muffins were moist, sweet enough and I love that they are good for you too!! Plus, they were kid-approved! I made them exactly like the recipe states. Only reason I didn't give them 5 stars is because I am not a fan of the little crunches the oat bran added but that is something I can easily get past. lol My 4 yr old even helped me make them and after he ate one he told me, "Thank you for adding the carrots mom! They are yummy!"

Love love.  Toddler loved it and they freeze well! I still make them occasionally even though toddler no longer, now a 6 year old.  I normally use less sugar and butter than the receipe calls out and I add apple sauce or butter squash sauce to soften it up since I use less butter. I even added moderate ground up flaxseeds.  Always turns out fluffy and hearty.

I have made these muffins several times and they always come out delicious! My 2 little ones gobble them up! I even subbed avocado for the butter this last time and really enjoyed the smooth richness. We also usually double the pumpkin pie spice and add 1 tsp of ginger. Using whole wheat flour works well, too and I imagine that there are several gluten free 'flours' that would do just fine.
I made changes and they still turned out great. I like that you can adjust things and they still turn out well. Thumbs up from my 3 yr old!

Yes, babies LOVE these!  I subbed grated zucchini for the jar of squash, used half white flour and half wheat, used half whole oats and half ground flaxseed.  Second time I made them, they turned out too wet even with extra oven time - probably used too much zucchini - and they're still super yummy.
I made no changes.  These were amazing!  Will definitely make them again.

These are soooo good! I used whole wheat flour and I only had 1 banana so I used a jar of strawberry banana baby food along with the squash. I also didn't have pumpkin pie spice so I used 1/2 tsp cinnamon, 1/4 tsp all spice and 1/4 tsp nutmeg. I didn't have enough butter so I used 1/2 coconut oil. They came out great and my 11 month old gobbles them up!! Anything to get veggies in him!!
My 2 year old is a very very picky eater.... and he loved these. Very simple, very yummy!
I make these muffins for every daycare party.  They're my go to potluck for toddler functions.  Very good!
Great healthy muffins, but still not enough to get my toddler to try them.  He loved helping to make them, but man is he a stubborn one!!!

My young girls love these every time! Instead of baby food I use applesauce. It works great. Sometimes I will throw in zucchini as well. And I have also added ground flax seed. They think these are a treat so it works out well to throw in anything healthy.
I have teenage boys and this is a simple way to sneak healthy things in without them knowing because they can be picky. This is a favourite in my house.

Delicious!  These were just wonderful straight out of the oven.  I look forward to trying different variations in the future.  The flavor of bananas really dominates the original recipe, which is fine if you want to "mask" the other vegetables.  I might double up the squash and carrots next time, since they were totally obscured by the banana in the original ratios.  And next time I plan to add dried cranberries.  Thank you for sharing!

My 1 year old loved this!  I used wheat germ instead of oats bc she has an oat sensitivity and used pumpkin instead of squash (both per different reviews).  She ate the whole, regular-sized muffin!  Will def make again.

My toddler has a true food aversion due to medical issues, and he gobbled these down (so did I).  The only changes I made were based on what I had in my pantry; I used oatmeal instead of oat bran, and I didn't have pumpkin spice so I used a few dashes of cinnamon and a dash of cloves. Thanks for this recipe--it was wonderful to see my toddler happily eating.
Yummy!  I had to use zucchini instead of carrots because my carrots were bad and I couldn't find pumpkin pie spice so I used pumpkin pie filling.  Was delicious!
Fabulous.  My two year old and my hubby raved about them.  I substituted canned pumpkin for squash since I had some leftover from another recipe and swapped whole oats for oat bran.
Toddler and I both loved them.  Have since done them with some zucchini added too.  Yum.
My toddler likes these.  I heat up a sweet potato in the microwave to soften and throw that in.  I shred zucchini and carrots and add ground flax.  I think they are pretty tasty, too.

They're gone in 2 days! Made two small changes - didn't have oat bran so used just regular oatmeal instead and used 1/2c pumpkin instead of squash since my kids are waaayyy past the baby food stage.  All 5 in my house from 20 months to 32 years loved them and because they're relatively healthy, quick, easy and made with 'everyday' ingredients this will become a regular in my kitchen!
Nice recipe, muffins came out great!

These are so good!  I couldn't find oat bran so I instead used regular oats and also subbed 1/4 cup ground flaxseed for 1/4 of the flour.  Sweet enough to keep the kids happy and healthy enough to keep momma happy!

I just made these and my 19 month old loves them! Neither of us likes a lot of spice so I cut the pumpkin pie spice amount in half. I also replaced the oat bran with quick cook oats and it turned out great. They are light, fluffy, and not too sweet.

These muffins are delicious! The name "Toddler Muffins" is a misnomer. Mommy loves them, too! Moist and just sweet enough, my 17 month old took one bite and said, "Yummmmmm!" I used a little bit of honey in addition to the brown sugar and 1/2 cup of rolled oats instead of oat bran since I didn't have that on hand. I will be making a double batch next time to have on hand in the freezer. I think you could also play around with the veggies you add. Zucchini would also be really good in them.
I made these with oatmeal instead of oat bran only because I didn't have any.  They were amazing.  I can't wait to buy some oat bran to make them again!  Thanks for a tasty recipe!
My 2 year old loves these muffins! He eats 2 mini muffins with his breakfast and 1 or 2 as snacks throughout the day!  So glad I found this recipe.  I highly recommend it!

My super picky 3-year-old has loved these muffins as long as she has been able to eat them.  They are relatively easy, although I had to search for the oat bran at first (ended up finding it at Whole Foods, where you can buy as much or as little as you need).  I make a double batch and then portion them out and freeze them in ziploc baggies.  They defrost great and taste like fresh-baked.  Excellent recipe!
Very good! This recipe made 24 mini and 7 regular sized muffins for me. I couldn't find oat bran in the store so I used oatmeal and it worked just fine.
Tasty. I sub'd in oatmeal since I didn't have oat bran but otherwise kept it the same.

These are a HUGE hit with me and a picky 4 year old! I used a zucchini and a carrot instead of 2 carrots and I use steelcut oatmeal since we don't have oat bran. I also make normal sized muffins rather than mini ones! Other than that, I follow the recipe exactly when I make them for the 4 year old. When I make them for myself, I make a few changes to make them a little healthier, ex. substitute greek yogurt and peanut butter for the butter, take out the brown sugar, etc. These muffins are really easy to adapt for different tastes, LOVE them!
Kids gobbled them up. The perfect sneaky snack.

These should be called family muffins, it wasn't only the toddlers who loved them!
They were moist and delicious and healthy too.
I didn't have baby food so substituted applesauce. Otherwise I followed the recipe exactly. 
Highly recommended!

Excellent! Followed the recipe pretty exact. I couldn't find oat bran so I substituted with just oats as others have done. Also used 1/2 pumpkin baby food and 1/2 squash baby food rather than just squash baby food. My two toddlers gobbled three up within the hour. Husband and I also enjoyed them! I will be making a few batches of these for my son's class for his birthday! Thanks for the great recipe!,

my 3 kids love these. they are 5, 3, and 1. my 3 year old eats almost nothing, especially veggies so these are a wonderful way to sneak them in. i made one change. i realized after i started making them that i didnt have any pumpkin pie spice so i used apple pie spice. still came out great. ! Thanks for the recipe!

I made these muffins for my 17 month old who is pretty picky when it comes to muffins. He LOVES them! I tried one and they are pretty good! You really don't taste veggies. I did use Greek yogurt in place of the 1/2 cup of butter though, because I try to keep everything as healthy as possible.

These are great!!! My stubborn 5yr old who refuses to eat vegetable LOVES these and has no clue they are packed with veggies!!!! I do recommend not using the baby food the recipe calls for, I purée real veggies and use that instead. It's more healthy and it's the real deal, not some processed shelf baby food. I take 1 raw yellow squash & 1 raw zucchini (with skin) and purée it in my food processor, that replaces the baby food (granted it's allot more than the 1 container it calls for, but It doesn't mess up the texture or the taste of the muffins) then I continue on with the recipe as it calls for...bananas, carrots, ect. They take more like 18-21 mins to cook and I make sure they cool on a baking rake due to being very moist cause of the extra veggies I put in them. I highly recommend these!!!!
Good recipe. Make sure that the butter is at room temperature or the texture of the muffins will not be homogeneous. Great flavour. My kids love them! A keeper.

I made these all the time when I worked as a nanny for a family full of extremely picky eaters. Each batch I made was gone in no time, and their mother was happy that they were more nutritional than most other baked goods. Followed the recipe exactly.

Recipe is perfect just the way it is, but next time I may try using half the butter and adding 1/2 cup applesauce. I also stuck the carrots in the food processor with the bananas to make for quicker "mashing"! I usually don't expect a recipe to turn out perfectly the first time, but this one did! My husband, toddler, and I all LOVE the results (half of them were gone within 30 minutes!) I can't wait to make these for my toddler's Mother's Day Out class for snack.

Great recipe. I tripled the recipe, worked fine.  Used my own frozen pumpkin, added some raisins and chopped walnuts.  I did not have oat brand so I added more flour. I left out the salt.  Baked for about 22 minutes.

I, personally, did not love them, but my toddler always gobbles them down (veggies and all!)  And so does every other toddler I have ever fed them to.  So, since they ARE toddler muffins and toddlers love them, they deserve 5 stars :)
These were delicious.  I substituted 1/2 C of pumpkin puree for the squash baby food.  Also, I used flax seed instead of oat bran and added some sweetened coconut.  Will make again for sure.

great recipe. only had one carrot so i used a few florets of cauliflower that i grated instead--wouldn't know the difference! also, used 1/2 C. oat flour (blended oats in a magic bullet) and 1/2 C. all purpose, didn't have the baby squash so i used applesauce and used wheat bran instead of oat bran and they were fabulous. my toddler was licking the crumbs off her plate!
Thank you so much!  I needed a recipe that had no dairy since my son is allergic.  This fit the bill!  I am so glad I found this!
These are absolutely amazing! I use 1/2 cup whole wheat flour and 1/2 cup all-purpose and I also replace 1 of the eggs with 1 tbsp flax seed + 3 tbsp water.

I make these all the time and freeze them for my 2 year old son.  in the morning I wet a paper towel, wring it out and wrap muffins in it and heat in the microwave for 30 seconds.  easy healthy breakfast!  He loves them so much he asks for muffins several times a day.

good recipe !  I have a hard time with people who think changing oil for butter and for sure don't eat a whole egg.
If you want to make it healthy leave out the flour.

Diabetic friendly!!! These are amazing!!!  My son and I had a lot of fun making this together, and he loved them so much he's scarfed like 5 of them down in a matter of hours!! Couldn't Find oat bran, so used a cup of instant oat meal (what I had on hand)

Thank you for this recipe!  I wanted one that was healthy enough for my tough standards as a diabetic for a quick breakfast or snack, and this was PERFECT!  I replaced the baby food squash with half a cup of pumpkin puree only because that's what I had, half the flour with whole wheat, used a little less sugar and added a few packs of Truvia sweetner and a half cup chocolate chips - have to get in those antioccidants, right?!  Anyway, these are yummy warm with butter - we heat them in the microwave cut in half and buttered - delicious!

LOVED these!  We all liked them - adults and a picky 18 month old!  We used the full amount of sugar but will cut that back next time.  We also used the pulp from some carrot/apple juice instead of the grated carrots but it worked perfect.  Didn't have the baby food so just left that out.  They were still perfect though!  I think we'll have to try some variations based on this recipe next.  So excited to find a healthy muffin (with veggies!) that we all love!

Made a batch of these simple muffins for my two VERY picky eaters. All three of us LOVE them! So moist, so flavorful. The recipe is perfect as written. I made a batch following the recipe exactly (except I did blend up 1/2 cup of oatmeal because I forgot to get the oat bran, but I'll just do that every time b/c it's what I would regularly have on hand) yesterday. And then today, since we loved them so much, I made another batch, this time subbing the butter with vanilla yogurt. They just came out of the oven. They haven't even had time to cool yet, but I just ate one and it tasted just as good, only is probably way more moist. It will probably still work for me though.

We have made this multiple times and they are are a huge hit from the kids to the adults.  The last time I made them I used real squash instead of baby food squash and they turned out perfect.  Making them now for a healthy camping snack.

I had some cooked butternut squash in the fridge - so I just scooped a bunch into the batter. I also blanch greens, blend them smooth & freeze into icecubes. I add 1 green icecube too. My kids devoured these!!! Thank you!

Mmmmm, excellent just as is.  Also works without squash baby food.  My 2 yr old loves them, and so do I!  BTW the pumpkin pie spice I used  is 1 tsp cinnamon, 1/2 tsp ground ginger, and 1/4 tsp ground cloves.  Tastes great!

This is a great recipe. It is very adaptable to what you have. For instance, I didn't have squash baby food but had carrot. Since I used carrot already, I used minced apples instead of carrots. And I used 1/2 whole wheat flour, 1/2 white flower. They were awesome. Next time I will try then with a little less butter.
These were easy and delicious.  I substituted 4.5 oz of baked acorn squash for the baby food squash.
These are great! My 2 year old grandson and I make these all the time! He loves to help and he loves to eat them!
Made this recipe exactly as instructed and it turned out great — 24 reasonably healthy mini muffins that my 1-year-old loves. I'll definitely make this again.

Mine turned out a little "chunky"...but I loved that! 
I used quick-cooking oats instead of oatbran.
I also had to substitute the baby food sqaush with another baby food vegetable blend.  
All in all, these were really, really good and I plan to make these more often in the future.

Really yummy little muffins! Wanted a treat for my little guy feeling under the weather, and these really did the trick. Great flavor with the pumpkin pie spice and jam packed with fruit and veggies! My husband and I did them too. Awesome, homemade, healthy snack.
My toddlers ate 1 each but did not ask for seconds. It flavor of the banana was overpowering. They love bananas but this was too much.
Just made these for my 2.5 yr old.  He loved them, I did and so did my husband.  Very easy and very tasty!
My 16 month old loved these muffins.

My kids loved these almost as much as I did... So moist and yummy. Definitely a new favorite!

(Used canned pumpkin, half ap/ half wheat flour, and I didn't have oat bran so I subbed 1/4 c flaxseed meal and 1/4 oatmeal. Also added 1tsp vanilla and 1tsp baking powder.)
moist,tasty & healthy
Very good! I used oatmeal instead, still great.

Gluten free and egg free version: I used 1/2 cup applesauce instead of the 2 eggs, and 3/4 cup brown sugar instead of 1/2 cup. I also used Cup 4 Cup brand gluten free flour instead of all purpose flour. I Replaced oat bran with more g-free flour, to eliminate aftertaste. I chopped carrots instead of shredding (easier). Forgot to put the squash in. Used 1 1/2 " scoop, which made 18 muffins. They were very good before changes, and even tastier after changes

So good, and perfect for quick breakfast. I have a hard time getting my 8 year old to eat in the morning. At least if she just has one or two of these I'll know she's getting lots of good stuff. Also perfect for resisting the drive through temptation. 

I used quick oats instead of bran because I didn't want to but something I know I wouldn't use for any thing else.

I made these for a trip down to the Kentucky Derby for the guys to have something to munch on.  They loved them!  The texture was nice and they were super moist.  I made as written only baking them in mini muffin pans.  This made a great size for the guys to pop in their mouth without making a mess in the car.  I would definitely make these again.

These are great.  I've followed the recipe exactly as well as changed it up for what I have on hand and it has always been a hit.  Adults love them just as much as the little ones.  I like to keep a few jars of banana baby food on hand for times when I don't have enough ripe bananas.

These muffins are delicious!  Just made my 2nd batch  in 24 hours!  My 11 month old loves them...And so does my husband.  I made mini muffins for my baby to freeze and big ones for my husband and I.  The only alteration I made was cutting the sugar in half.  Yum!  Such a great muffin!

We absolutely loved these muffins. So flavorful and moist! I made two small changes; I added one teaspoon of baking powder and added 1/2 cup of raisins that I "plumped up" in some unsweetened, hot chai before adding them to the batter. Out of the whole recipe, two muffins remain. Even my husband inhaled them!

Love it! The only change I made was using cinnamon instead of pumpkin pie spice. I did use thawed frozen bananas and the result was fine. Next time I will cut the spice to about 3/4 t. They only took 10 minutes in my oven and this recipe made 36 mini muffins. I filled the cups very close to the top and they didn't over-flow. 15-month old approved!
Delish! I cut the butter and added in apple sauce. Also increased the pumpkin pie spice slightly. My toddler daughter has been asking me to bake muffins and I feel,good about serving her these.
Very tasty! My son wolfed it down. Next time I might try adding zucchini instead of carrots. Great recipe! Thanks for helping me sneak some veggies into my boy's diet!
Very easy recipe, and was very popular with kids and grownups alike.

Super-easy, super-delish!  Made according to recipe, with the exception of needing to replace squash with canned pumpkin puree, as that's what was on hand, and we didn't want to wait to make these. :o)  These are TeRriFiC!  Topped a few with chopped toasted pecans we had on hand, and LOVED THAT!  

Will definitely make these often.  Will incorporate nuts into them, or sprinkle on top, as our family loves that nutty flavor & crunch.  Will add soaked raisins sometimes, just because we like them.  These muffins were great as written, though.  The recipe variation is just because of family likes.  Will try w/cranberries, as commented by another - sounds like a nice twist!

SO glad to add these to our breakfast/snack choices!
Thank you Lori!! My picky toddler is eating veggies -- and he doesn't even know it!!

These are a HUGE hit!! I always have to make a double batch because not only do my 18 month old and 4 year old devour these, so do my adult children! I only alter the recipe  by using ground flax instead of the oat bran, and i usually use at least 2 more carrots than it calls for. I use the organic rainbow carrots and I chop them up fine in my Nutribullet. These are AMAZING!! 
(These are easy to make all organic if your into that thing :)

Just made these for my 2yr old and he loves them. I wanted something packed with veggies that I could send in his lunch for preschool that he would actually eat. They just cooled and he's already eaten 5 of them in 5 min. I love that you can freeze them for later!
Great for the kids!

Great recipe.  Can easily be modified for what one has in the house.  Both of my kids (and me!) loved them.  We ate one every day for breakfast, until they were gone, and never grew tired of them.  Very moist - my 10 mos old, could eat small bits I pinched off for him.  Here's the substitutions I've tried so far.  I used canned pumpkin puree instead of baby food.  B/c that isn't quite as liquid-y as baby food, I used only one carrot and added a small zucchini (b/c it's moist), grated.  I've also used milled flax seed instead of oat bran.  Thanks!
Very delicious! The whole family enjoyed them!

I added 1 tsp. baking powder, and followed the rest of the recipe as written.  They turned out so good. They were nicely fluffy and not dense and heavy like some muffins are.  They had just the right amount of sweetness, too.  Tomorrow I'll see if my picky grand-toddlers will
like them. Thanks for this recipe.
Very yummy!!  My 2 1/2 year old loves these!  And so do I.
I did not care for this recipe. I followed the recipe exactly. They smelled good while they were cooking, but they tasted like carrots and squash with a hint of pumpkin pie spice.
These are really good!  I decreased the sugar to 1/3 c but otherwise followed the recipe.  My 1-year-old likes them and so does the rest of the family!

These were delicious & very moist!!  For the sugar I used 1/4cup applesauce & 1/4cup brown sugar.  I also used gluten-free oatmeal for the oat bran and gluten-free flour.  I didn't have any pumpkin spice so I substituted cinnamon.  My squash puree that I used from my freezer had some sweet potato and apple in it, too.  My toddler didn't like them but she's in a picky phase.  My husband and I gobbled them up!!  I will definitely make these again!  Yum!

OMG. My grandson has been loving these muffins for several months now. They are absolutely wonderful as the recipe is written, and I have made a couple of variations as others have suggested with much success. The best thing about this recipe is how well they freeze - I let them cool completely for at least an hour before storing them in a gallon ziploc bag and place them in the freezer. My 18 month old grandson calls them "muffies" and - seriously - takes a bite and closes his eyes in pure bliss and says "mmmmmmmmm!" Thank you, Lori!

A snack with vegetables and fruit that my 2 and 4 year old beg for?!  Amazing!  I am so happy that I found this recipe.  
I followed the recipe exacly as written, and they were delicious.  I might try replacing some of the butter with applesauce to make them even healthier.
My little guy really liked these. I used oats instead of oat bran and applesauce instead of baby food because that's what I had. Will definitely make again. Thanks for sharing.
I follwed the recipe exactly as written. My picky 2 year old is loving these!

My kids love these, and I don't think they're bad either. I used frozen pumpkin puree, ground up oats since I didn't have oat bran, and I threw in some raisins. Doubled the recipe and made 24 muffins, 24 mini-muffins and a mini loaf of bread.
I made this exactly as written and they are awesome for kids and adults.  Hard to stop eating!

These are delicious!  I have to admit...I'm not the healthiest adult, so stealing a couple from my kids on the way out the door could very well be my way to sneak a little fruit & veggie into my diet too:)

My 2 year old LOVED these muffins.  He ate almost 3 muffins in about 30 minutes.  I know he was stuffed and was still asking for more.

I used 1/2 can of pumpkin instead of squash because it was available and used whole wheat flour (and no all purpose flour).  I did have a to cook a bit longer (maybe 25 minutes), but still amazing.  These are a must try for anyone with a picky toddler.  Thank you for this recipe!

Awesome & super moist as everyone else says. I used a little less butter & brown sugar & substituted whole wheat flour & sweet potato & chicken baby food (all had in cupboard) & turned out great. Made mini-muffins & baked for 20 min & still could have left in few notes longer.

Terrific recipe and my toddler loves them! I used fresh pumpkin instead of canned squash and like someone else here replaced the oat bran with oatmeal and worked great. Think I'll add raisins next time.

Fantastic healthy muffins for all ages. I found them a little greasy for my liking so will try making them with less fat next time and more pumpkin. I used 100% whole wheat flour and they turned out just great. Thanks for the recipe!

Hi Kathy, I get the oat bran at the grocery store in the cereal isle.   It's near the hot cereals.  You can also use wheat bran but I think that that is different than wheat germ.  Oh and my son is now 5 and his sister is 1 and these are still a popular treat at our house :)

Just a quick edit, kids are now 8 and 4.  I'm making the muffins today for my father in law who loves them too!

Awesome recipe! My son is a very picker eater (3 y.o) but has been requesting muffins lately. I made the recipe almost exact except I didn't have oat bran so I used instead 1/4 cup of oatmeal and 1/4 ground flaxseed. Absolutely delicious. I plan on making a huge batch to keep in the freezer.

Wow! These are really yummy. What a great way to sneak some orange veggies into a family friendly breakfast or snack. We liked them so much I made a double batch the next day to freeze. These make wonderful snacks to send to school with the kids.

Awesome!  I did make a couple changes to make it even healthier still!  I didn't have oat bran so I used ground flax seed.  Instead of butter I used 1/4 cup vegetable oil, 1/4 cup vanilla yogart. 3 egg whites instead of 2 whole eggs.  1/2 cup whole wheat flour, 1/2 cup all purpose flour.  I had to cook them a few minutes longer and they turned out moist and tasty!

Just made these muffins, in hopes that my 18 month old son will enjoy them in the morning! I just ate a mini and it was delicious ;] I made a few small changes:
Rather then 1c flour- 3/4c flour & 1/4 wheat germ [plus a tablespoon or so for consistency]
I added about 3/4c mashed sweet potatoes
I added a handful of rasins
I added chipped pecans, approx. 1/8c. just sprinkled in
Rather than pumpkin pie spice, which I do no have, I used cloves, ginger, nutmeg, cinnamon and cardamom 
These things are SOOOO moist!
Amazing! I will now only eat veggies in muffin form.

These are pretty tasty!  I made some changes as I didn't have all the ingredients.  I put some oats in the food professor to substitute for oatbran. I didn't have squash baby food so used some applesauce and some squash/carror/chickpea toddler mush that I had on hand.  Also made my own pumpkin spice.  My toddler enjoyed making them and eating them.

I will definately make these muffins over and over!  The original recipe was delicious, the second time I added grated zuccinni just to up the vegetable intake, and didn't have oat bran so had to replace with hemp hearts.  Upped the healthiness and tasted equally as awesome!
These were really good, tasted like banana bread.  I used 4.5oz of fresh squash, rather than baby food jar.  Also ground up 1/2 oatmeal, rather than buying oat bran

I substituted canned pumpkin for the baby food and rolled oats for the oat bran. This made about 16 muffins. My first impression was that they were ...odd? I did not like them at all when they first came out of the oven. The texture was wonderful, but the carrot was too prominent or something. I started calling them "funk muffins". My roommate loved them. I was too lazy to cook the next day and I hadn't thrown them out yet, so I tried another one.  Suddenly they were amazing. I don't know if the flavors meshed better after they sat for a while or what, but I finished off the rest of them myself over the course of two days. Go figure. I think these beat out banana bread when I have overripe bananas now.
Thank you for this! I had bananas to use up, and the rest of the ingredients in hand. Very easy! My kids loved these!

I've made these four times in the last month.  I love them!  I hate to write all of my substitutions, but thought maybe it would be helpful for someone else.  I have a TON of baby food to use up and this is a great recipe for that.  I use one banana and one jar of baby food banana; one jar of squash; one jar of carrots (kids didn't like the grated carrots).  I also used 1/2 the amount of butter and one jar of applesauce (although I prefer the the taste slightly with the original amount of butter).  Also used whole wheat flour.  As another poster said, I used 1/4 c ground flax and 1/4 c baby food oatmeal instead of the oat bran.  I am tempted to try other kinds of baby food just to mix things up, but so far haven't done that.

Very good.  I had to use what I had on hand, so that was carrot baby food (2 3.5 containers) wheat germ instead of oat bran and cinnamon instead of pumpkin pie spice.  Also added a 1/2 tsp baking powder and no carrots because I only had baby carrots and I wasn't sure how many I would have to shred to equal 2 carrots.

These muffins were great! I liked them as well! My 13 month old loved them! She ate 2 mini muffins and reached for another! I did some minor changes because i didn't have certain ingredients.  I used cinnamon instead of the pumpkin pie spice and old fashioned oats instead of oat bran. They were delicious and I will definitely be making them again!

I loved it. They were pretty tasty, which I was skeptical of, and I liked them. my one year old niece ate an entire full size muffin in one sitting she loved them so much. I made them exactly as the recipe states except I used a 4oz jar of baby food, and a bit more brown sugar than called for.

Yum! My toddler loved these, and so did everyone else. We're low cholesterol, so I made these with oil, egg whites, and whole wheat flour. I also subbed 1/4 c acorn squash for the baby food and added a teaspoon of cinnamon. They are delicious.

I did end up making changes. I didn't have enough squash, so I used pumpkin puree instead, which I weighed. I thought I had oat bran, but what I ended up having was wheat bran so I looked up substitutions and used oatmeal instead...aaaaand I had EXPIRED pumpkin pie spice so I researched how to make that and THANK GOD I actually had the ingredients for that. Luckily for me, the chickens laid enough eggs. These came out moist and flavorful. I weighed the bananas too, which were baby bananas and they came to about 9.8 oz. I forgot to weigh the carrots because I was SO frustrated at a family member for using the grater to make homemade soap and they ruined the grater so I had to use the carrot peeler to slice the carrots and then the hand chopper to chop the slices to bits. In the end they came out YUMMY and beautiful... a little flat but, my toddler ate them. She even ate Gramma's when she wasn't looking. WE WILL be making these again.

I've made this recipe countless times now, and like to double it, giving me 18 medium-sized muffins. I use baked butternut squash, and like to add raisins or cranberries. My 2 1/2 year old son loves them.

My 15-month old loved these.  I used a jar of sweet potatoes instead of squash (I didn't have squash), rolled oats (didn't have oat bran), and Allspice (didn't have pumpkin pie spice).  We'll make these again!

I made these for my 10 month old with a couple substitutions based on what I had on hand. I only had one banana so I added more pumpkin and no oat bran so I used 1/4c flax and 1/4c oats. They turned out great and she loves them (although she eats anything)! Makes me feel better giving these to her with breakfast or as snacks than most muffin recipes that call for 4x as much sugar! Plus you get the extra fruits and veggies! Mom win!
Great recipe. Very versatile.  Sometimes I throw in apple or mashed sweet potato instead of the squash and we like to add raisins and walnuts pieces to it as well.  My hubby loves these

I've made at least 5 batches of these muffins for my baby.  I make my own squash puree so I'm not really sure if I'm using the suggested amount.  I substitute quick oaks for oat bran and zuchinni for carrot (I've tried carrot but I like it with zuchinni better.)  I also use whole wheat flour.  My baby loves these so much.  I started giving them to him at 12 months old for breakfast.  I recommend letting them cool to room temperature before freezing but they freeze very well.  Just defrost in the microwave for 20 seconds for a mini muffin or 40 seconds for a full sized muffin.

These are pretty good, and they smell great when baking. Only thing is, the directions are kind of arbitrary. Two carrots can really vary in size and affect the batter. I made twenty four minis and still had lots of batter left over, but I like this recipe. I added golden raisins and some cinnamon. Yum

Great start but I made a few changes. I used 1/2 cup of applesauce instead of butter. I didn't have enough bananas so I used one banana and another 1/4 cup applesauce. I had wheat bran at home so I used that instead of oatbran. I also used whole wheat flour to make them a little healthier. I also added a little extra pumpkin pie spice due to the fact my daughter likes things zippy. My 21 month old daughter couldn't shove them in her mouth fast enough and quickly asked for more:)The changes in the recipe also added an extra 12 muffins to the recipe which obviously was a bonus.

My daughter loved this recipe.  I did switch 1/4 c of yogurt and 1/4 c of oil for the butter and I pureed 1 zucchini cut into chunks with a teaspoon of water in place of the jar of baby food.  I actually ran the carrots and banana through the food processor as well.  I don't feel guilty now when she would rather have a muffin instead of dinner because it is packed with fruits and veggies.  I wonder if it would work as well with other vegetables like broccoli?  
Thank you for this recipe!

Thanks for this great recipe! I have a crazy 2 year old that won't touch fruits and vegetables. I tried to get nutrition into him with smoothies at first on the recommendation of my pediatrician. Somehow he always knew what was in there and refused to drink them. Then, I came upon this recipe, and everything changed! He loves these and gobbles them up. I changed some things. I made sure I used the fine part of my grater. He would notice bigger chunks of carrots?? I used unsweetened applesauce instead of the butter. Green vegetables are the hardest for me to get him to eat, so I used an asparagus/pea medley. I was a little worried that the taste might come through with my baby food choice, but they tasted great! I used all whole wheat flour and Stevia baking blend instead of sugar. Wonderful!

OMG these things are so dang tasty!  I think my husband and I like them even more than our picky toddler!  Just be sure that your grated carrot does not exceed 1 total cup of carrot, because they will be too moist and won't cook well if you do.  And I think they taste the best when made in the mini muffin pans because the edges get really brown and it adds to the taste.  When they are hot out of the oven I can hardly stop popping them in my mouth.  This is an excellent recipe and great not only for picky toddlers but the whole family as well!

Best recipe I've tried on AllRecipes and only one I've ever reviewed! I only gave it 4 stars for "as written" as I made the following alterations to make this the perfect healthy snack for my family: Subbed Whole Wheat flour for all of the all purpose flour. Subbed 1/4 c apple sauce for 1/2 the butter, and 1/4 c honey for 1/4 the sugar (though next time will try a complete 1:1 substitution). Also subbed 1/2 a can of pumpkin (about 7 oz total) for the baby food, and cinnamon for the pumpkin pie spice.  The flavors were PERFECT and my toddler can't get enough of them! I feel good about feeding them to him for breakfast or as an on-the-go snack, as they are packed full of good-for-you ingredients.  AND I love them too! The recipe made 24 high-rising mini muffins plus 4 regular size muffins. I will make these again and again!

Love all the nutritious ingredients in these muffins and they taste great too.  Tried these for my daughter at 1 year, she didn't care for them so I froze them and tried them a few weeks later.  She likes them now :)
absolutely delicious! were addicted.
Awesome recipe exactly as written!

I made them with all baby food. I used banana and strawberry, pear pineapple, mango, carrots, and squash. They turned out terrific! Everyone loved them. I did have to cook them longer but they were so yummy!

Not the easiest recipe with all the different ingredients.  I used organic frozen squash grated organic carrots, and mashed organic bananas, which added to the difficulty.  Pregrated and mashed food would have lessened the time.  I also used all other organic items so my kiddo could eat mommy-guilt-free.
I made these exactly as the recipe stated and they were delicious.  The toddlers in my life who are adverse to veggies, ate these right up and asked for more!

LOVE LOVE LOVE these!!! I've made these 4 or 5 times now and my kids go ga-ga for them! I've only used the baby food squash once, the rest of the times I've just puréed my own squash, I can't tell the difference. I highly recommend this recipe especially if you have kids who aren't so great at eating breakfast before school! My 5 year old is always up for a "toddler muffin" no matter how early it is!!!
Made this for my veggie-hating toddler, and unfortunately they were not a hit.  I have to agree with him.  Quite dense and not a very nice flavor.

Made it this morning. Used oats instead of oat bran. My daughter loves them. It made 24 mini muffins and 6 small "regular-sized" muffins. The muffins came out much better in greased pans as opposed to paper-lined pans. Next time I'll skip the papers.

Followed the recipe exactly except for using different baby food puree.  I doubled the recipe and used a jar of cinnamon sweet potato puree and a jar of squash.  They are wonderful.  My 5 year old and 2 year old loved them.  So did my husband and I.
These are just awesome!  I'll have to double the batch when I make them again, because they DON'T last!  =)  Thanks for sharing!!

Very smart!!! They are very tasty. Easy to make. Did not have to make any changes to the recipy. My 2 year old loves them! Even my mother loves them... She is worse then my 2 year old when it comes to veggies! Best of all I love them! *they satisfy my pregnancy cravings!*. Two thumbs up.
Very good muffin. I used carrot puree and butternut squash puree and added chocolate chips to mask that they are a healthy muffin. Yummy!
I made this recipe as written & it was great. My 6yr old & my 8m old both loved them. We put a small bit of cool whip on them for a dessert treat that we all enjoyed!! Thanks for sharing

Loved this recipe and so did my kids.  I made a few substitutions though due to what I had on hand. I put in an apple in place of the squash and pureed it with a bag of baby carrots.  I used whole wheat flour instead of oatbran, and all spice instead of pumpkin pie spice.  I added a few sprinkles of cinnamon and nutmeg as well.

Made these for the first time for my 18mo old and they were an absolute hit! He loved them and so does my husband!

I did change the recipe just a tiny bit, but will stick to the original recipe next time around. I used baby food pureed carrots instead of squash and the muffins came out a little too moist but they still had excellent flavor! When i'm ready to make it I put all the ingredients (which are adjusted) in the blender (besides the coffee and ice and microwave the coffee for 1 minute which melts it just enough for the coffee to melt but have a little iced coffee left.) After that, I take the ice out of the measuring cup and use a hard metal kitchen utensil (used for cooking) and break it on a tray and put the coffee and ice in the blender and use the crush ice and liquify options until the frappe is perfect and top it off with whipped cream and extra caramel! :) Hope this helps.

If you have a kitchen Aid stand mixer: this was my method- whipped 1C butter flav. crisco + 1/2 C. real butter & 3C sugar for 8 minutes at highest speed, occasionally scraping the sides of the bowl with a rubber spatula.  Then added one egg and whipped one more minute, added another egg and whipped one more minute, scraped the sides of the bowl, and repeated the process  until all 6 eggs were whipped in, which added 6 more minutes to whipping time.  Turned mixer to lowest speed, then added 1 cup of sour cream (was short on sour cream so used half and half to fill up the rest of the measurement), 2 teaspoons of coconut extract and 1 teaspoon of almond extract [cuz one reviewer said smelled like sun tan lotion while baking] and kept the mixer running while I sifted the flour and baking soda into a separate bowl. added a tiny pinch of salt. Then slowly poured in the dry ingredients into the mixing bowl at lowest speed still & as soon as it was all in and wet, turned mixer off & gentle stir with spatula then poured it into greased/floured bundt pan.Crucial: bake at 325* for 70 minutes! cool on wire rack 10 minutes b4 inverting from pan. glaze crown  w/ thick mixture of half&half,powdered sugar, & 1 tsp  coconut extract.  sprinkled 1 C. coconut on top of glaze, & 1/2 C. choc chps on top of that. I made this drink for my husband and myself one night and it was great. I made a bigger batch (double) for a party the following weekend and it was AMAZING!!!! The difference was in the technique and very minor ingredient changes. The night before the party I juiced the limes but prior to cutting/juicing them, I zested them. I added the zest to the lime juice and then combined it with the pomegranate juice and granulated sugar and put it all in the refrigerator. (Doing it this way really intensifies the lime flavor and allows you to use regular sugar.) I put the liquors in the freezer that night. The morning of the party, I strained the pom/lime juice and then combined the juice and liquor and put the whole thing in the freezer until party time. This means it is REALLY cold before serving and your ice won't melt right away and dilute the drink when you pour into the salted glasses. Doubling the recipe used 2/3 of the liquor in each 750 ml bottle and yielded a half-gallon of the cocktail. If you want enough for a gallon, be sure to buy the larger liquor bottles. ENJOY!

I make teas the following way: 

7 regular sized Orange Pekoe Tea Bags (orange peko is the type of tea leaf, its generally what is used in Lipton and your other brands...but double check. It doesn't taste like oranges either. 

1 1/2 Cups of Sugar for a 1 gallon pitcher.

Put tea bags in small pot and put on stove with about 3 cups of water...give or take. You want the tea bags covered, so the bigger the pot, the more water you have to use. Bring tea to a boil and let it roll for 2-3 minutes. Turn tea off. let tea sit in pot for 10-15 minutes. 

While this is happeneing, fill you pitcher up half way with WARM water. Hot is good too, but it takes longer to cool off. 

Put sugar in warm water in stir vigourously. The secert to sweet tea is adding your sugar to warm liquid to melt the sugar so it doesn't all all to the bottom. 

Next, add your tea, then, you can either fill the pitcher the rest of the way up with water and refridgerate or...put ice in it to fill it up and drink. But remember...if you drink it before the ice melts, it might be a little sweet.

In the corresponding video (nicely done, AllRecipes!), JJ the bartender specifically says an ounce and a half of vermouth, not half an ounce. This is a pervasive problem among martini/gibson drinkers. If they're not drinking sweet goo in a martini glass, they're drinking straight gin (or vodka). JJ over on Park Avenue is exactly right-- a good martini is a proper mix of vermouth and gin. 

On the other hand, the recipe tells you to stir and not shake, which is preferable. Why is this so important? Because when you shake the ice, you break the ice. This means little pieces of ice will melt into your martini, watering it down slightly. Bartenders need to shake for presentation-- a part of the job is to put on a little show, but at home you can safely stir.

We really loved this!  It has become something we just do any time the heavy cream has been sitting a few days and needs to be put to use.  It is so delicious and family have been taking it home with them whenever there is extra.

Quite delicious!  
I made this using RAW heavy cream and cultured buttermilk.

Thanks! Easy and great result.

Super easy. Make with BLT pasta salad, stroganoff, and mashed potatoes.

mmmmm this looks good.  Looking forward to trying it. Thank you, Chef John.

This is great and so easy. No more store bought sour cream for me!
Chef John, you've done it again! Would give it ten stars if I could.

Excellent! Works great on all food but I have found it to be very tasty in Scrambled Eggs. DH loves eggs, I don't, but have to confess I loved Scrambled Eggs this morning with milk and Creme Fraiche blended in. Yummm.
Creamy and decadent.

I will never buy tub sour cream again. Oh my this was so easy and is absolutely delicious. Could only find ultra pasteurized heavy whipping cream but it worked fine. I did not make any changes and I will continue to make this in place of sour cream.  I love this stuff.

Very good and super easy.  Now I need to figure out what to make with all of the leftover buttermilk!!!  My wife accidentally bought low fat cultured buttermilk, so I am not quite sure what it did to the taste, but I thought it tasted great anyway.

I came across this by accident while looking for something else, and it looked so simple I had to give it a go. I've done it a couple of times now, always turns out great! This recipe is the absolute BEST.  So easy, and so delicious!  Never going to the store for sour cream again.  I used ultra-pasteurized heavy whipping cream, since I could not find "pasteurized."  Work just fine.   Thank you Chef John for this delightful recipe.
FANTASTIC! Chef John was right, I'll never buy sour cream again.
Love this recipe.  It is delicious and creamy.

I used this basic idea to make one of the most refreshing summer drinks I've ever tasted.  Instead of just sugar, I made a simple syrup by melting a cup of sugar and a cup of water together.  Then I adjusted the fruit to 4 lemons, 3 limes, and 2 large navel oranges.  Once the syrup was added to the juice, I added additional cups of water (about 4 total) until I got the balance of tart to sweet that the family liked.  I made this several times over the weekend of the 4th!!

A light, fresh tasting lemonade. I followed the recipe as stated. However, I felt the limes overpowered it. It did not have a sweet or tart taste.  Next time I will only use 2 limes, plus add 2 more lemons.  Instead of juicing all of the fruit, I sliced them in 1/4" - 1/2" slices and removed the seed pieces. I placed the sliced fruit in a bowl and added the sugar. I mashed slightly with a potato masher and let sit for 1 hour before adding the water and ice.  This makes for a nicer presentation.
Tasted good.  I may put more ice in it next time because I like slushes...

Overall I did not find this to be anything special.  The taste was just ok.  Maybe my citrus wasn't flavorful enough. it is the winter season here so maybe that is making a difference.  Don't know if I would go out of my way to make this again.
I've made this recipe before, and it is absolutely wonderful!! I found this years ago in a home cooking magazine.  My aunt loved it so much, that I sent her the recipe.

Of course this is going to be refreshing and delicious...IF the proportions of juice, water and sugar are right.  Even though it was easy enough to fix, that unfortunately was not the case with this recipe.  Too watery.  And not sweet enough.

Just a few helpful secrets: 1) Serve on a hot summer day when you need something refreshing.  I think the refreshing factor works best when you need to be refreshed. 2) Adjust amounts to suit your tastes.  I used 5 limes, 5 lemons, 3 oranges (because they were so large) and approximately 1 1/2 c. sugar. (It needed more sugar, though.)  I also used only 4 c. water.  3) Use seedless fruit if possible.  That way you don't have to fish the seeds out of your juice!  :)

The real way to make one is equal parts of all the liquors, most times it's 1/2 oz. I say most times because if you are mixing them in big mason jars then you would use more! NEVER use orange juice or sweet and sour. Just make fresh sweet and sour with lemon juice and simple syrup. I will echo other reviews and say that you should never shake anything carbonated. This is how I make mine behind the bar.

1/2 oz Vodka
1/2 oz Tequila
1/2 oz Triple Sec or cointreau or similar
1/2 oz light rum
1/2 oz Gin
1 oz Lemon Juice (Fresh)
1/2 oz Simple Syrup (1:1 sugar and water)
Splash Coke

Add all liquors, lemon juice, and syrup into a cocktail tin. Fill a collins glass with ice then your shaker with ice. Shake ingredients for about 10 seconds and strain into the collins glass with ice. Top with coke. Garnish with a lemon and cherry.

soak the raisins with brandy (formnon-alcoholics),instead, used whatever juice I have on hand. You may use with or without sour cream.
Instead of raisins, I;m going to use chocolate chips!
This should be called Peaches and Cream Smoothie. It reminded me so much of peaches and cream. It was fabulous!
It was OK. Use more ice cream and add ICE to make the smoothie cold.

I am sure as a healthy smoothie this is a winner, but for me though it sounded pretty tasty, I found it to be flavorless and warm, which is not how I like my smoothies. It wasn't enjoyable. Determined to have a smoothie, I took the same concept and remade it using some Heavy Whipped Cream instead of Soy and added some berries that I happened to have around which amounted to about 1 and 1/2 cups of Blueberries and 1/2 cup of Raspberries. I then added ice and 2 tablespoons of sugar.    I do thank the author for the concept, I am always looking for new ideas!

The idea of using the combo of peaches and orange juice sounded good; however I'm not sure I'd care for the canned peaches, and we can get really tasty fresh peaches in the grocery store now.  So for 2 servings I used two fresh peaches (peeled), 1/2 cup 2% milk, 1/2 cup vanilla yogurt, 1/4 cup orange juice, 1 tsp sugar, 1 tsp vanilla, and 4 ice cubes to lighten it up.  A 5-star smoothie.
Good taste, but not enough of it. What I'm trying to say: It did not have nearly enough flavor for my liking.

Because I wanted to make it lighter, I used fat free plain yogurt instead of ice cream--about a cup. I also used nonfat milk. I did add a teaspoon of pure vanilla flavoring. Great way for me to use up a can of no-sugar-added peaches from my pantry and make a quick breakfast smoothie for the kids.
Excellent!  Yes, it is more of a peachsicle milkshare but ohhh so good.  If you want more consistency of a smoothie may want to try adding a little ice.  I used fresh peaches (4 med size).
I made this with regular milk. Also, I ran out of o.j. so I used pineapple juice as well. Wonderful fruity flavor and deliciously creamy. Thanks!

I used only 1 1/2 cups of plain soymilk (not vanilla) and three fresh peaches instead of canned.  I and my family loved this and I would definitely make it again, maybe doubling the recipe because it didn't yield as much volume as I'd expected.  Oddly, my brother thought it had a vaguely banana-y flavor.  Very creamy texture, though.
It was good, but I suggest adding ice and a little bit of sugar
This was satisfactory but I didn't think it was fabulous.  I would suggest adding ice and more ice cream to make it thicker and make sure it is blended well.

It sounded pretty tasty, but I found it to be flavorless and not enjoyable.  2nd time I used Vanilla Soy Milk instead of regular Soy Milk, frozen peaches instead of canned (make it cold), teaspoon of fresh lemon juice, Vanilla yogurt instead of ice cream and some maple syrup. That was excellent, real tasty.
tasty delight. used regular milk instead of soy. i do like strawberry-banana better though.

I also like this recipe but...yesterday when I made it the first time with fresh peaches,plain milk,added sugar,and used strawberry ice cream instead of vanilla,it was better. Today with the right ingriedents the recipe called for,it's well,just okay.

I didnt exactly stick to the recipe but I made smoothies for my girls 2 peaches, 1 banana, a tblspoon of honey, 3 drops of vanilla extract and 1 1/2 cup of Vanilla Almond milk.   OMG WOW!!!!  It was a huge huge hit!!!!

Great! It's really refreshing for summer.
My kids want more!

I think this smoothie called for a little too much milk.  I used three fresh peaches instead of a can, and I think I should have used four.  This is more of a peaches and cream milkshake, rather than a peach smoothie.
I would suggest putting in 3-4 tsp. of sugar and a cup of ice. This was a shoot and a miss!
very tasty and refreshing. I had this for breakfast with a muffin and I wasn't hungry for lunch for 5 hours!
This was very very good. I used frozen peaches and 1% cows milk. My kids keep asking me to make it again and again.
good, but I skipped the ice cream all together and added ice instead. About 8 cubes. Much more refreshing. :)
i used seeded jalapenos and this was actually good. for the love of god don't give it to kids.

This was fantastic! This is a new family favorite. I could see serving it with a nice cheese/cracker combo.  So delicious!  Mine could have been hotter, so I'll try letting the peppers simmer longer or buy bigger ones next time.  
I just tried it with habanero peppers, blackberries, white sugar and vanilla. It was also delicious, but be careful w/the vanilla or don't use it at all; it made the dish smell and taste a bit like a doughnut (filling).
Perfect combination of hot and sweet.  I grow habanero peppers and didn't know what to do with the overabundance.  This was a great recipe that everyone loved.

This is a fabulous recipe. Truly a unique taste experience. I have fixed it twice for company and everyone loved it, commenting that they'd never tasted anything quite like it.    I use habaneros from my garden to make this and it has just the right amount of heat. Habaneros have a wonderful, almost fruity (and yes, HOT!) quality and I think by substituting other types of peppers you would lose some of the sophistication of this dish.

I was expecting more heat. It's really not that hot... Just a tiny bit of heat at the end. That being said, the peaches turned out delicious and tasted so good over ice cream. I will make this again, but I think I will use more peppers next time.

I have been making this recipe for years. My husband will talk about it for 362 days of the year after I have let him eat it over ice cream.
I have a question though. Has anyone ever made these and froze them? I want to take this to my son and his family and I thought they would travel better if they were packed into a cooler for traveling.  just don't want them to get mushy!

such a great idea! this had my entire family going wild -- even those with the most sensitive stomachs. the flavors compliment each other so perfectly that not one overwhelms another. i would have to agree with pianobarry and say to serve the ice cream seperately, otherwise it quickly melts and takes the heat (both kinds) down a notch.

WOOOOHOO! I suspected this might be too hot for many of the people I was serving it for, but it really wasn't. Besides the ice cream that helps cool it off, the heat is just a little end note and doesn't overwhelm the peaches. I recommend making sure you don't dice the peppers too small. Maybe just chop them in quarters. The butter gets a little frothy and it can be hard to find the peppers to take them out. You wouldn't want someone to come across one on accident! YIKES! Everyone loved it. GREAT unique recipe. I'll definitely do this one again!
Excellent and very different. I reduced the servings to 4 so I only used 1 pepper and I subbed honey for the brown sugar. Served with frozen yogurt. Will make again...Thanks!

This is a fantastic recipe!  You can make this as spicy or mild as you like. We love spicy so I used fresh peppers from my garden and some ground red pepper and fresh Palisade Peaches from the farmers market. Thank you SO much for this recipe!

Pretty good, would make again but would include the seeds or add more peppers cuz it wasn't very hot even by itself (and with the ice cream it was even milder).  I liked the fact that the peaches stayed relatively crunchy.

I expected more heat, the ice cream really reduced the burn factor.  I would use a third habanero next time.  My peaches were so juicy I had to adjust the cooking technique.  After the peaches were cooked I pulled then out with a slotted spoon.  I then continued to cook the syrup until it thickened.  This topping would also be very good on a cream cheese stuffed French toast. I would keep the peppers at 2 if it is not being used with ice cream. Thanks Dave for the post!

Please make this with habanero peppers and not jalapenos.  Jalapenos do not have that sneak up power that the recipe talks about. They are just dare peaches not double dare without the habaneros.  Amazing recipe!  The only tweak I would do next time would be to keep the peaches and ice cream separate on the plate so the ice cream doesn't melt and mix with the peaches.  It dulls down the kick.  Also, if serving for a big party, don't tell them that it is spicy and just watch.  Priceless!

Well, I stole my wife's ID to write this review.  She saw the recipe and we just happened to pick peaches yesterday and I had picked a couple habeneros during the week (they're not quite ripe yet).  We had stuffed bell peppers for dinner with most ingredients from the garden, then she surprised me with this.  My mouth is still tingling.  The ice cream sweet and cool with the peaches hot and spicy is a perfect combination.  Can't wait to share it with the family!

I liked these peaches a lot - but it got mixed reviews from the fam. One son couldn't decide - he kinda liked it, kinda didn't. One son didn't expect the heat and despite loving hot and spicy food didn't care for it. Husband said it was good, but he probably wouldn't make it again. So - mixed bag. But, I enjoyed it! Thanks for sharing!

My whole family really likes this. I'm a weeny white girl and only used one habanero and it was fantastic.  Sweet soft peaches, then a little heat right in the back of the throat.  Even the kids love it, with or without ice cream.

I have made this recipe so many times in the last two years!  My husband and son love it!!  However, there are a few variables that make it a completely different experience.  First, using habanero pepper is critical.  Aside from the heat, habaneros have a different flavor from jalapeños.  Second, if you want heat, you must use fresh peppers. The first time I made this, I used habaneros straight from my garden, and the flavor and heat were  out of this world!!  Finally, the quality of the peaches makes a big difference. Blah peaches = blah outcome. I have never found a peach that compares to Colorado peaches.

This was delicious. I was too scared to even look at the habaneros in the store, so I used jalapenos. Someone had just given me a bunch of nectarines so I used those instead of peaches. I couldn't find a health bar or anything like that in the store, so I topped this with a little granola and some of the sauted jalapeno, diced up. A little heat, quite tasty. I'll make this again and maybe I'll get brave next time and swap out part of the jalapeno for some habanero.
These are incredible!  They taste EXACTLY as described.  Sweet peaches followed by the heat...ice cream required!  Thank you for sharing this recipe.

This is a very chunky sauce. After adding the chopped green chiles and smelling the pot, I was a little wary, but it turned out great. I had it on homemade pizza, and when I  was spreading it on the crust, again, I was a little wary about it being too chunky, but, again, it was great. I let it simmer longer than called for, and I think that helped break down the whole tomates. It has a great flavor and will be much better served plain on pasta than a regular sauce would be.
Horseradish makes this sauce.  Pretty good!
